structured_extraction.program_description: A regional media training and production facility that provides training in video and audio production, access to professional-grade equipment, and facility access to help businesses, nonprofits, schools, and government agencies develop media content and storytelling skills to support economic growth and competitiveness.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Center offers three core services: (1) training in practical skills including video shooting and editing, audio recording, production equipment operation, and audience identification and engagement; (2) access to professional-grade equipment including 4K-capable cameras, lighting kits, green screens, mobile stabilization tools, and portable podcasting kits for up to four participants; (3) facility access including a four-person podcasting suite, audio and video editing space connected to a 340-terabyte media server, and a five-camera HD television studio equipped with teleprompters and multi-channel recording.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, nonprofits, schools, government agencies, and individuals in Western Maryland, South Central Pennsylvania, and Northeastern West Virginia who need to develop media content and storytelling capabilities for marketing, recruitment, tourism, and communication purposes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating professional-quality video and audio content for websites, social media platforms, recruitment campaigns, tourism promotion, corporate communications, and internal organizational messaging.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves Western Maryland, South Central Pennsylvania, and Northeastern West Virginia. The Center is located at Frostburg State University in Allegany County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Not specified on this page. Contact the Center or Frostburg State University for information about enrollment and participation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Scholarship assistance to help students affected by flooding to continue their pursuit of higher education despite the financial challenges they face.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship funding to remove financial barriers caused by the flood and help students stay on track with their educational and career goals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current and newly admitted students at Allegany College of Maryland who have been impacted by flooding
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses and removal of financial barriers caused by flooding
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Allegany County
requirements_list: Must be a current student or newly admitted for upcoming term at Allegany College of Maryland
Must have been impacted by flooding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Allegany College of Maryland for application procedures and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program for Allegany County residents to pursue higher education at Allegany College of Maryland or Frostburg State University. The program is funded by a portion of the county government's annual revenue from video lottery machines at Rocky Gap Casino Resort.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship funds provided to eligible residents for educational expenses at the designated institutions. Funding comes from 2.25% of annual gross revenue generated by video lottery machines at Rocky Gap Casino Resort, distributed on a monthly basis.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Allegany College Foundation, Inc. / Frostburg State University Financial Aid Office
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Allegany County, Maryland with a minimum three-year residency requirement who wish to attend Allegany College of Maryland or Frostburg State University.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses at Allegany College of Maryland or Frostburg State University.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to residents of Allegany County, Maryland only. Applicants must meet a minimum three-year residency requirement in Allegany County.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Allegany County, Maryland
Must have a minimum three-year residency in Allegany County
Must be enrolling at or attending Allegany College of Maryland or Frostburg State University
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Allegany College of Maryland Foundation or Frostburg State University Financial Aid Office for application information and to apply. Applications are processed through each institution's scholarship application system.

structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund Financial Hardship Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows eligible residents to request a financial hardship exemption from the Bay Restoration Fund fee (flush tax) that is mandated by the State of Maryland for Chesapeake Bay restoration purposes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exemption from the Bay Restoration Fund fee (flush tax) for individuals facing financial hardship. Eligible residents may request an exemption from paying the annual Bay Restoration Fund fee. A new application must be completed every year to be considered for the exemption. The exemption, if approved, waives the mandatory Bay Restoration Fund fee collected for Chesapeake Bay restoration efforts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Allegany County residents who own properties subject to the Bay Restoration Fund fee and are experiencing financial hardship.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The exemption waives the mandatory Bay Restoration Fund fee (flush tax) collected for Chesapeake Bay restoration efforts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Allegany County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an Allegany County resident who owns a property subject to the Bay Restoration Fund fee
Must demonstrate financial hardship according to county standards
Must complete a new application every year
Applications must be submitted to Allegany County Department of Finance or designated office
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete the Bay Restoration Fund Financial Hardship Exemption Application form. The form requires documentation of financial hardship. A new application must be submitted annually to maintain or renew exemption status. Completed applications should be submitted to the Allegany County Department of Finance. Contact the county at 301-777-5965 for more information and to obtain application materials.

structured_extraction.program_description: A volunteer emergency services program that recruits and trains individuals to serve as firefighters or emergency medical services (EMS) providers in Allegany County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Volunteers receive free local training in firefighter and emergency medical technician courses provided by the Maryland Fire and Rescue Institute. Maryland residents who volunteer receive a $7,000 tax credit. The program also offers Length of Service Awards Program retirement benefits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals at least 18 years old who want to serve as volunteer firefighters or EMS providers in Allegany County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in firefighting, emergency medicine, and related courses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Allegany County, Maryland.
requirements_list: At least 18 years old
Willing to serve as a firefighter or emergency medical services provider
Must be a member of a local fire or EMS department to receive Maryland Fire and Rescue Institute training
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit an online volunteer interest form or visit your local fire or EMS department to discuss membership opportunities. Upon approval, applicants are placed on a probationary period during which free local training can begin.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frostburg Main Street Structural Stabilization Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program provides financial support to address critical structural barriers to redevelopment in downtown Frostburg. It funds essential repairs such as foundation work, framing, roof support beams, and roofing to stabilize at-risk historic and commercial buildings along the Main Street corridor.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Frostburg and Allegany County received $250,000 in state funding under the Strategic Demolition Fund to support structural stabilization work. Grants cover structural repairs including foundation repairs, framing, roof support beams, and roofing for eligible commercial and mixed-use properties. The funding is distributed based on competitive review of applications using a project rubric.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications will open later this summer
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit property owners in good standing with the city, county, and state who own commercial or mixed-use buildings within Frostburg's Main Street district.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Structural repairs including foundation repairs, framing, roof support beams, roofing, and other work that addresses the four walls and interior walls of buildings to make them safe and stable for redevelopment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within Frostburg's Main Street district in Frostburg, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within Frostburg's Main Street district
Property must be commercial or mixed-use (first floor storefront with residential units above)
Property must be owned by a for-profit, tax-paying entity in good standing with the city, county, and state
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: City staff manage applications and intake. A review committee evaluates applications based on a project rubric. County staff oversee fund distribution and compliance. Interested property owners should begin gathering information about their properties' structural needs and project timelines.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provided financial assistance to support adaptive reuse and redevelopment projects in Allegany County. The program made funds available to projects seeking to redevelop vacant or underutilized buildings in downtowns and main streets across Allegany County, with emphasis on mixed-use development and upper story living. It also supported the renovation and conversion of historic and deteriorated buildings into modern residential, commercial, or mixed-use spaces that revitalize the county's architectural landscape and support economic development.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A one-time, two-million dollar grant program that funded projects for downtown and main street redevelopment with special emphasis on mixed-use and upper story living. Individual projects could receive significant awards; for example, the McMullen Building project received $250,000 to support renovation costs associated with converting a historic former department store building into luxury apartments and commercial space.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, developers, and businesses seeking to redevelop vacant or underutilized buildings in Allegany County downtowns and main streets, including adaptive reuse and renovation of historic or deteriorated buildings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Redevelopment of vacant or underutilized buildings in downtowns and main streets, with special emphasis on mixed-use development and upper story living. Eligible costs include renovation and redevelopment costs associated with adaptive reuse projects, such as structural repairs, system replacements, interior improvements, and conversion of buildings into residential, commercial, or mixed-use spaces.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Downtown and main street areas in Allegany County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must involve adaptive reuse or redevelopment of an existing building
Property must be located in Allegany County
Projects in downtown and main street areas are prioritized, with emphasis on mixed-use and upper story living
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit proposals for adaptive reuse and redevelopment projects. The program awards grants to selected projects based on merit and potential community impact.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) Flood Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: Funding to replace furnaces and hot water tanks damaged in the flood. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development announced $1 million in new funding specifically for this purpose as a separate application from previous flood relief programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding to replace furnaces and hot water tanks damaged in the flood. Amount per applicant not specified in the source material.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Flood-impacted residents whose furnaces or hot water tanks were damaged
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of furnaces and hot water tanks damaged in the flood
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Counties affected by the flood including Allegany County
requirements_list: Primary residence furnace or hot water tank was damaged in the flood
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the DHCD website at https://news.maryland.gov/dhcd/2025/10/31/maryland-energy-assistance-program-meap-flood-assistance/

structured_extraction.program_description: Program Open Space Local provides financial and technical assistance to local subdivisions for the planning, acquisition, and development of recreation land or open space areas for public use. The program acquires outdoor recreation and open space areas and administers funds made available through the Outdoor Recreation Land Loan of 1969 and the Land and Water Conservation Fund of the National Park Service, U.S. Department of the Interior. Since its establishment in 1969, over 6,200 park and conservation area projects have been assisted through Program Open Space Local grants.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Program Open Space Local provides grants to local subdivisions for planning, acquisition, and development of recreation land or open space areas for public use. Funding is made available through the Outdoor Recreation Land Loan of 1969 and the Land and Water Conservation Fund of the National Park Service. Over 6,200 park and conservation area projects have been assisted through Program Open Space Local grants since 1969. Funds support the acquisition, development, and planning of outdoor recreation and open space areas available for public use, including parks, playgrounds, athletic fields, greenways, nature preserves, and conservation areas.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY26 public comment period through Thursday, October 16th
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local subdivisions in Allegany County, Maryland seeking to develop parks and conservation areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, acquisition, and development of recreation land or open space areas for public use, including parks, playgrounds, athletic fields, greenways, nature preserves, and conservation areas
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Allegany County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicants must be local subdivisions (municipalities, counties, or other governmental entities)
Projects must involve outdoor recreation land or open space areas available for public use
Projects must align with local recreation and land preservation plans
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact Andrew Cowan at the Allegany County Department of Community Development for application details and requirements. The county commissioners review and approve funding recommendations after the public comment period. Applications are evaluated based on project merit, public benefit, and alignment with county recreation and preservation goals.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual fund that awards capital grants to local businesses in Allegany County for projects that enhance their operations and benefit patrons at Rocky Gap Casino Resort. The fund is generated from slot machine revenue at Rocky Gap Casino Resort, with the county receiving 5.5% of revenue. By state law, 20% of this revenue must be awarded for capital requests.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual capital grants funded by 20% of the county's slot machine revenue from Rocky Gap Casino Resort. The exact amount awarded varies based on selected projects and Local Development Council deliberations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local for-profit businesses in Allegany County seeking capital funding for projects that benefit operations and enhance Rocky Gap Casino Resort offerings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects that expand business offerings, enhance operations, create local employment, and provide amenities for local residents and tourists at or near Rocky Gap Casino Resort.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Allegany County, Maryland
requirements_list: Projects must be evaluated by the Local Development Council
Projects should benefit Rocky Gap Casino Resort and local community
Projects should create local jobs and business expansion opportunities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses submit requests to the 15-member Local Development Council, which meets annually to deliberate and award funds generated from Rocky Gap Casino Resort slot machine revenue.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rocky Gap Slots Revenue Grant Program (Non-Profit & Municipal)
structured_extraction.program_description: A funding program for Allegany County non-profits and municipalities that distributes a portion of slot machine revenue generated from Rocky Gap Casino. By state law, 20% of Allegany County's 5.5% share of slots revenues must be spent on capital requests from eligible non-profits and municipalities. The program funds capital projects and improvements only; operating expenses are not eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded from 5.5% of slot machine revenues generated at Rocky Gap Casino. By state law, 20% of this revenue must be spent on capital requests from Allegany County municipalities and non-profits. Capital funding is awarded to eligible non-profits and municipalities in Allegany County. Funds may only be used for capital-related items and cannot be used for operating expenses. Awards are announced and disbursed within approximately six weeks after review. Grant amounts vary based on available revenue and submitted requests.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and municipalities located in Allegany County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital-related items and projects only. Funds cannot be used for operating expenses. Eligible capital projects may include facility improvements, equipment purchases, infrastructure upgrades, building renovations, and other one-time capital expenditures that benefit the organization or community.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Allegany County, Maryland only
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit organization or municipality
Located in Allegany County
Request must be for capital items or projects only, not operating expenses
Application or letter of request must include information on non-profit or municipality status, mission or purpose, description of capital needs, and total amount requested
Project must have identifiable public benefit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply using the Municipal & Non-Profit Grant Request Form available online. Alternatively, submit a letter of request via email or mail to Jason M. Bennett at jbennett@alleganygov.org or by mail to Allegany County Local Development Council. The application or letter should include: (1) proof of non-profit or municipality status; (2) mission or purpose statement; (3) detailed description of capital needs; and (4) total amount requested. Requests are reviewed by the Allegany County Local Development Council sub-committee, which evaluates applications and makes recommendations to the Allegany County Commissioners for final approval. Awards are announced and disbursed within approximately six weeks of final approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program that provides funding to support economic development and business expansion projects in eligible areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides grants to support business expansion projects. 1812 Brewery received a $750,000 grant to construct a new 4,000-square-foot building for brewing and canning operations and to add five additional barrels for brewing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses seeking to expand operations and create jobs in eligible counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for construction of new buildings, purchase of equipment, and other capital improvements related to business expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Allegany County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact their county's economic development staff for information about the application process and to discuss their business plans.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Business Administration (SBA) Disaster Loans (Flood Assistance)
structured_extraction.program_description: Low-interest loans available to homeowners, renters, businesses, and private non-profits located in disaster-declared counties who sustained damages from flooding. The program provides funds to replace or repair primary residences, personal property, and business losses not fully covered by insurance. Assistance is available under Pennsylvania Disaster Number PA-20019, which includes Allegany County and contiguous counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners can receive up to $500,000 to replace or repair primary residences and up to $100,000 to replace or repair personal property. Businesses and most private non-profits may apply for up to $2 million to cover disaster losses not fully covered by insurance. Long-term repayment options are available with terms up to a maximum of 30 years, determined on a case-by-case basis based on each borrower's ability to repay. Renters may also apply for assistance to repair or replace personal property damaged in the disaster.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 21, 2025 for physical damages; February 23, 2026 for economic injury disaster loans (EIDL applications)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, renters, businesses, and private non-profits located in disaster-declared counties who sustained damages from the May 13, 2025 flooding
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replace or repair primary residences, personal property, and business losses not fully covered by insurance
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Allegany County and contiguous counties (Garrett and Washington counties) included under Pennsylvania Disaster Number PA-20019 declaration
requirements_list: Must be located in a disaster-declared county under PA-20019
Must have sustained damages from the May 13, 2025 flooding
Must have losses not fully covered by insurance
Businesses and non-profits must demonstrate losses not fully covered by insurance
Applicants must meet SBA creditworthiness requirements
Applicants must be unable to obtain credit elsewhere
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can obtain information and loan applications by: (1) Calling the SBA's Customer Service Center at 1-800-659-2955 or 1-800-877-8339 (TTY); (2) Emailing DisasterCustomerService@sba.gov; (3) Visiting online at https://lending.sba.gov/; or (4) Visiting in person. Applicants should reference Pennsylvania Disaster Number PA-20019 when applying. Completed applications must be submitted before the respective deadline (July 21, 2025 for physical damage loans; February 23, 2026 for EIDL).

structured_extraction.program_name: Tri-County Council Small Business Flood Recovery Loans
structured_extraction.program_description: Low-interest loans up to $20,000 to assist businesses with flood recovery expenses, offered through the Tri-County Council.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $20,000 with 0% interest for 2-5 year terms to assist with flood recovery.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Flood-impacted businesses in the region
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Flood recovery expenses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Tri-County Council service area
requirements_list: Impacted by the flood
Business owner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email relief@tccwmd.org or call 301-689-1300 for more information and loan application form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A low-interest, partially forgivable loan program that helps Allegany County-based businesses grow their operations. The program supports new companies establishing themselves in Allegany County as well as existing companies looking to create more jobs, increase their ability to sell products outside the area, or improve their local community presence. Companies that meet their success metrics can have up to half of their loan forgiven over the agreed upon term.
structured_extraction.agency: Allegany County Economic and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers low-interest loans from $10,000 to $50,000. Businesses can have up to 50% of the loan forgiven if they meet performance goals, such as job creation. Loans over $40,000 require a one-to-one match from the business. The county may also defer payments for up to six months after the business receives the loan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, for-profit businesses in Allegany County with fewer than 15 full-time employees that are ready to expand operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used to purchase tangible assets that help the business grow, such as equipment and furniture. Funds cannot be used for staff salaries, buying or improving an existing building, or constructing a new building.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have a physical location in Allegany County. Must own the property or have a long-term commercial lease. A home-based business can apply if its expansion plan includes moving to a commercial location.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit entity in good standing with Allegany County and the State of Maryland.
Must have fewer than 15 full-time employees.
Must have a physical presence in Allegany County.
Must receive a formal invitation from Allegany County Economic and Community Development to apply.
A 1:1 funding match is required for loans over $40,000.
Must provide a business plan approved by the local Small Business Development Center.
Funds must be spent within 24 months of loan approval to qualify for forgiveness.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact the Allegany County Economic and Community Development team to discuss your project. You must meet certain criteria and then receive a formal invitation to apply. After you apply, a review committee will assess your application. The committee then submits its recommendations to the County Commissioners for final approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program supports businesses and research institutions in Allegany County in developing new environmental technologies. It provides grants to help pay for research conducted at the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science Appalachian Laboratory, with qualifying projects able to receive up to $50,000 in matching funds for the development of new environmental technology products or services.
structured_extraction.agency: Allegany County Economic and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a matching grant of up to $50,000 for research projects developing new environmental technology. The grant pays for half of a project's total cost (1:1 match required), with the maximum grant amount being $50,000. Funds are used for costs of research or lab use contracted through the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science Appalachian Laboratory.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses and research institutions in Allegany County that develop new products or services in environmental science and technology.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Research and development of new environmental technology; costs of research or lab use contracted through the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science Appalachian Laboratory for the purpose of developing a new product or service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Allegany County. Businesses must have a physical location in Allegany County through ownership or a long-term commercial lease. A home-based business can apply if it shows a clear plan to move into a commercial space.
requirements_list: Applicants must be for-profit, tax-paying entities in good standing with Allegany County and Maryland.
Businesses must apply by formal invitation only.
The business must demonstrate the ability to offer a tangible product or service.
A 1:1 match for research costs is required.
All research must be contracted through the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science (UMCES) Appalachian Laboratory.
A quote for services and a letter of approval from the Appalachian Lab is required for the application.
Grant recipients must keep a commercial presence in Allegany County for at least four years after receiving the award.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact the Allegany County Economic and Community Development team to discuss your project. If eligible, they will give you a formal invitation to apply. You must get a project quote and a letter of approval from the Appalachian Lab. Then, submit your application with these documents and a project narrative. County staff and the Lab review applications and send recommendations to the County Commissioners for final approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Agricultural Business Improvement Grant (ABIG) Program is a matching grant program administered by Anne Arundel County that provides funding of up to $10,000 to farm-based businesses and commercial watermen in Anne Arundel County to help them grow their operations, expand revenue, and support agricultural and seafood industries. Eligible projects include fencing, livestock, plant stock, equipment purchases, facility improvements, barn construction and repairs, storage facilities, software, infrastructure upgrades, and other capital projects. The program also supports agricultural education opportunities and increasing the local-grown food supply. Applications are numerically scored based on project impact criteria, and top-ranked projects receive funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants of up to $10,000 are awarded to farm-based businesses and commercial watermen in Anne Arundel County. Grant recipients are required to contribute at least 50% of their own project costs. Matching funds may not include labor or state and federal grants or cost share. Funds can be used for fencing, livestock, plant stock, equipment purchases, facility improvements, barn construction and repairs, storage facilities, software, infrastructure upgrades, and other capital projects. Proof of project completion must be submitted within one year of the grant award. Applications are numerically scored and top-ranked projects receive funding. Additional funding may be available through MARBIDCO cost-sharing for qualifying initiatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farm-based business owners, farm-based businesses, and commercial watermen operating in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fencing, livestock, plant stock, equipment purchases, facility improvements, barn construction and repairs, storage facilities, software, infrastructure upgrades, and other capital projects that increase revenue, retain or increase employees, expand operations or increase efficiency, increase the local-grown food supply, or provide agricultural education opportunities. Administrative expenses, events, and décor are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland only. Applicants must own and operate a farm or commercial watermen business in Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Applicant must own and operate a farm or be a commercial watermen business located in Anne Arundel County
Must submit a letter of reference from Anne Arundel Soil Conservation District, University of Maryland Extension, Anne Arundel County Farm Bureau, or 4-H/FFA Leader
Grant recipients must contribute at least 50% of their own money to the project
Matching funds may not include labor or state and federal grants or cost share
Proof of project completion must be submitted within one year of grant award

Projects are numerically scored based on impact to increase revenue, increase or retain employees, expand operations or increase efficiency, increase local-grown food supply, or provide agricultural education opportunities
Administrative expenses, events, and décor are not eligible uses of funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a grant application along with a letter of reference from an approved organization (Anne Arundel Soil Conservation District, University of Maryland Extension, Anne Arundel County Farm Bureau, or 4-H/FFA Leader) by the application deadline. Applications are numerically scored based on project impact criteria including potential to increase revenue, create or retain jobs, expand operations, improve efficiency, increase local food supply, or offer agricultural education. The highest-ranked projects are selected for funding.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that assists agricultural businesses and farms in Anne Arundel County with the disposal of scrap tires generated from farming operations, which is otherwise prohibited. It provides support for disposal costs and services for agricultural tires used in farming.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This program provides disposal services and financial support for scrap tire disposal costs for agricultural tires used in farming operations, addressing an otherwise prohibited disposal activity.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers, farm-based businesses, and farms in Anne Arundel County with agricultural scrap tires to dispose of.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Disposal of agricultural scrap tires generated from farming operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must be a farm or agricultural business
Tires must be agricultural tires used in farming operations

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Agricultural and Woodland Preservation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A purchase of development rights program begun in 1990 that permanently protects agricultural and woodland land from development in Anne Arundel County. Landowners voluntarily place easements on their property to preserve it for agricultural and forestry uses in perpetuity. The program allows parcels of 50 acres or greater of agricultural land (or a minimum of 25 acres of contiguous woodland) to participate and requires resource management plans as part of the protection element. Funds are contingent on approval by the County Executive and County Council during the annual capital budget cycle.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases a permanent easement on the property at 60% of the appraised Fair Market Value, depending on County funding availability. Recent easement offers have ranged from approximately $8,000 to $11,000 per acre, with cash paid at settlement. Funds are contingent on approval by the County Executive and County Council during the annual capital budget cycle.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in Anne Arundel County with agricultural or woodland property of 50 acres or greater
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding is used to purchase development rights on agricultural and woodland land. Permitted activities include timbering or any agricultural use of the land, preserving it from development in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland only. Properties must meet specific acreage and soils criteria within the County.
requirements_list: Parcel must have 50 acres of agricultural land or more, OR have a minimum of 25 acres of contiguous woodland
Must meet certain soils criteria
Must have an active Soil and Water Quality Conservation Plan (for agricultural land) or an active Forest Stewardship/Forest Management Plan (for woodland)
Easement is voluntary and permanent (in perpetuity)
Funds are contingent on approval by the County Executive and County Council during the annual capital budget cycle
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowner interest forms the basis for requesting county funds each year during the capital budget cycle. Contact the Agricultural Program Planner (Billy Gorski) to inquire about eligibility and the application process. Application deadlines are November 1 and April 1 each year. Funds are contingent on approval by the County Executive and County Council.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund (CRRF) Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funded by a portion of sales tax from adult-use recreational cannabis sales in Anne Arundel County. The program supports community-based initiatives intended to benefit low-income communities through 11 funds within a special revenue fund. Priority is given to organizations serving residents in Disproportionately Impacted Areas (DIAs) as designated by the Maryland Office of Social Equity. The Anne Arundel County Community Reinvestment and Repair Commission (CRRC) oversees the program and prioritizes projects addressing Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services, Education and Youth Enrichment and After School Activities, Housing and Homelessness Prevention Services, and Workforce Development and Employment Training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available for community-based initiatives benefiting low-income communities in Anne Arundel County through the Community Reinvestment and Repair Special Revenue Fund, which receives revenue from the State Cannabis Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund. The program supports multiple funding categories including Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services, Housing and Homelessness Prevention Services, Workforce Development and Employment Training, and Education, Youth Enrichment, and After-School Activities. In Fiscal Year 2026, total funding awarded was $1,691,200 across multiple grantees. Applications are submitted through the Neighborly Portal at https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/acds/Participant. Funding allocations are based on recommendations from the Anne Arundel County Community Reinvestment and Repair Commission (CRRC), which prioritizes projects addressing the four strategic priority areas. Funds may not be expended for law enforcement agencies or activities, and expended funds must be supplemental to and may not supplant funding that otherwise would be appropriated for county programs that existed prior to July 1, 2023.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and community-based organizations serving low-income communities in Anne Arundel County, with priority given to those serving residents in Disproportionately Impacted Areas (DIAs). Eight zip codes are designated as DIAs by the Maryland Office of Social Equity, and the CRRC has identified ten additional priority zip codes: 21060, 21061, 21113, 21122, 21144, 21225, 21401, 21403, 20724, and 20755.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding must address one or more of the following strategic priorities: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services, Education and Youth Enrichment and After School Activities, Housing and Homelessness Prevention Services, or Workforce Development and Employment Training. Funds may not be expended for law enforcement agencies or activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, with priority given to Disproportionately Impacted Areas (DIAs). Eight zip codes in Anne Arundel County have been designated as DIAs by the Maryland Office of Social Equity. The Anne Arundel County CRRC has identified ten additional priority zip codes: 21060, 21061, 21113, 21122, 21144, 21225, 21401, 21403, 20724, and 20755. Community-based initiatives must serve residents of Anne Arundel County or Disproportionately Impacted Areas as defined in the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article of the State Code.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization
Projects must be community-based initiatives intended to benefit low-income communities
Eligible organizations must serve residents, with priority given to those in Disproportionately Impacted Areas (DIAs)

Projects must address one or more of the following: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Services, Education and Youth Enrichment and After School Activities, Housing and Homelessness Prevention Services, or Workforce Development and Employment Training
Funds expended must be supplemental to and may not supplant funding that otherwise would be appropriated for county programs that existed prior to July 1, 2023
Funds may not be expended for law enforcement agencies or activities
Free registration for a Neighborly account is required to submit an application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Neighborly Portal at https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/acds/Participant. Free registration for a Neighborly account is required. Application trainings are provided on multiple dates in late January at various locations including Zoom, the Heritage Complex in Annapolis, Brooklyn Park Library, Severn Center, and Busch Annapolis Library. The Anne Arundel County Community Reinvestment and Repair Commission (CRRC) reviews applications and develops recommendations for fund use, which are submitted to the County Executive by March 1 each year. The Commission's recommendations are advisory in nature and do not require the County Executive to award any particular grant. For additional information, visit the ACDS website at https://acdsinc.org/funding-opportunities/community-reinvestment-and-repair-commission-grants/ or contact nonprofitcenter@aacounty.org or (410) 222-6999.

structured_extraction.program_name: Anne Arundel County Watershed Restoration Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program funds on-the-ground watershed restoration projects in Anne Arundel County and the City of Annapolis that reduce stormwater flowing into local waterways, treat and filter pollutants from impervious surfaces, and engage residents in restoring and protecting local rivers and streams. Administered by the Chesapeake Bay Trust on behalf of Anne Arundel County, the program awards grants to certified 501(c) nonprofit organizations including local watershed groups, community associations, homeowners associations, service and youth groups, and faith-based organizations.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers grants to fund watershed restoration projects. Total funding anticipated is $1,000,000 available for awards in Anne Arundel County and $300,000 available for awards in the City of Annapolis. Funding requests generally do not exceed $300,000, though requests larger than this amount may be approved with prior contact to the Trust's Senior Program Officer. Matching or leveraged resources are not required but are viewed favorably. Projects are evaluated based on site conditions including landowner support, site access, slope characteristics, right-of-way status, utility presence, downstream infrastructure concerns, and wetland/stream proximity. Projects with all or most favorable parameters ('Easy Sites') are most competitive. Projects with any parameters in the 'Poor Site' category are not competitive.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: RFPs typically open in the Fall and close in the Spring
structured_extraction.contact_name: Katie Mullen (BWPR Grants Manager), Sarah T. Koser (Chesapeake Bay Trust Senior Program Officer), Raghu Badami (PE), Melissa Harlinski, Melissa Bragg
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified 501(c) non-profit organizations based in Anne Arundel County, including local watershed groups, community associations, homeowners associations, service and youth groups, and faith-based organizations, seeking to implement watershed restoration projects on community or public property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects must accomplish on-the-ground restoration that treats rainwater runoff from impervious surfaces. Projects can include watershed restoration practices such as living shorelines, stream restoration, bioretention, rain gardens, stormwater management, and impervious surface removal. Small-scale projects (Category 1) have a disturbance footprint less than 5,000 square feet or disturb less than 100 cubic yards of earth. Large-scale projects (Category 2) have a disturbance footprint greater than 5,000 square feet or disturb more than 100 cubic yards of earth. Projects must be located on community or public property, including non-profit property, private property, City of Annapolis-owned property, or public school properties with landowner support. All projects must provide documentation including BMP metrics, design plans, as-builts upon completion, design protocol information, GIS files, and drainage area maps.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Anne Arundel County or the City of Annapolis, Maryland. At least one project partner must represent a stakeholder group based in Anne Arundel County or the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Eligible applicants must be certified 501(c) non-profit organizations
Applications must include at least one partner that represents a stakeholder group based in Anne Arundel County (including the City of Annapolis)

Projects must accomplish on-the-ground restoration that treats rainwater runoff from impervious surfaces at cost-effective prices or demonstrates accomplishment of another metric to help the County and City meet local water quality and runoff reduction improvement goals
Applicants must provide sound technical designs and project budgets
Landowner assurance of support must be included in the application if the project is on non-profit, private, City of Annapolis-owned, or public school properties
Project must be located on community or public property
Project must reduce stormwater flowing into local waterways

Applicants should evaluate project sites using site selection guidelines including single landowner preference, complete landowner support for maintenance agreement with Anne Arundel County DPW, sufficient site access away from buildings and infrastructure, gentle slopes (less than 8%), not in right of way, no existing utilities, and no threat to downstream infrastructure
Projects must provide as-builts, design plans, and reports upon completion
Projects must provide GIS shapefiles with project location, line features for linear projects (stream restoration, stabilization), polygon features for other BMPs, and drainage area maps
Projects must be assigned a Storm ID (Unique ID) by the County and reference this ID in all project documents

Projects located on steep slopes (8% to 15%) may be competitive if knowledgeable partners with experience in complex water quality projects are included; projects on very steep slopes (greater than 15%) require certification by a professional engineer

Projects in right of way, with existing utilities, with multiple landowners, or with downstream infrastructure concerns may be competitive if experienced partners are included and concerns are adequately addressed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a Request for Proposals (RFP) response to the Chesapeake Bay Trust, which administers the program on behalf of Anne Arundel County. RFPs are solicited annually, typically opening in the Fall and closing in the Spring. Applicants should review the Guidelines for Selecting the Right Project Site to evaluate whether their proposed project meets favorable site characteristics. For more information and this year's RFP, visit the application page on the Chesapeake Bay Trust website. Applicants should provide sound technical designs and project budgets as outlined in the application package. Prior to submitting an RFP, applicants are encouraged to contact the Chesapeake Bay Trust or Anne Arundel County Watershed Protection and Restoration Program staff to discuss potential project sites. Upon approval and implementation, applicants must report project data including BMP metrics, as-builts, design plans, drainage area maps, GIS files, and project status updates (Design, Under Construction, or Complete) on a fiscal year cycle. Small projects may have streamlined reporting requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A place-based community development model that engages local communities and brings wrap-around services and supports to families living in high-need areas to reduce poverty and the number of children in out-of-home placements. The program uses a collaborative, multi-dimensional approach involving local agencies, community organizations, residents, faith leaders, business owners, and service providers working together to create supports that address family wellness, stability, and child well-being.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides wrap-around services and community support through a collaborative partnership model. Services and supports are coordinated among local agencies, community organizations, and service providers to address family wellness and stability in designated high-need communities. Programming focuses on coordinating support systems for youth based on trusted relationships, developing enhanced positive pathways to economic opportunity, providing safe welcoming and hope-filled spaces in communities, and utilizing place-based and two-generation approaches. Services include coordination of resources for basic needs, job training and employment pathways, affordable childcare options, mental health and substance use support, healthcare access including prenatal care and dental care, safe transportation, housing assistance, early childhood education, youth mentorship and development, community schooling models, and trauma-informed programming. The program operates across four designated Communities of Hope neighborhoods with specific annual roadmaps and performance measures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families living in high-need communities in Anne Arundel County, local agencies, community organizations, faith leaders, business owners, and service providers. Specific focus on residents in Brooklyn Park (North County, zip code 21225), West County (Severn/Meade), Annapolis (zip codes 21401 and 21403), and South County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wrap-around services and community supports to address family wellness, stability, poverty reduction, and preventing children from entering out-of-home placements. Includes basic needs assistance, employment and job training services, affordable childcare, mental and behavioral health services, healthcare access, safe transportation, affordable housing resources, early childhood education and school readiness programming, youth development and mentorship, recreational opportunities, and community building initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Four designated Communities of Hope neighborhoods in Anne Arundel County: Brooklyn Park (North County, zip code 21225), West County (Severn/Meade), Annapolis (zip codes 21401 and 21403), and South County. These neighborhoods were identified based on concentrated poverty, health disparities, and other social determinants of health indicators documented in the county needs assessment.
requirements_list: Residents must live in one of the four designated Communities of Hope neighborhoods
Partnership with local agencies, community organizations, and service providers required for program participation
Collaboration and coordination among service providers needed to address identified community needs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested parties and potential partners should contact the Community of Hope Director or community liaison to learn more about the program and partnership opportunities. Each neighborhood has developed an annual roadmap with specific priorities and strategies. Residents and organizations can engage through community awareness and outreach efforts, partner communication channels, and collaborative planning meetings to address the shared priorities and strategies outlined in each community's roadmap.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program provided by Anne Arundel County to eligible nonprofit organizations to support programs and projects that improve and enrich the lives of Anne Arundel County residents and communities. Funding can support program operations, increase the impact of existing programs, pilot new programs, capacity building initiatives, or make one-time equipment purchases. Proposals must align with County Executive priorities, including providing services to underserved populations, addressing community health and well-being, promoting equity and inclusion, and eliminating the Opportunity Gap in education. Collaborative projects are preferred but not required.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $15,000 to $50,000 per organization, with approximately $2 million total anticipated to be available for FY2027. Grants support two types of activities: (1) Program/Project Support including program/project-specific staff costs, supplies, travel, equipment, and a percentage of administrative overhead proportional to the program's budget relative to the organization's overall operating budget; and (2) Capacity Building Support for one-time funds to assist nonprofits in building organizational efficiencies and sustainability, including strategic planning, governance, professional development, technology improvements, and systems innovation. Administrative overhead must not exceed 5% of the total grant award amount. Funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis following a fully executed grant agreement with ACDS.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: All applications are due by 12 p.m. on Wednesday, February 18, 2026.

Capacity building support for strategic planning, governance, professional development, technology improvements, and systems innovation. Eligible uses include operating existing programs, increasing program impact, piloting new programs, one-time projects, and small equipment purchases. Administrative overhead must not exceed 5% of total grant award.

If applying with a Fiscal Sponsor, must have a Letter of Partnership signed by both organizations
Faith-based organizations must adhere to Guidelines on Funding Faith-Based Organizations & Related Activities

Proposals should address at least one County Executive priority: providing services to underserved populations, addressing health and well-being of communities, promoting equity and inclusion, or eliminating the Opportunity Gap in education
Collaborative projects are preferred but not required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are completed online through Arundel Community Development Services' (ACDS) Neighborly Portal at https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/acds/participant. Applicants must create an account on the portal if not already done. Google Chrome is recommended for completing the application. Applications opened January 7, 2026, and a virtual training was held on Friday, January 9, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. via Zoom with recorded sessions available. All applications are due by 12:00 p.m. EST on Wednesday, February 18, 2026. Applications will be initially screened for basic eligibility and compliance by ACDS staff, then reviewed by a panel of County agency representatives. The County Agency Panel makes final recommendations for each award and funding amount to the County Executive's Office. Panel recommendations are reviewed and final decisions made by the County Executive. Applicants will be notified of award in writing by July 1, 2026. Upon award, grantees must enter into a grant agreement with ACDS defining organizational responsibilities and payment schedule. Grantees must provide an Insurance Certificate naming ACDS as additional insured and board resolution authorizing the grant signatory. Grantees should not begin incurring expenses until the fully executed grant agreement is in place. Once awarded, grantees must follow ACDS invoicing procedures, submit progress reports and final reports, and schedule a monitoring visit with ACDS staff. Grant funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: County Agricultural and Woodland District Agreements
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides property tax credits to landowners who agree to establish a 10-year District Agreement on their land to preserve agriculture and woodland resources. Landowners receive a tax credit against their annual County Property Tax bill in exchange for agreeing to protective covenants that preserve agricultural or woodland use.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners who qualify receive an Agricultural Tax Credit applied to the County Real Estate Tax portion of their Real Property Tax Bill. The credit is available for the 10-year term of the District Agreement and must be renewed every 10 years to maintain the benefit. Landowners are invoiced only for State property taxes, County fees and charges, not the County Real Estate Tax portion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are encouraged to be submitted by March 31 for a tax credit on the following fiscal year tax bill
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with agricultural or woodland property in Anne Arundel County who meet the acreage and land use requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit applies to the County Real Estate Tax portion of the Real Property Tax Bill for qualifying agricultural or woodland properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be within Rural Agricultural (RA) or Residential Low Density (RLD) zoning districts in Anne Arundel County and outside existing or planned Water and Sewer categories 1, 2, and 3.
requirements_list: For Agricultural Districts: at least 50 contiguous acres devoted to agriculture (or multiple contiguous properties with each at least 10 acres totaling 50 or more acres)
Meet certain USDA Soil Capability Classes criteria
Have an active Soil and Water Conservation Plan in place
Property must be within Rural Agricultural (RA) or Residential Low Density (RLD) zoning districts
Property must be outside existing or planned Water and Sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
For Woodland Districts: at least 10 contiguous acres of woodlands (or 10-acre minimum per landowner when adding to an existing woodland district)
Have a Forest Management Plan
Meet Zoning criteria for woodland districts
Meet Water and Sewer Categories requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Agricultural and Woodland Preservation staff to determine if your property qualifies and to receive assistance with the application process. Submit your application anytime, though applications submitted by March 31 are encouraged for a tax credit on the following fiscal year. Upon approval, the landowner enters into a District Agreement which is recorded in the County Land Records.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by Anne Arundel County that helps small brick-and-mortar businesses and nonprofits acquire digital tools and services to operate in an increasingly digital economy. Funded with $500,000 in federal American Recovery Act funds, the program provided grants of up to $10,000 per recipient to support digital transformation efforts including online sales, marketing, and customer engagement. The program launched in September 2021, awarding a total of $460,800 to 144 businesses. Eligible uses include new purchases of or subscriptions to email and mobile marketing platforms, customer relationship management (CRM) software, customer rewards and loyalty programs, e-commerce platforms for online ordering and sales, and website and social media advertising.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $10,000 per recipient (an earlier round provided $3,200 per business) for the new purchase of or subscription to digital platforms and services including email and mobile marketing, customer relationship management (CRM), customer rewards and loyalty programs, e-commerce platforms for online ordering and sales, and website and social media advertising. The program was funded with $500,000 in federal American Recovery Act funds and awarded a total of $460,800 to 144 businesses.

Businesses with fewer than ten employees were prioritized.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides emergency grants to Anne Arundel County businesses and nonprofits that suffered damage and operational disruptions from the tornado and tropical storm that struck on September 1, 2021. Funded in part by the TD Charitable Foundation ($25,000 total), grants of up to $5,000 help eligible organizations repair physical property, replace equipment and inventory, and cover other legitimate business expenses related to disaster recovery. Grants do not need to be repaid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grants of up to $5,000 per eligible business or nonprofit. Funds do not need to be repaid and may be used for physical property repairs, replacement of business equipment, replacement of inventory, lease/rental support, vendor bill support, or moving expenses support related to the September 1, 2021 tornado and tropical storm disaster. Funds cannot be used for expenses reimbursed by other relief programs or covered by insurance policies. Total program funding was $25,000 from the TD Charitable Foundation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and nonprofits in Anne Arundel County with brick-and-mortar locations that are in good standing with the State of Maryland and were affected by the September 1, 2021 tornado and tropical storm.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Physical property repairs, replacement of business equipment, replacement of inventory, lease/rental support, vendor bill support, or moving expenses support. Funds cannot be used for expenses reimbursed by other relief programs or covered by insurance policies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses and nonprofits must have a brick-and-mortar location in Anne Arundel County, Maryland.

Business must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Must have suffered damage or operational disruption from the September 1, 2021 tornado and tropical storm
Submit a grant application via web form
Submit a statement listing all damages with details of loss of income
Submit a budget detailing use of grant proceeds
Submit a completed W-9 form
Available for a site visit to review damages
Self-affirm that grant funds will not be used for expenses reimbursed by other relief programs or covered insurance
Save receipts for proof of purchase for audit purposes
Submit application by 5:00 p.m. on Friday, November 5, 2021

All applicants must be available for a site visit to verify damages. Applications must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. on Friday, November 5, 2021 to be considered.

structured_extraction.program_description: The ETA Rides-On-Demand program provides subsidized on-demand transportation services to eligible seniors and people with disabilities in Anne Arundel County. Rides are provided at approximately 50 percent of normal market cost by professional drivers in appropriately equipped vehicles, offering door-to-door service with same-day availability when requested with at least two hours notice. The county provides a match of up to $75 per month for qualified residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants purchase vouchers monthly at discounted rates. Maximum purchase of $150 per month in total voucher value. Vouchers can be purchased in increments where participants pay a reduced amount and receive greater value (e.g., pay $5 for $10 worth of rides, up to pay $75 for $150 worth of rides). Door-to-door service is provided within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line, excluding airport trips. Same-day service is available with at least two hours notice. Rides are provided by professional drivers in appropriately equipped vehicles.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents aged 55 and older, or residents aged 18 and older with a disability that prevents use of public transportation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation services including rides to errands, appointments, shopping, and other destinations within Anne Arundel County and up to 20 miles outside the county line, excluding airport trips

requirements_list: Must be an Anne Arundel County resident
Must be 55 years of age or older, or 18 years of age or older with a verifiable transportation disability which precludes the person's ability to use public transportation services
Must provide a completed ETA Application
Must provide a completed Liability Form
Must provide a copy of Maryland State driver's license or Maryland State Issued ID from the Motor Vehicle Administration with an Anne Arundel County address

For persons aged 18 or older with a disability, must include a copy of SSI or SSDI award letter or completed Disability Verification Form signed by a physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, or program director of a qualified social agency serving individuals with disabilities
Must purchase vouchers by submitting completed Order Form for Rides-On-Demand with payment by check or money order
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit one of two locations during walk-in hours (8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., Monday-Friday) at 2666 Riva Road, 2nd Floor, Annapolis or 7320 Ritchie Highway, Glen Burnie, or mail completed application documents. Required documents include: (1) completed ETA Application Form, (2) completed Liability Form, (3) proof of Anne Arundel County residency (Maryland State driver's license or Maryland State Issued ID with Anne Arundel County address), and (4) disability verification if applicable (SSI/SSDI award letter or completed Disability Verification Form). After enrollment, submit the completed Order Form for Rides-On-Demand with payment (check or money order) indicating the voucher package desired (maximum $150 per month in total value). Mail application and order forms to: Easy Travel Access (ETA) Program, Department of Aging and Disabilities, 2666 Riva Road, Suite 400, Annapolis, MD 21401. After payment is processed, participant receives Rides-on-Demand card and can call the Rides-On-Demand reservations number to schedule rides.

structured_extraction.program_name: Easy Travel Access (ETA) Taxi Voucher Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The ETA Taxi Voucher Program offers discounted taxi vouchers to help older adults and people with disabilities pay for taxi fares with participating cab companies in Anne Arundel County. Participants purchase voucher books at a discount and use them for subsidized transportation to run errands, visit polling places, shop, and pick up groceries, helping seniors and people with disabilities travel independently within the county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants purchase taxi voucher coupon books at $5.00 per book, with each book worth $10.00 in taxi fare value. Qualified residents may purchase up to 15 books per month, with a maximum total monthly value of $150.00 in Easy Travel Access vouchers (combining Taxi Vouchers and/or Rides-On-Demand). The county provides a match of up to $75 per month. Vouchers can be used with participating cab companies and cannot be used for tips. Payment is made by check or money order.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Taxi fares for transportation including running errands, visiting polling places, shopping, and picking up groceries within Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County residents only. Applicants must provide proof of Anne Arundel County residency via Maryland State driver's license or Maryland State Issued ID from the Motor Vehicle Administration with an Anne Arundel County address.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed ETA Application, Liability Form, proof of Anne Arundel County residency, disability verification if applicable, and payment by check or money order. Applications may be submitted in person at one of two locations during walk-in hours (8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., Monday-Friday): 2666 Riva Road, 2nd Floor, Annapolis or 7320 Ritchie Highway, Glen Burnie. Alternatively, mail completed application documents and payment to Easy Travel Access (ETA) Program, Department of Aging and Disabilities, 2666 Riva Road, Suite 400, Annapolis, MD 21401. Once approved, participants receive taxi voucher books and may reorder monthly up to the maximum allowed ($150 total monthly value).

structured_extraction.program_description: A county program administered by the Forestry Division (Department of Inspections and Permits) that provides appropriate emergent marsh grasses at no charge to Anne Arundel County residents for planting in marsh areas as part of living shoreline or other tidal projects. Two types of grasses are available: Spartina alterniflora (smooth cordgrass), which lives between high and low tides, and Spartina patens (saltmarsh hay), which lives above high tide but needs to get wet once daily. County personnel conduct a field visit to evaluate site conditions and determine which grass type is appropriate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides emergent marsh grasses at no cost to eligible Anne Arundel County residents. Two types of grasses are available: Spartina alterniflora (smooth cordgrass) for the intertidal zone (area between normal low and high tides), and Spartina patens (saltmarsh hay) for areas above the intertidal zone. The number of plants provided is calculated based on the planting area dimensions (length and width) and the recommended spacing for each plant type. County personnel conduct a field visit to evaluate site conditions and determine the appropriate grass type and quantity. Planting is generally completed after any additional shoreline work such as rip rap or breakwater installation.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Forestry Section, Department of Inspections and Permits
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anne Arundel County residents with qualifying living shoreline or other tidal projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergent marsh grasses for planting in marsh areas as part of living shoreline or other tidal projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland
requirements_list: Resident of Anne Arundel County or authorized representative (property owner or community association)
Have a qualifying living shoreline or other tidal project planned
Site must meet conditions for one of the two grass types provided (intertidal zone or area above intertidal zone)
If plantings are part of a more extensive project (rip rap, breakwater, beach replenishment), copies of relevant permit applications must be attached
If plantings are standalone, project description must be attached
Any additional shoreline work such as vegetation cutting or clearing within 100 feet of tidal waters requires proper permits and may require an approved Vegetation Management Plan (VMP)
All necessary permits and authorizations should be obtained in advance of planned project dates
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the completed Emergent Marsh Grasses Application form to the Inspections and Permits, Forestry Section at 2664 Riva Road, MS 6201, Annapolis, MD 21401. The application requires applicant contact information, property details (including authorization from property owner or community association president), location of plantings, dimensions of area to be planted (width and length for both intertidal and above-intertidal zones), and supporting documentation (permit copies for larger projects or project description for standalone plantings). County personnel will conduct a field visit to evaluate site conditions. Many applicants prefer to arrange a site visit prior to application submittal for assistance with initial project planning. Contact the Forestry Section at (410) 222-7441 to arrange a site visit or for plant descriptions and recommended spacing information.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2027 Laurel Race Course Impact Fund Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants funded through the Laurel Race Course Impact Fund to support nonprofit and community organizations providing services and facilities that benefit communities within three miles of the Laurel Race Course in Anne Arundel County. The program is administered by an advisory board and cycles annually, with grant awards ranging from $10,000 to $50,000. Funding is generated through fees and taxes from the operation of the Laurel Race Course, with the amount available varying each year based on revenues.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 (minimum request of $10,000) are available for eligible 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) nonprofit organizations. Grant funding can be used to purchase equipment and related supplies, make small capital improvements such as renovation, remodeling, or restoration/beautification of buildings or public community spaces, expand existing services, or pilot test new programs. Awards are paid on a reimbursement basis (except some capital projects), with ACDS striving to make payment within 30 days of receipt of a complete invoice. Last year, the LRCIF awarded $455,000 in total grants. FY 2027 awards will be for grant terms of July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, December 17, 2025 at 12:00pm (FY27); FY28 process will begin in December 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) nonprofit organizations serving communities within three miles of the Laurel Race Course in Anne Arundel County. Applications from organizations outside the three-mile radius will be considered if they demonstrate significant impacts for those who live and work within the three-mile area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment, supplies, small capital improvements (renovation, remodeling, restoration/beautification of buildings or public community spaces), expansion of existing services, or pilot testing of new programs that benefit communities within three miles of the Laurel Race Course.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County; applicant organization must be located within 3 miles of the Laurel Race Course. Applications from organizations outside the three-mile radius will be considered if they demonstrate significant impacts for those who live and work within the three-mile area. Organizations providing services beyond the three-mile radius must demonstrate how funds will be used in the target communities.
requirements_list: Applicant must have 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) nonprofit status

Minimum grant request of $10,000

Grantees must execute a signed award agreement before expending funds
