Capital Grants require site inspection and final report
Independent financial review of the organization as a whole is required
Direct deposit forms and authorized signatory confirmation must be provided
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through ACDS's Neighborly Portal at https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/acds/participant. For FY27: Applications are due Wednesday, December 17, 2025. In February 2026, the Advisory Committee reviews applications. In March 2026, selected applicants present at Committee meetings (March 4 and March 11 at 6:30 pm, virtual). The LRCIF Advisory Committee makes final Grant Award Recommendations to the County Executive. In June 2026, the FY 2027 Budget is approved by County Council and applicants are notified of award decisions. Summer 2026, grantees meet final grant award requirements and execute award agreements. Application training is provided. Grantees should not expend funding until agreements are executed by both parties and they speak to their ACDS grant manager. All invoicing is completed through the Neighborly portal on a reimbursement basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Fall 2025 Professional Development Cohort Program - Fundraising & Sustainability 2.0
structured_extraction.program_description: A recurring cohort-based professional development training program administered by the Anne Arundel County Nonprofit Center, designed to help nonprofit organizations diversify their revenue sources, develop or update resource development plans, and secure long-term financial sustainability. The program has been offered in multiple iterations (including a 3-month cohort format and a five-session advanced '2.0' format) and includes in-person group sessions, online or virtual coaching, expert facilitation, peer learning, networking, one-on-one consulting time, and lifetime access to resource materials and templates. The advanced 2.0 cohort is designed for nonprofit leaders who have completed a previous Fundraising & Sustainability cohort or have baseline knowledge of fundraising concepts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Fall 2025 cohort consists of five group training sessions held every two weeks from October 8, 2025 to December 3, 2025 (2:00 p.m. to 4:30 p.m.) at the Nonprofit Center in Crownsville, Maryland. Up to three members per organization can participate. The program includes expert facilitation by Dr. Lili Leonard of Black Dog Philanthropic, peer learning, networking, one-on-one consulting time, and lifetime access to resource materials, examples, and templates. Fees are based on organizational budget: $75 for organizations with budgets under $500,000 and $150 for organizations with budgets over $500,000. Earlier cohort iterations were free of charge and included four in-person sessions and two virtual sessions over three months.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The Fall 2025 cohort is now full. A Fundraising & Sustainability 1.0 Cohort will be offered in Spring 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit leaders and staff members from 501(c)(3) organizations located in and serving residents of Anne Arundel County. The advanced 2.0 cohort requires participants to have completed a previous Fundraising & Sustainability cohort or have baseline knowledge of fundraising concepts. Organizations must provide services to Anne Arundel County residents and have administrative offices in Anne Arundel County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance to help organizations develop or update a resource development plan, diversify funding sources, build a case for support, organizational storytelling, strategic prospecting, cultivation, grant development, and design a diverse fundraising and sustainability plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must be located in Anne Arundel County with administrative offices in the county, and at least 75 percent of the population served must reside in Anne Arundel County.

In good standing with the State of Maryland
Provide services to Anne Arundel County residents
Administrative offices located in Anne Arundel County
At least 75 percent of population served reside in Anne Arundel County
Agree to participate in all training and coaching sessions
Agree to share outcome data to help the Nonprofit Center improve its programs and services
Attendance at all sessions is required to complete the program successfully
At least one person from the organization must attend all sessions
Completed a previous Fundraising & Sustainability cohort OR those attending have baseline knowledge of fundraising concepts (for 2.0 cohort)
Organizations limited to twelve total, filled on first-come, first-served basis

For the 2.0 cohort, payment is collected once the cohort is full. At least one representative from the organization must attend all training sessions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Full Delivery of "Turnkey" Water Quality Improvements Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program funds design-build-maintain contracts with private firms to construct cost-effective stormwater best management practices on privately owned properties. Through public-private partnerships, contractors front the initial implementation costs and are reimbursed by the county after project completion and verification of water quality benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county provides reimbursement grants to private firms upon completion and verification of constructed stormwater best management practice projects. Award amounts vary based on project scope and water quality benefits delivered, ranging from approximately $363,000 to $3,000,000 in recent years. Ongoing maintenance payments are evaluated and released annually for 5 years after project completion.

structured_extraction.contact_name: Bureau of Watershed Protection and Restoration

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and construction of stormwater best management practices including living shorelines, stream restoration, wetland enhancement, and regenerative stormwater conveyance systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located on private property within Anne Arundel County's Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) geography and must not conflict with existing projects underway.
requirements_list: Site must be on private property within Anne Arundel County's MS4 geography
Project must not conflict with existing projects underway
Competitive proposals are prioritized based on technical merit and implementation likelihood
Cost-effectiveness metrics relating to the County's cost per equivalent impervious acre treated are evaluated annually
Project must generate verifiable water quality credits
Outside funding sources may be used if they do not diminish or encumber project benefits to the County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Private firms submit competitive bids through Anne Arundel County's Purchasing Office Bid Opportunities webpage, searching for "Full Delivery of Turnkey Water Quality Improvements." Proposals are evaluated based on technical merit, implementation likelihood, and cost-effectiveness. Upon award, contractors front implementation costs and are reimbursed by the County after project completion and verification of benefits, typically within one year of construction.

structured_extraction.program_description: A training program for nonprofit organizations to improve grant writing skills through eleven structured training sessions combining in-person and online learning. Participants work on grant proposals for funding opportunities of their choice.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eleven training sessions (five in-person, six online) held on Thursdays from 3-5pm from February through June. Participants work on competitive grant applications for funding sources of their choice and complete sections applicable to their needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations seeking to improve grant writing skills and success rates, both new and established
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant writing and fundraising
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online through the provided link on the program details page. Applications open immediately and remain open until December 13th.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps non-profits, homeowners associations, private landowners, and other organizations enhance the habitat and ecological balance of natural areas. Approved activities include pruning for vegetation health and safety, non-commercial timber stand improvement, and removal of invasive non-native vegetation with replanting of native species. The program applies to properties in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, Forest Conservation Easements, or Bog Protection Areas where more than 5,000 square feet of existing natural vegetation will be affected.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical assistance and approval process for habitat enhancement activities. Applicants must submit a Habitat Enhancement Plan application including a cover letter with contact information, completed application form with tax account number, scaled site plan showing limit of disturbance and environmentally protected zones, description of existing conditions and proposed work, timeline for invasive plant eradication with maintenance plan, and erosion and sediment controls. Once all required State and Federal permits are obtained, the application is reviewed and approved, valid for two years. The approved plan must be posted on-site during work for inspection purposes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profits, homeowners associations, private landowners, and other organizations seeking to enhance natural habitats and ecological balance on their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The approved funds and activities support pruning for vegetation health and safety, non-commercial timber stand improvement, and removal of invasive non-native vegetation with replanting of native species. Activities cannot include clearing vegetation for development or preparation of development applications.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, specifically properties in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, Forest Conservation Easements, or Bog Protection Areas where more than 5,000 square feet of existing natural vegetation is affected.
requirements_list: Must be for removal or enhancement of greater than 5,000 square feet of existing natural vegetation
Must be located in Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, Forest Conservation Easements, or Bog Protection Areas
Must not include clearing vegetation for development or development-related activities
All required State and Federal permits must be obtained prior to Forestry approval
Approved plan must be posted on-site during work for inspection purposes
Invasive plant eradication timeline and management plan required
Erosion and sediment controls are required and maintained

Submittal package must include cover letter with contact information, completed application with tax account number, scaled site plan at specified ratio showing limit of disturbance and protected zones, description of existing conditions and proposed work, and long-term maintenance plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the complete submittal package to the Department of Inspections & Permits, Permit Center Reception Desk, 1st Floor, 2664 Riva Road, Annapolis, MD 21401 or email as a PDF to forestry@aacounty.org. Package must include: cover letter with contact name, phone, and email; completed Habitat Enhancement Plan Application with tax account number; scaled site plan (minimum 1"=20', 1"=40', or 1"=50') showing property dimensions, limit of disturbance, vegetation to be removed, existing structures, critical areas and other protected zones; description of existing conditions and proposed work including size of disturbed area, eradication methods, replanting plan, timeline, and who will perform the work; invasive plant eradication timeline; and long-term management and maintenance plan. Contact Forestry Office at (410) 222-7441 or forestry@aacounty.org to schedule an on-site proposal review if needed. Obtain all required State and Federal permits. Approval is valid for two years. Post approved plan on-site during work for inspection.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the FABSCOM application process at https://www.fabscom.org/our-application-process.

Meals include one hot and one cold option, delivered Monday through Friday by friendly volunteers. The program can provide meals on a long-term or temporary basis and accommodates special dietary needs.

Able to receive meal deliveries

Some families in the North County Homelessness Prevention program are also eligible to receive family coaching through the 2 Generation Project.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to help hotels, inns, and bed-and-breakfast establishments in Anne Arundel County recover from pandemic-related revenue losses by providing funds for operating costs and COVID-19 related expenses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five million dollars in grants from the State of Maryland available to eligible hospitality businesses. Funds can be used for normal operating costs such as rent, payroll, job training, taxes, and debt service, or for COVID-19 related costs such as personal protective equipment and sanitization services. Cannot be used for equipment, soft goods, infrastructure improvements, or technology upgrades.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Hotels, motels, inns, and bed-and-breakfast establishments in Anne Arundel County that experienced at least 25 percent pandemic-related revenue reduction.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Normal operating costs including rent, payroll, job training, taxes, and debt service, or COVID-19 related costs including personal protective equipment and sanitization services. Cannot be used for equipment, soft goods, infrastructure improvements, or technology upgrades.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County only.
requirements_list: Hotels and motels must have at least ten sleeping rooms
Bed and breakfast establishments must have at least five sleeping rooms
Short-term residential rentals do not qualify
Business must have experienced pandemic-related reduction in year-over-year gross revenue of at least 25 percent for April to November 2020 compared to the same period in 2019
Business must be an Anne Arundel County hospitality business in good standing with the State of Maryland
Must submit a copy of valid occupancy license issued by Anne Arundel County Department of Inspections and Permits
Must submit a completed and signed W-9 form
Must upload a voided company check for ACH deposit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants visit the Hotel Relief Grant Program page on the AAEDC website to access the application. They complete the application form, submit required documentation including occupancy license and W-9 form, and upload a voided company check. Applications must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. on March 5.

structured_extraction.program_description: A venison food relief program that encourages hunters in Anne Arundel County to donate deer for processing. The program covers processing fees at participating processors and ensures the meat is delivered to the Anne Arundel County Food Bank to provide high-quality protein to food-insecure residents and help address deer overpopulation issues affecting local farmers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The AAEDC covers the processing fees for deer brought to Harwood Butcher in Harwood or Hitchcock Taxidermy in Severn. Previously the program offered a $50 per deer incentive, but this was discontinued due to state law restrictions on direct compensation for wild game.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Hunters in Anne Arundel County who hold necessary hunting licenses and permits
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Venison donation and processing for distribution to the Anne Arundel County Food Bank
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County only. Hunters must have permission from private land owners and follow DNR hunting rules.
requirements_list: Must hold necessary hunting licenses and permits
Must obtain permission from private land owners
Must follow Department of Natural Resources hunting rules
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Hunters donate deer they kill to either Harwood Butcher in Harwood or Hitchcock Taxidermy in Severn for processing. The AAEDC covers processing fees and ensures the meat reaches the Anne Arundel County Food Bank.

structured_extraction.program_description: A business development program that provides an eight-week online business education and training course, mentoring, and seed/operating capital to small, minority-owned, woman-owned, and Veteran-owned businesses based in Anne Arundel County. Participants receive business education, mentorship, and operating grants of $5,000 to $10,000 upon completion. In its first year, 23 businesses participated, employing 88 people and planning to create 50 new jobs, with participants reporting total revenue of more than $2.5 million before the program and projected revenue of more than $3.6 million after completing the program. A Spanish-language version was announced for 2024.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An eight-week online class providing business education and training, mentorship, and $5,000 to $10,000 in operating grants/seed capital upon completion. In its first year, 23 businesses participated, employing 88 people and planning to create 50 new jobs. Participants reported total revenue of more than $2.5 million before the program and projected total revenue of more than $3.6 million after completing the program. A Spanish-language version was announced for 2024.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The third cohort application period was 1/24/22 – 1/31/22; check website for current cohort application windows.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority-owned, woman-owned, and Veteran-owned businesses and entrepreneurs based in Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating capital and seed capital for businesses; funds may be used to grow the venture following completion of the eight-week training and mentoring program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County
requirements_list: Business must be based in Anne Arundel County
Must be a small business owner
Must be a minority-owned, woman-owned, or Veteran-owned business (priority given to minority, women, and veteran entrepreneurs)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted during specified cohort application periods announced by the program. Interested entrepreneurs should submit applications during the announced application window. Upon completing the eight-week online class, participants receive operating grants.

structured_extraction.program_name: Key Bridge Small Business Direct Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides direct cash assistance to small businesses severely impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse in March 2024. The program addresses loss of revenue, increased costs, and operational challenges to help businesses stabilize operations, pivot business models, and invest in long-term viability. Administered through local nonprofit partners in Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, and Baltimore County, the program offered grants ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 based on business revenues.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct cash grants ranging from $10,000 to $50,000 per business, with grant size determined by business revenues. Grants are dispersed to help businesses address losses in revenue, increased costs, and operational challenges resulting from the Key Bridge collapse, and to support stabilization, business model pivots, and long-term viability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses in Northern Anne Arundel County, Southeastern Baltimore City, and Southeastern Baltimore County that were severely impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse in March 2024.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants can be used to address loss of revenue and increased costs related to the bridge collapse, to help businesses adjust their operations model, stabilize operations, pivot business models, and invest in long-term viability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses located in Northern Anne Arundel County, Southeastern Baltimore City, or Southeastern Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Business must be located in Baltimore City, Southeast Baltimore County, or Northern Anne Arundel County
Business must have been in existence for at least two years as of March 26, 2024
Business must demonstrate ongoing viability
Business must provide evidence of loss of revenue or increased expenses related to the Key Bridge collapse
Business must have had revenue over $50,000
Business must have two or more employees
Business must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Business must be a small business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses applied through one of three designated small business grant partners: AAEDC (for Anne Arundel County or other Maryland areas), Baltimore Community Lending (for Baltimore City or other Maryland areas), or Latino Economic Development Center (for Baltimore County or other Maryland areas). Each partner offered free application assistance in Spanish and English. AAEDC accepted applications from February 18, 2025 through March 20, 2025. Applications were submitted online through the AAEDC Submittable portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A benefit offered to utility customers who face costly plumbing repairs and associated high utility bills due to leaks. The program provides relief from high utility charges resulting from water line breaks or leaks.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Heritage Areas Authority Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to support heritage tourism projects and activities that promote the mission of certified heritage areas, including the Chesapeake Crossroads Heritage Area. Funding is available for both capital projects (physical improvements) and non-capital projects (planning, education, promotion) that strengthen historic, cultural, and natural resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available to eligible municipalities and non-profit organizations for capital and non-capital projects that support heritage tourism within the Chesapeake Crossroads Heritage Area.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipalities and non-profit organizations within or serving the Chesapeake Crossroads Heritage Area
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects (physical improvements to historic, cultural, and natural resources) and non-capital projects (planning, education, recreational experiences, heritage tourism promotion)
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Chesapeake Crossroads Heritage Area, which stretches from Sandy Point State Park at the Chesapeake Bay Bridge through southern Anne Arundel County to Rose Haven at the Calvert County line, framed by the Chesapeake Bay on the east and Route 2/Solomon's Island Road on the west. Includes the municipalities of Annapolis and Highland Beach.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an eligible municipality or non-profit organization
Project must support heritage tourism and the mission of the Chesapeake Crossroads Heritage Area
Maryland Heritage Areas Authority may request easements on properties that receive capital project funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Preservation Planning division for information on grant applications and requirements.

requirements_list: Applicant must be a private individual or for-profit corporation

Maryland Heritage Areas Authority may request easements on properties that receive funding

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business COVID-19 Emergency Relief Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A $75 million emergency loan program that provides interim relief to Maryland-based businesses and manufacturers negatively impacted by COVID-19. The loan offers no interest or principal payments due for the first 12 months, then converts to a 36-month term loan with a 2% annual interest rate. Proceeds can be used to pay cash operating expenses including payroll, suppliers, rent, fixed debt payments, and other mission-critical operating costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $75 million loan fund offering no interest or principal payments due for the first 12 months. After 12 months, the loan converts to a 36-month term loan with monthly principal and interest payments at 2% annual interest rate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based for-profit businesses and manufacturers with under 50 full- and part-time employees that have been negatively impacted by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash operating expenses including payroll, suppliers, rent, fixed debt payments, and other mission-critical cash operating costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based businesses only.
requirements_list: Maryland-based business
Under 50 full- and part-time employees
Negatively impacted by COVID-19
For-profit business only

structured_extraction.program_name: Mobile Poultry Processing Unit Rental Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A rental program that provides access to a mobile poultry processing unit (MPU) for agricultural businesses and farmers. The unit is available for lease to help small and mid-sized poultry producers process their birds on-site or at their facility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental access to a mobile poultry processing unit. Applicants pay a rental fee to lease the unit for their poultry processing needs. The program is made possible through grant funds from the Southern Maryland Agricultural Development Commission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Poultry farmers and agricultural businesses in Anne Arundel County who process poultry on a small to mid-sized scale.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental of mobile poultry processing equipment for on-farm or facility-based poultry processing operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County.
requirements_list: Must have HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points) and SSOP (Sanitation Standard Operating Procedures) plans customized to your operation
Must complete Maryland State Poultry and Rabbit Certification (available online)
Must provide a certificate of liability insurance for a minimum of $1 million, listing AAEDC and Sarah Campbell/New Roots Farm as additional insured
Lessee assumes all liability when towing and using the MPU
Lessee is responsible for the cost of all repairs made necessary during the lease period beyond normal wear and tear
Lessee must inspect unit upon pick-up and notify Sarah Campbell/AAEDC of any damage prior to rental
Unit must be cleaned at conclusion of use
Lessee must complete the post-rental form upon return of the MPU
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the rental application through the online form at aaedc.submittable.com. Provide all required documentation including liability insurance certificate and certification. Upon approval, pick up the unit, inspect it, use it according to HACCP and SSOP plans, clean it, and return it with a completed post-rental form.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants, information, resources, and support services to help family caregivers care for their loved ones at home. Services include information and assistance locating resources, temporary respite (relief) care, supplies or devices to make caregiving easier, support groups, educational workshops, a quarterly newsletter, and an annual caregiver appreciation event. The program is funded through grants and targets family and informal caregivers of older adults, individuals with Alzheimer's disease, and people with disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund a range of supports for family caregivers including temporary respite care, supplies and devices, information and referral services, educational workshops, support groups, and other support services. Payment is issued approximately 4 to 6 weeks after approval and receipt of required forms (W-9 and Funds Acknowledgement form). Grant award is based on availability of funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family caregivers and informal caregivers age 18 and older caring for older adults (age 60+), individuals with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders, or people with disabilities; older relatives (not parents) age 55 and older caring for children under age 18; older relatives including parents age 55 and older caring for adults ages 18–59 with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary respite (relief) care, supplies and devices to support caregiving, information and resource assistance, educational workshops, support groups, quarterly newsletter, annual caregiver appreciation event, and other caregiver support services.

Adult family members or other informal caregivers age 18 and older providing care to individuals of any age with Alzheimer's disease and related disorders
Older relatives (not parents) age 55 and older providing care to children under age 18
Older relatives, including parents, age 55 and older providing care to adults ages 18 to 59 with disabilities
Care recipient must live in Anne Arundel County
Applicant must submit a W-9 form before payment can be processed
Applicant must submit a Funds Acknowledgement form before payment can be processed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Family Caregiver Program by phone at (410) 222-4375 or (410) 222-4339 or by email at caregiver_support@aacounty.org for information and to request assistance. Submit required W-9 and Funds Acknowledgement forms. Upon approval of the grant request, payment will be issued in approximately 4–6 weeks. If the care recipient is enrolled in a program with a case manager, assistance may be requested through the case manager.

structured_extraction.program_description: A zero percent loan program created for Anne Arundel County-based technology companies, particularly small government contractors and entrepreneurs, that work with government contractors and support the nation's cyber and defense industry. The fund assists technology companies at the mezzanine stage of growth—businesses that have launched, invested in themselves early, achieved initial success, but need support to scale up. It offers flexible terms and zero percent interest rates to innovative businesses that are ready to grow, hire, and expand their commercial products or operations while awaiting payment on federal contracts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent loans ranging from $50,000 to $250,000 with flexible payment terms structured between one to five years to accommodate a company's cash flow, designed to support business expansion, workforce growth, product development, and scaling operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Technology companies with gross revenue of less than $5 million and fewer than 100 employees located in Anne Arundel County, or with a signed lease demonstrating intent to move into the county, that are small government contractors or entrepreneurs in the cyber and defense industry seeking to expand operations and workforce.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business scaling and expansion including workforce expansion, hiring additional team members, upscaling operations, expanding marketing efforts, product development, taking advantage of business opportunities, and continuing operations while awaiting payment on federal contracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in Anne Arundel County or have a signed lease demonstrating their intent to move into the county.
requirements_list: Must be based in Anne Arundel County or have a signed lease demonstrating intent to move into the county
Must be a technology company providing products or services to government contractors
Must support the nation's cyber and defense industry
Must be ready to grow and hire
Gross revenue of less than $5 million
Fewer than 100 employees
Operate in the technology sector
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation (AAEDC). Contact AAEDC for application details and submission process. Applications are reviewed and awards are made based on program criteria.

Grants support purchases of personal protective equipment, sanitation products, protective barriers, digital signage, technology for e-commerce and virtual customer engagement, delivery vehicles, mobile operations, and professional consultation and training services. The program ran from June 3, 2020 through its application deadline, with approved grants averaging approximately $6,370 and a maximum of $10,000 per business.

Grants may be used as reimbursement for eligible purchases made after March 29, 2020. Past due bills for rent, utilities, and inventory do not qualify. Businesses must submit invoices as proof of purchases.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Substantial Financial Hardship Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: A program administered by the Anne Arundel County Office of Finance that reduces or waives the Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee for residential property owners experiencing substantial financial hardship who meet at least two specified eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee is reduced or waived for eligible residential property owners. Applicants must meet at least two of the following four criteria to demonstrate substantial financial hardship: (1) combined gross income does not exceed the federal poverty guidelines updated annually by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services; (2) at least one property owner who resides at the property receives an energy assistance subsidy through a Fuel and Utility Assistance Program; (3) at least one property owner who resides at the property receives Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or food stamps (SNAP); or (4) at least one property owner who resides at the property receives veterans or Social Security disability benefits. Any exemption granted is valid only for the year that payment of the stormwater remediation fee is due, and applicants must re-apply each year to maintain the exemption.

Mobile home park tenants with a valid lease or contract also qualify.

Applicants must check which of the four criteria apply and provide documentation such as: (1) a copy of the income tax return for calendar year 2024 if claiming poverty level income; (2) recent energy bill or documentation from energy assistance program; (3) letter from Social Security Administration or Maryland Department of Human Services regarding SSI or SNAP; or (4) documentation of veterans or Social Security disability benefits. Submit the completed application and documentation by mail to: Anne Arundel County, Office of Finance, Attn: Tax Credits, 44 Calvert Street, Room 110, Annapolis, MD 21401; or by email to taxcredits@aacounty.org. If mailing less than 14 days before the deadline, use a traceable form of delivery. If an email address is provided, a receipt confirmation will be sent within 10 business days. Written notification of approval or denial will be sent to the applicant.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Management Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Residential and commercial property owners in Anne Arundel County can receive a credit toward their County real property taxes for recently installing qualified stormwater management practices on their property. The program encourages voluntary adoption of stormwater management improvements beyond what is legally required.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The tax credit equals 10% of the cost of materials and installation for qualified improvements, capped at a maximum of $10,000 total over the five-year life of the credit. The credit is applied to County real property taxes only. The credit is effective beginning in the taxable year following approval and continues for four succeeding taxable years (five taxable years total), provided the property meets all requirements and improvements remain in working condition and are regularly maintained.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 45 days of completion of qualifying improvements
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial property owners in Anne Arundel County who have recently installed qualified stormwater management practices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit applies to County real property taxes for properties with approved stormwater management improvements. Eligible costs include materials and installation of qualified stormwater management practices, including but not limited to: rain barrels/cisterns, rain gardens, removal of impervious coverage, swales, dry wells, landscape infiltration, permeable pavers, infiltration trenches, sand filters, green roofs, bioretention, constructed wetlands, regenerative step pools, wet ponds, retrofitted wet ponds with CMAC systems, and living shorelines.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Application must be submitted within 45 days of completion of qualifying improvements
The credit cannot be combined with other tax credits
The qualified improvements cannot be installed as a requirement of any State or local law
The qualified improvements must be on the Department of Public Works' list of approved devices
Prior to credit approval, the practice(s) must pass inspection by County staff
The County reserves the right to inspect the practice during the life of the credit
Property owner must have recently installed qualified stormwater management practices
Property must be residential or commercial
Applicant must be current on all taxes owed to the County
Improvements must remain in working condition and regularly maintained for the duration the tax credit is applied
Failure to maintain improvements entitles the County to pursue a refund of the credit plus a penalty equal to 200% of the credit
Applicants must provide copies of all receipts and/or paid invoices relating to total cost of improvements
Required documentation may include permits (if applicable), before/during/after photographs, detailed plans of improvements, and soil type documentation depending on device type
County officers and employees may enter onto the property for inspection purposes during the life of the credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Stormwater Management Tax Credit Application Form. The application must include all required documentation, which may vary by device type (some require soil borings, design professional plans, photographs, permits, etc.). Submit the application by email to taxcredits@aacounty.org or by mail to Anne Arundel County, Office of Finance, Attn: Tax Credits, PO Box 427, Annapolis, MD 21404-0427. If mailing less than 14 days before the 45-day deadline, use traceable delivery. The Office of Finance reviews applications with input from Department of Public Works staff. The Department of Public Works certifies whether the property qualifies and conducts inspection of the improvements. Applicants receive written notification of approval or denial. If approved, the credit becomes effective in the taxable year following submission and appears on the real property tax bill for five taxable years total.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funded by Maryland's video lottery terminal (VLT) revenues that provides emergency financial assistance to small, minority-owned, woman-owned, and Veteran-owned businesses and non-profit organizations to recover from damage and operational disruptions caused by storm and coastal flooding events in Anne Arundel County. The program was established in 2021 following the October 29-30, 2021 coastal flooding event, expanded by the Maryland General Assembly in 2022, and activated again in January 2024 following flooding on January 9-10, 2024. The program is activated when a local state of emergency is declared by the Mayor of Annapolis and approved by the Maryland Department of Commerce. Grants are reimbursable and cover costs associated with physical property damage, equipment damage, inventory loss, and revenue losses not covered by business insurance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable grants of up to $50,000 per business or non-profit, funded from Maryland's video lottery terminal (VLT) revenues placed into the Small, Minority and Women-Owned business account (total pool of $1,000,000 per activation). Eligible businesses can use grant funds for any legitimate business expense including physical property repairs, replacement of equipment, loss of income from being closed, replacement of damaged inventory, and working capital needed to resume operations. Funds are limited to expenses not covered by the business's insurance or other relief programs. Priority is given to businesses with fewer than 20 employees (67% of grants in the 2021 activation went to such businesses).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications open the Tuesday following declaration of a local state of emergency and are accepted for 30 days. For the January 2024 activation, applications began January 16, 2024. The 2021 activation began accepting applications November 1, 2021. The program is currently closed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority-owned, woman-owned, and Veteran-owned businesses and non-profit organizations with commercial brick-and-mortar locations in the City of Annapolis (and surrounding areas of Anne Arundel County) that have sustained damage or operational disruption from a qualifying flooding or storm disaster event declared as a local state of emergency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Physical property repairs, replacement of equipment, loss of income from damage-related business closure, replacement of damaged inventory, and working capital needed to resume business operations. Funds may not be used for expenses covered by insurance or reimbursed by other relief programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily the City of Annapolis and Anne Arundel County, Maryland. The program is activated in response to specific disaster events when a local state of emergency is declared by the Mayor of Annapolis and approved by the Maryland Department of Commerce. For the January 2024 activation, eligibility was limited to businesses and non-profits with commercial brick-and-mortar locations within the City of Annapolis limits. The 2021 activation covered businesses in Anne Arundel County and surrounding areas affected by the October 29-30, 2021 storm and coastal flooding.
requirements_list: Business or non-profit must be located in the City of Annapolis (for non-profits) or in the area affected by the qualifying disaster event
Must be a small business, minority-owned, woman-owned, or Veteran-owned business, or a non-profit organization
Must have sustained damage or operational disruption from the qualifying disaster event
Local state of emergency must have been declared by the Mayor and approved by the Maryland Department of Commerce
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Must have a commercial brick-and-mortar location
Must submit a completed application
Must submit a copy of most recent business tax returns, schedule C or 990
Must submit a statement listing all damages with details of loss of income
Must submit pictures and/or videos of the damage
Must submit a budget detailing the use of grant proceeds
Must submit paid invoices and canceled checks for purchases made
Must submit a completed W-9 form
Must be available for a site visit to review damages to the property or business
Must self-affirm that grant funds will not be used for expenses reimbursed by other relief programs or covered by insurance policies
Must submit receipts for and proof of purchase of all expenditures
Businesses with fewer than 20 employees receive priority consideration
Grant amounts up to $50,000 are reimbursable
Expenses must not be covered by the business's insurance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open the Tuesday following declaration of a local state of emergency and are accepted for approximately 30 days. All applicants must be available for a site visit to review damages. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and grants are disbursed by AAEDC upon approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: An administrative appeals process for property owners who believe they have been billed in error for the Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee. The program reviews appeals based on criteria including incorrect zoning classification, impervious area calculation errors, mathematical errors, property exemption status, property owner identification errors, and homeowners association fee caps.

Refunds cannot be issued for charges more than three years old per Maryland State Code. Appeals are reviewed and written decisions are issued within 45 days of receipt. If the appeal is granted and results in a change to the stormwater remediation fee, a new bill will be issued. If aggrieved by the decision, property owners may appeal to the Maryland Tax Court in accordance with Article 24, § 9-710 and 9-712 of the Annotated Code of Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Appeals accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Anne Arundel County who believe they have been billed in error for the Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fee adjustments and refund checks for overbilled stormwater or watershed protection charges

requirements_list: Property owner must submit completed appeal application

Appeal must be based on one of the following criteria: Incorrect Zoning Classification of Real Property, Errors in Impervious Area Calculation for Non-Residential Property, Mathematical Errors in Calculation, Real Property is Not Subject to the Charge, Property Owner is Exempt From the Charge, Errors in the Identification of the Property Owner, Residential Property in a Non-Residential Zone, or Homeowners Association WPRF Cap

Exemptions include: unimproved property (contains no impervious surface), property in the City of Annapolis, property owned by the State of Maryland, property owned by a county or municipality, property owned by a regularly organized volunteer fire department used for public purpose, property owned by veterans organizations exempt under 501(c)(4) or (19) of the Internal Revenue Code, and property owned by religious organizations or charitable nonprofits certified under 501(c)(3) or (d)
Applicant must authorize the Department of Public Works to confirm information provided and inspect property to verify impervious surface area
For residential tier appeals, applicants must identify current and correct tier classification based on zoning district and dwelling type
For property classification appeals, applicants must identify current and correct property classification code
For HOA fee cap appeals, applicants must provide total WPRF charged to all HOA-owned properties and number of property tax accounts for homes and unimproved lots within HOA boundaries
For math error or impervious surface calculation appeals, applicants must provide documentation such as plans, reports, or photos
For exemption or property owner appeals, applicants must provide proof of location, ownership, lack of impervious area, or approved financial hardship exemption
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed appeal form online through the county portal at www.aarivers.org or by mail using one of five paper forms (13-1 through 13-5) depending on the type of appeal: Form 13-1 for Residential Property Wrong Tier, Form 13-2 for Incorrect Property Classification, Form 13-3 for Homeowners Association WPRF Cap, Form 13-4 for Math Error or Incorrect Impervious Surface, Form 13-5 for Exempt or Incorrect Property Owner. Mail completed paper forms to: WPRF Appeals, Anne Arundel County DPW, 2662 Riva Road, MS 7409, Annapolis, MD 21401. Attach supporting documentation as applicable. The County will review the application and issue a written decision within 45 days of receipt. For calculation formulas, see www.aacounty.org/departments/public-works/wprp/watershed-protection-restoration-fee/wprf-rate-information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (WPRF) Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program administered by Anne Arundel County that allows eligible property owners to reduce their annual Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (stormwater fee) by up to 50% by implementing, maintaining, and documenting stormwater runoff control measures on their property. The program includes a Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement for homeowners who install small-scale practices without a County grading permit, outlining maintenance responsibilities and granting the County access to inspect practices. Credits are calculated based on treated impervious area, total impervious area, and treatment value, and require a recent County inspection to verify proper design, construction, and maintenance.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible property owners can receive a credit reducing their annual Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee by up to 50%. For multi-family, non-residential, and residential properties, the credit is calculated using the formula: (Treated Impervious Area ÷ Total Impervious Area) × Treatment Value × 50%, where Treatment Value is 100% if at least 1 inch of rainfall is treated, or a proportional percentage if less. Non-residential properties with NPDES permits are eligible for up to 50% credit if the entire property is covered. Marina properties can receive up to 25% credit for NPDES permit compliance and/or up to 25% for Clean Marina certification, potentially totaling 50%. Full credit is available for practices that treat a minimum of 1 inch of rainfall; partial credit is available for practices treating less than 1 inch. Approved credits are valid for three-year periods and continue in perpetuity provided practices are maintained in good working condition. The maximum allowable credit by law is 50% of the stormwater remediation fee.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Anne Arundel County who have implemented or plan to implement stormwater management practices on their property, including residential homeowners, multi-family property owners, non-residential property owners, NPDES permit holders, and marina operators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credits are applied toward reducing the property owner's annual Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee (stormwater fee) based on the stormwater management practice installed and its effectiveness. Credits cannot be used for other purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County, Maryland only. Stormwater management practices must be located on land with the same owner as the parcel seeking credit, within the county.
requirements_list: Applicant must own property in Anne Arundel County
Stormwater management practices must be privately owned and maintained
Practices must be located on land with the same owner as the parcel seeking credit
Practices must not be under an existing Inspection and Maintenance Agreement for Private Stormwater Management (for Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement applicants)
Practices must provide water quality treatment of at least 1 inch of rainfall for full credit; partial credit available for less than 1 inch

Practices must be designed, approved, constructed, and maintained in accordance with County Standards, Stormwater Management Practices and Procedures Manual, or the 2000 Maryland Stormwater Design Manual
Practices must have passed a recent inspection by County staff verifying proper design, construction, and maintenance
Practices must be covered under an Inspection and Maintenance Agreement for Private Stormwater Management or a Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement
All property owners listed on the deed must sign the Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement (for small-scale practices not requiring a grading permit)
Agreement automatically terminates if property ownership transfers; new owner must enter into a new agreement to continue receiving credit
For NPDES permit properties: must be regulated through a National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System permit with stormwater management controls
For marina properties: must be regulated through an NPDES permit and/or certified by Maryland Department of Natural Resources as a Clean Marina
Application must be received or postmarked by October 1 of the taxable year
Property must receive a stormwater remediation fee on its property tax bill
For multi-family and non-residential properties: stormwater management practices must be designed, retrofitted, approved, constructed, inspected, and maintained per County standards
Applicant is responsible for continued maintenance, repair, and inspection records of stormwater practices
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications can be submitted online at www.aarivers.org or by mail using the appropriate application form. For multi-family, non-residential, and residential properties with Inspection and Maintenance Agreements or planning to enter Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreements, use the Multi-Family, Non-Residential, Residential Credit Application (Appendix A). For non-residential properties with NPDES permits and/or DNR Clean Marina Certification, use the NPDES and Clean Marina Credit Application (Appendix B). Submit application package including: completed application form, photographs of practices and drainage areas, site plan showing property layout and practice locations, copies of grading permit plans (if applicable), stormwater management reports, and installation documentation. For Stormwater Remediation Fee Credit Agreement pathway, the County provides an unsigned draft agreement; all owners listed on the deed must sign and return by mail. County staff will inspect practices to verify proper design, construction, and maintenance. Applications must be received or postmarked by October 1 of the taxable year; if received after October 1, credit will not start until the following taxable year. Send paper applications to: Attn: WPRF Credit Program, Anne Arundel County Department of Public Works, 2662 Riva Road, MS 7409, Annapolis, Maryland 21401. County will review and issue written decision within 90 calendar days. If approved, fee adjustments are made and any applicable refund checks are mailed separately from decision letter. Approved credits are valid for three-year periods; functional verification by County staff is required prior to end of three-year period to continue receiving credit. Renewal applications are not required; credit continues provided applicant abides by the agreement and maintains practices per most recent credit application. Note: If plans/documentation are not available, applicants should describe water quality treatment provided by practices; County staff will attempt to obtain information from available records, but applicant is ultimately responsible for documentation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program that allows property owners who revitalize commercially or industrially zoned properties in designated Commercial Revitalization Areas (districts) in Anne Arundel County to receive a property tax credit for up to five years equal to the incremental increase in real property tax assessment resulting from improvements of at least $100,000 in assessed value. The tax credit can be extended for an additional five years for investments of at least $10,000,000. Eligible activities include renovation, rehabilitation, new construction, or demolition and redevelopment.
structured_extraction.agency: Anne Arundel County / Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying property owners who make improvements of at least $100,000 in assessed value to their properties in a designated Commercial Revitalization Area receive a property tax credit for up to five years. The credit equals the incremental increase in real property tax assessment resulting from the improvements. For investments of at least $10,000,000, the tax credit can be extended for an additional five years. Qualifying improvements may include full site redevelopment, but also may include smaller measures such as new facades, landscaping and signage, lighting, replacing pavement with green spaces, or other measures that improve the physical appearance and aesthetics of the property and increase its economic viability. Property owners must apply to the County Office of Finance within 120 days after receiving notice of assessment from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 120 days after notice of assessment from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners with commercially or industrially zoned properties located in one of the nine designated Commercial Revitalization Areas in Anne Arundel County who are undertaking renovation, rehabilitation, new construction, or demolition and redevelopment projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit applies to property tax assessments resulting from improvements of at least $100,000 made to commercially or industrially zoned properties in Commercial Revitalization Areas. Eligible projects include renovating or rehabilitating an existing building, constructing a new building, or demolishing a building for redevelopment. Qualifying improvements may include full site redevelopment, façade improvements, landscaping, signage, lighting, replacing pavement with green spaces, or other measures that improve the physical appearance and aesthetics of the property and increase its economic viability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in one of the nine designated Commercial Revitalization Areas in Anne Arundel County: Area 1 (Brooklyn Park - Ritchie Highway), Area 2 (Glen Burnie Town Center North - Crain Highway and Ritchie Highway), Area 3 (Glen Burnie Town Center Core - B&A Boulevard), Area 4 (Glen Burnie Town Center South - Crain Highway), Area 5 (Pasadena - Mountain Road), Area 6 (Pasadena - Fort Smallwood Road), Area 7 (North Odenton - MD 175), Area 8 (Maryland City/Russett - MD 198), and Area 9 (Ferndale - B&A Boulevard).
requirements_list: Property must be commercially or industrially zoned
Property must be located in one of the nine designated Commercial Revitalization Areas
Property improvements must total at least $100,000 in assessed value
Property must be certified by the Office of Planning and Zoning as a qualified property
Application must be submitted to the County Office of Finance within 120 days after notice of assessment from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
For extended credit (additional five years), investments must total at least $10,000,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners who make qualifying improvements must apply to the County Office of Finance for the revitalization credit by submitting the Property Tax Credit Application within 120 days after receiving notice of assessment from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. The property must be certified by the Office of Planning and Zoning as a qualified property before approval. Applicants should contact the Anne Arundel Economic Development Corporation for assistance with the application process and to determine property eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A citywide public financing program that uses Tax Increment Financing (TIF) bonds to fund affordable housing development across Baltimore City. The program provides grants to support the redevelopment of vacant buildings for residential use (rental and homeownership), homeowner grants to help residents qualify for newly rehabbed homes, and public infrastructure improvements such as sidewalks, parks, and alleys. Funds help reduce the appraisal gap and support affordable housing preservation in historically disinvested neighborhoods including Broadway East, Harlem Park, Druid Heights, Park Heights, Upton, East Baltimore Midway, and Coldstream Homestead Montebello. The program is a non-contiguous TIF district covering approximately 8,587 properties citywide across 197 neighborhoods that have been issued a Vacant Building Notice. It prioritizes legacy residents, small and emerging developers, and women and minority-owned businesses. The program is part of a broader $3 billion vision to eliminate vacant housing in Baltimore over 15 years, with the first series of $28.8 million in TIF bonds closing on December 23, 2025, and a total of $150 million in TIF bonds planned.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TIF bonds totaling $28.8 million in the first series closed on December 23, 2025, with the City intending to issue a maximum of $150 million in bonds over a 15-year period. Funds are distributed as grants with no requirement for repayment. The average grant award for housing construction is anticipated to be around $50,000, varying based on property size and condition, use as rental or homeownership, affordability level, and appraisal gap. There is no stated maximum limit on TIF funds requested per project. Approximately $15-18 million is available in the first round, with approximately $3 million prioritized for legacy residents, small, emerging, and minority developers, and individuals renovating family-owned homes. Funds support households earning up to 115% of area median income (approximately $149,845 for a household of four as of 2025), with priority consideration for properties affordable at 60% and 80% of area median income. Hard construction costs covered include excavation, demolition, grading, site improvements, building structure, foundations, framing, floor and roof structure, roof cover, ceiling, building service equipment (electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, alarm systems, elevators, fire protection systems, computer/network/telecommunications cabling), and interior and exterior finishes subject to review for eligibility. Public infrastructure covered includes streets, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, lighting, landscaping, roads, water, and utilities for city-sponsored homeownership development projects. TIF bonds are repaid through increases in property tax assessments and related increases in property tax revenues from developed properties. TIF funds are provided on a reimbursement basis, requiring applicants to have funds to cover costs before reimbursement. Reimbursement requires completion inspection by a third-party inspector, City review, and Verification Agent approval.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 3, 2025 at 5:00 PM Eastern Standard Time for the first round of applications; subsequent rounds will be released with two-week application periods.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Legacy residents, homeowners, residents seeking homeownership, small and emerging developers, women and minority-owned businesses, nonprofit and affordable housing developers, established development organizations, community development organizations, business owners, individuals renovating family-owned homes, and individuals living in the TIF District. Eligible applicants must hold or seek to develop properties in the City-Wide Affordable Housing TIF District for households earning up to 115% of area median income, with priority for households at 60% and 80% AMI. Applicants may apply through three programs: City Award of Properties with executed Land Disposition Agreements (LDA), Developer Registry, or General Interest (for-profit/nonprofit developers, partnerships, or private property owners).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hard construction costs for redevelopment of vacant buildings for residential use, including excavation, demolition, grading, site preparation, building structure, foundations, framing, floor and roof structure, roof cover, ceiling, building service equipment (electrical, plumbing, HVAC, alarm systems, elevators, fire protection systems, telecommunications cabling), and interior and exterior finishes (subject to additional review for eligibility). Public infrastructure required for city-sponsored new construction homeownership projects, including streets, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, lighting, landscaping, roads, water, and utilities. Funds can close appraisal gaps and create or preserve affordable housing for rental or homeownership. Hard construction costs only; soft costs such as architectural, engineering, or administrative fees are not eligible. TIF funds cannot be used to acquire City-owned property and improvements cannot begin until title transfers and Grant Agreement is executed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties located in the City-Wide Affordable Housing Tax Increment Financing District, covering approximately 8,587 properties citywide across 197 neighborhoods that have been issued a Vacant Building Notice and are included in the Development District as established by Ordinance 24-443. The district is non-contiguous and covers properties across all of Baltimore City. Use the searchable database at https://bit.ly/TIFMAP to verify eligibility by address.
requirements_list: Property must be located in the City-Wide Affordable Housing Tax Increment Financing District (Ordinance 24-443)
Property must have been issued a Vacant Building Notice (VBN)
Proposed uses must be eligible uses of TIF Bond proceeds as confirmed by the City's Bond Counsel
Construction budgets subject to City review and approval
Residents in the property cannot earn more than 115% of area median income (approximately $149,845 for a household of four as of 2025)
Work must be completed by licensed contractors and subcontractors; failure to use licensed contractors could result in loss of award
Project must be financed and completed within 12 months of executing a Grant Agreement
Applicants must identify additional funding sources for costs not covered by TIF funds
Awardees must execute a Grant Agreement with DHCD before receiving funds
Projects must be able to obtain a Use and Occupancy Permit within 12 months of executing Grant Agreement
Priority given to properties affordable at 60% and 80% of area median income
Applicants must provide proof of site control (ownership, Purchase Agreement with closing date, or executed LDA)
Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financing committed or available to complete the project
For-profit applicants with annual budgets over $200,000 must provide audited financial statements; those with budgets $200,000-$500,000 must provide certified accounting firm statements
Nonprofit applicants must provide most recent Form 990 and Certificate of Good Standing
Grantees must carry liability insurance at limits of not less than $1 million and provide Certificate of Insurance prior to executing Grant Agreement
Commercial General Liability Insurance, Business Automobile Liability, Workers' Compensation, and All Risk Builders' Risk insurance required during construction
Partners must execute partnership agreements or MOUs prior to executing Grant Agreement with City
Applicants with fewer than 3 years development experience or who have completed fewer than 5 vacant residential buildings are strongly encouraged to partner with experienced developers
Applications must be submitted through the online Neighborly portal
All submissions must meet Threshold Review requirements to be considered for award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the online Neighborly portal (https://portal.neighborlysoftware.com/baltimoremd/Participant). The process consists of multiple steps: (1) Threshold Review—an internal administrative check by DHCD staff to verify eligibility, confirm application completeness, and check for discrepancies; applications with 3 or fewer deficiencies will be given opportunity to cure; applications with 4 or more deficiencies are deemed ineligible with no opportunity to cure. (2) Scoring—applications meeting Threshold Requirements are evaluated: LDA and Developer Registry applications are not scored but must meet Threshold Requirements; Legacy Resident applications are not scored; General Interest applications requesting funds for privately owned properties are scored on Financing and Ability to Spend (40 points), Scheduling (25 points), Applicant Capacity (25 points), and Site Control (10 points). (3) Conditional Award Letter—recommended applicants receive detailed budget review by City Bond Counsel and TIF Verification Agent, with request for executed construction contracts and financial information. (4) Execution of Grant Agreement—after approval, City and awardee execute the form Grant Agreement (previously approved by Board of Estimates and not subject to revision). (5) Project Implementation and Disbursement—grantees implement projects, provide quarterly progress reports, and submit requisitions for reimbursement upon third-party inspector verification and City/Verification Agent approval. Applicants strongly encouraged to attend Information Sessions (September 15 and September 16, 2025) or submit written questions by September 17, 2025 to AHTIF@baltimorecity.gov. Award recommendations made by review committee to Deputy Commissioner for Development and Housing Commissioner, who makes final determinations. All applicants notified via email of award decisions. Applicants receiving Award Letter must accept within 5 calendar days and execute Grant Agreement within 30 days of receipt. Funds disbursed on reimbursement basis requiring applicants to have funds to pay costs before reimbursement. Grantees must expend TIF Funds and obtain Use and Occupancy Permit no later than 12 months from executing Grant Agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fund established by voters to support both rental and for-sale affordable housing for very-low and low-income households in Baltimore City. The fund requires that all revenue be used to help those with incomes at or below 50 percent of the Area Median Income (AMI) as established by HUD, and that at least half of the funds be used to help those with incomes at or below 30 percent of AMI. The fund prioritizes families earning less than 50% of the area median income, with at least half of funding directed to families earning less than 30% of the area median income. City allocation amounts have grown from $2 million in FY2020 to $7 million in FY2023 and subsequent years.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides financial resources to support affordable housing development and preservation. City allocation amounts: FY2020 $2 million, FY2021 $3.5 million, FY2022 $5 million, FY2023 and subsequent years $7 million. Funds support both rental and for-sale affordable housing programs for households at or below 50 percent AMI, with at least half directed to households at or below 30 percent AMI. Grants are distributed through notices of funding for specific funding rounds. The fund is administered by the Department of Housing & Community Development (DHCD) and overseen by a 12-member advisory commission comprised of representatives from housing, community development, lending, social services, and affordable housing advocacy sectors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Very-low and low-income households; affordable housing developers, nonprofits, and for-profit organizations seeking to develop or preserve affordable housing for low-income families in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting rental and for-sale affordable housing development and preservation for households at or below 50 percent of Area Median Income, with at least half of funds directed to households at or below 30 percent of AMI. Funds support both acquisition and development of new affordable housing units as well as preservation of existing affordable housing stock.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Applicants must serve families/households earning less than 50% of Area Median Income (AMI) as established by HUD
At least 50% of funds must serve families/households earning less than 30% of area median income
Projects must be located in Baltimore City
Nonprofit and for-profit developers are eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Affordable Housing Trust Fund is administered by the City's Department of Housing & Community Development (DHCD) and overseen by a 12-member advisory commission that makes recommendations regarding policies, rules, and regulations pertaining to the implementation, expenditures, and operation of the Fund. The commission includes representatives from housing and community development, lending, social services, homeless services, fair housing advocacy, nonprofit affordable housing development, homebuilding/real estate, and tenants' rights. Applications are submitted through the Neighborly Application Portal. Applicants should review current Notices of Funding for specific funding rounds and requirements. Notices of Funding Availability (NOFAs) are issued periodically for competitive rounds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Affordable Housing Trust Fund - Community Land Trust Homeownership NOFA
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development provides grants from its Affordable Housing Trust Fund to support homeownership projects sponsored by Community Land Trusts (CLTs). The program aims to promote equitable community development and affordable single family homeownership in historically disinvested communities, serving low and very low income households. Multiple rounds of funding have been issued, with rolling applications accepted. Projects must serve households at or below 50% of Area Median Income (AMI), with at least half of units serving households at or below 30% AMI. The program supports acquisition and rehabilitation strategies, buyer-initiated/buyer choice programs, and innovative housing strategies. Community Land Trusts must be registered with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation and organized or managed by a nonprofit exempt from taxation under § 501(c)(2), (3), or (4) of the Internal Revenue Code.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants available from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund to support Community Land Trust homeownership projects. Funding limits: up to $1,000,000 per project. Trust funds can cover up to 50% of a project's Total Development Cost (TDC) for units restricted to persons with incomes at or below 50% AMI, or up to 66% of TDC for units restricted to persons with incomes at or below 30% AMI. Maximum per unit request: $75,000 for units at 50% AMI and $120,000 per unit for units at 30% AMI. Up to 25% of total award can be used for predevelopment and/or acquisition costs combined. Up to 20% of award can be used for operating costs directly related to project implementation. Award notifications provided within 90 days of application submission. Funding available on a rolling basis until June 30, 2026, or until all funds are allocated.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis until June 30, 2026 or until all funds allocated
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered Community Land Trusts sponsoring homeownership projects (acquisition and rehabilitation, buyer-initiated/buyer choice, or innovative strategies) serving low and very low income households (at or below 50% AMI, with at least half of units serving households at or below 30% AMI) in Baltimore City. CLTs must be organized or managed by a nonprofit exempt from taxation under § 501(c)(2), (3), or (4) of the Internal Revenue Code.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Homeownership projects including acquisition and stabilization of non-City owned properties, architectural and engineering, environmental assessment and testing, market and financial feasibility analysis, construction, carrying costs, financing and lender fees, legal fees associated with closing and financing, consultant fees, customary landscaping, project management staff, infrastructure and utilities, single family homes, condos and cooperatives, demolition, and direct subsidies for buyer-initiated programs. Funds may be used for predevelopment, acquisition, construction, and operating costs directly related to project implementation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, with focus on communities suffering from long-term and historical disinvestment. Projects should be consistent with and leverage revitalization plans for the community where the project will be built and support goals stated in the City's Framework for Community Development.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a registered Community Land Trust with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
CLT must be organized or managed by a nonprofit organization exempt from taxation under § 501(c)(2), (3), or (4) of the Internal Revenue Code
CLT must comply with State's Affordable Housing Land Trust Laws found in Section 14 of the Annotated Code of Maryland Real Property Article
CLT must have By-Laws establishing terms for board of directors, officers, stewardship, conflicts of interest, ownership, open membership criteria, resale limitations, and dissolution
