Pre-proposal conference held August 27, 2025 to review NOFA, application requirements, evaluation and award process. Questions can be submitted to DHCD.AHTFNOFA@baltimorecity.gov. Applications must include: Authorization to Submit signed by authorized member; Completed application form with summary request, project information, number and ownership structure of units; IRS Determination Letter; Certification of Compliance; Owned Property Disclosure; Commitment to Comply; Local Hire Certification; Organizational Documents; Corporate Resolution/Board approval; By-Laws; Evidence of Good Standing with State of Maryland; List of Board of Directors with titles and affiliations; Organizational chart with board structure; Copy of Ground Lease or Deed Restriction and Stewardship Standards; Memorandum of Understanding between land trust and developer if applicable; Progress reports for existing awardees; Commitment Letters from all funding sources; Most recent 990 Tax Return and audited/reviewed financial statements as applicable; Development budget template as Excel spreadsheet; Site plans; Local Hiring Plan if 15+ units for Acquisition Rehab or Innovation strategies. Applications meeting threshold requirements are scored on project feasibility (70 points), community engagement and participation (40 points), and achieving equity (15 points). structured_extraction.program_name: Affordable Housing Trust Fund - New Construction and/or Rehabilitation of Existing Affordable Rental Housing NOFA
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City's Affordable Housing Trust Fund (AHTF) provides grants to non-profit and for-profit developers to support new construction of affordable rental housing and/or rehabilitation of existing rental projects. The program operates through recurring Notices of Funding Availability (NOFA) rounds. Earlier rounds (Round 1: up to $2M, Round 2: up to $1.7M, Round 3: up to $6M) established the program framework, including set-asides for emerging developers (those who have completed at least 3 and no more than 5 projects). Round 4 expanded funding to $10.75M and added a set-aside for Community Land Trusts. Round 7 (FY26) made up to $7.5M available, with up to $1M set aside for Community Land Trusts and up to $1M for emerging developers. Projects must serve households at or below 50% of Area Median Income (AMI), with at least half of units serving households at or below 30% AMI.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund provided through recurring NOFA rounds. Round 7/FY26 made up to $7.5M available ($7,000,000 in the earlier 2024 NOFA). Individual project award amounts are limited to a maximum of $1,000,000 per project. Funds can be used to cover up to 50% of a project's Total Development Cost or a maximum of $1,000,000 per project, whichever is less. Maximum request per unit is $75,000 for households earning 50% AMI and $120,000 for fewer than 10 units or $150,000 for 10+ units at 30% AMI. Up to 25% of award can be used for predevelopment and/or acquisition costs (combined), with up to 10% allowed for operating costs directly related to project implementation including staff costs. Set-asides include: up to $1,000,000 for Community Land Trusts (registered entities providing affordable housing through land trust agreements) and up to $1,000,000 for emerging developers (those who have completed at least 3 and no more than 5 projects). Advanced funds of up to 25% of award may be used for predevelopment and/or acquisition costs for grant awards only (not available for loans).
structured_extraction.contact_name: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and for-profit developers, Community Land Trusts, and Joint Ventures proposing new construction or rehabilitation of affordable rental housing projects in Baltimore City. Emerging developers (those who have completed at least 3 and no more than 5 projects) are encouraged to apply and may access a dedicated set-aside. Community Land Trusts must be registered with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation and organized or managed by a nonprofit organization exempt from taxation under § 501(c)(2), (3), or (4) of the United States Internal Revenue Code.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction of affordable rental housing and rehabilitation/preservation of existing rental projects for affordable housing. Eligible uses include acquisition and stabilization of non-City owned properties, architectural and engineering, environmental assessment and testing, market and financial feasibility analysis, construction, financing and lender fees, legal fees, consultant fees, project management staff, infrastructure and utilities, single family/condos/co-op building projects, demolition, customary landscaping, parking, and mixed-use buildings with ground floor retail. Up to 25% of award can be used for predevelopment costs (including market feasibility, architect/engineer, environmental costs, soft costs, permits, survey, legal fees, property consultant, insurance costs, loan origination fees, and accounting costs) and/or acquisition costs. Up to 10% can be used for operating costs directly related to project implementation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City. All units funded through the Trust Fund must restrict leasing and occupancy for a period of at least 30 years to households earning incomes not exceeding 50% of Area Median Income (AMI).
requirements_list: Projects must serve households with incomes at or below 50 percent of the Area Median Income (AMI)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted exclusively through the Neighborly Portal as part of a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) process. Electronic submissions only; applicants must submit one (1) complete online application including all attachments and threshold requirements in PDF format, plus one (1) copy of development budget as Excel spreadsheet. For Round 7 (FY26): NOFA guidelines and application posted November 21, 2025; pre-proposal conference held December 10, 2025 (5:00-6:30 PM EST via Teams); written questions accepted through December 12, 2025; responses posted by December 22, 2025; application deadline January 9, 2026 (11:59 PM EST); review and scoring conducted January 20 through March 17, 2026; award notifications scheduled for week of April 13, 2026. Application consists of four parts: (1) Threshold information (organizational, financial, compliance documentation including Articles of Incorporation, By-Laws, certifications, disclosures), (2) Financial review (development budget, funding sources/uses status, letters of commitment/interest from funding sources, management company qualifications, construction budgets including prevailing wage rates, personnel budgets), (3) Scored criteria (project feasibility up to 70 points including 24-month completion capacity, experienced development team, leverage ability, budget feasibility, site plan, management experience; community engagement up to 25 points including neighborhood ownership participation, compatibility with existing plans, community engagement plan; achieving equity up to 25 points including race equity in geographic areas, returning residents priority, blight elimination), (4) Signed certifications and authorizations. Applicants may receive up to 70 bonus points for long-term affordability (10 points), supporting/growing local businesses (4 points), serving households at/below 30% AMI (10 points), permanent supportive housing services (5 points), apprenticeships/training programs (4 points), collaboration across neighborhoods (5 points), local hiring criteria (7 points), environmental sustainability (5 points), developer fee deferral (10 points), and markets of strength neighborhoods (10 points). Following submission deadline, DHCD provides summary of all applications (applicant name, project, location, units, total development cost, funds requested) posted on DHCD website. Threshold review determines eligibility; applications meeting threshold are scored by interagency panel which may request additional information, meet with applicants, or tour projects. Panel provides recommendations to Housing Commissioner who makes final award decisions. Awardees notified by phone and/or in writing; non-awardees may request 30-minute debriefing. No funds available until Board of Estimates approves Funding Agreement; advanced funds (up to 25% of grant award) may be released for predevelopment/acquisition costs; remaining funds disbursed based on approved structure. Awardees required to submit progress reports detailing project completion percentages, schedule status, MBE/WBE goal percentages, and local hiring plan updates.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps residents and organizations gate and green alleys in Baltimore City. The program facilitates the process of securing and improving alley spaces through gating and greening initiatives. Alley Gating limits access to alleys with locked gates to eliminate cars, noise, littering, and loitering. Alley Greening takes this further by making alterations that would make the alley impassable to vehicles, creating a green oasis for the neighborhood.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical assistance and facilitation for residents and community organizations seeking to gate and green alleys. The city assists with the process and administration of alley gating and greening projects. The applicant is responsible for purchasing the gate and all project costs. A $250 processing fee is required. For Alley Gating, a Lease Agreement is typically a five (5) year term that automatically renews for four (4) additional 5-year terms, assuming there are no unresolved issues. The lessee must be a Neighborhood Association or Non-Profit Entity.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - applications accepted at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents and community organizations seeking to gate and green alleys
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improving and securing alley spaces through gating and greening projects. Funds/costs are the responsibility of the applicants for purchasing and installing gates and conducting any necessary modifications.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City. Alleys are generally eligible if the adjacent structures are mostly residential and the gating and/or greening will promote public health, safety, or welfare. The alley is considered residential if the number of residential units exceeds the number of non-residential units.
requirements_list: Alleys must have adjacent structures that are mostly residential in nature
Gating and/or greening must promote public health, safety, or welfare

For Alley Gating: Must obtain written consents from at least 75% of affected abutting property owners (not including abandoned properties); abandoned properties may be excluded via affidavit per Section 8A-9 of the Ordinance
For Alley Greening: Must obtain written consents from 100% of affected abutting property owners
Applicant must submit Alley Gating/Greening Application with digital images and a marked-up City Block Plat
Applicant must submit $250 processing fee (check made payable to Director of Finance)
Approval required from Police Commissioner and Fire Marshall
For Alley Greening: Must submit engineered drawing and follow City's Developers Agreement process
For Alley Greening in historic neighborhoods: Must obtain approval from Baltimore City Commission for Historic and Architectural Preservation (CHAP)
For Alley Greening: If applicable, a Change of Grade Hearing must be held by DOT

Each gate must have three (3) lock boxes mounted on the gates or adjoining structure: one for Fire Department (Knox box), one for BGE, and one for other utilities, City agencies, and Police Department
Lessee may not impose rules relating to gates without written approval from Director
Lessee may not place permanent chattels (immovable items) in the alley
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact the Land Conveyance Section at 410-396-4283 or alley.gating@baltimorecity.gov to discuss project feasibility and obtain necessary forms. We strongly recommend organizers meet with City staff. 2. Submit the Alley Gating Application with digital images, marked-up City Block Plat, and reason(s) for gating to the Land Conveyance Section (Councilman Harry S Cummings Building, LL 401 E. Fayette Street, Baltimore City, MD 21202). 3. Land Conveyance Section emails the package to utilities and City agencies for comments. Approval from Police Commissioner and Fire Marshall is required. 4. If approved by review agencies, obtain list of abutting property owners and gather written consents from at least 75% of property owners (100% for Alley Greening). Use the two consent forms provided (one for individuals, one for entities). 5. Mail or email copies of: (A) written consents from at least 75% of property owners, (B) affidavits for abandoned properties if applicable, and (C) $250 processing fee check to Land Conveyance Section. 6. Land Conveyance Section will contact applicant with public hearing date, time, and location. 7. Applicant mails notice to all abutting property owners at least 10 days before hearing and posts notice (minimum 11" x 14") at each end of alley. 8. Applicant brings original signed consents and required documents to hearing. Land Conveyance Section prepares affidavit for execution. 9. Director issues written decision within 30 days of hearing. 10. If approved, Land Conveyance Section prepares Lease Agreement (typically 5-year term with four 4-year automatic renewals). Applicant executes and returns three copies. Agreement goes to City Law Department, Director, Mayor's Office, and Board of Estimates for approval. 11. Upon Board of Estimates approval, applicant/contractor obtains necessary permits from HCD Permit Office (417 E. Fayette Street, First Floor, Baltimore, MD 21202). 12. For historic neighborhoods, applicant must obtain CHAP approval. 13. Once permits approved, applicant may have gates built/installed with required lock boxes. For Alley Greening: Follow same procedures with these exceptions: (1) obtain 100% owner consent, (2) submit engineered drawing and follow Developers Agreement process (contact 410-396-3667), (3) schedule Change of Grade Hearing with DOT Transportation Engineering and Construction Division (410-396-6946) if applicable, (4) must have approved Developer's Agreement and executed Lease Agreement before beginning work.

structured_extraction.program_name: B'more Fresh: Online SNAP Produce Incentive
structured_extraction.program_description: B'more Fresh is an online SNAP incentive program administered by Baltimore City that encourages SNAP participants living in Baltimore City to purchase fresh and frozen fruits and vegetables through approved online retailers. Funded by $3.6 million in American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds, the program provides monthly $30 produce vouchers to SNAP participants who spend at least $5 on SNAP-eligible items through participating online retailers (Amazon Fresh, Giant, and Safeway). At Amazon Fresh, participants also receive a $20 delivery promotion coupon each month. The program aims to increase access to home-delivered groceries and address digital equity among Baltimore City residents. It is available until December 2026.

list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SNAP participants in Baltimore City receive a $30 monthly produce voucher after spending at least $5 on SNAP-eligible items through participating online retailers (Amazon Fresh, Giant, or Safeway). The $30 produce benefit coupon is valid for 60 days and can be used to purchase fresh or frozen fruits and vegetables with no added salt, sugar, or fat. Participants can receive one produce benefit coupon (and one delivery coupon at Amazon Fresh) each month. The program is funded by $3.6 million in ARPA funds and is available until December 2026.

The program offers working capital, equipment financing, and leasehold improvement financing with more accommodating terms than traditional lenders. Collateral may be required depending on the loan type. The Micro Loan Program serves businesses with maximum revenue of $5 million.

Eligible business types include sole proprietors, partnerships, corporations, LLCs, startups, retailers, service providers, and contractors.

requirements_list: Low-income eligibility

structured_extraction.program_description: The Fair Election Fund provides matching City funds to eligible candidates running for City elective office. It offers public campaign financing to reduce the influence of large contributions and encourage small private donations from residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides matching City funds to candidates who meet eligibility requirements. Candidates must be City residents running for Mayor, Comptroller, City Council President, or City Council in a contested primary and/or general election. Matching funds are provided based on qualifying contributions received. Eligibility requires receiving a minimum number of qualifying contributions (up to $150 each) from City residents: Mayor requires at least 500 qualifying contributions totaling $40,000; Council President requires at least 250 qualifying contributions totaling $15,000; Comptroller requires at least 250 qualifying contributions totaling $15,000; City Council requires at least 150 qualifying contributions totaling $5,000. Once certified, candidates receive matching funds for contributions up to $150 per contributor.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Campaign financing for candidates for City elective office.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City residents only. Candidates must be City residents running for City elective office.

Must be running in a contested primary and/or general election

Must receive minimum qualifying contributions from City residents (amounts vary by office)

Council President: at least 250 qualifying contributions totaling $15,000
Comptroller: at least 250 qualifying contributions totaling $15,000

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Candidates must be certified for public funding by the State Board of Elections and meet the minimum qualifying contribution thresholds for their office. Once certified, candidates are eligible to receive matching funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program that provides services and support to family caregivers caring for their loved ones in Baltimore City. The program offers individual counseling, educational classes and training, support groups, respite care (in-home, adult day care, overnight, weekend, emergency, and recreational), and supplemental services such as home repairs, medical supplies, and legal aid. Services are available for those caring for older adults (60+), relative caregivers (55+ caring for minors or adults with disabilities), or anyone providing unpaid family care. The program operates through the National Caregivers Support Program and awards are made on a first-come, first-served basis subject to fund availability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides non-emergency financial assistance to caregivers to pay for respite or supplemental services. Grant funds may be paid directly to the caregiver, the care recipient, or an outside agency for respite or in-home services. Funds can be used to hire providers for respite services or to reimburse out-of-pocket expenses related to caregiving. Supplemental services include medical expenses (prescription/over-the-counter medication, doctor/hospital bills, medical supplies), nutritional supplements, household repairs, household bills, clothing, bedding, household appliances, housing costs (rent/mortgage), school supplies, cleaning supplies, and respite services (adult/child day care, summer camp, after school programs). Receipts for food are not acceptable unless for nutritional supplements. Processing time may take up to 90 days. Awards are made on a first-come, first-served basis subject to fund availability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family caregivers caring for older adults age 60 and older, relative caregivers age 55 and older caring for minors or adults with disabilities, or anyone providing unpaid family care for a senior or adult with disabilities in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Individual counseling, educational classes, support groups, respite care services, caregiver training, referrals, home repairs, medical supplies, legal aid, household repairs, household bills, clothing, bedding, household appliances, housing costs (rent/mortgage), school supplies, cleaning supplies, nutritional supplements, and reimbursement for out-of-pocket caregiving expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. The care recipient must be a Baltimore City resident. The geographic distance between the caregiver and care recipient cannot exceed a 25-mile radius. If the caregiver and care recipient do not live in the same household, a notarized letter must be provided stating the name of the primary caregiver.

Care recipient for seniors must require assistance with at least two activities of daily living (ADLs), verified by medical doctor or medical practitioner on Medical Status Verification Form

Geographic distance between caregiver and care recipient cannot exceed 25-mile radius

Complete all application forms in the application packet

Complete caregiver assessment with program social worker
Provide copies of receipts, invoices, or bills accompanying the request
Complete W-9 form before payment is disbursed

Provide copy of unaltered Social Security card for both caregiver and care recipient
For seniors 60+: Medical Status Verification Form completed by care recipient's primary care physician indicating ADLs requiring assistance

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Baltimore City Family Caregivers at 410-396-1337 or 443-615-6233 to inquire about services and eligibility or download application packet online at https://health.baltimorecity.gov/family-caregivers-program. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis subject to fund availability. Processing time may take up to 90 days.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Local Hiring Law and Employ Baltimore Executive Order
structured_extraction.program_description: A set of regulatory requirements mandating that contractors and vendors doing business with Baltimore City on city-funded contracts must hire Baltimore City residents. The Baltimore City Local Hiring Law applies to city-awarded contracts over $300,000 and city-subsidized projects over $5,000,000, requiring that 51% of all new hires be Baltimore City residents. The Employ Baltimore Executive Order applies to city contracts between $50,000 and $300,000 (excluding emergency and professional services), requiring businesses to work with MOED to hire local residents. Both programs provide free MOED services including job posting, applicant pre-screening, interview space, tax credits, recruitment help, and training reimbursement to help businesses meet local hiring goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses contracting with Baltimore City receive free MOED services including tax credits, recruitment assistance, pre-screening of job applicants, free interview space, workforce consultation, and training reimbursement. The Local Hiring Law applies to city-awarded contracts over $300,000 and city-subsidized projects over $5,000,000, requiring a goal of 51% Baltimore City resident new hires and monthly employment reports. The Employ Baltimore Executive Order applies to city contracts between $50,000 and $300,000 (excluding emergency and professional services), requiring workforce meetings with MOED and bi-annual employment reports. Vendors and contractors subject to local hiring must add new hires to their vendor profile in the B2Gnow system, complete employment analyses projecting workforce needs, report new hire information including address and residency status, and track jobs posted with MOED.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Vendors, contractors, and subcontractors awarded city contracts of $50,000 or more, or involved in city-subsidized projects over $5,000,000. The Local Hiring Law covers contracts over $300,000 and city-subsidized projects over $5,000,000; the Employ Baltimore Executive Order covers contracts between $50,000 and $300,000 (excluding emergency and professional services).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Businesses use MOED services for workforce planning, recruitment, hiring support, job posting, pre-screening of applicants, free interview space, training reimbursement, and tax credit benefits when filling positions on city-funded projects with Baltimore City residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applies to city-funded contracts and city-subsidized projects in Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Meet with MOED within 2 weeks after contract award to complete an Employment Analysis (Local Hiring Law, contracts over $300,000)
Contact MOED to schedule a workforce meeting within two weeks after the contract award (Employ Baltimore Executive Order, contracts $50,000–$300,000)
Post new jobs with MOED for a period of seven days only
Utilize MOED's recruitment services for new hires
Meet the goal of 51% of all new hires being Baltimore City residents (Local Hiring Law)
Submit monthly employment reports with current workers, new workers, and Baltimore City residents on the project (Local Hiring Law)

All subcontractors must also comply (Local Hiring Law)

Add all new hires to vendor profile in B2Gnow system with employee information including first name, last name, SSN (last four digits), position, date hired, pay rate, referral source, education level, benefits offered, hours per week, and home address including city and zip code to verify residency
Complete employment analysis in B2Gnow projecting total company employees, workers needed for the contract, workers needed from subcontractors, and whether recruitment is needed

Report new hire information monthly including total workers on contract, Baltimore City residents, existing workers assigned, new openings created, openings posted with MOED, new hires, and Baltimore City residents hired

Vendors with collective bargaining agreements covering certain positions may apply for waivers to exempt union-hired positions from MOED recruitment requirements, but all non-union positions and the 51% residency goal must still be met
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: After a city contract is awarded, the business or vendor must contact MOED within two weeks to schedule a workforce meeting or employment analysis. For contracts over $300,000, businesses meet with MOED Employer Services staff to complete an Employment Analysis in B2Gnow, discuss staffing needs, and learn about available free services. For contracts between $50,000 and $300,000, businesses schedule a workforce meeting with MOED. MOED will contact the vendor upon receipt of the Vendor Contact Form from the City agency. When hiring, businesses must register in the B2Gnow system, add new hire employee information to their vendor profile, post job openings to MOED for seven days before hiring, and utilize MOED's recruitment services. The system generates monthly employment reports (due by the first business day of the month for the previous month) where vendors report total workers, new hires, residency status, and jobs posted with MOED. For the Local Hiring Law (contracts over $300,000), monthly reports are required throughout the contract term. For the Employ Baltimore Executive Order (contracts $50,000–$300,000), bi-annual employment reports are required. Vendors with questions can contact hirelocal@baltimorecity.gov for assistance completing employment analyses and other compliance documentation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore City Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Program (OADPOP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Program (OADPOP) provides clean syringes and allows disposal of used syringes to people who use drugs, aiming to reduce the circulation of contaminated needles and lower incidences of HIV, hepatitis C, and other blood-borne infections. The program helps individuals with substance use disorders access addiction treatment services through referrals to drug treatment centers. It also provides free and confidential counseling and testing for HIV and syphilis, and offers opioid overdose response training with naloxone at all program locations. Services are available at 11 locations during 18 weekly time slots throughout Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free and confidential syringe services at 11 locations during 18 weekly time slots throughout Baltimore City. Services include needle exchange (clean syringes and used syringe disposal), counseling and testing for HIV and syphilis, opioid overdose response training with naloxone kits, and referrals to drug treatment and addiction recovery services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with substance use disorders, people who use drugs, and other high-risk individuals in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Syringe exchange services (clean syringes and used syringe disposal), HIV and syphilis testing and counseling, opioid overdose response training and naloxone kits, and referrals to drug treatment and addiction recovery services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, with mobile outreach services available at 11 locations within the city.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Walk-in services available at designated mobile sites during scheduled hours throughout the week. No application process required. Individuals can access the program through Syringe Exchange Program sites throughout Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.program_name: CFY 2027 Transportation Services Request for Proposals (Shelter Transportation Grant)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Mayor's Office of Homeless Services provides competitive grant funding to organizations to deliver free transportation services to individuals and families experiencing homelessness in Baltimore City. The transportation takes people to shelters and other homeless services program locations within the Baltimore Continuum of Care. Services are required during both the winter shelter period (October 15 through March 31) and non-winter shelter period (April 1 through October 14). Services prioritize assistance based on vulnerability and severity of service needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding to provide free transportation services to homeless individuals and families to shelters and other homeless services program locations within the Baltimore Continuum of Care. Services must be offered during the winter shelter period (October 15 through March 31) operating 5:45 am to 10:00 pm daily, and non-winter shelter period (April 1 through October 14) operating 5:45 am to 9:00 am and 4:00 pm to 7:00 pm daily. During Code Blue Extreme Cold Alerts (when wind chill is 13°F or below), providers must operate a minimum of four 15-passenger wheelchair-accessible vehicles plus two replacement vehicles. During non-Code Blue weather, providers must operate a minimum of two to three 15-passenger wheelchair-accessible vehicles plus two replacement vehicles. Grant recipients must maintain vehicles at their own facility, establish communication systems for real-time dispatch, track ridership data, and provide monthly reports including financial expenditures, vehicle mileage and maintenance logs, and incident reports.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit, for-profit, and government organizations capable of providing transportation services for homeless populations in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing free transportation services to shelters and other homeless services program locations within the Baltimore Continuum of Care, including but not limited to staff salaries, fringe benefits, vehicle operations, maintenance, fuel, insurance, supplies, equipment, training, and administrative costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services must be provided within Baltimore City and the Baltimore Continuum of Care. Required service locations include: Pinderhughes School, Manna House, WHRC, Sarah's Hope, Monument Street Shelter, Project PLASE, My Sister's Place, Beans and Bread, Division of Vital Records, Birth and Death Records, DSS Broadway, DSS Penn, DSS Biddle, and Social Security Office.
requirements_list: Must be a registered non-profit 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization, for-profit organization, or another city agency

Must have two years of most recent independent audits (financial statements are not accepted)
Must agree to participate in the Baltimore Continuum of Care (BCOC) meetings and be part of the collaborative body if granted an award
Must provide non-discrimination approach regardless of where or how people present for services
Must identify service needs and gaps to assist in planning targeted transportation assistance
Must avoid conflicts of interest, with employees, officers, and volunteers required to sign a statement confirming they have read and will comply with conflict of interest policies
Religious organizations must provide services free from religious influences and cannot discriminate on the basis of religion in employment or service provision
Must conduct criminal background checks for all employees and maintain records for at least three years after termination
Must establish and enforce a code of conduct for transportation staff
Must ensure all staff adhere to MOHS conduct policies regarding incidents (altercations, injuries, illnesses, accidents)
Must provide vehicle operators with access to real-time communication devices (two-way radios or cell phones)
Must assist disabled clients with moving personal belongings
Must establish a data tracking system including daily ridership by location, call volume, and driver logs
Must maintain a financial tracking system with line-item categories for personnel, services, administrative fees, and other costs
Must maintain all original invoices and receipts in a secure location

Must develop and maintain comprehensive records including signed agreements, budgets, personnel lists, job descriptions, organizational chart, financial reports, Certificate of Occupancy, business license, fiscal controls certification, insurance policies, and workplace policies
Must develop and submit standard operating procedures, policy documents, training plans, and monitoring plans for MOHS approval
Must develop and submit a vehicle maintenance plan covering routine maintenance, minor repairs, major repairs, and fueling
Must provide monthly reports to MOHS including financial expenditure reports, vehicle mileage and maintenance logs, and shuttle incidents
Must utilize company-owned or leased vehicles and be responsible for establishing and maintaining appropriate liability insurance
Must park and maintain vehicles at provider's own facility

Must collaborate with MOHS in devising mandatory staff training including customer service, cultural competency and sensitivity, mental health first aid, trauma-informed care, non-violent crisis intervention, CPR/First Aid/Bloodborne Pathogens, and Critical Incident Reporting
Must ensure data and reports are stored electronically in an approved database system
Must cooperate with MOHS and any successor providers to ensure smooth transition of property, equipment, activities, and records upon award expiration or termination
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit a comprehensive proposal in response to the Request for Proposals during the designated window. The application must include a narrative addressing components outlined in the RFP, completed application forms, a detailed budget proposal, and supporting documentation. Proposals are reviewed by a committee comprised of MOHS staff, a Local Elected Official (LEC) member, CoC Board Leadership, and a Community Liaison member using a point-based scoring system. Organizations may be required to participate in a Bidder's Conference to discuss the request for proposals. MOHS reserves the right to request additional information from applicants and may conduct interviews prior to making final award decisions. Successful applicants will execute an Agreement and receive a Notice of Grant Award.

structured_extraction.program_description: An outreach program that provides short-term care coordination services to Baltimore City residents. The program assists Medicaid and HealthChoice eligible beneficiaries in accessing and using their Medicaid benefits, links clients to Maryland's Managed Care Program (HealthChoice), educates clients about health benefits, connects them to primary care and specialty services, works to improve birth outcomes with prenatal outreach strategies, and provides access to health services and community resources for vulnerable populations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term care coordination services including education about health benefits, linkage to primary care and specialty services, prenatal outreach support, and connection to health services and community resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents who are Medicaid or HealthChoice eligible beneficiaries, particularly pregnant and postpartum people
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Care coordination services, health benefit education, primary and specialty care linkage, and prenatal outreach support
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City resident
Must be Medicaid or HealthChoice eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 410-649-0500 or visit Healthcare Access Maryland's website at https://www.healthcareaccessmaryland.org/ to connect to care coordination services.

The program provides seasonal grant funding to help keep vacant lots clean and well-maintained, contributing to neighborhood beautification efforts.

Funds are awarded on a seasonal basis to eligible nonprofit organizations operating in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations registered as 501c3 nonprofits or those with 501c3 fiscal sponsors operating in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mowing and maintenance of up to 25 vacant lots during the growing season (April through October).

Must operate in Baltimore City

Not for landscaping, small haulers, or other small businesses

structured_extraction.program_description: The Casino Local Impact Funds Program distributes a portion of Maryland casino gaming revenues to benefit communities surrounding casinos. In Baltimore City, these funds support infrastructure investments, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development including housing, and other public services and investments within the designated South Baltimore Gateway area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Casino Local Impact Funds are allocated through annual spending plans developed by the City of Baltimore Department of Planning with the nine South Baltimore Gateway Master Plan goals as a foundation. According to Maryland State Government Article § 9-1A-31, local impact grants to Baltimore City for video lottery facilities may be used for improvements primarily in communities in immediate proximity to the facility, including: infrastructure improvements, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development including housing, and other public services and improvements. Beginning in fiscal year 2018, at least 50% of local impact grants shall be distributed directly to the South Baltimore Gateway Community Impact District Management Authority. Funds are allocated annually through the City budget process. The specific allocation amounts and project funding decisions are determined annually and included in the City budget based on the Local Development Council's input.
structured_extraction.program_audience: The City of Baltimore and communities in the South Baltimore Gateway area surrounding the Horseshoe Casino, including residents and businesses within immediate proximity to the facility
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure investments, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development including housing, and other public services and investments that align with the nine South Baltimore Gateway Master Plan goals: Transportation Connectivity, Environmental Sustainability, Safety, Community Development and Revitalization, Economic Growth, Education, Health and Wellness, Quality of Life, and Infrastructure. At least 50% must be distributed to the South Baltimore Gateway Community Impact District Management Authority beginning in fiscal year 2018.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Funds are designated for the South Baltimore Gateway, a geographic area in immediate proximity to the Horseshoe Casino within Baltimore City. The South Baltimore Gateway Master Plan boundaries define the eligible service area.
requirements_list: Video lottery facility must be operating in Baltimore City
Expenditures must be consistent with the South Baltimore Gateway Master Plan
At least 50% of funds must be distributed to the South Baltimore Gateway Community Impact District Management Authority (beginning fiscal year 2018)
County or municipality must develop multiyear plan for expenditure in consultation with Local Development Council
Plan must be submitted to Local Development Council for review and comment before adoption
Local Development Council has 45 days to review, comment, and make recommendations
Baltimore City must hold public hearing on expenditure plan
Best efforts must be made to accommodate Local Development Council recommendations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The City of Baltimore Department of Planning develops annual spending plans for Casino Local Impact Funds in consultation with the Local Development Council, City Agencies, community partners, and neighborhood associations. The process involves: (1) Development of a multiyear expenditure plan aligned with the nine South Baltimore Gateway Master Plan goals; (2) Submission of the plan to the Local Development Council for review and comment; (3) Public hearing held by Baltimore City on the proposed plan; (4) Local Development Council review period of 45 days for recommendations; (5) Best efforts made to accommodate Local Development Council recommendations; (6) Final funding decisions incorporated into the City budget for approval by the Mayor and City Council. Individual project applications are not accepted; funding is allocated through this annual City budgeting process.

High school diploma or GED

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Health Department works to reduce lead poisoning in children through primary prevention, lead testing, home visits and case management, advocacy, and enforcement of the city's lead laws.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides primary prevention services including preventative home visits to low-income pregnant women and families with children under age 6 to assess lead hazards, referrals to legal and financial resources, education and supplies for home environmental health issues, and blood lead testing. BCHD conducts Healthy Homes Gatherings in high-risk neighborhoods offering lead poisoning prevention education. Point of Care blood lead testing is provided at health fairs and community events. For families with lead-poisoned children, the program offers telephonic or in-person education and case management services lasting at least six months, including education about lead hazards, cleaning, nutrition, referrals to social and environmental programs, and re-testing reminders.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income pregnant women, families with children ages 1-6, children ages 1-2 for mandatory testing, families with children who have elevated blood lead levels
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services are provided at no cost to participants and include lead hazard assessment, education, testing, case management, referrals to legal and financial resources for lead abatement
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Families must have children under age 6 for prevention visits
Children ages 12 and 24 months must be tested per Baltimore City Health Code mandate
Families with children having blood lead levels at or above 5 micrograms per deciliter are eligible for case management services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For prevention services, eligible families are identified and offered home visits. For families with lead-poisoned children, contact is initiated based on lab results from Maryland Department of Environment, and families are offered education and case management. Community members can also access services through Healthy Homes Gatherings held in neighborhood communities, Head Start Centers, Judy Centers, Family Support Centers, Community Centers, and other settings. Point of Care testing is available at health fairs and community events.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Baltimore Lead Hazard Reduction and Healthy Homes Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive program providing lead hazard control measures and healthy homes interventions to assist low to moderate income households with children under age six who have elevated blood lead levels, living in homes built before 1978. Services include lead risk assessments, lead hazard reduction activities such as window replacement and paint stabilization, healthy homes housing assessments, environmental hazard interventions, outreach and education, and post-remediation home visits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HUD is providing $4,100,000 in grant funding through the Lead-Based Paint Hazard Reduction Program ($3,600,000) and Healthy Homes Supplemental grant ($500,000). The program will run for 48 months from April 1, 2026 to April 1, 2030. The City is providing $1,516,000 in matching local funds. The grant funds support comprehensive lead hazard control and healthy homes interventions including risk assessments, hazard reduction activities, housing assessments, interventions, outreach and education sessions, and home visits for eligible households.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low to moderate income households with children under age six who have elevated blood lead levels and reside in dwellings constructed prior to 1978 in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead-based paint risk assessments, lead hazard reduction including window replacement and paint stabilization, dust wipe clearance testing, healthy homes housing rating system assessments, environmental and safety hazard interventions, outreach and education sessions, and post-remediation home visits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Baltimore; specifically targeting dwellings constructed prior to 1978 where residents have elevated blood lead levels.
requirements_list: Household must be low to moderate income
Must have children under age six
Children must have elevated blood lead levels (5 ug/dL and above)
Dwelling must have been constructed prior to 1978
Dwelling must be located in City of Baltimore
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The City of Baltimore Department of Housing & Community Development submitted a request to HUD for release of funds on or about April 14, 2026. HUD will process the certification and release of funds. Program implementation will follow with lead risk assessments, hazard reduction activities, healthy homes assessments and interventions, and educational outreach to eligible households.

The program provides holistic support including trauma-informed counseling, rental assistance, expungement services, GED programs, driving license training, resume writing, interview coaching, and leadership development.

Employees receive trauma-informed counseling, rental assistance, expungement services, GED programs, Certified Driving License training, resume writing, interview coaching, conflict resolution training, and leadership training.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed and underemployed residents in the 42 targeted underinvested neighborhoods of Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment wages and supportive services for workforce development including counseling, rental assistance, expungement services, education and training programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Operates in 42 underinvested neighborhoods across Baltimore City including Belair Edison, Berea, Broadway East, Coldstream Homestead Montebello, Darley Park, East Baltimore-Midway, Four by Four, Johnston Square, Madison Eastend, McElderry Park, Milton-Montford, Oliver, South Clifton Park, Auchentoroly-Parkwood, Central Forest Park, Druid Heights, Edgewood, Forest Park, Fallstaff, Glen, Harlem Park, Midtown-Edmondson, Mondawmin, Mosher, Penn North, Sandtown-Winchester, Upton, Carroll-Camden, Carrollton Ridge, Cherry Hill, Franklin Square, FSO/Boyd Booth, Lakeland, Mount Clare, Mount Winans, Pigtown, Saint Paul, and Westport
requirements_list: Reside in one of the 42 target neighborhoods
Be unemployed or underemployed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested residents should contact the Clean Corps Program via email at cleancorpsbaltimore@gmail.com or call 410-396-2929 for information on how to apply and join the workforce.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 12-week, paid, in-person leadership course that helps residents and local leaders build skills in community development, violence prevention, environmental design, and neighborhood improvement to strengthen public safety and lead community revitalization in their neighborhoods.

Participants gain hands-on experience and practical skills in community leadership and organizing, environmental design and neighborhood improvement, public safety strategy and violence prevention, storytelling, grant writing, project planning, and data-informed problem solving. Participants also have the opportunity to design and implement grant-funded neighborhood improvement projects within their own communities.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants design and implement grant-funded neighborhood improvement projects within their own communities.

Must be interested in community development, violence prevention, and neighborhood improvement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants can register for information sessions on April 16, 2026 (in-person) or April 29, 2026 (virtual) to learn more about the program. Applications are submitted online through an Office Forms link and close on May 3, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Land Trusts - Operating Costs NOFA
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to Community Land Trust organizations for operational and capacity building support to provide affordable housing to low and very low income households in Baltimore City.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $500,000 total from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund are available. Qualified applicants can request up to $100,000 per Community Land Trust entity. Eligible uses of funds include: market and financial feasibility analysis, carrying costs, financing and lender fees, legal fees associated with closing, financing, and drafting CLT-required documents, project management staff, and general organizational operating costs such as rent, utilities, salaries, and operating supplies. Funds are limited to operating, predevelopment, and support costs directly related to creating affordable units for residents with 50% or below area median income (AMI).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Submission Deadline: October 6, 2023 by 4:00 PM EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Land Trust organizations registered as Affordable Housing Land Trusts in Maryland serving low and very low income households in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating, predevelopment and support costs for Community Land Trusts creating affordable housing units. Eligible uses include market and financial feasibility analysis, carrying costs, financing and lender fees, legal fees, project management staff, and general organizational operating costs such as rent, utilities, salaries, and operating supplies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Must be a Community Land Trust organization with 501(c)(2), (3), or (4) tax-exempt status or be a legally organized business entity managed by a nonprofit
Must be registered as an Affordable Housing Land Trust with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation and comply with Section 14 of the Annotated Code of Maryland Real Property Article
Must have By-Laws establishing terms for board of directors, officers, stewardship, conflicts of interest, ownership, open membership criteria, resale limitations, and dissolution

Must have a tri-partite board of directors comprised of one-third community members, one-third land trust residents (when available), and one-third local stakeholders and experts, or an equivalent balancing structure
Must have been in operation as a land trust for a minimum of 2 years
Must show proof of 5 or more affordable units built and/or in the process of being built under the land trust model for residents with 50% or below area median income (AMI)
Must have active projects/activities/partnerships with DHCD in the past 24 months and/or provide essential statewide/regional advocacy in affordable housing and/or fair housing
Must be in good standing with DHCD with no outstanding fees, reports, loan payments, or unresolved compliance issues
Must not be on the federal or state debarred list
Only one application may be made per organization
Applicants must be able to demonstrate organizational capacity to manage a Community Land Trust and leverage other sources of funds for operating costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted electronically through the Neighborly portal in PDF format with one Excel spreadsheet copy of the operating budget. Pre-proposal conference held on September 6, 2023. Written questions accepted through September 8, 2023. Submission deadline is October 6, 2023 by 4:00 PM EST. DHCD staff conducts threshold review of organizational, financial, and compliance requirements. Applications meeting threshold requirements are reviewed and ranked by staff. Final recommendations go to the Housing Commissioner who determines awards. Awardees notified by phone and in writing. Applicants may request a 30-minute debriefing. Following Board of Estimates approval of Funding Agreement, funds become available. Awardees required to submit annual reports by December 30, 2024.

structured_extraction.program_description: A citywide initiative that expands Baltimore's capacity to prevent violence through non-law enforcement interventions. The program mediates conflicts before they escalate into violence, changes community norms around gun violence acceptability, and addresses root causes through partnerships with community-based organizations providing outreach, mediation, violence intervention, hospital-based response, life coaching, and victim services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City has expanded from ten contracts to at least 50 contracts with community-based organizations. Over $3 million has been allocated specifically to support hospital-based violence intervention programs. The exact award amounts and terms for individual contracts are not detailed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations providing violence intervention, outreach, mediation, hospital-based response, life coaching, and victim services in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports outreach, mediation and violence intervention services, hospital-based violence response programs, life coaching, case management services, and victim services to prevent violence and support individuals at risk.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations are selected through a contracting process. MONSE is actively contracting with selected organizations.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Transportation lets community groups create fun and creative projects in public spaces like streets, sidewalks, and alleys to make neighborhoods look nicer, help slow down traffic, and give people more space to walk and gather. Projects can include artistic painting, landscape plantings, planters and barriers for traffic calming, signs, parklets or temporary public spaces, and other special projects like art installations or lighting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DOT provides technical assistance and approval processes for community groups to implement placemaking projects in public right-of-way spaces. The sponsoring group must pay for and implement the project themselves. For parklets and special projects, commercial liability insurance ($1 million per occurrence, $2 million aggregate) is required. DOT reviews applications and designs, and upon approval, issues a written agreement outlining what has been approved, project timeline, maintenance responsibilities, and any special rules.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community groups, neighborhood associations, local businesses, nonprofits, and school parent groups wanting to create placemaking projects in public spaces.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating artistic painting on streets or sidewalks, landscape plantings, planters and barriers for traffic calming, signs, parklets or temporary public spaces in the roadway, and other special projects like art installations or special lighting in public right-of-way spaces.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Submit design rendering showing the project
Identify the specific location(s) of the project
List the materials to be used

Provide letters of support or signed petitions from adjacent occupants (renters and owners): for parklets and mid-block projects 60% of block occupants must sign; for intersections 60% of occupants of three properties in each direction must sign
Provide proof of property owner support from properties directly abutting the project
Provide proof that the organization is in good standing with the State of Maryland
For parklets and special projects: obtain commercial liability insurance of $1 million per occurrence and $2 million in aggregate
Include a maintenance plan for the project
Paint designs cannot incorporate words or political messages and must use pre-approved paint types
Designs and materials must be reviewed and approved by DOT before installation
All projects must be open to the public
Designs must not contain obscene, vulgar, or violent messages
Projects must not block walkways or violate Americans with Disabilities Act requirements
Projects must not introduce roadway safety hazards or block sight distance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit your project designs and documents through the Community Based Programs Application available on the DOT website. If traffic calming elements are part of your project, traffic calming must be installed first either by submitting a request to 311 or by hiring a contractor with DOT-approved plans. DOT will review your application and designs for compliance with all requirements. When approved, you will receive a written agreement explaining what has been approved, project timeline, maintenance responsibilities, and any special rules. Projects are processed on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A recurring competitive grant opportunity administered by Baltimore City that combines funding from multiple sources to support qualified nonprofit organizations providing services to individuals and families who are at-risk of homelessness, currently homeless, or living with HIV or AIDS. Organizations submit one consolidated application and are considered for funding across multiple eligible funding streams simultaneously. The program has operated across multiple fiscal years (FY2022, FY2023, FY2024) and supports a broad range of housing and supportive services including emergency shelter, transitional housing, rapid re-housing, street outreach, permanent supportive housing, and HIV/AIDS services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding drawn from multiple sources: U.S.Department of Housing and Urban Development Emergency Solutions Grant (ESG), State of Maryland Homeless Solutions Program (HSP), Baltimore City Department of Social Services (DSS), U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Housing Opportunities forPersons with AIDS/HIV (HOPWA), Maryland Department of Health State Special Funds (SSF), and Baltimore City General Funds. Eligible programs must have a clearly defined budget, demonstrate organizational capacity, and provide services that align with the applicable funding stream requirements. Grant awards support program operations during the applicable City Fiscal Year (July 1through June 30). Organizations must submit separate budget workbooks by project type. Funding is competitive and awarded based on proposal quality, organizational capacity, and alignment with funding priorities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 17, 2023 at 4:00 p.m. EST (FY2024); March 14, 2022 at 4:00 pm EST (FY2023); March 26, 2021 at 4:00 pm (FY2022)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified nonprofit organizations providing services to individuals and families who are at-risk of homelessness, currently homeless, or living with HIV or AIDS in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used for emergency shelter, drop-in and day center services, transitional housing, rapid re-housing, housing stabilization, homelessness prevention, eviction prevention, street outreach, permanent supportive housing case management, and housing and supportive services for people living with HIV or AIDS.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Organizations must be qualified nonprofits providing services to individuals and families at-risk of homelessness, currently homeless, and/or living with HIV or AIDS
New and renewal project proposals are eligible
Organizations must submit a single consolidated application with required supporting documentation

Separate budget workbooks must be completed depending on project type (emergency shelter, transitional housing, housing stabilization, rapid re-housing, street outreach, permanent supportive housing, HIV/AIDS services, drop-in/day center, or homelessness/eviction prevention)
Programs must operate during the applicable City Fiscal Year performance period (July 1 through June 30)
Organizations must demonstrate organizational capacity and fiscal management capability
All applications must include required compliance documentation and organizational information
Projects must align with eligible funding stream requirements and program guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit a single Consolidated Funding Application that is reviewed for consideration across multiple eligible funding sources. Applicants must choose between a new project application or a renewal application template. A Bidder's Conference webinar is held prior to the application deadline to provide guidance on the application requirements and answer questions. Applicants complete the appropriate budget workbook(s) for their service type(s). Applications are submitted via email to HSPApplications@baltimorecity.gov by the stated deadline. Applications are evaluated competitively across all eligible funding streams. Award decisions are made based on proposal quality, organizational capacity, and alignment with funding priorities. Awards are announced following the application review period.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant competition through which the Mayor's Office of Homeless Services seeks proposals from qualified non-profit organizations to provide services to individuals and families who are at-risk of homelessness, currently homeless, low-income and living with HIV or AIDS, and those at risk of crises including those with behavioral health needs. Programs submit one application and can be considered for multiple eligible funding sources including federal, state, and city funds. Awards have a performance period of July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026 (City Fiscal Year 2026).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding drawn from multiple sources: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Emergency Solutions Grant (ESG) estimated $1,895,820.00 with approximately $1,853,633.00 available for projects; State of Maryland Homeless Solutions Program (HSP) estimated $3,297,802.00 with approximately $2,968,022.00 available; Baltimore City Department of Social Services (DSS) approximately $314,128.00 for emergency shelter and supportive services, plus $250,000-$500,000 for supportive services at Restoration Gardens; U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS/HIV (HOPWA) estimated $7,238,355.00 with approximately $200,000.00 available for Baltimore City programs; Baltimore City Opioid Restitution Fund (TBD) for 24/7 comprehensive outreach services; Baltimore City General Funds approximately $9,000,000.00 for comprehensive outreach and emergency shelter. Funding supports transitional housing, street outreach, rapid re-housing, permanent supportive housing, housing stabilization and homelessness prevention, housing and services for people with HIV/AIDS, emergency shelter, comprehensive street outreach, and essential services. Awards have a performance period of July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026. Conditional awards are announced in April 2025, followed by contract development in May 2025. All awards are conditional and subject to change until executed grant agreements are received from funding sources and a contract is fully executed by the Board of Estimates.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified non-profit organizations providing services to individuals and families who are at-risk of homelessness, currently homeless, low-income and living with HIV or AIDS, or at risk of crises including those with behavioral health needs. Organizations must have 501(c)(3) non-profit status, be in good standing with the State of Maryland, and be able to submit applications via the Neighborly portal.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services for individuals and families who are at-risk of homelessness, currently homeless, low-income and living with HIV or AIDS, or at risk of crises including those with behavioral health needs. Eligible service categories and activities include: comprehensive outreach services (24/7 operation with peer support and behavioral health clinical support, accessible to police and EMS); street outreach (engagement, case management, crisis counseling, transportation); emergency shelter (overnight or day shelter, essential support services, food, transportation, motel vouchers); rapid re-housing (housing identification, rental and financial assistance, case management); housing stabilization and homelessness prevention (rental and financial assistance, case management, relocation services); housing and services for people with HIV/AIDS (short-term rent, mortgage and utility assistance, permanent housing placement, employment and education services, childcare services, legal services); support services for permanent supportive housing (case management, linkage to job training, health care, budgeting, parenting skills, treatment); and transitional housing.

Lobbying Certification (SF-LLL form)

Record Retention Policy

Renewal projects: no significant monitoring findings
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted electronically via the Neighborly portal by March 21, 2025 at 5:00 p.m. EST. No submissions accepted via email. Create an account and log into the Neighborly portal before the deadline. Select your project type (Comprehensive Outreach, Street Outreach, Emergency Shelter, Rapid Re-Housing, Housing Stabilization & Homelessness Prevention, Housing and Services for People with HIV/AIDS, Support Services for Permanent Supportive Housing, or Transitional Housing renewal only). Answer all application questions listed in the Neighborly portal. Complete project budget workbook (Excel template provided for each project type). Upload all supporting documents (policies, procedures, insurance certificates, financial statements, board/staff lists, certifications). Ensure an authorized individual at your agency uploads all materials and certifies the submission. Add two points of contact for your organization in the portal. Review requirements including Housing First Agreement, Fair Housing Compliance form, and Lobbying Certification form—all must be signed in the portal. Neighborly will send an automated confirmation message upon receipt. All applications are reviewed in stages: (1) Completeness and timeliness review; (2) Eligibility review examining activities, costs, and financial health risk assessment; (3) If passing steps 1-2, projects proceed to scoring based on project intent and scope, approach and performance, budget, project design, overall quality of proposal, project compliance (renewal only), and performance outcomes (renewal only). Application review period runs from March 21-April 17, 2025. Conditional awards are announced in April 2025. Contract development begins in May 2025. Grant term begins July 1, 2025. Optional Bidder's Conference webinar was held on February 18, 2025 at 2:00 p.m. (recording and slide deck posted on MOHS website). Organizations with contracts exceeding $300,000 are subject to Local Hiring requirements and must meet with the Mayor's Office of Employment Development (MOED). Organizations with contracts between $50,001 and $300,001 are subject to Employ Baltimore Executive Order requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Continue COVID-19 Emergency Produce Box Distribution
structured_extraction.program_description: Distributes 15-pound boxes of fresh locally grown produce to residents in food desert communities to increase access to healthy affordable food and address food insecurity following the COVID-19 pandemic.
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City provides a 15-pound box of fresh locally grown produce at no cost to eligible residents. This is a $4.5 million ARPA investment. By the numbers: 133,000 produce boxes distributed, totaling 14 million fruit and vegetable servings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents in Baltimore City healthy food priority areas (food deserts) and communities facing food insecurity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fresh produce for household consumption to address food insecurity and improve nutritional security.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City healthy food priority areas, otherwise known as food deserts.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal funding opportunity to address and reduce homelessness by adding new units of permanent supportive housing through new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation. Approximately $175 million is available nationally, with approximately $110 million reserved for Continuums of Care in states with populations over 2.5 million people, including Baltimore City. The program supports creating permanent supportive housing that enables individuals and families experiencing homelessness where at least one household member has a disability to live independently.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $175 million in one-time federal grants available nationally to support creation of permanent supportive housing units through new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation. Baltimore City Continuum of Care (MD-501) may receive approximately $110 million as a CoC in a state with population over 2.5 million. Individual awards range from $1,000,000 to $10,000,000. No more than 20 percent of the award may be used for other eligible CoC Program activities (supportive services, operating costs, project-based rental assistance); no more than 10 percent may be used for project administration. The selected applicant must provide both supportive services and property management services, with proposals including a developer, property manager, and service provider. A 25 percent match (cash or in-kind) is required of the awarded grant amount, excluding funds for leasing. Grant terms may be 2, 3, 4, or 5 years based on project type.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Baltimore Mayor's Office of Homeless Services (MOHS)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Only the CoC-designated Collaborative Applicant (MOHS) may submit applications. Qualified organizations serving the Baltimore City Continuum of Care (nonprofit organizations, state governments, local governments, Indian Tribes, and public housing agencies) that can provide permanent supportive housing through development, property management, and supportive services may submit proposals to MOHS for consideration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital costs for new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of permanent supportive housing units. Up to 20 percent may be used for eligible CoC Program costs including project-based rental assistance, supportive services, and operating costs. Up to 10 percent may be used for project administrative costs. Eligible capital costs include: acquisition (24 CFR 578.43), rehabilitation (24 CFR 578.45), new construction (24 CFR 578.47), project-based rental assistance (24 CFR 578.51(e)), supportive services (24 CFR 578.53), operating costs (24 CFR 578.55), and project administrative costs (24 CFR 578.59).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City Continuum of Care (MD-501). Projects must be conveniently located near local services such as walking distance to services, reliable transportation access, and access to telehealth capabilities.
requirements_list: Only the CoC-designated Collaborative Applicant (MOHS) may submit applications to HUD
Each Collaborative Applicant may submit only one CoCBuilds application
Selected applicant must provide both supportive services and property management services
Proposals must include a developer, property manager, and service provider either within the same organization or with memoranda of understanding between organizations
Must provide Permanent Supportive Housing serving individuals with a disability and families where at least one household member has a disability and is experiencing homelessness
Projects must provide proof of site control prior to execution of the grant agreement
Completed environmental review required before awarded funds can be drawn
Must meet timeliness standards outlined in 24 CFR 578.85 for new construction and rehabilitation projects
All required federal assurances and certifications must be completed
25 percent match required (cash or in-kind resources) from non-federal sources
No paper or faxed applications accepted; all submissions must be electronic via Grants.gov
Project must demonstrate unmet need for permanent supportive housing
Must comply with Section 3 of the Housing and Urban Development Act of 1968 for employment and training opportunities
Must use CoC's coordinated entry process for referrals to PSH units
Must demonstrate coordination with housing providers, healthcare organizations, and social service providers
Must comply with all applicable federal nondiscrimination requirements including Title VI, Section 504, Fair Housing Act, and others
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The City of Baltimore Mayor's Office of Homeless Services (MOHS) released a Request for Proposals on August 30, 2024. A bidder's conference was held on September 12, 2024 at 3:00 p.m. EST to provide technical assistance. Questions were accepted through Friday, September 20, 2024 at 5:00 p.m. and an RFP Q&A Addendum was released by September 27, 2024. Proposals were submitted electronically to BaltimorePSH@lesardevelopment.com by Friday, October 18, 2024 at 3:00 p.m. EST deadline. Internal review and scoring of proposals occurred October 21-25, 2024. The Resource Allocation Committee (RAC) reviewed and scored proposals and made recommendations October 28-November 4, 2024, with selection panel discussions and interviews if applicable October 28-November 1, 2024. The CoC Board approved recommendations November 1-4, 2024. Final award notices were issued November 11-15, 2024. MOHS submitted the selected application to HUD via Grants.gov by the November 21, 2024 at 11:59:59 p.m. deadline. Grant terms may be 2, 3, 4, or 5 years depending on project type and realistic completion timeframe.
