structured_extraction.program_description: A community-driven grant program that provides funding to support meaningful and measurable community-led projects, including operating funds or physical improvements, in designated neighborhoods around Pimlico Racetrack. Funded through Pimlico Local Impact Aid, which is state revenue generated by video lottery terminal funds, the program supports projects that create tangible change for residents in the Park Heights Master Plan area and the One-Mile Radius.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $500 and $25,000 are awarded to tax-exempt organizations for community-led projects during the 2025 calendar year. Funding is provided through Pimlico Local Impact Aid, which is state revenue generated by video lottery terminal funds. Grant funding is generally disbursed on a 40-40-20 schedule with 40% provided at the start of the project, 40% at the midway point contingent on successful project progress, and 20% at project completion upon submission of a final report. Startup payments are issued within the first four weeks of the grant period upon approval of the final scope of work and grant agreement execution.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Priority Application Deadline: Friday, March 28, 2025 at 11:59 PM EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based non-profit organizations with 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status or fiscal sponsorship, faith-based organizations proposing non-religious public benefit projects, City agencies, and public schools proposing projects that benefit students. Eligible organizations must be based within Baltimore City and located in or serving the Liberty-Wabash, Northwest Community Planning Forum, Coldspring-Newtown areas, and the Park Heights Master Plan Area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community development projects including public art projects (murals, community sculptures), local arts initiatives (workshops, classes, performances), community signage, bicycle amenities, streetscaping and block projects, marketing efforts (website development, promotional activities), education opportunities (speaker series, academic enrichment), community events (neighborhood festivals, recreation), and technical assistance for community associations (professional design, financial, legal services, assistance securing 501(c)(3) status, strategic planning). Funds may support operating funds or physical improvements to create meaningful and measurable change for residents of all ages.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must occur within eligible areas in Baltimore City. In 2025, funding is available for the Park Heights Master Plan Area and the One Mile Radius around Pimlico Racetrack, including: Park Heights Master Plan Area (Northern Parkway (N), Wabash Ave. to Western Maryland Railroad (W), Liberty Heights Ave. (S), Druid Park Dr. (SE), Greenspring Ave. (E)); Northwest Community Planning Forum (Northern Parkway (S), County line (W/N), Jones Falls Expressway (E)); Liberty-Wabash area (Liberty Heights Avenue (S), Northern Parkway (W), Wabash (N/E)); and Coldspring-Newtown area (Northern Parkway (N), Greenspring Avenue (W), West Cold Spring Lane (S), Jones Falls Expressway (E)). All activities and services must take place in eligible areas. Priority is given to organizations based in eligible areas or partnering with organizations based in those neighborhoods.
requirements_list: Eligible organization must be a non-profit organization with 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status recognized by the IRS, a mission-based organization without 501(c)(3) status but with a tax-exempt fiscal sponsor, a faith-based organization proposing a non-religious project benefiting the public, or a public school proposing a community-based project benefiting students
Organization must be based within Baltimore City verified through tax-exempt status documentation
Organizations (or fiscal sponsors) must provide proof of tax-exempt designation through a copy of IRS Determination Letter
Organizations (or fiscal sponsors) must have an active tax identification number
Organizations (or fiscal sponsors) must provide most recent IRS 990 filing, financial statement, or independent audit depending on charitable contributions to organizational budget
Organizations must have a valid bank account in the name of the organization
Organizations must provide Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland Department of Commerce dated no earlier than January 1, 2024
Organizations must provide Board-Approved Organization Budget
Baltimore City may require insurance for projects
Organizations must be current with any City- or State-mandated quarterly reporting requirements tied to Pimlico Local Impact Aid previously received
Projects must be able to be completed within two years from the start of funding
Physical improvement or construction projects require land control or permission from the property owner

Organizations must not engage in activities that improperly discriminate based on race, gender, marital status, sexual preference, age, disability, creed, ethnicity, or grants for religious indoctrination or religious activities
Organizations must be located in and/or serving Park Heights Master Plan Area or One-Mile Radius in Northwest Baltimore City
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open Saturday, March 1, 2025 and are submitted online through JotForm (https://form.jotform.com/250146365495057) by the priority deadline of Friday, March 28, 2025 at 11:59 PM EDT. Applicant Information Session held Tuesday, March 11, 2025 at 7:00 PM EDT. Technical assistance requests and questions can be submitted to pcda@baltimorecity.gov with appropriate subject line. Applications undergo technical review beginning April 1, 2025 to assess eligibility and completeness; applicants with incomplete documentation receive at least 5 calendar days to provide information (cure period begins April 8, 2025). Panel review begins April 14, 2025 using a standard rubric; panels include staff from Department of Planning, Department of Housing and Community Development, and Pimlico Community Development Authority. Award announcements made by June 2025. Awarded grantees receive email with Grant Agreement link; grant agreement must be signed before project begins. Grantees are required to submit quarterly reports by: October 6, 2025; January 12, 2026; April 6, 2026; July 6, 2026; October 12, 2026; January 11, 2027; April 12, 2027; and final report by July 12, 2027. Reports include narrative, performance measures, financial records with proof of payment (receipts, invoices, bank statements), photographs, and videos. Grantees must create Supplier profiles in City's Workday system and submit invoices electronically. Final reports and supporting documentation must be submitted within 60 days of project completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to nonprofit organizations in Baltimore City working to address the opioid crisis through community-based initiatives in prevention, treatment, harm reduction, and recovery. The program is guided by Baltimore City's Overdose Response Strategic Plan and aims to address imminent risks of overdose death and health complications among people actively using drugs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Round 1 (Fiscal Year 2026) makes $2 million total available for allocation across three funding tiers. Tier 1 grants provide up to $50,000 (approximately 3-6 awards) for low-barrier social support services. Tier 2 grants provide up to $250,000 (approximately 2-4 awards) for comprehensive harm reduction services. Tier 3 grants provide up to $500,000 (approximately 2-3 awards) for low-barrier mobile treatment services. Proposed project funding amounts can span up to two years, though organizations may use their full award within a single year and reapply in the following year. Final award amounts may differ from proposed budgets based on scope of work and available funding. Funding supports prevention, treatment, recovery, harm reduction, social determinants of health, and related infrastructure. General organizational overhead is capped at 15% of the grant award.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Proposals due November 23, 2025 at 11:59 p.m. EST; Full applications due January 25, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and community-based organizations in Baltimore City leading efforts to address the opioid crisis through prevention, treatment, harm reduction, and recovery activities. Organizations must have proven experience in Baltimore City, including an operating location and direct experience serving populations impacted by the opioid overdose crisis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports community-based initiatives addressing the opioid crisis aligned with Baltimore City's Overdose Response Strategic Plan. Allowable uses include: (1) Programs, services, and supports for substance use prevention, treatment, recovery, and harm reduction, including social determinants of health addressing harms caused by the opioid epidemic; (2) Infrastructure required for such programs and services; (3) Oversight, planning, assessing, and monitoring of programs; (4) Evaluations of effectiveness and outcomes reporting. Specific allowable and unallowable uses are detailed in Appendix A. Unallowable uses include law enforcement-centered approaches, coercive or abstinence-only services, stigmatizing practices, large-scale construction or real estate purchases, and services already funded through statewide settlements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Organizations must be based in or operate in Baltimore City and serve Baltimore City residents. Physical brick-and-mortar location not required, but organization must demonstrate operational presence and history of serving people in Baltimore City (e.g., operating out of partner sites such as churches or community centers is acceptable).
requirements_list: Applicant organization must be a nonprofit (not for-profit)
For Tier 2 or Tier 3 funding, organization must have 501(c)(3) status; for Tier 1, community-based organizations are eligible if registered and in good standing with State of Maryland
Organization must be in good financial standing and have a valid Employer Identification Number (EIN)
Organization must not have already received funding or have an earmark to receive funds in FY26 from Baltimore City's ORF

Organization must have proven experience in Baltimore City, including an operating location in Baltimore City and direct experience serving populations impacted by the opioid overdose crisis in existing programs
Organization must not be a quasi-City entity, or an affiliate or subsidiary of that entity, that can be or is funded by the City through its annual budgeting process
Organization must not be named in the Baltimore City Opioid Settlement Agreements
Organization must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Projects must be clearly aligned with the Strategic Plan and prioritized activities
Projects must not include any unallowable costs as outlined in Appendix A
Must address at least one of the identified priority areas and tiers
Additional points allocated to organizations with a local yearly operating budget under $15 million
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process consists of five phases: (1) Proposal Phase: Organizations submit concise project proposals through the online portal by November 23, 2025. Proposals are screened for completeness and eligibility by BCMOOR and MORP. A 5-member RAB committee scores eligible proposals (75+ points advance to full RAB review). (2) Application Phase: Selected organizations are invited to submit detailed applications by January 25, 2026, including detailed project descriptions, budgets with justification, workplans with goals/objectives/outcomes, organizational risk assessment questionnaire, and performance measures. Applications are evaluated by RAB, MORP, and BCMOOR panels for feasibility, sustainability, risk, Strategic Plan alignment, duplication, and partnership quality. RAB creates ranked recommendations for each tier submitted to Mayor's Overdose Cabinet and Mayor for final approval. (3) Funding Phase: Executive-approved projects proceed to funding contingent on administrative requirements. Grant agreements are executed outlining terms, conditions, and disbursement procedures per City policies. (4) Administration Phase: Awardees must meet monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting requirements; comply with ORF guidelines and funding agreements; and participate in evaluation and technical assistance. (5) Closing Phase: Projects are closed upon fulfillment of agreement terms; all funds are reconciled; outstanding issues resolved; unused funds returned; and final reports filed and retained for audits. Submitting organizations must complete organizational information, project overview, implementation plan, evaluation strategy, and financial information in the proposal. Organizations may attend orientation sessions and access a detailed user guide for the application portal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Pimlico Community Development Authority Local Impact Aid Funding
structured_extraction.program_description: State-funded community development assistance generated by video lottery terminal (slots) revenue at Pimlico Racetrack. Allocates Local Impact Aid funding to support capital projects for economic and community development in the Pimlico area, including the Park Heights Master Plan area and surrounding neighborhoods within a 1-mile radius. Supports a wide variety of community development projects including infrastructure improvements, facilities, public safety, sanitation, economic and community development including housing, and other public services and improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Video lottery terminal (slots) Local Impact Aid revenues are appropriated to City agencies or partners designated to implement projects or administer grants. Funding is allocated primarily for capital purposes, with some operating funds available. Of available funds, 85% must be allocated to the Park Heights Master Plan area, and the remaining 15% is allocated to neighborhoods in the surrounding one-mile radius area. Starting in FY26, projects must be for at least $25,000. Recipients must be able to complete their project within two years from the start of their contract. Generally, capital grants will be disbursed on a reimbursement basis at the conclusion of a project. Generally, operating grants may be disbursed on a 40-40-20 schedule with 40% provided at the start of the project, 40% at the midway point contingent on successful project progress, and 20% at completion upon submission of a final report. Variable amounts of funding are awarded through the City budget process annually by State statute. The current statute provides for Pimlico Local Impact Aid through fiscal year 2032.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore City Department of Public Works (DPW) offers free cleaning, disinfection, and disposal services to residential customers (homeowners and tenants) whose homes or properties have been damaged by sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet weather events. The program deploys professional cleaning contractors contracted by DPW to disinfect and clean affected areas, remove and dispose of soiled materials, deodorize, and dry affected properties at no cost to the eligible customer.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free professional cleaning, disinfection, and disposal services provided at no cost to eligible residential customers. DPW contracts with third-party vendors and cleaning professionals to perform the work, including: disinfection and cleaning to eliminate viruses, bacteria, and microorganisms; removal and disposal of soiled carpet, flooring, furniture, and other affected property; deodorization using professional-grade equipment; and dehumidification and drying of affected areas. Services are available to both single-family and multi-family residential properties. On-call cleaning contractors will contact the customer within approximately one hour of notification and offer appointments from 8 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week. The program covers only sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet weather events (at least 1/4 inch of precipitation within a 24-hour period), not dry weather backups or water main breaks.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residential customers (homeowners and tenants) in single-family and multi-family residential properties whose homes have experienced sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet weather events (at least 1/4 inch of rain recorded within a 24-hour period causing sewer lines to surcharge or overflow).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional cleaning and disinfection of areas damaged by sewage backup; removal and disposal of soiled carpet, flooring, furniture, and other affected property; deodorization using professional-grade equipment; dehumidification and drying of affected areas. Services do not include mold and mildew remediation, property restoration (floor, drywall, paint), or restoration or replacement of personal belongings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available only to residential properties within Baltimore City that have experienced sewage backups caused by capacity-related wet weather events.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore City residential customer (homeowner or tenant)
Property must be a residential property (single-family or multi-family); commercial properties are not eligible
Sewage backup must be caused by a capacity-related wet weather event (at least 1/4 inch of precipitation within a 24-hour period causing sewer lines to surcharge or overflow)
The City must determine and confirm that the damage was caused by a capacity-related wet weather event
Backup must not be caused by dry weather events such as clogs from grease, tree roots, or improper disposal of fats, oils, grease, or other materials
Backup must not be caused by water main breaks or stormwater seeping in from outside
Report must be made to 311 (by phone at 311 or online at 311.baltimorecity.gov) as soon as the sewage backup is discovered
Customers are encouraged to report quickly; extended delays may result in eligibility for the Expedited Reimbursement Program instead
Eligibility is limited to either the SOS Cleanup Program or the Expedited Reimbursement Program for Sewage Backups — not both
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Call 311 or visit 311.baltimorecity.gov to report the sewage backup damage as soon as it is discovered. Step 2: DPW will send an inspector to determine the cause of the backup and confirm it was caused by a capacity-related wet weather event (at least 1/4 inch of precipitation within a 24-hour period). Step 3: If confirmed as a wet weather event, the DPW inspector will offer to schedule the SOS Program appointment and explain what services are included. Step 4: Once the customer accepts the SOS Program offer, the on-call cleaning contractor will contact the customer within approximately one hour of notification. Step 5: The cleaning contractor will schedule a service appointment based on customer availability; contractors offer appointments from 8 a.m. to midnight, seven days a week. Step 6: Professional cleaning services are provided at no cost. Following completion, the cleaning contractor will request a signature on a satisfaction/job completion form. Step 7: If dissatisfied with services, customers may call 410-396-3500 with concerns.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows property owners adjacent to city-owned vacant lots to purchase these side lots to expand their property. Owners can use the lots for gardens, landscaping, fencing, driveways, or property expansion. The program helps beautify neighborhoods while increasing property size and home value.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners can purchase adjacent city-owned vacant side lots at fixed pricing for lots up to 1,500 square feet. Lots larger than 1,500 SF are subject to additional cost per square foot. The maximum size for a potential side yard is 5,000 SF. Some properties are subject to annual ground rent that becomes the responsibility of the new owner after settlement. Payment is made via certified check, money order, or cashier's check in full at the time of approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners who are adjacent to city-owned vacant lots in Baltimore City and wish to purchase and develop these side lots.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and transformation of adjacent vacant lots into gardens, landscaping, fencing, driveways, or property expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Side yard properties must be physically contiguous to the adjacent owner's principal residence.
requirements_list: Side yard properties must be vacant and unimproved
Side yard properties must be physically contiguous to adjacent owner's principal residence
Priority given to owner-occupants
Side yard properties shall consist of no more than two lots incapable of independent development as determined by local zoning and code enforcement
Fixed side yard pricing applies only to lots up to 1,500 SF; lots greater than 1,500 SF subject to additional cost per square foot
Maximum size for a potential side yard is 5,000 SF
Applicant must have a record of responsible property ownership and management
Intended use must comply with Baltimore City Laws and Regulations
Deed contains language prohibiting owner or heirs from seeking zoning changes or relief for uses not identified in the application and approved in the award
Property taxes become responsibility of new owner from date of settlement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners must complete an application including disclosure of intended uses. The completed application is reviewed and a determination is made. If approved, the applicant must submit a certified check, money order, or cashier's check for the full purchase fee. The timeline includes 30 days for review and award decision, 45 days for Board of Estimates approval, and 45 days for settlement, totaling approximately 120 days estimated.

structured_extraction.program_description: A permit program that allows small commercial waste haulers to use Baltimore City's waste drop-off locations at the Northwest Transfer Station and Quarantine Road Landfill for a per-load fee.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Permits small commercial waste haulers with vehicles under 7,000 pounds to dump waste materials at Northwest Transfer Station and Quarantine Road Landfill. Fee structure: $20 per load up to 7,000 pounds, plus $3.38 per additional 100 pounds over 7,000 pounds. Permit registration fees are $35 per truck under 7,000 pounds. Permits are issued annually and must be renewed each year.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Small commercial waste haulers that collect, transport, or dispose of solid waste for others or themselves with vehicles under 7,000 pounds.

Vehicle must weigh under 7,000 pounds (gross vehicle weight rating)
Must bring vehicle registration forms to Environmental Inspection Services
Registration must include the weight of the vehicle
Vehicle must be a commercial hauling vehicle
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for a permit through the Baltimore City Health Department by visiting Environmental Inspection Services located at 1001 East Fayette Street, Baltimore, MD 21202. Bring each vehicle's registration forms showing the vehicle weight. Complete the Small Hauler Program application form. Pay the $35 registration fee per truck under 7,000 pounds. Once approved, receive permit card(s) to use at drop-off locations. Permits are valid for one year from issuance date and must be renewed annually.

Event flyer or official posting must be provided as proof of the cleanup event

structured_extraction.program_name: Staying Alive Drug Overdose Prevention and Response Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A public health intervention program that trains individuals to recognize signs and symptoms of opioid and heroin overdose and respond appropriately to maximize survival chances. The program provides access to naloxone (Narcan) training and kits at various treatment centers, Syringe Exchange Program sites, and the Baltimore City Detention Center.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides training in overdose prevention and response, including recognition of overdose signs and symptoms. Participants receive naloxone kits to carry and use in emergency situations. As of 2016, the program had trained over 18,000 individuals and dispensed thousands of naloxone kits, with hundreds of reported overdose reversals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with substance use disorders, inmates, healthcare providers, correctional staff, and third parties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Overdose prevention and response training and naloxone kits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, including treatment centers, Syringe Exchange Program sites, and the Baltimore City Detention Center.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Training is available at various treatment centers throughout Baltimore City, at Syringe Exchange Program sites, and at the Baltimore City Detention Center ACT-SAP.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows property owners in Baltimore City to receive credits on their stormwater fee by installing and maintaining stormwater treatment practices such as trees, rain gardens, and rain barrels, and by volunteering in hands-on community activities like clean-ups and tree plantings that provide water quality benefits. The program covers single-family property owners as well as businesses, churches, non-profits, industries, and other non-single-family property types. Credits are based on impervious area, permit status, property type, and qualifying stormwater best management practices maintained on the property.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive a credit applied to their stormwater fee. For single-family properties, credits are earned by volunteering for organized community activities that provide water quality benefits (such as tree planting and trash cleanups) at $10 per 4 hours of participation (maximum $30/year), or by installing and maintaining stormwater best management practices including rain gardens ($8-16/year depending on size), trees ($5/year per tree, minimum 2 trees), rain barrels ($25 one-time per 50+ gallon system), or other BMPs (up to 45% credit). For non-single-family properties (businesses, churches, non-profits, industries), credits or fee reductions are available based on: installing and maintaining stormwater best management practices (up to 45% credit); owning lots with less than 50 square feet of non-absorbent (impervious) area (45% credit); owning small developments with up to 820 square feet of impervious area (33% credit); holding an NPDES Industrial Stormwater Discharge Permit (55% credit); owning and maintaining private storm drains discharging to Baltimore Harbor (30% credit); owning cemetery streets that are privately maintained and open to the public; or qualifying for religious structure special fee ($1/ERU/month cap) or hardship exemption. Non-single family properties may also qualify for a 20% property tax cap if annual stormwater fee exceeds 0.75% of property tax and real property taxes are greater than $1,000 annually.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling applications accepted year-round. Renewal applications must be submitted within 30 days before the end of the credit period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family property owners, businesses, churches, non-profits, industries, veterans organizations, charitable organizations experiencing financial hardship, and other property owners in Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credits reduce stormwater fees. Eligible activities include installation and maintenance of stormwater treatment practices such as rain gardens, trees, rain barrels, and private storm drains; participation in organized volunteer Stormwater Participation Events such as community tree plantings and trash cleanups that provide water quality benefits; and implementation of approved alternative compliance plans for hardship exemptions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only. Credits are based on the property's location and drainage characteristics within Baltimore City's stormwater management system.
requirements_list: Complete and submit the appropriate Stormwater fee credit application (Single Family Property or Non-Single Family Property version)
Must be a property owner in Baltimore City

For single-family properties: install and maintain qualifying stormwater best management practices (rain gardens with minimum 50-100 sq ft and 500-1000 sq ft drainage area, trees 1 inch or greater in diameter with minimum 2 trees planted after 2010, rain barrels with minimum 50 gallons capacity, or other BMPs) or register for and participate in organized Stormwater Participation Events (volunteer activities) at certified City events

For non-single-family properties (businesses, churches, non-profits, industries): must meet one or more of the following eligibility categories: (1) install and maintain stormwater best management practices meeting Maryland Department of Environment standards; (2) own a lot with less than 50 square feet of impervious/non-absorbent area; (3) own a small development with 50-820 square feet of impervious area; (4) hold an NPDES Industrial Stormwater Discharge Permit; (5) own and maintain private storm drains discharging to Baltimore Harbor; (6) own cemetery streets privately maintained and open to the public; or (7) qualify for religious structure special fee or hardship exemption
For single-family properties, download and follow the Single Family Property Guidance Document
For non-single-family properties, download and follow the Non-Single Family Property Guidance Document
For Best Management Practice credits, execute a simple right-of-entry agreement or inspection and maintenance agreement with the Department to allow access for regular inspections
For participation credits, obtain Stormwater Participation Event certificates from certified City event organizers
For off-site treatment BMPs, submit narrative explaining why off-site treatment is appropriate and confirm BMP is in same 8-digit watershed as the property
For NPDES Industrial Permit credit, provide copy of permit or exemption certification with initial application and upon each renewal

For Harbor Discharger credit, provide detailed site drawing showing drainage areas, flow patterns, private stormwater collection systems, locations of outfalls, topographic contours, and delineation of impervious area eligible for credit
For Green Space or Small Development credit, provide photo documentation of the lot or impervious area
For religious structure credit, provide map of property identifying eligible structures and proof of tax exempt religious status certification

For hardship exemption, provide: IRS 501(c)(3) or (d) tax exemption documentation, proof that annual stormwater fee exceeds 0.75% of annual revenue (max $1,000,000), proof of property ownership or landlord/tenant lease, written alternative compliance plan, and annual recertification with implementation proof
For veterans organization exemption, provide proof of IRS 501(c)(4) or (19) tax exempt status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners complete and submit the appropriate Stormwater fee credit application (Single Family Property or Non-Single Family Property) along with required supporting documentation. Single-family property owners should download the Single Family Property Guidance Document for detailed instructions. For other property types, download the Non-Single Family Property Guidance Document. Applications and supporting materials should be submitted to the Bureau of Water and Wastewater at 200 Holliday Street, Room 404, Abel Wolman Municipal Building, Baltimore, MD 21202, or emailed to publicworks@baltimorecity.gov with 'STORMWATER CREDIT APPLICATION' in the subject line. To earn volunteer participation credits, single-family owners must register for organized Stormwater Participation Events and submit event certificates with the application. To earn best management practice credits, owners must install and maintain qualifying practices on their property, submit photo documentation and maintenance records, and execute required agreements. Customers receive a letter upon receipt of application materials, then another letter with the application decision. Credit applications are reviewed and decided within 30 days of receipt of a complete application package. Participation and simple credits may be processed in shorter timeframes. When the 30-day review period would have allowed a property to receive credit on a subsequent monthly bill but the Department cannot complete review within 30 days, the credit is applied retroactively. The customer is still obligated to pay the full fee during the credit application review. For credits with approval periods (typically 1-5 years depending on credit type), customers must submit renewal applications within 30 days before the end of the credit period or the credit may not be reflected on the subsequent water bill. Denied credit applicants may appeal in writing within 30 days of receiving the denial letter, providing customer name, account number, basis of appeal, and supporting evidence such as engineering drawings, land surveys, or ownership documentation. The Director of Public Works is the final authority on appeals. Customers aggrieved by the Director's final decision may seek review by the Board of Municipal Zoning Appeals or judicial review in the Circuit Court for Baltimore City.

structured_extraction.program_name: Stormwater Fee Hardship Exemption and Alternative Compliance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Baltimore City program that allows eligible tax-exempt organizations to apply for an exemption from their stormwater fee by submitting an alternative compliance plan that demonstrates how they will reduce stormwater runoff and pollution and protect the environment. Faith organizations can also receive stormwater fee reductions specifically for their places of worship and school properties. The program provides flexibility to reduce financial burden on qualifying organizations while encouraging environmental stewardship and reducing strain on the City's storm sewer system.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible tax-exempt organizations can receive a hardship exemption from their stormwater fee by submitting an alternative compliance plan that outlines practices to reduce stormwater runoff and pollution and protect the environment. Faith-based organizations operating places of worship and K-12 schools are eligible for a special religious structure fee capped at $1 per ERU per month. To qualify for hardship exemption, an organization must document: tax exemption under §501(c)(3) or (d) of the Internal Revenue Code; total annual stormwater fee exceeding 0.75% of total annual revenue; total annual revenue not exceeding $1,000,000; and property ownership or current lease agreement. Upon approval, the organization must initiate implementation within one year and re-certify eligibility annually, including proof of implementation of the approved alternative compliance plan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tax-exempt organizations, faith-based organizations, places of worship, and schools in Baltimore City seeking to reduce their stormwater remediation fees through hardship exemption or alternative compliance
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of stormwater management practices that reduce stormwater runoff and pollution as outlined in an alternative compliance plan; fee reductions lower stormwater bills for faith-based institutions' worship and school properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only
requirements_list: Must be a tax-exempt organization exempt from taxation under §501(c)(3) or (d) of the Internal Revenue Code
Must demonstrate financial hardship with total annual stormwater fee exceeding 0.75% of total annual revenue (after any applicable discounts or credits)
Total annual revenue must not exceed $1,000,000
Must own the property or provide current landlord/tenant lease agreement showing responsibility for stormwater remediation fee charges
Must submit written alternative compliance plan to the Department of Public Works for review and approval
Alternative compliance plan must demonstrate practices to reduce stormwater runoff and protect the environment
Upon approval, must initiate implementation of plan within one year
Must re-certify hardship exemption eligibility annually, including proof of implementation of approved alternative compliance plan
Failure to recertify or document implementation results in removal from hardship exemption
Faith organizations must operate place of worship or K-12 education to qualify for religious structure special fee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, download the Non-Single Family Property Guidance Document and the Stormwater Alternative Compliance Baltimore City Final Application form from PublicWorks.BaltimoreCity.gov or visit the Abel Wolman Municipal Building. Complete the application with supporting documentation including proof of tax-exempt status, financial records showing annual revenue and stormwater fees, proof of property ownership or lease agreement, and the written alternative compliance plan. Submit materials to the Bureau of Water and Wastewater at 200 Holliday Street, Room 404, Baltimore, MD 21202, or email to publicworks@baltimorecity.gov with 'STORMWATER CREDIT APPLICATION' in the subject line. The Department will send a letter confirming receipt and will provide the application decision within 30 days of receiving a complete application package. Credit applications may be reviewed more quickly for simple cases. Customers remain obligated to pay the full fee during the application review period. If application is denied, customers may submit a written appeal within 30 days to the Bureau of Water and Wastewater. The Director of Public Works makes the final decision on appeals.

structured_extraction.program_description: A financial tool that cities use to fund development projects in designated areas. Investment in a TIF district is expected to raise property values, and the increase in property tax revenue from this growth is set aside to repay bonds issued to finance the project. Once the TIF debt is repaid, the district is dissolved and increased tax revenue goes to the city's general fund.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TIF bonds fund development projects within designated TIF districts by issuing multiple series of bonds to finance infrastructure improvements, vacant property redevelopment, and rehabilitation of abandoned homes. Bonds are repaid using incremental property tax revenue generated by the development. The program supports hard construction costs to restore vacant properties as new homeownership and rental opportunities for households earning up to 115 percent of area median income (AMI), as well as construction of new public infrastructure. TIF bond proceeds are leveraged with additional private and public funds to achieve whole block outcomes, defined as restoring all vacant properties to a productive use. Developers submit applications to the Board of Finance detailing the specific district or area to be covered and providing estimates of future property value increases and fiscal impact analysis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers, non-profit and for-profit organizations, and community development corporations seeking to undertake development projects including housing, retail, office, and mixed-use developments in designated areas of Baltimore City
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development projects within designated TIF districts including residential and rental housing construction and rehabilitation, retail space development, office buildings, employment space, public infrastructure improvements, schools, parks, roads, and related infrastructure
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City designated TIF districts. Recent applications include citywide Impact Investment Areas and neighborhoods with high vacancy rates. Specific districts have been established for Center West at Poppleton, Perkins Somerset Oldtown neighborhoods, and Vacancy Reduction and Affordable Housing citywide program covering 4,285 properties in 126 neighborhoods.
requirements_list: Submit TIF bond application to the Board of Finance
Application must include detail on the specific district or area to be covered by the TIF
Application must include estimates on future property value increases
Developer must submit fiscal impact analysis including but-for test
Applicant must demonstrate project advances City's land use, economic development and public improvement goals
Project must generate positive net fiscal impact to the City
Developer must demonstrate private sector contribution to project
For affordable housing components, must meet inclusionary housing requirements
Application must include development team qualifications and experience
Must include project sources and uses analysis
Must provide site control documentation
Must address environmental and physical site constraints
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Department of Housing and Community Development submits a TIF application to the Board of Finance following a two-step process: Step 1 is preparation of the TIF plan and proposal; Step 2 is presentation of the application to the Board for concept approval. The application must detail the specific district or area to be covered, provide estimates of future property value increases, include comprehensive fiscal impact analysis and but-for test, demonstrate how the project advances City priorities, and show how TIF financing is necessary for project feasibility. Upon concept approval, Finance proceeds with drafting of TIF legislative package and issuance of debt. Subsequent approvals from the Board are required for legislative package and debt issuance. Developers work with the City to structure financing, secure additional public and private funding, and coordinate with various City departments.

structured_extraction.program_description: An annual Baltimore City program that removes properties from tax sale for the year of application by deferring unpaid property taxes and charges. The city sets aside $2 million in funding each year; once exhausted, the program closes. The program does not forgive unpaid bills—if bills remain unpaid after deferral, the property may qualify for tax sale in the following year. Applicants must reapply each year and are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The city sets aside $2 million annually. From that starting balance, the amount of each applicant's liens are deducted from the balance remaining. Once the $2 million is exhausted, the program closes. Successful applicants have their properties removed from tax sale for the year they apply. The program defers unpaid property taxes, city fines, and citations (excluding motor vehicle citations, utility bills, and water bills) for one year but does not forgive them; unpaid bills may result in tax sale eligibility the following year. Tax sale is held annually in May, with the deadline to pay outstanding liens to avoid tax sale typically April 30.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners who receive Final Bill and Legal Notices and meet income and residency requirements; Baltimore City property owners facing tax sale of their properties with more than $1,000 in unpaid city bills.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferral of property tax sale for one year; does not forgive unpaid bills. Applicable to unpaid property taxes, city fines, and citations (excluding motor vehicle citations, utility bills, and water bills).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only.
requirements_list: Property assessed value is $250,000 or less
Property is a primary residence
Homeowner has lived in property for at least 15 years
Have received a Final Bill and Legal Notice from the Department of Finance OR have more than $1,000 in unpaid city bills (excluding motor vehicle citations, utility bills, and water bills)

One of the following income criteria is met: (1) total annual household gross income of $36,000 or less; or (2) homeowner is at least 65 years old with annual gross income of $75,000 or less; or (3) homeowner receives Federal Social Security Disability Insurance Program (SSDI) benefits with annual gross income of $75,000 or less
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowners may apply online, by hand delivery, or by mail. Applications are accepted February 15 through April 15 each year. Option 1 (Online - Recommended): Apply through the Neighborly application portal at bit.ly/DHCD-Neighborly. Option 2 (Hand Delivery): Deliver completed application in an envelope labeled 'Tax Sale Deferral Program' to Department of Housing and Community Development, 417 E. Fayette Street, 11th Floor, Suite 1125, Baltimore, MD 21202, Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. All hand-delivered applications are date- and time-stamped upon receipt with a receipt confirmation provided. Option 3 (Mail): Mail completed application to Department of Housing and Community Development, Division of Homeownership & Housing Preservation, 417 E. Fayette Street, 11th Floor, Baltimore, MD 21202, Attn: Tax Sale Deferral Program. Confirmation of receipt will be provided by phone or email within five (5) business days. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis. Applicants must apply every year. Check eligibility by visiting the deferral program eligibility page at https://www.baltimorecity.gov/tax-sale/our-work/deferral-program or call (410) 396-3987 or (410) 396-3000.

structured_extraction.program_description: TreeBaltimore is a program led by the Mayor and run by Baltimore City Recreation and Parks aimed at growing and caring for more trees across the city. The program takes care of existing trees, helps forests grow naturally, and teaches people to care for trees in their neighborhoods. It provides free trees to residents and assistance to businesses, institutions, and community organizations for tree planting and maintenance.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TreeBaltimore provides free trees to residents and businesses for planting on private property. The program offers free tree giveaways in spring and fall at farmers markets, parks, and community events. For larger properties such as schools, apartment buildings, hospitals, industrial areas, colleges, places of worship, vacant lots, and public housing, TreeBaltimore will order and deliver trees. The program also offers discount trees and site visits to businesses and institutions. Residents can receive a $10 coupon from the Growing Home Campaign or a $25 coupon from the Marylanders Plant Trees campaign to purchase trees. The program provides free Tree Steward training classes for volunteers. Street trees are planted by the Forestry Division in existing planting locations or where concrete sidewalks exist with no tree pit. Trees planted in the public right-of-way must be at least 1.5 inches in caliper. Park trees must be at least 0.5 inches in caliper unless otherwise approved by Forestry. All trees must conform to American Standard for Nursery Stock (ANSI Z60.2) and have a single dominant leader. For each planting project, at least half of installed trees must be native species, preferably grown from local seed sources within 200 miles of Baltimore City. For plantings larger than 20 trees, no single species should exceed 10% of the total. A two-year maintenance plan including routine watering, mulching, weeding, and trunk protection is required for all plantings, with weekly summer watering being most critical for survivability.

requirements_list: Residents can receive free trees at giveaways
Businesses and institutions can contact TreeBaltimore for site visits and discount trees
Community organizations can conduct street tree pit inventories and submit requests
Volunteers can participate in tree planting and maintenance activities
For street tree planting, applicant must submit a dated and signed Tree Request and Agreement for Tree Care form
For street trees in existing planting locations, an inspector will visit to approve location before planting

Property owner permission is required for tree planting
Applicant must agree to regularly water tree with 20 gallons of water once to twice weekly (equivalent to 10 minutes slow faucet flow) from May through October for minimum two years
No planter boxes or items that impede water flow may be installed around trees
Trees planted in public right-of-way must be single trunk trees with defined leader

Two-year maintenance plan required for all plantings
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can pick up free trees at TreeBaltimore giveaways held in spring and fall at farmers markets, parks, and local events. For street tree planting, applicants must submit a dated and signed Tree Request and Agreement for Tree Care form to the Forestry Division by mail, fax, or email to Jahmilla Wilson, Planting Coordinator. An inspector will visit the site to approve the tree location. After approval, the applicant's tree will be placed on the planting order for the next planting season. For new tree pits in concrete sidewalks, applicants can request to be placed on the winter pit list or privately contract and pay for pit creation. If privately creating pits, applicants must contact Miss Utility (1-800-257-7777) to identify underground utilities and then perform the pit work according to specifications provided. Trees are typically planted anywhere from 4 to 10 months after initial request depending on when received and volume of requests. Residents can also plant trees on their own property or work with neighbors on yards or grassy areas of places of worship, schools, or businesses. For larger properties, businesses and institutions should contact TreeBaltimore for a site visit and information on discount trees and delivery options. Community organizations can contact TreeBaltimore to conduct street tree pit inventories or participate in the TreeNeighborhood Program. Volunteers can register to participate in tree planting and care activities by contacting the program. TreeNeighborhood group orders require completion of an order form with minimum 10 trees at $10 per tree. Commemorative tree donations can be made through a donation form with $300 purchasing a tree including installation.

structured_extraction.program_description: TreeNeighborhood provides free trees to residents living in designated Healthy Neighborhoods, and discounted trees at half price ($10 each) to residents in all other neighborhoods. The program aims to increase tree coverage and improve neighborhood environments by making trees accessible to residents for planting on their lawns and yards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residents in designated Healthy Neighborhoods receive free trees. Residents in all other Baltimore City neighborhoods receive trees at a 50% discount ($10 per tree). Trees are delivered free to neighborhoods that order a minimum of ten trees. Neighborhood groups collect orders from residents and large property owners such as schools, businesses, and hospitals using individual order forms and submit all requests together on the TreeNeighborhood Order Form to TreeBaltimore. TreeBaltimore coordinates delivery to a central location in each neighborhood.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Baltimore City neighborhoods, including individuals and large property owners such as schools, businesses, hospitals, and other organizations seeking to plant trees on their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Trees for planting on residential lawns and yards, and on properties owned by schools, businesses, hospitals, and other organizations. Trees must be planted on eligible property in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to all Baltimore City neighborhoods. Residents in designated Healthy Neighborhoods (Belair-Edison, Brooklyn and Curtis Bay, Charles Village, Coldstream/Homestead/Montebello, Coppin Heights, Cylburn and Levindale, Ednor Gardens-Lakeside, Edmondson Village, GarwynOaks/Hanlon/HowardPark, Glen, Greater Lauraville, Highlandtown and Bayview, Midtown, Mondawmin, Patterson Park, Remington, Reservoir Hill, and Waverly) receive free trees. All other Baltimore City neighborhoods can purchase trees at half price ($10 per tree).

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps Baltimore City property owners reduce their water or sewer bills when they experience higher-than-normal usage due to leaks or problems with toilets or appliances. Interior leaks and situational usage adjustments reduce the water bill portion by 50 percent of excess usage (or 100 percent for senior or hardship customers). Underground leak adjustments reduce both water and sewer charges, provided a licensed plumber repairs the leak and proof is submitted.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bill adjustment or credit applied to water and sewer charges. For interior leaks or situational usage, the water portion of the bill is reduced by 50 percent of the excess water used (or 100 percent for senior or hardship customers). For underground leaks, water and sewer charges are both reduced based on the average daily usage prior to the leak. The adjustment appears on the bill approximately 4 weeks after approval. Customers will only receive one underground leak adjustment per property every two years, and only one interior/situational usage adjustment per property every three years. Approval is not guaranteed, and customers will be notified by phone or letter if the request cannot be granted or if additional information is needed.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Water and Sewer Adjustment Request form online or print and mail it to DPW Customer Support and Services Division at 200 Holliday Street, First Floor, Room 8, Baltimore, MD 21202. The form requires information about the leak type (underground pipe, irrigation, toilet, extreme high use, or other), date the leak occurred, date it was repaired, description of the leak and repairs, water billing account number, service address, contact phone number, and email. Applicants must verify that necessary repairs have been completed before submitting. If approved, the adjustment will appear on the bill in approximately 4 weeks after the request is received. Customers will be notified by phone or letter if the request cannot be granted or if additional information is needed.

The program uses a formula to calculate the maximum a household should pay for yearly water and sewer services based on a percentage of their annual income, and assistance rates are adjusted to ensure recipients do not have to pay more as a result of new rate increases.

structured_extraction.program_description: YH2O is a pre-apprenticeship and mentoring program offered in partnership with the Baltimore City Department of Public Works. The program prepares young adults ages 18–24 for employment in full-time jobs within the public works industry, with a focus on water, wastewater, solid waste, and internet technology sectors. It educates participants about the water and public works industry and related career opportunities, provides hands-on training and career mentoring, and develops a pipeline of workers with skills to fill entry-level positions. Past graduates have attained positions such as Laborers, Community Aides, Operations Technician Apprentices, and Customer Care Analysts.

The program has expanded to include careers in solid waste and internet technology sections within the Department of Public Works, in addition to water and wastewater careers.

structured_extraction.program_description: A sales program administered by the Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development that allows individuals, non-profits, community land trusts, and developers to purchase City-owned vacant buildings and lots at fixed, below-market prices. The program streamlines property acquisition to reduce vacancy and revitalize neighborhoods by facilitating restoration and development for residential or mixed-use purposes. During an initial 90-day priority period (April 1 - June 30, 2024), Baltimore City residents planning to restore and occupy homes as their primary residence receive first access, after which applications are reviewed on a rolling basis for all eligible applicants.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore City Department of Housing & Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: City-owned vacant buildings and lots in Housing Market Typology categories E-J are sold at fixed prices. For vacant buildings: homeowners and community land trusts pay $1; non-profits with 50 or fewer employees pay $1,000; non-profits with 51 or more employees and for-profit developers pay $3,000. For vacant lots: homeowners and community land trusts pay $1; non-profits with 50 or fewer employees pay $500; non-profits with 51 or more employees and for-profit developers pay $1,000. Vacant lots may also be used for green space (side yards). Homeowners must provide proof of $90,000 available for rehabilitation per property and maintain the property as a primary residence for a minimum of 5 years after issuance of use and occupancy permit. If a homeowner sells within the 6-year period (12 months to obtain permit + 5 years residency), they must pay a pro-rated portion of $3,000 based on the year of sale. A $100 non-refundable application fee is required at submission; if approved, it is credited toward settlement costs; if rejected, it is refunded. Properties must be developed for residential or mixed-use (including residential) purposes with a use and occupancy permit obtained within 12 months of settlement. If a property is assessed for less than the fixed price, it sells for the assessed value. Properties assessed at $100,000 or more undergo internal valuation; if true value is less than $100,000, fixed pricing applies; if $100,000 or more, the property is not eligible for fixed pricing. Applicants may apply for up to 12 properties at any given time and can apply for additional properties as they obtain use and occupancy permits on previously purchased properties, not to exceed 12 properties at once. Board of Estimates approval is required for property sales.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing rolling applications. Phase One (homeowner priority): April 1 - June 30, 2024. Phase Two (Charm City Roots): April 15, 2024 onward. Phase Three (all applicant types): July 1, 2024 onward. Applications received before March 20, 2024 resumed processing April 1, 2024. Applications received after March 20, 2024 are reviewed beginning July 1, 2024.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents seeking to purchase and rehabilitate a home as their primary residence (Phase One priority, April 1 - June 30, 2024); individuals with familial or legacy connections to vacant properties not yet City-owned through Charm City Roots (Phase Two); community land trusts, non-profit organizations, and for-profit developers seeking to develop residential or mixed-use properties on City-owned vacant buildings and lots (Phase Three and beyond).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property acquisition and rehabilitation of City-owned vacant buildings and lots for residential use, mixed-use development including residential components, green space development (including side yard acquisition for adjacent primary residences), or new construction for residential use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must fall within Baltimore City's E-J Housing Market Typology. Phase One prioritizes Baltimore City residents. Charm City Roots (Phase Two) focuses on individuals with familial or legacy connections to properties not yet City-owned. Properties that are side yards can be sold in typologies A-J provided the applicant provides documentation verifying adjacent property ownership as primary residency and that adjacent property has confirmed use and occupancy.
requirements_list: Proof of available funding of at least $90,000 per property for rehabilitation (this is a minimum documentation requirement, not a maximum rehabilitation estimate; estimated actual rehabilitation costs are $125-$150 per square foot)
No unpaid federal or state liens, judgments, or court orders related to money from the government

For homeowners: must maintain property as primary residence for minimum 5 years after issuance of use and occupancy permit, as evidenced by homestead tax credit approval; if property is sold within 6 years, must pay pro-rated portion of $3,000

For community land trusts: must be registered as an Affordable Housing Land Trust with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation and in compliance with Maryland Real Property Article Section 14-501 et seq.

If applicant fails vetting, given 5 business days to remedy issues; if unable to remedy or property unable to move to settlement, property is re-offered

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit applications through the BuyIntoBmore interactive map portal at https://buyintobmore.baltimorecity.gov/. DHCD accepts applications on a rolling basis during respective phases. Phase One (April 1-June 30, 2024) prioritizes homeowner applications; Phase Two (Charm City Roots, starting April 15) accepts individuals with familial/legacy connections; Phase Three (starting July 1) accepts all applicant types. DHCD conducts reviews promptly and renders award or rejection decisions within two weeks of receipt. Each application undergoes vetting that includes checks on available rehabilitation funding, history of vacant property ownership, legal issues, financial standing, and cross-verification using identity-linking technology to prevent multi-entity abuse of the 12-property limit. If an applicant fails vetting, they are given five business days to remedy issues. If unable to remedy or property is unable to move forward to settlement for other reasons, the property is re-offered on BuyIntoBmore. If multiple applications are received for the same property and all applicants pass vetting, applications are reviewed by order of submission. Properties are awarded once an applicant successfully passes the vetting process. Prior to settlement, applicants must submit executed construction contracts, evidence of equity capital and/or mortgage financing commitments, and comply with any required federal programmatic agreements. Board of Estimates approval is required for all property sales. Settlement occurs within 90 days of agreement date (extensible at Commissioner discretion). Applicants must obtain all required permits within 90 days of conveyance and commence construction/rehabilitation within 30 days of obtaining permits. Use and occupancy permits must be obtained within 12 months of settlement (extensible upon request for good cause).

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Works for Wind connects residents of Baltimore City and Baltimore County with careers in offshore wind and related industries through job training, certifications, and apprenticeship programs. The program covers multiple specialties including construction (carpentry, crane and tower operation, electrical/telecommunications, heavy equipment operation, HVAC, ironworking and steelworking, rigging, specialty painting and glazing), manufacturing (CNC programming and operation, forklift operation, machining, welding), and transportation, distribution, and logistics (Class A CDL driving, diesel mechanics, distribution management, freight handling, maritime). Participants gain industry-recognized certifications and access to supportive services to address barriers to employment, including child-care aid, criminal record expungement, financial aid, tools and work attire, and transportation aid. The program leverages regional partnerships and works with multiple companies in the area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides job trainings, certifications, and apprenticeship programs in three key industry clusters: Construction (carpentry, crane and tower operation, electrical/telecommunication, heavy equipment operation, HVAC, ironworking and steelworking, rigging, specialty painting and glazing); Manufacturing (CNC programming and operation, forklift operation, machining, welding); and Transportation Distribution and Logistics (Class A CDL driving, diesel mechanics, distribution management, freight handling, maritime). Participants can train with multiple partner companies in the region. Support services available to participants include child-care aid, criminal record expungement, financial aid, tools and work attire, and transportation aid. The program is background-friendly and accepts individuals with criminal backgrounds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City and Baltimore County residents ages 18 and older, including youth and returning citizens, interested in careers in offshore wind energy, construction, manufacturing, and transportation distribution and logistics.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training, certifications, and apprenticeship programs leading to career-track employment in skilled trades related to offshore wind and associated industries, including construction, manufacturing, and transportation, distribution, and logistics.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City and Baltimore County residents; must be a Maryland resident. Program operates in the Baltimore metropolitan area.

Must be a Maryland resident

Must be able to pass a drug test
Background-friendly (program accepts individuals with criminal backgrounds)

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County Energy Conservation Devices Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit offered to single and multi-family residential property owners in Baltimore County who install solar or geothermal devices that meet national safety and performance standards for heating, cooling, electricity supply, and hot water provision. Eligible costs include device components, accessories, and reasonable installation expenses incurred within 12 months before application. The annual credit cannot exceed the Baltimore County real property taxes owed that year. Credits not used in the tax year may be carried forward for up to two additional tax years. Due to a $1.5 million annual budget limit, a waiting list is in effect with applications processed in the order received.

structured_extraction.program_name: Baltimore County Historic Rehabilitation Tax Credit Program (Historic Restorations and Rehabilitations)
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program administered by Baltimore County that provides financial incentives to residential and commercial property owners who undertake qualified historic rehabilitation or restoration work on eligible historic structures. For residential owner-occupied dwellings, the program offers a tax credit equal to 20 percent of qualified rehabilitation expenditures (minimum $1,000), which can be drawn over up to 10 years to reduce annual county property taxes, with unused portions carried over for up to 10 subsequent tax years. For commercial income-producing properties, the program caps the property's assessed value for a 10-year period following rehabilitation, preventing property taxes from rising due to the increased assessed value resulting from the rehabilitation work. The program recognizes properties that return historic structures to a state of utility through repair or alteration while preserving historically, architecturally, or culturally significant portions and features. The program may be used in conjunction with the Maryland Historical Trust's state tax credit program for eligible projects. Tax credits are fully transferable to new property owners.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residential owner-occupied dwellings receive a property tax credit equal to 20 percent of qualified rehabilitation expenditures (minimum $1,000 in total cost). The approved credit is a fixed amount that can be drawn over up to 10 years to reduce the annual county property tax bill on the property; unused portions of the total credit can be carried over for up to 10 subsequent tax years. Commercial income-producing properties receive a tax credit equal to the difference between the assessed value before rehabilitation work and the increase in assessment resulting from the work, functioning as a cap on the assessment for 10 years and preventing property taxes from rising due to the increased value from rehabilitation. The commercial credit may not exceed the actual amount of tax levied in any tax year and continues at the same amount each year for 10 subsequent tax years. Rehabilitation work for commercial properties must generally exceed $50,000 to generate a reassessment. Tax credits are fully transferable to new property owners. The program may be used in conjunction with the Maryland Historical Trust's state tax credit program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: County Part II applications submitted without State approval are due two weeks before the next scheduled Landmarks Preservation Commission meeting
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic residential and commercial properties in Baltimore County, including homeowners with owner-occupied dwellings and owners of commercial income-producing properties, where the property is listed on the Baltimore County Final Landmarks List, is a contributing resource within a Baltimore County Historic District, or is individually listed on or a contributing resource within a Historic District on the National Register of Historic Places.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified rehabilitation work that returns a historic structure to a state of utility or productive use while preserving historically, architecturally, or culturally significant portions and features. Eligible expenses include basement waterproofing, chimney repair and lining, exterior painting, interior plaster repair, masonry repointing, new storm windows, plumbing and electrical system upgrades, roof repair and replacement, structural repairs, window restoration, heating and air conditioning improvements, and stucco work. All work must conform to the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and Baltimore County's Historic Preservation Design Guidelines, with materials repaired or replaced in kind.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only. Properties must be located in Baltimore County and designated as historic through one of the following: listed on the Baltimore County Final Landmarks List, contributing resource within a Baltimore County Historic District, or individually listed on or contributing resource within a Historic District on the National Register of Historic Places.
requirements_list: Property must be designated as historic and located in Baltimore County

Property must be listed on the Baltimore County Final Landmarks List, be a contributing resource within a Baltimore County Historic District, or be individually listed on or a contributing resource within a Historic District on the National Register of Historic Places
For residential properties, qualified rehabilitation expenditures must be at least $1,000
For commercial properties, rehabilitation work must generally exceed $50,000 to generate a reassessment
Work must conform to the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and Baltimore County's Historic Preservation Design Guidelines, with materials repaired or replaced in kind
All work must be reviewed and approved by the Landmarks Preservation Commission or staff before starting
Pre-approval by the Baltimore County Landmarks Preservation Commission is required before any work begins
For residential tax credit, the property must be owner-occupied; owners of residential properties used for rental or investment purposes must complete a commercial application
A Historic Environmental Setting (HES) may be required if the property does not have National Register designation
Tax credits are fully transferable to new property owners
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process consists of three parts. Part 1 certifies that the building is eligible (not required if previously approved). Part 2 certifies that the proposed project meets the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and Baltimore County's Historic Design Guidelines; it must be submitted two weeks before a Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC) meeting or, with State approval, submitted for staff review. Part 3 certifies that the completed project meets the Standards and that expenditures are eligible, and is submitted after project completion. All applications must be approved before work begins. Contact the Preservation Services Office or the Historic Preservation Planner (Jessica Brannock) for application details. Separate residential and commercial application forms are available. Review the Department of Planning's County Historic Tax Credit frequently asked questions before applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax exemption and refund program for blind individuals and their surviving spouses. The program exempts $15,000 of a property's assessed value from real property tax obligations. Blind individuals may also be eligible for a refund of property taxes paid in prior taxable years when an exemption was authorized but not granted, retroactive up to three years.
