structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides an exemption of $15,000 of a property's assessed value from real property tax obligations. Blind individuals may also receive a refund of property taxes paid in prior taxable years (up to three years retroactively) in which an exemption was authorized but not granted. Refunds are available for property taxes paid in taxable years when exemption was authorized but not granted, retroactive for up to three years.
structured_extraction.contact_name: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Blind individuals and their surviving spouses who own property in Baltimore County and all Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption and refunds on real property taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County and all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Must be a blind individual or surviving spouse of a blind individual
Must own property subject to real property tax in Baltimore County
Must file an application for exemption with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
To receive a refund, must first obtain an approved exemption from SDAT
Cannot receive this relief if already receiving relief under the Disabled Veteran or Surviving Spouse Tax Exemption
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, obtain an application for exemption from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and file it with that agency. For refunds, after receiving an approved exemption from SDAT, forward a copy of the approved exemption to the Baltimore County Council along with a letter requesting a refund. Send the refund request to: Baltimore County Council, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 205, Towson, Maryland 21204.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Learn, Earn, Achieve and Progress (LEAP) Program provides out-of-school young adults with comprehensive training and support services including academic skills development, industry-recognized certifications, GED or Maryland high school diploma preparation, and employment and work-based learning experiences leading to entry-level employment and career pathways.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free program offering comprehensive education and employment services including leadership development, financial literacy, certificate training, job development, academic help, support services, mentoring and coaching, and life skills. Specific training options include Certified Apartment Maintenance Tech, Certified Medical Administrative Assistant, Certified Nursing Assistant, Child Care Provider, Dental Assistant, Patient Care Technician, Pharmacy Technician, Phlebotomy Technician, GED classes, and A+ IT Certification.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Out-of-school young adults ages 18 to 24 who are Baltimore County residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and training services including GED or high school diploma preparation, industry-recognized certifications, job development, and work-based learning experiences
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland. Participants attend one of five CCBC locations: Randallstown Extension Center, Catonsville, Dundalk, Essex, or Owings Mills.
requirements_list: Ages 18 to 24
Baltimore County resident
High school diploma (for training programs only)
Must meet income requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested candidates can learn more by calling the LEAP information line at 443-840-4292 or emailing jmoon@ccbcmd.edu. Candidates select one of five CCBC locations to participate.

structured_extraction.program_description: Virtual orientation on basic Career Center services and information on how to access Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) Intensive and Training services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Virtual workshop providing orientation to Career Center services and explaining how to access WIOA Intensive and Training services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults seeking information on Career Center services and workforce development support
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and guidance on accessing Career Center services and WIOA programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend the virtual workshop. Contact the Career Center for specific dates and registration information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County Career Centers provide free education and training programs to help county residents advance their education, enhance training skills, and improve their quality of life through job search assistance, career counseling, resume development, interview practice, and occupational training scholarships in high-demand fields.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Services are provided at no cost to eligible individuals. Training scholarships are available on an individual basis for occupational training in high-demand fields. Services include career consultation, resume development, interview practice, job development assistance, GED and ESOL courses, literacy courses, and occupational training scholarships. Individuals must be 18 years or older, have a valid Social Security number, be a U.S. citizen or authorized to work in the U.S., meet military selective service requirements (if applicable), and either be a Baltimore County resident or meet specific non-resident criteria (recently laid off from a Baltimore County employer or currently underemployed working for a Baltimore County employer).
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-887-8912 (Liberty Career Center), 410-887-7940 (Hunt Valley Career Center), 410-288-9050 (Eastpoint Career Center)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents and eligible non-residents seeking to advance their education, enhance training skills, and improve employment prospects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training scholarships support individuals pursuing skills, licensures, or certifications aligned with local labor market demand and high-demand occupational fields
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residents are eligible. Non-residents may be eligible if they have recently been laid off from a Baltimore County employer or are currently working for a Baltimore County employer but are underemployed (salary criteria must be met)
requirements_list: Age 18 years or older
Valid Social Security number
Citizenship or non-citizen authorized to work in the U.S.
Military Selective Service registration for males born on or after January 1, 1960

Baltimore County resident, OR non-resident recently laid off from a Baltimore County employer, OR non-resident currently working for a Baltimore County employer but underemployed (salary criteria must be considered)
Documentation of Unemployment Insurance records, public assistance benefits, veteran status, Baltimore County residency, and/or income verification may be required
For training scholarships: must demonstrate need for a particular skill, licensure, or certification that aligns with local labor market demand and meet federal WIOA eligibility guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Career Center nearest you to complete enrollment paperwork including the Receipt of Grievance Procedures and Authorization to Release Form and Center and Computer Use Agreement. Career Consultant staff will conduct an assessment for the WIOA program, establish eligibility, provide orientation to services and program requirements, conduct one-on-one career coaching and guidance, develop a personalized employment plan, and direct completion of a training scholarship application if applicable. Training is assessed by need and approved on a case-by-case basis as funds are available.

structured_extraction.program_name: Certified Food Service Manager Training—Level II
structured_extraction.program_description: Free training program for volunteers and nonprofit organizations that operate food service facilities. Participants learn food safety management and earn certification required by Baltimore County for certain food service operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free virtual or in-person training sessions offered on a first-come, first-served basis. Sessions include full certification (7-hour program) and recertification (5-hour program) options. Training is provided at no cost for eligible individuals from volunteer fire companies and nonprofit fraternal, civic, veteran, religious, or charitable organizations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling registration; training sessions scheduled throughout the year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Managers and staff of volunteer fire companies and nonprofit fraternal, civic, veteran, religious, or charitable organizations that operate high or medium priority food service facilities three days or less per week.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training to become a Certified Food Service Manager, which is required by Baltimore County for certain food service operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be affiliated with a volunteer fire company or bona fide nonprofit fraternal, civic, veteran, religious, or charitable organization
Organization must operate a high or medium priority food service facility
Facility must operate three days or less per week
Must pre-register for training
Must have computer access for virtual training sessions
Must have a valid email address
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete pre-registration form on the program website with name, address, organization details, phone number, and email. Select preferred training date and time. Registration is on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing free family support, case management, information, referral and advocacy services to children with developmental disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free family support, case management, information, referral and advocacy services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County residents between birth and 21 years old with developmental disabilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Family support, case management, information, referral and advocacy services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residents only
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident
Must be between birth and 21 years old
Must have a developmental disability

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding to help organize and operate volunteer neighborhood patrols that serve as crime prevention tools by reporting suspicious activity to police.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to supplement Citizens on Patrol groups for startup and operation costs. Grants usually open for applications around April each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community members and neighborhood groups interested in organizing volunteer crime prevention patrols.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Startup and operation costs for Citizens on Patrol groups.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County neighborhoods and communities.
requirements_list: Any community or neighborhood can organize a patrol with as few as two members
Patrollers are observers only and do not carry weapons or confront persons engaged in criminal or suspicious activity
Must establish a group of volunteers and coordinate a training session with Community Outreach Officer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Set up a community meeting, contact a Community Outreach Officer from your local precinct, recruit and sign up volunteers, create a flexible patrol schedule, and coordinate a training session once volunteers are established. Apply for grant funding when applications open around April.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps seniors age in place or improve the health and safety of any home through housing upgrades.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct services to help seniors age in place or improve the health and safety of homes through upgrades and improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior residents in Baltimore County seeking to age in place or improve home health and safety.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing upgrades to support aging in place and improve home health and safety.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County

structured_extraction.program_description: An online six-hour educational program required for parents in cases involving contested child custody issues. The program provides information about the impact of separation and divorce on children and teaches better communication and problem-solving techniques for co-parenting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants complete a six-hour online co-parenting class designed to improve understanding of the impact of separation and divorce on children, enhance problem-solving techniques, and improve communication between co-parents. Must be completed prior to the mediation session.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents involved in contested child custody cases in Baltimore County. Any interested person may also attend.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational instruction on co-parenting, child development, separation and divorce impacts, and communication strategies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Class must be completed prior to the mediation session for custody cases
Class is required in all cases involving contested child custody issues
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Parents are ordered to attend the online class through an external provider. Contact the Office of Family Mediation for more information and registration.

structured_extraction.program_name: Coastal Rural Legacy Program (Baltimore County protected area)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Rural Legacy Program area focused on protecting the richest and most threatened natural resources in Baltimore County. It preserves large blocks of forest, wetland, farmland and habitat along the Upper Western Shore of the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Purchases conservation easements to protect vital wetlands, forests, marshes, farmland and wildlife habitat along the Chesapeake Bay shoreline.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with property in the Coastal Rural Legacy area of Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to purchase conservation easements protecting wetlands, forests, marshes, farmland and habitat.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Coastal Rural Legacy area encompasses 15,433 acres along the Upper Western Shore of the Chesapeake Bay, including Gunpowder Delta, Bird River, Dundee and Saltpeter, Bowley's Quarters, Back River and Holly Neck, and Fort Howard
requirements_list: Property located in the Coastal Rural Legacy area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners interested in exploring conservation options for their property should contact County Land Preservation staff.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a $10,000 annual grant awarded to business associations for projects that benefit the overall commercial revitalization districts. Eligible projects include holiday lighting, welcome signs, website development, street trees, security cameras, and farmers markets.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $10,000 annual grant to business associations for district-wide improvement projects such as holiday lighting, welcome signs, website development, street trees, security cameras, and farmers markets.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business associations in Commercial Revitalization Districts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: District-wide projects including holiday lighting, welcome signs, website development, street trees, security cameras, and farmers markets
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must benefit Commercial Revitalization Districts in Baltimore County
requirements_list: Applicant must be a business association
Project must benefit the overall commercial revitalization district
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Domenico Romeo at dromeo@baltimorecountymd.gov to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial Revitalization District (CRD) Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit and loan program available to owners who make qualified improvements to mobile home parks, senior housing developments, or commercially zoned properties located in designated Commercial Revitalization Districts (CRDs) in Baltimore County. The credit reduces property tax obligations for five to ten years depending on the cost of improvements. Additionally, the Building Improvement Loan Program (BILP) offers interest-free loans up to $30,000 for facade improvements, along with free architectural design services for facade improvements such as awnings, landscaping, and signage. Baltimore County has 24 officially designated Commercial Revitalization Districts.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits are calculated as a percentage of the increase in Baltimore County property taxes resulting from qualified improvements. For senior housing in revitalization districts, the credit equals 100 percent of the tax increase. For senior housing outside revitalization districts, it equals 50 percent. For other commercial property in designated districts, it equals 100 percent of county property taxes charged. For mobile home parks, it equals 100 percent of the tax increase. Qualified improvements must have a full cash value of $100,000 or more as reflected in SDAT records. The credit runs for five years unless improvement costs exceed $10 million, in which case it runs for ten years. The credit applies to Baltimore County real property tax obligations only and cannot be used for other charges on the tax bill. Additionally, the Building Improvement Loan Program (BILP) provides interest-free loans up to $30,000 for facade improvements, and free architectural design services are available for facade improvements such as awnings, landscaping, and signage.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 120 days after the issuance of a notice of assessment by SDAT that includes the improvements for which the tax credit is sought
structured_extraction.contact_name: Department of Planning Neighborhood Response Team; Director of Budget and Finance
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and businesses in Baltimore County located in one of the 24 designated Commercial Revitalization Districts who make qualified improvements to mobile home parks, senior housing developments, or commercially zoned properties. Also includes senior housing owners outside revitalization districts who may receive a reduced credit.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Physical improvements to mobile home parks, senior housing developments, or commercially zoned properties with a full cash value of $100,000 or more. Facade improvements (awnings, landscaping, signage) are also eligible for the interest-free BILP loan and free architectural design services. The tax credit applies to Baltimore County real property tax obligations only.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in Baltimore County, specifically within one of the 24 officially designated Commercial Revitalization Districts. Senior housing developments outside designated revitalization districts may still receive a 50 percent credit. Properties cannot be used for railroad or public utility purposes and cannot be covered by the Maryland Condominium Act.
requirements_list: Owner must make qualified improvements with a full cash value of $100,000 or more
Qualified improvements must be documented in SDAT records
Property must be a mobile home park, senior housing development, or commercially zoned property
Property must be located in a designated Commercial Revitalization District (for full credit); senior housing outside districts qualifies for 50 percent credit
Property cannot be used for railroad or public utility purposes
Property cannot be covered by the Maryland Condominium Act
Detailed receipts for all related expenses must be submitted with the application
Application must be filed within 120 days after issuance of SDAT notice of assessment that includes the improvements
For the BILP loan and facade improvement services, business must be located in a designated Commercial Revitalization District
All BILP applicants must meet with staff prior to submitting applications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the property tax credit: Complete the Application for Revitalization Tax Credit form and submit it to the Director of Budget and Finance within 120 days after receiving a notice of assessment from SDAT that includes the improvements. Include detailed receipts for all expenses. For commercial properties in revitalization districts, contact the Department of Planning Neighborhood Response Team at 410-887-3480 for assistance. Mail the completed application to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 149, Towson, Maryland 21204. You may also contact taxcredits@baltimorecountymd.gov or financeinfo@baltimorecountymd.gov for more information. For the BILP loan and facade improvement services: Schedule a meeting with staff by emailing businesshelp@baltimorecountymd.gov or calling 410-887-8000. All applicants must meet with staff before submitting applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County allows communities of 50 or more households to host bulk trash events to collect trash not normally picked up in curbside collection. When an event is approved and sufficient funds are available, the County subsidizes the cost of renting roll-off dumpsters for these community cleanup events.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County subsidizes the cost of renting roll-off dumpsters for approved community cleanup events. Subsidy is provided only if sufficient funds are available. Each community association or cleanup area is limited to one event per fiscal year (July through June).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted at least one month before the event date
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community associations and neighborhood groups with 50 or more households that want to organize bulk trash collection events
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidies cover the rental cost of roll-off dumpsters for collecting bulk trash items that are not picked up in regular curbside collection, such as appliances, furniture, and other large items. Certain restricted items like electronics and tires can be transported to the landfill in a non-commercially marked vehicle at no charge with pre-approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland only. Events must be held within the boundaries of the applicant community.
requirements_list: Community organization must represent 50 or more households
One cleanup event per fiscal year (July through June) per community association or cleanup area
Event must be held on a Saturday from 7 a.m. to noon
Location must be available and have sufficient space for the required dumpsters
Organizer must obtain written permission from the property owner to use the location
If using Board of Education property, written permission from the public school system is required
Must contract with a County-approved waste management firm to provide dumpsters
Application must be submitted at least one month before the event
Event must be open to all residents within community boundaries regardless of membership status
Community organization is responsible for monitoring the site and ensuring compliance with disposal regulations
Containers cannot be filled above the sides
Organization must cover any additional costs incurred by the hauler due to delays, wasted trips, or rehandling of prohibited items
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Select a location and date for the event (Saturday, 7 a.m. to noon) within your community boundaries and obtain written permission from the property owner. 2. Contact an approved waste management contractor and request pricing. 3. Complete the Community Clean-Up Application form and submit it at least one month before your event via email to jpridgen@baltimorecountymd.gov, by fax to 410-887-2931, or by mail to the Bureau of Solid Waste Management address. Include written permission for the location and any documentation explaining reasons for not using the lowest bid vendor. 4. Wait for approval from Baltimore County before publicizing the event. 5. Once approved, advertise only within your community (flyers, newsletters) and not in general-circulation newspapers. 6. On event day, monitor the site and refuse loads, ensure compliance with disposal regulations, and confirm the contractor removes containers promptly.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides funding to support capital projects that strengthen neighborhoods and businesses, grow communities, and advance the goals of Master Plan 2030. Grants support projects with a durability of 15 years or more that benefit the overall community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards range from $3,000 to $200,000 for a total of $1.8 million available. Capital projects should have a durability of 15 years or more and benefit the overall community.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Spring 2026 application deadline is Friday, May 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations, businesses, and residents of Baltimore County seeking to strengthen neighborhoods and support community development projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects that strengthen neighborhoods and businesses, grow communities, and advance Master Plan 2030 goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Capital projects must have a durability of 15 years or more
Projects must benefit the overall community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application by the deadline. For detailed application process information, visit the program's grant opportunities page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund (CRRF) Community Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund (CRRF) Community Grants Program provides funding from the State of Maryland, generated through state cannabis sales and use tax revenue, to support community-based initiatives that benefit low-income communities and address the impacts of cannabis criminalization and related community reinvestment needs. The program aims to improve and revitalize underinvested or historically underserved communities, with funds intended for programs serving disproportionately impacted areas as defined by the Cannabis Reform Act of 2023.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This is a reimbursable grant program with the possibility of providing a small percentage of funds upfront, subject to county grant management policies. Applicants can apply for a minimum of $25,000 and a maximum of $200,000 for a one-year project period. A 10 percent monetary or in-kind match is required. Grant monies may fund no more than 50 percent of executive and administrative salaries, though direct service staff can be fully funded. Indirect costs can be included up to the federal de minimis rate of 15 percent. Funding is generated through state cannabis sales and use tax revenue.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based private businesses, nonprofit organizations, and government entities serving Baltimore County residents, particularly those in low-income communities or priority ZIP codes identified by the Maryland Office of Social Equity. Organizations do not need to be affiliated with cannabis-related businesses to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds must support community-based initiatives benefiting low-income communities and addressing impacts of cannabis criminalization. Eligible uses include adult professional development, education and afterschool programs, entrepreneurship and economic development, housing and unhoused prevention services, mental health and harm reduction, nonprofit training and management for BIPOC community leaders, reentry and reintegration, and workforce development and training. Funds can support project-based or operating expenses, though certain costs like building renovations, capital expenses, facility expansion, and professional conferences must clearly demonstrate direct support of eligible CRRF activities. Funds cannot be used for law enforcement activities or to supplant pre-existing local government programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must serve Baltimore County residents, particularly communities disproportionately impacted by cannabis prohibition enforcement. Organizations may serve the Greater Baltimore area, but funds must directly benefit eligible Baltimore County community members. Preference is given to organizations serving priority ZIP codes (21117, 21133, 21136, 21206, 21207, 21208, 21220, 21221, 21222, 21227, 21228, 21234, 21236, 21237, 21244) or low-income communities defined as Qualified Census Tracts where at least half of households have lower income than surrounding regions. Projects outside priority ZIP codes must serve populations from or re-entering into priority ZIP codes and must serve low-income communities.
requirements_list: Entities must be community-based private businesses, nonprofit organizations, or government entities
Organizations must be aligned with the County's CRRF priorities
Organizations must serve and benefit County residents, with funds directly benefiting eligible Baltimore County community members
Organizations must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Applicants must provide a 10 percent monetary or in-kind match
Applicants must submit all required financial documentation
Applicants must provide an organization chart showing all staff involved and structure relevant to the proposed project
If organizational structure is limited, applicants must provide documentation demonstrating capacity to manage the project
Applications must score a minimum of 70 out of 100 to be considered for funding

Organizations with an annual budget over $1 million are encouraged to subcontract with smaller, local-based organizations; if subgrantees are included, letters from subgrantees detailing the partnership and services must be included
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete all required CRRF Community Grants application materials and email them to grsigrants@baltimorecountymd.gov by the deadline. Required documents include the Community Grant Funding Application, Risk Assessment, Application Scoring Sheet, Baltimore County Application for Financial Assistance, Budget Application for Financial Assistance, Grant Affidavit, Form W-9, and any required financial documentation. All supporting documents should be submitted in one email. Applications are reviewed through an established evaluation and scoring process. The CRRF Commission weighs in on funding decisions. Grant agreements outline final reporting timelines and grant start dates are determined in coordination with the County. Grants are awarded for one fiscal year, with the project period beginning upon award execution and running for one year.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides rental and utility assistance for families with children enrolled in community schools to help eligible households prevent eviction and homelessness through emergency financial support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency rental and utility assistance to prevent eviction and homelessness for eligible families with children in community schools.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not accepting applications at this time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with school-aged children enrolled in designated community schools who are at risk of homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental and utility assistance to prevent eviction and homelessness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Households must have school-aged children enrolled in a designated community school
Family must be at-risk of homelessness
Must have a Failure to Pay Rent Notice, Eviction Notice, Notice of Intent or be awaiting a court hearing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Community Schools facilitator where your child is enrolled, or call Coordinated Entry at 410-887-8463 option 1 (Monday-Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 7 p.m.) or Cornerstone Franciscan Ministries at 410-538-2830 or participantservices@cfmins.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Baltimore County program providing grant funding and low-cost or no-cost loans to pay for accessibility features and structural modifications to improve dwellings for people with disabilities. The program serves both homeowners and renters, with a dedicated component for renters who hold Housing Choice Vouchers or other federally-issued housing vouchers. Modifications accommodate the needs of individuals with disabilities including hearing, physical, or vision impairment. Projects are structural and typically involve construction, modification, or rehabilitation work performed by experienced or licensed contractors. There is no cost to grant-eligible tenants or landlords under the voucher-focused component.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides both grant funding and low-cost or no-cost loans. For renters with Housing Choice Vouchers or other federally-issued housing vouchers, grant funding covers the full cost of approved structural modifications to rental units. All modifications are completed by licensed contractors selected by the Housing Opportunities and Finance Division, or the landlord may complete them. Completion typically takes approximately two to four months after approval from all parties. There is no cost to grant-eligible tenants or landlords. For other eligible homeowners and renters (household income at or below 80% of Area Median Income with a household member with a disability), low-cost or no-cost loans are available to pay for accessibility features and structural modifications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Renters and homeowners in Baltimore County where a member of the household has a disability and household income is at or below 80 percent of the Area Median Income. A dedicated component is available for individuals with disabilities who hold a Housing Choice Voucher or other federally-issued housing voucher and reside in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessibility features and structural modifications to improve a dwelling for people with disabilities, including modifications for hearing, physical, or vision impairment. Modifications are reviewed case-by-case, must be approved by the landlord (for rental units), and are performed by experienced or licensed contractors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County. The grant component for Housing Choice Voucher holders is limited to Baltimore County residents.
requirements_list: Member of household has a disability
Household income is at or below 80 percent of the Area Median Income (for loan component)
Open to both renters and homeowners (loan component)
Head of household must be an active Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) program recipient or have another federally-issued housing voucher (grant component)
Applicant must reside in Baltimore County
Applicant must have a current and signed lease (grant/rental component)
Landlord must agree to the referral to CHAMP for the modification (grant/rental component)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the grant component (voucher holders): Submit a completed application by email to rar@baltimorecountymd.gov, by fax to 410-887-8804, or by phone at 410-887-3435, or in person at the Office of Housing. Obtain landlord approval for the referral. The application is processed by the Housing and Finance Division, with an initial response timeframe of approximately 10 days. Once the scope of work and grant agreement are drafted, both the landlord and tenant sign off. After approval from all parties, modifications are completed, typically taking two to four months. For the loan component: Submit the HAMP Homeowner Application or HAMP Renter Application, or the CHAMP Renter Application (available as PDFs).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Continuum of Care program promotes communitywide commitment to ending homelessness by providing funding for efforts by nonprofit providers and Baltimore County and State governments. These efforts create and promote access to, and effect utilization of, mainstream programs by homeless individuals and families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HUD provides annual funding through a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for renewal of current CoC grants and for new providers interested in applying to offer services. Nonprofit providers and Baltimore County and State governments can apply for funding to support homeless services and programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit providers and Baltimore County and State governments seeking to provide homeless services and support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports creation and promotion of access to mainstream programs for homeless individuals and families, including street outreach, transitional housing, permanent supportive housing, coordinated entry, and Homeless Management Information System (HMIS) services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit provider or government entity
Must submit Notice of Intent to apply by the specified deadline
Must complete application in eSNAPS system
New and renewal applications scored by Rating and Ranking Committee
Projects evaluated based on rating and ranking procedures specific to project type
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit a Notice of Intent to apply, then complete applications in eSNAPS by the deadline. The Rating and Ranking Committee reviews and scores all applications based on established procedures. Applicants are notified of acceptance, rank, or rejection following the scoring process. The CoC lead agency (DHCD) submits the final consolidated application to HUD.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free workshop and 300-page guidebook provided. Workshop is held virtually and seating is limited to 20 participants. Internet access and technology are required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family and professional caregivers of people living with dementia
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in educational workshop and access to guidebook for dementia caregiving support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Must be a caregiver of someone living with dementia
Internet access and technology required for virtual workshop
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email or call the caregivers contact to register for the workshop. Seating is limited to 20 participants.

Technology Basics for Employment consists of four workshops that participants must attend in full. Microsoft Word and Excel courses require attendance at both introduction and intermediate levels.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults seeking to develop digital and technology skills for employment
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in computer basics, internet navigation, email, virtual meeting platforms, Microsoft Word, and Microsoft Excel
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County
requirements_list: Must attend all required workshops in the chosen course track

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Law Enforcement Officers or Rescue Workers Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit that helps law enforcement personnel, fire personnel, and rescue workers (including volunteers) who have suffered permanent and total disability during their service to Baltimore County. The credit equals 100 percent of the Baltimore County real property tax obligation and continues annually for the lifetime of the disabled person. The credit applies only to real property tax and not to other charges on the bill.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The credit equals 100 percent of the Baltimore County real property tax obligation and continues annually for the lifetime of the disabled person. The credit applies only to real property tax and not to other charges on the bill. The credit is awarded only during the lifetime of the disabled person and does not extend to surviving spouses or other individuals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before September 30 of the tax year for which the credit is requested to begin
structured_extraction.contact_name: Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration
structured_extraction.program_audience: Law enforcement officers, fire personnel, and rescue workers (including volunteers) who have suffered permanent and total disability during their service to Baltimore County citizens.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces Baltimore County real property tax obligations on the disabled worker's primary residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland. The applicant must have been domiciled in the state as of the date they were adjudged to be disabled.
requirements_list: The applicant must be a law enforcement officer, fire personnel member, or rescue worker (including volunteer)
The applicant must have suffered permanent and total disability during service to Baltimore County citizens
The applicant must be deemed disabled according to requirements established within their agency

The dwelling must have been owned by the disabled worker at the time of disability, or acquired within two years of the disability determination, or acquired after qualifying for the credit for a former dwelling
The applicant must provide a verifying Court Order or Administrative Notice
The dwelling cannot be eligible for any other Baltimore County real property tax credit
The credit is awarded only during the lifetime of the disabled person and does not extend to surviving spouses or other individuals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Send a copy of the verifying Court Order or Administrative Notice along with the tax credit application form to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration at 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204, on or before September 30 of the tax year for which the credit is requested to begin.

structured_extraction.program_name: Disabled Veteran and Surviving Spouse Property Tax Exemption or Refund
structured_extraction.program_description: This program exempts the home of a disabled veteran or surviving spouse of a disabled veteran from all Baltimore County real property tax obligations. Eligible individuals may also receive a refund of taxes paid for up to three years prior to receiving the exemption. The program is administered by Baltimore County and requires initial application through the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT).

Eligible individuals may also request a refund of property taxes paid for up to three years before the exemption is approved.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The exemption applies to the primary home and eliminates Baltimore County real property tax obligations. Retroactive refunds are available for taxes paid for up to three years prior to receiving the exemption.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a disabled veteran or surviving spouse of a disabled veteran
Must own residential property in Baltimore County

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal Medicare program that helps individuals with limited income pay for prescription drug costs under Medicare Part D, including monthly premiums, annual deductibles, and drug copayments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Extra Help reduces monthly Part D premiums, annual deductibles, and prescription drug copayments. Qualifying individuals typically pay only small copayments for medications. For single individuals with income under $24,180 per year ($2,015 per month) and assets under $16,590, benefits include no monthly premium, no deductible, $5.10 generic drug copayment, and $12.65 brand name drug copayment. For couples with income under $32,700 per year ($2,725 per month) and assets under $33,100, benefits are the same. Individuals with full medical assistance eligibility receive no premium, no deductible, and dual eligible status with $1.60 generic drug copayment and $4.90 brand name drug copayment. The 2026 Regional Premium Benchmark is $43.61; plans below this amount have no premium. Certain income and assets are excluded, including the first $65 of monthly wages, half of wages above $65, the first house and first car if owning multiple properties, and $1,500 per person burial allowance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Medicare beneficiaries with limited income and assets
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of Medicare Part D premiums, deductibles, and prescription drug copayments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All United States
requirements_list: Single individuals: gross income under $24,180 per year ($2,015 per month), assets under $16,590
Couples: gross income under $32,700 per year ($2,725 per month), assets under $33,100
Exclusions: first $65 of monthly wages, one-half of monthly wages after $65 deducted, first house (if owning more than one), first car (if owning more than one), $1,500 per person burial allowance
May automatically qualify if enrolled in QMB or SLMB
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Social Security Administration by calling 1-800-772-1213 or visiting www.ssa.gov. Individuals may also be eligible for QMB or SLMB; for applications call the Baltimore County SHIP at 410-887-2059 or the Department of Social Services. Those with full medical assistance eligibility (red and white card) are automatically enrolled and do not need to apply through Social Security; Medicare premiums, deductibles, and copayments are paid through the Department of Social Services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Free iPads or Chromebooks for Seniors
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore County Department of Aging distributes free iPads and Chromebooks to eligible older adults to increase access to technology and digital connectivity.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for commercial buildings that achieve at least a silver rating under the Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) Green Building rating system or the American National Standards Institute's National Green Building Standard (NGBS) rating system. The credit amount varies based on the rating level and category, ranging from 10 to 80 percent of the property's Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligation for 3 to 5 years. Eligible buildings include commercial properties and income-producing, residentially used buildings of at least 50 units.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit reducing Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligations. LEED-NC (new construction) provides 50 percent (silver), 60 percent (gold), or 70 percent (platinum) credits for 5 years. LEED-CS (core and shell) provides 40 percent (silver), 50 percent (gold), or 80 percent (platinum) credits for 5 years. LEED-EB (existing buildings) provides 10 percent (silver), 25 percent (gold), or 50 percent (platinum) credits for 3 years. NGBS ratings provide 50 percent (silver), 60 percent (gold), or 80 percent (emerald) credits for 5 years. A property owner may receive only one High Performance Building Credit per building. Other charges listed on property tax bills are not included in the credit calculation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought, except applications filed in conjunction with a Revitalization Property Tax Credit may be filed at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners and developers with buildings achieving at least a silver rating under LEED or NGBS rating systems, including income-producing, residentially used buildings of at least 50 units.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligations for commercial buildings achieving LEED silver or higher ratings (new construction, core and shell, or existing buildings) or NGBS certifications. Other charges listed on property tax bills are not included in the credit calculation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland. The credit applies to the Baltimore County Real Property Tax obligation only.
requirements_list: Building must be commercial or an income-producing, residentially used building of at least 50 units
Building must achieve at least a silver rating under LEED-NC (new construction), LEED-CS (core and shell), LEED-EB (existing buildings), or NGBS rating system
Documentation from an energy systems professional using LEED or NGBS rating system must be provided
Application must be filed under oath with sufficient documentation proving the building meets the High Performance Building definition
Only one High Performance Building Credit per building is permitted
Credit runs with the property and does not lapse upon change of ownership

For most applications, must be filed on or before June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought (exception for applications in conjunction with a Revitalization Property Tax Credit)

Applications must be submitted under oath to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for residential properties in Baltimore County that meet energy efficiency standards. The credit amount is based on the level of energy efficiency achieved, measured using one of three approved rating systems: HERS Index, LEED, or National Green Building Standard (NGBS). The credit reduces the Baltimore County real property tax obligation and runs for three consecutive years starting with the first year awarded. The credit value corresponds to the percentage of energy efficiency achieved and runs with the property, not lapsing upon change of ownership.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners receive a property tax credit that reduces their Baltimore County real property tax obligation by a percentage corresponding to the energy efficiency level achieved. New homes with a Home Energy Rating System (HERS) Index of 70 or lower qualify. Renovated homes must achieve at least 30 percent increase in energy efficiency. Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) Silver homes receive 40 percent property tax reduction, LEED Gold homes receive 60 percent, and LEED Platinum homes receive 100 percent. National Green Building Standard (NGBS) Silver provides 40 percent reduction, NGBS Gold provides 60 percent, and NGBS Emerald provides 100 percent. The credit runs for three consecutive years. Other charges or fees on the tax bill are not included in the credit calculation. New homes sold or leased after 2021 and before 2033 may also qualify under the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Baltimore County with newly constructed or renovated residential properties that meet energy efficiency standards, including those certified under HERS, LEED, or NGBS rating systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax reduction on Baltimore County real property taxes for residential structures meeting energy efficiency requirements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland only. The credit runs with the property and does not lapse upon change of ownership.
requirements_list: For HERS Index: newly constructed residence must receive a HERS Rating of 70 or lower, or renovated structures must achieve at least 30 percent increase in energy efficiency with HERS Ratings completed before and after renovation
For LEED: property must be rated Silver, Gold, or Platinum by the U.S. Green Building Council
For NGBS: property must be rated Silver, Gold, or Emerald by the American National Standards Institute-approved rating system
Property must have certificate indicating energy efficiency level provided by builder, contractor, or rater
Application must be submitted no later than June 1 immediately preceding the first taxable year for which credit is sought
Granting of credit is subject to funding availability
Property must be a residential structure
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Gather required documentation including the certificate indicating the efficiency level of the property from the builder, contractor, or rater, and for renovated structures, HERS Ratings completed before and after renovation. Step 2: Apply online with a valid email address and documentation, or print and complete the High Performance Homes Tax Credit application form and submit by mail or in person to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration, at 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Broadband Infrastructure Grant Program (Connect Maryland Network Infrastructure Grant)
structured_extraction.program_description: State funding through Connect Maryland and the Governor's Office of Rural Broadband to support broadband infrastructure construction in underserved areas of Baltimore County. Multiple grant awards have been made: the FY21 grant provided matching funds from the state, Comcast, and Baltimore County to bring high-speed internet service to over 850 homes, primarily in the northwest corner of the County (construction and activation now complete). The FY23 grant provided additional funding to serve approximately 440 homes, with an additional 40+ homes under review, targeting further underserved communities in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FY21 Award: State contributed $3.75 million; Comcast contributed $1.87 million; Baltimore County contributed $700,000. Total project funding supported construction and activation of broadband service to over 850 homes (complete). FY23 Award: State funding of just over $7.4 million; Comcast contribution of $1.2 million; Baltimore County contribution of $613,000. Project supports broadband construction to approximately 440 homes, with potential for an additional 40+ homes. All awards are matching grants requiring contributions from the state, Comcast, and Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents in underserved areas lacking reliable broadband access, and government entities seeking to expand broadband infrastructure to unserved and underserved communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Broadband infrastructure construction and activation to bring high-speed internet service to unserved and underserved homes in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, with priority in underserved communities including the northwest corner of the County (FY21) and additional underserved communities (FY23).
requirements_list: Located in an underserved area of Baltimore County lacking reliable broadband service
Project must serve a defined number of unserved homes (e.g., approximately 440 homes plus potentially 40 additional homes in FY23; over 850 homes in FY21)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Baltimore County applies for and receives awards from the state through Connect Maryland (Office of Statewide Broadband) and/or the Governor's Office of Rural Broadband. Funding is structured as a matching grant with contributions from the state, Comcast, and Baltimore County. Individual residents do not apply directly; the County administers the program on behalf of eligible communities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides transportation services for Medical Assistance (Medicaid) recipients who live in Baltimore County and need rides to medically necessary services. This is a last-resort program for people with no other transportation options, serving ambulatory, wheelchair, and stretcher-bound recipients.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Medical Assistance Program covers the full cost of transportation services at no charge to eligible recipients. Transportation is provided through contracted vendors (Hart to Heart for wheelchair and ambulance rides, and TransDev/Veolia for shared rides). Services operate Monday through Saturday for regular appointments (5 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. with TransDev, 5 a.m. to 8 p.m. with Hart to Heart), and Hart to Heart offers 24/7 service for medical facility discharges and transfers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents who are eligible Medical Assistance (Medicaid) recipients with no other means of transportation to medically necessary services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to and from medical appointments, medical facility discharges, and transfers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only to Baltimore County residents. This is a Baltimore County program.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore County resident with eligible, non-restrictive Medical Assistance (Medicaid)
Must have no other means of transportation available
Must have medical certification from a physician stating inability to use public transportation due to a specific medical condition
Medical certification must be renewed at least annually
Trips must be pre-scheduled one to seven days in advance
Must request transportation at least 24 hours prior to appointment (except for same-day rides under extreme circumstances)
Must be ready for pickup at designated time and place or ride counts as no-show
Cannot use Mobility transportation except under extreme circumstances (TransDev requirement)
Physician must certify inability to use public or ADA transportation (TransDev requirement)
For stretcher transports to doctor's offices, accommodation must be verified in advance
Children 17 years and under must be accompanied by an adult
Residents of skilled nursing facilities must be accompanied during transport
Children must be in car seats provided by parent or guardian
No eating, drinking, or smoking in vehicles
Conduct that jeopardizes safety may result in suspension of services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Baltimore County Department of Health at 410-887-2828 (Monday-Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:45 p.m.) to begin the enrollment process. Have your physician complete and sign the Baltimore County Certificate for Medical Transportation form and submit it to the Health Department. Once approved, contact the appropriate transportation vendor directly (Hart to Heart at 443-573-2037 for wheelchair/ambulance, or TransDev at 410-783-2465 for shared rides) to schedule individual trips. Trips can be booked one to seven days in advance and must be requested at least 24 hours before the appointment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state- and county-funded program that helps individuals aged 18 and over live in safe, protective family home settings with a maximum of four adults per home. The program has two tracks: Project Home (state-funded) and Adult Foster Care (county-funded). Both assist people who need protective housing but do not require nursing care, assisted living, or institutional care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program operates under two funding tracks. Under Project Home (state-funded), clients with insufficient income to cover care costs receive assistance applying for Public Assistance to Adults (PAA), a state payment made to the client or their representative payee. Anyone eligible for PAA also receives Medical Assistance. Clients receive a personal needs allowance of $82 and may keep $20 from outside income. Under Adult Foster Care (county-funded), clients with insufficient income or assets to pay for care costs receive a subsidy paid directly to the provider. Clients receive a personal needs allowance of $75 and may keep an additional $32.50 from outside income. For both tracks, monthly provider costs range from $776 (Level A/1) to $1,376 (Level D/4) depending on care needs.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Tina Savage, LCSW-C, Supervisor; Gem Wilson, LMSW, Housing Coordinator; Anna Chalker, LMSW, Housing Coordinator
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents aged 18 and over who need protective housing and cannot completely care for themselves or live independently, but do not need significant nursing care, assisted living, or institutional care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program covers care costs including housing, meals, personal care, supervision, transportation to medical appointments, medication monitoring, and other support services based on individual client needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residents only.
requirements_list: Must be at least 18 years old
Must be a Baltimore County resident
Must need protective housing
Cannot completely care for self or live independently
Do not need significant nursing care or institutional care
Do not require assisted living
Cannot be bedridden
Must be ambulatory or, if in wheelchair, able to perform all transfers safely without assistance
Clients with income insufficient to pay for care costs and personal expenses are eligible (Project Home)
Clients with insufficient income or assets to pay for care costs are eligible for subsidy (Adult Foster Care)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and mail the client application to the Department of Social Services, Drumcastle Government Center, 6401 York Road, Baltimore, Maryland 21212. Clients can be referred by a hospital, the community, or other Department of Social Services programs. A social worker assesses client appropriateness and need. The Housing Referral Committee suggests providers based on client needs. If interested, the client visits the potential provider home, followed by a paid overnight visit. If successful, a move-in date is set.

structured_extraction.program_description: An urban reforestation initiative that combines the County's two successful urban reforestation programs (Operation ReTree and Street Tree Replacement) into a community-based program. Project ReTree focuses on specific neighborhoods each spring and fall, planting large numbers of canopy trees in Baltimore County rights-of-way and providing free front yard trees to homeowners upon request.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County provides free tree planting in targeted neighborhoods during spring and fall seasons. Homeowners can request free front yard trees. Initial maintenance is included for one year with a 100 percent survival guarantee. Maintenance may include watering, pruning and shelter upkeep. EPS conducts two inspections during the initial maintenance period and continues monitoring for at least 10 years after planting.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents in targeted neighborhoods seeking free street trees and front yard trees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting in public rights-of-way and on private residential properties to increase and maintain urban tree canopy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only. Program focuses on specific neighborhoods each spring and fall.
requirements_list: Homeowner must request trees for their property
Property must be in a neighborhood selected for Project ReTree planting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Project ReTree page to learn more about the program and submit requests. Homeowners in selected neighborhoods can request free front yard trees during planting seasons.

structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County provides grants to help residential property owners implement flood mitigation solutions on their properties. The County determines on a case-by-case basis whether residential flood mitigation is the most impactful and economical option for addressing a flooding problem. Eligible solutions include basement waterproofing, elevation of mechanical systems, exterior curbs with fill and grading, stairwell elevation, and green infrastructure projects like rain barrels, permeable pavers, bioswales, rain gardens, and french drains. The program aims to reduce flood risk and water damage for homeowners throughout Baltimore County.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funding to eligible residential property owners to cover the costs of approved flood mitigation improvements, including structural floodproofing solutions and green infrastructure projects. The specific grant amount and terms are determined on a case-by-case basis following a thorough review of drainage conditions on the property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners and homeowners in Baltimore County experiencing flooding problems and seeking to protect their properties from flood risk and water damage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used for residential structural floodproofing solutions such as basement waterproofing, elevation of mechanical systems like water heaters and furnaces, exterior curbs with fill and grading around doors and windows, stairwell elevation, and green infrastructure projects including rain barrels, permeable pavers, bioswales, rain gardens, and french drains with sump pump installation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County, Maryland only
requirements_list: Property must be in Baltimore County
Flooding problem must be determined by the County to be best addressed through residential flood mitigation on a case-by-case basis
Property owner must submit an application
The County must complete a thorough review of drainage conditions on the property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Affected property owners are invited to apply for the program by reviewing the program documents and submitting an application. The County reviews drainage conditions on the property on a case-by-case basis to determine eligibility and appropriateness of residential flood mitigation as a solution.

structured_extraction.program_description: A low-cost spay and neuter surgical program for Baltimore County residents' cats and dogs. The program includes the surgery plus rabies vaccination, other vaccines, deworming, a county animal license, and microchip—all for a $20 total cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A comprehensive spay or neuter surgery package for $20 per pet. The package includes the surgical procedure, rabies vaccine (required by law), additional vaccines (distemper and Bordetella for dogs), deworming, a Baltimore County animal license for county residents, and microchip insertion. All services are included as a package; pet owners cannot opt out of individual services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents who own cats or dogs and want affordable spay and neuter services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Spay or neuter surgery and associated veterinary services including vaccinations, deworming, animal license, and microchip.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County residents only. Pets must reside in Baltimore County. Services are not available for pets living outside Baltimore County. Rescue and foster groups are not currently eligible.
requirements_list: Pet must be a cat or dog owned by a Baltimore County resident
Cat must be at least five months old and no older than six years
Dog must be at least four months old and no older than six years
Cat must weigh at least five pounds
Dog must weigh at least five pounds and no more than 60 pounds if female or 80 pounds if male
Dogs cannot be boxers, bulldogs (all breeds), pugs, or Shih Tzus (other short-faced and mixed breeds evaluated case by case)
Cats cannot be hairless, Himalayan, or Persian breeds
Pet cannot have a known illness, injury, or medical condition
Pet cannot present increased anesthetic risk (no feline leukemia, heart murmurs, kidney disease, seizure disorder, retained testicles, or upper respiratory infections)
Appointments are required; walk-ins not accepted
Payment of $20 required at time of scheduling
Valid email address required for pre-surgical documents
Pet must not be fed after midnight the night before surgery (water allowed)
Owner must drop off pet to sign consent and provide medical history
Complete rabies certificate required as proof of prior vaccination if available
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Check your pet's eligibility against breed, age, weight, and health restrictions. 2) Complete the online appointment request form at the designated Dundalk location. 3) Make payment of $20 by credit card at time of scheduling using the same email address as the appointment request. 4) Receive a confirmation email when your appointment is accepted. 5) Bring your pet (cats in carrier, dogs on non-retractable leash) and any medical records to the surgical center by 8 a.m. on your appointment date. 6) Drop off your pet; owner must sign consent and provide medical history. 7) Pick up your pet the same day after 3 p.m. at the assigned time. 8) Follow home care instructions provided at discharge.

structured_extraction.program_name: Surviving Spouses of Fallen Law Enforcement Officers or Rescue Workers Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore County offers a property tax credit to the surviving spouse of a law enforcement officer or rescue worker (including volunteers) who died in Maryland during the course of or as a result of their employment with Baltimore County. The credit equals 100 percent of the County real property tax obligation and continues year after year without requiring reapplication.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The surviving spouse receives a property tax credit equal to 100 percent of their Baltimore County real property tax obligation. The credit continues each year without requiring reapplication. The credit applies only to real property tax and does not include other charges on the tax bill.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before September 30 in the taxable year for which the credit is desired to begin
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses of fallen law enforcement officers or rescue workers (including volunteers) who died in Maryland during the course of or as a result of their employment with Baltimore County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax relief on Baltimore County real property tax obligations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The deceased must have died in the State of Maryland during the course of or as a result of employment with Baltimore County. The surviving spouse must have been domiciled in the state as of the date of death. Baltimore County only.
requirements_list: Applicant must be the surviving spouse of a law enforcement officer or rescue worker (including volunteers)
The death must have occurred in the State of Maryland during the course of or as a result of the individual's employment with Baltimore County

The dwelling was owned by the decedent at the time of death, OR the decedent or surviving spouse was domiciled in the state as of the date of death and the dwelling was acquired by the spouse within two years of the date of death, OR the dwelling was acquired after the surviving spouse qualified for a credit for a former dwelling
The credit cannot be combined with any other credit or tax relief program
Application must be submitted on or before September 30 of the taxable year for which the credit is desired to begin
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an Application for Surviving Spouse of a Fallen Law Enforcement Officer or Rescue Worker to the Office of Budget and Finance, Property Tax Credit Administration, 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, Maryland 21204 on or before September 30 of the taxable year for which the credit is desired to begin.
