structured_extraction.program_description: A rural reforestation program that converts lawn or grass areas of one acre or more into forest. The program plants approximately 200 native trees per acre, spaced 15 feet apart in staggered rows, and equips trees with stakes and shelters to protect them from deer and pest damage.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County provides free tree planting and initial three years of maintenance with a 90 percent survival guarantee. Maintenance includes seasonal mowing, vine and invasive species management, shelter upkeep, watering during drought, and pesticide or herbicide use as needed. EPS conducts yearly inspections during the initial maintenance period and continues to monitor reforestations for at least 10 years after planting, conducting additional maintenance and replacement plantings as needed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore County residents with one acre or more of open space (lawn or grass) away from utility easements, Forest Conservation Easements, and septic systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting and reforestation of private or public land to reduce stormwater runoff and improve Chesapeake Bay health.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only. Property must be open space (lawn or grass) away from utility easements, Forest Conservation Easements, septic and septic reserves.
requirements_list: Property must be one acre or more of open lawn or grass space
Property must be away from utility easements, Forest Conservation Easements, septic and septic reserves
Property owner must submit a Reforestation Property Form
Property owner must maintain trees and report their survival to EPS after initial contractor maintenance period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Reforestation Property Form to determine your eligibility. The form can be submitted via the Turf to Trees page. Upon approval, the County schedules tree planting and provides three years of maintenance.

structured_extraction.program_description: An urban reforestation program that provides free tree plantings for managed grounds such as homeowners associations (HOAs), apartment complexes, and businesses. The program plants landscape-style trees and larger shade trees in public rights-of-way, parks, or surrounding buildings to increase tree canopy in densely populated urban areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County provides free tree planting and one year of maintenance with a 100 percent survival guarantee. Maintenance may include watering, pruning and shelter upkeep. EPS conducts two inspections during the initial maintenance period and continues monitoring for at least 10 years after planting, conducting additional maintenance and replacement plantings as needed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: HOAs, apartment complexes, businesses, and property managers in Baltimore County seeking to increase tree canopy in urban areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting to increase and maintain tree canopy in densely populated urban areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County only, within more populated areas inside the Urban Rural Demarcation Line and Census Designated Places.
requirements_list: Each project must include 20 trees or more
Property must be managed grounds such as HOAs, apartment complexes, or businesses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Email forestmanagement@baltimorecountymd.gov to request an urban reforestation planting. Include details about your property and planting goals. Upon approval, the County schedules tree planting and provides one year of maintenance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Association Restoration, Planning and Implementation Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore County Department of Environmental Protection and Sustainability awards grants to locally-based watershed associations and nonprofit organizations to identify and implement restoration projects and educational activities that support water quality improvements, increase resident participation in watershed restoration planning, and leverage additional funding for environmental restoration work in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provide funding of up to $30,000 to cover staff hours and fringe benefits dedicated to conducting environmental restoration activities and increasing public awareness of environmental stewardship related to water quality. An amount up to 30 percent of salary can cover fringe benefits such as health insurance, paid sick leave and paid vacation. Up to 10 percent of combined salary and fringe can cover indirect overhead expenses including accounting, financial management, insurance, office rent and supplies. Materials and equipment are not funded. The ratio of staff hours to dollars must be a minimum of one hour of staff time for every $30 in grant funds requested.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Locally-based watershed associations and community groups with membership in Baltimore County that are registered as 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4) or 501(c)(6) organizations in good standing with the State of Maryland and have a demonstrated history of successfully identifying and conducting resident-based and community restoration projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses to foster staffing capacity for ongoing restoration work and watershed education and outreach. Eligible uses include tree plantings and maintenance, stormwater best management practice design and installation and maintenance, downspout disconnections, rain gardens, rain barrels, stream cleanups, stream watch programs, conservation landscapes, watershed education and outreach, invasive plant removal and storm drain marking. Materials and equipment are not funded.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All grant-funded activities must be implemented in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Organization must be a locally-based watershed association or community group with membership in Baltimore County
Organization must be registered as a 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4) or 501(c)(6) organization in good standing with the State of Maryland
Organization must have a demonstrated history of successfully identifying and conducting resident-based and community restoration projects
Organization must have fulfilled all grant requirements on past grants if previously funded through this grant program
Minimum ratio of one hour of staff time for every $30 in grant funds requested

All planned restoration actions must be linked to applicable Small Watershed Action Plans, Total Maximum Daily Load Implementation Plans, Trash and Litter Reduction Strategy or Phase II Watershed Implementation Plan
Organization must commit to offering a Stream Watch program to engage volunteers in regular stream observation and pollution reporting
Organization must participate in Baltimore County Watershed Planning steering and implementation committees in their watershed
Organization must follow Baltimore County guidance on tree plantings, tree giveaways and stormwater best management practices
Organization must coordinate with DEPS on inspection and verification of past planting projects and other best management practices
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete three steps: (1) Complete the DEPS Watershed Grant Application Questions addressing organization eligibility, restoration and stewardship planned, grant deliverables by quarter, Stream Watch program, watershed planning participation, linking actions to watershed plans, education and outreach, capacity building, project guidance and inspections, and past year accomplishments. (2) Complete the standard Baltimore County Application for Financial Assistance (AFA form). (3) Submit supporting documents including good standing certificate, budget proposal, financial statements, and any additional attachments. Submit all application materials as separate PDF files via email to Erin Watts at ewatts@baltimorecountymd.gov using the subject line format '[Organization Initials] – FY XX Grant Application'. The application must be signed by the Executive Director or President of the Board. Applicants will be notified of their status in May following County agencies' review and approvals.

The program offers loans of $50,000 to $250,000 with reduced down payment requirements and interest rates set at or below current market rates, with a maximum 20-year term and customized payment plans to help businesses maintain cash flow. The program has approved over $6 million in loans to key job-creating industries.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $50,000 to $250,000 with a maximum 20-year term. Interest rates are set at or below current market rates. Down payment requirements are reduced compared to traditional bank loans. Payment plans are customized to meet individual business cash flow needs. Loans are available as gap funding when a bank cannot provide the full project cost.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal rental assistance program that helps low-income, very low-income, and extremely low-income families, elderly individuals, and persons with disabilities afford safe, decent, and sanitary housing in the private market. Participating families receive vouchers that subsidize their rent, with the housing authority paying a portion of the rent directly to landlords on their behalf. Families pay the difference between the actual rent and the subsidized amount. Participants can choose their own housing including single-family homes, townhouses, and apartments that meet program requirements. Under certain circumstances, families may also use their voucher to purchase a modest home. The program is administered locally by housing authorities in Baltimore County, Cecil County, and Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.agency: Baltimore County; Cecil County; Prince George's County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A housing subsidy is paid directly to landlords on behalf of participating families. The housing authority pays the landlord the difference between approximately 30 percent of the family's adjusted income and a payment standard (based on HUD-established fair market rents), or the gross rent for the unit, whichever is lower. Families may choose a unit with higher rent and pay the difference themselves, not to exceed 40 percent of adjusted family income. All rents are subject to a comparability study of similar unassisted properties in the area. Families must find qualifying housing that meets HUD's Housing Quality Standards within 120 days of receiving a voucher. In Prince George's County, the program administered a total of 5,907 vouchers in Fiscal Year 2022. Maximum subsidy amounts vary by jurisdiction based on local payment standards and utility allowances. Cecil County residents receive preference, followed by Maryland residents, then all others. Portability allows families to find housing within or outside Maryland in jurisdictions that have a Housing Choice Voucher Program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Cecil County: open/rolling waiting list with approximately 3-year wait for Cecil County residents. Prince George's County: application period was Monday, December 1, 2025 at 12:01 a.m. to Friday, December 5, 2025 at 11:59 p.m. EST; waitlist is now closed; selected applicants notified by email and mail at least 45 days after waitlist closes. Baltimore County: no waiting lists are open; not accepting preliminary applications until further notice.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: Baltimore County: 410-887-2766; Cecil County: 410-996-5245; Prince George's County: 301-883-5501
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, very low-income, and extremely low-income families, elderly individuals, and persons with disabilities who meet federal income eligibility requirements. Served in Baltimore County, Cecil County, and Prince George's County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance to help families afford safe, decent housing in the private market. Funds pay the difference between what families can afford and the actual rent for units that meet housing quality standards. Under certain circumstances, vouchers may also be used toward down payment assistance for purchasing a modest home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is administered locally and serves residents within each respective jurisdiction: Baltimore County, Cecil County, and Prince George's County. For Cecil County, county residents receive preference, followed by Maryland residents, then all others. Families may use portability to find housing within or outside Maryland in jurisdictions that have a Housing Choice Voucher Program.
requirements_list: Household income must meet federal income guidelines for low-income, very low-income, or extremely low-income households
Must provide required information on Social Security numbers, citizenship or immigration status, and detailed income and family information at time of interview
Must be placed on waiting list and wait for selection
When selected, family must complete enrollment interview and eligibility determination
Family must attend briefing/certification session on program rules
Family must find qualifying housing within 120 days of receiving voucher
Housing unit must meet HUD's Housing Quality Standards
Rent must be reasonable and comparable to similar unassisted units in the area
Lease and unit must pass agency inspection and approval
Families may not pay more than 40 percent of adjusted family income toward rent
Emergency Housing Voucher (EHV) Program participants receive highest preference ranking if they apply during a waitlist opening (Prince George's County)
All applicants must complete eligibility verification and provide required documentation if selected from the lottery (Prince George's County)
Additional eligibility and documentation requirements apply
For Cecil County: County residents receive preference, followed by Maryland residents, then all others
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Submit a preliminary application during the designated application period (applications may be submitted online, dropped off, mailed, faxed, or emailed if signed in ink and scanned, depending on jurisdiction). 2) Be placed on the waiting list based on application date/time or via lottery selection (Prince George's County uses a random lottery selecting 5,000 applicants from applications received). 3) Wait for name to reach the top of the waiting list (approximately 3 years for Cecil County residents). 4) When selected, schedule and complete an enrollment interview and eligibility determination. 5) If determined eligible, attend a certification briefing on program rules and responsibilities. 6) Search for and find qualifying housing within 120 days of receiving voucher. 7) Negotiate lease terms with landlord. 8) Agency reviews lease and inspects dwelling for compliance with HUD Housing Quality Standards. 9) Agency approves or disapproves lease and unit based on inspection results. 10) Upon approval, the housing agency and owner enter into a housing assistance contract on behalf of the family. For Prince George's County, selected applicants are notified by email and mail at least 45 days after the waitlist closes.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that helps Housing Choice Voucher participants achieve economic independence within five years. Participants work with a case manager or FSS specialist to define career and financial goals, eliminate obstacles to self-sufficiency, set personal goals, and build an interest-bearing escrow savings account. The program is administered by multiple Maryland counties including Baltimore County and Harford County, and provides access to a wide range of supportive services including child care, credit counseling, education, employment assistance, English language instruction, homeownership guidance, and transportation assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive support services including childcare assistance, transportation help, education support, job search and job retention skills training, and financial planning services such as credit repair and homeownership counseling. When earned income increases, a portion of the resulting rent increase is placed into an interest-bearing escrow savings account. Upon successful completion of the five-year contract and achievement of self-sufficiency goals — including being free of Temporary Cash Assistance (welfare benefits) and employed at time of graduation — participants receive the accumulated escrow account balance and accrued interest. Housing Choice Voucher subsidy is maintained throughout participation and after graduation. Additional services include career counseling, money management and savings assistance, English as a second language instruction, and access to case management.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) participants in Baltimore County and Harford County who have employment goals and wish to achieve financial independence and economic self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Escrow savings account accumulation toward self-sufficiency goals; support for achieving financial independence including career development, financial planning, childcare, transportation, education, job retention, homeownership counseling, and credit repair.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore County and Harford County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) participant
Must have a goal of achieving economic independence
Must have employment goals
Head or co-head of household must sign an FSS Contract of Participation
All household members age 18 or older are eligible for services once contract is signed
Must complete and sign a contract with a current, signed training plan
Must maintain contact with FSS specialist or case manager
Must follow through on commitments in contract and plan
Must complete contract and all activities within five years to access escrow savings
Must be free of Maryland Temporary Cash Assistance (welfare benefits) and employed at time of graduation to access escrow account
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested Housing Choice Voucher participants can complete and submit the FSS Program interest form or call 410-638-3045 to make an appointment and learn more about the program. Eligible Housing Choice Voucher participants may also apply directly and sign an FSS Contract of Participation. Upon enrollment, participants are assigned a case manager or FSS specialist who helps assess strengths, identify barriers, develop a contract and training plan outlining goals and required activities, and work toward achievement of those goals over the five-year contract period, with periodic plan revisions as needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally designated area where companies can import or export international goods with cost-saving benefits. Businesses can hold warehouse, distribution, and manufacturing activities on U.S. soil with deferred duties, reduced processing fees, and streamlined logistics. The zone operates under the Alternative Site Framework allowing quick activation within a few weeks at any property in the designated service area. This program creates federally designated areas that are considered outside of U.S. Customs territory, helping companies that import or export international goods save money by deferring duties, reducing fees, and simplifying their supply chain.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides deferred duties on imported goods, reduced processing fees, and streamlined logistics for companies conducting warehouse, distribution, and manufacturing operations. Companies can activate their operations within a few weeks and locate at any property in the designated service area. Benefits include deferring payment of import duties until goods leave the zone or are entered into U.S. commerce, reduced Customs processing fees, and simplified supply chain management for international trade operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Companies importing or exporting international goods that operate warehouse, distribution, and manufacturing facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Warehouse, distribution, and manufacturing activities involving imported or exported international goods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service area consists of almost 1,000 total acres of designated industrial and distribution space across Baltimore City, Anne Arundel County, Baltimore County, Harford County, Cecil County, Howard County, and Queen Anne's County.
requirements_list: Must import or export international goods
Must be located within the designated Foreign Trade Zone #74 service area
Operations must involve warehouse, distribution, and/or manufacturing activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the FTZ Director (Will Cawthern) to inquire about activation. Companies can complete the activation process within a few weeks. The zone operates under the Alternative Site Framework allowing quick activation at any property within the designated service area.

structured_extraction.program_description: A matching grant program administered by the Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC) that provides funds to assist commercial and industrial property owners with exterior building upgrades, such as storefronts, signage, awnings, and other improvements that enhance the appearance of Baltimore's commercial areas. The program also supports the total redevelopment of vacant small commercial properties in neighborhood commercial areas throughout Baltimore City. Multiple FIG options exist to support different property types and contexts, including Citywide FIG, Corner Property FIG, Vacant Building FIG, Industrial FIG, and Shopping Center FIG.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grant funds structured as reimbursement-based awards. All FIG awards (except Shopping Center FIG) are structured as a 1:1 match of the applicant's investment up to the maximum award amount. Citywide FIG provides up to $7,500 (50% of eligible improvement costs). Corner Property FIG provides up to $15,000 with a $50,000 minimum investment requirement. Vacant Building FIG provides up to $15,000 with a $50,000 minimum investment requirement. Industrial FIG provides up to $15,000 for industrially zoned businesses over 10,000 square feet. Shopping Center FIG provides up to $50,000 (10% of total project costs) with a $100,000 minimum investment and requires a 5-year maintenance plan. All grants are reimbursement-based; applicants must complete and pay for the entire project before receiving funds. Architectural and design services are eligible but capped at 15% of project cost. Murals and custom/specialty elements are capped at 25% of project cost. Final reimbursement is based on the lowest bids for each component.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business owners, property owners, and developers with commercial and industrial properties in Baltimore City. Eligible applicants include businesses with signed leases, commercial property owners, and owners of vacant properties (with conditions regarding first-floor commercial tenant occupancy and Use & Occupancy permits).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible improvements include: Primary improvements such as business signage (building-mounted, blade signs, hand-painted), exterior painting, storefront windows/doors/carpentry, exterior lighting, awnings, and window/door upgrades with clear aesthetic improvement. Secondary improvements include masonry and cornice work, upper floor facade improvements, semi-permanent landscaping features, murals, interior-mounted door and window security features, and window decal signage. Ineligible expenses include deferred maintenance, roof work, structural repairs, security systems, wheelchair ramps, permit fees, landscaping materials, outdoor seating, and non-permanently affixed improvements. However, some ineligible items may qualify under BDC's Outdoor Spaces Grant.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City (citywide program), with a focus on neighborhood commercial areas. Properties must comply with zoning laws and urban renewal plans. Applicants in Baltimore City Historic Districts (CHAP) must receive CHAP authorization. Properties in Main Street Districts (Belair-Edison, Federal Hill, Fells Point, Hamilton-Lauraville, Highlandtown, Pennsylvania Avenue, Pigtown, and Waverly) may need to submit to local Main Streets Design Review Committee.
requirements_list: Property must be commercial or industrial
Applicant must provide matching funds (1:1 match for most FIGs)
Work must not begin before grant approval; work completed before approval is not eligible for reimbursement
Applicant must meet with a BDC representative at the project site prior to submitting an application
Applicant must be in compliance with all local, state, and federal regulations and in Good Standing with the State of Maryland
Each aspect of the project must have two separate quotes from licensed contractors in good standing with Maryland and not affiliated with applicant
Applicants must provide visual representations (renderings, sketches, or annotated photographs) of proposed improvements
Construction must be completed within 120 days of the award letter unless otherwise approved in writing
Final grant reimbursement is based on the lowest bids for each component
Property must have a Use & Occupancy permit (obtained before reimbursement if not present at application)
Properties must have clearly visible, permanent business signage installed prior to reimbursement
Applicant must maintain all improvements in good repair for five (5) years after project completion
Contractors must be properly registered, licensed, insured, and pass debarment checks
Applicants must submit proof of all contractor payments and at least 2 after photos showing completed work and business signage
Corner Property FIG requires $50,000 minimum investment and first-floor commercial tenant upon completion
Vacant Building FIG requires $50,000 minimum investment, first-floor commercial tenant, and signed lease with tenant before reimbursement
Industrial FIG is for buildings over 10,000 square feet with full building overhaul (not single elements)
Shopping Center FIG requires $100,000 minimum investment, 5-year maintenance plan, and specific improvements (lighting, parking, landscaping, signage)
Property cannot have received a FIG in the prior 12-month period
Property owner's building cannot be actively listed for sale
For vacant properties: no reimbursement until signed lease for first-floor tenant submitted, first-floor business open and operational, and Use & Occupancy permit issued
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply: 1) Request a grant application through the BDC website. 2) You will receive the application by email. 3) Meet with a BDC representative at the project site BEFORE submitting your application. 4) Compile your application package including: all application fields completed with signatures, W-9 form, two current photos of the property, conceptual drawings/renderings/plans of proposed work, two contractor estimates for all work, and signed lease or proof of commercial occupancy. 5) Submit complete application package. 6) BDC reviews application (discretionary; may require significant revisions). 7) Upon approval, DO NOT BEGIN WORK - work completed before approval is not eligible for reimbursement. 8) Complete construction within 120 days of award letter. 9) Request extension in writing if needed. 10) Upon completion, submit reimbursement request with: completed Reimbursement Request Form, at least 2 after photos showing entire completed work and business signage, and copies of all payments to contractors (cashed checks, paid invoices, or itemized receipts). 11) BDC processes reimbursement based on lowest bids and final project costs. For vacant properties, reimbursement requires signed lease with operating first-floor tenant and Use & Occupancy permit. For historic district properties, CHAP authorization required before work begins.

structured_extraction.program_name: Grocery Store Personal Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore City offers a personal property tax credit to grocery stores that are locating or making significant renovations in targeted Food Desert Retail Incentive Areas. The credit helps address food deserts by incentivizing quality supermarkets to open or expand in underserved neighborhoods, increasing resident access to healthy food and encouraging local economic development. The tax credit went into effect on January 31st, 2016 and was amended in 2018.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 10-year, 80 percent credit against personal property tax. Personal property typically covers furniture, fixtures and equipment. New construction requires at least $150,000 expended or $25 per square foot. Renovations require $5-$10 per square foot depending on store size: $5 per square foot for stores 20,000 square feet or less; $8 per square foot for stores more than 20,000 square feet and up to and including 45,000 square feet; $10 per square foot for stores more than 45,000 square feet. The tax credit went into effect on January 31st, 2016 and was amended in 2018.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Pre-qualification applications are accepted on a rolling basis (allow 30 days for processing). Initial applications must be received by October 1 for the tax year beginning January 1 of the next calendar year (allow 60 days for processing). Continuing eligibility forms must be received by November 30 of the year prior to the tax year for which continuing eligibility is sought.
structured_extraction.contact_email: info@BaltimoreDevelopment.com (pre-qualification and continuing eligibility); tax.credits@baltimorecity.gov (initial application)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Grocery store operators locating or renovating stores in Baltimore City's targeted grocery store incentive areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal property including furniture, fixtures and equipment for grocery stores locating or renovating in Food Desert Retail Incentive Areas
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located in a grocery store incentive area (Food Desert Retail Incentive Area) in Baltimore City. Use CityView to determine if a specific address qualifies.
requirements_list: Must be a supermarket or grocery store
Must locate or renovate in a Food Desert Retail Incentive Area (grocery store incentive area)
Must have a produce department, meat department, seafood department, and dairy department
Must derive more than 50% of sales from food
Must derive more than 50% of total sales floor space dedicated to food
Must have at least 500 square feet dedicated to sale of fruits and vegetables
Must have at least 500 square feet dedicated to sale of perishable goods including meat, seafood and dairy products
New stores must have expended at least $150,000 or $25 per square foot on new personal property

Renovated stores must have expended: $5 per square foot for stores 20,000 square feet or less; $8 per square foot for stores more than 20,000 up to 45,000 square feet; $10 per square foot for stores more than 45,000 square feet
Must comply with all requirements of the Baltimore City Health Article
Must comply with all requirements of the Baltimore City Building, Fire and Related Codes Article
Must remain current on all other taxes and fees owed to the City of Baltimore
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Submit pre-qualification form with store concept and rendering (for new stores) or sales data by food versus non-food items for most recent fiscal year (for existing stores seeking renovation credit). Email to info@baltimoredevelopment.com. Allow 30 days for processing. Pre-qualification expires in 24 months from date of grant for planned new construction projects and 180 days from date of issue for all others. Step 2: Once pre-qualified, proceed with construction or renovation. Upon completion, submit the initial application form by October 1 along with pre-qualification letter and invoices/receipts documenting personal property expenditures to tax.credits@baltimorecity.gov to request verification for the next tax year. Allow 60 days for processing. Step 3: Once a credit is granted, submit a continuing eligibility form by November 30 each year for the 10-year credit period to info@baltimoredevelopment.com to verify ongoing compliance with all program requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC) provides grants to help business owners pay for outdoor improvements that expand a business's use of outdoor space, activate public areas, and contribute to vibrant street life in Baltimore neighborhoods. Eligible improvements include outdoor seating, parklets, landscaping, lighting, and other features. The program aims to create more public space, encourage community interaction, and make Baltimore's neighborhood streets more lively.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grant of up to $5,000 in matching funds to offset the cost of outdoor space improvements. Applicants must contract for, complete, and pay for the entire project first. Grant funds will be reimbursed to the applicant following proof of completion and payment. Work completed prior to written grant approval is not eligible for reimbursement. The final grant reimbursement amount is based on the lowest bids for each component of the project. If the final project cost is lower than project costs provided at the time of application and approval, BDC will reduce the grant amount to maintain the required 1:1 matching ratio.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, non-profits with signed leases, commercial property owners, community groups, and non-profits without commercial leases in Baltimore City seeking to expand outdoor space usage and activate public areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of outdoor seating (cafe tables and chairs, benches), parklets, curbside facilities, shade structures (sails, pergolas, umbrellas), outdoor lighting (string lights, lighted trees), pots, planters, planter boxes, trellises, plants and landscaping (limited to 25% of total grant amount), and mobile vending structures. Architectural and design services are eligible (limited to 25% of total project cost).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City (citywide program). Eligible locations include: public right-of-way (sidewalk space immediately adjacent to a business, parking space(s) immediately adjacent to a business), outdoor seating areas/courtyards located on private property, and community spaces located on public or private property for use of the general public.
requirements_list: Work must not begin before receiving written grant approval
Applicant must meet with a BDC representative at the project site prior to submitting an application
Applicant must provide matching funds (1:1 ratio)
Applicant must pay for all project costs before receiving reimbursement
Project construction must be completed within 120 days of the award letter (or as otherwise approved in writing)
Applicant must be in good legal standing with federal, state, and local authorities and in Good Standing with the State of Maryland
For projects in the public right-of-way, a valid Curbside Commercial Permit and/or related Minor Privilege Permits are required
For community-led projects, a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signed by property owners is required

For community-led installations on private property, an MOU with the property owner is required; for installations in public right-of-way, an MOU with the Department of Transportation (DOT) is required
Applicants must obtain two quotes for work done by third-party contractors (except for retail items and architectural/design services)
For retail products (tables, chairs, planters, etc.), only one quote is required
Architectural or design services cannot exceed 25% of the total project cost and only require one estimate
The cost of plants and landscaping is limited to 25% of the total grant amount
The grant recipient must maintain the improvements for three years in good repair according to approved plans
Any plants that do not survive must be replaced by the applicant during the three-year maintenance period at the applicant's sole cost
Contractors must be properly registered, licensed, insured, and pass a debarment check as required by law
All contractors, sign fabricators, or construction tradespeople must hold proper construction licensure per their business or trade
Properties must be in compliance with applicable zoning laws and urban renewal plans, unless the project brings the property into compliance
Private property installations must be for use of the general public and not limited to members or tenants
Applicants cannot count self-performed work (time and labor) as an eligible or reimbursable expense
No furniture or outdoor space elements may be tied or secured to trees, lamp posts, street signs, or hydrants

Ineligible applicants include: residential properties, new construction (buildings erected within the last three years), properties actively listed for sale, properties that received an OSG in the prior 12-month period, and applicants who received an OSG but have not maintained improvements in good repair
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Request a grant application by filling out a form on the BDC website (https://www.baltimoredevelopment.com/doing-business/facade-improvement-grant). 2) Schedule and meet with a BDC representative at the project site prior to submitting an application. 3) Prepare required documents including: completed application with all fields and signatures, W-9 form, two photos of project location in current state, conceptual drawings/renderings/plans of proposed work, two contractor estimates for any professional services work, one estimate per retail item if applicable, proof of commercial occupancy (signed lease, letter of intent, or other documentation), and signed MOU if applicable. 4) Submit complete application package via email to info@BaltimoreDevelopment.com or by mail. 5) BDC reviews application (aesthetic considerations and discretionary review by internal committee; may require significant revisions). 6) Upon approval, receive written award letter with 120-day completion deadline. 7) Do not begin work until receiving written approval. 8) Complete project according to approved plans and all applicable codes and regulations. 9) Submit reimbursement request with: completed Reimbursement Request Form, at least 2 after photos showing entire completed scope and business signage, and copies of ALL payments to contractors and vendors (cashed checks, paid invoices, or itemized receipts). 10) BDC processes reimbursement and issues payment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Offers a tax credit against county property taxes for new or expanding businesses that meet specific employment, compensation, and capital investment criteria.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit against county property taxes imposed on real property. The amount of the credit shall not exceed 50 percent of the property tax due in any taxable year. If the business is engaged in electricity generation, the credit may be applied against county property tax on both personal property and real property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New or expanding businesses in Calvert County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credits for qualified businesses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County
requirements_list: Must be a new or expanding business
Must own the land, building, and personal property or be responsible for paying real property taxes on all or part of the land or building
Employ at least 25 new additional full-time employees in Board-identified target market sector industries
Provide individual compensation for new full-time positions greater than the annual average salary in Calvert County for similar or equivalent positions in the industry
Spend at least $2.5 million for land in Calvert County, improvements to land in Calvert County, or equipment to be located in Calvert County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses should contact the Department of Economic Development to discuss eligibility and apply for the tax credit program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A revolving loan fund that provides alternative funding for business expansion projects in Calvert County to increase the commercial tax base and create business and employment opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Revolving loans ranging from a minimum of $2,500 to a maximum of $150,000. Loans are designed to purchase fixed assets, equipment, inventory, and finance contracts for business expansion in Calvert County. Typical repayment terms range from 3 to 7 years depending on the use of funds and loan amount. Interest rates are competitive and based on current market conditions. The loan fund may not be used for debt refinancing, working capital, or operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses in manufacturing, wholesale trade, retail trade, and professional/scientific/technical services seeking expansion funding in Calvert County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of fixed assets, equipment, inventory, finance contracts, and business expansion. Loan fund may not be used for debt refinancing, working capital, or operational expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County, Maryland
requirements_list: Primary sales and activities in manufacturing, wholesale trade, retail trade, and/or professional, scientific, and technical services
Must be a legal entity qualified to do business in the State of Maryland
Minimum 2-year operating history with completed business plan
Selected business start-ups may be eligible with demonstrated capacity and business plan
Minimum loan request of $2,500
Maximum loan request of $150,000
Business must demonstrate ability to repay
Owner equity investment typically required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested businesses should contact Kathy MacAdams, Business Retention Specialist, to discuss their project and financing needs. Applicants will need to submit a completed business plan, financial statements, and loan application. The program provides assistance in preparing business plans. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted and reviewed on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides free native trees to property owners in Calvert County's Chesapeake Bay Critical Area who want to replant areas on their property. The program helps the County maintain 100% forest cover in the Critical Area by distributing trees funded through fees collected when onsite reforestation is not possible.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free native trees are provided to eligible property owners in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area. Only species listed on the Calvert County Native Plant List for the Critical Area Reforestation Program can be provided. Trees are distributed at no cost to property owners. Plant species availability varies year to year. Applicants receive native tree seedlings appropriate for Critical Area restoration.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications reviewed in January and June; rolling applications accepted throughout the year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners with land in Calvert County's Chesapeake Bay Critical Area who want to replant areas with trees and support forest conservation and environmental restoration
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reforestation and tree planting on eligible properties within the Critical Area to restore forest cover and improve water quality. Cannot be used to meet mitigation requirements for any project, permit, or violation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only available to property owners with land in Calvert County's Chesapeake Bay Critical Area. Properties must be located within the designated Critical Area boundaries as determined by Calvert County.
requirements_list: Property must be located in the Chesapeake Bay Critical Area
Applicant must complete the application package including property information form
Only native species on the Calvert County Native Plant List can be planted
Cannot be used to meet mitigation requirements for any project, permit, or violation
Applicant must own the property or have written permission from the property owner
Property must be suitable for tree planting and reforestation
Applicant must agree to maintain planted trees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the Critical Area Reforestation Application Package available from the Department of Planning & Zoning. 2. Submit the application package with required documentation including property information form and planting plan. 3. Applications are reviewed by the Critical Area Reforestation Evaluation (CARE) Committee at meetings held in January and June each year. 4. Applicants are notified of approval status following committee review. 5. Approved applicants receive native tree seedlings from the approved Calvert County Native Plant List. 6. Applicants are responsible for planting and maintaining the trees according to the approved planting plan.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Refund of property taxes paid for disabled veterans after they are deemed disabled by the Veterans Administration. The program provides a tax credit or refund for eligible disabled veterans who own property in Calvert County.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Refund of property taxes already paid
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County, Maryland
requirements_list: Veteran status verified by military service records
Deemed disabled by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA)
Own property subject to property taxes in Calvert County
Meet any income or other eligibility requirements as outlined in the ordinance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Veterans should first apply for a disability rating through the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. Once approved as disabled by the VA, veterans should contact the Calvert County Treasurer's Office with their VA disability rating documentation to apply for the property tax refund or credit. The Treasurer's Office will process the application and determine refund eligibility based on the veteran's disability status and property ownership.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five scholarships of $1,500 each are awarded annually, with one scholarship allocated to each of five geographic regions of Maryland: Area I (Western Maryland – Allegany, Garrett, Washington), Area II (National Capital – Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's), Area III (Central Maryland – Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Carroll, Harford, Howard), Area IV (Eastern Shore – Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester), and Area V (Southern Maryland – Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's).
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school seniors attending accredited Maryland high schools who have been accepted to a two- or four-year college or university and plan to major in emergency management or a closely related field, or students currently accepted or enrolled in two- or four-year colleges or universities pursuing degrees in emergency management or closely related fields.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education expenses for students pursuing associate or baccalaureate degrees in emergency management or closely related career fields.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students from all Maryland counties, distributed across five geographic regions: Area I (Allegany, Garrett, Washington), Area II (Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's), Area III (Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Carroll, Harford, Howard), Area IV (Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester), Area V (Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's).
requirements_list: Must be a high school senior attending an accredited Maryland high school who has been accepted to a two- or four-year college or university and plans to major in emergency management or a closely related field, OR be a student currently accepted or enrolled in a two- or four-year college or university pursuing a degree in emergency management or a closely related field
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications can be obtained from the MDEMA website at https://www.marylandema.org/scholarship.php. Completed applications must be submitted by the deadline. For additional application details and instructions, visit the MDEMA website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that cover up to 75% of project costs to help property owners reduce risk from natural hazards such as flooding and cliff erosion. The program funds projects like voluntary property acquisition and demolition, or elevation of structures above flood levels.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants cover up to 75% of eligible project costs. The property owner is responsible for the remaining 25% of costs and any cost overruns. Eligible projects include: (1) Acquisition and Demolition - purchase of high-hazard properties followed by demolition of structures; (2) Elevation - raising structures in flood plains above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE). For acquisition and demolition projects, required documentation includes property appraisal, plat survey, color photos, itemized demolition cost estimate, and for flood projects NFIP insurance copy and documentation of past flood events; for cliff projects a certified imminent threat letter from engineer. For elevation projects, required documentation includes plat survey, color photos, NFIP insurance policy documentation, documentation of past flood events, elevation certificate, certified structural stability letter from engineer, and itemized elevation cost estimate. The program timeline takes approximately two years from application to funding award: pre-screening questionnaire submitted by July 1, applications submitted by August 31, subapplications prepared in November, final versions submitted to FEMA in late January, funding decisions received in late summer, and funds allocated to begin projects in mid-spring.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process occurs on an annual cycle: (1) Applications are accepted from September through December; (2) Applications are reviewed and ranked by the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board from December through January; (3) Offer letters are sent to approved applicants based on ranking and available funding; (4) Transactions are completed by June. structured_extraction.program_name: Transferable Development Rights (TDR) Program and Reserve
structured_extraction.program_description: A Calvert County program that allows landowners in Agricultural Preservation Districts to sell the development potential of their property, either through private transactions or through the county-administered TDR Reserve. The sale requires recording restrictive covenants in land records, permanently restricting the property's development rights. Purchasers of TDRs can use them to achieve higher lot density on designated receiving area properties. The county operates a revolving Reserve Fund, purchasing TDRs from Agricultural Preservation District owners and reselling them to developers at set prices, providing a market mechanism for both sellers and buyers. The program aims to preserve farms and forest lands by redirecting development to targeted growth areas.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners in Agricultural Preservation Districts (APDs) can sell development rights through private negotiations or the county-administered TDR Reserve. Through private transactions, buyers and sellers negotiate terms directly. Through the TDR Reserve, the county purchases TDRs at $6,230 per TDR (plus 1% administrative fee) and resells them to developers at the same price paid by the county plus the 1% fee, on a first-come, first-served basis subject to funding availability. The TDR becomes a separate property right that can be sold independently from the land. Purchasers use TDRs to increase density potential on designated receiving area properties within Calvert County. Sellers in APDs receive compensation for permanently restricting development on their agricultural or forest land through recording of restrictive covenants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; applications accepted on ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Agricultural Preservation Districts who want to sell development rights (through private transactions or the county Reserve), and developers or individuals seeking to purchase TDRs to increase density on designated receiving area properties within Calvert County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: TDRs can be used by purchasers to increase lot density on designated receiving area properties within Calvert County. Sellers receive compensation for permanently restricting development on their agricultural or forest land through recordation of restrictive covenants limiting future development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Calvert County only; sending areas are Agricultural Preservation Districts (APDs), receiving areas are designated residential growth zones within the county.
requirements_list: Property must be located in an Agricultural Preservation District (APD) to sell TDRs
TDR certification applications require approval from the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board (APAB) and the Board of County Commissioners (BOCC)
Receiving area properties must be located in designated receiving areas within Calvert County
Applicant selling through the Reserve must be owner of record of TDRs
TDRs sold through the Reserve must have been conveyed from an original Agricultural Preservation District or be owned by record owner of such conveyed TDRs
Development rights must be permanently restricted through recordation of restrictive covenants in land records
TDR Reserve transactions processed on first-come, first-served basis subject to available funding and TDR supply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For TDR Certification: Landowners in APDs complete Application for TDR Certification form and submit to county. County staff calculates TDRs based on acreage and existing development potential. Application proceeds to Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board (APAB) for review and recommendation to Board of County Commissioners (BOCC). Once BOCC approves certification, the TDR certification is recorded in Land Records. For Private Sales: Once certified, buyers and sellers can negotiate private transactions independently. Restrictive covenants must be recorded. For TDR Reserve Program: Sellers submit Application to Sell TDRs to Reserve; Buyers submit separate Application to Purchase TDRs from Reserve. County processes transactions on first-come, first-served basis as funding and TDR supply allow. Both parties must complete required applications and forms.

structured_extraction.program_name: Caroline County Small Business Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A revolving loan fund administered by Caroline County that helps small businesses start up or expand by providing financing to fill gaps that traditional lenders cannot cover. The program provides direct loans, typically used for equipment purchases, inventory purchases, processing and packaging equipment, and working capital. Loans have a maximum of $20,000, though most loans are for less than $10,000. Funds must be repaid according to agreed-upon terms and cannot be used to finance existing debt, reimburse owners or equity partners, buy out partners, or pay delinquent taxes. The County Commissioners of Caroline County make final approval decisions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct loans with a maximum amount of $20,000, though exceptions may be made for large projects that create substantial new jobs. The interest rate is typically prime rate plus 1% but is at the discretion of the CCED Loan Committee based on risk level. Loan terms are 5 to 7 years based on risk level. Loans with monthly payments under $100 are set as quarterly payments; loans with monthly payments over $100 give borrowers the option of monthly or quarterly payments. Quarterly payments are due on January 1, April 1, July 1, and October 1. Late charges of 5% of the regular quarterly payment are assessed on the 16th day if payment is not made within 15 days of the due date. The program fills financing gaps after traditional financing has been arranged. Funds are disbursed only after all loan documents are signed by all parties. Loan repayment is required regardless of business performance or if the business relocates outside Caroline County. Funds cannot be used to finance existing debt, reimburse owners or equity partners, buy out partners, or pay delinquent federal, state, or local taxes. Allowable uses include commercial real estate acquisition, new construction, building improvements, inventory purchase, machinery or equipment purchase, business start-up costs, and no more than 12 months of operating capital.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners and entrepreneurs in Caroline County looking to start up or expand their operations, including agricultural businesses, manufacturers, retailers, and other industries. Eligible entities include existing businesses and start-ups.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commercial real estate acquisition, new construction, building improvements, inventory purchase, machinery or equipment purchase, business start-up costs, and no more than 12 months of operating capital. Funds cannot be used to finance existing debt, reimburse owners or equity partners, buy out partners, pay delinquent federal, state, or local taxes, for non-owner occupied real estate investment, or for personal expenses of business owners or employees.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application with a $50 application fee online or by mail to Caroline County Economic Development, 425 Colonial Drive, Denton, MD 21629. Include all required attachments: personal financial statements for each owner, credit reports, income tax returns for preceding two years, balance sheet and profit/loss statements for preceding two years, complete business plan, and three-year financial projections. Applications may be brought before the Caroline County Economic Development Advisory Board, which makes recommendations to the County Commissioners of Caroline County. structured_extraction.program_description: A free 8-week business training and education program designed to help small business owners increase revenue and sales, manage and hire employees, create sustainable business models, manage expenses, and prepare to access capital. Delivered by Will Holmes Consulting, the program empowers local entrepreneurs with tools, resources, and support to grow and manage their businesses. The curriculum covers organizational infrastructure, leadership, marketing and sales strategies, accounting, human resources, legal structure, taxes, insurance, and access to capital, with emphasis on mentorship and real-world applications. Graduates receive a Certificate of Completion.

Participants receive one-on-one mentoring sessions and must complete weekly assignments and a final 15-minute PowerPoint presentation to graduate. Graduates receive a Certificate of Completion. structured_extraction.program_description: A local tax credit program administered by the Caroline County Commissioners to encourage manufacturing businesses to locate, expand, or construct new facilities in Caroline County. Eligible companies that make a minimum capital investment of $50,000 and create at least 15 new full-time jobs receive a real property tax credit based on the increased assessable value of their facility expansion or new construction.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A real property tax credit equal to 100% of the real property tax attributable to the increased assessable value resulting from facility expansion or new construction. The credit may be claimed for five consecutive years, with the five-year eligibility period effective upon placement of the expanded or newly constructed property on the Caroline County tax roll and upon verification that requirements have been met. Taxes already paid shall not be refunded, and under no circumstances shall tax credits be extended or renewed beyond five years for the same expansion or new construction. The business must recertify its eligibility each year between May 1 and October 1. The tax credit applies only to Caroline County real property taxes, not municipal or state taxes. Minimum qualifying investment is $50,000 (assessed value of expansion or new construction must be greater than $50,000) and minimum new jobs required is 15 full-time positions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; application must be filed within one year of the expanded or newly constructed facility's placement on the Caroline County tax roll prepared by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Manufacturing, fabricating, and assembling companies expanding or constructing new facilities in Caroline County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Facility expansion or new construction by manufacturing, fabricating, and assembling companies; the tax credit applies to the increased property value resulting from new construction or facility expansion
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Caroline County, Maryland. The tax credit applies only to Caroline County real property taxes, not municipal or state taxes. Property must be placed on the Caroline County tax roll prepared by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.
requirements_list: Manufacturing, fabricating, or assembling industry
Minimum $50,000 capital investment (assessed value of expansion or new construction must be greater than $50,000)
Must create at least 15 additional full-time positions and hire at least 15 additional full-time employees at the facility location
Relocated employees cannot be counted as additional employees if relocating from another Caroline County location
The 15 additional employees must each receive at least the current federal mandatory minimum wage, substantiated by annual aggregate payroll
Employer must have in place a basic employee benefit plan including medical insurance, provision for leave, and pension for all full-time employees
The business must annually certify in writing between May 1 and October 1 that requirements continue to be met; credit will immediately cease if certification is not received
Applicants must not be in default on payment of any Caroline County taxes or tax penalties, or State of Maryland taxes or tax penalties of which Caroline County receives a portion
Application must be filed within one year of placement of the expanded or newly constructed facility on the Caroline County tax roll
All applications must be on a form supplied by the County Commissioners
Information furnished on the application must be given under oath
For leased property, application must be executed by both lessor and lessee with proof that lessee is liable for Caroline County real property taxes
Copy of Caroline County real property tax bill reflecting the expansion or new addition must be attached to application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download the Application for Five Year Manufacturer's Tax Credit Program form from the Caroline County Commissioners. 2. Complete all sections of the application under oath, including general information, description of the facility prior to and after expansion/new construction, tax information, and employee benefit information. 3. Attach a copy of the Caroline County real property tax bill reflecting the expansion or new addition. If the property is leased, also attach a copy of the lease or other proof that the lessee is liable for real property taxes. 4. Have the application notarized. 5. Mail the completed application packet to: County Commissioners of Caroline County, Attn: Sara Visintainer, Courthouse, 109 Market St., Room 123, Denton, MD 21629. 6. The application must be filed within one year of placement of the expanded or newly constructed facility on the Caroline County tax roll. 7. The County Commissioners will expeditiously approve or deny the filed application. Approval constitutes granting of the credit. 8. Once approved, the tax credit recipient must annually certify between May 1 and October 1 each year that requirements continue to be met. Contact the Caroline County Commissioners for additional assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by Carroll County that provides matching reimbursement to internet service providers (ISPs) and qualified business enterprises—including home-based and residentially-based businesses—to support the expansion of broadband infrastructure in unserved and underserved areas of Carroll County. The program helps businesses and ISPs gain access to high-speed internet by making last-mile fiber optic connections to serve commercial and industrial users. Carroll County also leases available fiber to ISPs or businesses directly through the Fiber Network Enterprise Fund. The program earmarks $200,000 in grant funding and covers costs related to construction, acquisition, or leasing of facilities, wireless spectrum, land, towers, or buildings used to deploy broadband service.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 50% matching reimbursement of qualified project expenses with a cap of $25,000 per approved project. A cap of $100,000 per entity or service provider is fixed per fiscal year, dependent on allocations approved by the Carroll County Board of Commissioners. The program earmarks $200,000 in total grant funding. Reimbursement requires submission of invoices from vendors referencing the project, copies of checks paid to vendors with check number, date and amount, and all supporting documentation. Projects must be paid no later than 30 days after the project period ends. Carroll County also leases available fiber to ISPs or businesses directly through the Fiber Network Enterprise Fund.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Internet Service Providers in good business standing that plan to provide service in unserved or underserved areas in Carroll County, and Carroll County-based business entities (including home-based and residentially-based businesses) with unmet broadband needs or requiring internet service redundancy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The construction, acquisition, or leasing of facilities or spectrum, land, towers, or buildings used to deploy broadband service for businesses and residentially-based businesses located within Carroll County, including last-mile fiber optic connections to provide high-speed internet access to commercial and industrial users. Eligible capital investments include equipment, construction, and infrastructure to expand broadband service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Unserved or underserved areas of Carroll County, Maryland. Unserved areas lack a fixed internet connection with speeds of 25 Mbps download/3 Mbps upload. Underserved areas lack a fixed internet connection with speeds of 100 Mbps download/20 Mbps upload from two or more providers.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an Internet Service Provider or Carroll County-based business entity in good business standing with federal, state, and local government authorities
For ISPs: must have legal authority to provide, construct, operate, and maintain proposed facilities or services
For qualified business enterprises: must have unmet broadband needs in an underserved or unserved area or require internet service redundancy for business continuity
Project must be located in an unserved or underserved area of Carroll County
Applicant must demonstrate documented business need in an underserved or unserved area of Carroll County
Located within Carroll County, Maryland
Qualified broadband infrastructure project
Broadband service must meet minimum standards of 25 Mbps downstream and 3 Mbps upstream with latency of 100ms or less
Applicant must provide required documentation at time of reimbursement including vendor invoices referencing the project, copies of checks paid to vendors, and all supporting documentation
Project costs must be paid no later than 30 days after the project period ends
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Jay Uebel, Broadband Project Manager, at juebel@carrollcountymd.gov or 410-386-2309 to apply. Applicants must complete the Carroll Broadband Grant Application form and submit a separate Project Detail form for each project, including project scope, cost information, proposed vendors, project timeline, and documentation of unserved/underserved area status. Applicants should provide company description, business type, years in operation, number of full-time employees, products/services, and expected project outcomes including distance wired or aerial distance covered and number of users served. Each application will be reviewed by a Carroll Broadband Enterprise committee consisting of county personnel. Applicants will be notified in writing of approval or denial within two weeks of receipt. If approved, the applicant and county will execute a Carroll Broadband Grant Agreement outlining the terms. Interested parties may also visit the Carroll Broadband website or contact the Carroll County Department of Economic Development or the Carroll County Chief Information Officer for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Carroll County Home Stretch – Difficult to Serve Properties Grant (Long Driveway Hard to Connect Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Carroll County has applied for the FY24 Home Stretch - Difficult to Serve Properties Grant from the state to assist homeowners whose driveways are too long for broadband providers to connect for free as part of standard installation. The grant provides up to $14,000 per eligible property to cover broadband connection costs. To qualify, a broadband provider must already pass the home with its service network. Costs exceeding $14,000 are the responsibility of the homeowner. The grant does not cover equipment or services and is not retroactive.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $14,000 per eligible property to cover broadband connection infrastructure costs for homes with long driveways that exceed standard provider connection distances. Costs exceeding $14,000 are the responsibility of the homeowner. The grant does not cover equipment or services and is not retroactive (cannot be used for reimbursement of costs already paid). Only one grant is available per house or address.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program is no longer accepting applications; grant award notification was expected in late spring 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Carroll County homeowners with long driveways who have a broadband provider service passing their property but cannot receive a free connection during standard installation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Broadband connection infrastructure costs for properties with driveways longer than standard provider connection distances. Does not cover equipment or services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Carroll County, Maryland. Properties must have existing broadband, internet, or cable TV infrastructure already passing by their homes. Homes located in areas scheduled for future broadband installation are not eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner in Carroll County
Must have a broadband provider currently passing the property with service (existing broadband, internet, or cable TV infrastructure must already pass the property)
Driveway must be longer than the distance the provider will connect for free during standard installation
Homes located in areas scheduled for future broadband installation are not eligible
Only one grant is available per house or address
Grants are not retroactive and cannot be used for reimbursement of costs already paid
The grant does not cover equipment or services
Maximum grant amount is $14,000; homeowner must cover any costs exceeding this amount
Must complete the Carroll County Broadband Survey and answer yes to the long driveway question, providing name, full address, phone number, and email
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested homeowners must complete the Carroll County Broadband Survey and indicate yes to the long driveway question, providing name, full address, phone number, and email address. After an application is received, the county verifies the address for eligibility with the service provider and applicants receive an email regarding their eligibility status. If the grant is awarded to Carroll County, all residents who answered yes to the long driveway question will be notified by email with further instructions. A press release will also be published. For eligibility questions, contact the Broadband Office.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing financial assistance to restaurants, breweries, distilleries, wineries, food trucks, food service organizations with commercial kitchens, and other eligible food and beverage businesses established in Carroll County. The program supports working capital expenses including rent, mortgage, utilities, and COVID-19 related costs, helping businesses recover from pandemic-related revenue losses.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants awarded based on verified full-time equivalent (FTE) employment, where FTE employees are counted as working 30 or more hours per week: businesses with 9 or fewer FTE employees receive $5,000; businesses with 10 to 50 FTE employees receive $10,000. Grant monies must be disbursed to recipients by December 31, 2020. Eligible working capital expenses include rent or mortgage, utility bills, information technology hardware and software, marketing, employee training, commercial cleaning, professional services, equipment and vehicle business expenses, and COVID-19 related expenses. Payroll expenses are not eligible. A grant agreement must be executed with the grantee before funds are disbursed. Previous Carroll Rebound restaurant grantees are eligible for this additional grant.

structured_extraction.program_name: Carroll County Small Business COVID-19 Emergency Relief Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A county-funded grant program that provided one-time emergency working capital assistance to small businesses in Carroll County that experienced disrupted operations due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The fund includes multiple rounds of funding, including a contribution from Baltimore Gas & Electric, providing grants to eligible small businesses to help them address the financial impact of COVID-19.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grants provided to eligible small businesses in two rounds. The initial round provided $1,250 per eligible business with $500,000 in total funding. The subsequent round funded by Baltimore Gas & Electric provided $1,000 grants with 45 grant awards available from a $45,500 contribution. Funding can be used for working capital including payroll, rent, mortgage payments, utility expenses, or other similar ordinary business expenses. Grant checks are mailed to approved recipients pending funding availability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Initial round: Applications accepted on a first-come, first-served basis starting April 7, 2020 at 5:00 PM; BGE-funded round: Applications considered on a first-come, first-served basis starting June 4, 2020 at 1:00 p.m.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital to support payroll, rent, mortgage payments, utility expenses, or other similar expenses that occur in the ordinary course of business operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have a Carroll County location, be registered in Maryland, and be in good standing with the State of Maryland and Carroll County.
