structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses applied online through the application portal at https://carrollbiz.org. The initial round portal opened on April 7, 2020 at 5:00 PM; the BGE-funded round portal opened on June 4, 2020 at 1:00 PM. Applications were reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis. Applicants must verify business status and provide required documentation including Federal EIN, Maryland Department of Assessment and Taxation ID number in good standing, number of full-time employees prior to March 5, 2020, business mailing address, business description, and purpose of request. Once verified and approved, pending funding availability, the applicant receives the grant check by mail. Businesses that received a grant in the initial round were not eligible for the BGE-funded round.

structured_extraction.program_name: Carroll County Small Business COVID-19 Emergency Relief Grant Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Emergency grant fund providing working capital to Carroll County small businesses, sole proprietors, and home-based businesses that experienced disrupted operations due to COVID-19. The program operated across three phases, distributing a total of $843,000 ($500,000 in phase 1, $250,000 in phase 2, and $93,000 in phase 3), supporting approximately 674 businesses. Grants were intended to complement actions taken with banks, business interruption insurance, and federal and state partners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant of $1,250 per approved business to support working capital. The program distributed a total of $843,000 across three phases ($500,000 phase 1, $250,000 phase 2, $93,000 phase 3), assisting approximately 674 small businesses, sole proprietors, and home-based businesses affected by COVID-19 disruptions. Phase 3 portal opened April 29, 2020 at 5:00 PM. Funds can be used for payroll, rent, mortgage payments, utility expenses, or other ordinary business operating expenses. Recipients must be in good standing with the State of Maryland and Carroll County. Ineligible uses include non-profits and medical service providers. Once verified and approved, grant checks are mailed to applicants pending funding availability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications considered on first-come, first-served basis; Phase 2 portal opened April 20, 2020 at 5:00 PM; Phase 3 portal opened April 29, 2020 at 5:00 PM
structured_extraction.contact_name: John T. Lyburn, Director of Economic Development

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps employers and apprenticeship sponsors offset the cost of training Registered Apprentices by providing up to $3,000 per newly registered adult apprentice or up to $7,500 per newly registered high school level apprentice.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $3,000 for each newly registered adult apprentice or up to $7,500 for each newly registered high school level apprentice to offset eligible training expenses. Funds may be used for: (1) related instruction costs including tuition, fees, books, and materials; (2) mentorship and on-the-job learning expenses; (3) apprentice recruitment expenses associated with the individual apprentice being hired; (4) costs associated with disability accommodations including adaptive equipment and services; and (5) supportive services such as transportation assistance, driver's licensing, uniforms, tools, child/dependent care, and union initiation fees. Expenses must be associated with Registered Apprenticeship program activities, connected to the specific apprentice, documented with records and receipts, and not covered by another funding source. An employer or sponsor may be awarded only one grant per each newly Registered Apprentice per year. Sponsors/employers are limited to awards for 10 Registered Apprentices per employer per calendar year (unlimited for high school level apprentices). Funds may not be used on prevailing wage projects (Davis-Bacon, Maryland Stadium Authority, local prevailing wage projects), except for high school level apprentices.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 30 days of an apprentice's initial registration with the MD Labor Office of Apprenticeship (one-time exception available for certain employers who hired apprentices between July 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026, allowing retroactive applications for apprentices registered since July 1, 2025)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Tayaabah Qazi, Grant Program Manager, Office of Strategic Initiatives
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland Registered Apprenticeship sponsors and employers in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Instructional expenses including tuition, fees, books, and materials; mentorship and on-the-job learning expenses; apprentice recruitment expenses associated with the individual apprentice being hired; costs associated with disability accommodations; supportive services for apprentices including transportation assistance, driver's licensing, uniforms, tools, child or dependent care, and union initiation fees
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Applicants must be Registered Apprenticeship Sponsors or employers approved by Maryland Department of Labor
Applicants must be in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)

Applications must be submitted within 30 days of an apprentice's initial registration with the MD Labor Office of Apprenticeship (or retroactively during fiscal year 2026 exception for apprentices registered since July 1, 2025)
Apprentices must be newly registered (not previously registered as an apprentice with the sponsor or employer)
Apprentices must be within their first year of employment as a Registered Apprentice
Apprentices must remain employed and registered for at least seven months following application submission to receive reimbursement

Employer or sponsor must attest to intent to retain the apprentice through the duration of the full Registered Apprenticeship and after completion unless the apprentice leaves on their own accord or is dismissed for cause
Limited to one grant per apprentice per employer per year
Limited to 10 adult Registered Apprentices per employer per calendar year (high school level apprentices exempt from this limitation)
Cannot apply for apprentices working on prevailing wage projects (Davis-Bacon, Maryland Stadium Authority, or local prevailing wage projects), except for high school level apprentices
Costs may not be covered by another funding source (no duplicate funding); if same costs are claimed through multiple programs, funds must be repaid
If one employer/sponsor has already been awarded funds for a specific newly Registered Apprentice, another employer/sponsor cannot apply for incentives for that same apprentice
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This is a rolling application program. Sponsors or employers must submit the Maryland Apprenticeship Incentive Program application (Excel form) electronically to marylandapprenticeship.incentiveprogram@maryland.gov within 30 days of the apprentice's initial registration with MD Labor (MD Labor encourages submission 30 days prior to registration but will accept applications up to 30 days after registration). Applications must be complete and accurate at time of submission. MD Labor will review and notify applicants of approval or denial within 14 calendar days. If approved, the sponsor or employer must invoice MD Labor once the apprentice completes at least seven months of employment as a Registered Apprentice. Applications are processed in the order received and awarded based on availability of funds. Applicants with denied applications may request reconsideration by emailing marylandapprenticeship.incentiveprogram@maryland.gov within 14 calendar days of denial, stating grounds for request and reasons for reconsideration. The DWDAL Assistant Secretary (or designee) will provide a written response within 30 calendar days, and their decision is final.

structured_extraction.program_description: A paid summer work experience program administered by Carroll County Government that connects local youth ages 16-18 with local businesses for six-week summer employment positions during July and August. The program targets youth who have never worked or face barriers to employment, pairing them with businesses in sectors such as recreation, retail, childcare, restaurants, offices, farms, and technology. Carroll County Government hires youth participants, handles all payroll, taxes, and insurance at no cost to employers, and provides enrichment days to develop professional and soft skills — including business panels, CareerScope Assessments, job fairs, mock interviews, and classroom instruction on essential workplace skills. Businesses receive no-cost workers, mentorship opportunities, and a pipeline for potential long-term hires. Funding sources include American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds (62% Federal, 29.54% State, 8.46% Local), with Federal funding for Program Year 2024 totaling $2,139,118.98.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Carroll County Government pays all wages (youth participants earn up to $12.50 per hour, previously $11.75/hour), taxes, and insurance for youth participants through dedicated grant funding, eliminating all financial risk for participating businesses. Youth receive six weeks of paid work experience (approximately July through mid-August) plus five enrichment days covering professional and soft skills development, including business panels, CareerScope Assessments, job fairs, and mock interviews. Businesses receive no-cost seasonal workers and mentorship opportunities. Federal Program Year 2024 funding totaled $2,139,118.98 (62% Federal ARPA, 29.54% State, 8.46% Local).
structured_extraction.contact_name: Heather Powell, Manager; Eileen Vozzella, Youth Program Coordinator; Tammy Haines, Employment Services Supervisor

Also covers enrichment and job readiness training days.

Positions can be in recreation, retail, childcare, restaurants, offices, farms, technology, or other sectors

Carroll County handles all hiring paperwork and logistics. Visit carrollworks.com/youth/ for details.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Farm Service Agency Emergency Loans for Natural Disaster Recovery
structured_extraction.program_description: Emergency credit extended by the USDA Farm Service Agency to producers recovering from natural disasters, including drought. Loans can be used to replace essential equipment or livestock, reorganize a farming operation, or refinance certain debts caused by disaster-related crop losses. Multiple FSA disaster assistance programs are also available to eligible producers in designated counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency loans available through the USDA Farm Service Agency to meet recovery needs including replacement of essential items such as equipment or livestock, reorganization of a farming operation, or refinancing of certain debts. Multiple FSA disaster assistance programs are eligible, including the Livestock Forage Disaster Program, Emergency Assistance for Livestock Program, Livestock Indemnity Program, Honeybees and Farm Raised Fish Program, Noninsured Crop Disaster Assistance, Emergency Conservation Program, and Tree Assistance Program. FSA reviews loans based on the extent of losses, security available, and repayment ability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers in Carroll County and contiguous counties, as well as farmers in central and western Maryland counties (Allegany, Frederick, Garrett, Howard, Montgomery, Washington), impacted by severe drought conditions and crop losses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of essential equipment or livestock, reorganization of a farming operation, or refinancing of certain debts related to disaster-caused crop losses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primary county: Carroll, Maryland. Contiguous counties also eligible: Baltimore County and Frederick (Maryland), Adams and York (Pennsylvania). Additional eligible counties include Allegany, Garrett, Howard, Montgomery, and Washington counties in Maryland. Allegany, Washington, and Garrett counties were among the hardest hit by drought conditions.
requirements_list: Farmers must be located in designated drought-affected counties
Crops must be experiencing drought conditions
Suffered drought intensity of D2 Drought-Severe for 8 or more consecutive weeks, or D3 Drought-Extreme, or D4 Drought-Exceptional during the growing season
Demonstrated losses from the qualifying drought event
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File a Notice of Loss and contact your local USDA Service Center to ask questions about available programs and apply for assistance. Farmers may also reach out to their local county Farm Service Agency office. A list of service centers and locations is available at offices.usda.gov or through the Farm Service Agency's disaster assistance tools at farmers.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit incentive program that provides a credit against Carroll County property tax for businesses that create new jobs. The credit applies to county property tax on real property owned by a business entity and is based on increased employment. To qualify, a business must construct or expand by at least 5,000 square feet and employ at least 25 new full-time workers within the first 24 months. The credit amount decreases over a six-year period.
structured_extraction.agency: Carroll County Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit against Carroll County property tax imposed on real property owned by a business entity. The credit is based on increased employment and decreases over six years: 52% of the increased property tax in years one and two, 39% in years three and four, and 26% in years five and six. To qualify, a business must construct or expand by at least 5,000 square feet and employ at least 25 new full-time positions within the first 24 months. New positions must be new to the state of Maryland and pay at least 125% of the Average Weekly Wage per worker as determined by the Maryland Department of Labor.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses that are constructing or expanding facilities in Carroll County and creating new full-time employment positions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit against Carroll County property tax on real property for job creation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Carroll County, Maryland. The business must be located in a designated Priority Funding Area within Carroll County.
requirements_list: Must construct or expand by at least 5,000 square feet
Must employ at least 25 new full-time positions within the first 24 months
New positions must be new to the state of Maryland
At least 50% of the new positions must pay 125% or more of the county's average weekly wage
Positions must pay at least 125% of the Average Weekly Wage per worker
Must create new full-time positions
The business must not have moved its operations from another Maryland county or Baltimore City
The business must not owe any delinquent taxes to Carroll County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A business must declare its intent to apply for the tax credit on a form provided by the County Comptroller. Once the business meets all eligibility requirements, it can apply for certification. An online application form is available at https://carrollcountymd.jotform.com/251755816401052. For more information, contact Paige Sunderland, Deputy Director / Business Development at psunderland@carrollbiz.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program designed to promote redevelopment and revitalization of commercial and industrial properties in the Finksburg MD 140 corridor. The program encourages property owners to visually enhance their properties through exterior and site improvements along the Maryland Route 140 corridor.
structured_extraction.agency: Carroll County Department of Economic Development, Department of Management and Budget, and Department of the Comptroller
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a property tax credit for up to five years. For existing buildings, the credit is 75% if improvement costs are more than 25% of the assessed property value, or 50% if costs are 25% or less. For new construction, the credit is 50% if improvement costs for the building's exterior exceed 50% of the property's assessed value. The total credit cannot exceed the total cost of improvements. Tax credits are based on the percentage of improvement cost compared to the current assessed value of the property.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: on or before May 1 immediately before the first taxable year for which the tax credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial or industrial properties in the Finksburg MD 140 corridor seeking to improve the visual appearance of their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior façade improvements including new windows, paint, or a new roof; landscaping; signage; lighting; sidewalks; pedestrian plazas; and other physical exterior site improvements that significantly improve the overall appearance of the property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties zoned for commercial or industrial use (C-1, C-2, C-3, I-1, or I-2) and located on or adjacent to the MD 140 corridor in the Finksburg area, from the Baltimore County/Carroll County line to Sandymount Road, fronting MD 140 or directly adjacent to a property that does.
requirements_list: Property must be used for business, commercial, or industrial purposes.
Property must be located within a C-1, C-2, C-3, I-1, or I-2 commercial or industrial zone.
Property must be located on or adjacent to MD 140 corridor from the Carroll County/Baltimore County line to Sandymount Road.
Improvements must significantly improve the overall appearance of the property.
Qualified improvements include exterior façade, landscaping, or other physical exterior site improvements such as signage, lighting, sidewalks and pedestrian plazas.
You must apply before starting the improvement project.
Application must be submitted on or before May 1 immediately before the first taxable year for which the tax credit is sought.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, obtain the application form from the Department of the Comptroller. Complete and sign the application, including a tax map, property photos, a detailed description of the planned improvements with drawings, and a summary of costs. Submit the complete application before beginning any work and by the May 1 deadline. Contact Paige Sunderland, Deputy Director / Business Development, for additional application details.

Income tax credits provide a one-time $1,000 credit per new worker, or $6,000 per economically disadvantaged employee over three years. Credits are available for job creation and business investments in designated enterprise zones.

structured_extraction.program_name: Opioid Restitution Fund (ORF) Community Grant Program (FY2027)
structured_extraction.program_description: An annual competitive grant program administered by Cecil County that distributes settlement funds received from opioid manufacturers and distributors to nonprofit, not-for-profit, and government agencies. Funds support projects addressing substance use prevention, overdose response, treatment, and recovery support services in alignment with State of Maryland legislative provisions. The program makes available approximately $1 million per fiscal year cycle, with individual grants of up to $100,000 per application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grant funding distributed through a competitive application process each spring for the following fiscal year. Grants of up to $100,000 per application are available, with a total funding pool of approximately $1 million. Funds are generated from settlements reached with certain manufacturers and distributors of prescription opioid pharmaceutical products and must meet legislative provisions prescribed by the State of Maryland. Organizations may submit no more than two applications, each addressing a different legislative provision. Eligible use of funds includes evidence-based or evidence-informed programs and projects that address: (1) Substance use prevention/education; (2) Overdose response including naloxone/Narcan distribution and training; (3) Medication-assisted treatment (MAT); (4) Recovery support services; and (5) Other opioid-related activities aligned with State legislative provisions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit, not-for-profit, and government agencies (state, county, and municipal) located within or serving Cecil County citizens.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects meeting State of Maryland legislative provisions to address substance use prevention, overdose response, treatment, and recovery support services. Eligible activities include evidence-based or evidence-informed programs and projects addressing substance use prevention/education, overdose response including naloxone distribution and training, medication-assisted treatment, recovery support services, and other opioid-related activities as specified in State legislative provisions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Agencies must be located within or serve Cecil County citizens.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit, not-for-profit, or government agency
Applicant must be located within or serve Cecil County citizens
Project must meet State of Maryland legislative provisions for opioid-related funding
Project must address one or more of: substance use prevention, overdose response, treatment, or recovery support services
Organizations may submit no more than two applications
Each application must address a different legislative provision
Project must be evidence-based or evidence-informed where applicable
Applicant must complete the FY27 ORF Application form and FY27 ORF Budget Template
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete and submit the FY27 ORF Application form and FY27 ORF Budget Template by May 1, 2026. The Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) explains the full process and required steps. Instructions and forms are available at https://www.cecilcountymd.gov/846/Local-Community-Grants. Applications are reviewed during the competitive process, and awards are determined based on alignment with legislative provisions, project impact, organizational capacity, and budget justification.

structured_extraction.program_description: A local Cecil County program established in 2005 to help preserve agricultural lands within Cecil County and supplement existing Federal, State, and local preservation programs by purchasing development rights from willing landowners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases development rights from qualifying agricultural lands, permanently restricting development and preserving the land for agricultural use. Payments are made to landowners who voluntarily sell their development rights, resulting in a permanent conservation easement on the property.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and retirement of development rights on agricultural properties; permanent preservation of farmland through conservation easements

Applications are reviewed by the County and the local Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board. The Board evaluates applications based on program criteria, funding availability, and property eligibility. Selected applicants proceed to appraisal and negotiation of the easement agreement.

The program supports revitalization projects and blight removal to enhance the visual appearance of the Route 40 corridor, increase community utilization of businesses, and drive economic development in the area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $25,000 for revitalization projects and up to $50,000 for blight removal projects. Applicants must match the grant funds dollar-for-dollar for revitalization projects (e.g., a $25,000 grant requires $25,000 in matching funds for a total project cost of $50,000). Blight removal projects may be awarded up to $50,000 with no matching funds required. Disbursement is made on a reimbursement basis after project completion and submission of invoices and proof of expenditures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit businesses and organizations located along Route 40 in Cecil County with a Route 40/Pulaski Highway address.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior improvements to business or organization properties that are visible from Route 40, including signage, lighting, siding, painting, entrance improvements, porch/deck, fencing, landscaping, hardscaping, sidewalks, driveways, parking areas, ADA ramps, and demolition or removal of blighted structures. Up to 20% of grant funds may be used for related, specified interior improvements with prior approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located along Route 40 in Cecil County with a Route 40/Pulaski Highway address. Improvements must be Route 40-front facing or easily visible from Route 40.

Property must be visible from Route 40
Applicant must be in good standing with the IRS, State of Maryland, and Cecil County
Applicant may be either the property owner or tenant; tenants must provide written authorization from the property owner

Documentation of matching funds required
Current property photos from Route 40 and close-up views of project area required
Non-profits must provide IRS exemption determination letter
Located on or serving Route 40 business corridor

Complete applications and all required supporting documents must be submitted with a cover sheet. Documents can be uploaded online, emailed to the Grant Administrator, mailed to the Cecil County Administration Building, or dropped off in person. The Grant Review Committee evaluates applications on a rolling basis and makes ongoing awards until funds are expended. Applicants are notified by email of the committee's decision.

structured_extraction.program_description: An incentive-based program adopted January 1, 2007 designed to preserve natural resources and agricultural lands by allowing development rights to be transferred from sending areas (agricultural zones) to receiving areas around towns, facilitating orderly growth in the County.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An incentive-based program allowing landowners in designated sending areas (NAR and SAR zones) to transfer development rights to designated receiving areas (SR and DR zones) around towns. Sending areas must be zoned NAR (Non-Agricultural Residential) or SAR (Suburban Agricultural Residential) with minimum criteria met. Receiving areas must be zoned SR (Suburban Residential) or DR (Development Residential) with adequate water and sewer facilities. Development rights are transferred at specified density ratios. Landowners in sending areas can monetize development rights by selling them to developers in receiving areas, while receiving areas can achieve higher density development through the transfer mechanism.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners in Cecil County with properties in sending or receiving areas defined by the zoning ordinance; property developers and landowners seeking to increase development density in receiving areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Landowners in sending areas can sell development rights to developers in receiving areas to preserve agricultural and natural resource lands; receiving areas can achieve higher density through transfer of development rights from sending areas, supporting orderly growth near towns and infrastructure
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland; sending areas are properties zoned NAR (Non-Agricultural Residential) and SAR (Suburban Agricultural Residential); receiving areas are properties zoned SR (Suburban Residential) and DR (Development Residential) typically around towns and areas with adequate infrastructure
requirements_list: Property must be zoned NAR (Non-Agricultural Residential) or SAR (Suburban Agricultural Residential) to be a sending area, or SR (Suburban Residential) or DR (Development Residential) to be a receiving area
Must meet minimum criteria established for sending or receiving area designation
Sending area properties must meet minimum acreage and other criteria to qualify for development rights transfer
Receiving areas must have adequate water and sewer facilities to support transferred density
Development density ratios and transfer mechanics determined by Cecil County zoning ordinance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners work with Cecil County Planning and Zoning Division to identify and evaluate TDR opportunities. The process involves: (1) verification that property meets sending or receiving area zoning requirements; (2) confirmation that minimum criteria are satisfied for the applicable area type; (3) assessment of water and sewer infrastructure adequacy for receiving areas; (4) negotiation of development rights transfer between sending and receiving area landowners/developers; (5) coordination with County to process and record TDR transactions. The County Planning and Zoning Division provides technical assistance throughout the process.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program reimburses a limited amount of transportation costs each fiscal year for qualified senior citizens, people with disabilities, and low-income individuals in Cecil County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses transportation costs for qualified individuals. For fiscal year 2026, the reimbursement limit is $350 per person, with a minimum reimbursement amount of $50. Riders must request receipts from their driver and submit reimbursement requests to Cecil Transit. Reimbursements are processed based on submitted receipts and documentation.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation costs for travel within and outside Cecil County.

requirements_list: Applicant must be a qualified senior citizen (age 60 or over), person with a disability, or low-income individual
Disability verification form required for those claiming disability status

Minimum reimbursement amount is $50
Maximum reimbursement limit for FY 26 is $350
Must request receipts from driver when riding Cecil Transit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Applicants complete the Transportation Reimbursement Program Application form and provide required verification documentation (disability verification form for those with disabilities or income certification form for low-income applicants). 2. When riding Cecil Transit, request receipts from the driver for each trip. 3. Submit the TRP Reimbursement Request Form along with the collected receipts to Cecil Transit for processing. 4. Cecil Transit will process the reimbursement request and reimburse eligible expenses up to the annual limit.

structured_extraction.program_description: A funding program that distributes Video Lottery Terminal revenue to nonprofit, not-for-profit, and government agencies located within or serving Cecil County. Grant funding is contingent on passage of the County Executive's budget by the County Council.

Funds are generated from the State's video lottery terminals and gaming facilities. Grant awards vary based on application quality and available funding. Grant funding is contingent on the passage of the County Executive's budget by the County Council. Applicants must complete the FY27 VLT Application form and FY27 VLT Budget Form as part of the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Cecil Catalyst is a low-interest loan program administered by the Cecil County Office of Economic Development that encourages small business growth, new investment, business retention, and job creation in Cecil County. It helps new and existing businesses — including creditworthy individuals — acquire land, buildings, equipment, inventory, and other business needs. The program is specifically designed for those who have difficulty obtaining financing through traditional sources due to limited equity, collateral requirements, or marginal cash flow.
structured_extraction.agency: Cecil County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans available in amounts from $5,000 up to a maximum of $75,000. The Loan Review Committee may approve larger amounts with County Executive approval. The interest rate is the Prime Rate plus 2%, fixed for up to five years; for longer loans, the rate adjusts after the first five years. A one-time, non-refundable application fee of $100 is due at the time of submission. The borrower is responsible for all closing costs. If buying real estate, the business must occupy at least 51% of the property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses (including start-ups) and individuals located in Cecil County who are creditworthy but have difficulty obtaining financing through traditional sources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquiring land, buildings, or building improvements; renovations; machinery and equipment; inventory; working capital; and other business needs including improvements to leased property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cecil County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicants must be creditworthy and demonstrate ability to repay the loan

Business owners must provide a personal guarantee for the loan
A non-refundable application fee of $100 is required at time of submission
The borrower pays for all closing costs
If buying real estate, the business must occupy at least 51% of the property

Step 3: The Loan Review Committee reviews the application and makes a decision; the Committee may approve loan maximum increases with County Executive approval.

Prince George's County provides an annual tax credit to qualifying surviving spouses. Both programs require annual application for the tax year in which the credit is being requested. Annual application required by April 1 prior to the tax year for which credit is requested

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply for this tax credit, surviving spouses must file an initial proof of claim with the Director of Finance by April 1 prior to the tax year for which the credit is being requested. Applicants will need to provide documentation proving the spouse's relationship to the deceased officer/rescue worker, proof of the officer/rescue worker's death from employment-related injury or disease, proof of ownership and occupancy of the dwelling, and any other documentation required by the respective County Code.

structured_extraction.program_description: This state-supported grant program, locally administered by the Charles County Health Department, provides funding to replace conventional septic tanks with nitrogen-reducing units or to fund sewer connections for existing dwellings where public sewer is available. For low-income households, the program can also fund replacement of failing septic systems. The program aims to reduce harmful nutrients like nitrogen that septic systems discharge into the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries. Previously, the program installed nitrogen removal units on 95 septic systems between November 2007 and December 2011.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Bay Restoration Fund provides grants to eligible homeowners in Charles County to replace conventional septic tanks with nitrogen-reducing units (such as Fuji Clean, Orenco, or Advantex systems), fund sewer connections where public sewer is available, or replace failing septic systems for low-income households. Grants cover the cost of approved nitrogen-removing septic system upgrades. Different application requirements and checklists apply depending on whether the property is located in a Priority Funding Area or non-Priority Funding Area. The program prioritizes applications for properties in Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; applications accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and Charles County residents with existing on-site septic systems who own an existing dwelling with a septic system or have access to public sewer. Low-income households with failing septic systems qualify for additional assistance. Eligible in both Priority Funding Areas and non-Priority Funding Areas, with Priority Funding Areas receiving priority consideration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of conventional septic tanks with nitrogen-reducing units (approved models including Fuji Clean, Orenco, Advantex RT, or SeptiTech), funding for sewer connections where public sewer is available, or replacement of failing septic systems for low-income households. Funds support nitrogen removal to reduce nutrient discharge into the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland. Program considers Priority Funding Areas and non-Priority Funding Areas. The Maryland Department of Planning provides an interactive map to identify Priority Funding Area status at http://mdpgis.mdp.state.md.us/PFA/publicinfotemplate/index.html
requirements_list: Must own an existing dwelling with a septic system or have access to public sewer
Must be a Charles County resident
Low-income households can qualify for failing septic system replacement
Property must be in Charles County
For Priority Funding Areas, must meet additional eligibility criteria per application checklist
For non-Priority Funding Areas, must meet additional eligibility criteria per application checklist
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Determine Priority Funding Area status using the Maryland Department of Planning interactive map. 2. Obtain the appropriate application checklist (Priority Funding Area or non-Priority Funding Area version). 3. Complete the Bay Restoration Fund application with required documentation. 4. Submit application to the Charles County Department of Health. 5. Contact the Charles County Department of Health at 301-609-6792 or Latoya.reeder1@maryland.gov for more information and to apply.
