structured_extraction.program_description: The SLBE Program certifies small, locally-based businesses and gives them exclusive access to certain Charles County government contracts under $50,000 and preferences on larger contracts between $50,000 to $500,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certified SLBE vendors receive exclusive access to Charles County government procurements under $50,000 as long as at least three registered SLBE firms are qualified. For formal procurements between $50,000 to $500,000, SLBE firms receive preferences: up to 10% cost advantage on Invitations to Bid (ITBs) and Requests for Quotation (RFQs), or up to 10 points on Requests for Proposals (RFPs).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, locally-based for-profit businesses located in Charles County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in Charles County government procurement opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have headquarters located in Charles County, or have a branch or satellite office in Charles County that generates at least 50% of the company's annual gross sales or has 50% of its full-time equivalent employees residing in Charles County.
requirements_list: Be a for-profit business and independently owned (no brokers or subsidiaries)

Have headquarters located in Charles County, or have a branch/satellite office in Charles County generating at least 50% of annual gross sales or employing 50% of full-time equivalent employees in the county
Meet Maryland Small Business Reserve (SBR) program industry-specific thresholds for gross sales and employees
Be certified in the State of Maryland's Small Business Reserve Program
Be registered with eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses must first achieve certification in Maryland's Small Business Reserve Program, then register with eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA). Complete a Charles County SLBE application and submit for approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charles County Tree Planting Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program aims to implement tree planting projects in Charles County that will increase tree cover in urban and rural spaces. The program brings benefits including increased forest habitat, improved water quality, and natural cooling systems. It is expected to improve the health and wellbeing of humans as well as the natural communities that comprise local watersheds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to fund tree planting projects that increase tree cover in urban and rural areas of Charles County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations and entities interested in implementing tree planting projects in Charles County to increase tree cover and improve environmental quality.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support tree planting projects that increase tree cover in urban and rural spaces, improve water quality, create forest habitat, and provide natural cooling benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling deadline basis. Applicants should visit the Charles County Tree Planting Grant Program website at cbtrust.org for specific application procedures and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charles County Watershed Protection and Restoration Fee Credit for Rain Barrels
structured_extraction.program_description: Property tax credit available to Charles County residents, homeowners, and business owners who install and register rain barrels to capture and use rainwater from their roofs. The program reduces stormwater runoff pollution, protects freshwater resources including local waterways and the Chesapeake Bay, and provides water savings during peak summer months. Properties outside the incorporated Towns of Indian Head and LaPlata are eligible.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit applied to your property tax bill for installing and registering a rain barrel to harvest rainwater from your roof. Charles County property owners located outside the incorporated Towns of Indian Head and LaPlata are eligible to apply for the tax credit after installing two rain barrels on their property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County homeowners, business owners, and schools who want to capture and use rainwater while reducing stormwater runoff and lowering water bills. Properties must be outside the incorporated Towns of Indian Head and LaPlata.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation and registration of rain barrels to capture rainwater from roof downspouts for use in gardens, lawns, trees, and other property needs, reducing stormwater runoff and water costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland only. Properties must be located outside the incorporated Towns of Indian Head and LaPlata to be eligible for the tax credit.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Charles County
Property must be outside the incorporated Towns of Indian Head and LaPlata
Install at least two rain barrels to capture rainwater from roof downspouts
Register the rain barrel(s) with Charles County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Install rain barrels on your property and register them with Charles County to qualify for the property tax credit. Contact the Watershed Protection Division at PGMadmin@charlescountymd.gov or 301-645-0692, or register through the online process via the Charles County Planning and Growth Management Department.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state initiative established under the Cannabis Reform Act of 2023 that allocates a portion of tax revenue from cannabis sales to local jurisdictions to support community-based initiatives benefiting low-income communities and those disproportionately affected by past cannabis prohibition enforcement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FY2026 approved budget of $811,000. Charles County Charitable Trust receives $411,000 to award grants to local non-profits supporting low-impact and disproportionately impacted communities in the Waldorf region of Charles County. Department of Community Services-Aging Division receives $400,000 to support essential services for the aging community in the Waldorf region, including Meals-on-Wheels and other senior assistance programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income communities and those disproportionately affected by past cannabis prohibition enforcement; aging community in the Waldorf region of Charles County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based initiatives supporting low-income communities; essential services for seniors including Meals-on-Wheels and senior assistance programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Waldorf region of Charles County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Grants are awarded through the Charles County Charitable Trust grant program for non-profits and through the Department of Community Services-Aging Division for senior services.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides support to family caregivers through information, outreach, training, counseling, and limited financial assistance. It helps caregivers access services, coordinate community-based care, learn caregiving skills, and receive temporary relief from caregiving responsibilities. The program offers respite care and supplemental services such as supplies, medical equipment, and prescription assistance to help fill gaps in care. It is designed to alleviate the emotional and financial burden of informal caregiving for older adults and others in Charles County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance is available for respite care to provide temporary relief from caregiving duties and supplemental services including supplies, durable medical equipment, and prescription assistance. These services are limited to one-time or short-term benefits. Priority for funded services is given to persons who are financially needy.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Family caregivers including caregivers of any age when caring for a Charles County resident age 60 or older; caregivers age 55 or older who are primary caregivers for children under 18 in Charles County; and caregivers of people with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders regardless of age.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Respite care to provide temporary relief from caregiving responsibilities; supplemental services including supplies, durable medical equipment, prescription assistance, and similar one-time or short-term benefits to complement informal care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The person being cared for must be a resident of Charles County and at least 60 years old, or the caregiver must be a Charles County resident at least 55 years old providing primary care for children under 18, or caregivers of people with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders regardless of location.
requirements_list: Caregiver must be providing care to a family member

Person cared for is a Charles County resident and at least 60 years old, OR caregiver is a Charles County resident at least 55 years old and primary caregiver for children under 18, OR caregiver of person with Alzheimer's disease or related disorder
Financial need is prioritized for receiving funded services
Priority given to financially needy persons
Services are limited to one-time or short-term benefits; persons needing long-term services are encouraged to apply for other programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Caregivers should contact the Charles County Aging Division to discuss eligibility, express interest, and receive information about available services and how to coordinate a plan of care. A caregiver support group meets at 2:00 p.m. on the last Wednesday of each month at the Richard R. Clark Senior Center in La Plata.

structured_extraction.program_name: First Time Home Buyers Settlement Expense Loan Program (SELP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides direct financial assistance of up to six thousand dollars for settlement expenses to qualified low-income and moderate-income first time home buyers in Charles County.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct financial assistance up to six thousand dollars for settlement expenses secured by a second mortgage. Repayment is deferred until the property is resold, transferred, refinanced, or the buyer stops occupying it as a principal residence.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified low-income and moderate-income first time home buyers in Charles County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Settlement expenses for home purchase, including closing costs, appraisals, inspections, and other expenses required to finalize a home purchase.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: First time home buyer
Low to moderate income (must meet program income guidelines)
Must be purchasing a primary residence in Charles County
Must meet program eligibility guidelines
Must have a valid purchase contract
Loan is secured by a second mortgage on the property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Charles County Housing Services office to request an application and learn about current income limits and program requirements. Applications are processed on a rolling basis subject to fund availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: Housing assistance program providing a deferred loan to qualified county employees purchasing a home in Charles County. The program offers financial support towards down payment and settlement expenses for homebuyers.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 0% interest deferred loan of $5,000 from the Charles County Commissioners to be used towards down payment and settlement expenses for purchasing a home in Charles County. The loan is deferred, meaning repayment is not required until the home is sold or the employee leaves County employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified Charles County employees who have been employed with the County for at least one year and are purchasing a home in Charles County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and settlement expenses for purchasing a home in Charles County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is limited to employees purchasing a home in Charles County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Have been employed with Charles County for at least one year
Be purchasing a home in Charles County
Be a current County employee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Human Resources for information on the program and participant requirements. The Department of Human Resources will review applications and verify employee eligibility before processing the loan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides eligible households with rental assistance to help pay rent for one year. Eligible households receive $1,000 per month in rental assistance, and up to an additional $2,000 per household for security deposit assistance. Rental payments are made directly to landlords, and units are inspected for habitability before occupancy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $1,000 per month in rental assistance for one year, plus up to $2,000 per household for security deposit assistance. Payments are made directly to landlords. Estimated to assist approximately 30 households. This is a temporary program that concludes when ARPA funds are no longer available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible households earning no more than 30% of Area Median Income (AMI) who are Charles County residents and have lived in the county for at least one year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental payments to landlords and security deposit assistance for eligible households.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County residents only. Applicants must have been Charles County residents for at least one year prior to receiving assistance.
requirements_list: Household income no more than 30% AMI
Charles County resident for at least one year prior to assistance
Pass criminal activity screening
Acceptable previous Housing Authority program participation history
Unit must pass habitability inspection prior to occupancy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application details coming soon.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides ongoing assistance to families to ensure that rental housing is affordable based on family income and is decent, safe, and sanitary in accordance with housing quality standards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Ongoing rental subsidy assistance to make housing affordable for eligible families based on income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low and moderate income families seeking rental housing assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing assistance to make housing affordable and ensure decent, safe, and sanitary living conditions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Low to moderate income family
Rental housing must meet housing quality standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants are seen by appointment only on Monday through Friday. Paperwork may be submitted via drop box located outside the building or in the lobby.

structured_extraction.program_description: A nine-month educational program for county executives and leaders that builds understanding of the Southern Maryland region and its key sectors. Participants join a cohort of up to 35 executives and engage with top leaders across defense, industry, economic development, education, energy, environment, healthcare, housing, human services, and public safety. The program includes an orientation retreat, nine monthly sessions, site visits, and a volunteer commitment to strengthen leadership capabilities and regional networks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides nine months of leadership training including an orientation retreat, nine monthly full-day sessions (typically Thursdays, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.), travel to Southern Maryland locations, and a 25-hour volunteer commitment or project to be completed by March 1. Participants must attend all sessions with no more than two absences permitted, or they forfeit program tuition and eligibility.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Enrollment dates to be announced via email; contact for specific information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time county employees with at least 12 months of employment; part-time employees who transition to full-time with continuous 12-month employment; members of the Executive Leadership Team; or professionals recommended by an ELT member. Applicants must have completed the County's Leadership Academy or equivalent program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program funds nine months of leadership education, training sessions, orientation retreat, travel to regional sites, and structured learning on regional topics including defense and industry, economic and workforce development, education, energy and environment, healthcare, housing and human services, public safety, and community narratives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program focuses on the Southern Maryland region and is open to eligible Charles County government employees.
requirements_list: Must have completed the County's Leadership Academy or an equivalent program
Full-time employees must have worked for the County for at least 12 months
Part-time employees transitioning to full-time must have worked continuously for the County for at least 12 months
Must be a member of the Executive Leadership Team (or recommended by an ELT member) or an employee in a professional position
Must attend the mandatory Orientation Retreat (missing one day makes participant ineligible)
Must fully participate in all nine monthly sessions (missing more than two program days results in ineligibility)
Must complete a 25-hour volunteer commitment or project by March 1 to be eligible to graduate
Participants who become ineligible forfeit the full program tuition
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and complete the Systemwide Training application form from the Forms section of the Internal County Group (ICG) portal, selecting the desired program from the drop-down menu on page 2. Submit the completed application to your supervisor for review and recommendation. Your supervisor forwards the application to your department director for their recommendation. Send the approved application to RizorE@CharlesCountyMD.gov. If selected by the Systemwide Training review panel and approved by the County Administrator, you will be directed to complete the program application. Enrollment notifications are sent via All CCG email when applications open.

structured_extraction.program_name: Loan Closet for Durable Medical Equipment
structured_extraction.program_description: The Aging & Senior Programs Division provides free temporary loans of durable medical equipment to qualified persons. Equipment includes walkers, canes, bath and shower benches, and transport wheelchairs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Equipment is provided free of charge for a 90-day loan period. An extension of up to an additional 90 days may be permitted on a case-by-case basis if inventory is available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors and individuals in Charles County who need temporary durable medical equipment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary use of durable medical equipment including walkers, canes, bath and shower benches, and transport wheelchairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Equipment must be returned sanitized and in good working condition at the end of the loan period
Client contact form must be completed and signed for all borrowed equipment
Eligibility may be verified as some equipment has been purchased with grant funds restricting eligibility to specified populations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-934-0103 to check on availability and eligibility for loan closet items. Complete and sign a client contact form for all borrowed equipment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides financial assistance for long driveway projects in Charles County, Maryland, classified under Category 3 eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Long driveway projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through online form with email address for confirmation copy.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funds to address plumbing poverty in the community by funding installation or repair of plumbing water systems in owner-occupied homes.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds to install or repair plumbing water systems in owner-occupied homes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low to moderate income homeowners in Charles County with plumbing needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation or repair of plumbing water systems in owner-occupied homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Owner-occupied home

structured_extraction.program_name: Perpetual Conservation Easement Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit available to property owners in Charles County who grant perpetual conservation easements on their real property, helping to preserve land and natural resources while reducing property tax liability.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit available to property owners in Charles County who have granted perpetual conservation easements on their real property. The credit provides a reduction of property tax liability for the affected property based on the value impact of the conservation easement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Charles County who have granted perpetual conservation easements on their real property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability for properties with perpetual conservation easements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must own real property located in Charles County
Must have granted a perpetual conservation easement on the real property
Property must have a perpetual conservation easement designation recorded
Applicant must be current on all property taxes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners interested in obtaining the Perpetual Conservation Easement Property Tax Credit must complete the Perpetual Conservation Easement Property Tax Credit Application form and submit it to the Charles County Treasury department along with supporting documentation that verifies the perpetual conservation easement on the property.

structured_extraction.program_name: Private Activity Bonds (Tax Exempt or Taxable)
structured_extraction.program_description: Bonds issued by the state government with proceeds used for qualified purposes by entities other than the government. These bonds can be either tax-exempt or taxable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bonds are issued by state government with proceeds allocated to defined, qualified purposes for entities other than the government issuing the bonds. Available as either tax-exempt or taxable instruments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entities seeking capital for qualified purposes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Defined, qualified purposes as determined by state guidelines
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Purpose must be qualified and defined
Entity must not be the state government issuing the bonds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Commerce for more information on Private Activity Bonds through the MIDFA program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A county program where Charles County purchases development rights directly from property owners. Development rights are permanently extinguished rather than transferred to other areas, permanently restricting the property to agricultural and open space uses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Charles County purchases development rights directly from property owners at fair market value as determined through independent appraisal. The development rights are permanently extinguished and cannot be transferred to other properties, ensuring the land remains restricted to agricultural and open space uses in perpetuity. Compensation is provided as a one-time payment to the property owner.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Periodic competitive application cycles as funding is available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Charles County who own eligible land and wish to sell their development rights to preserve their property for agricultural and open space uses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct payment from Charles County for the permanent purchase of development rights on the property. Funds cannot be used for other purposes as they represent compensation for the extinguishment of development rights.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland. Properties must be located within Charles County and meet land eligibility criteria established by the program.
requirements_list: Land must be eligible for preservation under the program criteria
Property must be in agricultural use or capable of supporting agricultural use
Applications are evaluated using the same ranking criteria applied to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation program
Landowner must hold legal title to the property
Property must not be currently under development rights purchase with another entity
Agricultural viability and preservation value are considered in ranking applications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners should contact Charles County Planning Staff to learn more about the program and eligibility requirements. Charles County holds periodic competitive application cycles for the program when funding becomes available. Landowners submit applications during open application periods. Applications are reviewed and ranked according to established criteria. Selected properties are then appraised independently to determine fair market value for the development rights. Once a property is selected for purchase, the county negotiates and finalizes the terms with the landowner, and development rights are permanently purchased through a recorded conservation easement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rural Housing Initiative and Indoor Plumbing Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: Helps low-income homeowners in Charles County obtain indoor plumbing and potable water for their principal residence. The program provides financial assistance for the installation or repair of indoor plumbing and potable water systems, with income limits ranging from $74,800 for a household of one person to $141,000 for a household of eight persons.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides financial assistance to qualified homeowners to obtain indoor plumbing and potable water for their principal residence. Homeowners must meet income limits ranging from $74,800 for a household of one person to $141,000 for a household of eight persons.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income homeowners in Charles County with principal residences lacking indoor plumbing or potable water.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation or repair of indoor plumbing and potable water systems for principal residences.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Household income must be at or below specified limits based on household size
Must be a homeowner
Property must be principal residence
Must lack indoor plumbing and/or potable water
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Qualified homeowners contact the Housing Authority to complete an application package. Applicants submit a complete Pre-application form, after which the Housing Authority will contact them. Applicants can first complete the Plumbing Program Pre-Qualification Form to determine eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program encourages property owners with existing septic systems to have tank risers installed when their septic system is pumped out. Property owners can apply for riser reimbursement at the same time as their septic pump-out reimbursement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a reimbursement of $100 per system for septic riser installation. Property owners must provide proof of purchase and installation by a hauler or contractor, or proof of purchase for risers independently installed with their application. Reimbursements are limited to one per property. Applications must be received within six months of riser installation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be received within six (6) months of riser installation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County property owners with existing septic systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for septic tank riser installation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a property owner with an existing septic system
Riser installation must be performed by a hauler or contractor, or independently installed
Must provide proof of purchase and installation with application
Limited to one riser reimbursement per property
Application must be received within six months of riser installation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners submit an application with proof of purchase and installation of the riser. This can be done at the same time as applying for septic pump-out reimbursement. Applications are verified and processed, with reimbursement checks mailed to the address provided.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program reimburses Charles County residents for the cost of pumping out their septic systems. Eligible residents can receive reimbursement once every 3 years. The program helps meet nutrient reduction targets by pumping out 20% of the county's septic systems annually to support the County's Watershed Implementation Plan goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a reimbursement check for septic system pump-outs performed by licensed septage haulers approved by the Charles County Health Department. The maximum reimbursement is $100 per system. Residents must submit an online application with a copy of the contractor's receipt. Applications must be received within six months of the pump-out. Reimbursement checks are processed and mailed within 12 weeks of receipt.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be received within six (6) months of the pump-out
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charles County residents with septic systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for septic system pump-out services performed by licensed septage haulers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Charles County resident with a septic system
Must have pump-out performed by a septage hauler approved by the Charles County Health Department
Must submit online application with a copy of the contractor's receipt
Eligible once every 3 years
Application must be received within six months of the pump-out
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents complete an online application and provide a copy of the contractor's receipt from an approved septage hauler. Applications are verified and processed within 12 weeks of receipt. A reimbursement check is mailed to the address provided in the application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides down payment assistance to help eligible first-time homebuyers purchase existing housing units in Charles County. Offers $14,000 in assistance that becomes a grant if the homebuyer remains in the home as their primary residence for at least five years.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $14,000 in down payment assistance for eligible first-time homebuyers. The funds are applied to reduce the purchase cost of the home. ARPA funds are provided as a grant if the homebuyer resides in the home as their principal residence for at least five years. This is a temporary program that concludes when ARPA funds are no longer available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers in Charles County who are approved for the county's Settlement Expense Loan Program (SELP).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance to reduce the purchase cost of existing housing units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County. Eligible applicants must have lived or worked full-time in the county continuously for the last three years.
requirements_list: First-time homebuyer
Approved for Charles County Settlement Expense Loan Program (SELP)
Household income no more than 100% AMI
Lived or worked full-time in Charles County continuously for the last three years
Purchasing existing housing unit (new construction excluded)
Must reside in home as principal residence for at least five years for funds to be treated as grant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants must work with a SELP-Approved lender to complete an application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Low-interest or deferred loans to improve the basic livability of single-family homes for low and moderate-income families.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest or deferred loans to finance home improvements and repairs that enhance basic livability in single-family homes, including indoor plumbing and total home replacements. Eligible uses include improvements to enhance basic livability such as indoor plumbing installation and total home replacements for low and moderate-income homeowners.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low and moderate-income families living in single-family homes in Charles County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home improvements and repairs to improve basic livability, including indoor plumbing installation and total home replacements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Low to moderate income
Single-family home owner
Reside in Charles County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program office at 301-934-0136 for more information and to determine eligibility. Applicants must complete a pre-qualification form to apply for the Indoor Plumbing Assistance program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that helps eligible for-profit companies relocate to or expand businesses within target industries in Charles County. The program serves as gap financing and offers loans with favorable terms up to $100,000 with repayment periods up to 15 years.
list_of_eligible_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $100,000 with terms up to 15 years at Wall Street Journal prime rate plus 1-2.5%. The loan is not intended to replace commercial bank financing and will take a subordinated position to bank financing. Personal guaranties are required. Loans can be used for working capital, inventory, equipment/machinery purchase, building acquisitions, leasehold improvements, contract financing, and gap financing. Application fee is $50. Collateral required is business assets.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses relocating or expanding in target industries in Charles County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, inventory, equipment/machinery purchase, building acquisitions, leasehold improvements, contract financing, and gap financing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primary business location must be in Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Legal for-profit business
Primary business location in Charles County, Maryland
Company operating in one of the target industries: Federal Contracting, Health Services, Technology, Innovative Entrepreneurial Activity, Business Services, Retail Development, or R&D and Engineering
Demonstrate that loan proceeds will help grow the business or enhance productivity or profitability
Demonstrate ability to repay the loan
Have not previously defaulted on an economic development loan with any local, state, or federal agency
No delinquent debt with Charles County or Maryland
Provide personal guaranties
Provide business assets as collateral
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download an application form from www.MeetCharlesCounty.com/BusinessSupport/Financing and submit to the Charles County Economic Development Department. Contact Lucretia Freeman-Buster at 301-885-1344 or BusterL@MeetCharlesCounty.com for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A government-created program that allows rural landowners to sell their development rights to private developers, who can then build at higher density in designated growth areas. The sale permanently restricts the selling property to agricultural, forestry, and open space uses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners sell development rights to developers at a negotiated price. The development rights are transferred and recorded in Charles County Land Records, permanently restricting the property to agricultural, forestry, and open space uses. Owners retain full ownership of the land and can continue agricultural and forestry operations. The program is completely voluntary.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural landowners in Charles County interested in selling development rights to preserve agricultural and forest land while generating revenue.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proceeds from the sale of development rights, with the price negotiated between buyer and seller. Property owners receive compensation for permanently restricting their land to agricultural, forestry, and open space uses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, with eligible properties being rural land outside designated growth areas. Properties must be located outside Priority Funding Areas and other designated development zones.
requirements_list: Property must be rural land in Charles County located outside designated growth areas
Property owner must certify the number of development rights associated with the property
Development rights must be based on property acreage and current zoning regulations
Price is negotiated between willing buyer and willing seller
Program is completely voluntary
Property restrictions are permanent once recorded in Charles County Land Records
Owners retain full ownership of land and can continue agricultural/forestry operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible property owners work with Charles County Planning Staff to certify the number of development rights (TDRs) associated with their property. Certified TDRs are tracked by the County and a list of available TDRs can be obtained. Property owners then negotiate sale of development rights with willing buyers. Once sale terms are agreed upon, the development rights are formally transferred and recorded in Charles County Land Records. Contact Charles County Planning Staff at RiceC@charlescountymd.gov for assistance with the certification and application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for volunteer emergency responders in Charles County, including volunteer firefighters, rescue squad members, and emergency medical services (EMS) personnel, recognizing their service to the community by reducing their property tax obligations.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit available to volunteer emergency responders including volunteer firefighters, rescue squad members, and emergency medical services personnel. The credit reduces the property tax liability of eligible individuals. Applicants must complete an application and provide an affidavit, and must meet all program service requirements. The tax credit is administered by Charles County Treasury.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Volunteer emergency responders in Charles County, including volunteer firefighters, rescue squad members, and EMS personnel who own property in Charles County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability for eligible volunteer emergency responders.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Charles County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a volunteer emergency responder (volunteer firefighter, rescue squad member, or emergency medical services personnel)
Must own property in Charles County
Must meet service requirements established by the program
Must provide a completed Affidavit for Volunteer Emergency Responders Tax Credit Application
Must submit completed application and affidavit to Charles County Treasury
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete the Volunteer Emergency Responders Tax Credit Application form and provide an Affidavit for Volunteer Emergency Responders Tax Credit Application. Both documents must be submitted to Charles County Treasury. The application requires certification from the volunteer organization confirming the applicant's volunteer status and service. Contact Charles County Treasury for additional details and to request application materials.

structured_extraction.program_name: Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC) Façade Improvement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides grants to existing commercial building owners in the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor to upgrade the visible, corridor-facing exterior components of their properties. The county matches 50% of approved improvement costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Fifty percent grant reimbursement match from Charles County covering approved façade improvements. Applicant must fund 50% of the project cost upfront. County reimburses within thirty days of receiving proof of payment. Incremental draws are possible depending on award amount. Maximum grant award amounts vary by project type and location within the WURC.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial business owners and property owners with commercial buildings located within the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor in Waldorf, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior building façade improvements including exterior wall materials, façade color, balconies, roof treatments, roof utilities, building base and storefront, entries and doorways, windows, awnings and canopies, upper façade, lighting, cornice and fascia, porches, door hoods and stoops, roofs, chimneys, permits, and signage. Interior improvements are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC) boundaries. Priority will be given to projects fronting Old Washington Road.
requirements_list: Applications must be for commercial buildings within the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor (WURC)
Applications must be received by the designated deadline
Projects can only be external building façade improvements
Applications cannot be for works started prior to receiving a commitment letter from Charles County
Applicant must maintain all improvements in their finished state per a maintenance agreement
Applicant must be the current owner or authorized representative of the property
Property must be in compliance with local codes and zoning regulations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants fill out and submit an application form available on the Charles County website or from the program contacts. The application must include project details, cost estimates, and photographs of the existing façade. Selected applicants will be notified by early fall 2025. Upon approval, the applicant pays 100% of project costs upfront and submits proof of payment and final completion documentation to receive 50% reimbursement from the county within thirty days. Construction must be completed within ninety days of the award letter unless an extension is approved in writing by the county. A maintenance agreement must be signed and recorded before reimbursement is issued.

structured_extraction.program_name: Watershed Assistance – Two-Year Milestone Support Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Supports design assistance, watershed planning and programmatic development for protection and restoration programs and projects that lead to improved water quality in the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, the Maryland portion of the Youghiogheny watershed, and the Maryland Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.agency: Chesapeake Bay Trust, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, and Maryland Department of the Environment
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for design assistance, watershed planning and programmatic development associated with protection and restoration programs and projects. The Watershed Assistance Grant Program has awarded over $8.1 million for planning and design projects throughout Maryland. Grants support planning, design and engineering of restoration projects that address nonpoint source pollution reduction and water quality improvement in eligible watersheds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local communities, local governments, and their partners interested in undertaking comprehensive watershed protection and restoration activities in the Chesapeake Bay watershed, Youghiogheny watershed, and Maryland Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design assistance, watershed planning, programmatic development, stormwater financing strategies, and technical assistance for protection and restoration programs and projects that improve water quality and reduce nonpoint source pollution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, Maryland portion of the Youghiogheny watershed, and Maryland Coastal Bays.
requirements_list: Communities must demonstrate capacity needs for restoration and protection efforts
Projects should address nonpoint source pollution reduction
Applicants should engage with regional Watershed Restoration Specialists and other Collaborative partners
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Communities interested in learning how the Collaborative can connect them to financial and technical resources should fill out the Request for Resources & Services Form. Communities can also work with Regional Watershed Restoration Specialists assigned to their region and access support through the University of Maryland Environmental Finance Center for watershed planning, financing strategies, and stakeholder development.

structured_extraction.program_name: Adopt a Community (Boots on the Ground Community Engagement Grant) - Building Resilient Communities Together
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant funds community-based organizations to develop programs that build resilient, empowered communities in Annapolis. Organizations work with hands-on outreach and engagement strategies responding directly to community needs, applying a public health lens to violence prevention in designated at-risk neighborhoods. The program emphasizes long-term relationships, community ownership, and trauma-informed approaches.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Annapolis will fund up to $200,000 in one-time grant awards to organizations with 501(c)(3) status. A maximum of $20,000 will be granted to each organization. Only one organization will be funded per neighborhood. Maximum of 10% of funds may be designated for overhead costs. Funding period is September 2023 through June 30, 2024. Grantees must submit an itemized budget proposal with detailed line-item justification, and all funds must be used to support the approved scope of work. The program prioritizes organizations that demonstrate a strong ability to maintain ongoing engagement with residents and implement evidence-based practices for violence prevention and community resilience.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; application will remain open until funds are used
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based non-profit organizations with 501(c)(3) status working in designated at-risk communities within Annapolis
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Programs and activities that build resilient communities through trauma-informed programming, mentorship, mental health services, community engagement, and neighborhood-targeted approaches. Funds can be used for direct services, staff salaries, training and professional development, community events, mental health and behavioral health services, youth programming, family support services, and other activities that strengthen community capacity and reduce violence. Funds cannot support one-time engagement projects, pop-up events, or programs outside Annapolis city limits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The grant is limited to the City of Annapolis. Targeted neighborhoods include Bay Ridge Gardens, Harbour House/Eastport Terrace, Madison Apartments, Bywater, Robinwood, Annapolis Gardens, Admiral Oaks, Clay Street/Obery Court/College Creek Apartments, Woodside, Parole, Allen Apartments, Admiral Farragut, Quiet Waters, and Watergate Village. Each organization focuses on one specific community only.
requirements_list: Organizations must have 501(c)(3) non-profit status
Only one organization will be funded per neighborhood
Proposals must include a practical work plan and timeline with SMARTIE goals and objectives
Proposals must include performance measures and expected outcomes
All applicants must submit an itemized budget proposal with detailed line-item justifications
Maximum of 10% of funds may be designated for overhead costs
All grantees must attend quarterly meetings to share progress and updates
Organizations must submit reports twice: mid-grant period and end of program period
Projects must focus on one specific Annapolis community only
One-on-one contact with residents in the target community is required
Work must apply a public health lens to violence prevention
Organizations must demonstrate experience working with the target population or community
Funding must support programs that build resilience and empower communities through long-term relationships
Applicants should prioritize evidence-based approaches to community engagement and violence prevention
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete all parts and questions in the online application portal at https://arcg.is/1XSnbT. Applicants should review the application questions document and budget template before submitting. Organizations unable to submit through the portal may contact communityservices@annapolis.gov for approval to submit a paper application at City Hall (160 Duke of Gloucester Street, Annapolis, MD 21401) or via email. All grantees must attend quarterly meetings during the funding period. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Applicants are encouraged to reach out to the City for technical assistance and clarification on program requirements before submitting. The City will notify applicants of funding decisions after the application review process is complete.

structured_extraction.program_name: Annapolis Arts and Entertainment District Tax Benefits and Incentives
structured_extraction.program_description: Tax benefits and incentives, including tax credits and tax exemptions, available to arts and entertainment businesses and organizations located in the Annapolis Arts and Entertainment District in Annapolis, Maryland. The program supports arts and entertainment activities and general business operations within the designated district.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits and tax exemptions are available to eligible arts and entertainment businesses and organizations located in the Annapolis Arts and Entertainment District. The program provides tax relief to support operations and activities within the district. Applicants must submit the Arts and Entertainment Tax Credit Application form to be considered for these benefits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Arts and entertainment businesses and organizations located in the Annapolis Arts and Entertainment District, Annapolis, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for arts and entertainment activities and general business operations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Annapolis Arts and Entertainment District, Annapolis, Maryland
requirements_list: Located in the Annapolis Arts and Entertainment District
Business or organization must be engaged in arts and entertainment activities
Applicant must complete and submit the Arts and Entertainment Tax Credit Application form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should complete the Arts and Entertainment Tax Credit Application form available from the City of Annapolis Finance Department. Submit the completed form according to instructions provided with the application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Trust Water Quality Improvement Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to fund the design of new stormwater treatment facilities and construction of new facilities. Projects may treat currently untreated run-off and improve drainage in communities. Design grants can fund engineering firms to design stormwater facilities, host public outreach meetings, and assist in gathering long-term maintenance agreements. Construction grants fund permitting and implementation of stormwater projects.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants awarded for project design or implementation of stormwater treatment facilities and watershed restoration projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Usually applications are due in the Spring
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, non-profits, and municipalities seeking to design or construct stormwater treatment facilities and improve water quality in the Chesapeake Bay watershed.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and construction of stormwater treatment facilities, engineering services, public outreach meetings, maintenance agreements, permitting, and project implementation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County area, specifically projects in partnership with the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Projects must include long-term maintenance agreements for facilities
Construction projects typically must be publicly bid
Final as-built plans and surveys of new stormwater facilities must be delivered to the City
Facilities are subject to City inspection every three years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted in the Spring. The City partners with Anne Arundel County and the Chesapeake Bay Trust to review and award grants for design and construction projects.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Annapolis Rental Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis provides financial assistance to help low and moderate-income households pay rent, security deposits, and utility bills to stabilize housing situations, prevent eviction, prevent utility shut-offs, and provide security deposit assistance. The program is designed for renters at risk of homelessness or housing instability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental assistance payments are made directly to the landlord or utility company on behalf of eligible applicants. The approved funding amount is based on the applicant's qualifications. Assistance covers past due rent and utility bills for households at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI). Account balances must not be more than 60 days past due. The program provides payments to prevent eviction, utility shut-offs, and also offers security deposit assistance for new leases.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low and moderate-income renters living in the City of Annapolis who are at risk of homelessness or housing instability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Past due rent, security deposits, and unpaid utility bills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to City of Annapolis residents. Applicants must be renting in a household with a current and valid City rental license.
requirements_list: Living in the City of Annapolis
Household income at or below 80% AMI
Demonstrates risk of homelessness or housing instability through past due utility notice, eviction notice, or similar evidence
Holds a lease or sublease in applicant's name or will hold a lease for security deposit assistance
Employed or employed within the last 90 days, or retired
Renting in a household with current and valid City rental license
Account balances must not be more than 60 days past due
Verification of household income required
Valid photo identification for all adult household members
Rental or lease agreement required
Evidence of eviction risk or utility arrears required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online application form through the City of Annapolis website or apply in person at Robinwood Community Services office located at 1453 Tyler Avenue, Annapolis, MD 21403 by appointment. Provide household information and income details with supporting documentation including income verification, lease agreement, photo identification for all adult household members, and proof of eviction risk or utility arrears. Application processing takes up to 4-6 weeks. Once approved, assistance payments are made directly to the landlord or utility company.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis offers low-interest loans to help property owners in the downtown Historic District pay for installing automatic fire sprinkler systems in their buildings.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five-year loans at one percent annual percentage rate (APR) for fire sprinkler system retrofits. Loan amounts up to twenty-five thousand dollars are available until the annual allocation of the fund is exhausted. Priority is given to applicants proposing residential use in upper floors and those utilizing a certified minority contractor.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in the downtown Historic District on Main Street and Francis Street with dedicated city water lines who need to retrofit their buildings with automatic fire sprinkler systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fire sprinkler system retrofits for buildings located on Main Street and Francis Street in the Annapolis Historic District.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Buildings on Main Street and Francis Street in the Annapolis Historic District with dedicated City water lines for sprinkler system connection. The geographic area is limited to the downtown historic district.
requirements_list: Building must be located on Main Street or Francis Street in the Annapolis Historic District
Building must have a dedicated City water line for sprinkler system connection
Applicant must use a licensed contractor to create a sprinkler retrofit plan
Building must comply with National Fire Protection Association Standard 13
Building must obtain a building permit before work begins
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, have a licensed contractor create a plan for your building sprinkler retrofit. Second, complete the online loan application available at www.annapolis.gov using the keyword 'sprinkler loan' or by scanning the QR code. Third, the finance office reviews the application and shares it with the Fire Marshal who coordinates with the permit office and signs off. Fourth, the City of Annapolis Office of Law draws up a contract. Fifth, once the contract is complete and building permits are issued, payment is disbursed as a check to the applicant.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Annapolis – Owner Occupied Housing Rehabilitation
structured_extraction.program_description: Eligible Annapolis homeowners can apply for forgiveness loans to make home improvements through licensed contractors. There is no monetary cost to homeowners unless the home is sold, rented, or transferred within 15 years. The program is funded by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Community Development Block Grant program and administered through Arundel Community Development Services.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Home improvement work performed by a licensed contractor at no cost to the homeowner, provided as a forgivable loan. If the home is not sold, rented, or transferred within 15 years, the loan is forgiven. If the property is transferred within 15 years, repayment is required over 11 years, with the loan reduced by 20% per year for the final five years. Maximum expenditure per household is $30,000. Eligible improvements include roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, kitchen and bathroom remodeling, and other necessary repairs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible Annapolis homeowners with household income below 60% of Area Median Income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home improvements including roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, kitchen and bathroom remodeling, and other necessary repairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Homeowner must reside in Annapolis, MD, and the property must be the resident's sole and principal residence.
requirements_list: Homeowner in Annapolis, MD
Combined household income less than 60% of Area Median Income
Property is the resident's sole and principal residence
Proof of income for all people living in the home
Proof of homeownership
Proof of homeowners insurance
Proof that mortgage payments are up to date
Property must meet minimum housing quality standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the property rehabilitation pre-application form and mail it to Arundel Community Development Services with required documentation including proof of income, homeownership, homeowners insurance, and current mortgage payment status. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program that provides funding for community development projects and activities in eligible areas.

The City of Annapolis administers federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds to support capital projects and services that benefit low- and moderate-income individuals and households. The program aims to develop viable urban communities by providing decent housing, suitable living environments, and expanding economic opportunities. Funded activities include capital projects involving physical infrastructure or construction, home repairs for low-income homeowners, and social services provided by organizations serving low-income populations in Annapolis.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Annapolis anticipates receiving approximately $278,182 in CDBG funds for fiscal year 2027 (beginning July 1, 2026). These federal grant funds are allocated to eligible activities including: capital projects involving physical infrastructure or construction that benefit low- and moderate-income residents; home repairs for low-income homeowners; and support for organizations providing social services to low-income populations. Funds are distributed to approved community organizations and projects selected through an application and approval process. Note: the CDBG program for community organizations no longer funds public service projects (service-oriented activities), which should be directed to the City Community Grants program instead.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Denise Ruffin; Alexis Robinson, AICP, Senior Comprehensive Planner
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations, non-profits, low-income homeowners, and social service organizations seeking capital or service funding for projects that serve low- and moderate-income individuals and households in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects involving physical infrastructure or construction; home repairs for low-income homeowners; and social services for low-income populations. Note: the CDBG program for community organizations no longer funds public service projects (service-oriented activities), which should be directed to the City Community Grants program instead.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: All proposed activities and projects must benefit low- and moderate-income individuals and households
Projects must be capital projects involving physical infrastructure or construction, or home repair/social service activities eligible under CDBG
Low-income household status required for homeowner repair assistance
Applications must follow the application process and be submitted by the deadline
Projects should address needs identified in the City's Five Year Housing and Community Development Consolidated Plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Community organizations and eligible applicants submit applications to the Planning and Zoning Department by the stated deadline. The City facilitates an annual CDBG application process for federal funds. The City allocates CDBG funds based on its Five Year Housing and Community Development Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plan. The Affordable Housing and Community Equity Development Commission provides oversight and recommends funding. The City Council approves all CDBG-funded projects, which then become part of the CDBG Action Plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: A low-cost do-it-yourself home energy audit option that allows homeowners to assess their home's energy efficiency themselves.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A low-cost do-it-yourself home energy audit tool that homeowners can use to identify energy efficiency opportunities in their homes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners seeking an affordable self-directed energy audit option.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Self-directed home energy assessment and recommendations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: BGE service area, Annapolis.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Access the DIY audit tool through the Home Boost website link provided.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis offers rebates to help residents and landscape businesses transition from gas-powered leaf blowers to electric models. Residents receive up to $100 and lawn care and landscape businesses receive up to $1,500 to purchase electric leaf blowers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates of up to $100 for residents and up to $1,500 for lawn care and landscape businesses to purchase electric leaf blowers. Applicants must fill out an application, provide proof of residency, and proof of purchase.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of the City of Annapolis and lawn care and landscape businesses operating in the city
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of electric leaf blowers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis limits only
requirements_list: Fill out application
Provide proof of residency
Provide proof of purchase of electric leaf blower
For businesses: must be a lawn care or landscape business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents and businesses fill out an application online, provide proof of residency and proof of purchase to receive the rebate.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides temporary rental and utility assistance to eligible renters whose employment income has been affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. The assistance is designed to prevent evictions and utility shutoffs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Temporary rental and utility assistance provided to prevent evictions and utility turn-offs. Assistance is subject to funding availability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families whose employment income has been impacted by COVID-19 and are at risk of eviction or utility shutoff.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental payments and utility assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Anne Arundel County and City of Annapolis.
requirements_list: Employment income must have been impacted by the COVID-19 public health crisis
Individual or family must be at risk of eviction or utility shutoff
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals and families seeking assistance should contact the Crisis Response Warmline to be screened. They will be evaluated and added to the wait list if eligible.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis provides operating and capital grants to non-profit organizations that support community priorities. Operating grants help cover day-to-day costs of running a non-profit. Capital grants support the purchase of property, construction, remodeling, expansion of facilities, or purchase of equipment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Operating grants provide support for day-to-day costs of running the non-profit organization. Capital grants provide support for the purchase of property, construction, remodeling, or expansion of a facility, or the purchase of equipment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations serving the City of Annapolis that meet at least one of the four community priorities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs for day-to-day non-profit operations, or capital expenses including property purchase, facility construction, remodeling, expansion, or equipment purchase.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program benefits organizations and programs that serve City of Annapolis residents. At least seventy-five percent of programming and work must benefit and engage City residents.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit organization with 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status
Applicant must have administrative and financial capacity to carry out the project successfully
Applicant must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation

Project must help meet one or more of the four priorities: sustain and empower youth, families and individuals toward improved quality of life and self-sufficiency; preserve and enhance community character; contribute to a vibrant economy; or support community revitalization, economic development and environmental sustainability
Applicant must demonstrate that the proposed activity provides maximum public benefit in relation to cost
Applicant must demonstrate ability to leverage additional funds
At least seventy-five percent of programming and work must benefit and engage City residents
Applicant must show strong collaboration with community members, local churches, schools, or other organizations sharing similar objectives
Applicant must have diverse funding sources outside city funding, such as in-kind donations, fundraising efforts, and federal grants
Past Community Grant recipients must show consistency with grant reporting requirements
Copy of last audit or financial statements (or most recent IRS Form 990 if audited financials unavailable)
Organization budget for current year
Board of Directors list with addresses and phone numbers
Copy of 501(c)(3) IRS determination letter
Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Copy of most recent annual report (if applicable)
Memorandum of Understanding or support letters for partner organizations (if applicable)
Summary of City support over previous year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the FY 2027 Community Grant Application form online through the City of Annapolis website. Include all required documents listed in the guidelines. A grants committee consisting of the Mayor's designated staff person, Finance Director's designated staff person, and two additional staff persons will review and evaluate applications according to the specified criteria. The committee makes recommendations to the Finance Committee for consideration as part of the annual budget process.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Annapolis Children and Families Success Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funding community-based organizations to open, expand, and enhance child care programs that provide structured activities for youth with adult supervision at physical locations within Annapolis. The program supports activities that develop physical, emotional, social, behavioral, and intellectual capacities for youth, including recreation, sports, arts, science and technology programs, youth development, enrichment, and life skill building. Priority is given to programs serving low-income families, preventing adverse childhood experiences, and demonstrating equity, diversity, and inclusion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: OCS will fund up to $10,000 per grant proposal. A minimum of five organizations will be funded. Funding is for fiscal year 2026 (July 2025 - June 2026) and is not intended to cover general operational expenses beyond what is necessary for successful implementation of the proposed project and its evaluation. The first 75% of funds will be disbursed during the week of August 25th upon return of the signed contract. The remaining 25% will be distributed upon submission and approval of final reports.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations with 501(c)(3) status or for-profit businesses that provide scholarships or free activities to youth from low-income families in Annapolis. Organizations working with youth to develop programs are encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support opening, expanding, or enhancing child care and youth development programs. Eligible uses include specialty programs such as recreation, sports, arts, science and technology, youth development, learning and education, enrichment, crafts, and life skill building. Programs must provide structured activities at a physical location within Annapolis with adult oversight and focus on youth from low-income families. Funding is not intended for general operational expenses beyond program implementation and evaluation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must be located within Annapolis and serve Annapolis youth. Special emphasis on low-income neighborhoods and projects serving low-income families in Annapolis.
requirements_list: Organization must have 501(c)(3) status or be a for-profit business using funds for scholarships or free programs
Programs must provide structured activities at a physical location within Annapolis
Programs must have adult oversight and develop youth capacities (physical, emotional, social, behavioral, intellectual)
Programs must show how they prevent adverse childhood experiences and provide access for youth from low-income families
Grantees must submit mid-program and final reports
Grantees must participate in three meetings with OCS staff
Organizations that accept Maryland Child Care subsidy program participants are encouraged
Programming offered from 2pm-7pm is especially encouraged
Complete all parts of the application portal or application will not be deemed fundable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open Monday, June 16th and close July 25th at 4:30pm. Submit through the online application portal at https://survey123.arcgis.com/share/72791ac85e5d47659d7a7d9fc9bf0d1a. Organizations unable to submit online may contact Iesha Young for approval to submit in paper format at City Hall (160 Duke of Gloucester Street, Annapolis, MD 21401) or via email to communityservices@annapolis.gov. Decisions will be made by August 8th and award letters emailed by August 13th. The first 75% of funds will be disbursed during the week of August 25th upon return of signed contract, with the remaining 25% distributed upon submission and approval of final reports.

structured_extraction.program_description: A weekly food assistance program that provides food-insecure individuals and families in Annapolis with fresh produce, fruits, vegetables, frozen meat, rice, pasta, and other non-perishable foods. Boxes can be customized for vegan or vegetarian dietary needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Weekly boxes of fresh and canned fruits and vegetables, frozen meat, rice, pasta, and non-perishable foods provided to eligible residents every Friday. Boxes can be customized for vegan or vegetarian needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Food-insecure individuals and families living in the City of Annapolis who are currently facing hardship and need assistance with food.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food assistance including fresh produce, fruits, vegetables, frozen meat, rice, pasta, and non-perishable foods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis only

Must be currently facing hardship and need food assistance
