structured_extraction.program_name: Free Tree Programs (Front Yard, Street Tree, and Community Canopy Programs)
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Annapolis offers free tree programs to residents and property owners to help grow the urban forest. The programs provide multiple pathways to obtain free trees: (1) the Front Yard and Street Tree Program, where City contractors plant free trees in the public right-of-way or front yards of qualifying properties at no cost; and (2) the Community Canopy Program, a partnership with the Arbor Day Foundation that distributes free trees to residents, supported by an online mapping tool that helps identify optimal planting locations on their property for maximum cooling, energy savings, and financial benefits. Together, the programs provide benefits such as shade, improved air quality, temperature stabilization, reduced stormwater runoff, and enhanced street aesthetics.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free trees are provided and, under the Front Yard and Street Tree Program, planted by City contractors at no cost to the recipient. Under the Community Canopy Program (in partnership with the Arbor Day Foundation), free trees are distributed to residents along with access to an online mapping tool that uses research-based analysis to determine optimal planting locations for cooling, energy, and money-saving benefits. Recipients of street/front yard trees must agree to water and care for the tree for the first three years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration for the Community Canopy Program begins on September 15
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Annapolis residents and property owners
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Trees for planting in the public right-of-way (typically the strip between the sidewalk and the curb), front yards, or residential yards
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis only; must have a suitable planting location in the public right-of-way or front/residential yard. The Community Canopy Program runs in the fall with registration beginning September 15.
requirements_list: Be a City of Annapolis resident or property owner
Have a suitable planting location in the public right-of-way (typically the strip between the sidewalk and the curb) or in the front/residential yard
Agree to water and care for the tree for the first 3 years (Front Yard and Street Tree Program)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the Front Yard and Street Tree Program, applicants complete a web form to request a tree or trees, and City contractors handle planting at no cost. For the Community Canopy Program, residents register online starting September 15; after registration, they use an online mapping tool to identify the best planting location on their property based on yard conditions and desired benefits.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Repair - Rebuilding Together Anne Arundel County
structured_extraction.program_description: Rebuilding Together Anne Arundel County provides home repairs for qualifying county homeowners in need. The program can assist with most types of repair needs up to $10,000 worth of work at no cost to eligible homeowners. The program is funded with Community Development Block Grant dollars.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $10,000 worth of home repairs provided at no cost to eligible homeowners. Repairs can include roof work, siding, windows, doors, ramps, flooring, plumbing, electrical, heating and cooling systems, and other structural improvements needed to make homes safe and habitable.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying homeowners in Annapolis and Anne Arundel County with household income below 50% of Area Median Income and legitimate repair needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Most types of home repairs to maintain and improve residential properties, including structural repairs, roof work, siding, windows, doors, accessibility modifications, plumbing, electrical, heating and cooling systems, and other critical home maintenance needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Homeowner in Annapolis, MD. All persons on the deed must reside in the home needing repair.
requirements_list: Homeowner in Annapolis, MD
All persons on deed must reside in the home needing repair
Combined household income less than 50% of Area Median Income
Demonstrate a legitimate need
Unable to perform the work themselves
Owned home for more than 2 years
Plan to reside in the home for at least two years after repairs
Property must be primary residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application for home repairs form and mail it to Rebuilding Together Anne Arundel County with required documentation including information about all people living in the home, proof of income (such as recent tax returns, pay stubs, or benefit statements), and proof of homeownership (such as deed or mortgage statement). Applications are reviewed and homeowners are contacted to discuss their repair needs and schedule the work.

Fire sprinkler system must be installed in compliance with applicable building codes and regulations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Installation of Fire Sprinkler System Tax Credit Application form to the City of Annapolis Finance Department.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides financial assistance to homebuyers who need help paying down payment and closing costs when purchasing a Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) home in the City of Annapolis.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to $10,000 as a zero percent interest rate loan to eligible homebuyers. The loan does not require monthly payments. Repayment is only required upon sale or transfer of the property, or at the end of 10 years, whichever comes first. A lien is placed on the property through a Deed of Trust to secure the loan. The homebuyer must contribute a minimum of one percent of the sales price from their own funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homebuyers purchasing MPDU homes in the City of Annapolis who have an MPDU Certificate of Eligibility, have completed HUD-certified homeownership counseling, and are prequalified or seeking prequalification by a lender.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing costs associated with the purchase of an MPDU home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Annapolis, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have an MPDU Certificate of Eligibility
Must be a graduate of a HUD-certified Homeownership Counseling Program
Must be prequalified by a participating lender or a lender of your choice
Must contribute a minimum of one percent of the sales price from own funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MPDU Eligibility Certificate Holders receive information about the program in their Home Buyer Packet when the city notifies them of available MPDUs for sale. Applicants may contact the office at 410-263-7961, ext. 7727 for more information. The applicant works with their lender and MPDU staff to determine the loan amount.

structured_extraction.program_description: A housing program administered by the City of Annapolis that requires 15% of houses for sale or rent in new subdivisions of 10 or more units to be priced below market rate. The program helps low- to moderate-income households (at or below 100% of the Baltimore Metropolitan Statistical Area median family income) purchase or rent affordable housing units in the City of Annapolis, ensuring housing choices remain available to city residents and employees with moderate incomes. Settlement expense assistance of up to $10,000 is available for eligible homebuyers to assist with down payment and closing costs.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The MPDU program provides below-market-rate housing through both rental and purchase options. For rentals, units are offered at reduced rates at Bell Annapolis on West Street on a first-come, first-served basis. For purchases, sales prices are set by the Department of Planning and Zoning and must be affordable for the household's income. Eligible homebuyers can also access up to $10,000 in settlement expense assistance to help with down payment and closing costs. Applicants must provide proof of income, assets, identification, credit report, and tax returns to qualify for a Certificate of Eligibility. The program operates on a rolling basis with no fixed application deadline, allowing continuous submissions of applications throughout the year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: City residents, city employees, teachers and staff in Annapolis Senior High School district schools, Naval Academy or Annapolis Naval Base employees, and Anne Arundel County residents with disabilities who have moderate incomes (100% or less of the median family income for the Baltimore Metropolitan Statistical Area). Also open to low- to moderate-income households generally seeking to purchase or rent affordable housing in Annapolis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used toward the purchase or rental of a moderately priced dwelling unit. Settlement expense assistance of up to $10,000 can be applied to down payment and closing costs associated with purchasing an MPDU.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available within Annapolis city limits and surrounding MPDU eligible school areas. Applicants must be a city resident or employed within city limits for at least 12 months, a City of Annapolis employee beyond probationary period, a teacher or staff member at an Annapolis Senior High School district school, employed at the Naval Academy or Annapolis Naval Base for at least 12 months, or an Anne Arundel County resident with a disability.
requirements_list: Have an income of 100% or less than the median family income for the Baltimore Metropolitan Statistical Area with adjustments for household size
Not currently own a home
Meet residency or employment requirements
Complete an MPDU Program application
Obtain a Certificate of Eligibility
For purchase: complete a Homeownership Counseling Program before signing a sales contract
For purchase: qualify for a mortgage and pay down payment and closing costs
For purchase: have acceptable credit and steady income
For rental: have an acceptable credit rating
Current gross household income documentation (pay stubs, child support, alimony, SSI/SSA or retirement statements) for one month
Last two statements from all asset accounts (checking, savings, investments)
Last two federal tax returns with all schedules and W2s for each applicant and co-applicant
Photo ID for each applicant and co-applicant
Verification of work or student status for dependents 18 years or older
Credit report with credit score for each applicant (not more than 6 months old)
Household income must meet moderate-income thresholds
Property must be within eligible MPDU areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an MPDU Program application and submit with all required documentation in person, by mail, or electronically on a rolling basis. Submit applications to the MPDU Program, Planning and Zoning Department, 145 Gorman Street, 3rd floor, Annapolis MD 21401. Applications missing required documentation will be returned. MPDU staff review applications and supporting documentation within four weeks. Upon approval, eligible purchasers receive a Certificate of Eligibility. For purchase, attend a homebuyer class through a HUD-certified agency before signing a sales contract. For rental, complete the MPDU Rental Certification Form and contact Bell Annapolis to be placed on the waiting list when units become available. Settlement expense assistance is available through the MPDU Settlement Expense Assistance Request Form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A youth poetry contest and publication project that invites young people to share their voices through poetry. Selected poems are published in a book called 'Around Each Corner' that celebrates the diverse backgrounds, experiences, and creativity of the city's youth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants submit original poems for consideration in a published poetry book. Selected poems are published and celebrated at a presentation event. This is a no-cost participation opportunity that provides youth with a platform to share their creative work and have it professionally published.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young people enrolled in Annapolis educational institutions, homeschools, or pursuing a degree at Anne Arundel Community College.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Poetry submissions on themes including where you are from, cultural heritage, community, diversity, family stories, and future dreams. Accompanying drawings are also welcome.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to students enrolled in Annapolis educational institutions, homeschools, or Anne Arundel Community College.
requirements_list: Be enrolled in an Annapolis educational institution, homeschool, or pursuing a degree at Anne Arundel Community College
Submit poem by August 17, 2026 through the online application form or by email to rjsmith@annapolis.gov
Poem should be inspired by George Ella Lyon's 'Where I Am From' poem template or written freestyle about cultural heritage, traditions, family, or personal identity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the poem application form online by August 17, 2026, or email your poem to rjsmith@annapolis.gov. Optional accompanying drawings may also be submitted. Contact enlace@annapolis.gov with subject line 'YOUTH POETRY' for questions or assistance with the application.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship fund that helps offset program registration fees for eligible participants in the Abilities Unlimited adaptive and inclusive recreation programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship funds are distributed to offset program registration fees. Full coverage (100% of program cost) is available for families with Adjusted Gross Income at or below 300% of the federal poverty line. Partial coverage (50% of program cost) is available for families with Adjusted Gross Income between 301% and 600% of the federal poverty line. Funds are distributed as available and are not guaranteed for all programs at all times.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible participants in Abilities Unlimited adaptive and inclusive recreation programs who meet income requirements and complete the Participant Questionnaire.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To offset the cost of program registration fees for Abilities Unlimited adaptive and inclusive recreation programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have a rectrac account set up through www.playfrederick.com
Must complete the Participant Questionnaire including accommodation information
For 100% coverage: Adjusted Gross Income must be 300% or less of the federal poverty line for the most recent tax year
For 50% coverage: Adjusted Gross Income must be between 301% and 600% of the federal poverty line for the most recent tax year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested parties must set up a rectrac account by visiting www.playfrederick.com and clicking 'register for programs' to create a new account. Then complete the Participant Questionnaire with accommodation information and provide Adjusted Gross Income documentation from the most recent tax year. Funds will be distributed based on eligibility criteria and availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: A rotating exhibition series that showcases artwork from the City's collection and work by local artists through collaborations with nonprofits, arts organizations, schools, libraries, and community groups. The program emphasizes inclusivity by highlighting historically underrepresented communities. All exhibitions are free and open to the public and typically remain on display for one to three months.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City provides exhibition space and display opportunities for local artists' work. Exhibitions are free and open to the public, with typical display periods of one to three months. Artists and arts organizations are invited to submit exhibition proposals that align with the program's emphasis on community engagement and inclusive representation.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Laila Jadallah, Manager of Arts and Culture
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local artists, nonprofits, arts organizations, schools, libraries, and community groups seeking exhibition opportunities in Frederick, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Art exhibition and display at City Hall
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Artists and organizations must submit exhibition proposals
Proposals must align with the program's mission of inclusive representation and community engagement
Exhibitions must be free and open to the public
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested artists, nonprofits, arts organizations, schools, libraries, and community groups should submit an art exhibition proposal. Proposals are reviewed on a rolling basis by the City's Manager of Arts and Culture. Selected proposals will be scheduled for exhibition at City Hall with typical display periods of one to three months.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) (City of Frederick)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal funding program that provides grants to support community development projects and public services that benefit low- and moderate-income residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants awarded through the City of Frederick to support community development projects and public services that benefit low- and moderate-income residents. Two application tracks are available: Public Service Applications (for ongoing programs and services) and Bricks & Mortar Applications (for capital/infrastructure projects). Grant amounts vary based on project scope and community need.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ms. Rebecca Gramling, CDBG Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and government agencies serving low- and moderate-income residents in Frederick.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public services and bricks and mortar (capital) projects that benefit low- and moderate-income residents, including community facilities, infrastructure improvements, and social services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Must benefit low- and moderate-income residents
Activities must be eligible CDBG activities under federal guidelines
Must meet CDBG national objectives (primarily benefiting low- and moderate-income persons)
Applications must be submitted digitally by deadline
For Public Service applications: programs must serve low-to-moderate income residents
For Bricks & Mortar applications: projects must address community development needs
Applicants must demonstrate organizational capacity and financial stability
Projects must comply with federal environmental and procurement regulations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete either a Public Service Application or Bricks & Mortar Application form and submit it digitally to cdbg@cityoffrederickmd.gov by Friday, February 13, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. The City of Frederick offers technical assistance sessions to help applicants complete their applications. Applicants must provide detailed project descriptions, budgets, organizational information, and documentation of how the project benefits low- and moderate-income residents. Selected applicants will be notified and may be required to present their proposals.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Promotion Grant program awards funding to nonprofit charitable and civic organizations to supplement existing funds that either create or enhance services that positively impact the greatest number of City of Frederick residents. Partial funding may be awarded in lieu of a full award, and funding is distributed after July 1 of the fiscal year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program awards funding to nonprofit charitable and civic organizations to supplement existing funds that create or enhance services that positively impact the greatest number of City of Frederick residents. Awards are distributed after July 1 of the fiscal year. Partial funding may be awarded in lieu of a full award.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for FY 2027 close at an unspecified date after opening November 3, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit charitable and civic organizations serving City of Frederick residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To create or enhance services that positively impact the greatest number of City of Frederick residents
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must benefit City of Frederick residents. Organizations are based in or serving the City of Frederick area.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit charitable or civic organization
All applicants must attend one of two virtual information sessions (December 15, 2025 or January 15, 2026)
Must have all previous grant reporting up to date if previously funded
Must complete online application through Foundant platform
Grantees must submit interim report by January 31, 2027 and final report by July 31, 2027
Must supplement existing funds to create or enhance services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Program Overview document. Ensure all prior reporting is current if you received previous funding. Attend one of two mandatory virtual information sessions on December 15, 2025 or January 15, 2026. Complete the online application through the Foundant system. Submit interim report by January 31, 2027 and final report by July 31, 2027. Funding is distributed after July 1 of the fiscal year.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant-funded emergency weatherization program for homeowners and renters who currently lack a working heating or cooling system in their home. Heating assistance is available during winter months and cooling assistance is available during summer months. The program provides free HVAC upgrades and tune-ups to restore essential climate control systems.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free grant-funded emergency repair or replacement of heating and cooling systems (HVAC) and tune-ups for eligible homeowners and renters who currently have no working heating or cooling system. Heating funding is provided during winter months and cooling funding is provided during summer months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income homeowners and renters in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties who currently lack a working heating or cooling system and meet income thresholds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: HVAC system repairs, replacements, and tune-ups to restore functioning heating and cooling systems in homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners and renters in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties in Maryland.
requirements_list: Household income at or below the threshold based on household size (ranging from $68,500 for 1 person to $129,100 for 8 people)
Currently without a working heating or cooling system in the home
For renters: landlord permission and a signed building owner agreement required
For landlords: proof of ownership and signed building owner agreement required
Home must be in Frederick, Carroll, or Washington County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the City of Frederick Crisis Application form. The application will be reviewed and approved by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Once approved, HVAC upgrades and tune-ups will be completed at no cost to the applicant.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling, mediation support, and mortgage assistance application guidance

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for property owners who undertake historic preservation work on qualifying properties in Frederick.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit is available to property owners who complete approved historic preservation work on eligible properties in Frederick's historic districts and designated landmarks. The program provides a credit against City of Frederick tax liability for qualifying historic preservation work that meets the Secretary of the Interior Standards for Historic Preservation. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with application deadlines occurring at set intervals throughout the year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis with periodic deadlines throughout the year; refer to HPC Schedule for specific dates
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and their agents undertaking historic preservation work on properties in Frederick's historic districts or designated landmarks.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Historic preservation work on eligible properties, including renovation, restoration, and rehabilitation that meets the Secretary of the Interior Standards for Historic Preservation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties located within Frederick's historic districts or designated as historic landmarks by the City of Frederick.
requirements_list: Property must be located in a historic district or be designated as a historic landmark
Work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior Standards for Historic Preservation
Applicant must obtain a Certificate of Approval from the Historic Preservation Commission before beginning work
Complete application must be submitted through the online portal
For properties in historic districts, exterior work must be reviewed and approved before commencement
Documentation must include detailed plans, elevations, photographs, and product literature for all proposed work
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the Design Guidelines and the Historic Preservation Commission Schedule to understand the review process and deadlines. Contact a historic preservation planner for guidance on proposed work. Create an account through the OpenGov online portal at the provided URL. Submit a complete application online including all required documentation such as architectural plans, elevations, photographs of existing conditions, and product literature for materials and finishes. Attend a public hearing before the Historic Preservation Commission if required for your project type. Upon approval, obtain a Certificate of Approval from the Commission before applying for building permits or commencing work. Work must be completed and documented for tax credit verification.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free monthly workshops held on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Class size is limited to 40 participants. The program provides educational training in homebuying basics, credit management, and budgeting. Participants who complete both workshop sessions and an individual consultation receive a certificate that is required by most down-payment assistance programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers in all of Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational training in homebuying, credit management, and budgeting
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service area is all of Maryland
requirements_list: First-time homebuyer status required
Must attend both Tuesday and Thursday workshop sessions
Must complete individual credit and budgeting consultation
Must provide completed budget worksheet at individual consultation
Class size limited to 40 participants per session
No income limits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete application at frederickmd.gov/homebuyers. Register online to secure a spot in the class. Participants select their preferred workshop dates (Tuesday or Thursday sessions are offered monthly). Upon registration, participants will receive confirmation and details about class location and time. Attend both required workshop sessions and schedule an individual consultation with staff to complete the program and earn certification.

structured_extraction.program_name: Landlord/Tenant Rental Counseling – City of Frederick Housing Council
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Frederick Housing Council provides free counseling services to both landlords and tenants in Frederick County, helping them understand their rights and responsibilities under Maryland law. Counselors can review leases, explain security deposit requirements, guide clients through rent court procedures, and clarify the eviction process. Services do not constitute legal advice and are available at no cost with no income limits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free counseling and information services for landlords and tenants in Frederick County. Counselors provide guidance on lease reviews, security deposit requirements, rent court procedures, and the eviction process. Services do not include legal advice. No income limits apply and there is no cost for services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landlords and tenants in Frederick County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Information and counseling on tenant and landlord rights and responsibilities, including lease reviews, security deposit issues, rent court procedures, and the eviction process
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County only
requirements_list: Must be a landlord or tenant in Frederick County
No income limits apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact housing counselors Steven Rose or Tina Weedon to schedule an appointment at the Housing Counseling Office.

structured_extraction.program_description: Counseling for homeowners who are delinquent on mortgage payments to help them understand their options and determine the best course of action to protect their home and credit rating.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free counseling for homeowners delinquent on mortgage payments. No income limits. Service area is all of Maryland. Counselors help determine the best options to address delinquency and protect long-term credit rating. Counseling services are provided to help clients understand loss mitigation options, communicate with lenders, and develop strategies to retain homeownership or transition to alternative housing if necessary.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners delinquent on mortgage payments
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling and guidance on mortgage delinquency options, loss mitigation strategies, and communication with lenders
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service area is all of Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner delinquent on mortgage payments
Must complete the Mortgage Default/Client Intake Packet
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Mortgage Default/Client Intake Packet and submit to the Housing Counseling Office. Contact housing counselors Steven Rose at (301) 600-2077 or Tina Weedon at (301) 600-3974 to schedule counseling sessions. Services are provided on an ongoing basis with no application deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Pride Visibility Grants provide reimbursable funding to support the LGBTQ+ community in Frederick during Pride Month 2026. These grants help community organizations and civic groups organize LGBTQ+ pride events in June 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursable grants to support LGBTQ+ pride events and community visibility activities. Funding is available subject to the availability and approval of FY27 funding. Partial funding may be awarded in lieu of a full award. Funds are distributed after July 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations and civic groups organizing LGBTQ+ pride events in the City of Frederick.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To host and promote events that celebrate visibility, inclusivity and support for the LGBTQ+ community in June 2026.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Events must be hosted in June 2026 in the City of Frederick.
requirements_list: Host an event in June 2026 that promotes visibility, inclusivity and support for the LGBTQ+ community in the City of Frederick
Submit an event budget and project budget
Submit a final report by December 31, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit applications through the online grant portal. Applications must be submitted by May 1, 2026. Requests received via email, phone, or direct mail will not be reviewed. Grant awards will be announced and funds distributed after July 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides eligible youth under age 18 with 50% off all youth programs offered by the City of Frederick Parks and Recreation Department.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible youth receive 50% off registration fees for all youth programs offered by the Parks and Recreation Department.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth under age 18 who meet eligibility criteria and are residents of the City of Frederick.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Registration fees for youth programs offered by the Parks and Recreation Department.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick residents only. Youth must live in the City of Frederick.
requirements_list: Must be under age 18
Must be a City of Frederick resident

Must meet one of the following eligibility criteria: (A) eligible to receive free or reduced-price lunch through Frederick County Public Schools with proof of residency and FCPS letter, (B) live in household receiving Food Supplement Program (FSP) or Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) benefits with proof of residency and orange Independence Card, or (C) live in one of the three public housing communities (Carver, Lincoln, or Lucas Village) owned by the Housing Authority of the City of Frederick with proof of residency
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested citizens must provide proof of program eligibility according to the listed criteria, proof of City residency (driver's license, MVA-issued ID, water bill, or electric bill), and appropriate documentation. Registration is taken at the Wm. Talley Recreation Center Registration Desk at 121 North Bentz Street, Monday through Friday from 8:30 am to 6:30 pm. Once eligibility is approved, households may register at any time online, in person, or by phone, and the RRP fee reduction will automatically apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: HUD-required comprehensive counseling for senior homeowners 62 years or older considering reverse mortgages (Home Equity Conversion Mortgages). Counselors help seniors understand how reverse mortgages work, explore other options, and answer questions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individual appointment-based counseling for homeowners 62 years or older. Cost is $100, but fee may be waived based on income. No income limits. Service area is all of Maryland. Provides HUD-required comprehensive reverse mortgage counseling to help clients understand reverse mortgage products, alternative options, and make informed decisions about whether a reverse mortgage is appropriate for their situation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners 62 years or older interested in reverse mortgages
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling on reverse mortgage options and alternatives
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service area is all of Maryland
requirements_list: Must be 62 years or older
Must be a homeowner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the HECM/HECM Packet intake packet and contact housing counselors at (301) 600-2077 or (301) 600-3974 to schedule an individual appointment. Counseling sessions are conducted on an appointment basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: The SECURE Initiative provides one-time emergency bridge funding to eligible local nonprofits in Frederick who have experienced disruptions in state or federal grant funding and serve the city's most vulnerable residents by delivering critical services such as food access, housing support, healthcare, youth development, and mental health care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides one-time, flexible bridge funding in the form of grants. The total available funding is $700,000 with a maximum award of up to $50,000 per organization. Funds are non-renewable and intended to provide emergency relief for nonprofits that have experienced funding disruptions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations in good standing (501(c)(3) or other nonprofit classifications) operating in Frederick County and providing services to City of Frederick residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used flexibly to support community needs or essential services, including food access, housing support, healthcare, youth development, mental health care, and other critical services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must operate in Frederick County and provide services to City of Frederick residents.
requirements_list: Be a nonprofit organization in good standing, including 501(c)(3), other nonprofit classifications, or fiscally sponsored projects
Operate in Frederick County and provide services to City of Frederick residents
Deliver programs that support community needs or essential services
Have experienced a loss in state or federally funded grants and/or subgrants that disrupted program timelines or operations
Have lost a previously reliable funding source due to non-renewal, reduced awards, or policy changes
Demonstrate an increased demand for services compared to the same time last year due to specific federal cuts within a similar or adjacent service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Login or create an account on the City's application portal at grantinterface.com. Ensure all reporting is up to date if previous funding has been granted by the City. Starting October 15, 2025, eligible organizations can apply through the online portal. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until the March 31, 2026 deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: A local property tax credit supplement for eligible seniors administered by the State of Maryland as part of the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program. Homeowners who qualify for the state credit and meet additional local requirements receive a supplemental tax credit on their property taxes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A local property tax credit supplement administered by the State of Maryland. Eligible homeowners receive a supplemental tax credit applied to their property taxes. The City of Frederick provides an additional supplemental credit on top of the state credit for eligible residents. The state determines eligibility and processes both the state and city supplemental credits together. Homeowners must qualify for the state credit first to be considered for the city supplement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners aged 70 or older with combined gross household income of $40,000 or less (City of Frederick requirement) or not exceeding $60,000 (State of Maryland requirement) who own their principal residence in the City of Frederick.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit reduces property tax liability for eligible homeowners.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The dwelling must be the applicant's principal residence in the City of Frederick, where the applicant lives at least six months of the year including July 1, unless the applicant is a recent home purchaser or unable to do so due to health or need of special care.
requirements_list: Must be at least 70 years old as of the end of the calendar year preceding the taxable year for which credit is sought
Must have combined gross household income of $40,000 or less (City of Frederick requirement) and not exceed $60,000 (State of Maryland requirement)
Must own or have a legal interest in the property
The dwelling must be the principal residence where applicant lives at least six months of the year, including July 1, unless recent home purchaser or unable due to health or special care needs
Net worth must be less than $200,000, not including the value of the property, qualified retirement savings, or Individual Retirement Accounts
Must be qualified for the state tax credit
Must file for the state credit to be considered for the city supplement
Cannot claim the homestead property tax credit or any other tax credit for the same property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowners file for the state Homeowners' Property Tax Credit through the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. The State of Maryland determines eligibility for both the state credit and the city supplemental credit. If the applicant qualifies for the city supplement, the state processes both credits together and applies them to the property tax bill. There is no separate application required for the city supplement - qualification is automatic for eligible residents through the state application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Loan program funded by the City of Frederick's Community Development Block Grant from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. Provides affordable homeownership access by offering up to $25,000 in interest-free loans for down payment and closing cost assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Interest-free loan of up to $25,000 for down payment and closing cost assistance. No payments are required until the property is sold, refinanced, or is no longer the primary residence of the borrower. Funded by Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents interested in purchasing a home in the City of Frederick
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing cost assistance for home purchases
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick only
requirements_list: Must be a resident interested in purchasing a home in the City of Frederick
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact housing counselors for information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides residential tree planting assistance through a 50/50 cost share for containerized trees in the spring. The program helps residents plant trees to increase tree canopy, improve air and water quality, and potentially reduce energy costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City provides a 50/50 cost share for containerized native trees. Trees are pre-discounted to reflect the cost shared by the City of Frederick. Residents purchase trees at the reduced price, covering their 50% share, while the City covers the other 50%. Each resident can purchase up to 5 trees in one transaction during the program period. Trees must be planted on private residential property in appropriate locations in front or back yards.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 26th, 2026 or until all trees sell out
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Frederick residents who wish to plant trees on their residential property
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and planting of native containerized trees in residential yards to increase tree canopy and provide environmental benefits including improved air quality, water quality, and potential energy cost reduction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is limited to residents of the City of Frederick, Maryland. Applicants must provide their address and confirm city residency to participate. Trees must be planted on private residential property within the City of Frederick.
requirements_list: Must be a City of Frederick resident
Must have a valid address within the City of Frederick limits
Must plant trees in an appropriate location in front or back yard on private property
Each resident is permitted to purchase up to 5 trees
All trees must be ordered and purchased together in one transaction
Renters must have landlord permission to plant trees
Trees are containerized native species selected for Frederick area
Participation limited to one transaction per resident during the program period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Enter your address on the online portal to verify City of Frederick residency. Step 2: Review available native tree options and select the trees you wish to purchase (up to 5 trees). Step 3: Complete your order with all trees in one transaction, paying the discounted price that reflects the City's 50% cost share contribution. Step 4: Pick up your trees on March 28, 2026 at Harry Grove Stadium (21 Stadium Drive, Frederick, MD 21703). Step 5: Plant your trees on your residential property in an appropriate location.

structured_extraction.program_name: Utility Service Protection Plan (City of Frederick)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to income-eligible households to help pay utility bills and prevent utility service interruptions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance provided to help income-eligible households pay utility bills, prevent service interruptions, and minimize energy-related crises. Assistance is delivered through the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible households in the City of Frederick.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Utility bills and energy-related expenses to prevent service interruptions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Frederick, Maryland.
requirements_list: Household must be income-eligible
Applicant must reside in City of Frederick
Must demonstrate need for utility assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should contact the Office of Home Energy Programs at 301-600-2410 or submit an application form. Required documentation typically includes income verification, utility bills, and proof of residency. Spanish-language materials are available.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant-funded weatherization program that helps low- to moderate-income residents make their homes more energy-efficient by conducting a full home energy audit and performing work like air sealing, adding insulation, upgrading ventilation systems, replacing lighting fixtures, and upgrading appliances. Households that receive weatherization upgrades save an average of $372 or more each year on energy bills.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free grant-funded weatherization work performed on eligible homes, including air sealing, insulation improvements, HVAC system upgrades, energy-efficient lighting, health and safety improvements, and thermostat installation. The specific work performed is determined by a professional energy audit of the home. Work may include: weatherstripping doors and windows, caulking and sealing air leaks, foam gaskets behind outlet and switch plates, foam sealant on larger gaps around window trims and baseboards, fireplace damper sealing, insulation additions to attics and walls, mechanical ventilation system repairs or replacements, energy-efficient lighting fixture replacements, smoke and carbon monoxide detector installation, and programmable or smart thermostat installation. Average annual savings after weatherization is $372 or more per household on energy bills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income homeowners and renters in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties who meet income thresholds. Also available to nonprofits serving income-eligible clients.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency home improvements including air sealing, weatherstripping, caulking and sealing air leaks, insulation additions to attics and walls, heating and cooling system repairs or replacements, energy-efficient lighting fixtures, mechanical ventilation system upgrades, combustion appliance venting, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, and programmable or smart thermostat installation. Work is prioritized based on professional energy audit findings to address the greatest energy losses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to homeowners and renters in Frederick, Carroll, and Washington Counties in Maryland.
requirements_list: Household income at or below the threshold based on household size (ranging from $68,500 for 1 person to $129,100 for 8 people)
For renters: landlord permission and a signed building owner agreement required
For landlords: proof of ownership and signed building owner agreement required
For apartment buildings: no more than 4 units per building for State weatherization funds eligibility; buildings with more than 4 units reviewed case-by-case
Home must be in Frederick, Carroll, or Washington County

Income-eligible applicants on certain assistance programs (Energy Assistance, Maryland Fuel Assistance Fund, SNAP, DHCD Rehab, TANF, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, SSI, Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids, HUD housing assistance, or Medicaid) may qualify for abbreviated application process
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete and submit the City of Frederick Weatherization Program application form (available online or by request). 2. For income-eligible clients already receiving certain assistance programs (Energy Assistance, Maryland Fuel Assistance Fund, SNAP, DHCD Rehab, TANF, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, SSI, Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids, HUD housing assistance, or Medicaid), an abbreviated application is available. 3. Submit application with supporting income documentation. 4. City staff will review application and verify income eligibility. 5. Once approved, a qualified professional energy auditor will schedule and conduct a comprehensive home energy audit to identify which weatherization improvements are needed. 6. The audit evaluates the home's energy systems, conducts tests and inspections to locate air leaks and assess insulation needs, and provides prioritized recommendations. 7. Qualified contractors will perform recommended weatherization work. 8. After completion, final evaluation and testing may be conducted to verify work quality and energy savings.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Hagerstown allocates American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding to eligible nonprofit organizations for project proposals in priority areas including children and families, seniors, education, economic recovery, mental health, health and health disparities, and transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nonprofit organizations can receive grants up to a maximum of $50,000 per category. The City of Hagerstown has allocated $600,000 for this funding round. Funds must be used for projects in one or more of the following priority areas: Children and Families, Seniors, Education, Economic Recovery, Mental Health, Health and Health Disparities, or Transportation. Projects should address community needs and demonstrate measurable outcomes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) status seeking to fund projects in children and families, seniors, education, economic recovery, mental health, health and health disparities, or transportation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Project proposals in one or more of these categories: Children and Families, Seniors, Education, Economic Recovery, Mental Health, Health and Health Disparities, or Transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown, Maryland
requirements_list: Only nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) status are eligible to apply
Must submit IRS Nonprofit Designation Letter
Must provide Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) dated within past 30 days or dated screenshot showing current status
Must include Project Budget with all current and anticipated funding sources
Must provide evidence of active SAM.gov registration showing the Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
Individuals, businesses, sole proprietors, partnerships, limited liability corporations, and any other for-profit organizations or groups are not eligible
Project must clearly identify the priority funding area(s) it addresses
Applicant organization must demonstrate ability to execute the proposed project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a completed ARPA Funding Request Application form along with all supporting documents to grantsmail@hagerstownmd.org by 4:00 p.m. on September 1, 2023. Required supporting documents include: (1) IRS Nonprofit Designation Letter confirming 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(19) status, (2) Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland SDAT dated within the past 30 days or current status screenshot, (3) Detailed Project Budget clearly showing all current and anticipated funding sources, and (4) Evidence of active SAM.gov registration displaying the Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). Late submissions will not be accepted. Questions about the application process should be submitted via email to grantsmail@hagerstownmd.org by 4:00 p.m. on August 25, 2023 to allow time for responses. The City will review all applications and notify applicants of funding decisions following the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: An exemption from Maryland's Admissions and Amusement Tax for arts and entertainment enterprises located in the designated Arts and Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Enterprises dedicated to visual or performing arts within the Arts and Entertainment District are exempt from collecting Maryland's Admissions and Amusement Tax. Qualifying businesses receive a full exemption from the state admissions and amusement tax on admission charges to performances, events, and entertainment activities. Businesses must register with the Maryland State Comptroller's Office using the Comptroller of Maryland Combined Registration Application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Arts and entertainment enterprises located in the Hagerstown Arts and Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The exemption reduces tax obligations for qualifying arts and entertainment businesses, allowing them to retain more revenue from ticket sales and admissions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Enterprises must be located within Hagerstown's designated Arts and Entertainment District in Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Enterprise must be dedicated to visual or performing arts
Business must be located in the Arts and Entertainment District
Business must be engaged in activities that generate admissions revenue
Applicant must register with Maryland State Comptroller's Office using Combined Registration Application (Form CRA)
Qualifying activities include theater productions, concert performances, art exhibitions, dance performances, and other live entertainment events
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply for the Admissions and Amusement Tax Exemption: 1) Verify that your business is located within the designated Arts and Entertainment District; 2) Complete the Comptroller of Maryland Combined Registration Application (Form CRA); 3) Submit the application to the Maryland State Comptroller's Office; 4) Upon approval, your business will be exempt from collecting Maryland's Admissions and Amusement Tax on eligible admissions; 5) Maintain proper documentation of tax-exempt status for audit purposes.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps Maryland families pay overdue utility bills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Assistance to help pay overdue or arrearage utility bills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with overdue utility bills.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Overdue utility bills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland, with local contact information for Washington County.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at https://www.wccac.org/our-services/energy-assistance or schedule an appointment by visiting or calling Washington County Community Action Council at 117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740, or (301) 797-4161.

structured_extraction.program_description: A designated district that supports and encourages arts and entertainment businesses and activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Designation and support for arts and entertainment businesses and cultural activities in the district. The program provides technical assistance and support to businesses and organizations located within the designated Arts & Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.contact_name: City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department
structured_extraction.program_audience: Arts and entertainment businesses, cultural organizations, and retail establishments located within the City of Hagerstown Arts & Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Arts and entertainment business operations and activities, including support for cultural programming and district development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown Arts & Entertainment District, located in Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business or organization must be located within the designated Arts & Entertainment District boundaries
Engagement in arts, entertainment, or related retail activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department for more information about the program, eligibility requirements, and available support services for businesses located within the Arts & Entertainment District.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax incentives and benefits available to artists, arts entrepreneurs, and property owners who locate or renovate within Hagerstown's designated Arts & Entertainment District. Incentives include a 50% property tax credit for 10 years on the increase in property assessment resulting from renovation projects that create artist housing or space for arts and entertainment enterprises, as well as additional tax benefits for arts and entertainment enterprises operating within the district.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 50% property tax credit applied for 10 years on the portion of property assessment increase resulting from renovation projects that create artist housing or space for arts and entertainment enterprises within the district. The credit applies only to the portion of the building occupied by a qualifying residing artist or arts and entertainment enterprise, and cannot be used simultaneously with the Enterprise Zone property tax credit. Additional tax incentives and benefits are also available to arts entrepreneurs operating businesses within the designated Arts & Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Artists, arts entrepreneurs, and property owners locating or renovating within Hagerstown's designated Arts & Entertainment District in Washington County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for arts and entertainment enterprises including galleries, performance venues, restaurants, and other cultural businesses; renovation projects to create artist housing or space for arts and entertainment enterprises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be located within Hagerstown's designated Arts & Entertainment District in Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Locate arts and entertainment enterprise within the A&E District
Property must be located in the Arts and Entertainment District
Project must create artist housing or space for arts and entertainment enterprises
Tax credit applies only to the portion of building occupied by qualifying artist or enterprise
Cannot be combined with Enterprise Zone property tax credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department or Community Engagement Department for application details, eligibility verification, and information on how to apply for tax incentives.

structured_extraction.program_name: City Center Vacant Storefront Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to revitalize vacant storefronts in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District by bringing first-floor commercial spaces up to current code standards. The program supports renovation projects that decrease blight, preserve structures, and generate employment opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants with no minimum amount and a maximum of $50,000. Funds are disbursed only after staff verify all work has been completed to code, including required site inspection approvals, and final receipts have been provided. The program operates on a rolling basis with no set application deadline, allowing property owners to apply at any time.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers with vacant first-floor commercial spaces in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District seeking to renovate and occupy storefronts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovation and upgrade of vacant first-floor commercial spaces to bring them up to current code standards, including addressing code violations, structural repairs, and improvements needed to meet all federal, State, and local codes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to properties in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) Zoning District in Hagerstown, which is part of the City's Sustainable Communities Area. Priority given to projects in proximity to Public Square, particularly Main Street locations.
requirements_list: Property must be a vacant storefront in the Downtown City-Center Mixed-Use Zoning District
All projects must comply with federal, State, and local codes, laws, and ordinances
All upgrades must be performed to City Code standards
A detailed development plan outlining the renovation schedule and major project components must accompany the application
Final receipts and documentation of all expenses must be provided
All required site inspection approvals must be obtained prior to fund disbursement
Work must be verified as complete to code before funds are disbursed
Applicant must demonstrate ability to complete project and occupy space
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application form with a detailed development plan outlining the renovation schedule and major project components. A cross-department Review Committee will evaluate applications using criteria including economic impact, proximity to Public Square, renovation budget, square footage being revitalized, building condition, and length of prior vacancy. Approved applications receive a Letter of Commitment from the City which may assist in project financing. Once the renovation work is completed and verified to meet all code requirements through site inspection, final receipts are submitted, and funds are disbursed to the applicant.

structured_extraction.program_name: City Center and City-Wide Redevelopment Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the City of Hagerstown that provides funding to support redevelopment projects both in Hagerstown's city center and throughout the city. The City Center component offers grants ranging from $150,000 to $250,000, with total projects typically ranging from $450,000 to $750,000 or more. The City-Wide component offers smaller grants ranging from $5,000 to $25,000, with total projects typically ranging from $15,000 to $75,000 or more. Both components require a minimum 2:1 match from the developer.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two grant tiers are available: City Center grants ranging from $150,000 to $250,000 (total projects $450,000–$750,000+) and City-Wide grants ranging from $5,000 to $25,000 (total projects $15,000–$75,000+). Both tiers require a minimum 2:1 match from the developer. The City Center component targets redevelopment in the designated city center incentive zone, while the City-Wide component supports projects throughout the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and property owners undertaking redevelopment projects in Hagerstown's city center or throughout the City of Hagerstown
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Redevelopment and revitalization projects including site preparation, infrastructure improvements, building rehabilitation, adaptive reuse, and other eligible redevelopment costs in the city center or citywide throughout Hagerstown
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City Center and City-wide throughout Hagerstown, Washington County, Maryland. City Center projects must be located within the designated City Center Incentive Zone.
requirements_list: Minimum 2:1 match from the developer
Projects must demonstrate redevelopment potential and community benefit
Applicants must complete the application form and submit supporting documentation
Applications reviewed and approved by the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should review the full Guidelines and Application Form available on the city website. Submit completed applications to the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Applicants are encouraged to contact the Planning & Economic Development Department during the planning phase to discuss project eligibility and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: City Wide Down Payment and Rehabilitation Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program providing assistance for down payment and rehabilitation costs for properties throughout the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to assist with down payments and property rehabilitation costs. The program provides financial assistance to eligible property buyers and owners undertaking rehabilitation projects on properties within the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property buyers and property owners undertaking rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance and property rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A matching grant program administered by the City of Hagerstown that provides financial incentives to businesses and property owners to improve their commercial building's appearance through upgraded storefronts, signage, and façade elements. The program aims to enhance the City Center, support successful businesses, and improve the overall presentation of commercial and mixed-use buildings to the public.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a 50% matching grant for reimbursement of approved projects. Applicants must match the grant dollar-for-dollar (1:1 match). Commercial sign grants range from a minimum of $250 to a maximum of $1,500 per project (with matching funds, total project costs range from $500 to $3,000). Façade grants range from a minimum of $2,500 to a maximum of $7,500 per project (with matching funds, total project costs range from $5,000 to $15,000). The program is subject to funding availability and operates on a first-come, first-served basis. Funds are distributed as reimbursement upon completion of approved work.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis, subject to funding availability
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and property owners with commercial or mixed-use buildings in the City of Hagerstown, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects must pertain to commercial or mixed-use buildings and include improvements such as enhanced storefront designs, façade elements, and attractive signage to improve the building's presentation to the public. Eligible improvements include storefront renovation, signage installation or replacement, façade restoration, and other exterior appearance enhancements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown, Maryland. Priority may be given to properties located in designated incentive zones including Main Street and City Center areas.
requirements_list: Projects must pertain to commercial or mixed-use buildings
Applicants must provide a 1:1 matching contribution for the grant amount
Commercial sign minimum grant is $250; maximum is $1,500
Façade minimum grant is $2,500; maximum is $7,500
Property must be located within the City of Hagerstown
Work must be completed before reimbursement is processed
All work must comply with local building codes and regulations
Applicants should obtain approval of project plans prior to starting work
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should review the full program guidelines and submit the Commercial Sign & Façade Grant Application form. The application should include project description, cost estimates, and evidence of the applicant's matching funds commitment. Contact the DCED Team Members for pre-application consultation and approval of project plans. Upon project completion and submission of receipts and documentation, the City will reimburse the approved grant amount. Additional information is available by contacting the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department.

structured_extraction.program_description: A designated geographic area offering incentives to businesses that locate or expand within zone boundaries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Designation as an Enterprise Zone business with access to incentives and support services. The program provides businesses located or expanding in the designated Enterprise Zone with access to various state incentive programs and technical assistance resources available through the Maryland Department of Commerce and local economic development initiatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses locating or expanding in the Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General business operations and expansion within the zone. Businesses can access incentive programs available to Enterprise Zone designees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown, specifically the CC-MU Zoning area and the Enterprise Zone with expanded boundaries effective June 2021.
requirements_list: Location within the designated Enterprise Zone
Business must be for-profit entity
Must meet any additional requirements of specific incentive programs accessed through Enterprise Zone designation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department for more information and to inquire about specific incentive programs available to Enterprise Zone businesses. The city can provide guidance on accessing state and local incentives tied to Enterprise Zone designation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps property owners install or upgrade fire suppression systems by funding the installation of water service lines, meter vaults, water meters, and other utility infrastructure needed for National Fire Protection Association compliant fire suppression systems.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants range from a minimum of $7,500 to a maximum of $50,000. Applicants must provide a dollar-for-dollar match (1:1) from their own funds. Matching costs can include all work related to fire suppression system installation, both interior and exterior. For example, a $25,000 grant requires an additional $25,000 investment from the applicant for a total project cost of $50,000. The grant can be used for automatic sprinkler system installation, costs related to increased water service or fire lines, installation or upgrade of meter vaults, installation of new or upgrade and replacement of outdated sprinkler heads and piping, and replacement of mains and backflow devices.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications processed on a first-come, first-served basis subject to funding availability
structured_extraction.contact_name: Department of Planning and Economic Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners with residential, commercial, professional office, retail, or mixed-use buildings in Hagerstown's Sustainable Communities Area who are in good standing with the City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of automatic sprinkler systems, costs related to increased water service or fire lines, installation or upgrade of meter vaults, installation of new or upgrade and replacement of outdated sprinkler heads and piping, and replacement of mains and backflow devices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be within the City of Hagerstown's Sustainable Communities Area.
requirements_list: Fully residential, commercial, professional office, retail, or mixed-use projects
Projects within the City's Sustainable Communities Area
Applicants must be in good standing with the City of Hagerstown
Minimum 1:1 match from the applicant required
Fire suppression projects related to water service installations with service meters that are four inches or larger
Application must be aligned with the City of Hagerstown's overall vision for the city
Property owner must have a valid property address within the eligible area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Fire Suppression System Grant Application form along with required supporting documentation. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis subject to funding availability. Applicants should contact the Department of Planning and Economic Development for guidance on the application process and required materials.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Hagerstown Fire Department provides free smoke detectors and installation to eligible residents. This long-standing program is a cornerstone of fire prevention efforts in the city.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free smoke detectors are provided and installed at no charge. Eligible residents living in 1 to 3 family dwellings can receive one free smoke detector on each living level of their home. Residents of apartment buildings with 4 or more units should have electric detectors installed by their landlord in accordance with city code.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Hagerstown living in 1 to 3 family dwellings
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Smoke detectors for residential fire safety and early detection of unsafe conditions
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hagerstown city limits
requirements_list: Live in a 1 to 3 family dwelling in Hagerstown
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents can request free smoke detectors by clicking the online form link on the Prevention & Education page or by calling the fire department at (301) 790-2476.

structured_extraction.program_description: Offers up to $7,500 in down payment and closing cost incentives to reduce barriers to homeownership within the City of Hagerstown through a forgivable loan-to-grant program. The program supports neighborhoods by reducing vacant homes and boosting new homeownership.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $7,500 provided as a forgivable loan-to-grant program for down payment and closing costs. The funds are provided as a forgivable loan; no payments are required to the City if the borrower meets program conditions including occupying the property as a primary residence for a specified period. After the loan forgiveness period expires, the loan balance is forgiven.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prospective homebuyers purchasing property within the City of Hagerstown, including first-time homebuyers, current renters, and those purchasing vacant or underutilized properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing costs for home purchases within the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within the City of Hagerstown limits. Eligible property types include single-family homes, townhomes, and condominiums of any age.
requirements_list: Applicant must be purchasing or refinancing property within the City of Hagerstown
Application must be submitted at least 30 days prior to settlement/closing
Property can be any age (no age restriction)
First-time homebuyers receive priority consideration
Current renters and vacant property purchasers also receive priority consideration
Borrower must occupy the property as primary residence
Must meet income and credit eligibility requirements
No previous participation in this program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective homebuyers must submit the Hagerstown Homeownership Initiative Application at least 30 days before the scheduled settlement date. The City reviews applications for eligibility and program compliance. Priority consideration is given to first-time homebuyers and those purchasing vacant properties. Upon approval, funds are provided at closing to assist with down payment and closing costs as a forgivable loan.
