structured_extraction.program_description: A revolving loan fund administered by the City of Hagerstown that provides financing to small businesses, developers, and entrepreneurs for growth, expansion, rehabilitation, code compliance, facade enhancement projects, and general business development. The program offers standard loans, micro-enterprise loans, and working capital loans to eligible businesses located within the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $200,000 or 80% of total project cost (whichever is less), with a fixed interest rate of PRIME plus 1% (minimum 3%). Terms up to 7 years (5 years for working capital). Minimum loan is $5,000. Requires 20% cash equity investment of total project costs (40% for new restaurants open 3 years or less). Repayment begins within one month of project completion or equipment purchase. Micro-enterprise loans available up to $5,000. Working capital loans available up to $30,000. Application fee required based on requested loan amount.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and developers with annual business sales less than five million dollars organized as proprietorships, partnerships, limited liability companies, or corporations, located within the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land improvements, building purchase or renovation, machinery or equipment purchase, building construction, leasehold improvements, micro-enterprise activities, and working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown, Maryland
requirements_list: Business sales must be less than $5,000,000 annually for each of the last two years
Minimum 20% cash equity investment of total project costs (40% for new restaurants open 3 years or less)
Useful life of machinery or equipment must be at least five years
Leasehold term must be equal to or greater than the loan term, with city securing a lien on land, building, and improvements
Credit check required
Non-refundable application fee based on requested loan amount
Business must be located within City of Hagerstown limits
Primary occupation test may apply for proprietorships and partnerships
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application with required documentation to the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department. Required documentation includes business financial statements, personal financial statements, proof of equity funds, and evidence of collateral. A credit check will be conducted. Application fee is required based on the requested loan amount. Complete program guidelines and application form are available on the program website or from the Planning & Economic Development Department. Applicants are encouraged to contact Amanda Gregg for assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program that funds life safety improvements and infrastructure upgrades for buildings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for life safety infrastructure improvements and upgrades.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and managers seeking life safety improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Life safety infrastructure and building upgrades.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program providing funding to support small businesses and microenterprises in the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to support the startup and growth of small businesses and microenterprises. The program provides financial assistance to eligible applicants to help establish or expand their businesses within the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners and microentrepreneurs located in or planning to locate in the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business startup costs, operational expenses, equipment purchases, and other business development activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown, Maryland. Businesses must be located in or planning to locate within the city limits.
requirements_list: Must be a small business or microenterprise
Must be located in or planning to locate in the City of Hagerstown
Applicant must be a for-profit, non-profit organization or individual entrepreneur
Business plan or proposal required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department for detailed information about the application process, eligibility requirements, grant amounts available, and application procedures. The department will provide guidance through all stages of the application and evaluation process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that offers incentives to building owners to renovate buildings within the PEP Zone in Hagerstown's City Center, and assists with attracting businesses to renovated buildings. The program provides grants, utility benefits, parking discounts, rent assistance for tenants, fee waivers, expedited review, building code flexibility, and historic tax credit consultation. It also provides broader business support and partnership services to companies in the City of Hagerstown.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive an annual grant equal to City property tax for 5 years, 2 free EDU utilities valued at $13,800, 1 year free parking and 50% discount for 4 years, waiver of development fees (building permits, plan review fees, occupancy and zoning fees), expedited planning review, building code flexibility using Maryland Building Rehabilitation Code, and 2 hours of historic tax credit consultation paid by the City. Tenant businesses in eligible buildings receive rent assistance of up to $30,000 total over 2-3 years of operation. Rent assistance is contingent on application and City approval. Additional business support and partnership services are also available to companies in Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing program with no defined deadline
structured_extraction.contact_name: City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department
structured_extraction.program_audience: Building owners and businesses interested in renovating or leasing space within the PEP Zone in Hagerstown's City Center, as well as businesses operating in the City of Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building renovation and improvement; property owner receives property tax grants and utility/parking benefits; tenant businesses receive rent assistance for operating costs; business support and development activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the PEP Zone in the City Center of Hagerstown, Maryland. Eligible building addresses listed are: 34-36 and 38 South Potomac St., 54 South Potomac St., 138-140 West Washington St., 20 West Washington St., 5 Public Square, and 34 W. Franklin St. Broader business support services are available throughout the City of Hagerstown.
requirements_list: Project must be located within the PEP Zone in the City Center
Minimum investment of $250,000 for commercial properties, $100,000 for residential projects, or $200,000 for mixed-use projects (not including property acquisition costs)
Commercial projects must participate in the Enterprise Zone Program
Applicant must not be delinquent on any City or County taxes or other financial obligations to the City
Building and all core systems must meet all City of Hagerstown Code requirements
For residential and artist live-work spaces, minimum square footage requirements apply
Prior renovation projects eligible if completed after January 1, 2007
For businesses: must be new or existing business moving into PEP Zone or existing business expanding within it
Business must occupy first-floor retail or restaurant space, or non-storefront commercial spaces in PEP approved buildings

Eligible business types include: business, professional, cultural, and medical offices; professional schools; educational services; medical and diagnostic laboratories; motion picture and sound recording industries; photo finishing; radio and television broadcasting; telecommunications; visual and performing arts studios and galleries; light manufacturing; artist live-work units; fitness centers
Business must maintain a lease and operate for minimum of 4 years
Rent assistance contingent on application and City approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit the PEP Application and comply with eligibility criteria. Applicants must receive building permits and implement approved development plan. If approved, developer must submit progress reports every 6 months on project milestones and anticipated changes. At construction completion, report square footage per use type of renovated space. Annual reports to City required if applicable for Enterprise Zone Tax Credit amounts. Contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program for property owners to rehabilitate rental properties to market-rate standards. The program provides matching grants to support improvements to rental properties.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from a minimum of $7,500 to a maximum of $20,000 for individual projects. A 2:1 match from the developer is required. Projects receiving grants greater than $7,500 must include renovation of two or more units within a single property or parcel. Total project costs can range from $22,500 to $60,000 or more.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis, applications accepted continuously until funding is exhausted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers seeking to rehabilitate rental properties in Hagerstown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation and renovation of rental properties to bring them to market-rate standards, including but not limited to exterior repairs, roof replacement, window and door installation, interior improvements, and systems upgrades.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hagerstown, Maryland - properties must be located within the City of Hagerstown
requirements_list: Property must be located within the City of Hagerstown
Minimum 2:1 match from the developer required
Projects receiving grants greater than $7,500 require renovation of two or more units within a single property or parcel
Properties must be rehabilitated to market-rate standards
Property owner must maintain affordable rental rates or market-rate as applicable per program terms
Grant funds must be used for eligible property rehabilitation expenses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application form with project guidelines including project description, budget details, timeline, and proof of developer match commitment. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Complete program guidelines apply to all applications. Applicants should contact the City of Hagerstown for specific submission procedures and current availability of funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants for for-profit businesses located in the City Center Mixed-Use zone in Hagerstown, Maryland, to increase business efficiency, provide competitive advantage, and increase storefront beautification. The program supports spring and seasonal business initiatives and projects with funding for a range of eligible expenses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $750 per business for eligible expenses including storefront merchandising displays, planters and flowers, new office equipment or software and hardware, marketing or professional services, and other approved uses. Funds are provided as reimbursement after receipts are submitted and approved.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 22, 2026 or until all allocated program funds have been distributed
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses located in the City Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) zone in Hagerstown, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Storefront merchandising displays, planters and flowers, new office equipment or software and hardware, marketing or professional services, and other approved uses to increase business efficiency, provide competitive advantage, and increase storefront beautification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City Center Mixed-Use (CC-MU) zone in Hagerstown, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must be for-profit
Business must be located in the City Center Mixed-Use zone
Application must be submitted on or before May 22, 2026
Receipt for purchased products or services must be submitted before June 5, 2026
Company must provide Business Status from Maryland Business Express
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Fill out the Spring Sprout Grant Application form available from the City of Hagerstown. 2. Complete required vendor forms. 3. Print a copy of your company's Business Status from Maryland Business Express. 4. Submit the complete application package before May 22, 2026 to the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department. 5. If approved, proceed with purchasing the products or services specified in your application. 6. Submit all receipts for purchased items before June 5, 2026. 7. Upon verification of receipts, the City will disburse the approved grant amount to the business.

structured_extraction.program_name: Voluntary Crime-Free Multi-Housing Program (Landlord Crime-Free Training)
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive program designed to help owners and managers of rental properties in Hagerstown reduce drugs and illegal activity on their properties. The program includes a basic 4-hour introductory training course covering best practices for crime prevention at rental properties, as well as a full three-phase process consisting of management training, premises security assessments, and resident training. The program educates property owners and residents to improve neighborhood livability and reduce crime. While largely voluntary, some property owners and managers may be required to attend if their property receives a certain number of notices from the city.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free program consisting of a 4-hour management training course held at Washington County Free Library, Room 334. The program provides three phases: Phase 1 includes management training; Phase 2 includes premises security assessments; Phase 3 includes resident training. No cost to participants. Tools and techniques for property safety and community livability provided. No obligation to continue after initial enrollment. Classes require minimum registrations 48 hours before the scheduled start time; classes without registrations will be cancelled.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landlords, property owners, and managers of rental properties in Hagerstown seeking to reduce crime, illegal activity, and improve property management and neighborhood livability
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational training and technical assistance for crime prevention and property management improvement, including management training, security assessments, and resident education
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Hagerstown, Maryland (Washington County)
requirements_list: Own or manage rental property located in Hagerstown
Some property owners and managers may be required to attend based on receiving multiple city notices regarding criminal activity or violations on their property
Register 48 hours prior to class start time to ensure class is held
No obligation to continue after initial enrollment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Lt. John Lehman at the Hagerstown Police Department to register or enroll in the program. Provide contact information via phone at 301-797-6408 or email at jlehman@hagerstownpd.org. Complete and submit a registration form (available through the city website). Confirm attendance 48 hours before the scheduled class date. Classes are held at Washington County Free Library, Room 334. The program is free with no obligation to continue participation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Commissions works of site-specific public art to be installed on property owned by the City of Rockville. The program has been a driving force behind Rockville's cultural identity since 1978. Works of art reference historical, cultural, or socially relevant themes and reflect the city's dynamism and diversity. The program nurtures, inspires and expands citizens' awareness and educational experience with the visual arts, enhancing the community's uniqueness in Montgomery County and the metropolitan Washington area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program is funded by an annual appropriation based on the city's budget from the previous year. Funding commissions site-specific public art installations on city-owned property. The Art in Public Places (AIPP) ordinance provides funding equal to one-tenth of one percent of the prior year's adopted General Fund budget to be transferred from the General Fund to the Art in Public Places program, subject to appropriation by the Mayor and Council. The Incorporation of Works of Art in Public Architecture (AIPA) ordinance provides additional funding vehicles through capital improvement projects. All project budgets are all-inclusive, covering design, fabrication, installation, site enhancements, and a two-year warranty on the artwork, with no in-kind supplemental funding by the city. Unawarded designated AIPP funding carries over on a continuing basis from year to year subject to annual allocation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Artists and art professionals interested in creating site-specific public art commissions for the City of Rockville
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commission and installation of site-specific public art on city-owned property, including paintings, sculptures, engravings, carvings, frescoes, mobiles, murals, collages, mosaics, statues, bas reliefs, tapestries, photographs, drawings, stained glass, fountains, or other artworks for exterior and interior sites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland. Art projects focus on gateways into the city, metro stations (Rockville and Twinbrook Stations), Town Center, neighborhood parks, and key neighborhood sites.
requirements_list: Artists must be encouraged to work collaboratively with designers or contractors at the project site where appropriate
Safety considerations are important in all project selections
Works of art become the property of the city and part of the city's public art collection
All commissions include a two-year warranty on the artwork
Artists are responsible for completing projects within the all-inclusive budget
Both emerging and established artists are encouraged to participate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Art in Public Places program uses three selection process options: 1) Full and Open Competition - the most widely used and equitable process that solicits artists nationwide with emphasis on regional and emerging artists. An artist nomination committee is established typically composed of three CAC members (one serving as chair), two neighborhood/user group representatives, and two local/regional art professionals. The committee visits selected sites, develops project guidelines, and the city staff prepares a Call for Entries. Artists submit requested materials (CDs, videos, published works, written materials). The committee selects finalists who receive an honorarium to prepare detailed proposals including concept, design/scope, maquettes if appropriate, and detailed budget. Finalists present proposals at a public meeting where the committee makes recommendations to the CAC, which then makes recommendations to the Mayor and Council for final approval and award. 2) Limited Invitational Competition - a limited number of pre-selected artists identified by the artist nomination committee or CAC are invited to develop proposals. Artists receive honorarium and present to the committee for recommendation through the same process as Full and Open Competition. This process may be most appropriate for projects requiring collaboration between artist and architect, engineer, or landscape architect. 3) Direct Invitation - used rarely, only when there is consensus that one artist is particularly well qualified for a project, bypassing the competition process. This requires agreement from project committee, art consultant if relevant, staff, and CAC.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville Bike Rack Grant Program provides and installs basic, inverted-U style bicycle racks for businesses to enhance bikeway networks and support local commerce. The program aims to increase bike parking options for customers and employees at local businesses and to encourage bicycle riding for transportation. Racks are provided and installed for free on a first-come, first-served basis either in public rights-of-way or on private property with permission. The program is intended to improve bicycle parking availability near shops and offices for business owners who currently lack such amenities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Rockville purchases and installs basic, inverted-U style bicycle racks at no cost to eligible businesses on a first-come, first-served basis. Each applicant may request 1 or 2 racks. The racks are adequate for short-term parking and are intended for public use, available to anyone at any time. The City of Rockville Department of Public Works handles all procurement and installation, whether on public rights-of-way or private property with a signed agreement. The City of Rockville has the final decision over all decisions on adherence to specifications and rack locations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Business owners and property managers in Rockville who want to provide bicycle parking near their storefront or office, particularly those who do not currently have bicycle parking nearby.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of bicycle parking racks for short-term public bicycle parking, installed in public rights-of-way or on private property with a signed agreement between the City and property owner.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rockville city limits (Montgomery County, Maryland). Racks can be installed in public rights-of-way or on private property with a signed agreement. The City of Rockville has final decision on rack locations.
requirements_list: Business must be located in Rockville city limits
Business owner or property manager must apply (applicant must be the liaison between City and property owner if private property)
Business must not have adequate bicycle parking on site
Each bicycle rack requires a parking space of at least 72 inches by 24 inches
If racks are placed along a sidewalk or pedestrian path, there must be at least a five-foot clear walkway once the bicycle racks have been installed
Racks installed are meant for public use and can be used by anyone at any time
Applicant may request 1 or 2 racks per application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, complete the Bike Rack Grant Program application form and submit it by email to bikeways@rockvillemd.gov or by mail to City of Rockville Bicycle Rack Grant Program, c/o Bryan Barnett-Woods, 111 Maryland Avenue, Rockville, MD 20850. Include a description of existing bike parking on site, the number of racks requested (1 or 2), and optionally a location suggestion with a photo. Once DPW staff reviews your application, they will contact you to discuss the project. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. You will be notified if you qualify for the program once your application is received.

structured_extraction.program_description: A cooperative group purchase program that helps residents and small business owners install solar panels on their roofs or lease them. The co-op works with local nonprofits and community partners to secure discounted pricing (typically about 20% lower than standard rates) for rooftop solar systems. Battery storage and electric vehicle charger options are also available through the program.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program secures group purchase discounts of approximately 20% below market rates for rooftop solar installation or leasing. Battery storage and electric vehicle charger options are included. Participants can choose to purchase or lease panels based on group pricing. Low- to moderate-income residents may also qualify for the Maryland Solar Access Grant Program offering up to $7,500 per system. Financing and leasing options are available for all income levels.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents and small business owners in the Rockville area who want to install or lease solar systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Solar panel installation or leasing for rooftops. Battery storage options. Electric vehicle charger options.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Capital Area Solar Switch Together program serves the Capital Area, which includes Rockville and surrounding regions in Maryland.
requirements_list: Residence or small business located in the service area
Roof or suitable property for solar installation
Registration on the contact list
Completion of roof evaluation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up for the contact list at solarswitch.com to register. The program will assess whether your roof is suitable for solar. After roof evaluations, members receive individual proposals and can choose whether to sign a contract with the installer. The decision deadline for the spring 2026 program is August 19, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program that funds housing and community development projects benefiting low- and moderate-income households or neighborhoods. In FY 2027, the City of Rockville prioritizes capital and physical improvements, excluding public services.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants fund housing rehabilitation, community development projects, and improvements that benefit low- and moderate-income residents. FY 2027 allocated funding for capital and physical improvements including home rehabilitation, facility upgrades, improvements to public facilities, economic development activities, and historic preservation. Minimum grant amount is $15,000. Applicants are encouraged to leverage CDBG funds with other funding sources. CDBG funds must be expended within a 12-month period. Recipients must maintain commercial liability insurance, comply with federal and county regulations including Davis-Bacon requirements (for construction/rehabilitation of 8+ unit residential properties or commercial buildings), Section 3 requirements for employment and business opportunities, Minority Business Enterprise participation requirements, environmental review requirements including radon testing assessment, and historic preservation review. Quarterly reporting on individuals/households served is required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations with 501(c)(3) IRS designation and government/quasi-governmental agencies seeking to fund housing and community development projects that benefit low- and moderate-income households or neighborhoods in Rockville. Government agencies are encouraged to partner with local nonprofit organizations as primary applicant.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing rehabilitation, acquisition and clearance of land for housing, acquisition and rehabilitation of rental housing, direct homeownership assistance (down payment/closing cost assistance), development of housing for homeless or formerly homeless individuals, improvements to public facilities and community facilities with accessibility improvements, economic development activities, and historic preservation activities. Public services and administrative costs for social services programs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rockville, Maryland
requirements_list: Projects must benefit low- and moderate-income households or neighborhoods; applicants must verify beneficiaries meet HUD income limits
Non-profit applicants must have 501(c)(3) IRS designation or have designation in place by July 1, 2026
Project must propose a CDBG-eligible activity (excluding public services)
Minimum grant amount request is $15,000
Davis-Bacon requirements apply to construction/rehabilitation of commercial buildings or residential properties with 8 or more units
Section 3 requirements mandate affirmative action for employment, training, and business opportunities for low-income project area residents and businesses
Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) participation and outreach required in bidding process for construction/rehabilitation projects
Environmental review by Montgomery County required prior to project work beginning
Radon testing consideration required as part of environmental review; mitigation required if levels at 4.0 pCi/L or greater (Montgomery County is Zone 1 with average levels greater than 4 pCi/L)
Historic preservation review (SHPO) by Montgomery County required prior to project work beginning
Commercial liability insurance meeting City and Montgomery County requirements with certificate of insurance required
Compliance with federal, county, and city regulations for financial management of CDBG funds
Quarterly reporting on number of individuals/households served including demographic information
CDBG funds must be expended within 12-month period; unspent funds may be recaptured
Submit separate application for each funding request
Complete all application information without altering content or format of questions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Contact Sarah Maizel at 240-314-8304 or smaizel@rockvillemd.gov prior to submission to confirm project eligibility. 2) Review FY 2027 CDBG Application Instructions and eligible activities fact sheet. 3) Attend virtual technical assistance sessions (dates to be announced). 4) Complete online application using required forms including CDBG Project Budget Form. 5) Submit application online by Monday, October 17, 2025 at 5:00 P.M. using both Completeness Checklist and Attachments Checklist to ensure application is complete. 6) Incomplete applications with minor omissions will be returned; applicants given 7 calendar days to provide missing information. 7) If approved by Mayor and Council, notification will be provided by December 31, 2025. 8) Approved applications submitted to Montgomery County; county staff make recommendations to County Executive in January/February 2025. 9) Applications incorporated into County budget approval process. 10) Funds available after October 1, 2026. Note: Projects may receive smaller funding amounts than requested.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that helps neighbors and community organizations work together to accomplish common goals that support the health, vitality, and inclusivity of their community. The program funds projects focused on building community, improving shared spaces, or strengthening social connections through education and outreach.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive matching grants ranging from $500 to $1,000. Applicants must match funding through cash, in-kind donations, or volunteer hours valued at $29.95 per hour. The total matching funds must equal or exceed the amount requested. All funds are subject to taxes. Funds must be used by December 14, 2026, and any unused funds must be returned to the City of Rockville by December 18, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Neighbors, community organizations, neighborhood associations, civic associations, homeowners associations, student groups, and community groups with at least three members located within Rockville city limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Programs or projects that promote community building, enhance shared neighborhood spaces, or strengthen community identity and social connections. Eligible uses include heritage celebrations, neighborhood improvement projects, education and outreach efforts, increasing safety, addressing neighborhood challenges, serving low-income residents, or welcoming newcomers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants and projects must benefit those who live within Rockville city limits.
requirements_list: Each group must have at least three members
One individual must be designated to manage the grant contracts and funds
If applying on behalf of an established organization, documentation of authorization must be provided
Projects must address at least one of the three objectives: building community, community improvement projects, or livability initiatives
Matching funds must be provided through cash, in-kind donations, or volunteer hours valued at $29.95 per hour
Total matching funds must equal or exceed the amount requested
All funds are subject to taxes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Download and complete the Community Empowerment Matching Grant Budget Worksheet to estimate costs and matching funds. 2) Create an account on the online grant portal and complete the eligibility form to determine if your project qualifies. 3) Complete and submit the full application by 11:59 p.m. on December 5, 2025. 4) Award notifications are sent by February 13, 2026. 5) Grant recipients submit project documentation including receipts, at least two visual items, and a brief report by December 18, 2026. 6) Any unused funds must be returned to the City of Rockville by December 18, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Services and Enrichment Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville provides grants annually to local nonprofit organizations that partner with the city to support community services and enrichment programs that benefit city residents and visitors. This program combines the former Human Services Nonprofit Grant and Community Organization Grant Programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $1.5 million in combined funding is awarded annually. Approximately 40 applicants are typically awarded grants. Funding is provided on a reimbursement basis for expenses incurred per the grant budget, with quarterly invoices required. Organizations must submit quarterly reports (July-September, October-December, January-March, April-June) within specified deadlines, a six-month program measures report due January 15, 2026, and a year-end program measures report due after July 4, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations providing human services or community enrichment programs to individuals residing in Rockville city limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community services and enrichment programs that benefit city residents and visitors. Funds support a wide range of services including but not limited to: scholarship programs, emergency response/safety services, theater and arts programming, cultural festivals, arts and science education, historic preservation, clothing distribution, elderly/disabled support services, food distribution, health care, information and referral services, language and citizenship education, mental health services, parenting support, youth development, housing services, and job training and placement services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only organizations serving individuals residing within the corporate city limits of Rockville are eligible. Organizations must verify that their services benefit Rockville residents, and the City may request client identifiers (initials or case numbers, not names) and addresses to verify Rockville residency of the service population.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must provide human services or community enrichment programs to individuals residing in Rockville city limits
Must complete Eligibility Form and pass eligibility quiz
Must attend one of four mandatory virtual technical assistance sessions held in September and early October
Must provide audit, financial statement, or compilation for most recent completed operating year
Must provide IRS Form 990 for most recent completed operating year
Must provide board roster identifying officers, term limits, addresses, and phone numbers
Must provide report from last formal and/or informal program evaluation if applicable
Must submit Document of Application Submission Authority signed by Executive Director and Board President on organization letterhead
Must submit Budget, Outputs, and Outcomes Worksheet
Must be able to provide supporting documentation with quarterly invoices
Must meet quarterly reporting deadlines (reports due after October 1, January 1, April 1, and July 1 for Q1-Q4 respectively)
Must meet six-month program measures report deadline (January 15, 2026)
Must meet year-end program measures report deadline (after July 4, 2026)
Must reply to all City of Rockville communications within 10 weekdays
Must comply with HIPAA regulations if a healthcare provider; if not, must obtain signed client authorization to share client address for grant reporting purposes
Must obtain and maintain required insurance coverage during contract term, including certificates of insurance prior to contract execution
Must maintain insurance as primary coverage with City's insurance as excess
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review eligibility requirements and complete the eligibility quiz to determine program qualification. 2. Attend one of four mandatory virtual technical assistance sessions: Tuesday, September 9, 10:00-11:00 a.m.; Wednesday, September 17, 2:00-3:00 p.m.; Wednesday, September 24, 4:00-5:00 p.m.; or another scheduled session. 3. Create an account in the online grant portal and complete the Eligibility Form to confirm qualification. 4. Complete the full application including: program description, logic model, unit of service definitions, outputs and outcomes by service area, budget and expenses, revenue sources, and all required supplemental documents. 5. Upload all required documents including financial statements (audit, financial statement, or compilation), IRS Form 990, board roster, program evaluation reports (if applicable), Document of Application Submission Authority, and Budget/Outputs/Outcomes Worksheet. 6. Submit completed application by October 17, 2025 deadline through the online portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville waives all permit fees assessed by the Inspection Services Division that are directly associated with the residential installation of solar photovoltaic systems, electric vehicle charging stations, and energy-efficient heating and cooling upgrades, such as heat pumps.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The city waives all permit fees assessed by Rockville's Inspection Services Division for eligible residential installations. Eligible projects include: Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Systems - installation of solar panels, inverters, conductors, disconnects, transfer switches, overcurrent devices, and other critical system components; upgrades to electrical panels and associated service equipment necessary to accommodate solar PV installation; and installation of Energy Storage Systems (ESS) up to 20kWh. Structural modifications are not included. Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Systems - installation of EV charging receptacles, packaged charging cord outlets, conductors, disconnects, and overcurrent devices; upgrades to electrical panels and associated service equipment; but not structural modifications, site modifications such as driveways, or right-of-way permits. Geothermal HVAC Upgrades - installation of geothermal and/or high-efficiency heat pump HVAC systems including associated electrical work and duct installation/modification; upgrades to electrical panels and associated service equipment; but not structural modifications. This is a temporary waiver offered during April as part of Earth Month celebration.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted by Thursday, April 30 and must be accepted by city staff by 5 p.m. Friday, May 1
structured_extraction.contact_name: Community Planning and Development Services Department, Inspection Services Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Rockville with single-family residential projects who are installing solar photovoltaic systems, electric vehicle charging stations, or energy-efficient heating and cooling upgrades such as geothermal or high-efficiency heat pump systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permit fees for residential installation of solar photovoltaic systems, electric vehicle charging stations, and energy-efficient heating and cooling upgrades such as geothermal or high-efficiency heat pump systems, including associated electrical panel upgrades and service equipment modifications necessary to accommodate these installations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville only. Single-family residential projects only; commercial and multifamily residential projects are not eligible.
requirements_list: Installation must be single-family residential only (commercial and multifamily residential projects are not eligible)
Installation must be one of the following: solar photovoltaic system, electric vehicle charging station, or geothermal/high-efficiency heat pump HVAC system
For solar PV systems: structural modifications are not included in the waiver; installation of Energy Storage Systems (ESS) up to 20kWh are included, but ESS over 20kWh are not eligible
For EV charging systems: structural modifications, site modifications (such as driveways), and right-of-way permits are not included in the waiver
For geothermal HVAC upgrades: structural modifications are not included in the waiver
For solar installations on roofs: a statement from a licensed engineer verifying that the existing structure is capable of supporting the proposed array is required
Permit application must include plans that clearly identify the location, nature, and extent of the proposed work
Application must be submitted by April 30, 2026
Application must be accepted by city staff by 5 p.m. on May 1, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a permit application through the City of Rockville's permit page at https://www.rockvillemd.gov/services/apply-for-a-building-or-trade-permit/ or directly through MGO Connect at https://www.mgoconnect.org/cp/portal if you have an existing account. Your application must include a set of plans that clearly identify the location, nature, and extent of the proposed work. For rooftop solar panel installations, include a statement from a licensed engineer verifying that the existing structure is capable of supporting the proposed array. Submit your application by April 30, 2026; it must be accepted by city staff by 5 p.m. on May 1, 2026. Once submitted, City of Rockville staff will process the fee waiver on your behalf. You will receive an email notification confirming that your permit has qualified for the waiver.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rebate program for the purchase of electric leaf blowers for landscapers and residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landscapers with revenue under $250,000 annually or five or fewer employees can receive up to $1,500 in one 12-month period. Landscapers with revenue over $250,000 or six or more employees can receive up to $1,000 in one 12-month period. Residents can receive up to $100 for one rebate. Rebates apply to equipment purchased after the program is open.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landscapers and residents
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of electric leaf blowers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville offers an online, same-day express process that allows eligible residential permits to be reviewed and issued within the same business day.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Express Permit Program provides an online, same-day review and issuance process for eligible residential permits. Applications are accepted on Tuesdays from 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. and are processed within the same business day.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on Tuesdays from 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Community Planning and Development Services Department, Inspection Services Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Rockville seeking expedited permit processing for eligible projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible residential permit applications including residential fence, accessory structure, mechanical, and water heater permits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville only
requirements_list: Project must be residential
Project must be on the list of eligible projects
Application must be submitted on a Tuesday between 8:30 a.m. and 12:30 p.m.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Express Permit Program page to see the list of eligible projects. Submit your application through MGO Connect on a Tuesday between 8:30 a.m. and 12:30 p.m. Your permit will be reviewed and issued on the same business day.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides financial assistance through matching reimbursement funds to residents and property owners in Rockville who have made improvements to their properties to reduce future damage from flooding events. Up to 50 percent of total costs for approved flood mitigation measures are reimbursed, with a maximum of $5,000 per property, distributed on a first-come, first-served basis.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to 50 percent reimbursement of total costs for approved flood mitigation measures, with a maximum reimbursement of $5,000 per property. Itemized receipts or invoices are required for reimbursement. Approved measures include sandless sandbags, flood socks, permanent flood doors, protective flood walls, impermeable materials around foundations, French drain systems, window protection, doorway flood stoppage equipment, basement protective materials, utility protection measures, surface grading, earthen berms, and other flood-proofing improvements. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis through matching reimbursement to property owners and residents who have made improvements to mitigate future flooding damage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents and property owners in Rockville seeking to mitigate flood damage to their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Improvements to properties that mitigate future damage from flooding events, including approved flood-proofing measures such as protective flood walls, French drain systems, window and doorway protection, flood stoppage equipment, utility protection, basement improvements, surface grading, earthen berms, sandless sandbags, flood socks, permanent flood doors, and other protective materials and equipment designed to reduce future flood-related damage.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a property owner or resident in Rockville
Must have made approved improvements to mitigate future flooding damage
Itemized receipts or invoices are required for reimbursement
Only approved flood mitigation measures will be reimbursed
Property must be located within City of Rockville boundaries
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website at cbtrust.org. Applicants should submit itemized receipts or invoices for approved flood mitigation improvements. The Chesapeake Bay Trust reviews and processes all applications. For more information on eligibility criteria and a list of approved flood-proofing measures, visit rockvillemd.gov/floodassistance. Additional details are available at the City of Rockville program application page at rockvillemd.gov/apply-for-flood-mitigation-assistance/.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides one-time financial assistance to eligible City of Rockville residents who live in homes with documented energy inefficiencies. It helps residents access local and statewide weatherization services, home energy assessments, and comprehensive energy audits, and supplements up to $1,000 for utility efficiency retrofits. The program includes referral to additional public and private resources to help supplement the financial assistance provided.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time financial assistance of up to $1,000 for qualifying energy-efficient home retrofits, including insulation, air infiltration reduction, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace maintenance and cleaning, and health and safety improvements such as moisture remediation, mold remediation, asbestos abatement, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, radon mitigation, roof repair and replacement, plumbing and electrical repair, structural repair, and lead hazard removal. Applicants must first be approved for Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP), EmPOWER Maryland Low-Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP), Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP), or Enhanced Weatherization Program. Past-due utility bills and non-energy-efficient household repairs are not eligible for assistance. The DHCD match amount is provided based on client contribution and program approval.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Housing and Community Development Department, Community Services Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Rockville residents who have documented energy inefficiencies in their primary residence and meet 60 percent average median income (AMI) guidelines and who are previous or new Emergency Assistance Program recipients. Program is designed for both homeowners and renters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy-efficient upgrades including insulation, air infiltration reduction, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and safety repairs, health and safety items (moisture and mold remediation, asbestos abatement, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, radon mitigation, roof repair and replacement, plumbing and electrical repair, structural repair, lead hazard removal, and approved electrical repairs). Can also address energy efficiency concerns including consistently high utility bills, water leaks, poor insulation, and leaks in building envelope.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must reside within the corporate city limits of Rockville and must have lived in Rockville for at least six months prior to application. Program is limited to residents served by PEPCO, BGE, Delmarva Power, SMECO, or First Energy.
requirements_list: Reside in the corporate city limits of Rockville at the time of application and for at least six months prior (180 days)

Meet 60 percent AMI guidelines based on 2018 income eligibility requirements (1-person: $24,280; 2-person: $32,920; 3-person: $41,560; 4-person: $50,200; 5-person: $58,840; add $8,640 for each additional person)
Be a previous or new Emergency Assistance Program recipient
Use electricity or natural gas for energy and heating purposes
Be a PEPCO, BGE, Delmarva Power, SMECO, or First Energy customer
Be either a renter or homeowner (renters must provide written landlord verification and documentation that landlord approves energy-efficient retrofits)

Have already applied and been approved for one of the following: Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP), EmPOWER Maryland Low-Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP), Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP), or Enhanced Weatherization Program
Provide documentation of three months of utility bills (water, gas, electric)
Provide documentation of a comprehensive home energy audit
Provide proof of home ownership OR current lease dated and signed
Provide one other proof of residency (utility bill, etc.)
Provide signed affidavit of income
Provide monthly budget
Provide driver's license or other photo ID with address for all adults in household
Provide Social Security Number/TIN Card for all family members
Provide two most recent paystubs for all adults
Provide documentation of any other income for all adults (Social Security, SSI, unemployment, child support, etc.)
Provide tax form 1040 from previous year for all adults
If applicable, provide documentation of portion of rent paid by client and RHE/HOC or other housing assistance
Agree to reside at the retrofitted property for one year post-retrofit
Provide documentation of three months of utility bills post-retrofit as defined in the service agreement
Use the retrofitted property as your primary residence (with limited exceptions requiring community services manager approval)
Demonstrate that previous rent payments have been made for the property being assisted
Have not filed a federal income tax return or provide evidence of filing and household income
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review eligibility criteria, eligible expenses, and ineligible expenses. Complete the Home Energy Assistance Program Application form (Pages 1-3) and return it to the Community Services Division at hcd@rockvillemd.gov or in person at 111 Maryland Avenue, Rockville, MD 20850. Prepare required documentation including photo ID, SSN card, income documentation, proof of residency, home energy audit documentation, and a signed affidavit of income. Submit completed application with all documentation. The community services referral coordinator will refer residents to appropriate available public and private resources as needed. Intake staff will verify address using SDAT property search, code enforcement, RHE/HOC, property management company, or other documentation. A HEAP counselor will be assigned for application processing. Once approved, a Payment Approval Form is submitted and a check is issued to the contractor or other approved payee.

structured_extraction.program_name: Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Homeownership Program - City of Rockville
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville requires some for-sale properties to be available to Rockville residents at more affordable prices than market-rate homes. The program helps first-time homebuyers purchase homes at reduced prices with a 30-year affordability period. Properties are offered at affordability levels based on 50%, 60%, or 80% of Area Median Income (AMI). The program is administered by the City of Rockville and aims to ensure long-term affordable homeownership opportunities for qualifying individuals and families.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The city designates certain for-sale properties to be sold at affordable prices to qualified first-time homebuyers. Properties are offered at reduced market rates based on affordability levels (50% AMI, 60% AMI, or 80% AMI). Buyers commit to a 30-year affordability period and must maintain the home as their primary residence. During the 30-year control period, owners must live in the MPDU as their primary residence and cannot rent the property without written city permission. If the MPDU is sold before the end of the 30-year control period, the seller can claim credit for permanent improvements (limited to 10% of the original purchase price), and a new 30-year control period commences for the next owner. Rockville Housing Enterprises has the right of first refusal on resales. After the 30-year control period expires, the original owner must pay 50% of the profit from the first sale on the open market to the City's Affordable Housing Fund. The owner cannot own a second home while owning the MPDU.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers who are Rockville residents or who work in Rockville and meet income limits
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of a moderately priced dwelling unit to be used as the buyer's primary residence
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The buyer must currently live or work in the City of Rockville to receive priority on the waiting list, though eligibility is not limited to Rockville residents only. Priority is given to households with members who currently live or work in Rockville, have a member older than 55, or have a larger household size.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time homebuyer (not owned a home or been on deed to a home in the past 5 years)
Must qualify for a minimum mortgage of $150,000
Home must be owner's primary residence for the full 30-year MPDU period and may not be rented without written City permission
Must qualify for bank financing
Must commit to own the home for 30 years (sales before this period must follow city guidelines and cannot exceed approved resale price)
All household members over 18 must submit proof of income
Household income must be within specified limits based on AMI (50%, 60%, or 80%) at time of sales agreement
Must attend a First-Time Homebuyer Class (Montgomery County's six-hour class or HUD-approved counseling agency)
Must obtain a Mortgage Pre-Approval Letter from a bank lender (on company letterhead, notarized, valid for one year)
Must complete the MPDU Homeownership Program Application and receive a Certificate of Eligibility (renewed every two years)
Cannot own another residential property during the control period
Must occupy the MPDU exclusively as primary residence; any interior or exterior alterations require permits from Department of Planning and Development Services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Attend a First-Time Homebuyer Class through Montgomery County's Housing Initiative Partnership or a HUD-approved counseling agency and obtain a completion certificate. Step 2: Obtain a Mortgage Pre-Approval Letter from your bank lender using the city's sample lender letter (form must be on company letterhead and notarized; pre-qualification is valid for one year). Step 3: Complete the MPDU Homeownership Program Application online or request a hard copy or PDF version. The application is reviewed and an MPDU Certificate of Eligibility is sent by email within three to four weeks. The household is then placed on the city's MPDU waiting list. When MPDUs become available, sellers or developers contact waiting list households about purchasing. Priority is given to households with members who currently live or work in Rockville, have a member older than 55, or have a larger household size. Upon purchase, buyer must sign the MPDU Purchaser Agreement acknowledging the 30-year control period, covenants, and City Code Chapter 13.5 requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Rental Program - City of Rockville
structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Rockville offers affordable rental units to income-eligible households through its Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit (MPDU) Program. Renters can access below-market rental apartments in properties throughout the city and may use Housing Choice Vouchers to help pay rent. The program aims to provide affordable rental housing options for low- and moderate-income individuals and families in Rockville, Maryland. Designated rental units are required to remain MPDUs for a period of either 30 or 99 years, depending on the date of first rental.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rent-regulated affordable housing units available at below-market rates. Monthly rental rates as of July 1, 2025 range from $1,322 for studios to $1,890 for three-bedroom units in older buildings, and $1,400 to $1,999 in newer buildings. Maximum household income eligibility for FY 2026 ranges from $68,840 for single-person households to $106,210 for five-person households. Housing Choice Vouchers can be applied toward rent payments. Amenity fees are subject to individual property MPDU program agreements. MPDU tenants cannot be charged fees for non-structured parking; structured parking may be offered at no more than 50% of market rate for the first space and full charge for additional spaces. Monthly pet fees and storage fees may apply if charged to market-rate tenants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling admission; applications accepted on a first-come, first-served basis as units become available
structured_extraction.contact_name: Housing Programs Division, Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible individuals and families seeking affordable rental housing in Rockville, including persons currently living in Rockville, persons currently working in Rockville, and persons over age 55 (who receive priority consideration during initial 90-day offering period)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing payments for moderately priced dwelling units
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland. Priority is given during the initial 90-day offering period to eligible persons who are currently living within the corporate boundaries of the City of Rockville, currently working within the corporate boundaries of the City of Rockville, or are over the age of 55.
requirements_list: Household gross annual income must not exceed maximum limits based on family size (ranging from $68,840 for one person to $106,210 for five people as of FY 2026)
Household income must be at least 2.5 times the MPDU rent adjusted for bedroom count
MPDU must be the household's primary place of residence; subleasing is prohibited unless written permission is granted by the Department of Housing and Community Development
No household member can currently own or have owned residential property within the last five (5) years in the DMV area
Family size includes dependents claimed on submitted federal tax forms and any minor children in the household (birth certificate required if child not listed on tax return)

Household size must comply with bedroom size requirements: 1 person eligible for studio or 1-bedroom; 2 persons for 1 or 2-bedroom; 3 persons for 2 or 3-bedroom; 4 persons for 2 or 3-bedroom; 5+ persons for 3+ bedroom units
Applicants must submit two most recent years of federal tax returns with W-2s for all adults; if no taxes were filed, a Verification of Non-Filing form from the IRS is required
Applicants must submit two most recent paystubs for each job (four paystubs if paid weekly) for all employed household members
Social Security benefit recipients must provide proof of benefits letter from Social Security Administration
Students 18 and over must provide current school transcript or class schedule, and any employment income must be counted
Applications must be submitted directly to the rental properties, not to the Department
MPDU tenants must recertify income and household size annually upon lease renewal
Tenants can continue in MPDU units if income remains at or below current limits adjusted for household size
Housing Choice Voucher holders must have vouchers issued by Rockville Housing Enterprises; vouchers from other agencies must be ported into Rockville Housing Enterprises program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Identify available MPDU rental units through properties throughout Rockville using the city's list and map of affordable housing opportunities. 2. Complete the MPDU Rental Certification Form with household income and composition information. 3. Submit application directly to the rental property's leasing office (not to the Department). 4. Provide required documentation: two most recent years of federal tax returns with W-2s, two most recent paystubs for all employed household members (four if paid weekly), proof of Social Security benefits if applicable, and birth certificates for dependent children not listed on tax returns. 5. Leasing agent will verify household income and determine eligibility, ensuring income is within limits and household size matches unit bedroom count. 6. If eligible, sign the MPDU Renter's Agreement Form and MPDU Lease Addendum. 7. Leasing agent sends signed Renter's Agreement to the Department within 14 days of lease signing. 8. Tenant must provide annual recertification information within 30 days of receiving recertification form from property, including updated tax returns, paystubs, and household composition documentation. Failure to provide recertification within 30 days results in 60-day notice to vacate. 9. If income exceeds limits at recertification, tenant receives 180-day notice to vacate.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants awarded to nonprofit organizations for projects within city limits that reduce stormwater pollution and protect natural resources. Projects include permeable pavers and pavements, native landscaping, large-scale tree plantings, community outreach and engagement to reduce pollution, and environmental and sustainability projects that benefit underserved communities.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to nonprofit organizations for environmental and stormwater pollution reduction projects
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations with projects in Rockville that reduce stormwater pollution and protect natural resources
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that reduce stormwater pollution and protect natural resources, including permeable pavers and pavements, native landscaping, large-scale tree plantings, community outreach and engagement, and environmental and sustainability projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Rockville city limits
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization
Project must be located within Rockville city limits
Project must reduce stormwater pollution and protect natural resources
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website at the 'Learn More and Apply' link provided

structured_extraction.program_name: Publicly Accessible Art in Private Development Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Requires most private development projects in Rockville to include an expenditure for publicly accessible art based on an annually adjusted fee schedule. The program promotes community welfare by incorporating works of art in private development to preserve and enrich the character and environment, improve quality of life, reduce the impact of urbanization, and foster economic vitality.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Private developers are required to make an expenditure for publicly accessible art based on an annually adjusted fee schedule (effective February 2025-June 30, 2026). For single-family/townhouse construction: $680.84 per unit (first 100), $510.57 per unit (second 100), $340.36 per unit (over 200). For multi-family: $1021.33 per unit (first 100), $766.02 per unit (second 100), $510.57 per unit (over 200). For commercial: $0.58 per sq ft (first 100,000), $0.45 per sq ft (second 100,000), $0.26 per sq ft (over 200,000). For industrial: $0.12 per gross sq ft. Developers may select from six compliance options: (1) install original site-specific visual art on site, (2) present visual, literary, or performing arts on site, (3) contribute monetarily to the Art in Public Places Program or City-Managed Arts Program, (4) provide an arts space (office, studio, gallery, theater, etc.), (5) provide arts-based infrastructure (audio/visual equipment, theater rigging, etc.), or (6) make a monetary donation to an eligible arts organization meeting specific IRS 501(c)(3) criteria. Options may be combined. Funds may cover artist fees, consultant fees (maximum 10%), freight, fabrication, installation, and construction costs associated with arts spaces. For on-site installations, art must be maintained in perpetuity and cannot be removed within five years without replacement or contribution penalty.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; applications accepted throughout development review process
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private development projects in Rockville, including single-family, townhouse, multi-family residential, commercial, and industrial construction projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Publicly accessible art installations, art presentations, contributions to public art programs, arts spaces, arts-based infrastructure, or donations to eligible arts organizations. Eligible costs include artist and consultant fees, fabrication, installation, equipment, and construction costs associated with arts spaces.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville, Maryland. The requirement applies to most private development projects within city limits. Certain projects are exempt from the requirement as determined by the Arts and Culture Program Manager.
requirements_list: Most private development projects in the city are subject to the requirement, as determined during initial development review
Projects must include expenditure for publicly accessible art or select approved alternative compliance option
Art must be publicly accessible to the community at all times

For on-site installed art: must be original, site-specific work demonstrating high aesthetic standards and artistic merit; must meet safety and durability standards; must be designed for accessibility, safety, and ease of maintenance

For on-site art installations: artist contract must comply with Visual Artists Rights Act of 1990; artwork must last at least 30 years with regular maintenance; on-site art cannot be removed within five years without replacement or contribution to City
For arts spaces: must meet identified community need; space must be suitable for intended arts use; business plan must demonstrate sustainability beyond first ten years
For arts-based infrastructure: must meet identified community need; must be suitable for intended location and purpose

For monetary donations to eligible arts organizations: organization must have primary mission of arts exhibition, presentation, production or performance; must hold 501(c)(3) status; must have primary office in City of Rockville; must be governed by independent board; must offer majority of programs in city open to public
Certain projects are exempt from the requirement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: (1) Arts and Culture Program Manager determines AIPD Ordinance applicability during initial development review and sends Development Review Committee Comment Letter. (2) Applicant meets with Arts and Culture Program staff to discuss requirements and available options. (3) Applicant reviews AIPD Ordinance, Implementation Manual, and Guidelines and selects compliance option(s). (4) Applicant submits completed AIPD Application with required attachments specific to chosen option(s): For on-site art installation: concept plan, cost itemization, artist qualifications/CV if consultant hired, artist selection process and criteria. For art presentation: concept plan with timeline, duration, location, artist selection process. For arts space: inclusion in site plan or detailed plan, valuation, cost itemization, business plan addressing space type, usage, market need, and intended users. For arts-based infrastructure: cost itemization and needs justification. For monetary contribution: specify recipient (Art in Public Places Program or City-Managed Arts Program). (5) Before Permit Issuance: If on-site art, developer and consultant present proposed artist concept and budget to Arts and Culture Program staff for approval; after approval, developer contracts with artist per VARA; developer and consultant present final artist concept for staff approval; any required conditions must be satisfied. If presenting art, submit itemized costs for staff approval. If providing arts space or infrastructure, submit fully executed agreement with recipient organization. If making monetary contribution, deliver AIPD Contribution Form and check to City Manager's Office Arts and Culture Program. (6) Before Certificate of Occupancy: Install approved art and interpretive signage and pass inspection; provide maintenance documentation and photos; or confirm presentation completion or arts space/infrastructure operational status. (7) For installations not completed by project completion, Agreement and Bond Form must be executed and bond posted prior to Permit Issuance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program administered by the City of Rockville that helps residents and nonprofits reduce stormwater pollution and flooding by installing small-scale green infrastructure and sustainable landscaping practices on their properties. Projects include rain gardens, permeable pavers, rain barrels, native plant landscaping, tree planting, and green roofs. The program improves water quality in local streams and provides cooling and wildlife habitat benefits. The program follows the principles of 'Slow it. Spread it. Sink it!' to manage stormwater runoff on residential properties.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates for stormwater management and green infrastructure projects installed on residential and nonprofit properties. Rebate amounts vary by project type: conservation landscaping ($5–$6 per square foot), rain gardens ($10 per square foot), pavement removal ($3–$6 per square foot), rain barrels and cisterns ($1 per gallon), tree canopy ($150 per tree), permeable paver retrofit ($14 per square foot), and green roofs ($9 per square foot). Maximum lifetime rebate per property is $5,000. The City of Rockville offers free educational workshops, on-site stormwater runoff evaluations, and cost-share assistance for implementing stormwater Best Management Practices (BMPs).
structured_extraction.contact_name: Chesapeake Bay Trust / City of Rockville Environmental Management Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family and townhome homeowners, homeowners associations, condominium associations, religious institutions, private schools, and other nonprofits located in the City of Rockville.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of stormwater management and green infrastructure projects including conservation landscaping, native plantings, rain gardens, pavement removal, rain barrels, cisterns, tree planting, permeable paver retrofit, and green roofs. Projects must follow BMPs designed to slow, spread, and sink stormwater runoff.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible properties must be located within the City of Rockville, Montgomery County, Maryland. Properties should be evaluated to determine soil infiltration rates and site-specific conditions before BMP installation.
requirements_list: Property must be located in the City of Rockville
Eligible property types include single-family residences, townhomes, homeowners associations, condominium associations, religious institutions, private schools, and other nonprofits

Prior to implementation of any practices, seek technical assistance from a licensed professional engineer or landscape architect, and/or certified professionals in erosion and sediment control for specifications
Site-specific designs that address each individual site's needs and constraints are essential
Permits or permission may be required for some techniques and when working in the right-of-way or on a City easement; always check with the City to determine if a permit is necessary
Soils with poor infiltration rates are NOT recommended for many techniques unless the soil is modified
Call Miss Utility (811 or 1-800-257-7777) at least two working days before any digging project to mark underground utilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website or the City of Rockville website at www.rockvillemd.gov/rainscapes. Applicants are encouraged to conduct a do-it-yourself stormwater runoff evaluation of their property by walking the property on a rainy day to identify runoff patterns and potential BMP locations. The City offers free on-site stormwater runoff evaluations to assist in identifying suitable projects. The Chesapeake Bay Trust reviews and processes applications, performs site visits, and provides support for questions. Additional inquiries can be directed to the City of Rockville Environmental Management Division at 240-314-8870 or www.rockvillemd.gov/environment.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Rockville Emergency Assistance Program provides emergency financial assistance to eligible Rockville residents in need of temporary relief. The program helps with evictions, utility shutoffs, prescription medications, medical and dental expenses, food, and other basic needs. Referrals for emergency food, clothing, financial and employment counseling, and other types of assistance are also provided.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides direct financial assistance to cover emergency expenses including rent payments to prevent eviction, utility payments to prevent shutoffs, prescription medications, medical and dental expenses, and food. Assistance is limited to residents meeting financial need criteria and current eviction or utility shutoff requirements. For residents over 60, prescription assistance is available for costs under $200.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current residents of the City of Rockville who have lived there for a minimum of six months and are experiencing a financial emergency
