structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eviction prevention and rent assistance, utility shutoff prevention and utility bill assistance, prescription medication payments, medical and dental expenses, food, and other basic needs related to emergency financial hardship
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only eligible applicants who are current residents of the City of Rockville. Rockville is located in Montgomery County, Maryland. Use the address finder at rockvillemd.gov/services to determine if your address is within Rockville city limits.
requirements_list: Must be a current resident of the City of Rockville for a minimum of six months
Must apply first through Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) and receive a referral

For rent assistance, must have a current eviction notice from the court (such as Summons to Appear for Failure to Pay Rent, Writ or Warrant of Restitution, or red-and-white Final Eviction Notice from Montgomery County Sheriff's Office)
For utility assistance, must have a current utility shutoff notice or service must already be disconnected
Must demonstrate financial need due to loss of employment, ongoing financial difficulty, loss of family wage earner, unexpected medical bills, or other financial emergencies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must first apply for emergency assistance through the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services. If eligible, Montgomery County DHHS submits a referral to the City of Rockville. Upon receiving a referral, applicants schedule an appointment with the City of Rockville Housing and Community Development Department by calling 240-314-8300. Note that Montgomery County DHHS does not cover payments to third-party utility providers, so referrals are still needed for those cases.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rockville Safe Waters: Swim Scholarship Program for Youth with Autism
structured_extraction.program_description: A targeted scholarship program to provide financial support for inclusive swim lessons for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder, fostering water safety, physical development, and family engagement at the Rockville Swim and Fitness Center.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 10 scholarships awarded on a rolling basis to provide financial support for one child to attend one class season of inclusive swim lessons for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder at Rockville Swim and Fitness Center. Specific scholarship amounts not stated on page.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis until 10 scholarships are awarded
structured_extraction.contact_name: Recreation and Parks Department / Program Access Team
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children aged 3-10 with confirmed Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis who are Rockville residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One season of inclusive swim lessons at Rockville Swim and Fitness Center for one child.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rockville residents only. Applicant must reside in the City of Rockville to be eligible for scholarship consideration.
requirements_list: Child must be aged 3–10 with a confirmed Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis
Child must be a resident of the City of Rockville
Commitment to attend in-person swim lessons at Rockville Swim and Fitness Center
Established youth readiness to engage in group swim lessons
Adult must be present at facility/on deck during lessons
Proof of residency required (current City of Rockville water and sewage bill, property tax bill, or state-issued identification with City of Rockville address)

Must meet one of the stated financial requirements (TCA, SNAP, TEMHA, WPA, medical assistance, rental assistance, shelter residency, SSI, FARMS, Care for Kids, MEAP, Montgomery County HHS Rental Assistance, unemployment benefits, or WIC)
Scholarship is for one child for one class season
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed scholarship application on a rolling basis by email to programaccess@rockvillemd.gov. Required documentation includes proof of residency and verification of financial eligibility. Applications must include applicant information, description of disability/illness, comfort level in water and group settings, and desired course number. Selection is done by the Rockville Safe Waters Committee. For additional information, call 240-314-8611 to speak to a Program Access team member.

structured_extraction.program_description: Financial assistance for senior classes, day trips, and Rockville Senior Center memberships for Rockville residents ages 60 and older.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participant pays 50% of the actual cost with a maximum subsidy of $50.00 per quarter. Assistance can be applied to senior classes, day trips, and Rockville Senior Center memberships.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Recreation and Parks Department - Senior Social Services
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents ages 60 and older seeking to participate in senior classes, day trips, and Rockville Senior Center activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Senior classes, day trips, and Rockville Senior Center memberships.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rockville residents only. Applicants must reside in the City of Rockville.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Rockville resident ages 60 and older

Applicant must provide proof of income (W-2 form, Social Security/VA/pension benefit letters, Medicaid/Food stamps/S.S.I. documentation, pay stubs, family support letter, income tax form, or other income verification)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete the Senior Assistance Fund Application form, which requires providing personal information, date of birth, income information, and proof of income documentation. The form is submitted to the Recreation and Parks Department - Senior Social Services. For each quarter, participants request assistance for specific trips, classes, or memberships and the department processes the subsidy, with the participant paying 50% of the actual cost up to the $50 maximum subsidy per quarter. For additional information, call 240-314-8810.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program funded by the Community Development Block Grant that provides no-interest, forgivable loans to low-to-moderate income homeowners in Rockville for necessary repairs and improvements to correct code deficiencies. A lien is placed on the property and forgiven over a five-year period at a rate of 20% per year. Assistance covers repairs like roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, and kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation. Lead-based paint risk assessment and remediation is included if the home was built before 1978 and lead-based paint is found in deteriorated condition. The homeowner is responsible for repaying the remaining percentage of the lien if the home is sold, rented, or ownership is transferred within five years of completion. Maximum assistance is $25,000 per household.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides no-interest, forgivable loans to cover the cost of necessary repairs and improvements. A lien is placed on the property and forgiven at a rate of 20% per year over a five-year period. If the home is sold, rented, or ownership is transferred during the five-year period, the recipient must immediately repay the remaining percentage of the lien. The maximum expenditure per household is $25,000. Work is assessed and prioritized by the Rehabilitation Specialist based on severity of repair need. Typical repairs include roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, and kitchen and bathroom repairs to correct code deficiencies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: City of Rockville low-to-moderate income homeowners with owner-occupied primary residences that need repairs to correct code deficiencies. Applicants are prioritized according to severity of repair need.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home repairs and improvements to correct code deficiencies, including roof replacement, plumbing and electrical upgrades, furnace replacement, kitchen and bathroom repairs. If the dwelling was built before 1978, a lead paint risk assessment will be performed; if lead-based paint is found in deteriorated condition, it must be addressed as part of the scope of work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available to residents of the City of Rockville, Maryland only. Applicant must live within the City Limits of Rockville.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a homeowner in Rockville, Maryland
Applicant must live within the City Limits of the City of Rockville
The home must be owner-occupied and be the owner's sole and principal residence
Applicant must currently reside at the property
The owner must not own another home or condominium
Family income must not exceed HUD maximum Gross Income requirements (ranging from $68,500 for one-person household to $129,100 for eight-person household, effective May 2024)
Total assets must not exceed $150,000 (excluding the value of the home being applied for)
Owner cannot be underwater (owe more on the home than the SDAT value)
Property taxes must be current
Applicant must be current on personal and property taxes
Ownership verified through property tax records and the deed
If home built before 1978, lead paint risk assessment will be performed
Properties with reverse mortgages are reviewed on a case-by-case basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Complete the eligibility assessment application and mail it to the City of Rockville Housing and Community Development Department at 111 Maryland Avenue, Rockville, MD 20850. Step 2: After the eligibility assessment is accepted, the Rehabilitation Specialist will notify you to complete the eligibility review. Submit copies of: most recent Federal and State of Maryland tax returns, all income statements (W-2s, 1099s, Social Security or pension benefit statements, retirement savings or investment account statements), current Homeowner's Insurance Declaration Page, most recent mortgage or home equity loan statement, and most recent checking and savings bank statements (last 2 months). Step 3: Application materials are reviewed and work is prioritized by the Rehabilitation Specialist. The review process takes seven to ten business days. Upon approval, work is assessed and prioritized based on severity of repair need.

structured_extraction.program_description: Scholarships for program fees available for Rockville residents ages 18 and younger to help reduce financial barriers to recreation and childcare programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participant pays $15 toward each program fee, and the fund covers the balance up to $100 maximum per person per session (fall, winter, spring, summer) and $1,000 maximum per family. For summer camp season, the fund covers up to $175 maximum per youth for each camp session and $1,000 maximum per child. Any remaining balance must be paid by the participant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rockville residents ages 18 and younger seeking to participate in recreation and childcare programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recreation and childcare program fees, including preschool, summer camps, after-school programs, sports leagues, swim lessons, and cultural arts programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rockville residents only. Applicants must reside in the City of Rockville.
requirements_list: Participant must be a Rockville resident ages 18 and younger
Participant must pay $15 toward each program fee (unless otherwise specified)
Cumulative subsidies are limited to $100 maximum per person per session and $1,000 maximum per family
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-314-8620 or email registration@rockvillemd.gov to apply for the Youth Recreation Fund.

structured_extraction.program_name: A&E District Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for the renovation of existing buildings or construction of new buildings used by qualifying resident artists or arts and entertainment enterprises in designated Arts & Entertainment districts.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit applied to the increased assessed value of renovated or newly constructed buildings dedicated to arts and entertainment use. The City of Salisbury offers the credit for 6 years from approval. The local jurisdiction determines the percentage credit (up to 100%) and duration (up to 10 years). The credit applies only to real property, not personal property or improvements that do not substantially add to the real property's value.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying resident artists and arts and entertainment enterprises (for-profit or nonprofit entities dedicated to visual or performing arts) in the A&E District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovation of existing buildings or construction of new buildings for use by qualifying resident artists or arts and entertainment enterprises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within a designated Arts & Entertainment District. The City of Salisbury and Wicomico County have established an A&E District with enabling legislation.
requirements_list: Property must be located in a designated A&E District
Building must be dedicated to visual or performing arts use or used by a qualifying resident artist
For renovations, a building permit must be obtained
The establishment must meet the statutory definition of an arts and entertainment enterprise or qualifying resident artist
The increased value must be determined by the Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (D.A.T.) to discuss your project. Submit plans for review by D.A.T. to determine eligibility. The local office of the State Department of Assessments and Taxation will determine on a case-by-case basis whether the establishment qualifies as an arts and entertainment enterprise.

structured_extraction.program_description: An exemption from the Admission and Amusement Tax for qualifying arts and entertainment enterprises and resident artists on gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges in an Arts & Entertainment district.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying arts and entertainment enterprises and resident artists are exempt from paying the Admission and Amusement Tax on gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges within the A&E District.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying arts and entertainment enterprises (for-profit or nonprofit entities dedicated to visual or performing arts) and resident artists generating admission or amusement charges within an A&E District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Relief from tax on admission and amusement charges (such as ticket sales, performance fees, cover charges).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The establishment must be located in a designated Arts & Entertainment District.
requirements_list: Must be a qualifying arts and entertainment enterprise or resident artist
Must charge admissions or amusement fees
Enterprise must be dedicated to visual or performing arts
Must be located within the A&E District
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the local office of the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation to discuss eligibility. The local office will determine on a case-by-case basis whether the establishment qualifies for the exemption.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows eligible residents to defer or postpone payment of their utility bills during times of financial hardship.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Salisbury experiencing financial hardship with utility bills
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Utility bill payment deferment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Salisbury, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Buy a Home, Build a Business
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides business and real estate resources to recent graduates of Salisbury University who want to start a business and establish residency in Salisbury.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides business and real estate resources to help recent graduates of Salisbury University start a business and call Salisbury home.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Recent graduates of Salisbury University looking to start a business and establish residency in Salisbury
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business and real estate resources to support starting a business and establishing a home in Salisbury
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Salisbury, Maryland
requirements_list: Recent graduate of Salisbury University
Intent to start a business
Intent to establish residency in Salisbury
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Housing and Community Development Department for more information about the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program offered by the City of Salisbury to assist businesses within the Main Street District. Each business is eligible for up to $20,000. The program provides one-time grant awards with no repayment required to help businesses recover from COVID-19 impacts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant awards up to $20,000 per business with no repayment required. Funds can be used for employee paid sick leave, maintaining payroll, obtaining materials due to supply chain interruptions, making past due or future rent or mortgage payments, repaying past due or future obligations, purchasing PPE or safety measures, building improvements to reduce COVID-19 spread, business equipment to expand services in response to COVID-19, or other COVID-related recovery uses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses registered with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury with a physical location in the designated Main Street area of Salisbury, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid sick leave for employees; maintaining payroll and retaining employees; obtaining materials due to supply chain interruptions; making past due or future rent or mortgage payments; repaying past due or future obligations; purchasing PPE or implementing safety measures; building improvements to reduce COVID-19 spread; business equipment to expand services in response to COVID-19; other COVID-related recovery uses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have a physical location within the designated Main Street area of Salisbury, Maryland. For verification of eligibility based on address, contact [email protected].
requirements_list: Must be a registered business entity in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury
Must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury within the designated Main Street area
Must have no pre-existing tax liens or legal judgements prior to March 5
Limited to one award per business entity
Employees must spend over 50% of their time doing work in the Main Street area for payroll-related uses
Home-based businesses are not eligible
Churches are not eligible
Banks and financial institutions are not eligible
Investment real estate entities are not eligible unless applying for payments for a business located in the Main Street area or COVID-related investments on a Main Street property
Food trucks are not eligible
Government agencies are not eligible
Contractors, construction, and service repair-based businesses are not eligible unless applying for COVID-related investments on a Main Street property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are graded by a committee based on three criteria: the degree the business has been negatively impacted by COVID-19, how the funds would help the business recover from COVID impacts, and the degree the business contributes to the vitality of the designated Main Street area. For businesses that receive funding, proof of use of funds must be submitted.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time grant program funded by donations from Delmarva Power and the City's Revolving Loan Fund to help small businesses in Salisbury that were impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and Maryland State Executive Orders.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grant award of $2,300 per business with no repayment required. Distributed through a lottery system prioritizing businesses mandated to fully close (Tier 1) before considering those mandated to partially close (Tier 2).
structured_extraction.contact_name: City of Salisbury Office of Business Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses registered with Maryland and the City of Salisbury that were impacted by COVID-19 closures or disruptions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid sick leave for employees unable to work due to coronavirus; maintaining payroll or retaining employees during shutdowns; obtaining materials due to supply chain interruptions; making rent or mortgage payments; repaying obligations unpaid due to revenue losses; purchasing personal protective equipment or safety measures to reduce COVID-19 spread.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses with a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury, within the Revolving Loan Boundary map. Businesses outside the Revolving Loan area may be eligible for funds donated by Delmarva Power.
requirements_list: Must be a registered business entity in good standing with the State of Maryland and City of Salisbury
Must have a physical establishment in the City of Salisbury within the Revolving Loan Boundary map or eligible for Delmarva Power funds
Must have no more than 25 full-time employees as of March 5, 2020
Must be engaged in activities regulated or impacted by COVID-19 Maryland's State of Emergency with proof of mandated closure or partial closure
Must have no pre-existing tax liens or legal judgments prior to March 5, 2020

Not eligible: home-based businesses, churches, medical service providers, nonprofits, banks and financial institutions, investment real estate entities, food trucks, national franchises, government agencies, or contractors and construction or service repair businesses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online or by email to the Office of Business Development. Applications are reviewed by the Director of Business Development, a Finance Department officer, and the Deputy City Administrator for completeness and demonstration of tangible and immediate need. Approved applicants are classified as Tier 1 (mandated full closure) or Tier 2 (mandated partial closure). Tier 1 applicants receive first priority in a lottery system. Selected awardees receive a grant check by mail and must complete a disbursement form and provide receipts within 60 days of City approval.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Owner-Occupied Housing Repair Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A housing repair program that provides grants to low-income homeowners to make critical repairs to their owner-occupied homes, bringing them into compliance with city codes. The program is administered through partnerships with Habitat for Humanity of Wicomico County and Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services using Community Development Block Grant funding.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to a maximum of $20,000 per property are provided to eligible homeowners to perform critical repairs. A 5-year Notice of Lien must be signed and recorded against the property. After receiving a grant, applicants are not eligible again until the 5-year lien term expires.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 410-546-1551 (Habitat for Humanity of Wicomico County) or 410-543-4626 (Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupied homeowners within the City of Salisbury corporate limits with household income below 80 percent of Area Median Income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repairs to bring owner-occupied homes into compliance with city codes, including repair or replacement of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems; building components and surfaces such as foundations, roofs, floors, walls, doors, and windows; energy conservation improvements; lead paint hazard reduction; accessibility improvements for disabled persons; and incipient repairs and general property improvements of a non-luxury nature.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located within the City of Salisbury corporate limits.
requirements_list: Total household gross income before taxes must be below 80 percent of Area Median Income
Applicant must own the property in fee simple, as joint tenants, or tenants by the entireties (no tenants in common)
At least one owner must reside in the property
All mortgage payments must be current for the previous 3 months
Must be free of tax liens and judgments
Bankruptcies must have been discharged for a minimum of 2 years
All property taxes and city invoices must be current
Applicant must have clear title to the property
Property must have flood insurance if in 100-year flood plain (properties in floodway are not eligible)
Owner-occupants must not own any other house and must not have substantial assets to secure rehabilitation funds elsewhere
A 5-year Notice of Lien must be signed and recorded
Property must be insured for the entire loan term
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should contact either Habitat for Humanity of Wicomico County at 410-546-1551 or Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services at 410-543-4626 for further information and to apply. The subrecipient agencies will administrate the application and award process.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Summer Youth Employment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A paid 8-week summer employment opportunity for high school students in grades 10-12 enrolled in Wicomico County school district. Participants work in various City of Salisbury departments to gain workforce readiness and career-specific skills. The program includes structured learning, mentoring through a Junior Achievement partnership, resume writing guidance, soft skills development, and on-the-job performance coaching. By the end of the program, participants gain work experience history, job skills, career knowledge, and access to business resources in the Salisbury area. The program runs annually each summer and is administered by the City of Salisbury Community Relations Division.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive paid employment working up to 28 hours per week for 8 weeks (June 22 to August 14, 2026). Includes on-the-job training, mentoring through Junior Achievement partnership, resume writing assistance, soft skills development counseling, and access to business resources in the Salisbury area.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for Summer 2026 are now closed. Applications for Summer 2027 will open in January.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students entering grades 10-12 for the 2026-2027 academic year currently enrolled in Wicomico County school district. Residency in City of Salisbury is preferred but not required.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid employment wages in City of Salisbury departments; participants gain work experience, job skills, career knowledge, and professional development through resume building and soft skills training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Students must be enrolled in Wicomico County school district. Residency in City of Salisbury is preferred but not required. Program is based in Salisbury, Maryland (Wicomico County).
requirements_list: Must be entering 10th-12th grade for the 2026-2027 academic year
Must be currently enrolled in Wicomico County school district
Must provide work permit by June 22, 2026
Must provide 2 forms of updated identification (birth certificate, social security card, current student ID, or state-issued ID)
Must have consistent reliable transportation to and from work
Must be able to work up to 28 hours per week for 8 weeks (June 22 - August 14, 2026)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application during the open application period via the City of Salisbury website. Applications for Summer 2026 are closed. Applications for Summer 2027 will open in January. Contact the Community Relations Division at 410-341-9550 with questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Salisbury Tax Abatement Program for Conversion from Rental to Homeowner-Occupied Dwelling
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax abatement program administered by the City of Salisbury that encourages property owners to purchase rental properties and convert them back to owner-occupied, single-family residences within Salisbury city limits. The program reduces or eliminates city property taxes for a period of up to nine years for qualifying conversions, supporting homeownership and neighborhood stabilization in Salisbury, Maryland.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified properties are exempt from city property taxes for five years. Beginning in year six, taxes are phased in gradually: year six at 20% of the prevailing residential tax rate, year seven at 40%, year eight at 60%, and year nine at 80%. After year nine, the property is taxed at the full prevailing residential tax rate. The program participation period is nine years total.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual certification must be filed by April 1 of each year to remain eligible
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners who are purchasing or have purchased rental properties and are converting them to owner-occupied, single-family residences within the City of Salisbury.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax reduction for owners converting rental properties to owner-occupied, single-family primary residences.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within City of Salisbury corporate limits, Wicomico County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within City of Salisbury corporate limits

Property must have been used exclusively as a rental property for at least three years immediately prior to purchase by the applicant, or was purchased from a person or entity that rehabilitated the property after rental use for three consecutive years
Must be converting property to an owner-occupied, single-family detached dwelling
The property must be a single-family detached dwelling arranged or designed for occupancy by only one family
Must intend to occupy the home within one year of purchase as an owner-occupied family residence

Applicant must agree to continue using the property as an owner-occupied family residence for the entire nine years of program participation, or sell it only to a person who will use it as an owner-occupied family residence until the program expires, or pay the city for all taxes abated during the period of ownership

Property must be occupied as the principal residence of the homeowner and actually occupied or expected to be actually occupied by the homeowner for more than six months of a twelve-month period beginning with the date of finality for the taxable year for which the property tax abatement is sought, unless the homeowner does not reside in the dwelling due to illness or need of special care
Must file annual certification of qualification by April 1 of each year with the Director of Internal Services to remain eligible for the tax abatement program
Property must qualify under all program requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should contact the City of Salisbury's Director of Internal Services to obtain application forms and the participation agreement. Applications can be obtained at the City Finance Office located at 125 N Division St., Room 103, Salisbury, MD 21801, or via the City of Salisbury website. Applicants must complete the application form and agreement form. Applicants must file a certificate of qualification by April 1 of each year with the Director of Internal Services in order to remain eligible for the tax abatement program. Contact the Housing and Community Development Department or the Director of Internal Services to determine if your property qualifies.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) – Entitlement Communities
structured_extraction.program_description: The CDBG Program provides annual federal grants to entitled metropolitan cities and urban counties to fund community and economic development activities. These funds support neighborhood revitalization, economic development, and improved community facilities and services. Activities must benefit low and moderate income persons, eliminate slums and blight, or meet urgent community development needs. The City of Salisbury is an entitled community that receives and administers CDBG funds, distributing them to subrecipients including nonprofits and government agencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual formula-based grants awarded to entitled cities. For program year 2021, the City of Salisbury received $399,903 total. Funds are distributed as administrative costs (up to 20% of grant plus program income), public service activities (up to 15% of grant plus prior year program income), and program/project funds. Grants are awarded on a reimbursement basis only. Maximum award per application is $150,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entitled metropolitan cities and urban counties. Subrecipients must be registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations or other government agencies implementing community and economic development activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for acquisition and clearance of real property, public improvements and facilities (senior centers, recreation centers, day care centers), public services (child care, health care, job training, education programs, recreation, drug abuse counseling, homeless services), relocation assistance, rehabilitation of buildings, historic preservation, lead-based paint hazard evaluation and reduction, code enforcement, assistance to micro-enterprises, homeownership assistance, urban renewal completion, technical assistance to increase organizational capacity, and assistance to institutions of higher education. Also supports neighborhood revitalization, economic development, and activities benefiting low and moderate income persons or eliminating slums and blight.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available in entitled metropolitan cities and urban counties as determined by federal formula. The City of Salisbury is an entitled community receiving and administering CDBG funds.
requirements_list: Grantees must have sufficient operating funds to expend on project expenses upfront and wait for reimbursement
Subrecipients must be a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization with supporting documentation confirming this status
For capital projects on property not held by the subrecipient, written approval from the property owner is required
Subrecipients requesting community services funds must be developing a new public service or proposing a quantifiable increase in service for an existing program
No more than 20 percent of the grant (plus program income) can be spent for planning and administrative costs
No more than 15 percent of the grant (plus prior year program income) can be spent for public service activities

Each activity must be eligible and meet one of three national objectives: benefit low and moderate income persons, aid in prevention or elimination of slums and blight, or meet other community development needs of particular urgency
Maximum amount any applicant may seek in any competitive funding round is $150,000
Activities must be eligible under CDBG program rules
Activities are developed at the local level based on community needs and priorities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible non-profit community groups or organizations may apply for either a public service or a capital grant. Applicants are called subrecipients. The grantee (City of Salisbury) may undertake some activities directly or sponsor activities through other government agencies or non-profit community groups. Activities can be carried out by the grantee, through contractors, sub-recipients, or Community Based Development Organizations (CBDOs). Each entitlement grantee receiving CDBG funds determines what activities it will fund as long as eligibility requirements and national objectives are met.

structured_extraction.program_description: Financial assistance to help homeowners repair critical home issues, including lead pipe replacement.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to help homeowners with critical home repairs, including replacement of lead pipes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Wicomico County needing critical home repairs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical home repairs, including lead pipe replacement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Wicomico County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Habitat for Humanity – Wicomico County at 410-436-1551 for application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: DHCD Low Income Energy Efficiency Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides energy efficiency improvements and assistance to low-income households to reduce energy costs and improve home efficiency.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides energy efficiency improvements and financial assistance to low-income households. Specific details about assistance amounts, terms, and mechanics are referenced in the program flyer.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households seeking to improve home energy efficiency and reduce energy costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements to homes including weatherization and related upgrades to reduce energy consumption.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through the City of Salisbury and Maryland DHCD service areas.
requirements_list: Low-income household status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Housing and Community Development or review the program flyer for application procedures and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides eligible businesses with property tax credits and state income tax credits for locating, expanding, or substantially improving commercial properties, or for hiring new employees in the designated Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of tax credits are available. The Real Property Credit provides a ten-year credit against local property taxes equal to 80% of the difference between the base property value and the newly assessed value after investment. The credit is 80% for five years, then declines 10% annually for the last five years (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%). Requires a minimum capital investment of $50,000 on commercial property only. The State Income Tax Credit is based on new employees hired: $1,000 per non-economically disadvantaged employee (one-time), or up to $3,000 for economically disadvantaged employees in year one, $2,000 in year two, and $1,000 in year three. Employees must have been hired after the Enterprise Zone designation or business relocation date (whichever is later), work at least 35 hours per week for at least six months, be paid at least 150% of federal minimum wage, spend at least half their working hours in the zone, and be new hires or rehired after being laid off for more than one year. Personal Property Tax Credit is also available for businesses located in Focus Area Zones.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: For property tax credits, the Zone Administrator must certify eligibility by December 31st of the preceding calendar year for the credit to appear on the next fiscal year tax bill beginning July 1st. Applications must be submitted prior to project completion date and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits. No specific deadline for income tax credit applications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, developers, and property owners located in or planning to locate in the Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone that are making capital improvements to commercial properties or hiring new employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements to commercial property including new construction, rehabilitation, machinery and equipment. New employee hiring.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is limited to properties located within the designated Salisbury Wicomico Enterprise Zone. Applicants should email to confirm if their business is eligible based on location.
requirements_list: For Real Property Credit: minimum capital investment of $50,000, commercial properties only (no residential use), base assessment must be completed before work begins, application submitted after receiving all building permits and before or at beginning of construction, property must change in value from improvements, if lessee makes improvements must have contractual agreement with owner regarding credit receipt, Zone Administrator must certify eligibility by December 31st for next fiscal year credit, application must be submitted prior to project completion date and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits

For State Income Tax Credit: must hire two or more qualifying employees, employees hired after Enterprise Zone designation or business relocation date (whichever is later), employees must fill new positions or replace previously certified economically disadvantaged employees, employees must work at least 35 hours per week for at least six months, employees must be paid at least 150% of federal minimum wage, employees must spend at least half working hours in the zone, employees must be new or rehired after being laid off for more than one year, applicant must answer all questions in Sections A and B of application form
For Personal Property Tax Credit: applicant must be located in Focus Area Zone
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the attached Maryland State Enterprise Zone Certification application form, selecting which credit(s) you are applying for (Income Tax Credit, Real Property Tax Credit, and/or Personal Property Tax Credit if in Focus Area). 2. Complete the applicable sections: Section A (Applicant Information), Section B (Enterprise Zone Property Information), Section C (Property Improvements Information if applying for property credit), Section D (Employment Tax Credit Information if applying for employment credit), and Section E if applying for Personal Property Tax Credit. 3. Submit application to the Business Development Specialist with all required documentation. 4. The Zone Administrator reviews the application and forwards to appropriate State entities for approval. 5. If eligible, receive a certification letter from City of Salisbury indicating which tax credit(s) you are eligible to receive. 6. For Real Property Tax Credit, the credit appears automatically on property taxes at the start of next fiscal year (July 1) or after next assessment cycle. 7. For State Income Tax Credit, claim credits when filing state income tax returns.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to property owners in Downtown Salisbury to help cover the costs of connecting to Maryland Broadband's high-speed fiber network that runs along Main Street. Grants reimburse eligible construction costs for bringing fiber into private properties, helping expand high-speed fiber internet access throughout the city.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available in amounts not to exceed $2,500 and are made on a reimbursement basis only. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis until funds run out for the fiscal year. The program is contingent upon the availability of appropriated funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners or tenants (with written property owner approval) located in Downtown Salisbury who wish to connect to high-speed fiber internet service.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible costs are limited to the construction cost of bringing fiber into the private property and ending at the termination point where the modem will be located. Construction costs cannot be passed on to those using the service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The property must be located within Downtown Salisbury (specifically the Salisbury Historic District), using existing conduits that have been installed along Main Street as part of the Main Street project. City of Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be located within Downtown Salisbury using existing conduits from the Main Street project
Application must be made by the legal property owner or by a tenant with written approval from the property owner
Applicant must use a licensed contractor to perform the work
Work must have approval from the Historic District if necessary
The City will not approve digging up sidewalks or work that would alter improvements from the Main Street Construction project (completed November 2020)
Grant amount cannot exceed $2,500
Applicant must agree not to pass construction costs on to those using the service
Grants are made on a reimbursement basis only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application with the required information including applicant details, property address, property tax number, a detailed description of the proposed method to bring fiber into the building, photographs of the building façade showing where the fiber will be tapped and how it will run into the property, anticipated project cost, and amount requested. If the project is already completed, submit copies of all receipts and paid invoices.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for eligible homeowners who live in their home for at least six months of the year, with income and net worth limits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible homeowners receive a tax credit. Eligibility requires living in the home for at least six months per year, net worth less than $200,000, and combined gross household income not exceeding $60,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners with qualifying income and net worth
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit to reduce state income tax liability
requirements_list: Must own and live in the home for at least six months per year
Net worth must be less than $200,000
Combined gross household income cannot exceed $60,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check eligibility based on income and net worth requirements, then apply through SDAT. You can verify if you are already receiving this credit by looking up your home at sdat.dat.maryland.gov/RealProperty.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax exemption program for businesses that locate, expand operations, or develop new products or industrial processes in Salisbury. The exemption applies to machinery, equipment, and tools used in manufacturing or research and development activities.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax exemption on machinery, equipment, and tools used in manufacturing or research and development. The exemption is granted for a specific equipment purchase year and can run for up to 5 years. To receive the maximum 5-year term, the application must be submitted within 2 years from December 31st of the calendar year the equipment was purchased. The exemption requires annual approval and annual submission of personal property tax returns. Exemptions require approval by the City of Salisbury Council, and receipt of exemption from Wicomico County does not guarantee approval by the City of Salisbury.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 2 years from December 31st of the calendar year in which equipment was purchased to receive the maximum 5-year exemption term
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sandra Green, Director of Finance; Phillip Menzel, Assistant Director Finance - Accounting
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses that manufacture products or conduct research and development in Salisbury, including those locating in the city, expanding existing operations, or developing new products or industrial processes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The exemption applies to machinery, equipment, and tools owned and operated by a manufacturing or research and development facility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must have a manufacturing or research and development operation located in Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Equipment must be owned and operated by a facility that locates in Salisbury, expands operations in Salisbury, or develops a new product or industrial process in Salisbury
Applicant must submit detailed explanation of how they meet eligibility requirements, including raw materials used, products produced or research and development activity being conducted
Applicant must provide number of employees used in manufacturing or research and development and number of administrative employees

Applicant must attach a detailed equipment schedule with description, original cost, and date of acquisition for each item; general descriptions such as Equipment, Various, or Miscellaneous are not acceptable
Applicant must attach a copy of the Maryland Personal Property Return for the year of equipment acquisition
Exemption requires approval by Salisbury City Council
If seeking maximum 5-year exemption term, application must be received within 2 years from December 31st of the calendar year equipment was purchased
A separate application must be made for each year
A copy of the personal property tax return must be sent in for each year of the exemption
Receipt of exemption from Wicomico County does not automatically guarantee approval by the City of Salisbury
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed Exemption Application form to the Finance Department. The application should include: business name, Maryland Department ID, mailing address, contact name, phone number, equipment year, address of the manufacturing or research and development operation, date the operation began in Salisbury, detailed explanation of how the business meets eligibility requirements, a complete equipment schedule listing each asset with specific description, original cost, and date of acquisition, and a copy of the Maryland Personal Property Return for the acquisition year. Mail the completed application to Finance Department, 125 North Division Street, Salisbury, Maryland 21801-4940. The application must be approved by the Salisbury City Council. A separate request must be made for each year. Once an exemption has been granted, a copy of the personal property tax return must be sent in for each year of the exemption.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for public safety officers employed by or serving the City of Salisbury Fire Department and Police Department, as well as retired officers and volunteers meeting service requirements. The credit reduces the real property tax on a primary residence owned by an eligible officer.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit applied to City real property tax for residential property owned by eligible public safety officers. The credit may be granted in an amount up to $2,500, but may not exceed the amount of the real property tax imposed on the dwelling. The tax credit is available for one taxable year and must be renewed annually by submitting a new application.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 immediately before the taxable year for which the credit is sought; if filed after April 1, the application shall be treated as an application for the next succeeding taxable year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time firefighters and paramedics employed by the City of Salisbury Fire Department with at least one year of full-time employment; full-time police officers employed by the City of Salisbury Police Department with at least one year of full-time employment; active volunteer members of the City of Salisbury Fire Department meeting service requirements; individuals who have received service-related disabilities; retired officers in good standing; and volunteer members with more than 20 years of active service who have become lifetime members. Applicant must own the residential property to which the credit will be applied and the property must be the applicant's primary residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit reduces real property tax owed on a primary residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Salisbury
requirements_list: Must be currently employed as a full-time firefighter, paramedic, or police officer for the City of Salisbury with at least one year of full-time employment, OR an active volunteer member meeting service requirements, OR have received a service-related disability, OR be retired in good standing, OR be a lifetime member volunteer with more than 20 years of service
Must own the residential property to which the credit will be applied
The property must be the applicant's primary residence
Must not have received another real property tax credit permitted under Title 9 of the Tax-Property Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland
Must file application on or before April 1 before the taxable year for which the credit is sought
Must provide supporting documentation such as a current paystub, letter of retirement or separation from the City, or letter evidencing volunteer status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form providing property parcel number, fiscal year, applicant name and contact information, property owner names and address, and public safety officer designation. Select the applicable designation category and provide supporting documentation such as a paystub, retirement letter, or volunteer status letter. Certify eligibility by agreeing to the terms and sign electronically. Submit the application on or before April 1 before the taxable year for which the credit is sought. Applications filed after April 1 are treated as applications for the next succeeding taxable year.

structured_extraction.program_description: Low-interest loan program to help homeowners repair their homes, including replacement of lead pipes.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 1% interest loan for up to $25,000 to help homeowners complete home repairs and maintenance including replacement of lead pipes inside homes. APR is 1.99%. Limited time offer based on available funds. Loan must be for owner-occupied properties within Salisbury city limits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupant homeowners in Salisbury needing home repairs and maintenance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home repairs and maintenance, including replacement of lead pipes inside homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties within Salisbury city limits, Wicomico County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Owner-occupied property
Property located within Salisbury city limits
Credit approval required
Loan amount up to $25,000
Limited time offer based on available funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services (SNHS) at 410-543-4626 or visit 560 Riverside Dr. Ste A102, Salisbury, MD 21801 for application details and to discuss eligibility requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A public art competition open to Maryland residents and artists that awards funding to create an original public art installation in Salisbury. The selected artist receives a $10,000 stipend plus up to $5,000 in reimbursable materials costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The winning artist receives $10,000 as a stipend for their design and creation of the public art installation. An additional up to $5,000 is provided for materials and supplies as reimbursement with proof of purchase. The artist is responsible for all applicable federal, state, and local taxes on the income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents and artists who are 18 years or older. Artists, architects, engineers, and creative teams are welcome. Salisbury and local-based artists are strongly encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to create an original public art installation to be placed at a designated public location (the kiosk in front of the Salisbury-Wicomico Government Office Building at 125 North Division Street). The $5,000 in materials funds can be used for supplies and materials needed to construct the artwork.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to all Maryland residents and organizations. Local Salisbury artists are strongly encouraged.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland resident or organization
Artist must be 18 years or older
Design must be original art with no trademarked, copyrighted, or AI-generated content
Design cannot be copied from existing photos or images created by someone other than the artist or creative team
Design must not be religious, political, or sexual in nature
Design must not include corporate logos or advertising
Design must be appropriate for broad-based public display suitable for all ages
Design must meet all applicable federal, state, and local codes
Design must be durable, safe, structurally sound, and resistant to theft, vandalism, weathering, and excessive maintenance
Artist or creative team must have sufficient experience with the proposed artistic medium
The winning design becomes the property of the City of Salisbury
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The competition is conducted in two rounds. Round 1: Artists submit initial applications using the online form. The top three candidates are selected and each receives $500 to develop an extended proposal. Round 2: The top three finalists present their extended proposals in-person or virtually to the Public Art Committee. The winning artist is notified in late April, an agreement is signed, and funds are encumbered by the City. The winning design is announced in May, and construction and installation commence in June.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program administered by the City of Salisbury that provides financial assistance to new businesses and existing businesses seeking to expand or renovate within designated eligible areas of Salisbury. The program offers revolving loans to help entrepreneurs start or grow their operations within the city, supporting business development and economic growth in Salisbury's designated Revolving Loan Fund boundary area.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Revolving loans up to $100,000 to provide funds for new businesses in Salisbury or for expansion and renovation of existing businesses in Salisbury. Applicants must demonstrate personal investment and provide detailed business plans with three-year financial projections. Specific loan terms, interest rates, and repayment conditions are detailed in the program guidelines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entrepreneurs and business owners seeking to start a new business or expand or renovate an existing business within the designated Revolving Loan Fund boundary area in Salisbury, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to start a new business in Salisbury or to support the expansion and renovation of existing businesses in Salisbury, including business development and expansion purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is limited to businesses located within the designated Revolving Loan Fund boundary area in Salisbury, Maryland, as defined on the Revolving Loan Eligible Areas map. Applicants must also have approval from the Salisbury Historic District Commission and City Infrastructure and Development department where applicable.
requirements_list: Business must be located within the designated Revolving Loan Fund boundary area in Salisbury
Business plan with three-year financial projections
Personal and company tax returns for the past two years
Evidence of personal financial investment into the project
Conceptual design illustration and detailed description
Project timeline
Three written cost estimates of proposed project costs
Copy of lease and written approval from landlord (if applicable)
Evidence that the Historic District Commission has approved the concept plan
Articles of incorporation or partnership agreement
Credit report dated no more than one month prior to application submission
Approval from City Infrastructure and Development
Approval from Salisbury Historic District Commission
Personal financial statement
Loan amount not to exceed $100,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must download and complete the Revolving Loan Application and Personal Financial Statement forms electronically and submit them to the Director of Business Development at the City of Salisbury, 110 N Division Street, Salisbury, MD 21801. Required documentation must be attached including business plans, tax returns, cost estimates, lease agreements, Historic District Commission approval, and credit reports. Applicants must authorize the City to review credit reports and financial information. Applications are reviewed by the Revolving Loan Advisory Committee.

structured_extraction.program_description: The City of Salisbury is seeking artist proposals for temporary designs of crosswalks at the intersection of South Division Street and West/East Market Street. The selected design should reflect the city's character, history, and artistic vibrancy through abstract patterns, geometric shapes, or elements inspired by the city's natural or architectural features while prioritizing pedestrian safety and visibility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Selected artist receives a $3,000 stipend for design and implementation. The artwork will be displayed for up to two years at the intersection of South Division Street and West/East Market Street.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All artists, designers, and creatives
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and implementation of temporary crosswalk artwork. Painting must be completed by September 14, 2025.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Intersection of South Division Street and West/East Market Street in Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Open to all artists, designers, and creatives
Design must reflect the city's character, history, and artistic vibrancy
Design may incorporate abstract patterns, geometric shapes, or elements inspired by the city's natural or architectural features
Design must prioritize pedestrian safety and ensure high visibility and durability
Design must not represent any specific political movement or cause
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Artists submit proposals through The Crosswalk Canvas Application starting May 5, 2025. The submission deadline is June 30, 2025. The Arts and Technical Advisory Group and Public Art Committee review applications on July 11, 2025. Selected artist is notified by July 14, 2025. The painting period runs from July 15 to September 14, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax exemption for 100% permanently disabled veterans and surviving spouses that exempts qualifying property from state property taxes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible 100% permanently disabled veterans and surviving spouses receive a full exemption from state property taxes on their primary residence.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 100% permanently disabled veterans and surviving spouses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption on primary residence
requirements_list: Must be 100% permanently disabled veteran or surviving spouse of such a veteran
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the veteran tax exemption application form available at dat.maryland.gov/SDAT%20Forms/veteran.pdf and contact your local SDAT office.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Water Incentive Program (WIN) is offered by the City of Salisbury to provide eligible households with annual financial assistance toward their water and sewer bills. Eligible households may receive one payment per year of up to $2,000 to help pay water and/or wastewater bills (or up to $1,000 if the property has a leak). Applicants must be Maryland residents responsible for payment of a water and/or wastewater bill issued by the City of Salisbury and must meet household income requirements, or be automatically eligible through participation in certain assistance programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households receive one payment per year of up to $2,000 applied directly toward water and/or sewer bills (or up to $1,000 one-time annual payment if the property has a leak). The amount of assistance is limited to the actual charges on the water and/or sewer bill. Applicants must be Maryland residents responsible for payment of a water and/or wastewater bill issued by the City of Salisbury. Household income must not exceed specified gross income thresholds based on 60% of the State Median Income: 1 person $3,574/month, 2 persons $4,639/month, 3 persons $5,730/month, 4 persons $6,822/month, 5 persons $7,913/month, 6 persons $9,005/month, 7 persons $9,209/month, 8 persons $9,414/month (for each additional household member, add $205/month). Applicants are automatically eligible if currently receiving energy assistance from the Office of Home Energy Programs, Temporary Cash Assistance, Temporary Disability Assistance Program, SNAP, Supplemental Security Income, Emergency Rental Assistance Program, or Means Tested Veteran Benefits (MTVB).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are responsible for paying a water and/or wastewater bill issued by the City of Salisbury and meet income eligibility requirements, including eligible households in Salisbury, Maryland. Both tenants and homeowners can apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance can be used toward water and/or sewer bills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents living at the property for which assistance is being provided. The property must receive water and/or wastewater service from the City of Salisbury, Salisbury, Maryland. Both tenants and homeowners are eligible if they live at the property for which assistance is being provided.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be responsible for payment of a water and/or wastewater bill from the City of Salisbury
Must live at the property for which assistance is sought
Total household income must not exceed specified gross income thresholds (60% of State Median Income)
Must provide government-issued identification (driver's license or other government-issued identification card)
Must provide proof of residency (water or wastewater bill)
Must provide copies of Social Security cards for all household members

Must provide proof of all gross income for all household members for the last 30 days (such as paystub, Social Security letter, child support letter, unemployment letter, self-employment documentation, etc.)
If household received no income in prior 30 days, must sign Declaration of Zero Income and provide information on how household meets basic needs
Must submit most recent water and/or sewer bill

Automatically eligible if currently receiving energy assistance from Office of Home Energy Programs, Temporary Cash Assistance, Temporary Disability Assistance Program, SNAP, Supplemental Security Income, Emergency Rental Assistance Program, or Means Tested Veteran Benefits (MTVB)
If renting and water bill is in landlord's name, must provide copy of most recent rental receipt or lease stating that water is covered in rental fee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply online at https://salisbury.md/win or https://salisbury.md/win-application, submit a printable application form in person at the Wicomico County Department of Social Services (201 Baptist Street, Ste. 27, Salisbury, MD 21801), or by mail. Provide applicant information, water/sewer account details, household member information, and income documentation. Submit required supporting documentation including government-issued identification, proof of residency, Social Security cards, and proof of income. The application requires signature and attestation under penalty of perjury. Applicants can expedite processing by attaching award letters and proof of other assistance received at the time of application. For more information, contact the Wicomico County Department of Social Services or the City of Salisbury utility billing office at 125 N. Division Street, Room 103, phone 410-548-3115.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comcast Internet Essentials is a low-cost internet service program for eligible low-income households, providing broadband internet access at reduced rates. The program offers two service tiers: basic service at 50/5 Mbps for $9.95 per month, or Internet Essentials Plus at 100/10 Mbps for $29.95 per month. The program is available to households that qualify for federal assistance programs including the National School Lunch Program, SNAP, Housing Assistance, Medicaid, SSI, and other qualifying programs. The program is available statewide through Comcast service areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Households receive discounted monthly internet service at reduced rates. Basic service provides 50/5 Mbps download/upload speeds for $9.95 per month. Internet Essentials Plus provides 100/10 Mbps for $29.95 per month. Service is available to households that qualify for federal assistance programs including the National School Lunch Program, SNAP, Housing Assistance, Medicaid, SSI, WIC, TANF, Headstart, Veteran's Administration Pension, LIHEAP, Pell Grant, and other qualifying programs. Customers also receive access to Comcast Xfinity hotspots. Comcast does not check credit history.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals, families, and older adults who participate in qualifying assistance programs such as Medicaid, Public Housing, SNAP, WIC, TANF, National School Lunch Program, Headstart, SSI, Veteran's Administration Pension, LIHEAP, or Pell Grant, and who reside in Comcast service areas across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Discounted home internet access and broadband service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through Comcast service areas, including Baltimore County, Somerset County, and Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Household qualifies for at least one eligible assistance program (National School Lunch Program, SNAP, Housing Assistance, Medicaid, SSI, WIC, TANF, Headstart, Veteran's Administration Pension, LIHEAP, Pell Grant, or other qualifying programs)
Have not been a Comcast customer within the last 90 days
Cannot be a current internet customer of Comcast, RCN, or Verizon
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up by visiting www.internetessentials.com or calling 855-846-8376 (English) or 855-765-6995 (Spanish). Video chat in American Sign Language is available on their website. Applicants should visit the Internet Essentials website to determine qualification and enroll in the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports the promotion and development of Maryland's beer, wine, and spirits manufacturing industry. The program funds activities that showcase state breweries, distilleries, and wineries, attract visitors, support special events, educate the public about alcohol manufacturing, conduct research on agricultural products used in production, and expand minority ownership in these businesses.
structured_extraction.agency: Department of Commerce, Office of Tourism
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded by the Secretary of Commerce based on recommendations from the Advisory Commission on Maryland Alcohol Manufacturing and Promotion. Grant amounts have ranged from approximately $10,000 to over $400,000 based on FY24-FY25 awards. Grant funds can be used for: creating or expanding breweries, distilleries, and wineries; attracting visitors; supporting special events; public education about alcohol manufacturing; research on agricultural products and production methods; marketing and promotional campaigns; digital and social media initiatives; heritage and tourism experiences; minority ownership expansion; and industry conferences and events. Projects must deliver tangible outputs aligned with stated goals within a 12-month grant period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations classified as 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) under the Internal Revenue Code and state or local government units that work to promote Maryland's alcohol manufacturing industry.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creating and expanding breweries, distilleries, and wineries; attracting visitors to these facilities; creating incentives for special events; educating the public about alcohol manufacturing history and production methods; conducting research on and promoting agricultural products used in beer, wine, and spirits production; supporting the expansion of minority ownership and participation in brewery, distillery, and winery operations; marketing and promotional campaigns using digital, social media, traditional advertising, and point-of-purchase strategies; heritage tourism initiatives; industry conferences and events; website development; research on production techniques and agricultural inputs; and workforce development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; any eligible applicant in Maryland may apply.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization under 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) of the Internal Revenue Code or a state or local government unit
Applications must be submitted online in the format stipulated by the Department of Commerce
Applicant must identify specific, tangible deliverables that directly support stated goals and programmatic activities
Applicant must develop a detailed project timeline with key milestones, phases (planning, implementation, evaluation, reporting), and realistic deadlines aligned with the 12-month grant period
Applicant must develop a detailed budget with each line item corresponding to a specific deliverable, including only essential and justifiable costs

Applicant must identify projected revenue generated by the project and itemize all funding sources (financial and in-kind support) separately, including only funding that is 'in-hand' at time of application
Applicant must describe specific project outcomes with quantitative and/or qualitative success measures
Applicant must explain project management approach and resource allocation strategy

For marketing and promotion projects, applicant must describe each marketing platform/product and identify specific markets, audiences, consumers, geographic areas, demographics, and market segments to be reached
Award recipients must submit a Final Report within 60 days after the grant term ends, including project accomplishments, financial expenditures, and impact information
Failure to submit the required Final Report may make the applicant ineligible for future funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Review the Tips & Hints guidance document before preparing your application. 2) Prepare detailed answers addressing: deliverables, timeline with milestones, detailed budget matching implementation timeline, project outcomes and success measures, and project management approach. 3) For marketing/promotion projects, include descriptions of marketing platforms, target audiences, and geographic/demographic information. 4) Submit your application online through the Department of Commerce using their required format. The deadline for FY26 applications is November 19, 2025. 5) Applications are reviewed by the Advisory Commission on Maryland Alcohol Manufacturing and Promotion, which evaluates alignment with the program's eligible activities and project feasibility. 6) The Secretary of Commerce gives final approval based on the commission's recommendations. 7) If awarded, you must submit a Final Report within 60 days after the 12-month grant period ends, documenting project accomplishments, financial expenditures, and measurable impact.
