structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for volunteer firefighters in Dorchester County who are members of a bona fide volunteer fire company and meet state eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual property tax credit of $500 against Dorchester County real property tax for qualifying volunteer firefighters, or $1,000 if the dwelling is owned by two or more qualifying members. The credit cannot exceed the actual amount of county property taxes owed on the dwelling. The credit must be renewed annually.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: on or before May 1st of each year
structured_extraction.contact_phone: Dorchester County Fire & EMS: 501 Court Lane, Cambridge, MD 21613
structured_extraction.program_audience: Volunteer firefighters in Dorchester County who are members of bona fide Dorchester County volunteer fire companies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit against county real property taxes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Dorchester County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a member of a bona fide Dorchester County Volunteer Fire Company recognized and in good standing with the Dorchester County Volunteer Firemen's Association
Must have maintained active service for three or more years
Must be eligible to reduce Maryland taxable income pursuant to Md. Code Ann., Tax - General § 10-208(i-1)
Must be eligible for the credit authorized under Md. Code Ann., Tax - Property § 9-105
Must own the property to which the credit will be applied
Property must be used as principal residence
Must occupy the property for more than 6 months of a 12-month period
Must submit application on or before May 1st of each year
Must include MSFA-P.2.2 form from the volunteer fire company
Tax credit terminates if member no longer qualifies as a Qualifying Member or no longer resides in or owns the dwelling
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Dorchester County Volunteer Fire Department Member - Property Tax Credit Application form and include the MSFA-P.2.2 form provided by your volunteer fire company. Submit the completed application and supporting documents to the Dorchester County Finance Office by May 1st of each year. The Finance Office will verify eligibility and process the credit. Annual renewal is required.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Structure Rehabilitation Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for property owners who rehabilitate structures, phasing in the taxation of increased assessed value.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners who have rehabilitated structures receive a tax credit that phases in the taxation of increased taxable assessed value from the rehabilitation. The credit amount is determined based on the cost of rehabilitation and is applied over multiple years. Applications must be submitted within twelve months of the Notice of Assessment reflecting the increased value.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within twelve months of Notice of Assessment reflecting increase
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Dorchester County undertaking structure rehabilitation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit to phase in taxation of the increased property value resulting from rehabilitation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Dorchester County
requirements_list: Must be a property owner in Dorchester County
Must have rehabilitated a structure
Must apply and be approved by the county
Application must be submitted within twelve months of Notice of Assessment reflecting increase
Cost of rehabilitation must equal or exceed 50% of pre-rehabilitation assessed value
Rehabilitated structure cannot expand pre-rehabilitation footprint by more than 20%
Property must be current on all property taxes and not otherwise indebted to County
Property must comply with all County building, fire, zoning, and development related ordinances
Must provide copy of County or Municipal building permit
Must provide copies of invoices and cancelled checks supporting cost of rehabilitation
Must provide copy of Notice of Assessment reflecting increased assessment resulting from rehabilitation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Property Structure Rehabilitation Real Property Tax Credit form. Required supporting documentation includes: (1) copy of County or Municipal building permit, (2) copies of invoices and cancelled checks supporting cost of rehabilitation, and (3) copy of Notice of Assessment reflecting increased assessment. Submit the completed application to Dorchester County Department of Finance, 501 Court Lane, Cambridge, MD 21613. Once approved, the tax credit phases in the taxation of the increased assessed value over the designated credit period.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for homeowners who installed qualified residential sprinkler systems during the eligible time period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved homeowners who installed qualified residential sprinkler systems with a Certificate of Occupancy date between July 1, 2019 and June 30, 2022 receive a tax credit equal to the lesser of $5,000 or actual cost against their county real property taxes. The credit can be taken in up to three years, limited by county tax levied each year, with any unused portion carrying over to subsequent years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: for systems with Certificate of Occupancy dated between July 1, 2019 and June 30, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners in Dorchester County who installed qualified residential sprinkler systems with Certificate of Occupancy between July 1, 2019 and June 30, 2022
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit for the cost of installing qualified residential sprinkler systems
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Dorchester County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a homeowner in Dorchester County
Must have installed a qualified residential sprinkler system with Certificate of Occupancy dated between July 1, 2019 and June 30, 2022
Must prove principal residency (approved homestead credit application, affidavit, etc.)
Must provide proof of total cost through invoices, contracts, or installer certification
Credit is limited to the lesser of $5,000 or actual cost
Credit can be taken over up to three years, limited by county tax levied each year
Must apply and be approved by the county
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Application for Residential Sprinkler System Tax Credit form and submit it to the Dorchester County Department of Finance at 501 Court Lane, Cambridge, MD 21613. Required supporting documentation includes: copy of Certificate of Occupancy, proof of principal residency, and copies of invoices, contracts, or installer certification supporting total cost of sprinkler system. Once approved, the tax credit is applied against county real property taxes over up to three years as limited by county tax levied.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shoreline Erosion Control Structure Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for residents who have installed qualified shoreline erosion control structures to prevent coastal erosion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approved residents who installed qualified shoreline erosion control structures after June 30, 2006 receive 30% of the cost of the structure as a tax credit against their real property taxes. The credit is calculated as (Cost of Structure × 30%) / 15 years and is distributed over 15 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Dorchester County with qualifying shoreline erosion control structures
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit for the cost of installing qualified shoreline erosion control structures
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Dorchester County, for structures installed after June 30, 2006
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Dorchester County
Must have installed a qualified shoreline erosion control structure after June 30, 2006

Structure must be one of the following types: Steel Bulkhead, Timber Bulkhead, Vinyl Bulkhead, Concrete Wall, Stone Masonry Wall, Stone Revetment, Stone Reinforcement, Stone Breakwater, or Jetty/Groin

Must obtain permits from Maryland Department of Environment - Tidal Wetlands Division, United States Army Corps of Engineers, and Dorchester County, or obtain Letter of Exemption from Maryland Department of Environment
Must provide copies of invoices and cancelled checks supporting total cost of structure
Must apply and be approved by the county
Application must be submitted in the same year the structure is installed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Shoreline Erosion Control Structure Real Property Tax Credit Application form and submit to Dorchester County Department of Finance, 501 Court Lane, Cambridge, MD 21613. Required supporting documentation includes: 1) copies of permits from Maryland Department of Environment - Tidal Wetlands Division, United States Army Corps of Engineers, and Dorchester County, or copy of Letter of Exemption from Maryland Department of Environment; and 2) copies of invoices and cancelled checks supporting total cost of structure. Once approved, the tax credit is applied against real property taxes over a 15-year period.

structured_extraction.program_description: A policy that allows Dorchester County to waive landfill disposal and tipping fees on the disposal of construction debris for certain community development projects. The program is designed to encourage community development, reduce blight, and increase assessable property values.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County waives tipping fees (landfill disposal charges) on the disposal of construction debris at the Dorchester County Landfill at Beulah. Fees are waived at $65 per ton (as of FY2021). Maximum award per project is determined annually as part of the budget request. Each organization can receive up to $20,000 per year or $100,000 over the lifetime of the organization, unless special approval is granted by County Council. If actual tonnage exceeds the estimate by more than 10%, the request must be resubmitted for approval.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: Dorchester County Office Building, Room 108, 501 Court Lane, Cambridge, MD 21613
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, developers, organizations, and the County undertaking community development projects, blight removal, school construction, or economic development projects in Dorchester County that involve construction debris disposal.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Waiver of landfill disposal tipping fees for construction debris from qualifying community development, blight removal, school construction, and economic development projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Dorchester County, Maryland. Projects must be located in Dorchester County.
requirements_list: Project must qualify under one of the approved categories: County projects funded by grants; Economic development projects supported by County or grant funds; School construction; or other economic development, blight removal projects as approved by the Review Committee
Disposal must involve construction debris at the Dorchester County Landfill at Beulah

Requestor must complete and submit the Tipping Fee Waiver Request Form including organization name, address, contact information, project location, project description, estimated tonnage, and estimated cost
Each organization limited to maximum of $20,000 per year or $100,000 over the lifetime of the organization unless special approval from County Council is obtained
If actual tonnage exceeds estimate by more than 10%, request must be resubmitted to Review Committee for approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Requestor completes the Tipping Fee Waiver Request Form (Attachment A) with project details, estimated tonnage, and estimated costs. 2. Submit completed form to Dorchester County Office Building, Room 108, 501 Court Lane, Cambridge, MD 21613 by August 15th, November 15th, February 15th, or May 15th for consideration at the next quarterly meeting. 3. The Review Committee (consisting of one County Council member, County Manager, Finance Director, Public Works Director, and one other County staff member) reviews requests at quarterly meetings held on the first business day of September, December, March, and June. 4. Requests may be deferred if more information or review time is needed. 5. Upon approval, awardee receives an Award Letter to present at the Landfill. 6. Upon delivery of debris, Award Letter and Tonnage Tracking Form must be presented to Landfill personnel who record the tonnage. 7. Upon project completion, Receipts and Tonnage Tracking Form must be forwarded to Finance for recording.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensees, managers, employees, and others in the alcohol service industry in Frederick County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Attendance at training sessions covering alcohol beverage laws and regulations specific to Frederick County.

Must register for class attendance

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to improve the economic viability of agriculture by encouraging Frederick County agricultural producers to expand or diversify their business operations. Eligible applicants can receive grants for research and development, production buildings, major fixtures, and processing facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to eligible agricultural producers, value-added producers, agricultural cooperatives, seafood processors, and timber products processors for research and development, production buildings, major fixtures, and processing facilities. Grants can range up to a maximum award amount determined annually. Grant recipients must submit monthly Expense Substantiation Forms with backup documentation by the 30th of each month until all grant funds are expended. Funds must be used for eligible capital improvements as approved by Frederick County.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The next cycle will open October 1, 2026
structured_extraction.contact_name: Becca Tucker, Senior Business Development Manager of Agriculture
structured_extraction.program_audience: Frederick County agricultural producers, crop or livestock producers, value-added producers, agricultural cooperatives, seafood processors, and primary or secondary timber products processors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Research and development, production buildings, major fixtures, and processing facilities to expand or diversify farm business operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must be currently operating in Frederick County for at least one year
Must have recorded at least $2,500 in annual sales or include an outline of investment and impact on future sales in business plan
Must provide documented evidence of outreach to Frederick County Planning & Zoning discussing proposed project requirements

Must fall into one of the eligible applicant categories: crop or livestock producer, value-added producer, agricultural cooperative, seafood processor, or primary or secondary timber products processor
Must contact Frederick County Zoning Office during current grant cycle to verify project is an allowed use
Projects involving waste discharge require contact with Frederick County Health Department
Projects involving land in a Land Preservation Easement require verification that project is an allowed use
If property owner or immediate family member is not the applicant, a signed rental agreement with terms must be submitted
Must develop a business plan with executive summary, operations plan, marketing plan, and financial projections
Must prepare a detailed budget with breakdown by expense category and identify other funding sources
Must prepare a Capital Needed Description with brief description of equipment or facilities and estimated useful life
Must write an Economic Impact Description explaining impact on farm enterprise
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Develop a comprehensive business plan including executive summary, operations plan, marketing plan, and financial projections. Resources available include suggested table of contents, University of Minnesota draft plans, and free counseling from Maryland Small Business Development Center or Maryland Women's Business Center. 2. Contact Frederick County Zoning Office to ensure planned project is an allowed use; provide project description, property address, existing structures, and whether public will be invited. 3. For projects with waste discharge, contact Frederick County Health Department before applying. 4. For projects on land in a Land Preservation Easement, contact Shannon O'Neil to verify allowed use. 5. Prepare a detailed budget broken down by expense category and identify other funding sources. 6. Prepare a Capital Needed Description with brief description of equipment or facilities and estimated useful life. 7. Write an Economic Impact Description explaining impact on farm enterprise. 8. Submit completed application with all supporting documentation. Applications are scored on a 100-point rubric evaluating project description, budget and capital needed, innovation, economic impact, and business plan components. Bonus points awarded if business has never been a recipient of a Frederick County Agriculture Innovation Grant.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a state match of the builder's contribution up to $5,000 per qualifying project. Clients must receive a mortgage through the Maryland Mortgage Program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary, non-adversarial judicial program for non-violent, drug-involved offenders charged in Circuit Court. It is a post-plea, pre-sentence program where defendants plead guilty and sentencing is deferred. Participants receive comprehensive supervision and treatment including substance use and mental health treatment, case management, education, peer recovery services, and vocational and rehabilitative services. The program aims to help participants achieve self-sufficiency and become responsible, drug-free community members.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides comprehensive supervision and treatment services including substance use disorder treatment, mental health treatment, case management, education, peer recovery support, vocational services, and rehabilitative services. Participants must plead guilty with sentencing deferred. Upon successful completion or program termination, sentencing occurs. The program typically lasts 12-18 months and includes regular court appearances, drug testing, treatment sessions, and compliance with all program requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-violent, drug-involved offenders charged in Frederick County Circuit Court. Many participants are unemployed, indigent, single parents with educational, job training, housing, and social issues.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supervision and treatment services including substance use treatment, mental health treatment, case management, education, peer recovery services, and vocational and rehabilitative services.

requirements_list: Must be charged with a non-violent, drug-involved offense in Frederick County Circuit Court
Must plead guilty to enter the program
Must participate fully with all prescribed treatment and instructions of DTC staff
Must comply with regular drug testing and court appearances
Must actively engage in substance use treatment and mental health services as needed
Must participate in case management and education services
Eligibility requirements are blind to race, ethnicity, gender, and/or religious orientation
Must not have serious disciplinary violations or be a danger to the community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Defendants, defense attorneys, or treatment providers can submit a referral form to the DTC Coordinator. The DTC Coordinator reviews referrals for eligibility based on established criteria. Eligible defendants are notified and can enter the program as a post-plea, pre-sentence option. Initial orientation and assessment occur upon acceptance into the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Grant and Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funds to homeowners and landlords to reduce or eliminate lead-based paint hazards in their homes and preserve the housing stock. Eligible activities include treating doors and windows, treating floors, removing paint, stabilizing and repainting surfaces, encapsulating hazards, enclosing hazards, and specialized cleaning.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funds are issued as either a grant or a loan based on the applicant's ability to repay. Grants are available to eligible low-income homeowners and landlords whose properties are located in targeted census tracts. Loans have a maximum term of 20 years. Interest rates are competitive and based on creditworthiness. No income limits apply to the loan program, though grant funding prioritizes lower-income applicants. Loan amounts and grant awards vary based on the scope of work needed and property value.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who own homes used as their principal residence, landlords who own rental properties, and licensed childcare facilities in Frederick County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reducing or eliminating lead-based paint hazards through door and window treatment, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, and specialized cleaning. Work must result in units that are structurally sound and free from lead hazards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in targeted census tracts in Frederick County to qualify for a grant. Loan program is available throughout Frederick County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland resident
Property must be owner-occupied and used as principal residence, OR a rental property, OR a licensed childcare facility
Units must be in need of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be structurally sound upon completion of lead reduction work
Units must be in a targeted census tract to qualify for a grant
Rental properties built prior to 1950 must be registered with the Maryland Department of the Environment Lead Poisoning Prevention Program
Property must be located in Frederick County
For grants, applicants must meet income eligibility requirements for targeted census tracts
All work must comply with EPA lead-safe work practices standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Frederick County Department of Housing and Community Development to request an application package and to schedule a property inspection. The inspection determines eligibility and scope of work needed. Applicants submit a completed application with supporting documentation including proof of residency, property ownership, and income verification (for grant applicants). Applications are reviewed and processed on a rolling basis. Once approved, eligible work is contracted and completed by certified lead abatement contractors. The county provides grant or loan funds directly to contractors upon completion of approved work.

structured_extraction.program_name: Rehabilitated Vacant Commercial Structures Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit that encourages property owners to rehabilitate vacant commercial buildings and invest in infrastructure. Vacant properties must have been empty for at least 18 of the last 24 months and must be for non-residential use in areas zoned for commercial or industrial purposes. The structure must have been built before 2000.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit for rehabilitation of qualifying vacant commercial structures. The credit is calculated by determining the increase in assessed property value attributable to the reconstruction and improvements, applying the applicable tax rate, and then applying a percentage exemption for the applicable fiscal year. The credit is applied to the property tax bill in the first full year that the improvements are added to the assessment roll.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 30th for the tax credit to be applied on the following Fiscal Year's tax bill (mailed July 1)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners rehabilitating vacant commercial buildings in Frederick County and the City of Frederick, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit applies to property taxes on rehabilitated vacant commercial structures. Credits can be applied to either Frederick County or City of Frederick property tax bills depending on the property location.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County and the City of Frederick, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must have been vacant for at least 18 of the last 24 months prior to lease or sale
Property must be used for non-residential purposes
Property must be located in an area permitting commercial or industrial use
Structure must have been constructed before 2000
Property must have been actively listed for sale or lease during the vacancy period
Pedestrian and vehicular connections to adjacent commercial properties must be provided, or documentation from Planning Department must demonstrate such connections are not feasible
Application must include certification from a commercial real estate broker confirming vacancy period and active listing status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply for the tax credit, submit the application form and all backup documentation to the State Department of Assessment & Taxation located at 5310 Spectrum Drive, Frederick, MD 21703. Applications must be submitted before April 30th for the tax credit to be applied on the following Fiscal Year's tax bill. The application requires the property owner's oath that they are the present owner and information is true and correct. A commercial real estate broker must certify the property location and vacancy history. The State Department of Assessment and Taxation determines the increase in assessment attributable to reconstruction and improvements. The applicable city or county then calculates the tax credit by multiplying the assessment increase by the tax rate and the percentage of exemption for the year.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $200,000 in grant funding is available to support eligible municipalities with roadway safety projects. Grants support infrastructure improvements, traffic calming measures, pedestrian safety enhancements, and other initiatives that align with the Toward Zero Deaths Action Plan. Applications are accepted as long as funding is available on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted as long as funding is available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible municipalities in Frederick County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Roadway safety projects and infrastructure improvements that enhance traffic safety, reduce speeds in high-risk areas, improve pedestrian and bicycle safety, enhance visibility, and reduce traffic-related deaths and serious injuries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County municipalities
requirements_list: Must be an eligible municipality within Frederick County
Project must improve roadway safety and align with Toward Zero Deaths priorities
Project must address traffic-related safety concerns
Municipality must have capacity to implement and maintain the project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Municipalities interested in applying should contact Mark Mishler at the Frederick County Department of Transportation to discuss project ideas and alignment with Toward Zero Deaths priorities. Applicants submit project proposals detailing the safety issue, proposed solution, expected outcomes, and budget. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as long as funding remains available. Award decisions are made based on project merit, safety impact, and alignment with program goals.

structured_extraction.program_name: Golden Mile Tax Credit and Arts and Entertainment Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A state, county, and city tax credit program designed to incentivize rehabilitation of existing commercial structures along the Route 40 West Corridor (Golden Mile) in Frederick and within the Downtown Frederick Arts and Entertainment District. The program provides decreasing tax abatement over seven years on building improvements for qualifying property owners and developers.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A decreasing tax abatement over seven years. Year 1: 100% of eligible rehabilitation costs on building improvements; Year 2: 80%; Year 3: 60%; Year 4: 40%; Year 5: 20%; Years 6-7: 0%. Credits apply to property taxes for qualifying building improvements and rehabilitation of existing commercial structures in eligible districts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers rehabilitating existing commercial structures along the Golden Mile (Route 40 West Corridor) and within the Downtown Frederick Arts and Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credits apply to property taxes for building improvements and rehabilitation of existing commercial structures, including exterior facade work, interior renovations, signage, and other structural improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Route 40 West (Golden Mile) corridor through the City of Frederick and the Downtown Frederick Arts and Entertainment District. Program applies to commercial properties within these designated areas.
requirements_list: Rehabilitate existing structures with a minimum rehabilitation cost threshold
Located in the Golden Mile (Route 40 West Corridor) or the Downtown Frederick Arts and Entertainment District
Property must be a commercial building
Property owner must own the building or have development rights
Improvements must meet program standards and guidelines
Application must be submitted prior to beginning rehabilitation work
Projects must be completed within specified timeframes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Golden Mile Tax Credit Application form to the City of Frederick Development Services Department. Applications should be submitted before beginning rehabilitation work. The application includes project details, cost estimates, property information, and owner/developer identification. Staff reviews applications for eligibility and program compliance. Upon approval and project completion, property owners claim the tax credits on their property tax returns over the seven-year period.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County Commercial & Industrial Business Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers a 10-year real property tax credit for manufacturing, fabricating, or assembling businesses in Frederick County. It supports businesses that build new facilities or expand existing ones. The credit reduces the amount of property tax owed on the value of new improvements. To qualify, businesses must make a total new investment of at least $5 million and create at least 25 new permanent jobs paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county provides a 10-year tax credit on real property taxes resulting from building or expanding a facility. The credit is calculated as a percentage of the new property tax liability on the value of the improvements. The credit is equal to a percentage of the increase in real property taxes on the value of new improvements to real property used in manufacturing, fabricating, or assembling operations. If the average credit over the 10 years exceeds 60% of the new tax amount, the Frederick County Council must approve it. The credit applies only to the incremental tax increase from the new improvements and does not apply to the underlying property value.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1 of the tax year which the facility is first eligible
structured_extraction.contact_name: Frederick County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Manufacturing, fabricating, and assembling businesses in Frederick County seeking to expand or establish new facilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit applies to real property taxes on new facility construction or expansion. The credit is a property tax reduction on the value of new improvements to real property used in manufacturing, fabricating, or assembling operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Frederick County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must conduct manufacturing, fabricating, or assembling operations within Frederick County
Must have a total new investment of at least $5 million
Must create at least 25 new permanent jobs
New jobs must pay at least 150% of the federal minimum wage
New positions may not be transferred from another location in Frederick County
Facility must be new construction or expansion of existing facility
Business must maintain operations for the entire 10-year credit period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process begins by contacting the Frederick County Office of Economic Development at 301-600-1058 to discuss your project and determine eligibility. Next, submit an application to the County Treasurer by October 1 of the first tax year your facility is eligible for the credit. The application should include information about the investment amount, number of new jobs created, wage levels, and details about the facility. After the initial approval, file a form every year by April 30 to demonstrate continued eligibility for the credit. The County Council reviews applications where the average annual credit exceeds 60% of the new tax amount and must approve those applications.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A 12-year real property tax credit for businesses that expand their facilities by at least 250,000 square feet and create a large number of new jobs within Frederick County. The credit applies to property tax increases on new or expanded premises and substantially renovated adjacent properties. Businesses must be located in a Priority Funding Area within Frederick County.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 12-year credit equal to 58.5% of the property tax imposed on the increase in assessment of new or expanded premises and substantially renovated adjoining or neighboring real property. The credit begins after substantial completion of the capital improvement. A substantial renovation is defined as at least 50% of each building on the property. The credit applies to the increased real property tax amount that results from a business expansion and is forfeited if the business relocates outside of Frederick County or reduces employment below the required thresholds during the 12-year period.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Frederick County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses making major expansions and capital investments that are already located in Frederick County or are relocating to the county from outside of Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit applies to property taxes on the increased assessment from new construction, expansion, or substantial renovation of real property. The credit cannot be transferred or assigned.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located in a Priority Funding Area within Frederick County.
requirements_list: Must be established in Frederick County or relocate to the county from outside Maryland
Must construct or expand premises by at least 250,000 square feet

Must create at least 1,250 full-time permanent jobs paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage, OR create at least 2,500 full-time jobs and add 500 more positions, all paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage
New construction only (substantial renovation of adjoining property qualifies if at least 50% of each building is renovated)
Must notify the County's Director of Finance of the intent to claim the credit before the expansion begins
Must maintain the required number of jobs and facility size throughout the 12-year credit period
Credit is forfeited if business relocates outside Frederick County or employment falls below required levels
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Frederick County Office of Economic Development to discuss the project and eligibility. Notify the County's Director of Finance in writing of the plan to claim the credit before the expansion begins. Submit application materials including business information, expansion plans, job creation projections, and payroll documentation. The county will review the application for compliance with program requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County New Jobs Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a six-year tax credit on real property to businesses that construct or expand their facilities by at least 5,000 square feet in a Frederick County priority funding area and create at least 25 full-time jobs within the first two years of expansion. Available for new construction only, the credit helps businesses new to Frederick County, already located there, or relocating from outside Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a tax credit on the increased value of a business's real property after an expansion. The credit amount decreases over six years: 52% for years one and two, 39% for years three and four, and 26% for years five and six. The credit applies to property taxes on the increased assessed value resulting from the expansion. Applicants must notify the County's Director of Finance of their intent to claim the credit before expanding.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Frederick County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses that are new to Frederick County, already located there, or relocating to the county from outside Maryland, that are constructing or expanding facilities in a priority funding area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The benefit is a reduction in real property taxes for businesses that expand their facilities in a priority funding area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Priority funding areas in Frederick County
requirements_list: Must be established in Frederick County or relocate to the county from outside Maryland.
Must construct or expand premises by at least 5,000 square feet.
Must create at least 25 full-time jobs within the first 24 months after occupying the new or expanded premises.
Must maintain the 25 full-time permanent positions for three years after each year a tax credit is allowed.
Project must be located in a priority funding area.
New construction only.
Must notify the County's Director of Finance of intent to claim the credit before expansion begins.
Businesses must occupy the new or expanded premises.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact the Frederick County Office of Economic Development at 301-600-1058 to discuss eligibility and obtain application materials. Before beginning expansion, notify the County's Director of Finance of your intent to claim the credit. Complete the application form and submit supporting documentation. After expansion is complete and the required 25 jobs have been created, submit documentation of job creation and the increase in assessed property value to claim the tax credit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Frederick County Small Business Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A six-year tax credit on real property taxes for businesses that expand their location or relocate to Frederick County and hire additional staff. Businesses must obtain at least 2,500 square feet of new or expanded premises and employ at least five full-time workers within 24 months of occupying the space. The credit applies to the incremental increase in property tax value resulting from the expansion.
structured_extraction.agency: Frederick County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a six-year tax credit based on the incremental increase in real property tax value resulting from a business expansion or relocation. The credit decreases over six years: 40% of the incremental tax increase in years one and two, 30% in years three and four, and 20% in years five and six. The credit applies only to the tax increase attributable to the expansion; the original property tax liability remains unchanged. After six years, no further credit is available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: on or before October 1 of the tax year for which the real property is first eligible and must reapply annually
structured_extraction.contact_name: Frederick County Office of Economic Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses expanding in or relocating to Frederick County from outside of Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit applies to real property taxes resulting from a business expansion or relocation. Credits reduce the incremental tax liability associated with the expanded or new property footprint.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The business must be located in a Frederick County Priority Funding Area. Eligible businesses include existing county businesses expanding their footprint or businesses relocating from outside Maryland to Frederick County.
requirements_list: Business must obtain at least 2,500 square feet of new or expanded premises
Business must employ at least five full-time workers within the first 24 months of occupying the new or expanded space
Business must meet both job creation and space requirements within a 24-month period from occupancy
Business location must be in a Frederick County Priority Funding Area
Applicant must notify the County's Director of Finance of intent to claim the credit on or before October 1 of the first eligible tax year
Business must reapply for the credit annually to continue receiving benefits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact the Frederick County Office of Economic Development at 301-600-1058 to discuss your expansion or relocation plans and confirm eligibility. Next, notify the County's Director of Finance in writing of your intent to claim the credit on or before October 1 of the tax year for which the property first becomes eligible. You must meet the space and employment requirements within 24 months of occupying the new or expanded premises. You must reapply for the credit annually to continue receiving the tax credit benefit for the six-year period.

structured_extraction.program_description: Garrett County Government provides subsidies to help residents in difficult-to-serve areas access broadband service when the cost to connect their home is beyond their budget. The program helps bridge the gap between what a resident can afford to pay and the total cost charged by internet service providers to extend service to their address.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program pays directly to internet service providers to help cover the cost of extending broadband service to residences in Garrett County. Residents in situations where they cannot afford the full customer contribution (or can only afford part of it) may receive assistance. The customer may be asked to contribute up to 10 percent of the requested subsidy amount if possible. Funding per project is limited, and internet service providers must also contribute to each project and must participate in the Affordable Connectivity Program to qualify. Only valid expenses directly related to connecting a customer to broadband service qualify—no direct customer expenses can be paid or reimbursed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Garrett County who have been quoted a price to bring broadband service to their home and cannot afford the full customer contribution.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The subsidy covers only valid expenses directly related to connecting a customer to broadband service. Payments are made directly to internet service providers and cannot be used for direct customer expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is limited to difficult-to-serve addresses in Garrett County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Resident must have requested service from an internet service provider
Internet service provider must have developed a budget to reach the home
Customer must not be able to afford the full customer contribution or can only afford part of it
Address must not already be served by a broadband service provider with minimum service of 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload
If another provider can serve the address without a subsidy, no subsidy will be given to a different provider
Internet service providers must be willing to contribute to the project
Internet service providers must participate in the Affordable Connectivity Program to qualify (if the program is funded)
Permits, easements, and other legal requirements may apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A potential customer contacts an internet service provider requesting service. The provider assesses the situation and develops a budget. If the customer cannot afford the full amount or can only afford part of it, the customer can ask the internet service provider to request a subsidy from Garrett County, or the customer can request the subsidy directly by contacting Cheryl DeBerry at the Broadband Division. If the customer requests the subsidy directly, the County will work with the internet service provider to develop a project budget. Upon approval, the internet service provider can begin the project.

structured_extraction.program_description: A license that permits non-profit organizations in Garrett County to operate paper gaming devices — including tip jars, pull tabs, bingo, raffles, and 50/50 drawings — to raise funds for their organization. The license renews automatically unless suspended by the county. The permit is non-transferable and may be revoked at any time by the county. Applicants must agree to abide by all regulations established by the Board of County Commissioners of Garrett County.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fundraising through paper gaming devices such as tip jars, pull tabs, bingo, raffles, and 50/50 drawings for organizational purposes.

requirements_list: Must be a non-profit charitable, civic, volunteer fire/rescue, ambulance, youth activities, fraternal, war veterans, religious, school/PTA, or similar organization
Must obtain a Paper Gaming License from Garrett County
Must provide Maryland State Tax ID and/or Federal Tax ID if organization has one
Must designate an authorized representative with contact information
Must select all applicable gaming types (tip jars, raffle, bingo, pull tabs, 50/50)
Must agree that the Gaming Permit is an annual permit that may be revoked at any time
Must agree that the license is non-transferable
Must abide by all regulations pertaining to the license established by the Board of County Commissioners of Garrett County
If in doubt about eligibility, applicants are encouraged to apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the fillable Paper Gaming License Application form with organization details, authorized representative information, and selected gaming types. Applications can be submitted online at garrettcountymd.gov/community-development/paper-gaming or mailed to the address above. Contact gaming@garrettcountymd.gov or call 301-334-8970 for submission details.

structured_extraction.program_name: County Business Property Tax Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for new and expanding businesses in Garrett County that make improvements to business property. The program provides a credit against the county portion of real property tax on the improvements for five years, starting at 50% of the assessed value of improvements and decreasing by 10% each year (40%, 30%, 20%, 10%) in years 2-5. The credit helps offset the cost of property expansions, renovations, or capital improvements for commercial and industrial businesses. After five years, the improved property returns to the tax rolls at its full assessed value.
structured_extraction.agency: Garrett County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit against the county portion of real property tax on business property improvements. The credit is based on the increase in assessed value of improvements only. The credit is 50% of the assessed increase in year one, then decreases by 10% annually to 40%, 30%, 20%, and 10% in years 2-5 respectively. The minimum improvement threshold is $100,000 in real property capital improvements as determined by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. Improvements must be completed on or after July 1, 2007. The tax credit applies only to full tax years beginning July 1, 2008, and does not apply to state property tax or municipal property tax levies. The credit is based on the initial assessment of improvements at the time of assessment by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation and is not affected by subsequent general property value increases. If a business is also eligible for enterprise zone property tax credits, the combined credit cannot exceed 100% of the real property tax levied on the improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and expanding commercial or industrial businesses in Garrett County making property improvements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real property capital improvements including expansion, renovation, or capital improvement to business property that increases the tax assessment by at least $100,000. Improvements must be made on or after July 1, 2007.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Garrett County, Maryland. Improvements must be made on or after July 1, 2007, and the property tax credit applies to full tax years beginning July 1, 2008.
requirements_list: Minimum of $100,000 in real property capital improvements as determined by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation

Business must be certified by the Department as a qualified business entity
If property is purchased (new business), improvements must be made to the property for eligibility
If existing business is sold, remaining tax credits pass through to new owner for remaining years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, the business must notify the Department of Economic Development's designated contact (Kim E. Durst) of its intent to seek certification for the property tax credit immediately upon completion of any expansion, renovation, or capital improvement to the property. Second, the business must complete and submit the application form (provided by the Department) to the designated contact. If the business qualifies based on meeting all eligibility requirements, the designated contact will issue a certificate of eligibility. Businesses are required to pay any partial year County tax bills that may be issued, then receive the County property tax credit for a five-year period as set forth in the program guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that enables local jurisdictions to implement or maintain a Day Reporting Center providing community-based services and treatment to individuals under parole, probation, pretrial supervision, or individuals sentenced directly to a Day Reporting Center. The program aims to reduce recidivism, jail and prison populations, and corrections-related costs. Participants receive services including counseling, cognitive behavioral therapy, drug treatment, educational remediation, job training, and intensive supervision. Day reporting centers serve as an alternative to incarceration for non-violent adult offenders.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to local government agencies to establish and operate Day Reporting Centers. Funding range is $135,000 to $270,000, with up to two awards anticipated. Funding categories include personnel (counselors, case managers, peer recovery staff), operating expenses (rent, communication, postage), travel, contractual services (up to $81.25/hour or $650/day for consultants), equipment ($10,000 or more per unit), and other costs (program supplies, drug/alcohol test kits, medications for opioid use disorder, equipment under $10,000). Grant funds are reimbursed based on actual quarterly expenditures. Period of performance is July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

structured_extraction.program_name: Body Armor for Local Law Enforcement (BARM)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded reimbursement grant that helps local law enforcement agencies purchase and replace bullet-resistant body armor and stab-resistant vests for sworn officers. The program reimburses eligible non-state local law enforcement agencies for 50% of the cost of body armor vests, supporting the safety of law enforcement personnel across Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a reimbursement grant covering 50% of the cost of bullet-resistant body armor vests and stab-resistant vests purchased by eligible local law enforcement agencies. For SFY 2027, the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy anticipates $49,088 in available funding to make between 5-15 awards not to exceed $5,000 each. A 50% cash or in-kind cost share (match) is required. Grant funds are reimbursed based on actual quarterly expenditures. Vests must comply with National Institute of Justice Standard NIJ 0101.07 (or current edition) for ballistic-resistant armor and NIJ 0115.00 for stab-resistant armor. Applicants may not purchase any vests containing Zylon material. All vests must be approved by the National Institute of Justice. The cost of vests and carriers must be separated into distinct line items in the budget.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local law enforcement agencies from any Maryland county, incorporated city or town, including Baltimore City. State agencies are not eligible. Agencies that received BARM funding in FY 2026 are not eligible to apply for SFY 2027 funds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and replacement of bullet-resistant body armor vests and stab-resistant vests for sworn law enforcement officers. Funding is for sworn officers only and cannot extend past the grant period ending June 30, 2027. Agencies may purchase new vests for officers not currently assigned protective body armor or replacement vests for officers with armor that is five years old or older or shows signs of wear or age-related degradation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to local law enforcement agencies in any Maryland county, incorporated city or town, including Baltimore City. State agencies are excluded.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Sex Trafficking Screening and Services Act Regional Navigator Program (RGNV)
structured_extraction.program_description: The program expands regional navigator services to help identify and assist child victims of sex trafficking across Maryland. Law enforcement and local social services are required to notify a Regional Navigator when they have reason to believe a child is a victim of sex trafficking to obtain needed services. The program screens for and provides services to child sex trafficking victims, helping them achieve self-sufficiency, improve safety, and ensure awareness of their rights and resources. Funding supports community-based nonprofit organizations, designated Child Advocacy Centers, and Rape Crisis Centers in establishing and operating regional navigator programs. Services are available to suspected child sex or labor trafficking victims until age 24.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support regional navigator programs. Grantees can receive awards ranging from $50,000 to $200,000 for single jurisdiction or up to $500,000 for multiple jurisdictions. Funds are distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis following submission of quarterly fiscal and programmatic reports. Allowable costs include personnel, operating expenses, contractual services, equipment, supplies, training, and other direct costs essential to providing services. Grant funding covers safety planning, emergency response, basic living needs (excluding housing), trauma counseling and mental health services, drug and alcohol abuse treatment, legal services, victim advocacy, and case management for child sex and labor trafficking victims until age 24. Unallowable costs include housing, construction projects, prosecution activities, research and studies, active investigations, fundraising, capital expenses, compensation for victims, medical care, perpetrator rehabilitation, property insurance, and food/beverage for events.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel costs, travel, and other expenses related to establishing and operating regional navigator programs to screen for and provide services to child sex and labor trafficking victims. Specific allowable services include safety planning, emergency response, basic living needs (excluding housing), trauma counseling and mental health services, drug and alcohol abuse treatment, legal services, victim advocacy, case management, public awareness, forensic interviews, restorative justice, and coordination of activities. Grant funds can support skills training for staff, training materials, training-related travel, equipment and furniture, advanced technologies, contracts for professional services, supervision of direct service providers, and other necessary costs essential to providing quality direct services to crime victims.

Available statewide across all Maryland counties to comply with the Child Sex Trafficking Screening and Services Act of 2019. structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations apply through the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy's web-based Grant Management System (GMS). The application process includes: (1) Requesting a GMS User ID and password from the website http://gocpp.maryland.gov/grants/requesting-access/ (deadline typically 2 weeks before application deadline); (2) Accessing the GMS at https://grants.goccp.maryland.gov using login credentials; (3) Completing the Face Sheet with project title, applicant agency, authorized official, implementing agency, service sites, grant award period, and preparer information; (4) Entering required grant personnel (Project Director, Fiscal Officer, Civil Rights Contact); (5) Completing the Project Summary (100 words or less); (6) Submitting the narrative sections including Overall Organization Information, Problem Statement/Needs Justification, Program Purpose Area, Project Design, Project Goals and Objectives with past performance indicators, Data Collection Plan, Grant Personnel with organizational structure for nonprofits, Sustainability, Disclosure of Pending Applications, and Budget & Spending Plan; (7) Uploading required documents including Certified Assurances, Certification Regarding Lobbying, W-9 Form, SAM.gov UEI screenshot, Certificate of Applicable Financial Reporting Requirements, Determination of Suitability to Interact with Minors Form, Subrecipient Organizational Capacity Questionnaire, most recent organizational chart, and proof of 501(c)(3) status for new nonprofits; (8) Submitting the budget with all line items placed in appropriate categories (Personnel, Operating Expenses, Travel, Contractual Services, Equipment, Other); (9) Completing the Budget Priority tab to prioritize funding line items; (10) Submitting the application through GMS before the deadline (hard copy applications not accepted). Technical assistance is available through GMS help videos, application instructions, and technical assistance conference calls. Post-award, grantees must submit quarterly fiscal reports within 30 calendar days and programmatic reports within 15 calendar days of quarter end through the GMS. Funds are distributed quarterly on a reimbursement basis following timely submission of reports. For SFY 2026, only programs funded through SFY 2025 RNPG are eligible for continuation funding.

Funds support front-end, intake, and investigative stage activities in child welfare. Grant funds are reimbursed based on actual quarterly expenditures. Allowable costs include: Personnel (salaries for grant-funded staff); Contractual Services (training, consulting, victim advocacy); Equipment (purchase of items with unit cost over $5,000 with prior approval); Other Direct Costs (travel, equipment under $5,000, communications, office supplies, stipends); and Indirect Costs (if approved cognizant agency). Direct services to victims are not permitted. Priority implementation areas: Law enforcement training and capacity-building for child maltreatment investigation; Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) capacity within Child Advocacy Centers; and Forensic interviewing enhancements.

Specific use of funds must align with one or more of three priority areas: (1) Law Enforcement - improve capacity to recognize, assess, and investigate child maltreatment through training, new investigative models, human trafficking awareness, enhanced law enforcement/social services communication, youth engagement training, and quality assurance protocols; (2) Multidisciplinary Teams (MDTs) - improve MDT capacity within Child Advocacy Centers through facilitator training, implementation plan updates, data sharing, role clarification, policy development, collaborative partnership training, and incorporation of youth voice; (3) Forensic Interviews - enhance forensic interviewing capacity through training for new staff, recruitment and retention strategies, continuous best practices training, special populations training, cross-training with detectives, prompt reporting systems, and incorporation of youth voice. Direct services to victims are not permitted.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Grant Program Fund assists local law enforcement agencies with establishing community programs and helps local government agencies establish violence intervention programs. Eligible programs provide recreational or athletic opportunities for community members, improve relations between citizens and law enforcement, otherwise benefit or improve the community, or serve as violence intervention programs established and supported by local law enforcement or another local government agency. The program also supports crime prevention and community engagement initiatives.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to fund community programs and violence intervention programs administered by local law enforcement and local government agencies. Up to $500,000 in total funding is available under SFY 2027 CGPF, with the Office anticipating making 15-25 awards ranging from $5,000 to $50,000 per award. Grant funds are reimbursed based on actual quarterly expenditures. Eligible funding categories include personnel (overtime for law enforcement participating in programming), operating expenses (rental costs for grant-related activities), travel (staff travel to competitions or events using Maryland per diem rates), contractual services (third-party contracting at pre-approved rate of $81.25/hour), equipment (per-unit cost of $10,000 or more, or lasting over one year), and other costs (items under $10,000 or with useful life under one year, including sports equipment, uniforms, instructional materials, and branded educational items). Indirect costs are allowable at either the federal de minimis rate of 15% or from NICRA. Unallowable costs include alcoholic beverages, bad debt, bonuses, construction/capital expenses, fundraising, honoraria, lobbying costs, meals (except pre-approved client food), and promotional trinkets.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Melissa Bitting (Grant Monitor), Sharon Leason (Fund Manager), and Abangolee (Lee) Caulcrick (Fiscal Specialist)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local law enforcement agencies and local government agencies seeking to establish community programs, crime prevention initiatives, or violence intervention programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishing community programs that provide recreational or athletic opportunities, improve community-law enforcement relations, or benefit the community generally. Establishing violence intervention programs. Funds may be used for contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel (overtime), travel, and other eligible expenses. Examples of eligible programs include National Night Out events, violence intervention programs, School Resource Officer programs, partnerships with community organizations (food pantries, recreational leagues, Boys and Girls Club, The Y, Police Explorers), and mentorship programs to encourage youth to consider public safety careers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide eligibility for all Maryland jurisdictions.

structured_extraction.program_description: COAP provides funding to states, tribes, territories, and local governments to respond to illicit substance use and misuse, reduce overdose deaths, promote public safety, and support access to prevention, harm-reduction, treatment, and recovery services in the community and justice system. The program supports implementation of evidence-based, site-based interventions including the Law Enforcement Assisted Diversion (LEAD) program, medication-assisted treatment, harm reduction efforts, prevention programs, workforce expansion, and recovery support services. It is formally known as the Comprehensive Opioid, Stimulant, and Substance Use Site-Based Program (COSSUP).
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support expansion of existing comprehensive programs in response to the opioid and stimulant crisis. The SFY 2026 grant cycle anticipates $894,500 in total funding, with up to 8 awards available. Minimum award amount is $50,000 and maximum is $150,000 per application. Grant funds are reimbursed based on actual quarterly expenditures. Allowable costs include contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other eligible costs aligned with federal guidelines (2 CFR Part 200). Funds support expansion of evidence-based interventions such as Law Enforcement Assisted Diversion (LEAD), medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD) and medication-assisted treatment (MAT), naloxone distribution, harm reduction services, transitional/recovery housing (no more than 30% of total funds), jail-based treatment programs, and recovery support services. This funding opportunity is designed for short-term initiatives and expansion of existing programs, not development of new programs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Online submission deadline Friday, September 5, 2025, by 11:59 PM for SFY 2026
structured_extraction.contact_name: Nikita Stackhouse (Grant Monitor), Jacqueline Adams (Funding Manager), Genevra Farrare (Fiscal Specialist), Brandi Cahn (Assistant Director, Justice Reinvestment), Micah Ferguson (Correctional Health Coordinator)
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local health departments (including local behavioral health authorities) and local government agencies in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support expansion of existing comprehensive programs addressing opioid, stimulant, and substance use through: (1) connecting individuals at risk for overdose with treatment and recovery support providers; (2) supporting law enforcement in identifying individuals needing treatment and connecting them to services; (3) enhancing programs in rural communities using technology for expanded access; (4) providing transitional or recovery housing as part of comprehensive response (max 30% of funds); (5) enhancing programs to reduce overdose risk and improve treatment engagement among pretrial, post-trial, and jail populations, including medication-assisted treatment and cognitive behavioral treatment. Allowable costs include contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, and travel.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide availability in all Maryland counties. COAP prioritizes support for efforts serving those who have been historically underserved, marginalized, and adversely affected by persistent poverty and inequality.
