structured_extraction.program_description: A remedial program administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy that provides financial assistance and support to victims of crime in Maryland. The program helps cover expenses resulting from criminal injuries, including medical, funeral, and psychological expenses, and offers victim advocacy services. Financial assistance is provided as a payer of last resort, meaning all other available reimbursement sources must be exhausted before a possible award is made. The program also assists families of homicide victims and dependents of deceased victims.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses crime victims for: medical/dental expenses related to physical injury (maximum $45,000); expenses for psychological injury from certain offenses (maximum $5,000, or $1,000 for parent/child/spouse residing with victim); loss of earnings or disability, total or partial, temporary or permanent (maximum $25,000); bereavement leave up to 2 weeks or $2,000 for parent/child/spouse of homicide victim; crime scene cleanup (maximum $250); funeral expenses in cases of homicide (maximum $5,000, provided life insurance does not exceed $25,000); loss of support/dependency when a homicide victim was providing support to the claimant (maximum $25,000); up to 30 days (minimum 2 weeks) in lost wages for a parent or guardian caring for a child injured by crime; and other expenses as approved by the Criminal Injuries Compensation Board. Victims must have incurred at least $100 in reimbursable expenses or lost wages to qualify. CICB is a payer of last resort, meaning all other available reimbursement sources (private insurance, Medicaid, Medicare, Social Security, workers' compensation, life insurance, automobile or boat insurance, homeowners/renters insurance, charity, court-ordered restitution, and civil judgment) must be exhausted before a possible award is made.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Within 3 years of the date of discovery of the crime; in cases of child abuse, victim has until age 25 to apply, or later with good cause
structured_extraction.program_audience: Victims of crime in Maryland, including persons who suffer physical injury as a result of a crime, surviving spouses or family members of homicide victims, persons who assumed responsibility for funeral expenses of homicide victims, dependents of homicide victims, persons who suffer psychological injury as a result of certain offenses, persons injured while preventing crime or assisting police officers, and parents or guardians of minor victims.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical/dental expenses related to physical injury; psychological injury expenses from certain offenses; loss of earnings directly related to inability to work following crime; bereavement leave up to 2 weeks or $2,000; total or partial permanent or temporary disability; crime scene cleanup; funeral expenses for homicide victims; loss of support when homicide victim was providing support to claimant; up to 30 days lost wages for a parent or guardian caring for a child injured by crime; and other board-approved expenses. Not covered: property loss, mileage, lock changes, relocation, child care, pain and suffering.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Crime must have occurred in the state of Maryland (exceptions may apply for acts of terrorism). CICB office located at 6776 Reisterstown Rd, Suite 206, Baltimore, MD 21215-2340.
requirements_list: Unless good cause is shown, report the crime to appropriate authorities within 48 hours of the crime occurring
Submit a completed claim form to CICB within 3 years of the date of discovery of the crime (in cases of child abuse, until age 25, or later with good cause)
Have incurred at least $100 in reimbursable expenses or lost wages
Suffer physical injury as a result of a crime or delinquent act, or be a surviving family member of a homicide victim, or suffer psychological injury from certain offenses

Victim must be innocent and bear no substantial responsibility for causing, provoking, or contributing to the crime or injury; victim must not have initiated, consented to, provoked, participated in, or unreasonably failed to avoid a confrontation with the offender
Unless good cause is shown, cooperate with law enforcement authorities and CICB
Claimants must be at least 18 years of age (parents or guardians must apply for those under 18)
Provide all documentation required and requested by CICB
Not be participating in a crime or delinquent act at the time of the incident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Report the crime to police within 48 hours of the crime occurring (unless good cause for delay). 2. Complete the Application for Crime Victim Compensation form (available online or in paper form) and submit it to the Criminal Injuries Compensation Board within 3 years of the date of discovery of the crime. 3. Submit the completed application by mail, email, or in person to: Criminal Injuries Compensation Board, 6776 Reisterstown Road, Suite 206, Baltimore, MD 21215-2340. 4. Include required documentation such as police report number, medical bills, employment verification, and proof of other benefits. 5. A claims examiner will be assigned to verify all losses and collect necessary documentation. 6. The CICB Board will review the claim and make a determination as to whether it meets statutory requirements. 7. Claimant will be notified of the Board's tentative decision. 8. If claimant disagrees with the decision, they have 15 days to appeal in writing to CICB. 9. If appealed, the Board will hold an administrative hearing. 10. Upon expiration of the 15-day appeal period, the claim will be sent to the Secretary of the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services for final approval. 11. Once approved, payment is processed. 12. If claim is denied, claimant may appeal to local Circuit Court within 30 days. 13. Claimant may be represented by an attorney at any stage of the process. The program provides application assistance, compassionate listening, status updates, resource referrals, interpretation services, and notification/accompaniment to hearings. Emergency and supplemental awards are available.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to domestic violence centers to respond to incidents of family violence, intimate partner stalking, domestic violence, and dating violence, and to develop and strengthen victim services for people affected by these crimes. It supports comprehensive domestic violence programs, government agencies, law enforcement, and direct victim services providers throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are available in two categories: Category A provides up to $1,500,000 for COMAR domestic violence programs with up to 19 awards of $78,947 each; Category B provides up to $1,500,000 for domestic violence programs and centers with up to 30 awards ranging from $50,000 to $100,000 each. Total program funding is $3,000,000. Funds support allowable costs including personnel, operating expenses, contractual services, equipment, supplies, and other direct costs related to providing victim services such as safety planning, shelter or short-term housing, transitional housing, transportation, trauma counseling and mental health services, legal services and representation, court accompaniment, case management, culturally sensitive services, bilingual victim advocates/case managers, basic living needs, abuse intervention programming, victim witness services, and prosecution activities. Funds are paid on a quarterly reimbursable basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Online Submission Deadline: Monday, September 19, 2022 by 3 PM (FY 2023 NOFA); Projected Application Month: August; Projected NOFA Release Month: September
structured_extraction.contact_name: Gary Richardson (Chief of Grants); Paulette Williams-Tillery (Fund Manager); Will van Wisse (Fiscal Grants Manager); Heather Amador (Deputy Director of Victim Services Policy and Programs); Chaylah Steverson (Grant Monitor); Sharon Leason (Fund Manager)
structured_extraction.program_audience: State government agencies, local government agencies, non-profit organizations, state domestic violence coalition, law enforcement, comprehensive domestic violence programs, direct victim services providers, faith-based organizations, and community-based victim services providers serving victims of domestic violence, intimate partner violence, dating violence, and family violence throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Allowable costs include personnel, operating expenses, contractual services, equipment, supplies, and other items with direct correlation to project objectives. Eligible services include: safety planning, shelter or short-term housing, transitional housing, transportation, trauma counseling and mental health services, legal services and representation, court accompaniment, case management, culturally sensitive services for all populations regardless of sexual orientation, gender identity, race, ethnicity, religion, or language proficiency, bilingual victim advocates/case managers, basic living needs, abuse intervention programming, victim witness services in state's attorney's offices and law enforcement, and prosecution activities. Advanced technologies, professional service contracts, operating and administrative costs, and supervision of direct service providers may be supported if agreed upon by the Office and sub-recipient. Unallowable costs include lobbying, construction, research, training, public awareness, fundraising, capital expenses, victim compensation, medical care, executive salaries, property insurance, food/beverage (except per diem and direct food for shelters), and trinkets.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available to eligible organizations throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicants must be state government agencies, local government agencies, non-profit organizations with 501(c)(3) status (proof required via IRS letter or authorized official documentation), state domestic violence coalition, law enforcement, or qualified community-based victim services providers
Each eligible entity may submit no more than one (1) application for DVC funding

Qualified community-based victim services providers must be nonprofit organizations with demonstrated expertise in providing direct services to victims of domestic violence/intimate partner violence, capacity to provide victim-centered trauma-informed services, demonstrated history of working in the community where services will be provided, and ability to collaborate with other agencies including law enforcement and other direct services providers

Faith-based organizations are eligible but grant funding cannot be used for inherently religious activities such as prayer or worship, and such activities must be separate in time and place from grant-funded activities
Applicants must have Unique Entity Identifier (UEI/DUNS number) and SAM Registration
Applications must fall within the specified budget ranges for the category (Category A: $78,947; Category B: $50,000-$100,000) or may be removed from consideration

Grantees must track and measure program outputs and outcomes and submit quarterly programmatic reports (due within 15 calendar days of end of quarter) and financial reports (due within 30 calendar days of end of quarter)
Grantees must submit a fiscal year-end report within 15 days after the end of the performance period
No match required, but supplanting is prohibited—grant funds must supplement existing budget and not replace previously appropriated or budgeted funds

Grantees must not use grant funds for lobbying, construction, research, training, public awareness, fundraising, capital expenses, victim compensation, medical care, executive salaries, or property insurance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit applications through the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services' web-based Grant Management System (GMS) at https://grants.goccp.maryland.gov. Hard copy applications are not accepted. Applicants must first obtain a User ID by September 7, 2022 (deadline varies by NOFA cycle) by visiting http://goccp.maryland.gov/grants/requesting-access/. The application includes: Face Sheet, Project Summary, Narrative (Problem Statement/Needs Justification, Program Goals and Objectives, Program Strategy/Logic, Program Measurement, Timeline, Sustainability, Management Capabilities), Spending Plan and Budget Justification, Personnel, Operating Expenses, Travel, Contractual Services, Equipment, Other Costs, Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (if applicable), Budget Prioritization, Certified Assurances, Certification Regarding Lobbying, Audit Findings/Corrective Action Plan (if applicable), Single Audit Requirements (if applicable), and Proof of 501(c)(3) Status (if applicable). The narrative must be completed in outline-style format retaining all numbering, lettering, and section headers. Applicants should review training videos at http://goccp.maryland.gov/grants/gms-help-videos/ and application instructions at http://goccp.maryland.gov/wp-content/uploads/NOFA-application-instructions.pdf. A technical assistance conference call is typically held prior to the deadline. Applications are evaluated on problem statement/needs justification (15 points), program goals and objectives (20 points), spending plan and budget (20 points), management capabilities (5 points), program strategy/program logic (10 points), performance measurement (20 points), timeline (5 points), and sustainability (5 points) for a total of 100 points. Internal staff and external independent reviewers conduct a three-tier competitive review considering geographic distribution, scope, reach, audit findings, and performance history.

The program aims to reduce and minimize the time between the issuance of ex parte and protective orders and their entry into the MILES/NCIC database, supporting dedicated domestic violence units within local and state law enforcement agencies.

structured_extraction.program_description: Byrne Justice Assistance Grants support a broad range of state and local criminal justice initiatives critical to Maryland's criminal justice goals. The funds are intended to reduce existing gaps in service that impact violent crime, crime victims, enforcement, prosecution, adjudication, detention, and rehabilitation, while also improving sentencing and correction policies, reducing crime, providing public safety, protecting victims, tracking DNA, training local law enforcement, and providing technology to law enforcement.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This is a project grant. Funds support contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel costs, travel, and other criminal justice initiatives addressing violent crime, victim services, law enforcement, prosecution, adjudication, detention, and rehabilitation.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for personnel, equipment, travel, contractual services, and operating expenses. The money supports programs that address violent crime, help victims, and improve law enforcement, prosecution, adjudication, detention, and rehabilitation services.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program provides temporary shelter environments and supportive services through a network of local domestic violence services programs. The program offers comprehensive services to meet the specific needs of domestic violence victims and their families, and fosters a coordinated community approach to serving victims through partnerships with law enforcement, courts, hospitals, local departments of social services, and other support agencies. FVPS supports the establishment, maintenance, and expansion of programs to prevent family violence, domestic violence, and dating violence; provide immediate shelter and supportive services for victims and their dependents; and provide specialized services for children exposed to violence, underserved populations, and victims from racial and ethnic minority populations.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, and travel costs for domestic violence services programs providing shelter and supportive services to victims and their families.

requirements_list: Eligible applicant types include Rape Crisis Centers

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funds assist law enforcement agencies and/or prosecutors who have a demonstrated need, combined with a viable plan to address firearms-related violence in their jurisdictions. The program supports local and state law enforcement agencies and prosecution offices through funding for contractual services, equipment, personnel, travel, and other approved categories to reduce gun violence across Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funds ranging from $15,000 to $100,000 (depending on jurisdiction impact level) can be used for personnel costs (salaries and overtime for law enforcement and prosecutors supporting gun violence reduction), travel expenses for conferences and training, contractual services with consultants and research organizations, equipment including firearm detection and tracing technology, safety equipment, forensic testing services, case management systems, and other costs such as educational materials and public awareness campaigns. Law Enforcement Funding Limitations: Low-Impact Jurisdictions (up to 100 firearm-related crimes annually) can request up to $25,000; Moderate-Impact Jurisdictions (101-300 crimes annually) can request up to $50,000; Jurisdictions with 301-500 crimes annually and State law enforcement agencies can request up to $75,000; High-Impact Jurisdictions (more than 500 crimes annually) can request up to $100,000. State's Attorney's Offices can request up to $100,000. Up to 25 awards are anticipated for SFY 2027.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Matika Palmer; Tabitha Wilson; Dorothy Lennig; Richard Alban; Courtney Thomas
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local law enforcement agencies, state law enforcement agencies, and State's Attorney's Offices with demonstrated need and viable plans to address firearms-related violence in their jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel costs (salaries and overtime for law enforcement officers, prosecutors, and crime analysts supporting gun violence reduction initiatives), travel expenses for conferences and training, contractual services with expert consultants and research organizations, equipment for firearm detection and tracing technology (ballistic identification, gunshot detection systems), safety equipment, forensic testing services, case management and data sharing systems, educational materials, and public awareness campaigns targeting illegal firearm possession and manufacturing/trafficking.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Funding priority is given to law enforcement agencies and local state's attorney's offices that do not currently receive Maryland Criminal Intelligence Network (MCIN) funds. Allied MCIN partners are encouraged to submit applications. MCIN lead sites are not eligible to apply.
requirements_list: Demonstrated need for addressing firearms-related violence in jurisdiction

structured_extraction.program_description: The Law Enforcement Training Scholarship Program (LETS) provides up to $5,000 per recipient to support specialized investigative and law enforcement training for criminal justice professionals. Grant funds may be used for non-degree courses and to cover related expenses, including travel, lodging, registration fees, training materials, and crime scene investigation, laboratory procedures, crime analysis, data-driven policing strategies, and investigative techniques. In certain cases, funds may also be used to bring trainers directly to a law enforcement agency. The program is open to state and local law enforcement agencies, State's Attorneys Offices, and the Maryland Attorney General's Office throughout Maryland and is administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provide up to $5,000 per individual per course to support specialized investigative and law enforcement training. Eligible training may include courses or seminars focused on investigation, crime prevention, waste, abuse, crime analysis, and related topics such as crime scene investigation, laboratory procedures, crime lab certification, data-driven policing strategies (e.g., crime mapping and analysis), law enforcement information sharing, victim services, witness protection, and investigative techniques. Funding covers registration fees, training materials, travel expenses (airfare, mileage, parking, ground transportation), lodging, and per diem for meals. Funding may also support bringing certified trainers onsite to conduct training. No matching funds are required. Funding is distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis. Unallowable costs include overtime, equipment, and backfilling officers. Funding cannot be used for training that primarily offers academic credit toward a degree, general management courses, or networking-focused seminars.

Funds cover registration fees, travel, lodging, training materials, per diem for meals, and bringing trainers directly to agencies. Cannot be used for academic degree credit, general management courses, or networking seminars.

The fund uses money from unclaimed restitution to award annual grants for legal counsel to victims of crime and delinquent acts. Administered by the State Board of Victim Services under the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Warrant Apprehension & Absconding Grant Program (WAAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program supports law enforcement agencies across Maryland to reduce the number of open warrants, especially warrants for violent crimes, and to apprehend individuals who have absconded from a court-ordered drug and/or alcohol treatment facility. It funds warrant apprehension and enforcement activities statewide.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding up to $1,000,000 total anticipated availability for SFY 2026. Up to 30 awards with individual award amounts ranging from $10,000 to $75,000. Funding amounts vary by agency size: Small Agencies (up to 50 sworn officers) eligible for awards up to $30,000; Medium Agencies (51-300 sworn officers) eligible for awards up to $50,000; Large Agencies (more than 300 sworn officers) eligible for awards up to $75,000. Funds may be used for officer overtime to serve warrants and conduct targeted warrant operations, analyst overtime to identify and track wanted/absconded individuals prioritizing violent crime warrants, program administration overtime to support oversight and management of warrant apprehension program, extradition costs for travel expenses related to execution of extradition warrants, and equipment procurement for safe execution of warrant arrests (shackles, handcuffs, protective face masks, etc.). Additional allowable costs include contractual services, operating expenses (communication, postage), and other supplies or items necessary for warrant apprehension activities. Funds are reimbursed quarterly based on actual expenditures.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program that provides temporary shelter and supportive services to domestic violence victims and their families through a network of local domestic violence services programs. The program offers comprehensive services to meet victim needs and fosters coordinated community approaches involving partnerships with law enforcement, courts, hospitals, local departments of social services, and other support agencies. Grants are awarded to comprehensive domestic violence programs to fund temporary shelter environments and a full range of supportive services, including 24-hour hotlines, safe accommodations, therapeutic counseling, legal counseling, and court accompaniment. The program also supports community awareness activities and abuse intervention programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

Eligible uses include contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs directly related to providing services to domestic violence victims and their families. Maximum award per jurisdiction is $116,099. Funds are paid on a quarterly reimbursable basis. Unallowable costs include lobbying, perpetrator rehabilitation, audit costs, property insurance, printing, telephone/fax, food/beverage (except per diem for travel), and promotional items. Consultant rates should not exceed $650 per day or $81.25 per hour without additional justification. There is no match requirement.

Employ professional and paraprofessional staff and volunteers with training or experience in interviewing persons in crisis and providing supportive services
Collaborate with appropriate entities within the geographic area and enhance service provision to victims and their families
Collect and retain basic identifying and demographic data concerning applicants for service and nature of requests
Collect and retain data concerning services rendered to each applicant
Maintain statutorily required civil rights statistical data on victims served by race, national origin, sex, age, and disability
Maintain confidentiality of client-counselor information as required by state and federal law
Submit an annual performance report covering July 1 through June 30 to the Family and Youth Services Bureau
Comply with all policies and regulations set forth by Maryland Department of Health and local departments related to permits and inspections

Keep location of shelter programs confidential except with written authorization
Track and report on mandatory performance measures including number of victims served, victim safety and self-sufficiency outcomes, and awareness metrics
No application can exceed one per organization for DOMV funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted through the Grant Management System (GMS) at https://grants.goccp.maryland.gov. Applicants must first obtain a User ID by the deadline specified (last day to request User ID was March 31, 2023). The online application must be submitted by the deadline (Friday, April 7, 2023 by 11:59 PM). Applications require completion of the Face Sheet, Project Summary, detailed Narrative addressing problem statement, program goals, strategy, performance measurement, timeline, spending plan, management capabilities, and sustainability, along with budget and budget justification. Required documents include Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and SAM.gov registration, letters of support if required, indirect cost rate agreement if applicable, certified assurances, certification regarding lobbying, audit findings if applicable, and proof of 501(c)(3) status. The narrative section should be completed in outline-style format retaining all numbering, lettering, and section headers. Training videos and detailed application instructions are available on the GOCPP website. A technical assistance conference call was held on February 22, 2023. Post-award, a Subrecipient Organizational Capacity Questionnaire may be required. Applications are evaluated on a competitive basis by internal staff and external independent reviewers across eight criteria: problem statement/needs justification (15 points), program goals and objectives (20 points), program strategy (10 points), performance measurement (20 points), timeline (5 points), spending plan and budget (20 points), management capabilities (5 points), and sustainability (5 points). Evaluation also considers crime rate, geographic distribution, reach to underserved populations, audit findings, and performance history.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides advocacy and support services to victims of crime through the creation of new ideas and the enhancement of existing programs in Maryland. The fund supports implementation of the Declaration of Crime Victims' Rights Amendment to the Maryland Constitution and Federal Guidelines for treatment of and assistance to crime victims and witnesses. MVOC ensures compliance with Maryland Criminal Procedure Article §11–916 and supports child advocacy centers. Administered by the State Board of Victim Services under the authority of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to provide advocacy and support services to victims of crime for developing new services, enhancing existing programs, or providing additional assistance for crime victims and witnesses, or for services that directly support a specific population of victims. SFY 2027 funding: $524,836 total available, with 8-10 awards anticipated ranging from $50,000 to $75,000. Funding period: July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Allowable costs include personnel (victim advocates, legal assistants, crime investigators, etc.), operating expenses (rent, communication, postage), travel, contractual services, equipment, supplies, and other eligible victim services expenses. Grant funds are reimbursed based on actual quarterly expenditures. Cost sharing/match is not required.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Erika Wilson Wells (Grant Specialist II), Terri Ricks (Victims Services Grants Manager), Courtney Thomas (Fiscal Grants Specialist), Heather Amador (Director of Victim Services Policy and Programs), Rebecca Allyn (Manager of Victim Services Initiatives)
structured_extraction.program_audience: State government agencies, local government agencies, local law enforcement agencies, non-profit organizations (including faith-based and community organizations), and direct victim services providers that serve victims of crime in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, supplies, and other eligible expenses related to victim advocacy and support services. Allowable costs include direct services for victims of crime, victim service providers in law enforcement, victim/witness service providers in state's attorneys' offices, enhanced services and support for child advocacy centers, and enhanced services to crime victims that aid in the distribution of mandated brochures educating them on their rights. Unallowable costs include perpetrator rehabilitation, audit costs, property insurance, printing, alcoholic beverages, bad debt, bonuses, construction/capital expenses, corporate formation, fundraising, honorarium, lobbying costs, meals (except pre-approved client food), and trinkets.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Youth Advisory Council Small Grant Project

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps community organizations, nonprofit organizations, and local governments fund security operations during times of high pedestrian traffic in entertainment districts where there are higher than average calls for police assistance in response to reported crimes. The program aims to strengthen security in Maryland's entertainment districts through collaborative efforts among local governments, community organizations, and law enforcement by supporting enhanced security and crime prevention activities to reduce criminal activity, improve crowd management, and enhance public safety.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funding to eligible entities. Local governments may request up to $50,000, while community organizations and nonprofits may apply for up to $30,000. The total funding available is $250,166 with plans to make up to 10 awards. Funds are reimbursed on a quarterly basis based on actual expenditures. Allowable costs include: (1) Personnel - overtime for law enforcement officers and security personnel; (2) Contractual Services - security officers and administrators to oversee daily safety operations (consultant rate maximum $81.25/hour or $650/day); (3) Equipment - surveillance cameras, installation and maintenance of camera systems, safety equipment such as reflective vests and communication devices (equipment with unit cost of $10,000 or more); (4) Other - emergency response training, conflict de-escalation training, crowd management training, lighting improvements and installation in public areas, public safety signage creation and installation, and equipment with unit cost less than $10,000. There is no cost-share requirement for this funding source.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Zahra Isaacs (Grant Monitor), Tabitha Wilson (Fund Manager), Janene Dyson (Fiscal Specialist), and Shawn Green (P.R.O.T.E.C.T. Coordinator)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based nonprofit organizations, county government agencies, faith-based organizations, local government agencies, local law enforcement, and nonprofit organizations that operate in or serve entertainment districts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Security and law enforcement overtime for personnel to manage crowd flow and crime hotspots during peak hours, procurement of security equipment including surveillance cameras and enhanced lighting, hiring security administrators and officers to manage daily safety operations, emergency response and crowd management training, public safety signage, and public safety awareness initiatives that promote crime prevention during peak pedestrian activity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Entertainment districts are defined as concentrated areas up to a half-square-mile with a documented high concentration of establishments serving alcohol for on-site consumption, hookah bars, or venues that regularly host live entertainment, as well as demonstrating a pattern of increased calls for police assistance during times of high pedestrian traffic. Eligible throughout Maryland. Applicants in districts designated as Maryland Arts & Entertainment Districts under the Maryland State Arts Council program are eligible for funding only if they meet the specific criteria of an Entertainment District as noted above.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit community organization (neighborhood association officially recognized by the political subdivision), nonprofit organization with 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) status, or local government agency responsible for public safety in the jurisdiction

structured_extraction.program_name: Paul Coverdell National Forensic Sciences Improvement Program (CFSI)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal funding to crime laboratories and medical examiner's offices to improve the quality and timeliness of forensic science and medical examiner services, eliminate backlogs in forensic evidence analysis, purchase equipment, provide training on new techniques, support accreditation, and supply crime laboratories. The program builds overall forensic science capabilities and capacity across Maryland state and local forensic science laboratories.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants to certified state and local forensic science laboratories for funding contractual services, equipment, personnel, travel, and other costs related to forensic science improvement and backlog reduction. Applicants may apply for up to $47,482. Funds are provided on a quarterly reimbursement of expenditures basis following timely submission of quarterly fiscal and programmatic reports. Allowable costs include: salary and benefits of laboratory employees, overtime for laboratory staff, computerization, laboratory equipment, supplies, accreditation preparation and fees, education/training/certification, and facilities improvements. Administrative expenses cannot exceed 10% of the total grant amount. Consultant rates have a threshold of $650 per day. There is no match requirement.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Contractual services, equipment, personnel, travel, and other costs to improve forensic science quality, timeliness, and credibility; eliminate backlogs in forensic evidence analysis; train forensic staff on new techniques; support accreditation; and purchase supplies. Funds may be used to improve quality and timeliness of forensic science or medical examiner/coroner services; eliminate backlogs in forensic evidence analysis (firearms, latent prints, toxicology, controlled substances, forensic pathology, questioned documents, trace evidence); train and employ forensic laboratory and medical examiner/coroner personnel; address emerging forensic science issues and technology; educate and train forensic pathologists; and fund medicolegal death investigation systems to facilitate accreditation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland state and local forensic science laboratories, statewide across Maryland. Forensic science laboratories within state and local law enforcement agencies and medical examiner's offices are eligible.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funded by savings from Maryland's Justice Reinvestment Act that supports evidence-based programming to safely reduce the prison population, improve reentry outcomes, reduce impacts of incarceration on communities, provide resources to victims of crime, and connect nonviolent offenders with behavioral health needs to community treatment and support.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants support contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, and travel for evidence-based programs. Category A funding (state agencies up to $450,000; nonprofits up to $200,000) supports reentry programming, behavioral health treatment, restitution collection processes for victims, and training for criminal justice decision-makers. Category B funding (local government up to $350,000; nonprofits up to $200,000) supports reentry programming, behavioral health treatment, victim support, deflection and diversion programming, and pretrial services. Nonprofit applicants may not request funds exceeding 40% of their annual operating budget. Minimum of $595,824 will be awarded to victim-focused initiatives. Allowable costs include personnel, operating expenses, travel, equipment ($10,000+), and other direct costs. Unallowable costs include alcoholic beverages, bonuses, construction, fundraising, lobbying, meals (except pre-approved client food), vehicles, and activities serving individuals under 18. Grant reimbursement is based on quarterly expenditures.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kyah Edwards (Grant Monitor), Jacqueline Adams (Fund Manager), Brandi Cahn (Assistant Director, Justice Reinvestment), and Lindsey McCullough (Justice Reinvestment Coordinator)
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies, local government entities (including local detention centers, local health departments, local courts, and county government organizations), community-based nonprofit organizations (501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4)), state and local courts, faith-based organizations, and nonprofits managing victim services programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other direct costs for evidence-based programs that safely reduce incarceration through reentry programming and services, behavioral health treatment and resources, restitution collection processes and victim support, deflection and diversion strategies, pretrial services, training for criminal justice decision-makers, workforce development, housing support, educational programming, mediation, and expansion of medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) in corrections. Applications allocating 50% or more to priority populations (justice-impacted women and veterans, emerging adults 18-26, reentry hubs with wraparound services, MOUD expansion, or pretrial services expansion) receive priority consideration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. All Maryland counties are eligible. Performance measures are set by the Local Government Justice Reinvestment Commission. Applicants must comply with System of Award Management (SAM.gov) and unique entity identifier (UEI) requirements.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted online through the Grants Management System (GMS) by Friday, April 3, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Hard copy applications are not accepted. structured_extraction.program_name: Police Accountability, Community, and Transparency Grant (PACT)
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant supports law enforcement agencies across Maryland with developing effective accountability procedures to achieve lawfulness and legitimacy while enhancing community relations and transparency. Funds help increase safety and training for law enforcement, promote safe communities, and encourage community engagement between law enforcement and the communities they serve. The program supports compliance with the Maryland Police Accountability Act of 2021.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to law enforcement agencies and eligible organizations for contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other expenses to support the development of accountability procedures and compliance with the Maryland Police Accountability Act of 2021. Funding availability is anticipated at $4 million with plans to make up to 50 awards ranging from $20,000 to $300,000. Grant funds are reimbursed based on actual quarterly expenditures. Eligible expenses include: support for Police Accountability Boards (PABs) and Administrative Charging Committees (ACCs); Early Intervention Systems (EIS); Victim's Rights Advocate Programs; specialized training in use of force, de-escalation, and peer intervention; implicit bias testing and training; body-worn camera equipment; Employee Assistance Programs (EAP); mental health screenings; Citizens' Police Academy programs; community engagement and outreach; misconduct databases; virtual reality training simulators; and research initiatives.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sun Jang (PACT Grant Monitor); Sharon Leason (PACT Grant Manager); Courtney Thomas (PACT Fiscal Specialist); Greggory Warner (PROTECT Coordinator, Criminal Justice Programs)
structured_extraction.program_audience: County law enforcement agencies, local law enforcement agencies, state government agencies, state law enforcement agencies, local State's Attorney Offices, Maryland Attorney Offices, and Maryland-based non-profit 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) organizations across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other expenses related to developing effective accountability procedures, enhancing community relations and transparency, and supporting initiatives in three priority categories: (1) Core Priorities - Accountability, Training, and Transparency including Police Accountability Boards, Early Intervention Systems, Victim's Rights Advocate Programs, specialized training, implicit bias testing, and body-worn cameras; (2) High Impact Support Initiatives - Officer Wellness and Community Engagement including Employee Assistance Programs, mental health screenings, Citizens' Police Academy programs, town halls, and community outreach; (3) Innovation and Research Initiatives including misconduct databases, virtual reality simulators, research on policing practices, and expanded data collection efforts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland. All counties are eligible.

structured_extraction.program_name: Police Recruitment and Retention Grant Program (PRAR)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to local and state law enforcement agencies to recruit and retain qualified sworn police officers through evidence-informed, data-driven, and sustainable workforce strategies. Funding may be used for hiring bonuses, retention incentives, tuition reimbursement, health incentives, contractual services, equipment, personnel costs, and travel expenses.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $10,000 to $150,000 depending on agency size (based on number of sworn officers as of July 1, 2026). Small agencies with up to 20 sworn officers can request up to $15,000; 21-50 sworn officers up to $25,000. Medium agencies with 51-100 sworn officers can request up to $50,000; 101-300 sworn officers up to $75,000. Large agencies with 301-500 sworn officers can request up to $100,000; more than 500 sworn officers up to $150,000. Total anticipated funding of $1,300,000 with up to 40 awards expected. Funds support hiring bonuses (up to $2,000 for bilingual, veterans, or degree holders), retention incentives tied to service milestones (up to $1,000 per 3 years of service), tuition reimbursement (up to $2,000 per year), health club memberships (up to $50/month), dependent care reimbursement (up to $3,000/year), officer wellness programs, training and travel, recruitment modernization, contractual services, and equipment. Grant funds are reimbursed based on actual quarterly expenditures. Award period is July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available to state and local law enforcement agencies throughout Maryland. Grant funds cannot be used for recruitment of lateral hires (sworn officers already working for an agency in a similar role moving to another agency in Maryland).
requirements_list: Must be a state or local law enforcement agency in Maryland
Must be recruiting and retaining qualified sworn police officers
Must submit no more than one application per agency
Must provide a copy of agency's current Staffing Plan Chart including number of current sworn officers and total vacancies
Must clearly specify the number of sworn officers budgeted in the Problem Statement/Needs Justification section

Applicants must detail agency's recruitment and retention efforts for the past three fiscal years
Applicants must explain agency's staffing plan strategy for the upcoming fiscal year

Must propose strategies consistent with PRAR guidelines and demonstrate data-driven decision-making
Must include measurable outcomes and sustainability plans

To access GMS, applicants must have a User ID and password (deadline to request: Friday, March 13, 2026). structured_extraction.program_name: Program for Preventing Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Infection for Rape Victims
structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program that provides rape victims and victims of child sexual abuse with a full course of non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis (nPEP) treatment and follow-up care to prevent HIV infection after sexual assault. As of October 1st, 2019, Maryland law requires the State to pay for a full course of nPEP medication for survivors of rape and sexual assault deemed at risk for contracting HIV.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses physicians, qualified healthcare providers, hospitals, and pharmacies for the full course of nPEP treatment and follow-up care. The total amount paid cannot exceed $750,000 annually. Reimbursement covers nPEP therapy and follow-up care at four to six weeks, three months, and six months following sexual assault. The medication regimen must begin within 72 hours of the assault and must be taken consistently for 28 days. CDC-recommended regimens include 3-drug combinations such as Truvada + Isentress or Tivicay for healthy patients 13 years and older. A partnership with Altruix Pharmacy (formerly Terrapin Pharmacy) provides medication delivery via mail or courier when hospitals cannot provide the full 28-day medication supply. Patients may elect to use their own health insurance, participate in a manufacturer's financial assistance program, or have the State pay directly. Follow-up care within 180 days of the sexual assault for nPEP services will be reimbursed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/Ongoing - Reimbursement claims must be submitted within 90 days from date of service
structured_extraction.program_audience: Victims of alleged rape, sexual offense, or child sexual abuse
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis (nPEP) treatment and follow-up care for the prevention of HIV infection following sexual assault. Reimbursement covers nPEP medication regimens, follow-up medical assessments, laboratory services, and associated healthcare provider fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland
requirements_list: Victim of alleged rape, sexual offense, or child sexual abuse
At risk for contracting HIV as a result of sexual assault
Medication regimen must begin within 72 hours of the sexual assault
Must meet Centers for Disease Control guidelines for patient qualification for nPEP therapy
Reimbursement claims must be submitted within 90 days from date of service
Patient must take the full 28-day course of nPEP medication consistently for effectiveness
Patients do not have to obtain a full Sexual Assault Forensic Exam (SAFE) in order to access the full course of nPEP/HIV prophylaxis treatment

Healthcare providers may consider factors including physical trauma, site of penetration, pre-existing medical conditions, pregnancy status, and potential HIV status of the offender before prescribing nPEP
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Physicians, qualified healthcare providers, hospitals, and pharmacies submit the nPEP Reimbursement Form and Prescription Form to claim reimbursement along with an itemized bill and UB-04, CMS-1450, or OMB-0938-1197 1500 form to the Sexual Assault Reimbursement Unit (SARU) within 90 days of the exam or HIV exposure assessment. Facilities should provide patients with at least a 3-7 day dose of nPEP medication upon discharge. If a facility cannot provide a full course of therapy at discharge, the completed form should be sent to Altruix Pharmacy (meds@altruix.com or 877-829-1935 fax) which will provide the remaining medication by mail or courier. The form must be completed in its entirety and include the qualified healthcare professional's certification that the patient was treated for alleged rape, sexual assault, or child sexual abuse. Patient authorization and consent forms must be signed prior to treatment and reimbursement processing.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project Safe Neighborhoods Grants develop, implement, and support anti-gang prevention and violent crime enforcement strategies in Maryland through dedicated partnerships forming a PSN task force. Funds help create and foster safer neighborhoods through a sustained reduction in violent crime, including addressing criminal gangs and the felonious possession and use of firearms.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, and travel to support anti-gang prevention and violent crime enforcement strategies through PSN task forces.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government agencies, local law enforcement, state law enforcement, and state's attorney offices in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, other costs, personnel, and travel related to anti-gang prevention and violent crime enforcement strategies.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides support to nonprofit organizations, including faith-based organizations, with facilities and membership that can be targeted for hate crimes to provide security enhancements. The program supports the development of criminal justice and victim services strategies through collaboration, information sharing, and knowledge transfer between law enforcement, victim services, and communities targeted for hate crimes. The program addresses documented and recent risks of hate crime victimization by providing funding for physical security enhancements, community engagement and education, and emergency preparedness activities.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for nonprofit and faith-based organizations to implement security enhancements and hate crime prevention activities. Funding amounts are based on organizational annual budget: organizations with annual budget under $500,000 can receive up to $50,000; organizations with budget between $500,000 to $5,000,000 can receive up to $100,000; organizations with budget over $5,000,000 can receive up to $200,000. Funds can be used for contractual services, equipment, personnel, travel, and other eligible categories. Eligible use of funds includes: physical security enhancements (surveillance cameras, alarm systems, hardened doors/windows, security fences, improved lighting, cybersecurity measures, and security personnel); community engagement and education (anti-hate public awareness campaigns, cultural competency workshops, bystander intervention training); and emergency preparedness (development of emergency response plans and active threat drills). Grant funds are reimbursed based on actual quarterly expenditures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and faith-based organizations with facilities and membership that can be targeted for hate crimes, specifically those serving or regularly used by individuals belonging to protected classes (religion, race, color, sexual orientation, gender, disability, national origin, or homelessness).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Security enhancements and related activities for facilities at risk of hate crimes. Eligible uses include: physical security enhancements such as surveillance cameras, alarm systems, hardened doors and windows, security fences, improved lighting, cybersecurity measures, and security personnel; community engagement and education such as anti-hate public awareness campaigns, cultural competency workshops, and bystander intervention training; emergency preparedness such as development of emergency response plans and active threat drills; contractual services, equipment, personnel, travel, and other approved expenses. Grant funds cannot be used to fund inherently religious activities such as prayer or worship, and cannot support school-based facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Facilities must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization recognized under 501(c)(3) or faith-based organization
Must have facilities located in Maryland
Must have facilities and membership that can be targeted for hate crimes
Must demonstrate direct or immediate threats related to hate crimes or have recently experienced hate crime incidents
Must serve or regularly use facilities by individuals belonging to protected classes (religion, race, color, sexual orientation, gender, disability, national origin, or homelessness)
Must be a registered user of the Grants Management System (GMS) to apply
Must submit a copy of IRS 501(c)(3) status letter or equivalent nonprofit verification documentation
Must submit most recent financial documentation (IRS Form 990, audited financial statements, certified organizational operating budget, or equivalent) to verify annual budget

Faith-based organizations must submit IRS Employer Identification Number (EIN) Confirmation Letter, signed board statement confirming exempt religious status, governing documents (Bylaws/Articles), and Group Exemption Letter from national denomination if applicable
Must submit current W-9 form
Must comply with System of Award Management (SAM.gov) and unique entity identifier (UEI) requirements
Must register and maintain profile in Grants Management System (GMS)
School-based facilities are not eligible; organizations with school-based facilities must exclude them from the application but may request funding for other eligible portions of campus
Organizations with multiple eligible facilities must combine all funding requests into a single application

Must clearly demonstrate need for funding based on documented or demonstrable risks related to hate crimes
Applications must clearly align with documented or demonstrable risks related to hate crimes to be eligible for PAHC funding

structured_extraction.program_description: Training developed for mandated reporters — professionals who work with children and youth — to educate them about their legal obligations to report suspicions of child abuse or neglect to local department of social services or law enforcement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Residential Substance Abuse Treatment (RSAT) for State Prisoners Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program assists state and local governments in developing and implementing substance abuse treatment programs in correctional and detention facilities. It also funds community reintegration services for offenders after release from incarceration. The goal is to break the cycle of drugs and violence by reducing demand for and use of illegal drugs, while preparing offenders for successful reentry into their communities through evidence-based treatment and aftercare services. The program supports residential substance abuse treatment services for individuals in the criminal justice system, including pre-trial defendants, incarcerated persons, and those in need of post-incarceration treatment.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to state, local, and tribal governments for developing and implementing residential substance abuse treatment programs in correctional and detention facilities, as well as community reintegration and aftercare services for released offenders. The SFY 2026 grant cycle anticipates availability of $559,505 for up to 3 awards. Minimum funding request is $50,000 and maximum is $225,000 per award. Funded categories include contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other costs. Grant funds are reimbursed based on actual quarterly expenditures. Eligible entities include Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS), Maryland Department of Juvenile Services (DJS), and Local Detention Centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local governmental agencies, including Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS), Maryland Department of Juvenile Services (DJS), and Local Detention Centers. Secondary contacts for program requirements include Brandi Cahn (brandi.cahn1@maryland.gov), Jackie Adams (jacqueline.adams1@maryland.gov), Micah Ferguson (Micah.Ferguson@maryland.gov), and Genevra Farrare (Genevra.Farrare@maryland.gov).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing and implementing residential substance abuse treatment programs in state, local, and tribal correctional and detention facilities for pre-trial defendants, incarcerated persons, and post-release individuals; creating and maintaining community reintegration and aftercare services; contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel costs, and travel. Programs must provide comprehensive individual and group substance use treatment services that are evidence-based, medication-assisted treatment (MAT) as part of comprehensive treatment strategy, periodic and random drug testing, trauma-informed services, integrated treatment for co-occurring substance use and mental health disorders, and continuity of care for opioid use disorder treatment upon release.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Funding is available to state and local governmental agencies in Maryland.
requirements_list: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS), Maryland Department of Juvenile Services (DJS), or Local Detention Centers are eligible to apply
Each entity may submit no more than one (1) application for RSAT funding

Residential SUD treatment programs in prisons must engage individuals for 6-12 months, require periodic and random drug testing, establish a therapeutic community separate from general population, and provide aftercare services

Residential SUD treatment programs in jails must engage individuals for at least 3 months, require periodic and random drug testing, make every effort to establish a therapeutic community, and provide aftercare services
Jail-based pretrial SUD treatment programs must initiate or continue evidence-based treatment including medication-assisted treatment and foster connections to community treatment upon release

All participants must receive aftercare services involving coordination between correctional treatment program and social service/rehabilitation programs including education, job training, parole supervision, housing, peer support, and recovery support services
Treatment practices and services should be evidence-based to the extent possible
Programs must provide medication-assisted treatment (MAT) as part of comprehensive treatment strategy
Staff should receive training on substance use disorders, mental health disorders, trauma, and RSAT program specifics including cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and Motivational Interviewing (MI)

Programs must implement data collection and performance measures including participant screening, enrollment, urine testing, connections to community providers, referrals to housing and employment, and outcome measures such as rearrests and reincarcerations
Applications involving partnerships with community-based substance abuse treatment programs will be given priority consideration
Minimum funding request is $50,000 and maximum is $225,000
Applications must comply with System of Award Management (SAM.gov) and unique entity identifier (UEI) requirements
All applications must be submitted online in the Grants Management System (GMS); hard copy applications are not accepted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Grant Management System (GMS) online portal. The SFY 2026 submission deadline is Friday, October 17, 2025, by 11:59 PM. The Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) was reissued September 9, 2025, and was originally published in July 2025. Applicants must complete a narrative addressing Overall Organization Information, Problem Statement/Needs Justification, Program Purpose Area, Project Design, Goals & Objectives, Data Collection Plan, Grant Personnel, Sustainability, Applicant Disclosure of Pending Applications, and Budget Details and Spending Plan. The anticipated period of performance is November 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026. Applicants are encouraged to draft their narrative in a word processing program before transferring to GMS to ensure compliance with technical requirements and word limits for each section. Applications that are incomplete, do not meet minimum funding requirements, exceed maximum award allocation, or do not adhere to word limits may be disqualified during initial technical review. For assistance with applications or program questions, contact Tabitha Wilson (Tabitha.Wilson@maryland.gov); for program requirements or project design assistance, contact Brandi Cahn (brandi.cahn1@maryland.gov) or Micah Ferguson (Micah.Ferguson@maryland.gov).

structured_extraction.program_name: STOP (Services * Training * Officers * Prosecutors) Violence Against Women Formula Grant Program (STOP VAWA)
structured_extraction.program_description: The STOP VAWA Program encourages the development and strengthening of effective, victim-centered law enforcement, prosecution, and court strategies to combat violent crimes against women in Maryland. The program distributes funds among victim-centered law enforcement, prosecution, courts, and nonprofit victim service providers, and supports criminal justice entities in holding offenders accountable. It also strengthens services for victims of violent crimes against women and supports underserved populations through culturally and linguistically specific community-based organizations.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Formula grant program distributing $3,018,680 in FFY 2024 continuation funds according to statutory allocations: 25% to law enforcement, 25% to prosecution, 30% to nonprofit victim services, 5% to courts, and up to 15% at the State's discretion. Ten percent of victim service allocation must be distributed to linguistically and culturally specific community-based organizations. At least 20% of total funds across two or more allocations must meaningfully address sexual assault. Funds are paid on a quarterly reimbursable basis. Allowable uses include contractual services, equipment (unit cost $5,000 or more with useful life exceeding one year), operating expenses, personnel, travel (following Maryland reimbursement rates), and other eligible categories. Unallowable costs include forensic medical exams requiring victim insurance reimbursement, lobbying, construction, fundraising, real property purchase, property insurance, physical building modifications, food/beverage for meetings or conferences (except per diem and direct food for victims), and promotional trinkets.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Erika Wells (Grant Specialist II), Terri Ricks (Maryland VAWA/STOP Administrator), Heather Amador (Director of Victim Services Policy and Programs), Rebecca Allyn (Victim Services Program Manager), Courtney Thomas (Agency Fiscal Grant Specialist II), Marianne Camino (Victim Services Coordinator)
structured_extraction.contact_email: erika.wells@maryland.gov, terri.ricks1@maryland.gov, heather.amador@maryland.gov, rebecca.allyn@maryland.gov, courtney.thomas@maryland.gov, marianne.camino@maryland.gov
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government agencies, local law enforcement, nonprofit organizations, state and local courts, state domestic violence coalition, state government agencies, state law enforcement, state sexual assault coalition, and previous FFY 2023 VAWA subrecipients (for continuation funding).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel, contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, and travel to support victim-centered law enforcement, prosecution, and court strategies to combat violent crimes against women including domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, stalking, strangulation, and sex trafficking. Funds support specialized training, culturally competent services, victim advocacy, crisis intervention, counseling, legal representation, housing support, case management, coordinated community responses, Sexual Assault Response Teams, Domestic Violence Fatality Review Teams, and services for underserved and culturally specific populations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. All counties are eligible for participation.
requirements_list: Applicant must be one of the eligible entity types (local government agencies, law enforcement, nonprofit organizations, courts, state coalitions, or state agencies)
Recipients must maintain victim-centered approaches
Recipients must meaningfully respond to the needs of underserved populations
Linguistically and culturally specific community-based organizations must receive at least 10% of victim service allocation
At least 20% of total funds across two or more allocations must meaningfully address sexual assault, including stranger rape, acquaintance rape, and rape facilitated by alcohol or drugs
Applicant must maintain active SAM.gov registration and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) for duration of award
Time and Effort reports must be maintained for all personnel
All contracted services must include uploaded contracts with application
Consultant rates limited to $650 per day or $81.25 per hour (may be exceeded case-by-case with justification)
Equipment with unit cost $5,000 or more requires Property Inventory Report Form (PIRF) post-award
Applicants must comply with all applicable certifications including Certified Assurances, Certification Regarding Lobbying, Equal Employment Opportunity Plan, and others
All applicants must disclose pending applications for federally funded assistance supporting the same project
Funding is contingent upon Governor's Office receiving specified grant funds from Office on Violence Against Women (OVW) and state budgetary approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) for continuation funding is released in the Grant Management System (GMS) to FFY 2023 VAWA subrecipients. Applicants must submit an abbreviated application via GMS by the deadline including: Face Sheet (with project title, implementing agency, authorized official, service sites, and proposed dates of October 1, 2024 - September 30, 2025), Project Summary (100 words or less), 10 required narrative sections (Problem Statement/Needs Justification, Goals and Objectives, Project Strategy/Logic Model, Program Measurement, Management Capabilities, Timeline, Spending Plan, Sustainability, Disclosure of Pending Applications, and SAM Registration documentation), Budget with justifications in 6 categories (Personnel, Operating Expenses, Travel, Contractual Services, Equipment, Other including indirect costs), Budget Prioritization (rank line items by funding priority), and Required Documents (UEI/SAM registration screenshot, Certified Assurances, Certification Regarding Lobbying, Equal Employment Opportunity Plan, Financial Reporting Certification, Determination of Suitability to Interact with Minors Form, Subrecipient Organizational Capacity Questionnaire, Appendix forms for confidentiality and certifications). All applications undergo internal technical review to verify required forms are submitted, proposal evaluation against NOFA criteria, and final approval by GOCPP Executive Director. Technical assistance is available through GMS Help Desk (support@goccp.freshdesk.com) and GMS Help Videos. Award period runs October 1, 2024 - September 30, 2025 with funds paid on a quarterly reimbursable basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Sex Offender and Compliance Enforcement in Maryland (SOCM)
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program funds the twenty-four (24) designated Maryland law enforcement agencies responsible for sex offender registration and compliance enforcement to ensure compliance with Maryland law by persons required to register or re-register with the Maryland Sex Offender Registry. The funds assist law enforcement in sex offender registration, compliance verification, and enforcement activities throughout the state.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding is provided to the 24 designated local law enforcement agencies for sex offender registration and compliance enforcement. Each jurisdiction receives an allocated amount based on the number of registered sex offenders in their jurisdiction (ranging from $2,608 to $163,111 for SFY 2027). Funds may be used for contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, overtime/fringe benefits for personnel, travel for approved training, supplies, and equipment with unit cost less than $10,000. Funding is provided on a quarterly reimbursement basis based on actual expenditures. Total anticipated funding for SFY 2027 is $728,916.00. Grant period is July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: The twenty-four (24) designated Maryland law enforcement agencies responsible for sex offender registration and compliance enforcement in their jurisdictions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Contractual services for personnel tasked with sex offender compliance enforcement; personnel costs including overtime and fringe benefits; operating expenses including telecommunication needs specific to sex offender monitoring; travel for approved training in sex offender and compliance enforcement; supplies; equipment with unit cost less than $10,000; and OffenderWatch software costs. Funds must supplement existing budgets and cannot supplant state or local funds previously appropriated for these purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; restricted to the 24 designated Maryland law enforcement agencies responsible for sex offender registration and compliance enforcement. Each designated agency in the jurisdiction is eligible to apply for the specific funding amount allocated to their jurisdiction based on registered sex offender population.
requirements_list: Applicant must be one of the 24 designated Maryland law enforcement agencies responsible for sex offender registration and compliance enforcement
Applicant must be a registered user of the Grants Management System (GMS)

Only one application may be submitted per agency/organization

Application must include Project Design describing monitoring strategies, use of tools such as OffenderWatch and METERS/NCIC
Application must include Goals & Objectives, Data Collection Plan, Grant Personnel description, and Sustainability plan
Application must adhere to specified word limits for each narrative section
