structured_extraction.program_name: Sexual Assault Kit Testing Grant Program (SAKT)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to eligible entities including the Office of the Attorney General, the Federally Recognized State Sexual Assault Coalition, and peer-to-peer telehealth providers that meet statutory requirements for forensic evidence collection. Funding supports testing of sexual assault kits collected since May 1, 2018, victim notification services, and telehealth forensic examinations. The SFY 2026 program makes $450,400 available in total grant funding.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SFY 2026 funding of $450,400 available in total grant funding. The Office anticipates making up to 3 awards. Eligible entities may request nine months of funding (October 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026) to align with the state fiscal year for FY26. Funding supports: (1) Office of the Attorney General - assisting law enforcement agency investigations of crimes involving sexual assault evidence collection kits that have not been tested; (2) Federally Recognized State Sexual Assault Coalition - maintaining a statewide victim notification hotline and related personnel to provide advocacy, support, information about untested rape kits, and victims rights information to victims of sexual assault; (3) Peer-to-peer telehealth providers - providing sexual assault forensic examinations. Allowable costs include personnel (investigators, victim notification advocates, forensic nurse examiners), operating expenses (rent, communication, postage), travel, contractual services, equipment, supplies, and indirect costs. Funds are reimbursed quarterly based on actual expenditures. No cost-share is required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Office of the Attorney General, Federally Recognized State Sexual Assault Coalition, and peer-to-peer telehealth providers that meet statutory requirements for forensic evidence collection.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Testing of sexual assault evidence collection kits collected since May 1, 2018; victim notification services including hotline operations and victim advocacy; sexual assault forensic examinations via telehealth; personnel and supplies for in-house testing; outsourcing of testing services; purchase and upgrade of forensic laboratory equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Only testing of sexual assault kits collected since May 1, 2018 is eligible for funding.
requirements_list: Applicant must be one of the following eligible entities: (1) Federally Recognized State Sexual Assault Coalition, (2) Office of the Attorney General, or (3) Peer-to-peer telehealth providers that meet statutory requirements for forensic evidence collection pursuant to Criminal Procedures Article 11-1007
Funding is limited to testing of sexual assault kits collected since May 1, 2018
Each eligible entity may submit no more than one application
Applicant must comply with all applicable System of Award Management (SAM.gov) and unique entity identifier (UEI) requirements
All applications must be submitted online through the Grants Management System (GMS)
Funding requests must be reasonable and directly align with the number of cases anticipated to be provided for the nine-month award period
Incomplete applications may be disqualified during the initial technical review
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply online through the Grants Management System (GMS) at https://grants.goccp.maryland.gov. Applicants must have a User ID to access the system; requests for new User IDs must be made by August 28, 2025. A technical assistance conference call will be held on August 26, 2025 from 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM. Applications must be submitted by Friday, September 8, 2025 at 11:59 PM. The application process requires submission of narrative responses in GMS addressing: overall organization information, problem statement/needs justification, program purpose area, project design, goals and objectives, data collection plan, grant personnel, sustainability, applicant disclosure of pending applications, and budget details and spending plan. Applications will be reviewed competitively through a three-tier review process including internal staff and external independent reviewers, evaluated on overall organization information (10%), problem statement/needs justification and program purpose area (20%), project design (20%), goals and objectives and data collection plan (20%), key grant personnel (5%), and budget details, spending plan, and sustainability (25%). Applicants are encouraged to draft narratives in a word processing program before transferring to GMS.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Sexual Assault Reimbursement Unit provides reimbursement for physical examinations, evidence collection, and emergency treatment of individuals for injuries resulting from alleged rape, sexual assault, or child sexual abuse. The program aims to prevent re-victimization by easing the reimbursement process associated with medical-forensic claims. Reimbursement is provided directly to medical providers on behalf of victims.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement is provided directly to physicians, hospitals, pharmacies, laboratories, and other eligible providers on behalf of victims. Physicians receive up to $80 for examination and evidence collection for rape or sexual offense victims, or up to $80 per hour for up to 5 hours for child sexual abuse victims. Hospitals are reimbursed at rates determined by the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) for emergency room, outpatient clinic, and in-hospital care. Laboratories and pharmacies are reimbursed at established rates for laboratory tests and medications including HIV prophylaxis (nPEP). Reimbursement includes medical screening exams, forensic exams, laboratory services (blood panels, pregnancy tests, STI testing, toxicology screening), radiology, surgical consults, medications (emergency contraception, pain medications, antibiotics, tetanus, anti-nausea medications, and HIV prophylaxis), and follow-up medical testing obtained within 90 days of the initial examination. Eligible vendors include hospitals, urgent cares, individual physicians, non-SAFE hospitals, and other qualified providers. Services must be related to the alleged assault and within the provider's scope of practice. Neither patients, families, nor insurance should receive a bill for sexual assault-related services. As of October 1, 2019, the State pays for a full course of nPEP medication for survivors deemed at risk for HIV contraction.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Claims must be submitted within 90 days from the date of service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Victims of rape, sexual assault, and child sexual abuse, and the medical providers treating them. This includes survivors who choose to report to law enforcement and those who do not, as well as inmates treated outside of prison facilities (county/state inmates only).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency room treatment, in-hospital treatment, outpatient clinic services, and follow-up medical testing obtained within 90 days of the initial examination for injuries sustained from alleged rape or sexual assault. Covered services include medical screening exams, forensic exams, physical trauma assessment, screening for pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections, diagnostic tests directly associated with the assault, laboratory tests (blood panels, STI cultures, toxicology screening for drug-facilitated sexual assault), radiology, surgical consults, postcoital medications, prophylactic medications for sexually transmitted infections and tetanus, pain and antiemetic medications, emergency contraception, any medication directly related to the assault, and non-occupational post-exposure prophylaxis (nPEP) for HIV prevention. Follow-up care and nPEP follow-up are also covered. The program does not cover testing or treatment for preexisting conditions or mental health services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. If a victim is sexually assaulted outside of Maryland, SARU will reimburse for medical care provided within the state of Maryland if all other criteria for reimbursement are met. Medical care provided outside of Maryland will not be reimbursed. Services may be provided at SAFE hospitals, urgent cares, individual physician offices, non-SAFE hospitals, and other qualified providers, as well as via telehealth when within the provider's scope of practice.
requirements_list: A police complaint number must be documented for victims who choose to report to police. For victims who do not wish to report, a property held number, Jane Doe number, CPS/CHESSIE number, Medical Record Number (MRN), or similar case identifier for evidence collection must be documented. If unable to obtain a case number from law enforcement, the exam should still be completed and 'not provided but requested' should be written on the police case identifier line.

Signed SARU SAFE Reimbursement Form (SSRF, formerly Maryland Department of Health Form #2923) or Form #4456 for child sexual assault services provided by Child Advocacy Centers, signed by a physician and forensic nurse examiner (Physician Assistants and Nurse Practitioners may sign in place of the ED provider if necessary). Patient authorization and informed consent must be obtained and documented.

Payment sheet (CMS Form #1450 [UB-04], CMS Form #1500, or self-designed payment form) with vendor name, address, federal tax identification number, patient's name, patient date of birth, date of service, and amount due.
Itemized bill including documentation of laboratory/diagnostic tests and medications ordered with corresponding lab codes.
Claims must be submitted within 90 days from the date of service.
All necessary documentation must be submitted as outlined in regulations.
Any injury directly associated with the assault may be considered for reimbursement. The Unit does not cover testing or treatment for preexisting conditions or mental health services.
Multiple hospitals or providers should not bill SARU for the same services provided to the same patient.

For drug-facilitated sexual assault (DFSA) testing claims: Specimens must be submitted to a qualified forensic toxicology laboratory with a Forensic Laboratory License issued by the Maryland Department of Health Office of Health Care Quality. Blood samples must be collected within 24 hours of suspected ingestion for reimbursement. Urine samples must be collected within 120 hours of suspected ingestion for reimbursement. Completed DFSA portion of SSRF must be submitted. Standard 12-panel drug and alcohol screening will not be documented as DFSA toxicology; only outsourced testing or in-house screening beyond the 12-panel will be tracked as DFSA.

For nPEP reimbursement: nPEP must be started within 72 hours (3 days) after exposure and taken for 28 days to be effective. If the facility provides less than a full 28-day regimen, the patient must be referred to obtain the balance of treatment. Facilities providing less than full course should refer patients to Altruix Pharmacy or other appropriate providers and submit the nPEP/HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Claim & Prescription Form.
Care provided must be within the provider's scope of practice as determined by the licensing authority.
Providers must establish a pay-to account with the Comptroller to receive reimbursement.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Medical providers treating sexual assault victims submit claims for reimbursement to SARU with all required documentation. The process includes: (1) Complete the SARU SAFE Reimbursement Form (SSRF) or Form #4456 (for CAC services), obtain patient/victim authorization and informed consent signatures, and have it signed by qualified healthcare provider; (2) Obtain payment sheet (CMS Form #1450, CMS Form #1500, or self-designed form) with required vendor and patient information; (3) Prepare itemized bill with documentation of all services, tests, and medications with corresponding lab codes; (4) Submit all documentation to SARU within 90 days of the date of service. For nPEP provided by outside pharmacies (such as Altruix), facilities should send the completed nPEP/HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Claim & Prescription Form (page 6 of SSRF) directly to the pharmacy (meds@altruix.com or 877-829-1935 fax). For drug-facilitated sexual assault testing beyond standard 12-panel screening, ensure the DFSA box is checked on the SSRF and include invoice with testing details. Questions and submission inquiries can be directed to saru.claims@maryland.gov or 410-697-9338. Reimbursement rates are tied to Maryland Medicaid rates, with hospital service rates determined by HSCRC. Multiple providers should not bill for duplicate services. If a patient receives care at multiple facilities, each must submit separate documentation for their services.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Sexual Assault Services Program provides intervention, advocacy, accompaniment (i.e., accompanying victims to court, medical facilities, police departments, etc.), support services, and related assistance for adult, youth, and child victims of sexual assault, family and household members of victims, and those collaterally affected by the sexual assault. The Sexual Assault Services Program was created by the Violence Against Women and Department of Justice Reauthorization Act of 2005, 42 U.S.C. §14043g, and is the first federal funding stream solely dedicated to the provision of direct intervention and related assistance for victims of sexual assault.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides federal funding for rape crisis centers to deliver direct intervention and related assistance for victims of sexual assault. Eligible categories for funding include: 24-hour hotline services providing crisis intervention and referral; accompaniment and advocacy through medical, criminal justice, and social support systems; crisis intervention and short-term individual and group support services; comprehensive service coordination and supervision; information and referral services; community-based and culturally specific services and support mechanisms including outreach to underserved communities; and development and distribution of materials related to these services. Funding is distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis. Rape crisis centers serving one jurisdiction are eligible to apply for up to $32,750 in funding, while MCASA and rape crisis centers serving multiple jurisdictions are eligible to apply for up to $42,750 in funding. Eligible cost categories include contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other eligible expenses. Unallowable costs include lobbying, fundraising, real property purchases, construction, physical building modifications, food/beverages (except per diem for travel), research projects (except up to 1% for program effectiveness assessment), prevention efforts, public education, Sexual Assault Forensic Examiner programs, training to allied professionals, criminal justice-related projects, and domestic violence services unrelated to sexual violence. Consultant rates are limited to $650 per day. There is no match requirement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 16, 2023 for SFY2024 cycle; typically released in February with applications due in March for subsequent cycles
structured_extraction.contact_name: Peyton Adams (Grants Specialist I) / Erika Wells (Grants Specialist II)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local full-service rape crisis centers as identified by the Maryland Coalition Against Sexual Assault (MCASA) and MCASA itself serving adult, youth, and child victims of sexual assault and their families
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: 24-hour hotline services providing crisis intervention and referral; accompaniment and advocacy through medical, criminal justice, and social support systems including medical facilities, police, and court proceedings; crisis intervention and short-term individual and group support services; comprehensive service coordination and supervision to assist sexual assault victims and family or household members; information and referral services; community-based and culturally specific services and support mechanisms including outreach to underserved communities; development and distribution of materials on issues related to sexual assault services; accessibility accommodations including American Sign Language interpreter services, language interpretation, translation services, and adaptive equipment; and websites, videos, and materials accessible to persons with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland; all 18 local full-service rape crisis centers identified by the Maryland Coalition Against Sexual Assault (MCASA) are eligible to apply.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local full-service rape crisis center as identified by the Maryland Coalition Against Sexual Assault (MCASA) or MCASA itself
Must be a designated Rape Crisis Center
Must provide services to adult, youth, and child victims of sexual assault
No more than one application per eligible organization
Must ensure victim safety as the guiding principle

Must not exclude victims based on sex, age, immigration status, race, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, mental health condition, physical health condition, criminal record, work in sex industry, or age/gender of children
Must maintain confidentiality of victim information and privacy
Must not impose requirements on victims to receive services (e.g., seeking protection orders, reporting to law enforcement)
Must conduct safety planning with victims
Must account for accessibility needs of participants with disabilities and those with limited English proficiency or who are Deaf or hard of hearing
Must track and report program outputs and outcomes on a quarterly basis
Must register with Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and SAM
Must submit certified assurances and certification regarding lobbying
Must have 501(c)(3) status if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply through the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services web-based Grant Management System (GMS) at https://grants.goccp.maryland.gov. Applicants must first obtain a User ID and password by going to http://goccp.maryland.gov/grants/requesting-access/. The last day to request a User ID is specified in each Notice of Funding Availability (typically several weeks before the application deadline). Technical assistance is provided through training videos at http://goccp.maryland.gov/grants/gms-help-videos/ and application instructions are available at http://goccp.maryland.gov/grants/programs/. A technical assistance conference call is typically held a few weeks before the deadline. Applications must include: Face Sheet, Project Summary (100 words or less), Narrative (Problem Statement/Needs Justification, Program Goals and Objectives, Program Strategy, Program Measurement, Timeline, Spending Plan, Management Capabilities, Sustainability), Letters of Support/Commitment if required, Budget and Budget Justification (Personnel, Operating Expenses, Travel, Contractual Services, Equipment, Other), Indirect Cost Rate Agreement or documentation supporting use of de minimis rate if applicable, Budget Prioritization, Certified Assurances, Certification Regarding Lobbying, Audit Findings/Corrective Action Plan if applicable, Single Audit Requirements if applicable, and Proof of 501(c)(3) Status if applicable. Narrative section must be in outline-style format retaining all numbering, lettering, and section headers. Applications are evaluated on Program Goals and Objectives, Program Strategy/Program Logic, Performance Measurement (outputs, outcomes, and impacts), and Spending Plan and Budget (reasonableness, cost effectiveness, detailed justification per line item). Programmatic electronic reports are due within 15 calendar days of the end of each quarter. Financial electronic reports are due within 30 calendar days of the end of each quarter. All reporting occurs through the Grant Management System. Grantees will be required to track and report quarterly outputs and outcomes including: number of victims served, number of victims who felt safer as a result of the program, number of victims who felt more self-sufficient, number of victims who felt more informed of available services, and number of victims who felt more informed of their rights. Hard copy applications are not accepted.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Sexual Assault/Rape Crisis Grant Program provides state funding through general funds to support local rape crisis centers that serve victims of rape and other sexual offenses. Services are available in every jurisdiction in Maryland through a network of community-based rape crisis programs and include a 24-hour hotline, counseling, medical accompaniment, and assistance in accessing legal support and other services for adult and child victims. The program is administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services (formerly known as Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy).
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides project grants through state general funds to rape crisis centers. Funds can be used for personnel, counseling, medical accompaniment, assistance with supportive services (mental health, social, medical, law enforcement, and legal services), information/referrals, hotlines, and other specialized services designed to help adults and child victims and their families. Other allowable costs include skills training for staff, training materials, training-related travel, equipment, and furniture, provided that direct services cannot be offered without these expenses. Funds are distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis. Consultant rates are capped at $650 per day or $81.25 per hour unless higher rates are justified. Unallowable costs include lobbying, administrative advocacy, property insurance, food/beverage, and fundraising.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Peyton Adams (Program Monitor); Glenn Grayman (Assistant Director of Grants Administration); Will vanWise (Fiscal Grant Manager); Heather Amador (Director of Victim Services Policy and Programs)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seventeen local full-service sexual assault crisis programs identified by the Maryland Coalition Against Sexual Assault (MCASA), and MCASA itself, providing services to victims of rape and other sexual offenses in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other expenses related to providing victim services including 24-hour hotlines, counseling, medical accompaniment, legal assistance access, information/referrals, and other support services for adult and child victims of rape and sexual offenses. Funds may also support skills training for staff, training materials, and equipment necessary to ensure quality direct services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services are available in every jurisdiction in Maryland. The program is statewide with designated rape crisis programs serving specific geographic areas.
requirements_list: Must be a full-service sexual assault crisis program identified by the Maryland Coalition Against Sexual Assault (MCASA) or be MCASA itself
Must be a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization with proof of tax-exempt status from the IRS
Must provide specialized support services to adult and minor alleged victims of sexual assault crimes, including a hotline and counseling service
Must provide information to alleged victims regarding criminal prosecutions, civil law remedies, sexual assault evidence collection, and victim rights
Must participate in the sexual assault response team in each county where the program provides services
Must provide crisis call receipt and response on a 24-hour basis
Must provide counseling with alleged victims and friends/relatives to alleviate immediate crisis
Must provide medical accompaniment for services
Must provide assistance and support for victims accessing mental health, social, medical, police, and legal services
Must provide information and referrals
Must provide information and education to the general public regarding prevention and treatment of rape and sexual offenses
May offer ongoing counseling, specialized services for incest victims, assistance in legal and judicial proceedings, and training for professionals

Must track and measure program outputs and outcomes including number of victims served, victim responses to assessment tools, victims who felt safer, victims who felt more self-sufficient, victims who felt more informed of services and rights, and human trafficking victims served
Faith-based organizations must not use grant funds for inherently religious activities and must ensure any participation in religious activities by service recipients is voluntary
No match is required for this funding source
Cannot use funds for lobbying, administrative advocacy, property insurance, food/beverage, or fundraising
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted through the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services' web-based Grant Management System (GMS) at https://grants.goccp.maryland.gov. Applicants must obtain a User ID by visiting http://goccp.maryland.gov/grants/requesting-access/. The application includes required sections such as Face Sheet, Project Summary, Application Narrative (including Problem Statement, Program Goals and Objectives, Program Strategy, Program Measurement, Timeline, Spending Plan, Management Capabilities, and Sustainability), Budget, Budget Justification, and Budget Prioritization. Required supporting documents include proof of 501(c)(3) status, Indirect Cost Rate Agreement or De minimis documentation, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and SAM.gov registration, Certified Assurances, Certification Regarding Lobbying, and MOUs or letters of support. Hard copy applications are not accepted. A technical assistance call is typically held before the deadline to assist applicants. Training videos are available on the Office's website.

structured_extraction.program_name: State Aid for Police Protection Fund (SAPP)
structured_extraction.program_description: SAPP is a formula-driven funding program that supplements resources for police protection in local communities across Maryland. State funds provide additional revenue to support the operational costs of local and county police agencies. Funds are distributed based on a formula derived through a subdivision's population, number of police officers in the agency, and the total jurisdictional taxable income. The fund was established under Title 4, Subtitle 5 of the Public Safety Article, Annotated Code of Maryland, to ensure that residents throughout the State have access to an adequate level of police protection, regardless of a jurisdiction's tax base or fiscal capacity.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SAPP funding is distributed through two primary components: (1) Formula Funds distributed pursuant to statutory provisions in the Public Safety Article §§ 4-501–4-507, calculated based on expenditures for police protection, share in basic expenditure, share over basic expenditure, minimum grant, incentive grant, additional grant, minimum payment in certain years, crime laboratory and wealth reduction adjustment, Washington D.C. proximity adjustment, municipal grant, and supplemental grant; and (2) Enhancement Funds distributed to jurisdictions in proportion to the number of violent crimes reported based on the most recently published Uniform Crime Report (UCR) by the Maryland Department of State Police. Funds are paid out on a quarterly basis. SAPP recipients are required to track and report on expenses and efforts related to violent crime reduction. There is no match required for this funding source.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, November 26, 2025 by 11:59 PM for SFY 2027 Application submission; Thursday, January 15, 2026 by 11:59 PM for SFY 2026 Award documents submission
structured_extraction.contact_name: Tabitha Wilson (SAPP Grant Monitor) and Quentin Jones (SAPP Fund Manager)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local and county police agencies, including incorporated municipalities and counties in Maryland with qualified full-time or part-time police officers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operational costs of local and county police agencies devoted to police protection, including salaries and wages for officers, capital outlay for equipment, debt service, communications, travel, fuel and utilities, contractual services, supplies and materials, fixed charges (rent, insurance), motor vehicle operations and maintenance, retirement and social security contributions, traffic control, and central alarm system costs. Funds must be used exclusively to provide adequate police protection.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland jurisdictions are eligible for formula-based distribution. Counties and qualifying municipalities must be located in Maryland to receive SAPP funding.
requirements_list: Must be a county or incorporated municipality with annual expenditures for police protection in excess of $5,000 and employ at least one qualified full-time officer as determined by the Executive Director; OR have expenditures for police protection that exceed $80,000 and employ at least two qualified part-time police officers from a county police department or sheriff's department
Must comply with all applicable System of Award Management (SAM.gov) and unique entity identifier (UEI) requirements throughout the grant cycle
Must complete and submit Face Sheet with accurate Applicant Agency and Implementing Agency contact information

Must complete and submit Project Summary and SAPP Narrative with responses to three sections: Eligibility and Certification, Use of Funds and Impact, and Unique Entity Identifier and SAM.gov Expiration Date
Must submit Form 2 (Estimated Expenditures for Police Protection for SFY 2026) with backup documentation supporting each line-item expenditure by November 26, 2025

Must submit Form 3 (Sworn Officer Count) certified by Police Chief, Sheriff, and/or Chief Executive Officer, with Maryland Police and Correctional Training Commission (MPCTC) roster of full-time sworn officers by November 26, 2025
Must submit Form 1 (Actual Expenditures for Police Protection for SFY 2025) with supporting worksheets by January 15, 2026 under SFY 2026 Award
Must submit Comprehensive Audited Financial Statements (CAFR) Reconciliation Form cross-referenced with Form 1 by January 15, 2026
Must submit SFY 2025 Annual Audit Report (or marked UNAUDITED if unavailable by due date, then resubmit as AUDITED when available)
Must ensure SAM.gov registration is current with valid Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
Must report crime data to Maryland Department of State Police by November 1st deadline to avoid withholding of 15-50% of award
Must submit aggregate data on police officers' use of force to Maryland Police and Correctional Training Commissions (MPCTC) by July 1 for previous calendar year per Public Safety Article § 3-514
Only one application may be submitted per agency
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply through the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy's web-based Grants Management System (GMS) at https://grants.goccp.maryland.gov/. New users must request a User ID by November 19, 2025, at https://gocpp.maryland.gov/grants/requesting-access/. The budget section should be left blank as the budget is formula-based and completed internally by GOCPP. Technical assistance is available through training videos at http://gocpp.maryland.gov/grants/gms-help-videos/ and an application instructions document. A technical assistance conference call will be held on Friday, November 14, 2025, from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM via Google Meet (meet.google.com/nin-gbbs-rby, PIN: 136 433 138#). Award notification is expected in June 2026, with funding period July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2027. Funds are distributed quarterly via Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT).

structured_extraction.program_name: State's Attorney's Office Case Automation System Enhancement Grant Program (SACM)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to State's Attorney Offices to establish or enhance automated case management systems that improve efficiency and effectiveness of case management through advanced technology. The systems must track key data on case information, law enforcement and prosecution details, defendant characteristics, and victim characteristics to support data-driven decision-making and promote fairness and equity. GOCPP anticipates awarding up to eight grants, with individual awards ranging from $25,000 to $100,000 per State's Attorney's Office.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding of $500,000 total is available for State Fiscal Year 2025. GOCPP anticipates awarding up to eight grants, with individual awards ranging from $25,000 to $100,000 per State's Attorney's Office. Eligible costs include: (1) Contractual Services - costs related to system development, customization, or technical support for automated case management systems, and consultant fees for services directly tied to system implementation or enhancement (maximum $81.25/hour or $650/day unless pre-approved); (2) Equipment - automated case management system hardware and software essential for project implementation; (3) Other - minor technology-related supplies necessary for enhancement of the case management system (e.g., cabling, peripherals), and indirect costs if applicable with a valid Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA) or use of the 10% de minimis rate. There is no match requirement. Post-award, awarded funds are distributed on a quarterly reimbursement basis following timely submission of quarterly fiscal and programmatic reports.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Zahra Isaacs (Grant Specialist) and Tabitha Wilson (Grant Manager); Marty Hammond (Director, Criminal Justice Programs)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local State's Attorney's Offices in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used for contractual services (system development, customization, technical support, and consultant fees), equipment (automated case management system hardware and software), and other technology-related supplies necessary for implementing or upgrading automated case management systems that capture charges at arrest, filed charges, final disposition, plea offers, dismissal reasons, declination reasons, corresponding dates, referring law enforcement agency, assigned prosecutors, defendant characteristics (race/ethnicity, age, gender, zip code), and victim characteristics (race/ethnicity, age, gender, zip code).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to local State's Attorney's Offices throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Eligible applicants: Local State's Attorney's Offices only; each office may submit no more than one (1) application

Newly developed or upgraded case management system must be capable of capturing charges at arrest, filed charges, final disposition, plea offers, dismissal reasons, declination reasons, and corresponding dates
System must track referring law enforcement agency and assigned prosecutors
System must record defendant characteristics including race/ethnicity, age, gender, and zip code
System must record victim characteristics including race/ethnicity, age, gender, and zip code
Applicants must comply with all applicable System of Award Management (SAM.gov) and unique entity identifier (UEI) requirements throughout the grant cycle

Grantees must submit quarterly programmatic reports within 15 calendar days of the end of each quarter and financial reports within 30 calendar days of the end of each quarter through the Grant Management System
Applicants must have an active SAM.gov registration with a valid expiration date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must request a User ID by Friday, February 7, 2025, to access the web-based Grant Management System (GMS) at https://grants.goccp.maryland.gov or www.goccp.maryland.gov. All applications must be submitted online through GMS; hard copy applications are not accepted. The deadline for online submission is Friday, February 14, 2025, by 11:59 PM. GMS Help Desk operates Monday-Friday from 9 AM to 5 PM with normal response time of 24-72 hours. Applicants may contact Zahra Isaacs (Zahra.Isaacs@maryland.gov) or Tabitha Wilson (Tabitha.Wilson@maryland.gov) for assistance with program-specific information, or support@goccp.freshdesk.com for technical issues.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant assistance to Baltimore City Public Schools and community-based nonprofit organizations in Baltimore City to establish student peer mediation programs that reduce juvenile violence. The program aims to fund projects utilizing best practices and recommended standards for conflict resolution. Funds may be used for contractual services, equipment, personnel, travel, and other eligible expenses. structured_extraction.program_name: Title II Juvenile Justice Delinquency Prevention Formula Grant (JJAC)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds reform in Maryland's juvenile justice system and supports initiatives and strategies that align with the Developmental Approach to Juvenile Justice Reform. The approach emphasizes accountability without criminalization, alternatives to justice system involvement, individualized response based on assessment of needs and risks, confinement only when necessary for public safety, fairness, sensitivity to disparate treatment, and family engagement. It aims to improve outcomes for children and youth by strengthening programs in aftercare and reentry, alternatives to detention, diversion, and probation. The program is authorized under Sections 221–223 of the Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention Act of 1974, as amended in 2002, 42 U.S.C. §§ 5631–5633. The primary purpose is to improve outcomes for children and youth within the juvenile justice system by increasing and strengthening community-based programs and services, expanding community-based alternatives to confinement, and bringing the state back into compliance with federal limitations on holding youth in adult jails or lock-ups.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Victims of Crime Act program aims to improve how victims of crime are treated by providing them with assistance and services to help them recover after a violent crime and support them through the criminal justice process. Services include crisis intervention, counseling, emergency transportation to court, temporary housing, and criminal justice support and advocacy. The program also helps assure that victims receive information about and assistance in filing for Crime Victim Compensation. The program is fully competitive and supports the most critical crime victims' needs statewide through funding victim service providers with a proven track record of service.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants from the Crime Victims Fund and State General Funds (VOCG). Federal funds are financed by fines and penalties paid by persons convicted in federal cases, not tax dollars. The state budget ensures VOCA/VOCG funding at $60 million regardless of federal award amounts (per Senate Bill 148/HB186, the Victim Services Stabilization Act). Funds can be used for contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, travel, and other approved categories to support victim assistance services. Grants are reimbursed based on actual quarterly expenditures. Administrative costs are capped at 30% of the budget. The indirect cost de minimus rate is 15% of Modified Total Direct Cost (MTDC). A non-mandatory 20% cash or in-kind cost share (match) is encouraged and earns bonus points; matching funds may be waived in full or part upon request. Federal funds cannot be used to meet the cost share requirement. No cap on funding requests, but all line items must be justified as vital needs. Minimum application request is $50,000. Approximately 150 awards are anticipated.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program supports effective violence reduction strategies, specifically gun violence, through evidence-based and evidence-informed health programs. It funds initiatives that use public health principles to demonstrate measurable positive outcomes in preventing gun violence, including hospital-based violence intervention programs that provide intensive counseling, case management, and social services to individuals recovering from violence-related injuries. Established through House Bill 432 of Maryland's 2018 Legislative Session (Chapter 148 of 2018), codified in §4-902 of the Public Safety Article.

structured_extraction.program_description: The SBP Program provides Certified Small Businesses (CSBs) with a designated price preference on state procurement bids. The program allows small businesses to win contracts even if their bid is slightly higher than a larger competitor's bid. The procurement agency will accept the most favorable responsive bid from a responsible CSB if the bid does not exceed the most favorable responsive bid received from a non-small business by specified percentages: 5% for regular small businesses, 7% for veteran-owned small businesses, or 8% for disabled-veteran-owned small businesses. The base 5% preference may have up to 2% added for veteran-owned businesses and up to 3% added for disabled-veteran-owned businesses, or the percentage otherwise identified in the solicitation.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The SBP Program provides Certified Small Businesses with a price preference on state procurements. The procurement agency will accept the most favorable responsive bid from a responsible CSB if the bid does not exceed the most favorable bid from a non-small business by: (1) more than 5 percent for regular small businesses; (2) more than 7% for veteran-owned small businesses; (3) more than 8% for disabled-veteran-owned small businesses; or (4) the percentage otherwise identified in the solicitation. The base 5% preference may have up to 2% added for veteran-owned businesses and up to 3% added for disabled-veteran-owned businesses. To participate in the SBP program, vendors must first complete Certified Small Business (CSB) certification through eMMA.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - no application deadline; rolling program
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Small Businesses (CSBs), including veteran-owned and disabled-veteran-owned small businesses, bidding on state procurement contracts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides a price preference advantage when bidding on state-funded procurement contracts, allowing CSBs to compete more effectively against larger businesses. It does not provide direct funding but rather gives CSBs a competitive advantage in bidding on state procurement contracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available throughout Maryland for all participating Maryland agencies that participate in the SBP Program. Vendors must access eMMA at https://emma.maryland.gov to apply for CSB certification.
requirements_list: Business must be Certified Small Business (CSB)
Business must meet CSB size and ownership standards, including being independently owned and operated
Business cannot be a subsidiary of another business
Business must be for-profit (not a not-for-profit/non-profit)
Business cannot be a broker
Business cannot be dominant in its field of operation at the national level
For size: Total number of employees on payroll must meet CSB size thresholds
For vendor eligibility: Gross sales must meet CSB gross sales requirements based on previous three years of tax returns or projected first year gross sales for new businesses
Business must be bidding on a state procurement that includes SBP designation
For veteran-owned small business preference: business must be verified as veteran-owned
For disabled-veteran-owned small business preference: business must be verified as disabled-veteran-owned
Bid must be from a responsible bidder
Bid must be responsive to the solicitation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To participate in the SBP Program, businesses must first obtain Certified Small Business (CSB) certification through eMMA (https://emma.maryland.gov). Step 1: Register in eMMA and log in with credentials. Step 2: Navigate to the General Info tab, select Company Profile from the dropdown menu. Step 3: Scroll to the State Programs section and select 'Yes' for 'Apply for CSB Certification?' and click Save. Step 4: Navigate to the Documents tab and click the plus icon to add a new CSB Application (only click once). Step 5: Review and agree to the CSB Disclaimer by reading the eligibility standards and checking the agreement checkbox. Step 6: Complete all required fields marked with red asterisks (*), including Organization Type, whether business is independently owned and operated, whether it is a subsidiary, not-for-profit status, broker status, dominance in field, total employees, and gross sales information. Step 7: Click Save at the top of the form. Step 8: Click Submit Application button and confirm submission in the prompt. Step 9: After submission, close the form to view program status in eMMA. If eligible, the vendor profile will include a CSB number and three-year expiration date visible in the Documents tab under Attestations & General Documents. Vendors will receive an email notification of approval or non-compliance status. CSB certification is valid for three years and must be renewed within 30 days of expiration notice. Once certified, CSBs automatically receive the price preference when bidding on SBP-designated procurements with no separate application required for the preference itself.

structured_extraction.program_description: The SBR Program provides Certified Small Businesses (CSBs) with the opportunity to participate as prime contractors by establishing a unique marketplace where small businesses only compete against other small businesses instead of larger, more established companies. Approximately 20% of all open state-funded solicitations advertised on Maryland's online procurement platform (eMaryland Marketplace Advantage/eMMA) are designated as SBR, and an award can only be made to a CSB on designated procurements. Under an enhanced executive order, all state procurement units must reserve all contracts valued between $50,000 and $500,000 for small business bidders, with encouragement to consider higher dollar procurements for the program as well.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The SBR Program designates certain state-funded procurements exclusively for Certified Small Businesses to bid on, creating a reserved marketplace where small businesses compete only against other small businesses rather than larger established companies. State procurement units are required to reserve all contracts valued between $50,000 and $500,000 for small business bidders, and the state encourages consideration of higher dollar procurements as well. Awards can only be made to CSBs on designated SBR solicitations. To participate, businesses must complete the CSB (Certified Small Business) certification process through eMMA (eMaryland Marketplace Advantage). There is no cost to become a CSB, and certification is valid for three years before recertification is required. Businesses must recertify within a 30-day window prior to expiration or their certification will expire; however, expired certifications can reapply for a new certification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling - applications accepted continuously; recertification required within 30-day window before expiration date
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses in Maryland that meet Certified Small Business (CSB) eligibility size and ownership standards in their industry and want to bid on state-funded procurement contracts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program reserves state government procurement contract opportunities (particularly contracts valued between $50,000 and $500,000) exclusively for certified small businesses. Funds are not directly provided; rather, businesses gain access to reserved contracting opportunities where they compete only against other small businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - applies to all state-funded solicitations advertised on eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) and all executive branch procurement units under the governor's authority.
requirements_list: Business must be a for-profit enterprise
Business must not be a broker
Business must be independently owned and operated
Business must not be a subsidiary of another business (a subsidiary is a company for which a majority of the voting stock is owned by a holding company)
Business must not be dominant in its field of operation at the national level
For wholesale operations: did not employ more than 50 persons in the most recently completed 3 fiscal years and gross sales did not exceed an average of $4,000,000
For retail operations: did not employ more than 25 persons in the most recently completed 3 fiscal years and gross sales did not exceed an average of $3,000,000
For manufacturing operations: did not employ more than 100 persons in the most recently completed 3 fiscal years and gross sales did not exceed an average of $2,000,000
For service operations: did not employ more than 100 persons in the most recently completed 3 fiscal years and gross sales did not exceed an average of $10,000,000
For construction operations: did not employ more than 50 persons in the most recently completed 3 fiscal years and gross sales did not exceed an average of $7,000,000
For architect and engineering services: did not employ more than 100 persons in the most recently completed 3 fiscal years and gross sales did not exceed an average of $4,500,000
Employees are counted as persons who work full-time or part-time more than 20 hours per week as they appear on the business certified payroll roster or payroll list
Gross Sales (gross receipts) is the total amount the business received from all sources during the tax year without subtracting any cost or expenses
Documentation may be required to verify CSB eligibility prior to contract award
For newly formed businesses: gross sales estimate required if business has not submitted tax return yet
For established businesses: most recent years tax filing (up to three years) required to enter gross sales information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Register for a free eMMA (eMaryland Marketplace Advantage) account at https://emma.maryland.gov if not already registered. Step 2: Log into eMMA with your credentials. Step 3: Click the General Info tab and select Company Profile from the drop-down menu. Step 4: Scroll to the State Programs section, click 'Apply for the CSB Certification?' field, and select 'Yes' from the drop-down menu. Click Save. Step 5: Navigate to the Documents tab on the left-hand side panel and scroll to the Attestations & General Documents section. The CSB application displays in a pink row with red lettering. Step 6: Click the Add (plus) icon to the far left of the CSB Application ONLY ONCE to create an application form. Step 7: Click the blue CSB Disclaimer link to review the CSB Eligibility Standards and Disclaimer in a new browser tab. Step 8: Return to eMMA and check the checkbox confirming you have read and agree to the Certified Small Business disclaimer. Step 9: Complete all required fields marked with a red asterisk (*), including: Organization Type, independent ownership and operation status, subsidiary status, for-profit status, broker status, dominance in field of operation, total number of employees, new business status, and gross sales information for the last three tax years (or projected first-year gross sales for new businesses). Step 10: Click Save at the top of the application window. Step 11: Click Submit Application button and confirm submission by clicking OK in the prompt. A notification banner will display confirmation of successful or unsuccessful submission. Step 12: Close the form and check your Documents tab for your CSB number and three-year expiration date in the Attestations & General Documents section. You will also receive an email notification regarding approval or non-compliance status (check Spam/Junk folders). Step 13: For recertification, a 30-day expiration notice will appear on your Company Info page. You must recertify within this 30-day window or your certification will expire. Submit a recertification application before the expiration date using similar steps. Step 14: Optionally register for the free Training & Insights for Procurement Success (T.I.P.S.) Webinar series to learn how to do business with Maryland agencies. For technical support, email emma.helpdesk@maryland.gov or call 410-697-9600 and ask to speak with a SBR Program Compliance Manager. Use Google Chrome browser for best results.

structured_extraction.program_name: T.I.P.S. (Training & Insights for Procurement Success) Small Business Webinar Series
structured_extraction.program_description: A free training program offered by the Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs to help small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses compete in state contracting and improve business operations. The program has evolved from in-person classroom sessions (held on the fourth Tuesday of each month at the Governor's Coordinating Offices in Crownsville) to a virtual webinar format now known as T.I.P.S. (Training & Insights for Procurement Success), offering two sessions per month throughout the year. Topics covered include navigating state and federal procurement processes, Maryland's MBE and VSBE program rules and responsibilities, e-Procurement/eMMA platform navigation, solicitation anatomy, bid and proposal preparation, capabilities statements, cash flow management, prevailing wage laws, negotiation strategies, financial capacity building, subcontractor rights and responsibilities, and professional communication. The program also includes companion series: 'Small Biz Resource Connections' (periodic webinars featuring guest speakers on topics like business lending, employment law, accessibility requirements, and non-discrimination in contracting) and 'Maryland VSBE/CSB Certification Workshop Series' (monthly in-person workshops at various county locations covering VSBE and Small Business Reserve certification and re-certification). All sessions are free to attend, recorded, and made available on YouTube. Slide materials are posted after each session.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free virtual webinars delivered online via Zoom, offered twice monthly (approximately 24 sessions per year). Sessions are typically 1–2 hours, held at 10 a.m., and include live instruction from staff of the Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs, experienced small business owners, and resource organizations. Sessions feature interactive polls and Q&A. Participants attend in listen-only mode with camera off and microphone muted. All sessions are recorded and made available on YouTube; slide presentations are posted after each webinar. Participants receive a unique Zoom link upon registration confirmation. A companion in-person series — the Maryland VSBE/SBR Certification Workshop Series — is held monthly at various county locations statewide covering VSBE and Small Business Reserve certification and re-certification. An additional 'Small Biz Resource Connections' webinar series covers topics such as business lending resources, federal contracting, employment law compliance, labor standards, accessibility requirements, and non-discrimination policies in state contracting. No cost to attend any session; advance registration required for all formats.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens approximately 3 weeks in advance of each webinar or workshop. Ongoing program with rolling monthly registration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners, minority business enterprise (MBE) owners, women-owned business owners, veteran-owned small business enterprise (VSBE) owners, prime contractors, subcontractors, and entrepreneurs across Maryland interested in performing state contracting work or improving business operations and competitiveness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance covering: state and federal procurement processes; Maryland MBE and VSBE program requirements and rights; e-Procurement/eMMA platform navigation; solicitation anatomy; bid and proposal preparation; capabilities statements; cash flow management; prevailing wage laws; negotiation strategies; financial capacity building; subcontractor rights and responsibilities; professional communication; business lending resources; federal contracting opportunities; employment law compliance; labor standards; accessibility requirements; and non-discrimination policies in state contracting.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Virtual webinar sessions are accessible to any business owner in Maryland (and out-of-state businesses interested in contracting with Maryland) with no geographic barriers. In-person VSBE/SBR Certification Workshops are held at multiple county locations including Charles County, Montgomery County, Anne Arundel County, Frederick County, Baltimore City, Prince George's County, Dorchester County, Howard County, Calvert County, and St. Mary's County. Earlier in-person classroom sessions were held at the Governor's Coordinating Offices at 100 Community Place in Crownsville, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a small, minority, women, or veteran-owned business owner or entrepreneur
Advance registration required
Seating/participation is limited — registration on a first-come, first-served basis
Must attend via Zoom webinar link (for virtual sessions)
Consent to be recorded by registering
Must attend in-person at designated county location (for VSBE/SBR Certification Workshops)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the program home page at gomdsmallbiz.maryland.gov and sign up in the 'STAY CONNECTED' box to receive email notification when registration opens. Registration opens approximately 3 weeks before each webinar or workshop. Register for the specific session via the Zoom registration link (for webinars) or the posted registration link (for in-person workshops). Upon registration confirmation, participants receive a unique link to join the webinar or details for the in-person session. Sessions are also promoted on the program website with full annual schedules posted. Recordings and slide decks are available on the website and YouTube after each session.

structured_extraction.program_description: The VSBE Program provides contracting opportunities on state-funded procurements for qualified veteran-owned small businesses. Designated state agencies and departments are directed to spend at least 3% of the dollar value of their procurement contracts with certified VSBE firms. The work of a certified VSBE firm, whether performing as a prime contractor or subcontractor, can be counted toward an established VSBE contract goal. Certification is free, must be renewed every 3 years, and requires vendor registration on the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) platform along with veteran verification.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Small, Minority and Women Business Affairs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides access to state-funded procurement contracts reserved for certified veteran-owned small businesses. There is no cost to obtain certification. Certified firms must meet size standards adopted by the United States Small Business Administration in 13 C.F.R. 121.201. Certification requires vendor registration on the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) platform, veteran verification, and VSBE certification. Once certified, firms must renew every 3 years, with the next renewal effective September 1st, 2025. Vendors registered in eMMA receive email notices of procurement opportunities from state agencies and departments valued over $15,000. County and local governments also use the platform to advertise their procurements.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Danielle Davis (Department of Veterans and Military Families Veterans Services Specialist)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veteran-owned small businesses seeking state contracting opportunities. Businesses must be at least 51% owned and controlled by one or more individuals who are veterans, where a veteran is defined as an individual verified as having served on active duty in the Uniformed Services of the United States, other than for training, and was discharged or released under conditions other than dishonorable.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to state-funded procurement contracts for goods and services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. The program applies to state-funded procurements and state agencies and departments. County and local governments also use the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage platform to advertise their procurements.
requirements_list: Business must meet size standards adopted by the United States Small Business Administration in 13 C.F.R. 121.201 and any subsequent revision
Business must be at least 51% owned and controlled by one or more individuals who are veterans
Veteran must have served on active duty in the Uniformed Services of the United States, other than for training
Veteran must have been discharged or released under conditions other than dishonorable
Firm must be registered as a vendor on the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) platform
Veteran status must be verified by the Maryland Department of Veterans & Military Families or through Federal Veteran Verification
Must notify the Office of Small, Minority and Women's Business Affairs within 30 days of any change affecting ability to meet VSBE Program eligibility requirements
Certification must be renewed every 3 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: STEP 1: Register as a vendor on the eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) platform at no cost. When registering, select the Procurement Programs section, navigate to Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise (VSBE), select 'No' to indicate you are not currently enrolled, then select 'Yes' to apply. After successful registration, log in and follow the link for 'Missing Mandatory Credentials/Documents', navigate to the Certifications section, and select 'Add Certifications'. Under the Type category, choose 'Certification/VSBE Application' and answer questions verifying you meet eligibility standards and accept terms and conditions. STEP 2: Complete veteran verification by submitting required documentation including DD Form 214 (Member 4 Page), DD215, NGB22, NGB23, DD Form 5016, Order Memo, Certificate of Release, or copy of the United States Department of Veterans Affairs Rating Decision or Federal Benefit Letter/Summary. Veteran status must be verified by either the Maryland Department of Veterans & Military Families or through Federal Veteran Verification. Upload the VSBE Veteran Verification Form 2025 in the eMMA VSBE Application. STEP 3: Upon completing eMMA registration and verifying veteran status, log into your eMMA account and complete the VSBE certification application. Select the Company Profile tab to access Company Info. Under Procurement Programs and State Programs, select 'Yes' to enroll in the VSBE Program. This will populate the VSBE Application under Documents to be completed. Enter your veteran verification type (state or federal) and save changes before exiting eMMA. All veteran verification numbers are verified during the certification process.

Property must be agricultural land

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME)
structured_extraction.program_description: Harford County receives annual HUD entitlement grants through both the CDBG and HOME programs. The CDBG program helps local governments address serious challenges facing their communities by funding projects that provide decent affordable housing, create a suitable living environment, and expand economic opportunities for low- to moderate-income persons. The HOME program provides formula grants to expand the supply of decent, safe, sanitary, affordable housing for low-income families and to expand the capacity of nonprofit Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) to develop and manage affordable housing. Funding amounts depend on a pre-determined HUD formula. Projects and activities must be submitted to and approved by HUD through a 5-year Consolidated Plan.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Harford County receives annual allocations of CDBG and HOME funds from HUD and disperses these funds to various nonprofit organizations, for-profit entities (in some cases under CDBG), nonprofit developers, and Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs). Funds are not available to individuals directly. CDBG funds support projects that benefit low-to-moderate-income persons, address slum and blight, or address urgent community needs. For HOME, affordability restrictions apply based on the amount of assistance: assistance of $15,000 to $40,000 must remain affordable for 15 years, amounts over $40,000 for 15 years, new construction of rental housing for 20 years, and refinancing of rental housing for 15 years. HUD requires a 25% non-federal match for each eligible HOME activity. The exact award amounts depend on project selection and HUD funding availability. Funds are awarded through a competitive application process based on community needs identified in the Consolidated Plan.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Typically January/February; rolling basis following annual funding allocation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, private nonprofit organizations with IRS 501(c)(3) status, Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs), nonprofit developers, existing housing programs, and in some cases for-profit entities serving low- to moderate-income residents and families in Harford County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: CDBG funds can be used for capital projects that provide decent housing, create a suitable living environment, reduce slum and blight, or expand economic opportunities for low- to moderate-income persons or households. Projects must meet one of three national objectives: benefit low-moderate-income persons (through housing, limited clientele benefit, area benefit, or job creation), address slum and blight, or address urgent need. HOME funds can be used to expand the supply of decent, safe, sanitary, affordable housing for low-income families and to support CHDOs in developing and managing affordable housing. Eligible HOME activities include rental housing development, homeownership programs, supportive housing with services such as case management or job readiness training, public facility improvements, tenant-based rental assistance, low-moderate income housing construction, first-time homebuyer support, and critical repairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland, including the Town of Bel Air and City of Aberdeen under the Urban County Partnership agreement.
requirements_list: Projects and activities must be submitted to and approved by HUD through a 5-year Consolidated Plan
Must benefit low- to moderate-income citizens
Private nonprofit organizations must have IRS 501(c)(3) status
In some cases for-profit entities may be eligible for CDBG funding
All proposed programs and projects must meet applicable federal regulations
Projects must meet one of the CDBG national objectives: benefit low-moderate-income persons, address slum and blight, or address urgent need
All selected programs and projects are subject to the availability of funding and Harford County's budget review process
HOME applicant organizations must be nonprofit
Community Housing Development Organizations must be organized under state or local laws and exempt from taxes under 501(c)(3)
CHDOs must have effectively carried out activities financed by HOME funds
CHDOs must have a history of serving the community where HOME-funded housing will be located
CHDOs must meet standards of financial accountability
One-third of CHDO governing board must be composed of low-income community residents or elected representatives
CHDOs must maintain a formal process allowing low-income residents and program beneficiaries to provide input on relevant decisions
A 25% non-federal match is required for each eligible HOME activity
Affordability restrictions must be maintained for specified time periods based on assistance amount and activity type
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The typical application period runs during January and February each year, though applications may be accepted on a rolling basis. Applicants must view the Harford County Grants Portal to see open grant applications and submit proposals according to published timelines and requirements. Applications are reviewed by Harford County's Community Development Department. Harford County's budget review process determines which projects receive CDBG funding. For HOME, applicants are encouraged to contact Housing & Community Development at 410-638-3045 to discuss project feasibility before submitting applications. Each year Harford County submits a Consolidated Annual Action Plan (AAP) to HUD detailing how funds will be used, developed through broad community consultation as part of the 5-year Consolidated Plan (ConPlan). A Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (CAPER) is submitted annually showing how goals were met.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funding supports rapid rehousing, transitional housing, permanent supportive housing, and supportive services for homeless individuals and families.

structured_extraction.program_name: Drinking Water State Revolving Fund Bipartisan Infrastructure Law Funding for PFAS/Emerging Contaminants
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides 100% loan principal forgiveness for water system projects that address emerging contaminants, including perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), in drinking water.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% forgiveness of loan principal for drinking water infrastructure projects addressing PFAS and other emerging contaminants. Applicants receive low-interest loans with 100% principal forgiveness under this program funded through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public water systems and water utilities addressing PFAS and emerging contaminants in drinking water across Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure projects that address emerging contaminants, including PFAS, in drinking water systems. Eligible uses include treatment systems, distribution system improvements, and related infrastructure modifications.

requirements_list: Project must address emerging contaminants, including PFAS, in drinking water
Applicant must be a public water system or government entity
Project must comply with Safe Drinking Water Act requirements

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review MDE's Drinking Water IPPS (Intended Use Plan) and application guidelines available at https://mde.maryland.gov/programs/water/WQFA/pages/index.aspx. 2. Technical assistance available through MDE Funding Technical Assistance Points of Contact.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program funds renovation and new construction projects to improve business exteriors along designated stretches of U.S. Route 40 and MD-755 in the Edgewood Sustainable Community Area. The goal is to transform business exteriors to generate economic development and increase investment in a historically underserved community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Total program funding is $200,000. For eligible projects costing up to $10,000, businesses receive a 100% reimbursement grant with zero match required. For projects over $10,000, businesses receive a reimbursement grant covering up to 80% of approved costs above the first $10,000, with the business required to provide a 20% cash match. Funds are used for project reimbursement only. Matching type is cash.

ADA compliant accessibility improvements and exterior cleaning and repair are also eligible. Interior renovation, equipment purchase, inventory purchase, property purchase, roofing, and structural repairs are not permitted.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located within the designated eligibility area bordering U.S. Route 40 (Pulaski Highway) or MD-755 (Edgewood Road) in the Edgewood Sustainable Community Area overlay, as shown on the program map.
