Project subject to final inspection and site visit before reimbursement
All receipts, invoices, and documentation relating to the project and grant application must be maintained by the business for a minimum of three years for audit purposes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed Supplier Package along with detailed project description, architectural rendering, detailed budget, project scope of work, and invoices and proofs of payment. Applications are reviewed by the Harford County Department of Economic Development and subject to Maryland Historical Trust approval. Projects must comply with all Harford County planning, zoning, licensing, permitting, and public works requirements. Upon project completion, a final inspection and site visit occurs before reimbursement is paid.

structured_extraction.program_description: An expedited permitting program for major capital projects that bring economic impact to Harford County. Qualified projects receive prioritized reviews, a dedicated county liaison, and online progress tracking.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants receive expedited permitting and processing of permits, assignment of a dedicated Harford County liaison to assist throughout the permitting process, and access to an online portal to track project progress. The Fast Track Coordination Team reviews applications, with final approval from the County Executive.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses undertaking major capital projects in Harford County that will bring economic impact to the area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This is a technical assistance program providing expedited permitting services. It does not provide direct funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must be a major capital project
Project must bring economic impact to Harford County
Application must be submitted to Karen Holt, Director of Economic Development, at 220 S. Main Street, Bel Air, MD 21014
Applications are reviewed by the Fast Track Coordination Team and require final approval by the County Executive
Project must demonstrate significant economic benefit including job creation, capital investment, or other measurable economic impact
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Fast Track 2.0 application form and submit it to Karen Holt, Director of Economic Development, at the Harford County Office of Economic Development, 220 S. Main Street, Bel Air, MD 21014. The Fast Track Coordination Team reviews the application for approval, and the County Executive provides final designation. Once approved, applicants receive a dedicated liaison, expedited permitting review, and access to an online portal to track progress. Contact Shawn Krout by email or phone for assistance with the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that enhances the ability of public and private sector organizations to provide human services and address the resource needs of organizations that serve the emergency and daily needs of citizens in Harford County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to qualifying non-profit organizations to support human services delivery. Grantees must enter into an agreement with the county and comply with financial and programmatic procedures and submit required forms.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit, tax-exempt organizations that provide human services and primarily serve low to moderate income populations in Harford County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Human services programs that address emergency and daily needs of Harford County citizens.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County only.
requirements_list: Must be incorporated as a non-profit, tax-exempt organization with 501(c)(3) status
Must primarily serve low to moderate income populations and provide documentation of who is served
Must provide human services
Must be soundly managed and financially accountable and provide proof thereof
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations must enter into an agreement with Harford County. All grantees must comply with financial and programmatic procedures and submit required forms. Applications are submitted through the Grants Portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: Harford County allocates more than $1 million each year to support local nonprofits working in a full range of supportive services, including housing and homeless prevention services. The program provides operating funds to eligible non-profit organizations that offer assistance to people experiencing homelessness, those at risk of homelessness, and affordable housing programs. New applicants are eligible to receive up to $5,000 in starter funds to give growing service providers financial and technical support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Harford County allocates over $1 million annually to support nonprofits in a full range of supportive services, including housing and homeless prevention programs. New applicants can receive up to $5,000 in starter funds. All organizations receiving grant funds must enter into an agreement with Harford County and comply with financial and programmatic procedures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local non-profit organizations in Harford County providing supportive services, including housing and homeless prevention services, to low- to moderate-income residents. New and growing service providers are particularly encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs for organizations providing supportive services including homeless prevention services, affordable housing programs, and support to people experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland. Organizations must primarily serve low- to moderate-income residents and must hold activities in spaces accessible to people with disabilities.
requirements_list: Incorporated as a non-profit, tax-exempt 501(c)(3) organization
Primarily serve low- to moderate-income populations and document who is served
Serve homeless individuals, those at-risk for homelessness, or provide affordable housing
Be soundly managed and financially accountable with proof thereof (professional audit required)
Hold activities in spaces available to the disabled
Meet the needs of visually and hearing impaired individuals upon notification of need
Prohibited from using funding to promote or further non-secular purposes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are reviewed by the Community Development Review Board, which makes funding recommendations. All grantees must comply with financial and programmatic procedures and submit required forms. New applicants may be eligible for up to $5,000 in starter funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides funding to address homelessness and support vulnerable populations through production or preservation of affordable housing, tenant-based rental assistance, supportive services, homeless prevention services, housing counseling, and purchase and development of non-congregate shelter.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Harford County's total HOME-ARP allocation is $1,821,904 in federal funds to be distributed across four activities: (1) production or preservation of affordable housing; (2) tenant-based rental assistance; (3) supportive services and homeless prevention services and housing counseling; and (4) purchase and development of non-congregate shelter. Funds primarily benefit qualifying individuals and families who are homeless, at risk of homelessness, or in other vulnerable populations. The allocation plan details the specific funding amounts and implementation strategies for each activity category.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families who are homeless, at risk of homelessness, or in other vulnerable populations in Harford County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Production or preservation of affordable housing, tenant-based rental assistance, supportive services, homeless prevention services, housing counseling, and purchase and development of non-congregate shelter.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Individuals and families must be homeless, at risk of homelessness, or in other vulnerable populations
Applicants must be residents of Harford County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants and organizations should contact Housing & Community Services (HCS) at 410-638-3045 for detailed information about application procedures and funding availability for specific program activities.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County African American Heritage Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to support projects that help the public understand and learn about African American history in Harford County, including restoration of historic buildings, preservation planning, research, and educational programming.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding is provided for eligible projects related to African American heritage preservation and interpretation in Harford County. Grants may be awarded for rehabilitation, restoration, or acquisition of historic resources; preservation planning services; architectural and archeological survey; research; and interpretation and programming. The program does not specify a maximum award amount per grant or specific grant terms on the publicly available materials.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, non-profit organizations, businesses, and local governments working on African American heritage and historic preservation projects in Harford County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding may be used for rehabilitation, restoration, or acquisition of historic resources listed or eligible for listing as Harford County Landmarks; preservation planning services; architectural and archeological survey; research; and interpretation and programming.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Harford County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must contribute to public understanding and interpretation of African American history in Harford County

Project must involve rehabilitation, restoration, or acquisition of a resource eligible for or listed as a Harford County Landmark, preservation planning, survey, research, or interpretation and programming
Applicants must review the Information Packet before submitting
Applicants are encouraged to contact Historic Preservation staff to discuss their project before applying
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit applications through the Harford County Grants Portal (online submission is strongly preferred), or hard copy applications are available upon request. Applicants should review the Information Packet prior to submitting. Interested parties should contact Historic Preservation staff before applying to discuss their project.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports individual nonprofits or municipalities with creating, expanding, or enhancing events that drive tourism and economic growth in the county. This can include festivals, events, exhibits, and other programming that attract individuals to either overnight stays or day trips. Funds not used by the Partnership Grant program are set aside for use by the Community Impact Grant program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for tourism-related and community-focused festivals, events, exhibits, and programming by individual nonprofits or municipalities. Funds are distributed based on priority order: (1) direct tourism-related marketing costs for festivals and events; (2) non-marketing expenses for festivals and events attracting out-of-county visitors; (3) internal operational expenses for tourism-related organizations including up to 75% of salaries of key employees; (4) festivals and events beneficial to community culture by non-tourism nonprofits; (5) program sponsorships by nonprofits and municipalities. Staff salaries are capped at 75% for first-year awards, 50% for second-year awards, 25% for third-year awards, and 0% for any subsequent year awards. Funds not used by the Partnership Grant program are allocated to this program. The 2027 budget allocation is determined by the County Executive after review and recommendation by the Economic Development Advisory Board Tourism Activity Review Committee.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual nonprofits (501(c)3 or 501(c)6 organizations) registered in Harford County or Harford County municipalities that seek to create, expand, or enhance tourism-related or community-focused events and programming.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct tourism-related festivals, events, exhibits, and programming; marketing and non-marketing expenses for events; and internal operational expenses including key employee salaries (capped at decreasing percentages over multiple years). Funds must be directly attributed to tourism-related activities or community-focused programming and cannot be used for daily operating costs, capital improvements, property acquisition, capital building projects, retirement, debt reduction, equipment such as computers and copiers used for daily office functions, or any expenses not directly attributed to tourism-related festivals, events, exhibits, and other programming as outlined in the executed grant agreement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland. Organizations must be registered in Harford County with the State of Maryland to be eligible. Programs should attract out-of-county visitors or provide benefits to the local community.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)3 or 501(c)6 nonprofit organization registered in Harford County or a Harford County municipality
Must be in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessment and Taxation
Must be in good standing with Maryland Office of the Secretary of State, Charitable Organization Division
Must be compliant with all past and current Harford County grant requirements
Must demonstrate ability to secure additional funding sources beyond Harford County Government through sponsorships, grants, fundraising, or philanthropic donations
Must be able to capture data and objective outcomes for measuring success, with focus on projected calculations of tourism spending in the county
Must demonstrate track record with past initiatives and ability to deliver successful programming
Must demonstrate financial need for funds
Must demonstrate compliance with reporting and execution of past Harford County grant awards
Applicant cannot have history of non-compliance with past Harford County grant programs
For operational expenses, must demonstrate ability to work towards self-sustainability

If non-compliance history exists from FY26 award or first three-quarters of FY26, funding may be denied entirely or disbursed in installments; continued non-compliance may result in delayed grant execution or termination of future installments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through the online eCivis portal at https://portal.ecivis.com/#login3/FCB224D2-CFDB-464F-82EC-D36B254A9685. Applicants must complete and upload the Tourism Grant Budget and Expense Report (spreadsheet provided) and the Quarterly Narrative Activity Report (QNAR) with program overview and objectives. Applications must include list of all partners, shareholders, and board members; list of key staff; proof of good standing with Maryland state agencies; 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) documentation; most recently filed Form 990; balance sheets and income statements for fiscal years 2023 and 2024; and completed Supplier Package with payment and bank account information. The Economic Development Advisory Board Tourism Activity Review Committee evaluates applications based on evaluation criteria including program identifiability, ability to attract out-of-county visitors and overnight stays, ability to secure additional funding, data collection capability, track record, financial need, and compliance history. Final award amounts are at the discretion of the County Executive. Reporting requirements include quarterly budget and activity reporting with receipts, invoices, and proof of payment, and completion of the QNAR and Tourism Grant Budget and Expense Report forms.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Enterprise Zone Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing tax incentives to businesses that invest in Harford County's Enterprise Zone in Aberdeen and Havre de Grace. The program encourages job creation, business retention and expansion, and development of vacant or underutilized properties in older industrial areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of tax credits are available. Local Real Property Tax Credits provide up to 10 years of credits on capital investments, with 80% credit on increases in assessed value of real property for the first five years, then decreasing by 10% annually for the remaining five years. State Income and Job Creation Tax Credits include a one-time $1,000 tax credit per new job created, submitted with annual tax filing using Maryland Form 500CR. An additional credit is available for businesses hiring economically-disadvantaged employees, providing $6,000 total per eligible employee distributed over three years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses located within the Harford County Enterprise Zone in Aberdeen and Havre de Grace seeking to make capital investments or create new jobs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital investments in construction and rehabilitation of real property, and job creation with wages at least 150% of minimum wage.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Enterprise Zone is located in Aberdeen and Havre de Grace, including properties along U.S. Route 40, portions of Aberdeen Proving Ground to the east, south to Belcamp and Perryman, and west to the HEAT Center (now CONVERGE). The zone encompasses 9,738 acres with designated business parks including 40 East Industrial Park, Aberdeen Industrial Center, Advantage Business Center, Chesapeake Industrial Park, Cranberry Run Business Park, Enterprise Business Park, Hardee's Industrial Park, Harford Gateway, Hickory Ridge Industrial Park, North Gate Business Park, Perryman Industrial Park, Rock Glenn Business Park, CONVERGE, and Water's Edge Corporate Campus.
requirements_list: Business must be located within the Enterprise Zone
Minimum capital investment: $100,000 for businesses with 10 or fewer employees, or $125,000 for businesses with 11 or more employees
Minimum job creation: Two new jobs for businesses with 10 or fewer employees, or five new jobs for businesses with 11 or more employees
New jobs must be working 35 hours per week or more at hourly pay of at least 150% of minimum wage
At least half of work time must be within the Enterprise Zone
Must meet specified design standards
Contact Enterprise Zone Administrator prior to construction to discuss timing and ensure real property tax credits align with July 1st
Building must be occupied to receive real property tax credits
Submit itemized cost breakdown for construction and renovation with application
Submit site plan showing interior and exterior building changes with application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Karen Holt, Enterprise Zone Administrator, at klholt@harfordcountymd.gov or 410-638-3059 prior to construction to discuss timeline and ensure coordinated planning. Submit application by October 1st deadline with itemized construction costs, site plan, and supporting documentation. For income and job creation tax credits, submit Maryland Form 500CR with annual tax filing. The program accepts applications on a rolling basis during each application year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Historic Preservation Tax Credits
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides financial incentives for owners of Harford County Historic Landmarks who undertake approved historic preservation, rehabilitation, and restoration work on their historic properties. Property owners may reduce their county real property tax based on qualified rehabilitation and restoration expenses, receiving a credit equal to 10% of those expenses (capped at $7,500 based on $75,000 in expenses), as well as a credit based on the amount their assessment increased due to the rehabilitation or restoration.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive a county real property tax credit equal to 10% of qualified restoration and rehabilitation expenses, capped at $7,500 (based on expenses of $75,000). Additionally, owners receive a tax credit based on the assessed value increase resulting from the rehabilitation or restoration work. Credits can be applied repeatedly as long as the previous credit amount is exhausted before a new credit is granted. Work must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Historic Rehabilitation and the Harford County Historic Preservation Design Guidelines.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/Ongoing - Applications accepted throughout the year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of properties designated as Harford County Historic Landmarks undertaking historic rehabilitation and preservation work in Harford County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified restoration and rehabilitation expenses for historic properties, including approved historic preservation and rehabilitation work that complies with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Historic Rehabilitation and the Harford County Historic Preservation Design Guidelines. Examples include structural repairs, window restoration, exterior restoration, interior rehabilitation, and other approved work that enhances the historic character of the property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in Harford County and designated as Harford County Historic Landmarks by the County Council. The program is limited to Harford County only.
requirements_list: Property must be designated as a Harford County Historic Landmark by the County Council
Rehabilitation plans must be approved by the Harford County Historic Preservation Commission through a Certificate of Appropriateness application before work begins
All work must meet the Harford County Historic Preservation Design Guidelines and the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Historic Rehabilitation
Work must be completed according to plans approved in the Certificate of Appropriateness
Applicant must submit a Certification of Completed Work Application upon project completion
Applicant must submit an Itemized Expenses spreadsheet documenting all qualified rehabilitation expenses
A staff site visit and review by the Historic Preservation Commission must occur prior to approval
Previous tax credit amount must be exhausted before another credit can be granted
Applicants must submit detailed documentation of completed work and expenses with receipts or invoices
Owner must have paid property taxes on the historic landmark property
The property must remain designated as a Harford County Historic Landmark
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Part 1 - Pre-Project: Submit an Application for Certificate of Appropriateness to the Harford County Historic Preservation Commission for approval of rehabilitation plans before beginning any work. Include detailed plans, specifications, and photographs of the proposed work. The Commission reviews applications at their monthly public meetings. Once the Certificate of Appropriateness is approved, work may proceed. Part 2 - Post-Project: Upon project completion, submit a Certification of Completed Work Application and an Itemized Expenses spreadsheet documenting all qualified expenses with supporting documentation (receipts, invoices, contractor statements). Schedule a staff site visit for inspection and verification that work was completed according to approved plans. The Historic Preservation Commission reviews the application and site visit results at their monthly public meeting. Upon approval, the tax credit is calculated and applied to the property owner's county real property tax account.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Purchase of Development Rights Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows agricultural landowners to permanently preserve their property by selling development rights through easement contracts. These easements permanently extinguish all development potential and prevent further commercial or residential subdivision while allowing the landowner to retain full ownership of the land.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county purchases development rights from agricultural property owners through permanent easement contracts. Landowners receive compensation for permanently extinguishing development potential on their property. The county values the development rights based on the difference between the fair market value of the land with development potential and its value restricted to agricultural use only.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Harford County Department of Planning and Zoning
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Harford County seeking to permanently preserve their property and receive compensation for development rights
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property owners receive compensation for permanently preserving agricultural land and extinguishing development rights through easement contracts
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be agricultural land
Owner must be willing to enter into permanent easement contract
Development rights must be extinguished permanently
Property must meet county agricultural preservation standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners interested in participating should contact the Harford County Department of Planning and Zoning at 410-638-3103 to express interest and request program information. The department will evaluate the property and discuss the appraisal and valuation process. Properties are prioritized based on county preservation goals and available funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Harford County Solar & Geothermal Energy Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides real property tax credits for property owners in Harford County who install qualifying solar or geothermal energy conservation devices. For geothermal systems specifically, qualified individuals who meet age and property value requirements may receive a 20% tax credit on county property taxes for up to 20 years.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A real property tax credit for installation of qualifying solar or geothermal energy conservation devices. For qualifying geothermal installations, eligible individuals may receive a 20% tax credit on county property taxes for up to 20 years, subject to age and property value requirements. Solar energy tax credits are also available. The credit is applied against county property taxes owed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Harford County who install qualifying solar or geothermal energy conservation devices; geothermal-specific credits are available to qualified individuals over age 65 meeting property value and residency criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax relief for installation of qualifying solar or geothermal energy conservation devices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County only.
requirements_list: Installation of qualifying solar or geothermal energy conservation device
For geothermal 20% credit: individual must be over 65 years of age
For geothermal 20% credit: dwelling assessed value of $600,000 or less
For geothermal 20% credit: either owned and lived in dwelling for at least 35 years, or applicant is a retiree or surviving spouse of US Uniformed Services retiree who has not remarried
Device must meet applicable equipment standards and installation requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Solar/Geothermal Energy Application form to Harford County. Submit the form along with supporting documentation including proof of equipment installation, property assessment information, and any required eligibility documentation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Assistance for Families With Disabilities (HAFD)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides tenant-based rental assistance and supportive services to income-eligible families with HIV/AIDS. Supportive services assist with short-term rent, utilities, security deposit, and moving expenses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tenant-based rental assistance and supportive services for income-eligible families with HIV/AIDS. Services cover short-term rent, utilities, security deposit, and moving expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible families with HIV/AIDS in Harford County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Short-term rent, utilities, security deposit, and moving expenses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be income-eligible
Must have HIV/AIDS diagnosis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Harford County Health Department to apply

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program that provides rental subsidies to help very low-income families, elderly individuals, and people with disabilities afford decent, safe, and sanitary housing in the private rental market. The program pays a housing subsidy directly to the landlord on behalf of participating families, making rental housing more affordable for eligible households in Harford County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides rental subsidies paid directly to landlords on behalf of eligible families. Families must have household income at or below federal income limits (30%, 50%, or 80% of area median income depending on category). Payment standards vary by number of bedrooms, ranging from $1,082 to $3,703 per month as of November 1, 2025. Families are responsible for finding housing that meets HUD Housing Quality Standards within 60 days and must pay the difference between the subsidy amount and actual rent. A limited waitlist opening is scheduled for December 8-12, 2025.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, December 12 at 4:30 p.m. (one-time opening December 8-12, 2025); ongoing waiting list otherwise
structured_extraction.program_audience: Very low-income families, elderly individuals, and people with disabilities who live or work in Harford County. Priority preferences for families with dependent children, working families, elderly families, disabled families, veterans or surviving spouses of veterans, and homeless individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly rental subsidies paid directly to landlords to help pay rent for decent, safe, and sanitary housing in the private rental market.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland. Priority given to applicants who live or work in Harford County.
requirements_list: Household income must meet federal income limits (30%, 50%, or 80% of area median income)
Must meet income eligibility requirements
Must qualify based on family composition and circumstances
Applicant or family member must live or work in Harford County to receive priority consideration
Housing must meet HUD Housing Quality Standards
Rent must be within allowable limits set by the program
Family must complete preliminary application and be placed on waiting list
Must provide current contact information and maintain updated address on wait list
Must attend enrollment interview and briefing session if selected from waiting list
Must find suitable housing within 60 days of selection
Must reach agreement with landlord on lease terms
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Family completes preliminary application and is placed on waiting list (applications accepted during limited opening periods, e.g., December 8-12, 2025). 2. After successful application, applicants receive a confirmation number and can check their wait list status at www.waitlistcheck.com or by calling 1-877-204-9098. 3. When selected from waiting list, enrollment interview is scheduled to determine eligibility. 4. If eligible, family attends briefing session to learn about program and housing search process. 5. Family finds housing within 60 days meeting HUD standards and rent limits. 6. Family negotiates lease terms with landlord. 7. Harford County Housing & Community Services reviews lease and inspects dwelling unit. 8. Agency approves or disapproves lease and unit. 9. Upon approval, Harford County and landlord enter into contract on behalf of family.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Historical Trust provides support for a wide range of historic preservation activities, including acquiring and rehabilitating historic properties, documenting and surveying historic sites, developing heritage tourism, and conducting educational programs related to historic preservation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple grant programs available with varying amounts and terms. Programs include Historic Preservation Capital Grants, Historic Preservation Non-Capital Grants, African American Heritage grants, Certified Local Government grants, and Maryland Heritage Areas Program grants. Each program has different eligibility standards and operating regulations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, government agencies, and local jurisdictions involved in historic preservation activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property acquisition and rehabilitation, documentation and survey, heritage tourism development, and educational programs related to historic preservation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide.
requirements_list: Applicant must review specific program guidelines for eligibility requirements as they vary by program
Project must be related to historic preservation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review each program's specific guidelines to ensure project eligibility before applying.

structured_extraction.program_name: NEXT GEN Responders Student Loan Relief
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides student loan relief assistance to volunteer first responders in Harford County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Student loan relief for volunteer first responders. Assistance is provided through a grant-based program that helps eligible volunteer firefighters, emergency medical technicians (EMTs), and other qualified first responders pay down or eliminate student loan debt.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Volunteer first responders in Harford County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Student loan relief and debt reduction for qualified volunteer first responders
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a volunteer first responder (firefighter, EMT, or other qualified first responder)
Must be serving in Harford County
Must have eligible student loan debt
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a fillable application form available on the program webpage. The completed application is then reviewed for eligibility and approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: Community Development may choose to subgrant its HUD entitlement funds to partner organizations who serve Harford County's low- to moderate-income citizens. Funding can support a wide range of projects and programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subgrants of HUD entitlement funds to partner organizations. Funding can support public facility improvements, nonprofit services, tenant-based rental assistance, low-moderate income housing construction, first-time homebuyer support, and critical repairs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Typical application period runs during January/February
structured_extraction.program_audience: Partner organizations and nonprofits serving Harford County's low- to moderate-income residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public facility improvements, nonprofit services, tenant-based rental assistance, low-moderate income housing construction, first-time homebuyer support, and critical repairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County.
requirements_list: Must serve Harford County's low- to moderate-income citizens
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Grants Portal during the typical application period which runs in January and February.

structured_extraction.program_description: Harford County offers a 50 percent tax credit on real and personal property taxes of eligible nonprofit swim clubs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nonprofit swim clubs in Harford County are eligible for a 50 percent tax credit on real and personal property taxes. The credit applies to properties used for swim club operations. Applicants must submit the Nonprofit Swim Club Tax Credit Application along with required documentation demonstrating nonprofit status and swim club operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit swim clubs in Harford County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax relief on real and personal property used for nonprofit swim club operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be organized and operated as a nonprofit organization
Must be operating a swim club
Must own or operate property in Harford County
Property must be used for swim club operations
Must demonstrate nonprofit status with IRS documentation or Maryland incorporation records
Must comply with all applicable Harford County regulations for nonprofit swim clubs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a completed Nonprofit Swim Club Tax Credit Application form to Harford County. The application must include documentation of nonprofit status, proof of swim club operations, property information, and a detailed description of how the property is used for swim club activities. Applications are reviewed by the County for compliance with program requirements and eligibility criteria. Approved applicants receive the 50 percent tax credit applied to their real and personal property tax bills.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for Harford County residents who qualify. Available credits include programs for senior citizens, veterans, owners of historic properties, homeowners, properties near landfills (specifically the Scarboro Landfill), and solar or geothermal energy installations. Taxpayers who reside on their property within 1,000 feet of the Scarboro Landfill may receive a specific tax credit for being adversely impacted by their property's proximity to the landfill.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits are available to qualifying Harford County residents for real property. Specific credit types include senior citizen, veterans, historic properties, homeowner, landfill (including a dedicated credit for residents within 1,000 feet of the Scarboro Landfill), and solar/geothermal energy credits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Harford County residents who qualify for one or more of the available tax credits, including taxpayers who reside on properties within 1,000 feet of the Scarboro Landfill.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits reduce real property tax liability for eligible applicants, providing property tax relief for qualifying residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland. The Scarboro Landfill credit specifically applies to properties within 1,000 feet of the Scarboro Landfill in Harford County.
requirements_list: Reside on property within 1,000 feet of the Scarboro Landfill (for the Scarboro Landfill tax credit)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents should contact the Treasury Department at 410-638-3450 or Jason Boyle at 410-638-3455 to apply for and receive the tax credits for which they qualify.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Citizen and Veteran Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for senior citizens over 65 years old and veterans with service-connected disabilities. Eligible individuals receive a 20% credit on county property taxes for up to 20 years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 20% tax credit on county property taxes for a maximum of 20 years. Eligible seniors must be over 65 years old, own a dwelling with an assessed value of $600,000 or less, and either have lived in the dwelling for at least 35 years or be a retiree or surviving spouse of a retiree of the United States Uniformed Services who has not remarried. Eligible veterans must have a service-connected disability with a combined evaluation of 50% or higher that substantially limits one or more major life activities, own a dwelling with an assessed value of $600,000 or less, and be a veteran or surviving spouse of a veteran of the United States Uniformed Services who has not remarried. The credit is applied annually to the applicant's county property tax bill. Renewal applications are mailed to eligible households each year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are available January 15 and are due by April 1.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Harford County residents who are senior citizens over 65 years old or veterans with service-connected disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit applied to county property taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland. Applicant must own a dwelling in Harford County.
requirements_list: For senior citizens: age 65 or older at time of application, dwelling assessed value of $600,000 or less, either lived in dwelling for at least 35 years OR retiree or surviving spouse of retiree of United States Uniformed Services who has not remarried

For veterans: service-connected disability with combined VA evaluation of 50% or higher that substantially limits one or more major life activities, dwelling assessed value of $600,000 or less, veteran or surviving spouse of veteran of United States Uniformed Services who has not remarried
Applicant must own the dwelling (not rent)
Dwelling must be the primary residence
Must be a resident of Harford County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications become available on January 15 each year and must be submitted by April 1. New applicants must complete the appropriate application form (Senior Credit Application or Disabled Veteran Application) and submit it to Harford County. Renewal applicants receive their applications by mail and may renew by mail or in person. Supporting documentation required includes proof of age, proof of residency, VA rating letter (for veterans), property deed or tax assessment, and proof of length of residency (for senior citizens). Approved applicants receive their tax credit applied to their county property tax bill for up to 20 consecutive years.

structured_extraction.program_description: A down payment and closing cost assistance program designed for first-time homebuyers purchasing a home in Harford County, MD. The program provides deferred loans with zero percent interest to help qualified buyers cover down payment, closing costs, and loan reduction expenses.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A deferred loan with zero percent interest, recorded as a Deed of Trust lien. Maximum assistance is $20,000 for properties within the Southern County Task Force Area, or $10,000 for properties outside that area. Assistance can be used for down payment, closing costs, or loan reduction. Borrower must contribute a minimum of 1% of sales price in cash. No cash to pocket is permitted. The loan is structured as a deferred second mortgage that must be repaid upon sale or refinance of the property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers in Harford County with household income at or below 80% of County Area Median Income seeking to purchase a primary residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance, closing costs, and loan reduction on the purchase of a 1-4 unit single-family dwelling, attached home, condominium, townhome, planned unit development (PUD), or manufactured home in Harford County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in Harford County, MD. Preference is given to properties within the Southern County Task Force Area (SCTFA). Properties located in flood zones are not eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time homebuyer

Household income must not exceed 80% of County Area Median Income (limits vary by household size: 1 person $72,950, 2 persons $83,400, 3 persons $93,700, 4 persons $104,000, 5 persons $112,400, 6 persons $120,800, 7 persons $129,150, 8 persons $137,550)
Purchase price must not exceed 95% of Area Median (existing properties maximum $342,000; new construction maximum $444,000)
Minimum 1% cash contribution from borrower on sales price
First lien mortgage must be LP Accept or DU Approve/Eligible
First lien mortgage must be 30-year, fixed-rate, fully amortizing
Borrower must occupy property as primary residence
Property must be inspected by a Harford County Housing Inspector
Applicant must complete first-time homebuyer counseling
Property must be 1-4 unit single-family, attached, condominium, townhome, PUD, or manufactured home
Properties in flood zones are not eligible
No cash to pocket is permitted
Debt-to-income ratio limits apply (maximum 50% based on first mortgage lender requirements)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact S. Gasparovic at 410-638-3045 before submitting an application to discuss eligibility and program details. Complete the SELP Pre-Qualification Form and submit to smgasparovic@harfordcountymd.gov. A monthly cash flow analysis is required by the housing agency. After pre-qualification approval, applicants work with a participating lender to obtain first mortgage approval. Once first mortgage is approved, final SELP loan approval and closing occurs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Trader Foundation for Maryland Burial Sites
structured_extraction.program_description: The Trader Foundation provides grants to support projects that benefit burial grounds in Maryland. Eligible projects include rescuing endangered burial sites, conserving or restoring gravestones, documenting cemetery sites, protecting burial grounds from damage, cleaning up cemeteries, and planning for restoration work.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $3,000 per project. Trader Foundation funds must be matched by the grantee. Some grants have been used to match funding from other public and private sources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, government agencies, and individuals with projects that benefit specific burial grounds in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rescue of endangered burial sites, gravestone conservation or restoration, documentation, protection of burial sites from desecration, cemetery clean-up, and planning for restoration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must benefit a specific burial ground within the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must benefit a specific burial ground within Maryland
Trader Foundation funds must be matched by the grantee

structured_extraction.program_description: The Harford County Department of Economic Development offers grant funding to support festivals, events, exhibits, and other programming initiatives that foster collaboration between two or more organizations to attract visitors from outside the county's borders and drive overnight hotel stays within the county. This grant seeks to fund experiences that combine cultural attractions, outdoor recreation, arts, heritage, sports, or other unique tourism opportunities with coordinated efforts to enhance partnerships and visitor engagement. The program is funded through the county's hotel tax.
structured_extraction.agency: Harford County Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for tourism-related collaborative festivals, events, exhibits, and programming. Funds are awarded to the lead partner nonprofit organization, which is responsible for distributing funds to partner organizations based on the agreement outlined in the application. Applications are approved based on priority order, with highest priority given to projects involving partnerships between two or more nonprofit tourism-related organizations with majority grant funds used for direct tourism-related marketing costs, followed by projects involving partnerships between nonprofits and for-profits (where grant funds are awarded to and must be utilized by the nonprofit partner, with no direct payments to for-profit partners). The FY27 budget total is at the discretion of the County Executive after review and recommendation by the Economic Development Advisory Board Tourism Activity Review Committee. No matching funds are required. Funds may be used for direct tourism-related festivals, events, exhibits, programming, and marketing costs, including some non-marketing and operational costs such as salaries with certain limits. Funds must be directly attributed to tourism-related activities and cannot be used for daily operating costs, capital improvements, property acquisition, capital building projects, retirement, debt reduction, or equipment such as computers and copiers used for daily office functions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified nonprofits (501(c)3 or 501(c)6 organizations) registered in Harford County that are tourism-related, meaning their activities, events, and programs primarily attract visitors from outside Harford County borders with a targeted approach to result in overnight hotel stays. Municipal governments in Harford County may also be eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct tourism-related festivals, events, exhibits, and programming including marketing costs. Funds may also cover some non-marketing and operational costs like salaries with certain limits. Funds must be directly attributed to tourism-related activities and cannot be used for daily operating costs, capital improvements, property acquisition, capital building projects, retirement, debt reduction, or equipment such as computers and copiers used for daily office functions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland. Organizations must be registered with the State of Maryland at an address in Harford County to be eligible. Programs must attract visitors from outside Harford County borders and promote overnight hotel stays.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)3 or 501(c)6 organization registered in Harford County, or a Harford County municipality
Must be in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessment and Taxation
Must be in good standing with Maryland Office of the Secretary of State, Charitable Organization Division
Must be compliant with all past and current Harford County grant requirements
Must involve partnerships between two or more organizations
Must demonstrate ability to attract visitors from outside Harford County borders
Must promote and encourage overnight hotel stays
Must provide letters of commitment from all partnering organizations
Must demonstrate involvement and consent of all partnerships
Must be able to capture data and objective outcomes for measuring success
Must provide projections of number of hotel rooms generated
Must pursue additional funding sources beyond Harford County Government (sponsorships, grants, donors, fundraising efforts)
Must demonstrate track record of successful past initiatives
Applicant cannot have history of non-compliance with past Harford County grant programs
Must submit all required documentation including financial statements, proof of non-profit status, and letters of support from partners

If applicant has history of non-compliance with any past Harford County grant program, funding may be denied entirely or disbursed in installments; continued non-compliance may result in delayed grant agreement execution or termination of future installments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the online portal at https://portal.ecivis.com/. Applicants must complete and upload required forms: (1) Quarterly Narrative Activity Report (QNAR) summary tab with program/event overview and objectives, and (2) Tourism Grant Budget and Expense Report spreadsheet. Note: applicants do NOT need to complete budget fields within eCivis, but must complete and upload the provided spreadsheet. Additional required documentation includes list of all partners, shareholders, and board members; list of key staff; proof of good standing with Maryland state agencies; 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) documentation; most recently filed Form 990; balance sheets and income statements for fiscal years 2023 and 2024; and letters of support/commitment from all partnering organizations. Applicants must also submit Supplier Package (payment information, bank account information, and W-9). The review committee (comprised of members of the Economic Development Advisory Board Tourism Activity Review Committee) evaluates applications and submits recommendations; final award amounts are at the discretion of the County Executive. Reporting requirements include quarterly budget and activity reporting with receipts, invoices, and proof of payment, reflective of the approved budget in the executed grant agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive reimbursement grant program administered by the Harford County Department of Economic Development that assists Harford County employers in becoming more productive and competitive by providing matching funds to help pay for technical training delivered to existing full-time permanent employees.
structured_extraction.agency: Harford County Department of Economic Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants up to 50% of training costs, not to exceed $10,000 per business per program year and $2,000 per person per program year. For Round 2 (FY26), training must be completed on or after October 18, 2025 but prior to or on May 23, 2026. Matching funds are not required. Funds available: $62,500.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Round 2: Training must be completed on or after October 18, 2025 but prior to or on May 23, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses (under SBA size standards) in Harford County seeking to provide intermediate or advanced technical training to existing full-time permanent employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Intermediate or advanced technical training resulting in industry-wide recognized credentials or certifications that are transferable. Eligible uses include: external training (class costs and employee wages if paid during regular work week), internal training (employee wages for on-the-job training, required books, and software packages for self-training or group training). Prohibited uses include introductory classes, remedial education, safety training, forklift/aerial lift training, internships, travel, tuition reimbursement, and routine entry-level training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Harford County, Maryland. Businesses must have a physical location in Harford County. Employees must work in Harford County and be paid directly by the Harford County business but do not have to reside in Harford County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Harford County employer with a physical location in Harford County

Business must be a small business under SBA size standards (NAICS Code and SBA size standards can be found at https://www.naics.com/ and https://www.sba.gov/sites/sbagov/files/2023-06/Table%20of%20Size%20Standards_Effective%20March%2017%2C%202023%20%282%29.pdf)
No outstanding business indebtedness to Harford County Government
Training must be intermediate or advanced technical training resulting in an industry-wide recognized credential or certification and is transferable
Eligible employees are full-time (average 30 hours or more per week) employees making at least 150% of State Minimum Wage ($22.50 effective 1/1/2024)
Employee must work in Harford County and be paid directly by the applicant company
Completed Workforce Technical Training Grant Application through eCivis Portal
Employee spreadsheet completed in its entirety using form provided
In-house training certified by external trainer or Learning Management system must submit curriculum/training outline with application
Apprenticeships must achieve certification through Maryland school system, Maryland college, or State of MD apprenticeship program
Evidence of direct cost of training or wage reimbursement
Proof of successful completion of approved training
Proof of payment for approved training
Direct and indirect economic impact documentation
Training and backup documentation must be complete at time of submittal
Applicant must maintain all records pertaining to the grant for three years following award
Final approval subject to recommendation of EDAB Workforce Committee and availability of funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download all files from the Files tab and complete in full prior to beginning the application process. Required files include: Supplier Package, Workforce Technical Training Grant Spreadsheet, and Portal Applicant Guide. Submit the completed Supplier Package and Workforce Technical Training Grant Spreadsheet through the eCivis Portal. A webinar is available to explain eligibility and application process. For technical issues with the Portal, contact support@ecivis.com. For programmatic questions, contact ded@harfordcountymd.gov. If additional assistance is needed with Supplier Package, contact Harford County Treasury Department at 410-638-3450.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for eligible Howard County homeowners who are 65 years or older and have lived in their home for at least 25 years, helping them remain in their homes as they age. The program reduces property tax obligations for qualifying seniors and may also apply to property owners who make accessibility modifications to their homes to enable aging in place safely and independently.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit applied against Howard County property taxes for qualifying homeowners aged 65 or older who have lived in their home for at least 25 years. The credit may also apply to property owners who make aging-in-place modifications such as accessibility improvements, reducing their property tax obligations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Howard County homeowners aged 65 or older who have lived in their home for at least 25 years, as well as property owners who make aging-in-place modifications to enable seniors to remain safely and independently in their homes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction of property tax liability to help older residents remain in their homes, including for home modifications that enable aging in place.

requirements_list: Must be 65 years of age or older

Must be a Howard County homeowner

structured_extraction.program_description: Howard County's Agricultural Land Preservation program protects farmland from development by purchasing agricultural land preservation easements (also called development rights) from landowners. By selling an easement, a landowner gives up the right to develop the land while retaining ownership and the ability to continue farming. Participating landowners receive direct payment in exchange for permanently restricting their land from non-agricultural development, helping keep farms in active production and preserving Howard County's agricultural heritage.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Howard County purchases a permanent agricultural land preservation easement (development rights) from eligible farmland owners, providing direct payment to landowners in exchange for permanently restricting the property to agricultural use. The landowner retains ownership and can continue farming the land, while the development rights are permanently extinguished.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmland owners in Howard County who wish to permanently preserve their agricultural land from development while retaining ownership and farming rights, and who wish to receive compensation for restricting those development rights.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Compensation paid to landowners for voluntarily selling an easement that permanently limits land use to agriculture, effectively extinguishing development rights on the property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Howard County, Maryland

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public health response, addressing negative economic impacts of the pandemic, replacing lost public sector revenue, water and sewer infrastructure, broadband infrastructure.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive on-the-job training through registered apprenticeships, earning wages while gaining skills and working toward industry-recognized credentials. structured_extraction.program_description: A residential stormwater management program that reimburses Howard County homeowners for installing green infrastructure projects such as rain gardens, permeable pavers, rainwater harvesting systems, tree canopy expansion, conservation landscaping, dry wells, green roofs, and pavement removal. Participants can reduce their Watershed Protection Fee and receive reimbursement for approved projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners receive reimbursement for 75% of the project cost for approved stormwater management projects. Reimbursement caps vary by project type: Rain Gardens up to $5,000; Rainwater Harvesting up to $750 or $2 per gallon; Conservation Landscaping up to $3,000; Permeable Hardscaping up to $5,000; Dry Wells up to $2,000; Impervious Surface Removal up to $2,000; Green Roofs up to $7,000; Urban Tree Canopy Expansion up to $1,000 per project with maximum $150 per tree. Up to 100% reimbursement may be available for homeowners meeting hardship criteria based on income limits. Additionally, homeowners can reduce their annual Watershed Protection Fee based on the environmental benefits of their installed projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Site Visit Request Form opens April 1st and remains open until all 75 spots are reserved. Project applications must be submitted by November 30th.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Howard County homeowners whose homes were built before 2003. Renters may participate with homeowner permission.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of stormwater best management practices including rain gardens, conservation landscaping, rainwater harvesting systems (rain barrels or cisterns), permeable hardscaping, tree canopy expansion, dry wells, green roofs, and pavement removal/impervious surface removal.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Howard County, Maryland. Homes must have been built before 2003.
requirements_list: Home must have been built before 2003
Applicant must be a homeowner or a renter working with the homeowner
Projects must be installed by a licensed contractor (green roofs and permeable hardscaping require certified installers)
Projects must be approved before installation
Projects cannot be installed before November 2011 program start date
Reimbursements not granted for structural BMPs installed at time of development as those are required by development regulations
Rain gardens must have minimum 75 square feet, maximum sheet flow distance of 25 feet, and comply with Maryland Department of Environment Stormwater Design Manual chapter 5 (2000)

Conservation landscaping must have minimum 150 square feet, 2-3 inch ponding, 6 inch soil de-compaction with 2 inch soil amendment, and comply with Maryland Department of Environment Stormwater Design Manual chapter 5 (2009)
Rainwater harvesting systems must have minimum 250 gallon capacity for single family homes or 100 gallon minimum for townhomes, and must be recertified every 3 years
Permeable hardscaping must have minimum 100 square feet and comply with Maryland Department of Environment Stormwater Design Manual chapter 5 (2009)

Dry wells must demonstrate A or B Hydrologic Soil Groups or 0.52 inch per hour or higher infiltration rate within 50 feet of proposed site, and comply with Maryland Department of Environment Stormwater Design Manual chapter 5 (2009)
Impervious surface removal must restore minimum 100 square feet to natural planted state or permeable hardscaping
Urban tree canopy expansion requires minimum 2 trees with minimum 1 inch caliper for deciduous trees or 3 feet tall for evergreens, species must be native to the region and not invasive
Green roofs must cover minimum 300 square feet or 1/4 of roof area and comply with Maryland Department of Environment Stormwater Design Manual chapter 5 (2009)

All vegetated BMPs must contain 75% native plants (by number, not size, cost or coverage area), no invasive plants, planting density assuming full coverage after 3 years, and minimum 2 inch mulch at initial planting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Site Visit Request Form between April 1st and when all 75 spots are reserved. Attend a site visit conducted between August 1st and September 13th to receive project recommendations. Contact a licensed contractor to develop a project design and estimate. Submit a Project Application by November 30th with a copy of the project proposal provided by your contractor. The Technical Review Committee reviews applications between December 1st and February 21st and notifies applicants of approval. Once approved, install the project with your contractor ensuring compliance with all technical requirements and specifications. Submit a reimbursement request after installation including a signed Credit and Reimbursement Agreement. County staff conduct post-installation inspections and process reimbursements on a bi-weekly basis starting April 15th.

structured_extraction.program_description: Howard County's Youth Engagement Programming (YEP!) Grant funds nonprofit and community organizations to create free, accessible programs that promote youth engagement outside of traditional school hours. The program supports activities and initiatives designed to engage young people in the community, with a focus on social-emotional learning, mental health, wellness, career exploration, and career readiness to help young people prepare for successful transitions into adulthood and the workforce. Grant recipients use funding to offer a wide range of programming including field/sports days, environmental groups, community service activities, gardening programs, seminars, cultural events, mental health discussions, civic engagement workshops, virtual career training, internships, job placement services, and ongoing job coaching and mentorship.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program administered by Howard County that provides financial incentives to owners of commercial and industrial properties along the Route 1 corridor. The program supports visible improvements and transformational development efforts to encourage investment and economic revitalization in the Route 1 corridor area.
structured_extraction.agency: Howard County Department of Planning & Zoning
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a tax credit up to a maximum of $100,000 per property. You may be eligible for up to 125% of approved expenses if costs exceed the initial estimate, not to exceed the $100,000 cap. The full credit is available over five years if the property's taxes are high enough. The credit stays with the property, not the owner, if it is sold. The program has a total annual allocation of $250,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications open each July and are reviewed on a rolling basis until the annual allocation is used.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial and industrial properties along the Route 1 corridor in Howard County, as well as businesses and property owners locating or expanding in the Route 1 corridor area.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible uses include: exterior renovations or cleaning; structural improvements to the facade; replacing false facades; restoring architectural features; adding streetscape items like landscaping, walkways, or lighting; repairing doors and windows; new signs, canopies, or awnings; visible roof repairs; screening for utility or trash areas; enhanced exterior lighting; fencing that does not hide the building; sidewalks; new construction that improves the property's appearance; and necessary interior structural work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located along the Route 1 corridor in Howard County, Maryland.
requirements_list: You must be current on property taxes.
The property must have no outstanding violations for zoning, licensing, permits, or fire codes.
Proposed improvements must comply with the Route 1 Manual and county development standards.
Approval for the tax credit does not replace the need for any required building or sign permits.
The program has a total annual allocation of $250,000.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact the agency to discuss your proposed project. If you decide to apply, submit an application with contractor cost estimates and photos of the property's current condition. County staff review the application to ensure you meet all requirements. An inter-departmental committee then votes to approve or deny the project. You must not begin any work until you receive a Certificate of Eligibility. After completing the work, submit a final application with a maintenance agreement and invoices by April 1st. A county representative will inspect the site to verify the work was completed as approved.
