structured_extraction.program_name: Upper Shore Regional Council (USRC) Business Mentoring Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A free and confidential business mentoring program administered through the Upper Shore Regional Council that connects small business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's Counties with experienced volunteer business mentors. The program provides personalized guidance and coaching on all aspects of starting and running a business, including business planning, financial planning, marketing, funding sources, licensing, permits, and ongoing business operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free and confidential mentoring services provided by volunteer business professionals through the Upper Shore Regional Council. Mentors work one-on-one with business owners and entrepreneurs to develop business plans, provide guidance on financial planning, marketing plan development, funding and financing sources, preparing financial documents, business registration, licensing and permits, marketing and sales, customer relations and retention, ongoing business operations, and long-range planning. Services are available for both startups and established small businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs who own or want to start a business in Cecil, Kent, or Queen Anne's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides technical assistance and guidance rather than direct financial assistance. It covers business planning, financial planning, marketing plan development, funding and financing sources, preparing financial documents, business registration, licensing and permits, marketing and sales, customer relations and retention, ongoing business operations, and long-range planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's Counties in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must own or want to start a small business in Cecil, Kent, or Queen Anne's County
Must complete the Business Mentor Request Form
Must sign the USRC Mentee Agreement outlining the terms and conditions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Business Mentor Request Form by clicking the 'Request a Business Mentor' button. USRC staff will review the request and match you with an appropriate mentor based on your business's needs and goals. You will receive a Mentee Agreement outlining the terms and conditions. Once you sign the agreement and USRC confirms your mentor match, you will be connected with your assigned mentor to begin.

structured_extraction.program_name: Agribusiness Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program administered by the Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) designed to help rural agribusinesses and agricultural/resource-based industry firms in Maryland innovate, diversify, and capitalize on emerging market opportunities. The program provides low-interest financing for working capital and equipment purchases when traditional commercial lenders such as banks or farm credit associations cannot meet their needs. MARBIDCO can supply additional loan proceeds ranging from 20% to 40% of total commercial financing required, working in collaboration with a commercial bank and/or public sector lender.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $15,000 to $100,000. Equipment loans have terms of 3 to 8 years with up to 12 months interest-only possible. Operating/working capital loans have terms of 1 to 2 years with up to six months interest-only possible. Interest rates are 4.75% with a partnering public sector lender or 6.75% without one. Eligible veterans receiving an Honorable or General (Under Honorable Conditions) discharge with at least 50% ownership and management control may receive a Home Town Hero Interest Rate Reduction of 0.25% (25 basis points). Loan origination fee is 1% of the loan amount. Typically requires 10% equity contribution from the applicant. Personal guarantee required from all business owners. MARBIDCO can supply additional loan proceeds ranging from 20% to 40% of total commercial financing required, working in collaboration with a commercial bank and/or public sector lender. MARBIDCO may not provide financing in an amount greater than another participating public lender. MARBIDCO will take a shared (pari-passu) or senior lien position on collateral.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland agribusinesses and agricultural/resource-based industry firms and producers that need financing for working capital and equipment purchases but cannot obtain sufficient commercial financing from traditional lenders such as banks or farm credit associations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital and equipment purchases for agribusiness and agricultural/resource-based industry operations. Eligible project types include value-added food processing, agri-tourism/rural recreation, timber growing or harvesting, primary/secondary wood processing, environmental/water quality projects, biomass/energy production, niche market production, and aquaculture/fishing/seafood operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. The Upper Shore Regional Council offers an additional equity incentive grant for farmers in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties.
requirements_list: Minimum loan amount of $15,000
Maximum loan amount of $100,000
Typically 10% equity contribution required from the applicant
Personal guarantee required from all business owners
Must be unable to obtain sufficient commercial financing from traditional lenders such as banks or farm credit associations
Applications must be originated by the applicant and a partnering lending organization
Must be established agricultural or resource-based industry firm or producer
Applicant must partner with either a public sector lender (who commits to matching financing) or obtain a credit denial letter or commercial lender referral form from a commercial lender

Applicant must submit: business description and history, business plan for the project, resume(s) or working history of principal business owner(s) and/or farm manager(s), applicant and farm operation tax returns for the two preceding years, completed partnering public sector lender form or signed commercial lender denial letter, completed balance sheet, completed income statement for the past 2 years, completed pro forma income statement, completed debt repayment schedule, real estate appraisal if offering real estate as collateral, and supporting documentation for veteran status if applicable

U.S. military veterans with Honorable or General (Under Honorable Conditions) discharge with at least 50% ownership and management control are eligible for Home Town Hero Interest Rate Reduction if they provide supporting letter from commanding officer or federal form DD-214
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application form from MARBIDCO website. Complete the application with all required information and attachments. Applicants may seek assistance from Cooperative Extension agents, county agricultural marketing officials, or other business professionals. Applicants must partner with either a public sector lender (who commits to matching financing) or obtain a credit denial letter or commercial lender referral form from a commercial lender. Submit the completed application package to MARBIDCO Agribusiness Loan Program at 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or email info@marbidco.org. Applications are processed on a rolling basis as they are received. Required attachments include business description and history, business plan, resume(s), tax returns for two preceding years, partnering public sector lender form or commercial lender referral form/denial letter, balance sheet, income statements (past 2 years and pro forma), debt repayment schedule, real estate appraisal if applicable, and veteran documentation if eligible.

structured_extraction.program_name: Forestry Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that helps forest products-related businesses in Maryland obtain financing for working capital and equipment purchases to support innovation, take advantage of emerging market opportunities, or make operations more sustainable. The program aims to complement financial services offered by private commercial lenders by helping make rural business financing both available and affordable.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $15,000 to $150,000. Equipment loans have terms of 3 to 6 years; operating loans have terms of 1 to 2 years. Interest rates are fixed at a minimum of 6.25% and established on a case-by-case basis based on credit risk. A 1% loan origination fee applies. An equity contribution of typically 5-10% of the project's total cost is required. Commercial lender participation is mandatory. MARBIDCO utilizes slightly more liberal underwriting guidelines than normal, including a minimum cash flow coverage ratio of 1.0/1.0 and partially relaxed collateral security requirements where appropriate. The maximum outstanding aggregate portfolio balance under this program cannot exceed $400,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are processed as they are received
structured_extraction.program_audience: Forest products-related businesses in Maryland seeking financing for equipment purchases and working capital, including value-added secondary wood processing operations, timber growing or harvesting businesses, environmental/water quality projects, and biomass/energy product businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital and equipment purchases for forest products businesses. Project types include value-added secondary wood processing, timber growing or harvesting, environmental/water quality improvements, and biomass/energy products.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide, including Eastern Shore and Western Shore forest products businesses. All Maryland counties are eligible.
requirements_list: Commercial lender must participate by providing a letter of referral
5-10% equity contribution of project's total cost required
Minimum loan amount of $15,000
Maximum loan amount of $150,000
Current outstanding aggregate portfolio balance cannot exceed $400,000
Personal guarantee required from all business entity owners
Applicant must contact MARBIDCO office for guidance before completing application due to the $400,000 portfolio limit
Loan requests to be funded in part by USDA-RD resources must be approved by USDA-RD
Business must be established in Maryland
Minimum cash flow coverage ratio of 1.0/1.0 required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be originated by the applicant and are processed as they are received. Cooperative Extension agents, Maryland Forest Service, county agricultural marketing officials, and other business professionals may assist in application development. Applicants must contact the MARBIDCO office for guidance prior to completing an application due to the $400,000 portfolio limitation. Submit completed application with all required attachments to: MARBIDCO Loan Programs, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or email to bcadden@marbidco.org. Required attachments include: company description and history, business plan, resumes of owners/managers, two years of tax returns, completed balance sheet, completed debt repayment schedule, real estate appraisal if applicable, and supporting documentation for veteran status if applicable. MARBIDCO will make and service all loans.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program offering U.S. military service members and veterans an interest rate reduction of 0.25% (25 basis points) on specific MARBIDCO loan programs for agribusiness and farming operations.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An interest rate reduction of 0.25% or 25 basis points applied to qualifying MARBIDCO loan programs including the Maryland Resource-Based Industry Financing Fund, Maryland Vineyard/Hopyard/Orchard Planting Loan Fund, Agribusiness Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund, Forestry Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund, and Maryland Large Animal Veterinarian Assistance Loan Program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: U.S. military service members currently serving or veterans who have received an Honorable or General (Under Honorable Conditions) characterization of service, with at least 50% veteran ownership and 50% veteran management control of the agribusiness or farming operation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: For agribusiness and farming operations, including equipment, working capital, vineyard/hopyard/orchard planting, and large animal veterinary services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; programs delivered in cooperation with commercial banks, Farm Credit Associations, USDA Farm Service Agency, and other federal, state, and local agencies.
requirements_list: Currently serving in any branch of the United States military with a letter of support from commanding officer or designated representative, OR has served and received an Honorable or General (Under Honorable Conditions) characterization of service with proof via Department of Defense Form DD-214
Minimum 50% veteran ownership of the agribusiness or farming operation
Minimum 50% veteran management control of the agribusiness or farming operation
Practical farm and/or business experience required (may be supplemented by academic or hands-on training)
Business plan required
Borrower financial information required
Applicant must notify MARBIDCO at time of loan application about intent to seek Hometown Hero interest rate reduction eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact MARBIDCO to determine which programs are right for your business. Submit a loan application for one of the qualifying MARBIDCO loan programs along with proof of military service (DD-214 or letter from commanding officer), business plan, and financial information. Notify MARBIDCO of intent to seek Hometown Hero rate reduction.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Government Agriculture & Resource-Based Industry Project Cost Share Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that matches rural business development investments made by local governments and rural regional development councils to support agricultural, forestry, seafood, and resource-based businesses in Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants provided by MARBIDCO to local governments and regional councils for cost-share projects. Maximum individual grant amounts include $10,000 as the standard maximum, $5,000 for Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) matching grants, and $3,000 for deer fences, farm operation solar systems, or generators that provide commercial business energy. Total grants awarded to any single government jurisdiction in a fiscal year are capped at $25,000, with a $15,000 lifetime maximum for individual farmers or business owners (designees). The MARBIDCO grant amount cannot exceed the local government's investment in the project.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling - applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local government economic development offices and rural regional development councils seeking to support agricultural and resource-based businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that assist Maryland's farming, forestry, or seafood industries, including agritourism activities. Eligible uses include support for businesses that produce foodstuffs or other goods grown in soil or water, packaging, value-added processing, marketing of such products, and water and air quality improvement projects that contribute to business sustainability. Eligible project types include: Value-Added Food Processing, Young/Beginning Farmer Support, Agri-Tourism/Rural Recreation, Timber Growing or Harvesting, Primary/Secondary Wood Processing, Environmental/Water Quality, Biomass/Energy Production, Niche Market Production, and Aquaculture/Fishing/Seafood.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program partners include Anne Arundel, Cecil, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Queen Anne's, Salisbury-Wicomico Economic Development Inc., Town of Mount Airy, and Worcester counties.
requirements_list: Application must be submitted by a local or regional economic development office
Governmental entity's funds must be own-source funding, not pass-through
Project must fit within MARBIDCO's statutorily established economic development profile
Project must assist Maryland's farming, forestry, or seafood industries in some fashion
If a project directly benefits an individual farmer or rural business owner, the farmer or business owner must make a financial contribution to the project
Projects not directly involving individual business owners may not require private equity contributions
MARBIDCO grant amount cannot exceed the local government's investment in the project
Applicant must document local government's cash contribution as well as contributions of other partners and supporters
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed applications to MARBIDCO Programs, Attention Daniela Merkle, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or electronically to dmerkle@marbidco.org. Applications must include: detailed explanatory letter signed by the economic development director providing project overview, roles of partners, expected outcomes, and economic/community development benefits; documentation of all sources and uses of funds; project budget with equipment and facility costs; grant recipient information if different from requesting local government; and estimated employment data. For questions, call 410-267-6807.

structured_extraction.program_name: MARBIDCO Rural Business Energy Efficiency Improvement Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A low-interest loan program administered by the Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) that helps farmers, agricultural businesses, and rural business owners reduce energy consumption and increase profitability. The program finances equipment and technology improvements recommended by qualified third-party energy auditors, covering agricultural operations, food and fiber processing, and other rural businesses statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest microloans for energy efficiency improvements with a fixed interest rate of 4.50%. Loan amounts range from $5,000 to $30,000. A grant incentive of 10 percent of the loan amount (up to $1,000) is provided to borrowers in good standing upon loan completion. Loans must be fully amortized with terms between two and seven years, not exceeding the anticipated energy savings payback period, with at least a 1.0-to-1.0 annual energy savings payback ratio. A $75 loan origination fee is required at closing. Loan advances may not exceed the cost of making the improvements minus any other grant funding received for the project.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline stated; applications processed in order received on a funds-available basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers, agricultural producers, dairy and poultry operations, and agricultural-based industry business owners in food and fiber processing, as well as other rural businesses in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment or technology related to lowering business-related energy consumption, based on recommendations from a qualified third-party energy audit or agricultural energy management plan report
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, with focus on rural areas and agricultural operations
requirements_list: Credit score of at least 650
No bankruptcy filed within the last seven years
Energy audit, agricultural energy management plan report, or energy savings confirmation letter from a qualified third-party energy auditor (required attachment)
Simple commercial lender referral (required attachment)
Personal guarantee from all principal owners of the business (loans are unsecured)
Debt service coverage ratio of at least 1.0-to-1.0 on annual energy savings payback
Loan terms set between two and seven years based on anticipated energy savings payback period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application form to MARBIDCO Loan Programs along with required attachments: (1) copy of energy audit report or agricultural energy management plan report or energy savings confirmation letter from a qualified third-party energy auditor, and (2) resume and description of owners and farm operation. All applications must be originated by the applicant. Applications are processed in the order received on a funds-available basis. Send to: MARBIDCO Loan Programs, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or email to info@marbidco.org.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) Agribusiness Financing Loans and Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: MARBIDCO helps Maryland's typically small and family-owned farm, forestry, and seafood businesses to prosper through the provision of more than 20 targeted low and moderate-cost loan and grant incentive programs. These programs help agricultural, forestry, and seafood businesses secure affordable capital and credit for equipment, commercial facilities, and real estate purchases. The organization assists qualifying businesses including farmers, watermen, aquaculture operators, seafood processors, wood processors, vineyard operators, and veterinarians. Programs include beginning farmer farmland access financing, specialty incentive grants for local farm food aggregation, and partnerships with commercial lenders to maximize rural lending opportunities. MARBIDCO's mission is to retain existing resource-based industry production and commerce, promote rural entrepreneurship, and nurture emerging or expanding agricultural enterprises statewide, including businesses in Caroline County and all other Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MARBIDCO provides more than 20 targeted low and moderate-cost agricultural loans and agribusiness loan programs for farmers, watermen, aquaculture operators, seafood processors, wood processors, vineyard operators, and veterinarians. The organization offers beginning farmer farmland access financing to help preserve productive agricultural land, targeted specialty incentive grants for local farm food aggregation and certain agribusinesses, and partnership arrangements with commercial lenders to help maximize rural lending opportunities. Financial and technical services are available for farm, forestry, and seafood businesses including loans, financing assistance, and business support. Assistance is used for equipment, commercial facilities, and real estate purchases. Specific terms, amounts, and conditions are available through MARBIDCO's website.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers, watermen, aquaculture operators, seafood processors, wood processors, vineyard operators, veterinarians, beginning farmers, young farmers, small farm operators, and resource-based business owners in Maryland's commercial farming, forestry, and seafood industries. Includes small and family-owned farm, forestry, and seafood businesses statewide.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment, commercial facilities, real estate purchases, farmland acquisition, agricultural business development, working capital for agricultural and resource-based enterprises, and general agricultural operations and enterprise development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland, including all counties such as Caroline County.
requirements_list: Must be a qualifying agricultural, forestry, or seafood business
Businesses must demonstrate need for affordable capital and credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: MARBIDCO's experienced staff can consult with individuals and businesses to determine which programs are the best fit. Applicants should contact MARBIDCO to discuss their specific financing needs and explore available loan and grant programs. Applicants may also visit the MARBIDCO website for detailed application procedures and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Large Animal Veterinarian Assistance Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program designed to help attract and retain licensed large animal veterinarians in Maryland by providing financing to purchase trucks and specialized equipment needed for large animal veterinary care services. The program addresses the challenge of high student loan debt burdens that inhibit veterinarians' ability to secure commercial financing for necessary equipment. The program supports veterinarians establishing new or expanding existing large animal practices serving cattle, horses, hogs, sheep, goats, and similar animals.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans between $25,000 and $100,000 at a 4.50% interest rate. Loan terms vary based on loan amount: 3.5 years for $25,000-$39,999; 4 years for $40,000-$59,999; 4.5 years for $60,000-$79,999; and 5 years for $80,000-$100,000. A loan origination fee of 0.25% applies. A maximum six-month interest-only repayment option is available for eligible applicants requesting it, particularly those setting up new practices or with cash flow needs. Borrowers must provide a minimum 10% of project costs. Collateral security may not exceed 95% of fair market value. A minimum credit score of 620 is required. MARBIDCO must be a first lien-holder on all collateral except real estate.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications processed in the order received; rolling admission
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed large animal veterinarians in Maryland starting new or expanding existing large animal veterinary practices, particularly those carrying significant student loan debt.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of trucks and specialized equipment necessary for providing large animal veterinary care services, including business establishment and equipment needs for large animal veterinary practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must reside in Maryland on the date the loan is settled and agree to have a majority of their large animal practice in Maryland during the loan term.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers loans to eligible applicants to help start up or expand small- and medium-sized USDA-inspected slaughter facilities in Maryland to increase the processing of meat, poultry, and blue catfish. The program complements USDA's Meat and Poultry Intermediary Lending Program and can offer standalone financing or work in conjunction with other commercial lenders.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loan amounts range from $250,000 to $2,500,000 with a fixed interest rate of 4.00% and a 0.25% origination fee (up to $5,000 maximum). Loan proceeds can be used to purchase real estate, construct new or expand existing livestock processing facilities, and purchase processing equipment. Loan terms correspond to the useful life of financed assets, with an initial interest-only period up to 12 months. MARBIDCO will match the equity contribution on a dollar-for-dollar basis up to 10% of project costs, with a maximum equity grant award of $250,000. Borrowers must provide at least 7.5% of project cost as equity contribution. Applicants constructing new facilities must demonstrate minimum working capital of at least 10% of project cost. Personal guarantees are required unless the applicant provides 20% equity contribution including MARBIDCO's equity grant. Veterans with Honorable or General discharge and at least 50% ownership and management control may receive a Home Town Heroes Interest Rate Reduction of 0.25% (25 basis points). Priority is given to the construction of new facilities, especially in underserved parts of Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small- and medium-sized USDA-inspected slaughter facility operators in Maryland seeking to start up or expand meat, poultry, and blue catfish processing operations. Large meat and poultry processing companies are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase real estate, construct new or expand existing livestock processing facilities, and purchase livestock processing equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Priority given to construction of new facilities in underserved parts of Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Oyster Shucking House Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program established to help finance the cost of eligible seafood processing projects, including historic oyster shucking facilities, and to facilitate an increase in the amount of oyster shells retained in the State and returned to the Chesapeake Bay. The program was created through legislation enacted in 2022 (Senate Bill 830) and provides loans up to $250,000 to finance the eligible costs of qualifying oyster processing business projects.

Applicants must provide at least 3% equity contribution. MARBIDCO will match the equity contribution dollar-for-dollar, up to 5% of project cost (capped at $12,500) in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties. Veterans with at least 50% ownership and management control who have received an Honorable or General (Under Honorable Conditions) discharge, or active duty military personnel, may receive a Home Town Hero Interest Rate Reduction of 0.25% (25 basis points).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed Maryland Seafood Dealers with at least three years of experience, or Tidal Fisheries License (TFL) holders with at least five years of experience who agree to obtain a Seafood Dealer License if approved.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loan proceeds can be used to renovate or construct a new oyster processing facility, expand an existing facility, or purchase oyster processing equipment. Additionally, under debt forgiveness provisions, if oyster shell is returned to Maryland Department of Natural Resources, MARBIDCO will forgive a portion of the debt based on the market value of each bushel of oyster shell, or if oyster shell is directly returned to public fishery oyster bars, $25 for each bushel of spat-on-shell that is planted.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Remote Setting Shellfish Aquaculture Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides affordable financing to commercial watermen who want to start or expand shellfish remote-setting aquaculture operations (nursery operations) for raising oysters or clams in Maryland. Remote setting is a process for growers to produce cost-effective seed oysters for aquaculture by purchasing larvae from a hatchery and placing it in a tank containing cultch for the larvae to set on.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans from $5,000 to $30,000 with a 5.25% MARBIDCO interest rate and no application fee. Borrowers must contribute at least 10% equity as cash. During the first year, only interest-only payments are required. Starting in year two, regular amortizing payments are due with the final year of repayments forgiven for borrowers in good standing, effectively resulting in a grant of 22% to 27% of the principal amount. Loan terms are 5 years for loans of $5,000 to $15,000 and 6 years for loans of $15,001 to $30,000. All borrowers must make quarterly loan repayments. Borrowers not in good standing will not receive the partial loan forgiveness and will be obligated to repay the entire amount of the original loan.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment and supplies for commercial remote-setting aquaculture projects, including seed (larvae), shell (substrate), tanks, pumps, blowers, valves, and tank heaters for raising oysters or clams.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland locations where applicable permits are held.

Projects with insufficient production and business plans and future projections will not be approved, but may be revised and resubmitted in the future. structured_extraction.program_description: MARBIDCO provides low-interest, below-market-rate loans to farmers, young and beginning farmers, and established agricultural and resource-based industry enterprises statewide. The program offers gap financing to help reduce borrower costs and improve debt service coverage ratios, available through direct loan or participation loan options in partnership with commercial banks and Farm Credit lenders. MARBIDCO takes a junior collateral lien position behind the commercial lender and aims to graduate borrowers to conventional commercial financing over time. Eligible uses include purchasing land and capital equipment for production and processing activities, diversifying or expanding agricultural operations, purchasing a first farm, and environmental or water-quality enhancement projects. The program also supports resource-based industries such as poultry operations and other agricultural businesses.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MARBIDCO provides below-market-rate, low-interest gap financing loans available through direct loan or participation loan options (with commercial bank, Farm Credit lender, or public instrumentality involvement). Under the Participation Loan program, loans are originated and serviced by a Lead Lender using a "First Lien / Last Out" co-lending structure where the Lead Lender sells up to 49% interest in a first priority promissory note to MARBIDCO. MARBIDCO provides between 30-49% of total commercial financing needed (minimum 30%, maximum 49%), with the Lead Lender providing a greater percentage. MARBIDCO charges a fixed below-market interest rate of 4.25% on funds advanced to the bank; Lead Lenders may add up to 75 basis points (0.75%) as a servicing fee. Maximum loan amounts: $350,000 for equipment and fixed assets (including building construction and working capital); $700,000 for real estate purchase or food processing and renewable energy projects; $1,000,000 for large commercial food or fiber processing projects. MARBIDCO requires a minimum debt service coverage ratio of 1.1 to 1 for most loans (1.2 to 1 for poultry loans). Amortizations can be up to 30 years, with MARBIDCO receiving payment within 15 years via balloon payment. Loan repayments can be monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, or annual; certain loans may be offered on an interest-only basis for up to two years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers, young and beginning farmers, established agricultural and resource-based industry business owners, and entrepreneurs seeking financing to establish, diversify, or expand operations, including poultry production and other agricultural sectors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of land and capital equipment for production and processing; diversification or expansion of agricultural operations; purchase of first farm for young and beginning farmers; environmental or water-quality enhancement projects; business establishment and expansion in resource-based industries; food/feed/fiber production or processing projects; on-farm value-added processing activities; renewable energy projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Must work with a commercial lender or Farm Credit lender to apply
Participation from a commercial bank, Farm Credit lender, or public instrumentality is required
Commercial lender or public instrumentality must have at least an equal financial commitment (minimum 51%)
MARBIDCO provides between 30-49% of total commercial financing needed for a project
Borrower credit score must be 620 or higher; recent bankruptcy history disqualifies applicants
Satisfactory AgScore of 160 or above preferred (may be lower in certain circumstances)
All loans must involve senior priority collateral security instrument with loan-to-value ratios not exceeding 100% FMV
First lien security must be on real estate offered as collateral; MARBIDCO does not accept crops, livestock, chattel, or inventory as collateral
Minimum debt service coverage ratio of 1.1 to 1 for standard MRBIFF loans; 1.2 to 1 for poultry loans
Owner equity of 10% or more ideal, but as little as 0% is possible
Poultry farm purchases involving "pole houses" are no longer permitted and are ineligible
Must be an agricultural or resource-based industry firm or individual
For poultry loans: combined loan-to-value ratio cannot exceed 92%
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must work in partnership with commercial banks or Farm Credit lenders. The Lead Lender completes the MARBIDCO participation loan application and submits it via email to participation@marbidco.org. A complete application includes: the completed and signed application form, lender's loan/credit underwriting (loan officer narrative, balance sheet dated within 90 days, income statements for past two years, pro forma income statements for at least one year), business plan for the next three years if available, tax returns for both applicant and farm operation for the past two years, and most recent appraisal of real estate used as collateral. MARBIDCO staff will respond within 2 business days of submission. Submit applications a minimum of 30 days ahead of anticipated closing date (45-60 days recommended to avoid delays). MARBIDCO targets issuing an approval notice within 21 days of complete application submission. MARBIDCO's approval process includes credit underwriting analysis by MARBIDCO staff followed by review and approval by a Loan Review Committee (experienced commercial and agricultural lenders plus agribusiness development experts). Loans exceeding $300,000 must also be approved by the MARBIDCO Board of Directors. Closing typically occurs within 7-10 days of approval notice if pre-closing checklist items are received timely. Loan closing documents and checklist items are reviewed by the Office of the Attorney General in conjunction with MARBIDCO's lending team; allow a minimum of 5 calendar days for review and revision. The Participation loan must normally close within 60 calendar days after approval unless extended in writing by MARBIDCO. In exceptional circumstances with favorable factors, closing could occur in as little as 3 weeks. Contact MARBIDCO's Financial Programs Office early with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: MARBIDCO provides affordable, subsidized loans to help commercial watermen and entrepreneurs start or expand shellfish aquaculture operations. The program is a partnership between MARBIDCO and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, with training and business planning support from the University of Maryland. It helps new and existing shellfish aquaculture businesses obtain the financing they need for substrate, seed, and capital equipment. Eligible applicants must hold or have applied for a State submerged land or water column aquaculture lease and plan to raise oysters or clams in the waters of the Chesapeake or Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $5,000 to $100,000 with a maximum interest rate of 5.25% (as low as 3.00% during the interest-only period). No loan application fee or loan origination fee. Repayment terms vary by purchase type: substrate and seed up to 5 years (1-3 years interest-only and 2 years principal & interest), capital equipment up to 7 years (1-3 years interest-only and 4 years principal & interest), or blended purchases up to 6 years (1-3 years interest-only and 3 years principal & interest). First-time borrowers receive 40% principal forgiveness (up to $100,000 maximum). Existing borrowers in good standing receive 25% principal forgiveness on loans between $100,001 and $300,000. Requires minimum 10% equity contribution (cash or ownership of commercial workboat). Quarterly loan repayments required. These loans do not require traditional collateral security, only personal guarantees of all borrowers. Priority is given to applicants who have received less than $100,000 in Shellfish Aquaculture funding previously from MARBIDCO. Grant funds from NRCS or Chesapeake Bay Watershed Initiative programs can be assigned to MARBIDCO to pay down interest and principal.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open and continuous based on funding availability. Applications processed in the order received.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used to purchase substrate (such as shell), seed or larvae, or capital equipment with a 15-year life expectancy for on-bottom and water column (cages or floats) aquaculture production projects. Motor vehicles including boats and trucks are not eligible expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Upper Shore counties (Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's) have access to an additional equity incentive program. Projects must be located in the waters of the Chesapeake or Coastal Bays of Maryland.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the application form (available at https://www.marbidco.org/s/App_Shellfish_5324.pdf) with all required attachments listed in the submission checklist. Applications are processed in the order received, so submit as soon as completed. Mail the original signed application and all required attachments to MARBIDCO Loan Programs Office, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, Attn: Brittany Rawlings, or email to brawlings@marbidco.org. A Shellfish Aquaculture Financing Committee consisting of representatives from DNR, University of Maryland Extension, and MARBIDCO will evaluate the credit worthiness of the prospective borrower(s) and the viability of the proposed project production and business plan including financial projections. Projects with insufficient production and business plans will not be approved but may be revised and resubmitted. For additional resources and information about shellfish aquaculture, visit http://dnr.maryland.gov/fisheries/Pages/aquaculture/shellfish.aspx or contact DNR at aquaculture.dnr@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Urban Agriculture Commercial Lending Incentive Grant (MUACLIG)

The program supports commercial food or fiber growing operations located in urban areas as defined by the U.S. Census Bureau or any incorporated municipality recognized by the State of Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: An affordable loan program that helps Maryland landowners establish or expand vineyards, orchards, and hopyards. MARBIDCO partners with private commercial lenders to provide low-cost financing for eligible planting and preparation expenses. The program aims to increase the acreage of viable commercial vineyards and tree fruit orchards in Maryland and to complement the financial services offered by private commercial lenders by helping to make rural enterprise financing both available and affordable.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans ranging from $15,000 to $100,000. Option 1: 5.00% interest for the first three years, then 6.25% for the remainder. Option 2: Fixed 6.25% rate with option to pay interest-only for the first three years, then principal and interest thereafter. Loan origination fee is 1% of the loan amount. Maximum loan term is 10 years. Typically requires 10% equity contribution from the borrower (though grant funds can count toward equity). All loans must be fully collateralized. Borrowers can choose repayment terms that fit their needs. Personal guarantee required. Eligible applicants who are U.S. military veterans with an Honorable or General (Under Honorable Conditions) discharge and at least 50% ownership and management control of the operation may receive a Home Town Hero interest rate reduction of 0.25% (25 basis points).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications reviewed as received; rolling admissions
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland landowners wanting to establish or expand vineyards, orchards, or hopyards
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land preparation for plant installation, purchase of vines or trees, and equipment and supplies for vineyard, orchard, or hopyard establishment. Tractors, pick-up trucks, and wine-making equipment are not eligible under this program. Other MARBIDCO programs such as the MRBIFF and the Agribusiness Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund may provide financing for these items.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Upper Shore Regional Council (Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's counties) offers an additional equity incentive grant matching program in partnership with MARBIDCO.
requirements_list: Must be a landowner in Maryland
Commercial lender must participate by providing a letter of referral
Typically 10% equity contribution of project total cost (grant funds may qualify)
All loans must be fully collateralized
Personal guarantee required; all loans made to a business entity must be personally guaranteed by the owners of the business

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicant submits completed application with all required attachments to MARBIDCO Loan Programs at 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403, or via email to info@marbidco.org. A commercial lender must provide a letter of referral as part of the application. Applications are reviewed as they are received. A panel of agricultural lenders at MARBIDCO reviews financial viability, while members of the wine/grape industry's viticulture committee or other appropriate university experts review operational, viticultural, and/or enological viability. Processing typically takes 3-4 weeks. Incomplete applications will delay the review process. MARBIDCO makes and services all loans.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides low-interest, unsecured loans to help commercial watermen purchase necessary equipment or commercial fishing boats, and to help seafood processing businesses purchase processing equipment. Commercial watermen can purchase physical equipment such as boats, motors, and harvesting tools, while seafood processors are limited to acquiring only seafood processing machinery. The program also offers partial loan forgiveness for borrowers who make all payments on time. Beginning July 1, 2025, the program expanded eligibility to include Beginner Watermen and seafood processors in addition to Generational Watermen.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unsecured microloans with a fixed interest rate of 3.00%. Loan amounts range from $7,000 to $20,000 for equipment purchases, up to $30,000 for commercial workboat purchases, and up to $40,000 for combined workboat and equipment purchases (with equipment limited to $20,000). Lifetime aggregate limit of all microloans is $40,000. Repayment includes at least a 6-month interest-only period followed by quarterly amortizing payments: 4 years (16 quarters) for loans $20,000 or less; 4 or 5 years (16 or 20 quarters) for loans $20,001 to $35,000; and 5 or 6 years (20 or 24 quarters) for loans $35,001 to $40,000. Borrowers who make all payments on time receive partial loan forgiveness: the final 4 quarters (for loans up to $20,000), final 5 quarters (for loans $20,001 to $35,000), or final 6 quarters (for loans $35,001 to $40,000) of the amortization period will be forgiven. For example, a $7,000 loan forgives approximately $1,871; a $20,000 loan forgives approximately $5,324; a $35,001 loan forgives approximately $9,455; and a $40,000 loan forgives approximately $10,964. Equipment must have a useful lifespan of at least 7 years. Loan funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis or paid directly to the vendor. Equipment cannot be purchased prior to application submission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed commercial watermen (Generational or Beginner) who are Maryland residents and derive or plan to derive substantial income from commercial seafood harvesting, and seafood processing businesses licensed by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. Beginning July 1, 2025, Beginner Watermen and seafood processors became eligible in addition to Generational Watermen.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commercial watermen may purchase tangible equipment including boats, motors, and harvesting gear. Seafood processors may purchase only seafood processing equipment. Equipment purchased must have a useful lifespan of at least 7 years. Equipment cannot be purchased prior to loan application submission.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be residents of the State of Maryland. The program serves all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Generational Waterman, Beginner Waterman, or Seafood Processor

Generational Waterman: Must be a resident of Maryland and hold a TFL (Tidal Fish License) issued by the Department of Natural Resources or a commercial license to catch finfish, crabs, clams, and oysters issued by the Potomac River Fisheries Commission; must derive 50% or more of annual income from commercial seafood harvesting; must submit two most recent federal income tax returns

Beginner Waterman: Must be a resident of Maryland and at least 18 years old; must hold a TFL or commercial license from Potomac River Fisheries Commission; must demonstrate at least two years but not more than 10 years of commercial seafood harvesting experience through a written narrative and reference letter; must submit two most recently available tax returns if available

Seafood Processing Business: Must hold a TFL or commercial license from the Potomac River Fisheries Commission; must hold a Seafood Dealer License issued by the Department of Natural Resources for at least two years; must demonstrate commercial seafood processing income through two most recent federal income tax returns
Minimum credit score of 620
May not have more than one active microloan at a time
Equipment must have a useful lifespan of at least 7 years
No collateral security required
Equipment cannot be purchased prior to loan application submission
Income from spouse filing jointly will be excluded from income calculations where feasible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application with all requested information and required attachments to MARBIDCO. Required attachments include: (1) completed and signed Application Form; (2) copy of Tidal Fisheries License or Potomac River Fisheries Commission license; (3) two preceding years of complete federal income tax returns including all schedules; and (4) for Generational Watermen: completed Income Verification Form (Attachment A); for Beginner Watermen: brief narrative describing commercial fishing experience, letter of reference attesting to commercial waterman experience with writer's name/address/phone/signature, completed Experience Verification Form (Attachment B), and tax returns if available; for Seafood Processors: copy of Seafood Dealer License and federal income tax returns. Applications are processed in the order they are received. Submit electronically to brawlings@marbidco.org or mail to MARBIDCO c/o Brittany Rawlings, 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403. Contact MARBIDCO at 410-267-6807 for questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program provided emergency funding to businesses in agriculture and food production sectors affected by the COVID-19 pandemic to help them adjust and acquire needed equipment.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants were provided to help businesses acquire equipment needed to adjust operations during the pandemic.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural and food production businesses impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases to adjust operations during the pandemic.

structured_extraction.program_name: Southern Maryland Livestock Processing Revolving Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: This collaborative program provides loan and grant funding to establish and improve local livestock processing facilities in Southern Maryland, enhancing access to USDA-inspected meat processing for regional livestock producers.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding packages including both loan and grant funds are provided to support the establishment and improvement of livestock processing facilities. Specific amounts are not detailed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Livestock processors and meat processing facilities in Southern Maryland that provide USDA-inspected processing services for regional livestock producers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Facility improvements and expansion of livestock processing capabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program focuses on Southern Maryland, specifically serving livestock producers in the region.

structured_extraction.program_name: Southern Maryland Revolving Loan Fund for Agriculture
structured_extraction.program_description: A subsidized low-cost loan program designed to help Southern Maryland farmers with agricultural projects that traditional commercial lenders may not finance. The program offers loans at favorable rates with the added incentive of partial loan forgiveness for borrowers in good standing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $10,000 to $20,000 at a 4.50% interest rate with loan terms of one to four years following an initial interest-only period. No loan origination fees are charged. Borrowers in good standing receive approximately 20-25% loan forgiveness at the end of the loan term by foregoing final loan payments. The interest-only period varies by project type: Beef (18 months), Pigs (9 months), Goats/Lambs (12 months), Poultry/Rabbits (3 months), Turkeys (6 months), and Shellfish Aquaculture (18 months). For Small Fruits and Hops, GAP/Food Safety Upgrades, Value-Added Farm Products, and Equine Industry projects, up to 12 months of interest-only payments may be authorized. All loan repayments are made quarterly. Loan origination fees are paid by SMADC on the borrower's behalf.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and agricultural businesses in Southern Maryland counties seeking financing for agricultural expansion and development projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used for: purchase of livestock and shellfish aquaculture foundation; production of small fruits and hops; upgrades for safe growing, harvesting, packing, and holding of produce in compliance with Good Agricultural Practices and the Food Safety Modernization Act; value-added processing equipment and services for on-farm production of products such as jams, jellies, acidified foods, pickles, ferments, artisanal grains, processed meats and poultry, forestry products, and fiber; foundation development and expansion of the regional equine farm industry including fencing, school horses/ponies, barns, stalls, and arena equipment; and related professional industry support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is limited to five Southern Maryland counties: Anne Arel, Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, and St. Mary's.
requirements_list: Must be a farmer or agricultural business in one of the five eligible Southern Maryland counties
Minimum credit score of 620
Personal guarantee required if farm business entity is the borrower
Business entity owners must provide personal guarantees
All owners of business entities (e.g., LLC) must provide personal guarantees
Application must be originated by the applicant, though agricultural service professionals may assist in development

Submit completed application including business description, farm business plan, resumes of principal owners/managers, personal and farm tax returns for two preceding years, completed balance sheet, income statement for past year, pro forma income statement for current year to year 3, debt repayment schedule, and organizational documents if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants download the application form and submit completed applications to MARBIDCO at 1410 Forest Drive, Suite 21, Annapolis, MD 21403 or email to info@marbidco.org. Agricultural service professionals may assist in developing applications. Applications are processed as they are received on a rolling basis. During the interest-only period, borrowers must submit disbursement request forms to MARBIDCO for eligible expense item reimbursement or direct vendor payment before the end of the interest-only period. Once the interest-only period ends, no additional funds can be disbursed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Upper Shore Regional Council Farm Loan Equity Incentive Matching Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership program between the Upper Shore Regional Council and MARBIDCO offering a lending incentive grant with a 5% equity contribution towards eligible MARBIDCO loans for farmers in the Upper Shore region. The program is designed to help farmers meet down-payment and equity requirements for MARBIDCO financing programs, improving their loan applications and supporting farm development and operations in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's Counties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program makes a 5% equity contribution towards a project funded by a MARBIDCO loan, helping farmers meet equity and down-payment requirements. For most MARBIDCO funds except MRBIFF, the maximum grant amount is the lesser of 5% of the hard costs of the project or $5,000. For MRBIFF (Maryland Resource-Based Industry Financing Fund), the maximum grant amount is the lesser of 5% of the hard costs or $15,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and agricultural businesses in Cecil, Kent, and Queen Anne's Counties in Maryland's Upper Shore region seeking to access MARBIDCO financing programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equity contribution towards projects funded by MARBIDCO loans, including those under the Maryland Resource-Based Industry Financing Loan Fund, Oyster Shucking House Loan Fund, Agribusiness Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund, Vineyard/Hopyard/Orchard Planting Loan Fund, Shellfish Aquaculture Financing Fund, Remote Setting Shellfish Aquaculture Loan Fund, Forestry Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund, and Rural Business Energy Efficiency Improvement Loan Fund; as well as general farm development and operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited to the Upper Shore region: Cecil County, Kent County, and Queen Anne's County in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a farmer or agricultural business in Cecil, Kent, or Queen Anne's County
Must be applying for an eligible MARBIDCO loan
Must follow the regular application process for the specific MARBIDCO loan program
Must meet MARBIDCO's underwriting criteria for the chosen loan program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Upper Shore applicants should follow the regular application process for the specific MARBIDCO loan program they are applying for, meet MARBIDCO's underwriting criteria for that program, and apply through the Upper Shore Regional Council Farm Loan Equity Incentive Matching Fund in conjunction with their MARBIDCO loan application.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Energy Initiative, administered through the Office of Sustainable Energy in partnership with Healthy Neighborhoods Inc. and The Reinvestment Fund, offers low-interest loans to building owners, nonprofits, and for-profit small businesses to finance energy efficiency upgrades. The program helps reduce energy consumption and lower utility bills by financing improvements such as lighting efficiency upgrades, replacement of old boilers, hot water heaters, and HVAC equipment, conversion to efficient kitchen appliances, building envelope improvements, and new construction energy efficiency projects.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans financing up to $2 million per project with interest rates from 3.0% to 4.0% and loan terms up to 15 years. Healthy Neighborhoods Inc. provides loans under $150,000, and The Reinvestment Fund finances projects $150,000 and above. Funds can be used for energy efficiency upgrades including lighting improvements, boiler and hot water heater replacement, HVAC equipment upgrades, efficient kitchen equipment conversion, building envelope improvements, and new construction energy efficiency projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Building owners, nonprofit organizations, for-profit small businesses, and real estate project developers in Baltimore City seeking to make energy efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency upgrades including lighting improvements, boiler and hot water heater replacement, efficient kitchen equipment conversion, HVAC equipment upgrades, building envelope improvements, plumbing, plug loads, and other energy-reducing improvements in existing building retrofits, gut rehabilitation projects, and new construction.
