requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization, for-profit small business, or real estate project developer
Project must involve energy efficiency improvements that reduce building energy use
Qualifying projects include retrofits of existing buildings, gut rehabilitation projects, and new construction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Baltimore Energy Initiative Loan Program website, review available documents, and submit the two-page Initial Financing Request Form.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Bridge Finance Facility (BFF) is a financing program administered by the Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) in partnership with the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA), designed to accelerate the development of Maryland-sited solar photovoltaic (PV) and solar-plus-storage projects by addressing critical pre-construction and early-construction financing gaps. The program provides short-term bridge loans to community solar and affordable multifamily housing solar projects that deliver significant energy cost savings to low- and moderate-income (LMI) households. It targets otherwise viable projects that lack access to early-stage capital needed to advance toward construction.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The BFF provides short-term bridge loans ranging from $500,000 to $1,500,000 maximum per developer. Loan sizes and terms vary based on development needs, risk profile, and repayment strategy. The maximum initial interest rate for the first round is 7%, with final rates fixed at approval based on the SOFR rate plus a risk-based spread. No additional fees such as origination or legal fees apply. Loans are typically structured for 12 months with an optional 6-month extension. Interest-only payments are made during the loan term with principal repaid at maturity. Collateral includes a first-priority UCC lien and/or guaranty. Funds are disbursed through one draw based on approved uses, documentation, and project milestones, with a goal of disbursement by May 2026. Eligible uses include interconnection applications, studies and deposits, engineering and system design, permitting and related fees, equipment deposits and procurement, site preparation, EPC mobilization, and initial construction and commissioning-related costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private or nonprofit solar developers, project special purpose entities (SPEs), affordable housing owners or affiliates, and mission-driven organizations developing Maryland-sited solar or solar-plus-storage projects that serve low- and moderate-income households. Applicants may be based outside Maryland provided the project is located in Maryland and meets all program requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-construction and early-construction development costs including: utility interconnection applications, studies, and deposits; engineering and system design; permitting and related fees; equipment deposits and procurement; site preparation and EPC mobilization; initial construction and commissioning-related costs. Early construction and equipment procurement costs may also be eligible once construction financing is identified or clearly anticipated.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be sited in Maryland. Applicants may be based outside Maryland provided the project is located in Maryland and meets all program requirements. Projects must be up to 2 MW AC per project (for community solar, front of the meter).
requirements_list: Projects must be community solar or affordable multifamily housing solar installations (rooftop or carport)

At least 51% (more than 50%) of total project energy or financial benefits must be delivered directly to low- and moderate-income households at or below 150% of the applicable Area Median Income for the State
Projects must reduce energy burdens for LMI households by at least 20%
Eligible project models are community solar projects (front of the meter, at or below 2 MW AC) and affordable multifamily housing projects (behind the meter)
Solar-plus-storage projects are eligible but battery storage is not required
Projects must have identified sites and an initial development plan
Site control or credible path to site control must be demonstrated (lease, option, or letter of intent)
Applicants must demonstrate project readiness and progress toward construction including site control
Borrower types must be corporate entities, special purpose entities (SPEs), nonprofits, or multifamily housing cooperatives that own or control Maryland-sited solar PV project assets
Projects must demonstrate a realistic plan for repaying the BFF loan through grants, construction financing, permanent debt, tax equity, sponsor equity, or other capital sources
Interconnection approval not required at intake but current status and expected timelines must be clearly stated
BFF loans must be repaid prior to construction financing or other capital sources requiring liens on the same project or business assets
If application is made via a project special purpose entity, the controlling ownership entity must provide audited financials and tax returns
Previous 2 years of business tax returns and 3 years of company financial statements required
Articles of Organization or Incorporation, operating agreement or bylaws, W-9, and company information required
Projects are evaluated competitively based on eligibility, readiness, risk, and alignment with program priorities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Sourcing and Intake: Applicants complete a preliminary BFF Intake online application. Upon successful submission, applicants receive a link to upload supporting attachments to the OneHub secure document management platform. Required documents include site control documentation, interconnection application confirmation, project site map, construction timeline, subscriber acquisition plan (for community solar), affordable housing evidence (for multifamily), business tax returns, financial statements, EPC scope or budget, project pro forma, sponsor financial projections, capital stack summary, and sources and uses documentation. Each individual project requires a separate application. 2. Qualification Screening: MCEC conducts initial eligibility and risk/impact screening and may request additional information or invite the project to the next review stage. 3. Due Diligence and Underwriting: Selected projects undergo detailed reviews to confirm project readiness, financial viability, developer capacity, and repayment pathway. 4. Approval and Processing: Projects proceed through review and approval in accordance with BFF Credit Policy and governance requirements, with approval by MCEC Board of Directors. 5. Legal Documentation and Closing: Loan terms and conditions are finalized and legal documentation is executed. 6. Funding, Draws, and Portfolio Management: Borrowers request funds based on agreed draw structure and MCEC verifies and disburses funds. 7. Loan Repayment: Borrowers make principal and interest payments per agreed terms.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charging and Fueling Infrastructure (CFI) Discretionary Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program administered by the U.S. Department of Transportation/FHWA and implemented in Maryland through the Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) and its partners via the Maryland Equitable Charging Infrastructure Partnership (MECIP). The program provides funding to install electric vehicle (EV) charging stations along Alternative Fuel Corridors and in low-to-moderate income communities across Maryland, while also investing in innovative workforce development related to EV charging infrastructure. It supports statewide public and private partners to expand equitable charging infrastructure throughout Maryland, with priority consideration for Justice40 Initiative communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Discretionary grant funding to install electric vehicle charging stations along Alternative Fuel Corridors and in low-to-moderate income communities throughout Maryland, and to support innovative workforce development initiatives related to EV charging infrastructure. The program is a federal discretionary grant program created by the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), codified at 23 U.S.C. § 151, with $2.5 billion allocated over five years nationally. The program provides two funding categories: (1) Community Charging and Alternative Fueling Grants (Community Program) for public and private charging stations; and (2) Charging and Alternative Fuel Corridor Grants (Corridor Program) for charging infrastructure along Alternative Fuel Corridors.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Please check Grants.gov for current funding opportunities and deadlines
structured_extraction.program_audience: Statewide public and private partners — including state and local governments, nonprofits, for-profit entities, metropolitan planning organizations, special purpose districts, port authorities, Indian Tribes, and public authorities with ownership of publicly accessible transportation facilities — seeking to expand equitable electric vehicle charging infrastructure and alternative fueling infrastructure across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used to install electric vehicle charging stations and alternative fueling infrastructure (for hydrogen, propane, and natural gas vehicles) along Alternative Fuel Corridors and in low-to-moderate income communities, and to support innovative workforce development related to charging and fueling infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland, with priority consideration for Alternative Fuel Corridor locations, low-to-moderate income communities, and Justice40 Initiative communities.
requirements_list: Applicants must be eligible entities including states, political subdivisions of states, metropolitan planning organizations, units of local governments, special purpose districts or public authorities with a transportation function, Indian Tribes, U.S. Territories, or authorities/agencies/instrumentalities owned by such entities
EV charging stations must be designed to be accessible to and usable by people with disabilities in compliance with ADA, ABA, and Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act standards
Charging stations must include accessible routes, clear floor space, operable parts within reach range, accessible communication features, and comply with ADA accessibility standards
For Community Program: applicants must be state or local authorities with ownership of publicly accessible transportation facilities
EV chargers must have accessible user interfaces, payment systems, and customer service options for people with disabilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application windows are announced periodically on Grants.gov and the FHWA CFI website. Past grant rounds (Round 1A, 1B, and Round 2) have been completed with recipients announced. For future opportunities, applicants should monitor Grants.gov (https://grants.gov/search-grants) and the CFI website regularly for Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) announcements. No estimated date for the next NOFO release is currently available. When applications are open, eligible entities submit proposals through Grants.gov following the specific NOFO requirements for either the Community Charging and Alternative Fueling Grants or the Charging and Alternative Fuel Corridor Grants categories.

structured_extraction.program_description: A year-long service program administered through the Chesapeake Bay Trust that places young adults aged 18-25 as Climate Coordinators at host organizations across Maryland. Participants support environmental restoration and conservation efforts, including working with entities such as the City of Annapolis Resilience and Sustainability Division to implement Climate Action Plans and Resilience Plans, conduct research on climate-related legislation and policy, assist with grant opportunities, and organize community engagement events. The program supports and trains the next generation of stewards in professions that restore and protect the environment and natural resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive a $33,280 annual stipend disbursed bimonthly for a year of service (August 19, 2026 to August 19, 2027). The program includes health care coverage for those without private insurance, 15 professional development trainings, 4 all-cohort project days, 4-10 networking visits, 1 capstone project, 1 grant opportunity, and funding to attend a regional professional conference. Approximately 50 Corps Members are placed at host organizations across Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students, college students, and recent college graduates ages 18-25 interested in climate and environmental work, including careers in environmental restoration and conservation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Stipend supports year-long service as a Climate Coordinator working on climate adaptation, community resilience, environmental initiatives, and training and education in environmental stewardship professions
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program places approximately 50 Corps Members at host organizations across the state of Maryland, serving the broader Chesapeake Bay region. Applicants interested in working with specific host organizations such as the City of Annapolis should indicate this during the application process.
requirements_list: Age 18-25 at the start of the program
U.S. citizen, permanent resident alien, or has documentation confirming permission to work in the U.S. during the year-long term of service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website at cbtrust.org and should indicate during the application process if interested in working with a specific host organization such as the City of Annapolis.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Clean Energy Advantage (CEA) Loan Program is a pilot loan program offering Maryland residents a convenient and affordable financing option for residential energy improvements, regardless of income level. The program provides 0% APR financing for the first 24 months to help make energy upgrades accessible for more Maryland households. Eligible improvements include home energy efficient heating and air conditioning systems, water heating systems, windows and doors, whole home insulation, and weatherproofing. The program aims to reduce energy bills while improving home comfort for all income levels across the state.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 0% APR loan for the first 24 months to finance residential energy improvements. Eligible uses include energy-efficient heating and air conditioning systems, water heating systems, windows and doors, whole home insulation, and weatherproofing. Available to all income levels statewide.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners and residents of all income levels seeking to make residential energy improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residential energy improvements including energy-efficient HVAC systems, water heating systems, windows and doors, whole home insulation, and weatherproofing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to all Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a homeowner
Available to all income levels

structured_extraction.program_description: The C3 Fund provides financing to increase implementation of clean energy measures and technologies that reduce greenhouse gas emissions and mitigate the effects of climate change, helping Maryland meet the Climate Solutions Now Act goals. The fund supports projects, companies, and technologies focused on building decarbonization, transportation electrification, clean energy generation and storage, energy weatherization for low-to-moderate-income households, community-scale infrastructure resilience, advanced clean energy technology deployment, and a Maryland Green Bond Program. A minimum of 40% of the Fund's investments are targeted to assist low-income households and communities throughout the state. An allocation of $15 million over three fiscal years was committed to the fund beginning in fiscal year 2024.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The C3 Fund provides capital financing through multiple investment mechanisms: (1) Revolving Loan Fund - provides direct and leveraged lending with rate subsidies, loss reserves, gap financing, reduced cost, and patient capital; (2) Equity Investment Fund - used for direct and/or equity-linked investments in projects and initiatives that will generate revenue, income, or profit, with a portion reinvested in the fund; (3) Block Grant Program - provides grants in whole or in part to fund eligible qualified projects and programs, which may be awarded as matching and/or reimbursable investments; (4) Capacity Building Grant - provides matching and/or reimbursable grants to assist organizations and communities to plan and develop projects and initiatives to achieve greenhouse gas reductions; (5) MDPACE financing for energy efficiency, electric vehicle charging, stormwater management, and resiliency projects; and (6) Maryland Clean Energy Capital Program (MCAP) - provides taxable and tax-exempt bond financing for project investments in excess of $5M. An allocation of $15 million over three fiscal years was committed beginning in fiscal year 2024. The fund may consist of appropriated state budget money, private contributions, federal grants, repayment of prior financing, interest earnings, and other sources, and is designed to be leveraged with additional private capital investments. No more than 5% of the fund balance may be used for administrative purposes. At least 40% of fund investments must benefit low-income households and communities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications due by the 15th of each month for award approximately 60 days thereafter (rolling basis)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, businesses, organizations, municipalities, institutions, non-profit organizations, and private partners throughout Maryland seeking financing for clean energy implementation and greenhouse gas emission reduction, with priority for low-income households and communities. Applicants must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments & Taxation, with an active Federal Tax ID or Social Security number.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financing for projects and technologies that: (1) facilitate electrification of the transportation sector and use of sustainable alternative fuels in aviation; (2) improve building energy management and efficiency to reduce greenhouse gas emissions; (3) expand deployment of clean energy generation and energy storage capacity; (4) implement energy weatherization measures for low-to-moderate-income households; (5) optimize economic, health, social, and environmental value of community-scale infrastructure for resilience and energy equity; (6) deploy advanced clean energy technology; (7) support a Maryland Green Bond Program; (8) reduce greenhouse gas emissions with significant estimated GHG reduction, demonstrated net zero impact or transition; (9) support renewable energy generation, transmission, and distribution supply and efficiencies including grid resilience; (10) enable building electrification, weatherization, storage and resilience; and (11) support biomass energy and waste-to-value applications and carbon capture technologies.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The C3 Fund Oversight Committee evaluates investment proposals through three selection processes: (1) Competitive Selection - Applicants submit responses to a published Request for Proposal (RFP) following formal qualifications and selection criteria. RFPs are published on the Center website. Applications are due by the 15th of each month with awards made approximately 60 days thereafter. Selection criteria include proposer eligibility and qualifications, financial feasibility, greenhouse gas/climate vulnerability reductions, environmental/energy sustainability, cost-effectiveness, technological characteristics and scale-up potential, jobs created, and contributions to statutory C3 Fund purposes. Multiple proposers may be selected for negotiations. (2) Programmatic Selection - Applications admitted on a continuing or periodic basis using the same criteria as competitive selection. Applications are due by the 15th of each month with awards approximately 60 days thereafter. (3) Strategic Selection - Used when Committee determines direct participation is required based on uniqueness of opportunity, urgency of need, or cost factors. Committee must adopt affirmative resolution and find at least three of the following characteristics: exceptional experience/expertise/availability/proprietary rights; unique location/technology/implementation; great alignment with C3 Fund purpose; urgent need or risk of unavailability; or connection to multiphase project or existing investment. Award recipients must report annually on construction status, C3 Funds spent, operations and activities, and any material impairments to objectives. Recipients maintain records for at least five years. The Committee meets at least four times per calendar year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) / MDPACE (Maryland Property Assessed Clean Energy)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) program, administered statewide by the Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) as MDPACE through its agent Abacus Property Solutions, LLC, is a financing mechanism that allows commercial property owners and builders to fund energy efficiency, water conservation, renewable energy, resiliency, and environmental remediation improvements with no upfront cost. Financing is structured as a voluntary tax assessment (lien) on the property and repaid through annual or semi-annual surcharges on the property tax bill, typically over 10 to 30+ years, with terms based on the Weighted Average Expected Useful Life (EUL) of the installed improvements. Because the assessment is tied to the property rather than the owner, the financing obligation transfers to the new owner if the property is sold. The program provides 100% upfront capital coverage with no money down, and underwriting focuses on the underlying building rather than owner creditworthiness, making it accessible even to borrowers with non-investment-grade credit. Minimum project size is $50,000. Montgomery County and Prince George's County administer their own independent C-PACE programs; all other participating Maryland counties are served through MDPACE managed by MCEC. Counties use the program to create jobs, retain businesses, and keep dollars in the local economy without raising taxes. Capital providers (financial institutions and lenders) may also participate by becoming approved MDPACE Capital Providers and executing the Standard Offer agreement with MCEC.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: C-PACE/MDPACE provides 100% upfront private financing for qualifying commercial property improvements through a voluntary special assessment lien with senior lien status equivalent to real property tax assessments. Financing is structured with no money down required and is secured through the property tax bill collection process. Loan terms are fixed-rate and typically range from 10 to 30+ years, determined by the Weighted Average Expected Useful Life (EUL) of the installed improvements, with amortization over 15–25 years and the option to defer initial payments through interest capitalization. Minimum project size is $50,000; projects typically range from $50,000 to $100,000+ for standardized MDPACE financing but can be larger for private capital provider deals. The assessment transfers with the property upon sale, releasing the prior owner from obligation and transferring surcharge payments to the subsequent owner. Loan payments are collected annually or semi-annually as separate line items on the property tax bill. Property owners may also realize tax credits including the federal solar Investment Tax Credit (ITC) and accelerated depreciation (MACRS). Capital providers participate by executing a Standard Offer agreement with MCEC and can finance both the C-PACE and senior debt component of projects. Program fees include application fees, closing fees, servicing fees, and county administration fees, which vary by jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.contact_name: MCEC Finance Team (Program Administrator: Abacus Property Solutions, LLC)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners and developers seeking to finance energy efficiency, water conservation, renewable energy, resiliency, or environmental remediation improvements; approved capital providers (financial institutions and lenders); registered contractors; and local governments in Maryland jurisdictions that have adopted C-PACE enabling legislation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements (HVAC, lighting and electrical upgrades, building envelope improvements, windows, doors, chillers, boilers, elevators, insulation); renewable energy installations (solar photovoltaic, wind, geothermal); water conservation and efficiency measures (toilets, urinals, car wash equipment, pre-rinse spray valves, dishwashers, icemakers, plumbing); resiliency measures (flood mitigation, stormwater management, hurricane shutters, EV charging stations, energy storage); environmental remediation (asbestos, mold, lead paint, lead pipe removal, indoor air quality improvements, indoor water quality improvements); and other qualifying building retrofit and new construction improvements for both existing buildings and new developments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland counties that have adopted C-PACE enabling legislation through an ordinance and signed a Locality Agreement with the Maryland Clean Energy Center. Montgomery County and Prince George's County administer their own independent C-PACE programs with their respective procedures. All other participating Maryland counties are served through MDPACE managed by MCEC through Abacus Property Solutions, LLC. Garrett County is a participating county; Garrett County applicants should contact the Garrett County Energy Division for local guidance and visit md-pace.com. Loan administration procedures vary by county based on each jurisdiction's enabling ordinance.
requirements_list: Property must be commercial (or industrial) in nature
County must have enacted C-PACE enabling legislation through an ordinance
County must sign a Locality Agreement with the Maryland Clean Energy Center
Improvements must qualify as energy efficiency, renewable energy, water conservation, resiliency, or environmental remediation measures
Mortgage holder approval required before loan closing
Minimum project size of $50,000
Property must be located in a participating Maryland jurisdiction
Project analysis and technical review approval required based on improvement type
For energy/water efficiency projects: energy/water savings must be demonstrated
For renewable energy projects: technical feasibility and performance analysis required
For resiliency projects: hazard assessment and mitigation strategy required
For environmental remediation: documentation of remediation scope required
Registered contractor must be used for project implementation
Technical reviewer credentials must meet program standards for applicable improvement category
For capital providers: must become an approved MDPACE Capital Provider and execute the Standard Offer agreement with MCEC
Counties choosing to opt in must execute agreement with MCEC and adopt enabling ordinance compliant with state C-PACE Act
Loan cannot exceed the Weighted Average Expected Useful Life of improvements
Loan-to-value thresholds and underwriting parameters established by program guidelines
Property owner must develop qualifying project and arrange financing with qualified Capital Provider
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. DETERMINE ELIGIBILITY: Confirm property is commercial, located in a participating Maryland county, and meets minimum project size ($50,000). 2. COMPLETE PRE-APPLICATION: Contact appropriate C-PACE program administrator for your county (Montgomery County C-PACE Program, Prince George's County C-PACE Program administered through FSC First, or MCEC Finance Team for all other eligible counties). 3. DEVELOP PROJECT: Work with registered contractor to design qualifying improvements (energy efficiency, renewable energy, water conservation, resiliency, or environmental remediation). 4. PROJECT ANALYSIS: Engage technical reviewer with appropriate credentials to prepare project analysis and supporting documentation demonstrating project viability and expected savings/benefits. 5. OBTAIN MORTGAGE HOLDER CONSENT: Secure written approval from mortgage holder before proceeding (required for all mortgaged properties; special procedures apply for HUD-backed mortgages). 6. SUBMIT FINAL APPLICATION: Submit complete application package with supporting documentation, technical review, project specifications, and mortgage holder consent through online portal or directly to program administrator. 7. UNDERWRITING & APPROVAL: Program administrator reviews application for compliance with underwriting parameters (loan amount, loan-to-value ratio, property valuation, etc.) and program guidelines. 8. CLOSE C-PACE LOAN: Execute tri-party Statement of Levy and Lien of Surcharge Agreement among county, property owner, and capital provider; property owner and capital provider execute Clean Energy Loan Financing Agreement defining loan terms and conditions. Record surcharge lien with local government. 9. LOAN DISBURSEMENT: Capital provider funds C-PACE loan proceeds; surcharge is added to property tax bill as separate line item. 10. PROJECT COMPLETION: Contractor completes improvements; program administrator verifies completion. 11. ONGOING SERVICING: Surcharge payments collected annually or semi-annually through property tax bill; program administrator services account and enforces delinquent payments. For capital providers: Contact MCEC Finance Team to register as approved MDPACE Capital Provider, then complete and execute Standard Offer agreement between Capital Provider and MCEC. For jurisdictions: Adopt enabling legislation through ordinance adhering to Maryland C-PACE Act principles, then sign Locality Agreement with Maryland Clean Energy Center. For Garrett County applicants, contact Garrett County Energy Division for local guidance and visit md-pace.com.

Participants can join one or all phases and benefit from specialized guidance, mentorship, expert connections, and investor relationships to support commercialization of early-stage energy and climate technologies. structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Smart Energy Communities (MSEC) program encourages local governments, state agencies, non-profit organizations, educational institutions, and communities to adopt smart energy policies and goals by providing grants to support sustainable, long-term clean energy projects and initiatives. The program aims to reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, increase cost savings, and promote clean energy and economic development. As an example, Baltimore County received a $100,000 grant to fund energy efficient HVAC systems and LED lighting upgrades at public facilities such as the Reisterstown Library.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided to support clean energy policies, projects, and initiatives that reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. Award amounts vary by project; for example, Baltimore County received a $100,000 grant to fund energy efficient HVAC system upgrades and LED lighting installation at public facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, state agencies, non-profit organizations, educational institutions, and communities seeking to adopt smart energy policies and goals
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sustainable clean energy policies and projects, energy efficiency improvements including HVAC system upgrades, LED lighting installation at public facilities, and renewable energy projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; available to all Maryland local governments and eligible organizations

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Solar for All Program provides rebates, financing, and financial support to help low-income, financially vulnerable, and underserved residents across Maryland access affordable solar energy. The program supports rooftop solar installations on single-family homes, multifamily housing, and community solar projects to reduce energy costs and boost efficiency. It is funded by a $62 million grant from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's Solar for All program.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides rebates, financing options, grants, and subsidies for rooftop solar installations on single-family homes, multifamily housing, and community solar projects. It is funded by a $62 million grant from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's Solar for All program, targeting financially vulnerable and under-resourced households across Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, financially vulnerable, and underserved Maryland residents seeking to install solar power on their homes or participate in community solar projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rooftop solar photovoltaic system installations on single-family homes, multifamily housing, and community solar projects to reduce energy costs and improve efficiency.

Applicants must be financially vulnerable or under-resourced households

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financing for energy efficiency, renewable energy, and clean energy projects through a public nonprofit corporation.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements, renewable energy projects, clean energy investments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: State-Based Home Energy Efficiency Contractor Training Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The State-Based Home Energy Efficiency Contractor Training Grants makes $200 million available to state energy offices so they can train, test, and certify residential energy efficiency and electrification contractors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants totaling $200 million to state energy offices for training, testing, and certification of residential energy efficiency and electrification contractors.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training, testing, and certification programs for residential energy efficiency and electrification contractors

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Clean Energy Center, in partnership with the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA), has launched a $5 million Strategic Revolving Fund designed to accelerate the deployment of solar photovoltaic (PV) and energy storage systems across affordable housing communities in Maryland. The fund provides capital for early-stage development costs to help sustainable energy projects move from concept to construction. As projects are completed and repaid, the capital is recycled back into the fund to finance new projects.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $5 million revolving line of credit (with $4.5 million deployed to Enterprise Community Development) to finance solar PV and energy storage projects at affordable housing properties. The line of credit covers engineering and design, interconnection and commissioning, and procurement and construction costs. As projects are completed and repaid, the capital is recycled back into the fund to finance new projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Affordable housing providers, communities, and organizations in Maryland seeking to deploy solar photovoltaic and energy storage systems at affordable housing properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Engineering and design, interconnection and commissioning, procurement and construction costs for solar photovoltaic and energy storage system installation at affordable housing properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must be at affordable housing properties or serve affordable housing communities
Focus on solar photovoltaic (PV) and energy storage systems
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested parties should contact the MCEC Finance Team through the contact form on the website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the U.S. Department of Agriculture in partnership with the Maryland Clean Energy Center, Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service, and the Maryland Wood Energy Team. The program expands access to renewable, clean thermal energy through locally-sourced woody biomass by identifying high-potential facilities with limited renewable energy access and high heating oil dependency located near forest stands needing active management.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The grant provides comprehensive services to help facilities switch from fossil fuels to thermal woody biomass systems, including engineering and analysis services from the USFS Wood Education and Resource Center (WERC), IMPLAN analyses showing regional economic impact, bid-ready designs, wood supply chain development, pathways to economic development partners and funding programs, and community education and outreach materials. The program leverages locally-sourced renewable woody biomass from forest management activities and urban wood waste recycling to create clean thermal energy systems.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Facilities with high dependency on heating oil located near large forest stands with a need for active forest management practices, and an opportunity for employment within the community. The program serves non-profits, for-profit businesses, and government entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Switching from fossil fuels to thermal woody biomass heating systems, including engineering analysis, design development, supply chain establishment, and conversion infrastructure. Funds support the transition to renewable woody biomass sourced from sustainable forestry practices and urban wood waste recycling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland and adjacent counties in Pennsylvania, West Virginia, Delaware, and Virginia where the forest industry and wood fuel supply chain extends across state boundaries.
requirements_list: Currently have little or no access to renewable energy
High dependency on heating oil or other fossil fuels for thermal energy
Located near large forest stands with a need for active forest management practices
Identified as a high-potential facility for woody biomass system conversion
Opportunity for employment within the community
Commitment to sustainable forestry practices and carbon sequestration goals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Facilities interested in the grant should contact the Maryland Clean Energy Center for more information on the application process and requirements. The MCEC works with partners including the USFS Wood Education and Resource Center, Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service, and the Maryland Wood Energy Team to evaluate applications and provide technical assistance throughout the conversion process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to support local Area Agencies on Aging, Senior Villages, and nonprofit organizations serving older Marylanders and their caregivers to provide high-quality services and supports, develop social connection, and foster community engagement, enabling older Marylanders to thrive in their communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDOA awarded $261,173 to 11 organizations in FY26 grants. Individual grant amounts ranged from $9,500 to $45,000. Funds support local Area Agencies on Aging, Senior Villages, and nonprofit organizations to provide services, social activities, transportation, food delivery, case management, housing counseling, caregiver support, and home accessibility improvements for older adults.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Area Agencies on Aging, Senior Villages, and nonprofit organizations serving older Marylanders and their caregivers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to provide high-quality services and supports, develop social connection, foster community engagement, transportation services, food delivery and nutrition programs, care coordination, community gardens, financial counseling, housing counseling, caregiver support programs, home safety improvements and wheelchair ramps, and online resources for caregivers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. FY26 grantees served Kent County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Allegany County, Baltimore City, Howard County, Worcester County, and the Lower Eastern Shore.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should visit the Grant Availability page for information on Aging-in-Place and other funding opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides waivers to Marylanders with developmental disabilities for access to assistive technology and services to help with activities of daily living. Includes an assessment of needs and assistance in locating and using assistive technology. Products and services available can include speech and communications devices, visual or hearing support, adaptations for computers, toys, equipment, software, training, and other supportive technology to improve independence, safety, and quality of life.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides waivers and funding for assistive technology and services including speech and communications devices, visual or hearing support, computer adaptations, toys, equipment, software, training, and other technology to support activities of daily living. Includes assessment of needs and assistance in locating and using assistive technology to improve independence, safety, and quality of life.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders with developmental disabilities needing assistive technology and services for activities of daily living and improved independence and quality of life
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and provision of assistive technology, services, and support to help with activities of daily living and improve independence, safety, and quality of life
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide
requirements_list: Must have a developmental disability
Must be a Maryland resident
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration for information about eligibility, assessment, and waiver services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Housing/Healthy Aging Program (Formerly Congregate Housing Services Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides housing and support services to help eligible older adults live independently in their own homes or designated apartment buildings. Services include meals, housekeeping, medication management, and limited personal assistance with daily activities such as bathing, dressing, and laundry. The program is designed to support low- to moderate-income seniors who need assistance with one or more activities of daily living.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Aging awards grant funding to housing and senior service provider organizations to operate the program. For FY26, the state awarded over $1.9 million in grant funding to 10 organizations across the state. Funding amounts to individual organizations range from approximately $48,000 to $527,000. The program also provides subsidized housing with assistance for activities of daily living in apartment buildings for eligible older adults.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents who are at least 62 years of age with low or no income (low- to moderate-income) and in need of assistance with one or more activities of daily living.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports the provision of meals, housekeeping, medication management, and limited personal assistance with activities of daily living for eligible residents in designated apartment buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program operates in designated buildings across multiple Maryland counties. Eligible residents must live in buildings designated as part of the program.
requirements_list: Must be at least 62 years of age
Must have low or no income (low- to moderate-income)
Must need assistance with one or more activities of daily living
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Maryland Access Point for information on local housing programs and application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: Meal sites located in over 250 locations across Maryland where older adults can dine and participate in social, health-related, and educational activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provision of meals at congregate dining sites with opportunities for social engagement, nutrition education, physical activity, and health screening.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults seeking meal services and social engagement
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nutritious meals and participation in social and health-related programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at more than 250 locations across Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an older adult
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Area Agency on Aging or search for programs near you using the Maryland Access Point search tool.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY24 Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementia Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants awarded to non-profit organizations to support the implementation of comprehensive home- and community-based supportive services, improve coordination of care, and expand opportunities for social support for people with Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) and their caregivers. Funded programs include day center scholarships, dementia training programs, transportation services, companionship and home visits, and dementia capability programming at adult day centers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants totaling approximately $134,000 distributed to six non-profit organizations. Individual award amounts ranged from $11,500 to $27,000. Funds support implementation of home- and community-based services, care coordination, and social support programs including day center scholarships, dementia training programs, transportation services, companionship and home visits, and dementia capability programming at adult day centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations providing services to people with Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias and their caregivers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used to provide home- and community-based supportive services, care coordination, day center scholarships, dementia training programs, transportation services, companionship and home visits, scholarships for program attendance, and dementia capability programming at adult day centers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Past grantees served Worcester County, Kensington/Montgomery County, Baltimore City, Salisbury/Wicomico County, Hagerstown, and Silver Spring areas.
requirements_list: Must be a non-profit organization
Must provide home- and community-based supportive services related to ADRD
Must improve coordination of care for people with ADRD and caregivers
Must support implementation of comprehensive home- and community-based services for ADRD patients and caregivers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are reviewed and awarded by the Maryland Department of Aging. The FY24 grants have already been awarded. Future grant cycles may be available; contact Mark Tesoro at mark.tesoro@maryland.gov or (410) 767-1119 for application procedures and timeline information.

structured_extraction.program_description: MAP is a gateway to long-term services and support in Maryland that helps individuals and caregivers plan, identify, connect to, and access private and public resources for long-term care. Services include information on health, transportation, income, financial aid, senior and community centers, nutrition and meals, pharmacy assistance, housing, and volunteer opportunities. MAP also provides Options Counseling, a person-centered service where trained counselors help individuals and caregivers make informed decisions about long-term care by matching their needs and preferences with community services and developing personalized action plans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MAP provides information and referral services, options counseling, and connection to resources for long-term services and supports at no direct financial assistance from MAP itself. The program connects individuals to community services and resources available through partner agencies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with long-term care needs, caregivers, and professionals seeking long-term services and support information and planning assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services provide information, referral, options counseling, and connection to community resources for long-term care including health services, transportation, income assistance, housing, nutrition, pharmacy assistance, and volunteer opportunities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide with 20 local MAP offices covering all counties.
requirements_list: Refer to eligibility memo for select income-based federal and state programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 1-844-MAP-LINK (1-844-627-5465) to speak with a 211 Maryland information and referral specialist who will identify local resources and direct those with long-term and complex needs to their local MAP office for options counseling. Individuals can also access MAP online at marylandaccesspoint.211md.org. MAP specialists work with callers to plan and identify resources.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Durable Medical Equipment (DME) Re-Use Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Aging provides free durable medical equipment (DME) to Maryland residents with any illness, injury, or disability, regardless of age, to help them remain safe at home and connected to their communities. Pediatric equipment is also available. All equipment is collected via donation, sanitized, repaired, and redistributed at no cost to eligible residents. The program improves quality of life by providing access to mobility and medical equipment, helps people avoid costlier levels of care, and diverts discarded equipment from landfills. Equipment includes both basic items (canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails, bedrails) and complex items (manual wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, mechanical lifts, knee scooters, overbed tables, trapeze bars). The application process is typically less complicated and faster than through many insurance providers, and products are available for pickup at several distribution centers across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free, gently-used, sanitized, and refurbished durable medical equipment at no cost to eligible Maryland residents. Equipment is provided on a first-come, first-served basis subject to availability and becomes the permanent property of the recipient. Basic DME includes canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails, and bedrails. Complex DME includes manual wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, mechanical lifts, knee scooters, overbed tables, and trapeze bars. Complex DME must be picked up at the Re-Use Center in Cheltenham, Maryland; basic DME may be picked up at satellite sites around the state. Equipment pickup is by appointment only; delivery and installation are not available. Individuals must have exhausted all other means of obtaining equipment, including through insurance providers (Medicare, Medicaid, or private insurance).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents of any age with any illness, injury, or disability who need durable medical equipment and have exhausted other means of obtaining it. Pediatric equipment is available. Healthcare providers can also initiate requests on behalf of patients.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Durable and home medical equipment for mobility, medical support, and home safety, including: canes, crutches, walkers, rollators, shower chairs, tub transfer benches, bedside commodes, toilet safety rails, bedrails, manual wheelchairs, transport wheelchairs, power wheelchairs, power scooters, home hospital beds, mechanical lifts, knee scooters, overbed tables, and trapeze bars.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents only. Equipment can be picked up at satellite sites throughout the state for basic DME, or at the main Re-Use Center located at 11701 Crain Highway, Cheltenham, MD 20623 for complex DME.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must have any illness, injury, or disability (any age eligible, including pediatric)
Must have exhausted all other means of obtaining the equipment, including through insurance coverage (Medicare, Medicaid, or private insurance)
Complete the appropriate DME Request Form: Basic DME Request Form or Complex DME Request Form

For Basic DME: Part C of the Request Form must be completed by a healthcare professional treating the beneficiary (physician, physical therapist, occupational therapist, physician's assistant, or certified registered nurse practitioner)
For Complex DME: Request form must be completed in three parts — Part A by the requestor/caregiver, Parts B and C by a healthcare professional (Physician, PA, CRNP, PT, or OT)
Requests for power wheelchairs and power scooters must be completed by a Physical Therapist or Occupational Therapist only
A formal prescription is not required
All required fields on the request form must be completed
Requestor must be willing to pick up equipment or arrange for another trusted individual to pick it up
Equipment is provided subject to availability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants may request Basic or Complex DME through the following methods: Option 1 - Online through Maryland OneStop: create an account, verify email, complete Part A of the form online, and select how the healthcare provider will submit Parts B and C (online or hard copy). Option 2 - By mail: download and print the appropriate request form (Basic or Complex), complete Part A (patient/caregiver), have the healthcare professional complete Parts B and C, and mail to Maryland Durable Medical Equipment Re-Use, 11701 Crain Highway, Cheltenham, MD 20623. Option 3 - By email: scan and email the completed form to DME.MDOA@maryland.gov. After submission, the program contacts the requestor by phone to confirm equipment availability. If equipment is in stock, a pickup appointment is scheduled. Equipment pickup is by appointment only at designated distribution sites.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program administered by local Area Agencies on Aging that helps family and informal caregivers care for their loved ones at home for as long as possible. The program offers five types of caregiver services and works with state and community-based services to provide coordinated support for caregivers of older adults, disabled individuals, and children.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers five types of caregiver services. Services can reduce caregiver depression, anxiety, and stress and enable caregivers to provide care longer, thereby avoiding or delaying the need for costly institutional care.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult family members or other informal caregivers age 18 and older providing care to individuals 60 years of age and older; adult family members or other informal caregivers age 18 and older providing care to individuals of any age with Alzheimer's disease and related disorders; grandparents and other relatives (not parents) 55 years of age and older providing care to children under the age of 18; and grandparents and other relatives (not parents) 55 years of age and older providing care to adults age 18-59 with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to support family and informal caregivers in caring for their loved ones at home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, available through the local network of Area Agencies on Aging.
requirements_list: Be an adult family member or other informal caregiver age 18 or older caring for someone 60 or older
OR be an adult family member or other informal caregiver age 18 or older caring for someone of any age with Alzheimer's disease and related disorders
OR be a grandparent or other relative (not parent) age 55 or older caring for a child under age 18
OR be a grandparent or other relative (not parent) age 55 or older caring for an adult age 18-59 with disabilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Area Agencies on Aging to learn about services and apply for the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Miriam Kelty Aging and Senior Social Connection Hub and Spoke Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program that supports villages in expanding services to more residents in their geographic region by leveraging operational proficiencies and existing systems, skills, and resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A three-year pilot program designed to support villages by enhancing operational efficiencies and enabling expansion of services to additional residents across a geographic region
structured_extraction.program_audience: Villages in Montgomery County, specifically the Montgomery County Village Consortium
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To expand village services and programs to more residents in the geographic region by strengthening operational systems and leveraging existing resources
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County
requirements_list: Must be part of the Montgomery County Village Consortium
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Montgomery County Village Consortium was selected by MDOA to implement the pilot program for a three-year period

structured_extraction.program_description: A program supporting neighborhoods or housing developments where a large percentage of residents have aged in place and are predominantly older adults. The program provides programming, service coordination, and community support to concentrated areas where low-income older adults face problems of declining health, isolation, financial hardship, and language barriers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Aging awarded $1.3 million in state funds to 7 community-based organizations in FY26 to provide programming, service coordination, and community support. The program encompasses three complementary projects: Elder Abuse Prevention, Holocaust Survivors Program, and Traditional NORC.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations serving low-income older adults in concentrated areas where residents have aged in place
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To provide programming, service coordination, and community support to older adults in naturally occurring retirement communities, including elder abuse prevention services, support for Holocaust survivors, and traditional aging-in-place community services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications available through the Grant Availability page on the Maryland Department of Aging website

structured_extraction.program_description: A daily automated check-in phone call or text message service for Maryland residents age 60 and older. Participants receive calls between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. during a one-hour time block they select. If the participant does not answer, up to two additional automated calls are made. If those go unanswered, an alternate emergency contact is called to check on the participant. If both the participant and alternate do not answer, the program notifies local non-emergency services. Service is available every day of the year except 6 holidays (New Year's Day, Memorial Day, July 4th, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free daily automated phone calls or text messages providing wellness check-ins and emergency monitoring for seniors. Service is available every day of the year except 6 holidays (New Year's Day, Memorial Day, July 4th, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas). Phone lines are open Monday through Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Saturday 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. TTY is available for those who need it.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are 60 years of age or older
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program provides daily wellness check-in calls and emergency monitoring services for seniors; not a funding program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to any Maryland resident age 60 or older; program is statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident age 60 or older
Must have a landline phone or cell phone
TTY is available for those who need it
Participant and alternates should not have automated call blocking technology enabled, or should disable that feature for this program
Must provide contact information for an alternate emergency contact person, or the program will assign a limited alternate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can register online by clicking 'Register Now' on the website, or call toll-free at 1-866-502-0560 to request a hard copy application be mailed to their home. During enrollment, participants pre-select a one-hour time block for receiving calls between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. After application submission, the program will call the applicant to verify all information and conduct a test automated call to both the participant and alternate where applicable. Once information is validated, a Welcome Packet will be mailed with the start date and contact method. If an application is denied, the applicant will be informed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Senior Farmers' Market Nutrition Program provides low-income older adults (age 60 and over) with coupons or an electronic card worth $50 to purchase fresh, locally grown fruits, vegetables, herbs, honey, and cut herbs at authorized farmers' markets and from approved farmers throughout Maryland. The program promotes healthy eating habits, increases awareness of Maryland's farmers' markets, and is available statewide with distribution and application processes varying by county. Cards are typically valid from July 1 through November 30 each year and are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. Each qualified senior may only receive the $50 SFMNP benefit once each year.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible low-income seniors receive an electronic card worth $50 (or equivalent coupons/electronic payments through the Healthy Together app) that can be used to purchase fresh fruits, vegetables, herbs, honey, and cut herbs at designated farmers' markets and approved farmers throughout Maryland. Cards are valid from July 1 through November 30 annually and are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. Each qualified senior may only receive the $50 SFMNP benefit once each year. Distribution sites, application processes, and specific income thresholds may vary by county. Income eligibility is based on 185% of federal poverty guidelines (e.g., annual income limits for 48 contiguous states, D.C., Guam and territories range from $28,953 for a household of 1 to $100,178 for a household of 8, with an additional $10,175 for each additional family member). Participants must provide self-verification of income with signature.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Online applications begin May 15th; distribution dates vary by county (e.g., Anne Arundel County: applications accepted year-round; Baltimore City: distribution during designated distribution dates in July; Baltimore County: call for specific dates). Cards are valid from July 1 through November 30 each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income adults age 60 and older residing in Maryland, including Baltimore City residents, Baltimore County residents, Anne Arundel County residents, and residents of all other Maryland counties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of fresh fruits, vegetables, herbs, honey, and cut herbs at authorized farmers' markets and from approved farmers throughout Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in all Maryland counties; services, distribution dates, and application processes vary by county. Cards can be used at designated farmers' markets and approved farmers throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be at least 60 years old with proof of age (born on or before June 30, 2026 for 2025 season)

Must meet low-income qualifications based on 185% of federal poverty guidelines (annual income limits range from $28,953 for a household of 1 to $100,178 for a household of 8, plus $10,175 for each additional family member)
Must be a Maryland resident; some counties require county-specific residency (e.g., Baltimore City or Baltimore County residency)
Self-verification of income with participant's signature is required
Must provide name, address, contact information, date of birth, ethnicity, and race (requirements vary by county)
Must agree not to seek additional SFMNP cards from other locations after receiving one
Must agree to receive text message communications from Healthy Together regarding the program (standard messaging rates apply; participants may opt out at any time)
Did not receive an FMNP card in the prior year, or if received, does not still possess that card
Participant or authorized proxy must complete application form and submit to designated distribution site in county of residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application processes vary by county. Statewide online applications begin May 15th through your county's designated contact or the Maryland Department of Agriculture. In Anne Arundel County, complete the application form (available in English, Spanish, and Korean) and submit by visiting a local Senior Activity Center, emailing senior_nutrition@aacounty.org, or mailing to 7320 Ritchie HWY, Glen Burnie, MD 21061; accepted applicants are notified within 15 business days. Participants may complete the application in person at a distribution site, with agency staff signatures required. In Baltimore City, eligible older adults obtain a card at senior centers during designated distribution dates in July (no senior center membership required; a proxy may collect for up to 2 eligible adults). In Baltimore County, apply by calling 410-887-0311 or completing an online form. Proxy option available: if using a proxy to pick up the card, the proxy must complete the proxy section of the form and take it to a distribution site in the county where the participant resides. Application forms must include participant signature and staff certification.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides legal advice, counseling, and representation to older Marylanders and their caregivers. The program prioritizes issues involving income maintenance, nutrition, public and disability benefits, health care, protective services, abuse, housing, utilities, consumer protection, employment, age discrimination, civil rights, and advocacy for institutionalized persons.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free legal advice, counseling, and representation provided through local Area Agencies on Aging that contract with local attorneys and law centers. structured_extraction.program_description: A regulatory program that requires farmers and livestock producers to follow nutrient management plans when fertilizing crops and managing animal manure. The plans specify how much fertilizer, manure, or other nutrient sources can be safely applied to achieve crop yields while preventing excess nutrients from impacting waterways.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical assistance through certified nutrient management specialists and consultants who prepare nutrient management plans for farmers. Training is available through a Nutrient Management Certification Program that includes classroom training and a certification exam. Farmers applying nutrients to 10 or more acres annually must attend a two-hour nutrient applicator course once every three years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers who gross $2,500 or more annually, or livestock producers with 8,000 pounds or more of live animal weight. Also for certified consultants and plan writers who provide nutrient management services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nutrient management planning, training, and certification. Plans specify application rates for fertilizer, manure, and other nutrient sources on farmland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Regional nutrient management specialists are available by county.
requirements_list: Farmers must gross $2,500 or more annually, or have 8,000 pounds or more of live animal weight
Nutrient management plans must be prepared by a certified University of Maryland specialist, certified private consultant, or certified farmer
Farmers must submit initial nutrient management plans to the program
Plans must be updated before they expire
New soil samples must be taken at least once every three years
Manure analyses must be obtained at least every other year if using manure
Annual Implementation Reports must be submitted by March 1 documenting how plans were implemented during the previous year
Farmers applying nutrients to 10 or more acres annually must attend a two-hour nutrient applicator course once every three years
Farmers with Soil Phosphorus Fertility Index Values of 150 or greater must follow Phosphorus Management Tool guidelines
Farmers cannot spread manure or food processing residuals during winter (December 16 through March 1)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Farmers work with a certified nutrient management specialist or consultant to develop a nutrient management plan. Plans must be submitted to the Nutrient Management Program. Farmers must attend training courses and pass a certification exam if they want to prepare their own plans. Annual Implementation Reports must be submitted each year by March 1.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to individuals, vendors, and businesses to develop and showcase proven, innovative technologies for managing animal waste in Maryland. Technologies may reduce nutrient levels in animal waste, change its form or function for other uses, or generate energy and marketable products from waste.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $750,000 available to invest in innovative technologies during Fiscal Year 2026, ending June 30, 2026. Funding support is provided by the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund. Grant awards support development and deployment of proven, innovative animal waste technologies including anaerobic digestion, gasification, pyrolysis, composting, manure injection, and other technologies that reduce nutrient levels in animal waste, change waste form or function for other uses, or generate energy and marketable products from waste.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Letter of Intent due October 17, 2025; full grant proposal due December 23, 2025. The application window for 2026 grant proposals is now closed as of the page update date of January 5, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, vendors, and businesses with proven, innovative technologies for managing animal waste generated by on-farm animals or through animal production processes involving Maryland livestock.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and deployment of innovative technologies that manage animal waste by reducing nutrient levels, changing waste form or function for other uses, or generating energy and marketable products from waste. Supported technologies include anaerobic digestion, thermochemical processing (gasification, pyrolysis, combustion), composting, manure injection, and other proven waste management innovations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Animal waste must be generated by on-farm animals or through an animal production process involving Maryland livestock. Priority consideration may be given to projects in counties with high concentrations of animal waste nutrients: Frederick, Washington, Carroll, and Garrett counties (cattle-heavy areas) and Worcester, Caroline, Somerset, and Wicomico counties (poultry-heavy Eastern Shore areas).
requirements_list: Project must demonstrate potential to enhance public health and environmental well-being
Project must offer alternative waste management solutions for the agricultural sector
Project must have a positive economic development impact in the state
Projects must be proven technologies, not in research and development stage
Additional consideration given to projects that address climate and community benefits
Technology must be innovative and demonstrate feasibility in Maryland conditions
Project must address Maryland's climate change goals and GHG emission reductions
Environmental justice considerations and community engagement are evaluated as part of the proposal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a Letter of Intent by October 17, 2025. Submissions are reviewed and ranked by the Maryland Department of Agriculture in consultation with the Animal Waste Technology Evaluation Committee. High-ranking projects are invited to submit a full grant proposal due by December 23, 2025. Evaluation criteria include environmental impact, economic feasibility, GHG emission reductions, alignment with state climate goals, and community engagement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Certified Local Farm and Fish Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state program that encourages Maryland state agencies and public universities to purchase food from certified local farms and seafood dealers. State agencies work toward a goal of buying 20 percent of their food from businesses listed in the Certified Local Farm and Fish Directory.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Farmers and seafood dealers become certified and listed in the online directory at no cost. There is no application fee. Once certified, producers and Chesapeake invasive species providers are automatically listed in the public Certified Local Farm and Fish Directory, which is used by Maryland state agencies, universities, and other institutions interested in purchasing from certified businesses. MDA asks certified businesses to update their directory information (contact information, list of products, and certification number) once a year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farms with nutrient management plans and seafood dealers licensed as Tidal Fish Dealers with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. State agencies and public universities purchase food under this program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable - this is not a funding program. It creates a certification and directory listing for farms and seafood dealers to be eligible for state procurement contracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - open to farms and seafood dealers throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: For farms: must have a nutrient management plan or meet nutrient management requirements (apiarists or aquaculturists) with the Maryland Department of Agriculture
For seafood dealers: must be licensed as a Tidal Fish Dealer with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources
Maintain current directory information with annual updates
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Create a Maryland OneStop account (register with first name, last name, email address, and password). 2. Verify your email address by clicking the verification link sent from noreply@onestop.md.gov. 3. Click Apply Online and complete all required fields in the application (takes approximately 5-10 minutes). 4. MDA verifies that farms have a nutrient management plan or that seafood dealers have an active DNR Tidal Fish Dealer license. 5. Upon verification, you will receive notification about certification status through OneStop. Once certified, your contact information, list of products, and certification number are placed in the public Certified Local Farm and Fish Directory for state agencies to access.

The incentive allows farmers to subtract eligible equipment purchases from taxable income on Maryland individual and corporate tax returns, reducing their overall tax liability.
