structured_extraction.program_description: A premium incentive program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture that pays farmers higher rates to plant cover crop mixes on the same fields for 3 consecutive years to improve soil health, encourage biodiversity, and increase residue management. Farmers agree to maintain a living root system throughout the year and use enhanced cover crop practices. The program offers enhanced grants and payments for cover crop adoption with additional conservation benefits beyond standard cover crop programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Base payment of $125 per acre per year for growing cover crop mixes. Optional add-on practices can increase reimbursement up to $180 per acre per year. Farmers sign a 3-year contract and may enroll up to 500 acres. Enhanced grants for cover crop adoption with additional conservation incentives are also available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers who operate agricultural land in Maryland and want to improve soil health through cover crop practices, including those seeking additional conservation benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cover crop seed and management on enrolled fields for 3 consecutive years. Farmers must maintain multispecies cover crop mixes with at least 50% cereal grain or ryegrass and at least 25% legume, with 30% residue maintained. Funds support cover crop installation and adoption with additional conservation practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Farmers must meet the State of Maryland's definition of an agricultural operation.
requirements_list: Must meet Maryland's definition of an agricultural operation
If leasing land, must confirm enrolled acres will be under your care for the entire 3-year contract period

Must be in good standing with the Maryland Nutrient Management Program, Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program, Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation Program, and other MDA conservation grant programs
Must submit current Nutrient Management Plan Certification with application
Fall cover crops must be planted by October 15 or within 10 days of harvesting the previous crop
Only no-till or conservation tillage may be used throughout the 3-year contract
Multispecies cover crop mixes required with cereal grain/ryegrass making up at least 50% and legume making up at least 25%
Must maintain 30% residue
May enroll up to 500 acres
Optional add-on practices must be new practices not used in the previous 3 years on the enrolled field

Wait for your approval letter before proceeding. Contact your local soil conservation district for technical assistance if needed.

The program uses a tiered system to reward farms that adopt practices like conservation tillage, cover crops, buffers, wildlife habitats, renewable energy, and community involvement such as research participation, mentorship, and food security initiatives. The program also promotes and supports environmentally engaged farming practices among agricultural producers in Maryland through training and technical assistance.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Farms earning points through implementation of conservation and community practices qualify for tiered certification (Certified, Silver, Gold, Platinum). Technical assistance and training are also provided to support environmentally engaged farming practices.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds or incentives support implementation of conservation practices such as conservation tillage, nutrient input reductions, cover crops, natural filters, buffers, wildlife and pollinator habitats, healthy soils practices, and on-farm renewable energy adoption. Community-focused activities include participation in research, mentorship, food bank service, and nutrition programs. Training and technical support for sustainable farming practices are also provided.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program helps cover the cost of transporting manure to farms with low phosphorus fields or to alternative use facilities. Payments are available to eligible farmers or registered manure brokers to move poultry, dairy, and livestock manure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For poultry manure: up to $28 per ton to transport poultry litter. For dairy and livestock manure: up to 87.5 percent of all eligible costs, with payment rates based on transport distance and type of manure (liquid or solid). FastTrack option allows farmers or manure brokers to haul manure now and apply for reimbursement later.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible farmers and registered manure brokers in Maryland who raise broiler chickens for participating Delmarva poultry companies or operate dairy and livestock operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To cover the cost of transporting manure to farms with low phosphorus fields or to alternative use facilities. Poultry litter must be land applied as a nutrient source for an agricultural crop or sent to an approved alternative use facility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Sending farm must be located in Maryland and raise broiler chickens for one of the participating Delmarva poultry companies. Poultry litter must be transported more than 7 miles from the sending farm. Dairy and livestock manure must be transported more than 1 mile from the sending source.
requirements_list: Applicants must submit a current nutrient management plan
For poultry: receiving farm fields must have a soil phosphorus Fertility Index Value of 100 or less (nitrogen-based) or 101-150 (phosphorus-based); fields with value greater than 150 are not eligible
For dairy and livestock: receiving farm fields must have a phosphorus Fertility Index Value below 101
Manure must be applied to crops or hay fields containing less than 25 percent legumes
For dairy and livestock: grants based on maximum application rates of 6,000 gallons per acre for liquid/slurry manure or 10 tons per acre for solid/semi-solid manure
Either the farmer or the manure broker (not both) may apply for cost-share reimbursement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Farmers apply through the local soil conservation district or directly to the Maryland Department of Agriculture (for registered manure brokers). Applicants submit a current nutrient management plan. FastTrack option allows hauling now with application for reimbursement later. Completed forms are mailed to the Maryland Department of Agriculture, Conservation Grants, 50 Harry S. Truman Parkway, Room 207, Annapolis, MD 21401.

structured_extraction.program_description: A USDA-certified agricultural mediation program that helps farmers, agricultural lenders, agencies, families, and members of the public resolve disputes collaboratively outside of traditional legal and regulatory processes. The service provides neutral, voluntary, and confidential mediation to address agricultural conflicts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Initial consultation with program staff and the initial mediation session are provided at no cost. If additional sessions are necessary, nominal costs are shared between participants. Full or partial fee waivers may be negotiated based on income. Participants pay for any legal, financial, or technical advisors if needed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers, farmers, agricultural lenders, agencies, families, and members of the general public with disputes related to agricultural operations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mediation services to resolve disputes including unfavorable USDA agency decisions, conflicts between farmers and non-farming neighbors, agricultural credit issues, land or equipment leasing disputes, family farm planning, and retirement or transition planning
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Dispute must concern agricultural production or involve agricultural operations
Both parties must be willing to participate in mediation
Participants must complete the ACReS Mediation Intake Form
Agricultural operations include aquaculture, tree farms, beekeeping, horticulture, and urban farming
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An agricultural producer or individual with a dispute contacts Maryland ACReS and completes the ACReS Mediation Intake Form. Maryland ACReS staff confirms the other party's willingness to participate and gathers a brief description of the situation. A mediator is assigned by the Mediation Coordinator. All parties are notified of the mediation session date, time, and neutral location. Most mediation sessions conclude in two to three hours.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial aid is provided to qualifying agricultural fair and show organizations for premium awards to exhibitors of agricultural displays at county fairs and shows held in July, August, September, and October, as well as the Maryland State Fair held annually at Timonium in Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural fair and show organizations throughout Maryland that provide premium awards to exhibitors of agricultural products and livestock.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Established in 1977, the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) is a statewide purchase of development rights program that permanently protects productive agricultural land and woodland from residential, commercial, or industrial development. The Foundation purchases perpetual agricultural conservation easements from qualifying landowners, who retain ownership and continue farming while permanently restricting development on the property. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture with local participation through county program administrators and Agricultural Preservation Advisory Boards. It helps maintain a viable local base of food and fiber production, prevents random urban sprawl, protects open spaces and wildlife habitats, and improves the environmental quality of the Chesapeake Bay. The state has invested over $900 million in the program, preserving land across all 23 Maryland counties.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Foundation purchases perpetual agricultural conservation easements on qualifying farmland and woodland at a price equal to the asking price or the difference between appraised fair market value and agricultural value, whichever is less, up to a maximum of 75% of the appraised fair market value. Recent payments have ranged from approximately $600 to over $10,000 per acre. Landowners retain ownership and may continue all agricultural uses. The program is completely voluntary and administered at the county level through a Program Administrator and local Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board. Landowners who sell easements for less than full appraised value may also qualify for federal and state tax benefits. Baltimore County landowners may alternatively donate easements for tax benefits. Applications are accepted in spring each cycle year, ranked by the local Agricultural Land Preservation Advisory Board, approved by County Commissioners, and submitted to MALPF prior to July 1st.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Spring of each cycle year; submitted to MALPF prior to July 1st; Talbot County deadline: April 1, 2026; Cecil County deadlines vary by funding round
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of productive farmland and/or woodland throughout Maryland who wish to voluntarily sell or donate development rights to permanently preserve their land for agricultural use. Program is administered locally by county program administrators and Agricultural Preservation Advisory Boards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Proceeds from easement sales can be used by landowners for any purpose including financing farm purchases, retirement, estate planning, improving farming operations, investing in new farm products, financing home restoration, or paying off debt. Easements permanently restrict the property to agricultural use in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across all 23 Maryland counties. Property must be located outside a ten-year water and sewer service area. Individual county programs may have additional geographic requirements such as Agricultural Preservation Protection Areas (Baltimore County) or Priority Preservation Areas (Washington County). Cecil County has designated APOD (Agricultural Preservation Overlay District) areas.
requirements_list: Land must be productive agricultural land or woodland
Property must meet minimum size criteria (e.g., Anne Arundel County: 50+ acres of agricultural land OR 25+ acres of contiguous woodland; Baltimore County: 20+ acres if contiguous to a preserved farm)
Property must meet soil eligibility criteria
Must have a valid Soil Conservation and Water Quality Plan (SCWQP) on file with local Soil Conservation District (for agricultural land) or an active Forest Stewardship Plan (for woodland)
Property must be located outside a ten-year water and sewer service area
Easements are permanent and run with the land in perpetuity
Participation is completely voluntary
Property must be ranked competitively against other applicants
Landowner must commit to not develop, subdivide, or transfer the property while an easement application is pending
If farm is owned by an entity, required entity documents must be provided
Properties in Washington County must be enrolled in the County's Agricultural District program
All owners in title to the property must sign the application
For entity-owned properties, specific documentation is required including bylaws, partnership agreements, and proof of authority
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners submit applications through a competitive process administered at the county level. Applications are typically accepted in the spring each cycle year, with specific deadlines varying by county. The local Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board reviews and ranks properties based on soil quality, proximity to other easements, agricultural operation intensity, and proximity to growth areas. The County Commissioners approve ranked applications, which are then submitted to MALPF prior to July 1st. MALPF and local governments make offers based on available funding. Once an easement is purchased, properties are permanently restricted. Interested landowners should contact their local county program administrator or Foundation staff for information specific to their county. Applications may also include requests for lot exclusions and property subdivisions within the preservation program. County-specific forms and guidelines must be used, as they vary.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share (MACS) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program that provides farmers and landowners with financial assistance to help cover the cost of installing best management practices (BMPs) on their farms. These practices control soil erosion, manage nutrients, reduce agricultural sources of water pollution, and support Chesapeake Bay cleanup goals. The program also supports stream protection practices for livestock farmers including livestock watering facilities, stream fencing, stream crossings, and riparian forest buffers, helping farmers comply with nutrient management program setback requirements while protecting water quality and improving herd health.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants covering up to 100% of the cost for farmers to install conservation best management practices. For stream protection, provides up to 87.5% cost-share for livestock watering facilities, livestock exclusion fencing, and stream crossings. Up to 100% cost-share to plant riparian forest buffers, plus $2 per tree planted. Examples of eligible BMPs include grassed waterways to prevent gully erosion, streamside buffers of grass and trees to filter runoff, frost-free waterers, spring developments, and systems to safely handle and store animal manure.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Nutrient Management Training and Certification Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive training and certification program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) that provides education and credentialing for farmers, agricultural consultants, and green industry professionals in nutrient management. The program encompasses multiple components: (1) Nutrient Management Voucher Training — a mandatory 2-hour training course every three years for farmers who apply nutrients to 10 acres or more, offered in-person and online; (2) Fundamentals of Nutrient Management — an intensive two-day training course covering state nutrient management regulations, nutrient management principles, basic soil science, and soil fertility recommendations, held in early summer at MDA Headquarters in Annapolis; (3) Maryland Nutrient Management Certification Examination — a 100-question multiple-choice exam across twelve knowledge areas, offered annually in August at locations in Annapolis, Keedysville, and Easton, for those seeking to become certified nutrient management plan writers; and (4) Turfgrass Nutrient Management Training and Certification for green industry professionals, including in-person seminars, virtual webinars, and on-demand recorded courses covering enhanced efficiency fertilizers, soil testing, soil health, and nutrient management. Certified consultants must complete continuing education requirements to maintain their certification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program encompasses multiple training and certification components: (1) Nutrient Management Voucher Training: Free 2-hour training course (in-person and online) required every three years for farmers applying nutrients to 10 or more acres, offered by University of Maryland Extension and MDA through April 9, 2026. (2) Fundamentals of Nutrient Management: A two-day intensive training course held June 24-25, 2026 at MDA Headquarters in Annapolis, covering state nutrient management regulations, nutrient management principles, basic soil science, and soil fertility recommendations; taught by university and government experts. (3) Maryland Nutrient Management Certification Examination: A 100 multiple-choice question exam covering twelve knowledge areas, offered August 7, 2026 at locations in Annapolis, Keedysville, and Easton. Non-refundable $50 certification fee required; government personnel exempt with a Government Sales and Use Tax Exempt certificate. (4) Turfgrass Nutrient Management Training for Green Industry Professionals: In-person seminar on February 6, 2026 ($105, 3 CEUs), virtual webinars (2 CEUs each), and on-demand recorded webinars (1-2 CEUs each) covering enhanced efficiency fertilizers, soil testing, soil health, and nutrient management. Certified consultants must complete 6 hours of continuing education after the first year and 12 hours of continuing education every three years thereafter to renew certification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; specific sessions include: Nutrient Voucher Training through April 9, 2026; Fundamentals of Nutrient Management Training June 24-25, 2026; Certification Exam August 7, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers who apply nutrients to 10 acres or more (voucher training requirement); individuals planning to take the Maryland Nutrient Management Certification Examination; agricultural consultants and natural resource personnel seeking to become certified nutrient management plan writers; green industry professionals including pesticide and fertilizer applicators seeking recertification or professional development in turf nutrient management.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and education in nutrient management planning, soil science, soil fertility recommendations, state nutrient management regulations, and agricultural best practices. Covers compliance with Maryland nutrient management requirements, professional certification as a nutrient management plan writer, and continuing education for maintaining certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Training sessions held at multiple locations across Maryland including MDA Headquarters in Annapolis, Keedysville, and Easton. Turfgrass in-person seminar held in Annandale, Virginia but available to Maryland applicators. Online and virtual sessions available statewide. Some sessions offered in Baltimore County, Frederick County, and Washington County.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Spay and Neuter Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) that provides funding to local governments and non-profit animal welfare organizations to offer free spay and neuter services for pets of low-income Marylanders and for colonies of unowned, free-roaming community (feral) cats. Two grant opportunities are offered annually: a Pet Focused Grant for owned dogs and cats belonging to low-income Marylanders, and a Feral Cat Focused Grant for unowned, free-roaming community cats (where not prohibited by local law). Services may be delivered through in-house clinics, partnerships with area veterinarians and clinics, or a combination of both. Services may also include a free rabies vaccine. The program is funded entirely through mandatory annual fees of $100 per product paid by pet food manufacturers that sell cat or dog food in Maryland — not by taxpayer funds. The program's goal is to reduce the number of cats and dogs surrendered to and euthanized in Maryland shelters. Grant applications are reviewed by the Spay and Neuter Advisory Board (SNAB), which makes funding recommendations to the Maryland Secretary of Agriculture. MDA-funded organizations then deliver free spay and neuter services directly to eligible low-income pet owners in participating counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two competitive grants are awarded annually: (1) Pet Focused Grant — for providing free spay and neuter services to owned dogs and cats of low-income Marylanders; and (2) Feral Cat Focused Grant — for providing free spay and neuter services for unowned, free-roaming community cats. Services may also include a free rabies vaccine. The first fund allocation consists of 50% of the surgery funding amount and 100% of rabies vaccine and other applicable funding amounts. The second allocation is released once the grantee has spent 35% of their budget, consisting of the remaining 50% of surgery funding. First allocations typically arrive mid to late December. This is supplemental funding and is not intended to be the sole or primary source of funding for an organization. The program is funded entirely by fees from pet food manufacturers selling products in Maryland, not by taxpayer funds. Funding does not go directly to individuals; it flows to organizations that then deliver free services to eligible pet owners.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application window opens in early January and closes in early April; FY27 cycle closes April 17, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Primary applicants: local governments and non-profit animal welfare organizations providing spay and neuter services in Maryland. End beneficiaries: low-income pet owners in Maryland who own cats or dogs, and colonies of unowned, free-roaming community cats.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding must be used to provide free spay and neuter veterinary services (and may include free rabies vaccines) for: (1) owned dogs and cats belonging to low-income Marylanders (Pet Focused Grant); or (2) unowned, free-roaming community (feral) cats (Feral Cat Focused Grant). Services may be delivered via in-house clinic, partnership with area veterinarians and clinics, or a combination. Funding may not be used to spay/neuter shelter or rescue animals prior to placement, and does not fund services for both owned pets and feral cats within the same grant.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. All animals and owners receiving services must reside in Maryland. Applying organizations and veterinary clinics do not need to be based in Maryland. Individual projects may cover specific areas or zip codes within counties; coverage varies by MDA-funded organization. Low-income individuals in Queen Anne's County must have a household income under $60,000 annually to qualify through that county's program.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit competitive grant applications during the annual open window (typically early January to early April; FY27 closes April 17, 2026). The Program Coordinator completes due diligence on submitted applications by mid-May and forwards them to the Spay and Neuter Advisory Board (SNAB) for review. The SNAB reviews and scores applications during May–July. In August, the SNAB meets to determine funding recommendations to the Maryland Secretary of Agriculture. Recommendations are provided to the Secretary shortly after the SNAB meeting. The Program Coordinator then notifies applicants of the SNAB's recommendations. If the project remains feasible with any recommended changes, a Grant Contract is created (typically mid to late September) and signed by the applicant in September–October. First fund allocations typically arrive in mid to late December. For individual low-income pet owners seeking free services: find the MDA-funded organization serving your county or area, contact that organization directly to verify eligibility, and arrange spay or neuter services. Queen Anne's County residents may submit the Maryland Spay/Neuter Grant Application and required documents directly through the Queen Anne's County Animal Services online portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides farmers and landowners with incentive payments to plant streamside buffers on farmland to improve stream health and Chesapeake Bay water quality. Offers payment for establishing forest buffers, grass buffers, or watercourse access control areas adjacent to streams, ditches, or pastures. Also supports the establishment of riparian forest buffers with pasture fencing to protect water quality and wildlife habitat. Contracts are for 5 or 10 years, with maintenance payments available during the first five years after planting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Payment rates range from $500 per acre for an existing grass buffer to a maximum of $4,500 per acre to install a riparian forest buffer with pasture fencing. Farmers receive 75% of project costs upfront and 25% after verification of planting. Additional one-time tree bonus payments of $1,000 per acre are available for forest buffers. Annual maintenance payments up to $330 per acre per year are available for forest buffers during the first five years after planting. Contracts are for 5 or 10 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and landowners who manage eligible lands and are responsible for cropland or pasture management next to streams or ditches.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting and establishing streamside buffers (forest buffers, grass buffers, or watercourse access control areas) on farmland adjacent to streams, ditches, or pastures. Funds can be used for installation costs and maintenance of forest buffers for the first five years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland program. Eligible land must be adjacent to streams, ditches, or pastures and have established cropping history or be adjacent to highly erodible or hydric soils. Farmers apply through their local soil conservation district.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a farmer or landowner responsible for managing eligible lands
Farmers who lease land must certify an active lease for the term of the buffer or provide written agreement from landowner
Applicant must be in good standing with USDA and state cost-share programs
Current Nutrient Management Plan Certification is required
Cropland must have established cropping history in pasture, commodity crops, or hay
Areas must be adjacent to streams, ditches, or pastures with highly erodible or hydric soils as determined by soil conservation district
Existing buffers or lands actively enrolled in state (MACS) or federal programs (CRP, CREP, EQIP) or mandated by easement are not eligible
Forest buffers must be between 35 and 100 feet wide
Grass buffers must be between 10 and 100 feet wide
Watercourse access control areas must be 10 to 100 feet wide (minimum 35 feet if establishing woody vegetation)
Planting must occur within 1 year of signed agreement
Mowing and hay harvesting for own use allowed; nutrient applications not allowed
No grazing allowed in access control areas
Must plant riparian forest buffer with pasture fencing (for riparian forest buffer payments)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local soil conservation district to apply during the annual open enrollment period from November 1, 2025 through April 30, 2026. Download the fillable application form and complete it with required documentation. Submit the application along with a map showing buffer location and acreage, a signed Nutrient Management Plan Certification Form, and a signed IRS Form W-9 to your local soil conservation district. Soil conservation districts provide free technical assistance with buffer installation. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture that awards funds to Maryland farmers and organizations working with farmers to implement innovative soil health conservation practices over 3 years. The program supports practices that minimize soil disturbance, maximize soil cover, enhance biodiversity, and increase living roots presence, including agroforestry practices to improve soil health and build climate resilience.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants award up to $50,000 per applicant to support 3 years of enhanced soil health practices. Grant recipients receive a portion of funds (not to exceed 30%) upfront, with the remainder distributed annually following verification of progress. Funds may be used for conservation practice implementation, equipment purchase, project staff time, and research costs. Applicants are encouraged to rent equipment or purchase used equipment where possible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application period for 2025-2026 is now closed; typically begins in January and runs for approximately 8 weeks
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual farmers or groups of farmers operating in Maryland, and individuals or organizations working with farmers in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of soil health conservation practices including cover crops, conservation tillage, pasture and hay planting, conservation cover, critical area planting, conservation crop rotation, nutrient management, integrated pest management, prescribed grazing, soil carbon amendment, and agroforestry practices such as alley cropping, hedgerow planting, windbreak or shelterbelt establishment, silvopasture, and tree and shrub establishment. Funds may also cover equipment purchase, project staff time, and research costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to agricultural operations operating in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must propose enhanced soil health practices

Agricultural operation(s) applying or partnering must have gross annual income of $2,500 or more (or $2,500 or more of donated agricultural products if a non-profit entity) and/or manage 8 or more animal units (8,000 pounds of live animal weight)
No minimum or maximum acreage requirements
Applicants must provide proof of compliance with Maryland's nutrient management requirements at time of application by submitting a Current Nutrient Management Plan Certification Form

Labor included in application budgets must be directly related to project implementation and should not be connected to existing activities, general farm operations, or long-term implementation of practices
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a completed application including project narrative, project budget, and appropriate templates (cover crop, grazing, tree and shrub planting, or grass and forb planting), along with proof of compliance with Maryland's nutrient management requirements. The application period typically begins in January and runs for approximately 8 weeks. Visit the Healthy Soils website for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program established by the Maryland Department of Agriculture in conjunction with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to test the feasibility of controlling midge populations in the Back River area using Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis (Bti), a naturally occurring soil bacterium. The program aims to determine the impact of Bti on midge populations and identify the most cost-effective dosage and frequency of treatments.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This is an informational page about a pilot program focused on midge control through the application of Bti by boat and/or helicopter. The page does not describe direct financial or technical assistance provided to eligible recipients.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Back River area

structured_extraction.program_description: A free service that collects and properly disposes of unusable or unwanted pesticide materials for farmers and agricultural producers. The program collects any product with a registration number from the EPA or USDA, and tests unknown materials to ensure safe disposal.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free collection and disposal of pesticide materials. MDA contracts a licensed hazardous waste hauler to collect pesticide materials directly from the storage site and transport to an EPA-approved disposal facility. Funding comes from licensing, certification, and registration fees collected from pesticide businesses, certified applicators, and pesticide manufacturers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current or retired farmers and agricultural producers, including orchardists, nurserymen, greenhouse operators, and Christmas tree growers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Disposal of unusable or unwanted pesticide materials and products with EPA or USDA registration numbers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a current or retired farmer or agricultural producer (orchardists, nurserymen, greenhouse operators, or Christmas tree growers)
Complete and submit the registration form to the Pesticide Regulation Section
Must have pesticide materials that need disposal
An MDA inspector will verify information with a site visit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the registration form (available as a fillable PDF) and submit it via email to rob.hofstetter@maryland.gov or mail to the Pesticide Regulation Section. After reviewing applications, an MDA inspector will schedule a site visit to verify information. Once MDA has a complete inventory of materials needing disposal, they will contract a licensed hazardous waste hauler to collect the materials and transport them to an EPA-approved disposal facility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that builds resilience in the middle of the food supply chain by providing funding for infrastructure projects that expand markets for small farms and food businesses, support value-added product development, encourage fair prices and wages, and create safe job opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from a minimum of $100,000 to a maximum of $3 million for three-year projects. Applicants must contribute 50 percent of the total project cost as matching funds. Historically underserved farmers and ranchers and small businesses qualifying under Small Business Administration standards including small disadvantaged businesses, women-owned small businesses, and veteran-owned small businesses only need to contribute 25 percent matching funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small farms, food businesses, food processors, aggregators, distributors, and other entities working with local food products. Priority consideration for historically underserved farmers and ranchers and small businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cold storage equipment, processing and aggregation facilities, distribution infrastructure, construction of new facilities, employee training, and modernizing manufacturing, tracking, storage, and information technology systems. Funds support aggregation, processing, storing, transporting, wholesaling, and distribution of local food products including specialty crops, dairy, grains for human consumption, aquaculture, and other food products, excluding meat and poultry.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Based on statewide outreach through surveys and virtual meetings.
requirements_list: Applicants must provide 50 percent matching funds (25 percent for historically underserved farmers, ranchers, and qualifying small businesses)
Projects must be for three years
Applicants must include a USDA Applicant Environmental Questionnaire with their application
Applicants must demonstrate critical resources and infrastructure
Minimum grant award is $100,000
Maximum grant award is $3 million
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an Infrastructure Equipment Grant application or Equipment Only Grant application. Applications must include the USDA Applicant Environmental Questionnaire, match verification documentation, and evidence of critical resources and infrastructure. Applicants use the RFSI Budget-Match Worksheet to document matching funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports cover crop adoption on smaller acreage farms.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to support cover crop adoption on small acreage farms.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small acreage farm owners
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cover crop adoption and implementation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Small Farm and Urban Agriculture Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides financial assistance to support small-scale agricultural operations located in urban, peri-urban, rural, and suburban areas. It aims to increase community access to healthy foods by helping farmers improve their management of natural resources by adopting Bay-friendly and climate-smart farming practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers Small Acreage Cover Crop Grants in the spring and fall, and Water and Power Grants for qualifying operations located in urban areas. Specific funding amounts and terms are not detailed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, organized for-profit agricultural businesses, or non-profit organizations with farm operations that generate a minimum of $1,000 of sales or donations annually.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants support farmers in improving their management of natural resources by adopting Bay-friendly and climate-smart farming practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The farm product must be grown or raised in the state of Maryland. Operations must be located in urban, peri-urban, rural, or suburban areas.
requirements_list: Operation must produce a farm product that generates a minimum of $1,000 of sales or donations annually
Grantee is responsible for all local, state, or federal regulations and permits necessary for the agricultural operation
Farm product must be grown or raised in the state of Maryland

Eligible farm products include any agricultural, horticultural, vegetable, or fruit product; livestock, meats, marine food products, poultry, eggs, or dairy products; equine operations; wool, hides, feathers, or honey; or any product of farm, forest, orchard, garden, or water

structured_extraction.program_description: An incentive program that provides bonus payments to farmers and landowners who install qualifying conservation practices financed through the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program. The incentive aims to help Maryland achieve its tree-planting goal to capture greenhouse gas emissions that contribute to climate change.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible farmers receive $2 for each new tree planted as part of an approved conservation practice. This payment is in addition to the regular cost-share rate for the qualifying practice. Available for Windbreak Establishment ($2 per tree plus up to 100% cost-share), Silvopasture ($2 per tree plus up to 87.5% cost-share), Riparian Forest Buffer ($2 per tree plus up to 100% cost-share), Hedgerow Planting ($2 per tree plus up to 100% cost-share), and Tree and Shrub Establishment ($2 per tree plus up to 100% cost-share).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and landowners in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting as part of qualifying conservation practices including windbreak establishment, silvopasture, riparian forest buffer, hedgerow planting, and tree and shrub establishment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be eligible for the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program
Must install a qualifying conservation practice
Must plant new trees as part of an approved conservation practice
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share Program

structured_extraction.program_name: Urban Agriculture Water and Power Infrastructure Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program helps urban farms and community gardens purchase and install equipment to access water and electricity needed for their operations. It provides up to 87.5% of the total project cost, with a maximum funding limit of $75,000 per application. The program supports water and power infrastructure improvements for urban agriculture operations statewide in Maryland, with annual program funding of up to $500,000 through Fiscal Year 2027.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants cover up to 87.5% of total project costs for purchasing and installing water and electricity infrastructure. Eligible expenses include water meters, water pipes, irrigation hoses, electric meters, electrical lines, and other department-authorized equipment. Maximum funding per application is $75,000. Annual program funding is up to $500,000 through Fiscal Year 2027.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis as long as funds remain available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Urban farms and community gardens that produce farm products generating a minimum of $1,000 in annual sales or donations and are located in urban areas or incorporated municipalities in Maryland, including urban farmers and agricultural organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water meters, water pipes, irrigation hoses, electric meters, electrical lines, and other equipment authorized by the department for accessing water and electricity infrastructure for urban farms.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Operations must be located in urban areas as defined by the United States Census Bureau and any incorporated municipality recognized by the State of Maryland. Applicants should use the interactive map to verify property eligibility. Program is available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Produce a farm product generating a minimum of $1,000 in annual sales or donations
Comply with all local, state, and federal regulations and secure required project permits
Property must be located in an urban area or incorporated municipality (verify using interactive map)
Applicant must have controlled the land for at least 5 years through ownership or leasing
Bids required from authorized contractors for work on public roads, sidewalks, water mains, and transformers
Bids required from private contractors for on-site installation services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Check the interactive map to verify your property meets location criteria. If eligible, download the application packet and complete it. Submit applications on an ongoing basis as long as funds remain available. Contact the Program Administrator for questions or assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Assessment Exemption for an Improvement Required for the Health or Medical Condition of a Resident
structured_extraction.program_description: Property tax exemption for new improvements, changes, or additions to residential buildings that are medically necessary for the health or medical condition of a resident. The exemption applies statewide and is designed to ensure that property owners who make health-required modifications—such as wheelchair ramps, accessibility modifications, or other structural changes mandated by a resident's medical need—are not penalized with higher property tax assessments for those improvements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exemption from property tax assessment for the value added by new improvements, changes, or additions to residential buildings necessitated by the health or medical condition of a resident. The exemption amount may not exceed 10% of the total market value of the property (10% of land and improvement combined). The exemption is based on an application prepared by the property owner's physician demonstrating medical necessity or required physical convenience. Upon approval, the exemption is given for the current tax year in which the application is received. The exemption is removed for the next full tax year after transfer or notification that the individual whose medical condition required the improvement no longer resides in the building.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners making health or medically necessary improvements or modifications to their residential buildings, including residents with disabilities or health conditions requiring structural changes such as wheelchair ramps or accessibility modifications.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption for new improvements, changes, or additions to residential buildings made necessary by the health or medical condition of a resident, such as wheelchair ramps, accessibility modifications, or structural changes required by medical need.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Applies to residential real estate only. Application must be submitted to the local county assessment office where the property is located.
requirements_list: Improvement must be made to a residential building
Improvement must be necessitated by the health or medical condition of a resident
Sufficient evidence of medical necessity or required physical convenience must be presented
Application must be prepared by the physician of the property owner
Exemption amount may not exceed 10% of total market value of real property (land and improvement combined)
Improvement must add value to the property
Exemption is removed if property is transferred or if individual whose medical condition required the improvement no longer resides in the building
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Improvement Required for Health or Medical Condition of Resident Exemption Application to the local county assessment office where the property is located. The application form is available on the Maryland SDAT website. The application must be prepared by the property owner's physician and include sufficient evidence of medical necessity or required physical convenience.

structured_extraction.program_description: Property tax exemption for real property owned and actually used exclusively for charitable purposes by eligible charitable organizations.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Complete exemption from state, county, and municipal property taxes for real property owned by a charitable organization and used exclusively for charitable purposes. Organization must own the property prior to the beginning of the tax year (July 1) for which exemption is sought. Organization may apply by September 1 following the beginning of the taxable year for which exemption is sought. Property must meet ownership and actual exclusive use tests. For newly constructed buildings, the building permit must be issued as of July 1. Once exemption is granted based on building permit issuance, the organization must make continual progress in building permanent improvements or the exemption may be withdrawn.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: By September 1 following the beginning of the taxable year for which exemption is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charitable organizations that own property used exclusively for charitable purposes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption applies to real property used exclusively for charitable purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Application must be submitted to the local county office where the property is located.
requirements_list: Organization must be a charitable organization
Organization must own the property prior to July 1 of the tax year for which exemption is sought
Property must be actually used exclusively for charitable purposes
Organization must apply by September 1 following the beginning of the taxable year
For new construction, building permit must be issued as of July 1
Organization must demonstrate continual progress if exemption granted based on building permit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Charitable Exemption Application to the local county assessment office where the property is located by September 1 following the beginning of the taxable year for which exemption is sought. Application must demonstrate ownership and actual exclusive use for charitable purposes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Churches, Parsonages, Convents, Religious Educational Buildings, and Church Cemeteries Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: Property tax exemption for real property owned and actually used exclusively for religious purposes, including churches, parsonages, convents, religious educational buildings, and church cemeteries.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Complete exemption from state, county, and municipal property taxes for real property owned by a religious organization and used exclusively for religious purposes such as churches, parsonages, convents, religious educational buildings, and church cemeteries. Organization must own the property prior to the beginning of the tax year (July 1) for which exemption is sought. Organization may apply by September 1 following the beginning of the taxable year for which exemption is sought. Property must meet ownership and actual exclusive use tests. For newly constructed buildings, the building permit must be issued as of July 1. Property used for caretakers' houses or other purposes not directly related to the stated exempt purpose will not qualify.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: By September 1 following the beginning of the taxable year for which exemption is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Religious organizations that own property used exclusively for religious purposes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption applies to real property used exclusively for religious purposes including churches, parsonages, convents, religious educational buildings, and church cemeteries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Application must be submitted to the local county office where the property is located.
requirements_list: Organization must be a religious organization
Organization must own the property prior to July 1 of the tax year for which exemption is sought
Property must be used exclusively for religious purposes such as public religious worship, education related to religious purposes, or cemetery purposes
Organization must apply by September 1 following the beginning of the taxable year
For new construction, building permit must be issued as of July 1
Property cannot include uses such as caretakers' houses that are not directly related to the exempt religious purposes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Religious Organization-Owned Property Exemption Application to the local county assessment office where the property is located by September 1 following the beginning of the taxable year for which exemption is sought. Application must demonstrate ownership and actual exclusive use for religious purposes.

structured_extraction.program_description: Property tax exemption for the principal residence of an active-duty service member who has a service-connected physical disability reasonably certain to continue for the life of the service member.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Complete exemption from state, county, and municipal property taxes on the principal residence of a disabled active-duty service member. The disability must be service-connected, not caused by misconduct, and reasonably certain to continue for the life of the service member. Applicant must provide physician certification or VA certification of the disability and proof of active duty status verified by Commanding Officer. Certification of active-duty status must be provided annually to continue receiving the exemption.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active-duty service members with service-connected physical disabilities who own their principal residence in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption applies to the principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Applicant must be legally resident in the State of Maryland. Application must be submitted to the local county office where the property is located.
requirements_list: Service member must be on active military duty
Service-connected physical disability must be reasonably certain to continue for the life of the service member
Disability cannot be caused by misconduct of the service member
Service member must provide certification of disability from a Maryland-licensed physician or Veterans Administration
Service member must provide proof of active duty status verified by Commanding Officer
Service member must be a legal resident of Maryland
Service member must provide updated Certification of Active-Duty Status annually
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Disabled Active-Duty Service Member Exemption Application to the local county assessment office where the property is located. Application must include physician or VA certification of disability, proof of active-duty status from Commanding Officer, and annual Certification of Active-Duty Status.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide Maryland program that helps homeowners of limited income avoid tax sale by keeping their home out of tax sale for at least three years and assisting them with paying back property taxes owed so they can keep their home. The program is available in all Maryland counties, including Queen Anne's and Talbot Counties. Enrollment is limited and eligibility does not guarantee enrollment. Priority enrollment is given to homeowners aged 60 or older, those receiving federal disability benefits (Social Security Disability Insurance or Supplemental Security Income), or those whose dwelling has been their principal residence for 10 or more years.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides financial assistance to help homeowners of limited income pay back property taxes owed on their principal residence, protecting the home from tax sale for at least three years. Eligible homeowners must have an assessed value not exceeding $300,000, combined annual household income not exceeding $60,000, and total assets not exceeding $200,000 (excluding the dwelling). Enrollment is limited and eligibility does not guarantee enrollment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners of limited income whose home is their principal residence and who are at risk of tax sale.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance with paying back property taxes owed to prevent tax sale of the homeowner's principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland program available in all counties, including Queen Anne's County and Talbot County.
requirements_list: Dwelling must be applicant homeowner's principal residence
Assessed value must not exceed $300,000
Combined annual household income must not exceed $60,000
Total value of assets must not exceed $200,000, not including the value of the dwelling
Must be a homeowner of limited income
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply online through the Maryland One-Stop portal (recommended for faster processing) or submit the HPP application form. Visit https://dat.maryland.gov/homeowners for more information or contact the State Tax Sale Ombudsman at (410) 767-4994 or (833) 732-8411 (toll free), or email sdat.taxsale@maryland.gov. Priority enrollment is given to homeowners aged 60 or older, those receiving federal disability benefits (Social Security Disability Insurance or Supplemental Security Income), or those whose dwelling has been their principal residence for 10 or more years.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland State program, administered by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, that provides credits against the real property tax bill for homeowners whose property taxes exceed a fixed percentage of their gross household income. The program sets a limit on the amount of property taxes any homeowner must pay based on their income level, making it available to all homeowners regardless of age. The credit formula is: 0% of the first $8,000 of household income, 4% of the next $4,000, 6.5% of the next $4,000, and 9% of all income above $16,000. The credit only applies to taxes on the first $300,000 of assessed property valuation. Several counties — including Baltimore County, Calvert County, Montgomery County, and St. Mary's County — offer supplemental local credits on top of the state credit. St. Mary's County residents age 70 and older who receive the state credit may also receive an additional county credit up to the remaining tax bill. The program was originally created in 1975 to assist the elderly but has since been expanded to people of all ages based on income requirements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners receive a credit applied directly to their property tax bill if property taxes exceed a calculated limit based on household income. The credit is determined by a formula: 0% of the first $8,000 of household income, 4% of the next $4,000, 6.5% of the next $4,000, and 9% of all income above $16,000. The credit applies only to taxes on the first $300,000 of assessed property valuation. Homeowners who apply by April 15 receive the credit deducted from their initial July tax bill; those who apply between April 16 and October 1 receive a revised tax bill or refund check. Several counties offer supplemental local credits: Baltimore County provides a supplemental credit for homeowners with documented hardship; Montgomery County offers a supplemental credit and a Senior Tax Credit (age 65+); Calvert County supplements the state credit using county funds (program in effect since July 1, 2006); and St. Mary's County provides an additional credit for residents age 70 and older equal to or up to the remaining tax bill less the Bay Restoration Fund fee. Property taxes eligible for the credit do not include metropolitan charges or taxes on business-use portions, excess land acreage, or other buildings. The maximum household income to qualify is $60,000 and net worth (excluding home value and qualified retirement savings/IRAs) cannot exceed $200,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1 of each year; apply by April 15 for credit to be deducted from the initial July tax bill. Applications accepted between February 1 and October 1. Some counties extend the deadline to October 31. Baltimore County and Calvert County deadline is September 1 (often extended to October 31).
structured_extraction.contact_name: Eric Jackson (Chief of Treasury, Charles County); State Department of Assessments and Taxation Tax Credit Office
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners of all ages whose property taxes exceed a fixed percentage of their gross household income, including seniors age 65 and older and residents age 70 and older in certain counties who may qualify for additional local credits. Homeowners must meet income and net worth requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit applied directly to the homeowner's real property tax bill to reduce property tax liability on the principal residence. Local supplemental credits further reduce county property tax obligations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. The dwelling must be the applicant's principal residence where they live at least six months of the year, including July 1, unless they are a recent home purchaser or are unable to do so due to health or need of special care. County-specific supplemental credits apply only within the respective county (Baltimore County, Calvert County, Montgomery County, St. Mary's County, Charles County, Queen Anne's County, Cecil County, Somerset County, etc.).
requirements_list: Must own or have a legal interest in the property

The dwelling must be the applicant's principal residence where they live at least six months of the year, including July 1 (exceptions for recent home purchasers or those with health/special care needs)
Net worth (excluding home value and qualified retirement savings/IRAs) must be less than $200,000
Combined gross household income cannot exceed $60,000
Must report total income from all sources including nontaxable retirement benefits such as Social Security and Railroad Retirement
Must submit copies of prior year federal income tax returns
Must provide permission to verify income with other State and Federal agencies
Property assessment for credit purposes cannot exceed $300,000
Property taxes must exceed the specified tax limit for the household income level
Property taxes eligible for credit do not include metropolitan charges or taxes on business use portions
Must file a new application every year
Homeowners 70 or older in St. Mary's County who received the HTC may qualify for an additional county credit up to the remaining tax bill
Homeowners 70 or older in Baltimore County may qualify for an additional credit with different requirements
For Baltimore County supplemental credit: property must be primary residence and applicant must already receive Homeowners Tax Credit or other specified credits
For Montgomery County Senior Tax Credit: must be age 65 and over with additional restrictions
Must be a residential homeowner meeting income requirements (Charles County)
Completed HTC-60 application form with copy of federal income tax return (Calvert County)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications can be filed online at onestop.md.gov or mailed to the State Department of Assessments & Taxation at P.O. Box 49005, Baltimore, MD 21297. Do not email applications. For prospective home buyers, apply at least 30 days before the expected settlement date. Homeowners who file by April 15 receive the credit deducted from their July tax bill; those filing after April 15 (up to October 1) receive a revised tax bill or refund check. Homeowners must reapply each year between February 1 and October 1. Once approved, homeowners receive renewal applications by mail annually. Benefits Data Trust can help low-income homeowners complete applications. In Charles County, complete Application Form HTC and submit to the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. In Calvert County, complete the HTC-60 form with a copy of your federal income tax return — one application covers both state and county credits; forms are available from the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation or the Calvert County Treasurer's Office. In Cecil County, obtain the first application from the Assessment Office or Cecil County Finance Office; credits approved for applications received after May 1 will be refunded by the Cecil County Finance Office after tax bill payment. In Somerset County, apply online at onestop.md.gov or obtain a paper copy from the Somerset County Tax Collection Office, 11916 Somerset Avenue, Room 116, Princess Anne, MD 21853. In Montgomery County, a single application form covers the State HOTC, Montgomery County Supplemental Homeowners Property Tax Credit, and Montgomery County Senior Tax Credit. Applications are also available at senior centers in Calvert County and all senior activity centers in St. Mary's County.

structured_extraction.program_name: Manufacturing and Research and Development Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax exemption program that allows local governments to exempt personal property used in manufacturing or research and development activities from taxation, designed to encourage the growth of manufacturing businesses in Maryland. Businesses engaged in manufacturing and research and development operations may apply annually to their local jurisdiction for exemption on qualifying personal property assets.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local governments may exempt from taxation personal property used in manufacturing or research and development operations. Businesses apply annually by submitting a detailed application that includes an explanation of their manufacturing or R&D process, an itemized list of assets for which exemption is claimed, and documentation of how the assets are used in the process. Applicants must provide a categorized detailed depreciation schedule and report all expenses and fully depreciated property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Manufacturing businesses and research and development operations in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The exemption applies to personal property used in manufacturing or research and development activities, including equipment and operations. Applicants must provide a categorized detailed depreciation schedule and itemized list of assets for which exemption is claimed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland. Local governments administer the exemption at the local level.
requirements_list: Business must engage in manufacturing or research and development activities
Detailed explanation of the manufacturing or research and development process required
Itemized list of assets for which exemption is claimed
Description of how assets are used in the manufacturing or research and development process
Copies of supporting documents must be supplied
All expenses and fully depreciated property must be reported
Application must be submitted by September 1st of each year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete the 14-question application form and provide the required documentation including an explanation of their manufacturing or R&D process, an itemized list of assets with depreciation schedules, and documentation of asset use. Optional materials such as photos, flowcharts, technical brochures, or product catalogs may be submitted to help support the application. The completed application should be submitted to the local jurisdiction by September 1st annually. For assistance, contact the Personal Property Division at (410) 767-1170 or toll free 1-888-246-5941.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Homestead Property Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state property tax relief program enacted in 1977 that protects homeowners from large increases in property taxes on their principal residence by limiting the annual increase in taxable assessments to a fixed percentage. Every county and municipality in Maryland is required to limit taxable assessment increases to 10% or less each year for state tax purposes, while counties and municipalities may set their own Homestead Credit Percentage between 0% and 10% for local property taxation (e.g., Cecil County caps county increases at 8%). The credit is calculated on any assessment increase exceeding the annual cap, meaning homeowners pay no property tax on the market value increase above the limit. Beginning in 2008, homeowners are required to submit a one-time tax credit application to establish eligibility; once qualified, the credit is automatically applied to subsequent tax bills when assessment increases exceed the applicable threshold. New homeowners are mailed an application after their deed is recorded.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A state tax credit calculated on any assessment increase exceeding the homestead cap (10% for state tax purposes, or the lower cap enacted by local governments — e.g., 8% in Cecil County) from one year to the next. The credit is applied to property taxes owed on the excess assessment. For example, if the old assessment was $100,000 and the new assessment is $120,000, a 10% cap means the taxable assessment is capped at $110,000; the credit applies to taxes on the $10,000 difference. The credit is automatically applied to the tax bill upon qualification following a one-time application. Homeowners have been receiving substantial homestead credits each year on their property tax bills.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: One-time application required; ongoing program with no annual deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners whose principal residence has experienced or may experience assessment increases, including owner-occupants in all counties and municipalities statewide. The owner must have lived in the property for at least six months of the previous tax year, including July 1 of the year for which the credit is applicable (unless temporarily unable due to illness or need of special care). The credit applies to only one property — the principal residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax relief through capped assessment increases on the homeowner's principal residence. The credit reduces property taxes owed on the portion of the assessment increase that exceeds the annual homestead cap.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in every county and municipality in Maryland. Every local jurisdiction is required to limit taxable assessment increases to 10% or less each year. Local governments may set lower caps (e.g., Cecil County caps county increases at 8%). The dwelling must be the owner's principal residence where the owner has lived for at least 6 months of the year, including July 1.
requirements_list: Property must be the owner's principal residence

Owner must have lived in the property for at least six months of the previous tax year, including July 1 of the year for which the credit is applicable (unless temporarily unable due to illness or special care)
Owner can receive the credit on only one property
Property was not transferred to new ownership during the previous tax year
No change in zoning classification requested by the homeowner that resulted in increased property value
No substantial change occurred in the use of the property
Previous assessment was not clearly erroneous
Must submit a one-time tax credit application (required beginning in 2008)
Property must not be a vacation home or rental property

For properties being razed or substantially improved: owner must have owned and occupied the property as principal residence for at least 3 full tax years immediately preceding the razing or commencement of improvements, and the replacement home or improvements must be completed within the next succeeding tax year
Assessment must increase more than the applicable annual cap (10% for state, or lower threshold set by local jurisdiction) to trigger the credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowners must submit a one-time application to establish eligibility — no need to reapply unless circumstances change. Applications can be filed: (1) online through Maryland OneStop at https://onestop.md.gov/ (select Department of Assessments & Taxation, then Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application); (2) online at https://sdathtc.dat.maryland.gov/; or (3) by mail or fax using the paper application form available at https://dat.maryland.gov/SDAT%20Forms/Homestead_application.pdf. New homeowners are mailed an application by the Department once the new deed is recorded and records are updated. Applicants can verify whether they have already filed an application or are receiving the credit by looking up their property in SDAT's Real Property database at https://sdat.dat.maryland.gov/RealProperty/. In-person service appointments are available by scheduling at https://telegov.egov.com/sdattaxcredits. Charles County residents should complete the Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application (HST) and submit to the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation; contact Eric Jackson (Chief of Treasury) at 301-645-0685 or 301-870-2249 for assistance. Once qualified, the credit is automatically applied to the tax bill when assessment increases exceed the applicable threshold.
