structured_extraction.program_description: The State of Maryland provides a tax credit to eligible renters who indirectly pay property taxes as part of their rent. Modeled on the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program, the credit recognizes that renters bear a share of property taxes through their rent payments. Eligible renters may receive a direct check payment of up to $1,000 per year. The credit is calculated based on the difference between 15% of annual rent (excluding utilities) and a tax threshold determined by gross household income. Renters must have lived in the dwelling for at least six months of the prior year and meet age, disability, or dependent child requirements, as well as income and net worth limits. Montgomery County additionally provides a supplement equal to 50% of the State credit (under Bill 21-15) to qualifying renters in that county, with no separate application required. Applications are accepted statewide and are due by October 1 each year.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible renters receive a direct check payment of up to $1,000 per year from the State. The credit is calculated based on the difference between 15% of annual rent (excluding utilities) and an income-based tax threshold. For renters age 60 or older or 100% disabled, the State uses income and rent thresholds provided in Chart 1 of the application to determine preliminary eligibility. For renters under age 60 with at least one dependent child under 18, the State uses income limits and a rent-to-income formula as shown in Chart 2. Montgomery County provides an additional supplement equal to 50% of the State credit to qualifying Montgomery County renters, also delivered as a check, with no separate application required. Payment is made by direct check from the State and County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland renters who are age 60 or older, OR under age 60 with at least one dependent child under 18, OR 100% disabled, and who meet gross household income and net worth requirements. Also renters of any age who qualify based on gross household income relative to rent paid (per the general income-based version of the program). Montgomery County renters who receive the State credit are also eligible for a County supplement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To offset the share of rent that goes toward property taxes; delivered as a direct check to the eligible renter. Montgomery County supplement provides additional rental property tax relief.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Montgomery County provides an additional county-level supplement for renters in that county.
requirements_list: Must be a renter in Maryland
Must have a bona fide leasehold interest and be legally responsible for the rent
Must have rented the dwelling as primary residence for at least six months of calendar year 2024
Unit must not be rented from a public housing authority or exempt organization
Combined net worth (applicant and spouse/co-tenant) must be under $200,000 as of December 31, 2024

Applicant must be age 60 or older as of December 31, 2024, OR 100% totally and permanently disabled with proof from Social Security Administration, other federal retirement system, Federal Armed Services, or local City/County Health Officer, OR under age 60 with at least one dependent under age 18 living in household during the year

For applicants under 60 with dependents: must not have received federal or state housing subsidies and must not have resided in public housing; total household income must be below limits specified in Chart 2 (e.g., $31,200 for family of four)
Must provide proof of rent paid through cancelled checks, money order receipts, lease agreements, or other documentation
First-time applicants and those who moved during the previous year must submit copy of lease(s) and proof of rent paid
If totally disabled, must submit proof of disability from Social Security Administration, other federal retirement system, Federal Armed Services, or local City/County Health Officer
If under age 60 with dependents, must include copy of dependent social security cards and birth certificates

If filed federal income tax return, must submit photocopy of completed 2024 return including all schedules and forms; if self-employed, also include partnership (Form 1065 with Schedule K-1) or corporate returns (Form 1120/1120S with Schedule K-1)
Must report all household income from all sources, including taxable and non-taxable income
Monthly rent must be high relative to total household income (assessed using State formulas in Charts 1 and 2)
For Montgomery County supplement: must have received State Renters' Tax Credit and be a renter in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at www.taxcredits.sdat.maryland.gov or download and mail paper application RTC-1 to: Department of Assessments and Taxation, Renters' Tax Credit Program, P.O. Box 49006, Baltimore, Maryland 21297. Applications must be received by October 1, 2025. A properly completed application requires all questions answered, form signed, and all required documentation included (federal income tax returns with schedules, Social Security Form SSA-1099 or Railroad Retirement Verification/Rate Letter, proof of rent paid, proof of disability if applicable, dependent documentation if applicable). Paper applications are available at senior activity centers. For questions or to schedule in-person appointment, contact: Email sdat.renters@maryland.gov; Telephone 1-800-944-7403 (toll-free statewide) or 410-767-4433 (Baltimore area); or visit in person at 123 Market Place, Baltimore, MD 21202, Suite 2700, 700 East Pratt Street, Baltimore, MD 21202-6377. Do not staple documents and do not send original documents. Montgomery County renters do not need a separate application for the County supplement—the State forwards information to the County, which calculates and mails the 50% supplement check automatically.

structured_extraction.program_description: MarylandSaves is a state-sponsored workplace retirement and emergency savings program facilitated by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). The program allows employers to offer employees an easy way to save for retirement and emergencies through automatic payroll deductions into a personal WorkLife Savings Account. The program is free for employers to set up and maintain, requires no employer contributions, no administrative fees, and no fiduciary liabilities. Employees control how much they contribute, can opt out and rejoin at any time, and their account remains portable through career changes. Employers who register and submit payroll contributions or claim their exemption by December 31 each year receive a $300 waiver on their annual SDAT report filing fee. Most Maryland employers are required by state law to offer some form of retirement savings plan, making MarylandSaves a straightforward compliance option.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers who register and submit payroll contributions for employees who participate, or who claim their exemption, by December 31 each year receive a $300 waiver of their annual SDAT filing fee for the following year. The program is free to establish and maintain for employers, with no employer contributions required and no fiduciary liability. Employees contribute a voluntary percentage of their paycheck to a personal WorkLife Savings Account invested in a Roth IRA; contributions are invested and have the potential to grow over time. The default contribution rate is 5% of gross salary, but employees can increase or decrease this percentage at any time. Employees control their contribution amount, can access funds for emergencies (through a default $1,000 emergency savings feature) or retirement, and can opt out and rejoin at any time. The account is portable, staying with the employee through career changes without complicated rollovers. Employees may also contribute directly to a Roth IRA if they are self-employed or their employer is not registered. A small annual administrative fee is charged to participants to cover program costs. Employers who already offer a qualified retirement plan may certify an exemption using their EIN to still receive the filing fee waiver.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 31 each year to qualify for the $300 SDAT filing fee waiver; employers can register at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers (for-profit, non-profit, and government entities) required by state law to offer a retirement savings plan, and their employees seeking portable emergency and retirement savings options. Businesses must be registered to conduct business in Maryland, have at least one W-2 employee, have been founded on or before January 1, 2021, and must use an automated payroll system to register for the employer program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employees can use contributions for emergency savings (up to $1,000 default emergency savings feature for unexpected expenses) and retirement savings through a WorkLife Savings Account invested in a Roth IRA. Employees can change contribution rates and investment options to meet personal goals. The $300 annual SDAT filing fee waiver reduces employer administrative costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all employers conducting business in Maryland and their employees. Businesses must be registered to conduct business in the state of Maryland.
requirements_list: Employer must register with MarylandSaves by visiting marylandsaves.vestwell.com/register/employer
Employer must have a State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) number and unique Access Code (sent via mail or email)
Employer must provide payroll provider information or payroll schedule(s)
Employer must provide company bank information including routing number, bank name, account number, and account type
Employer must provide latest employee roster with personal information (employee name, contact info, date of birth, SSN)
Employer must submit payroll contributions for employees who participate or claim exemption by December 31 each year to receive the SDAT filing fee waiver
Employer must have a federal Employer Identification Number (EIN)
Employer must maintain employee records and update changes such as new hires, terminations, and contribution rate changes
Employer must keep employee roster up to date by adding new hires, employees who opt-in later, and employees who reach age of eligibility (18 years old)
Employers who already offer a qualified retirement plan must certify exemption using their EIN
Employers must remain qualified each year to maintain the annual report fee waiver
Businesses with no employees or that run manual payroll are not required to register but can certify their exemption
Most Maryland employers are required by law to offer a retirement savings plan
Employer must be registered to conduct business in Maryland
Employer must have at least one employee earning a W-2 Maryland salary
Employer must not currently offer a retirement savings plan (unless claiming exemption)
Employer company must have been founded on or before January 1, 2021
Employer must pay employees through an automated payroll system
Employees must be at least 18 years old to be eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers receive enrollment communications from MarylandSaves indicating when they must participate, with an opportunity to certify exemption if they already offer a qualified retirement plan. Step 1: Set up business account online at marylandsaves.vestwell.com/register/employer using company SDAT number and unique Access Code. Create username (email address) and password. Step 2: Complete onboarding flow by adding payroll provider information, payroll schedules, company bank information, and latest employee roster with personal information (name, contact info, date of birth, SSN). A CSV template is available to compile employee information in advance. Step 3: Employers can authorize additional 'Admins' (designated employees or payroll provider staff) to help facilitate the program. Step 4: After 30 days, employees receive notification and have 30 days to decide to stay enrolled, opt out, or customize account settings. Step 5: After the 30-day opt-out period, update participating employees' contribution rates (default 5%) in payroll system and submit employee contribution amounts with next payroll. Step 6: Ongoing maintenance involves continuing to submit payroll contributions each pay period, maintaining employee deferral changes, and keeping employee roster up to date with new hires, terminations, and contribution changes. Employers who already offer a qualified retirement plan can claim a waiver without full registration. Employers with no employees or using manual payroll can certify exemption. 24/7 online resources available and call center open 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. ET. Registration takes less than 15 minutes. Employees sign in or set up account through MarylandSaves website to manage WorkLife Savings Account, choose contribution rates and investment options, and designate beneficiaries.

structured_extraction.program_name: Personal Property Tax Exemption for Home-based Businesses
structured_extraction.program_description: Small home-based businesses in Maryland may be exempt from personal property taxation if they meet specific criteria, including being a sole proprietorship with business property valued under $10,000 located at the owner's principal residence. After an initial filing, eligible businesses receive one-time approval and no further returns are required as long as criteria continue to be met.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible personal property owned by home-based sole proprietorships is exempt from personal property taxation. After initial filing of a Personal Property Return for Sole Proprietors (Form 2), eligible businesses receive one-time approval and no further returns are required as long as criteria continue to be met.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small home-based sole proprietors and for-profit businesses operating from their principal residence in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from personal property taxation for business property located at the owner's principal residence
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be a sole proprietorship (not a corporation, LLC, LP, or LLP)
Personal property must be located at the individual's principal residence which is also the principal place of business
Total original cost of all business personal property including average inventory value and excluding exempt vehicles must be less than $10,000
Initial filing of Personal Property Return for Sole Proprietors (Form 2) is required
Businesses requiring a Traders License should submit a Declaration of Inventory form to the Clerk of the Court instead
Amended returns for prior years must be filed within 3 years from the April 15th date the original report was due
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File a Personal Property Return for Sole Proprietors (Form 2). Eligible businesses will receive a one-time approval email near the beginning of the calendar year after their initial filing if they meet all criteria. Businesses needing a Traders License should submit a Declaration of Inventory form with the license application. Amended returns can be filed for prior years within 3 years of the original due date.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax relief program that allows property owners age 65 or older to elect to defer the increase in their property tax bill. Each local government must first adopt the program and may impose income restrictions and set interest rates. The deferred taxes become a lien on the property and must be repaid when the property is transferred. Montgomery County offers this program to homeowners of all ages who meet certain residency and income requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: State Property Tax Exemptions for Veterans and Surviving Spouses
structured_extraction.program_description: Exemption from real property taxes on the dwelling house and surrounding yard for veterans with a disability determined by the Veterans Administration to be 100% service connected, permanently, and totally disabling. The exemption covers the veteran's principal residence including the lot, curtilage, and structures necessary to use the property as a residence (such as a garage or utility shed). The program also covers disabled active duty service members and certain surviving spouses of disabled veterans or military personnel killed in the line of duty. The exemption applies to state, county, and municipal property taxes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Complete exemption from state, county, and municipal real property taxes on the disabled veteran's dwelling house and surrounding yard, which must be their principal residence. The dwelling includes the lot, curtilage, and structures necessary to use the property as a residence such as a garage or utility shed. The veteran must own the dwelling and provide proof of honorable discharge and 100% disability rating from the VA. Exemption also available to disabled active duty service members and certain surviving spouses. Veterans and surviving spouses may apply at any time without meeting the September 1 filing deadline.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: By September 1 following the beginning of the taxable year for which exemption is sought; however, veterans and surviving spouses may apply at any time and do not have to meet the September 1 filing deadline.
structured_extraction.contact_name: DVMF service program office in Baltimore
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans with 100% service-connected permanent and total disability ratings who own their principal residence in Maryland, disabled active duty service members, un-remarried surviving spouses of 100% disabled veterans, and surviving spouses of military personnel killed in the line of duty.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption on the dwelling house and surrounding yard used as principal residence, covering state, county, and municipal property taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Application must be submitted to the local county assessment office where the property is located. Local assessment offices are listed on the State Department of Assessments and Taxation website.
requirements_list: Veteran must have a disability determined by the Veterans Administration to be 100% service connected, permanently, and totally disabling
Disability rating cannot be due to misconduct of the veteran
Veteran must own the dwelling
Dwelling must be the veteran's principal residence
Veteran must provide VA certification or copy of final disability rating decision from VA
Veteran must provide DD-214 form showing honorable discharge or release under honorable circumstances
Veteran must demonstrate Maryland residency with Maryland Driver's License or previous year Maryland Tax Return
Or be a disabled active duty service member (some active duty service members may be eligible based on disability recognized by their individual branch of service)
Or be an un-remarried surviving spouse of a veteran with 100% service-connected disability
Or be a surviving spouse of military personnel killed in the line of duty
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out and submit the appropriate application form based on your eligibility category. Forms are available for: 100 percent disabled veteran exemption, disabled active duty service member exemption, surviving spouse of military casualty exemption, and surviving spouse of a 100 percent disabled veteran exemption. Submit the completed form along with VA certification or copy of disability rating decision, DD-214 form, and proof of Maryland residency to your local Maryland assessment office where the property is located. Contact the DVMF service program office in Baltimore at 800-446-4926, ext. 6450 to streamline Veterans Administration disability verification for the application.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Complete exemption from state, county, and municipal property taxes on the principal residence of a surviving spouse of an individual who died in the line of duty while in active military service. The dwelling must be owned by the surviving spouse and either was owned by the individual at the time of death, or was acquired by the surviving spouse within 2 years of the death if the individual or surviving spouse was domiciled in Maryland at the time of death, or was acquired after the surviving spouse qualified for the exemption on a former dwelling.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: By September 1 following the beginning of the taxable year for which exemption is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses of military personnel who died in the line of duty while on active service.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption applies to the principal residence, covering state, county, and municipal property taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. The individual or surviving spouse must have been domiciled (had their principal residence) in Maryland as of the date of death. Application must be submitted to the local county office where the property is located.
requirements_list: Dwelling must be owned by the surviving spouse
Individual must have died while in active service as a result of an injury or disease incurred in the line of duty

Dwelling must meet one of three conditions: (1) owned by the deceased individual at time of death, (2) acquired by surviving spouse within 2 years of death with domicile in Maryland at time of death, or (3) acquired after qualifying for exemption on former dwelling
Surviving spouse must provide certification that the individual died in the line of duty
Must be surviving spouse of military personnel killed in the line of duty
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Surviving Spouse of Military Casualty Exemption Application to the local county assessment office where the property is located. Application must include certification that the individual died while in active service as a result of an injury or disease incurred in the line of duty. The state application form is available on the Maryland SDAT website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Surviving Spouse of a 100 Percent Disabled Veteran Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: Property tax exemption for the principal residence of a surviving spouse of a veteran who had or received a 100% service-connected permanent and total disability rating.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Complete exemption from state, county, and municipal property taxes on the principal residence of the surviving spouse of a disabled veteran. The surviving spouse must own and reside in the dwelling. The exemption applies if the disabled veteran had a 100% service-connected permanent and total disability, owned the dwelling at death, the dwelling had received a disabled veteran's exemption, and the surviving spouse owns and resides in the dwelling. Alternatively, the exemption applies if the spouse now owns and resides in a dwelling that was occupied by the disabled veteran but not owned by them, as long as the disabled veteran resided and died in Maryland. An unmarried surviving spouse of a disabled veteran is entitled to the exemption on any subsequently acquired dwelling in an amount equal to the exemption allowed on the preceding dwelling.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: By September 1 following the beginning of the taxable year for which exemption is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Surviving spouses of 100% disabled veterans who own and reside in a qualifying dwelling.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption applies to the principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. The disabled veteran must have resided and died in Maryland. Application must be submitted to the local county office where the property is located.
requirements_list: Surviving spouse must own and reside in the dwelling
Disabled veteran must have had 100% service-connected permanent and total disability rating

One of three conditions must be met: (1) disabled veteran owned dwelling at time of death and dwelling had received disabled veteran's exemption, or (2) surviving spouse now owns and resides in dwelling that was occupied but not owned by disabled veteran who resided and died in Maryland, or (3) subsequently acquired dwelling as unmarried surviving spouse with exemption amount equal to prior dwelling exemption
Surviving spouse must not have remarried after veteran's death, unless remarriage was later annulled
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Surviving Spouse of a 100 Percent Disabled Veteran Exemption Application to the local county assessment office where the property is located.

structured_extraction.program_name: Surviving Spouse of a Blind Person Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a property tax exemption for the surviving spouse of a blind individual, allowing continuation of the blind person's exemption after the blind individual dies. The program offers an assessment reduction on the dwelling house and surrounding yard, exempting a portion of the property's assessed value from state, county, and municipal property taxes, as long as the surviving spouse remains unmarried and continues to own and reside in the property.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Exemption of $40,000 of the property's assessed value from state, county, and municipal property taxes (with an additional $15,000 assessment reduction on the dwelling house and surrounding yard in some jurisdictions such as Cecil County). The surviving spouse may continue receiving this exemption after the blind individual dies as long as they have not remarried.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: By September 1 following the beginning of the taxable year for which exemption is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unmarried surviving spouses of legally blind individuals who previously qualified for the Blind Persons Exemption.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax exemption applies to principal residence (dwelling house and surrounding yard).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Application must be submitted to the local county assessment office where the property is located.
requirements_list: Surviving spouse must be unmarried
Blind individual must have been receiving the Blind Persons Exemption prior to death
Surviving spouse must own and reside in the dwelling
Must be surviving spouse of person who qualified for the Blind Persons Exemption
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Surviving Spouse of a Blind Person Exemption Application to the local county assessment office where the property is located. The State application form is available on the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing financial incentives to support business growth and development in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Advantage Maryland (MEDAAF) – Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Advantage Maryland, also known as the Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF), provides conditional grants, loans, and investments to support economic development initiatives across Maryland. The program helps with business attraction and retention, infrastructure improvements, brownfield redevelopment, arts and entertainment districts, daycare facilities, revolving loan funds, and local strategic planning. It offers five financing capabilities: Strategic Economic Development Opportunities, Local Economic Development Opportunities, Direct Assistance to Local Jurisdictions or MEDCO, Regional or Local Revolving Loan Funds, and Special Purpose Programs. Projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas and support eligible industry sectors. Awards are made on a competitive basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five financing capabilities are offered: (1) Strategic Economic Development Opportunities – loans up to the lesser of $10 million or 20% of current fund balance; assistance cannot exceed 70% of total project costs; (2) Local Economic Development Opportunities – loans up to $5 million, or conditional loans and grants up to $2 million; local jurisdiction must sponsor the business and participate with a guarantee, direct loan, or grant equal to at least 10% of state assistance; (3) Direct Assistance to Local Jurisdictions or MEDCO; (4) Regional or Local Revolving Loan Funds; and (5) Special Purpose Programs for brownfield revitalization, seafood and aquaculture, animal waste, arts and entertainment, and child care centers – loan terms determined by specific program. Example conditional loans awarded include $700,000, $400,000, $315,000, and $300,000 for qualifying business expansions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in eligible industry sectors, for-profit and non-profit organizations, and political jurisdictions (including local governments) seeking to support economic development initiatives in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business attraction and retention, infrastructure support, brownfield redevelopment, arts and entertainment districts, daycare facilities, revolving loan funds, local strategic planning, capital investment, and job creation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Priority Funding Areas as determined by the state of Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must include a County Resolution supporting the project
Projects must support significant economic development initiatives
Projects must be within Priority Funding Areas
Projects must be in eligible industry sectors
For Local Economic Development Opportunities: must be a priority for the governing body of the jurisdiction and local jurisdiction must sponsor the business
For Local Economic Development Opportunities: local participation required (guarantee, direct loan, or grant equal to at least 10% of state assistance)
For Strategic Economic Development Opportunities: assistance cannot exceed 70% of total project costs
Significant capital expenditure commitment (where applicable)
Job creation commitment (where applicable)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the business development representative in your region for more information and to apply. Regional representative contact information is available through the Office of Business Development and Business Retention at the Maryland Department of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides refundable income tax credits to qualified investors who make eligible investments in Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Companies (QMBCs). Investors receive a tax credit equal to a percentage of their investment, with enhanced credits available for investments in QMBCs located in designated priority counties, Opportunity Zones, or RISE Zones.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Investors receive an income tax credit equal to 33% of eligible investment up to $250,000 in tax credits per investor per year, or 50% of eligible investment up to $500,000 in tax credits if the QMBC is located in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, or Somerset County or in a RISE Zone with technology developed at a qualified institution within that zone and in business less than 7 years. Enhanced credits are available for Opportunity Zone fund investors: 65% credit up to $575,000 (Level 1) or 75% credit up to $750,000 (Level 2). A single QMBC cannot receive more than 10% of the program's fiscal year funding, with a maximum of $1.2 million per company per fiscal year and $7 million aggregate per company. The credit is refundable if the investor has no Maryland income tax liability. Credits are issued on a first-come, first-served basis and cannot exceed the fiscal year budget. Investors must have a minimum investment of $25,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Form B QMBC applications: 03/31/2026. Form A Investor applications: 04/30/2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified individual and entity investors making investments of at least $25,000 in Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Companies engaged in research, development, or commercialization of innovative biotechnology products.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Companies (QMBCs) engaged in research, development, or commercialization of innovative biotechnology products or biological materials (DNA, RNA, protein), cells, tissues, or organs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: QMBCs must have headquarters and base of operations in Maryland. Enhanced credits available for investments in QMBCs located in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, or Somerset County, RISE Zones, or Opportunity Zones.
requirements_list: Qualified investor must invest at least $25,000 in a QMBC
Investor must be required to file an income tax return in any non-tax-haven jurisdiction
Investor cannot be a qualified pension plan, IRA, or other qualified retirement plan under ERISA, fiduciary, or custodian of such plans, or similar tax-favored plans from other countries
QMBC must have headquarters and base of operations in Maryland
QMBC must have fewer than 50 full-time employees
QMBC must have been in active business no longer than 12 years
QMBC must be organized for profit and primarily engaged in research, development, or commercialization of innovative and proprietary biotechnology
QMBC must have at least 1 R&D employee
QMBC must not have publicly traded securities
QMBC must be certified by Commerce
Qualified investors in the QMBC cannot have received more than $7,000,000 in biotechnology investment incentive tax credits in aggregate
Investors must submit all required documentation within two weeks of application date
Founder or current employee of QMBC cannot participate if company has been in active business for more than 5 years
Investor cannot own or control more than 25% of equity interests in QMBC after investment
Investment must be made within 30 days of receiving initial tax credit certificate from Commerce
Investor must provide proof of investment within 10 days of making investment or within 40 days of certificate issuance (certificate will be rescinded if not provided)
For non-Maryland companies: must submit Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments & Taxation no older than 30 days
For non-Maryland companies: must submit certificate of status from state/jurisdiction of organization
QMBC must be duly organized and in good standing in its jurisdiction
QMBC must be in good standing and authorized or registered to do business in Maryland
QMBC must be current in payment of all tax obligations to Maryland
QMBC must not be in default under contracts, indebtedness, or grants from Maryland
Investor must be duly organized and in good standing if a company
Investor must be in good standing and authorized or registered to do business in Maryland
Investor must be current in payment of all tax obligations to Maryland
Investor must not be in default under contracts, indebtedness, or grants from Maryland
Investment cannot be made by or funded directly or indirectly by the QMBC
No part of investment funding can be returned to investor after investment
No part of tax credit can be returned to QMBC
Spouse and minor children of disqualified persons are ineligible
Entities owned directly or indirectly by ineligible individuals or entities are ineligible
Investment instrument (if convertible debt/notes/SAFEs) must be no older than 1 year at time of application
Investment instrument must be issued to investor contemporaneously in exchange for investment funds
Convertible instruments must be converted to stock and stock issued within 30-day period after authorized by Commerce
QMBC must qualify as QMBC within 2 months after investment is made
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Investment Agreement - Company and investor come to preliminary investment terms and prepare draft investment agreement, convertible note, or similar contract. Step 2: QMBC Certification - Company must obtain certification as a QMBC. Company prepares and submits Form B QMBC Application through Commerce's online system beginning August 19, 2025 with required documentation including business plan, employment records, IP list, capitalization table, financial statements, proposed investment information, grants and awards, company location description, and intended use of funds. Commerce reviews application and may request additional documentation or issue determination letter; QMBC certification can occur at any time up to 2 months after investment completion. Step 3: Investor Application - Investor submits Form A investor application through online system beginning September 2, 2025, with deadline of September 15, 2025 at 11:59 p.m. to be eligible for electronic queue registration. Investors receive 5-character user ID and 6-digit reference number. Incomplete applications will be rejected after two weeks. Step 4: Electronic Queue Registration - Online Electronic Queue Investor Registration opens September 16, 2025 at 9:00 a.m. EST; investors use username and reference number from Form A submission to register. Submission order in queue determines first-come, first-served allocation of funds. Step 5: Initial Certificate of Approval - If approved, Commerce issues Initial Certificate of Approval authorizing investment. Step 6: Execute Investment - Investor makes investment in QMBC within 30 days of certificate issuance and provides proof to Commerce within 10 days of making investment. Step 7: Final Certificate of Approval - Commerce issues Final Certificate of Approval awarding tax credit. Step 8: Claim Credit - Investor claims credit on Maryland tax return (Form 500CR/CRW or 502CR) and attaches Final Certificate of Approval. Comptroller processes return and issues refund if applicable.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that promotes economic development and environmental improvement, especially in distressed urban areas, by identifying and redeploying underutilized properties that may be complicated by the presence or potential presence of hazardous substances, pollutants, or contaminants. The program offers financial incentives including grants, loans, and real property tax credits to help organize and assess brownfield properties, perform environmental evaluations, and complete remedial action cleanups. Property tax abatement is available for qualifying properties in participating jurisdictions.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For each of the five taxable years immediately following the first revaluation of the property after completion of a voluntary cleanup or corrective action plan, a qualified brownfields site in a participating taxing jurisdiction receives a property tax credit equal to 50% of the property tax attributable to the increase in the assessed value of the site, including improvements added within 5 years after reassessment. Participating jurisdictions must contribute 30% of the property tax attributable to the increase in assessment to the Maryland Economic Development Assistance Fund. Taxing jurisdictions may grant an additional property tax credit not exceeding an additional 20% of the remaining property tax attributable to the increase in assessment. In a designated enterprise zone or opportunity zone, the tax credit may be extended up to an additional 5 years (total of up to 10 years). Competitive grant and loan funding supports economic development and is managed through the Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF). Tax credits are administered separately through the Department of Commerce.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers interested in remediating and reusing brownfield properties in participating jurisdictions within Maryland to promote economic development and revitalization.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Organizing and assessing brownfield properties, performing environmental evaluations, completing remedial action cleanups, and real property tax credits for sites that have undergone cleanup or corrective action.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The site must be located in a jurisdiction that participates in BRIP. Participating jurisdictions include: Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Cecil, Dorchester, Frederick, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, and Worcester counties, plus the municipalities of Colmar Manor, Cumberland, Frederick, Salisbury, and Taneytown. Properties may also be located in designated enterprise zones or opportunity zones.
requirements_list: Site must be located in a participating jurisdiction that has enacted BRIP legislation
Property must be owned or operated by an inculpable person (not responsible for the contamination)
Site must be accepted into the Maryland Department of Environment's Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP)
Applicant must have Inculpable Person status from MDE
Site remediation must be completed to MDE satisfaction with closure documentation (Certificate of Completion or No Further Requirements Determination)
Building permit must be issued by the jurisdiction for the project
Combined with other real property tax credits, the total tax credit may not exceed 100% of the tax on the increased value of the site
Property must qualify as a brownfield (qualified brownfields site as defined in § 5–301 of the Economic Development Article)
Property tax credit cannot be calculated on an increase in assessment due to the termination of a use value
If the qualified brownfields site had a use value immediately before cleanup, the credit shall be calculated on an assessment as if the parcel had been valued at market value
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete a General Application and the BRIP addendum related to the project. 2. Provide copies of all required letters from the Maryland Department of Environment evidencing acceptance into the Voluntary Cleanup Program, Inculpable Person status, and a closure document once remediation is completed. 3. Provide a copy of the building permit issued by the jurisdiction. 4. Qualifying property owners will receive a letter from Commerce which can be taken to the local jurisdiction to apply for the tax credit. For competitive grants and loans, visit the Department of Commerce Advantage Maryland website (MEDAAF). Applicants should contact the appropriate department for specific application procedures and requirements. Note: A taxing jurisdiction's tax credit contribution for each qualified brownfields site to the Maryland Economic Development Assistance Fund shall be used only for brownfields sites in the taxing jurisdictions that have enacted a brownfields property tax credit ordinance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program and Fund provides grants for innovative and transformative infrastructure projects that accelerate the growth of eligible strategic industry sectors in Maryland. Grant awards can be used to acquire, construct, rehabilitate, install, improve, or equip eligible innovation infrastructure across eligible technology sectors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants up to $2 million for innovation infrastructure projects. For grants up to $1 million, applicants must provide matching funds equal to at least 200% of the grant amount. For grants over $1 million (up to $2 million), applicants must provide matching funds equal to at least 400% of the grant amount. Funds may be used to acquire, construct, rehabilitate, install, improve, or equip eligible innovation infrastructure such as wet laboratories, cyber ranges, and specialized training spaces. Grant funds cannot be used for indirect costs like salaries or management fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private companies, non-profit organizations, local governments, municipalities, colleges, and universities in Maryland working in eligible technology sectors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, installation, improvement, or equipping of eligible innovation infrastructure projects such as wet laboratories, cyber ranges, and specialized training spaces. Grant funds cannot be used for indirect costs like salaries or management fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Project must be in an eligible technology sector: Advanced Manufacturing, Aerospace, Agriculture, AI, Biotechnology, Blue Technology, Cybersecurity, Defense, Energy and Sustainability, Life Sciences, Quantum, Sensors and Robotics
Applicants must provide matching funds: 200% match for grants up to $1 million; 400% match for grants between $1 million and $2 million
Funds from other State grant programs do not count toward the matching requirement
Applicants must show they can pay for their share of the project costs
A single organization cannot receive more than $2 million in one fiscal year
Colleges and universities cannot receive more than 50% of the total funds available in a fiscal year
Projects from colleges and universities must collaborate with private industry or show a significant potential for economic impact
Grant funds must be spent within two years of the agreement date
The project must be fully operational within two years of the agreement date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application has two steps. First, applicants submit an initial project summary. A review committee then invites a limited number of applicants to submit a more detailed second application.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides an incentive for qualified Maryland companies with 50 or fewer employees to purchase cybersecurity technologies and services from qualified Maryland cybersecurity sellers, helping small businesses protect their information systems while supporting the state's cybersecurity industry.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified Maryland companies can claim a tax credit for 50% of the net purchase price of cybersecurity technologies and services purchased from a Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Seller. The maximum credit is $50,000 per year, covering up to $100,000 in purchases. The program has $4 million available annually — $3 million for technology purchases and $1 million for service purchases. The tax credit must be claimed for the tax year in which a purchase is made.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses with fewer than 50 employees that are required to file a state income tax return and purchase cybersecurity goods, products, or services from qualified Maryland cybersecurity sellers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of eligible cybersecurity technologies and services from a Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Seller. Technologies must be proprietary products designed to protect information systems and data. Services must align with the most recent National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Qualified sellers in Anne Arundel County include About Computing and Consulting LLC DBA Atruent, Luminary Automation Cybersecurity and Engineering LLC, Optic Cyber Solutions LLC, Penacity LLC, and Summit Business Technologies LLC.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland company
Must have fewer than 50 employees in Maryland
Must be required to file a Maryland income tax return
Purchase must be from a Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Seller
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Before applying, contact Cindy Zeng at cindy.zeng@maryland.gov, as some sellers may have reached their funding cap for the current tax year. After confirming eligibility, submit an application online through the Department of Commerce (no other formats accepted). If approved, you will receive a Certificate of Approval, which must be attached to your Maryland income tax return.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Commerce runs the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund. This fund provides grants and loans to small businesses entering the adult-use cannabis industry, with a focus on minority-owned and women-owned companies. The fund also offers grants to Historically Black Colleges and Universities for cannabis-related programs and to business development organizations that train and assist licensed small cannabis entrepreneurs. A current grant opportunity is available for Social Equity Applicants with a conditional license.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants and loans. A specific grant for Social Equity licensees offers funding based on license type. A standard dispensary can get up to $131,250, a processor up to $183,750, and a grower up to $525,000. Businesses with micro-licenses receive smaller amounts. The grant is paid in four parts as the business meets specific goals. Funds can also support HBCUs and business development organizations training cannabis entrepreneurs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application portal opened on June 3, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program helps small businesses entering the adult cannabis market, with a focus on minority-owned and women-owned companies. It also supports Historically Black Colleges and Universities and business organizations that train cannabis entrepreneurs. Current funding is for Social Equity Applicants who have a conditional cannabis license.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can help pay for license applications, operating costs, and capital expenses. Funds can also pay for targeted training to support participation in the adult-use cannabis industry.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must meet the minimum Adequate Capital Requirement set by the Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA).
Must be an existing business in Good Standing with the State of Maryland.
Must be a small business with 0-50 employees per license.
The business must hold a Maryland Social Equity Cannabis Business Conditional License.
The business must be at least 51% owned by individuals with a personal net worth not exceeding $1.7 million.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, register for access to the application portal on the Department of Commerce website. It is best to register before you request your first payment. You will need several documents, including your lottery number, conditional license letter, personal net worth information for owners, a W-9 form, and proof that your business is in Good Standing with Maryland. Visit the Maryland Cannabis Administration website or the fund information page for additional details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides financial incentives for businesses investing in cellulosic ethanol technology and production.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses investing in cellulosic ethanol technology

structured_extraction.program_description: A training program for commercial bankers and other lenders designed to increase lending throughout Maryland. The program leverages state and federal finance programs to enhance the credit of borrowers and reduce the risk assumed by lenders. Credit Connections features workshops by the Maryland Department of Commerce, the U.S. Small Business Administration, U.S. Department of Agriculture, and the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Workshops conducted by the Maryland Department of Commerce, the U.S. Small Business Administration, U.S. Department of Agriculture, and the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development to train commercial bankers and lenders on state and federal finance programs that can enhance borrower credit and reduce lender risk. The program covers financing incentives provided by the Office of Finance Programs, including programs such as MEDAAF, MIDFA, Sunny Day Fund, MSBDFA, MPVOLP, CDBG, and MEAF, as well as major tax incentives for economic development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial bankers and other lenders in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional training and education on state and federal financing programs available to businesses, including grants, loans, tax credits, and other economic development incentives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of Finance Programs for workshop information and registration details. Participants can reach Andy Fish at andy.fish@maryland.gov, 410-767-6376, or 1-877-821-0099 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce that provides a refundable income tax credit to qualified investors who invest in a Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Company (QMCC). The program provides financial incentives to support cybersecurity investment and help businesses strengthen their cybersecurity measures and infrastructure to protect their operations from cyber threats.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Refundable income tax credit available to qualified investors making equity investments in Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Companies (QMCCs).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified investors investing in Maryland cybersecurity companies (Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Companies), as well as businesses investing in cybersecurity measures and infrastructure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equity investment in Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Companies; cybersecurity investments and infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_name: Data Center Maryland Sales and Use Tax Exemption Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers a sales and use tax exemption to data centers that locate or expand in Maryland and create new full-time positions. Businesses must be certified as a Qualified Data Center by the Maryland Department of Commerce. Eligible projects that meet investment and job creation requirements may receive this benefit for up to 20 years, with an extended period available for those investing at least $250 million within the first ten years.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible businesses receive an exemption from Maryland's sales and use tax on qualifying data center personal property for 10 years. The benefit period can extend to 20 years if the business invests at least $250 million within the first ten years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses that operate data centers and plan to locate or expand in Maryland, including those in Frederick County and other jurisdictions statewide.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax exemption applies to the purchase of qualified data center personal property, including servers, equipment, and related infrastructure used in data center operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide but has different investment requirements based on location. Tier 1 areas, which include specific counties and all Opportunity Zones, have a lower investment threshold.
requirements_list: Must be certified as a 'Qualified Data Center' by the Maryland Department of Commerce.
Business must be locating or expanding in Maryland.
Business must create new full-time positions.
Invest at least $2 million in qualified data center personal property if located in a Tier 1 Area.
Invest at least $5 million in qualified data center personal property if located in any other area of the State.
Create at least five new, full-time qualified positions within a three-year period.
Qualified positions must pay at least 150% of the State minimum wage, be filled for at least 12 months, and be new to Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, submit an Eligibility Application to the Department of Commerce. Then, Commerce reviews the application and issues a Certificate of Eligibility. Finally, Commerce notifies the Comptroller's Office, which issues the sales and use tax exemption certificate to the business.

structured_extraction.program_name: Employer Security Clearance Costs (ESCC) Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: An income tax credit program for businesses that incur qualified federal security clearance administrative expenses, construction and renovation costs for sensitive compartmented information facilities (SCIFs), and first-year leasing costs for qualified small businesses performing security-based contract work in Maryland. The program offers three types of credits to help offset the costs of obtaining federal security clearances, constructing SCIFs, and first-year leasing costs for sensitive work.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses may claim up to $200,000 per taxable year for security clearance administrative expenses (processing applications, maintaining or upgrading computer systems required for clearance, and training employees). For SCIF construction or renovation, the credit is the lesser of 50 percent of costs or $200,000 for a single facility, or up to $500,000 per calendar year for multiple facilities. Qualified small businesses may claim up to $200,000 for first-year leasing costs of spaces used for security-based contracting. The total credits approved across all businesses cannot exceed $2 million per calendar year. If total applications exceed the cap, credits are approved on a pro-rata basis. Excess credits may be carried forward until fully used. For pass-through entities (partnerships, S corporations, LLCs, business trusts), credits are allocated to owners according to written agreement and Internal Revenue Service rules. For estates and trusts, credits are apportioned among the estate/trust and beneficiaries based on allocable income.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 15th following the tax year in which expenses were incurred. The Tax Year 2024 program is now closed and Commerce is no longer accepting applications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses organized and operated for profit, including individuals, sole proprietorships, partnerships, limited partnerships, corporations, limited liability companies, and other business entities doing business in Maryland with 500 or fewer employees that incur qualified federal security clearance administrative expenses, construct or renovate sensitive compartmented information facilities in Maryland, or are qualified small businesses leasing space for security-based contracting work.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Processing application requests for federal security clearance, maintaining, upgrading or installing computer systems required for federal security clearance, training employees to administer the clearance application process, construction or renovation of accredited sensitive compartmented information facilities in Maryland, and rental payments during the first year of leasing agreements for spaces used for security-based contracting. All expenses and costs must be incurred in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Expenses and costs must be incurred in Maryland.
requirements_list: Businesses must apply to and be certified by Maryland Department of Commerce
Companies may not employ more than 500 employees
For security clearance administrative expenses: must provide detailed itemized accounting or spreadsheet of qualifying expenses and invoices and proof of payment for each expense

For first-year leasing costs: must be a qualified small business (independently owned and operated, not a subsidiary, not dominant in its field, and did not employ more than 25 individuals in most recently completed fiscal year), provide copy of rental agreement, payment schedule, proof of payment of all claimed rent expenses, and signed Small Business Affidavit

For SCIF costs: SCIF must be accredited by appropriate federal agency, must provide detailed itemized accounting showing SCIF assets and equipment for each facility, proof of service and equipment purchases such as invoices from SCIF contractors, proof of payment such as cancelled check or bank statement, and proof of SCIF construction or renovation performed in Maryland
Eligible expenses for tax years beginning after December 31, 2012, but before January 1, 2017 (or as extended by regulation)
Cash transactions are generally not eligible as they cannot be easily tracked
Wages and salaries for employees applying for security clearance are not eligible expenses
Business must incur security clearance costs or conduct security-based business
Different caps apply to different credit types

Application must include legal name of business entity, street address of principal place of business, mailing address, email address, telephone number, name and contact information for individual with authority to act on behalf of business entity, federal employer identification number (or federal taxpayer identification number for individuals or sole proprietorships), verification of SCIF accreditation by appropriate federal agency, and detailed account of eligible costs incurred
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses must submit an application through the Department form approved by the Maryland Department of Commerce by September 15th following the end of the tax year for which expenses are being claimed. Late applications will not be accepted. The application must include detailed itemized accounting of eligible costs and supporting documentation such as invoices, proof of payment, rental agreements, and SCIF accreditation verification. The Department will certify the approved credit amount by December 15th of that year. If total applications exceed the $2 million annual cap, the Department approves credits on a pro-rata basis by multiplying each applicant's requested credit by a fraction where the numerator is the $2 million cap and the denominator is the total of all credits applied for. The applicant must then file an amended Maryland income tax return with the Comptroller of Maryland to claim the credit and attach a copy of the Department's certification. For pass-through entities, credits are allocated among owners and each owner attaches a Maryland Form 510, Schedule K-1 to their individual tax return. Unused credits may be carried forward to succeeding taxable years until fully used.

structured_extraction.program_description: The ExportMD Program helps small and mid-sized Maryland companies offset the costs of marketing internationally by providing reimbursement for expenses associated with international marketing projects. Eligible companies that receive an ExportMD Award may be reimbursed for up to $5,000 (50% of eligible expenses) for international marketing initiatives including trade shows, airfare, translation services, and website development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Companies that receive an ExportMD award may be reimbursed for up to $5,000 (50% of eligible expenses) for expenses associated with an international marketing project. Eligible expenses include trade show fees, airfare, translation of brochures, website development, and other international marketing activities. Grants are awarded on a monthly basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are due on the 1st of each month
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and mid-sized Maryland companies seeking to expand into international markets
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: International marketing project expenses including travel expenses, trade show fees and registration, airfare, translation of brochures and materials, website development, and other international market development activities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must have business operations in Maryland and be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.
Must be in existence for at least one year.
Must be export ready.
Must not have received an ExportMD Award in the last year.
Must be a "small business" as defined by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA).
Must be planning an international business initiative that will start and finish within six months of the application deadline.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a monthly basis, due on the 1st of each month. First, contact the program specialist to discuss your international marketing plan. A regional manager will then provide more details and the application form. You must schedule an export counseling meeting before the deadline. Contact the office at least two weeks before the application deadline to start the process. Submit reimbursement request for approved international marketing expenses upon completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A refundable tax credit available to film production entities that incur certain production costs in Maryland. The credit applies to direct costs necessary to carry out a film production activity in the State, including costs for goods and services from qualified Maryland vendors.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified film productions can receive a refundable tax credit of up to 28% of their direct costs. A television series can receive a credit of up to 30% of direct costs. The maximum credit per project is $10 million. Qualified Maryland Small Films can receive a tax credit of up to 28% of direct costs, with a maximum of $125,000 per project.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling; first come, first served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Film production companies filming in Maryland, including Maryland-based small film companies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct costs for film production in Maryland, including goods and services from qualified Maryland vendors. A detailed list of authorized direct costs is available on the program website.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide in Maryland. At least 50% of the principal photography must take place in Maryland.
requirements_list: Total direct costs must be over $250,000 ($25,000 for Maryland Small Films).
At least 50% of principal photography must happen in Maryland.
Applicants must show proof of financing and national distribution.
Principal photography must start within 120 days of receiving a Letter of Qualification.
Maryland Small Films must be organized in Maryland for at least 3 months, be independently owned, and have 25 or fewer full-time employees.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, submit an Application for Qualification with all required documents before starting any work in Maryland. You can submit it by email, mail, or in person. The Department reviews complete applications in the order they are received. Within 30 days, the Department will issue a Letter of Qualification or a denial. After production is complete, you must submit an Application for Final Tax Credit Certification no later than 180 days after the completion date.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a state income tax credit to small businesses that hire qualified veterans after January 1, 2017. Employers may qualify for a credit equal to 30% of up to the first $6,000 of wages paid to a qualified veteran employee in the first year of employment, with a maximum credit of $1,800 per veteran. Small businesses can claim the credit for up to five qualified veterans per tax year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credit equal to 30% of the first $6,000 in wages paid to a qualified veteran employee, up to a maximum of $1,800 per veteran. The credit is valid for wages paid during the employee's first year of employment. Small businesses may claim the credit for up to five qualified veteran employees per tax year. The credit is non-refundable and cannot be carried forward or backward.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with 50 or fewer full-time employees that hire qualified veterans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit against state income tax liability based on wages paid to newly hired qualified veteran employees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide.
requirements_list: Business must have 50 or fewer full-time employees.
Small business must hire a qualified veteran after January 1, 2017.
Hired employee must be a qualified veteran under program guidelines.
A business may claim the credit for up to 5 qualified veteran employees per tax year.
The tax credit is non-refundable and cannot be carried forward or backward.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To receive the credit, a business submits application forms, employee self-certification, W-2s or paystubs, and military discharge forms to the Maryland Department of Commerce for certification. After receiving the certificate, the employer files it with their state tax return using Maryland Tax Form 500CR.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state income tax credit program that encourages eligible businesses to expand or relocate in Maryland and create net new full-time jobs. Businesses that create a minimum number of net new full-time jobs receive tax credits ranging from $3,000 to $6,000 per job depending on location and veteran status. Enhanced credits are available for jobs created in designated revitalization areas (enterprise zones, sustainable communities, Tier 1 counties) and for hiring qualified military veterans. Small businesses with 50 or fewer employees that hire qualified veterans are also eligible for a separate credit. The program remains in effect until January 1, 2027, subject to extension by the Maryland General Assembly.
list_of_eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible businesses receive an income tax credit against Maryland state income tax. The base credit is $3,000 per newly created qualified full-time job. The credit increases to $5,000 per job if located in a revitalization area (state enterprise zone, federal empowerment zone, federal enterprise zone, DHCD Sustainable Community, or Tier 1 County). Enhanced credits are available for hiring qualified veterans: $4,000 per job filled by a qualified veteran employee, or $6,000 if the veteran is hired in a revitalization area. Small businesses with 50 or fewer total full-time employees may claim an additional $2,500 per qualified veteran employee hired for at least one year, up to five veterans per credit year. The credit may be carried forward for five years if not fully used. Maximum credit per business is $1 million per credit year, with program capped at $4 million in tax credits annually. Credits are certified on a first-come, first-served basis based on when the Department receives the final application.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Credits are certified on a first-come, first-served basis; program capped at $4 million in annual credits
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible businesses that locate or expand in Maryland and create net new full-time jobs, and small businesses with 50 or fewer employees that hire qualified veteran employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Income tax credit applied against Maryland state income tax liability for job creation and hiring qualified veterans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Reduced job creation minimums apply in Priority Funding Areas (25 jobs) and lower-income counties (10 jobs). Enhanced credits available in Tier 1 Counties: Allegany, Baltimore City, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester. Lower-income counties with 10-job minimum (subject to annual change) currently include Allegany, Baltimore City, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Queen Anneís, Saint Maryís, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties.
requirements_list: For non-small businesses: must declare intent to Commerce before hiring qualified employees
For small businesses hiring veterans: no intent declaration required before hiring, but must meet all other requirements
Minimum net new full-time jobs required: 60 statewide, 25 in Priority Funding Areas, or 10 in designated lower-income counties
Each position must be full-time (at least 840 hours during at least 24 weeks in a six-month period, averaging 35 hours per week)
Positions must be filled for at least 12 months before applying for final certification
For positions filled before October 1, 2021: must pay at least 120% of state minimum wage

For positions filled on or after October 1, 2021: must pay prevailing wage rate or 150% of state minimum wage, provide career advancement training, afford collective bargaining rights, provide paid leave, be covered by unemployment insurance and workers' compensation, offer employer health insurance with premiums not exceeding 8.5% of net monthly earnings, and offer retirement benefits
Must be primarily engaged in qualifying business activities
Expansion or establishment must be at a single location (single firm may have multiple certified eligible locations)
Jobs must be created within a 24-month period
For small business veteran hiring: qualified veteran must be honorably discharged from active military service and qualify as a qualified veteran for Federal Work Opportunity Tax Credit purposes
Small businesses must employ 50 or fewer total full-time employees
Small business may not claim credit for more than five qualified veteran employees per credit year
Small business may not claim credit for veteran hired to replace laid-off employee or employee on strike
Jobs must remain filled for at least three years following the credit year to avoid recapture
Business cannot claim both One Maryland Tax Credit and Job Creation Tax Credit in same tax year
Annual statewide cap of $4 million in credits available on first-come, first-served basis
Notify the Department of Commerce of intent to apply before creating the new jobs (not required for small business veteran hiring)
New positions must be filled for at least 12 months before applying for certification
Base employment calculated as average of prior two years or employment at intent date, whichever is higher
If during any of 3 years after credit year, qualified positions fall more than 5% below average during credit year, credit is recaptured and recomputed
If during 3 years after credit year, average qualified positions fall below applicable minimum threshold, all credits are recaptured
Temporary vacancies do not constitute position abolition if filled within 4 months and no more than 10% of positions vacant at any time
Business is subject to audit and periodic employment and wage data verification by Department of Labor and Department of Commerce
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Non-small businesses submit Notice of Intent form to taxincentives.commerce@maryland.gov before hiring qualified employees; only positions hired after intent date may qualify. Small businesses hiring veterans do not require intent notification. Step 2: Submit Employment Affidavit with Preliminary Application to Department of Commerce to determine preliminary qualification and establish base employment level. Step 3: Once qualified positions are filled and have been maintained for at least 12 months, submit Final Application with List of Qualified Employees form and supporting documentation verifying job quality requirements. Step 4: For veteran employees, submit Qualified Veteran Employee Self-Certification Form with copy of federal Certificate of Discharge (DD-214). Step 5: Department of Commerce calculates credit amount and issues Final Certificate of Eligibility. Step 6: Business claims credit on Maryland Tax Form 500CR and attaches Final Certificate to tax return. Step 7: For 3 years following credit year, submit Annual Report to abigail.mcknight@maryland.gov documenting employment levels and verifying recapture conditions are not triggered (third year requires CPA statement). Applications processed online through Commerce portal. Preliminary certification typically takes 30 days; final certification typically takes 60 days. Submit applications to: Maryland Department of Commerce, Office of Finance Programs, Tax Incentives, 401 E. Pratt Street, 17th Floor, Baltimore, MD 21202, or taxincentives.commerce@maryland.gov

structured_extraction.program_description: A financing resource that encourages banks and other financial institutions to make loans to small businesses that have difficulty obtaining financing by establishing a Loan Loss Reserve Program. The program helps small businesses access capital for start-up, expansion, or working capital by providing lenders with reserve account coverage on loan defaults.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MD CAP provides up to 100% coverage to participating lenders on losses resulting from certain loan defaults. The program works through a reserve account funded by contributions from the lender, borrower, and MD CAP.
