Typically, the lender contributes a minimum of 2.0 percent and the borrower contributes 1.0 percent of the loan amount, and MD CAP matches that combined amount. Loans may not exceed $250,000 and must have a term not exceeding ten years. Loans can be short or long term, have fixed or variable interest rates, and be secured or unsecured.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, including nonprofit organizations, that need financing for start-up, expansion, or working capital and have difficulty obtaining business loans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business financing for start-up, expansion, or working capital. Loans cannot be used for financing of passive real estate ownership, residential living facilities, certain adult entertainment facilities, check cashing facilities, gambling facilities, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn or gun shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, or financing for sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Most Maryland small businesses are eligible.
requirements_list: Borrower must qualify as a small business under SBA size standards
Borrower must have fewer than 50 employees
Borrower must apply to a participating lender for business financing
Loan must satisfy the lending criteria of the lender
Loan term may not exceed ten years
Loan may not exceed $250,000
Lender must be a credit union, financial institution, or community development financial institution
Lender must complete the MD CAP application and become certified by Commerce as a participating MD CAP lender
Lender must enroll a qualifying loan not more than 30 days after the date of the first disbursement of the loan
Lender may enroll all or a portion of a qualifying loan in an amount not more than $250,000
Financial Institution must not be subject to a cease and desist order or other regulatory sanction that would impair its ability to participate in the Program
Financial Institution must agree to follow the Program's procedures as set forth in Economic Development Article, Section 5, Subtitle 17
Financial Institution must permit an audit of any records relating to enrolled Qualified Loans during normal business hours
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A small business applies to a participating lender for financing. The lender underwrites and enrolls a qualifying loan (or portion of a loan) with MD CAP. The lender, borrower, and Maryland Capital Access Program each deposit contributions into a reserve account, typically with the lender and borrower each contributing a percentage of the loan amount and MD CAP matching that combined amount. The lender submits a one-page Loan enrollment form with summary information to Maryland Capital Access Program. If a loan defaults and the lender has performed normal collection methods, at the time of charge-off the lender files a one-page claim form for all or part of the enrolled loan. Financial institutions interested in becoming MD CAP participants must complete the Financial Institution Application (available on the Department's website) and email it to fpaaworkflowcoordinator.commerce@maryland.gov for approval and enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: MEAF provides loans to small and underserved businesses to upgrade or modernize operations, develop or expand commercial applications for technology, or enter into and compete in new or different markets. Eligible companies must have no more than 50 employees and must be unable to qualify for loans from traditional lending sources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEAF provides loans of up to $150,000 for small and underserved businesses with fewer than 50 employees. Funds can be used for working capital, equipment, building renovation, real estate acquisition and site improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and underserved businesses with fewer than 50 employees in all regions of Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, equipment, building renovation, real estate acquisition and site improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Funding assistance is available to small businesses in all regions of the state.
requirements_list: Fewer than 50 employees
Demonstrate credit worthiness
Demonstrate ability to repay the obligation
Unable to qualify for loans from traditional lending sources
Business plan with 3 years of projections, cost budget, and sources and uses of funds
Current personal financial statement
Listing of all owners and percentages of ownership
Resume of principal owner(s)
Personal federal tax returns with all schedules for most recent two years
Business federal tax returns with all schedules for most recent two years
Explain amount of personal or business funds to be contributed to the project
Explain type of collateral to be provided to secure the loan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the Maryland Department of Commerce with required supporting documents including business plan, financial statements, tax returns, and collateral documentation. The Commerce team reviews each application using standard commercial credit criteria to determine if it meets the program's financial and other requirements for loan approval. Commerce recommends approval of financing for projects deemed to present the best chance of succeeding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF) - Economic Development Opportunities Program Fund (Sunny Day)
structured_extraction.program_description: Supports extraordinary economic development opportunities that create and retain employment as well as generate significant capital investments. Projects must create substantial jobs, particularly in areas of high unemployment, and are evaluated competitively based on consistency with the state's strategic economic development plan. The program promotes Maryland's participation in major economic development projects that provide significant returns through job creation and capital investment in priority funding areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and loans provided to support extraordinary economic development projects. Applicants must provide a minimum capital investment of at least five times the amount of Sunny Day assistance requested. Recipients must have a strong balance sheet and be creditworthy. Projects must create substantial employment, particularly in areas of high unemployment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses pursuing extraordinary economic development opportunities that create and retain jobs, particularly in areas of high unemployment throughout Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for economic development projects that create and retain employment and generate significant capital investments
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland; prioritizes projects located in areas with high unemployment and in Priority Funding Areas
requirements_list: Must generate substantial employment, particularly in areas of high unemployment
Must provide a minimum capital investment of at least five times the amount of Sunny Day assistance
Must possess a strong balance sheet
Must be creditworthy
Project must be consistent with the state's strategic economic development plan
Projects must be located in or consistent with Priority Funding Areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For more information and to apply, contact the Program Manager Timothy Doyle at the Maryland Department of Commerce, Office of Finance Programs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Global Gateway Soft Landing Program for International Companies
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive business support program for international companies seeking to establish a physical presence in the U.S. market. The program provides eligible foreign companies with up to $10,000 in funding toward rent, services, and other market entry costs through a statewide network of incubators and accelerators. It also offers subsidized office space for up to six months, one-on-one mentoring, business development support, assistance with business registration, immigration, accounting, and recruitment, as well as training workshops, customer introductions, and access to public and private funding tools and tax incentives. The program has a specific focus on Korean businesses through the South Korea Trade Mission initiative with Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $10,000 Maryland Global Gateway Grant toward rent, services, and other market entry costs. Up to 6 months of subsidized office space (private or collaborative workspaces) to test the U.S. market. One-on-one professional business mentoring, business development support, assistance with business registration, immigration and accounting, recruitment help, training workshops and strategic educational programming, customer introductions, and access to public and private funding tools and tax incentives. Companies must physically locate in Maryland and sign an agreement with a Global Gateway partner (such as Innovation Station Business Incubator at Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation) to receive funds. Participants can locate up to two staff members at an incubator for the six-month period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Foreign companies, including particularly Korean businesses, that want to explore entering the U.S. market by establishing a physical presence in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Office space rental, business startup and expansion activities, staff recruitment and training, business development and market entry support, program participation costs, and other related market entry expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide through a network of partner organizations. Companies must physically locate in Maryland within six months of the application round. Prince George's County participates with a specific focus on Korean companies as part of the South Korea Trade Mission initiative and houses the Innovation Station Business Incubator. Prince George's County offers strategic advantages including proximity to three international airports with daily direct flights to Asia (Seoul, Hong Kong, Tokyo, Delhi, and Beijing), foreign trade zone designation, access to major highways, interstates and the Port of Baltimore, 91 metro stations, and strong industry focus areas including tech ecosystem, quantum computing, energy, aerospace, military, cybersecurity, healthcare, and warehouse and logistics.
requirements_list: Must be legally registered as a business in its home country for at least one year.
Must have at least five full-time equivalent employees.
Must have at least $500,000 USD in sales revenue and/or external investment in a single year (2023 or 2024).
Must be able to locate physically in Maryland within six months of the application round.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application through the online portal at commerce.maryland.gov/softlanding. The Department of Commerce will help find a partner organization. To receive funds, applicants must sign an agreement with a Global Gateway partner. International companies, particularly Korean businesses, should contact Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation through the Innovation Station Business Incubator for program enrollment and participation details. For Prince George's County: Martin U. Ezemma, Director of International Business, (301) 583-4650, www.pgcedc.com. Additional support available through ExportMD grant program covering project costs up to $5,000 and up to 40 hours of services from a Commerce foreign trade representative.

structured_extraction.program_description: MIDFA promotes private sector investment in economic development projects by insuring financial obligations and issuing taxable and tax-exempt revenue bonds. The program increases access to capital for small- and medium-sized businesses, historically disadvantaged businesses, and businesses in rural areas. It also facilitates long-term capital market access for fixed asset financing through bond issuance and credit insurance for projects located in Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MIDFA issues private activity revenue bonds (taxable and tax-exempt) and provides credit insurance in the form of loan guaranties to reduce lender risk. The Conventional Program insures up to 80% of transactions, not to exceed $2.5 million (up to 90% for export transactions). The Bond Program insures bonds up to 100%, not to exceed $7.5 million of taxable or tax-exempt bonds. Taxable bonds provide access to long-term capital markets primarily for fixed asset financing. Tax-exempt bonds are limited to 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations, manufacturing facilities, and certain solid waste projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial and industrial businesses, manufacturers, not-for-profit entities, day care providers, and small- and medium-sized businesses in Priority Funding Areas, including historically disadvantaged businesses and businesses in rural areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition, building acquisition, construction costs, machinery and equipment, furniture and fixtures, leasehold improvements, eligible soft costs, energy-related projects, and working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in a designated Priority Funding Area statewide. Retail businesses are not eligible.
requirements_list: Must be located in a Priority Funding Area (except retail businesses are not eligible)
Commercial and industrial businesses, manufacturers, not-for-profit entities, or day care providers
Tax-exempt bond eligibility is limited by Federal law to 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations, manufacturing facilities, and certain solid waste projects
Eligibility for tax-exempt bonds is limited to 501(c)(3) non-profits, manufacturing, and certain solid waste projects
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Finance Specialist at the Maryland Department of Commerce, Office of Finance Programs for more information and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce that provides grants to small and mid-sized Maryland manufacturers to invest in Industry 4.0 technologies, machinery, robotics, and digital business practices in order to remain competitive and drive growth. The program also provides education, technical, and financial assistance to encourage manufacturers to adopt and implement advanced, energy efficient manufacturing technologies, including smart manufacturing improvements that increase energy efficiency and reduce carbon emissions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $25,000 to $500,000, covering up to 75% of eligible costs for small manufacturers (3–50 employees) and up to 50% of eligible costs for mid-sized manufacturers (51–250 employees). A mini-grant of up to $15,000 is also available for manufacturers with 3–75 full-time employees on a first come, first served basis. In addition to grants, the program provides education and technical support to help manufacturers adopt advanced, energy efficient manufacturing technologies including robotics, artificial intelligence, enterprise resource planning systems, and digital process improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and mid-sized manufacturing businesses in Maryland with 3 to 250 full-time employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in Industry 4.0 technologies including robotics, artificial intelligence, enterprise resource planning systems, advanced sensors, data analytics, cloud computing, cybersecurity, machinery, equipment, software, training, systems integration, and digital process improvements that increase energy efficiency and reduce carbon emissions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be an established manufacturing business in Maryland. Program is available statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a business in good standing with the State of Maryland.
Must have between 3 and 250 full-time employees.
Must have a NAICS code of 31, 32, or 33.
Must be established for at least 2 years.
Must be in good standing with OSHA and Maryland Occupational Safety and Health regulations.
Must demonstrate ability to successfully implement the project.
Must show a commitment to or strategy for Industry 4.0 adoption.
Must provide matching funds (25% for businesses with 3–50 employees; 50% for businesses with 51–250 employees).
Must complete the CESMII Technology Assessment through Maryland MEP.
Must be a small or mid-sized manufacturer.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications for the 2026 program were accepted from August 1, 2025 to August 29, 2025. Applicants submit proposals through an online portal. Funding decisions are competitive. Mini-grants are reviewed on a first come, first served basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Nonprofit Development Center Program and Funds - Nonprofit, Interest-Free Micro Bridge Loan Account (NIMBL)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Nonprofit, Interest-Free Micro Bridge Loan Account (NIMBL) provides short-term, interest-free loans of up to $25,000 to qualifying nonprofit organizations to cover operating costs while waiting to receive funds from a government grant or contract that has already been awarded. The program is administered through the Maryland Nonprofit Development Center.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Interest-free bridge loans of up to $25,000 to support operating costs while nonprofits wait to receive disbursement of funds from an already-awarded government grant or contract. Loans must be repaid by the date of the final payment from the government grant or contract. Applications are reviewed on a rolling, first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations located in Maryland that have been awarded a government grant or contract and need operating funds while awaiting disbursement of those funds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs and operating expenses only.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be located in Maryland. Program is available statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3), (4), or (6) nonprofit organization.
Must have a government grant or contract in place to pay back the bridge loan.
Must provide written confirmation of funding from a government grant or contract.
Must not have received the government funds yet.
Must repay the loan by the date of the final payment from the government grant or contract.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Les Hall at les.hall@maryland.gov to request an application form. Submit the completed application and all required documents by email. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as they are received.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers increased tax credit benefits to businesses located in Maryland Opportunity Zones. To receive these benefits, a business must first qualify for one of several other state economic development tax credit programs, including the Job Creation Tax Credit, One Maryland Tax Credit, More Jobs for Marylanders, Enterprise Zone Income Tax Credit, Enterprise Zone Focus Area Income Tax Credit, Biotechnology Investor Incentive Tax Credit, and Maryland Innovation Investment Tax Credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This program provides larger tax credits than what is normally available through other state programs. Businesses can apply for Level 1 or Level 2 enhancements, with Level 2 offering the highest credit amounts. The specific credit amount depends on the base program, such as the Job Creation Tax Credit, One Maryland Tax Credit, More Jobs for Marylanders, Enterprise Zone Income Tax Credit, Enterprise Zone Focus Area Income Tax Credit, Biotechnology Investor Incentive Tax Credit, or Maryland Innovation Investment Tax Credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for businesses and investors operating within designated Maryland Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This program enhances the value of other state tax credits. Businesses receive a larger reduction in their state tax liability for job creation and business investments in Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: To be eligible, a business or investment must be located within a designated Maryland Opportunity Zone.
requirements_list: Business must be located in a Maryland Opportunity Zone.
Must first qualify for an underlying tax credit program, such as the Job Creation Tax Credit or One Maryland Tax Credit.
For most credits, the business must be a Qualified Opportunity Zone Business that has received an investment from a Qualified Opportunity Fund.
For investment-based credits like the BIITC or IITC, the investor must be a Qualified Opportunity Fund.
To qualify for Level 2 enhancements, the business must meet additional community engagement requirements, such as having local residents on its board or a community benefits agreement.
Level 2 enhancements also require a letter of approval from the local municipality or county government.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must attach the Opportunity Zone Enhancement program application as an addendum to their application for the specific underlying tax credit.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business COVID-19 Emergency Relief Grant Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded emergency grant program providing financial assistance to Maryland small businesses and non-profits that have been negatively impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The program includes a $50 million emergency grant fund offering grants up to $10,000 per applicant, as well as a subsequent $10 million Small Business COVID Relief Grant Program established in 2021 through bipartisan legislation. Funding is available on a first-come, first-served basis with extremely limited funds.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency grants up to $10,000 per applicant, not to exceed 3 months of demonstrated cash operating expenses for the first quarter of 2020. A subsequent $10 million relief fund was established in 2021. Funding operated on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 30 at 9 am EST through April 6 at 11:59 pm EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based small businesses and non-profits with under 50 full- and part-time employees that have been negatively impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash operating expenses including payroll, suppliers, rent, fixed debt payments, and other mission-critical cash operating costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based businesses and non-profits only. Program available statewide.
requirements_list: Maryland-based business or non-profit
Under 50 full- and part-time employees
Negatively impacted by COVID-19
Business must have been negatively impacted by COVID-19
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses must first create an account at https://programs.commerce.maryland.gov/ReliefRegistration. Once an account is created, applicants receive an email with a link to the application and login instructions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Small Business Development Financing Authority (MSBDFA)
structured_extraction.program_description: MSBDFA promotes the viability and expansion of all small businesses in Maryland, with a priority focus on businesses owned by economically and socially disadvantaged entrepreneurs who are unable to obtain adequate business financing on reasonable terms through normal financing channels. The program provides financing through multiple components including contract financing, equity participation, long-term loan guarantees, state small business credit initiatives, and surety bonding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSBDFA provides financing through five program components: Contract Financing Program, Equity Participation Program, Long Term Guaranty Program, State Small Business Credit Initiative, and Surety Bonding Program. Equity investments range from $25,000 to $1,000,000 in the form of preferred stock, common stock, warrants, partnership interests, and other equity-like structures with a minimum 1:1 private capital match required. Uses include working capital, supplies and materials, machinery and equipment acquisition, acquisition of real estate, leasehold improvements, purchase of an existing business, and financing of contracts that receive majority funding from federal, state, local government, or regulated utilities. The program can also provide bid, payment, and performance bonds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses unable to obtain adequate business financing on reasonable terms through normal financing channels, with priority focus on businesses owned by economically and socially disadvantaged entrepreneurs seeking financing for expansion and growth.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, supplies and materials, machinery and equipment acquisition, acquisition of real estate, leasehold improvements, purchase of an existing business, financing of contracts that receive majority funding from federal, state, local government, or regulated utilities, bid, payment, and performance bonds, and equity investments for expansion and growth.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a small business unable to obtain adequate business financing on reasonable terms through normal financing channels
Priority focus on businesses owned by economically and socially disadvantaged entrepreneurs
Equity investments require a minimum 1:1 private capital match
Equity investment size between $25,000 and $1,000,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should review the full MSBDFA guidelines, qualifications, and frequently asked questions on the Meridian Management Group website. To apply, complete the online application at programs.commerce.maryland.gov/m. Before completing an application, users must create an account by clicking 'Register' on the online application webpage. Users with existing accounts in the Maryland Commerce Financial Incentive Program Application Portal should click 'Log In' or 'Forgot Password' if needed. After account creation, an email with further instructions will be sent.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Soft Landing Exchange for Maryland Companies
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps Maryland companies test expanding into new international markets at affordable rates. Companies get access to facilities, resources, networking, advisors, and support through a network of official partner organizations in strategic markets around the world.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating Maryland companies can receive up to $10,000 in funding to help offset costs associated with the program. This funding can be used to help pay for travel costs (flight, lodging, transportation) and program participation costs charged by partner programs. Companies also receive access to facilities, resources, networking opportunities, and advisory support through partner organizations in Australia, France, Ireland, Netherlands, Japan, and United Kingdom.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland companies seeking to expand into new international markets
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Travel costs (flight, lodging, transportation) and program participation costs charged by partner programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Companies must be based in Maryland to participate.
requirements_list: Company must be based in Maryland
Company must be seeking to expand to new markets abroad
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible companies can apply for funding to help offset costs associated with participation in the program. Contact Jason Callejas for application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Military Personnel and Veteran-Owned Small Business Loan Program (MPVSBLP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides no-interest loans of up to $50,000 (with some records indicating up to $100,000) from one to eight years for businesses owned by military veterans, Reservists, or National Guard personnel, as well as for small businesses of fifty or fewer employees that employ or are owned by such persons. Eligible uses include general business expenses caused by deployment and accessibility improvements for service-disabled veterans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-interest loans up to $50,000 (up to $100,000 per some program details) with repayment terms from one to eight years. The repayment period may align with the useful life of any equipment purchased with the funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Military veterans, Reservists, National Guard personnel who own businesses, and small businesses of fifty or fewer employees that employ or are owned by such persons.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General business expenses, including costs caused by owner deployment to active duty; accessibility improvements for homes, vehicles, or workplaces for service-disabled veterans; equipment purchases; and other necessary business costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must be owned by a military veteran, Reservist, or National Guard member, or be a small business of fifty or fewer employees employing such persons.
Must be a small business with fewer than 50 employees.
Submit a Business Plan with 3-year projections.
Provide a current Personal Financial Statement.
Provide a list of all owners and their ownership percentages.
Submit a resume for the principal owner(s).
Include personal federal tax returns with all schedules for the two most recent years.
Include business federal tax returns with all schedules for the two most recent years.
Explain the amount of personal or business funds contributed to the project.
Explain the type of collateral provided to secure the loan.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the Maryland Department of Commerce. The Maryland Department of Veterans & Military Families then reviews it for basic eligibility. If eligible, the Department of Commerce conducts a financial review and underwriting.

structured_extraction.program_name: More Jobs for Marylanders Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax incentive program that provides refundable income tax credits to manufacturing businesses and non-manufacturing businesses located in Opportunity Zones that create new full-time jobs in Maryland. Manufacturers must be primarily engaged in production activities (NAICS sectors 31, 32, or 33) and non-manufacturers must locate in Opportunity Zones. The program sunsetted on June 1, 2024, and is no longer accepting new applications.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description:
For businesses enrolled before June 1, 2022: New businesses in Tier 1 jurisdictions receive a refundable State income tax credit of 5.75% of wages for each qualified position, a credit against State property tax ($0.112 per $100 assessed), refund of Sales and Use Tax, and waiver of SDAT fees for the creation of 5 or more new jobs. Existing businesses in Tier 1 and Tier 2 jurisdictions receive a refundable State income tax credit of 5.75% of wages for each qualified position for the creation of 5 new jobs (Tier 1) or 10 new jobs (Tier 2). Benefits are available for a 10-year consecutive period.

For businesses enrolled on or after June 1, 2022 and before June 1, 2024: Businesses in Tier 1 jurisdictions receive a refundable State income tax credit of 4.75% of wages for each qualified position for a 10-year consecutive benefit period. Businesses in Tier 2 jurisdictions receive a refundable State income tax credit of 4.75% of wages for each qualified position for a 5-year consecutive benefit period. Real property tax credit, sales and use tax refund, and SDAT fee waiver were eliminated for this cohort.

Tier 1 Areas include Baltimore City, Allegany, Baltimore County, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Prince Geor ge's, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties, plus Opportunity Zones located in any Maryland county. Tier 2 Areas are any areas not designated as Tier 1. Total income tax credits are capped in each fiscal year, with funding priority given first to Tier 1 projects that received final certificates in the previous fiscal year, then Tier 2 projects from the previous year, then new Tier 1 projects, then new Tier 2 projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program sunsetted June 1, 2024. No longer accepting applications. Only businesses that received an Enrollment Certificate prior to June 1, 2024 can participate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Manufacturing businesses primarily engaged in production activities (NAICS sectors 31, 32, 33, except refiners) and non-manufacturing businesses located in Opportunity Zones that create new full-time jobs. Program is closed to new enrollments as of June 1, 2024.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit is based on wages paid to qualified positions. For enrolled businesses, manufacturers may also benefit from accelerated and bonus depreciation, Maryland sales and use tax exemption on machinery and equipment used in production, and job training grants through the Partnership for Workforce Quality and Apprenticeship Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Tier 1 Areas include Baltimore City, Allegany, Baltimore County, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Prince George's, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties. Tier 1 Areas also include Opportunity Zones located in any Maryland county. Tier 2 Areas are any areas not designated as Tier 1. Non-manufacturers must be located in Opportunity Zones.
requirements_list: Manufacturers must be primarily engaged in activities under NAICS sectors 31, 32, or 33 (except refiners)

For businesses enrolled before June 1, 2022: Manufacturers in Tier 1 Areas must create at least 5 new qualified full-time positions; manufacturers in Tier 2 Areas must create at least 10 new qualified positions. For businesses enrolled on or after June 1, 2022: Manufacturers in Tier 1 counties must create at least 10 new qualified jobs; manufacturers in Tier 2 counties must create at least 20 new qualified jobs

Non-manufacturers must create at least 5 new qualified positions (for businesses enrolled before June 1, 2022) or at least 10 new qualified positions (for businesses enrolled on or after June 1, 2022)

For businesses enrolled before June 1, 2022, a qualified position for manufacturers is full-time, pays at least 120% of state minimum wage, is newly created, was not moved from another Maryland facility, and is filled for at least 12 months. For businesses enrolled on or after June 1, 2022, a qualified position for manufacturers is full-time, pays at least 150% of state minimum wage (as of 1/1/2025, minimum wage requirement is $22.50 per hour), is newly created, was not moved from another Maryland facility, and is filled for at least 12 months
A qualified position for non-manufacturers is full-time, pays at least $50,000 per year, is newly created, was not moved from another Maryland facility, and is filled for at least 12 months
Business must offer ongoing job training or a post-secondary education program (such as tuition reimbursement) and must continue offering training for the entire benefit period
Business must provide a Notice of Intent to Commerce before beginning hiring
Business must begin hiring within 12 months of Notice of Intent
Business must add the required minimum number of qualified positions within 12 months after the date of first new hire
Existing businesses that moved their facility from one Maryland county to another after June 1, 2017 are not eligible

Non-manufacturing businesses cannot provide adult entertainment, be primarily engaged in retail activities (except grocery stores), be primarily engaged in sale or distribution of alcoholic beverages, be a private or commercial golf course or country club, be a tanning salon, or be a bail bondsman
Business must have received a Program Enrollment Certificate of Approval prior to June 1, 2024 to participate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process consists of multiple stages. First, businesses must provide a Notice of Intent (NOI) to Commerce before beginning hiring. Commerce then provides an enrollment application. Upon receipt of the completed Project Enrollment Application, Commerce certifies the company as a Qualified Business Entity. Enrolled businesses submit an Initial Income Tax Application no sooner than July of the fiscal year following the close of their first fully completed fiscal year in the program, including a list of projected jobs and wages for that year. Commerce calculates a maximum credit for the business for that benefit year and issues an Initial Income Tax Credit Certificate (Initial Certificate), which reserves the income tax credit. After designated positions are filled for a period of 12 months, the business applies for the Final Income Tax Credit Certification (Final Certificate). The amount of credit on the Final Certificate is the amount of credit the business may claim for that benefit year and cannot exceed the amount reserved on the Initial Certificate. Applicants must register for an account and login to the online system at https://programs.commerce.maryland.gov/jobcredits to complete applications. NOTE: Commerce is no longer accepting Notices of Intent or new Enrollment Applications as the program sunsetted on June 1, 2024. Only businesses that received an Enrollment Certificate prior to that date can participate. Businesses that received certification may continue to submit Initial and Final Income Tax Credit applications for their remaining benefit years.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state income tax credit for businesses that invest in an economic development project in a Tier 1 County and create a minimum number of new full-time qualified jobs. The credit amount depends on the number of jobs created and qualified costs incurred, with a maximum credit of up to $5 million. Eligible Tier 1 Counties include Allegany, Baltimore City, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester. The program also allows qualified opportunity zones in Allegany County, Garrett County, Somerset County, or Wicomico County.
list_of_eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A state income tax credit of up to $5 million based on job creation and eligible project costs. For businesses creating 10-24 qualified positions with at least $1 million in eligible project costs, maximum credit is $1 million. For 25-49 qualified positions with at least $2.5 million in eligible project costs, maximum credit is $2.5 million. For at least 50 qualified positions with at least $5 million in eligible project costs, maximum credit is $5 million. The credit is applied against Maryland state income tax and may be carried forward for up to 10 years following the credit year (the first taxable year in which the project is placed in service). Beginning the 4th year after the credit year, a business may apply the credit against state income tax liability and request a refund limited to payroll withholding attributable to qualified positions. For insurance companies, the credit may be claimed against insurance premium tax. The business must report annually to the Department the amount of project tax credit claimed on its tax return; failure to provide this information will disqualify the entity from claiming any unclaimed amount of credit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit businesses that invest in economic development projects in Tier 1 Counties and create new full-time jobs paying at least 120% of state minimum wage within 24 months.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible project costs including land acquisition, performance and contract bonds, insurance, architectural and engineering services, environmental mitigation, utility installation, interest costs prior to and during acquisition and construction and for up to 2 years after completion, legal and accounting fees, fixed telecommunication equipment, office furniture and equipment, costs related to acquiring, constructing, rehabilitating, installing, and equipping an economic development project, furnishings to equip a new location for ordinary business functions (computers, nonrecurring telecommunications equipment), and moving costs directly related to relocation from outside Maryland to a Tier 1 County location.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The project must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) in a Tier 1 County, or in a qualified opportunity zone in Allegany County, Garrett County, Somerset County, or Wicomico County. Tier 1 Counties include Allegany, Baltimore City, Caroline, Dorchester, Garrett, Kent, Somerset, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester (subject to change based on 24-month look back provision). PFAs include state enterprise zones, federal empowerment zones, Department of Housing and Community Development Sustainable Communities, incorporated municipalities, areas between I-495 beltway and Washington D.C. and I-695 beltway and Baltimore City, and growth areas designated by each county.
requirements_list: Must declare intent to Maryland Commerce in writing prior to incurring eligible costs or creating new jobs by submitting Notice of Intent to taxincentives.commerce@maryland.gov
Must be certified as a qualified business entity eligible for One Maryland Tax Credit
Must create at least 10 new full-time qualified positions within 24 months; more positions yield higher maximum credits (25+ positions for $2.5M max, 50+ positions for $5M max)

Positions must be full-time (at least 840 hours during at least 24 weeks in a 6-month period), pay at least 120% of State Minimum Wage (as of January 1, 2024, $18.00 per hour), be filled for 12 months, and be a net new job to Maryland
Must incur at least $500,000 of eligible project costs

Project must be primarily engaged in an eligible activity including manufacturing, mining, transportation, communications, filmmaking, resort/recreational business, agriculture, forestry, fishing, research/development/testing, biotechnology, computer programming/IT services, central financial/real estate/insurance services, central administrative offices, company headquarters, public utility, warehousing, or other business services
Must not claim both One Maryland Tax Credit and Job Creation Tax Credit in the same tax year
If moving from another Maryland location, Secretary must determine the move would not have significant deleterious effect on the other location
Full-time position requires at least 840 hours during at least 24 weeks in a 6-month period (average 35 hours per week)
New jobs cannot result from change in ownership, consolidation, merger, restructuring, or contractual shift of employment function
Business must establish or expand facility at a single location in a Tier 1 County within a Priority Funding Area or qualified opportunity zone
Must begin hiring within 12 months after notifying Department of intent
Must begin construction, acquisition, or installation of project within 12 months after notifying Department of intent
Must complete the economic development project within 3 years of commencement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit Notice of Intent to taxincentives.commerce@maryland.gov declaring intent to seek certification before incurring any eligible costs or hiring qualified employees. 2. Receive preliminary application and employment affidavit from Commerce with projected job and wage data. 3. Commerce issues Preliminary Certificate of Eligibility if business qualifies. 4. Business has 12 months from intent date to start project and 3 years to complete it. 5. Once project is complete and minimum required jobs are created and filled for 12 months, submit final application including list of qualified positions/employees, eligible costs documentation, and other required information. Commerce may require sample documentation to verify costs. 6. Commerce issues Final Certificate listing certified credit amount. 7. Attach Final Certificate to tax return claiming the credit. 8. Apply through online portal at https://programs.commerce.maryland.gov/jobcredits (must register first at https://programs.commerce.maryland.gov/jobcreditsregister). 9. Report to Commerce annually the amount of project tax credit claimed on tax return; failure to report disqualifies unclaimed credits.

structured_extraction.program_description: A matching grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Commerce that provides funding to help small and mid-sized manufacturing and technology companies improve the skills and competitiveness of their workers. The program supports on-the-job training, classroom or offsite training, purchase of training software, and train-the-trainer scenarios to benefit new and incumbent workers, with a focus on new technologies and production processes to improve employee productivity and employment stability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants reimburse up to 50% of qualified training project costs. The minimum grant award is $10,000 (requiring a total project cost of at least $20,000), and a company can receive a maximum of $200,000 per year. Eligible costs include curriculum development, course books, materials, instructor salaries and expenses. Employers pay for training upfront; upon successful completion of training, employers submit certificates and purchase order or invoice paperwork for review and reimbursement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and mid-sized manufacturing and technology companies in Maryland with at least 10 full-time employees, including Anne Arundel County-based technology companies and for-profit businesses creating jobs through expansion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: On-the-job training, classroom or offsite training, purchase of training software, train-the-trainer scenarios, curriculum development, course books, materials, and instructor salaries and expenses for new and incumbent workers focused on new technologies and production processes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; Anne Arundel County-based technology companies are specifically eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland employer.
Must have a minimum of ten full-time employees.
Must not be in arrears with any State taxing agency.
Must not be in default with any Commerce program.
The total training project cost must be at least $20,000.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the regional representative from the Maryland Department of Commerce for your county or region. Submit a matching grant application. Upon approval and agreement finalization, the employer pays for training upfront. After successful completion of training, the employer submits certificates and purchase order or invoice paperwork for review and reimbursement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland provides income tax credits to businesses that invest in research and development in Maryland. The credit equals ten percent of eligible R&D expenses incurred during the taxable year that exceed a calculated Maryland Base Amount. The total amount of available credits is capped each year at $12 million, with a $3.5 million set-aside for small businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The tax credit equals ten percent (10%) of eligible R&D expenses incurred during the taxable year in excess of the Maryland Base Amount. The Maryland Base Amount is calculated using the base amount formula from Section 41(c) of the Internal Revenue Code, adjusted for Maryland qualified research and development expenses and Maryland gross receipts. For first-time applicants with no prior taxable years of R&D expenses in Maryland, the Base Amount equals zero. The maximum credit for a single applicant is $250,000. The total statutory cap is $12 million annually, with a $3.5 million set-aside for small businesses and an $8.5 million cap for non-small businesses. If the total credits applied for exceed the applicable cap, the business's R&D tax credit is prorated proportionally. For small businesses (with net book value assets less than $5 million), R&D tax credits are refundable to the extent that the tax credits exceed the income tax liability for that taxable year. For non-small businesses, unused credits can be carried forward and applied against State income tax for up to 7 taxable years following the year the expenses were incurred. The tax credit remains in effect until June 30, 2027, subject to extension by the General Assembly.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: NO LATER THAN NOVEMBER 15 of the calendar year following the tax year in which the Maryland Qualified Research and Development expenses were incurred. Applications for Tax Year 2025 will be available from June 1, 2026, through November 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses, individuals, corporations, limited liability companies, partnerships, and sole proprietorships that incur qualified research and development expenses in Maryland, including small businesses with net book value assets less than $5 million.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit applies to qualified research and development expenses as defined by Section 41(b) of the Internal Revenue Code that are incurred in Maryland. Maryland qualified research and development means qualified research as defined in Section 41(d) of the Internal Revenue Code that is conducted in this State.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Expenses must be incurred in Maryland. Maryland qualified research and development must be conducted within the State. The program applies statewide to all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Business must incur Qualified Research and Development Expenses as defined by Section 41(b) of the Internal Revenue Code in Maryland
Maryland qualified research and development must be conducted in Maryland as defined by Section 41(d) of the Internal Revenue Code
Business must follow the federal definition of qualified R&D and qualified R&D expenses

For small business designation, net book value assets must total less than $5,000,000 at the beginning or end of the taxable year as reported on the balance sheet; small businesses include for-profit corporations, limited liability companies, partnerships, or sole proprietorships
Net book value assets includes total net value of assets including intangibles but not including liabilities, minus depreciation and amortization
Application must be submitted by November 15 of the calendar year following the tax year in which expenses were incurred
Small businesses must submit documentation showing net book value assets of less than $5 million
Credit cannot exceed $250,000 for a single applicant
If first year incurring R&D expenses, Maryland Base Amount equals zero
All members of the same controlled group of corporations shall be treated as a single taxpayer
Maryland gross receipts must be reasonably attributable to conduct of trade or business in Maryland, determined under methods prescribed by the Comptroller
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses submit an application through the Department of Commerce by November 15 of the calendar year following the taxable year in which expenses were incurred. The application must include qualified R&D expenses incurred in Maryland, and for small businesses, documentation of net book value assets less than $5 million. The Maryland Department of Commerce reviews the application and certifies the approved credit amount by February 15 of the calendar year following the application year. If approved credits exceed the annual cap, credits are prorated proportionally. After receiving certification, the business may either: (1) file an amended tax return for the year the expenses were incurred with a copy of the Department's certification attached, or (2) attach a copy of the Department's certification to an income tax return filed for any of the 7 taxable years following the year the expenses were incurred. For non-small businesses, unused credits can be carried forward against State income tax for up to 7 taxable years after the expense year. Small businesses may claim a refund of excess credits that exceed their income tax liability for that taxable year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small, Minority and Women-Owned Business Account - Video Lottery Terminal Fund (VLT)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state program using 1.5% of proceeds from video lottery terminals at Maryland casinos to provide below-market-rate loans to small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses. At least 50% of allocations are deployed to businesses located in targeted areas surrounding Maryland's six casinos, while the remaining 50% is available to eligible businesses throughout the state. Distribution is overseen by eligible regional fund managers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $10,000 to $1,000,000 (up to $500,000 for some fund managers). Interest rates are tied to the Prime Rate and currently set at Prime plus 1%. Terms are up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets. Loan amounts are flexible but typically between $25,000 and $250,000 depending on fund manager. At least 50% of VLT allocations go to small, minority, and women-owned businesses located within targeted areas around six Maryland casinos: Maryland Live! (Anne Arundel County), Hollywood Casino Perryville (Cecil County), Rocky Gap (Allegany County), Ocean Downs (Worcester County), Horseshoe Casino (Baltimore City), and National Harbor (Prince George's County). The remaining 50% is available to eligible businesses throughout Maryland. A non-refundable application fee of $250 is required for loans over $25,000, or $25 for loans between $10,000–$25,000. A 1% loan origination fee is assessed at closing. As of June 30, 2024, since program inception: 1,381 transactions approved for $154.1 million, projected to create 6,177 new jobs and retain 10,094 jobs, leveraging $262.3 million in private sector capital. A total of 1,240 transactions have settled for $130.2 million, expected to create 5,266 jobs and retain 9,038 jobs, leveraging $240.8 million in private sector capital. For FY 2024: 176 transactions approved for $22.2 million, projected to create 609 jobs and retain 1,709 jobs, leveraging $15.6 million in private sector capital. 173 transactions settled for $21.3 million, expected to create 732 jobs and retain 1,866 jobs, leveraging $16.4 million in private sector capital. Legislation allows fund managers to provide grants up to $10,000 when paired with SMWOBA loan.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling — applications accepted on a continual basis.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Multiple fund managers; see program website. Regional fund managers include: Anne Arundel County Economic Development Corporation (AAEDC), Baltimore County Department of Economic and Workforce Development (DEWD), Baltimore Development Corporation (BDC), FSC First (Prince George's Financial Services Corporation), Howard County Economic Development Authority (HCEDA), Maryland Capital Enterprises (MCE), Meridian Management Group (MMG), Montgomery County Economic Development Corporation (MCEDC), and Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (TCCWMD).
structured_extraction.contact_email: jsmith@fscfirst.com; sprimosch@aaedc.org; tim.smoot@mmgcapitalgroup.com; mames@marylandcapital.org; sjacobs@baltimorecountymd.gov; jpillas@baltimoredevelopment.com; dhpatel@hceda.org; cfunk@tccwmd.org; laurie@thinkmoco.com; applummer@co.pg.md.us; info@tccwmd.org
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses throughout Maryland, with priority consideration for businesses located within targeted areas surrounding Maryland's six casinos.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business acquisition and expansion, owner-occupied commercial real estate, leasehold improvements, purchase of equipment, start-up costs, working capital, professional and technical assistance, refinancing of existing debt under certain circumstances, vehicles, furniture and fixtures, inventory expansion, and marketing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to eligible small, minority, and women-owned businesses. At least 50% of funds are allocated to businesses in targeted areas surrounding six Maryland casinos: Maryland Live! (Anne Arundel County), Hollywood Casino Perryville (Cecil County), Rocky Gap (Allegany County), Ocean Downs (Worcester County), Horseshoe Casino (Baltimore City), and National Harbor (Prince George's County). All of Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties are also recognized as a targeted area. Individual fund managers serve specific geographic regions: AAEDC serves Anne Arundel County; DEWD serves Baltimore County; BDC serves Baltimore City; FSC First serves Prince George's County with expanded service into Montgomery, Howard, Charles, and Calvert Counties; HCEDA serves Howard County and statewide through Catalyst Fund; MCE serves the Eastern Shore (Worcester, Wicomico, Somerset, Dorchester, Talbot, Queen Anne's, Kent, and Caroline Counties) and Baltimore City, Baltimore, and Anne Arundel Counties; MMG serves businesses statewide with geographic focus on casino-adjacent areas; MCEDC serves Montgomery County; TCCWMD serves the three Western Maryland counties (Allegany, Garrett, and Washington).
requirements_list: Must be a small, minority, women, or veteran-owned business
Business plan is required
Personal credit score of 650 is generally required; lower scores may be considered
Personal guarantees required from all owners with 20% or greater interest
Minimum equity injection of 10% generally required for start-up businesses
Non-refundable application fee of $250 for loans over $25,000; $25 for loans between $10,000–$25,000
1% loan origination fee assessed at closing
Collateral required, including Deeds of Trust, Machinery and Equipment liens, Personal Guarantees, and Key Man Life Insurance
Standard underwriting practices apply: repayment capacity, debt service coverage, financial strength, industry and management experience, and collateral protection
Business must be located in a targeted area surrounding a Maryland casino (for priority allocation) or anywhere in Maryland (for general allocation)
Business must demonstrate ability to repay the loan with documentable income
Business must be legally organized as a for-profit entity (for MCE loans)
Business must create and/or retain employment (requirements vary by fund manager)

For MCE loans: must have been turned down by a traditional lender prior to application; must agree to financial business counseling before and after loan closing; must submit to periodic site visits and credit checks as deemed necessary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the fund manager serving your geographic area. Submit an inquiry form and personal financial statement along with a business plan. Provide business and personal financial documentation demonstrating repayment capacity. Applications are reviewed using standard underwriting practices. Multiple regional fund managers oversee VLT distribution; see the program website for the full list of fund managers by region and their specific service areas. Fund managers offer complementary development services to support business operations. Commerce conducts annual customer satisfaction surveys; recent surveys show 87% of borrowers are satisfied with service received from fund managers, 72% state the loan was helpful for growing their business, and 67% are likely to hire new employees in the next year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Small, Minority and Women-Owned Business Account COVID-19 RELIEF Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Small, Minority and Women-Owned Business Account COVID-19 RELIEF Program provides $10 million in state relief funds to small, minority, and women-owned businesses impacted by COVID-19. Established in 2021 through bipartisan legislation, the program is administered through existing regional fund managers across Maryland, also known as the Video Lottery Terminal (VLT) program. It supports businesses facing continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus pandemic.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $10 million in relief funding available through regional fund managers for small, minority, and women-owned businesses impacted by COVID-19. Funds are administered through existing fund managers in various regions of the state as part of the Video Lottery Terminal (VLT) program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, minority, and women-owned businesses in Maryland facing financial impacts from COVID-19
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: COVID-19 relief and recovery for businesses negatively impacted by the pandemic
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland through regional fund managers
requirements_list: Business must be small, minority, or women-owned
Business must have been negatively impacted by COVID-19
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available through regional fund managers located in various regions of the state. Contact the appropriate fund manager for application details and availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: A refundable tax credit equal to 25% of qualified production costs incurred in Maryland by eligible theatrical production entities. The credit applies to live stage theatrical productions that meet specific criteria, with a minimum production cost requirement of $100,000 in Maryland and a maximum credit of $2 million per production.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A refundable credit of 25% against Maryland state income tax for qualified production costs incurred in Maryland. The maximum tax credit is limited to $2 million per theatrical production. Costs must be incurred in Maryland and include items such as set construction and operation, special and visual effects, wardrobe, makeup, sound, lighting, salaries and wages for work performed in Maryland, advertising and public relations, facility and equipment rental, vehicle leasing, food and lodging, and travel expenses for bringing cast and crew to Maryland. Direct costs must exceed $100,000 to qualify. The credit is applied by filing the applicable Maryland state income tax return, completing Form 500CR, and including a copy of the Tax Credit Certificate. The credit is only available through electronic filing. If the tax credit allowed in any taxable year exceeds the total tax otherwise payable, the entity may claim a refund for the excess amount.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted for FY2023 tax credits through June 1, 2023; rolling basis with no permanent deadline specified
structured_extraction.contact_name: Robin Bailey, Director of Policy and Program Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit theatrical production entities that produce National Touring Productions or Pre-Broadway Productions in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified direct production costs incurred in Maryland, including set construction and operation, special and visual effects, wardrobe and makeup, sound and lighting, salaries and wages for work performed in Maryland, advertising and public relations, facility and equipment rental, vehicle leasing, food and lodging, travel expenses for bringing cast and crew to Maryland, and other authorized direct costs as specified in the Authorized Direct Costs list. Costs must be reasonable and negotiated at arms-length. Direct costs may only be attributed to the production once and must be the net cost of goods or services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All production costs must be incurred within Maryland. National Touring Productions must perform for a total of four weeks or more in at least four cities outside the State after completing performances in Maryland. Pre-Broadway Productions must be prepared exclusively in a qualified theatrical production facility in Maryland for presentation in the Broadway theater district within twelve months after the final performance in Maryland. Principal production must begin within 120 days after issuance of the Letter of Qualification, which may be extended at the Department's discretion.
requirements_list: Production must be for-profit
Production must be a live stage theatrical production performed in a qualified theatrical production facility (theater)
Production must be either a National Touring Production or Pre-Broadway Production
National Touring Productions must have at least two public performances
Pre-Broadway Productions must have at least eight public performances
Estimated total direct production costs incurred in Maryland must exceed $100,000
For National Touring Productions: production must perform for a total of four weeks or more in at least four cities outside the State after final performance in Maryland

For Pre-Broadway Productions: production must be in original or adaptive version, never performed or performed on limited basis in preceding five years, and prepared exclusively for Broadway presentation within twelve months of final Maryland performance
All statutory requirements must be met
Application for Qualification must be complete and signed with completed Application Addendum
Theatrical Production Entity must demonstrate financing
Principal production must begin within 120 days after Letter of Qualification issuance (may be extended at Department discretion)
No salary, wages, or compensation to any individual can exceed $100,000 per week (includes all forms of compensation and other compensation)
All outstanding amounts owed to Maryland entities providing goods or services must be paid before Tax Credit Certificate is issued

All goods and services must be provided by a qualified vendor (registered and in good standing with Maryland, maintains physical location in State, provides services in vendor's ordinary course of business)
For specialized/technical goods or services not reasonably available from qualified vendors, prior Department approval required via Due Diligence form
Direct costs must be for time or use in Maryland and pro-rated based on time personnel or materials are in Maryland
Only travel expenses into Maryland are authorized; round trip fares divided in half
Either relocation fee or housing/living allowance authorized, not both
For materials/goods over $1,000, direct cost equals initial cost less resale value upon completion
Costs for writers, directors, and producers (whose credited position contains these titles) are excluded; technical crew with these titles may be included
Costs for entertainment, gifts, gratuities, vehicle purchases for personal use, penalties, fines, taxes to other jurisdictions, and recouped insurance costs are not eligible
All Maryland tax obligations must be current and all Maryland contracts must not be in default
If non-resident entity, must register to do business in Maryland before beginning production activity
Theatrical Production company must comply with all applicable Maryland laws, rules, and regulations
All loan out and personal services companies are subject to Maryland withholding requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Before beginning any work on the theatrical production in the State, submit a complete and signed Application for Qualification with all required attachments (Application Addendum, proof of financing, evidence of qualifying performances, copy of script/libretto/score, expected production schedule, and pre-production budget) to the Department via email at robin.bailey1@maryland.gov. Applications are reviewed and approved in the order received. Materially incomplete applications will not be considered. Step 2: Within 30 days of receiving a complete application, the Department issues a Letter of Qualification stating the maximum tax credit amount available and the fiscal year from which credits will be drawn. Applicants who do not meet minimum statutory requirements or submit an incomplete application will be notified they are not eligible. Step 3: Before the first rehearsal, submit the completed Application Addendum with proof of registration to do business in Maryland (if applicable), good standing certificates, and insurance certificates showing general liability, excess liability/umbrella, all risk/property, and worker's compensation coverage, along with unemployment insurance account number and information about chief internal accountant, independent CPA/bond company, payroll service, and production accountant. Step 4: Principal production must begin within 120 days of Letter of Qualification issuance (may be extended at Department discretion based on facts and circumstances beyond control). Step 5: After completing all required performances, within 180 days of the completion date (may be extended at Department discretion), submit the Application for Final Tax Credit Certification with all required final documentation including: complete final payroll/earnings reports for all employees, complete final general ledger and GL by production expenditure codes, complete final vendor/accounts payable list, list of all employees employed in Maryland with resident state, list of all Maryland residents employed, list of all Maryland businesses that provided goods or services (including minority and small business designations), list of all loan out/personal services companies with FEIN and address, completed Maryland Theatrical Production Expenditure Report, copy of final production schedule, copy of final crew list, copies of all call sheets, and copy of final contact list. If total authorized direct costs exceed $250,000, include copy of independent auditor's report meeting minimum criteria for Agreed Upon Procedures (must be approved draft engagement letter from licensed Maryland CPA). Step 6: The Department reviews all documentation for completeness, accuracy, and confirmation of total direct costs. Department determines sample sizes and percentages for auditor review. Theatrical Production entity must certify no amounts are owed to any Maryland entity providing goods or services. Step 7: Based on actual total of direct costs (authorized costs only) as established by Department review, Department issues Tax Credit Certificate not exceeding the amount specified in the Letter of Qualification. Step 8: The qualified theatrical production entity owner or designee files the applicable Maryland state income tax return, completes Form 500CR, and includes a copy of the Tax Credit Certificate. The credit is only available through electronic filing. Any decision made by the Department during the application process is considered final. Qualification may be rescinded for failure to meet any deadline or requirement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Winery and Vineyard Economic Development Grant Program (WVEDG)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Winery and Vineyard Economic Development Grant Program (WVEDG) provides financial assistance to individuals and corporations to establish a new winery or vineyard in Maryland, or to complete capital improvements at an existing winery or vineyard. Commerce provides a grant equal to 25% of qualified capital expenses, supporting growth in Maryland's wine industry.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a grant for 25% of qualified capital expenses for establishing a new winery or vineyard, or making capital improvements to an existing one. Total of $1 million is available for the program per cycle. Eligible expenses include barrels and bins, canopy management machines, fermenters or other fermentation devices, fruit harvesters, irrigation equipment, presses, seeders, tanks, bottling equipment, and other agricultural materials. Grants do not cover costs of constructing buildings, utilities, labor, or general supplies. A related state income tax credit of 25% of qualified capital expenses (up to $500,000 total per tax year, prorated if applications exceed this amount) is also available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually on September 15; most recent cycle: January 16, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals or corporations that operate or want to establish a winery or vineyard in Maryland, including new entities looking to establish a winery or vineyard presence and existing operations seeking capital improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified capital expenses for establishing a new winery or vineyard, or making capital improvements to an existing one. Eligible expenses include barrels and bins, canopy management machines, fermenters or other fermentation devices, fruit harvesters, irrigation equipment, presses, seeders, tanks, bottling equipment, tractors, and fruit plants. Funds may not be used for constructing buildings, utilities, labor, or general supplies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The winery or vineyard must be located in Maryland. Program is available statewide.
requirements_list: Must be an individual or corporation establishing a new winery or vineyard in Maryland, or making capital improvements to an existing one
A qualified winery must hold a Class 3 or Class 4 winery license from the Comptroller of Maryland
A qualified vineyard must be at least one continuous acre of agricultural land in Maryland used only for growing grapes for a licensed Maryland winery
Applicants must submit a detailed report of expenses with proof of purchase
Capital expenses must be for either establishing a new winery or vineyard, or making capital improvements to an existing one
Maximum $500,000 in total tax credits per tax year (credits prorated if total applications exceed $500,000)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit an online application to the Maryland Department of Commerce by the deadline (annually on September 15, with awards made by December 15). The application must include a detailed report of expenses with supporting documents. Commerce will review the application and certify the grant amount. For more information, visit commerce.maryland.gov/wvedg.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Enterprise Zone Tax Credit program provides real property and state income tax credits to businesses located in Maryland enterprise zones in return for job creation and investments. Businesses in designated focus areas may also qualify for personal property tax credits and enhanced income tax credits. The program was created in 1982 and currently includes 34 enterprise zones across 19 Maryland jurisdictions, with two jurisdictions (Baltimore City and Prince George's County) also operating focus areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Commerce, Office of Finance Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses receive state income tax credits and real property tax credits based on job creation and capital improvements. General income tax credit is $1,000 per qualified new employee in an enterprise zone, or $1,500 in a focus area (one-time credit). Income tax credit for economically disadvantaged employees provides $3,000 first year, $2,000 second year, and $1,000 third year in enterprise zones; $4,500, $3,000, and $1,500 respectively in focus areas (three-year credit totaling $6,000 in EZ or $9,000 in focus area). Real property tax credits provide 80% of eligible assessment for 10 years (for properties constructed between January 1, 2019 and January 1, 2022, the credit extends to 13 years with 80% for first 8 years, then decreasing 10% annually). Focus area businesses also receive personal property tax credits at 80% of eligible assessment for 10 years. In FY 2025, businesses received property tax credits totaling $56.3 million based on real property investments of $5 billion. The State reimburses participating local jurisdictions 50% of the foregone local property tax revenue.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 15 and October 15 annually for new designations and expansions
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses located in designated Maryland enterprise zones that create new jobs or make capital improvements. Businesses must be certified by the local enterprise zone administrator as eligible for the credit.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits are applied against state income tax liability or local property taxes for businesses that hire new employees or make investments in real or personal property within enterprise zones. Credits can be used for capital improvements, renovation, or expansion of real property, and investment in new personal property (in focus areas only).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in one of 34 designated Enterprise Zones across 19 Maryland jurisdictions (Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties), or in one of 6 designated focus areas in Baltimore City or Prince George's County. An interactive map is available at commerce.maryland.gov to verify if a specific address falls within an Enterprise Zone.
requirements_list: Business must be certified by the local enterprise zone administrator as eligible for the credit
For income tax credits: employee must be hired after business located in zone or after zone designated
Employee must be employed at least 35 hours per week for six months (12 months in focus areas) before or during taxable year credit is taken
Employee must spend at least 50% of work time in the enterprise zone or on activities resulting from business location in zone
Employee must be hired to fill a new position, increasing firm's full-time positions by the number of credits taken
