Employee must earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage
For economically disadvantaged employee credit: business must obtain certification from Maryland Department of Labor, Licensing, and Regulation (Department of Labor)
Economically disadvantaged employees must remain in position for three years to receive full credit
For property tax credits: business must make capital improvements or hire new employees and meet all state and local eligibility requirements
Business entity does not include persons owning, operating, developing, constructing, or rehabilitating property intended for use primarily as single or multifamily residential property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Contact the local enterprise zone administrator for your jurisdiction to determine eligibility and obtain certification. A list of administrators and their contact information is available on the Department of Commerce website. Step 2: Once certified by the local administrator, businesses claiming income tax credits file Maryland Tax Form 500CR with their state tax return to the Maryland Comptroller. For income tax credits, the credit is claimed in the year it is earned. If the credit exceeds state income tax liability in a given year, the excess can be carried forward up to 5 years. Step 3: For property tax credits, the business must be certified, and the credit is administered through local property tax assessments handled by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). Businesses should work with their local jurisdiction's tax assessor after receiving certification from the enterprise zone administrator.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: A no-interest loan program operated by the Department of Commerce that provides financing for capital expenses to licensed child care providers participating in the State Department of Education's Child Care Scholarship Program. The program supports acquisition, expansion, renovation, and new construction of child care facilities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Commerce, with support from the State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-interest loans for capital expenses related to child care facilities including acquisition, expansion, renovations, and new construction. Loans must be repaid within five years after receiving proceeds. No application fees or prepayment penalties are charged. Collateral is required and may include personal guarantees, liens on business assets, and pledges of accounts. For loans of $50,000 or less, collateral can be a leased property if the lease is in effect for the five-year repayment period. For loans exceeding $50,000, owned property must be used as collateral. Loan amounts and specific terms vary based on project needs and borrower qualifications. A financial hardship exemption may be granted to allow additional time to repay the loan. Eligible uses include driveway expansion for parking, decks, outdoor patios, fences, playgrounds, and furniture for the child care facility. Funds cannot be used for vehicles, working capital, operations (marketing, payroll, lease/rent, supplies, utilities), refinancing existing debt, or paying outstanding state or federal taxes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application period closed January 30, 2026. Please revisit this webpage for updates on when the next round of funding will occur this calendar year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers participating in the Maryland State Department of Education's Child Care Scholarship Program, including both existing licensed providers and new providers or those opening additional locations (evaluated on a case-by-case basis).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital expenses for child care facilities including acquisition (purchase of existing facilities), expansion (construction or purchase of additional space), renovation (repairs, upgrades), and new construction. Eligible uses include driveway expansion for parking, decks, patios, fences, playgrounds, and furniture for the child care facility. Funds cannot be used for working capital or operations such as marketing, payroll, lease or rent expense, supplies, or utilities; vehicles; refinancing existing debt; or payment of outstanding state or federal taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Loan proceeds must be used for a child care facility location operating in Maryland. Priority is given to providers located in: (1) rural communities; (2) underserved communities or areas lacking available child care slots; (3) areas serving primarily low-income populations in high poverty areas; (4) facilities serving children with special needs; and (5) facilities serving children ages 2 and younger.
requirements_list: Must be licensed by the State Department of Education (or applying as new provider or additional location, evaluated case-by-case)
Must be a participant in the State Department of Education's Child Care Scholarship Program
Must possess a valid child care license at time of application (or be in process of obtaining licensure)
Must be in good standing with the Maryland Comptroller and the Internal Revenue Service
Cannot have outstanding state or federal taxes (unless on a repayment program and current on payments)
Must provide a listing of all owners and percentages of ownership with resumes of principal owners
Must provide evidence of participation in MSDE Child Care Scholarship Program
Must provide a description of the child care facility including when established, location, staffing, enrollment figures, and programs provided
Must provide a summary of how the loan will be used
Must provide financial projections demonstrating capacity to meet operating expenses and repay the loan within five years
Must provide current Personal Financial Statement of principal owner(s)
Must provide Personal Federal Income Tax Returns with all Schedules for most recent three years
Must provide Business Federal Income Tax Returns with all Schedules for most recent three years
Must provide description and estimated value of collateral to be provided to secure the loan
Cannot use loan to refinance existing debt
Cannot use loan to pay outstanding state or federal taxes
Cannot use loan to pay off existing loans including EIDL and PPP loans or credit card debt
For loans over $50,000, borrower must provide evidence that lease will remain in effect for the five-year loan repayment period (if facility is leased)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants work with advisors to complete the application and submit all required documentation through an electronic portal. The username for portal registration must not contain spaces, commas, or special characters. All required documents must be uploaded into the portal and cannot be mailed or emailed. Incomplete applications cannot be considered. Applicants must sign a document attesting to completing the project for which the loan was requested. The program is subject to random audits. If audited, applicants must provide all receipts and proof of project completion. For assistance with portal access, completion, or submission, applicants should email childcare.commerce@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: Access Maryland provides funding to state-owned facilities, University System of Maryland campuses, and state-owned parks to make accessibility upgrades in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accessible Design Standards of 2010. The program ensures that individuals with a range of physical disabilities can fully interact and engage with buildings, parks, universities, and other state-owned facilities across Maryland. The program brings state-owned facilities into compliance with state and federal mandates requiring access for persons with disabilities through removal of physical barriers and ensures programmatic accessibility of all programs, services, and employment opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides capital budget funding to state agencies, University System of Maryland campuses, and state parks for accessibility upgrade projects. Funding covers design and construction phases for barrier-removal projects. The total capital budget request is up to $1.6 million annually. Applicants may request funding for design-only, construction-only, or both phases. Higher education institutions must contribute a minimum of 30% of project costs from sources other than Access Maryland funding. The Maryland Department of Disabilities receives requests from state agencies and higher education institutions, prioritizes projects through the Access Maryland Review Panel, recommends approved projects to the Department of Budget and Management for inclusion in the Capital Budget, and provides oversight through the design and construction phases. Funded projects must complete design within one year of funding authorization, and construction contracts must be awarded within 6 months of design approval or risk losing funding eligibility.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications typically due by March 1st; solicitations sent in January/February each year
structured_extraction.contact_name: Keyonna Baker, Director, Access Maryland & Accessibility Programs
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state agencies, University System of Maryland campuses, and state-owned parks seeking to make accessibility improvements for individuals with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding is used for capital (brick and mortar) accessibility upgrades at state-owned facilities, university campuses, and state parks to ensure compliance with ADA Accessible Design Standards, achieve programmatic accessibility, and remove physical barriers that impact access to programs, services, and activities. Projects must focus on programmatic access and cost more than $2,500. Funds cannot be used for maintenance, repairs, or projects that are part of larger building renovations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all state-owned facilities, University System of Maryland campuses, and state parks in Maryland are eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a state-owned facility, University System of Maryland campus, or state-owned park
Projects must focus on programmatic access
Projects must be capital (brick and mortar) improvements
Project costs must exceed $2,500 and include a cost estimate
Projects cannot be part of a larger building renovation
Projects should not be located in a building scheduled for renovations in the five-year capital plan
Projects cannot be maintenance or repairs
Projects should not be located in auxiliary facilities
Projects cannot be requests previously deemed ineligible due to inaction
Must be consistent with Americans with Disabilities Act Accessible Design Standards of 2010
For higher education institutions: minimum 30% of project costs must be contributed from sources other than Access Maryland funding
ADA Transition Plan Executive Summary must be submitted with application
Each agency/university is limited to three (3) open projects actively receiving Access MD funding at any time
Projects exceeding anticipated costs by more than 8% (or 16% for projects approved for both design and construction in same cycle) must be resubmitted for future funding
Design phase must be completed within one year of funding authorization or project becomes permanently ineligible
Construction contract must be awarded within 6 months of design approval or project loses eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: In January/February each year, MDOD notifies all Maryland state agencies, USM campuses, and state park administrators to submit requests for funds. Applications are submitted online with all supporting documentation uploaded directly into the application system. The application must include: (1) a cover letter signed by the Department Secretary or University President with the name and contact information for the ADA Coordinator and a brief project summary with requested funding amount, (2) Access Maryland Application form, (3) ADA Transition Plan Executive Summary indicating the date of the most current Transition Plan on file, and (4) supporting documentation such as photos and/or architectural drawings. For higher education institutions, a fund source letter identifying the alternate 30% funding must be provided. The application deadline is typically March 1st. From mid-March through mid-April, projects are reviewed and scored by the Access Maryland Review Panel comprised of MDOD staff and community stakeholders using a Project Score Sheet. Reviewers prioritize facilities with high degree of public use, requests that involved people with disabilities, and requests providing programmatic access requiring capital modifications. The highest scoring projects are given priority for funding up to the $1.6 million total capital budget. MDOD prepares a prioritized funding list and submits it to the Department of Budget and Management for inclusion in the Capital Budget by June 30th. The Governor's Capital Budget is then considered by the Legislature during the January-April legislative session. Approved projects are included in the Capital Budget and referred to the Department of General Services for design and construction processes. Once a project is approved for funding, the agency or campus must request a Fund Approval Letter from MDOD before beginning design or construction phases. When ready to pay for design or construction services, the agency/campus must submit a Payment Disbursement Letter request to MDOD along with copies of quotes/invoices/statements. MDOD then authorizes the fund transfer and notifies DGS. Mandatory training webinars on the funding process are required for project managers managing funded projects beginning FY23.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Attendant Care Program provides financial reimbursement to help individuals with severe chronic or permanent physical disabilities direct their own care and select their own service providers. Reimbursement covers attendant care services provided in the home, school, workplace, or other community locations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial reimbursement to eligible individuals for attendant care services. The program operates on a waiting list system. Once your name is placed on the registry through a short application on the OneStop portal, you will receive a link by email to complete the full application as space becomes available on the waiting list.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible adults age 18 to 64 with severe chronic or severe physical disabilities who meet specific employment, education, or community living criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Attendant care services provided in the home, school, workplace, or other community locations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be between 18 and 64 years old
Must have severe chronic or severe physical disabilities

Must meet at least one of the following: be self-employed or competitively employed with compensation, be actively seeking employment, be attending post-secondary or higher education or apprenticeship training, be a resident of a nursing facility seeking to transition to the community, or be at risk of nursing home placement if attendant care services are not provided
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for a OneStop account at onestop.md.gov with your name and email. Return to the home screen and select Maryland Department of Disabilities. Complete the short application to place your name on the registry for the ACP program. As space becomes available on the waiting list, you will receive a link by email to complete the full application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Centers for Independent Living Technical Assistance (CIL-TA) Project
structured_extraction.program_description: A technical assistance project to enhance Maryland's seven Centers for Independent Living and support the state's Aging and Disability Resource Centers. The project provides consulting services to help CILs improve their operational infrastructure and program sustainability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Center for Developmental Disabilities at Kennedy Krieger Institute provides technical assistance and training to the state's seven Centers for Independent Living to enhance operational infrastructure and program sustainability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's Centers for Independent Living
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance and training to enhance operational infrastructure and program sustainability for Centers for Independent Living
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide, serving Maryland's seven Centers for Independent Living

structured_extraction.program_description: A service for Marylanders who are DeafBlind that provides equal access to communication through skilled facilitators who use American Sign Language, close-vision, tactile sign language, and other communication methods to facilitate conversations between DeafBlind consumers and other people through video calls on platforms like videophone, Video Relay Services, FaceTime, Zoom, Skype, Google Hangouts, and Google Meet.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Communication Facilitator service is administered through the Maryland Accessible Telecommunications (MAT) program and provides skilled facilitators who participate in video calls with DeafBlind individuals to copy sign language from other callers and provide visual information through close-vision, tactile sign language, tracking, or other communication methods. The service can be initiated in a person's home or other public space. Facilitators can communicate using spoken English, spoken English with some sign language, close-visual sign language, tracking, tactile sign language, or ProTactile methods based on individual preferences.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders living with combined hearing and vision loss who are DeafBlind
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To facilitate communication between DeafBlind individuals and other people through skilled sign language interpretation and tactile communication during video calls.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Must be DeafBlind
Must complete the Communication Facilitator Service DeafBlind Consumer Application
Must be approved by the MAT program
May specify communication preferences including spoken English, spoken English with some sign language, close-visual sign language, tracking, tactile sign language, or ProTactile
May specify facilitator preferences
May specify location preferences including residence, library, coffee shop, or other location
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To be eligible for CF services, first complete the DeafBlind Consumer Application (available at MDRelay.org) and submit it to the MAT program for approval. Once approved, complete and submit the Communication Facilitator Service Request Form to CF.Scheduler@Maryland.gov to request services. Include service date, hours needed, communication preferences, facilitator preferences, location preferences, and reason for service.

structured_extraction.program_description: CAP facilitates the donation of working, adapted vehicles to eligible individuals with disabilities who do not qualify for other programs or financing to purchase adapted vehicles. The program is an Adapted Vehicle Access Pilot Program in effect until September 30, 2030, designed to provide adapted vehicles to eligible individuals and prioritizes those residing in areas with limited access to public transportation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Donation of working, adapted vehicles to eligible individuals with disabilities. The Department facilitates donations of vehicles, vehicle modification and adaptation services, and funds from individuals or public or private corporations. Recipients receive a working, adapted vehicle for personal use.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities who use mobility aids, are the primary driver of a vehicle, possess a valid driver's license with appropriate adaptation restrictions or a current vehicle modification prescription, and have been turned down for an AT Financial Loan or voluntarily self-disqualified. Priority consideration given to individuals who reside in areas with limited access to public transportation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MAT program provides assistive telecommunications equipment at no cost to qualified Maryland residents who have difficulty using a standard telephone due to disabilities. The program serves people who are Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind, blind, low vision, or have cognitive, mobility, or speech-related difficulties. Equipment is customized to meet individual needs and may include large-button phones for low vision, picture phones for memory loss, hands-free phones for mobility issues, TTYs for speech difficulties, amplified phones, captioned telephones, tablets, Braille TTYs, Hearing Carry-Over (HCO) phones, Voice Carry-Over (VCO) phones, and wheelchair pad phone switches. All applicants receive a free one-on-one evaluation with a specialist to determine the right solution.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides assistive telecommunications equipment at no cost to qualified applicants. Equipment types include text telephones (TTYs), Braille TTYs for people who are deaf and blind, Hearing Carry-Over (HCO) phones, Voice Carry-Over (VCO) phones, tablets, captioned telephones, amplified phones, wheelchair pad phone switches, large-button phones, picture phones, and hands-free phones. After application approval, applicants receive a free one-on-one evaluation with a MAT specialist to determine which equipment options best meet their needs. Equipment is ordered and shipped to the home via UPS within 4–6 weeks after the completed evaluation. All equipment is state property provided on long-term loan to the participant. Initial training is provided during the evaluation, with detailed instructions included in the shipment. Additional free training is available through the Talk, Text, Train (TTT) program for blind and low vision customers, with up to 2 one-on-one sessions with trained independent trainers or the in-house trainer.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing - applications accepted at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Any Maryland resident age three or older who has difficulty using a standard telephone due to vision loss, hearing loss, DeafBlindness, speech difficulty, mobility limitations, cognitive impairment, or other disabilities. Applicants ages 18 and under must have the application signed by a parent or legal guardian.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistive telecommunications equipment for personal residential use to enable independent phone communication, including phones with large or high contrast buttons for low vision, picture phones for memory loss, hands-free phones and wheelchair pad phone switches for mobility issues, TTYs and HCO phones for speech difficulties, amplified phones, captioned telephones, tablets, and other customized solutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland residents statewide. Equipment must be returned if the recipient moves out of state, unless moving temporarily with official address remaining in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be at least three years old (applicants ages 18 and under must have application signed by parent or legal guardian)
Must have difficulty using a standard telephone due to disability
Must be certified as Deaf, hard of hearing, DeafBlind, blind, low vision, or having cognitive, mobility, or speech-related difficulties by a licensed professional

Disability certification must be provided by a licensed professional (physician, audiologist, speech pathologist, rehabilitation counselor, social worker, psychologist, mental health counselor, registered nurse, licensed practical nurse, or physical therapist)

Must be on a fixed income or receive at least one of the following: Social Security (SSA) benefits, Veterans (VA) benefits, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI), Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), or pharmacy, medical, or housing assistance
Must have home phone service, high speed/WiFi, or be applying for phone service and/or high speed/WiFi
Must provide proof of income eligibility (e.g., Social Security Award Letter, VA benefits paperwork, or other assistance documentation)
Must provide copy of Maryland-issued photo ID, driver's license, or identification card
Must provide copy of telephone, Internet bill, or other utility bill
Applicant or parent/guardian (if under 18) or power of attorney must sign application
Cannot be receiving similar equipment through other State or Federal agencies or departments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the qualification criteria to ensure eligibility. 2. Complete the application online at mat-apply.org or download and complete the paper application (available in English and Spanish). 3. Have the Disability Certification Form (Part 4 or Part 5) certified by a licensed professional such as a physician, audiologist, speech pathologist, rehabilitation counselor, social worker, psychologist, mental health counselor, registered nurse, licensed practical nurse, or physical therapist. 4. Enclose proper documentation including proof of income eligibility (Social Security Award Letter, VA benefits paperwork, or other assistance documentation), a copy of Maryland-issued photo ID or driver's license, and a copy of a telephone, Internet, or utility bill. Do not send originals as they will not be returned. 5. Sign and submit the completed application and documentation online or mail to the MAT Program address at 301 W. Preston Street, Suite 1008A, Baltimore, MD 21201 (prepaid envelopes provided). Applications can also be scanned and emailed to MAT.Program1@Maryland.gov or faxed to 410-767-4276. 6. Once your completed application is received and approved, you will receive an acceptance letter within approximately two weeks with information on scheduling your evaluation. 7. After the free one-on-one evaluation with a MAT specialist, equipment is ordered and shipped to the home via UPS within 4–6 weeks. 8. Training is provided during the evaluation, with detailed instructions included in equipment shipment. Additional free training is available through the Talk, Text, Train (TTT) program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Assistive Technology Financial Loan Program (ATLP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Assistive Technology Financial Loan Program (ATLP) helps Maryland residents with disabilities, older Marylanders, and their families qualify for low-interest loans to purchase assistive technology equipment, devices, accessibility modifications to homes and vehicles, and adapted and non-adapted vehicles. The program supports individuals in living, working, and learning more independently and achieving employment goals. In 2021, 25 approved loans were made totaling $644,719 in assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans with extended repayment terms and lenient lending parameters. Loan amounts range from $500 to $70,000 depending on equipment type: unsecured assistive technology loans up to $10,000, unsecured vehicle and home modification loans up to $20,000, non-adapted vehicles up to $40,000, and adapted vehicles up to $70,000. All loans carry below-market fixed interest rates that vary based on creditworthiness and are disclosed at the time of application processing and approval. Most loans approved on their own merit receive preferred/discounted interest rates through the ATLP process. For loans declined by the lender, the ATLP submits requests to the ATLP Board of Directors for evaluation and consideration for loan guarantees.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Tanya Goodman, Program Director; Michelle Watson, AT Loan Administrator; Heather Ferguson and Sarah Calhoun
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anyone who intends to use the loan to buy assistive technology for a Maryland resident with a disability, including people with disabilities, older Marylanders, family members, and friends.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of assistive technology equipment including home modifications, accessibility modifications to homes and vehicles, adapted and non-adapted vehicles, scooters, wheelchairs, Braille equipment, hearing and vision aids, augmentative communication devices, environmental control units, computers and adaptive peripherals, smart home technology, and other devices that help a person with a disability live more independently and productively.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents with disabilities.
requirements_list: Intend to use the loan to buy assistive technology for a Maryland resident with a disability
Must have a disability or need for assistive technology or accessibility
Be a Maryland resident
Meet income compared to debt requirements
Demonstrate stability in residence or job
Have acceptable payment history with existing creditors
Demonstrate financial ability to repay the loan
Must have or intend to purchase assistive technology to help a Maryland resident with a disability live, work, or learn more independently
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with no specific deadline. Complete and submit the ATLP application online through the One Stop portal at https://onestop.md.gov/forms/mdod-assistive-technology-loan-program-application-6322337acffd140001989667 or download the fillable application form and email the completed application with supporting documents to mdtap.atlp@maryland.gov. Step 1: Create a OneStop Account and log in to the application portal. Step 2: Upload a photo or scan of your passport, driver's license, or state-issued ID. Step 3: Submit your completed application to ATLP staff for review of completeness. Step 4: ATLP staff verifies that the loan will be used to purchase assistive technology for a Maryland resident with a disability and processes the application for further review. Step 5: Application is submitted to the lender for review. If approved on merit, the lender determines the interest rate and the loan closes at the lender's branch office or by mail. If the lender declines, ATLP submits the application to the ATLP Board of Directors for consideration of a loan guarantee. Step 6: For loans guaranteed by ATLP, ATLP staff coordinates with the lender to finalize the loan. Typical approval time is 30-45 days. Application completion time is 20-60 minutes. Applicants have the right to appeal ATLP Board decisions in writing with supporting documentation addressing the reasons for denial. Appeals should be sent to the ATLP Board at 2301 Argonne Drive, Room T-42, Baltimore, MD 21218, or via email to mdtap.atlp@maryland.gov. Applicants will receive a decision on appeal within 7 days of the Board meeting, and the Board's decision is final.

MDTAP also administers a financial loan program, operates a reuse and recycling program for donated AT equipment, and coordinates a cooperative buying program for discounted assistive technology pricing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MDTAP offers multiple forms of assistance: (1) Short-term loans and comprehensive demonstrations of AT devices to help constituents make informed decisions about long-term device procurement; (2) Assistive Technology Financial Loan Program (ATLP) providing low-interest loans to Maryland residents with disabilities and their families to purchase equipment for independent living, working, and learning; (3) AT Reuse & Recycling program providing gently used, refurbished, sanitized assistive technology at low or no cost to those who cannot otherwise afford it; (4) Cooperative Buying Program coordinating discounted prices on assistive technology through collaboration with AT vendors and passing savings to organizations, agencies, and individuals.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland High-Tech Assistive Technology Reuse (MATR) Center
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland High-Tech Assistive Technology Reuse (MATR) Center is the state's high-tech assistive technology reuse program operated under MDTAP (Maryland Assistive Technology Program). It accepts donations of gently used assistive technology devices, sanitizes and refurbishes them, and distributes them for free to Marylanders with disabilities who need them. Supporting the Technology First framework, the program provides innovative resources paired with training and support to help users integrate assistive technology into daily life for living, working, and learning more independently. The center partners with organizations including the Lollipop Kids Foundation, Equipment Connections for Children, and the Loan Closet of Howard County. In 2021, 236 devices were refurbished and 358 low-cost or free devices were provided, creating $556,441 in total consumer savings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free refurbished and repaired high-tech assistive technology devices are provided to Marylanders with disabilities who cannot otherwise afford them. In 2021, 236 devices were refurbished and 358 low-cost or free devices were provided, creating $556,441 in total consumer savings. Devices include closed-circuit televisions (CCTVs), video magnifiers, magnifiers, Apple devices (iDevices), adapted computer keyboards, mice, switches, speech communication devices, personal sound amplifiers, amplified telephones, and eye-gaze systems. Devices are sourced from donations and availability varies based on donations received. Training and support are also provided to help users integrate devices into daily life. Equipment is available for pickup at the center located at 7125 Riverwood Drive, Suite D1, Columbia, MD 21046 (within the Howard County Loan Closet).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with disabilities who need high-tech assistive technology, particularly low-income individuals who cannot otherwise afford such devices.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Provision of free refurbished high-tech assistive technology devices to support communication, visual support, computer access, and daily living activities, enabling people with disabilities to live, work, and learn more independently.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland. The MATR Center is located at 7125 Riverwood Drive, Suite D1, Columbia, MD 21046, within the Howard County Loan Closet. Equipment is distributed through partnerships with various organizations statewide.
requirements_list: Must have a disability
Must be a Maryland resident
Must complete the MATR Application online
Unable to otherwise afford assistive technology (priority for low-income individuals)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the MATR Application online at the provided link. The center will follow up to coordinate a consultation and device pickup. You can also contact Shawn Bateman directly at MDTAP.AT-Reuse@maryland.gov or 410-554-9232 to schedule a donation, consultation, or pickup. structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation and the State of Maryland to provide accessible, affordable, and independent rental housing opportunities in the community for very low-income persons with disabilities. The program provides rent subsidies and capital grants to incentivize owners of eligible rental housing developments with non-profit involvement to designate units for occupancy at affordable rents. Weinberg-funded units house non-elderly disabled persons at 10 to 30 percent of Area Gross Median Income (AGMI), with tenants paying 30 percent of their income for rent and utilities. Funding includes $7 million in grants from The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation and financial assistance from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development through its Multifamily Rental Housing Programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants are available as an incentive for owners of eligible rental housing developments with non-profit involvement to designate units for occupancy at affordable rents. Weinberg-funded units house non-elderly disabled persons at 10 to 30 percent of Area Gross Median Income (AGMI). Tenants pay 30 percent of their income for rent and utilities. Funding includes $7 million in grants from The Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation and financial assistance from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development through its Multifamily Rental Housing Programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-elderly persons with disabilities (ages 18–62) who are very low-income and receiving SSI or SSDI benefits, seeking affordable rental housing in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable rental housing costs for persons with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: As of February 2020, Weinberg Apartments are located in Dorchester, Harford, Montgomery, Prince George's, Somerset, and Wicomico counties. Additional units are under construction or in the pipeline for Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Howard County, and Baltimore City. Program is available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be between the ages of 18 and 62
Be disabled and receiving SSI or SSDI
Have a gross household income at or between 10 to 30 percent of Area Gross Median Income (AGMI) in the Maryland county where you wish to reside
Not have a criminal background that includes a lifetime sex offense registry requirement
Not have a criminal background that includes conviction of the production of methamphetamines in Federally-assisted property
Be referred by a case manager, support planner, resource coordinator, coordinator of community service, or community health worker to complete pre-screening and application
Low income
Person with disabilities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants must be referred by their case manager, support planner, resource coordinator, coordinator of community service, or community health worker to complete pre-screening and application. Applicants are drawn from a waiting list as units that meet their needs become available. The Maryland Department of Disabilities qualifies eligible households and refers potential tenants to property managers. Contact MDOD at 410-767-3660 or 1-800-637-4113 for additional application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: The Model Waiver for Medically Fragile Children
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides services for medically fragile children with complex medical needs, from birth through age 21, to live in their own homes instead of a hospital, nursing facility, or other long-term care facility. This Medicaid waiver allows children who meet the definition of a disabled child (chronically ill or severely impaired) to receive necessary community-based care at home with their families, with a maximum enrollment of 200 individuals statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid waiver enabling medically fragile children to live at home with their families instead of in hospitals, nursing facilities, or other long-term care settings. Provides in-home and community-based support services necessary to maintain the child at home. Maximum of 200 individuals can be enrolled in the Model Waiver. Services are cost-neutral compared to institutional care costs. No specific dollar amounts are stated. Parents' income and assets are waived during the financial eligibility process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Judith P. Hoyer Early Child Care and Education Enhancement Program (Judy Center Early Learning Hubs)
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant-funded comprehensive hubs located in elementary schools that serve families with young children from prenatal stages through age 5. Judy Centers provide or connect families with developmental screenings, family learning activities, parenting classes, adult education connections, playgroups, service referrals, early intervention identification, home visiting, and case management to prepare children for school success and increase school readiness.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Judy Center Early Learning Hubs are grant-funded programs located in Title I elementary schools across Maryland. Individual Judy Centers serve families with children living within the school zone. Services are provided at no cost to families and include: developmental screenings, family learning activities and evidence-based playgroups (minimum 2 on-site parent and child playgroups per week), parenting classes and workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development programs, service referrals and case management, early intervention identification, evidence-based home visiting, full-day/full-year care coordination, meals for children during school days, breaks, weekends and after-school hours, health-related services (dental, vision, hearing screenings), and mental health referrals. In FY2024, 86 Judy Centers served 17,681 children from birth to kindergarten and 14,750 families. Under the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, Judy Centers are expanding by 9 sites annually until 2025, then 18 sites annually from 2026-2030.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager; Nancy Garcia, Judy Center Specialist (Spanish language assistance)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with young children from prenatal stages through age 5 living within a Judy Center school zone in Title I elementary schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services include developmental screenings, family learning activities, parenting classes and workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based family and child playgroups, referrals for services and supports, early intervention identification, evidence-based home visiting, case management with families, health-related services, and full-day/full-year care coordination. In FY2024, Judy Centers made 80,367 referrals to community partners and agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Judy Center Early Learning Hubs are located in Title I elementary schools across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions (all counties and Baltimore City). Judy Centers serve children who live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located. As of FY2024, there are 86 Judy Center sites operating statewide.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal FEMA program that provides financial assistance to states, local governments, tribal, and territorial governments to develop hazard mitigation plans and implement long-term mitigation projects following a presidentially declared major disaster. The program aims to reduce loss of life and property by funding mitigation measures during the recovery phase of a disaster, including projects related to flooding, wildfires, and other natural hazards. Funds support a wide range of projects such as property purchases, house relocations, house elevations for properties within the 100-year floodplain, backup power systems, drainage improvements, and infrastructure resilience improvements for transit systems. The program also addresses secondary hazards from wildfires such as floods, erosion, and mudflows. Funding is matched on a 75/25 federal/non-federal basis, with FEMA providing states an amount equal to 7.5% of the emergency financial assistance rendered immediately following a declared disaster.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Emergency Management / FEMA
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FEMA provides states with an amount equal to 7.5% of the emergency financial assistance rendered immediately following a declared disaster. HMGP funds are matched on a 75/25 basis (75% federal, 25% state and local). Eligible sub-applicants must provide a 25% non-federal cost share and cannot use federal funds for this purpose. Funds support projects including property acquisitions, house relocations, house elevations (within the 100-year floodplain), hazard mitigation plans, backup power systems, drainage improvements, structural retrofitting, non-structural retrofitting, wind retrofits, infrastructure retrofits, soil stabilization, capacity and capability building, and other infrastructure resilience measures for transit systems. For small impoverished communities, federal share may reach 90%. For repetitive loss properties, up to 90% federal share may apply. For severe repetitive loss properties, up to 100% federal funding is available. Awarded projects cannot be started or completed before the kick-off meeting with the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM). Management costs cannot exceed 5% of total project cost estimate.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application timeframe varies based on Notices of Funding Opportunities (NOFO) announcement from federal government; Notices of Interest received after August of each year will be kept in repository for next cycle. Rolling basis following presidential disaster declaration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State, local, tribal, and territorial governments; private nonprofit organizations; transit authorities and public agencies managing critical infrastructure; and individuals in declared disaster areas seeking to reduce future flood and disaster risk
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hazard mitigation measures that reduce or eliminate long-term risk to people and property from future disasters, including property acquisitions and demolition, house relocations, house elevations, structure elevation, mitigation reconstruction, floodproofing, wildfire mitigation and secondary hazard mitigation (floods, erosion, mudflows), planning and engineering, backup power systems, drainage improvements, generators/emergency power backup, localized and non-localized flood risk reduction, structural and non-structural retrofitting, wind retrofits, infrastructure retrofits, soil stabilization, hazard mitigation planning, capacity and capability building projects (project scoping, building codes, partnership building), transit system resilience measures, and warning systems
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland and nationally to eligible jurisdictions following a federally declared major disaster. Montgomery County sub-applicants apply through the Office of Emergency Management and Homeland Security (OEMHS). Properties must be located within the 100-year floodplain for flood-related projects. Maryland transit systems are eligible for infrastructure resilience projects. Program is only activated following a Presidential Disaster Declaration.
requirements_list: Area must have been subject to a federally declared major disaster (HMGP activation requirement)
Sub-applicant must be a state agency, local government, tribal government, private nonprofit organization, or individual (for specific project types)
Sub-applicant is responsible for 25% non-federal cost share (or lower percentage for small impoverished communities or repetitive/severe repetitive loss properties)
Sub-applicant must not use federal funds for non-federal cost share
Project must be aligned with FEMA-approved County Hazard Mitigation Plan
Hazard Mitigation Plan must be current and compliant with 44 CFR Part 201
Projects cannot be started or completed prior to kick-off meeting with MDEM
Must be located within the 100-year floodplain (for flood-related projects)
For Post Fire HMGP: area must be affected by a presidentially declared wildfire disaster
Project must improve infrastructure resilience and reduce long-term community disaster risk
Hazard mitigation focus required
Engineering and design plans needed (for infrastructure/transit projects and structure elevation projects)
Applicants must not be delinquent on any Federal debt
Project must comply with environmental and historic preservation requirements
Property must have active NFIP policy if applicable (for flood mitigation projects)
Community must be in good standing with NFIP if applicable
Project costs must be reasonable and eligible under FEMA guidelines
Cost-effectiveness must be demonstrated through benefit-cost analysis (BCR ≥ 1.0) unless exempt
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Following a presidentially declared disaster, funding becomes available. For Montgomery County sub-applicants: (1) Submit a Notice of Interest (NOI) to the Office of Emergency Management and Homeland Security (OEMHS) in August indicating interest in pursuing HMGP activities. NOI submission timeframe: Notices of Interest received after August will be kept in repository for next funding cycle. (2) OEMHS reviews NOI for basic applicability and eligibility. (3) Upon State (MDEM) recommendation and approval, OEMHS provides technical assistance to develop the subapplication. (4) OEMHS submits recommended sub-applications to FEMA through MDEM. (5) FEMA reviews and awards grants to eligible sub-applicants. (6) MDEM disburses grant awards to awarded sub-applicants. (7) Kickoff meeting held with MDEM before project start. For infrastructure/transit projects: submit resilience and mitigation project proposals including engineering plans and hazard analysis to FEMA. Fillable NOI and subapplication forms are provided. Project scoping and advance assistance may be available for developing project applications. Subapplications must include: Scope of Work (activities, description, implementation plan), Schedule (tasks with timelines), Budget (cost estimates, management costs up to 5%), Cost-Effectiveness documentation (BCA or pre-calculated benefits), Environmental and Historic Preservation documentation, and all required certifications and assurances.

structured_extraction.program_name: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) - DDA Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Competitive grants administered by the Maryland Department of Health's Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) to support strategic funding priorities for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. The program funds initiatives across four approved grant activity areas: Advancing Innovation, Supporting Systems Transformation, Enhancing Independence and Inclusive Opportunities, and Developing Resources and Infrastructure. Grants are available to DDA licensed or certified providers, nonprofits, and other eligible organizations supporting the IDD community across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding from ARPA reinvestment funds totaling $5 million available. Individual awards range from $50,000 to $350,000 and may be approved in part or in full. The grant period of performance runs from May 1, 2023 through March 31, 2025. Funding is provided 50% upfront with the remainder upon completion of specified milestones. All awardees must submit quarterly reports via GrantVantage to document expenditures, activities, and outcomes in accordance with the approved budget and work plan, plus a detailed final report summarizing grant activities and outcomes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: DDA licensed or certified providers, nonprofit organizations supporting the Maryland IDD community, local health departments providing CCS services, and other eligible organizations serving individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant activities must align with four approved activity areas: (1) Advancing Innovation - peer advocacy programs and crisis support services; (2) Supporting Systems Transformation - supports for transitioning youth and families, addressing systemic service gaps; (3) Enhancing Independence and Inclusive Opportunities - services and programs that enhance independence and inclusive opportunities; (4) Developing Resources and Infrastructure - technical assistance and sustainable practices to build provider capacity. Funds cannot be used for salary/bonus enhancements for CCS providers. New positions may be funded if sustainability is demonstrated.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Eligible applicants must be DDA licensed or certified providers, or nonprofit organizations doing work in Maryland reimbursed under the DDA budget.
requirements_list: Must be a DDA licensed or certified provider OR a nonprofit organization supporting the Maryland IDD community
Must demonstrate work in Maryland reimbursed under the DDA budget
Must provide latest audited financial statements
Organizations with recent nonprofit status must demonstrate how they support/enhance the IDD community
Expenses must occur during the period of performance (May 1, 2023 - March 31, 2025)
Grant activities must align with one of four approved activity areas
Organizations must document sustainability plans for new positions created with grant funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: (1) Register your organization on GrantVantage; (2) Complete the Applicant Profile including primary and financial contacts; (3) Upload all documents requested in the MDH Funding Announcement; (4) Review the Funding Announcement and attachments on the DDA website; (5) Complete the Application, Objective Template, and Budget Template with narrative; (6) Ensure all three check marks appear indicating completion; (7) Select 'NEXT' button and complete final screen; (8) Submit through GrantVantage at https://mdh.gvgrantcloud.com/account/Announcement. Applications were released February 1, 2023 with a deadline of February 28, 2023. Grant awards were issued April 3, 2023. Active requests for proposals are announced on the DDA ARPA Grants page and in the DDA's bi-weekly newsletter. For program-related budget questions contact elizabeth.peters@maryland.gov. For technical questions on GrantVantage platform contact applicantsupport@grantvantage.com.

structured_extraction.program_description: ACIS is a Maryland Medicaid program that delivers housing and tenancy-based services to eligible individuals who are experiencing homelessness or at risk of becoming homeless. An ACIS case manager works with participants to create a supportive housing plan and helps connect them with needed services, including community integration assessments, person-centered planning, help connecting with social services, advocating with landlords for accommodations, and training and resource support for managing one's home. The program does not cover room and board or rental costs. Local health departments and other local government agencies may apply to become ACIS providers and deliver services within their jurisdiction, billing reimbursement through Maryland Medicaid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For providers: Local health departments and other local government agencies (or consortiums of entities) deliver housing and tenancy-based services to eligible individuals. Providers are reimbursed through Maryland Medicaid at a bundled rate of $725 per member per month (PMPM) that requires delivery of a minimum of three eligible services per month to each ACIS participant. Additional compliance activities including completion of the Housing Supports Care Plan (HSCP) are reimbursed at $100 per member per year (PMPY). Services are billed through Maryland Medicaid using home-grown billing codes. ACIS is a Fee-For-Service (FFS) benefit; providers do not bill Managed Care Organizations (MCOs). For individuals: An ACIS case manager works with the participant to create a supportive Housing Supports Care Plan (HSCP) and helps connect them with needed services, including community integration assessments, person-centered planning, help connecting with social services, advocating with landlords for accommodations, and training and resource support for managing one's home. The program does not cover room and board or rental costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 27, 2026 by 5 p.m. (Application due; LOI was due March 13, 2026 by 5 p.m.)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Two audiences: (1) Local health departments, other local government entities (such as local management boards), or consortiums of entities serving a county or multiple counties interested in becoming ACIS Lead Entities and delivering services within their jurisdiction; (2) Individuals with Medicaid in Maryland who are experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness and meet specific health and housing criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing and tenancy-based services for individuals experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, including community integration assessments, person-centered planning, coordination and connection to social and supportive services, assistance communicating with landlords or property managers regarding accommodation needs, participation in housing or service coordination meetings, and training and resource support related to tenancy, housing stability, and household management. Does not cover room and board or rental costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The provider program is statewide — local health departments and other local government agencies may apply to become ACIS providers and deliver services within their jurisdiction. Individual participant services are currently available in Baltimore City, Cecil County, Montgomery County, and Prince George's County. Maryland is expanding ACIS statewide with 1,520 participant spaces available for new and existing Lead Entities through this 2026 solicitation.
requirements_list: Must be a local health department, county government entity, or consortium of entities serving one or more counties (for Lead Entities/providers)
May not have multiple competing applications from the same county; entities are encouraged to submit joint applications

Must have ability to submit billing claims to MDH for service delivery reimbursements, disperse funds to Participating Entities, collect performance metrics, engage in data sharing and submit reports to MDH
Must be a member of the local Continuum of Care (CoC)
Must become an enrolled Medicaid ACIS Lead Entity by enrolling through Maryland Medicaid's electronic Provider Revalidation and Enrollment Portal (ePREP) as Provider Type 'GH'
Must meet all participation requirements in COMAR 10.09.36
Must comply with Conflict-Free Case Management (CFCM) guidelines
Must ensure participants have active full Medicaid coverage prior to enrollment and service delivery

Must retain all records for a minimum of 6 years

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For providers: 1. Attend ACIS presentation at Local Health Officers' Roundtable (held February 11, 2026) or review program materials. 2. Request the mandatory Letter of Intent (LOI) template and instructions by emailing mdh.medicaidacis@maryland.gov. 3. Complete and submit LOI by March 13, 2026 by 5 p.m. (Incomplete LOIs or those received after deadline will not be accepted; MDH will confirm receipt via email). 4. Complete and submit the full Request for Responses/Application form and all required components by March 27, 2026 by 5 p.m., including cover letter, project abstract and narrative, target population and referral process description, Lead Entity and Participating Entity capability statement, key personnel information, daily operations and communication plan, Conflict-Free Case Management work plan, data sharing and reporting plan, quality improvement demonstration, and financial capacity documentation. 5. MDH will review applications from April 6-24, 2026. 6. MDH will notify award winners on May 1, 2026. 7. Program onboarding begins May 18, 2026. 8. Upon Award Letter receipt, Lead Entities must enroll as Maryland Medicaid providers (Provider Type GH) through ePREP, which requires obtaining a separate NPI number (Type 2 Organizational) with taxonomy code 251B00000X Case Management. For individuals: Email your county contact or mdh.medicaidacis@maryland.gov for more information and to access services in your jurisdiction.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Health Resources Commission (CHRC) Annual Request for Applications (RFA) Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Community Health Resources Commission (CHRC), administered by the Maryland Department of Health, awards competitive grants to expand access to affordable, high-quality health care services in underserved areas throughout Maryland. Grants support expanding access to primary care, reducing infant mortality, increasing access to dental care, integrating behavioral health and substance use disorder treatment services in the community, facilitating the adoption of health information technology among safety net providers, chronic disease prevention and management, maternal and child health, hospital-community partnerships, and support for medically vulnerable populations. Since its inception in 2005, the CHRC has awarded 985 grants totaling $396 million supporting programs in every jurisdiction of the state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The CHRC awards competitive grants through an annual Request for Applications (RFA) process. For fiscal year 2026, the CHRC is awarding $7 million in total funding. Grant amounts range from $25,000 to $500,000 per award. Funding supports staff salaries, equipment, supplies, program implementation, service expansion, electronic health record systems, community health worker positions, clinical services, preventive care, and care coordination. Since its inception in 2005, the CHRC has awarded 985 grants totaling $396 million supporting programs in every jurisdiction of the state.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations, non-profit organizations, community health centers, government agencies, higher education institutions, and for-profit entities working to expand access to affordable, high-quality health care services for low-income, uninsured, and underserved populations throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds support programs addressing barriers to accessing health care, including chronic disease prevention and management, dental care, behavioral health and substance use disorder treatment, maternal and child health, primary care expansion, infant mortality reduction, hospital-community partnerships, health information technology adoption among safety net providers, staff salaries, equipment purchases, supplies, service expansion, program implementation, electronic health record systems, community health worker positions, clinical services, preventive care, and care coordination services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All jurisdictions throughout Maryland. Some funded programs also serve cross-county populations (e.g., Montgomery and Prince George's Counties).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The CHRC issues an annual Request for Applications (RFA). Interested applicants must first submit a Letter of Intent by the stated deadline (March 26, 2026 for FY2026). Applicants who submitted Letters of Intent will be notified of eligibility. Full proposals are then submitted by April 23, 2026 at 3:00 pm EST. Grant proposals are evaluated by independent subject matter experts on a range of criteria outlined in each RFA, including evidence-based practices, outcomes data capacity, community need, sustainability, and likelihood of success. Grants are awarded in a competitive process, with priority areas and review criteria determined by CHRC Commissioners. Awards are expected to be announced in late June.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's official certification program for Community Health Workers (CHWs). The certification is issued at no cost, is valid for two years from the date of issuance, and can be renewed at no cost. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through the Maryland OneStop portal, with paper applications available in English and Spanish upon request. CHW certification in Maryland is a voluntary process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland issues an official CHW certification credential to individuals who meet eligibility requirements. structured_extraction.program_description: A rent subsidy program that helps people with developmental disabilities afford housing in Maryland by providing financial assistance to reduce their rental costs. The program allows eligible individuals to rent a home and pay just 30% of their total household income for rent and basic utilities (gas, water and electricity), with the program paying the remaining rent.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides rent subsidy assistance to eligible individuals with developmental disabilities. Participants pay 30% of their total household income for rent and basic utilities (gas, water, and electricity). The program pays the difference between the participant's share and the total rent for the unit. Rental units must not exceed the maximum Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the area as determined by HUD and must pass housing quality standards (HQS) inspection. Participants receive ongoing support from Housing Support Service providers for lease review, tenant education, and troubleshooting housing concerns.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 18 and older with intellectual and developmental disabilities who are receiving DDA-funded services or on the DDA waitlist for services in the Crisis Resolution category, seeking affordable housing options in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rent payment assistance and basic utility allowances (gas, water, electricity) for individuals with developmental disabilities. Participants must maintain the unit in a clean and sanitary manner and comply with lease terms.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Applicants can choose up to 5 counties in which they are willing to live. Household income must be at or below 50% of area median income in the county where the housing will be located.
requirements_list: Must be 18 years of age or older
Must have household income at or below 50% of area median income in the county where housing will be located
Must be receiving at least one DDA-funded service OR be on the DDA waitlist for services in the Crisis Resolution category
Must not currently receive a rent subsidy from another public source or reside in public housing as head of household or co-head
Must not be convicted of manufacturing or producing methamphetamine on premises of any federally assisted housing project
Must not be a registrant under a national or state sex offender registration program
Must not be engaged in violent or drug-related criminal activity within a reasonable time before admission
Must have a housing goal in their Person Centered Plan (PCP)
Must follow lease terms and not commit serious or repeated violations
Must maintain unit in clean and sanitary manner
Must disclose income increases above $200 per month within 15 days
Must permit DHCD to periodically inspect the unit for HQS compliance
Must apply for other housing resources and maintain updated contact with waitlist administrators
Must accept other housing assistance offers to free up state resources
Participants and household members must not engage in abusive or violent behavior against program personnel
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Meet with your Coordinator of Community Services (CCS) and express desire to live independently, requesting Housing Support Services (HSS) be added to your Person Centered Plan (PCP). 2. Once HSS is approved and a provider is chosen, the HSS professional makes the referral to the DDA Rent Subsidy Program through the Department of Disabilities Social Serve Network Waitlist Registry at https://www.myhousingsearch.com/. 3. The HSS provider monitors your status on the waitlist and keeps you informed. 4. When a subsidy becomes available based on your priority category and application date/time stamp, MDOD Waitlist Manager contacts your HSS provider to verify your continued interest. HSS has 5 working days to respond. 5. If interested, you will receive a full application and required documentation list. Completed applications must be submitted within 14 calendar days. 6. MDOD Waitlist Manager reviews the application for completeness and sends it to DHCD within one week. 7. DHCD verifies income, conducts criminal background check, and determines final eligibility. Approved applicants receive a program authorization form. 8. You have 90 days (extendable by 60 days) to locate housing that meets your needs and Fair Market Rent limits. 9. HSS assists with identifying rental units, gathering required information, and submitting the unit to DHCD for rent reasonableness verification and HQS inspection. 10. HSS reviews the lease with you before signing and accompanies you when signing. 11. DHCD conducts pre-move-in inspection. Once you move in, HSS provides tenant education and ongoing support. 12. DHCD makes monthly payments to landlords and conducts annual inspections. Income is recertified annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid buy-in program that allows workers with disabilities to maintain Medicaid coverage even if their earnings would normally make them ineligible. Participants pay monthly premiums based on their income level, with premiums tiered according to individual or couple income ranges. The program removes the financial disincentive to work by allowing employed individuals with disabilities to retain Medicaid health insurance coverage despite having earnings that would otherwise disqualify them.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid coverage is provided to eligible working individuals with disabilities. Monthly premiums are tiered based on income, ranging from $0 per month for those earning less than $15,960 annually (individual) or $21,640 (couples) to 7.5% of monthly countable income for those earning $95,760 or more annually (individual) or $129,840 or more (couples). Applicants must submit recent consecutive weeks of pay stubs or a signed and dated statement from employer showing regular pay before deductions. Self-employed individuals must provide earnings records and copies of most recent tax returns filed with the IRS. The program allows workers with disabilities to maintain Medicaid eligibility despite having earnings that would otherwise disqualify them. A hardship exemption is available to waive monthly premiums for up to 6 months for those experiencing severe financial hardship that would compromise their ability to obtain basic food, shelter, and clothing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employed individuals aged 16 to 64 with disabilities who have earnings subject to taxes and meet Social Security disability medical criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medicaid health insurance coverage for eligible working individuals with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must live in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be at least 16 years old but not yet 65 years old
Be working for pay with earnings subject to withholding taxes or pay estimated taxes if self-employed
Have a disability that meets Social Security's medical criteria

Be a U.S. Citizen or a qualified non-citizen as defined by immigration status requirements (Permanent Resident, Asylee, Alien granted conditional entry, Parolee 1 year or more, Alien whose deportation is withheld, Refugee, Battered alien spouse/child/parent, or other qualified status)
Live in Maryland
Meet the asset limit of $10,000 (for married individuals, only joint assets and assets owned solely by the applicant count toward the limit, not spouse-only assets)
Have earnings subject to withholding taxes or pay estimated taxes if self-employed
Provide proof of income such as recent pay stubs, employer statements, or tax returns
Provide identification including birth verification and social security card
Provide marriage certificate if applicable and divorce decrees if previously married
Not have dropped health insurance coverage or if so, provide explanation
Agree to apply for all benefits applicant may be entitled to receive
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain the EID Program application form (9701 Application for Employed Individuals with Disabilities). 2. Complete all sections including household information, earned income, resources/assets, citizenship status, medical insurance, and life insurance. 3. Gather required supporting documents: four consecutive weeks of recent pay stubs (or signed employer statement showing regular pay if employed), tax returns or Schedule C if self-employed, social security card, birth certificate or Medicare card, marriage certificate if applicable, current bank statements (must include first day of application month), proof of assets, and health insurance identification cards if applicable. 4. Read and sign the rights and responsibilities section, understanding the penalties for providing false information and the authority to verify information with employers, banks, and other agencies. 5. Mail the completed application and all required supporting documents to: Eligibility Determination Division, Schaefer Tower, 6 St. Paul Street, Suite 400, Baltimore, MD 21202. Alternatively, applicants can seek assistance from disability agencies in Maryland or Centers for Independent Living. 6. Applicants may be interviewed by telephone in most cases. 7. Processing typically occurs within 30 days of application submission. 8. For hardship exemption requests, complete the Claim of Hardship Exemption form (DHMH EID 2A) and mail to the same address; decisions are made within 30 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: A special category of eligibility and priority for developmental disability services for young people ages 21 to 22 who are leaving school. The program funds supported employment and other day services for eligible students transitioning from school to adult services, preventing placement on the lengthy DDA waiting list. Services are provided regardless of the severity of the disability or relative need for immediate services. Funding comes from one of DDA's three federal waiver programs (Community Pathways, Family Supports, or Community Supports) and from Governor's Transitioning Youth Initiative funds earmarked in the DDA budget. The GTYI is a collaboration between the DDA and Maryland's Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The DDA earmarks funds in its budget to provide supported employment and other meaningful day services for eligible transitioning youth. Services include career discovery, exploration, learning new skills, and planning assistance. The DDA is realigning its service delivery system with Employment First principles. Services are funded regardless of the severity of the individual's disability and their relative need for immediate services. Once found eligible, the individual receives targeted case management from a Coordination of Community Services (CCS) agency and develops a person-centered plan that considers the youth's goals and preferences to identify desired services and support needs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: All DDA waiver applications must be completed by June 30 of the eligibility year to be considered for funding. Applications submitted later will be placed on a waiting list.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Regional Office Contacts: Beryl Parker (Central Maryland), Jim Sullivan (Eastern Shore), Nicole Sheppard (Southern Maryland), Brenda Sperow (Western Maryland)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students ages 21 to 22 with a developmental disability who are transitioning from school to adult services. Students must have a severe chronic disability attributable to a physical or mental impairment (other than sole diagnosis of mental illness), or combination of mental and physical impairments, that is manifested before age 22, likely to continue indefinitely, results in inability to live independently without external support, and reflects a need for special, interdisciplinary or generic care, treatment, or services that are individually planned and coordinated. Eligibility runs from the 21st birthday until the 22nd birthday, or for one year after graduation if graduation occurs after the 21st birthday.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supported employment services and other meaningful day services for individuals with developmental disabilities transitioning from school to adult services, including career discovery, exploration, learning new skills, and planning assistance to help people make informed choices about employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide through four regional offices: Central Maryland (serving Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford, and Howard Counties), Eastern Shore (serving Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester Counties), Southern Maryland (serving Calvert, Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's, and St. Mary's Counties), and Western Maryland (serving Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, and Washington Counties).
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be found fully eligible as developmentally disabled
Must be waiver eligible
Disability must be a severe chronic disability attributable to a physical or mental impairment (other than sole diagnosis of mental illness), or combination of mental and physical impairments
Disability must be manifested before the individual attains age 22
Disability must be likely to continue indefinitely

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can apply for DDA services at any time and at any age. All DDA waiver applications must be completed by June 30 of the eligibility year to be considered for funding. Services are coordinated by Coordinators of Community Services. Once a person moves into their home, they receive tenant training and ongoing support to maintain tenancy.
