structured_extraction.program_name: Low Intensity Support Services (LISS) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Low Intensity Support Services (LISS) Program is operated by the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) under the Maryland Department of Health. It serves children living at home with their family and adults with developmental and/or intellectual disabilities living in their own home in the community who are not receiving any support services from the DDA. The program provides up to $1,000 in funding to assist eligible individuals with purchasing eligible services and/or items to address their needs, enhance quality of life, promote independence, and support community integration. Funding is distributed through a random selection process. The program is delivered statewide through two program providers: Maryland Community Connection and Penn-Mar Human Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to $1,000 (previously $2,000, reduced due to budget constraints) to eligible children and adults with developmental and/or intellectual disabilities to purchase eligible services and/or items to address their identified needs. Eligible services and items include: adaptive items, assistive technology, attendant/personal care, child care, community integration and recreational services/items, educational services/items, home modification and barrier removal, identification services, respite care, summer camps and therapeutic summer programs, transportation, and wellness services/items. Reimbursement is available for eligible services and items purchased during the current fiscal year (July 1 through June 30, with summer camps extended through August 31). Funding is distributed based on random selection from among eligible applicants. If selected, recipients must provide documentation verifying identity, disability, residency, and the identified eligible service or item delivered by an approved vendor. A LISS agency representative will contact selected applicants to assist with the process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Round 1 FY 2026: Online access closes September 15, 2025. Random selection takes place September 30, 2025.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 301-583-8880 (Maryland Community Connection); 877-282-8202 (Penn-Mar Human Services); 877-622-6688 (Maryland Community Connection toll-free); 410-767-5600 (DDA main)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children living at home with their family and adults with developmental and/or intellectual disabilities living in their own home in the community who are not currently receiving any support services from the Developmental Disabilities Administration. Applicants may be on the DDA Waiting List and receiving Coordination of Community Services (CCS) only, or may be enrolled in the Model Waiver program or Medicaid's Rare & Expensive Case Management (REM) Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible services and/or items to address the needs of children and adults with developmental and/or intellectual disabilities, including personal and attendant care, respite care, adaptive items, assistive technology, child care, community integration and recreational services/items, educational services/items, home modification and barrier removal, identification services, summer camps and therapeutic summer programs, transportation, and wellness services/items that enhance quality of life, promote independence, and support community integration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in all Maryland counties through two program providers: Maryland Community Connection (serving Calvert, Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, and Worcester counties) and Penn-Mar Human Services (serving Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, and Washington counties).
requirements_list: Must have a developmental and/or intellectual disability
Must be living in their own home in the community (children living at home with family, or adults living independently in the community)

Must not be currently receiving any support services from the Developmental Disabilities Administration, except may be on DDA Waiting List receiving only Coordination of Community Services (CCS), or enrolled in Model Waiver or Medicaid's Rare & Expensive Case Management (REM) Program
Must have an eligible developmental disability diagnosis (learning disabilities, emotional disabilities, ADHD, or developmental delays alone may not qualify)
Must be a resident of Maryland
Must be requesting funding for an eligible service or item as defined in LISS Program regulations
Must participate in the random selection process by submitting a Random Selection Application online during the designated application round (applications only accepted online)
If selected, must provide documentation verifying identity, disability, residency, and identified eligible service or item delivered by an eligible vendor
If applicant is under age 21 without a court-ordered legal guardian, a natural or adoptive parent must submit the Random Selection Application
If applicant has a court-ordered legal guardian, the guardian must submit the Random Selection Application
If applicant is over age 21 without a legal guardian and only requires physical assistance, a parent, relative, friend, case manager, or social worker may assist under the applicant's direction
Must not have received LISS Program funding in Round 1 in the same Fiscal Year
Services/items must be provided during the current fiscal year (July 1 through June 30, with exception for summer camps extended through August 31)
Required proof of identity, parent/guardian identity (if under 21), Maryland residency, and disability must be submitted with Services Eligibility Application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a Random Selection Application online during the designated application round. Applications are only accepted online; hardcopy applications are not accepted. Complete the application with demographic information for the child or adult applicant and representative information if applicable. The applicant must be the focus of the application (not the parent/guardian), though a vendor or LISS program provider may assist with submission. 2. Upon submission, receive a confirmation receipt with a confirmation number via email. 3. Random selection takes place after the application deadline closes (for FY 2026, random selection occurs September 30, 2025). 4. Applicants are notified by letter of their random selection status within twenty business days after random selection is completed. 5. If selected, submit a complete Services Eligibility Application including required supporting documentation (proof of identity, proof of disability, proof of Maryland residency, completed Services Eligibility Application form, invoices/quotes/estimates or online shopping cart printouts for requested services/items, W-9 forms from vendors, and other documents specific to the requested service). 6. structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP) provides free or low-cost health insurance coverage to eligible uninsured children under age 19 and pregnant women of any age whose family income is too high to qualify for Medicaid but insufficient to afford private health insurance. Funded with federal and state money, MCHP provides full health benefits through Maryland's HealthChoice managed care organizations. Coverage includes dental care, doctor visits, hospital care, immunizations, lab work and tests, mental health services, prescription medicine, substance abuse treatment, transportation to medical care, and vision care. Children of employed parents whose employer does not offer family health insurance may also qualify. There are no fees or payments required for eligible beneficiaries, and coverage is available statewide across all Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full Medicaid-equivalent health insurance coverage for eligible children under age 19 and pregnant women of any age through one of Maryland's HealthChoice managed care organizations (MCOs: Aetna Better Health, CareFirst BlueCross BlueShield, Community Health Plan Maryland, Jai Medical Systems, Kaiser Permanente Maryland, Physicians Care, MedStar Family Choice, Priority Partners, United Healthcare Community Plan, and Wellpoint Maryland), with no fees or payments required from beneficiaries. Coverage includes dental care (through Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program), doctor visits including regular check-ups and Healthy Kids immunization check-ups, hospital services, urgent care center services, emergency services (including out-of-state emergencies), prescription drugs (no pharmacy copays for children under 21 and pregnant women), X-ray and lab services, well women care, prenatal and postpartum care, family planning and birth control (no pharmacy copays), home health services, vision exam and glasses for children under 21 (adult vision services vary by MCO), mental health services and substance use disorder treatment (call 800-888-1965 for behavioral health services), and transportation services to medical appointments. Children whose countable income is at or below 200% of the federal poverty level qualify at no cost; coverage is available up to 300% of the federal poverty level with a premium. Enrollees choose a HealthChoice managed care organization and primary care doctor; if no selection is made, the State will assign one. MCO availability varies by county.

structured_extraction.program_description: A community-based care coordination program for individuals with chronic conditions and behavioral health needs, including those with serious persistent mental illness, serious emotional disturbance, and opioid substance use disorders. The program provides enhanced care coordination services and six core services: comprehensive care management, care coordination, health promotion, comprehensive transitional care, individual and family support, and referral to community and social support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive enhanced care coordination services from providers including psychiatric rehabilitation programs (PRPs), mobile treatment service providers, and opioid treatment programs (OTPs). Services include comprehensive care management, care coordination, health promotion, comprehensive transitional care, individual and family support, and referral to community and social support. Health Home providers receive a monthly reimbursement rate of $131.03, contingent upon minimum service delivery and adherence to all requirements. Providers receive support including real-time hospital encounter alerts and pharmacy use data from the Chesapeake Regional Information System for our Patients (CRISP), as well as an eMedicaid online portal for enrollment, reporting, and tracking. This is designed to help individuals manage and prevent chronic conditions and reduce avoidable hospital encounters while improving overall health outcomes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Nurses and Nursing Support Staff (MLARP NNSS)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Loan Repayment Program (MLRP) provides state-funded loan repayment assistance to qualified nurses, advanced practice registered nurses, and nursing support staff who commit to working at approved eligible health care practice sites in Maryland that serve underserved populations or areas with health care workforce shortages or public health needs. The program covers education loans obtained for undergraduate or graduate study leading to licensure or certification in nursing disciplines. Funds are paid directly to verified education loan holders on behalf of awarded participants. Eligibility criteria and award amounts may change from year to year based on authorizing legislation and funding availability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Health pays MLRP funds directly to verified education loan holders to repay qualifying education loans on behalf of awarded participants. Maximum awards vary by credential and service obligation: Advanced Practice Registered Nurses (CRNP - Nurse Practitioner, CNM - Certified Nurse-Midwife, CRNA - Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist, CNS - Clinical Nurse Specialist) can receive up to $100,000 for full-time work (40+ hours per week) or $50,000 for part-time work (20-39 hours per week) with a 2-year service obligation; Registered Nurses (RN) and Licensed Practical Nurses (LPN) can receive up to $50,000 for full-time work or $25,000 for part-time work with a 2-year service obligation; Nursing Support Staff (CMT - Certified Medication Technician, CMA - Certified Medicine Aide, CNA - Certified Nursing Assistant, GNA - Geriatric Nursing Assistant) can receive up to $5,000 for full-time work or $2,500 for part-time work with a 1-year service obligation. Two full payments are made over the course of the service obligation: one during the first service obligation year and one during the second service obligation year (or final year for 1-year obligations). Funds are disbursed directly to lenders as directed by participants. Actual payments may be lower than the award amount if lender verification forms cannot demonstrate educational loan debt at the full award amount. Service obligations typically commence July 1 following the application cycle.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 15, 2026, at 11:59 pm (annual cycle: March 1 through April 15; eligibility criteria can change from year-to-year based on authorizing legislation and funding availability)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nurses (RN, LPN), Advanced Practice Registered Nurses (including Nurse Practitioners/CRNP, Certified Nurse-Midwives/CNM, Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetists/CRNA, and Clinical Nurse Specialists/CNS), and Nursing Support Staff (including Certified Medication Technicians/CMT, Certified Medicine Aides/CMA, Certified Nursing Assistants/CNA, and Geriatric Nursing Assistants/GNA) who are United States citizens or nationals, hold active valid Maryland licenses without restrictions or encumbrances, have personally accumulated education loan debt from accredited nursing training programs, and have valid employment contracts at eligible practice sites in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of qualifying education loans obtained for tuition, educational expenses, or living expenses for undergraduate or graduate study leading to practice as an advanced practice registered nurse, nurse, or nursing support staff. Loans obtained beyond licensure or certification are not eligible. Funds are paid directly to verified education loan holders and cannot be used for any other purpose.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must have valid employment contracts to work at eligible practice sites physically located in Maryland. As of FY26, approved practice sites must be either: (1) public or non-profit facilities exempt from taxation under Internal Revenue Code sections 501(c)(3) or (4), OR (2) for-profit sites located in areas of the state identified by the Maryland Department of Health as having a health care workforce shortage or public health need. Practice sites must provide services to all patients regardless of ability to pay: for those with incomes at or below 100% of U.S. Health and Human Services Poverty Guidelines, services must be at no charge or nominal charge; for those between 100-200% of poverty guidelines, sites must provide a schedule of discounts. Practice sites must maintain financial aid policies and accept reimbursement from Medicare, Maryland Medical Assistance Program, and Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program when applicable.

Eligible discipline: Advanced Practice Registered Nurses (CRNP, CNM, CRNA, CNS), Registered Nurses (RN), Licensed Practical Nurses (LPN), or Nursing Support Staff (CMT, CMA, CNA, GNA)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The annual application cycle runs from March 1 through April 15 at 11:59 p.m. EST. There is one annual application process for all nursing disciplines. Applicants must submit a complete application in specified formats by the deadline, including all required attachments and three complete references from parties noted in application instructions. Application components cannot be accepted prior to the opening date or after the deadline. The Department may request additional information; if not provided within stated deadlines, the application is deemed incomplete. Applicants must verify and demonstrate compliance with discipline, participant, and practice site eligibility criteria. Required documentation includes evidence of accredited training completion, active Maryland license, U.S. citizenship or national status, education loan debt documentation, and a valid employment contract at an eligible practice site. Eligible individuals may be awarded up to two MLRP service obligations per lifetime; those currently under a service obligation must be in the second obligation year to reapply, and two consecutive MLRP obligations cannot overlap. Applications are reviewed for eligibility, then ranked through a technical scoring process based on state and federal priorities, including discipline, area of practice (primary care prioritized), practice site geographic location (health professional shortage areas, medically underserved areas/populations, and rural areas prioritized), inpatient/outpatient practice type (outpatient prioritized), and practice site status (non-profit/public prioritized). Funds are distributed in a cascading process by priority tier with highest technical scoring funded first. Applicants are generally notified of application status by July 1 with offer or denial. Awardees receive a Welcome Packet explaining next steps. To accept the award, awardees must complete and submit a promissory note, service obligation agreement, and lender verification form (completed by the lender) by established deadlines. Once these documents are signed, awardees become program participants legally obligated to complete the service obligation. For year 2 participants (renewal), the Department must receive all renewal documentation (employment verification, impact data collection, cultural competency training completion, and updated lender verification) by established deadlines to remain in compliance; extensions cannot exceed 180 days. Awarded participants must fulfill service obligations at the approved practice site commencing July 1 following the application cycle and comply with ongoing monitoring requirements including employment verification and organizational reporting.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Repayment Programs (MLRP) / State Loan Repayment Program (SLRP) / Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Physicians (MLARP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Maryland Loan Repayment Programs (MLRP), which encompass the State Loan Repayment Program (SLRP), the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Physicians and Physician Assistants (MLARP PPA), and the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Nurses and Nursing Support Staff (MLARP NNSS). These programs provide educational loan repayment assistance to a broad range of health professionals—including physicians (MD/DO), physician assistants (PA), final-year medical residents, advanced practice registered nurses (CRNP, CNM, CRNA, CNS), registered nurses (RN), licensed practical nurses (LPN), and nursing support staff (CMT, CMA, CNA, GNA)—in exchange for a service obligation at an eligible practice site in areas of Maryland experiencing health professional shortages. The SLRP is funded in part by the U.S. Health Resources and Services Administration. The program is designed to improve recruitment and retention of the healthcare workforce in underserved areas and settings, with funds paid directly to lenders or student loan servicers on behalf of awarded participants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description:
Educational loan repayment assistance is provided in exchange for a service obligation at an eligible practice site. Award amounts and service obligations vary by discipline and employment status:

Physicians (MD/DO), physician assistants, and medical residents: up to $100,000 for full-time work (40+ hours/week) or $50,000 for part-time work (20–39 hours/week) for a 2-year service obligation. Final-year medical residents are eligible for a 3-year obligation (1 year during residency plus 2 years post-residency).

Advanced Practice Registered Nurses (CRNP, CNM, CRNA, CNS): up to $100,000 (full-time) or $50,000 (part-time) for a 2-year obligation.

Registered Nurses (RN) and Licensed Practical Nurses (LPN): up to $50,000 (full-time) or $25,000 (part-time) for a 2-year obligation.

Nursing support staff (CMT, CMA, CNA, GNA): up to $5,000 (full-time) or $2,500 (part-time) for a 1-year obligation.

Full-time is defined as 40 or more hours per week; part-time is 20–39 hours per week. At least 80% of work hours must be dedicated to direct patient care (exception: OB/GYN physicians must provide at least 50% in an ambulatory care setting; Certified Nurse Midwives must provide at least 50% in normally scheduled clinical hours in the ambulatory care setting). Time spent on-call does not count toward practice hours. A recipient's total cumulative award cannot exceed $200,000. Funds are paid directly to verified education loan holders/servicers on behalf of the participant. Two full payments are made over the course of the service obligation—once during the first service obligation year and once during the second service obligation year. Participants may designate the full annual award amount to one lender or distribute it to up to two lenders if the award exceeds any one lender balance. MLRP can only pay up to the current educational loan debt of each participant; actual payments may be lower than the award if lender verification forms do not demonstrate sufficient outstanding loan debt.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview:
Applications are accepted during the annual application cycle, which opens March 1 and closes April 15 at 11:59 p.m. EST. There is one annual application process for all disciplines and funding sources. Applicants must verify eligibility across three critical areas: Discipline, Participant, and Practice Site. All application components must be submitted in the formats noted in current application instructions, including components that must be submitted by application contributors such as employers and professional references. An application is not considered complete until all components have been submitted, including attachments and three complete references from the designated parties. Application components cannot be accepted prior to opening or after the deadline; MDH staff may contact applicants or contributors to request additional details, and if not provided within stated deadlines, the application will be deemed incomplete. Applicants and contributors attest to accuracy and completeness of application components upon submission.

Applications are reviewed for eligibility against current published MLRP eligibility criteria. Eligible applications undergo technical scoring based on State and Federal priorities, including discipline (Federal fund eligibility prioritized), specialty/area of practice (primary care prioritized), practice site geographic location (HPSAs, MUAs, rural areas prioritized), inpatient/outpatient practice (outpatient prioritized), and practice site not-for-profit/for-profit status (not-for-profit/public prioritized). Applications are assigned priority tiers based on overarching funding priorities; ranked applications receive consideration for award within available funding. If more eligible applications than funds are available, funds are distributed in a cascading process (priority tier by priority tier, highest technical scoring funded first). Applicants in highest scoring bracket may receive maximum awards; those scoring high enough in lower brackets may receive less than maximum amounts. When funds are no longer available, not all eligible applications will be awarded.

Applications received by the deadline are generally notified of status by July 1 of the application year. If offered an award, applicants must respond with required response documentation by stated deadlines to accept the obligation and become a participant.

To accept the MLRP service obligation/award, awardees complete agreements and provide supplementary documentation including: Promissory Note, Service Obligation Agreement, and Lender Verification Form (completed by lender/student loan servicer). All documents must be received by established deadlines; if not received, awardees no longer qualify and must reapply. Upon signing the Promissory Note and Service Obligation Agreement, awardees become program participants and are legally obligated to complete service obligation terms.

Final-year medical residents complete residency training without interruption and begin service obligation at an eligible practice site no later than three (3) months after completion of residency training. Upon commencement, they fulfill the same obligations as other physician participants.

Throughout the service obligation, participants must continue to meet all Discipline, Participant, and Practice Site eligibility criteria approved at application. Participants must participate in data collection exercises including surveys to collect experience and retention data, submission of aggregate de-identified patient data and key practice site health outcomes quality priorities, and verification of ongoing eligibility. Participants must respond accurately and within stated timelines to remain in compliance.

For 2-year service obligation participants, a renewal process occurs at end of first year/start of second year. Participants receive a Renewal Packet to complete and must submit all requested documentation by established deadlines to stay in compliance and trigger second-year payment. If all documentation is not received by the deadline, participants will be in breach. Any extensions must not exceed 180 days. Renewal requirements include employment verification (confirming participant worked 45+ weeks, at least 80% direct patient care, and work week not compressed to less than 4 days with no more than 12 hours in any 24-hour period), impact data collection, cultural competency training and assessment documentation (minimum 6 hours of training in cultural, linguistic, and health literacy competency), and updated lender verification. Practice sites must submit organizational assessment tools evaluating integration of National Standards for Culturally and Linguistically Appropriate Services in Health Care (CLAS) issued by HHS. The 2-year service obligation remains mandatory even if participant pays loan off early or receives full loan repayment; completing loan payments does not grant early release.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Maternal Opioid Misuse (MOM) Case Management Services
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive case management program administered by the Maryland Department of Health that provides enhanced case management services for pregnant individuals and those up to one year postpartum who have opioid use disorder or a history of opioid use and are enrolled in Maryland Medicaid. The program delivers person-centered care planning, goal-setting, screenings for depression, anxiety, and social determinants of health, and coordinates maternal and infant health services including prenatal and postpartum visits, medication for opioid treatment, behavioral health treatment, and overdose prevention education. Services are delivered through Maryland Medicaid's nine managed care organizations, and care plans are shared through CRISP, the statewide health information exchange, to participating providers. There are no costs to eligible participants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free enhanced case management services delivered through Maryland Medicaid's nine managed care organizations. Eligible Medicaid members receive at least monthly meetings with a case manager who develops a personalized care plan addressing mental and physical health needs, treatment goals, healthy lifestyle supports, overdose prevention, and medication for opioid treatment. Services include care coordination, person-centered care planning, goal-setting, screenings for depression and anxiety and social determinants of health, behavioral health treatment coordination, health care utilization support, prenatal and postpartum care, and connections to community and local support resources. Care plans are shared through CRISP, the statewide health information exchange, to participating providers. Services are available during pregnancy and for up to one year after birth at no cost to eligible participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant individuals and individuals up to one year postpartum who have opioid use disorder or a history of opioid use and are enrolled in Maryland Medicaid.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Enhanced case management services to support health care coordination, medication for opioid treatment, prenatal and postpartum care, behavioral health treatment, mental and physical health services, overdose prevention education, screenings for depression, anxiety, and social determinants of health, and connection to local recovery and community resources and supports.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland Medicaid members across all counties.
requirements_list: Must have health insurance through Maryland Medicaid
Must be pregnant or up to one year postpartum
Must have opioid use disorder or a history of opioid use
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible individuals can enroll by visiting the enrollment portal at http://health.maryland.gov/EnrollMOM. Pregnant people should start prenatal care as soon as they know they are having a baby and can contact their health care provider or health plan for help getting started. Marylanders across all sectors are encouraged to identify and refer potential participants to the program. For questions, contact the Maryland Medicaid MOM program at MDH.MOMModel@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A group-based prenatal and postpartum care program for pregnant individuals administered through Maryland Medicaid. Participants meet together with their healthcare provider in groups of eight to ten people who have similar due dates. Each visit lasts 90 minutes to two hours and combines individual medical/health exams with group education and peer support sessions. Topics covered include pregnancy side effects, labor and delivery, breastfeeding, baby care, stress management, and healthy eating. The program is free for eligible Maryland Medicaid members and is available statewide through Medicaid Managed Care Organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free prenatal and postpartum group-based care and support services for Maryland Medicaid members. Each visit lasts 90 minutes to two hours and includes individual health exams, group education, and peer support. No cost to participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant individuals who are Maryland Medicaid members
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prenatal and postpartum group care, education, and support services including pregnancy side effects, labor and delivery, breastfeeding, baby care, stress management, and healthy eating
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through Maryland Medicaid Managed Care Organizations
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland Medicaid member
Must be pregnant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Medicaid Managed Care Organization (the insurance plan listed on your Medicaid card) to ask about CenteringPregnancy providers in your area. Your MCO will help you find a provider and enroll in the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides doula and birth worker services to eligible Maryland Medicaid members. Doulas offer physical, emotional, and informational support to pregnant people and birthing parents before, during, and after birth. Services include prenatal visits to discuss labor, birth anatomy, medical procedures, comfort measures, mental health, self-advocacy, breastfeeding, and community resources; attendance at birth to provide emotional and physical support, positioning help, communication with medical teams, and breathing exercises; and postpartum visits for continued support of the birthing parent and baby. The program particularly focuses on supporting families of color and diverse racial, ethnic, and cultural communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Doula and birth worker services are provided at no cost to eligible Maryland Medicaid members. Services include: prenatal visits (typically in the birthing parent's home) to discuss labor and birth anatomy, medical procedures, comfort measures, mental health and self-care, communication skills, self-advocacy, breastfeeding support, and community resources; attendance at birth to provide emotional and physical support, positioning help, communication with medical teams, and breathing exercises; and postpartum visits (typically in the birthing parent's home) for continued support of the birthing parent and baby. Services do not cover clinical nursing, nurse-midwifery, nurse practitioner, or doctor services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant people and birthing parents who are Maryland Medicaid members, with particular attention to supporting families of color and diverse racial, ethnic, and cultural communities. Also eligible are those who have been pregnant within the last 180 days.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Doula and birth worker services including prenatal support visits, attendance at birth, and postpartum support visits. Services cover discussion of labor and birth anatomy, medical procedures, comfort measures, mental health and self-care, communication skills, self-advocacy, breastfeeding support, and community resources. Services cannot be used for clinical nursing, nurse-midwifery, nurse practitioner, or doctor services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide for eligible Medicaid members.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland Medicaid member
Must be pregnant or have been pregnant within the last 180 days
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Medicaid HealthChoice Managed Care Organization (MCO), which is your healthcare provider. Your MCO will help connect you to a doula when one becomes available and provide more information about services and support.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides resources, screenings, support, and services for children under three years old to promote healthy growth and development. A child development specialist is added to the child's pediatric care team to work with parents and families during the first three years of life, attending health care visits and providing ongoing support from newborn through the child's 4th birthday.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free program for eligible Medicaid members that includes child development screening and assessment, care coordination with a child development specialist, parenting resources and support, guidance on child growth and learning, breastfeeding support, mental health resources, and connections to additional community resources such as housing or transportation assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents and families with children under three years old who are Maryland Medicaid members.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides developmental screenings, parenting education and support, guidance on child development and learning, breastfeeding support, mental health resources, and referrals to community services such as housing and transportation assistance for eligible children and families. No direct financial assistance is provided to families.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland to Medicaid members through Medicaid Managed Care Organizations (MCOs).
requirements_list: Child must be a Maryland Medicaid member
Child must be newborn to their 4th birthday
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Medicaid Managed Care Organization (MCO), which is listed on your Medicaid insurance card. The MCO will help you find a HealthySteps provider in your area.

structured_extraction.program_description: Home Visiting Services provide support and teach parenting skills to pregnant people and birth parents before and after birth. Services are designed to help pregnant people get the care and support they need to have a healthy pregnancy and healthy child. Services are delivered in the home by specially trained professionals or nurses and continue after pregnancy to support the parent and child up to their second or third birthday, depending on the program. Topics covered include baby growth and development, parenting skills, self-care, community resources, diet and nutrition, future planning, and mental health and stress control. Two evidence-based home visiting models are available: Healthy Families America and Nurse Family Partnership.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Home Visiting Services are provided at no cost to eligible Maryland Medicaid members. Services are delivered through specially trained professionals or nurses who visit the home. The program offers two evidence-based home visiting models: Healthy Families America and Nurse Family Partnership. Services are tailored to the specific needs of the family and can continue from pregnancy through the child's second or third birthday, depending on which program is appropriate. Services include teaching about child development and learning, parenting skills, self-care, community resources, diet and nutrition, future planning, and mental health and stress management.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pregnant people and birth parents (recently postpartum individuals who have delivered within three months) who are Maryland Medicaid members, and families with children up to their second or third birthday.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home visiting services to support healthy pregnancy and postpartum care, including teaching about baby growth and development, parenting skills, self-care, community resources, diet and nutrition, future planning, and mental health and stress management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; available to Maryland Medicaid members.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland Medicaid member
Be pregnant or have delivered a child within three months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To access these services, contact your Managed Care Organization (MCO) to enroll in Home Visiting Services. Your health care provider or health plan can help find the right home visiting program for you.

structured_extraction.program_description: Medicaid Waiver programs serve as the primary funding mechanism through which the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) provides services to individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Services are available through both self-directed (where individuals hire and manage their own staff) and provider-managed (where a licensed provider directs and manages staff and services) delivery models, covering Meaningful Day Services, Support Services, and Residential Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid Waiver programs provide funding for services and supports to eligible individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, including meaningful day services, support services, and residential services. Services are delivered through either self-directed models where individuals hire and manage their own staff, or provider-managed models where licensed providers direct and manage staff and services. Additional covered services include Nursing Support Services and Clinical/Behavioral Services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities who are eligible for DDA Medicaid Waiver services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services and supports including Meaningful Day Services, Support Services, Residential Services, Nursing Support Services, and Clinical/Behavioral Services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be eligible for DDA services
Must apply for eligibility through the DDA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals apply for DDA services eligibility through the application process described on the Apply for Services page. More information about applying for services is available through the DDA application portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A home and community-based services (HCBS) Medicaid waiver administered by the Maryland Department of Health that helps eligible individuals receive medical day care services and support in their home and community instead of in an institutional setting such as a nursing facility. The waiver provides medical day care services along with a range of related support services for people who require nursing facility level of care, offering a community-based alternative to institutional care delivered by licensed medical day care providers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The waiver provides all Medicaid-covered services and benefits, plus waiver-specific services including medical day care (at least four hours per day, up to seven days per week), activity programs, meals, medication monitoring, nutrition services, skilled nursing and nursing assessments, social work services, therapy, personal care, daily living skills training, and transportation. All services are delivered by licensed medical day care providers as an alternative to institutional nursing facility care. No specific dollar amounts are stated; costs are covered through Medicaid waiver funding provided that the cost of community-based services does not exceed the cost of institutional care.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals age 16 or older who require nursing facility level of care, have full Medicaid coverage (red and white card), have a medical order for medical day care, and are not enrolled in another home and community-based waiver program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical day care services, activity programs, meals, medication monitoring, nutrition services, skilled nursing and nursing assessments, social work services, therapy, personal care, daily living skills training, and transportation provided in the home and community setting.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Individuals should contact their local health department or Maryland Access Point at 1-844-627-5465 to apply.
requirements_list: Must be age 16 or older
Must need nursing facility level of care
Must have a medical order for medical day care
Must not be enrolled in another home and community-based waiver program at the same time
Must have full Medicaid coverage (red and white card)
Must qualify for Medicaid in the community
The cost of community-based services must not exceed the cost of institutional care
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request a medical assessment to determine if you meet the level of care requirement by calling your local health department or Maryland Access Point at 1-844-627-5465 (Toll Free). You may also contact the Maryland Department of Health at 410-767-1100 or 1-800-535-0182 (Toll Free) to inquire about eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Medicare Savings Programs (MSP) / Medicare Buy-In Program (QMB/SLMB)
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Medicare Savings Programs are Medicaid-administered programs that help low-income Medicare beneficiaries pay for Medicare Part A (Hospital Insurance) and Part B (Medical Insurance) premiums, as well as Part A and Part B deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments. The program encompasses four sub-programs determined at the time of application: Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB), Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB), Qualifying Individual (QI), and Qualifying Disabled & Working Individuals (QDWI). QMB pays Medicare Part B premiums and full cost-sharing; SLMB pays only the Part B premium for those with slightly higher incomes; QI and QDWI serve additional qualifying groups. Eligibility is based on income relative to the federal poverty level and asset limits. QMB enrollees cannot be billed for Medicare-covered services and receive a gray and white card. Benefits are available statewide through local departments of social services and must be renewed annually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program pays Medicare Part A and Part B premiums and, depending on which sub-program the applicant qualifies for, may also cover Part A and Part B deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments. QMB Program: For individuals with modest assets up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple and combined incomes not exceeding 100% of the federal poverty level; pays Medicare Part B premiums and full cost-sharing amounts (deductibles and co-payments). Single individuals must have gross income under $16,200/year ($1,350/month); couples under $21,888/year ($1,824/month); assets under $9,950 (individual) or $14,910 (couple). Certain income exclusions apply: first $65 of monthly wages and half of wages above $65 are excluded; a $1,500 per person burial allowance is not counted as an asset. QMB enrollees cannot be billed for Medicare-covered services and receive a gray and white card. SLMB Program: Pays only the Part B premium for those with incomes between 100% and 120% of the federal poverty level with assets up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple. QI and QDWI Programs: Additional programs determined at time of application for other qualifying groups. No fees or payments required from beneficiaries. Beneficiaries must reapply annually. Once found eligible, each year the local department of social services will mail a case information form (CIF) to be reviewed and returned so eligibility for continued QMB/SLMB benefits can be redetermined. If the form is not returned by the due date, benefits will end.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing - applications accepted at any time. Must reapply annually.
structured_extraction.contact_name: State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP); Maryland Department of Human Services
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 1-800-638-3403; Baltimore County SHIP: 410-887-2059; Maryland DHS: 1-800-332-6347 (TTY: 1-800-735-2258); County-specific SHIP phone numbers available in attachment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Medicare beneficiaries in Maryland with income and assets below the program's limits, including residents of all counties. Individuals or married couples who receive or have applied for Medicare benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of Medicare Part A and Part B premiums, deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments, including out-of-pocket cost-sharing expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local departments of social services. Montgomery County residents may apply at regional offices in Silver Spring (8818 Georgia Avenue, 1st Floor), Rockville (1301 Piccard Drive, 2nd Floor), or Germantown (12900 Middlebrook Road, 1st Floor). Baltimore County residents may request an application by calling SHIP at 410-887-2059.
requirements_list: Must be a Medicare beneficiary
Must be a Maryland resident
Income and assets must be below the program's limits

QMB: combined income not exceeding 100% of the federal poverty level; assets up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple (or gross income under $16,200/year for singles, $21,888/year for couples; assets under $9,950 for singles, $14,910 for couples)
SLMB: income between 100% and 120% of the federal poverty level; assets up to $9,090 per individual or $13,630 per couple
Income exclusions: first $65 of monthly wages and one-half of monthly wages above $65 are excluded
$1,500 per person burial allowance is not counted as an asset
Must reapply each year
Provide proof of identity
Provide Social Security number
Provide proof of income
Must be a U.S. citizen or lawfully admitted alien
Proof of lawful immigration status is required
Report any changes in income, assets, address, or living arrangements to local department of social services within 10 days after the change occurs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply by mail, online at marylandbenefits.gov, by fax, or in person at your local department of social services or local health department. Download the current application form (DHS Form 9705) from the Department of Human Services website or local DSS office. Mail pages 1-4 of the completed application to the local department of social services in your county (addresses provided in application packet). Baltimore County residents may request an application by calling SHIP at 410-887-2059. Montgomery County residents may apply at one of three regional offices: Silver Spring (8818 Georgia Avenue, 1st Floor), Rockville (1301 Piccard Drive, 2nd Floor), or Germantown (12900 Middlebrook Road, 1st Floor). Interpreters are available for non-English speakers. Processing takes approximately 30 days. When you apply, the state determines which of the four Medicare Savings Programs (QMB, SLMB, QI, or QDWI) you qualify for. You may designate an authorized representative (relative, friend, or attorney) to receive copies of all letters about your eligibility, complete yearly applications on your behalf, and receive identification cards on your behalf. Annual redetermination: Once found eligible, each year your local department of social services will mail you a case information form (CIF) to be reviewed and returned. If you do not return the form by the due date, your benefits will end.

Completion of the training counts toward meeting MATE Act training requirements for practitioners registering for or renewing a DEA license.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free training and mentoring services for healthcare providers to effectively treat opioid use disorder with buprenorphine and other medications in high-need communities. Training counts toward MATE Act requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A chronic disease prevention and education program that provides outreach, technical assistance, and linkage to care services for community organizations. The program funds organizations to conduct preventative programming through community engagement, partnerships, and ongoing intervention for individuals in need. Focus areas include asthma, cardiovascular disease, cancer, obesity, diabetes and prediabetes, pregnancy and birth outcomes, and mental health. The program aims to improve health outcomes of racial and ethnic minority communities through community-based education and health promotion interventions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant awards of $25,000 to $75,000 per organization for one-year funding period (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027), with potential non-competitive continuation funding into FY 2028 based on satisfactory initial year performance. Up to 18 awards anticipated. Payments are made quarterly as reimbursement for invoiced expenses (no advance payments). Grantees must support the first three months of program activities from their own funds. Quarterly invoices are due 15 days after the end of each quarter, with approximately 30 days for invoice processing. Grantees are monitored through monthly narrative reports and performance measures throughout the funding period.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Shirlene Carr (Contract Officer); Lindsay Lotter (Grant Monitor)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and government agencies providing preventative health programming in chronic disease areas including asthma, cardiovascular disease, cancer, obesity, diabetes and prediabetes, pregnancy and birth outcomes, and mental health, as well as community organizations and faith-based organizations providing preventative health services to racial and ethnic minority populations within Maryland jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports general community-based health education and longitudinal health promotion programming to a cohort of enrolled participants, including preventative programming, community engagement, partnerships, outreach, technical assistance, and ongoing intervention services focused on asthma, cardiovascular diseases, cancer, obesity, diabetes and prediabetes, pregnancy and birth outcomes, and mental health. Funding may support staffing, program implementation, health screening activities, and linkage to care services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; open to all Maryland jurisdictions including Baltimore City. Applicants must maintain an operational office within the specific Maryland jurisdiction where services are proposed. If an organization serves minorities in more than one non-neighboring jurisdiction, only one application may be submitted for the specific jurisdiction where the organization intends to offer the program.

Must provide proof of tax-exempt status (IRS tax exempt status determination letter)
Must have a certificate of good standing issued by the Maryland State Government

Must be registered on eMMA (eMaryland Marketplace Advantage)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted via eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA) system at https://emma.maryland.gov using Solicitation ID BPM055355. This is a competitive Request for Applications (RFA) process. A pre-application webinar will be held on February 25, 2026, from 12:00 PM to 2:00 PM to explain the application process and answer questions. Registration is available at https://www.eventbrite.com/e/mota-pre-application-webinar-tickets-1980494078101?aff=oddtdtcreator. Applicants can download fillable forms from the MHHD website at Grant Application Documents. Applications must include: Volume I - Technical Proposal (transmittal letter, table of contents, project narrative, and application attachments) and Volume II - Budget Proposal. Required attachments include budget form, budget narrative, work plan, work plan Gantt chart, performance measures table, and monthly performance measures table. Written questions should be submitted via email to mdh.healthdisparitiesRFAapplications@maryland.gov and mdh.motamhhd@maryland.gov at least seven (7) days prior to the application deadline, with 'MOTA FY2027' in the subject line. Applications are reviewed through competitive evaluation by an evaluation committee based on technical proposal and budget criteria. Selected grantees are notified and awards are issued as Standard Grant Agreements. Grantees must submit monthly narrative progress reports and performance data using MHHD-provided templates, with reports due on the 10th of the month following completion (or following business day if 10th falls on weekend/holiday). An end-of-year annual report is due by August 31, 2027.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid program administered by the Maryland Department of Health that helps eligible individuals move from nursing homes or intermediate care facilities (including those for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities) into the community to live in homes, apartments, assisted living facilities, or group homes with four or fewer people. The program provides long-term care services that follow the person to their chosen living arrangement, with support from a team that includes a peer mentor to help find housing, care, and services needed for community living. The program also enhances outreach efforts and increases public awareness through options counseling for individuals wanting to return to the community or 'age in place,' and is implemented statewide with local support through Area Agencies on Aging and county agencies such as Prince George's County Aging & Disabilities Services Division and Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid long-term care services follow the eligible individual from an institutional setting (nursing home or intermediate care facility) to a community residence such as a home, apartment, assisted living facility, or group home with four or fewer people. A support team including a peer mentor helps locate housing, arrange care, and coordinate services needed for the person to live independently in the community. The program also provides options counseling and support planning services, including assistance with 'aging in place' and transitioning from institutional or nursing facility care to community living.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals currently residing in nursing homes or intermediate care facilities for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities who have Medicaid eligibility and want to transition to community-based living. Also open to nursing home residents seeking to transition to community or assisted living, including those wanting to 'age in place.' Must be at least 18 years of age.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medicaid long-term care services to support living in the community, including housing support, care coordination, options counseling, support planning, and related services to enable independent community living or transition to assisted living settings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Local support available through Area Agencies on Aging, Baltimore City, and Prince George's County, among others.

structured_extraction.program_description: An incentive program that awards nursing facilities monetary bonuses based on performance on quality indicators. One percent of the Program's nursing facility budget is distributed annually to facilities with the highest quality scores, with 85 percent going to top performers and 15 percent going to facilities showing year-over-year improvement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual monetary awards distributed from one percent of the nursing facility Medicaid budget. Facilities achieving the highest performance scores on quality indicators receive 85 percent of the total available funds. Facilities that did not rank highest but showed measurable improvement from the previous year receive 15 percent of the total available funds. Awards are based on scores in five areas: staffing levels (0-20 points), staff stability (0-15 points), MDS quality indicators for long-stay residents (0-30 points), family satisfaction survey results (0-30 points), and staff immunization rates (0-5 points). Staffing measures include nursing hours per resident per day based on acuity and percent of nursing staff with greater than 2 years tenure. MDS outcomes are collected through submissions to CMS and Maryland's Office of Health Care Quality. Staff immunization benchmarks: greater than 95% receives 5 points, greater than 90% receives 2 points, less than 90% receives 0 points. Awards are calculated on a per Medicaid day basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nursing facilities participating in Medicaid
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Facilities may use awards as discretionary funds to support operations and quality improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all eligible nursing facilities in Maryland participating in Medicaid.
requirements_list: Must have 45 or more beds
Must not be a continuing care retirement center (CCRC)
Must be participating in Medicaid
Must not have been identified as a federally-designated special focus facility in the previous year ending March 31
Must not have had a denial of payment for new admissions (DPNA) by CMS in the previous year ending March 31
Must not have been determined to have provided substandard quality of care as defined in federal Medicaid regulations in the previous year ending March 31
Facilities receiving a Performance award will not receive an Improvement score or award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Facilities do not submit applications. Performance is measured automatically using submitted staffing data, MDS data, payroll information, family satisfaction survey responses, and immunization records. Scores are calculated based on established metrics in five areas: Staffing Measures from Payroll Base Journal Data (total 35 points including staffing level up to 20 points and staff stability up to 15 points), MHCC Resident Satisfaction Survey (30 points), MDS Outcomes (30 points from six outcome measures), and Staff Immunization Rates (5 points). Facilities with the highest total scores receive Pay-For-Performance awards, and facilities with improved scores from the prior year receive Pay-For-Improvement recognition and a portion of available funds. Rankings include Overall rank (all facilities), P4P rank (eligible facilities), and Improvement rank (improvement award recipients).

structured_extraction.program_name: Rare and Expensive Case Management (REM) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The REM program provides medical case management and other services for eligible individuals with specific rare and expensive medical conditions. It is a voluntary program where an REM case manager helps develop a care plan and connects individuals with necessary services. Participants receive all Medicaid covered services and benefits in addition to REM-specific services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides comprehensive medical case management services including needs assessments, care plan development, assistance applying for services, ongoing monitoring and adjustment of care plans, education and information, and access to covered services. Covered REM services include: Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) and CNA Certified Medication Technician (CMT) services; chiropractic services; Home Health Aide (HHA) and HHA Certified Medication Technician (CMT) services; nutrition counseling and supplements; occupational therapy; speech-language pathology; and private duty nursing and shift nursing services. Participants receive all Medicaid covered services and benefits in addition to REM services. All services must be medically necessary, ordered by a health care provider, and may require preauthorization. The program is voluntary and participants work with an assigned REM case manager.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals eligible for the HealthChoice managed care program who have at least one rare and expensive medical condition specified on the REM disease list for their age group and choose to voluntarily participate in the REM program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical case management and supportive services including Certified Nursing Assistant and Certified Medication Technician services, chiropractic services, Home Health Aide and Certified Medication Technician services, nutrition counseling and supplements, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, private duty nursing, and shift nursing services. All services must be medically necessary, ordered by a health care provider, and may require preauthorization. Participants also receive all standard Medicaid covered services and benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to eligible HealthChoice participants in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be eligible for the HealthChoice managed care program
Have at least one rare and expensive condition for your age group as defined on the REM disease list
Choose to voluntarily participate in the REM program
Services must be medically necessary and ordered by a health care provider
Services may require preauthorization
Patient information and appropriate clinical documentation must be submitted with referral form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Anyone can refer an individual to the program. A licensed health care provider (physician, nurse practitioner, or physician assistant) must complete the REM Intake and Referral Form, including patient information, clinical information with ICD-10 codes, supporting clinical documentation (history and physical completed within past 12 months, specialist consultation notes, laboratory values, or imaging studies as required for the specific diagnosis), and must sign and date the form. The completed form with all required supporting clinical documentation should be submitted by fax to 410-333-5426 or emailed to mdh.remreferralfax@maryland.gov. Forms can also be mailed to: Maryland Department of Health, REM Intake Unit, 201 W. Preston Street, Room 208, Baltimore, Maryland 21201. The REM Intake Unit will review the referral for completeness and clinical eligibility. Services may require preauthorization before beginning.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicare Savings Program that helps people with limited income pay for Medicare Part B premiums, providing financial relief by eliminating the monthly Part B premium cost. Eligibility is based on income and assets below program limits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program pays Medicare Part B monthly premiums ($202.90) and may also pay Medicare Part A and Part B premiums, deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments. Eligibility is based on income and assets: Single individuals must have gross income under $21,792 per year ($1,816 per month) with assets under $9,950. Couples must have gross income under $29,460 per year ($2,455 per month) with assets under $14,910. Certain income types are excluded, including the first $65 of monthly wages and half of wages above $65. A $1,500 per person burial allowance is not counted as an asset. Beneficiaries must reapply annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: This law facilitates expedited licensing and certification for active military personnel, veterans, and their spouses. It helps qualified veterans and military spouses who hold valid licenses in other states obtain certain professional licenses and certifications in Maryland more quickly. The program covers occupational and professional licenses issued by licensing units and boards across multiple state agencies, including those overseen by the Departments of Health, Labor/Licensing/Regulation, Education, and other regulatory bodies. Military training, education, and experience are credited toward licensing requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program expedites the licensing and certification process for eligible veterans, active military members, and military spouses who already hold valid professional licenses in other states. Key provisions include: (1) Expedited temporary licenses valid for up to 6 months or until final determination; (2) Credit for all relevant military training, education, and experience toward licensing requirements if substantially equivalent; (3) Assignment of an advisor to assist with the application process; (4) For health occupations boards, issuance of permanent licenses within 15 business days of receiving a completed application when requirements are met; (5) Assistance in identifying education/training programs if additional requirements must be completed; (6) Waiver or suspension of certain licensing requirements (such as state criminal history records checks) where permitted; (7) Late renewal without penalty for active duty members deployed outside the state; (8) Extension of time to complete continuing education requirements after renewal. Health occupations boards may also issue temporary licenses for fields where requirements are not substantially equivalent, allowing service to be provided while additional requirements are completed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Veterans must apply within one year of discharge or separation from active military service. Current service members may apply when assigned to Maryland. Military spouses may apply when their spouse is assigned to Maryland. Surviving spouses must apply within one year of the service member's death or within one year of the veteran's honorable discharge.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Recently discharged veterans (within 1 year of discharge), active military personnel assigned to a Maryland duty station, military spouses of service members assigned to a Maryland duty station, military spouses of recently discharged veterans or service members, and surviving spouses of deceased service members or veterans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide direct financial assistance but rather expedites the professional licensing and certification process and credits military experience toward licensing requirements for eligible individuals in occupational and professional fields regulated by Maryland licensing units and boards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Current service members and military spouses must have a spouse assigned to a duty station located in Maryland or have established legal residence in Maryland to be eligible. Veterans must apply within one year of discharge or separation.
requirements_list: Must hold a valid license in good standing issued by another state in an occupation or profession regulated in Maryland

Must have received an honorable discharge or other than dishonorable discharge from U.S. Armed Forces (Army, Navy, Marines, Air Force, Coast Guard) or Reserve component, or be a current member of U.S. Armed Forces on active duty or reserve/national guard
If a veteran: must apply within 1 year of discharge or separation from active duty
If a current service member: must be assigned to a duty station in Maryland or have established legal residence in Maryland
If a military spouse of current service member: spouse must be assigned to a duty station in Maryland or have established legal residence in Maryland
If a military spouse of veteran: must have applied within 1 year of the veteran's discharge
If a surviving spouse: the service member must have died within 1 year before application, OR the veteran must have died within 1 year after discharge
Surviving spouses must apply within 1 year of the service member's death or within 1 year of the veteran's discharge
If a criminal background check is required by the licensing unit, must provide proof of application for background check
Must submit proof of military status or service member/spouse status in required form

For temporary licenses: requirements in other state must be substantially equivalent to or exceed Maryland requirements (except for alternative temporary licenses where board determines not substantially equivalent but public safety is not at risk)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should apply through the appropriate Maryland licensing unit or board for their specific occupation or profession. The application process includes: (1) Submit identification as a service member, veteran, or military spouse; (2) Provide proof of valid license in good standing from another state; (3) Provide proof of military status or assignment to Maryland duty station or legal residence in Maryland; (4) If required, submit proof of application for criminal background check; (5) Submit full application for licensure; (6) Pay applicable application fee. Upon receiving a completed application, the licensing unit shall assign an advisor to assist the applicant. For health occupations, the licensing unit must issue a permanent license within 15 business days if requirements are met. A temporary expedited license valid up to 6 months may be issued while the application is being processed. Each licensing unit publishes the expedited process on its website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community First Choice (CFC) and Home and Community-Based Options Waiver Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A set of Maryland Medicaid programs — including Community First Choice (CFC), the Community Options Waiver, and related Home and Community-Based Options Waivers — that provide community-based services and supports to enable older adults and individuals with disabilities to live in their own homes or assisted living facilities rather than in institutional settings such as nursing homes. Community First Choice is a Medicaid state plan benefit available statewide to individuals of any age who receive full community Medicaid and meet an institutional level of care. It consolidated personal care services from the former Living at Home Waiver and Older Adults Waiver programs. The Community Options Waiver enables individuals age 18 and older to remain in community settings by allowing Medicaid-covered services normally provided in nursing facilities to be delivered in individuals' homes or assisted living facilities. Services across these programs include personal assistance services, supports planning (case management), nurse monitoring, personal emergency response systems, assistive technology and devices, environmental assessments and accessibility adaptations, consumer and family training, home-delivered meals, respite care, medical adult day care, Senior Center Plus, behavior consultation, dietitian and nutritional services, medical equipment, and assistance with transitional costs. Participants are assigned a support planner to develop an individualized care plan.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Health, Maryland Medicaid / Maryland Department of Disabilities
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid-funded community-based services and supports delivered in individual homes or assisted living facilities. Services include personal assistance with activities of daily living, supports planning, nurse monitoring, personal emergency response systems, assistive technology and devices, environmental assessments and accessibility adaptations, consumer and family training, transition services, home-delivered meals, respite care, medical adult day care, Senior Center Plus, behavior consultation services, dietitian and nutritional services, medical equipment, case management, and assistance with transitional costs. No specific dollar amounts are stated; the State pays for covered services as a Medicaid benefit. For the Community Options Waiver, income eligibility is up to $2,199/month with asset limits of $2,000–$2,500.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides capital grants to assist in the acquisition, design, construction, renovation, and equipping of facilities that provide mental health, developmental disabilities, and drug and alcohol abuse treatment services. The primary focus is to develop and expand supported housing units for eligible populations, particularly to support housing for those with forensic involvement and to integrate behavioral health services that promote prevention, provide crisis and diversion services, and integrate with somatic services. The program serves non-profit and government organizations providing these services in community settings statewide.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Facilities Management and Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants to assist in the acquisition, design, construction, renovation, and equipping of community health facilities providing mental health, developmental disabilities, and substance use disorder treatment services. Grants support facility acquisition, design, construction, renovation, and equipping. Primary focus is on developing and expanding supported housing units and behavioral health service capacity. The program has provided millions of dollars in capital grants since the 1970s. Grant awards are made through the State's General Obligation Bond program, contingent on Board of Public Works approval, anticipated July 2027. State grant funding typically covers 50-90% of eligible project costs, with grantees required to provide matching funds. Fifty percent (50%) of the project must be supported by matching funds from sources other than State funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY 2028 Applications are due April 10, 2026 at 12:00 p.m., local time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and public (government) organizations providing mental health, developmental disabilities, and substance use disorder treatment services in community settings throughout Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, design, construction, renovation, and equipping of facilities that provide mental health, developmental disabilities, and drug and alcohol abuse treatment services. Primary focus on supported housing units (minimum 5 or more scattered-site housing units for behavioral health projects), crisis and diversion services, and integration of behavioral health services with somatic services. Projects may also support facility expansion for outpatient services, day programs, treatment centers, and administrative spaces.
