structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the FY 2028 Application using all required sections and attachments organized using the provided Checklist. Required for all applicants: Attachment A (Cost Application with Project Summary Sheet, Cost Estimate Worksheet, Capital Financial Summary, Operating Cost Projections if applicable, and Equipment/Furnishing Request if applicable); Attachment B (Listing of All Principals/Board Members); Attachment C (Civil Rights Compliance Assurance); Attachment D (Applicant Certification). Additional attachments required based on project type: Attachment E and F for behavioral health projects (Additional Information and Existing/Proposed Capacity); Attachment G for developmental disabilities projects; Attachments H and I for FQHC projects. Include Project Description addressing location, current and projected space requirements, scope of work, project site description, transportation access, and construction schedule. Include Administrative Information section with agency mission/history, strategic plan relevance, project justification, measurable outcomes, unmet need documentation, poverty area funding requests if applicable, admission policies, staffing patterns, rate schedules, and previous project information. Compile complete application with Checklist as table of contents and paginated sections. All documentation must be submitted in one PDF file via electronic mail to the contacts listed in application instructions by April 10, 2026 at 12:00 p.m., local time. Questions should be directed to the Project Manager at the Office of Facilities Management and Development.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides breast and cervical cancer screening, diagnosis, and patient navigation services to eligible women across Maryland. Services include clinical breast exams, mammograms, breast ultrasounds, Pap tests, HPV tests, colposcopy, cervical biopsies, and patient navigation assistance such as scheduling appointments, finding transportation, and interpretation services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Health, Public Health and Prevention Administration
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers free or low-cost breast and cervical cancer screening, diagnostic services, and patient navigation support to eligible women with limited income. Services include clinical breast exams, mammograms, breast ultrasounds, Pap tests, HPV tests, colposcopy, cervical biopsies, surgical consultation, and assistance with appointment scheduling, transportation, and interpretation services. Linkage to treatment is provided as needed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Women living in Maryland who are ages 18-64 (or 65+ without Medicare Part B), have limited income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level, and have no health insurance, inadequate health insurance coverage, or need help accessing screening and follow-up testing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Breast and cervical cancer screening, diagnostic testing including mammograms, breast ultrasounds, Pap tests, HPV tests, colposcopy, cervical and breast biopsies, surgical consultation, and patient navigation services including appointment scheduling, transportation assistance, and interpretation services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves women throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Live in Maryland

Be between ages 18-39 for diagnostics if symptomatic or screening if at increased risk, 40-64 for breast cancer screening, or 21-64 for cervical cancer screening (women 65+ without Medicare Part B also eligible)
Have limited income equal to or less than 250% of Federal Poverty Level
Have no health insurance, have health insurance that does not completely cover needed services, or need help accessing screening or follow-up testing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 1-800-477-9774 to access screening services. The program helps women find the nearest services and schedule appointments.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, in partnership with the Maryland Department of Aging, that provides zero percent interest, deferred loans or grants to help seniors age 55 and older make accessibility improvements to their homes. Improvements such as installing grab bars, railings, widening doorways, adding ramps, and bathroom modifications help older people remain in their homes and maintain independence. The program is available statewide and has been implemented as a pilot project in counties including Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest, deferred loans for up to 30 years, repayable upon sale, transfer, or refinance of the property. Loans are available for up to 110 percent of the property value (accounting for superior mortgages) statewide, or up to 85 percent of property value in Baltimore County, with all closing costs included in the loan. Alternatively, grants up to $25,000 are available for seniors who do not qualify for loan funding. Interest rates generally range from 0% to 6% based on applicant's ability to pay. Maximum loan amount is $50,000. Loans that serve families with incomes at or below 50 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may have deferred payments if necessary for project feasibility. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 55 or older who own and occupy their home as their principal residence. Seniors living with relatives may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of the Statewide or Washington DC MSA median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessibility improvements to make homes functional for seniors, including widening doorways, installation of accessible showers, ramps, grab bars, railings, lever handles, wheelchair ramps, bathroom modifications, and additions to accommodate first floor bathrooms and laundry rooms.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of the Statewide or Washington DC MSA median income. Baltimore County residents may also apply through the Baltimore County Senior Information and Assistance office.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident with at least one resident age 55 or older
Own and occupy the home as principal residence (seniors living with relatives considered on case-by-case basis)
Reside in a home that is structurally sound and free of health and safety hazards
Have no outstanding federal or state tax liens, open bankruptcy, or foreclosure

Meet income requirements (maximum 80 percent of Statewide or Washington DC MSA median income; for example, as of July 1, 2025, less than $72,950 for one person, less than $83,400 for two people, less than $93,800 for three people, less than $104,200 for four people in Rest of State, or $74,800, $85,450, $96,150, $106,800 respectively in Washington DC PMSA)
Provide proof of home ownership via copy of deed and current mortgage statement
Provide photo ID for applicant and any co-applicant
Provide most recent Property Tax Bill
Provide Declaration Page of Homeowners Insurance Policy
Applicants at or below 50 percent of median income may qualify for deferred principal and interest if no repayment capability exists
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available at local County Housing Offices or Maryland Access Point Agencies. Assistance in completing the application is available at the agency or through an in-home appointment. Baltimore County residents may call Senior Information and Assistance at 410-887-2594 to apply. Completed applications and supporting documentation must be submitted via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mailed to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Required documentation includes income verification documents (recent paystubs, tax returns, bank statements, award letters), proof of home ownership, property tax bills, and homeowners insurance documentation. Once submitted, the application is processed by the department and the applicant will be contacted. For more information, contact Special Loan Programs at DHCD.SpecialLoans@maryland.gov, 301-429-7409, or toll-free 877-218-8101.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state revitalization program that demonstrates how strategic investment in local housing and businesses can lead to healthy, sustainable communities with a growing tax base and enhanced quality of life. The program focuses on areas in the Baltimore region where modest investment and a coordinated strategy will have a meaningful neighborhood revitalization impact, providing capital and operating funding to support neighborhood improvement projects targeted by eligible applicants in their strategic plans.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides approximately $20 million in capital funding and $2 million in operating funding for Baltimore regional neighborhood improvement projects. Funding is provided to Community Development Organizations for projects located in Sustainable Community Areas in Baltimore City and the inner beltway of Baltimore and Anne Arundel counties. Projects may include down payment assistance for home buyers, acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant or blighted properties, improvements to residential and business properties, energy efficiency programs, mixed-use development, community open space or public infrastructure enhancement, workforce development programs, strategic demolition, and operating costs for community enhancement projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Organizations with an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan; Baltimore region organizations and local governments pursuing neighborhood revitalization
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance to attract home buyers, acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant or blighted properties, improvements to existing residential and business properties, energy efficiency through weatherization and energy retrofits, mixed-use development combining housing retail and office space, community open space or public infrastructure development or enhancement, workforce and employment development programs, strategic demolition, and operating costs for community enhancement projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Sustainable Community Areas in Baltimore City and the inner beltway of Baltimore County and Anne Arundel County. In addition, projects should be located in an area targeted by an eligible BRNI applicant in their five-year strategic plan. Regional Project Managers cover the following areas: Region 1 (Northwest Baltimore City and County), Region 2 (Northeast Baltimore City and County), Region 3 (Southeast Baltimore City and County), and Region 4 (Southwest Baltimore City and County and Northern Anne Arundel).
requirements_list: Community Development Organization must have an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan
If organization lacks an approved plan, it must submit one at time of application
Projects must be in a Sustainable Community
Projects must capitalize on community strengths
Projects must be targeted in specific neighborhoods or sets of neighborhoods
Projects must be part of the approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan
Projects should be located in an area targeted by an eligible BRNI applicant in their five-year strategic plan
Cross-jurisdictional partnerships are eligible
Applying with partner organizations, like Community Development Financial Institutions, is strongly recommended
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Community Development Organizations with an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan may apply for funding. Organizations without an approved plan must submit one at the time of application. First-time applicants are advised to contact a regional project manager for more information and eligibility determination. Application training is available via webinar. Register for training and view application information at the DHCD State Revitalization Programs website. Questions about specific address eligibility should be directed to the Regional Project Manager. Regional Project Managers by area: Region 1 (Northwest Baltimore City/County) - Jessica DeGaine (jessica.degaine@maryland.gov, 410-209-5851), Region 2 (Northeast Baltimore City/County) - Kate Howard (katherine.howard@maryland.gov, 410-209-5824), Region 3 (Southeast Baltimore City/County) - Sarah Kim (sarah.kim1@maryland.gov, 410-209-5836), Region 4 (Southwest Baltimore City/County and Northern Anne Arundel) - Erin Lavitt (erin.lavitt@maryland.gov, 410-209-5828).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative provides capital to Baltimore City, the Maryland Stadium Authority, and Baltimore City's community-based development organizations to redevelop vacant properties and strengthen neighborhoods. The program focuses on eliminating vacant properties through renovation, acquisition, and redevelopment activities in clusters of contiguous blocks to achieve whole block outcomes where every property on a block has a productive use. Grant and loan funding helps community development organizations acquire, stabilize, renovate, or demolish properties with vacant building notices to improve neighborhoods and create green space, affordable housing, and mixed-use developments. The program is part of Reinvest Baltimore, a coordinated effort signed into Executive Order by Governor Moore on October 1, 2024, to move at least 5,000 vacant properties into homeownership or other positive outcomes over the next five years.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FY27 BVRI funds will be provided as partially forgivable subordinate loans from the Maryland Community Investment Corporation (MCIC). Grant funds and loans are used to finance: acquisition, stabilization, renovation and new construction of vacant buildings with priority on those with city-issued Vacant Building Notices (VBNs); acquisition and aggregation of vacant lots for new infill housing construction, mixed-use projects, and community-managed open space; urgent demolition of vacant properties that pose a community health risk or further near-term redevelopment; predevelopment activities including architectural and engineering work, site infrastructure, and site development for renovation and new construction projects. Forgivable loan funds are based on Net Sale/Refinance Proceeds and project appraisal gap. BVRI loans are available for acquisition and pre-development soft costs, construction financing gaps, and closeout appraisal gap coverage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community development organizations (CDOs) and nonprofit organizations with a track record of completing the rehabilitation of vacant property and/or infill new construction projects, and with an organizational mission that includes community development work and a service area in Baltimore City. CDOs may partner with for-profit or non-profit developers. Local governments are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, stabilization, and renovation of vacant buildings, prioritizing those with city-issued Vacant Building Notices (VBNs); vacant lot acquisition and aggregation for new infill housing construction; vacant lot acquisition and aggregation for community-managed open space; urgent demolition of properties posing a community health risk or furthering near-term redevelopment; architectural and engineering work, site infrastructure, and site development for renovation and new construction projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Activities must be located in Sustainable Community Areas in Baltimore City. Special consideration is given to projects in Baltimore City Vacancy Reduction Priority Geographies (VRPGs), which include Impact Investment Areas. Projects located in designated ENOUGH (Engaging Neighborhoods, Organizations, Unions, Governments and Households) areas and Just Communities areas will receive up to 10 bonus points each. All projects must be located in clusters of contiguous blocks where the applicant can demonstrate capacity and a plan to address all vacant property over time. Whole block outcomes occur when every property on a block has a productive use, including removal of all vacant building notices on a block.
requirements_list: Must be a community development organization (CDO) or nonprofit organization with a track record of completing rehabilitation of vacant property and/or infill new construction projects over the past five years (FY22 through FY26)
Organizational mission must include community development work and a service area in Baltimore City
CDO must demonstrate capacity and a plan to address all vacant property over time within the target area
Projects must be located in clusters of contiguous blocks (approximately 5 blocks by 5 blocks, walkable)

Applicant must submit all required organizational documents: By-Laws, Articles of Incorporation, Current Board Roster, Annual Report, IRS Letter of Determination, Financial Audit, Operating Budget, Profit & Loss Statement, Balance Sheet, and Public Disclosure Authorization

Applicant must submit completed property pipeline spreadsheet listing all properties expected to be redeveloped with FY27 BVRI funding; applications without completed spreadsheets will not be accepted
Applicant must provide target area map showing neighborhood boundaries and target area boundaries
Applicant must provide letters of support from all development partners that will be sub-recipients of BVRI funding
All applications must include incomplete property spreadsheets and required partner letters; applications missing required information may not be considered for funding
Awarded funds will primarily support activities that accelerate remediation of vacant buildings with city-issued Vacant Building Notices
If funded, may be required to provide a government resolution, corporate board resolution, and charitable registration
Applicants must be nimble, efficient, and fast; organizations that can scale up their production will gain more ongoing BVRI investment over time
Projects must align with values and principles agreed upon by the Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Council (BVRC)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted exclusively through the Survey123 online portal; paper applications are not accepted. The application will not be available in DHCD's IGX Project Portal. Use the specific link provided on the BVRI website to access the application. The application is automatically saved in your browser and does not require account creation. DHCD cannot see your application until you press submit. All required documents (organizational documents, property pipeline spreadsheet, target area map, partner letters, budgets, and other supporting materials) must be uploaded with the application before submission. Applications including all necessary attachments must be submitted by 11:59 pm on April 1, 2026. DHCD provides application support throughout the submission period. An application training recording and step-by-step instructions are available on the website. One-on-one scheduling links are available for applicants to discuss questions specific to their organization. During the application review process, review teams may make site visits and/or hold meetings with applicants. Applicants may be contacted by the Department for follow-up discussions prior to awards.

structured_extraction.program_name: BeSMART Energy Efficiency Loan for Homeowners Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The BeSMART Loan Program is an innovative financing program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that provides Maryland homeowners with low-interest, unsecured loans to improve the energy efficiency, safety, and comfort of their homes. The program supports replacement and upgrading of appliances, heating, ventilation and cooling systems, and whole house envelope improvements. By financing energy efficiency and clean energy projects—including heat pump systems, solar photovoltaic installations, and more—the program helps homeowners reduce utility bills, improve home safety and comfort, and increase home value. Homeowners work with eligible weatherization and energy efficiency professionals whose qualifications have been reviewed by DHCD.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unsecured loan with a 6.99% APR. Up to $30,000 in financing is available for energy efficiency measures for a term of up to 10 years, though borrowers may choose a shorter repayment period. The minimum loan amount is $5,000. The loan is based on verification of credit and ability to pay, requiring a credit score of 640 or greater and a debt-to-income ratio not exceeding 50%. Solar photovoltaic projects can finance up to 50% of the total loan amount (1:1 match to energy efficiency measures cost). Funding is provided in two draws: an initial 30% down payment as a 2-party check (to borrower and contractor, or 1-party check for retail purchases), with the remaining 70% provided upon project completion. No pre-payment penalties apply, allowing borrowers to pay off the loan early and avoid additional interest.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners seeking to finance energy efficiency and clean energy improvements to their homes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency measures including insulation and air sealing, ENERGY STAR heating and cooling systems, ENERGY STAR hot water heating equipment, ENERGY STAR appliances (excluding stoves, ovens, and microwave ovens), windows and doors, lighting and controls, programmable and smart thermostats, ceiling fans and ventilation fans, geothermal heat pumps, solar photovoltaic installations (capped at 50% of total loan or 1:1 match to energy efficiency measures cost), heat pump systems, health and safety costs related to energy improvements including mold remediation and radon mitigation (up to 25% of total loan cost), and other improvements identified in a certified energy audit. Projects must not have been previously purchased or already completed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland homeowner
Credit score of 640 or greater
Debt to income ratio that does not exceed 50%
Projects or upgrades must not be already purchased or already completed
Contractor must be licensed and insured in Maryland
No re-financing of previously completed work or purchased items allowed; borrowers must not have any work done or make purchases until receiving BeSMART funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online BeSMART Loan Application or request a paper application via email. Provide drivers license, 30 days of pay stubs, and a recent mortgage statement. A DocuSign will be sent to allow you to privately provide your Social Security number and consent to a credit check. Submit an estimate or proposal from your contractor or retailer for items to be financed. Upon approval, DHCD sends loan documents which must be signed and returned. DHCD then sends an initial 30% down payment as a 2-party check (with borrower and contractor names, or 1-party check for retail purchases with no contractor). Begin project work. Upon completion, both borrower and contractor sign a Certificate of Completion and submit photos. DHCD then sends the remaining 70% payment. Borrower then begins making loan payments. Borrowers may work with any contractor of their choice who is licensed and insured in Maryland; there is no pre-approved contractor list.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Business Boost Microgrant Program, administered through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Neighborhood BusinessWorks program, provides microgrants ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 to support new and expanding small businesses seeking capital for growth and expansion opportunities. The program has a preference for home-based businesses establishing their first commercial location outside of the home. Businesses must be located in a designated Sustainable Communities area. The program supports businesses that contribute to economic growth through innovation, new industries, regional strengths, or partnerships with educational institutions, and gives priority to minority and women-owned businesses, businesses driving innovation or technology advancements, and those leveraging existing regional strengths.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Microgrants ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 are available to support small businesses needing capital for growth and expansion opportunities. Total program funding is up to $2,000,000 through the Neighborhood BusinessWorks program. Applicants must provide a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount. Funds can be used towards capital and operating expenses supporting revenue growth from September 23, 2024, to March 23, 2025, including but not limited to: salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, and professional services. Only new expenses are eligible; existing expenses such as current rent or payroll cannot be used as eligible expenses. Priority funding is based on: (1) business location, (2) expansion impact including new employees to be hired, capital investment for expansion, and additional square footage, and (3) presentation of business financials and supporting documents. Priority is also given to innovative businesses driving technology advancements, businesses growing in new industries, businesses focused on regional strengths, businesses leveraging partnerships with educational institutions, and Minority Business Enterprises (MBE).
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small business owners with greater than 2 and 50 or fewer full-time equivalent employees and annual revenue between $50,000 and $1 million, seeking to expand or establish a commercial location in a designated Sustainable Communities area. Preference is given to home-based businesses establishing their first commercial location outside of the home.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and operating expenses supporting revenue growth including salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, and professional services. Only new expenses are eligible (e.g., increased rent or payroll for new hires); existing expenses cannot be used. Funds support business expansion by covering increased rent, increased payroll for hiring new employees, new equipment, and marketing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located within a Maryland Sustainable Communities area to be eligible to apply. Applicants should use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper at https://portal.dhcd.state.md.us/GIS/revitalize/index.html to verify their business location qualifies.
requirements_list: Be a for-profit business
Be located in a Sustainable Communities area in Maryland
Have greater than 2 employees and 50 or fewer employees (full-time equivalent) as of September 23, 2024
Have an annual revenue greater than $50,000 but less than $1 million
Be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Have a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount (e.g., $50,000 grant requires $50,000 matching contribution)
Not be a professional services or sales-based business such as Insurance, Accounting, Real Estate, Legal, or Finance

Not be a non-profit organization, cannabis-based business, pawn shop, gun shop, massage parlor, adult video or book shop, adult entertainment facility, rental real estate business, Insurance company, tanning salon, check-cashing facility, gambling facility, tattoo parlor, or liquor store
Not be a previous award winner of an NBW Opportunity Zone grant or NBW Business Boost grant

Must meet one or more priority impact attributes such as supporting minority and women-owned businesses, driving innovation or technology advancements, growing new industries, or leveraging existing regional strengths
Application must be complete by deadline; incomplete applications are ineligible
Business name on application must exactly match SDAT's Good Standing Certificate and W-9
Applicants should have cash in business account to match grant request amount (preference given to those with cash available at time of application)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application window opened on Monday, September 23, 2024 at 12:00 noon and closes on Monday, October 14, 2024 at 5:00 p.m. EST (note: round may close sooner if grant requests exceed available funding). Applicants create an account in the online application portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/NBWOZGrant/account/login to submit applications. All applications must be fully completed at the time of submission; incomplete applications will be returned and processed when resources are available. Required documents include: (1) Articles of Organization, (2) By-laws, (3) Most recent annual tax return (Tax year 2023), (4) Financial statements as of August 31, 2024, (5) Screenshot showing eligible location, (6) Proof of matching funds (bank statement or loan statement as of August 31, 2024), (7) Screenshot of Certificate of Good Standing from SDAT, and (8) IRS W-9. Applications are evaluated based on meeting eligibility requirements, business financials and supporting documents, location, expansion impact (new hires, capital investment, square footage), and application completeness. Award announcements will be made on a rolling basis during December 2024 to January 2025. Grant funds are expected to be paid in February-March 2025. DHCD will initiate the process with the local governing body to seek a local resolution approving the grant. The local jurisdiction will have 45 days to respond; if approved within 45 days, DHCD will process the grant for payment. If no response within 45 days, funding is deemed approved and DHCD will implement the funding process. Grant awardees must submit a final report by March 31, 2026 detailing how funds were used and will be contacted nine months after receiving funds to complete a questionnaire and provide a one-page summary of grant impact.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that supports 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations by awarding allocations of State tax credits. These credits serve as incentives to attract charitable contributions from individuals and businesses to benefit local projects and services in Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program awards a total of $1.75M in Maryland income tax credits annually to successful applicants. Donors who contribute $500 or more to a qualified nonprofit's approved project can earn tax credits equal to 50% of the value of their cash donation, goods, or real property contribution. The maximum award request is $50,000, and awardees must raise double the amount of tax credits requested (e.g., if requesting $50,000 in credits, $100,000 must be raised). These credits are in addition to Federal and State tax deductions for the charitable contribution. Tax credits must be used against taxes owed for the year the contribution was made and cannot be applied retroactively. All CITC award contracts have a 24-month life, during which awarded credits must be used.
structured_extraction.program_audience: IRS designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations seeking tax credit allocations to support community projects. Also available to individuals and businesses making charitable contributions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects can be capital and/or operating initiatives including education and youth services, housing and community development, job and self-sufficiency training, neighborhood and business district enhancement, arts culture and historic preservation, economic development and tourism promotion, technical assistance and capacity building, and services for at-risk populations. Eligible budget line items include staff costs, rent, utilities, program supplies, training, travel, construction soft costs such as planning, design, engineering, and permitting, as well as direct construction expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area. For capital projects, the project site must be located within a PFA boundary. For operating projects, organizations can request funding if they document that clients served reside within a Priority Funding Area.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an IRS designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization with valid IRS 501(c)(3) Determination Letter
Organization must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Organization must be registered as a charity with the Office of the Secretary of State or have a religious exemption letter
Project must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area
Donors must contribute $500 or more to be eligible for tax credits
Donors must obtain a Donor Acknowledgement Form from the nonprofit
For real property donations, donors must contact the nonprofit prior to making the donation
Tax credits must be used against taxes owed for the year the contribution was made
For capital projects, organization must document site control via deed, lease, real estate settlement documents, or similar evidence
Organization must maintain charitable registration and good standing status throughout the award period
Organization must submit Tax Credit Certification Requests within 30 days of receiving each donation
Organization must submit four semi-annual reports during the 24-month award period (due July 10 and January 10)
Organization must maintain records for seven years following award completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Nonprofit organizations submit competitive applications through the Department's IGX Project Portal (DHCD-NR Project Portal). If not already registered, applicants must submit a New User registration request, which takes up to 72 hours to approve. Organization records and legal documents must be completed on the Profile pages before creating an application. Applications must include current copies of Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, IRS 501(c)(3) Determination Letter, Board of Directors list, Charitable Registration or Exemption Letter from Maryland Secretary of State, SDAT Good Standing status screenshot, executed Corporate Resolution, and Priority Funding Area (PFA) maps for each project location. Applications must also include evidence of site control for capital projects. All documents must be uploaded in PDF format. The FY26 application round opens May 19, 2025, and closes June 19, 2025, at 5 p.m. Award decisions will be announced in Fall 2025. Awardees may begin accepting donations starting January 1, 2026, or upon full execution of the award agreement, whichever occurs last. The 24-month contract period runs from January 1, 2026, through December 31, 2027.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides local governments and community development organizations with funding for essential projects aimed at strengthening communities through activities such as business retention and attraction, encouraging homeownership and commercial revitalization, mixed-use development, streetscape improvements, home rehabilitation, façade improvements, real estate acquisition, and strategic demolition.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides $8 million in capital funding for community legacy projects. Funding supports projects located in Sustainable Communities or in Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. Eligible projects include mixed-use development, business retention and expansion initiatives, streetscape improvements, homeownership and home rehabilitation programs, façade improvements, real estate acquisition including land banking, and strategic demolition. Technical assistance and information are also available.
