structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business retention and attraction, encouraging homeownership and commercial revitalization, mixed-use development, streetscape improvements, home rehabilitation, façade improvements, real estate acquisition including land banking, strategic demolition, and site development and construction for community multi-use areas and buildings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in a designated Sustainable Community or in an Opportunity Zone in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility.
requirements_list: Projects must be in a Sustainable Community or in an Opportunity Zone in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties
Projects should capitalize on the strengths of a community while addressing its challenges to revitalization
Projects should help achieve a local government's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Projects should aim to stabilize a community, reverse social, economic or physical decline, or encourage sustainable growth
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First-time applicants are advised to contact a regional project manager for more information and eligibility determination. Application training is available via webinar. Register for training and view application information at the DHCD State Revitalization Programs website at https://dhcd.maryland.gov/Communities/Pages/StateRevitalizationPrograms/default.aspx

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Schools Rental Assistance Program (CSRAP) is a state-funded rental assistance initiative that supports housing stability for families with children enrolled in Maryland community schools. It helps families and students at risk of eviction, losing housing, or experiencing homelessness to secure or maintain rental homes. The program provides emergency financial assistance to cover past due rent, utility bills (including water), moving costs, deposits, and up to 3 months of future rent or utility payments related to housing instability. Participating jurisdictions include Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's, Washington, and Wicomico counties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible families receive emergency financial assistance on a need and availability basis. Assistance can cover: past due rent or utility bills (including late fees, court fees related to eviction, and water bills); moving costs and deposits needed to rent a new home such as security deposit, application fees, first month's rent, and utility deposits; and up to 3 months of prospective (future) rent and/or utility assistance related to housing instability. The maximum length of assistance a household can receive is 15 months total. Eligible households may receive repeat assistance contingent on availability of program funds and qualifying circumstances. Households receiving prospective assistance must recertify eligibility every 3 months to determine continued eligibility. Assistance is provided based on need and availability of funds per local providers. For voucher holders and those in subsidized housing, assistance is limited to the portion of rent legally owed by the tenant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and students enrolled in designated community schools who are at risk of eviction, losing housing, or experiencing homelessness. In Montgomery County, eligibility is limited to families with students in designated Community Schools. Unaccompanied minors attending community schools are also eligible if other criteria are met.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Past due rent or utility bills including late fees and court fees related to eviction; utility bills including water; moving costs and deposits needed to rent a new home such as security deposit, application fees, first month's rent, and utility deposit; relocation assistance for uninhabitable or unsafe housing units; and up to 3 months of future rent and/or utility assistance related to housing instability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Frederick County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Washington County, and Wicomico County. Assistance can only be provided to households that have a student enrolled in a community school in the county where they are requesting assistance. Montgomery County eligibility is limited to families with students in designated Community Schools. Most jurisdictions currently have limited or no funding available.
requirements_list: At least one student in the household is enrolled in a community school in a participating jurisdiction
You are experiencing homelessness or at risk of housing instability (such as past due utility or rent notice, eviction notice, or unsafe/unhealthy living conditions)
You are responsible for paying rent or utilities in a qualifying rental unit
Be renting your home or trying to rent a new home (homeowners are not eligible)
Proof of student's community school enrollment must be provided
Proof of rental agreement must be provided
Invoice or proof of missed rent or utility payments must be provided
Residency can be documented by lease, rental agreement, or proof of history of paying rent
Proof of citizenship is not required; eligibility is based on renter status and community school enrollment, not immigration status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications can be obtained from the local agency supporting your county. For Montgomery County residents, applications can also be submitted through hiphomes.org. Links to local agencies are available on DHCD's website at https://dhcd.maryland.gov/HomelessSolutions/Pages/Community-Schools.aspx. If you are unable to complete the application online, you can request a paper copy from the local agency. School staff may help identify eligible families, coordinate referrals, and support outreach and engagement, though involvement may vary by county.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to Community Action Agencies and other non-profit organizations across Maryland to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization. The program distributes 90% of Maryland's allocated funds to seventeen designated Community Action Agencies, which use the money to offer services helping low-income individuals and families achieve self-sufficiency in areas such as employment, education, housing, nutrition, emergency services, and health. The remaining funds support discretionary anti-poverty activities, training, technical assistance, and coordination among Community Action Agencies.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Formula grants to Community Action Agencies and non-profit organizations to support anti-poverty programs, self-sufficiency initiatives, and community revitalization. The program distributes 90% of Maryland's allocated federal funds to designated Community Action Agencies, with 5% reserved for discretionary funding to support additional poverty-fighting activities. May also include training, technical assistance, and coordination support among agencies.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The FY25 application round is closed. Check this page for information about future funding rounds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's designated Community Action Agencies, non-profit organizations, and local government units that serve low-income individuals and families working to address poverty and promote community development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Activities and programs to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization. This includes direct services for low-income individuals in areas of employment, education, housing, nutrition, emergency services, and health, as well as training, technical assistance, and coordination support among Community Action Agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Services must benefit individuals and households with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines.
Community Action Agencies must have a specific board composition: one-third public officials, one-third representatives of low-income persons, and one-third from community groups.
Applicants for discretionary funds must propose a program with measurable outcomes for self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application period for fiscal year 2025 has closed. Check the program's webpage for information about future application opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports the creation, upgrade, and retrofit of computer labs and centers to provide public computer and internet access for vulnerable populations including individuals with disabilities, homeless individuals, veterans, and incarcerated or returning citizens.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $65,000 for computer equipment purchase (up to 100% of eligible costs) and up to $10,000 for internet service subscription costs for up to three years (up to 100% of eligible costs). Total program funding of $2 million available. Funds may be used for: computer equipment (desktops, laptops, keyboards, mice, monitors, webcams, headphones, microphones); networking equipment (routers, switches, network cables, Wi-Fi access points, firewalls); internet service subscription (wired internet connection only, up to 3 years); marketing and outreach (up to 10% of total project budget); operational expenses including staff salaries and lab maintenance (up to 15% of total project budget); administrative expenses including training and security monitoring costs (up to 15% of total project budget); software (operating systems, office productivity suites, educational and training software, antivirus and security software); audiovisual equipment (projectors, screens, smartboards for training, speakers and sound systems); and assistive technology (screen readers, magnifiers, adaptive keyboards and mice, accessibility features). Majority of those served (50% or higher) must fall into covered populations: individuals with disabilities, homeless persons, veterans, and incarcerated or returning citizens.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ronnie Hammond (for paper submissions); OSB Digital Equity Team for general inquiries
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, incorporated municipalities, local government agencies, community-based organizations, nonprofits, and community anchor institutions serving individuals with disabilities, homeless individuals, veterans, and incarcerated or returning citizens
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creation, upgrade, and retrofit of computer labs and centers providing public computer and internet access for vulnerable populations. Funding may be used for computer equipment, networking equipment, internet service subscription, marketing and outreach, operational expenses, administrative expenses, software, audiovisual equipment, and assistive technology.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all Maryland communities. Funding source is American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds.
requirements_list: Applicant must be Maryland local jurisdiction, incorporated municipality, local government agency delegated by local jurisdiction, not-for-profit IRS-approved 501(c) entity providing services within Maryland, or Community Anchor Institution within Maryland
Majority (50% or higher) of lab users must be individuals with disabilities, homeless individuals, veterans, or incarcerated/returning citizens
Maximum grant for computer equipment: $65,000
Maximum grant for internet service subscription: $10,000
Covers up to 100% of eligible project costs
Must have Federal EIN Number, UEI Number, and DUNS Number (if applicable)
Must provide IRS W-9 Form and Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
501(c) documentation required for nonprofit organizations
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2026
Majority of covered population must be one or more of: individuals with disabilities, individuals without permanent residence (homeless/unhoused), incarcerated or returning citizens, or veterans
Marketing and outreach limited to 10% of total project budget
Operational expenses limited to 15% of total project budget
Administrative expenses limited to 15% of total project budget
All federal rules regarding ARPA funding must be adhered to
Successful applicants must execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining obligations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the MD-CLP Application Form in its entirety with all required information including applicant information, budget request, and project information. 2. Prepare a Written Executive Summary and Scope of Work including timeline describing the project's purpose, covered populations served, needs of populations, and how funding will advance digital equity. 3. Discuss potential barriers to project implementation. 4. Provide a list of community partners and describe their involvement in lab development or digital inclusion support. 5. Describe intended outcomes and metrics, including how success will be measured. 6. Submit a Statement of Experience describing demonstrated capability and experience relevant to the proposed project, including principal employees' relevant work experience. 7. Provide a project timeline with estimated key milestones. 8. Submit a detailed, itemized project budget broken down by categories: Operations (payroll, supplies, materials), Contracted Services, Travel (must be related to program deployment), and other funding sources with anticipated sources. 9. Attach required documentation: IRS W-9 Form, Certificate of Good Standing, 501(c) documents for nonprofits, proof of nonprofit status or local jurisdiction documentation, letters of support, and certification agreeing to comply with all grant terms and reporting requirements. 10. Submit application by November 29, 2024 at 11:59 PM ET via email to osb.de@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Computer Labs Program Application – [Organizational Applicant Name]', or by mail to Ronnie Hammond, Office of Statewide Broadband, Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706, or by hand delivery between 8:00 AM and 4:00 PM ET (except weekends and state/federal holidays). Paper applications must show proof of mailing with dated USPS postmark, dated USPS mail receipt, or commercial carrier shipping label dated on or before deadline. 11. Technical assistance available through November 22, 2024 by request.

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY23 Network Infrastructure Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to construct new broadband networks to serve unserved households and businesses in underserved areas of Maryland. The program utilizes $95 million in Federal Coronavirus Capital Projects Funding (ARPA) to support broadband infrastructure expansion in areas where broadband service does not currently exist.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $800,000 and $4,500,000 covering 70% to 90% of eligible capital construction costs for new broadband network deployment. Match requirements vary based on premise density: Wired projects require 10% match for fewer than 8 premises per mile, 20% for 8-14 premises per mile, or 30% for 15+ premises per mile. Wireless projects require 10% match for fewer than 40 premises per tower, 20% for 40-69 premises per tower, or 30% for 70+ premises per tower. Match must be in cash and available upon execution of grant agreement. Exceptions allow federal funds or Maryland Broadband Cooperative backhaul costs (up to 3 years) to count as match. Tower construction/improvements may be treated as match but not as grant-eligible expenses. Grant funds must be expended by August 31, 2026, with at least 50% expended by the second anniversary of the agreement effective date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland local jurisdictions, internet service provider partners, cooperatives, private corporations, and limited liability companies (for-profit or non-profit) seeking to construct new broadband networks for unserved areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband network infrastructure including: outside plant (fiber, coaxial, copper); last mile and middle mile infrastructure; electronic equipment (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radios, antennas, equipment cabinets/shelters); and customer drops. Funds may serve residents, businesses, and anchor institutions at the Broadband Grant Speed of 100 Mbps download/100 Mbps upload (or 100 Mbps down/20 Mbps up if scalable and certified necessary due to geography, topography, or cost).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland service. Eligible areas must have no existing Broadband Service (defined as service at 100 Mbps download/20 Mbps upload). Areas that have previously received state broadband grant funding are ineligible. The Proposed Funded Service Area (PFSA) may span single or multiple jurisdictions but must be entirely within eligible unserved areas and need not be contiguous.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local jurisdiction, incorporated organization recognized as a partner by local jurisdiction, or other legal entity (cooperative, private corporation, limited liability company) organized for-profit or non-profit and recognized as a partner by local jurisdiction
Applicant may not be an individual or partnership
Applicant must have legal capacity and authority to own and operate broadband facilities and enter into contracts
Applicant must demonstrate legal existence and good standing with State of Maryland
All applicants must have a Unique Entity ID from SAM.gov
Applicant must attach current IRS Form W-9
Grant request minimum: $800,000; maximum: $4,500,000
Must serve entirely unserved areas with no existing Broadband Service (100 Mbps down/20 Mbps up)
Must serve all unserved premises in the proposed funded service area at Broadband Grant Speed or reduced speed (if certified and approved)
Minimum network requirement: 100 Mbps download/100 Mbps upload with maximum 50 millisecond latency (or 100 Mbps down/20 Mbps up if scalable and certified due to geography, topography, or cost)
All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated
Match funds must be cash and available at time of award (unless federal funds or MBDC backhaul exception applies)
Project must not supplant previously awarded federal funds for the same PFSA
If partnering with another entity to operate system, draft partnership agreement with financial terms must be included
Project commencement required by September 1, 2023
Project completion required by August 31, 2026
At least 50% of grant funds must be expended by second anniversary of agreement effective date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a complete FY23 Network Infrastructure Grant Application Package including: (1) Completed Broadband Grant Application Form (Schedule A-1) with signatures; (2) IRS Form W-9; (3) Evidence of legal existence and good standing; (4) Partnership documentation if applicable; (5) Executive Summary of the Project covering project description, benefits, applicant history, and partnership details; (6) Scoring Criteria Documentation; (7) System Design with network diagram; (8) Service Area Map (.shp or .kml/.kmz file) and Demographics; (9) Scope of Work including construction milestones and project budget; (10) Financial Information including historical and pro forma financial statements with assumptions; (11) Statement of Experience; and (12) Evidence of funding commitments. Applications must be submitted by December 5, 2022 at 11:59 PM ET via: (a) Postmarked/shipped paper copy with original signatures plus electronic version on USB flash drive to Kenrick M. Gordon, Director, Office of Statewide Broadband, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706; or (b) Email to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Network Infrastructure Grant Application – [company name]'. Technical assistance available upon request prior to November 18, 2022. Applicants may request clarification information after submission.

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY24 Network Infrastructure Grant Program – Smith Island (specialized geographic program)
structured_extraction.program_description: A specialized grant program that provides funding to construct new broadband networks to serve unserved households on Smith Island, Maryland. The program offers grants up to 90% of capital construction costs for broadband infrastructure deployment to deliver service at 100 Mbps download/100 Mbps upload speeds (or reduced speeds in certain circumstances) to all unserved premises on Smith Island.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $1,000,000 to $3,000,000, with the program providing up to 90% of eligible capital construction costs for broadband infrastructure necessary to bring service to all locations on Smith Island. Applicants must provide a minimum cash match of 10% of total construction cost (11.11% of requested grant amount). Grant funds support capital expenses including outside plant construction (fiber optic cabling, microwave equipment, last mile and middle mile infrastructure), electronic equipment (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, wireless radios, antennas, equipment shelters), and other capital costs directly necessary to provide broadband service. Operating expenses and equipment beyond the ONT or fixed wireless antenna are not eligible. Exceptions to match requirements may apply for federal funding, Maryland Broadband Cooperative backhaul services (up to 3 years of costs), and tower construction/structural improvements. All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, incorporated organizations recognized as partners by local jurisdictions, cooperatives, private corporations, and limited liability companies (for-profit or non-profit) seeking to construct new broadband networks on Smith Island to serve unserved residents and businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband network infrastructure including outside plant (fiber, coaxial, copper cabling), electronic equipment (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, wireless radios, antennas, equipment shelters), middle mile infrastructure directly necessary to provide service to end users, and other capital expenses directly necessary to provide broadband service at minimum speeds of 100 Mbps download/100 Mbps upload (or approved reduced speeds that are scalable to 100x100). Costs must be capitalized with final assets owned by applicant. Ineligible uses include duplication of existing broadband service, operating expenses, telephone/video service expenses not necessary for broadband delivery, tower/land/building purchases or renovations, and customer premise equipment beyond the ONT or fixed wireless antenna.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Smith Island, Somerset County, Maryland. The Identified Service Area (ISA) includes all locations on Smith Island where broadband service does not currently exist at 100 Mbps download/20 Mbps upload speeds. Latitude/longitude coordinates for each location requiring service are provided in program documentation.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local jurisdiction, incorporated organization recognized as a partner by the local jurisdiction, cooperative legally formed in Maryland and recognized as a partner, limited liability company recognized as a partner by the local jurisdiction, or other legal entity (excluding individuals and partnerships)

Applicant must be legally organized and have legal capacity and authority to own and operate broadband facilities, enter into contracts, and comply with applicable federal and state statutes and regulations

Applicant must demonstrate good standing with the State of Maryland and legal existence (verified through Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation corporate information or Maryland Manual On-Line for jurisdictions)
Applicant must have a DUNS Number and Unique Entity ID from SAM.gov
Applicant must submit current IRS Form W-9

Local jurisdiction partnerships require a letter from sponsoring jurisdiction acknowledging partnership and documenting participation and support; documentation required from each local jurisdiction if multiple are involved
Project must serve entire Identified Service Area where broadband service does not currently exist, verified by OSB prior to award

Project must provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload with maximum 50 millisecond latency at served subscribers' location, or if certified circumstances prevent this, minimum 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload that is scalable to 100x100 based on future technology advances
Minimum grant request is $1,000,000; maximum grant request is $3,000,000

Applicant must provide matching funds of minimum 10% of total construction cost (11.11% of requested grant amount) in the form of available cash at time of award, except for approved exceptions (federal funding, MBDC backhaul services up to 3 years, tower construction/improvements)
Matching funds must be cash and cannot be used for operational costs; in-kind contributions, manufacturer discounts, and non-cash items are ineligible as match
All grant eligible capital expenditures must be for new, non-depreciated items
Purchase or construction of towers, land, buildings, or building renovations are not allowable as grant expenses (tower construction may be match)
Laptops, handsets, tablets, and similar customer devices are not eligible expenses
If applicant seeks to partner with another entity to operate the system, a draft or final agreement must be provided addressing specific financial terms and identifying partner qualifications
All equipment and materials purchased must be new and non-depreciated
Work performed prior to application submission is not eligible for funding
Project must commence by September 1, 2024 and be completed by August 31, 2027
If other federal funds have been awarded for broadband construction within the ISA, grant funds may only supplement (not supplant) those federal funds
Applicant must have not been debarred by any federal, state, or local government entity in past four years and is not subject to civil claims for non-payment of $30,000 or more
Prior to commencement of project, applicant must obtain all federal, state, and local government approvals, permits, and licenses required

Applicant must comply with all applicable laws and regulations, including Title VI and VII of Civil Rights Act of 1964, Title 20 of State Government Article, Minority Business Enterprise Program requirements, Drug and Alcohol Free Workplaces requirements, and Americans with Disabilities Act
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted by 11:59pm ET on January 31, 2024 in one of three ways: (1) Postmarked or shipped paper copy with original signatures and electronic version on USB Flash Drive sent to Kenrick M. Gordon, P.E., Director, Office of Statewide Broadband, DHCD, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706 (paper must show proof of USPS postmark, mail receipt, or dated shipping label from commercial carrier); (2) Electronic submission via email to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Network Infrastructure Grant Application – Smith Island – your company name' with files attached as zipped file (files may be split into multiple emails if too large, labeled '1 of 2', '2 of 2', etc.); (3) Applicants late submitting applications will be notified applications will not be considered and will be returned. Prior to official submission, applicants may request technical assistance or application guidance from OSB prior to January 19, 2024. Complete application must include: Broadband Grant Application Form (Schedule A-1), IRS Form W-9, evidence of good standing/legal existence/jurisdictional partnership, Executive Summary covering project description/ISA/applicant description/total costs/system overview, Scoring Criteria Documentation, System Design with network diagram, Scope of Work with construction build-out/project milestones and project budget, Service Area Demographics, Financial Information and Sustainability with historical financial statements and pro forma financial statement (Schedule G-1) with assumptions (Schedule G-2), Statement of Experience, and evidence of funding commitments from other sources. All documents should be in PDF format except where specific file formats are called out; files should be clearly named. Applications deemed incomplete may be rejected.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MD-GAPS Connected Communities Grant Program assists local jurisdictions, community-based organizations, nonprofits, anchor institutions, and local governments in creating Gap Networks and Community Networks designed to address broadband affordability challenges for low to moderate income households. The program helps communities close existing digital divides and improve broadband access, adoption, and utilization for covered populations including individuals with household income at or below 150 percent of the federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, and members of racial or ethnic minority groups. Total program funding of $5 million is available statewide. Funding source is the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA), Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds administered by the US Treasury.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of $25,000 to $250,000 covering up to 100% of eligible project costs for construction, deployment, expansion, or continuation of community-based gap networks and community networks. Funds support equipment, instrumentation, networking capability, hardware and software, and digital network technology to deliver broadband services to covered populations at low or no cost. Total program funding of $5 million is available. Projects must reliably provide a minimum of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with limited exceptions. The OSB will support projects providing 100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up if the network is scalable to 100 Mbps symmetrical speeds based on future technology advances. Maximum latency of 50 milliseconds measured at served subscribers' location is required. While not required, applicants are highly encouraged to identify other funding sources to leverage the available grant funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities), foundations, corporations, institutions, associations, coalitions that are 501(c)(3) non-profits, community-based anchor institutions, and other community-based organizations providing services in Maryland. Programs serve covered populations including individuals with household income at or below 150 percent of the federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers including English learners and individuals with low levels of literacy, and individuals who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment, instrumentation, networking capability, hardware and software, and digital network technology to deliver broadband services to covered populations at low or no cost. Eligible uses include: building and deploying new gap networks or community networks at required speeds; upgrading or expanding existing networks; operating and maintaining networks; acquiring electronics necessary to deliver service such as Optical Line Terminals (OLTs), Optical Network Terminals (ONTs), routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennas, access points, modems, and equipment shelters. Projects must reliably provide a minimum of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with limited exceptions as identified in the application guide. Travel costs related to program deployment are eligible. Budget categories include Operations (equipment, payroll, supplies, materials), Contracted Services (payments to independent contractors, external organizations), and Travel.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all Maryland communities. An eligible project area is identified as having a need for additional broadband investment, including lack of access to a connection that reliably meets or exceeds symmetrical 100 Mbps download and upload speeds, lack of affordable access to broadband service, or lack of reliable broadband.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government (counties and municipalities), 501(c)(3) non-profit, community-based anchor institution, or other community-based organization
Applicant must be registered and, if applicable, in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation

Project must serve covered populations (individuals with household income at or below 150 percent of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers including English learners and individuals with low levels of literacy, or members of racial or ethnic minority groups)

Project must be designed to reliably provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds at served subscribers' location (exceptions as identified in application guide)
Minimum grant amount: $25,000; Maximum grant amount: $250,000
Grant covers up to 100% of eligible project costs
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023
Application must be fully complete at submission to be considered for funding; any missing information may result in ineligibility
Applicant must provide IRS Determination Letter of nonprofit status (if applicable)
Applicant must provide online verification of Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Applicant must provide IRS Form W-9
Applicant must provide Dun & Bradstreet DUNS Number
Technology neutral requirement: any technology capable of meeting speed and latency requirements is permissible
Successful applicants will be required to execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining obligations of the awardee and State to the Project
All federal rules regarding ARPA funding must be adhered to by the applicant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicant must submit a completed and signed application form with all required attachments via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov (subject line: 'MD-GAPS: Name of Applying Organization') by March 31, 2022. Application must be fully complete at submission. Use the provided MD-GAPS Application Guide and Form. The application must include: (1) Applicant Information section with legal name, Federal EIN Number, DUNS Number, address, and contact information; (2) Project Information section identifying funding sources (applicant, local jurisdiction, state request, and other sources) and proposed project area; (3) Project Summary addressing all required items including Executive Summary, Statement of Experience, Network Design, Community Profile, Subscriber Cost (if applicable), Potential Barriers, Partners and Local Engagement Plan, Intended Outcomes and Sustainability (including metrics and four-year sustainability plan), Implementation Schedule with key milestones, and Funding Scope and Budget; (4) Supporting documents including Project Summary, Project Budget (categorized by Operations, Contracted Services, Travel, and other funding sources), Federal Form W-9, and Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. The OSB intends to award funds beginning in May 2022. Successful applicants will be chosen based on qualifications, evaluation of responses, and possible interviews. The OSB reserves the right to conduct investigations, discussions, and negotiations as deemed necessary. No reimbursement will be made for costs incurred in responding to the RFA.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides new, internet-enabled devices to eligible households to support digital equity and inclusion efforts, particularly for families at greatest economic need. The program procures approximately 145,000 HP Chromebook 14 G7 or similar devices for distribution by county and municipal governments.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of new HP Chromebook 14 G7 (or similar) internet-enabled devices with a minimum 13-inch screen, Chrome OS, SD card reader, dual-band Wi-Fi, 2 USB ports, and one-year manufacturer warranty to county and municipal governments for distribution to eligible households. Total of approximately 145,000 devices procured over six months. A stipend of $6 per device is provided to help offset storage, distribution venue, and personnel costs associated with distribution. Eligible households are those with income at or below 200% of Federal Poverty Guidelines or enrolled in qualifying assistance programs (ACP, SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, SSI, FPHA, Veterans benefits, free/reduced school lunch, or recipients of Federal Pell Grants). One device per household address maximum. Devices must be distributed within six months from delivery of first allotment; undistributed devices must be returned at awardee's expense.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal governments distributing devices to eligible households; households with income at or below 200% of Federal Poverty Guidelines or enrolled in qualifying government assistance programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internet-enabled devices for eligible households to improve digital access and equity; one device per household address maximum. Stipend funds may be used for: cost of securing devices in storage, cost of securing devices during distribution, cost of distribution venue, and personnel costs associated with distribution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all Maryland counties and municipalities. Eligible distribution partners include libraries/library systems, local education agencies, municipalities, nonprofit 501(c) entities providing services in Maryland, and community-based anchor institutions.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local jurisdiction (county or incorporated municipality) with legal existence per Maryland Manual On-Line

Eligible households must have income at or below 200% of Federal Poverty Guidelines OR be enrolled in ACP, SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, SSI, FPHA, Veterans benefits, free/reduced school lunch program, or recipients of Federal Pell Grants
One device per household address maximum (or recognized MDU unit)
Applicant must be registered in System for Award Management (SAM.gov) and provide valid unique entity identifier before submitting application
Applicant must provide Federal EIN Number and DUNS number
Applicant must develop an eligibility verification process and maintain documentation
Applicant must develop an outreach program to inform eligible community of program terms, location, and times of distribution
Devices must be stored in a secure facility with loading/unloading capabilities for potential multiple shipments
Devices must be inspected upon receipt and OSB notified immediately of any damage
Distribution must be completed within six months from delivery of first device shipment
Devices must be tracked using Department Device Tracking Portal which requires internet connectivity at distribution points
If both municipality and county apply, entities must coordinate efforts to ensure complementary and not conflicting distribution
Jurisdiction must be able to provide household-level data to OSB upon request showing verification documentation reviewed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted electronically to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with subject line "Maryland Connected Devices Program Application – your jurisdictional name" or by USPS/commercial carrier postmarked by September 29, 2023, 11:59pm ET to: Ronnie Hammond, Office of Statewide Broadband, Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Paper submissions must include proof of mailing (USPS postmark, USPS receipt, or dated shipping label). Application packet must include: completed Application Form with EIN, DUNS, SAM.gov unique identifier, partnership information, and receiver details; Project Narrative (executive summary not to exceed 2 pages addressing covered population, community problems, how devices will help, and income/eligibility restrictions); Scope of Work detailing partnerships, data collection, storage, distribution method, eligibility verification, and methodology to ensure one device per household; Project Schedule with milestones for outreach start, distribution start, distribution events, and distribution end; Monthly Device Delivery Request schedule; and Federal Form W-9. Technical assistance available prior to September 22, 2023. Round 1 awarded 91,300 devices. Round 2 provides remaining devices, prioritizing new eligible applicants over returning applicants. If total requests exceed available devices, equal percentage reduction applied across all applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that furthers Maryland's digital inclusion efforts by providing funding to local jurisdictions, nonprofit organizations, and community-based anchor institutions for digital inclusion planning and implementation projects. The program helps residents gain access to high-speed internet, expand digital literacy, and develop skills for using broadband and digital technologies, with a focus on advancing digital equity and technology access for covered populations across all Maryland communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two funding tracks: Digital Inclusion Planning grants covering up to 50% of plan costs (minimum $5,000, maximum $30,000) and Digital Inclusion Implementation grants covering up to 100% of implementation costs (minimum $10,000, maximum $75,000). Grant amounts may be reduced based on impact and ability to deploy funds responsibly. Total program funding of $2 million available. Funded through American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds. Grant funds may be used for developing digital inclusion plans; implementing digital inclusion activities; facilitating broadband adoption for educational and employment opportunities; implementing training programs covering basic, advanced, and applied skills or workforce development programs; constructing, upgrading, expanding, or operating public access computing centers for covered populations through community anchor institutions; researching and identifying populations with low adoption rates for home internet and computers; or furthering other qualifying digital inclusion or equity goals. Grant funds cannot be used for construction of broadband infrastructure.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities), non-profit IRS-approved 501(c) entities providing services in Maryland, and community-based anchor institutions serving covered populations including individuals below 150% of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers or low literacy, individuals from racial or ethnic minority groups, and individuals in rural areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing digital inclusion plans; implementing digital inclusion activities; facilitating broadband adoption by covered populations for educational and employment opportunities; implementing training programs covering basic, advanced, and applied skills or workforce development programs; constructing, upgrading, expanding, or operating public access computing centers for covered populations through community anchor institutions; researching and identifying populations with low adoption rates for home internet and computers; furthering other qualifying digital inclusion or equity goals. Grant funds may not be used for construction of broadband infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. The grant program can serve all communities in Maryland, though covered populations most in need receive priority. Covered populations include: individuals living in households with income less than or equal to 150 percent of federal poverty level; aging individuals; individuals with disabilities; individuals with language barriers including English learners and those with low literacy levels; individuals who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups; and individuals who primarily reside in rural areas.
requirements_list: Be a local government (counties or municipalities), a non-profit IRS-approved 501(c) entity providing services within Maryland, or a community-based anchor institution
Submit fully complete applications at submission time
Provide executive summary including project overview, population needs, potential barriers, partners, engagement plan, intended outcomes, metrics, and statement of experience
Provide funding scope and budget with categories for operations, contracted services, travel, and other funding sources
Submit completed and signed application form
Submit IRS Determination Letter of nonprofit status if applicable
Submit online verification of Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Submit IRS W-9 Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification
Submit Dun and Bradstreet DUNS Number for organization
Planning grants: maximum $30,000, minimum $5,000; covers up to 50% of costs
Implementation grants: maximum $75,000, minimum $10,000; covers up to 100% of costs
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023
All awardees must execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining obligations of the awardee and State to the Project
Applicants should identify other funding sources to leverage available grant funding where possible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the MD-DIG Application Form in its entirety with all required information. Prepare an executive summary addressing project overview, population needs, potential barriers, community partners and local engagement, intended outcomes and metrics, and statement of experience. Develop a simple budget showing planned spending in categories: Operations (payroll, supplies, materials); Contracted services (payments to independent contractors, external organizations); Travel (related to program deployment); and any other funding sources. Gather all required attachments: signed application form, IRS W-9 Form, IRS nonprofit determination letter if applicable, Certificate of Good Standing verification, and Dun and Bradstreet DUNS Number. Submit all materials via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov with subject line 'MD-DIG: Name of Applying Organization' by March 31, 2022. Selected applicants may be chosen based on qualifications, evaluation of responses, and possible interviews. Successful applicants will be notified and awards are expected to begin in May 2022.

structured_extraction.program_name: EmPOWER Maryland Limited Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The EmPOWER Maryland Limited Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP) helps limited income households reduce energy use by providing free installation of energy efficiency materials and equipment in their homes. The program includes energy audits, weatherization improvements such as insulation in attics, floors, and walls, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and safety repairs, refrigerator retrofits where applicable, and health and safety items. All work and materials are provided at no charge to eligible households. The program aims to lower monthly utility bills, increase comfort, and improve indoor air quality and family health. Eligible households must be located in EmPOWER utility service territories and meet income qualifications. Follow-up evaluations are conducted to ensure homes operate more efficiently after improvements are made.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free installation of energy efficiency and conservation upgrades including insulation in attic, floors and walls; hot water system improvements; lighting retrofits; furnace cleaning, tuning and safety repairs; refrigerator retrofit if applicable; and health and safety items. All work and materials are provided at no charge to eligible households. Households are screened for this program upon completion of a one-stop-shop energy programs application or through the Department of Human Services Energy Assistance application. Eligible households must have household income at or below 250% of federal poverty level. Automatically income-eligible if currently participating in OHEP Utility Bill Pay Assistance, SNAP, TANF, SSI, HUD housing assistance programs, Fuel Fund Assistance, DHCD Rehab Programs, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, Medicaid, MEA Energy Equity Grant, or MEEHA. The program is delivered through energy audits conducted by local agencies, with contractors then performing recommended improvements and follow-up evaluations to ensure efficiency gains.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Limited income homeowners and renters with utility accounts through BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas who meet income qualifications based on household size (at or below 250% of the federal poverty level).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency and weatherization improvements to reduce household energy use and lower monthly utility bills, including insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and safety repairs, refrigerator retrofits, and health and safety items.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available statewide in Maryland to households with utility accounts through six participating EmPOWER utility companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, and Washington Gas. Coverage applies wherever these utilities operate in Maryland.
requirements_list: Household income must be at or below 250% of federal poverty level based on household size (ranging from $72,950 for single person to $165,050 for household of 10, with $13,750 added for each additional person beyond 10)
Must be a customer of one of six participating EmPOWER utility companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas

Automatically income-eligible if currently participating in OHEP Utility Bill Pay Assistance, SNAP, TANF, SSI, HUD housing assistance programs, Fuel Fund Assistance, DHCD Rehab Programs, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, Medicaid, MEA Energy Equity Grant, or MEEHA
Must be located in an EmPOWER utility service territory
Income eligibility required as determined by the Maryland Department of Housing & Community Development
Must have power to the home
Application must include copy of most recent electric utility bill for one of the six participating utilities
Must provide documentation of benefits if claiming automatic income eligibility
Households may be prioritized if they have documented medical conditions requiring functioning heating, cooling, or water heating systems (physician's letter required)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply through one of two pathways: (1) Quick Application - Complete an online or paper energy programs application with Client Information, Household Income Information, Energy Consent Form, and most recent electric utility bill. This application is available in English and Spanish. (2) Standard Application - For those applying for repair assistance or heating/cooling crisis aid, submit complete application including Client Information, Household Information, Energy Consent Form, most recent electric utility bill, proof of last 30 days GROSS household income, copy of Social Security cards for all household members, copy of Photo ID for applicant, and Zero Income Form for any household member 18+ claiming no income. For mobile home residents, provide copy of title or bill of sale. If approved, a local agency will contact you to schedule a home energy audit. After the audit, a contractor will perform recommended improvements. A follow-up evaluation ensures the home is operating more efficiently. Submit applications to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Attn: Weatherization, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Alternatively, apply for Energy Assistance through the Department of Human Services and be screened for this program and others. If currently approved for Energy Assistance payments from the Maryland Department of Human Services, you may contact the intake line directly at 1-855-583-8976.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides income-eligible homeowners and single-family renters with energy-saving upgrades at no cost.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible homeowners and single-family renters
