structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Income eligibility

structured_extraction.program_name: FY24 Home Stretch - Difficult to Serve Properties Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to local county jurisdictions to assist with capital construction costs for broadband service installation to premises that are difficult to serve due to remoteness, distance from existing broadband infrastructure, or other geographic challenges. The program utilizes Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund (CPF) administered by the U.S. Treasury to bring high-speed internet access to unserved difficult-to-reach premises.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $1,100,000 per eligible county applicant for capital construction costs of broadband service installation to difficult-to-serve locations. Maximum funding per individual location is $8,000. County must provide 25% cash match of eligible project costs. Match can be contributed by the local jurisdiction, ISP partner, property owner, or combination of these sources. Grant funds support new, non-depreciated capital assets including construction of service delivery infrastructure, equipment, and materials necessary to serve unserved difficult-to-serve premises. Projects must provide minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds (or 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload with certification and scalability commitment) with maximum 50 milliseconds latency.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County jurisdictions with ISP partners seeking to provide broadband service to unserved difficult-to-serve premises in their jurisdiction
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for broadband service installation including: construction of facilities to deploy service, optical network terminals, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, access points, modems, equipment shelters, and other electronics necessary to deliver broadband service to difficult-to-serve premises. Not eligible: middle mile infrastructure, duplication of existing service, telephone or video service expenses, land or tower purchases, building construction or renovations, or operating expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all Maryland county jurisdictions eligible. Funded projects must connect unserved difficult-to-serve premises to existing broadband networks.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local county jurisdiction with an established partnership with one or more ISP partner(s)
All partnering ISPs must participate in the federal Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP)
Unserved premises must lack terrestrial fixed internet service at 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload speeds with latency below 50 milliseconds
Network must provide minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds (or 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload with proper certification) with maximum 50 milliseconds latency
County must provide 25% cash match of eligible project costs (in-kind matches not acceptable)
Maximum grant funding per location: $8,000
Maximum grant funding per applicant: $1,100,000
Match must be available for each reimbursement request

Jurisdiction must develop jurisdictional-specific funding program outlining: end user selection process, assistance for low-income users, ISP billing methods, acceptable ISP costs, ACP assistance and promotion, and program outreach component
Jurisdiction must address how financially distressed property owners will be treated in program plan
ISPs must promote ACP and provide assistance to subscribers wishing to utilize the program
All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2025
No duplication of funding from other federal or state sources for same location
Applicant responsible for all non-capital expenses related to state and federal reporting and ongoing administrative costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. County jurisdiction identifies ISP partner(s) and establishes partnership prior to application. 2. Complete FY24 Connect Maryland-Broadband for Difficult to Serve Premises Grant Application Form (fillable PDF available). 3. Prepare comprehensive response addressing: Executive Summary (community needs and project benefits), Application Partnership (ISP partner description and support), Experience (senior team qualifications from both applicant and ISP partner), Network Discussion (technology, speeds, capabilities), Subscriber Profile (unserved locations and demographics), Subscriber Costs and Limitations (ISP service options and pricing), Budget (capital construction cost estimates), Program Overview (detailed program design), Eligible/Ineligible Grant Purposes, and Schedule (implementation timeline). 4. Submit one electronic PDF copy with all items combined into one zip file to osb.md@maryland.gov with subject line including 'Difficult to Serve Premises Grant Application' and local county jurisdiction name by December 22, 2023. 5. Applications scored on 45-point maximum based on need assessment, match contribution source and percentage, network delivery speed, and subscriber options. 6. Awards anticipated February 2024 with project completion deadline December 31, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program designed to help Housing Voucher participants achieve higher education, improve employment status, and guide them toward self-sufficiency. The program evaluates skills and determines family needs, providing guidance, training, and support services including financial literacy, job training, childcare assistance, and other instruments to help participants gain success in the workforce and achieve economic independence.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides guidance, training, and support to help Housing Voucher participants pursue higher education, improve their employment prospects, and work toward self-sufficiency. Services include financial literacy training, job training, childcare support, education counseling, employment counseling, health services information, homeownership guidance, job retention support, and transportation assistance. Participants receive an interest-bearing FSS escrow account where increased rent portions from earned income are credited monthly in accordance with HUD guidelines. Upon successful completion of contract goals (becoming free of TANF benefits or reaching 30% of adjusted income exceeding HUD fair market rent while maintaining suitable employment), participants receive all funds in the escrow account plus accrued interest, which are nontaxable per IRS ruling.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Housing Voucher participants seeking to achieve self-sufficiency and economic independence
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for higher education, employment improvement, and self-sufficiency services including educational guidance, employment counseling, financial literacy training, job training, childcare assistance, health services, homeownership preparation, job retention, and transportation support. Escrow account funds can be used for program-related expenses such as vehicle repair or testing fees, or after contract completion for any purpose including down payment on a home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cambridge, Maryland and the Midshore region; administered through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Eastern Shore Regional Office located at 411 Dorchester Ave, Suite 202, Cambridge, Maryland 21613
requirements_list: Must be a Housing Voucher participant
Head of household must complete and submit an application
Must sign a Contract of Participation
Must complete a Needs Assessment outlining rights, goals, and responsibilities
Must establish goals including obtaining employment and becoming free of TANF benefits (social security and assistance for disabled family members do not count toward TANF requirement)
Contract term is 5 years, extendable for additional 2 years with good cause
Participants can graduate early if goals are completed before allotted time
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DHCD at (410) 901-4080, email fss.dhcd@maryland.gov, visit dhcd.maryland.gov/CambridgeCEC, or ask your case manager at any meeting or redetermination. You will meet with an FSS coordinator who will review your family's strengths, barriers, and goals. You will create an individual family plan with required long-term goals of obtaining employment and being free of temporary cash assistance. Complete an online form at dhcd.wufoo.com/forms/family-selfsufficiency-program for more information. The head of household then signs a Contract of Participation, and the applicant and coordinator complete a Needs Assessment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program created to help homeowners buy out (redeem) ground leases. Ground leases are long-term leases (usually 99 years) that are renewable forever and require periodic ground rent payments from the tenant to the ground lease holder.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $3,500 (including transactional costs of up to $1,000) to homeowners to redeem (buy out) ground leases at 0% interest over 30 years. The redemption amount is calculated by dividing the annual ground rent fee by a capitalization rate based on when the ground lease was established (0.04 for leases April 8, 1884 to April 5, 1888; 0.06 for leases April 6, 1888 to July 1, 1982; 0.12 for leases July 2, 1982 or later). A lien is recorded against the property for the loan amount. The program cannot provide grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners with ground leases who want to redeem (buy out) their leases. Applicants must own the subject property, occupy it as their principal residence, and meet household income limits established for the program (based on 80% of statewide median income by household size).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To redeem (buy out) ground leases, including transactional costs associated with title search and loan closing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Ground rents are most prevalent in Baltimore City but are held in some other counties as well.
requirements_list: Must own the subject property
Must occupy the property as principal residence
Must meet household income limits based on 80% of statewide median income (varies by household size and region)
Must provide proof of ownership (copy of deed)
Must provide evidence of ground rent (copy of recorded document with ground rent)

Must provide documentation of household income (recent pay stubs, 2 years of federal tax returns and W-2 statements or signed Affidavit of Tax Filing Status, award letters for pension or public assistance income)
Must provide mortgage verification form or current mortgage statement if applicable
Must provide copy of homeowners insurance and flood insurance policies verifying coverage and premium
Must provide copy of most recent county and local property tax bill
Must provide copy of most recent bank statements (all pages)
Must provide copy of most recent Ground Rent Billing statement
If named on deed but does not occupy property, must provide proof of residence elsewhere (driver's license, utility bill, notarized statement, or other evidence)
Can apply even if behind in paying ground rent
For ground leases established before April 9, 1884, may be subject to irredeemability provisions unless notice was not filed or has lapsed by December 31, 2010
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicant must complete a DHCD Ground Rent Redemption Loan application and provide evidence of ownership and ground rent documentation, along with household income verification. Submit the completed application with all required documentation to Special Loan Programs. The borrower will choose any qualified title company to conduct the title search and loan closing. Contact Special Loan Programs at (301) 429-7409, (844) 369-4150, or DHCD.SpecialLoans@maryland.gov for more information or assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Group Home Program helps individuals, qualified limited partnerships, and nonprofit organizations construct, acquire, or acquire and modify existing housing to serve as group homes or assisted living units for people with special housing needs. The program also refinances mortgages on existing group homes. Funding comes from state Group Home Financing Program funds and proceeds from tax exempt mortgage revenue bonds under the Special Housing Opportunities Program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans to finance newly constructed buildings, acquisition or acquisition and rehabilitation of existing residential buildings, or refinance mortgages on existing group homes. Interest rates range from 0 to 7 percent depending on the source of funds and project cash flow. Maximum term is generally 30 years, though may extend to 40 years. The construction term may not exceed one year. Maximum loan amounts are $125,000 per bedroom (including caretaker bedrooms), with a 15% increase permitted in high housing cost areas (Montgomery, Prince George's, and Howard Counties). Maximum loan amounts cannot exceed the appraised property value. Nonprofit sponsors must contribute 5 percent equity; individual sponsors must contribute 10 percent. Loans may be secured by either a first or second mortgage. Eligible costs include acquisition, closing costs, appraisal and inspection fees, modification costs, repair or replacement of major systems, accessibility modifications, lead paint abatement, general repairs and upgrades, and minor improvements to meet occupancy codes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, qualified limited partnerships, and nonprofit organizations that provide group homes to eligible residents with special housing needs, including developmentally or physically disabled, elderly, juveniles, and homeless persons.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction or acquisition of new housing or modification of existing housing to serve as group homes or assisted living units; refinancing mortgages on existing group homes; acquisition costs, closing costs, appraisal and inspection fees, repairs or replacement of major systems such as heating, roofing, electrical or plumbing, accessibility modifications, lead paint abatement, general repairs and upgrades, and minor improvements to bring property into compliance with occupancy codes. Group homes may dedicate up to 10 percent of building space to nonresidential uses offering goods or services that benefit lower-income or otherwise disadvantaged persons, if permitted by local zoning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in Maryland. Properties must be located in a Priority Funding Area for Special Housing Opportunities Program funding (unless an exceptional waiver is granted for existing construction). State Group Home Financing Program loans are not geographically limited. Priority Funding Area maps are available on the Department of Planning's website.
requirements_list: Applicants must be licensed by the appropriate Maryland licensing authority
Nonprofits must have 501(c)(3) IRS designation for Special Housing Opportunities Program funding
Property must be in good repair and comply with applicable state and local housing and occupancy codes, or be able to be made so with loan proceeds or other funds
Appraisal must be completed by an appraiser on the approved appraiser list; appraisals cannot be more than 120 days old at time of approval, or more than one year old at the Note date
Property must have a home inspection acceptable to the department and cannot be more than 120 days old at time of approval
All properties built prior to 1978 must have lead paint risk assessment prepared by certified and accredited lead paint testing company
Residents must be special needs groups such as developmentally or physically disabled, elderly, juveniles, or homeless
Sponsors must maintain 51 percent of all beds available for residents with incomes 60 percent or less of area median income
Nonprofit sponsors must contribute 5 percent equity towards the project
Individual sponsors must contribute 10 percent equity towards the project
Federal Funds Notice must be completed by borrower and executed by seller prior to entering binding sales contract
Property must meet local government zoning codes
Property must be located in Maryland
Eligible Sponsors must have a contract with a State agency or county government that provides operating income and/or grant funds for the project

For nonprofit organizations, the entity must be authorized to conduct business in Maryland, authorized to incur debt for special needs housing, have a purpose consistent with the proposed project, have an estimated life at least as long as the loan term, and have provisions prohibiting discrimination based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability or familial status
Sponsor must not have defaulted on a Department or other government loan
Sponsor must not be on the Department's or other government debarred list
Credit reports must demonstrate history of meeting both long- and short-term credit obligations
Personal financial statements required for individual sponsors and guarantors
For nonprofit sponsors, audited financial statements for prior three years required, along with previous quarter balance sheet and income statement if most recent audit is older than six months
Sponsors without prior group home experience may be approved if they can demonstrate capacity based on other business endeavors and prior satisfactory financial and credit management
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Special Loans Program at the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. An initial meeting with the GHFP Manager is encouraged for new sponsors to discuss the proposed project and review program requirements. Sponsors should submit a completed application form with all required supporting documentation to: Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, 369B, Lanham, Maryland 20706, ATTN: Group Home Financing Program. Upon receipt, the application will be date-stamped and assigned a case number. Within 30 days of receipt, applicants will receive an acknowledgement letter identifying any missing documentation, with generally 30 days allowed to submit missing items. The Department will obtain Dun & Bradstreet credit reports for organizations and consumer credit reports for individuals. The eligibility review will generally be completed within 90-120 days of receiving a complete application. Applicants must submit an appraisal from an approved appraiser, a home inspection, and a completed Federal Funds Notice. For projects requesting Special Housing Opportunities Program financing, contact the department to verify funds are available before submitting an application. The department will determine the most appropriate source of funds based on eligibility requirements and project underwriting. An application fee of $800 is required ($400 for department processing costs and $400 legal fee), paid at settlement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids Lead Initiative
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership initiative that helps families reduce lead exposure in homes built before 1978 by covering lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to keep lead paint properly sealed.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed for eligible families with children who have elevated blood lead levels.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children age 18 or younger living in Maryland who have elevated blood lead levels.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Maryland.
requirements_list: Child must be 18 years old or younger and live in Maryland
Child must have a recent blood lead test of 3.5 micrograms per deciliter or higher
Child must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid or Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP)
Child must spend 10 hours or more per week in the location where lead exposure occurred
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families should call the Environmental Health Help Line at 1-866-703-3266 or email mdh.healthyhomes@maryland.gov for more information and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to assist in digital equity and inclusion efforts by providing broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units in publicly owned low-income housing. The program aims to close the digital divide and ensure covered populations have access to reliable high-speed internet services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two rounds available. Round 1 (FY24): Grants between $500,000 and $9,000,000 covering 95% of eligible project costs with 5% match required. Expanded Round/Affordable Housing Round (FY24): Grants between $250,000 and $5,000,000 covering 95% of eligible project costs with 5% match required. Grants cover installation or extension of fiber optic facilities, installation of end user facilities including wiring and wireless access points, and educational/technical assistance outreach to support adoption. Engineering design services are eligible. Non-capital administrative costs capped at 1% of total project costs for Round 1; engagement-related costs capped at 3% of total project cost not to exceed $15,000. Match funds must be capital construction costs and can include other state or federal funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (county and municipal), housing authorities, nonprofit organizations, and internet service providers seeking to provide broadband to low-income public housing residents and municipally owned/nonprofit low-income multi-dwelling units
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units in publicly owned low-income housing; extension of fiber optic facilities; installation of wireless access points in public and common areas; community engagement and broadband adoption support including ACP registration assistance; broadband networking equipment, modems, switches, routers, firewalls; low voltage contracting for inside wiring and network infrastructure; engineering and design documentation; installation, provisioning, and configuration labor costs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all Maryland communities. Round 1 eligibility: publicly owned housing developments identified as having need for additional broadband investment. Expanded Round eligibility: municipally owned or nonprofit low-income multi-dwelling units.
requirements_list: Applicant must be owner of public housing (municipal, county, or nonprofit housing authority for Round 1; ISP must be existing Internet Service Provider for Expanded Round)
Must provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds at each dwelling unit
Projects must be able to achieve scalable minimum of 100 Mbps symmetrical for download and upload speeds based on future technology advances
Must provide broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units
Must install wireless access points in public and common areas that provide free internet service to residents
95% grant coverage with 5% cash match required (match can be state or federal funds)
Must commit to maintaining and securing project equipment and technology with hardware warranty and service agreement for at least 5 years after project completion
For Expanded Round: Must offer low-price option for low-income residents and affordable pricing for different tiers of speed starting at 100/20 Mbps
For Expanded Round: Must demonstrate financial stability and compliance with all federal, state, and local regulations including Treasury CPF rules
Property must remain affordable housing during 5-year maintenance period
All equipment purchased must be new and non-depreciated
Applicant must provide strong letter of support and commitment documentation

Applicant must identify covered populations: individuals with income ≤150% of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, English learners, individuals with low literacy, individuals who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit complete application package including: completed Application Form, Project Summary with Executive Summary, Statement of Experience, Community Profile, Network Design with diagrams, Project Schedule, Funding Scope and detailed line-item capital construction budget, Sustainability Plan, and supporting documentation. For Expanded Round: include Letter of Support from property owner, MDU prioritization information with physical assessment results, subscriber cost information, financial information and sustainability plan. Applicants must certify that information is true and correct and comply with all program requirements. For Round 1, applications were due December 22, 2023. For Expanded Round, applications are due January 31, 2025. Submit via email to osb.md@maryland.gov with project name and local jurisdiction in subject line. Include in submission: completed Application Form, IRS W-9, and all required documentation. Projects must demonstrate technical feasibility and financial sustainability. OSB may request revisions to address technical issues before final consideration.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide Maryland program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that provides federal and state funding and technical support to local Continuums of Care and Local Homeless Coalitions. The program coordinates funding and resources for service providers across the state, covering emergency solutions, rental assistance, emergency and transitional housing and services, homeless women's crisis shelter homes, service-linked housing, housing navigator and aftercare services, and homeless prevention efforts.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal and state funding and technical support are provided to local Continuums of Care and Local Homeless Coalitions throughout Maryland to coordinate and distribute resources for homeless service providers. Funded activities include emergency solutions, rental assistance, emergency and transitional housing and services, homeless women's crisis shelters, service-linked housing, and housing navigator and aftercare programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Continuums of Care and Local Homeless Coalitions that coordinate services for homeless populations statewide, as well as low-income individuals and families experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency solutions, rental assistance, emergency and transitional housing and services, homeless women's crisis shelter operations, service-linked housing, housing navigation and aftercare services, and coordination of homeless prevention resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland; funding is distributed to local Continuums of Care in each jurisdiction, including Harford County.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Funding is provided to local Continuums of Care and nonprofit providers to implement homelessness prevention and housing assistance programs. Local Continuums of Care coordinate funding and distribute resources to service providers across the state.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) WholeHome Critical Home Repairs Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps Maryland homeowners facing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic pay for critical repairs in their primary residences that could lead to displacement if not addressed. Repairs include heating/cooling systems, water heaters, electrical and plumbing repairs, roof repairs, mold remediation, lead paint and asbestos removal, and structural issues. Funding is limited and subject to availability.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Standard grant up to $10,000 per household for critical home repairs. No minimum grant amount. Exceptions may allow up to $15,000 for extenuating circumstances on a case-by-case basis with documented need. Grant funds are used to pay for critical home repairs performed by a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractor. Payment terms include options for either 33% deposit with 67% at completion, or 0% deposit with 100% at completion. This is one-time financial assistance per household. No reimbursement available for prior deposits or material purchases made by homeowners.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 2, 2026 (closed early because funds ran out)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners who experienced financial hardship after January 21, 2020, and have income at or below 150% of their county's Area Median Income, facing displacement due to critical home repair needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical home repairs in primary residences, including mold and mildew remediation, asbestos removal, non-functioning heating and cooling systems (no heat/no air), electrical repairs, plumbing and septic repairs, wells, roof repair or replacement, lead paint hazard reduction or elimination, structural and maintenance issues, and trip/slip safety issues. These are health and safety repairs only; remodeling and non-critical repairs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Applicants must reside in the primary residence and be named on the deed. Income limits are based on household size and county Area Median Income (150% AMI cap). If other persons are named on the deed but do not live at the property, they must provide proof of residence elsewhere.
requirements_list: Experienced financial hardship after January 21, 2020 (including hardships that began before January 21, 2020 but continued after that date)
Income at or below 150% of County Area Median Income
Must be a Maryland homeowner
Must reside in the primary residence
Must be named on the deed
Must provide at least one detailed estimate from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor dated within the last 60 days
Bid must include photographs documenting the critical repairs
Contractor must be currently licensed as a Maryland Home Improvement Contractor with appropriate trade license (MHIC, Electrical, Plumbing, HVAC, etc.)
Contractor must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Contractor must have active limited liability insurance with per occurrence limits equal to or greater than $1 million
Contractor must provide current Certificate of Liability Insurance (COI)
Contractor must provide Letter of Good Standing from State of Maryland
Contractor must provide completed and signed W-9 form
No minimum credit score required
Not available to renters or tenants
One-time financial assistance per household
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the WholeHome Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) grant application and submit with required documentation: (1) Income verification documents including two months of paystubs for employed household members, or for self-employed individuals two years of Federal Income Tax Returns, or current award letters and statements for Social Security/disability/pension/public assistance income, or a signed and notarized Zero Income Statement if no income; (2) Photo ID(s) for applicant and any co-applicant; (3) Documentation of home ownership and proof that anyone else named on the deed lives elsewhere; (4) At least one detailed estimate from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor dated within the past 60 days, not exceeding $10,000 total, including photographs and contractor contact information; (5) Completed Bid Cover Page for each contractor; (6) Contractor's current MHIC or appropriate trade license; (7) Certificate of Liability Insurance; (8) Letter of Good Standing; (9) Completed W-9 from contractor. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. Once approved, applicant must sign commitment letter, grant agreement, rehabilitation contract, W-9 form, and final invoice from contractor confirming work completion. No deed of trust or lien is recorded on the property. Submit completed application and supporting documentation by email to Rehab.HAFApplications@Maryland.gov or by mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA Special Loan Programs - Rehab Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF), 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides low- or no-interest loans to local housing authorities or county governments partnering with housing developers to increase housing production and support innovative solutions to housing scarcity. The program may also be used for projects where a county, in conjunction with a local housing authority or housing developer, purchases existing privately owned housing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low- or no-interest loans provided to local housing authorities or county governments partnering with housing developers through the Housing Innovation Fund. Loans can be used for new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of rental housing, or for purchasing existing privately owned housing. Two loan structures available: Short-term loans (3-5 years) at approximately 3% interest rate, or longer-term loans (7-10 years) at approximately 5.5% interest rate. Loans will be subordinate in position, though positioning may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Maximum award per project is $2.5 million. Total FY2026 funding available is $5 million with a maximum of one award per jurisdiction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public housing authorities and county governments, particularly those partnering with housing developers to create mixed-income rental housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities. Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing with at least 20% of units for households earning 50% or less of area median income, or at least 40% of units for households earning 60% or less of area median income. Funds may also be used to purchase existing privately owned housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland. Priority consideration given to projects within ¾ mile of rail stations, within ENOUGH Act approved award locations or Just Community designations, or within Community of Opportunity areas.
requirements_list: Must be a public housing authority or county government partnering with a housing developer
Must have ownership interest in the project's ownership entity, as demonstrated by organizational chart and/or partnership agreement
Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing

At least 20% of units must be set aside for households with gross annual income of 50% or less of area median income, OR at least 40% of units must be set aside for households with gross annual income of 60% or less of area median income
For acquisition and purchase projects, applicants may include counties in conjunction with local housing authorities or housing developers
Project must be ready for occupancy within two (2) years of award selection date
Application fee of $2,500 must be submitted separately to Community Development Administration, PO Box 2524, Landover Hills, MD 20784
Must comply with affirmative fair housing marketing requirements
Projects must adhere to DHCD Multifamily Policies regarding construction standards, individual unit health and safety requirements, and ongoing compliance, asset management, and inspections
Must provide all information required for listing affordable rental units on DHCD's Housing Registry Website
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact DHCD to request an electronic application folder using the Electronic Submission Package Request Form available in the Multifamily Library. Applicants may submit a waiver request for exceptions to project threshold criteria or competitive criteria at least 15 days prior to the application deadline (by May 4, 2026). Submit one complete electronic application including all attachments and exhibits via Procorem WorkCenter with clear tabs for easy navigation. Application forms should not be retyped or modified. All required exhibits must be included. A virtual information session was held on March 11, 2026 at 12 p.m. Complete application materials include: Housing Innovation Pilot Program Application Submission Package, CDA Form 202 Multifamily Rental Financing Application with instructions, Certifications, Threshold Checklist, Applicant Self-Scoring form, Organizational Chart (proposed or current), Form 203 (Developer's Qualifications), and Form 209 (Management Agent's Qualifications). Submit application fee of $2,500 separately via check payable to Community Development Administration. Applications will be date-stamped to verify receipt by the submission deadline. Incomplete submissions will not be processed. Complete applications will be scored by a committee convened by DHCD, with possible participation from other State and local government agencies. Projects will be ranked according to scoring results, with the highest-scored project recommended to the CDA Director for approval, then to the Secretary for final approval and allocation. DHCD may only select one project per jurisdiction.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit for Maryland residents who make their homes more accessible by adding accessibility features. Homeowners can receive up to 50% of renovation costs back, up to $5,000 total.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland residents who complete home renovations that add accessibility features can claim a tax credit of up to 50% of renovation costs, with a maximum credit of $5,000 per year. The credit is claimed on Maryland tax returns using the provided tax credit certification from DHCD. Applicants must submit a completed application and supporting documentation by June 1st of the current calendar year. If approved, the applicant will receive a certificate by August 31st of the current calendar year, which is then filed with an amended tax return (Form 502X). Annual program cap is $1,000,000 in total credits; if demand exceeds this, individual credits may be reduced.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1st of the current calendar year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who have completed home renovations with accessibility features during the previous tax year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home renovations that add accessibility features such as no-step entrances, grab bars, handrails, accessible doorways, chairlifts, elevators, roll-in showers, accessible parking spaces, rocker panel light switches, accessible door hardware, lever water controls, slip-resistant floors, visual alarms for individuals with sensory disabilities, railings, accessible kitchen and bathroom modifications, and other modifications to make homes more accessible for people with mobility or sensory disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents who file taxes in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident
File taxes in Maryland for the same calendar year the renovations were completed
Have proof of payment for home renovations that include accessibility features
Submit completed application to DHCD with supporting documentation by June 1st of the current calendar year
Provide detailed invoices, proof of payment, and before-and-after photos
Complete renovations during the previous tax year
Certify that accessibility features were paid for by the applicant
Declare that no other funding or tax credits from other sources were received for the same renovations
Maintain documentation (invoices and receipts) for verification purposes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete home renovations with accessibility features during the tax year. File your taxes for the year you completed the renovation. Submit a completed application and supporting documentation (detailed invoices, proof of payment, before-and-after photos, and other supporting documentation) by June 1st of the current calendar year either online at DHCD.SLP_Documentation@Maryland.gov or by mailing the paper application to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs- Independent Living Tax Credit Application, Attention: SLP Intake Team, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. DHCD will review your application and notify you by August 31st of the current calendar year. If approved, you will receive a tax credit certificate, which you then file with an amended tax return (Form 502X).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Indoor Plumbing Program provides financing for indoor plumbing improvements to residential properties, including single-family owner-occupied homes and rental properties with one to twenty units. The program helps limited-income property owners install or upgrade plumbing systems, septic systems, wells, and related facilities. It also supports homeowners in replacing lead pipes inside their homes following municipal lead service line replacements. Loans are processed by local administering agencies including county housing offices, nonprofit organizations, and local banks.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on ability to pay and percentage of median family income. For applicants at or below 60% of median income, interest rates range from 0% to 4.5%. For applicants at or below 50% of median income, deferred principal and interest payments may be available for borrowers with no repayment capability. Maximum loan amount is generally $50,000. Maximum loan term is 30 years; for some local programs the maximum term is 20 years. Maximum loan amount is generally 95 percent of the property value (accounting for any superior mortgage). Deferred loans are available for borrowers needing health, safety, or accessibility improvements; deferred amounts may be forgiven annually for families with incomes below 30 percent of statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Landlords are not eligible for deferred loans. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes and owners of rental residential properties (1–20 units) with income at or below 80 percent of statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Also homeowners seeking to replace lead pipes inside their homes after municipal lead service line replacement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wells, septic tanks and drain fields, piping, connection expenses to public water or sewer systems, plumbing fixtures and equipment including handicapped fixtures, additions and modifications for toilet and bath facilities, sand mound systems, purification systems, percolation tests, alternative or innovative septic and water systems, and replacement of lead pipes inside homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Processed by local government housing offices for properties within their jurisdiction, including Frederick County and Wicomico County (City of Salisbury). Income limits are based on the statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income depending on property location. Washington, D.C. PMSA income limits apply to Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's Counties.
requirements_list: Owner-occupied single-family homes or rental residential properties with one to twenty units
Inoperative or unsafe plumbing
Property must be structurally sound
Owner-occupants must have income at or below 80 percent of statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
For rental units, residents must be income-eligible households with income at or below 80 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
For lead pipe replacement, service line must be found to contain lead
Landlords are not eligible for deferred loans
Primary residence must be the subject property
Applicants must provide current homeowner's insurance documentation
Applicants must provide proof of home ownership (deed and current mortgage statement)
Applicants must provide photo identification
Property tax bill and homeowner's insurance declaration page required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact your local housing office by county or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Special Loan Programs directly at (301) 429-7409, 877-218-8101, or 1-844-369-4150. 2. Obtain bids from licensed Maryland contractors for the plumbing improvements needed. Bids should not be more than 60 days old and should not exceed $50,000 in total. 3. Prepare application materials including completed application form, income verification documents (two months of paystubs or two years of tax returns), proof of home ownership (deed, mortgage statement, property tax bill), homeowner's insurance documentation, photo identification, and contractor bids with required contractor documentation (MHIC license or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, W-9 form). 4. Submit completed application and supporting documentation to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mail to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 5. Loans are processed by local administering agencies including county housing offices, nonprofit organizations, and local banks.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Loan and Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program funded by HUD's Office of Lead Hazard Control and Healthy Homes and state resources that helps make Maryland homes safer by removing or reducing lead hazards in owner-occupied single family homes, rental properties, multi-family residential units, and licensed residential childcare facilities. Financial assistance is provided to eligible homeowners and landlords statewide.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance in the form of grants or loans. Grants: Available up to $25,000 per eligible property in target areas with no income limits, or up to $25,000 per unit in non-target areas for owner-occupants with income at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI). Match requirements: 20% for for-profit sponsors, 10% for nonprofit sponsors, 10% for owner-occupants with income above 80% AMI. Amortizing Loans: Up to $25,000 per unit at 0%-7% interest for 20 years for properties where underwriting shows affordability to repay. Deferred Loans: Up to $25,000 per unit at 0% interest for 20 years, available only when underwriting shows no affordability to repay; loan forgiveness may be considered after 20 years if no equity is available upon resale or transfer. Annual sponsor maximum: $100,000 for grants and deferred loans. Debt-to-value ratio: 100% for loans (with exceptions for owner-occupant properties with lead-affected households). For-profit sponsors must pay all fees and charges; nonprofit sponsors and owner-occupants of limited income may include fees in financing. Eligible costs include door and window treatments and replacement, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, and specialized cleaning. Work must be performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor. Clearance testing is required. Funding is available until April 1, 2029.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident homeowners and landlords of owner-occupied single family homes, rental properties, multi-family residential units, and licensed residential childcare facilities that need lead hazard reduction. Licensed day care centers are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead hazard reduction activities including door and window treatments and replacement, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, specialized cleaning, and other lead-related costs required to meet lead dust clearance standards. Work must be performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor. Clearance testing is required.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide. Grants available in certain target areas or for innovative lead hazard reduction treatments. Note: the HUD-funded grant component excludes the City of Baltimore. Income limits vary by location: Washington, D.C. PMSA (includes Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties) has higher income limits than the rest of the state.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland resident if owner-occupant
Property must be owner-occupied single family home, rental property, multi-family residential unit, or licensed residential childcare facility
Owner-occupants must own and occupy the dwelling as a principal residence
Units must be in need of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be structurally sound upon completion of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be registered with the Maryland Department of the Environment Lead Poisoning Prevention Program
Licensed childcare facilities are eligible to apply
Owner-occupants: income at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) for non-targeted areas; no income limit in targeted areas or for innovative treatments
For-profit sponsors: income-based eligibility; must provide 20% match
Nonprofit sponsors: must provide 10% match
Owner-occupants with income above 80% AMI in non-target areas: must provide 10% match
Work plan must fully address all lead hazards present in the project
Work must be performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor
Clearance testing is required
For-profit sponsors must pay all fees and charges; nonprofit sponsors and owner-occupants of limited income may include fees in financing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact Special Loan Programs at 301-429-7409, 877-218-8101 (toll-free in Maryland), TTY 711, or 1-800-735-2258, or email DHCD.SpecialLoans@maryland.gov. Applicants can also contact their local county housing rehabilitation office. For owner-occupants, submit completed application with supporting documentation including income verification, proof of home ownership (deed, mortgage statement, property tax bill, homeowners insurance declaration page), lead testing results, and contractor proposal. For sponsors (nonprofit and for-profit entities), submit completed sponsor application with organizational documents, financial statements, deed, mortgages, insurance policies, property tax bill, photographs, zoning compliance evidence, residential lease, lead testing results, and contractor proposal. All applications must include evidence that property is registered with the Maryland Department of the Environment Lead Poisoning Prevention Program. Submit applications to: Email: DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or Mail: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Incomplete applications will not be processed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development issues tax-exempt bonds on behalf of counties, municipalities, and their agencies to provide long-term capital financing for community infrastructure projects. The program pools local government demand to reduce bond issuance costs through economies of scale, making affordable financing accessible to smaller entities that do not routinely issue bonds. It supports essential physical elements of public service systems across all Maryland jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Community Development Administration issues tax-exempt bonds and loans the bond proceeds to local governments. The interest rate on loans is based on market conditions at the time of bond sale and the rate attained on the pooled bond issue. Local governments are responsible for repaying the debt and paying their pro-rata share of bond issuance costs. Loan terms are set by the local government but cannot exceed the useful life of the project or 30 years, whichever is less. Projects can range from $150,000 to $10 million or more.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies that have legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain infrastructure projects and to pledge security for loan repayment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Streetscape improvements, transportation enhancements, street lighting, landscaping, sidewalks and public space improvements, public safety vehicles and equipment, water production and distribution systems, water and sewer treatment facilities, stormwater control facilities, government office and meeting facilities, police and fire facilities and stations, transportation facilities, education and health facilities, recreation facilities, maintenance facilities, and refinancing of existing debt for eligible projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties and municipalities.
requirements_list: Local government must have legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain the proposed project
Local government must have legal authority to pledge security for and repay the proposed loan
Local government must have legal authority to pledge income tax payments and various shared revenue from the State
Proposed project must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system
Project must meet federal tax law requirements
Project must be undertaken by or on behalf of a local government or its agencies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The local government completes an application that requires information similar to what a bond rating agency would need to evaluate creditworthiness. Technical assistance is available from the Community Development Administration to help with application completion. Those requesting technical assistance may submit an Expression of Interest form outlining the proposed project or asking specific questions. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Timing of bond issuance is influenced by the volume and frequency of participation by local governments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Housing Tax Credit Program (LIHTC)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program that encourages private sector investment in the construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. Tax credits are awarded competitively to nonprofit and for-profit sponsors based on criteria in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan. Sponsors or their investor partners claim the tax credit on their federal income tax return. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible for tax credits outside of the competitive process.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits equal the applicable percentage of the qualified basis of each qualified low-income rental housing building. The applicable percentage is determined by the Internal Revenue Service. Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis per criteria in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible for tax credits outside of the competitive process. Ten percent of the state's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors. Property owners and their investor partners claim the tax credit on their federal income tax return. The building must remain in compliance with affordability requirements for a minimum of 40 years, with an extended use period of at least an additional 15 years beyond the initial 15-year compliance period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; End-of-Year data uploads typically May 16 through June 20 annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit sponsors of eligible residential rental housing projects, including developers and organizations building or rehabilitating rental housing for lower-income households.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and rehabilitation of residential rental housing for low- and moderate-income families, including purchasing, rehabilitating, or building rental housing targeted at lower-income households.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Projects must be placed in service in or within two years after the year in which the allocation is made.
requirements_list: Residential rental building eligible for placement in service in Maryland
Must provide housing for low-income occupancy

Owner must rent either 20 percent of units to households with incomes of 50 percent or less of area median income OR 40 percent of units to households with incomes of 60 percent or less of area median income
Building must comply with tenant income and maximum rent level requirements
Building must remain in compliance and is subject to a covenant to enforce compliance for a minimum of 40 years, followed by an extended use period of at least 15 additional years
Ten percent of annual state allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors
Housing must be rental property
Targeted at lower-income households
Owner must submit annual certifications of continuing compliance
Properties must comply with income restrictions and rent limits
Utility allowances must comply with program standards
Student status must be verified at move-in

For buildings without 100% LIHTC units, owners may apply for exemptions from annual recertification during the extended use period if initial inspection is satisfactory and no outstanding compliance issues exist
Physical inspections conducted at least once every five years during extended use period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis to nonprofit and for-profit sponsors of eligible housing projects. Applications are submitted for competitive review based on criteria outlined in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible for tax credits outside of the competitive process. End-of-year reporting is required through the LIHTC Tenant Demographic End-of-Year Reporting System portal, which opens annually for tenant demographic data uploads. Property owners register through the portal using manual data entry or XML file upload. Ongoing compliance monitoring is conducted by the Division of Credit Assurance during both the initial 15-year compliance period and the extended use period. Contact the program for additional information on how to apply and current QAP requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: MEER: Maryland Emergency Education Relief Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to provide relief to K-12 students and school staff by closing the gap for students who lack internet access or devices needed to connect to classrooms.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $250,000 covering eligible program costs for projects to close internet access gaps and provide devices for K-12 students and school staff. Funding distributed to schools, libraries, and community organizations across Maryland counties including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Cecil County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and Wicomico County. Total program funding of approximately $5 million available based on FY22 awards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools, libraries, and anchor institutions serving K-12 students and school staff, including public schools, educational nonprofits, community organizations, and government entities providing educational services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs to close internet access gaps and provide devices for students to connect to classrooms, broadband access infrastructure, and educational technology equipment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all Maryland communities. FY22 awards distributed to Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Frederick, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, Washington, and Wicomico counties.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a school, library, or anchor institution
Project must close internet access gaps or provide devices for K-12 students and school staff
Eligible applicants include public schools, educational nonprofits, community-based organizations, and government entities
Project must serve K-12 students or school staff
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were accepted during the specified program period (September 1, 2021 to September 15, 2022). Eligible organizations submitted proposals for broadband access and device distribution projects. Awards ranged from approximately $34,000 to $250,000 based on project scope and need.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Main Street Improvement Program provides operating assistance grants to designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods to build capacity and achieve community revitalization and economic development goals in Sustainable Community areas throughout the state.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Operating assistance grants allocated to eligible Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City neighborhoods based on accreditation status. Designated Main Street Maryland Communities with full accreditation receive approximately $33,000 each; designated communities with affiliate accreditation receive approximately $25,000 each; and Main Street Maryland Aspiring Communities receive approximately $12,000 each. Final amounts are subject to General Assembly approval during the FY2027 legislative session. Funds support operating expenses only, including staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other costs related to administering the Main Street program. Grants can be used for salary, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other expenses identified in the applicant's work plan as key to its Main Street efforts. No funding match is required, and all projects and activities must be completed within one year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses only, including staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, salary, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other costs related to administering the Main Street program. Projects and activities must align with the applicant's annual work plan and contribute to the community's transformation strategy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland's designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods located in designated Sustainable Community areas throughout the state.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the DHCD Project Portal at https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/. New users must register through the portal and wait up to 72 hours for approval. First-time applicants must contact their project manager for eligibility verification and system access. New organizations should request access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. Applicants should ensure their organization profile includes all required documents before submitting. Applications must align with the applicant's Main Street annual work plan. A virtual application training was scheduled for Tuesday, March 3, 2026, and individual technical assistance sessions are available through Calendly. The authorized signatory for your organization must sign and return the award agreement via DocuSign within five business days of receipt. Upon award execution, funds cannot be drawn down until after execution and all Special Conditions have been met. An initial advance of up to 25% of the total award amount is permitted for the first payment request without supporting documentation. It is recommended that individual payment requests exceed $3,000 to optimize processing efficiency. Progress reports are due either 6 months from the grant agreement execution date or whenever a payment request is submitted. The final report is due no later than 30 days after the award agreement's expiration date.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Affordable Housing Trust makes affordable housing more available throughout Maryland by funding capital costs of rental and ownership housing, providing financial assistance for nonprofit-developer capacity building, funding supportive services for affordable housing occupants, and funding operating expenses of affordable housing developments. It serves households earning less than 50% of area or statewide median income.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding for project-specific capacity building, operating expenses, and supportive services are generally made as grants. Funding for capital costs are offered as deferred-payment loans or recoverable grants payable if the project is sold and/or ceases to be used for low-income occupancy. Pre-development awards are generally repayable. Grants may support acquisition, pre-development costs, construction, rehabilitation, and operating assistance for affordable housing. Loan terms and conditions are determined by MAHT in consultation with applicants.

Eligible project types include acquisition, pre-development costs, construction, rehabilitation, and operating assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Capital Access Program (MCAP) is a credit enhancement program that helps small businesses access financing by enabling private lenders to establish a loan loss reserve fund from fees paid by lenders, borrowers, and the State of Maryland. The program supports the growth and success of small businesses in Priority Funding Areas throughout Maryland, including nonprofit organizations that may have difficulty obtaining conventional business financing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program creates a loan loss reserve fund through contributions from lenders, borrowers, and the State of Maryland. Enrolled loan amounts range from $10,000 to $1,000,000. Typically, the borrower and lender each contribute between 1.5 percent of the loan amount, and the Maryland Capital Access Program matches that contribution. The reserve account protects against loan defaults. If a loan defaults after the lender performs normal collection methods, the lender files a claim to recover losses from the reserve account. The program can cover up to 100% of losses for participating lenders, and loans can have a term of up to ten years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and nonprofit organizations located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas, including businesses that may have difficulty obtaining conventional financing. Borrowers must qualify as a small business under SBA size standards with fewer than 50 employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, start-up costs, equipment purchases, expansion, and other business purposes. Cannot be used for passive real estate ownership, residential or transient living facilities, public facilities, adult entertainment establishments, check cashing facilities, gambling facilities, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, gun shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, or furtherance of sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area approved by the Maryland Department of Planning for State funding in accordance with the Smart Growth Act of 1997. The program is available to businesses located anywhere in Maryland that fall within designated Priority Funding Areas.
requirements_list: Small business must be located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas
Most Maryland small businesses and nonprofit organizations are eligible
Loan amount must be between $10,000 and $1,000,000
Borrower and lender must make contributions to the reserve account
Borrower must qualify as a small business under SBA size standards
Borrower must have fewer than 50 employees
Loan term may not exceed ten years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Small business applies to a participating lender. The lender underwrites and enrolls the appropriate loan (or portion of a loan). The lender determines if the loan qualifies for the program. Lender, borrower, and the Maryland Capital Access Program make contributions to a reserve account. A one-page enrollment form is submitted to the program by the lender.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to improve the exterior facades of businesses and facilities located in Maryland Sustainable Communities. Applicants (local governments and community development organizations) capitalize a grants fund and develop an application process for local businesses to improve their building exteriors, supporting community revitalization.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides $5 million in capital funding for facade improvement projects on buildings located in Sustainable Communities. Applicants apply to create a local grant fund, which local businesses can then use for their facade projects. Eligible capital improvements include signage, exterior painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, exterior lighting, window and door upgrades, public-facing masonry or cornices, murals, removal of unattractive exterior finishes, and roofs. Individual business improvements must be between $1,000 and $50,000 of MFIP funding during a single award cycle. Projects should prioritize aesthetic improvements over routine maintenance and focus on primary elevations of commercial properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, groups of local governments, community development organizations, and businesses seeking to improve building exteriors in designated Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital costs for improving exterior facades of business buildings and facilities, including signage, exterior painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, exterior lighting, window and door upgrades, public-facing masonry or cornices, murals, removal of unattractive exterior finishes, and roofs. Interior work, electric charging stations, solar panels, and improvements outside designated Sustainable Communities are ineligible. Individual business improvements must be between $1,000 and $50,000 of MFIP funding per award cycle.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in designated Sustainable Communities, which are geographic areas targeted for revitalization by local governments. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility. All MFIP projects are subject to the Maryland Historical Trust Act and the Federal Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation for properties over 50 years old.
requirements_list: Projects must be located in a designated Sustainable Community
Projects should capitalize on community strengths while addressing revitalization challenges
Projects should help achieve a local government's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Applicants must capitalize a grants fund and develop an application process for local businesses
Individual business improvements must be between $1,000 and $50,000 of MFIP funding during a single award cycle
Changes to completed improvements that received MFIP funding within the last 12 months are ineligible
Improvements must not be banned by local building codes or zoning
Work completed prior to receipt of a letter of commitment is ineligible for funding
Applicants must provide evidence of expenditures including receipts or canceled checks
Applicants must maintain valid insurance coverage for property damage and personal injury
Applicants agree to maintain the property and improvements and return pro-rated grant money if improvements are removed within two years
All improvements must comply with Maryland Historical Trust Act requirements and Federal Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First-time applicants are advised to contact a regional project manager or Allison Foster for more information and eligibility determination. Application training is available via webinar. Register for training and view application information at the DHCD State Revitalization Programs website. Applicants complete the Maryland Façade Improvement Program Application and must attach required documents including evidence of site control, photographs of existing conditions, written consent from landlord and lessee if applicable, project description with two cost estimates and detailed sketches, and a screenshot from the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation website showing business is in good standing. Applicants apply to create a grants fund and must develop their own application process for local businesses. Local program guidelines must include criteria for rating and awarding grants to qualified businesses. All improvements are subject to historic preservation review by DHCD's Preservation Officer, and if necessary, the Maryland Historical Trust.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Counseling Fund (MHCF) supports non-profit and local government organizations that provide a range of housing counseling services and free or low-cost legal assistance to help people with homebuying, foreclosure prevention, rental issues, and eviction concerns. Awards are made annually on a competitive basis. HUD-approved housing counseling agencies with HUD-certified counselors on staff receive priority funding consideration.

The program also supports non-profit legal services providers that assist homeowners concerned about foreclosure and renters concerned about eviction. The program additionally offers technical assistance and information resources.
