structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program provides rehabilitation loans and grants to income-eligible homeowners and small rental property owners to bring properties up to applicable building codes and standards. The program addresses exterior and interior deficiencies, accessibility improvements, health and safety violations, energy conservation, and elimination of lead-based paint hazards. It serves owner-occupants of single-family homes and owners of one to four unit rental properties. Also offered through the Maryland WholeHome Program, which provides grants and low-interest loans for home repairs, energy efficiency upgrades, and accessibility enhancements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans and grants based on the type of work needed, household income, and ability to repay. Interest rates range from zero to six percent (maximum 4% for energy efficiency improvements) based on income, with a 20-year term. Very low-income families (at or below 50% of median income) may qualify for deferred payment loans; in exceptional cases borrowers up to 80% of median income may be considered for deferred loans. Landlords are not eligible for deferred loans. Secured debt including the loan may not exceed 110% of the after-rehab value. Administrative fee, closing, and recording costs may be included in the loan. Loan must be repaid upon discontinuance of owner occupancy or sale of home. County programs (e.g., Baltimore County Single Family Rehabilitation Loan) offer low-cost or no-cost loans limited to one loan per household per lifetime of ownership. No application fee is charged. Grants may be available for very low-income households and persons with disabilities in some cases.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible homeowners of single-family, owner-occupied dwellings and owners of one to four unit rental properties in Maryland, including Baltimore County and Frederick County residents. Household income generally may not exceed 80% of the area median income. Very low-income families at or below 50% of median income receive priority consideration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation and renovation to bring properties up to building codes and standards, including: correction of exterior and interior deficiencies, elimination of safety and health hazards, repair or replacement of major systems, energy conservation and energy efficiency improvements, accessibility modifications for persons with disabilities, removal and elimination of lead-based paint hazards, plumbing and septic repairs, roof repair/replacement, structural and maintenance issues, and some general improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland; administered locally through county and municipal partners including Baltimore County, Frederick County, and Annapolis. Income limits based on applicable area median income (e.g., Washington D.C. MSA median income for Frederick County).

Call toll-free 1-844-369-4150 to start an application for home repairs or 1-855-583-8976 for energy efficiency improvements. Submit the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program Application form. Baltimore County applicants may submit a completed Universal Programs Application via email to dhcd@baltimorecountymd.gov. Annapolis and Frederick County residents should contact their respective local program offices for application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program designed to help certified minority business enterprises and small businesses access affordable capital by reducing the interest rate on loans they obtain from participating banks. Eligible borrowers can receive up to a 2% discount on their loans.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Borrowers who are certified minority business enterprises or small businesses can receive up to a 2% discount on the interest rate of loans from participating banks. The State Treasurer deposits an amount equal to the loan with the issuing bank at a reduced rate to facilitate the discount. Loans are for a term of up to 10 years with fixed rates and one disbursement. Lenders cannot charge more than 1% in points. Participating lenders include Bank Annapolis, Industrial Bank, and Columbia Bank.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified minority business enterprises in good standing with the Maryland Department of Transportation, and small businesses in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loans must be used for projects or activities located in Maryland. Proceeds cannot be used for the furtherance of sectarian or religious purposes or instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Loan proceeds must be used for projects located in Maryland. Statewide program.

Loan purpose must be for a project or activity located in Maryland
Borrower must apply to the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development to be eligible
Loan term cannot exceed 10 years
Points charged by lender cannot exceed 1% of loan amount
Loan cannot be used for sectarian or religious purposes or instruction
Borrower must remain in good standing as a certified Minority Business Enterprise or small business with the State of Maryland to continue receiving the interest rate reduction benefit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An eligible applicant or participating lender submits a brief application via the Internet or paper form to the Linked Deposit Program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. After the department verifies eligibility, it forwards the application to all enrolled banks. The department provides the borrower with a list of participating banks. The borrower contacts participating banks to complete their full application requirements. The bank underwrites the loan with an interest rate up to 2% less than standard rates. Upon loan approval and acceptance, the bank enrolls the loan in the program. The State Treasurer then deposits an amount equal to the loan with the issuing bank at a reduced rate. Participating lenders include Bank Annapolis (410-224-4455), Industrial Bank (202-722-2000), and Columbia Bank (301-791-8444).

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) is a federal program administered by the states that expands access to capital to small businesses. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development offers flexible loans and other financial assistance under the program to catalyze small businesses across the state. The program provides funding for small business financing programs, including capital access programs, loan participations, loan guarantees, collateral support, and venture equity investments. Federal funds are used to support small businesses, targeting communities and areas with high concentrations of small, micro, and Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual (SEDI) businesses. The program is administered in partnership with the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO), which allocates up to $50 million through four programs supporting technology and life sciences businesses. SSBCI does not provide grant funds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The SSBCI Direct Loan Program offers flexible loans to catalyze small businesses. Loan amounts range from a minimum of $500,000 to a maximum of $5 million, with total project costs not to exceed $20 million. Loans require a minimum 1:1 private capital match. Loan terms are flexible with focus on maximizing community benefit, with terms of up to 30 years available in senior or subordinate loan positions. Interest rates are determined by underwriting analysis. Personal guarantees are required from owners with greater than 20% equity interest, and adequate collateral is required. Program fees include a $250 application fee, $250 closing fee, and 1% origination fee. Eligible uses include costs to sustain or expand a small business such as purchasing machinery or equipment and working capital; and owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation (renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion, and new construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion). Special focus is given to projects with significant community impacts, including job retention or creation, child care access, fresh food access, and community revitalization. Through TEDCO, up to $50 million is allocated into four programs: the Venture Equity Fund, Venture Capital Limited Partnership Equity program, Seed Funds Equity program, and Social Impact Funds, providing equity investments to technology-based Maryland businesses and entrepreneurs. Applications can be made through participating lenders or directly through the DHCD application portal. Technical assistance is available through the MD Business Opportunity Center and F3Tech SEDI Program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with fewer than 500 employees, micro-businesses, and businesses owned by Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI) with limited opportunities for growth, as well as small technology and life sciences businesses and entrepreneurs across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs to sustain or expand a small business, such as purchasing machinery or equipment, and working capital; owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation (renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion, and new construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion); business growth and expansion; job creation and retention; child care access; fresh food access; community revitalization.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland, with focus on communities and areas with high concentration of small, micro, and SEDI businesses.

Adequate collateral required

Cannot use funds for passive real estate, refinancing existing debt with same lender, delinquent tax repayment (unless repayment plan in place), equity buyouts, lobbying activities, federally guaranteed loans, or if SSBCI insider has financial interest
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the application portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication or directly with SSBCI lending partners. Email dhcd.businesslending@maryland.gov for a consultation about whether SSBCI is the right solution for your business. For TEDCO programs, apply through one of the four sub-programs: Social Impact Funds, Seed Funds, or Venture Funds, each with their own application process. Technical assistance is available through the MD Business Opportunity Center and F3Tech SEDI Program. All applications are subject to underwriting and final DHCD approval. Program participation does not guarantee loan approval or funding.

It provides flexible financing for the start-up, rehabilitation, or expansion of businesses and nonprofits that offer fresh food options, with emphasis on sourcing from Maryland farmers. The program serves designated Food Desert Areas and Sustainable Communities.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants work through selected community-based lending intermediaries (Community Development Financial Institutions, local governments, or quasi-public agencies) who recruit, capitalize, originate and administer loans and provide technical assistance. Intermediaries must apply and be selected as partners.

structured_extraction.program_description: A financing program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that provides flexible loans to microenterprise entrepreneurs for starting up or expanding small businesses located in designated Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas. The program partners with community-based microlenders (CDFIs) to give business owners easier access to capital, training, and technical assistance, while also expanding opportunities for microenterprise development and sustaining local economies in Maryland communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans of up to $50,000 at interest rates up to 12 percent with loan terms not exceeding 5 years. Additional funds may be provided by the intermediary lender. Collateral is required and may include personal guarantees, liens on business assets, and pledges of accounts. No prepayment penalties apply. Funds can be used for working capital, equipment, leasehold improvements, and other eligible business expenses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Microenterprise entrepreneurs and small business owners with no more than 5 employees and annual revenue not exceeding $500,000 located in designated Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, marketing, planning, feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payments, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment, and certain other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Loans are available for businesses located in designated Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas throughout Maryland. Service areas vary by intermediary partner.
requirements_list: Business must be located in a designated Sustainable Community or Priority Funding Area
Business must not exceed $500,000 in annual revenue
Business must not have more than 5 employees at time of application
Business may be retail, manufacturing, or goods and services related
Business cannot be home-based
Collateral is required
No residential or transient living businesses
No multifamily or single-family housing developments
No nursing homes, assisted living facilities, crisis care centers, group homes, transitional housing, or homeless shelters
No facilities such as community halls, fire stations, hospitals, colleges, or universities
No adult bookstores, adult video shops, or adult entertainment facilities
No gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, or tattoo parlors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the intermediary microlender serving your county or region directly to receive an application. Intermediaries include Baltimore Community Lending, Enterprise Development Group, Latino Economic Development Center, Maryland Capital Enterprises Inc., and Prince George's Financial Service Corporation. The program accepts applications on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides tax-exempt bonds and notes to increase the construction and rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing for families with limited incomes. Financing can be used for new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of existing housing with a minimum of five units, and leverages federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds and notes provide construction and permanent financing through multiple structures. Interest rates are based on the Community Development Administration's bond rate. Permanent loan terms are generally 30 to 40 years. A first lien position is generally required. All loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program. The program participates in the Federal Housing Administration/Housing Finance Agency Risk Sharing Program and accepts a variety of financing structures including 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits financing options. Available financing options include: (1) FHA-CDA Risk Sharing (Section 542(c)) with 40-year or 17-year maturity; (2) GNMA MBS (FHA Section 221(d)(4)) with 40-year maturity; (3) Freddie Mac Tax Exempt Loans with 17-year maturity; (4) Cash Collateral/GNMA MBS with 2-year construction period; (5) FNMA MBS Collateral for Tax Exempt Bonds with immediate or forward start options at 17-year maturity. CDA may also structure Tax/Taxable Exempt (Tax/TE) financing combining taxable GNMA loans with tax-exempt bonds to achieve lower interest rates. Estimated all-in rates range from 5.72% to 6.67% depending on financing structure. Estimated upfront costs range from approximately $1,093,000 to $2,062,000 based on loan amount and financing option. Underwriting fees depend on bond amount, paid at closing. CDA Financing Fee is 1.625% on bond/loan amount. CDA Bond Loan Closing Attorney's Fee is $45,000 for first loan plus $9,000 for each additional loan. CDA State Loan Closing Attorney's Fee is $9,000 for each additional loan. Various other fees apply including bond counsel fees, financial advisor fees, trustee fees, and trustee legal fees. Ongoing fees include annual CDA Issuer Fee of 0.40% of outstanding principal, Trustee Fee of $4,250 annually, and CDA Servicing Fee of 0.25% of outstanding principal. Additional fees vary based on financing structure and bond characteristics. For Tax/TE financing, borrower must provide an entity to purchase unrated bonds as private placement, and entity must retain bonds for entire term without selling or transferring ownership.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit developers seeking to finance, build, or rehabilitate multifamily rental housing projects for families with limited incomes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of existing multifamily rental housing with a minimum of five units. Loans may be provided to refinance existing high-interest-rate private loans if the refinance is in conjunction with rehabilitation of the housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must contain a minimum of five units
Projects must contain complete independent dwelling units
Projects must contain complete independent dwelling units when using tax-exempt bond financing

A sponsor must make either 20 units available to households earning 50 percent or less of the area median income, or make 40 percent of units available to households earning 60 percent or less of the area median income
Projects using tax-exempt bonds must comply with Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan to receive unallocated 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits
All loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program
First lien position is generally required
All loans must comply with federal requirements for tax-exempt revenue bonds
Housing must be for families with limited incomes
For Tax/TE financing with unrated bonds, borrower must identify an entity approved by CDA to purchase bonds as private placement
Entity purchasing unrated bonds must retain bonds and not sell, pledge, transfer or otherwise dispose for entire term
For Tax/TE financing with unrated bonds, entity must provide investment letter acknowledging sufficient knowledge, capability to evaluate risks, and ability to bear economic risk including total loss
GNMA Loan must have HUD/GNMA credit enhancement via Section 221(d), 220, or similar HUD programs; FHA Risk Sharing with CDA is not eligible for Tax/TE financing
MAP Lender must be engaged by borrower for GNMA financing
Bond amounts must be sufficient to satisfy 50% test for Tax Credits when using Tax/TE financing
Full amount of bonds must be secured 100% by cash collateral; Letter of Credit is not sufficient
GNMA Loan payments must be interest-only during construction period; principal and interest amortized over 40-year permanent loan period
Bond payments must be not less than 24 months; interest capitalized and paid in full at initial closing; principal due in full at maturity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Developers submit applications for tax-exempt bond financing on a rolling basis. Applications must include project financing structure details and proposed loan terms. For projects requiring TEFRA approval, a public hearing notice must be filed with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Contact information for TEFRA filings: Benedict DuRant at benedict.durant@maryland.gov or 301-429-7823. The Community Development Administration reviews financing structures and provides bond rate-based interest rates. For Tax/TE financing, borrowers must identify an entity to purchase unrated bonds or CDA may require rated bonds at borrower expense. Applicants should contact the Housing Development Programs office for detailed application procedures, financing option comparisons, fee schedules, and specific guidance on Tax/TE financing structures. CDA Multifamily staff available to meet with prospective borrowers.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability Program (MEEHA)
structured_extraction.program_description: MEEHA promotes energy efficiency and housing affordability in affordable multifamily rental housing developments statewide. The program provides funding for energy efficiency improvements and greenhouse gas reduction measures through two sub-programs: EmPOWER (grants or 0% interest deferred-payment loans for reducing electric or gas consumption) and the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP) (grants to replace fossil fuel-powered equipment with electric equipment such as heat pumps). The program supports both rehabilitation and new construction projects for income-qualified affordable multifamily properties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEEHA provides two sub-programs: (1) EmPOWER offers grants or loans at 0% interest with deferred payments, totaling $134.9 million for 2024–2026, for reducing electric or gas consumption, with limited health and safety or incidental repairs. Gas-reducing measures are allowed for projects in BGE or WGL utility territory. Tier 1 funding (minimum 5 years affordability) and Tier 2 funding (minimum 15 years affordability) available with different maximum amounts per measure. Funding provided as work is completed and verified during construction. (2) The Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP) offers grants only—$8.75 million in FY2024, $5 million each in FY2025 and FY2026—for replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment, building energy conservation, and alternative energy generating systems. GHGRP funding is limited to $15,000 per unit with a project cap of $1.25 million. Funding is provided on a reimbursement basis through a requisition process during construction as work is completed and verified.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and developers of affordable multifamily rental housing developments, including for-profit and non-profit entities, seeking to improve energy efficiency and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: EmPOWER: Reduce electric or gas consumption, including air sealing, insulation, HVAC system replacements, domestic hot water systems, fenestration, appliances, lighting, and duct sealing, with limited health and safety or incidental repairs. Gas-reducing measures allowed for projects in Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) or Washington Gas Light Company (WGL) utility territory. GHGRP: Reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions by replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment (e.g., heat pumps), building energy conservation measures, alternative energy generating systems such as solar photovoltaics, electric panel upgrades, and incidental repairs necessary to change fossil fuel infrastructure to electric infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. For gas-reducing measures under EmPOWER, limited to BGE or WGL utility territory.
requirements_list: EmPOWER: Minimum 20% of households must be at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for minimum 5 years (Tier 1) or 15 years (Tier 2)
GHGRP: Minimum 51% of households must be at 80% AMI or less for minimum 15 years

GHGRP: Single building with 35,000 gross square feet of floor area or more (excluding parking garages), OR two or more buildings with combined 35,000+ sq ft (excluding parking garages) served by same meter or heating/cooling system
EmPOWER rehabilitation projects: Must achieve at least 20% energy savings where applicable
EmPOWER projects must work with a Qualified Energy Professional from DHCD's approved list to complete energy audits (rehabilitation) or energy certification reviews (new construction)

For rehabilitation projects: Qualified Energy Professional conducts comprehensive on-site energy audit per BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards, inspecting representative sample of units (minimum 10% or 5 units, whichever is greater, up to 20 units)
For new construction projects: Qualified Energy Professional verifies energy efficiency certification achievement (Energy Star, Zero Energy Ready Home, or Passive House)
Must comply with current ASHRAE 62.2 ventilation standards
For GHGRP: Buildings must be Covered Buildings under Maryland Department of Environment's Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS)
For GHGRP: Energy Star Portfolio Manager account required with baseline benchmarking report
Must be above minimum code and performance standards
Measures must meet minimum efficiency specifications as detailed in program guidance
Health and Safety and Incidental Repair costs cannot exceed 10% of total energy efficiency measure funding
Electrification Costs cannot exceed 10% of total electrification measure funding
All projects subject to DHCD Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) requirements
Affordability period monitoring required during compliance period after construction completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Prospective applicant sets up Energy Star Portfolio Manager account and generates benchmarking report (for GHGRP). 2. Owner/applicant submits MEEHA Application Form or 202 form (if also applying for DHCD Rental Lending programs) to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov, including required documents such as commercial utility bills, customer consent forms, proof of affordability, SDAT checks, MBE plan, and W-9 form. 3. Owner commissions a DHCD Qualified Energy Professional to complete comprehensive energy audit (rehabilitation projects) including on-site inspections of representative sample of units, or energy certification review (new construction projects). 4. Qualified Energy Professional completes energy audit report per BPI standards, including ASHRAE ventilation calculations, demand/load calculations, and recommended energy conservation measures (ECMs). For GHGRP projects, QEP includes greenhouse gas emissions reduction data using specified conversion factors. 5. Qualified Energy Professional submits Funding Request to DHCD using the Rehab Funding Request Form or Hancock Mobile Intake Tool (MINT) when operational, including estimated costs and detailed measure specifications with photographs. 6. DHCD reviews Funding Request for completeness and compliance; may request clarifications or additional documentation within 10 business days. 7. DHCD reviews and finalizes Funding Request and creates funding agreement (grant or loan agreement) to be executed. 8. Funding agreement is executed by property owner and DHCD. 9. Project installs energy efficiency or greenhouse gas reduction measures in accordance with approved scope of work. 10. DHCD Project Manager conducts monthly meetings and visual inspections to track construction progress (GHGRP). 11. Project team submits requisitions with supporting documentation and proof of work completion. 12. DHCD performs inspection on sample of installed measures to verify quality and compliance. 13. DHCD processes payment after approval (usually 4–5 weeks); funding disbursed on reimbursement basis as work is verified. 14. After construction completion, project enters affordability compliance period. For GHGRP, annual energy use benchmarking reports must be provided to DHCD for minimum of two (2) years after construction completion via updated Portfolio Manager.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund (NED) provides competitive funds to support commercial and residential development activities in areas targeted for revitalization in the National Capital region (Prince George's and Montgomery Counties). The program focuses on areas where modest investment and a coordinated strategy will have meaningful neighborhood revitalization impact, providing capital and operating funding for economic development projects in eligible Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides $19 million in capital funding and $1.2 million in operating funding. Competitive grants support commercial and residential development, down payment assistance for homebuyers, property acquisition and rehabilitation, residential and business property improvements, energy efficiency and weatherization programs, affordable housing development, mixed-use projects combining housing retail and office space, community open space and public infrastructure development, and strategic demolition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and community development organizations in designated revitalization areas in the National Capital region (Prince George's and Montgomery Counties)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for homebuyers, property acquisition and rehabilitation, residential and business property improvements, energy efficiency and weatherization, affordable housing development, mixed-use development combining housing retail and office space, community open space and public infrastructure, and strategic demolition
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities located either 1) in Prince George's County, at least in part within the boundary created by Interstate 495 and the District of Columbia, OR 2) in Montgomery County, within an Enterprise Zone or the boundary created by Prince George's County, Maryland Route 200, Interstate 270, Interstate 495 to the Maryland state line, and the District of Columbia.
requirements_list: Eligible applicants are local governments and community development organizations
Projects must support goals and objectives outlined in the targeted area's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Projects must be located in designated Sustainable Communities areas within specified geographic boundaries
Prince George's County projects must be at least partially within the boundary created by Interstate 495 and the District of Columbia
Montgomery County projects must be within an Enterprise Zone or the specified boundary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First-time applicants are advised to contact a regional project manager for more information and eligibility determination. Application training is available via webinar. Register for training and view application information at the DHCD State Revitalization Programs website. Contact your Regional Project Manager with questions about whether a specific address is eligible. For Prince George's and St. Mary's County questions, contact Jean Cannon (Program Officer, Region 6) at 410-209-5806 or jean.cannon@maryland.gov. For Montgomery County questions, contact Jessica Argueta (Project Manager, Region 8) at 410-209-5848 or jessica.argueta@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal affordable housing production program that increases and preserves the supply of decent, safe and sanitary affordable housing for extremely low-income and very low-income households. The program targets permanent rental housing for ELI households with incomes at or below 30% of Area Median Income (AMI) or at or below the poverty line.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HTF funds may be used as broadly and flexibly as permitted by federal regulations. Forms of assistance include equity investments, interest-bearing loans or advances, non-interest-bearing loans or advances, deferred payment loans, and grants. Ninety percent (90%) of annual HTF allocation is used for production, preservation and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing through acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury housing. Up to one-third of the annual HTF allocation may be used for operating/rental assistance, with such assistance fully utilized within 5 years of award and subsequently renewable during the 30-year affordability period. The Department retains 10% of annual allocation for administrative and planning expenses. HTF funds must be committed within 24 months of HUD's execution of the grant agreement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit developers and housing organizations with demonstrated financial capacity and experience, working to create and preserve affordable housing for extremely low-income and very low-income households. Recipients must demonstrate ability to own, construct, rehabilitate, manage and operate affordable multifamily rental housing developments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Production, preservation and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing for extremely low-income and very low-income households through acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury housing with suitable amenities. Eligible uses include development hard costs, acquisition costs, related soft costs, relocation costs, and operating/rental assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland. For new construction projects, sites must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) under Maryland's Smart Growth and Green Initiative, including incorporated municipalities, areas between Baltimore and Washington DC beltways, Sustainable Communities, Federal and State enterprise zones, county-designated PFAs including rural villages, and certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas.
requirements_list: Recipient must provide certification of compliance with HTF program requirements
Demonstrate financial capacity and experience to complete and manage eligible activities
Demonstrate familiarity with requirements of other federal, state, or local housing programs used with HTF
Demonstrate experience owning, constructing, rehabilitating, managing and operating affordable multifamily rental housing
Market assessment of housing needs of ELI individuals must be submitted
Sufficient site control required extending at least 180 calendar days after application date
Capital Needs Assessment (CNA) required for projects acquiring existing property
Phase I Environmental Site Assessment required; must be not more than 1 year old
Lead-based paint and asbestos testing required for acquisition/rehabilitation projects
Evidence of public utilities availability (water, sewer, electric, gas, telephone, internet, cable)
Sites must be properly zoned for intended use; zoning changes/variances require documentation and schedule
New construction projects must be located in Priority Funding Area (PFA)
Anticipated Development Schedule required; firm written financial commitments for other financing required prior to HTF commitment
All projects must be financially feasible per Department underwriting standards
Market Study prepared by independent professional with affordable multifamily rental housing experience, peer-reviewed by NCHMA, not more than 6 months old
Market Study must demonstrate need for affordable rental housing and sufficient demand to rent units within 18 months of project completion
Minimum 5% vacancy rate required; projects requiring 10% or more vacancy will be rejected as infeasible
Annual operating expenses $4,000-$7,000 per unit per year (waivers available for projects up to 40 units or with master-metered utilities)
Minimum $300 per unit per year in reserves for replacement deposits
Operating reserve of 3-6 months of underwritten operating expenses, debt service, and required reserve deposits
Rents and revenue projected to increase no more than 2% annually; operating expenses at least 3% annually
Minimum debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) of 1.15 in first year of stabilized operations
Developer/Owner must have demonstrated experience with similar projects in past 5 years
Financial statements required for 3 fiscal years prior to application plus interim statements through previous quarter
Primary Development Team (Developer/Owner, general contractor, architect, property manager) subject to capacity review
Projects must comply with Site and Neighborhood Standards per 24 CFR §93.150 for new construction
All rehabilitation projects must meet HTF rehabilitation standards and 24 CFR §93.301(b) requirements
30-year minimum affordability period required
Affirmative Fair Housing requirements must be met
Tenant selection must comply with program requirements
Section 3 requirements apply to projects with construction costs over $200,000 in federal funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: HTF projects are selected by the Department for funding consideration subject to availability of funds. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and evaluated using Threshold Criteria. HTF funds are awarded on a non-competitive, first-ready first-served basis. Applications must include: (1) description of eligible activities; (2) market assessment; (3) evidence of site control; (4) Capital Needs Assessment for acquisitions; (5) Phase I Environmental Site Assessment; (6) utility availability documentation; (7) zoning certification; (8) Anticipated Development Schedule; (9) Market Study; (10) financial statements; (11) developer experience documentation; and (12) other threshold requirement evidence. HTF funds may be requested by a Sponsor as part of a project application or Department staff may propose use of HTF funds during project review and underwriting. Successful recipients receive a Notice of Award stating Department's intent to award HTF funds. Funds must be committed within 24 months of HUD's execution of the HTF grant agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that provides flexible financing to new or expanding small businesses and nonprofit organizations. The program supports projects located in Sustainable Communities, Priority Funding Areas, Opportunity Zones, Transit-Oriented Development areas, and BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zones. It works with small businesses and lending partners during all phases of business growth, helping to improve and revitalize existing commercial districts and town centers throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $5 million with flexible terms up to 30 years depending on loan size and underwriting. Interest rates are determined by underwriting analysis and market conditions. Applicants must provide minimum 10% cash contribution from total project cost. Personal guarantees and collateral are required. Program charges a $250 application fee, $250 closing fee, and 1% origination fee. Loans serve as first money in or gap financing for small businesses with capital needs. Program provides senior or subordinate loans, or a combination of both. Bonds may be issued to fund loans for business projects including acquisition and permanent financing of commercial and mixed-use real estate, refinance of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects, and non-profit facility loans. Debt service reserve required equal to 6 months of maximum annual debt service. Minimum pro-forma debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) of 1.50 throughout the life of the loan for CDA-funded loans.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specific deadline; first-come, first-serve basis. Applications currently exceed available funds until July 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based small businesses with 500 or fewer employees and nonprofit organizations seeking financing for commercial projects in targeted geographic areas, including businesses in Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas. Special focus is given to projects with significant community impacts, including job retention or creation, child care access, fresh food access, and community revitalization.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Real estate acquisition, construction, or rehabilitation; leasehold improvements; machinery and equipment purchases; working capital (as part of total project costs); market, planning, or feasibility studies; and other costs associated with opening, operating, or expanding a Maryland small business. Construction projects are reviewed by the Maryland Historical Trust and Codes Administration prior to funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Sustainable Communities, Priority Funding Areas, Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico counties, Transit-Oriented Development areas designated by the Maryland Department of Transportation, or BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zones. Also available in Frederick County's seven designated Sustainable Communities.
requirements_list: Maryland-based small business with 500 or fewer employees or nonprofit organization

Project located in eligible targeted geography (Sustainable Communities, Priority Funding Areas, Opportunity Zones in Allegany/Garrett/Somerset/Wicomico counties, TOD areas, or BRAC Revitalization and Incentive Zones)
Demonstrate project viability and positive neighborhood impact
Appropriate debt service levels and positive net operating income (NOI)
Sufficient collateral and personal guarantee

For-profit borrowers: minimum 10% equity or total cost borrower contribution; Maximum 90% combined loan-to-value (CLTV) financing based on one or multiple senior loan(s), or maximum 100% CLTV based on one senior loan of up to 70% LTV and one subordinate loan

Non-profit borrowers: minimum 5% equity or total cost borrower contribution; Maximum 95% CLTV financing based on one or multiple senior loan(s), or maximum 100% CLTV based on one senior loan of up to 70% LTV and one subordinate loan
Loan debt service reserve equal to 6 months of maximum annual debt service
Minimum pro-forma 1.50 DSCR throughout the life of the loan (for CDA-funded loans)
Strong business plan and readiness to proceed
Project viability and financial soundness
Impact on the surrounding neighborhood and community
Creation or retention of jobs
Visible improvements to underutilized or vacant properties
Activation of street-level retail or commercial space
Introduction of needed goods or services
Project must not be residential or transient living facilities unless part of eligible mixed-use project
Project cannot be public facilities, adult entertainment businesses, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, cannabis businesses, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, or tattoo parlors
Residential or speculative developments not eligible except for mixed-use projects with qualifying commercial components
Project must be acquired, owned, developed, constructed, reconstructed, rehabilitated or improved for the purposes of carrying on a business
Local governments are not eligible applicants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a complete NBW loan application with all items listed in the application checklist through the online Application Portal (create an account or log in). Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-serve basis. Submit application with $250 application fee. If the application is approved, additional documentation will be required to finalize and close the loan. All loans over $250,000 are reviewed and recommended for approval to the Secretary of DHCD by the NBW Loan Review Committee. Contact the Business Lending Team for additional information or to discuss program fit with DHCD team.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas by providing funding to local jurisdictions and their ISP partners for capital construction costs. The program was funded through the American Rescue Plan Act (ARP) with a minimum of $13 million available for FY22.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $50,000 and $500,000 covering 70% to 90% of eligible capital construction costs for broadband service extension to unserved areas. Match requirements vary by project density: Wired Infrastructure Projects require 10% match for fewer than 8 households per mile, 20% for 8-14 households per mile, and 30% for 15+ households per mile. Wireless Infrastructure Projects require 10% match for fewer than 40 households per tower, 20% for 40-69 households per tower, and 30% for 70+ households per tower. Match can be provided as cash or in-kind contributions (for ISP partners only). Funding is provided on a reimbursement basis after eligible costs are incurred and supporting documentation is submitted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (counties and municipalities) and internet service provider partners seeking to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for extending broadband service to unserved areas, including: construction of facilities to deploy service at grant speeds to all end users; middle mile infrastructure directly necessary to provide service to end users including interconnections between non-contiguous service areas; and electronics necessary to deliver service including Optical Line Terminals, Optical Network Terminals, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, access points, modems, and necessary equipment shelters. Tower construction costs (when owned by applicant) and related structural improvements may be included as match only.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; areas that have not previously received state broadband grant funding. Eligible project areas must be unserved, defined as areas lacking terrestrial, fixed internet service at speeds above 25 Megabits per second (Mbps) download and/or 3 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds. Areas of past awards are ineligible.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction (county or municipality) listed on the Maryland Manual On-Line website
Must partner with an ISP Partner prior to entering into a funding agreement
Eligible project area must be unserved with no locations receiving broadband service at 25 Mbps download by 3 Mbps upload speeds with latency at or below 50ms

Projects must be able to provide a minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps down and 100 Mbps up with a maximum latency of 50 milliseconds measured at served subscribers' location (reduced requirements of 100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up allowable only if network is scalable to 100 Mbps symmetrical and ISP submits certification of circumstances preventing higher speeds)
Grant covers 70-90% of capital construction costs depending on project density; 10-30% match required
Match can be cash or in-kind (for ISP partners)
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023
Sufficient match must be available for each reimbursement requested
All equipment purchased must be new and non-depreciated
Costs incurred prior to submission of completed application are ineligible for grant or match purposes
For wired projects: must include total route miles, total number of unserved households and businesses passed, and average number of households and businesses per mile
For wireless projects: must include number of towers, total number of unserved households and businesses capable of receiving service, and average number per tower
Applicant or ISP must be intended owner of facilities constructed as part of project
Grant funds may not duplicate existing broadband service provided by other entities
Grant funds may not be used for engineering design services, land/tower purchase, building construction or renovations, or operating expenses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit electronic PDF applications including: completed Grant Application Form; Executive Summary describing the unserved area and project benefits; Application Partnership information naming the ISP Partner; Statement of experience from senior team members; Network Design and Construction details; Subscriber Profile and demographic data; Subscriber Costs and Limitations; line-item capital construction budget on required form; and proposed project schedule. Applications must include GIS shape, kmz or kml files showing properties to receive service and broadband infrastructure proposed for funding. All application materials must be combined into one zip file and submitted to osb.md@maryland.gov with 'Neighborhood Connect', local jurisdiction name, and project name in the subject line. Applications are evaluated based on Need for Service and Project Benefits (up to 5 points), Match Contribution Source (up to 6 points), Network Delivery Speed (up to 10 points), and Subscriber Options (up to 4 points), for a maximum score of 25 points. Awards are made high to low score as funding permits.

structured_extraction.program_description: The state supports operating costs of certified Neighborhood Housing Services (NHS) corporations through matching grants. These nonprofits partner with residents, financial institutions, community organizations, local governments, and the State to stabilize and improve the housing market in targeted low- and moderate-income neighborhoods. NHS corporations provide homeownership opportunities, home rehabilitation, homebuyer education and counseling, closing cost assistance, and community-organizing activities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each eligible NHS corporation may apply for a grant up to $50,000 that does not exceed one-third of its annual operating budget. NHS umbrella corporations may apply for a grant for each program under their supervision up to $50,000 that does not exceed one-third of the annual operating budget of that program. State grants must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Poverty Solutions Team, Division of Neighborhood Revitalization

Eligible projects must achieve a Home Energy Rating System (HERS) rating of 50 or lower through advanced energy efficient design, renewable energy resources, and other technologies. The program serves Maryland homeowners, builders, developers, and investors undertaking new construction or deep energy retrofits of existing homes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development

list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest construction loans with rates ranging from 2% to 5% depending on HERS score and income level of occupants. Loans up to 90% loan-to-value ratio. Closing fees include 1% administration fee, $290 appraisal fee, and title fees. Typical 12-month construction period with 12-month loan repayment period for projects for sale. Loan enhancements available for applicants securing private construction loans. An additional fee may apply if funding is provided as a loan.

The Department may require additional documents as part of the underwriting process, which applicants agree to submit in a timely manner when requested. structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax incentive program established by the U.S. Treasury that encourages long-term, private investment in economically distressed low-income communities by providing capital gains tax benefits to investors who reinvest unrealized capital gains through Qualified Opportunity Funds into designated Opportunity Zone census tracts. The program aims to spur investment and entrepreneurialism in designated low-income areas to promote economic vitality, fund workforce and affordable housing development, support infrastructure, invest in start-up businesses, and upgrade existing underutilized assets. In Maryland, 149 Opportunity Zones are designated across counties including Caroline County (Denton and Federalsburg), Washington County, Baltimore City (42 designated census tracts), Garrett County, Prince George's County, St. Mary's County, and Wicomico County, among others. Three tax incentives are available: (1) a temporary deferral of capital gains taxes on amounts reinvested in an Opportunity Fund, (2) a step-up in basis for capital gains reinvested in an Opportunity Fund, (3) a permanent exclusion from taxable income of capital gains from investments held for at least 10 years.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three types of federal tax incentives are available: (1) Temporary Deferral — investors can defer paying taxes on capital gains reinvested in a Qualified Opportunity Fund until the earlier of when the investment is sold or December 31, 2026; (2) Step-Up in Basis — the basis of the original investment increases by 10 percent if held for at least 5 years, and by an additional 5 percent if held for at least 7 years, excluding up to 15 percent of the original gain from taxation; (3) Permanent Exclusion — a permanent exclusion from taxes on capital gains from investments held for at least 10 years (applies only to gains accrued after the Opportunity Fund investment). Opportunity Funds must invest at least 90 percent of their capital in designated Opportunity Zones. There is no authorized cap on available capital, making the program flexible for various investment types including small businesses and real estate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual and institutional investors seeking to defer and reduce federal tax liability on capital gains by reinvesting those gains through Qualified Opportunity Funds into designated low-income Opportunity Zone census tracts, including investors in real estate, infrastructure, small businesses, and residential projects in distressed communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital gains reinvested through Qualified Opportunity Funds into eligible property located in designated Opportunity Zones, including: real estate and infrastructure development, small business creation and expansion, workforce and affordable housing development, start-up businesses with export potential, capital improvements to underutilized assets, and business and residential projects in designated zones.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: 149 designated Opportunity Zone census tracts across Maryland, which are economically distressed census tracts with at least 20 percent individual poverty rate and median family income no greater than 80 percent of area median. Specific locations include: 42 designated census tracts in Baltimore City; Denton and Federalsburg in Caroline County; designated zones in Washington County and the City of Hagerstown; Garrett County; Prince George's County; St. Mary's County; and Wicomico County. Zones are designated by state and territory chief executives and certified by the U.S. Treasury. Each county in Maryland has at least one Opportunity Zone.
requirements_list: Investment must be made through a Qualified Opportunity Fund set up as a partnership or corporation
Qualified Opportunity Fund must be self-certified as a QOF by completing and submitting Form 8996 to IRS
Qualified Opportunity Fund must invest at least 90 percent of its capital in designated Opportunity Zones
Investment must consist of unrealized capital gains reinvested from asset sales
Project or business must be located within a designated Opportunity Zone census tract
For 10% step-up in basis: investment must be held for at least 5 years
For additional 5% step-up in basis: investment must be held for at least 7 years
For permanent exclusion of gains: investment must be held for at least 10 years and gains must accrue after the Opportunity Fund investment
Deferred gains are recognized by the earlier of the date the investment is sold or December 31, 2026
Investment must be in real estate, infrastructure, or businesses within the designated zone
For QOZ business: at least 50% of gross income must be from active conduct of trade or business within QOZ
For QOZ business: at least 70% of tangible property must be QOZ business property
For QOZ business: no more than 5% of assets can be nonqualified financial assets
For QOZ business: business may not be a sin business
For QOZ business property: must be purchased by QOF or QOZ business after December 31, 2017
For QOZ business property: must come into original use with QOF or QOZ Business or be substantially improved
Substantial improvement is 100% of value of assets, excluding land value for real estate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Investors identify a designated Opportunity Zone using the Maryland Opportunity Zones map available through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development at dhcd.maryland.gov/OpportunityZones. They then form or invest through a Qualified Opportunity Fund (structured as a partnership or corporation) that invests in eligible property within the designated zone. The QOF must complete and submit Form 8996 (Qualified Opportunity Fund) to the IRS for self-certification. Opportunity Funds pool capital to support investments in small businesses and real estate within Opportunity Zones. The fund must invest at least 90 percent of its capital in Opportunity Zone property. Specific procedures for fund formation and investment are outlined in U.S. Treasury guidelines and IRS regulations (Form 8996 and related guidance available at IRS.gov). Local contacts for additional assistance include the Baltimore Development Corporation, Caroline County Economic Development, Washington County Department of Business and Economic Development (Hagerstown), and Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation. The program is administered with support from the Maryland Department of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial assistance to help small businesses purchase or renovate commercial real estate they can operate in and use to build wealth. The program is funded by the federal State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI).

Loan amounts range from a minimum of $500,000 to a maximum of $5 million. Interest rates are determined by underwriting analysis. Businesses must provide a minimum 1:1 private capital match and adequate collateral. Personal guarantees required from all owners with more than 20% equity. structured_extraction.program_description: The Partnership Rental Housing Program expands the supply of affordable rental housing for low-income households. It finances new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of rental housing through partnerships between state and local governments, and also supports housing for individuals with disabilities or special needs through non-governmental entities. The program provides loans for rental housing occupied by households with incomes at or below 50 percent of statewide median income.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides direct loans for rental housing occupied by households with incomes at or below 50 percent of statewide median income. Loan amounts are limited to $75,000 per unit for large projects and up to $2 million without a per-unit cap for small projects (40 units or fewer). For individuals with disabilities or special needs units, residents must have income not exceeding 30 percent of Area Median Income. Loan repayment is generally deferred for up to 40 years as long as the local government entity continues to own and rent the housing to income-eligible households. Any profits from project sale must be used for other low-income housing purposes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, housing authorities, entities owned in part by local government or housing authority, for-profit and non-profit rental housing developers, and non-governmental entities seeking to create housing for individuals with disabilities or special needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities for developing and preserving affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Projects must be located in priority funding areas.
requirements_list: Rental housing must be occupied by households with incomes at or below 50 percent of statewide median income (or 30 percent for disabilities or special needs units)
Local government must make a contribution of land or equal value from non-state resources
Local participant must manage the project or arrange for another party to manage it
Resident households must contribute maintenance or other services to the facility, grounds, or neighborhood (except for individuals with disabilities or special needs units)

Any profits from project sale must be used for other low-income housing purposes

If funding is requested with other department funds, the application requirements and deadlines of the other funding must be met. Applicants can find application documents in the agency's Multifamily Document Library. Contact the program representative for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project C.O.R.E. (Creating Opportunities for Renewal and Enterprise)
structured_extraction.program_description: A four-year partnership between the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, the Maryland Stadium Authority, and the Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development to demolish thousands of vacant and blighted buildings and catalyze redevelopment, reinvestment, and stabilization in Baltimore neighborhoods. The program focuses on removing half- and whole-blocks of blight to maximize neighborhood impact, and also funds stabilization of selected properties for future rehabilitation and redevelopment. Once properties are demolished or stabilized, sites are graded, seeded, and fenced. The program aims to catalyze additional public, private, and nonprofit investment in affected communities, with the State committing to leverage an estimated $600 million through existing programs to encourage new investment in challenged communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State has committed $75 million and the City has committed $18.5 million over four years to demolish blighted properties and stabilize selected properties for future rehabilitation and redevelopment. In Fiscal Year 2017, Project C.O.R.E. awarded $15,860,000 across 30 projects to applicants including Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development, nonprofit community development corporations, and private developers. Awards ranged from $120,000 to $2,000,000 per project. The City provides in-kind services valued at $0.25 for every $1 in state allocations. The State has also committed to leverage an estimated $600 million through existing programs to encourage new investment in challenged communities.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Demolition of vacant and blighted buildings, stabilization of selected properties for future rehabilitation and redevelopment, grading, seeding, and fencing of sites, neighborhood redevelopment projects, and neighborhood reinvestment

Property owners and residents can also suggest properties for demolition, stabilization, or greening through the program. Awards are announced and funds are distributed to support approved projects. Detailed application process information is available on the State's Project C.O.R.E. webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project Restore 2.0 is a Maryland state grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development that provides financial support to place-based economic development organizations, Main Streets organizations, and Arts and Entertainment Districts to activate vacant buildings, support small businesses, create jobs, improve commercial corridors, and increase local economic activity. These organizations identify priority vacant storefronts or buildings in their local business districts and subgrant funds to businesses for rental assistance, renovation, and equipment to activate those spaces. Businesses opening or expanding into vacant retail and commercial properties may also receive direct grants to help with rent payments and operating costs in their first year. The program focuses on commercial investment in downtowns and business districts, including the restoration and adaptive reuse of historic buildings.

Businesses receiving subgrants must open and be operational by December 2025. The program has also provided up to $25 million in total funding to help new and growing businesses with rent payments and operating costs during their first year in a vacant retail or commercial property.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Rental Housing Program provides financing to rehabilitate or create rental housing. It aims to develop quality rental housing for low-income residents through loans that can be combined with federal HOME funds, tax-exempt or taxable bond financing, low-income housing tax credits, and other public or private funding sources. The program supports the development and preservation of affordable multifamily rental housing statewide.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with a term of up to 40 years at 2 percent interest per annum, repayable from cash flow. Maximum loan amount is $2 million. Funds can be used for acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs including lender fees, architectural and engineering fees, market studies, appraisals, legal fees, and other development-related costs. Funds may be combined with federal HOME funds, tax-exempt or taxable bond financing, low-income housing tax credits, and other public or private funding sources.

structured_extraction.contact_name: Housing Development Programs, Community Development Administration

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs for rental housing projects including congregate housing, single-room occupancy, emergency shelters, and shared living facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: New construction projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas. General statewide eligibility for rehabilitation projects.
requirements_list: Eligible residents must have incomes of no more than 60 percent of the area median income

Priority is given to projects that restrict units to tenants with incomes below 60% of median income, restrict units to low-income tenants for more than 40 years, provide tenant service packages, use non-State funds in addition to State funds, provide quality housing in a good location, and are sponsored by teams with demonstrated development and management ability. Applicants can download application documents from the agency's Multifamily Document Library.

structured_extraction.program_description: Subordinate gap financing to create jobs and strengthen the Maryland economy by providing funding for the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing. Projects must be financed through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subordinate loans with a maximum of $2.5 million per project (waivable under certain circumstances). Loans carry a 40-year term, 2% simple interest, and are due on sale, refinancing, transfer of property, or default. Payments are limited to 75% of annual cash flow. Loans are funded from State general obligation bonds. Loan terms include contingent interest provisions: during the permanent loan period, borrowers pay principal surplus cash as a percentage of annual surplus cash (50% until developer fee is paid in full, then as specified in the note). After principal repayment, contingent interest payments are made from surplus cash at a specified percentage until the maximum contingent interest amount is reached. Upon capital events (sale, refinancing, transfer), a payment equal to the lesser of the contingent interest percentage of borrower net proceeds or outstanding indebtedness plus contingent interest is due. Maximum contingent interest amount equals aggregate annual simple interest at 4% on the outstanding principal balance through the permanent loan period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; applications accepted on rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers, owners, for-profit businesses, non-profit organizations, county governments, and municipalities involved in affordable rental housing projects that meet Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credit requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap financing for the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing. Funds can be used in conjunction with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's tax-exempt bonds and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits, as well as other department funding sources such as Partnership Rental Housing Program or energy efficiency programs.

Award of competitive public and private sources of funding necessary for project financial feasibility must have been made
Project's projected Full Time Equivalent must be documented using the Rental Housing Works Full Time Equivalent Job Calculator
Must meet all Multifamily Bond Program and Tax Credit requirements
Must meet scoring criteria for bond loans outlined in the Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide
Board of Public Works approval required

Applicant must certify that any competitive sources of public and private funding necessary for project financial feasibility have been awarded
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on an ongoing/rolling basis in conjunction with Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credit applications. Applicants must submit a completed RHW Application Submission Package including: completed CDA Form 202 identifying RHW funds and conforming to RHW funding limitations; written documentation of required zoning approval from local zoning office or approved PUD resolution; completed FTE Job Calculator to estimate full-time equivalent jobs created; and certification to RHW application package. A separate application for Multifamily Bond Program (MBP), LIHTC and any other DHCD funding must be completed using the Department's standard Application Submission Package and submitted in advance of or simultaneously with the RHW application. Applications are tracked by date of receipt and reviewed with Multifamily Bond Program applications. Projects passing threshold are scored using Evaluation Criteria. Kick-off meetings are scheduled after scoring. Projects are funded on a first-ready, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Request for Interest: Federal Funding Application Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that pays for the costs of preparing federal funding applications, including market studies, engineering, legal, financial, and other approved consulting services needed to help entities qualify for federal broadband financing opportunities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development

Federal broadband funding programs typically restrict funding to areas without previous federal investments.
requirements_list: Must be a local jurisdiction or ISP partner
Must have a broadband expansion project to fund
Project must serve unserved rural residents and businesses
Applicant must submit completed application for federal funding program
Project must meet all federal program requirements and terms and conditions
Project must be able to provide minimum internet connectivity of 1000 Mbps down and 1000 Mbps up with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds (unless federal funding program is more restrictive)
Response must include cover letter with authorized representative contact information
Must complete and sign the Grant Application Form
Must provide business model summary, team experience statement, network design and construction description, customer profile, and implementation schedule
No reimbursement will be made for costs incurred in responding to the RFP or developing submissions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should submit one electronic copy of their response to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with the applicant name and 'Federal Funding Assistance RFP response' in the subject line. Response should include: cover letter with local jurisdiction and partner contact information, completed and signed Grant Application Form, business model summary, team experience statement, network design and construction description, customer profile, and implementation schedule. The OSB will evaluate responses to determine partnerships and funding allocations on a rolling basis. Evaluation is based on qualifications, evaluation of submittals, and possible interview. structured_extraction.program_name: SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) Loan Participation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development designed to assist small businesses with working capital and owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation. The program offers below-market interest rates and can lend up to $5 million to qualifying businesses for new space or expansion opportunities. Priority is given to very small businesses and those owned or operated by Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Senior or Junior Debt loans ranging from $350,000 to $5,000,000 with up to 30% program match. Interest rates are determined by underwriting analysis. Loan terms are flexible up to 30 years depending on use and loan amount. A private capital match is required with a target ratio of 4:1 (80-20) for non-SEDI/VSB businesses and 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI/VSB businesses, with a minimum required match of 1:1. An application fee of $250 and closing fee of $250 apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses operating in Maryland with fewer than 500 employees. Priority is given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and businesses owned or operated by Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI) who own or operate for-profit or nonprofit Maryland-based small businesses. Local governments are not eligible applicants.
