structured_extraction.program_name: SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks Loan to Lender Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program designed exclusively for Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) to relend to small businesses, combined with required private capital match. The program provides targeted loans up to $500,000 to CDFIs (with overall CDFI loan amounts ranging from $2,000,000 to $15,000,000 based on CDFI capacity), with a focus on businesses owned and operated by Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI), very small businesses (fewer than 10 employees), and businesses located in CDFI Investment Areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SSBCI Loans to CDFIs ranging from $2,000,000 to $15,000,000 based on CDFI capacity and ability to leverage private capital match. DHCD proposes funding structure with 20% SSBCI funds and 80% private match capital for non-SEDI and non-VSB businesses, and 30% SSBCI funds and 70% private match capital for SEDI and VSB businesses. SSBCI Loans bear interest at 0%-2% with terms up to 7 years and annual renewal options. CDFIs must provide 20% at-risk capital. Small business loans (SBLs) from CDFIs to end borrowers cannot exceed $250,000 unless DHCD provides prior written approval, with interest rates capped at 18%, terms up to 5 years (longer for asset acquisition), combined origination fee and points not to exceed 1%, and application fees not to exceed $100. SBL repayments may be recycled into new SBLs or used to repay SSBCI Loans. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis with draw-down periods beginning on closing date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) seeking capital to relend to small businesses, particularly those owned and operated by Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI), very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees, and businesses located in CDFI Investment Areas. Includes startup, newly established, and growing small businesses including nonprofit organizations and small businesses as defined by the U.S. Small Business Administration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: For CDFIs: Capital for relending to small businesses. For end borrowers (SBLs): Working capital, marketing/planning/feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payments, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment acquisition, and certain other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business. Ineligible uses include residential or transient living businesses, multifamily or single-family housing, nursing homes, assisted living facilities, community halls, fire stations, hospitals, colleges, universities, adult entertainment facilities, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, and tattoo parlors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; priority focus on CDFI Investment Areas as defined in 12 C.F.R. § 1805.201(b)(3)(ii). Treasury requires 34.46% of SSBCI funds to be expended on very small businesses and SEDI businesses combined.

structured_extraction.program_name: SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks Venture Funds Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An equity investment program dedicated to funding and growing the next generation of outstanding early-stage businesses in Maryland. structured_extraction.program_description: The Section 811 Project Rental Assistance Program is a federally funded program that expands affordable housing for low-income adults with disabilities. It provides project-based rental assistance tied to specific units in approved rental housing, linking affordable housing with supportive services and allowing participants to live independently in the community. Operated through a partnership between the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD), and the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), the program subsidizes rent so that tenants pay no more than 30% of their income for rent and utilities, with the program paying the remaining rent directly to the landlord. Eligible residents are adults aged 18 to under 62 who have qualifying disabilities, receive Medicaid, and have household income at or below 30% of the Area Median Income (AMI). The program aims to transform and increase housing for extremely low-income persons with disabilities while making available appropriate support and services through collaborative state-level strategies.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides long-term project-based rental assistance to subsidize the contract rent of eligible participants in multifamily rental housing properties with at least 5 units. Tenants pay no more than 30% of their income for rent and utilities combined; the program pays the remaining contract rent directly to the landlord through Rental Assistance Payments. The tenant's rental payment is calculated based on the tenant's income and adjusted only when income changes. Rent adjustments to the contract rent are made annually based on HUD's Operating Cost Adjustment Factor (OCAF) or other HUD-approved operating cost indices. Initial lease terms are typically 1 year. Properties must receive financing through federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC) or State Rental Housing Funds. DHCD awards Section 811 PRA funds through Cooperative Agreements and executes Rental Assistance Contracts (RACs) with eligible property owners. Vacancy payments may be provided to owners when a PRA unit remains vacant despite timely and reasonable efforts to cooperate with referrals. Administrative costs are allowable at up to 8% of the total amount awarded for planning, infrastructure, technology, and program administration costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rental housing properties with at least 5 units that serve low-income adults with disabilities, and individuals with disabilities aged 18 to under 62 who are Medicaid recipients with very low income (at or below 30% of Area Median Income). Also serves non-profit and for-profit sponsors and owners of affordable rental housing developments seeking to integrate permanent supportive housing for persons with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Project-based rental assistance to subsidize the contract rent of eligible participants in approved multifamily rental housing properties, including rental payments and utilities for program participants. Administrative costs (up to 8% of award) for planning and other costs associated with developing and operating the Section 811 PRA program, including infrastructure and technology needed to administer the program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Historically, distribution has included approximately 75% of units in the Baltimore and Washington D.C. metropolitan areas and 25% on the Eastern Shore and Western Maryland, though this distribution may change as the program evolves. All properties must be located in Priority Funding Areas. DHCD will strive to limit PRA units in any housing development to no more than 20% to increase integration and expand housing choice.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Property Owners: Applications are submitted through a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) process. DHCD meets with an Interagency Committee (including representatives from MDOD and MDH) to review projects that align with program goals and serve the target population. Once a project is selected, DHCD issues a Reservation Award Letter to the developer/owner confirming the property is eligible for funding to support unit subsidies. The owner must then execute a Rental Assistance Contract (RAC) with DHCD and a Use Agreement recorded in local land records. The property owner must have written tenant selection procedures approved by DHCD and consistent with the DHCD Referral and Tenant Selection Plan for Section 811 PRA. For Individuals Seeking Rental Assistance: Interested individuals should contact their case manager, support planner, resource coordinator, coordinator of community services, or community health worker to complete pre-screening and application. Referrals are made by the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD) from a maintained referral list based on priority criteria including: Priority 1 - Institutionalized Medicaid recipients; Priority 2 - At risk of institutionalization due to current housing situation; Priority 3 - DDA Community Pathways Waiver participants moving to independent renting, Behavioral Health Administration participants, Brain Injury waiver participants, or Home and Community-based Options waiver participants; Priority 4 - Medicaid recipients who are homeless. MDOD works closely with property owners to ensure timely referrals, beginning outreach 6-9 months before initial occupancy for new construction/substantial rehabilitation. For existing properties, outreach begins when vacancies are anticipated. Documentation for referral must be complete and delivered to the property manager at least 90 days in advance of anticipated move-in. Contact MDOD at 410-767-3660 or 1-800-637-4113 for application details and referral information. Contact DHCD at dhcd.targetedprograms@maryland.gov for property owner/developer inquiries.

The program supports neighborhood improvement in Sustainable Communities and areas of blight, generating jobs, strengthening partnerships between anchor institutions and their surrounding communities, and creating safer, healthier, and more attractive communities. Funded projects may include construction of facilities for workforce training, skilled trades education, and entrepreneurship programs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shelter and Transitional Housing Facilities Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to nonprofit organizations and local governments to improve, create, and equip transitional housing and emergency shelters that provide supportive services to reduce homelessness in Maryland. The program provides capital financing for emergency shelters and transitional housing facilities that provide housing and support services to households to prevent homelessness and assist households to be able to live independently.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants support new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters. Grant funds typically cover up to one-half of total project costs, though under certain conditions may cover up to 75 percent of costs. Eligible project activities include acquiring land and buildings, site preparation, cost of labor and materials for construction and rehabilitation, acquisition of necessary machinery and equipment (including HVAC systems), architectural and engineering services, and fees and premiums normally incurred in real estate development. Recipients must maintain the project as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years; if discontinued earlier, the grant must be repaid. Ineligible uses include refinancing existing debt, operating assistance, salaries and wages, administrative or legal costs, and maintenance.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters that include supportive services. Program funds may be used for acquiring land and buildings, site preparation, cost of labor and materials for construction and rehabilitation, acquisition of machinery and equipment installed at the project (including HVAC systems and household equipment), architectural and engineering services, and fees and premiums normally incurred in real estate development.

Applicants must provide a letter from local government certifying project location in a PFA. Local government letters of support are required for all projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: The STAR Program is a loan program designed to preserve and improve single-family properties by bringing them up to applicable building codes and standards or a minimum housing quality standard. The program provides zero-percent interest, fully deferred loans to low-income homeowners for rehabilitation of owner-occupied single-family homes. STAR loans may also be used to build replacement houses under certain conditions. STAR loans are funded with federal HOME funds and certain HUD requirements apply.

list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

The maximum loan is generally 100 percent of the value of the property statewide, and up to 110 percent of the after-rehab value of the property in Frederick County. Exceptions to the debt-to-value limit will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Loans are secured by a mortgage. Grants may also be considered on a case-by-case basis in Frederick County. Loans may be made for up to 30 years. Interest rates may range from 0% to 6% based on applicant's ability to pay, with lower rates available for households at or below 50% of HUD median income limits.

STAR loans may also be used to build replacement houses under certain conditions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Strategic Demolition Fund seeks to catalyze activities that accelerate economic development and job creation in existing Maryland communities. The fund aims to improve the economic viability of 'greyfield development' (redevelopment of previously developed land), which often faces more barriers than 'green field development' (development of undeveloped land). Since funds are limited, awards focus on projects that can have a high economic and revitalization impact in their existing communities. The program provides capital funding for strategic demolition of vacant and abandoned properties in eligible Sustainable Communities and Opportunity Zones statewide.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Sustainable Communities Program is a state designation program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) that supports community development, revitalization, and sustainability through coordinated strategies. It provides local governments with resources to improve older communities and promote growth that is environmentally, economically, and socially responsible. The program combines resources for historic preservation, housing, and economic development, focusing on infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, and development that strengthens existing communities. Designated areas become eligible to apply for state revitalization funding and programs such as Community Legacy and the Strategic Demolition Fund. All state-designated Transit Oriented Development areas approved after 2023 automatically constitute Sustainable Community Areas. The designation is valid for five years and can be renewed. In Howard County and other jurisdictions, the designation also unlocks eligibility for local funding, tax credits, and other financial incentives for property owners, businesses, non-profits, and community organizations within designated areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a geographic designation that enables local governments to access coordinated state resources for revitalization and sustainability initiatives. Designated communities become eligible to apply for state programs including Community Legacy Program, Strategic Demolition Fund, Neighborhood BusinessWorks, Operating Assistance Grants, National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund, Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Program, Main Street Maryland Program, Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI), Maryland Façade Improvement Program (MFIP), Job Creation Tax Credit, Enhanced Local Tax Increment Financing (TIF) Authority, Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC), Sustainable Maryland Certified, Water Quality Financing Administration Programs, State Highway Administration Programs, Sidewalk Retrofit Program, and Kim Lamphier Bikeways Network Program. The designation also unlocks eligibility for state and local revitalization funding, tax credits, and other financial incentives targeted at community improvement and development projects. For example, the Job Creation Tax Credit provides up to $5,000 per new job for Sustainable Communities (compared to $3,000 in other areas), with a lower threshold of 25 jobs created (compared to 60 jobs). LIHTC applications for projects in Sustainable Communities receive additional points in the Community Context category. The designation is valid for five years and can be renewed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - applications accepted upon request. Renewal applications must be submitted on or before the expiration date of the Sustainable Communities designation.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Tynan Stevenson (for new designations); Olivia Ceccarelli-McGonigal (for renewal applications)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (municipal or county) seeking to designate community areas for revitalization and sustainability initiatives. Once designated, property owners, businesses, non-profits, and community organizations located within designated Sustainable Community areas may access associated funding and incentives.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The designation enables access to state and local resources and programs supporting historic preservation, housing development, economic development, infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, strengthening of existing communities, support for nonprofit organizations, strengthening older commercial districts and residential communities, and improving public amenities. Revitalization, community development, and environmental improvement projects within designated Sustainable Community areas are all eligible uses. Specific eligible project types include: business retention and attraction, mixed-use development, streetscape improvements, gap financing for new or expanding small businesses and nonprofits, demolition and land assembly for housing and revitalization projects, building restoration and adaptive re-use, parking facilities, affordable or mixed-income housing, public infrastructure, environmental remediation, historic preservation and rehabilitation, and green infrastructure projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All proposed Sustainable Communities areas must be within a Priority Funding Area and within or near a town center or transportation center. The entire area must be within a Priority Funding Area and demonstrate a targeted approach. Areas must demonstrate financial need for local revitalization. All state-designated Transit Oriented Development areas approved after 2023 automatically constitute Sustainable Community Areas. In Howard County, eligibility is specifically within designated Sustainable Community areas.
requirements_list: Entire area must be within a Priority Funding Area
Proposed community must be within or near a town center or transportation center, OR there is a need for financing assistance for small businesses, nonprofit organizations or microenterprises
Must show financial need for local revitalization
Area must have documented financial need for local revitalization
Must include support for nonprofit organizations and strengthening older commercial districts and residential communities
Must show need for improving public amenities
Must have a defined geographic area with existing built environment requiring revitalization or additional state investment
Must submit a Sustainable Community Action Plan summarizing key initiatives and projects
Action Plan must address six key elements: Environment, Economy, Transportation, Housing, Community Health and Quality of Life, and Local Planning and Staffing Capacity
Plan must be consistent with other existing community or comprehensive plans
Must have local government resolution supporting both boundary designation and Action Plan
Must reconvene or maintain a Sustainable Communities Workgroup
Project or property must be located within a designated Sustainable Community area (for local incentive eligibility)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For new designations: 1. Contact Tynan Stevenson at tynan.stevenson@maryland.gov or 410-209-5811 with subject line indicating 'New Designation' and the community name. 2. Schedule a meeting with program staff before applying. 3. Submit application including defined geographic area, Sustainable Community Action Plan, and local government resolution. 4. An interagency panel led by DHCD reviews the application. 5. The panel presents the application to the Governor's Smart Growth Subcabinet for final approval. 6. Once approved, the designation is valid for five years and can be renewed. For renewal applications: 1. Contact Olivia Ceccarelli-McGonigal at olivia.ceccarelli@maryland.gov or 410-209-5826 to schedule a mandatory application consultation session. 2. Reconvene the Sustainable Communities Workgroup to discuss accomplishments, challenges, and updates to the Action Plan. 3. Submit renewal application including updated contact information, demographic information, organizational capacity assessment, report on accomplishments from past five years, and updated Action Plan with six elements. 4. Submit all materials via email including application, maps (PDF), photos (JPEG), GIS shapefiles, and CD-ROM with digital copies. 5. An interagency review team led by DHCD evaluates the application based on strengths, weaknesses, and connection of outcomes to local conditions. 6. The Governor's Smart Growth Coordinating Committee makes approval on recommendation of the interagency team. 7. Approved designations are valid for five years and can be renewed again.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Technical Assistance Grant (TAG) program assists nonprofit organizations and local governments with operating costs associated with community and economic revitalization efforts. The program provides funding to support operating and technical assistance costs for housing and community and economic revitalization projects and/or initiatives located in or serving designated Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $50,000 with no required funding match. Funds cover operating costs including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses. Capital project costs are not supported. Projects should be completed within one year. An initial advance of up to 25% of the total award amount is permitted for the first payment request without supporting documentation; subsequent payment requests must include evidence of expenditures such as paid invoices, contracts, or other documentation to substantiate reimbursement. The grant term is one year from the date the award agreement is signed by DHCD. Funds cannot be drawn down until after award agreement execution and all special conditions have been met.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and local governments in Maryland engaged in community and economic revitalization activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs associated with administering housing and community revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and related administrative expenses. Funds may be used for staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, and placemaking initiatives. Capital project costs are not supported. Funds cannot be used for alcohol, controlled substances, entertainment, personal items, fines, or costs for travel companions not on the team.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas. Organizations and/or projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) to be eligible. Additional consideration given to projects in ENOUGH areas and Just Communities.
requirements_list: Eligible applicants must be nonprofit organizations or local governments in Maryland engaged in community and economic revitalization activities
Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area
Organizations must be in full compliance with all existing award agreements, including meeting all reporting deadlines and submitting all required final reports and payment requests from prior awards
Projects and/or initiatives should align with local Sustainable Community Action Plans and/or support activities related to capital projects receiving funds from other Department or state agencies
Maximum grant request is $50,000
All projects or activities should be completed within one year
No matching funds are required
Funds cannot be used for capital project costs
Organization profile must include all required documents before submitting application

Nonprofit applicants must submit evidence of nonprofit status (Bylaws, Articles of Incorporation, IRS Determination Letter), evidence of good standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and evidence of charitable registration from Maryland Secretary of State
For projects involving acquisition, demolition, construction, or rehabilitation, site control must be established at the time of award agreement execution
Awardees must disclose any actual or potential conflicts of interest
Awardees must complete a corporate diversity affidavit per HB 1210
Awardees must draw down at least 50% of awarded funds within six months of award execution date
All awarded funds must be drawn down by the award agreement's expiration date
A progress report is due 6 months from the grant agreement execution date or whenever a payment request is submitted
Final report is due no later than 30 days after the award agreement's expiration date
Records must be retained for a minimum of three years after official close-out of the award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register as a new user in the DHCD Project Portal by selecting 'New User?' and completing the registration form (approval may take up to 72 hours). New organizations should request access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. Ensure your organization profile includes all required documents (for nonprofits: evidence of nonprofit status, good standing, and charitable registration). Submit your application through the Project Portal by the stated deadline. All applications must be submitted online through the DHCD Project Portal; late applications will not be accepted. For first-time applicants, contact your assigned project manager for eligibility verification and system access. TAG applications will be evaluated using a 5-point scoring scale reflecting overall application strength and readiness. Bonus points may be awarded: projects in ENOUGH areas receive up to 10 bonus points, projects in Just Communities receive 10 bonus points. Virtual training and step-by-step application guides are available in the Project Portal.

structured_extraction.program_name: UPLIFT (Utilizing Progressive Lending Investments to Finance Transformation)
structured_extraction.program_description: UPLIFT helps close the appraisal gap in historically redlined and disinvested communities by providing funding to cover the difference between the cost to build or renovate affordable housing and what the property can sell for on the market. This enables qualified development teams to acquire, develop, build, and sell quality affordable homes in targeted neighborhoods. The program also couples development loans with a commitment from DHCD to offer grants and loans to nearby 'Legacy Homeowners,' often living in energy inefficient and deteriorated housing, with the aim of building household wealth and elevating property values.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State covers the appraisal gap (the difference between the cost to build or renovate a property and the price it can sell for on the market) through UPLIFT development loans and homeowner financing. Selected development teams use a combination of public and private financing to acquire, develop, build, and sell quality affordable housing. Development loans are provided with terms including an origination fee of 1% of the loan amount (paid at initial closing). Homebuyers acquire fee simple title using a combination of down payment, down payment assistance, first mortgage loans (e.g., Maryland Mortgage Program), and a soft promissory note from the Department representing the appraisal gap. The program also provides grants and loans to nearby Legacy Homeowners to improve existing housing and build household wealth. A non-refundable application fee of $1,000 per project is required at submission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit developers and builders engaged in homeownership production in targeted low-income census tracts and Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding is used to close the appraisal gap for quality affordable housing development and construction in targeted neighborhoods, enabling homes to be sold at prices affordable to targeted households. Funds help with costs to acquire, develop, build, and sell affordable homes. Development costs include acquisition, construction, professional/third-party fees, and developer fees. Homebuyers use assistance for down payment support and to bridge the gap between development costs and market sales prices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Low-Income Census Tracts (where 50% of households have incomes below 60% of Area Median Income or poverty rate is 25% or more) AND areas designated as Maryland Sustainable Communities. Specific qualified areas can be viewed on the UPLIFT Qualified Areas Map. New construction projects are not permitted in FEMA Flood Zone A, but may be considered in Zone C or X with appropriate waivers and flood mitigation documentation.
requirements_list: Must be located in Low-Income Census Tract and designated Sustainable Community
Projects must consist of newly constructed or substantially rehabilitated formerly vacant structures
Must submit Pre-Application Meeting Request Form before applying and complete pre-application meeting
Must submit required documentation at least two business days before pre-application meeting
Must submit Electronic Application Submission Request Form after pre-app meeting to receive Dropbox access
Must complete full application with all seven parts: General Elements, Development Team, Project Economics, Project Location, Design and Construction, Marketing and Sales, Neighborhood Engagement
Must prepare two application copies: one electronic and one hard copy
Must pay $1,000 non-refundable application fee per project at submission (via ACH or check)
Must submit hard copy application to Brien O'Toole, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706
Projects must meet UPLIFT Design and Construction Standards
Projects must comply with New Construction or Rehabilitation Cost Limits
Development team must have minimum experience as significant participant in comparably scaled projects
Development team must meet financial capacity requirements with acceptable credit history
Developer entities and guarantors must submit audited, reviewed, or compiled financial statements per GAAP
Projects must demonstrate site control
All environmental assessments must be current (less than twelve months old)
Projects must demonstrate neighborhood engagement plan alignment
Projects must meet Energy Star, Enterprise Green Communities, LEED, Earthcraft, or NGBS Green Promise standards
Lead Developer must have determinative/controlling position in project entity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 0: Review UPLIFT Program Guide; compile project details, timelines, plans, and logistics; schedule and complete Pre-Application Meeting with DHCD staff; submit required pre-application materials at least two business days before meeting date. Step 1: After pre-app meeting, complete UPLIFT Electronic Application Submission Request Form; upon DHCD internal review, receive Dropbox folder access. Step 2: Download Application Documents Package from UPLIFT website; complete all seven application parts (General Elements, Development Team, Project Economics, Project Location, Design and Construction, Marketing and Sales, Neighborhood Engagement) using provided Excel templates and narrative documents. Step 3: Pay $1,000 non-refundable application fee via ACH or check; include proof of payment. Step 4: Upload all completed documents to Dropbox in correct subfolders; complete and sign Final Submission Checklist; deliver hard copy application and checklist in person to DHCD Operations & Administration Office, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Step 5: DHCD conducts threshold review to verify compliance with Threshold Criteria and evaluation against Evaluative Scoring Criteria (Development Team Capacity, Project Impact, Leveraging and Cost Effectiveness, Readiness to Proceed, Development Quality, State Bonus Points). Step 6: Applications passing threshold are scored; recommendations made by UPLIFT Loan Committee to Secretary. Step 7: If approved, DHCD issues Commitment Letter specifying terms and conditions. Step 8: Selected projects enter underwriting pipeline; Kick-off Meeting held 45-60 days after complete application submission to determine underwriting schedule. Step 9: Final Underwriting Submission updates financing, design, construction, and marketing elements. Step 10: Upon underwriting approval, Secretary authorizes commitment of resources; office of Attorney General represents Department at initial closing. Step 11: Construction Kick-off Meeting held to coordinate construction phase, marketing, and occupancy requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP) is the largest residential energy conservation program in the country. WAP assists income-eligible homeowners and renters in Maryland by reducing heating and cooling costs through free energy-conservation measures, while also addressing health and safety issues in their homes. The program is designed to lower energy bills by an average of 30 to 35 percent through improvements such as insulation, air sealing, and heating system upgrades. The program is administered statewide through local weatherization agencies and is also accessible through the Maryland Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) one-stop-shop application process.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free energy efficiency and weatherization improvements to eligible homes at no cost to participants. Services include blower door air infiltration reduction; insulation in attics, floors, walls, basements, and crawl spaces; caulking and air sealing around windows, doors, and other openings; hot water system improvements including wrapping of hot water heaters and pipes; lighting retrofit; furnace cleaning, tune-up, burner retrofit or replacement; and health and safety repairs. No lien or claim is filed against the home. The program utilizes Hancock Energy Software (HES) and Hancock Energy Audit Tool (MINT/HEAT) for tracking all stages of work in real-time. Quality control inspections are performed on 100% of completed units. Applicants to OHEP programs are automatically referred to WAP unless they opt out. Households are also screened upon completion of the one-stop-shop energy programs application. The program leverages different funding sources including DOE WAP Formula Funds, BIL (Bipartisan Infrastructure Law) funds, EmPOWER Maryland funds, and LIHEAP funds to maximize service delivery.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling application; ongoing program accepting applications at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible homeowners and renters in Maryland. Priority is given to persons older than 60, those with disabilities, those with children in the home (including families with children under 5 years old), households with high energy usage or energy burden, particularly vulnerable populations such as the elderly, and low-income households referred through OHEP programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy conservation and weatherization improvements including blower door air infiltration reduction; insulation of attics, floors, walls, basements, and crawl spaces; caulking and air sealing around windows, doors, and other openings; hot water system improvements and pipe wrapping; lighting retrofit; furnace cleaning, tune-up, and replacement; HVAC and domestic water heating equipment removal and replacement with high efficiency equipment; structural repairs; installation of thermostats, carbon monoxide detectors, and smoke detectors; and health and safety measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland through local weatherization agencies serving all 24 Maryland counties and Baltimore City. Each county/jurisdiction has designated Local Weatherization Agencies (LWAs). Geographic service areas include: Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. Prince George's County residents can also access services through the Maryland Office of Energy Efficiency at 844-400-3423 or 1-800-756-0119.
requirements_list: Household income must not exceed 60% of State Median Income (SMI) or 200% of Federal Poverty Level (FPL), whichever is higher
Automatically income-eligible if currently receiving Utility Bill Pay Assistance, SNAP, TANF, SSI, or HUD housing assistance
Must submit an application to apply for services
Must schedule an energy audit inspection once eligibility is determined
Must qualify for OHEP programs (if applying via OHEP referral pathway)
Must not opt out of WAP on OHEP application (if applying via OHEP)
Must prove homeownership (for homeowner applicants in Prince George's County)
Cannot have received prior weatherization services through Prince George's County WAP or MD Office of Energy Efficiency (Prince George's County applicants)
Home must be structurally sound
Tenants must have landlord authorization for weatherization work
Property owners must enter into contracts with subgrantees for services to be provided
Households must meet categorical eligibility or income eligibility verification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Local Weatherization Agency (LWA) by calling 1-855-583-8976 to submit an application. The local weatherization agency will contact you to verify income eligibility within 30 days. Once eligibility is determined, the local weatherization agency will schedule an energy audit inspection. An energy auditor will conduct a comprehensive home evaluation identifying all possible energy saving opportunities and modeling a feasible improvements package. If the dwelling condition permits, energy improvements will be provided at no cost. Quality control inspections are performed on 100% of completed units. Alternatively, applicants to OHEP programs are automatically referred to WAP when they complete the one-stop-shop energy programs application, unless they opt out. In Prince George's County, call 844-400-3423 or 1-800-756-0119 to apply for services through the Maryland Office of Energy Efficiency.

structured_extraction.program_description: A targeted investment that expands access to healthy and fresh foods in Maryland communities experiencing food insecurity by providing direct grants to eligible food retailers to support operations, facility improvements, and inventory expansion.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $25,000 to $150,000 with up to $2 million in total funding available. A $250 processing fee is required for all applications; if approved for funding, the fee may be deducted from the awarded grant funds. Funds support improved healthy food access through equipment purchases (furniture, fixtures, refrigeration, shelving, etc.), buildout and facility upgrades, capital costs for inventory expansion, initial inventory costs, working capital tied to expansion or construction, and infrastructure and technology for SNAP/EBT. Additionally, applicants may request supplemental loan funding through DHCD's Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) business development division, which will undergo a thorough financial review to assess debt management capacity.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit or nonprofit food retailers — including grocery stores, corner stores, co-ops, farm stands, farmers' markets, delivery retailers, and small food-focused stores — serving communities with a Maryland Community Business Compass Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher. Businesses must employ a maximum of 500 workers and be registered in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases such as furniture, fixtures, refrigeration and shelving, buildout and facility upgrades, facility renovations, capital costs for inventory expansion, initial inventory costs (non-prepared foods), working capital tied to expansion or construction, and infrastructure and technology for SNAP/EBT acceptance and setup.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher, defined as any area with a score of 60% or higher pursuant to Annotated Code of Maryland - Housing and Community Development Article §6–308. Exceptions may be granted on an individual basis. Your business does not need to be listed on the Maryland Community Business Compass to be eligible. If you don't see your business on the Maryland Community Business Compass and would like to add it, email compass@maryland.gov.
requirements_list: For-profit or nonprofit food retailer
Serve a community with Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher
Operate at least 5 days per week, year round (farmer's markets and on-farm markets exempt from 5-day requirement but must operate year round)
Employ a maximum of 500 workers
Registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Currently or plan to offer fresh, frozen, or minimally processed healthy foods
Dedicate at least 20% of inventory or food-sales space to healthy food items based on square footage of food display space or dollar value of inventory for sale
Must meet SNAP eligibility or plan to adopt SNAP functionality
Submit a detailed written plan describing how grant funds will be used (not to exceed 2 pages)
Provide information demonstrating how the business meets or will meet NourishMD's healthy and fresh food criteria
Submit one year of business tax returns or audited financial statements (or alternative documentation if operating less than one year)
If applicable, provide relocation and expansion documentation such as lease agreement, letter of intent, or proof of site control
A $250 processing fee is required for all applications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a complete application through the DHCD online portal including all required documentation (use of funds plan, healthy food criteria information, financial documentation, and relocation/expansion documentation if applicable). The application window opened January 20, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. EST and closed February 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EST. No applications are accepted after the deadline. DHCD staff evaluate eligible applications for completeness, impact, and alignment with program priorities February–March 2026, and refer the final list of eligible applications to the Review Committee (comprised of representatives from DHCD Division of Business Development, Maryland Department of Agriculture, Maryland Department of Health, and DHCD Division of Neighborhood Revitalization) for determinations. Funding recommendations are finalized in April 2026, award announcements and notifications are made in May 2026, and the Board of Public Works approves grants with disbursements made in June 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides housing and other financial assistance to former foster youth. If you were in foster care until age 18 and are currently under 21 years old and need housing or other assistance, you may be eligible to receive financial assistance for room and board from the Department of Social Services. Services include housing assistance, financial assistance for utilities and emergency items, employment assistance, educational assistance, and other support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance provided to eligible former foster youth for multiple purposes including: housing assistance (rent/room and board, security deposits, eviction prevention, household items/furniture), financial assistance (utility bills, emergency clothing and personal items), employment assistance (job readiness training, job search support), educational assistance (GED enrollment, college enrollment, FAFSA assistance, college tuition waiver information, college prep exams), and other supports (substance abuse/addiction referrals, mental health referrals, food assistance, day care referral, obtaining government documents, community support/mentoring, budgeting and independent living skills).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Former foster youth who were in foster care until age 18 and are currently under 21 years old.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Room and board expenses, utility bills, security deposits, household items, furniture, emergency clothing and personal items, job training, educational enrollment and preparation, medical care, food, day care, and other independent living support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through DSS offices in your area. Baltimore City Department of Social Services located at 3007 East Biddle Street, Baltimore, Maryland 21213.
requirements_list: Were in foster care until age 18
Currently under 21 years old
Need housing or other assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Aftercare Services Application Form with detailed information about your education, employment, current housing, health, and specific services needed. Submit to your local DSS office or Independent Living Coordinator. Categories of assistance include: Housing Assistance (eviction notice, rent/room and board, security deposit, household items/furniture), Financial Assistance (BGE/utility turn-off, water bill, emergency clothing and personal items), Employment Assistance (job readiness training, job search), Educational Assistance (GED enrollment, college enrollment, FAFSA, college tuition waiver information, college prep exams), and Other Supports (substance abuse/addiction referrals, mental health referrals, food, day care, obtaining government documents, community support, budgeting and independent living skills).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Arrearage Retirement Assistance Program helps eligible low-income customers reduce or eliminate large, past-due electric and gas bills through grants. Administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), the program provides financial assistance to customers who have accumulated significant arrears on their utility accounts. If eligible, customers can receive a grant paid directly to their electric or gas utility company to retire unpaid balances.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible customers may receive a grant of up to $2,000 towards their past-due electric bill and up to $1,000 towards their past-due gas bill. The grant amount is determined by the outstanding arrearage and is sent directly to the utility company. Customers must have a past-due bill of $300 or greater to be considered eligible. Customers may only receive an arrearage grant once every five years, with certain exceptions. Arrearage grants received between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2021 do not count towards the five-year limitation. Customers must also be eligible to receive an Energy Utility Service Program (EUSP) grant.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Year-round program with no deadline. You can apply at any time during the year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households in Maryland with past-due electric or gas bills of $300 or greater
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of past-due electric and gas utility bills
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. In Prince George's County, applicants can apply online, by email, by mail, or by fax through the Prince George's County Department of Social Services, Office of Home Energy Programs, 805 Brightseat Road, Landover, Maryland 20785 (fax: 301-909-6331). In-person assistance available at 425 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785.
requirements_list: Must have a past-due bill of $300 or greater
Must meet Energy Assistance program income eligibility requirements
Must be eligible to receive a EUSP grant
Must have an outstanding electric or gas utility arrearage
May only receive an arrearage grant once every five years, with certain exceptions
Arrearage grants received between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2021 do not count towards the five-year limitation
Must provide required documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply using the same application methods as the Energy Assistance program: submit a paper application to a secure drop box, apply online through MarylandBenefits.gov or dhs.maryland.gov/office-of-home-energy-programs/, apply by mail, call an Energy Assistance office, or apply in person. In Prince George's County, applicants may also apply by email to pgcdss.energy@maryland.gov or by fax to 301-909-6331. After approval and processing, the grant is sent directly to the utility company. Applicants can check the status of their application at myohepstatus.maryland.gov.

AOP staff lead outreach activities statewide to ensure that new and existing asylee populations are aware of their eligibility for programming funded by MORA and others.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides limited financial help with funeral expenses for deceased recipients of Public Assistance programs when their families cannot afford funeral costs. A cash benefit is paid directly to the funeral director when the deceased individual was already receiving assistance or met the eligibility requirements of a Department of Human Services program, including Foster Care, Public Assistance to Adults (PAA), Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), Medical Assistance (MA), or Supplemental Security Income (SSI). Newborn children not receiving TCA may also be eligible. Certain expenses are excluded from coverage, including burial plots, vaults, grave digging, and burial clothing, and funds cannot be used to reimburse expenses already paid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A cash benefit is provided directly to the funeral director to help cover funeral expenses for eligible deceased individuals. Covered expenses include items such as casket, service fees, and transportation. Excluded from coverage are burial plots, vaults, grave digging, and burial clothing. Burial assistance funds cannot be used towards reimbursement of expenses already paid.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families of deceased individuals who were receiving or were eligible for Public Assistance programs administered by the Department of Human Services, including Foster Care, Public Assistance to Adults (PAA), Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), Medical Assistance (MA), and Supplemental Security Income (SSI). Also includes families of newborn children who were not receiving TCA.

Eligible programs include Foster Care, Public Assistance to Adults (PAA), Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), Medical Assistance (MA), or Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
Newborn children not receiving TCA may also be eligible

Verification of assets required

structured_extraction.program_description: Ensures that local communities on Maryland's Eastern Shore are connected with available resources, comprehensive assistance, federal and state benefits they may be eligible for, and essential support to overcome barriers and become self-sufficient. Services are culturally informed, linguistically appropriate, and trauma sensitive.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Case management, application support for financial, medical, or nutritional assistance, employment and job placement assistance, career counseling, training and skill-building, English language instruction, youth programming, psycho-social support, immigration-related legal assistance, and other services.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugees and asylees on Maryland's Eastern Shore
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management, employment assistance, training, education, legal assistance, and support services
