structured_extraction.program_name: Commodity Supplemental Food Program (CSFP) / My Groceries To Go!
structured_extraction.program_description: The program reduces food insecurity for seniors 60 and older by providing monthly food packages valued at approximately $50. Seniors can pick up packages through a food bank or local sponsor, have an authorized designee pick them up, or receive delivery in some communities. The program helps seniors avoid choosing between healthy food and other necessities like medicine or rent, and reduces costly hospitalizations and nursing home stays. The program is funded by the USDA and aims to improve the health of low-income elderly persons by supplementing their diets with nutritious USDA Foods.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) funds monthly food packages valued at approximately $50 per participant. Each package contains nutritious USDA Foods selected to supplement the diets of low-income seniors. The number of seniors served depends on available USDA funding and state caseload allocation. Participants receive pre-packed food packages distributed through local agencies at predetermined distribution sites, through group delivery, home delivery in some communities, or via authorized proxies. Food packages are distributed in accordance with approved food package guide rates on a monthly basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors 60 years or older with incomes at or below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level living in eligible Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly food packages containing healthy, nutritious USDA Foods for household consumption.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available in Allegany County, Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll County, Garrett County, Harford County, Howard County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and Queen Anne's County. The program is expanding beyond its original service area of Baltimore City to serve additional counties with demonstrated need.
requirements_list: Must be 60 years or older

Income must be at or below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level (approximately $15,650 for a single senior based on current guidelines; specific amounts vary by household size as outlined in USDA poverty guidelines)
Must live in an eligible Maryland county (Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, or Queen Anne's)
Must complete application and certification form with acceptable government-issued identification verifying name and age/date of birth
Must verify current address with acceptable proof of residence if not on ID
Household size must be identified on application
Cannot participate in CSFP in another state simultaneously
Must re-certify eligibility annually through simplified re-certification process (every 3 years for full certification)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested seniors should contact one of Maryland's CSFP local agency providers to apply: The Salvation Army Central Maryland Area Command, Capital Area Food Bank, or Allegany County Human Resources Development Commission (AHRDC). Applicants must complete an application and certification form and provide acceptable government-issued identification verifying name, age, and date of birth. Proof of current address is required if address is not on ID. Income must be reported and certified by CSFP staff or trained volunteers. Applicants will be notified of eligibility or ineligibility within 10 days of application date. Ineligible applicants will be notified in writing of their right to a fair hearing to appeal the decision. Once certified, participants receive their monthly food packages at designated distribution sites, through designated proxies, or via home delivery arrangements. Participants must complete simplified re-certification annually (full re-certification every 3 years) to verify address, income, and continued program interest.

structured_extraction.program_description: A job-training and employment support program for non-custodial parents owing child support in Washington County. The program offers free training in industries including welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, and hospitality, with support services to help overcome employment barriers and jumpstart careers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free job-training and support services including hard skills training in in-demand industries, soft skills training in communication and customer service, job readiness preparation, job search and placement assistance, industry-recognized certifications and credentialing, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, resolution of employment barriers (criminal records, legal services, driver's license suspension), access to work-related items (clothing, tools, textbooks), and personal career navigator and success coach support. Participants who successfully complete the program may earn forgiveness for child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-custodial parties (parents) who have a child support case in Washington County and are unemployed or underemployed.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training for careers in welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, and hospitality. Funds support the cost of training, certifications, job readiness, transportation, work clothing, tools, textbooks, and other support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Non-custodial party with a child support case in Washington County
Must complete an employability assessment to determine employment status, employment-related skills, and abilities
Counselors will review employment history, education, literacy levels, communication skills, and career interests
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program coordinator for Washington County to start the enrollment process. Once enrolled, parents will join a training program offered by one of the CAPE participating partners.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that replaces 100% of Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) benefits, including Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), cash assistance, and Pandemic-EBT (P-EBT) benefits, when benefits are stolen or used without the cardholder's permission.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program replaces 100% of stolen EBT and P-EBT benefits. Benefits will be reissued on a new EBT card. The state will make an eligibility decision within 10 business days of claim submission. Stolen benefits dating back to January 1, 2021 are eligible for reimbursement. The program does not require filing a police report to receive reimbursement, though filing one is encouraged.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Claims must be submitted within 45 days of becoming aware of the theft.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families in Maryland who receive Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), cash assistance, or Pandemic-EBT (P-EBT) benefits and have experienced theft or unauthorized use of their EBT card.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of stolen food and cash benefits on an EBT card.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: EBT benefits must have been stolen or used without the cardholder's permission.
Stolen benefits must have occurred on or after January 1, 2021.
Cardholder must not have willingly given their EBT card and PIN to the person who stole the benefits.
Claims must be submitted within 45 days of becoming aware of the theft.
Cardholder must complete and submit an EBT Stolen Benefits Attestation Claim Form.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To receive reimbursement, complete the EBT Stolen Benefits Attestation Claim Form online through the Maryland Benefits portal at marylandbenefits.gov, or submit a paper form in person at your local Department of Social Services office. You may also call one of the SNAP Community Partner Organizations for phone assistance in completing the form. The department will review your claim within 10 business days and notify you of approval or denial. If denied, you may request a Fair Hearing by contacting the Office of Administrative Hearings at 1-800-332-6347 or by completing the Request for Fair Hearing form (DHS/FIA 334). You must request a hearing within 90 days of the date of the notice. If you request a hearing within 10 days of the notice and were receiving benefits, you can continue to receive them while you wait for the hearing decision, unless your benefit period ends.

structured_extraction.program_name: Emergency Assistance to Families with Children (EAFC)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides one-time emergency cash assistance to families with children who need help paying rent, utilities, or facing other emergencies such as eviction or emergency heating/fuel shortages. Funds are available through the local Department of Social Services once every two years (24 months) when funds are available. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Human Services through local departments of social services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time emergency cash assistance provided once every 24 months (two years) per household when funds are available. Assistance is distributed through local departments of social services to help eligible families pay emergency rent, utilities, heating/fuel costs, or other emergency expenses. Funds are available to a household only once in a 24-month period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with one or more children under 21 living with them who are facing an immediate emergency such as eviction, utility cutoff, or heating/fuel shortage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency rent payments, emergency fuel or heating assistance, emergency utility payments, or other emergency needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local Department of Social Services offices.
requirements_list: Must have at least one related child under 21 living in the household
Must present proof of an emergency not caused by a family member quitting a job
Must present an eviction notice, utility cutoff notice, or other proof of emergency
Must provide proof that the household can maintain ongoing monthly rent and utilities
Available to a household only once in a 24-month period
Must provide proof of identification
Must provide proof of address
Must provide proof of income for the past 2 months
All household members receiving services must have a Social Security number
Must provide proof of other cash or non-cash resources
Must provide proof of household expenses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply in person at your local Department of Social Services office during business hours, or file an application by mail, fax, or other electronic means. You can also apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov or have someone drop off an application on your behalf. You will need to provide identification, proof of address, proof of income for the past 2 months, proof of emergency, proof of other resources, Social Security numbers for all household members receiving services, and proof of household expenses.

structured_extraction.program_description: MORA provides employment assistance to help refugees achieve economic self-sufficiency soon after arriving in the United States. Services are delivered through a network of experienced providers and include job readiness training, resume writing, case management, job search assistance, vocational training, interview preparation, transportation assistance, interpretation during interviews, and post-placement support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Job readiness training, resume writing, case management to address employment barriers, job search assistance, vocational training, interview preparation, transportation assistance, interpretation services during job interviews, and post-placement support tailored to individual client needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugees and asylees who are employable and seeking to achieve economic self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment and vocational services including training, job search support, and placement assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services are available in the Baltimore Metropolitan Area, Suburban Washington Area (including Silver Spring and Greenbelt), and Frederick Area.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can enroll in employment programs by contacting one of the MORA grantee providers at their local offices in Baltimore, Silver Spring, Greenbelt, or Frederick.

structured_extraction.program_description: MORA provides free English language classes to help refugees develop English proficiency for faster social integration and economic self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free English language training classes offered online and in-person through partner community colleges. Classes are available to newly arrived refugees in Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and the Baltimore Metropolitan Area.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Baltimore City Community College (BCCC) Refugee Assistance Program; Montgomery College Refugee Training Center; Prince George's Community College (PGCC) English for Refugees and Asylees Program
structured_extraction.program_audience: Newly arrived refugees in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: English language instruction through online and in-person classes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Prince George's County, and Baltimore Metropolitan Area (Baltimore City and surrounding counties)
requirements_list: Must be a newly arrived refugee
Must be residing in eligible counties
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Newly arrived refugees should inquire about this service with their assigned MORA caseworker. Classes are offered through three community college locations with online instruction and in-person testing.

structured_extraction.program_name: Enhanced After Care Voluntary Placement Agreement
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows former Maryland foster youth to re-enter foster care on a voluntary basis so they can continue learning and practicing independent living skills while receiving all services available to youth in out-of-home placement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Youth in enhanced aftercare receive all services provided to youth in out-of-home placement, including housing, support, and independent living skills development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Former Maryland foster youth who left foster care before age 21 and are now working toward self-sufficiency through education, employment, or other approved activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing, support services, and all services available to youth in out-of-home placement to support independent living skills development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through all local departments of social services in Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Youth was in the care and custody or guardianship of a Maryland local department of social services on his or her 18th birthday
Youth left foster care prior to age 21
Youth is not older than 20 years 6 months at the time of application
Youth cannot have exited foster care due to reunification, adoption, guardianship, marriage, or military duty

Must agree to enter into one of the following within 30 days of signing the agreement: completing secondary education or program leading to equivalent credential, enrolled in institution providing post-secondary or vocational training, participating in program or activity to promote employment or remove barriers to unemployment, employed at least 80 hours per month, or incapable of doing any of the above due to a medical condition
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local department of social services to apply for enhanced after care voluntary placement services.

structured_extraction.program_description: Designed to provide ongoing and intensive support and assistance to eligible populations not already receiving such help from other programs. Provides eligible clients with help needed to overcome barriers preventing them from achieving self-sufficiency, social integration, and access to benefits and community resources necessary for success and well-being in the U.S.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Ongoing and intensive case management support to address barriers including lack of childcare, limited transportation, language illiteracy, financial illiteracy or instability, food insecurity, lack of healthcare, inability to obtain or maintain permanent housing, unfamiliarity with U.S. work culture and customs, need for legal or immigration assistance, and others.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ethiopian Community Development Council (ECDC) African Community Center DC Metro, International Rescue Committee (IRC) in Baltimore or Silver Spring, Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area (LSSNCA) in Arbutus, Greenbelt, or Frederick
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugees and asylees not already receiving intensive case management from other programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management support to help clients and their families achieve self-sufficiency and integration goals in the U.S.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland, with grantees in DC Metro area, Baltimore, Silver Spring, and Frederick areas
requirements_list: Must be eligible refugee or asylee population
Not already receiving intensive case management from other programs

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal reimbursement program for individuals who incurred funeral expenses for a deceased person whose death may have been caused by or was likely a result of COVID-19.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FEMA reimburses eligible individuals for funeral expenses incurred for a deceased person whose death may have been caused by or was likely a result of COVID-19. Reimbursement covers eligible funeral expenses including transportation for identifying the deceased, transfer of remains, casket or urn, burial plot or cremation niche, marker or headstone, clergy or officiant services, arrangement of the funeral ceremony, use of funeral home equipment or staff, cremation or interment costs, costs for producing and certifying multiple death certificates, and costs mandated by local or state government laws or ordinances. Only one application per deceased individual is allowed. If multiple people contributed to funeral expenses, they register as applicant and co-applicant on a single application. Applicants cannot resubmit expenses already reimbursed through government agencies, non-profits, voluntary agencies, burial or funeral insurance, though reimbursement from life insurance does not disqualify applicants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: U.S. citizens, legal residents, asylees, refugees, or non-citizen nationals who incurred funeral expenses for a person whose death was related to COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funeral-related expenses including transportation, transfer of remains, casket or urn, burial plot or cremation niche, marker or headstone, clergy services, funeral arrangement, funeral home use, cremation or interment costs, death certificate production and certification, and government-mandated funeral costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide.
requirements_list: Applicant must be U.S. citizen, legal resident, asylee, refugee, or non-citizen national
Death certificate must indicate death 'may have been caused by' or 'was likely a result of' COVID-19 or COVID-19-like symptoms
Applicant or co-applicant must have personally incurred the funeral expenses
Proof of funeral expenses must include applicant name as responsible person, decedent name, expense amount, and that expenses were incurred after January 20, 2020
If outside assistance was received, documentation must be included in application
Cannot resubmit expenses already reimbursed through government agencies, voluntary agencies, non-profits, or burial or funeral insurance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families call the FEMA Funeral Assistance Line at 844-684-6333 (TTY: 800-462-7585) to begin the application process. Applicants must gather required documentation including a death certificate showing COVID-19 causation and proof of funeral expenses. Applicants should decide who will serve as applicant and any co-applicants. Submit documentation to FEMA for reimbursement consideration.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal refundable tax credit for low- to moderate-income working individuals and families that reduces the amount of federal income tax owed or provides a refund. The maximum federal credit is $8,046. Eligibility and credit amount depend on income, family size, and other factors. The Maryland Department of Human Services promotes awareness of this credit as a resource for limited-income workers statewide and provides free tax preparation assistance through certified nonprofit and local agency partners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A refundable federal tax credit with a maximum of $8,046 for eligible working individuals and families. The credit reduces federal income tax liability or provides a refund if the credit exceeds taxes owed. The amount depends on income, family size, and other factors as determined by the IRS. Refunds can be received via direct deposit into up to three separate bank accounts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- to moderate-income working individuals and families, including limited-income workers who worked during the tax year and meet IRS income and family size requirements. Taxpayers with income less than $67,000 in 2024 may qualify for free tax preparation assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces federal income tax liability or provides a tax refund if the credit exceeds taxes owed. Direct deposit available for faster refund processing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Federal program available nationwide, including all counties in Maryland. Free tax preparation sites are available in Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Calvert, Carroll, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Somerset, St. Mary's, and Wicomico counties.
requirements_list: Must have worked and earned income during the tax year
Must meet IRS income requirements (less than $67,000 for 2024 tax year)
Eligibility depends on family size and other factors
Must be a limited-income worker
Must meet IRS income limits
For free tax preparation: must bring Social Security card and photo ID for each taxpayer
For free tax preparation: must bring W-2 forms for all jobs worked in 2024
For free tax preparation: must bring Form 1099-G for unemployment income
For free tax preparation: must bring Form 1095-A for health insurance if applicable
For free tax preparation: must bring child care provider letter with address, Tax ID, child name, and amount paid if applicable
For free tax preparation: must bring banking account information (routing and account numbers) for direct deposit
For free tax preparation: must bring copy of prior year tax return if available
All adults on tax return must come to sign for free tax preparation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: File a federal tax return claiming the EITC. Three options available: (1) File independently using free Direct File service at cashmd.org for simple returns with no hidden fees; (2) Use free IRS-approved tax software at cashmd.org; (3) Visit a free tax preparation site staffed by IRS-certified volunteers at nonprofits and local agencies who will e-file your return and direct deposit your refund. Contact 1-800-829-1040 for IRS information or 800-492-0618 for a list of free tax preparation sites near you. Visit cashmd.org for more information on all options.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports employment opportunities and training for foster youth in Maryland, administered by the Caroline County Department of Social Services on behalf of the Mid-Shore Departments of Social Services (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, and Talbot Counties).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding is provided to eligible organizations to support employment opportunities and training programs for foster care youth. The program is an 18-month grant intended to award one grant as a result of this Request for Grant Proposals. Eligible applicants include public, non-public, or private organizations that provide services in the State of Maryland. The scope of work includes job placement services matching individuals with jobs in the public or private sector based on skill level, maturity, and interest, as well as supportive employment services for foster care youth.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, February 17, 2017 at 11:00 AM Local Time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Foster youth seeking employment opportunities and organizations providing employment services to foster youth in the Mid-Shore region (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, and Talbot Counties).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment opportunities and training programs for foster care youth, including job placement services and supportive employment services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide, with primary service areas in the Mid-Shore region including Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, and Talbot Counties.
requirements_list: Organizations must be eligible grant applicants
Proposal must address foster youth employment services
Applicants must be registered with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) before award
Applicants must not be in arrears in payment of obligations due to the State
Applicants must comply with all Federal, State, and local laws
Applicants must complete and submit Bid/Proposal Affidavit (Attachment B)
Applicants must complete Conflict of Interest Affidavit (Attachment E)
Applicants must agree to Non-Disclosure Agreement (Attachment F)
Applicants must agree to accept payments by Electronic Funds Transfer
Minority Business Enterprises are encouraged to participate
Organizations must be able to serve throughout the Multi-State region as needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit proposals in two parts: Technical Proposal (Volume I) and Financial Proposal (Volume II) by the deadline of February 17, 2017 at 11:00 AM Local Time to Caroline County Department of Social Services, 207 S. Third Street, Denton, MD 21629, Attention: Christy Reid. Proposals may not be submitted by email or facsimile. A Pre-Proposal Conference was held on Monday, January 30, 2017 at 10:00 A.M. at 207 S. Third Street, Denton, MD 21629. Prospective applicants are encouraged to attend. Written questions from prospective applicants are accepted by the Procurement Officer prior to and after the Conference. Proposals received after the due date and time will not be considered. Applicants may be required to make oral presentations to State representatives. The evaluation committee will review proposals based on technical and financial proposal evaluation criteria.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Fuel Fund of Maryland is a non-profit organization that provides emergency financial assistance to low-income households facing an energy crisis, including those with an impending utility shutoff notice or those currently without power. The program helps resolve outstanding energy bills through a combination of client resources and charitable funds, and also assists with one-time bulk fuel heating purchases. It can assist households who exceed standard Energy Assistance income limits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency grants and financial assistance are provided to households with an impending utility shutoff notice or those currently without power. Assistance helps resolve outstanding energy bills and covers one-time bulk fuel heating purchases (not outstanding bulk fuel bills). Households that exceed standard Energy Assistance income limits may still be eligible. Allow at least 14 days for a response after applying.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 9:00 am to 12:00 pm, based on availability
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households facing an energy crisis, including those with an impending utility shutoff notice, those currently without power, or those exceeding Energy Assistance income limits
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Resolving outstanding utility energy bills and one-time bulk fuel heating purchases; utility bill payments to BGE and other participating energy companies
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — available to all Maryland residents
requirements_list: Must have a utility turn-off notice or be without power
Must have completed an application for Energy Assistance through the Office of Home Energy Programs, or may still be eligible if exceeding Energy Assistance income limits
Low-income household meeting Fuel Fund of Maryland eligibility requirements
Eligible for assistance once every 12 months
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online only at https://fuelfundmaryland.org/apply. The application link is available on Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 9:00 am to 12:00 pm, based on availability. Allow at least 14 days for a response after submitting your application.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Agriculture partners with the Farmer Veteran Coalition and Mid-Atlantic Farm Credit to support Maryland veteran farmers by branding products with the Maryland's Best – Homegrown by Heroes logo and offering business services assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Product branding with Maryland's Best – Homegrown by Heroes logo and business services assistance for veteran farmers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland veteran farmers interested in participating in the program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Product branding and business services assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a veteran farmer in Maryland
Must register with the Farmer Veteran Coalition at farmvetco.org
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Veteran farmers interested in participating should first sign up with the Farmer Veteran Coalition at farmvetco.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program assists individuals and families facing a housing crisis by providing small one-time crisis grants to keep people facing eviction safely housed. It includes case management, counseling, and early intervention services to prevent eviction. The program offers training on budgeting and life skills, education on tenant rights and responsibilities, and mediation between landlord and tenant. One-time direct grants are provided to landlords to prevent eviction.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Small one-time crisis grants are provided directly to landlords to prevent eviction. The program also provides case management and counseling services, training on budgeting and life skills, education on tenant rights and responsibilities, and mediation between landlord and tenant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families facing a housing crisis and at risk of eviction who have a lease in their name and the ability to pay rent going forward
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants are paid to landlords to prevent eviction. Funding is also used for case management, counseling, training on budgeting and life skills, education on tenant rights and responsibilities, and mediation between landlord and tenant.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland through local departments of social services
requirements_list: Qualifying household must have a lease in their name
The household must have the ability to pay rent moving forward

Local DSS or service provider must determine the family unit will be able to continue to stay in permanent housing or move to other permanent housing through payment to or arrangement with the landlord
Clients must comply with a documented case plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local department of social services for application and eligibility information

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides aide services in a consumer's home to help adults with disabilities with personal care (dressing, bathing, transferring, grooming, eating), chores (cooking, laundry, light cleaning, shopping), transportation/escort, training in self-care and care-giving skills, and other activities of daily living. The program also includes ongoing case management to help with planning and exploring other needed services. The goal is to allow adults with disabilities to remain living at home and avoid unnecessary moves to nursing homes or other out-of-home placements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides aide services in the home, including assistance with personal care, transportation/escort, training in self-care and care-giving skills, and minor household chores. Depending on income and family size, applicants may need to contribute toward the hourly cost of the aide service using a sliding scale fee paid to the local department of social services. Availability of funding determines how many individuals can be served statewide, and a ranking scale is used to prioritize those with the greatest need.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults aged 18 and older residing in Maryland who have functional disabilities and need assistance with personal care, chores, and activities of daily living to remain in their own homes. Vulnerable adults with no willing or capable caregiver, those at risk of institutional placement, and those at risk of abuse or neglect receive priority.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance with personal care (dressing, bathing, transferring, grooming, eating), chores (cooking, laundry, light cleaning, shopping), transportation/escort, training in self-care and care-giving skills, and other activities of daily living.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Adults residing in Maryland. Applicants should contact the local Department of Social Services in the county or city where they live.
requirements_list: Must be aged 18 or older
Must reside in Maryland
Must have functional disabilities
Must need assistance with personal care, chores, transportation/escort, training, and/or activities of daily living to remain in their own home
Vulnerable adults with no willing or capable caregiver available, those at risk of institutional placement, and those at risk of abuse or neglect receive priority using a ranking scale
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals or their caregivers should call the local Department of Social Services in the county or city where the applicant lives at 1-800-332-6347. A local department representative will arrange a home visit to conduct an interview to determine the applicant's specific needs. A ranking scale is used to prioritize those with the greatest need based on funding availability. The availability of funding for the program determines the number of individuals who can be served statewide.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to promote the safety and well-being of children and their families. In-Home Services strengthens parents' ability to create a safe and stable home environment while keeping the family together. Participants work with caseworkers to develop a plan tailored to their family's needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides support for families affected by substance use, parental resources, referrals for therapy and behavior support, education plans, healthcare assistance, and connecting with community providers. Families meet with their Local Department of Social Services and caseworkers work closely with each family member.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children seeking support to maintain safety and stability in their home.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for families affected by substance use, parental resources, therapy and behavior support referrals, education plans, healthcare assistance, and community provider connections.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through local departments of social services throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Families must contact their local department of social services

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary support program for former foster youth ages 18-21 who have exited out-of-home placement. The program helps youth achieve self-sufficiency through financial assistance and referrals for counseling, employment, education, and medical help.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Time-limited financial assistance to purchase goods and services needed for self-sufficiency, plus referrals for counseling, employment, education, and medical assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth ages 18-21 who have exited out-of-home foster care placement and need continued help transitioning to self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial assistance to purchase goods and services needed for self-sufficiency; referrals for counseling, employment, education, and medical assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through all local departments of social services in the jurisdiction where the youth resides.

Need continued help in making the transition to self-sufficiency
Participate in the development of a service agreement and sign and comply with its terms
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local department of social services where you reside to apply for Independent Living Aftercare services.

structured_extraction.program_description: An employment and training program that provides career counseling, employment support services, and job placement assistance for noncustodial parents who owe child support and are unemployed or underemployed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Job Network provides career counseling, employment support services, and unsubsidized employment placement services. The program hires and manages part-time noncustodial parent employment program case managers and benefit eligibility specialists in metropolitan counties to build connections among courts, Department of Social Services, and American Job Centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents who have a Baltimore County child support case, are unemployed or underemployed, and can commit to working upon program completion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment and training services, career support, and job placement assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Currently operating in Baltimore County with services available to noncustodial parents statewide through the program based in Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Have a Baltimore County child support case
Be unemployed or underemployed
Be able to commit to working upon program completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Noncustodial parties who meet eligibility criteria can apply to participate. Contact Job Network for application details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Long Term Care Medical Assistance (LTC) / Medicaid - Long Term Care (Nursing Home Medicaid)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state program designed to cover the cost of nursing home and residential care for low-income individuals who meet financial, technical, and medical eligibility requirements. The program helps Maryland residents living in a nursing home pay for their cost of care, and also helps pay for doctor, hospital, and other Medicaid-eligible medical care services. It is funded by federal and state taxes. Eligibility includes a look-back review of resources from the five years prior to application. The program is available statewide, with a dedicated Office of Long Term Care in Catonsville serving applicants from Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, and Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program covers the cost of nursing home and residential care for low-income individuals who meet eligibility requirements, and also helps pay for doctor, hospital, and other Medicaid-eligible medical care services. No fees or payments are required to apply. The applicant may be required to contribute a portion of their income to the nursing home based on their financial situation. Applications are subject to a look-back review of resources in the five years (60 months) prior to application. Applicants must provide extensive financial documentation including federal tax returns for the current year and preceding four years, bank and financial statements for current month, previous month, and the last five years of anniversary months, statements of retirement accounts (IRA, Keogh), stocks, bonds, money market funds, mutual funds, life insurance policies with face and cash value, burial accounts, burial plot deeds, life estate deeds, promissory notes, mortgage notes and deeds, trusts with all appendices and amendments for the past five years, private health insurance cards including Medicare, and verification of all income sources including VA pensions, railroad retirement, pensions, annuities, and business income.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Office of Long Term Care / Eligibility Specialist
structured_extraction.program_audience: U.S. citizens and Maryland residents who need nursing home or residential care and meet the program's financial, technical, and medical criteria, including low-income individuals and seniors. Individuals under age 65 must also meet disability criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for nursing home and residential care costs, doctor services, hospital services, and other Medicaid-eligible medical care services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in all Maryland counties. The Office of Long Term Care, located at 746 Frederick Road, Catonsville, Maryland 21228, specifically covers applications from Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, and Prince George's County. Montgomery County applicants may apply at 401 Hungerford Drive, 4th floor, Rockville, Maryland 20850.
requirements_list: Must be a U.S. citizen
Must be a Maryland resident
Must meet income and asset requirements for low-income individuals based on 2023 guidelines (income limits vary by family size and program category)
Must meet disability criteria if under age 65
Must qualify for a nursing home level of care
Financial history (resources) over the past 60 months (five years) will be reviewed via look-back
Must provide complete and accurate financial documentation including tax returns, bank statements, investment statements, insurance information, and proof of all income sources
If married, spouse's income and assets subject to spousal impoverishment rules
Must report all asset transfers, gifts, or disposals from the past five years

Must disclose all current assets including cash, checking accounts, savings accounts, credit union accounts, trust funds, IRAs, retirement accounts, stocks, bonds, annuities, life insurance policies, burial accounts, and real property
Do not wait to apply if all documents are not available; applicants may submit available documents and provide additional documentation later
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at https://marylandbenefits.gov (Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal), or through MyMDTHINK. Alternatively, call 240-777-3995 (Montgomery County) or 1-800-332-6347 to request an application packet by mail, or pick up a packet at 401 Hungerford Drive, 4th floor, Rockville, Maryland 20850, or at 746 Frederick Road, Catonsville, Maryland 21228. Complete the Long-Term Care/Waiver Medical Assistance Application (Form DHS FIA 9709) by answering all questions in each section: Benefit Selection, Applicant Information, Immigration Status (if applicable), Current Address, Previous Addresses, Authorized Representative, Spousal Information, Disability, Veteran Information, Medical Insurance, Income from Working, Benefits and Other Income, Assets, Other Assets, Potential Assets or Income, Real Property, Life Insurance and Funeral Plans, Transfer of Assets, Spousal Benefits and Income, Spousal Needs/Spousal Impoverishment, Residential/Spousal/Dependent Allowance, Tax Returns, and Pre-Eligibility Medical Expenses. Submit the completed application with all required supporting documents (copies, not originals) by mail or in person to your local health department or local department of social services, or fax to 240-777-1330 (Montgomery County). The Office of Long Term Care at 746 Frederick Road, Catonsville, Maryland 21228 handles applications from Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, and Prince George's County. Applications are processed on a rolling basis. For redetermination of existing benefits, complete Form DHS FIA 9709R annually, providing current verification of income, assets, medical expenses, and asset transfers from the past 12 months.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Household Water Assistance Program (LIHWAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: LIHWAP provides financial assistance to income-eligible renters, homeowners, and residents of public housing to help pay water and wastewater bills. The program helps make water and wastewater costs more affordable, prevents disconnection of service, and can restore services for households that have had water service disconnected due to past-due balances. It is administered statewide through the Maryland Department of Human Services Office of Home Energy Programs, with local application assistance available through county departments of social services and community action councils. LIHWAP is part of a federally-funded American Rescue Plan program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Water and wastewater assistance grants range from $100 to $2,000. Benefits are paid directly to the public water supplier or treatment works to cover restoration of services, prevention of disconnection, standard charges, billing fees, and reconnection fees. Applicants may qualify for: (1) Reconnect Household Water/Wastewater Services - up to $2,000 to pay off past-due balances and reconnection fees if service has been disconnected; (2) Prevent Disconnection of Household Water/Wastewater Services - to pay all or part of bills if a termination notice has been received; or (3) Reduce Current Household Water/Wastewater Past Due Balance - temporary assistance to pay current water bills. Minimum arrearage balance of $100 required. Only one water/wastewater bill account per service address is eligible to receive benefits. All assistance dollars are grants and do not need to be repaid.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling enrollment; applications processed first-come, first-served until funding is depleted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible renters, homeowners, and public housing residents in Maryland who are struggling to pay water and wastewater bills, including those at risk of disconnection or who have already had service disconnected due to past-due balances.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of water and wastewater bills, including past-due balances (arrearages of 30 days or more past due), reconnection fees, standard charges, billing fees, and prevention of service disconnection.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. Local assistance available through county departments of social services and community action councils, including Washington County Department of Social Services (122 North Potomac Street, Hagerstown, MD 21740; 240-420-2100) and Washington County Community Action Council (117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740; 301-797-4161).
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must be responsible for payment of water and/or wastewater bill issued by a public water system or treatment works
Must live at the property for which assistance is being provided
Only one water/wastewater bill account per service address is eligible

Gross household income must not exceed eligibility limits based on household size (effective July 1, 2021 - June 30, 2022: 1 person: $3,121/month; 2 people: $4,081/month; 3 people: $5,041/month; 4 people: $6,000/month; 5 people: $6,962/month; 6 people: $7,922/month; 7 people: $8,102/month; 8 people: $8,283/month; for each additional person add $180/month)
Service address must have a minimum arrearage balance of $100
Proof of identity (government-issued photo ID such as Driver's license or other government-issued identification card)
Social Security cards or other federal government-issued documents for all household members
Copy of water and/or wastewater utility bill or termination notice

Documentation of all gross (pre-tax) income for everyone in household for the last 30 days (pay stubs, Social Security award letters, pension statements, SNAP/TCA/TDAP award letters, child support letters, unemployment letters, self-employment documentation)
Proof of living at the service address (can be utility bill, lease, or rental receipt)
If household received no income in the 30 days prior to application, must sign Declaration of Zero Income and provide additional information on how household is meeting basic needs

For categorical eligibility: at least one household member must currently receive benefits from MEAP, Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP), Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Energy Assistance from OHEP, Means-Tested veterans' benefits, or Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP)
At least one household member must be a U.S. citizen and have a Social Security number
If renting and water bill is in landlord's name, must provide copy of most recent rental receipt or lease stating water is covered in rental fee and provide landlord name and contact information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications may be submitted through multiple methods: (1) Online at mymdthink.maryland.gov; (2) By mail; (3) By drop-off; (4) By email to ohep@montgomerycountymd.gov; (5) By fax to 240-777-4099; or (6) In person at local county departments of social services or community action councils. Submit all required supporting documents with your application for faster processing. The office will review your application and supporting documents within 14 days of receiving a complete packet and make a final determination within 45 days. Free translation services are available by calling 1-800-332-6347 (available in Spanish and other languages). Check application status at myohepstatus.org or call 1-800-332-6347 or contact TTY 1-800-735-2258 for hearing impaired. For Washington County applicants, may schedule an appointment by visiting or calling the Washington County Department of Social Services at 122 North Potomac Street, Hagerstown, MD 21740 (240-420-2100) or the Washington County Community Action Council at 117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740 (301-797-4161). Applicants can also request assistance through their local OHEP office.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Commission for Women Internship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An internship program that mentors and supports young leaders by providing undergraduate and graduate students with opportunities to work on policy, communications, research, and administrative tasks focused on advancing social, political, and economic opportunities for women in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid internships offering work experience and mentorship. Interns are paid $16.85 per hour and are typically required to commit 20 hours per week. Positions are hybrid, with work conducted both remotely and at the Commission office in Rockville, Maryland. Internships are available during fall, spring, and summer terms.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Undergraduate and graduate students with demonstrated interest in women's issues, social justice, and civic engagement, strong writing and research skills, comfort with social media, and experience with community or student organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Work experience and paid compensation for internship positions. Interns support policy analysis, legislative monitoring, research, communications, event coordination, and social media management related to women's issues in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The internship program operates from the Commission for Women office in Rockville, Maryland, with hybrid work arrangements available.
requirements_list: Be an undergraduate or graduate student
Demonstrate interest in women's issues, social justice, and civic engagement
Have strong writing and research skills
Have comfort with social media
Have experience with community or student organizations
Participate in an in-person interview
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a résumé, cover letter explaining reasons for applying and interests within the commission, dates and hours of availability, a list of goals to achieve during the internship, and a small writing sample of no more than 2-3 paragraphs. Email all materials to Ariana Kelly, Executive Director. Applicants will be asked to participate in an in-person interview following submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state tax credit for working people with low to moderate income. If you qualify for the federal earned income tax credit and claim it on your federal return, you may receive a Maryland earned income tax credit equal to 50% of the federal tax credit for filers with dependents, or 100% of the federal tax credit for single filers unable to claim dependents. Eligible ITIN filers may also receive this credit. The Maryland credit reduces or eliminates the state and local income tax you owe, and may provide a tax refund for limited-income workers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State tax credit matching the federal EITC at 50% for filers with dependents and 100% for single filers without dependents. Eligible ITIN filers may receive this credit. The credit reduces or eliminates state and local income tax owed and may result in a tax refund for limited-income workers. Free tax preparation assistance is available at VITA sites and through Direct File for eligible taxpayers. For those earning less than $67,000, free tax prep services are available with e-filing and direct deposit of refunds into bank accounts (up to three separate accounts).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Working people with low to moderate income who qualify for the federal earned income tax credit, including ITIN filers and limited-income workers in Maryland. Those earning less than $67,000 in 2024 may qualify for free tax preparation services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied against Maryland state and local income tax liability; may reduce or eliminate taxes owed or provide a tax refund.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available to all Maryland residents. Free tax preparation services available in Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Calvert, Carroll, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Somerset, St. Mary's, and Wicomico counties.
requirements_list: Must qualify for the federal earned income tax credit
Must claim the federal EITC on your federal tax return
Must file a Maryland tax return
ITIN filers are eligible
Must be a limited-income worker
Must meet state income limits
For free tax prep: income must be less than $67,000 in 2024
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: If you qualify for the federal EITC and claim it on your federal return, you automatically qualify for the Maryland EITC on your state return. File a Maryland tax return claiming the state EITC. You can use the IRS EITC Assistant to determine eligibility by answering questions about income and dependents. Free tax preparation help is available at VITA (Volunteer Income Tax Assistance) sites throughout Maryland and via the new Direct File service for eligible taxpayers. Call 800-492-0618 for a list of free tax prep sites or visit cashmd.org. Free software is available at cashmd.org for self-filers. When visiting a free tax location, bring: Social Security card for each family member and photo ID for each taxpayer; W-2 forms for all 2024 jobs; Form 1099-G for unemployment; child care provider letter with address, Tax ID, child name and amount paid; banking information for direct deposit; copy of last year's tax return; Form 1095-A (health insurance form); and all other tax-related documents. Every adult on the return must come to sign. For additional information, contact the Maryland Taxpayer Service at 1-800-638-2937.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Education and Training Voucher Program (ETV)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Education and Training Voucher (ETV) Program, administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services in partnership with Foster Care to Success, provides financial assistance to students currently in foster care and former foster care youth to help pay for education-related expenses. Eligible youth may receive up to $5,000 annually for full-time enrollment or up to $2,500 for part-time enrollment in college or vocational school. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual financial assistance of up to $5,000 for full-time students or up to $2,500 for part-time students enrolled in college or vocational school. Funds are provided on a first-come, first-served basis and must be applied for by the March 1st annual deadline to meet Maryland's student financial aid requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students currently in foster care and former foster care youth in Maryland, including youth currently in out-of-home placement or placed into guardianship or adopted after age 16, who are enrolled full-time or part-time in college or vocational school.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and training expenses for college or vocational school enrollment, including education-related expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Maryland foster care youth statewide.
requirements_list: Must be currently in foster care or a former foster care youth
Must be currently in out-of-home placement or placed into guardianship or adopted after age 16
Must be enrolled in college or vocational school as a full-time or part-time student
Must meet Maryland's student financial aid deadline of March 1st to be eligible
Funds are provided on a first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply by the March 1st annual deadline. Contact your case worker or Independent Living Coordinator to apply for the Education and Training Voucher Program. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Emergency Food Program administers annual grants to non-profit feeding organizations and local government-run programs to purchase food and provide groceries and meals to individuals and families in need at no charge. Funding supports soup kitchens, food banks, food pantries, shelters, residential treatment programs, and after-school programs across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. Funds are allocated based on available funding and demographic indicators including current population size, percentage of unemployment, number of individuals and families living in poverty, and number receiving SNAP benefits.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants are provided to Emergency Food Providers (tax-exempt organizations) and local government-run programs to purchase food for distribution at no charge to eligible individuals and families. For FY 2026, a total of $1,241,661 is allocated to jurisdictions across Maryland. The maximum award is $50,000; minimum award is $2,000. First-time grantees and those who have not received MEFP funding in the past three years receive capped funding of $2,000. Funds must be used exclusively to purchase food for meals and/or groceries distributed at no cost to eligible individuals and households. MEFP funds may not be used for food-related items such as cutlery, food storage containers, grocery store or other gift cards (unless designated as food-only), paper or cleaning products. Organizations are strongly encouraged to purchase food produced, grown, and harvested in Maryland, and to purchase from local farmers markets when feasible and cost-effective. Grant awards cover one fiscal year (July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2026). All MEFP funds must be expended by June 1, 2026, with any unexpended funds returned by June 30, 2026. Organizations must submit quarterly reports with receipts, canceled checks, and service data; late report submissions will be documented as non-compliant and considered when reviewing future applications.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The FY 2026 application process is now closed (as of May 9, 2025). Applications must be received electronically no later than 5:00 PM on May 9, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tax-exempt feeding organizations (including soup kitchens, food banks, food pantries, shelters, residential treatment programs, and after-school programs) and local government-run food programs that serve individuals and families experiencing food insecurity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds must be used exclusively to purchase food for meals and/or groceries distributed at no cost to eligible individuals and families. MEFP funds may not be used for cutlery, food storage containers, grocery store or other gift cards (unless food-only), paper products, or cleaning products. Grantees are encouraged to purchase food produced and grown in Maryland and to purchase from local farmers markets when feasible and cost-effective.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Funds are allocated to all 24 jurisdictions (24 counties and Baltimore City) in Maryland based on population, poverty rates, unemployment rates, and number of individuals/families receiving SNAP benefits.
requirements_list: Be a local government-run program administered and operated directly by a government agency or in partnership with a government entity, OR be a tax-exempt Emergency Food Provider
Have verifiable tax-exempt status as defined by the Federal Internal Revenue Service (IRS) as a 501(c)(3) organization
Have a physical location that provides related services (community services, church outreach services, housing services)
Be an established Emergency Food Provider for at least three years
Demonstrate community support in the form of cash or food donations from outside entities (such as local schools, churches, community food drives)
Be in good standing with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT); applicants with tax offsets or liens are ineligible
Must have federal tax ID number (EIN)
Must have anti-discrimination policy
Must agree to abide by MEFP guidelines including submitting requested reports, receipts, and quarterly activity reports

Must evidence sound financial and program management
Must have ability to distribute food for emergency need
Must provide food at no charge to those in need (neither cash nor service requirement, including Electronic Benefits Transfer Cards)
Must maintain clean, appropriate environment for food storage and/or preparation compliant with local health department regulations
Must post hours so people who need food know when to come and conduct outreach in the community
Must designate a person to submit reports and manage program operations
Must keep MEFP funds separate from other funds on financial statements or bookkeeping systems
Must maintain secure storage of records and customer files
Must maintain detailed records regarding use of MEFP funds including customer demographic information and units of service for three years
Must document all MEFP purchases with proof of payment (invoices with canceled checks and/or receipts)

If repackaging food, must ensure kitchen and pantry staff follow USDA safe food handling program protocols
Must follow local health department regulations for sanitation, food service, quality control, and cleanliness
Must have rodent and insect infestation controls for facility
Must submit quarterly reports with receipts, canceled checks, and services provided on or before specified deadlines, even if no funds were expended
If organization has not received MEFP grant in last three years, must provide two letters of reference with original signatures from community groups or businesses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit completed applications electronically through the FY26 MEFP Application Submission Form. The application period opens annually and typically closes approximately 30 days after the funding opportunity is published. For FY 2026, the application deadline was May 9, 2025 at 5:00 PM, and this window is now closed. Applications must include all required documentation and signatures; incomplete applications or those submitted without required documentation will be deemed ineligible. Late applications will not be considered and late applicants will be notified in writing of their ineligibility. Required documentation includes: current tax-exempt status verification (IRS 501(c)(3) letter), screenshot of EIN from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation website, two letters of reference (for first-time applicants or those who have not received MEFP funding in the past three years), completed application with all sections thoroughly filled out, demographic and service data, accurate budget information, and proposed outcomes. Applications are evaluated based on completeness of required documentation and signatures; thorough completion of all information; specific description of how grant funds will be used; goals for increasing outreach; explanation of need; and prior performance of previously funded applicants. New programs receive a site visit prior to award decision. Eligible applicants receive awards based on available funding and demographic indicators of need. Grantees receive an award letter stating terms of agreement including award amount, grant year, deliverables with timelines, and DHS contact information, and must sign a DHS 655 Grant Agreement. Grantees will be scheduled for annual or semi-annual site visits during the fiscal year covered by the grant. Organizations must submit quarterly reports by specified deadlines: 1st Quarter (July-September) due October 10, 2025; 2nd Quarter (October-December) due January 9, 2026; 3rd Quarter (January-March) due April 10, 2026; 4th Quarter (April-June) due July 10, 2026. Check the program website for future application cycles.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) / Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services, provides energy assistance to low-income households across Maryland to help make energy costs more affordable and prevent loss of home energy services. The program operates year-round and includes multiple components: the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP), which provides annual grants to help pay home heating bills sent directly to the fuel supplier or utility company on the customer's behalf; the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP), which provides annual grants applied directly to electric bills to cover current or past-due charges; the Arrearage Retirement Assistance (ARA) grant, which helps reduce or eliminate past-due electric bills (up to $2,000); and the Gas Arrearage Retirement Assistance (GARA) grant, which helps reduce or eliminate past-due natural gas bills (up to $1,000). Grant amounts are determined based on household income, fuel type, electric usage, and geographic area. Benefits are available once per fiscal year (July through June), and applicants must reapply annually. A turn-off notice is not required to qualify. Households receiving SNAP or TCA benefits are categorically eligible and do not need to complete an application or provide additional documentation. The program also connects eligible households to the MEAP repair/replacement program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), which provides free repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems. Special flood-related heating system assistance is available for homes in Allegany and Garrett Counties affected by flooding. The Utility Service Protection Program (USPP) is also available to protect low-income families from utility turn-offs during the heating season. Locally, OHEP offices in each county administer the program, including dedicated offices in Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, Calvert, Charles, and Washington Counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants to help eligible low-income households pay utility and heating bills. MEAP provides a one-time annual grant per heating season sent directly to the heating supplier to cover a portion of heating costs. Grant amounts are based on fuel type (natural gas, electricity, oil, propane, or other), household income, and geographic area within Maryland. EUSP provides an annual grant applied directly to the electric utility account, determined based on household income and electric use over the past 12 months. The Arrearage Retirement Assistance (ARA) grant provides up to $2,000 to help reduce or eliminate past-due electric bills for households with at least $300 in past-due charges who are approved for MEAP and/or EUSP; available once every five years with certain exceptions. The Gas Arrearage Retirement Assistance (GARA) grant provides up to $1,000 for past-due natural gas bills under the same conditions. Recipients may enroll in budget billing to spread costs evenly throughout the year. Benefits are available once per fiscal year (July through June). Additionally, through DHCD's MEAP component, eligible households can receive free repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems at no cost. Processing typically takes up to 45 days. Applicants can check application status online at myohepstatus.org or myohepstatus.maryland.gov. All energy assistance dollars are grants and do not need to be repaid.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Year-round program with no deadline. Applications accepted at any time during the fiscal year (July through June). Benefits available once per fiscal year; must reapply each year. In St. Mary's County, applications are accepted between July and May each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income Maryland households — including homeowners, renters, boarders, and residents of public housing — who need help paying heating, electric, natural gas, and other utility bills. Also eligible are households with non-functioning heating, cooling, or water heating systems whose income is below 200% of the federal poverty level, or who are currently eligible for Utility Bill Pay Assistance through OHEP, SNAP, TANF, SSI, or HUD housing assistance programs. Households receiving SNAP or Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) are categorically eligible without needing to submit an application.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home heating bills (paid directly to fuel supplier or utility company); electric utility bills (applied directly to electric account); natural gas bills; past-due utility amounts (through ARA and GARA grants); repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems (through DHCD's MEAP component); weatherization and energy efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in all Maryland counties through local Home Energy Program Offices in each jurisdiction. Special flood-related heating system assistance is available for homes in Allegany or Garrett County affected by flooding. Baltimore City residents should drop applications at the nearest Community Action Program (CAP) Center. Local offices also serve Frederick County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, St. Mary's County, Calvert County, Charles County, and Washington County. Applications from other areas should be submitted to the local county or regional OHEP office.
requirements_list: Household income must be at or below income limits based on household size (FY26 monthly limits: 1 person: $2,608; 2 persons: $3,525; 3 persons: $4,441; 4 persons: $5,358; 5 persons: $6,275; 6 persons: $7,191; 7 persons: $8,108; 8 persons: $9,025; for each person over 8, contact local OHEP office)
Must be a Maryland resident
Income eligibility is based on 200% of the Federal Poverty Level for DHCD MEAP system repair/replacement component
Must provide a copy of photo identification for the applicant
Must provide proof of residency (lease, mortgage statement, or utility bill)
Must provide copies of Social Security cards for all household members including children
Must provide proof of household gross income for the last 30 days (includes wages, unemployment, Social Security, etc.; bank statements are not valid)
Must provide a copy of most recent utility bill or termination notice if applicable
Must provide a copy of most recent heating fuel bill or receipt if applicable
Do not need a utility turn-off notice to qualify
Can only receive benefits once each fiscal year (July through June)
Must reapply each fiscal year
For EUSP: must have an electric utility bill in the applicant's name; customers may choose to enroll in Budget Billing with utility company

For DHCD MEAP system repair: must have a non-functioning heating, cooling, and/or water heating system, OR be currently eligible for Utility Bill Pay Assistance through OHEP, SNAP, TANF, SSI, or HUD housing assistance

For ARA/GARA (Arrearage Retirement Assistance): must have a past-due bill of at least $300 in applicant's name and be approved for MEAP and/or EUSP; available once every five years with certain exceptions
For EUSP (Prince George's County): must participate in budget billing with utility company
At least one household member must be a legal resident with a Social Security number (Montgomery County)
