For EmPOWER Maryland/LIEEP component: must have a utility account with one of six participating companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas
Households receiving SNAP or Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) are categorically eligible and do not need to provide application or additional documentation

For Crisis Season Declaration (November 1 – March 31): applicants unable to provide complete application may declare income and must provide required documentation within 15 days or repay crisis benefit
For zero income declaration: all household members age 18 and older with no income in past 30 days must complete Declaration of Zero Income form
For landlord-assisted applications: landlord must agree to reduce tenant's rent or utility charge by the amount of benefit received
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply through multiple methods: (1) Online at MarylandBenefits.gov or MyDHR (mydhrbenefits.dhr.state.md.us) available 24/7; (2) By submitting a paper application to a secure drop box at the local OHEP office; (3) By mail to the local OHEP office; (4) By phone by calling the statewide line at 1-800-332-6347 or a local office; (5) In person at the local office; (6) By email with completed application and supporting documents to the local office email; (7) By proxy authorization if applicant cannot apply in person. Home visits can be arranged for senior citizens or other persons with special medical needs. Required documents include: photo ID, proof of residency, Social Security cards for all household members, proof of gross household income for the last 30 days, most recent utility bill and/or termination notice, and most recent heating fuel bill or receipt if applicable. For zero-income households, a completed Zero Income Declaration form is required. For self-employment income, Schedule SE from tax return or business documentation is required. For applicants unable to provide full documentation during crisis season (November 1-March 31), a Crisis Season Declaration form may be used; applicants must provide remaining documentation within 15 days. Applications are available in English and Spanish and can be filled out electronically or by hand but must be printed and signed by hand. Clear pictures of documents are acceptable instead of scanned documents. After approval and processing (typically up to 45 days), grants are sent directly to the heating supplier or electric company. For rental properties, a completed Landlord Agreement form must be submitted with landlord's agreement to apply benefits to tenant's rent or utility charge. For applicants with safety concerns unable to provide an address, a Concern for Personal Safety/Privacy form with third-party verification is required. Applicants can check application status online at myohepstatus.org or myohepstatus.maryland.gov. For DHCD MEAP system repair/replacement: complete a DHCD Energy & Repair Programs Application and submit all required documents to DHCD at 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706 or call intake line at 1-855-583-8976; if currently approved for Energy Assistance payments from DHS, contact the intake line at 1-855-583-8976. Once eligibility is determined, a local agency will schedule a home assessment and a contractor will complete the recommended work. Supplementary applications and forms available include: Alimony/Child Support Verification (DHS FIA 803), Concern for Personal Safety/Privacy (DHS FIA 804), Crisis Season Declaration (DHS FIA 805), Declaration of Zero Income (DHS FIA 806), Household Worksheet (DHS FIA 807), Income Verification of Self-Employment (DHS FIA 808), Landlord Agreement (DHS FIA 809), Physician Certification (DHS FIA 810), Proxy Authorization (DHS FIA 811), Rent/Living Arrangements Verification (DHS FIA 812), Resource Provider Statement (DHS FIA 813), and Wage Verification (DHS FIA 814). Local office contacts: Frederick County — PO Box 3929 Frederick, MD 21705, email ohep@cityoffrederickmd.gov, drop off at 420 East Patrick Street; Montgomery County — 1301 Piccard Drive 4th Floor, call 240-777-4450, email ohep@montgomerycountymd.gov, fax 240-777-4099; Prince George's County — email pgcdss.energy@maryland.gov, mail to 805 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785, fax 301-909-6331, call 301-909-6300; Southern Maryland (Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's) — contact Tri-County Community Action Committee at 301-274-4474 or email OHEP@smtccac.org; Washington County — contact Washington County Community Action Council at 117 Summit Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21740, call 301-797-4161, email WashingtonCountyOHEP@wccac.org. TTY for the hearing impaired: 1-800-735-2258.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Legal Services Program - Adult Representation
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides legal representation to indigent alleged vulnerable adults involved in Adult Protective Services and Adult Public Guardianship Review Board proceedings in Maryland. Legal services are secured through contracts with law firms to ensure high-quality legal representation for eligible adults throughout the duration of their cases.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Legal representation is provided to indigent alleged vulnerable adults at no cost to the client. The program compensates attorneys who provide legal services when the local Department of Social Services or the Office on Aging is a party to the case and the alleged vulnerable adult is indigent. Legal services are provided for the duration of the client's time in need.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Indigent alleged vulnerable adults involved in Adult Protective Services and Adult Public Guardianship Review Board proceedings in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Legal representation in Adult Protective Services and Adult Public Guardianship Review Board cases
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all Maryland counties
requirements_list: Must be alleged vulnerable adult involved in Adult Protective Services or Adult Public Guardianship Review Board proceedings
Must be indigent
Local Department of Social Services or Office on Aging must be a party to the case
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals do not directly apply for this program. Legal representation is provided when cases arise involving indigent vulnerable adults in Adult Protective Services or Adult Public Guardianship Review Board proceedings. Contact information for legal service providers serving each jurisdiction is available through the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland SUN Bucks provides financial assistance to families with school-aged children (ages 5-18) during the summer months when school meals are unavailable. The program issues $120 per eligible child per summer ($40 per month for June, July, and August), loaded onto an Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card for purchasing groceries and eligible food items. The program builds on Maryland's existing state Summer SNAP program and implements the federal Summer EBT Program, expanding reach to serve students across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. Most eligible families are automatically enrolled; some households must apply. Benefits can be used at most grocery stores, some farmers' markets, and authorized online retailers that accept EBT.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible students receive $40 in benefits for June, $40 for July, and $40 for August, totaling $120 per eligible child per summer. Benefits are issued in the last week of each month and loaded onto an Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card. For families already receiving SNAP benefits, benefits are automatically applied to the head-of-household's Independence Card. For families not receiving SNAP, a white Maryland SUN Bucks card is issued in the child's name. Benefits can be used to purchase eligible food items at stores and retailers that accept EBT, including most grocery stores, some farmers' markets, and authorized online retailers. Benefits expire 122 days after issuance. Benefits cannot be used for alcohol, cigarettes, tobacco, non-food items (pet food, soap, household supplies, vitamins, medicines), or hot or prepared food. To activate an issued card, call 1-800-997-2222 and enter the card number and date of birth; enter 0000 when prompted for the last four digits of the child's Social Security Number; then set a new four-digit Personal Identification Number (PIN).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with school-aged children (ages 5-18) who received free or reduced-price meals during the school year, receive SNAP, Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), or Medicaid benefits, or who have children in out-of-home care (foster care, homeless, migrant, or runaway). Children are eligible regardless of immigration status.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Benefits can be used to purchase eligible food items at stores and vendors that accept Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT), including most grocery stores, some farmers' markets, and authorized online retailers. Cannot be used for alcohol, cigarettes, tobacco, non-food items (pet food, soap, household supplies, vitamins, medicines), or hot or prepared food.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in all 24 Maryland local jurisdictions. Children must be enrolled in a Maryland school that participates in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP). Most public schools participate; some charter and private schools do as well. Virtual schools and homeschools do not qualify.
requirements_list: Child must be school-aged (ages 5-18)
Child must be enrolled in a Maryland school that participates in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Free and Reduced-Price School Meals (FARMS) program

Household must participate in SNAP, Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), or Medical Assistance/Medicaid (MA); OR child applied for and was enrolled in Free or Reduced-Price School Meals (FARMS) or School Breakfast Program (SBP) during the current or prior school year; OR child is in foster care, homeless, migrant, or runaway; OR child is in Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) school; OR child meets income eligibility requirements for the National School Lunch Program (NSLP)
Family must meet Maryland SUN Bucks income guidelines as published on the Maryland Public Schools website
Children are eligible regardless of immigration status
Most eligible families automatically receive benefits; some households may need to apply
A household may not receive more than $120 Maryland SUN Bucks per eligible child per program year
Child cannot be receiving these benefits from another state, Indian Tribal Organization, or jurisdiction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Most eligible students are automatically enrolled with no action required by parents or guardians if the child applied for and received free or reduced-price meals in the last school year, is ages 5-18 in a household receiving SNAP, TCA, or Medicaid, or is in foster care. Automatically enrolled households receive an enrollment notice from DHS by the end of June. Children not automatically enrolled must apply online at marylandbenefits.gov or submit a paper application at a local Department of Social Services office. Applications are accepted year-round. After application, households receive an application confirmation letter followed by either an approval or denial letter based on eligibility. The state reviews applications and determines eligibility within 15 days from the date of application. To activate an issued card, call 1-800-997-2222 and enter the card number and date of birth; enter 0000 when prompted for the last four digits of the child's Social Security Number; then set a new four-digit Personal Identification Number (PIN). Families with questions can check application status or get more information by calling 1-800-332-6347 and selecting the Maryland SUN Bucks option.

structured_extraction.program_description: Medicaid (Medical Assistance) is a joint federal and state program administered by the State of Maryland that provides comprehensive health care insurance and pays medical bills for aged, blind, disabled adults, and families with low income. Coverage is based on income and assets and is available statewide. The program covers a wide range of health services and helps individuals and families pay for doctor visits, prescriptions, hospital bills, and Medicare premium payments. Special provisions exist for aged (65+), blind, and disabled individuals, including those receiving SSI who automatically qualify. Retroactive coverage for up to 3 months prior to application is available for outstanding medical bills. A spend-down provision applies when income exceeds the limit. Emergency Medicaid and coverage for pregnant women do not require immigration status. The program is funded with both federal and state money and administered through 24 local departments of social services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Comprehensive health care insurance coverage for eligible low-income individuals and families, administered by the State using federal and state funds. Coverage includes doctor visits (including regular checkups and specialists), pregnancy care, family planning and birth control, inpatient and outpatient hospital care, X-ray and laboratory services, prescription medication, emergency services, emergency dental care, vision care, immunizations, hospital services, and Medicare premium payments. Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP) covers full health benefits for children up to age 19. Coverage amount varies based on income and assets. As of March 1, 2025, monthly income limits for Medicaid are approximately: individual $1,801; family of 2 $2,433; family of 3 $3,065; family of 4 $3,698; family of 5 $4,330; family of 6 $4,962; family of 7 $5,596; family of 8 $6,228; each additional person $632. Children (MCHP) have higher limits: individual $4,202; family of 2 $5,677; family of 3 $7,152; family of 4 $8,630; family of 5 $10,104; family of 6 $11,579; family of 7 $13,057; family of 8 $14,532; each additional child $1,475. Pregnant individuals: family of 2 $4,654; family of 3 $5,863; family of 4 $7,075; family of 5 $8,284; family of 6 $9,493; family of 7 $10,705; family of 8 $11,914; each additional person $1,209. Applicants can be covered retroactively for medical bills from the 3 months prior to the month of application if they have outstanding medical expenses. Income limits may be exceeded through a spend-down provision where applicants are responsible for a portion of medical expenses before coverage begins. Enrollment is open year-round and coverage begins on the first day of the month that you applied. Renewal occurs once annually. No fees or payments required from beneficiaries. For aged, blind, or disabled individuals, full Medicaid health coverage is available with income and asset testing; those receiving SSI automatically qualify.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Aged, blind, and disabled adults; families with low income; children under 19; pregnant women (of any immigration status); former foster care children; needy and low-income individuals statewide; individuals receiving SSI; low-income residents aged 65 and older; individuals under 65 with a qualifying disability; lawfully residing children under 21 (regardless of immigration status)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Doctor visits (including regular checkups and specialists), pregnancy care, family planning and birth control, inpatient and outpatient hospital care, X-ray and laboratory services, prescription medication, emergency services, emergency dental care, vision care, immunizations, hospital services including lab work and tests, family planning services, limited transportation to covered providers, home health services, physical therapy, personal care services, Medicare premium payments, Qualified Medicare Beneficiary Program (QMB) and Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary Program (SLMB), and other medical bills and healthcare expenses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through 24 local departments of social services. Must be a Maryland resident.
requirements_list: Must be a U.S. citizen or meet alien status requirements; however, lawfully residing children under 21 are not subject to the five-year bar; noncitizen pregnant individuals of any immigration status are eligible; Emergency Medicaid is available regardless of immigration status for medical emergencies including labor and delivery
Must be a Maryland resident
Proof of identity required
Social Security numbers for everyone in household required
Proof of address required
Proof of income for everyone in entire household required
Proof of household expenses required
Applicants can apply even if they have private health insurance or third-party coverage
Must meet income and asset requirements (needy or low-income status) based on family size and household income limits
For aged, blind, or disabled category: must be aged 65 or older, blind, or disabled (including those under 65 with a qualifying disability or those receiving Social Security or SSI)
Retroactive coverage for 3 months prior to application available for outstanding medical expenses
Spend-down provision applies if income exceeds the limit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov (https://benefits.maryland.gov), MarylandHealthConnection.gov, or MyDHR; by mail, by fax, or in person at one of DHS's 24 local departments of social services; or by calling 1-855-642-8572 (Deaf and hard of hearing use Relay service). For persons under 65, apply through Maryland Health Connection. For persons 65 and older, people with disabilities, those receiving Medicare, or those applying for aged, blind, disabled, medically needy, QMB, or SLMB benefits, contact your local Department of Social Services or apply online at mymdthink.maryland.gov/. Montgomery County residents may apply at regional offices: Silver Spring Office (8818 Georgia Avenue, 1st Floor), Rockville Office (1301 Piccard Drive, 2nd Floor), or Germantown Office (12900 Middlebrook Road, 1st Floor). Free, in-person help is available at MarylandHealthConnection.gov/help. A free mobile app, Enroll MHC, is available for downloads. Bring proof of identity, Social Security numbers for all household members, proof of address, proof of income, and proof of household expenses. Enrollment is open year-round and coverage begins on the first day of the month of application. Most cases are decided within 30 days; disability determinations may take 90 days or more. Interpreters are available for non-English speakers. Renewal occurs once annually and you will be contacted when it is time to renew.

structured_extraction.program_description: Re-Engaging Individuals through Successful Employment (RISE) is a free employment training and placement program for unemployed and underemployed noncustodial parents in the Mid-Shore Region. The program assists participants in securing employment through industry training, job readiness preparation, and partnerships with local employers and temporary employment agencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides no-cost employment training and placement services including hard skills training in in-demand industries (forklift training, flagger certification, ServSafe, HVAC, security training, commercial driver's license, bartending, welding), soft skills training, job readiness preparation, industry-recognized certifications, work experience, transportation assistance, referrals to community services, barrier removal support (criminal record, legal services, driver's license suspension resolution), access to work items (clothing, tools, textbooks), and support from a personal career navigator and success coach.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Damien Ransome (Cecil, Kent, Queen Anne's); Louis Nichols (Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot); Kameka Sampson and Jada Johnson (Wicomico, Worcester, Somerset)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents with a Mid-Shore child support case who are unemployed or underemployed and able to commit to working upon program completion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment training in healthcare, construction, welding, hospitality, warehousing, biotechnology, and related fields. Training programs include forklift operation, flagger certification, food safety (ServSafe), HVAC systems, security training, commercial driver's license, bartending, and welding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Mid-Shore Region of Maryland, covering Cecil, Kent, Queen Anne's, Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester, and Somerset Counties.
requirements_list: Noncustodial party with an active Mid-Shore child support case
Currently unemployed or underemployed
Ability to commit to working upon program completion
No cost to participants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals should contact one of the Program Coordinators for their county or region. Contact information is provided for three regional coordinators covering the nine-county Mid-Shore area. The DHS help-line is available at 1-800-332-6347 for additional assistance. Enrollment sessions include an intake coordination meeting.

structured_extraction.program_name: Mobile Point of Sale Equipment Program (MPOSEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: MPOSEP provides grants to farmers markets and individual farmers or vendors to purchase mobile point of sale (mPOS) equipment that processes Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) transactions. The program aims to help farmers and vendors accept SNAP benefits and access the market of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program recipients. With over $1.1 billion in food assistance issued by Maryland DHS annually, the program seeks to help Maryland farmers realize improved access to the untapped market that SNAP recipients represent.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The programprovides grants to farmers markets and individual farmers or vendors for the purchase of ONE mobile point of sale (mPOS) device or system per market or vendor with a maximum grant amount of $600.00. mPOS equipment must be SNAP-compatible and may be used exclusively at Maryland Farmers Markets. Market-level systems operate through one centralized SNAP-EBT device for the entire market, while vendor-level systems allow each vendor to operate their own equipment to accept SNAP, debit, and credit payments directly from customers. Grantees must submit an Annual Activity Report indicating the number of SNAP transactions processed during the farmers market season. MPOSEP funds may not be used to purchase credit/debit card readers that do not accept SNAP, traditional POS terminals, or for any other purpose.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open application until all grant funds have been exhausted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers markets and individual farmers or vendors that are SNAP-authorized retailers in Maryland and operate at Maryland Farmers Markets that meet the state definition of a farmers market
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of ONE mobile point of sale (mPOS) device, system, or application (app) that accepts SNAP/EBT transactions. Maximum allowance is $600.00 per market or vendor. Equipment must only be used at Maryland Farmers Markets and may not be sub-contracted to third parties or used at locations outside of the Farmers Market(s).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be farmers markets or dedicated vendors in at least one of the Maryland Farmers Markets that meet the state definition of a farmers market and are able to accept SNAP. Applicants' inclusion in the annual Maryland Farmers Market Directory demonstrates eligibility. The program is available statewide to all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Be a farmers market or dedicated vendor in at least one of the Maryland Farmers Markets that meet the state definition and are able to accept SNAP (demonstrated through inclusion in Maryland Farmers Market Directory)
Complete USDA eAuthentication Account Registration
Apply and become authorized as a SNAP-authorized retailer
Provide proof of farmers market vendor membership(s) and authorized FNS number (via executed vendor agreement or letter from market manager, and copy of USDA FNS authorization letter)
For vendor applicants: Indicate vendor category (Farmer Vendor, Value Added Vendor, or Prepared Food Vendor) and provide permits and/or certifications for category products
Choose an mPOS device/application service that accepts SNAP
Submit complete MPOSEP grant application with all requested documentation including advertisements or web pages for listed mPOS equipment model numbers
Submit Annual Activity Report (AAR) indicating number of SNAP transactions processed during farmers market season (due October 31 each year)
Maintain records of all SNAP transactions and provide monthly receipt documentation logs or physical receipts
Provide proof of purchase for the mPOS device or system/app
Grantees must adhere to all SNAP laws, regulations, and the terms of Maryland state or private POS device retailer agreements
Post FNS-provided sign with information on reporting SNAP program abuses
Safeguard mPOS device from skimming and/or tampering; notify Bureau of Special Grants of any breaches
Guard against fraud and trafficking (exchange of SNAP benefits for cash or non-eligible items)

If market or vendor closes or suspends operations for more than 60 days during farmers market season, all award funds must be returned before terminating operations (applies only to fiscal year award was made)
Report any changes to organizational structure, leadership, location, vendor category, or business closure within 30 days to Bureau of Special Grants
Majority of mPOS transactions should be for SNAP-approved products; report 'no SNAP transactions' with explanation if applicable
Equipment may only be used by grantee at Maryland Farmers Markets; may not require customers to purchase SNAP-approved foods exclusively
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must first complete USDA eAuthentication Account Registration at https://identitymanager.eems.usda.gov/registration/selfRegistrationForm.aspx?level=1 and apply to become SNAP-authorized retailers at https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/store-farmers-market-application. Applicants must then gather proof of farmers market participation (executed vendor agreement or letter from market manager) and USDA FNS authorization letter. For individual vendor applicants, indicate vendor category and provide permits/certifications. Select an mPOS device/application service using guidance from https://farmersmarketcoalition.org/education/snap/ebt-equipment-services/. Complete the FY20 MPOSEP Grant Application form, providing all required information and documentation including advertisements/web pages for mPOS equipment model numbers, estimated monthly SNAP transactions, outreach plans, and SNAP-approved product list. Applications are evaluated based on inclusion of required documentation and signatures, thorough completion of all information, proposed outcomes including goals for increased outreach, and explanation of need. Submit completed application via email (preferred) to BureauOf.SpecialGrants@maryland.gov or mail to Department of Human Services, Attn: Bureau of Special Grants, 311 W. Saratoga Street, Room 216, Baltimore, Maryland 21201. Applicants approved to receive an MPOSEP grant will receive an award letter stating the terms of the agreement including award amount, grant year, deliverables with timelines, and DHS contact information. Following award, grantees must submit Annual Activity Reports on or before October 31 each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: The NETWorks Program serves non-custodial parents by providing a broad scope of resources to overcome barriers to employment and increase the likelihood that parents owing child support will be able to provide for themselves and their families. It operates as a supplemental service for the State's Tri Pep Program, which provides assessment and employment services.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers one-time financial support to help participants pay for identification, work boots, glasses, uniforms, interview attire, and transportation costs in connection with traveling to and from job interviews. Case managers work with participants to remove barriers to employment by potentially expunging criminal records or mitigating the negative impact of previous conduct. Training initiatives include GED and Driver Improvement courses, regional flagger certifications, work experience offerings for immediate employment, and CDL courses to advance employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-custodial parents owing child support who are residents of Somerset, Wicomico, or Worcester counties and who agree to the stipulations put forth by program administrators.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One-time financial support for identification, work boots, glasses, uniforms, interview attire, and transportation costs. Training for GED, driver improvement, regional flagger certifications, work experience, and CDL courses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program serves non-custodial parties in Somerset County, Wicomico County, and Worcester County through their respective Offices of Child Support.
requirements_list: Must be a non-custodial party owing child support
Must agree to the stipulations put forth by program administrators
Must be a resident of Somerset, Wicomico, or Worcester County
Applications will be reviewed on the merits and financial aid dependencies
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Non-custodial parties living in Somerset, Wicomico, or Worcester counties may apply. Applications will be reviewed on the merits and financial aid dependencies. Interested individuals should contact the program administrators at the phone numbers or email addresses provided.

structured_extraction.program_description: A family-focused initiative that empowers non-custodial parents to be financially, emotionally and physically supportive of their families through relationship and parental skill development, mediation, job readiness training, employment development, life skills counseling, and job placement and retention assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A no-cost program providing professional skills training, relationship and parental skill development, mediation services, job readiness training, employment development assistance, life skills counseling, and job placement and retention support. Program partners include local staffing agencies that help participants develop plans of action to improve employment prospects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-custodial parents with a Caroline County child support case who are unemployed or underemployed and can commit to working upon program completion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants receive training and support services to develop professional skills, improve relationships with co-parents and children, overcome barriers to employment, and transition successfully into employment with greater financial stability.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Caroline County only. Participants must have a Caroline County child support case.
requirements_list: Have a Caroline County child support case
Be unemployed or underemployed
Commit to working upon program completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested non-custodial parents should contact the Program Coordinator or call DHS's helpline for enrollment information and next steps.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program encourages noncustodial parents to make consistent child support payments by reducing or eliminating arrears owed to the State of Maryland. Noncustodial parents whose gross income is below 225% of the Federal Poverty Level can qualify to have state-owed arrears reduced by 50% after 12 consecutive months of on-time, court-ordered payments, or eliminated entirely after 24 consecutive months of on-time payments. Credit is given for uninterrupted court-ordered payments made immediately prior to program participation, and consideration is given for periods of unemployment due to seasonal work and no-fault job termination. Arrears owed directly to the family are not affected by this program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Arrears owed to the State of Maryland are reduced by 50% if the noncustodial parent pays child support as ordered for 12 consecutive months. Arrears are eliminated entirely (reduced to zero) if the parent pays as ordered for 24 consecutive months. Eligibility is limited to parents whose gross income is less than 225% of the Federal Poverty Level (number of household members is considered). Credit is given for uninterrupted court-ordered payments made immediately prior to program participation. Consideration is given for periods of unemployment due to seasonal work and no-fault job termination. Arrears owed directly to the family are not reduced.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents with a Maryland court order, state-owed child support arrears (arising because the custodial party received public assistance), and gross income below 225% of the Federal Poverty Level.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction or elimination of child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland through incentives for consistent, on-time court-ordered payments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicant must have a Maryland court order. Applications can be submitted to local child support offices in all 24 Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Applicant has a Maryland court order and there is an arrears balance owed to the state because the custodial party received public assistance
Applicant's gross income is less than 225% of the Federal Poverty Level (number of household members is considered)
Applicant has not been terminated from this program three or more times
Parent must pay child support as ordered for 12 consecutive months to receive a 50% reduction in state-owed arrears, or 24 consecutive months to have arrears eliminated entirely
A separate application must be completed for each case
Provide copies of most recent pay stubs, if available
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download and print the Payment Incentive Program application or complete the application online at www.dhs.maryland.gov/child-support-services/noncustodial-parents/payment-incentive-program. A separate application must be completed for each case. Submit the completed application to your local child support office by one of the following methods: bring it in personally, mail it to the local office address, email it (take a picture or scan), or fill it out online. Provide copies of the most recent pay stubs if available. Contact the Child Support Administration at 1-800-332-6347 for additional information. Local county offices and email addresses are available on the application form.

structured_extraction.program_description: A supportive housing program for adults with mental illness or other disabilities that provides a family-like living arrangement in a home setting. Residents receive case management services, assistance with daily living activities, medication supervision, and help connecting to community supports and activities. The program offers a more home-like and less costly alternative to nursing homes, psychiatric hospitals, and other institutional settings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residents receive room, board, supervision, assistance with activities of daily living, recreational and social activities, medication supervision, and transportation assistance to medical appointments. Care providers are reimbursed according to the resident's needs based on a level of care system established by the Project Home program. Reimbursements are not considered taxable income. Residents contribute to their cost of care and may be eligible to receive financial assistance from the local department of social services through the Public Assistance to Adults and Medical Assistance programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 18 or over with a mental, developmental, or physical disability or who are elderly and unable to live alone, who are willing and able to live in a family setting.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing, meals, supervision, assistance with daily living activities, medication management, recreational and social activities, and transportation to medical appointments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide through local Department of Social Services offices in all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Must be age 18 or over
Must have a documented mental, developmental, or physical disability or be elderly
Must be able to live in a family setting
Must be able to take advantage of community resources and program activities
Must be able to maintain or develop skills needed to live in the least restrictive environment possible
If taking medication, must be able to self-medicate or learn to self-medicate with cuing and coaching
Documentation of disability, income, and functional capability required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Adults interested in applying should contact their local Department of Social Services office. Applicants will be assigned a case manager by the local Department of Social Services who will assess the resident, inform the provider of the resident's strengths, weaknesses, and needs, develop an individualized service plan agreement, and assist in resolving concerns and obtaining supportive services. Documentation of disability, income, and functional capability will be required.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that pays for the cost of care and a personal needs allowance for individuals who live in assisted living facilities licensed by the Maryland Department of Health and in Certified Adult Residential Environmental homes (also known as Project Home). The program pays only the personal needs allowance to people in MDH Rehabilitative Residences. Recipients are eligible for Medical Assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program pays for the cost of care and a personal needs allowance for individuals in assisted living facilities and Certified Adult Residential Environmental homes. Recipients are eligible for Medical Assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals living in assisted living facilities licensed by the Maryland Department of Health, in Certified Adult Residential Environmental homes (Project Home), or in MDH Rehabilitative Residences who meet technical and financial eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for the cost of care and personal needs allowance for individuals in assisted living facilities, Certified Adult Residential Environmental homes, and MDH Rehabilitative Residences.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicants must meet technical and financial eligibility criteria
Applicants must apply for SSA (Social Security Administration) benefits as a condition of eligibility
The cost of care must be greater than the individual's countable income
Assets must not exceed the allowable limit
The assistance unit is always one person
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply online through the MarylandBenefits website at https://MarylandBenefits.gov/home/#/

structured_extraction.program_description: A workforce development and training program administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services that helps people receiving public assistance start and grow their own small businesses. The program offers eight business courses over approximately six weeks, delivered both virtually and in classroom settings, in partnership with Small Business Development Centers (SBDCs) across Maryland. Courses meet 1–2 times per week for approximately two hours each, and are offered in Spring and Fall sessions. The curriculum covers Entrepreneurship 101, Marketing Research, Financial Statements, Creating a Business Plan, Credit Restoration, A to Z Loan Process, Social Media Marketing, and Business Plan Presentation. Participants also receive ongoing consulting support from SBDC business consultants and workforce development training credit. The program is available statewide through local Departments of Social Services and has been specifically noted in jurisdictions including Howard County, Frederick County, and Washington County, as well as Eastern Shore and Western Maryland regions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive eight business courses over a six-week period covering Entrepreneurship 101, Marketing Research, Financial Statements, Creating a Business Plan, Credit Restoration, A to Z Loan Process, Social Media Marketing, and Business Plan Presentation. Classes meet 1–2 times per week for approximately two hours each, offered in Spring and Fall sessions both virtually and in classroom settings. The program includes ongoing consulting and support from the Maryland Small Business Development Center (SBDC), workforce development training credit, and instruction in a group setting with peers. Available statewide through local Departments of Social Services in Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) recipients, Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) recipients, Non-Custodial Parents, Foster Youth, and Veterans on Assistance who want to start or expand a small business. Broadly, any public assistance customer receiving services from a local Department of Social Services who has entrepreneurial goals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Entrepreneurship training and business development education, including instruction in business fundamentals, marketing, financial statements, business plan creation, credit restoration, loan processes, and social media marketing, as well as access to SBDC business consultants and ongoing consulting support to help participants start and operate a small business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local Departments of Social Services in Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City. Specific delivery noted in Howard County, Frederick County, Washington County, Eastern Shore, and Western Maryland regions, in partnership with regional Small Business Development Centers.
requirements_list: Must be receiving Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), or be a Non-Custodial Parent, Foster Youth, or Veteran on Assistance
Must be receiving assistance from a local Department of Social Services
Must be interested in starting or expanding a small business
Must attend all eight business classes
Must have ideas and talent in pursuit of entrepreneurial dreams of starting a small business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Marylanders receiving assistance from their local Department of Social Services can learn more and apply by visiting dhs.maryland.gov/PA2E or contacting their local family investment specialists to register for the next round of classes. In Howard County, contact howco.dss@maryland.gov or 410-872-8700. In Washington County, contact Steve Chapman at 240-420-2507 or Jarena Griffin at 240-420-2559. In Frederick County, contact the Frederick County Department of Social Services. Courses are offered in Spring and Fall sessions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial assistance to youth in foster care to help cover graduation expenses and support their transition to adulthood.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program covers various expenses for foster youth including graduation-related costs (class rings, senior pictures, prom attire, graduation fees), educational expenses (books, college application fees, scientific calculators, tutoring), transportation (bus passes, driver's education, driver's license), housing and household items (college dorm supplies, furniture, security deposit, start-up/household supplies), childcare (daycare), employment-related costs (business attire, job equipment), and other support services. These are referred to as Chafee expenditures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Foster youth in Maryland ages 14-20
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Graduation expenses, educational supplies and fees, transportation costs, housing and household items, childcare, employment-related attire and equipment, and other transition support services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a foster youth in Maryland
Must be ages 14 through 20 years old
Must be in out-of-home placement
Must have completed the Casey Life Skills Assessment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your case worker, attorney, or the Ready by 21 Independent Living Coordinators to apply and confirm eligibility requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: RFEP addresses childcare barriers for refugee parents attending English as a Second Language (ESOL) courses by providing simultaneous programming for young children ages 0-5 and their parents. Services include English classes and tutoring for parents, childhood enrichment courses and playgroups for children, and support services using a multi-generational approach.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MORA partners with Solutions in Hometown Connections to provide English classes, tutoring, childhood enrichment courses, playgroups, and support services for eligible refugee parents and children ages 0-5.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugee parents and their children ages 0-5 who are eligible for Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: English language training, tutoring, childhood enrichment, playgroup activities, and family support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an eligible refugee parent or child ages 0-5
Must be ORR-eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Solutions in Hometown Connections directly for enrollment information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A health education and wellness program that provides services to increase health literacy, coordinate and support navigation of the healthcare system, and organize wellness groups including mental wellness and peer support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MORA provides health education services for eligible clients to increase health literacy and support navigation of healthcare. Services include coordination of healthcare navigation, organization of wellness groups, and mental wellness and peer support services. Services are provided in coordination with medical screenings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible refugee clients interested in health education and wellness services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health education services, healthcare navigation support, wellness groups, mental wellness services, and peer support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Be an eligible refugee client
Meet program eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Clients interested in Refugee Health Promotion Program services may inquire during their medical screening appointment. Services are provided in coordination with medical screenings. For additional information and resources, clients may contact the Center for Global Migration and Immigrant Health at https://health.maryland.gov/phpa/OIDPCS/OIH/pages/home.aspx.

structured_extraction.program_description: Short-term medical coverage providing healthcare benefits similar to Medicaid for refugee populations who are ineligible for regular Medicaid. Coverage is available for up to 12 months after arrival in the United States, grant of asylum, eligible humanitarian parole status, or victim of trafficking certification.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: RMA provides medical coverage with similar benefits to Medicaid for eligible refugees. Families may be eligible for 12 months after arrival in the U.S. or grant of asylum, eligible humanitarian parole status, or victim of trafficking certification. Means-tested individuals under age 65 with no disabilities must first complete Medicaid application requirements through Maryland Health Connection. Those screened ineligible and over-scale income for Medicaid may apply for RMA through the MarylandBenefits portal.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugees, asylees, individuals with eligible humanitarian parole status, and victims of trafficking who are ineligible for Medicaid.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical coverage and healthcare services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Be a refugee, asylee, individual with eligible humanitarian parole status, or victim of trafficking
Be ineligible for Medicaid
Be within 12 months of U.S. arrival, grant of asylum, eligible humanitarian parole status, or victim of trafficking certification
For means-tested individuals under age 65 with no disabilities: complete Medicaid application requirements and be screened ineligible and over-scale income for Medicaid
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: All means-tested individuals under age 65 with no disabilities must first complete Medicaid application requirements to be screened for Medicaid eligibility through Maryland Health Connection. Upon being screened ineligible and over-scale income for Medicaid, clients may apply for RMA through the MarylandBenefits portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A health assessment program that provides comprehensive health evaluations for newly arrived refugees, asylees, parolees, and other immigrants. The program aims to initiate health assessment exams within 90 days of arrival or grant of asylum and complete them within 180 days. Screenings include physical and mental health evaluations, immunizations for school enrollment, and referrals to primary care physicians.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible refugees receive a comprehensive physical and mental health screening upon arrival to the United States. Screenings determine if new arrivals have medical conditions requiring immediate attention. Children also receive immunizations required for school enrollment. Clients are referred to a primary care physician for preventive health and ongoing care. Resettlement agencies are responsible for ensuring newly arrived refugees receive the screening.
structured_extraction.contact_email: RefugeeHealth@bmsi.org or RHA@cciweb.org depending on region
structured_extraction.program_audience: Newly arrived refugees, asylees, parolees, and other eligible immigrants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health assessment exams, mental health screening, immunizations, and referrals to primary care physicians.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services available in Baltimore Metropolitan Area (Baltimore City and surrounding counties) and Suburban Washington Area (Montgomery and Prince George's Counties). Local Health Departments throughout Maryland also provide services.
requirements_list: Be a newly arrived refugee, asylee, parolee, or other eligible immigrant
Meet eligibility requirements for the refugee health program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals who meet eligibility requirements may visit their local Health Department or one of the federally-qualified health clinics providing refugee medical screening services to access an initial health screening. In the Baltimore Metropolitan Area, contact Baltimore Medical Systems Highlandtown Clinic at 443-703-3404 or RefugeeHealth@bmsi.org. In the Suburban Washington Area (Montgomery and Prince George's Counties), contact CCI Health Services at 301-979-7656 or RHA@cciweb.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: RSIG supports school-aged refugee youth (primarily ages 0-18) to achieve academic success and provides support to public school systems serving refugee populations. The program ensures students have access to academic support outside the classroom, parents participate in their children's education, and school staff have cultural competence to address refugee needs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MORA provides grant funding through partnerships with the International Rescue Committee (IRC) and Baltimore City Community College (BCCC) to deliver academic support, English language acquisition, parent engagement activities, and culturally responsive education training for school staff.
structured_extraction.contact_name: International Rescue Committee (IRC) Silver Spring, International Rescue Committee (IRC) Baltimore, Baltimore City Community College (BCCC)
structured_extraction.program_audience: School-aged refugee youth ages 0-18, their parents, and public school systems in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic support, English language acquisition, parent engagement in school activities, and cultural competence training for school staff.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Throughout Maryland via partnership agencies in Silver Spring, Baltimore, and Baltimore City Community College.
requirements_list: Must be school-aged refugee youth ages 0-18
Must be ORR-eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the International Rescue Committee (Silver Spring or Baltimore) or Baltimore City Community College for program enrollment and participation details.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-administered and federally-funded temporary financial assistance program that provides cash support to eligible refugees and asylees until they can secure employment and become economically independent.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Temporary cash assistance benefits provided to eligible clients to support them until they secure employment and become economically independent. The program is limited to individuals who have held an eligible and documented immigration status in the U.S. for less than 4 months after arrival or after an asylum grant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugees and asylees who meet eligibility requirements and can provide proof of eligible immigration status.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary financial assistance for living expenses until employment and economic independence are achieved.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties. Application is made through local Resettlement Agencies located in the Baltimore Metropolitan Area, Suburban Washington Area, and Frederick Area.
requirements_list: Have held an eligible and documented immigration status in the U.S. less than 4 months after arrival to the U.S. or after an asylum grant
Be ineligible for other cash assistance programs including TANF, SSI, OAA, AB, APTD, and AABD
Not be a full-time student in institutions of higher education
Meet income eligibility guidelines
Complete all required paperwork to be enrolled in RCA or RTCA, including providing proof of an eligible immigration status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must contact one of the local Resettlement Agencies in Maryland to apply. MORA administers RTCA in partnership with local Resettlement Agencies. Contact information is provided for agencies in the Baltimore Metropolitan Area, Suburban Washington Area, and Frederick Area. Applications can be submitted either remotely or in-person.

structured_extraction.program_description: RYMP promotes positive civic and social engagement and supports academic and vocational achievement for refugee youth ages 15-24. The program provides grant funding to help youth achieve academic success, advance vocational and career goals, and become socially integrated. Local resettlement agencies match eligible youth with mentors who provide personalized guidance and support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MORA provides grant funding to local resettlement agencies to match eligible youth ages 15-24 with mentors who deliver personalized guidance, support services, and mentoring to facilitate social integration and economic self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ethiopian Community Development Council (ECDC), International Rescue Committee (IRC) Baltimore, International Rescue Committee (IRC) Silver Spring, Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area (LSSNCA)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Refugee youth ages 15-24 who are eligible for Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mentoring services, academic achievement support, vocational and career advancement guidance, and social inclusion activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Throughout Maryland via partnership agencies.
requirements_list: Must be refugee youth ages 15-24
Must be ORR-eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Ethiopian Community Development Council (ECDC), International Rescue Committee (Baltimore or Silver Spring), or Lutheran Social Services of the National Capital Area (LSSNCA) for enrollment and mentorship matching.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Restaurant Meals Program allows eligible SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) recipients who are elderly, homeless, or disabled to use their EBT benefits card to purchase prepared or hot meals from participating restaurants and delis. SNAP households experiencing homelessness can also use their Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) benefits to purchase meals at restaurants that have contracted with the federal government to participate in the program, sometimes at a concessional (discount) price. The program is available statewide in Maryland at participating restaurants and is expanding to additional jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible SNAP recipients can use their EBT card to purchase prepared meals (breakfast, lunch, or dinner) directly from participating restaurants and delis. Homeless households can also purchase meals at a concessional (discount) price through restaurants contracted with the federal government. Eligible recipients are those who are experiencing homelessness, are age 60 or older (including spouses), or are disabled (including the spouse of the disabled individual if the two are the only participants on the SNAP case). There is no change to the recipient's benefit amount. Sales receipts show the meal cost and remaining SNAP benefit balance. Participating restaurants cannot charge tax on Restaurant Meals Program (RMP) transactions. Benefits cannot be used to purchase alcoholic beverages or non-food items. For restaurants to participate, they must submit a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Maryland Department of Human Services and complete an application for certification with the USDA Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) form FNS-252-2. After DHS reviews these forms, they will be elevated to FNS for final certification. FNS will issue a certification number to accept SNAP benefits under the Restaurant Meals Program if the restaurant qualifies. A store cannot be both a restaurant participating in the Restaurant Meals Program and a traditional SNAP retailer by definition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: SNAP recipients who are elderly (age 60 or older), experiencing homelessness, or disabled. Spouses of elderly or disabled SNAP recipients may also qualify if they are the only other participant on the SNAP case. For restaurant owners: Private for-profit restaurants seeking to increase revenue while serving their community by allowing customers to use SNAP/EBT benefits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing prepared breakfast, lunch, or dinner meals from participating restaurants and delis. Benefits cannot be used for alcoholic beverages or non-food items. For restaurants: The program provides an opportunity to increase revenue.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available at participating restaurants throughout Maryland, currently including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Calvert, Cecil, Charles, Frederick, Harford, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, and Washington counties, with expansion to additional jurisdictions ongoing. Recipients are not able to purchase meals at restaurants outside of Maryland under the standard program; however, eligible RMP participants from Maryland can use their SNAP EBT benefits at restaurants in other states that are authorized to run a Restaurant Meals Program, such as Virginia.
requirements_list: Must be a SNAP recipient experiencing homelessness, age 60 or older, or disabled
If age 60 or older, spouse is also eligible
If disabled, spouse eligibility requires that the two are the only participants on the SNAP case
Eligibility is reviewed and must be reconfirmed at every SNAP redetermination
Must use EBT card at a participating restaurant
For restaurants: Must be a private for-profit establishment that contracts with an appropriate state or local agency
For restaurants: Must agree to offer meals at concessional prices to eligible SNAP recipients
For restaurants: Cannot be both a restaurant in the Restaurant Meals Program and a traditional SNAP retailer
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For SNAP recipients: Recipients do not need to apply separately to participate in the Restaurant Meals Program. Eligibility is determined during the standard SNAP application and recertification/redetermination process. To use the program: (1) Find a participating restaurant on the DHS list or ask your Eligibility Worker for a list in your county, (2) Call 1-800-997-2222 or visit www.connectebt.com to confirm your EBT card balance, (3) Purchase a meal at a participating restaurant using your EBT card, (4) Receive a receipt showing the meal cost and remaining SNAP benefit balance. For restaurants: (1) Complete a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Maryland Department of Human Services, (2) Complete an application for certification with the USDA Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) form FNS-252-2, (3) Submit both forms to the Maryland Department of Human Services, (4) DHS will review the forms and elevate them to FNS, (5) FNS will send certification number if restaurant qualifies. Contact Annette Jones-Wilson at annette.jones-wilson@maryland.gov for more information on restaurant participation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Safe Haven Program allows a mother or responsible adult to surrender a newborn without the risk of arrest or prosecution. The newborn must be 60 days or younger and unharmed. The program aims to reduce newborn mortality and promote a healthy beginning for newborns by offering a safe alternative for a parent who is unable or unwilling to care for their child. Once surrendered, the newborn receives necessary medical care before being placed with the Local Department of Social Services for permanent family placement. Parents may change their mind by contacting the Local Department of Social Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Parents or responsible adults can surrender a newborn at a designated facility including hospitals, licensed medical providers, police departments, state police barracks, and insured fire companies (whether volunteer or professional). The responsible adult must be 18 years or older. The newborn receives any necessary medical care to ensure their well-being before being placed with the Local Department of Social Services (LDSS) with the goal of adoption and placement with a permanent, stable family. The program provides a safe way for parents to surrender a newborn without legal consequences. Parents can change their mind by contacting the Local Department of Social Services at 1-800-917-7383. All calls can be made anonymously.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Mothers, parents, or responsible adults who are unable or unwilling to care for a newborn 60 days or younger.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides care coordination and placement services for surrendered newborns, including medical care at the surrender facility and placement with the Local Department of Social Services for adoption and placement with a permanent, stable family home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout all Maryland counties. Designated facilities include hospitals, licensed medical providers, police departments, state police barracks, and insured fire companies located throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Newborn must be 60 days or younger
Newborn must be unharmed (no evidence of physical injury or failure to provide proper care and attention)
Responsible adult must be 18 years or older
Can be surrendered at hospitals, licensed medical providers, police departments, state police barracks, or insured fire companies
Direct handover must occur between the mother/responsible adult and a designated facility staff member; newborn must never be left unattended
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Local Department of Social Services at 1-800-917-7383 to notify DHS of a surrender or to get a list of designated facilities. Call 2-1-1 to locate the nearest Safe Haven facility. Upon arrival at a designated facility, state 'This is a Safe Haven baby.' Staff may ask questions about the newborn's health and family health history, but you are not required to answer. The newborn receives medical attention at the facility before being discharged to the LDSS for adoption and placement with a permanent, stable family. A direct handover must occur; the newborn must never be left unattended.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps foster youth ages 16-21 learn and practice independent living skills while receiving support from their local department of social services. Youth in SILA can live in various settings including renting a room, living in their own apartments, or staying on campus in a dorm. Each month, SILA youth receive a check from the department to help cover living expenses. Youth work or attend school while developing skills needed for self-sufficiency, and must contribute to living costs through earned income, scholarships, stipends, grants, work study, Social Security, or combinations thereof.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each month, SILA youth receive a check from their local department of social services to help cover living expenses. Youth receive housing support and services from the local department and provider agency. Youth must contribute to living costs through earned income, scholarships, stipends, grants, work study, Social Security, or combinations thereof. SILA payments continue each month until the youth's 21st birthday.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ready by 21 Specialist / Independent Living Coordinator
structured_extraction.program_audience: Foster youth ages 16-21 in out-of-home placement who are sufficiently mature, demonstrate the ability to manage money, and are continually enrolled in school or vocational training or working at least 80 hours per month, and need help transitioning to self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing, basic living expenses including rent, utilities, and other costs associated with semi-independent living, as well as independent living skills development support.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through all 24 local departments of social services in Maryland statewide, including Baltimore City. For Baltimore City residents, applications are processed through the Ready by 21 Program at 1920 N. Broadway, Baltimore, MD 21213.
requirements_list: Between 16-21 years old
Sufficiently mature
Demonstrate an ability to manage money
Continually enrolled in and regularly attending school or vocational training, or working at least 80 hours per month
Maintain employment
Have a goal of self-sufficiency
Agrees to the requirements of the independent living service agreement
Needs help in transitioning to self-sufficiency
Is capable of contributing to the cost of living through earned income, scholarships, stipends, grants, work study, Social Security, or any combination
Able and willing to contribute to the cost of semi-independent living
Youth with documented disability in living skills may be eligible if case plan documents how disability can be accommodated
Independent living assessment must be completed
Life skills training must be completed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain a SILA application and information packet from your local department of social services case worker, attorney, or by calling the Ready by 21 Program at 443-423-6134. 2. Review the program information to determine if SILA is right for you. 3. Complete the application fully and sign it. Contact your caseworker or attorney if you have questions. 4. Give the completed application to your caseworker for review. The caseworker will sign the application and provide you a copy. Any problems will be corrected with caseworker assistance. 5. Your caseworker returns the completed application to: Angela Smith, Ready by 21 Program, 1920 N. Broadway, Baltimore, MD 21213, 443-423-6134. 6. The Ready by 21 Specialist will review your application and schedule an interview with you and your caseworker within three business days. You, your caseworker, and attorney will receive a letter confirming the interview. 7. At the SILA interview, you will be asked why you want to be in the program and how you will manage expenses and maintain your living arrangement. 8. You will receive a letter the next business day notifying you of admission or denial. If denied, the letter will explain why and how to request a review. 9. If approved, you will be assigned a SILA worker who will meet with you within 30 days to set up a SILA budget, develop a service agreement, and answer questions. 10. You will receive a SILA payment each month until your 21st birthday.

structured_extraction.program_name: Services Helping the Involvement of Non-Custodial Parents and Employment (SHINE)
structured_extraction.program_description: A free, comprehensive 12-month case management program designed for noncustodial parents obligated to pay child support. The program helps participants overcome barriers to employment, secure financial stability, and strengthen relationships with their children through employment services, legal aid, family resources, and basic needs support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free case management and connections to community resources including: job readiness activities, skill building (resume development, interview skills, job retention strategies), occupational and vocational training, GED classes, assistance obtaining vital documents (birth certificates, Social Security cards, photo IDs, driver's licenses), legal aid (expungement, mediation), parenting resources, mental health and substance abuse referrals, housing assistance, transportation resources, financial assistance for state benefits, work clothing, hygiene products, and child care resources. Participants meet regularly with a Non-Custodial Parent Employment Program (NPEP) Specialist over 12 months. The program includes comprehensive intake assessment to identify strengths, needs, barriers to employment, and personalized service planning with goal-setting and progress monitoring.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents in Allegany County who are obligated to pay child support and seeking stable employment. Participants are typically ordered into the program by a Magistrate during a contempt hearing for outstanding child support arrearages or referred by the Child Support Administration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program participants receive case management, employment support services, job training and education (including GED classes and vocational training), legal assistance, documentation support (birth certificates, Social Security cards, photo IDs, driver's licenses), parenting resources, mental health and substance abuse referrals, housing assistance, transportation support, financial benefits assistance, work clothing, hygiene products, and child care resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available only in Allegany County, Maryland. Participants must be referred by a court order or the Child Support Administration.
requirements_list: Must be a noncustodial parent obligated to pay child support
Must be seeking stable employment
Must require support to comply with child support order
Must not have known physical or mental disabilities that prevent working
Typically ordered by Magistrate during contempt hearing for outstanding arrearages or referred by Child Support Administration
Must complete intake assessment with NPEP Specialist
Must attend set interval meetings with NPEP Specialist throughout 12-month program
Must report weekly job search activities
Must report current employment status and income
Must report child support payment history
Must immediately report changes of address, phone number, or employment status
Must provide demographic information and documentation status during intake (driver's license, Social Security card, birth certificate, photo ID)
Must participate in goal-setting and service planning process
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants are typically referred through court order or by the Child Support Administration. The local DSS office schedules an intake appointment. During intake, participants meet with a Non-Custodial Parent Employment Program (NPEP) Specialist at the Allegany County DSS office. The NPEP Specialist conducts a comprehensive strengths and needs assessment using the SHINE Intake Assessment Form (DES-499) to evaluate demographics, documentation status, transportation, substance abuse and legal history, financial resources, living arrangements, dependents, health and mental health conditions, education and employment background, skills and interests, and employment barriers. Based on the assessment, the specialist and participant develop a personalized service plan with goals and action steps. Participants then enter a 12-month case management phase with ongoing monitoring and meetings at set intervals to track progress and address needs.
