structured_extraction.program_description: SNAP (formerly known as Food Stamps) is the largest federal nutrition assistance program in the nation, administered in Maryland by the Maryland Department of Human Services. It helps low-income households buy the food they need for good health by increasing their purchasing power based on the USDA's Thrifty Food Plan and Maximum Allotment guidelines. Eligible households receive monthly benefits loaded onto an EBT Independence Card that works like a debit card at participating retail stores, authorized online retailers (including Amazon, Walmart, ShopRite, Food Lion, Giant of Maryland, Martin's, Aldi, Weis, and Safeway), and authorized restaurants. The program feeds more than 680,000 Marylanders each month, including nearly 270,000 children, with an average monthly benefit of $180 per customer. Benefits are calculated based on household size, gross household income, and allowable expenses, and must be supplemented with the household's own funds to cover the full monthly food budget. Some households with little or no money may qualify for Expedited SNAP benefits within 7 days of applying. As of July 4, 2025, expanded work requirements apply to adults ages 18–64 without a child under 14 in the home (previously ages 18–54 with exemptions for those with children under 18), and restrictions on immigrant eligibility have been implemented. Benefits can also be used at certain restaurants under the Restaurant Meals Program for eligible elderly, disabled, or homeless individuals. Interpreter services are available for free in multiple languages.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly food benefits issued on an EBT Independence Card based on household size, gross household income, and allowable expenses, calculated according to the USDA Maximum Allotment and Thrifty Food Plan. The average monthly benefit is approximately $180 per customer. Benefits are deposited into the EBT account within 30 days from the date the application is filed. Applicants who qualify for expedited benefits due to very low income or little/no money may receive benefits within 7 days of filing. As of October 1, 2025, the Standard Utility Allowance is $572 for households with an elderly or disabled member; other households must provide proof of utility bills from the last 30 days to receive utility deductions. Households must supplement benefits with their own cash to cover the full monthly food budget. Benefits can be used to purchase eligible food items at authorized retail stores and online retailers (Amazon, Walmart, ShopRite, Food Lion, Giant of Maryland, Martin's, Aldi, Weis, Safeway), and under the Restaurant Meals Program, at certain participating restaurants for eligible elderly, disabled, or homeless individuals. Benefits cannot be used to pay for shipping or delivery costs. As of July 4, 2025, new federal restrictions on eligible immigrants apply, limiting eligibility to lawful permanent residents, Cuban or Haitian entrants, and individuals from the Federated States of Micronesia and the Republic of the Marshall Islands. Expanded work requirements now apply to adults ages 18–64 without a child under 14 in the home; veterans, people experiencing homelessness, and young adults who aged out of out-of-home care and are under age 24 are now subject to work requirements. Benefits are issued by last name between the 4th and 23rd of each month for SNAP (schedule varies by first three letters of last name).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals and families statewide in Maryland, including those who work for low wages, are unemployed or work part-time, receive Temporary Cash Assistance or other public assistance, are elderly or disabled with small incomes, or are homeless. As of July 4, 2025, eligible applicants include U.S. citizens and qualified non-citizens limited to lawful permanent residents (green card holders), Cuban or Haitian entrants, and people from the Federated States of Micronesia and the Republic of the Marshall Islands. Refugees and people granted asylum who have not yet obtained Lawful Permanent Resident status are no longer eligible as of July 4, 2025. Everyone meeting citizenship/immigrant status requirements has the right to apply for SNAP.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of eligible food items at authorized participating retail stores, online retailers (Amazon, Walmart, ShopRite, Food Lion, Giant of Maryland, Martin's, Aldi, Weis, Safeway), and under the Restaurant Meals Program at certain participating restaurants for eligible elderly, disabled, or homeless individuals. Benefits support the purchase of nutritious food to prepare meals at home. Benefits cannot be used for non-food items, prepared meals (except under the Restaurant Meals Program for eligible individuals), alcohol, tobacco, hot foods, or delivery/shipping costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland. Applications are filed with the Local Department of Social Services in the applicant's county, including all 23 counties and Baltimore City. County-level administration is available in Montgomery County, Howard County, Prince George's County, Calvert County, and all other jurisdictions. For Montgomery County residents, apply through the Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal or in person at one of three regional offices or the TESS Center. For Howard County residents, apply in person at Howard County DSS (9780 Patuxent Woods Drive, Columbia, MD 21046) or drop off the application at the front desk. For Calvert County residents, contact Calvert County DSS at 200 Duke Street, Prince Frederick, MD 20678, or call 443-550-6900.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov (https://mydhrbenefits.dhr.state.md.us/dashboardClient/#/home) using a smartphone, tablet, or computer. Alternatively, download the application form (DHS/FIA 9701) and submit it by mail, fax, in person at your Local Department of Social Services, or through an authorized representative. The application is accepted the same day it is submitted. Applicants may sign and submit the first page of the application and complete the rest at home, returning it within 90 days. After submission, the office will review the application within 7 days to determine initial eligibility. If not interviewed on the day of submission, the local department will contact you to schedule an interview, which may be conducted by telephone when possible. A case manager will review rules and help complete any missing sections. Required verifications (income, shelter costs, identity, residence, citizenship/immigration status) must be submitted within 90 days. Benefits are issued within 30 days of application receipt. Households with very low income (less than $150 monthly gross income and $100 or less in resources) or little/no money may qualify for expedited benefits within 7 days of filing if they meet expedited eligibility criteria and complete required documents. For expedited benefits, household must meet one of three conditions: (1) total household monthly rent/mortgage plus utilities exceed household income and resources, (2) gross monthly income less than $150 and resources $100 or less, or (3) household is destitute migrant or seasonal farm worker with $100 or less in cash and savings. SSI recipients may apply at Social Security district offices. Households applying for public assistance or medical assistance can apply simultaneously. Interpreter services are available at no cost in multiple languages. For Montgomery County residents, apply through the Maryland Benefits Programs & Services Portal or in person at one of three regional offices or the TESS Center. For Howard County residents, apply in person at Howard County DSS (9780 Patuxent Woods Drive, Columbia, MD 21046) or drop off application at front desk. For Calvert County residents, contact Calvert County DSS at 200 Duke Street, Prince Frederick, MD 20678, or call 443-550-6900. Contact your local department of social services or the Customer Service hotline at 1-800-332-6347 for assistance. Maryland EBT Card Balance and account inquiries: 1-800-997-2222 (24/7). Online balance checking available at www.connectebt.com.

structured_extraction.program_name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program Employment and Training (SNAP E&T)
structured_extraction.program_description: SNAP E&T is a free job training program that connects SNAP recipients to employment in job-driven industries. The program runs for an average of 12 to 16 weeks and provides hard skills training in fields such as welding, construction, machine operation, manufacturing, healthcare, hospitality, and computer technology/IT; soft skills development; job readiness; job placement and retention; industry-recognized certifications and credentials; work experience; transportation assistance; referrals to community services; help resolving employment barriers such as criminal records, legal services, or driver's licenses; and access to work items such as clothing, tools, or textbooks. All programs include support from a personal career navigator and success coach. Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) may be required to participate to maintain benefit eligibility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free training programs lasting an average of 12 to 16 weeks that provide hard skills training in in-demand industries including welding, construction, machine operation, machining, manufacturing, healthcare, hospitality, and computer technology/IT; soft skills training; job readiness; job search and placement assistance; industry-recognized certifications and credentials; work experience; transportation assistance; referrals to community services; resolution of employment barriers (e.g., criminal records, legal services, driver's licenses); access to work-related items such as clothing, uniforms, tools, protective gear, or textbooks; childcare support; dependent care assistance; legal services; and support from a personal career navigator and success coach. Specific SNAP E&T providers may offer additional services such as case management, supervised job search, job retention follow-up, mental health and crisis intervention support tied to retention, enhanced coaching time, and barrier mitigation services. Many programs provide wraparound support services including snacks and refreshments, participation stipends, bus passes, vision correction, dental work, and other services to ensure participants can fully engage in training.
structured_extraction.program_audience: SNAP recipients who are at least 16 years old, do not receive Cash Assistance/Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), and are able to work upon completion of the program. Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) may be required to participate to maintain SNAP benefit eligibility. Programs serve underemployed and unemployed adults, including young adults ages 18-24 disconnected from school or work, returning citizens, individuals with barriers to employment such as low educational attainment, limited transportation, childcare needs, low literacy, limited English proficiency, single parents, individuals involved with the justice system, and those with insufficient financial stability or other employment barriers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training in in-demand industries including welding, construction, machine operation, machining, manufacturing, healthcare, hospitality, and computer technology/IT. Support covers hard skills and soft skills training, job readiness, job placement and retention, transportation assistance, work experience, access to work-related items including clothing, uniforms, tools, protective gear, textbooks, childcare support, dependent care assistance, legal services, and removal of employment barriers. Individual SNAP E&T programs may offer specific certifications and credentials aligned with employer partnerships and local labor market needs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland statewide through multiple third-party providers serving specific service areas. Statewide providers include Baltimore Cyber Range LLC (serving statewide), Biotechnical Institute of Maryland (serving statewide), and Codex Academy Technologies (serving statewide). Regional providers serve specific counties and service areas including Allegany County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Prince George's County, Montgomery County, Anne Arundel County, Carroll County, Harford County, Howard County, St. Mary's County, and Charles County.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: There is no formal application for SNAP E&T. To enroll, contact your local Department of Social Services (DSS) or call the DHS helpline at (800) 332-6347. If you are not currently receiving SNAP benefits but are interested in the program, you can apply for SNAP benefits online at marylandbenefits.gov or in person at your local department of social services. A list of SNAP E&T providers is available through the Third Party Partner Public Database at https://dhs.maryland.gov/documents/SNAP/FFY 26-28 Third Party Partner Public Database.pdf. Contact the specific SNAP E&T training programs in your area for enrollment details. Each provider has designated intake coordinators and enrollment specialists available during specific office hours to assist with enrollment, assessment, and placement into appropriate training programs based on participant goals and barriers.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides partial child support payments to families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA). When a noncustodial parent pays current child support, a portion of that payment is passed through to the custodial party receiving cash assistance, up to a maximum amount based on the number of children in the household.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides monthly pass-through payments to custodial parties. The maximum monthly payment is $100 for families with one child or $200 for families with two or more children. A family receives the maximum payment or the court-ordered child support amount for that month, whichever is less. The payment is based on current support paid in the prior calendar month. Payments on back child support (arrears) are not eligible for pass through.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Custodial parties (typically parents or caregivers) receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) who have court-ordered child support obligations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The pass-through payments go directly to the custodial party receiving cash assistance and can be used for any purpose.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have an active Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) case
Must have an active child support case with current support obligations
Noncustodial parent must have made a current support payment in the prior calendar month
Payments on child support arrears do not qualify for pass through
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application is required. Eligibility is automatic when a family has both an active TCA case and an active child support case with current support payments. Once a noncustodial parent makes a current support payment, the pass-through amount is calculated based on the total current support paid in that calendar month and the number of children in the TCA household, then paid to the custodial party in the following month.

structured_extraction.program_name: Supporting, Training, and Employing Parents Program (STEP Up)
structured_extraction.program_description: Supporting, Training, and Employing Parents (STEP Up) is a job-driven pilot program administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services that provides free job training and support services to unemployed or underemployed noncustodial parents with a Baltimore City child support case. The program helps participants overcome employment barriers and develop careers in in-demand industries such as welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, hospitality, warehousing, biotechnology, building deconstruction, culinary arts, retail customer service, solar energy installation, brownfields remediation, and administrative professional skills. Participants receive hard skills and soft skills training, industry-recognized certifications, work experience, transportation assistance, job readiness and placement services, and access to a personal career navigator and success coach. Those who successfully complete the program can earn forgiveness for child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: STEP Up provides no-cost job training and comprehensive support services to noncustodial parents. Services include: hard skills training in in-demand industries (welding, green construction, machining, healthcare, hospitality, warehousing, biotechnology, building deconstruction, culinary arts, retail customer service, solar energy installation, brownfields remediation, and administrative professional skills); soft skills training in communication and customer service; job readiness preparation; job search and placement assistance; industry-recognized certifications and credentialing; work experience; transportation assistance; referrals to community services; assistance resolving employment barriers such as criminal record issues, legal issues, and driver's license suspensions; access to work-related items such as clothing, tools, and textbooks; and support from a personal career navigator and success coach. Participants who successfully complete their training and employment commitment can earn forgiveness for child support arrears owed to the State of Maryland.

Funds also support industry certifications, job search and placement services, transportation assistance, work supplies (clothing, tools, textbooks), legal services, and support to overcome employment barriers.

structured_extraction.program_description: Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) is Maryland's Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) program, administered by the Maryland Department of Human Services. It provides time-limited cash assistance to families with dependent children under 18 years of age when available resources do not fully address the family's needs. The program promotes individual responsibility and self-sufficiency by preparing participants for independence through work-related activities, job readiness programs, volunteer work experience placement, and vocational education and training. Benefits are issued via an Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card called the Independence Card and are available statewide through local Departments of Social Services offices. The program also offers Welfare Avoidance Grants (WAG) to help with employment-related expenses such as transportation, temporary childcare, tools, uniforms, or other items.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Time-limited cash assistance for eligible families with dependent children under 18 years of age. The benefit amount is based on the assistance unit size and benefit level according to an income standard table (e.g., $328/month for family of 1, $575/month for family of 2, $870/month for family of 4, up to $1,372/month for family of 8). Earned and unearned income (excluding SSI income) cannot exceed the benefit level paid for the assistance unit size. Families with minor children have a lifetime limit of 60 months (5 years) of assistance. Benefits are issued via an Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card (the Independence Card), made available between the 2nd and 4th of each month based on the first letter of the applicant's last name. Cash can be accessed at ATMs or as a direct payment. Participants must complete 40 hours per week of approved work activities to receive the full TCA benefit amount. The program includes job readiness training, job search assistance, volunteer work experience placement, and vocational education and training. Childcare and transportation assistance may be provided to help participants attend job readiness classes and work programs. Welfare Avoidance Grants (WAG) are available to help with employment-related expenses for those who may exceed TCA income limits or to retain current employment.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jordyn Cooke, Julia Feaster, Jean-Marie Benishay, Stephanie Paulino
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with dependent children under 18 years of age and qualifying individuals who have low income and whose available resources do not fully meet their needs. Pregnant women may also be eligible. U.S. citizens and qualified immigrants are eligible. Caretaker relatives applying for children who are not their own may have different requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash assistance to help meet basic family needs and living expenses while participants prepare for independence through work and employment activities. Welfare Avoidance Grants can be used for employment-related expenses including transportation, temporary childcare, tools, uniforms, and other items needed to obtain or retain employment.

County-level offices include Prince George's County (805 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785), Howard County DSS, and Montgomery County DHHS locations in Rockville (1301 Piccard Drive), Silver Spring (8818 Georgia Ave), and Germantown (12900 Middlebrook Rd).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at MarylandBenefits.gov or through MyDHR (Maryland Department of Human Resources benefits portal); apply in person at your local Department of Social Services; or file an application by mail, fax, email, or other electronic means. Someone may also drop off an application on your behalf. Applicants must complete a face-to-face interview with a case manager at the local DHHS office. In Montgomery County, the application process includes: (1) View the DHHS Orientation video; (2) Download and complete the DHHS Orientation packet including the Personal Responsibility Plan and Work Opportunities Customer Information Form; (3) Submit the orientation packet via email to Employment.Services@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov or by fax; (4) Contact Equus to register for the Work Program and schedule the mandatory substance abuse screening appointment the day after attending orientation; (5) Attend work program registration and begin mandatory work activities within 30 days of TCA case approval. In Prince George's County, applications may also be mailed to the Administrative Office at 805 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785. Free interpretation services are available for customers with limited English proficiency. All applicants must provide required verifications including proof of identity, Social Security numbers, residence, income (wage stubs), birth certificates, monthly expenses, and citizenship/immigration status. Once TCA case is approved, recipients must sign a Personal Responsibility Plan outlining rights and responsibilities.

structured_extraction.program_description: TDAP provides short-term cash assistance to low-income disabled individuals without dependent children who are unable to work due to a physical or mental disability. The program supports eligible Marylanders during a period of short-term disability or while they are awaiting approval of federal disability support such as Supplemental Security Income (SSI). Recipients may receive benefits for only 12 months out of a 36-month period unless they are actively pursuing SSI. Those disabled for 12 months or more must file an application for SSI, and recipients must agree to reimburse the program from any future SSI payment received.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Time-limited cash assistance provided to eligible low-income disabled individuals without dependent children and no other resources. Recipients may receive benefits for only 12 months out of a 36-month period unless they are pursuing SSI. Those disabled for 12 months or more must file an application for SSI. Income from a spouse in the household (except SSI benefits) is counted when determining eligibility. Recipients must agree to reimburse the program from any future SSI payment received.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income disabled individuals (physical or mental disability) without dependent children who are unable to work and are awaiting SSI/SSDI determination or experiencing a period of short-term disability. Available statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Basic living expenses and cash benefits during a period of disability while disability status is verified and/or while an SSI/SSDI application is being processed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Local Department of Social Services offices administer the program in each county, including Howard County and Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Cannot be working
Cannot have the capacity to work for at least 3 months
Cannot be receiving unemployment benefits
Disability (physical or mental) must be verified by a licensed medical practitioner who completes a medical report
Applicants disabled for 12 months or more must file an application for Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
May be required to apply for SSI and SSDI
Must agree to reimbursement from any SSI payment received
Must be a U.S. citizen or legally admitted alien for permanent residency
Must be low-income
Must not have dependent children
Must have no other resources
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply online through MarylandBenefits.gov at https://MarylandBenefits.gov/home/#/ or at https://mydhrbenefits.dhr.state.md.us/. Applicants may also apply in person at their Local Department of Social Services, by mail, by fax, by other electronic means, or have someone drop off an application on their behalf.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program created through the Emergency Assistance Act of 1983 that provides USDA Foods and federal funds to eligible agencies like soup kitchens, food pantries, and shelters to distribute emergency food assistance to low-income individuals and families. The program operates in partnership with the Maryland Food Bank and Capital Area Food Bank across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides USDA Foods at no cost to eligible agencies. USDA Foods include canned fruits, canned vegetables, fruit juice, dried egg mix, meat, poultry, fish, dried beans, pasta products, milk, rice, grits, cereal, and soups. Foods are distributed through eligible agencies (Eligible Recipient Agencies/ERAs including soup kitchens, food pantries, and shelters) and Emergency Feeding Organizations (EFOs) across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. Distribution is based on jurisdictional allocations calculated using a formula weighted by population (primary factor), poverty rate (60% weighting), and unemployment rate (40% weighting). Each jurisdiction receives a target percentage allocation of total food pounds distributed. Administrative funds are provided to cover all costs of receiving, storing, tracking, and distributing TEFAP food, with no costs incurred by ERAs or end recipients. Sponsoring Agencies utilize transportation fleets including refrigerated vehicles to deliver foods. Both refrigerated and fresh produce are available. Entitlement foods are ordered from catalogs and funded through annual allocations. Bonus foods are offered periodically at no additional cost when available. Technical assistance and training in civil rights compliance are provided to participating organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals and families seeking emergency food assistance through eligible agencies such as soup kitchens, food pantries, and shelters. Eligibility includes SNAP recipients, Medical Assistance recipients, TANF recipients, unemployment recipients, Energy Assistance recipients, or households with income at or below 185% of Federal Poverty Guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency food assistance in the form of USDA-provided food items distributed through eligible agencies to people in need. Food items include canned fruits and vegetables, fruit juice, dried egg mix, meat, poultry, fish, dried beans, pasta products, milk, rice, grits, cereal, and soups. For eligible agencies (ERAs/EFOs), administrative funds cover costs of ordering, receiving, storing, tracking, and distributing TEFAP foods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions. Residents in Montgomery and Prince George's counties should contact the Capital Area Food Bank. Residents in other Maryland counties should contact the Maryland Food Bank. MFB serves 22 jurisdictions: Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, Worcester counties and Baltimore City. CAFB serves Montgomery and Prince George's counties. Distribution targets are based on county population, poverty rate, and unemployment rate.
requirements_list: For eligible agencies (ERAs/EFOs): Must have current IRS tax-exempt status
Must be a charitable institution providing food directly to needy individuals and families
Must have a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with the Sponsoring Agency prior to receiving TEFAP foods
Must comply with non-discrimination policies and procedures
Must attend annual Civil Rights training
Must maintain monthly inventory reports and damage reports
Must submit household distribution reports (monthly or quarterly depending on Sponsoring Agency requirements)
Must maintain alphabetized customer applications with Self-Disclosure of Income forms
Must have access to food other than TEFAP USDA foods
Must conduct at least one distribution per month

For end recipients: Income at or below 185% of Federal Poverty Guidelines OR receipt of SNAP, Medical Assistance, TANF, unemployment benefits, or Energy Assistance. 2026 income eligibility: Individual $29,526 annually; Family of 2 $40,034 annually; Family of 3 $50,542 annually; Family of 4 $61,050 annually; Family of 5 $71,558 annually; Family of 6 $82,066 annually; Family of 7 $92,574 annually; Family of 8 $103,082 annually; plus $10,508 for each additional household member
Subject to annual monitoring visits from Sponsoring Agency and DHS
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For End Recipients: (1) Locate the nearest TEFAP provider by visiting www.mdfoodbank.org for counties other than Montgomery or Prince George's, or www.capitalareafoodbank.org for Montgomery or Prince George's counties. (2) Look for the 'Find Food' link (or 'Get Help' link for Capital Area Food Bank) at the top right of the homepage. (3) Input your zip code and select the number of miles you are willing to travel. (4) Receive a complete listing of nearby food programs including program name, type, address, hours, and contact information. (5) Visit the food program and complete a Self-Disclosure of Income (SDI) form to verify eligibility. For Eligible Agencies Seeking to Participate: (1) Submit an application and contract to the Sponsoring Agency (Maryland Food Bank or Capital Area Food Bank depending on jurisdiction). (2) Undergo a site visit. (3) Receive program orientation conducted by the Sponsoring Agency TEFAP Coordinator. (4) Establish a Memorandum of Agreement with the Sponsoring Agency. (5) Once approved, access TEFAP foods through online ordering systems. For Capital Area Food Bank ERAs: Orders are placed through NetSuite and Waerlinx systems; ERAs may withdraw foods as often as they prefer each month without exceeding allocated amounts; free delivery is provided; ERAs may pick up gradually if storage is limited. For Maryland Food Bank ERAs/EFOs: Orders are placed through Navision system (transitioning to NetSuite and Waerlinx in February 2025); EFOs and ERAs submit monthly activity reports. All participating agencies must complete annual Civil Rights training and pass annual monitoring reviews.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Transportation Assistance Program (TAP) provides reliable used vehicles to eligible families and low-income individuals for two years or 24,000 miles to help them access better employment opportunities, reduce commute times, increase mobility, access higher-paying jobs or shifts, and improve overall quality of life. The program aims to remove transportation barriers that prevent families from finding gainful employment and moving toward financial independence. Vehicles are distributed through a network of partners across Maryland, including Vehicles for Change as the statewide TAP partner.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a reliable used vehicle to eligible families and low-income individuals for a term of two years or 24,000 miles, whichever comes first. Vehicles are distributed through a network of partners across Maryland, including Vehicles for Change, the statewide TAP partner.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and low-income individuals across Maryland, especially recipients of Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program funds, who face transportation barriers to finding and maintaining employment and achieving financial independence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vehicles provided can be used for transportation to employment, commuting to work, accessing medical care, grocery shopping, and other activities that support family stability and economic self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through a network of partners across Maryland. Potential participants should contact their local department of social services TAP Coordinator or the statewide TAP partner, Vehicles for Change.
requirements_list: Must be eligible for or recipient of Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program funds
Must be low-income
Must be able to utilize vehicle for employment or related purposes
Must contact local department of social services to determine eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals should inquire through their local department of social services TAP Coordinator or contact Vehicles for Change, the statewide TAP partner, to learn about participation and vehicle availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: Designed to protect low-income families from utility service shut-offs and disconnections during the heating season by providing utility bill payment assistance. Eligible customers must enroll in a year-round even monthly budget billing plan through their utility company. All customers eligible for the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) may participate in USPP. The program is administered statewide by the Maryland Department of Human Services Office of Home Energy Programs, with county-level administration available through local departments of social services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Protects low-income families from utility turn-offs and disconnections during the heating season. All customers eligible for the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) may participate in USPP. Participation requires enrollment in a year-round even monthly budget billing plan through their utility company. Failure to make consecutive monthly payments may result in removal from the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households in Maryland eligible for the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) who need protection from utility service disconnection during the heating season
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Utility bill payment assistance to prevent utility service disconnection or shut-off during the heating season
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland; county-level administration available including through Prince George's County Department of Social Services
requirements_list: Must be eligible for the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP)
Must enroll in year-round even monthly budget billing with utility company
Must make consecutive monthly payments to remain in the program
Failure to make consecutive payments may result in removal from USPP
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible MEAP customers can enroll in USPP by applying online 24/7 at dhs.maryland.gov/office-of-home-energy-programs/, by email with completed application and supporting documentation to pgcdss.energy@maryland.gov, by mail to Prince George's County Department of Social Services, Office of Home Energy Programs, 805 Brightseat Road, Landover, Maryland 20785, or by fax to 301-909-6331. Applicants can check application status online at myohepstatus.org. In-person assistance is available at 425 Brightseat Road, Landover, MD 20785. Must contact utility company to set up budget billing. Refer to utility company bill or PSC website at www.psc.state.md.us for utility contact information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Veteran-Directed Home and Community Based Services Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Veterans of all ages who need skilled services, support, and assistance with activities of daily living (bathing and getting dressed) or instrumental activities of daily living (fixing meals and taking medication) receive Home and Community Based Services in a consumer-directed way.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Consumer-directed Home and Community Based Services including skilled services and assistance with activities of daily living and instrumental activities of daily living.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Veterans of all ages who need skilled services and support with activities of daily living.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Skilled services, support, and assistance with activities of daily living or instrumental activities of daily living.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a veteran
Must need skilled services and support with activities of daily living or instrumental activities of daily living
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Not specified in the source material.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that empowers incarcerated fathers to develop job readiness skills and prepare for successful transition back into employment and community after release from detention. Participants receive training in soft skills, resume writing, interviewing, and other employment preparation areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides job readiness classes, resume writing assistance, cover letter writing, interview techniques training, and dressing for success guidance. It includes soft skills development in communication, self-confidence, social skills, time management, problem solving, and anger management. The program also connects participants to additional resources including background and credit check information, employment law education, legal resources, federal bonding, and expungement assistance. A full-time Job Developer and two full-time Social Workers assist participants during their transition from incarceration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Incarcerated fathers in the Baltimore County Men's Detention Center with a court-ordered child support obligation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job readiness training, employment skills development, and preparation for return to the workforce and community
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program operates from the Baltimore County Detention Center in Towson, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be incarcerated in the Baltimore County Men's Detention Center
Must have a minimum of 120 days remaining on sentence
Must have a court-ordered child support obligation
Should possess a positive attitude and eagerness to create a better life
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested fathers should contact one of the Program Coordinators at the numbers provided for information on how to enroll.

structured_extraction.program_description: A progressive employment and support initiative that serves fathers and noncustodial parties in Talbot County by helping them become more responsible and active participants in their children's lives. The program provides job readiness training, employment development, life skills counseling, parenting skill development, and case management to help participants increase child support payments and build stable economic environments for their families.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides no-cost training to help participants develop job-readiness skills, secure employment, and gain life skills counseling. Participants receive case management support, parenting classes, and assistance overcoming barriers to employment. The program partners with local organizations to provide job placement and retention assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Noncustodial parents who have a Talbot County child support case and are unemployed or underemployed
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides job readiness training, employment development, life skills counseling, parenting skills development, case management, legal representation assistance with housing, foreclosure, family law, and debt matters, and services related to homelessness and wellness recovery.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to noncustodial parties with a Talbot County child support case. Services are hosted at the Caroline County Social Services Building at 300 Market Street, Denton, Maryland.
requirements_list: Have a Talbot County child support case
Be unemployed or underemployed
Be able to commit to working upon program completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested participants can contact the program coordinator Isaiah Greene at 410-819-4471 or isaiah.green@maryland.gov, or Lori Keel at lori.keel@maryland.gov, or call DHS's helpline at 1-800-332-6347 to start the enrollment process.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 26 Continuation Grant for Consolidated Adult Education & Family Literacy Services
structured_extraction.program_description: A continuation grant program that funds consolidated adult education and family literacy services, including adult basic education (ABE), English as a Second Language (ESL), Integrated English Literacy and Civics Education (IELCE), Integrated English Literacy and Civics Education with Integrated Education and Training (IET), and National External Diploma Program (NEDP) services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Continuation grant funding for consolidated adult education and family literacy services over a 12-month grant period (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026). Funding covers adult basic education (ABE), English as a Second Language (ESL), Integrated English Literacy and Civics Education (IELCE), Integrated Education and Training (IET), and National External Diploma Program (NEDP) services. Grantees must provide a matching contribution equal to 20% of total funds expended on allowable activities (calculated as 25% of grant funds requested). A minimum of 35% of the match must be in cash, with up to 65% as in-kind contribution. The match requirement cannot decrease from FY 25 even if requesting less funding in FY 26. Administrative costs are capped at 5% of the total budget. All instructional staff and NEDP advisors/assessors must participate in a minimum of 10 hours of professional development annually.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Helen Coupe; Ramona Kunkel; Ahu Moser; Grayla Reneau; Echo Salisbury; Douglas Weimer (SAM Registry questions)
structured_extraction.contact_email: helen.coupe@maryland.gov; ramona.kunkel@maryland.gov; ahu.moser@maryland.gov; grayla.reneau@maryland.gov; echo.salisbury@maryland.gov; douglas.weimer@maryland.gov
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adult education and family literacy service providers in Maryland, including community colleges, non-profit organizations, and other eligible entities providing consolidated adult education services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports adult basic education (ABE), English as a Second Language (ESL) instruction, Integrated English Literacy and Civics Education (IELCE), Integrated Education and Training (IET) programs, and National External Diploma Program (NEDP) services. Allowable expenditures include instructor and staff salaries and benefits, instructional materials and supplies, professional development (minimum 10 hours annually for instructional staff), childcare during classroom time, public transportation for students, technology and equipment (with prior MD Labor approval), contracted services, indirect costs, and administrative expenses (capped at 5%). Funds may support family literacy partnerships that integrate all four components: parent literacy training, parent education, interactive literacy activities between parents and children, and age-appropriate educational activities for children. Funds cannot support K-12 services, non-instructional activities, graduation events, or items not directly related to instruction. Fees for NEDP services cannot exceed $225 per client.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, all counties
requirements_list: Applicant must register with System for Award Management (SAM.gov) and obtain a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
Applicant must provide Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN)
Applicant must submit Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation Certificate of Good Standing or Letter of Ineligibility
Applicant must submit documentation of tax-exempt status if applicable (IRC 501(c) organizations)
Applicant must be in compliance with Unemployment Insurance (UI) obligations to the State
Applicant must submit updated W-9 form
Grantee must maintain matching funds at 20% of total expended funds; match cannot decrease from FY 25
Grantee must maintain Maintenance of Effort (MOE) requirements through all years of the multi-year FY 24-FY 27 grant period
Administrative costs capped at 5% of total budget (MIS, data entry clerk, and staff professional development on specific funding lines do not count toward cap)
All instructional staff and NEDP advisors/assessors must participate in minimum 10 hours of professional development annually
Programs must identify two SMART goals (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-Bound), with at least one data-driven goal tied to performance metrics
Programs must implement exact NEDP model as defined by MD Labor and CASAS (if operating NEDP)
NEDP programs require minimum two certified advisors/assessors per site; three or more recommended based on program size
NEDP advisors/assessors must hold minimum four-year college degree from accredited post-secondary institution
All NEDP advisors/assessors must complete CASAS NEDP Implementation Training and obtain certification prior to serving clients
NEDP programs must verify Maryland residency of all clients using approved photo identification prior to enrollment
NEDP programs must provide acceptable facilities with confidentiality, privacy, accessibility, secure storage, adequate technology, convenient parking, and year-round day and evening hours
NEDP programs must meet specific hardware/software requirements including Windows 10 or later, 100 kbps upload bandwidth, and necessary equipment
Family Literacy partners must deliver all four required components with sufficient intensity and duration to make sustainable changes
Grantee must not charge fees to ABE or ESL Beginning or Intermediate learners for instructional services; only nominal fees for consumable materials allowed
Grantee must not use funds for K-12 services or in-school youth
Grantee must enroll clients using managed enrollment system with documented waitlist when capacity exceeded
Classes must begin and end within the grant award period
Grantee must enter valid and accurate data into LACES (Literacy, Adult and Community Education System) database per annual schedule
Grantee must maintain program records for three years after grant termination
Grantee must receive prior written MD Labor approval before implementing programmatic changes
Grantee must receive prior written MD Labor approval for budgetary realignment of $1,000 or 10% of total object/program/category, whichever is greater
Grantee must encumber federal grant funds by June 30 of fiscal year and expend by September 30
Grantee must expend state grant funds by June 30 of fiscal year
Grantee must provide Notice of Projected Under-Expended Funds by March 31 if applicable
IET proposals must include funding source and require pre-approval by MD Labor before implementation
IET applications must show occupational instructor calculations separately and as separate line item in budget narrative
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit continuation grant applications electronically in Adobe PDF format (except budgets in Excel) with a file size not exceeding 25MB. The process includes: (1) Attend optional Technical Assistance Webinar on April 9, 2025, 9:30-11:00 A.M. to review application requirements; (2) Complete all required application components including Goals, Qualification of Personnel Chart, Quality of Staff and Professional Development, Data Quality Checklist, Family Literacy Partnership Expectations (if applicable), General Assurances and Certifications, and required supplementary documents; (3) Submit all parts of the application electronically to program's Google Drive folder by May 12, 2025 at 4:00 P.M. using the path: [Your agency folder] -> FY 2026 Files -> FY 2026 Submissions from program (or email to assigned Adult Education Program Specialist if no Google Drive access); (4) Applications must include overview documents, budget worksheets in Excel, class schedules, assurances and certifications, and program-specific applications for ABE, ESL, IELCE, IET, and NEDP components; (5) Use provided pre-formatted application with specified font and single-spacing; electronic signatures permitted via DocuSign or Adobe Sign; (6) Include completed Application Checklist ensuring all required documents are included; (7) Final approved budget workbook must be printed, signed and dated in blue ink, then scanned to PDF and uploaded to Google Drive; (8) Upon receipt of Notice of Grant Award, submit final Professional Development Plan within 30 days; (9) Submit Yearly Statistical Report to CASAS (NEDP programs only) at close of fiscal year. Office hours available April 14, 2025 (9:00-11:00 A.M. and 1:00-3:00 P.M.). Contact assigned Adult Education Program Specialist with questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides financial assistance to Maryland-based employers impacted by Covid-19 who are engaged in infrastructure projects to implement innovative workforce solutions, including employee support programs and payroll incentives to improve recruitment, training, and employee retention.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding provided upfront in lump sum to employers to establish employee support programs and payroll incentives. Maximum grant amounts are capped based on employer size: $500,000 for employers with 750+ employees, $400,000 for employers with 500-749 employees, and $300,000 for employers with fewer than 500 employees. Maximum benefit per employee is $10,000. Employee Support Programs can include transportation assistance (vehicle maintenance, purchase, lease, driver's license, public transit, rideshare, company vehicles), housing assistance (rental assistance, security deposits, relocation), and child and dependent care. Payroll Incentives can include signing bonuses for new or underemployed employees, retention bonuses for employees who stay employed for a defined period, and wages for employee training or professional development. Funds must be deposited in a non-interest bearing account and fully spent by December 1, 2024. All grant funds that have not been spent must be returned to MD Labor.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling, first-come, first-served basis until program funds are exhausted. Program is no longer accepting applications as of the announcement date.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Heather Evans (Jobs that Build Project Manager) and Erin Roth (Deputy Assistant Secretary)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based employers impacted by Covid-19 who are actively engaged in or have a contract to perform construction or maintenance of infrastructure projects (including roads, bridges, tunnels, transit, walking/biking facilities, rail, ports, airports, broadband, energy grids, and drinking water/wastewater facilities) and are experiencing significant difficulty hiring and/or retaining employees for construction and maintenance work on these projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds can be used for employee support programs including transportation assistance (vehicle maintenance, purchase, lease, driver's license, public transit, rideshare, company vehicles), housing assistance (rental assistance, security deposits, relocation), child and dependent care, and other supportive services with MD Labor approval. Funds can also support payroll incentives including signing bonuses for new or underemployed employees, retention bonuses for employees who stay employed for a defined period, and wages for employee training and professional development. Funds must only be used to support Maryland-based employees (those for which the employer is required to withhold Maryland State income taxes). Prohibited uses include: executive-level staff or positions such as superintendent, foreman, site supervisor, or controller; previous employees no longer employed; intentionally recruiting employees away from other employers in the same industry; pension fund contributions to reduce unfunded liability; debt service payments; settlement and judgment payments; and any uses that violate ARPA or federal law.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all Maryland employers engaged in infrastructure projects are eligible. Employers must be actively engaged in construction or maintenance of an infrastructure project within Maryland or have a contract to perform such work on or before January 1, 2024.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland-based employer
Employer must have been negatively impacted by COVID-19
Employer must be actively engaged in construction or maintenance of an infrastructure project within Maryland, or have a contract to perform such work on or before January 1, 2024
Infrastructure projects include roads, bridges, tunnels, transit, walking/biking facilities, rail, ports, airports, broadband, energy grids, and drinking water/wastewater facilities
All applicants must attest to having difficulty in hiring and/or retaining employees for construction and maintenance work performed on these projects
Applicants must propose a program that includes elements of Employee Support Programs and/or Payroll Incentives
Employers should identify which benefits will be provided in the application
Employers should specify how employees will access and be approved for benefits
Employers should identify benefit amounts and allowances per employee (maximum $10,000 per employee total)
Program must align with all funding limits, guidance, and policies for the Jobs that Build Employer Fund
Employer must be in good standing with the State Comptroller's Office
Employer must not be debarred, suspended, or otherwise excluded from federal assistance programs
All grant funds must be fully spent by December 1, 2024
Employers must design program with input from human resources, payroll, and accounting staff
Employers must maintain records for four years following exit date
Documentation of eligible expenses must be maintained including receipts, payroll records, and proof of payment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers complete and electronically submit a grant application consisting of two documents: the Jobs That Build Application - Budget Component (Excel file) and the Jobs That Build Application - Program Component. The Budget Component requires employers to specify support or incentive items to implement and identify the maximum benefit per employee and number of employees to be served. The Program Component requires applicants to provide business background, workforce issues justification, employee eligibility determination process, implementation details, and timeline. Employers should design their program with input from human resources, payroll, and accounting staff. Application must also include a Certificate of Good Standing from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, attestation of good standing with the State Comptroller's Office, and a signed W-9 form. Submit all documents via email to labor.jobsthatbuild@maryland.gov. Applications are reviewed on a rolling, first-come, first-served basis. A dedicated Jobs That Build review team will review applications within 14 calendar days. Applicants will be notified via email of approval or denial. Approved applicants receive a Grant Award Notification to sign and must return the completed award agreement within 14 calendar days. Once the award agreement is executed, MD Labor provides the full award amount upfront to be deposited in a non-interest bearing account. Denied applicants may reapply and are encouraged to consult with MD Labor for technical assistance.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: An assessment credit to Maryland state-chartered banks and credit unions that operate branches in low-to-moderate income communities. The credit reduces the annual regulatory assessment fee charged to eligible depository institutions. Specific credit amounts are not stated on this page.
