structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides a state income tax credit for the donation of a conservation easement to the Maryland Environmental Trust or the Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners donating conservation easements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State income tax credit for conservation easement donations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must donate a conservation easement to the Maryland Environmental Trust or the Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation

structured_extraction.program_name: Conservation Reserve Enhancement Permanent Easement Program (CREP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A perpetual conservation easement program that provides a written legal agreement between agricultural landowners and the State of Maryland to install or maintain conservation practices that protect water quality and natural resources. Landowners with expiring federal CREP or CRP contracts can enroll to keep their land in approved conservation practices permanently, with the easement filed with county land records and conveyed to a qualified government agency or nonprofit conservation organization.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program acquires a permanent interest in the land through a conservation easement. Landowners with existing federal CREP or CRP contracts who have installed prescribed conservation practices can enroll. After the federal contract expires, the landowner agrees to maintain the land in an approved conservation practice as detailed in a conservation management plan or forest stewardship plan in perpetuity. The conservation easement is filed with county land records and conveyed to a government agency or nonprofit conservation organization. Land use restrictions specify that the land must be maintained in the vegetation type indicated in the conservation plan, and no structures may be built on enrolled lands.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners with expiring federal CREP or CRP contracts who have installed prescribed conservation practices and want to maintain conservation practices on their land permanently.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The easement assistance supports the installation and maintenance of conservation practices that protect water quality and natural resources, such as maintaining vegetation in approved conservation practices and forest stewardship. Land must be maintained in the vegetation type indicated in the conservation plan, and no structures may be built on enrolled lands.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide throughout all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Landowner must have an existing federal CREP or CRP contract
Landowner must have already installed the prescribed CREP or CRP conservation practice(s)
Landowner must agree to keep the land in an approved conservation practice as defined in a conservation management plan or forest stewardship plan forever
No structures may be built on the enrolled lands
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners with expiring federal contracts can apply to establish a perpetual conservation easement with the State of Maryland. The easement is detailed in a legal document that is filed with county land records and conveyed to a qualified government agency or nonprofit conservation organization.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program supports forest buffers and wetlands on working farmland to protect and restore water quality and wildlife. It offers cost-share and technical assistance to farmers to maximize their agriculture land use while enhancing environmental protection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share payments and technical assistance for establishing forest buffers and wetlands on working farmland to protect water quality and wildlife.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and agricultural landowners.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishment and management of forest buffers and wetlands on working farmland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Own working farmland
Agree to establish forest buffers or wetlands on eligible land
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Farmers work with participating agencies to apply for cost-share assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A cost-share program administered by the Maryland Forest Service that provides financial assistance to public land managers for treating ash trees infested with Emerald Ash Borer. The program covers 50% of treatment costs for trunk injections with emamectin benzoate performed by licensed pesticide applicators on public land. It is designed to help local governments and conservation lands protect valuable ash tree populations from EAB infestation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Forest Service offers a 50/50 cost share, covering 50% of the cost for Emerald Ash Borer treatment on public land. Eligible treatments consist of trunk injections with emamectin benzoate (such as TREE-äge or ArborMectin), which must be conducted by licensed or certified pesticide applicators. Trunk injection treatments with emamectin benzoate are effective for 2-3 years. Treatment costs typically range from $8-17 per diameter inch for trunk injections. The program targets ash trees on public lands with less than 30% canopy loss, as treating trees with greater canopy loss may result in less likelihood of success. Preventative treatments have a higher likelihood for success than treating already infested trees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public land managers including local governments and conservation lands managing ash trees affected by or at risk from Emerald Ash Borer.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cost-sharing for trunk injection treatments with emamectin benzoate applied by licensed or certified pesticide applicators on ash trees on public land. Treatments should be applied in spring (late April to late May) or fall (August-September) for optimal timing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Public lands throughout Maryland. All ash tree species native to North America are vulnerable to Emerald Ash Borer.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public land manager, local government, or conservation lands organization
Treatment must be trunk injection with emamectin benzoate (restricted use pesticide)
Treatment must be conducted by a licensed or certified pesticide applicator
Trees must be on public land
Treated ash trees must have less than 30% canopy loss
Application of insecticides should avoid areas within 25 feet of water bodies (streams, lakes, ponds, wetlands, street curbs, or storm drains)
Do not apply insecticides when heavy rainfall is expected within 24 hours
Do not apply when soil is frozen or saturated
All North American ash species (Fraxinus species) are eligible; Mountain ash and prickly ash are not true ash species and are not susceptible to EAB
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Forest Service Emerald Ash Borer Forester for information on the application process and cost-share eligibility. Applicants should conduct a tree inventory first, identify ash trees (looking for opposite branching, compound leaves with 5-11 leaflets, and diamond-shaped bark ridges on mature trees), assess infestation status or risk level, develop a response plan, and work with licensed or certified pesticide applicators to conduct trunk injection treatments. Treatments are most effective when applied in spring (late April-late May) or fall (August-September). For best results, apply insecticides when trees are actively transpiring (after leaf-out and before leaf drop).

structured_extraction.program_name: Explore the Patuxent Teen Leadership Paddle
structured_extraction.program_description: A week-long canoeing expedition for high school students that combines outdoor adventure with environmental education. Participants practice leadership and teamwork skills while navigating the Patuxent River, conducting water quality tests, studying plant communities, participating in stewardship projects, and camping riverside. The program builds environmental stewardship and culminates in a final presentation to local leaders and community members. Scholarships are available through Friends of Jug Bay to ensure cost is never a barrier to participation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three-tier voluntary pricing for participation: Tier III costs $200 (reduced rate made possible by Friends of Jug Bay and CBNERR-MD), Tier II costs $250 (partially subsidized, covers staff, utilities, and operational costs), and Tier I costs $300 (accounts for full costs including food, maintenance, and administrative expenses). Scholarships are available through Friends of Jug Bay for participants who need additional financial assistance beyond Tier III. Cost is never a barrier to participation. Includes five days of instruction, meals, lodging, canoe equipment, and all program activities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling, first come, first served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students interested in environmental leadership, outdoor adventure, and water-based learning about river systems and stewardship.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participation in a five-day residential canoeing and environmental education program. Covers instruction, meals, camping accommodations, canoe equipment, water quality testing, stewardship projects, and a culminating presentation to community leaders.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program operates along the Patuxent River, based at Patuxent River Park in Prince George's County, Maryland. Open to participants from across Maryland and potentially beyond.
requirements_list: Must be a high school student
COVID vaccination is recommended for all participants and staff
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students apply using an online Google Form linked on the program page. Applications are reviewed on a rolling, first-come-first-served basis. Interested applicants should submit their application as soon as possible to secure a spot. For questions or to inquire about scholarships, contact Olivia Wisner directly by email at olivia.wisner1@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A training program offered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that provides participants with the skills and knowledge to run beginner fishing lessons through their organization. Upon completion, participants qualify to borrow fishing gear from the state for extended use at no cost. Certificates of completion are available upon request.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free instructor training provided by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources, scheduled Tuesday through Thursday, 8 AM to 4 PM, November through April. A minimum of 10 participants is required per training session. Participants who complete the training qualify to borrow state fishing equipment at no cost for extended use in delivering beginner fishing lessons. Certificates of completion are available upon request.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specific deadline; scheduling available on a rolling basis with advance booking recommended
structured_extraction.program_audience: Youth organizations, schools, scout troops, parks, nature centers, 4-H clubs, libraries, summer camps, and community groups seeking to offer beginner fishing instruction to their participants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training to develop skills and knowledge for running beginner fishing lessons, plus access to borrowed state fishing equipment for program delivery.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have at least 10 participants to request training
Participants must be 18 years of age or older
Participants must have and/or acquire a fishing license prior to the training
Organizations must report on use of borrowed equipment
Organizations must maintain all borrowed equipment in good condition
Organizations must return all borrowed equipment upon completion of fishing lessons
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in scheduling a Fishing Instructor Training should contact Chelsea Kenworthy at the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. Training should be scheduled far in advance as availability is limited, and booking up to a year in advance may be necessary for preferred dates and times.

structured_extraction.program_description: A law that requires forest protection to be integrated into land planning and development projects. Projects involving 40,000 square feet or more that require subdivision, grading, or sediment control permits must submit a Forest Stand Delineation and Forest Conservation Plan for approval. The program prioritizes protection of forests adjacent to streams and wetlands, steep or erodible slopes, and large forest blocks or wildlife corridors. When forest clearing is unavoidable, developers must replant trees on-site or at approved off-site locations to maintain forest cover. As of 2022, the program shifted from a 'no net loss' benchmark to a 'net gain' standard for Maryland's forests.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical oversight and guidance through Qualified Professionals (Maryland licensed Foresters, Landscape Architects, or other qualified professionals) who prepare and review Forest Stand Delineations and Forest Conservation Plans. Local counties and municipalities implement the program with state oversight to ensure forests are protected during development projects through conservation planning, identification of priority forest areas, and requirements for reforestation or afforestation when clearing occurs. The program requires: (1) Forest Stand Delineation to inventory existing forest conditions and identify priority areas; (2) Forest Conservation Plan detailing retention, reforestation, and afforestation strategies; (3) Long-term forest protection measures including conservation easements; and (4) Planting Plans with two-year maintenance agreements when trees must be replaced. Developers may plant trees on-site, at approved off-site locations, or pay a fee-in-lieu to the Forest Conservation Fund if planting is not feasible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers, landowners, and project planners undertaking development projects of 40,000 square feet or more that require subdivision, grading, or sediment control permits. Also includes architects, engineers, surveyors, and professional foresters involved in site planning and development design.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide direct financial assistance. It requires forest protection measures including forest conservation planning, identification and protection of priority forest areas (forests adjacent to streams and wetlands, steep or erodible slopes, large forest blocks or wildlife corridors, priority urban forests for retention), tree save fencing, root zone protection, erosion control measures, and reforestation or afforestation when forest clearing is necessary. Developers may also contribute to local Forest Conservation Funds through fee-in-lieu payments when on-site or off-site planting is not feasible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Administered by the Maryland Forest Service with implementation by local counties and municipalities with approved forest conservation programs. The program applies to all development sites of 40,000 square feet or greater that require subdivision, grading, or sediment control permits.
requirements_list: Project must involve 40,000 square feet or more
Project must require a subdivision, grading, or sediment control permit
Must submit a Forest Stand Delineation prepared by a qualified professional for approval
Must submit a Forest Conservation Plan prepared by a qualified professional for approval before proceeding

Must identify valuable forest areas and environmentally sensitive features including streams and buffers, floodplains, steep slopes, critical habitats, nontidal wetlands, and priority urban forests for retention
Priority given to forests adjacent to streams and wetlands, steep or erodible slopes (greater than 25% grade), and large blocks of contiguous forest or wildlife corridors
When forest clearing is unavoidable, reforestation or afforestation must occur on-site or at approved off-site locations to maintain or increase forest cover
Minimum forest cover thresholds must be met based on land-use category (e.g., 25% for medium density residential)
Forest retention areas must be placed under permanent protection through conservation easements

If forest clearing exceeds the break-even point, developers must plant one-quarter acre per acre cleared above the Conservation Threshold, or two acres per acre cleared below the Conservation Threshold
New plantings must use native Maryland species within 100-mile radius genetic stock
Minimum five different species required for reforestation on a single site
Two-year maintenance agreement required for all planted areas including watering, fertilizing, disease control, vegetation management, and replacement of dead trees
Specimen trees (diameter 30 inches or more at breast height) and champion trees receive special protected status
Commercial logging exempt but must file Declaration of Intent stating no development for at least five years after logging
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Projects subject to the Forest Conservation Act must work with a Qualified Professional (Maryland licensed Forester, Landscape Architect, or other qualified professional) to prepare a Forest Stand Delineation (FSD) and Forest Conservation Plan (FCP). The FSD involves resource mapping, field assessment, and documentation of existing forest conditions, sensitive areas, and priority retention areas. The process typically takes 30 days for FSD approval. The FCP is then submitted, detailing conservation strategies, protection measures, and planting requirements, with 45 days for approval. The FCP must include identification of forested and sensitive areas, development of conservation strategies, designation of areas for long-term protection through preservation or conservation easements, planting plans with species selection, and two-year maintenance agreements. These documents are submitted to the State or local Forest Conservation Program Coordinator for approval before the project can proceed. Construction must incorporate forest protection measures as specified in the approved FCP. Reforestation or afforestation must occur within one year of project completion, followed by a two-year management agreement period. Citizens can provide input during the planning review process and monitor protection activities during construction.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Forest Conservation and Management Program (FCMP) provides landowners with financial incentives to conserve and responsibly manage their forestland by offering reduced and stabilized property tax assessments for at least 15 years. The program makes it easier for landowners to maintain forest cover and commit to long-term stewardship of private forests. It also minimizes the loss of Maryland's forest resources during land development through identification and protection of forests and other sensitive areas, and creation of private property forest management plans. Resident forest owners can have a forest management plan prepared by a Maryland Forest Service forester. Approximately 1,300 agreements are currently in place covering more than 84,000 acres of forestland across Maryland.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Enrolled forestland receives a reduced property tax assessment, generally at the agricultural rate, which remains frozen for the life of the agreement (minimum 15 years). The program also provides free forest management plan preparation by a Maryland Forest Service forester, and technical assistance for the identification and protection of forests and other sensitive areas during land development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners (individuals, for-profit entities, and government) with five or more contiguous acres of forestland in Maryland, as well as developers and property managers seeking to protect forest resources during development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax assessment reduction for forest conservation and management; forest management planning; protection of forest resources during land development; and long-term stewardship of private forestland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Approximately 1,300 agreements are currently in place covering more than 84,000 acres of forestland across Maryland. Open land recently planted with tree seedlings can be included after one growing season.
requirements_list: Landowner must own five or more contiguous acres of forestland
Eligible land includes forested tracts, newly reforested land once it has completed one growing season, and Christmas tree plantations if trees are harvested at maturity
House sites, crop land, and other non-forest open spaces are not eligible
Landowner must enter into a legally binding Forest Conservation and Management Agreement (FCMA) with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources
Agreement is recorded in county land records and guided by a forest management plan prepared specifically for the property
Minimum term of agreement is fifteen years
Landowner must follow the forest management plan and maintain the forestland according to agreement terms
Breaking the agreement results in retroactive back taxes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Maryland Forest Service office to determine if a Forest Conservation and Management Agreement is right for your property. Forestry staff are available to answer questions, explain program requirements, prepare or review forest management plans, and guide landowners through enrollment. An agreement is established through a Forest Conservation and Management Agreement (FCMA) between the landowner and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: A licensing program for businesses engaged in forest products operations, including sawmills, pulpwood and logging contractors, firewood dealers, mulch suppliers, land clearing companies, tree removal companies, and lumber brokers. Any person engaged in a forest products business must obtain a license from the Department of Natural Resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program is a licensing requirement and authorization to operate a forest products business. Applicants must submit an application and pay an annual licensee fee of $20.00. Applicants must demonstrate compliance with the Maryland Workers' Compensation Act and provide either a Certificate of Workers' Compensation Insurance or a declaration of sole proprietor status with no employees. The license term is one calendar year and must be renewed annually. No direct financial assistance is provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses engaged in forest products operations, including sawmills, pulpwood and logging contractors, firewood dealers, mulch suppliers, land clearing companies, tree removal companies, and lumber brokers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable; this is a licensing program with no direct funding component. The license authorizes the holder to legally engage in commercial forest products operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; applicable to all of Maryland. Applicants must report the top 3 counties where timber was harvested or purchased during the previous calendar year.
requirements_list: Must be engaged in a forest products business
Must submit application form provided by the Department
Must pay annual licensee fee of $20.00

Must demonstrate compliance with Maryland Workers' Compensation Act (Title 9 of Labor and Employment Article) by providing either a Certificate of Workers' Compensation Insurance or certification of sole proprietor status with no employees
Forest harvest operations disturbing more than 5,000 square feet or 100 cubic yards of soil must have an approved erosion and sediment control plan
Must maintain Workers' Compensation insurance protection for the period the license is in effect
Must disclose license number in all advertisements and notices for sale of forest products
Must retain documentation of all forest product sales transactions for one year from the date of sale
Must inform Department within 30 days of any change in business address or telephone number
Must comply with all applicable statutes and regulations pertaining to forest products operations
May not engage in false or misleading advertising or misrepresentation of qualifications, experience, or licensing status
May not falsely represent species, quantity, or records of forest products sold
License holder is responsible for quality and content of all work performed by those working under the license
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply online through the Department's website or download the PDF application form (FPO Application for Maryland Forest Products Operators License) and submit a hardcopy along with payment to the Maryland Forest Service. The application requires personal information, company information, primary and secondary business types, products bought and sold, annual consumption estimates, harvesting location information, species information, and Workers' Compensation documentation. Current licenseholders renewing their license can update only the sections where information has changed. Applications should be sent to: Maryland Forest Service, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, 580 Taylor Ave, E-1, Annapolis MD 21401. Make checks payable to Maryland Forest Service.

structured_extraction.program_name: Glatfelter Pulpwood Company Cost Share Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A cost-share program available to private landowners to support timber, forestry, and pulpwood management practices in partnership with Glatfelter Pulpwood Company, administered through the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share assistance providing financial support for timber, forestry, and pulpwood management practices to private landowners through partnership with Glatfelter Pulpwood Company.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners in timber and forestry industries
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Timber, forestry, and pulpwood management practices
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: The Greenspace Equity Program provides competitive grant funding to eligible applicants for enhancing public health and livability in overburdened and underserved communities by implementing projects to preserve, create, and enhance public greenspace. Established through Chapter 487 of 2023 legislation, the program is funded from the state share of Program Open Space and supports both acquisition and stewardship/development projects. The program also offers an Appraisal Grant to help eligible applicants obtain independent appraisals for properties they plan to acquire as part of greenspace projects, in preparation for submission of acquisition applications in the following year's main grant round.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides reimbursable grant funding for eligible projects. Applicants must pay project costs upfront before receiving reimbursement; partial project reimbursements and advance payments may be considered on a case-by-case basis after Maryland Board of Public Works approval. Grants may be for up to 100% of the project cost and are selected on a competitive basis. Eligible acquisition project costs include: acquisition of land in fee simple or perpetual conservation easements to create new community greenspace; two independent appraisals by licensed real estate appraisers; related due diligence expenses (surveys, title work, environmental assessments); administrative costs not exceeding 3% of the grant amount; and program compliance costs for easement monitoring not exceeding 1.5% of the grant amount. Eligible stewardship/development project costs include: site clearing and development for community greenspace use; project design and construction costs; related due diligence expenses; administrative costs not exceeding 3% of the grant amount; and costs must comply with National Playground Safety Standards, Americans with Disabilities Act, stormwater management, and sustainability standards. Maintenance, operating expenses, and contingency costs are not eligible. Funds cannot be used for business ventures. The program also offers an Appraisal Grant that funds the cost of up to two independent appraisals from certified general real estate appraisers for properties proposed for acquisition under the main grant program; appraisals must meet Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP); up to $100,000 in funding is available for the appraisal grant round. Funding is subject to annual budget actions. Costs incurred prior to Board of Public Works approval are not eligible for reimbursement except for certain eligible acquisition planning costs listed in the application and approved.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Appraisal Grant FY2027: Wednesday, May 13, 2026, by 3:00 p.m.; FY 2027 main grant round: Wednesday, January 14, 2026, by 3:00 p.m.; FY 2028 main grant round application materials to be posted at a future date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Land Trusts, nongovernmental organizations, county governments, and municipal governments located in or working in overburdened or underserved communities. Non-profit organizations and government agencies seeking to preserve, create, or improve public greenspace in overburdened and underserved communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used for: acquiring land in fee simple or perpetual conservation easements to create new community greenspace; stewardship activities to develop property for public use (community gardens, gathering spaces, woodlands, green networks, parks, trails, and urban farms); related due diligence expenses such as appraisals, environmental assessments, surveys, and title work; site clearing and development costs for stewardship projects; eligible administrative costs (up to 3% of grant amount for actual time spent on project work including negotiations with landowners, site visits, working with title attorneys/appraisers/surveyors, preparing documents, and implementing projects); program compliance costs for easement monitoring (up to 1.5% of grant amount, which must be invested in a long-term managed investment account with principal not withdrawable without DNR approval); and for stewardship/development projects, costs must comply with National Playground Safety Standards, Americans with Disabilities Act, stormwater management, sustainability and energy efficiency standards, and lead/PFAS requirements for playground surfacing. The Appraisal Grant specifically covers costs for obtaining up to two independent property appraisals from certified general real estate appraisers meeting industry standards; appraisals must meet Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP). Projects must have Greenspace Equity Program funding acknowledgement signs installed prior to completion. Funds cannot be used for maintenance, operating expenses, contingency costs, or business ventures. Any income or fees generated from the project must be invested back into maintaining the project.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in overburdened communities or underserved communities as defined by census tract indicators in the Maryland Environmental Article §1-701. Overburdened communities are census tracts where three or more environmental health indicators are above the 75th percentile statewide. Underserved communities are census tracts meeting one or more social and economic indicators. Projects may also take place on properties adjacent to these communities if the applicant holds conservation easements or owns the property in fee simple. Applicants can use the Greenspace Equity Qualifying Census Tracts map or the MDEnviroScreen tool to verify eligibility. Program is available statewide in all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Land Trust, nongovernmental organization, county government, or municipal government
Land Trusts must be qualified organizations under Internal Revenue Code §170(H)(3), have executed a cooperative agreement with Maryland Environmental Trust, or be an Affordable Housing Land Trust
Land Trusts and nongovernmental organizations must be in good standing
Land Trusts and nongovernmental organizations must be located or working in an overburdened or underserved community where the project is proposed
Nongovernmental organizations that are not Land Trusts are not eligible for acquisition projects

If the applicant is not a Land Trust, a county or municipal government must co-hold the fee simple deed or conservation easement, or the applicant must demonstrate plans for property protection in case of dissolution
If a Land Trust holds exclusive title, must include organizing documents outlining steps to ensure continuing protection and transfer of property upon dissolution

For properties not owned by applicant, applicant must hold development rights through easement, lease with more than 15 years remaining with no termination for convenience clause, or a project-specific Joint Use Agreement
Project must be located in an overburdened or underserved community, or adjacent to such a community if applicant holds conservation easement or owns property in fee simple

Land acquired must be maintained for public use in perpetuity; conversion of use requires replacement with land of equal or greater recreational use, acreage, and equal or greater appraised value approved by the program
Land developed or improved must be operated and maintained for public use for at least 15 years from project completion
Two independent appraisals required for property acquisition; if the value difference between high and low appraisals exceeds 20%, a third appraisal may be necessary
Land acquisition costs are limited to the fair market value determined by the average of two appraisals or the amount actually paid, whichever is less
Cost estimates must be realistic and documented; contingency costs are not eligible
Administrative costs documentation must relate to actual project work
Projects must be open for public use at all reasonable hours and times, according to facility type; available hours must be posted

Projects must be open to entry and use by all persons regardless of race, color, religion, sex, age, handicap, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, ancestry or national origin; must comply with Title VII Civil Rights Act and Americans with Disabilities Act
Entry may not be limited to only residents of a specific community
Projects must be within applicant's jurisdiction or within service area of Land Trust or Nongovernmental Organization
For stewardship/development projects, applicant must hold rights to develop on the property
For stewardship/development projects, project must be consistent with National Playground Safety Standards and Americans with Disabilities Act
For stewardship/development projects, project must address stormwater drainage issues and discharge requirements
For stewardship/development projects, project must consider sustainability and energy efficiency; any lighting must be energy efficient and reduce light spill-over to maximum extent possible
For stewardship/development projects, playground surfacing materials cannot have more than 90 parts per million (ppm) of lead or contain PFAs (per- and polyfluoroalkyl) chemicals

Projects cannot have been funded with Program Open Space Local or Community Parks and Playgrounds grants within the last 20 years or a Local Parks and Playgrounds Infrastructure grant within the last 15 years
For acquisition projects, applicant must have an accepted offer or agreement with the seller to purchase property or easement at time of application submission and can settle after project approval
For stewardship/development projects, applicant is ready to begin design/construction immediately after Board of Public Works approval

Projects must be properly maintained in a safe and usable state; if grantee fails to do so, grantee must replace project with one of equal or greater value approved by the program at no expense to the State
For the Appraisal Grant: property proposed for acquisition must meet the general requirements of the Greenspace Equity Program
For the Appraisal Grant: applicants must procure and complete appraisals in time to submit an acquisition application for the FY 2028 Greenspace Equity Program Grant round
For the Appraisal Grant: applicants who receive funds must submit an application for the subject property in the upcoming FY 2028 grant round

For the Appraisal Grant: funds can only be used to obtain appraisals from certified general real estate appraisers with qualifications consistent with industry standards and all applicable Local, State, and Federal statutes
For the Appraisal Grant: any funds remaining or not used to procure appraisals must be returned to the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the main Greenspace Equity Program Grant: Applicants submit a completed Greenspace Equity Program Application and Project Agreement with responses to specific program questions, supported by required accompanying documentation listed in the Accompanying Document Checklist. Supporting documentation must include area maps, site plans, deeds/property SDAT, easements/leases/Joint Use Agreements (if applicable), evidence of partnership and collaboration among local governments, land trusts, nongovernmental organizations, and community organizations, evidence of support from local government and the overburdened or underserved community, and pre-project photos. For acquisition projects, must also provide two independent appraisals and succession plan (required if governmental agency is not applicant). Nongovernmental organizations must provide documentation of nonprofit status 501(c)(3), Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, Business SDAT, or if not a Land Trust, documentation of how organized, examples of past projects completed, Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, and Business SDAT. Applicants must include community involvement in project development and demonstrate capacity to plan, implement and maintain the project. Applicants should contact the Greenspace Equity Program Administrator in advance to review project eligibility and required attachments. Applications must be completed and signed by the authorized representative of the applicant, acknowledging agreement to complete the project in accordance with all applicable Local, State, and Federal laws, statutes, and regulations. Applications for FY 2027 main grant round were due January 14, 2026 by 3:00 p.m.; FY 2028 application materials to be posted at a future date. For the Appraisal Grant: Complete the FY 2027 Greenspace Equity Program Appraisal Funding Grant Application and Project Agreement with all necessary accompanying documents including area map, parcel map, current deed and property SDAT, pre-project photos, and for Land Trusts, documentation of qualification (501c3 status, cooperative agreement with Maryland Environmental Trust, or Affordable Housing Land Trust status), Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, Business SDAT, and Succession Plan. Submit completed application to laplocalgrants.dnr@maryland.gov by the deadline (May 13, 2026, by 3:00 p.m.). Incomplete or late applications may not be considered for funding. Grant selection process: DNR staff reviews complete applications and evaluates projects based on consistency with program purpose, eligibility requirements and criteria, applicant responses, and status of any previously awarded grants. Evaluations consider the extent to which the project serves overburdened and underserved communities, improves conservation value, demonstrates partnerships and collaboration, enhances public health and livability, geographic diversity, and amount of financial or in-kind contributions. DNR staff makes recommendations; Greenspace Equity Advisory Board reviews and comments on applications; State Clearinghouse reviews recommended projects prior to Board of Public Works submission. Recommended projects are submitted to Board of Public Works for final approval before funds can be made available. DNR sends letter of award to applicants for grants approved by Board of Public Works. Grant recipients may be required to submit revised itemized budget. Approved grant recipients must procure and complete projects as proposed. Greenspace Equity is a reimbursable grant program; DNR reimburses applicants for approved project costs when proper documentation is provided. Reimbursement does not exceed Board of Public Works approved funding amount. DNR staff monitors progress according to stated timelines, performance criteria, and goals.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership program that provides participating landowners with a free tree planting project of one acre or more on open land they want to convert into a forest. The program provides all necessary supplies, labor, and at least 3 years of maintenance and technical advice at no cost to the landowner. Landowners must maintain the newly planted forest for a minimum of 10 years.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free tree planting project covering one acre or more, including all supplies, labor, and at least 3 years of maintenance and technical advice at no cost to the landowner.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural landowners in Maryland who want to convert open land of at least one acre into forest.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting supplies, labor, and maintenance for converting one acre or more of open land to forest.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Own open land of at least one acre available for conversion to forest
Commit to maintaining the newly planted forest for a minimum of 10 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners contact the program administrators/partners to discuss their project and apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Income Tax Modification for Reforestation & Timber Stand Improvement
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a modification to personal income taxes for initiating forest management practices, such as timber stand improvement and reforestation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Modification to personal income taxes for initiating forest management practices including timber stand improvement and reforestation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals initiating forest management practices
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Timber stand improvement and reforestation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership between Maryland DNR, the University of Maryland, and the Environmental Protection Agency that provides funding to accelerate Chesapeake Bay restoration through two components: (1) a Research and Development fund offering grants to students, faculty, and staff within the University of Maryland System to develop innovative technologies that reduce nutrient and sediment pollution and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions; and (2) a Seed Capital Fund providing equity investment to Maryland-based companies to commercialize and deploy innovative environmental technologies that advance Bay restoration goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund has two components. The Research and Development fund provides grants ranging from $30,000 to $100,000 to students, faculty, and staff from the University of Maryland System for research and development of new technologies that reduce non-point source nutrients and sediment, mitigate greenhouse gas emissions, or otherwise accelerate Chesapeake Bay restoration. The Seed Capital Fund provides equity investment ranging from $50,000 to $450,000 to Maryland-based companies to support the development, commercialization, and deployment of innovative environmental technologies for Chesapeake Bay restoration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students, faculty, and staff from the University of Maryland System developing innovative technologies for Bay restoration, as well as Maryland-based companies developing and commercializing environmental technologies that advance Chesapeake Bay restoration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Research, development, and commercialization of new technologies that accelerate Chesapeake Bay restoration, including technologies that reduce non-point source nutrient and sediment pollution, mitigate greenhouse gas emissions, reduce stormwater runoff, or reduce ammonia emissions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Research and Development fund is limited to personnel within the University of Maryland System. The Seed Capital Fund is open to any company based in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicants for the Research and Development fund must be students, faculty, or staff from the University of Maryland System.
Applicants for the Seed Capital Fund must be a Maryland-based company.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program has two components. For the Research and Development fund, contact Ronnie Gist at rgist@umd.edu or visit www.mips.umd.edu for application details. For the Seed Capital Fund, contact Scott Christensen at schris14@umd.edu or visit http://mtech.umd.edu/ventures/chesapeake-bay-seed-capital-fund.html for application details. For general program questions, contact Ari Engelberg at ari.engelberg@maryland.gov or (410) 260-8734.

structured_extraction.program_description: A land trust capacity, excellence, and stewardship grant intended to increase land trust capacity, support programming and innovation, and foster stronger, better connected land trusts that will protect all natural resources and enhance the lives of Maryland citizens and future generations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for local land trusts in Maryland to increase capacity, support programming and innovation, and strengthen land trust operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local land trusts in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land trust capacity building, programming, and innovation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a local land trust in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants awarded to volunteer-based nonprofit groups, communities, land trusts, schools, and municipalities in Maryland to support environmental education projects, litter removal, citizen stewardship, and protection of natural resources in urban and rural areas. The program includes several sub-grants: the Community Stewardship Grant (up to $5,000 for schools and nonprofits engaging community members in environmental education and stewardship), the Bill James Environmental Education Grant (up to $1,000 for school groups and nonprofit youth organizations), the Capacity Building for Land Trusts grant (up to $10,000), the Aileen Hughes Award (up to $5,000 for individual land trust leaders), and the Tree Planting on Agricultural Lands grant (up to $50,000).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded annually to support environmental education projects, litter removal, citizen stewardship activities, neighborhood greening, and natural resource protection. The program provides multiple funding tracks: Community Stewardship Grants award up to $5,000 per organization for schools and nonprofits engaging community members in environmental education and stewardship; Bill James Environmental Education Grants award up to $1,000 for school groups and nonprofit youth organizations; Capacity Building for Land Trusts grants award up to $10,000 for organizational strengthening activities; the Aileen Hughes Award provides up to $5,000 to individuals representing Maryland land trusts for outstanding leadership and innovation; and Tree Planting on Agricultural Lands grants award up to $10,000 for small-scale projects (less than 2 acres) or up to $50,000 for large-scale projects (greater than 2 acres). The 2026 grant cycle awarded $205,134 total: $47,000 for Community Stewardship, $55,000 for Land Trusts Assistance, $5,000 for Aileen Hughes Award, and $98,134 for Tree Planting. Project funds for the 2026 cycle are to be used from March 30, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Award winners are announced on March 20 (Keep Maryland Beautiful Day) and grant money is received by April 15.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 1, 2025 (for 2026 cycle); applications accepted on rolling basis annually with typical deadline in late November/early December
structured_extraction.program_audience: Volunteer-based nonprofit groups, communities, land trusts, schools, science and ecology clubs, nonprofit youth organizations, municipalities, community and homeowners associations, service and civic groups, and other community organizations in Maryland working on environmental education, stewardship, and conservation projects. Individuals representing Maryland land trusts are eligible for the Aileen Hughes Award. The program strongly encourages applications from underrepresented groups and projects serving communities that are traditionally underrepresented, such as communities of color.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Environmental education projects, litter removal, citizen stewardship activities, neighborhood greening and beautification, litter prevention, tree planting and reforestation on agricultural lands, establishing and enhancing riparian buffers, creating forest habitat, providing livestock shade, improving water quality, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, natural resource protection in urban and rural areas, and developing innovative solutions to local environmental problems. For Tree Planting projects specifically: site preparation costs (soil amendment, invasive species removal, herbicide application), plant material and mulch, planting costs, tree protection costs, two-year maintenance costs, and project management costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland, covering both urban and rural areas. All Maryland counties are eligible. Funding partners include Maryland Environmental Trust (MET), Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT), and Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA).
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization, school, municipality, land trust, community and homeowners association, service or civic group, or government agency (for most tracks)
For Aileen Hughes Award: individual must represent a Maryland land trust with current Cooperative Agreement with MET (dated on or after November 2, 2020)
Land trusts must have a current Cooperative Agreement with MET (dated on or after November 2, 2020)
Projects must focus on environmental education, litter removal, citizen stewardship, natural resource protection, or land trust capacity building
Missions must be centered on directly engaging community members, especially children and young adults, in environmental education and stewardship
Active engagement in developing innovative solutions to local environmental problems

For Community Stewardship projects: applicants are encouraged to integrate environmental education best practices and align projects with the Meaningful Watershed Educational Experience (MWEE) framework

For Tree Planting projects: must implement cost-effective reforestation or afforestation on qualifying agricultural land; projects must include planting design and plan development, obtaining required permits, providing planting activities (contractual or volunteer), and providing two-year monitoring and maintenance to ensure survivorship rates consistent with Maryland State Forest Conservation Technical Manual Third Edition of 1997
Applicants must be in good standing with the state of Maryland and provide a Certificate of Good Standing
Applications must be submitted online through the Chesapeake Bay Trust portal at https://www.grantrequest.com
For Tree Planting Track 3 projects: applicants must procure landowner permission as demonstrated through a landowner letter of commitment and property agreement
Grant Receipt Forms must be signed and returned within one month of receiving grant money
Final grant reports are due within two months of project completion or by March 2, 2027
Grant funds for 2026 cycle must be used from March 30, 2026 through February 28, 2027
Both an Executive Officer and a Project Leader (two separate individuals) must be identified; individuals associated with for-profit entities to be engaged in the project cannot serve in either role
Project completion required within 12 months of award receipt (extensions reviewed on case-by-case basis)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through the Chesapeake Bay Trust website at https://www.grantrequest.com/SID_1520?SA=SNA&FID=35748. The application portal opens on September 1 annually. Applicants must log in or create an account on the online system. Required application components include: eligibility quiz (three questions to determine project eligibility), Applicant Information tab (organization name, address, phone, type, mission, EIN, UEI, Executive Officer and Project Leader information), Project Information tab (project title, abstract, watershed, county, legislative district, latitude and longitude), Timeline tab (project start and end dates with major tasks), Deliverables tab (estimated metrics for participants and outcomes), Volunteers tab (volunteer activities description and hours), Project Partnerships tab (partner organizations and commitment letters), Narrative & Supporting Documents tab (completed narrative questions template uploaded as Word or PDF), Certificate of Good Standing (required upload), Budget tab (Financial Management Spreadsheet with Application Budget, budget information, and budget narrative justification), Terms and Conditions tab (required agreement), and Demographics tab (optional DEIJ information). Applicants must submit completed applications by 4:00 PM EST on the deadline date (typically December 1 for the following year's cycle, though the Aileen Hughes Award deadline may differ). Late applications are not accepted. Award notifications are announced on March 20 (Keep Maryland Beautiful Day). Grantees receive award agreements with conditions and due dates. Awardees must sign and return Grant Receipt Forms within one month of receiving funds and submit final reports within two months of project completion. Ten percent of the total award is held until the final report is approved. Organizations with outstanding reports will not be awarded additional grants. The Trust recommends contacting Program Coordinator Amber Cameron at least two weeks prior to the deadline for guidance on applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant is awarded to Maryland land trusts to increase organizational capacity, support community programming and innovation, and foster stronger, better connected land trusts that protect natural resources and enhance the lives of Maryland citizens. It supports land trusts to develop community programs and services, implement standards and practices, and increase public support for conservation, stewardship, and land trust activities. Also referred to as the Capacity Building for Land Trusts Grant under the Keep Maryland Beautiful program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant of up to $10,000 awarded to land trusts within Maryland to build sustainable organizations by increasing capacity, developing community programs and services, implementing standards and practices, and increasing public support for conservation and stewardship activities. Land trusts receiving grants are expected to provide matching funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local land trusts in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building sustainable land trusts, increasing organizational capacity, developing community programs and services, implementing standards and practices, and increasing public support for conservation, stewardship, and related land trust activities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to land trusts located within Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a land trust located in Maryland
Use funds to increase organizational capacity or develop community programs and services
Applicant must provide a matching fund contribution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the application portal at https://cbtrust.org/grants/keep-maryland-beautiful/ to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that provides matching grants to state and local government entities for projects that improve outdoor recreation through the acquisition of land and development or renovation of public outdoor recreation areas and facilities. Maryland qualifies to receive this funding through its approved Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan. The program requires a 1:1 match of non-federal funds and is reimbursement-based, with funds issued after project completion.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement-based 50/50 matching grants with a 1:1 matching requirement; LWCF funding must be matched with non-federal funds. Acceptable federal funding sources for matching include Recreational Trails Fund, Community Development Block Grants, and Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration programs. Program Open Space and Community Parks and Playground grants may also be used to match LWCF funds. Maximum grant request is $3,000,000 (for a $6,000,000 total project) and minimum request is $50,000 (for a $100,000 total project). Funds are issued on a reimbursement basis after project completion. Projects must be completed within 3 years of award date with a possibility of a 2-year extension.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Government entities including state agencies, federally recognized tribes, counties, municipalities, and special districts seeking to improve outdoor recreation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of land for conservation and park purposes, and development or renovation of public outdoor recreation areas and facilities. The entire park must be permanently protected and dedicated exclusively to recreational use.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. All Maryland counties and municipalities are eligible. Projects must comply with the state's most current Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan.
requirements_list: Must be a government entity (state agency, federally recognized tribe, county, municipality, or special district)
LWCF funding must be matched 1:1 with non-federal funds
Acceptable federal funding sources for matching include Recreational Trails Fund, Community Development Block Grants, and Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration
Program Open Space and Community Parks and Playground grants may be used to match LWCF funds
The entire park must be permanently protected and dedicated exclusively to recreational use
Projects must be completed within 3 years of award date (with possibility of 2-year extension)
All eligible projects must reflect the state's policies and priorities of its most current Statewide Comprehensive Outdoor Recreation Plan
County or City of Baltimore must have an approved or updated Local Land Preservation, Parks and Recreation Plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: LWCF grants have a 2-step application process. Applicants submit projects to Maryland DNR for consideration during the Open Project Selection Process (OPSP). Optional individual meetings to review application proposals are available May 1-29 by scheduling through the provided Google Calendar link. Applications are due June 24 at 5pm to the contact email. Successful applicants will be notified by September 15 and invited to prepare a full application for submission to the National Park Service.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Parks and Playgrounds Infrastructure Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to local governments for park and recreation acquisition and development projects that are accessible to the general public without membership requirements or excessive fees. Funded through FY 2022 and FY 2023 capital budgets, the program emphasizes accessibility and general public use, with the matching requirement waived for eligible applicants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding from FY 2022 and FY 2023 capital budgets for park and recreation acquisition and development projects. Matching requirement is waived. Funds cannot be used for projects that are inaccessible to the general public, require memberships, exclude the public due to higher use fees, or include residential or elaborate lodging facilities. Projects are administered in a similar manner as Program Open Space local grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments in Maryland for park and recreation projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and development of park and recreation projects that are accessible to the general public, including parks and playgrounds.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; administered to local governments throughout Maryland, including all counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Projects must be accessible to the general public
Projects cannot require memberships
Projects cannot exclude the public because of higher use fees
Projects cannot include residential or elaborate lodging facilities
Matching requirement is waived
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit either LPPI Acquisition Project Application or LPPI Development Project Application and Project Agreement. Submit LPPI Funding Authorization Form. Request reimbursement using appropriate form for acquisition or development projects. Projects are administered in a similar manner as Program Open Space local grants with specific requirements related to general public access.

structured_extraction.program_description: Professional certification program validating competency to identify and classify fish species collected during Maryland Biological Stream Survey (MBSS) sampling from streams, following MBSS protocols for water quality and ecological assessment. Certification is valid for three years and is required by some Maryland counties and state agencies for fish sample analysis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certification obtained after attending MBSS summer training, passing a written test administered at training, and successfully completing a field audit conducted by a DNR Quality Control Officer. Valid for three years. Fee payment occurs only after passing the written test. Pricing is the same for non-profit and for-profit organizations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specific deadline; apply at any time through training program
structured_extraction.program_audience: Biologists, environmental professionals, individuals, and organizations involved in stream biomonitoring who need certification in fish taxonomy and identification for water quality assessment and MBSS sampling work.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification training and assessment demonstrating competency to identify and classify fish specimens consistent with MBSS protocols for biomonitoring and water quality assessment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland organizations and individuals. Required by some Maryland counties and state agencies for fish sample analysis.
requirements_list: Attend MBSS summer training
Pass written test administered at training
Complete successful field audit conducted by DNR Quality Control Officer
Pass quality assurance procedures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend MBSS summer training, take and pass the written test (fee payment occurs after passing the written test), then complete a field audit evaluation by a Department of Natural Resources Quality Control Officer and satisfy quality assurance requirements to receive certification.

structured_extraction.program_description: Professional certification program validating competency to identify and classify freshwater mussel species from streams and other aquatic systems using Maryland Biological Stream Survey (MBSS) protocols and regionally standard survey methods. Certification remains valid indefinitely with annual documentation of training or field work.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certification is obtained after attending MBSS training, passing a written test, passing a field audit, and providing documentation of adequate prior experience conducting surveys using regionally standard mussel survey protocols. Certification remains valid indefinitely as long as the individual provides annual documentation of training and/or field work. Pricing is the same for non-profit and for-profit organizations. Fee payment occurs only after passing the written test.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specific deadline; apply at any time through the training program
structured_extraction.program_audience: Malacologists, environmental professionals, and individuals or organizations conducting freshwater mussel surveys and taxonomy work for stream and aquatic ecosystem assessment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification training and assessment for freshwater mussel identification and species documentation, demonstrating competency to identify mussel species and conduct mussel surveys consistent with regional protocols.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; available to all Maryland organizations and individuals.
requirements_list: Attend MBSS training
Pass written test
Pass field audit
Provide documentation of adequate prior experience conducting surveys using regionally standard mussel survey protocols
Maintain annual documentation of training and/or field work to keep certification active
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend MBSS training, take and pass the written test (fee payment occurs only after passing), complete a field audit evaluation by DNR staff, and submit documentation demonstrating adequate prior experience with mussel surveys using regional protocols.

structured_extraction.program_description: Professional certification program validating competency to conduct and document physical habitat assessments using Maryland Biological Stream Survey (MBSS) protocols for water quality and ecosystem health evaluation. Certification is valid for one year and is used by Maryland counties, state agencies, environmental professionals, and field scientists for habitat assessment requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certification is obtained after attending MBSS training and passing a written test and field audit. Certification is valid for one year. Fee payment occurs only after passing the written test. Pricing is the same for non-profit and for-profit organizations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specific deadline; apply at any time through training program
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, environmental professionals, and field scientists seeking certification in physical habitat assessment of streams for water quality and ecological monitoring, including those working for Maryland counties and state agencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Certification training and assessment to demonstrate competency in evaluating physical habitat characteristics of streams consistent with MBSS standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Available to all Maryland organizations and individuals. Used by some Maryland counties and state agencies for habitat assessment requirements.
requirements_list: Attend MBSS training
Pass written test
Complete field audit
Pay certification fee after passing written test
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Attend MBSS training, take and pass the written test, and complete a field audit evaluation. Fee payment occurs only after passing the written test.

structured_extraction.program_description: A conservation easement program administered by the Maryland Environmental Trust (MET) that protects Maryland's lands by allowing landowners to voluntarily restrict future development on their property while retaining ownership. The program accepts conservation easement donations on a case-by-case basis for significant rural properties with agricultural, historic, natural, scenic, scientific, open space, or recreational values, as well as exceptional urban properties of all sizes that would provide public access. The program operates statewide, from forested mountains in Garrett County to the shores of the Chesapeake Bay.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland Environmental Trust works with landowners to establish conservation easements on their properties. The program provides technical assistance through the Conservation Easement Program Team in evaluating property eligibility, developing conservation goals, and processing easement agreements. Land trust partners often assist in the easement process. Property owners can donate conservation easements on their land. Significant rural properties containing agricultural, historic, natural, scenic, scientific, open space, or recreational values may be considered, as well as exceptional urban properties of all sizes that would provide public access.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with significant rural properties containing agricultural, historic, natural, scenic, scientific, open space, or recreational values; owners of exceptional urban properties that would provide public access; property owners in Maryland interested in protecting their land through conservation easements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Landowners can use conservation easements to restrict future development on their property while maintaining ownership, protecting agricultural land, natural areas, scenic beauty, historic sites, and creating public access opportunities. Easements allow owners to retain ownership and manage their land according to easement terms.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland, from forested mountains in Garrett County to the shores of the Chesapeake Bay
requirements_list: Property must contain significant agricultural, historic, natural, scenic, scientific, open space, or recreational values (for rural properties)
Exceptional urban properties of all sizes may be considered, especially those providing public access
Urban properties must be exceptional and ideally provide public access
Easements are considered on a case-by-case basis
Landowner must be willing to work with Maryland Environmental Trust and potentially land trust partners on the easement
Property owner must consult program policy for further details
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners should consider their long-term plans and goals for their property. Contact the Conservation Easement Program Team to discuss whether a conservation easement matches their goals and if their property is eligible. The program will evaluate the property on a case-by-case basis. Maryland Environmental Trust often works with land trust partners throughout the process. Typical steps are outlined in the Conservation Easement Processing Steps document. See the program policy and processing steps documents for detailed information.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $2,000 provided for ongoing environmental projects that have demonstrated success.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit groups and communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Ongoing environmental projects that have demonstrated success in solving environmental issues
