structured_extraction.program_description: Provides reimbursement grants to marinas for the purchase and installation of marine sewage pumpout facilities, as well as for pumpout operations and maintenance, upgrades, and replacements. The program's goal is to give boaters a proper way to dispose of sewage and to help clean Maryland's waters. Funded 75% by the Federal Clean Vessel Act with 25% from the Maryland Waterway Improvement Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement of up to $15,000 for the purchase and installation of marine sewage pumpout facilities. Grant funding is also available for pumpout operations and maintenance, upgrades, and replacement. Funded 75% by the Federal Clean Vessel Act with 25% support from the Maryland Waterway Improvement Fund.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and operators of public and private marinas in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of marine sewage pumpout facilities, pumpout operations and maintenance, pumpout upgrades and replacement
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to marinas located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must operate a marina
Applicants must receive written approval from the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) before purchasing any equipment.
A project proposal must be submitted, including a project description, equipment list with prices, and a location drawing.
Applicants must obtain at least two competitive bids for installation work.
Applicants must complete a Coordinated Environmental Review Form.
Applicants must complete a Chesapeake and Coastal Risk Assessment Form.
Applicants must obtain all necessary local permits for plumbing, electrical, or building work.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview:
Step 1: Download and complete the grant application. Do not buy equipment before receiving written approval.
Step 2: Submit the application with a project proposal. The proposal must include a project description, equipment list with prices, installation bids, and a location drawing.
Step 3: Complete and send the Coordinated Environmental Review Form to DNR. You must also obtain any needed local permits and forward copies to DNR.
Step 4: Complete the Chesapeake and Coastal Risk Assessment Form.
Step 5: After DNR approves the application, you can purchase and install the pumpout facility.
Step 6: Submit the reimbursement invoice with receipts and proof of payment. You must also submit a current W-9 form.
Step 7: Final reimbursement occurs after a final inspection by DNR staff.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Biological Stream Survey (MBSS) Training and Certification
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources offers a comprehensive training and certification program for individuals and organizations that conduct stream sampling and biological assessments. The program includes a 4-day in-person Summer Training (held May 26-29, 2026 at Bowie State University) combining classroom, laboratory, and field instruction in stream sampling protocols and ecological assessment techniques. Topics covered include benthic macroinvertebrate sampling, fish sampling, physical habitat assessment, fish taxonomy, mussel taxonomy, and laboratory processing methods. Following training, participants may pursue up to six professional certifications: (1) Benthic Macroinvertebrate Sampling, (2) Benthic Macroinvertebrate Laboratory Processing and Subsampling, (3) Fish Crew Leader, (4) Fish Taxonomy, (5) Mussel Taxonomy, and (6) Physical Habitat Assessment. Certifications are valid for one to three years depending on type, with mussel taxonomy valid indefinitely provided annual documentation of training or fieldwork is submitted. MBSS protocols are required by some Maryland counties and state agencies for stream sampling and biomonitoring work. Successful certified individuals are listed on the MBSS Registry of Certifications on the DNR website.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MBSS Summer Training is held May 26-29, 2026 at Bowie State University and consists of 4 days of in-person instruction combining classroom, laboratory, and field protocol demonstrations. Participants may register for 1-2 days at $75 per day or 3 or more days for a total fee of $200. After completing training, participants may pursue six certifications: (1) Benthic Macroinvertebrate Sampling — valid 3 years, requires annual spring training attendance, passing written test, and field audit by DNR Quality Control Officer; (2) Benthic Macroinvertebrate Laboratory Processing and Subsampling — valid 3 years, requires passing a laboratory audit and written test; (3) Fish Crew Leader — valid 3 years, requires annual attendance at fish sampling protocol portion of summer training, passing written test, and field audit; (4) Fish Taxonomy — valid 3 years, requires written test and field audit; (5) Mussel Taxonomy — valid indefinitely with annual documentation of training or fieldwork, requires documentation of adequate prior experience with regionally standard mussel survey protocols; (6) Physical Habitat Assessment — requires written test and field audit. Certification fees are paid only after passing the written test, and pricing is the same for non-profit and for-profit organizations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration for summer training is open now; training held May 26-29, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, non-profit organizations, for-profit organizations, and government agencies seeking training and/or professional certification in Maryland Biological Stream Survey protocols, including stream biomonitoring professionals, environmental consultants, laboratory personnel, and field crew leaders involved in water quality assessment and stream sampling work.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification in stream sampling protocols including benthic macroinvertebrate field sampling and laboratory processing, fish sampling and taxonomy, mussel taxonomy, physical habitat assessment, and related aquatic survey techniques for water quality and stream health assessment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open statewide to all Maryland individuals and organizations, as well as out-of-state participants. Training is held at Bowie State University in Maryland. MBSS protocols and certifications are required by some Maryland counties and state agencies for stream sampling and biomonitoring work.
requirements_list: Registration required prior to attending training
Payment of $75 per day for 1-2 days of training, or $200 total for 3 or more days
For Benthic Macroinvertebrate Sampling Certification: attend MBSS spring training each year during the three-year certification term
For Benthic Macroinvertebrate Sampling Certification: pass written test administered at training
For Benthic Macroinvertebrate Sampling Certification: pass field audit conducted by DNR Quality Control Officer (at actual biomonitoring site or mutually agreed upon site)
For Benthic Macroinvertebrate Sampling Certification: pass quality assurance procedures
For Benthic Macroinvertebrate Laboratory Processing and Subsampling Certification: attend MBSS spring or summer training
For Benthic Macroinvertebrate Laboratory Processing and Subsampling Certification: pass laboratory audit conducted by DNR staff
For Benthic Macroinvertebrate Laboratory Processing and Subsampling Certification: pass written test
For Fish Crew Leader Certification: attend fish sampling protocol portion of MBSS summer training (usually Day 1) each year for the three-year certification term
For Fish Crew Leader Certification: pass written test administered at training
For Fish Crew Leader Certification: pass field audit conducted by DNR Quality Control Officer
For Fish Crew Leader Certification: pass quality assurance procedures
For Mussel Taxonomy Certification: documentation of adequate prior experience conducting surveys using regionally standard mussel survey protocols
For Mussel Taxonomy Certification: provide annual documentation of training or fieldwork to maintain validity
Certification fees are paid only after passing the written test
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for Summer Training using the provided online Google Form registration link. Pay training fees ($75 per day for 1-2 days, or $200 total for 3 or more days) through the DNR Outdoor Store online portal. Attend in-person training sessions at Bowie State University. Pass written tests administered at training. Complete field or laboratory audits conducted by DNR Quality Control Officers. Certification fees are paid only after passing the written test. Upon successful completion of all requirements, the certified person's name is added to the MBSS Registry of Certifications published on the MBSS website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A workforce development program that provides training, career development pathways, and service opportunities in the outdoor recreation and environmental sector.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Training and workforce development program that connects participants with career pathways in outdoor recreation through team-building and service opportunities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking career development and training in outdoor recreation and environmental fields.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training, skill development, and team-building activities in outdoor recreation careers.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Environmental Trust (MET), formed in 1967, is a conservation organization that conserves, improves, and perpetuates the aesthetic, natural, scenic, and cultural aspects of Maryland's environment. Programs include Land Conservation, Monitoring and Stewardship, Local Land Trust Assistance, and the Keep Maryland Beautiful Grants Program, supporting the protection of open space and appreciation of the environment statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and other financial assistance are provided through multiple programs: Land Conservation, Monitoring and Stewardship, Local Land Trust Assistance, and the Keep Maryland Beautiful Grants Program. These programs support environmental conservation, open space protection, stewardship of protected lands, local land trust operations, and beautification projects throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, local land trusts, and local governments involved in environmental conservation and beautification in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land conservation, monitoring and stewardship of protected lands, local land trust support and assistance, and environmental beautification projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Chesapeake Bay Foundation initiative administered in partnership with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that provides free plant material, implementation labor, and three years of maintenance for streamside forest buffers and upland tree plantings. The program partners with other agency programs for associated practices such as stream bank fencing and livestock watering. Livestock producers interested in grazing can also receive funding for converting row crop fields to pasture for rotational grazing, plus grazing mentors and technical assistance on farm economics and marketing through the CBF-led Maryland Grazers Network, which has expanded to a Bay-wide effort through the Mountains to Bay Grazers Alliance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free plant material, implementation labor, and three years of maintenance for streamside forest buffers and upland tree plantings. For livestock producers, funding is available for converting row crop fields to pasture for rotational grazing, plus access to grazing mentors and technical assistance on farm economics and marketing through the Maryland Grazers Network and the Mountains to Bay Grazers Alliance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland farmers, landowners, and livestock producers interested in establishing streamside forest buffers, upland tree plantings, or rotational grazing systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Streamside forest buffer and upland tree planting establishment and maintenance, conversion of row crop fields to pasture for rotational grazing, and grazing management technical assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; part of the Mountains to Bay Grazers Alliance serving the broader Chesapeake Bay region.
requirements_list: Be an active farmer, landowner, or livestock producer in Maryland
Own agricultural or forestry land
For livestock/grazing program: be a livestock producer interested in rotational grazing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners and producers should contact Rob Schnabel at rschnabel@cbf.org or visit m2balliance.org for more information and to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal-state partnership program that protects environmentally important and sensitive forests from conversion to non-forest uses through the purchase of perpetual conservation easements from willing sellers at market value. The program provides up to 75 percent federal cost-share funding for conservation easements on private forest land, with at least 25 percent of funding coming from state, local, or non-governmental organization sources, or donated by the landowner. Conservation easements are legal agreements that restrict future activities on the land to protect its conservation values, including wildlife habitat, water quality, and wood products industry support.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The federal government supplies up to 75% of funding to purchase perpetual conservation easements on private forest land at market value from willing sellers. At least 25% of funding must come from state, local, or non-governmental organization funds, or be donated by the landowner. Conservation easements are legal agreements that restrict future activities on the land to protect conservation values.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications evaluated and ranked on an annual basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private forest landowners with forest property in designated Forest Legacy Areas who are willing to sell development rights and place their land under a perpetual conservation easement. Also open to conservation organizations and government entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of perpetual conservation easements on private forest land to protect environmentally important forests from conversion to non-forest uses. Protected forests must be at least 75% forested with the remaining 25% in compatible land uses such as agriculture.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available only in Forest Legacy Areas, which are geographically defined areas in Maryland identified in the Forest Legacy Program Assessment of Need as having some of the highest economic and environmental values for wildlife, wood products industry, water quality, and residents.
requirements_list: Private forest land only - publicly owned forests are not eligible
Property must be located within a designated Forest Legacy Area
At least 75% of the area put under easement must be forested
Remaining 25% must be in compatible land use such as agriculture
Landowner must be willing to sell development rights
Applicants will be evaluated and ranked annually
Projects ranked on forest importance, threat of development, and strategic value to other protected lands or conservation initiatives
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners apply using the Landowner Application form on an annual basis. All applications are evaluated and ranked based on forest importance, threat of development, and strategic value to other protected lands or conservation initiatives. Highest-ranked applications enter the national ranking process for federal funding consideration. If selected for funding and negotiations produce acceptable easement terms, the conservation easement is purchased at market value. If a project does not receive federal funding or acceptable terms cannot be negotiated, landowners may reapply in future years.

structured_extraction.program_description: A recognition program that certifies Maryland schools that integrate environmental education into their curricula, implement best management practices at the school, and address community environmental issues. The program provides a range of support services including tree plantings on school grounds, teacher training, small grants for aquatic-based projects, and assistance with the certification application process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive support including tree plantings on school grounds and buffer areas, teacher training in environmental education programs (Projects WET, WILD, and Learning Tree), teacher guides for conducting waste, energy, and water audits, small grants for aquatic-based school yard or classroom projects, support for stream and aquatic vegetation restoration projects (such as submerged aquatic vegetation), assistance in completing the Green School application, and integration of environmental education into school instruction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland public and private schools seeking environmental education certification, recognition, and support
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Small grants can be used for aquatic-based school yard or classroom projects. Technical assistance and other resources support environmental education integration into curricula, school ground improvements including tree plantings, aquatic and submerged vegetation restoration projects, teacher professional development, and waste, energy, and water reduction initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland schools are eligible to participate in the program.
requirements_list: Include environmental education in school curricula
Model best management practices at the school
Address community environmental issues
Document school program and activities during a two-year period
Complete a formal application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools complete an application that documents the school's environmental education program and activities during a two-year period. A review panel evaluates the applications, and an award celebration is held in the spring. For detailed information and application procedures, visit www.maeoe.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: A series of comprehensive training courses designed for logging professionals to promote excellence in forestry, sustainable timber harvesting, and forest management. The program covers best management practices, logging aesthetics, forest management, field practicum, logging safety and OSHA requirements, first aid and CPR, and continuing education. Participation is voluntary and open to loggers, landowners, foresters, and all interested individuals. Loggers who complete the initial training must attend at least one continuing education course annually and participate in periodic jobsite visits to maintain their Master Logger designation. The program also maintains a Directory of Maryland Master Loggers updated biannually.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers comprehensive training courses for logging professionals covering five core areas: (1) best management practices for timber harvest design including stream crossings and erosion prevention; (2) logging aesthetics to improve the visual appearance of harvests; (3) forest management principles including forest science, ecology, and wildlife management; (4) field practicum where loggers apply harvest principles on actual harvest areas; and (5) logging safety and OSHA compliance. Courses on first aid and CPR are also required. Most courses range from $20 to $40. Upon completing the five initial training courses, participants receive Master Logger endorsement. To maintain the designation, Master Loggers must attend at least one continuing education course annually on topics such as log grading and marketing, environmental regulations, or timber estimations, and participate in periodic jobsite visits. The program maintains a Directory of Maryland Master Loggers updated biannually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Logging professionals, landowners, foresters, and all interested individuals seeking training in sustainable forestry, timber harvesting practices, and forest management.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and professional development in forestry and logging practices, including instruction in best management practices, logging aesthetics, forest management, forest ecology, wildlife management, field applications, safety procedures, OSHA compliance, first aid and CPR, and continuing education on current industry laws and techniques.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland in all counties.
requirements_list: Voluntary program attendance
Completion of five initial training courses covering best management practices, logging aesthetics, forest management, field practicum, and logging safety and OSHA
Completion of first aid and CPR training as part of initial coursework
Attendance of at least one continuing education course annually to maintain Master Logger designation
Participation in periodic jobsite visits to maintain Master Logger status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals register for and attend the comprehensive training courses offered through the program. Upon completion of the five core training areas and first aid/CPR requirements, participants receive Master Logger endorsement. To maintain this designation, Master Loggers must attend at least one continuing education course each year on topics related to their profession, such as log grading and marketing, environmental regulations, or timber estimations, and participate in periodic jobsite visits as required.

Funds may be available for bulkhead stabilization, temporary ice service support, business development, harbor maintenance, and support for new entrants to the local fishing industry. requirements_list: Must be a commercial or for-hire fishing vessel, operator, crew member, or related shoreside support business
Must be impacted by offshore wind development

Specific details are also found in Exhibit B of the Memorandum of Understanding. Contact the Fisheries Compensation Program for Atlantic Coast Offshore Wind at rfainfo.com for the most up-to-date information about the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to support equitable access to outdoor recreation for communities that have been historically underserved. The program funds community-based projects that help Marylanders overcome social, geographic, cultural, physical, and economic barriers to outdoor recreation, such as distance and transportation, cost of activities or entry charges, equipment costs, lack of exposure to outdoor activities, and feeling unwelcome in outdoor spaces. Grants are intended to increase equitable access to nature and outdoor activities across Maryland communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grants ranging from $2,500 to $7,500. Approximately 5 awards are estimated. No matching funds are required, but leveraging other resources is encouraged. Funds may be used for program staff, materials, transportation, outreach, gear, event costs, or other eligible expenses that directly support project goals and advance equity and access to outdoor recreation. Projects must be completed by September 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofits, Tribal entities, school districts, government agencies, or for-profit organizations with a mission aligned with outdoor equity that are based in Maryland and serve Maryland communities. Intended to reach communities that have historically faced social, geographic, cultural, physical, and economic barriers to outdoor recreation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program staff, materials, transportation, outreach, gear, event costs, or other eligible expenses that directly support project goals and advance equity and access to outdoor recreation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be based in Maryland, serve communities within Maryland, and host events or activities within Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, Tribal entity, school district, government agency, or for-profit organization with a mission aligned with outdoor equity
Must be based in, serving communities, and hosting the event or activity within Maryland
Must demonstrate readiness to manage and complete a small-scale community project within one year

Project must address at least one of the following themes: creating opportunities for outdoor recreation, outdoor and environmental education and stewardship, community capacity-building for long-term engagement with outdoor access, or connecting outdoor recreation to physical, emotional, or community health benefits
Recipient must fill out a W-9 with the State of Maryland to receive funds
Project must be completed by September 30, 2026
Final report must be submitted no later than October 15, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a grant application by filling out the online Google form by June 30, 2025 at 5:00 p.m. The application requires organization information, project description, budget and budget narrative, timeline with key milestones, evaluation plan, and optional letters of support or collaboration. Applications are reviewed based on project alignment with focus areas, demonstrated need and community involvement, clear scope and goals, feasibility and budget clarity, and outcomes evaluation plan. Award notification will be provided after the application deadline. Awardees must submit a final report upon project completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A law requiring that forests cleared or cut during highway construction projects using State funds be replaced on an acre-for-acre basis on public lands within two years or three growing seasons of project completion. Replacement can occur on sites in the same county or watershed (first priority), through forest mitigation bank credits, or through deposits to the Reforestation Fund at ten cents per square foot ($4,356 per acre) if on-site replacement is not possible. Funds deposited into the Reforestation Fund are used by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to plant replacement trees. The law applies to any construction activity involving forest cutting or clearing of 1 acre or more by a unit of State or local government or any other person using State funding.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: When State-funded highway construction or other construction activities result in forest clearing of 1 acre or more, the constructing agency must replant trees on a one-to-one acre ratio. Reforestation must be completed within 2 years or three growing seasons after project completion. Options include: (1) replanting on public lands within the same county or watershed where the construction activity occurred (first priority); (2) if not reasonably possible in the same county/watershed, replanting on public lands in the county or watershed elsewhere in the State; (3) purchasing credits from a forest mitigation bank in the county and watershed where the construction occurred; or (4) if mitigation banking is not available, depositing ten cents per square foot (approximately $4,356 per acre) into the Reforestation Fund, which the Maryland Department of Natural Resources uses to plant replacement trees. Administrative costs may be deducted from Fund contributions according to State Finance and Procurement regulations. Money deposited in the Fund must be used within 2 years or three growing seasons, or will be returned to the constructing agency.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Daniel Coy, Urban & Community Forestry Supervisor
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local government units, and any other persons using State funding for highway construction or other construction activities involving forest clearing of 1 acre or more.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree replacement and reforestation on public lands to mitigate forest loss from highway construction and other construction activities. Deposited funds are used by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to plant trees on land located in the county and watershed where construction projects occurred, or if reforestation cannot be reasonably accomplished there, on State or publicly owned lands in the county or watershed elsewhere in the State, or to purchase forest mitigation bank credits. Funds may also be used to replace trees destroyed by Department of Agriculture pest treatment applications and to finance prevention of and response to forest health emergencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applies to all construction activities in Maryland utilizing $1 or more of State funding that result in forest clearing or cutting of 1 acre or more. Replacement sites are prioritized within the same county and watershed as the impacted area, then in the same county or watershed elsewhere in the State.
requirements_list: Construction activity must involve forest cutting or clearing of 1 acre or more using $1 or more of State funding
Forest is defined as a biological community dominated by trees or other woody plants covering 1 acre or more, including areas that have been cut but not cleared
Constructing agency must minimize cutting and clearing to only the minimum necessary and consistent with sound design practices
Consult with Maryland Department of Natural Resources before cutting or clearing forests and before locating reforestation areas

Submit a completed Reforestation Site Review form (DNR Form UF920) to the appropriate regional Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service office while project is in initial design stages and prior to construction start
Submit site plans showing the site location, forest areas to be removed (highlighted on plan), and removal amount documented on drawings
Replacement of forest must be on an acre-for-acre, one-to-one ratio on State-owned or other publicly owned lands
Replacement must be accomplished within 2 years or three growing seasons of project completion
First priority given to locating reforestation sites on-site or in the project right-of-way being used for the construction activity
If sufficient area is not available at the site or within the project right-of-way, reforestation shall occur on State-owned or other publicly owned land in the same county and watershed
If reforestation cannot be reasonably accomplished in the same county and watershed, it may occur in the same county or watershed elsewhere in the State

If reforestation cannot be reasonably accomplished on State or publicly owned land in the county or watershed in the State, forest mitigation bank credits must be used in the watershed where the construction occurred
If sufficient mitigation bank credits are not available, contribute money to the Reforestation Fund at 10 cents per square foot of required planting area

Applicants requesting to transfer funds to DNR in lieu of on-site or off-site planting must provide detailed explanation of why planting obligations cannot be accomplished and must receive Forest Service approval before payments accepted
Does not apply to agricultural practices implemented under a soil and water conservation plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed Reforestation Site Review form (DNR Form UF920) along with project site plans to the appropriate regional Maryland Department of Natural Resources Forest Service office based on project location while the project is in initial design stages and prior to construction start (before any removal occurs). Site plans must show the site location, forest areas to be removed (highlighted on plan), and removal amount noted on drawings. The form must include estimated tree clearing and reforestation summary information, including estimated acreage to be cleared, acres available for on-site replacement, and proposed location for any off-site planting. DNR Forestry Personnel will complete a Construction Site Review within 20 working days of form receipt, including field review, verification of acres to be planted on-site, identification of dominant tree species found, areas of special concern, and watershed designation. Regional offices are organized as follows: Central Region (Montgomery, Howard, Baltimore, Harford, Carroll, Cecil Counties), Eastern Region (Kent, Queen Anne's, Caroline, Talbot, Dorchester, Somerset, Wicomico, Worcester Counties), Southern Region (Anne Arundel, Prince George's, Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's Counties), or Western Region (Garrett, Allegany, Washington, Frederick Counties).

structured_extraction.program_description: A regulatory program that requires the maintenance and reproduction of pine resources on harvested forestland to provide recreational, aesthetic, wildlife, and environmental benefits while supporting wood fiber production for commerce and industry.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This is a regulatory requirement, not a financial or technical assistance program. Landowners with harvested pine areas of at least five acres that were at least 25 percent loblolly, shortleaf, or pond pine prior to harvest must regenerate the land to pine either by leaving seed trees (at least 8 cone-bearing trees per acre) or by planting seedlings according to a pine reforestation plan. Regeneration is considered successful when at least 400 well-distributed seedlings that are free to grow are established.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dan Rider or your local DNR forester
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private landowners and forestry operations conducting pine harvests on at least five acres
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable - this is a regulatory mandate, not an assistance program
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland, applies to all harvested pine areas meeting the size and composition thresholds
requirements_list: Harvested area must be at least five acres in size
Area must be at least 25 percent loblolly, shortleaf, or pond pine prior to harvest
Land will not be converted to non-forest use such as agricultural or residential development
Must regenerate to pine through seed trees or seedlings per a pine reforestation plan
If using seed trees, must leave at least 8 cone-bearing loblolly, shortleaf, or pond pine per acre that are healthy, wind-firm, and well-distributed
Regeneration is successful when at least 400 seedlings that are well-distributed and free to grow are established
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local DNR forester or the Maryland DNR Forest Service for guidance on compliance with the Seed Tree Law requirements

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Urban and Community Forestry Committee (MUCFC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Urban and Community Forestry Committee (MUCFC) Grant Program provides funding to support community-based tree planting and forestry education projects that strengthen Maryland's urban forests. Grants are open to organizations statewide for work on public lands that improves the urban tree canopy, engages citizens, and promotes long-term environmental stewardship. The program also provides grants up to $1,000 through local Forestry Boards to communities, schools, and organizations for planting and maintaining street trees in urban settings, with funding sourced from the USDA Forest Service. Urban Forestry is defined as management of trees and forested areas in towns and cities with populations of 2,500 or more. MUCFC is a sub-committee of the Maryland Association of Forest Conservancy District Boards.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program awards grants to support tree planting projects on public property and forestry education initiatives. The maximum grant awarded per project is $1,000. Grants fund community-based tree planting projects and forestry education efforts on public lands, including parks, school grounds, town centers, streetscapes, and municipal properties. Funding can be used for purchasing trees and native plant materials, tree planting supplies (mulch, shovels, etc.), signage with MUCFC acknowledgment, and equipment with detailed future-use plans. Projects that include matching funds or in-kind support are given priority. All unused funds must be returned to the Maryland Forestry Boards Foundation, Inc. with the final report. Funding is available to organizations only, not individual applicants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Grant proposals are due by 11:59 p.m. on January 15 and July 15
structured_extraction.contact_name: Wanda MacLachlan (MUCFC Grant Chair); Dan Coy; Wayne Lucas
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations, nonprofits, government agencies, schools, and civic organizations seeking to improve urban tree canopy, plant and maintain street trees, and conduct forestry education in Maryland cities and towns with populations of 2,500 or more.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports tree planting projects on public lands such as school grounds, parks, town centers, or municipal properties and streetscapes; maintenance of street trees in urban settings; educational or outreach projects that raise public awareness about the value of trees in urban environments; tree and plant materials; planting supplies; signage; and equipment with detailed future-use plans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All funded projects must occur on public lands in urban areas across Maryland with populations of 2,500 or more. Projects statewide are eligible. Grants are distributed through local County Forestry Boards.
requirements_list: Projects must occur on public lands (school grounds, parks, town centers, municipal properties, streetscapes)
Funding is only available to organizations, not individual applicants
Applications must be approved by MUCFC and signed by the local County Forestry Board prior to starting the project
Local Forestry Board member original signature is required on the application
For tree planting projects: clear site plan and project description required
For tree planting projects: itemized list of tree species and sizes required with cost per item (native, shade-providing trees preferred; invasive species will not be funded)
For tree planting projects: map showing planting locations required
For tree planting projects: maintenance plan describing watering, mulching, weeding, and long-term care required, including responsible persons and maintenance schedule
Projects should use reasonably priced plant materials and source trees from John S. Ayton State Tree Nursery or TreeMendous Maryland when possible
For educational projects: draft content or images for signage or publications required
For educational projects: description of target audience and distribution plan required
For educational projects: explanation of how project addresses unmet informational need required
For signage: mockup of signage showing MUCFC acknowledgement and price quote from sign maker required
For equipment requests: detailed plan of future use of equipment required
Clear credit to MUCFC must be given on all printed materials and signage
Signage must display MUCFC logo
Final reports due one month after proposed completion date
Any unused funds must be returned with final report to Maryland Forestry Boards Foundation, Inc.
Failure to submit final report or return unused funds may disqualify applicants from future grants
Projects that promote urban tree canopy and long-term maintenance receive preference
Priority given to tree planting projects on public property that involve volunteers and have matching support from other organizations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Grant Guidelines at https://dnr.maryland.gov/forests/Documents/MUCFCGrantGuidelines.pdf. 2. Download and complete the grant application form available at https://dnr.maryland.gov/forests/Documents/Online-Grant-Application.pdf using Adobe Acrobat Reader. 3. Contact your local Forestry Board office for assistance and to request a forestry board member signature. 4. Submit the completed application with all required attachments (itemized species list, map showing planting locations, signage mockup with price quote, equipment future-use plan, and other supporting documents as necessary) to your local Forestry Board for signature. 5. Once signed and returned to you, email the finalized application packet to Wanda MacLachlan, MUCFC Grant Chair, at wtm@umd.edu. 6. Grant proposals must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. on January 15 or July 15. 7. Grants are reviewed on or about January 15 and July 15. 8. Complete the approved project by the proposed completion date. 9. Submit a Final Report one month after the proposed completion date using the Final Report form available at https://dnr.maryland.gov/forests/Documents/MUCFC-FinalReport-Form-Example.pdf. 10. Include an itemized accounting of expenditures with receipts and determine if any refund is due. For additional information, contact Dan Coy at daniel.coy@maryland.gov or call the Grants Program Chair, Wanda MacLachlan, at 410-531-5973.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's Rural Legacy Program (RLP), created in 1997, preserves large blocks of working rural lands for future generations by protecting natural, cultural, agricultural, and forest land across the state. The program encourages local governments and private land trusts to identify Rural Legacy Areas — delineated areas within a county that include both working farms and ecologically significant landscapes — and competitively apply for funds to purchase conservation easements and fee simple estates from willing landowners. The program protects areas vulnerable to sprawl development, enhances natural resources, farms, and forests through cooperative efforts among state and local governments and land trusts, and supports sustainable land bases for natural resource-based industries. Currently there are 35+ designated Rural Legacy Areas throughout the state, covering portions of all 24 Maryland counties. Since 1997, the program has awarded over $403.5 million and conserved over 135,000 acres through over 1,000 easements statewide.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides annual grant funding to local sponsors (local governments and private land trusts acting as Rural Legacy Sponsors) to conserve land through easement and fee simple purchases within designated Rural Legacy Areas. Funding is sourced from Maryland Program Open Space dollars and general obligation bonds from the state's capital budget; local jurisdictions also contribute matching funds. Grant funds are encumbered following approval by the Board of Public Works, typically between August and September of each year, and Grant Agreements are prepared for awarded sponsors between September and October. The program uses an objective scoring approach to review and allocate its limited grant funds. Recent easement offers through county-administered versions of the program have ranged from $8,000 to $10,000 per acre. Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity. Conservation easements are recorded in perpetuity and cannot be amended or modified without approval of the Grantee, the Rural Legacy Board, and the Board of Public Works. The Rural Legacy Board determines the grant amount for each new or existing Area based on application evaluation and available funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Second Tuesday in February by close of business, 5:00 p.m. (annual cycle); Washington County landowners apply prior to February 1st of each cycle year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and private land trusts acting as Rural Legacy Sponsors seeking to protect working farms and ecologically significant landscapes in designated Rural Legacy Areas, as well as individual willing landowners in designated Rural Legacy Areas seeking to sell conservation easements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition and conservation, including purchase of conservation easements and fee simple estates from willing landowners, to preserve agricultural land, forest land, wetlands, historic sites, and other natural areas within designated Rural Legacy Areas and protect them from sprawl development. Funds may also support transactional costs including administrative, indirect, and program compliance costs associated with acquisitions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Rural Legacy Areas throughout Maryland. At least one Rural Legacy Area exists in every county of Maryland. Total acreage designated in all Rural Legacy Areas exceeds 1.3 million acres. The program operates through 35+ designated Rural Legacy Areas across the state. Washington County-specific areas surround the Towns of Sharpsburg, Keedysville, and Boonsboro and the Rural Villages of St. James, Lappans, Fairplay, Rohrersville, and Gapland. Baltimore County-approved Rural Legacy areas include Coastal, Gunpowder, Long Green, Manor, and Piney Run.
requirements_list: Applicants (sponsors) must be a local government or private land trust
Local sponsors must apply annually to the Rural Legacy Board for participation in the program and to receive funding
Applications must focus on protecting large contiguous tracts of land rich in natural and cultural resources
Projects must be located within a designated Rural Legacy Area
New Rural Legacy Area applications require a Full Application submission per the format identified in the Rural Legacy Grants Manual
Grant renewals and boundary expansion requests for existing Rural Legacy Areas require an Abbreviated Application with Property List Form
All applications must comply with GIS Submittal Guidelines
Property must meet program evaluation criteria including natural resource value, agricultural productivity, and cultural significance
Recommendations from Rural Legacy Advisory Committee required
Approval from Rural Legacy Board required
Final approval from Maryland Board of Public Works required
Individual landowners must be willing sellers or donors of conservation easements
Land must be ecologically valuable and impact the health of the Chesapeake Bay or local waterways
Washington County: property must be located within a specified Rural Legacy Area boundary surrounding designated towns and rural villages

Washington County: applications ranked based on property size, number of development rights, proximity to other permanent easements, agricultural characteristics, historic characteristics, and environmental characteristics
Baltimore County (Coastal area): contact County Land Preservation staff; other areas contact the area sponsor land trust
Anne Arundel County: 100-foot grass buffer and 100-foot forest buffer required; priority focus on stream buffer protection
Sponsors must demonstrate adequate public participation in development of applications
Sponsors of land trusts must consult with each local government in proposed areas prior to filing applications
Local government approval required for all applications and amendments
If proposed area is within one mile of a municipality, the municipality has forty-five days to review and comment before submission
Sponsors must identify existing protected lands in proposed area
Sponsors must prepare a monitoring protocol for conservation easements
Sponsors responsible for adequate monitoring, stewardship, and enforcement of conservation easements
Property interests acquired with program funds must be retained in perpetuity for conservation purposes
GIS data for protected lands administered by sponsoring programs must be submitted by January 15th prior to application deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Conduct pre-application activities: Review law, regulations, and program guidance including the Rural Legacy Program Grants Manual. Initiate public participation procedures and determine anticipated level of initial landowner participation through methods such as Agricultural Preservation District identification or written questionnaires from interested landowners expressing willingness to sell interests in real property. Develop partnerships among federal, State, and local governments and land trusts as needed. Consult with each local government in proposed area; if within one mile of a municipality, provide forty-five days for municipal review and comment. Identify existing protected lands in proposed area. Prepare a Plan for the proposed area (list of proposed acquisitions prioritized by resource value and conservation impact) and a monitoring protocol. 2. Submit GIS data: By January 15th, submit GIS data for lands protected by local land preservation programs administered by sponsoring jurisdiction or land trust, in accordance with GIS Submittal Guidelines (NAD_1983_StatePlane_Maryland_FIPS_1900 meters projection, zipped shapefile or geodatabase format) to KatrinaL.Tucker@maryland.gov. 3. Complete and submit application: For new Rural Legacy Areas, complete the Full Application form including Cover Sheet, Executive Summary (narrative and numbers), Criteria and General Description, Funding Request, Proposed Acquisitions Form, color map showing Area boundary and protected/proposed properties, and 10 color digital photos. For existing areas seeking continued funding, complete the Abbreviated Application with Property List Form and annual report. Submit one reproducible and four double-sided copies plus electronic copy (Word or PDF) to Rural Legacy Program, Land Acquisition and Planning Unit, Katrina L. Tucker, KatrinaL.Tucker@maryland.gov. 4. Submit by deadline: Applications due Second Tuesday in February by 5:00 p.m. (Washington County: prior to February 1st). Submissions may be mailed or delivered by hand. 5. State agency review: State agencies review applications February through April. 6. Advisory Committee and Board review: Rural Legacy Advisory Committee (eleven volunteers appointed by Governor) and Rural Legacy Board review applications April through May; may request presentations or site visits from Sponsors. 7. Advisory Committee recommendation: Advisory Committee holds annual meeting June/July, submits recommendations to Rural Legacy Board. 8. Board decision: Rural Legacy Board reviews recommendations July/August, submits final recommendations to Governor and Board of Public Works. 9. Board of Public Works approval: Board of Public Works (Governor, Comptroller, and Treasurer) designates Rural Legacy Areas and approves grants, typically August or September. 10. Grant Agreement: Rural Legacy Program Staff notify selected Sponsors of Board decisions; Program Director submits Board decisions to Board of Public Works for approval. After BPW approval, Program Staff transmit Grant Agreement to Sponsor for signature. Chairman of Board signs Grant Agreement upon Sponsor approval. Grant period begins when Chairman approves and signs the Grant Agreement. 11. Project implementation: After receipt of signed Grant Agreement, Sponsor can begin negotiations with interested landowners for conservation easements or fee simple purchases. 12. Project submission and approval: Sponsor submits completed projects with all required documentation to Rural Legacy Program Staff for review and BPW approval. After BPW approval, Program Staff process project for payment and Sponsor may proceed to settlement with landowner. 13. Annual reporting: During term of grant agreement, Sponsor submits annual report to Program. Sponsors holding Rural Legacy conservation easements assume responsibility for monitoring and enforcement in accordance with monitoring protocols.

structured_extraction.program_description: A coupon/rebate program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that provides Maryland residents and organizations with a $25 discount coupon toward the purchase of a native or recommended tree costing $50 or more at participating retail nurseries and garden centers throughout Maryland. The program encourages citizens and organizations to plant new trees to improve air and water quality, reduce energy costs, increase property values, support ecological benefits, and beautify neighborhoods and highways. Program funding comes from a settlement with a major power generator for Clean Air Act violations, in partnership with the Office of the Attorney General and Maryland's participating tree vendors.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a coupon worth $25 off the purchase of one native or recommended tree with a retail value of $50 or more from a participating retail nursery or garden center. The discount is applied at the register at the time of sale. One coupon must be filled in for each tree purchased. The coupon must be completely filled in and signed by the customer to be valid. The discount applies to retail sales only, not wholesale tree sales. Trees must be listed on the Marylanders Plant Trees Native and Recommended Tree List to qualify. The State funds the $25 per coupon cost through a settlement from a major power generator for Clean Air Act violations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents and organizations interested in planting native or recommended trees on their property, who wish to purchase from participating retail nurseries and garden centers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of one native or recommended tree from a participating retail nursery or garden center.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at all participating retail nurseries and garden centers across Maryland. Only MPT Nurseries will accept and honor the $25 tree coupons.
requirements_list: Tree must have a retail value of $50 or more
Tree must be listed on the Marylanders Plant Trees Native and Recommended Tree List
Coupon must be completely filled in and signed by the customer
Purchase must be from a participating retail nursery or garden center
Coupon applies to retail sales only, not wholesale tree sales
One coupon per tree purchased
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Print the $25 coupon from the program website or obtain it from a participating nursery. Step 2: Find a participating MPT nursery or garden center in your area. Step 3: Fill in the coupon completely and sign it. Step 4: Present the coupon at the participating retail nursery or garden center when purchasing a qualifying native or recommended tree. The $25 discount is applied at the register at the time of sale.

structured_extraction.program_description: Multi-state wildfire training academy providing comprehensive fire management and wildland fire training courses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Wildfire training academy held June 8-12, 2026 at Garrett College in McHenry, Maryland. Public registration opens March 9, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fire management professionals and wildland fire personnel in the Mid-Atlantic region
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wildfire training and education
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Mid-Atlantic region; training held in Garrett County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Registration opens to the public on March 9, 2026 through the Mid-Atlantic Fire Compact website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A seven-day educational camp designed for high school students interested in careers in natural resources. The camp offers training in traditional forestry, GIS and GPS technology, urban forestry, wildlife habitat, fisheries, and watershed ecology, taught by natural resource professionals. Students aged 16 and older may earn two college credits from Allegany College of Maryland by completing the full week and passing an exam.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A seven-day residential camp providing instruction in natural resources topics including forestry, GIS/GPS technology, urban forestry, wildlife habitat, fisheries, and watershed ecology. Participants aged 16 or older may earn two college credits from Allegany College of Maryland. Forestry Boards recruit two students from their counties and provide partial scholarships to offset costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students interested in natural resources careers, particularly those aged 16 or older who wish to earn college credit.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants receive training and instruction in natural resources topics; students 16+ may earn two college credits from Allegany College of Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Forestry Boards from each Maryland county are responsible for recruiting two students from their counties.
requirements_list: Must be a high school student
Must have reached age 16 by the first day of camp to earn college credits
Attend the entire week to earn college credits and complete required exam
County Forestry Board nomination and interview required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through local Forestry Boards. Forestry Boards are responsible for recruiting students from their counties, conducting interviews, and providing partial scholarships. Applicants should contact their county Forestry Board for application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to Maryland and Delaware commercial fishing captains and vessel operators for safety equipment and navigation training to enhance safety and navigation in and around the offshore wind energy area. Participants may choose from options including radar training, navigation equipment upgrades, or other navigation enhancements for their vessels. The program determined eligible equipment and vendors based on preferences of coastal fishing industries and calculated the eligible number of vessels and individuals. Program is specific to Maryland and Delaware.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The NETP provides $1.04 million in funding for navigation and safety enhancements. Eligible Maryland and Delaware ocean-going commercial fishing captains and vessel operators may choose equipment upgrades and training vendors based on fishing industry preferences. Participants may choose radar training, navigation equipment upgrades, or other navigation enhancements to improve safety in the offshore wind project area. Eligible equipment and vendors were determined based on preferences of coastal fishing industries, with the eligible number of vessels and individuals calculated during program development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland and Delaware ocean-going commercial fishing captains and vessel operators operating in and around the offshore wind energy area, seeking to enhance navigation and safety equipment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Navigation and safety equipment upgrades and training, including radar equipment, navigation system upgrades, and captain/operator training to enhance safety and navigation in and around the offshore wind energy area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland and Delaware. Open to ocean-going commercial fishing vessels and operators engaged in commercial fishing operations in or around the offshore wind energy area.
requirements_list: Must be an ocean-going commercial fishing captain or operator
Must operate in Maryland or Delaware waters
Must be eligible under the determined number of vessels and individuals criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible participants may choose preferred navigation equipment upgrades and training vendors from available options. Eligibility is based on the number of eligible vessels and individuals as determined during program development. Details available through the Regional Fund Administrator process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant and technical assistance program that helps communities understand and enhance their capacity to plan for impacts from coastal and precipitation-based flood events. The program supports planning projects that assess flood hazards, vulnerabilities, and adaptation strategies to reduce flood risk at the community, county, or municipal level. Projects may result in risk assessments, adaptation strategies, conceptual designs, and engineered solutions for flood mitigation, as well as higher regulatory standards that enable implementation of adaptation projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants can receive direct financial support through a grant award or technical assistance through a DNR-selected contractor. Proposal requests typically range from $40,000 to $100,000 for projects with a maximum duration of one year. The maximum individual grant request is $125,000. Funding becomes available October 1, 2026. Grant awards provide direct financial support to implement flood resilience planning projects within Maryland's Coastal Zone.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, non-governmental organizations, and institutions of higher education seeking to develop flood resilience plans, strategies, and climate adaptation planning within Maryland's Coastal Zone.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports planning projects including risk assessments, vulnerability evaluations, flood hazard mapping, stormwater infrastructure analysis, green infrastructure planning, ordinance updates, adoption of planning processes, and development of conceptual designs or engineered solutions for flood adaptation. Projects must support understanding of flood impacts and vulnerabilities, identify and incorporate adaptation strategies into planning processes, and result in risk-reduction strategies and higher regulatory standards that enable implementation of adaptation projects. Funds may also support engagement with environmental justice communities and historically underserved, overburdened, and BIPOC populations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Maryland's Coastal Zone, which encompasses Maryland's 16 coastal counties and Baltimore City. The project area can encompass both public and private lands within the coastal zone.
requirements_list: Projects must be located within Maryland's Coastal Zone
Projects must address flood impacts at community, county, or municipal level resulting from high tide flooding, changing sea levels, and/or increased precipitation events
Final products must serve as the foundation for implementable projects
Projects addressing tidal flooding must reference the jurisdiction's nuisance flood plan, flood mitigation plan, or other planning processes
Projects addressing sea level rise should use Guidance for Using Maryland's 2018 Sea Level Rise Projections to determine flood risk tolerance
Projects addressing precipitation-induced flooding should be consistent with the Northeast chapter of the Fourth National Climate Assessment
Applicants must demonstrate commitment to achieving program change in local programs, policies, or decisions that reduce vulnerability to flood impacts
Proposals must describe community and stakeholder engagement including environmental justice and needs of historically underserved, overburdened, and BIPOC communities
For sea level rise projects, applicants must complete Appendix A from Maryland's 2023 Sea Level Rise Projections Guidance
Project duration must not exceed one year
Partners must be identified with demonstrated commitment to participate
Transmittal letter on official letterhead signed by authorized executive required
Letters of support from county or town council, town administrator, county executive, or appropriate decision-making body required
Photographs of impacted areas required
Complete budget table required
Communication and engagement strategy required
Must align with Maryland's Coastal Zone Management goals and climate resilience objectives
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit proposals through the Grants Gateway portal (webportalapp.com/sp/login/grants_gateway). Proposals must include a transmittal letter on official letterhead signed by an authorized executive, letters of support from relevant decision-making bodies, photographs of impacted areas, a complete budget table, required appendices (including Appendix A for sea level rise projects), and a communication and engagement strategy. Proposals are reviewed for completeness, description of local need, technical and financial feasibility, use of climate resources and tools, alignment with flood risk reduction efforts, community engagement approach, identified partners with demonstrated commitment, and readiness to proceed. Award decisions typically result in either direct financial support through a grant or technical assistance through a DNR-selected contractor. Funding becomes available October 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Outdoor Recreation Legacy Partnership Program (ORLP) provides matching grants for park projects in underserved communities. The program is subject to Land and Water Conservation Fund rules and has additional eligibility requirements: projects must be located in communities with populations of 25,000 or more (per the 2020 Census) that are determined to be underserved based on environmental justice screening tools such as CEJST or EJScreen. Grants are competitive at the federal level, with the National Park Service selecting applicants through a multi-stage process.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants for park projects in underserved communities. Grants are competitive at the federal level. The National Park Service selects applicants based on a pre-application, then requires a final application to be submitted within a year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Spring Round: April 15 for pre-applications to DNR, June 1 for full applications to NPS, September 1 for notification. Fall Round: September 15 for pre-applications to DNR, November 1 for full applications to NPS, February 1 for notification.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities with populations of 25,000 or more in the 2020 Census that are determined to be underserved, seeking to develop park projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Park projects in underserved communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Communities with a population of 25,000 or more in the 2020 Census determined to be underserved using CEJST, EJScreen, or other written documentation.
requirements_list: Located in a community with a population of 25,000 or more in the 2020 Census
Located within a community determined to be underserved using CEJST, EJScreen, or other written documentation
Project must comply with Land and Water Conservation Fund rules and regulations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Spring Round: Submit pre-applications by April 15 to DNR for eligibility and completeness review. If selected, submit full applications to NPS by June 1. Successful applicants are notified September 1. For Fall Round: Submit pre-applications by September 15 to DNR for eligibility and completeness review. If selected, submit full applications to NPS by November 1. Successful applicants are notified February 1. Contact Molly Pickel to discuss potential projects.

structured_extraction.program_name: PLANT Award Program (People Loving and Nurturing Trees)
structured_extraction.program_description: The PLANT Award (People Loving and Nurturing Trees) is a recognition program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that honors Maryland communities that plant, care for, and promote trees. The program supports communities of all sizes—including schools, homeowner associations, parks, local governments, government facilities, scout groups, and faith-based organizations—in building urban and community forestry programs, from single planting events to sustained, structured programs with ongoing stewardship. Communities that have hosted plantings, organized tree care activities, or taken steps to improve their local tree canopy are eligible to apply.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The PLANT Award provides recognition at four levels based on a community's tree-related activities: Bronze for single events or one-time efforts like tree plantings or Arbor Day activities; Silver for communities beginning to organize such as forming a tree committee or starting an inventory; Gold for communities actively managing trees through policies, planning, or coordinated programs; and Green for established programs with sustained effort, dedicated expertise, and ongoing support. Communities recognized through Tree City USA or Tree Campus USA automatically qualify at the Green level.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland communities of all types, including schools, homeowner associations, parks, local governments, government facilities, scout groups, and faith-based organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This is a recognition program rather than a funding program. It recognizes communities that have planted trees, organized tree care activities, or improved their local tree canopy. Awards are given at four levels (Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Green) based on the scope and sustainability of the community's tree-related efforts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Community must have hosted a tree planting, organized around tree care, or taken steps to improve local tree canopy within the past year
Application must match one of the four award levels (Bronze, Silver, Gold, or Green)
Communities recognized through Tree City USA or Tree Campus USA automatically qualify at the Green level

The partnership works to restore and protect the Potomac River watershed through shared watershed knowledge, riparian and wetland restoration, riparian forest buffer establishment, land protection and stewardship, wildfire risk reduction, livable community creation, urban forest canopy development, and partnership expansion.

structured_extraction.program_description: Program Open Space (POS) Local, established in 1969, provides financial and technical assistance to local subdivisions (counties and municipalities) for the planning, acquisition, and/or development of public recreation land or open space areas. The program helps communities create and improve parks and recreational facilities consistent with local Land Preservation, Parks and Recreation Plans (LPPRP). Funding comes from a 0.5% state property transfer tax and federal Land and Water Conservation Fund grants. Over 6,700 projects have been funded through POS Local to date. The broader Program Open Space also includes a Stateside component that acquires fee simple land and conservation easements for state parks, forests, and wildlife and fisheries management areas, and funds capital improvements, critical maintenance, and operations in state parks.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funds are allocated annually to the 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City based on a formula. The program is reimbursable, meaning grant recipients must pay costs upfront before reimbursement. Partial project reimbursements are permitted to help with cash flow. Development projects require a 10% or 25% local match based on the county's Land Preservation, Parks and Recreation Plan results. Acquisition and planning projects do not require a local match. Advance payments may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Technical assistance is also provided to local jurisdictions for planning, acquisition, and development activities. Individual projects are determined by the local jurisdiction, must be included in the county's Annual Program for that fiscal year, and must be approved by the Maryland Board of Public Works. POS funds may be used to reimburse local governments up to 100% of costs for acquisition projects. Counties that have not met the land acquisition goals of either their Local Land Preservation and Recreation Plan or the State's Land Preservation and Recreation Plan must use at least 50% of their total POS annual allocation exclusively for acquisition projects. Those that have met their goals may request certification to use up to 75% of their allocation received prior to FY2003 and 100% of their allocations subsequent to their receiving certification for acquisition or development projects. A local governing body may use up to $25,000 annually from its acquisition funds to fund planning projects that update the Local Land Preservation and Recreation Plans.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual Program submission no later than the first day of July each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal governing bodies in Maryland (all 23 counties and Baltimore City) seeking to plan, acquire, or develop public recreation land or open space areas. Homeowners associations and nonprofit organizations cannot directly apply but may partner with counties or municipalities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used for planning, acquisition, and/or development of public recreation land or open space areas. Planning grants fund completion of the county's Land Preservation, Parks and Recreation Plan (LPPRP). Acquisition projects acquire land for public recreation or open space. Development projects create or improve recreational facilities. Funds cannot be used for operating and maintenance costs, contingency costs, or reserves. Project planning costs are allowable project costs. The broader POS program also funds capital improvements, critical maintenance, and operations in state parks, forests, and wildlife management areas, as well as acquisition of fee simple land and conservation easements. Acknowledgment sign costs are allowable costs for assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Funds are allocated annually to all 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City based on a formula. Projects must be open and available to all users and not restricted to specific interest groups or homeowners associations. POS Stateside projects are driven by a Targeting System using scientific information to prioritize funds statewide.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local jurisdictions select and authorize projects to be included in their POS Local Annual Program. The proposed project must be included in the county's Annual Program for that fiscal year and submitted to DNR and Maryland Department of Planning no later than July 1st each year. Local governing bodies may choose to submit individual applications along with the traditional Annual Program, or submit all proposed projects as components of a Consolidated Annual Program and Grant Application to expedite review. For individual applications, applicants must prepare and assemble required elements including city/county road map, acquisition line map, local or regional planning agency approval and infrastructure review, project photographs, two independent appraisal reports (for acquisitions), copy of deed, retention of rights explanation (if applicable), and funding authorization signed by County Liaison Officer. The Consolidated Annual Program and Grant Application provides an overview of the local jurisdiction's proposed use of its annual POS allocation and how projects will fulfill the goals of the local plan. Once submitted, the project application is reviewed by the Local Grants Administrator for completeness and consistency with program requirements. The application is then submitted to the State Clearinghouse and other DNR units for review. After reviews are complete, the project is scheduled on the next available Board of Public Works (BPW) agenda. Projects must be approved by the BPW before funds may be encumbered. This process takes approximately 2-3 months but may take longer if issues need resolution. After Board of Public Works approval and fund encumbrance, DNR will sign the Application and Project Agreement thus agreeing to reimburse the applicant upon submission of proof of expenditure. Costs are reimbursable, and partial reimbursements are permitted. Each State POS Regional Administrator and/or Assistant Regional Administrator is required to inspect each project site and prepare and sign inspection reports (1) prior to approval of each project by the Board of Public Works and (2) prior to final reimbursement on each project. Applications are submitted using provided forms including Acquisition Application and Project Agreement, Development and Capital Renewal Application and Project Agreement, or Planning Grant Application. Applicants are required to contact their POS Program Administrator for an inspection of the project site and review of the application and program agreement with required attachments.

structured_extraction.program_description: Program Open Space Stateside preserves natural areas for public recreation and watershed and wildlife protection across Maryland through the acquisition of fee simple land and conservation easements. Established in 1969, it represents Maryland's long-term commitment to conserving natural resources while providing exceptional outdoor recreation opportunities for all citizens. Fee simple purchases are managed by the Department of Natural Resources primarily as State Parks, Forests, and Wildlife and Fisheries Management Areas. The program also acquires permanent Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP) easements to support climate change mitigation and resilience efforts.
