structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial and technical assistance for living shoreline and other nature-based restoration projects designed to protect communities from erosion, flooding, and storm impacts. The program supports implementation of projects that provide community-wide benefits to community infrastructure or assets, address climate change impacts, and help protect local governments and communities from coastal hazards. Funding is available for different project phases and is administered through the Grants Gateway.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for design, permitting, construction, and adaptive management of shoreline restoration or stormwater projects addressing flooding and erosion. Permitting fees are not eligible. Funding is available for different project phases and is administered through the Grants Gateway. Projects must provide community-wide coastal protection benefits to community infrastructure or assets, be nature-based, and consider climate change data. Community public property is prioritized; funding on private residential properties may be difficult to obtain.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design, permitting, construction, and adaptive management of shoreline restoration and stormwater projects that address flooding or erosion and provide community-wide coastal protection benefits. Permitting fees are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Maryland and provide community-wide coastal protection benefits. Public, private, and community properties in Maryland are eligible. Community public property is prioritized, and funding on private residential properties can be difficult to obtain.

structured_extraction.program_description: An initiative designed to help Maryland's lower Eastern Shore adapt to climate change by enhancing nature's ability to store carbon and buffer climate impacts through tree planting, coastal habitat restoration, living shorelines for marsh protection, wetland restoration, tidal reconnection, sustainable forest management, and community engagement. The initiative strengthens natural defenses while reducing carbon emissions. The program also seeks construction, design/build, and design proposals for living shoreline projects that protect communities from erosion, flooding, and storm impacts while maintaining natural coastal processes and habitat. DNR collaborates with nonprofit partners and leverages conservation easements to restore and protect critical habitats. Funded through a Climate Pollution Reduction Grant (CPRG) from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) awarded to the Atlantic Conservation Coalition.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding through Request for Proposal (RFP) solicitation for living shoreline projects. Total funding available: approximately $17 million to be disbursed by July 2029. Minimum grant request: $1,000,000 for design, permitting, and construction expenses (lower amounts allowed for design-only applications with DNR approval). Funding covers design, permitting, and construction costs including: costs directly related to implementation of living shoreline projects; engineering and technical services; permit application fees and related documentation; community engagement and coordination; contractor or consultant services; native plants and vegetation; staff time; and indirect costs per federally negotiated rates. Match funding is not required but projects demonstrating leveraged funding are reviewed favorably. Projects are prioritized into three tiers: 1) First Priority—permit-authorized or permit-ready construction projects (shovel-ready); 2) Second Priority—Design/build applications; 3) Third Priority—Design-only and permitting funding. Projects on public lands are prioritized. Competitive proposals should aim to stay under $1,000 per linear foot, with each 100 feet of living shoreline protecting a minimum of 2.3 acres of marsh. Invoicing occurs monthly on a reimbursable basis unless otherwise authorized.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, nonprofit organizations, institutions of higher education, private landowners, contractors, designers, and communities on the lower Eastern Shore seeking to implement nature-based climate resilience and habitat restoration projects, including organizations and individuals seeking to design and construct living shoreline projects that protect tidal marsh habitat.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting and wetland vegetation restoration to absorb carbon and reduce flooding; restoring tidal marsh habitats; implementing living shorelines to protect existing marshes and prevent conversion to open water; promoting improved forestry practices; building regional resilience through adaptation strategies; community outreach and engagement; design, engineering, and construction of living shoreline projects that restore and protect tidal marsh habitat; monitoring and long-term maintenance planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Living shoreline (marsh protection) projects are eligible in Dorchester, Somerset, and Wicomico counties within the Chesapeake Bay portions only. Enhanced forestry management and afforestation projects are eligible in Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot, Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. Coastal resilience management plans are eligible in Dorchester, Somerset, Wicomico, and Worcester counties. Projects proposed on public lands are highly encouraged and preferred, though projects on private property are also considered.
requirements_list: Projects must focus on nature-based solutions for climate resilience and adaptation
Projects must support ecosystem reconnection and deliver multiple conservation benefits
Projects must be located in eligible lower Eastern Shore counties
Living shoreline projects must be located in Dorchester, Somerset, or Wicomico counties (Chesapeake Bay portions)
Forestry and afforestation projects must be in Caroline, Dorchester, Talbot, Somerset, Wicomico, or Worcester counties
Coastal resilience plans must be in Dorchester, Somerset, Wicomico, or Worcester counties

Projects must be for voluntary restoration; funds cannot be used to bank water quality credits or meet compensatory mitigation requirements

Applicants must answer required narrative questions as specified in the application

For projects with contractors over $10,000, applicants must obtain at least three cost estimates or use a publicly advertised competitive bid process; over $250,000 requires competitive procurement
Current designs must be provided with landowner signature on plans indicating project endorsement
Applicants must have and maintain liability insurance coverage during project term

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Identify potential shoreline sites with active erosion that protect extensive marsh habitat using the Living Shoreline Targeting Map. 2) Confirm site eligibility, marsh protection potential, erosion rates, and climate vulnerability using the map tool. 3) Confirm landowner support and long-term site access. 4) Determine project readiness (construction-ready, design/build, or design-only). 5) Contact DNR early to discuss project ideas and schedule a site visit with Ari Engelberg. 6) Complete and submit the Living Shoreline Grant Application through the online Google Form by 11:59 PM ET on April 6, 2026. Applications must include: transmittal letter on official letterhead; project abstract (5 sentences maximum); description of project need, context, climate considerations, and benefits; partner roles and outreach plans; key milestones and timeline; sustainability plan; success metrics; signed letters of support and commitment from partners and landowners; budget using provided template; current designs with landowner signatures; permits or schedule for obtaining permits; site details including coordinates and acreage; photos of current conditions; site-specific outputs from the Targeting Map; landowner agreements (if applicable); and any additional supporting documentation. Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact DNR before applying to discuss project ideas and arrange site visits. An Information Session will be held on January 14, 2026, and a Mapping Tutorial on February 3, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Schoolyard Forests Program helps schools create outdoor spaces that support student well-being, enrich learning, and strengthen connections to the natural world. A Five Million Trees partnership initiative with the Maryland Association of Environmental & Outdoor Education, the program is offered to public schools across the state to promote healthier campus landscapes where students of all backgrounds can have access to the benefits of nature. The program provides guidance, tools, and support to transform school grounds into healthier, more inviting environments that enhance learning and help communities adapt to a changing climate. It offers campus planning and technical support, hands-on training, educational opportunities, and microgrants to schools across Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools may receive campus planning and technical support to identify opportunities for improving outdoor spaces and caring for existing trees. The program provides hands-on assistance and training for facilities teams, teachers, and staff. Services available include teacher workshops, landscape stewardship manuals, specimen tree inventory and mapping, arbor day and earth day activities, forest health assessments, professional development and continuing education, hazard tree evaluation and removal, native tree planting, edible food plots, and summer tree maintenance. Schools can access educational and student-centered opportunities that integrate outdoor learning into the school day, engagement and celebration events, youth career exploration demonstrations, and microgrants and classroom support materials for schools advancing toward Green School certification or developing outdoor projects. All services are provided for free.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland public schools of all types and sizes, with priority given to schools and communities with the greatest need. District-level facility teams and community partners working directly with school campuses are also welcome. Privately funded schools may participate, though program resources are primarily directed toward public schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Schools may use support to strengthen outdoor learning, enhance existing green spaces, address campus heat and comfort, care for existing trees, introduce native plantings, improve outdoor spaces through tree planting, increase tree canopy cover, create pathways for the discovery of nature, support local climate resiliency priorities, and advance toward Maryland Green School certification.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides 0% interest revolving loans and technical assistance to waterfront property owners, non-profit organizations, community organizations, counties, and municipalities experiencing shoreline erosion. The program funds living shoreline projects that protect property from erosion while maintaining natural coastal processes and habitat along the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries. Formerly known as Shore Erosion Control, the program also offers technical support through site visit evaluations and problem assessments for shoreline stabilization and streambank restoration.

An administrative fee ranging from 3% to 10% is applied based on project construction cost. An upfront cash contribution is required for individuals and groups of homeowners for loans greater than $60,000. Funds are dispersed for portions of completed work, with the loan applicant providing proof of payment to the department. A county-sponsored shore erosion control tax district or shore erosion control lien must be established, with the department providing assistance in this process. Technical assistance is also provided through site visit evaluations and problem assessments.

A county-sponsored shore erosion control tax district (for community projects) or a shore erosion control lien (for private property projects) must be established
Applicant must provide proof of payment to the department for fund dispersal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the MD DNR Grants Gateway at http://mddnr.info/grantsgateway. Interested applicants can also fill out a technical assistance request form on the program website to indicate interest and receive a site visit evaluation and problem assessment. The department will assist with establishing required tax districts or liens.

structured_extraction.program_name: Solar Generation Facilities - Pollinator-Friendly Designation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A certification program that recognizes commercial ground-mounted solar facilities that have been designed and managed to support pollinator habitats. Solar developers can apply for a pollinator-friendly designation by submitting an application, developing a pollinator habitat management plan, using appropriate native seed mixes, undergoing site inspections, and demonstrating compliance with habitat management standards. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) and the certification is valid for two years, with renewal available.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides certification recognition for solar facilities that meet pollinator-friendly standards. Facilities undergo a review process that includes submission of a pollinator habitat management plan, site inspection by a DNR-approved site inspector, and submission of a final Solar Site Pollinator Habitat Planning and Assessment Scorecard. Upon approval, the facility receives a pollinator-friendly designation valid for two years. Renewal can be requested within 90 days of certification expiration. The program does not provide direct financial assistance but offers technical guidance and regulatory recognition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial solar facility developers and owners who own or operate ground-mounted solar generation facilities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide direct funding. It certifies facilities based on pollinator habitat management practices. Applicants must implement pollinator habitat management plans using appropriate native seed mixes appropriate for the Maryland region and maintain these habitats according to DNR standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide for any commercial ground-mounted solar facility in Maryland.
requirements_list: Submit an application with facility name, location, tax map information, acreage, and contact details
Include a pollinator habitat management plan with the application
Use a seed mix appropriate for the Maryland region
Undergo a site inspection by a DNR-approved site inspector
Submit a final Solar Site Pollinator Habitat Planning and Assessment Scorecard within 30 days of site inspection completion
Submit a final pollinator habitat management plan and letter from site inspector confirming site has been planted and managed according to the habitat plan
Site must be planted and managed prior to certification
Submit any additional information requested by the Department within 30 days of the Department's request
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit an application to the Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) at pprp@maryland.gov with your intent to apply, including facility name, location, tax map information, acreage, contact details, and a pollinator habitat management plan. 2. Coordinate with a DNR-approved site inspector to review the plan and conduct a site inspection. 3. Plant and manage the pollinator habitat according to the approved plan prior to certification. 4. Within 30 days of site inspection completion, submit the final Solar Site Pollinator Habitat Planning and Assessment Scorecard, the final habitat management plan, and the site inspector's letter confirming the site has been planted and managed according to the habitat plan. 5. DNR reviews the submission and approves certification if standards are met. Certification is valid for two years and renewal can be requested within 90 days of expiration.

structured_extraction.program_name: Special Rivers Chesapeake Bay Implementation Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A watershed-based forestry initiative funded by the US Environmental Protection Agency since 1983 to improve water quality for the Chesapeake Bay by encouraging restoration, enhancement, and management of forests. The program helps implement goals related to riparian forest buffer restoration, watershed planning, stream corridor restoration, land conservation and stewardship, and community engagement across priority Chesapeake Bay watersheds in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance and funding for riparian forest buffer restoration (minimum 30 miles per year), forest stewardship planning for private and public forests (minimum 1,800 acres per year), and education and outreach on forest benefits for watersheds and water quality (reaching at least 600 people per year including students, general public, and resource professionals).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private and public forest landowners, watershed planners, educators, community organizations, students, general public, and resource professionals in Chesapeake Bay priority watersheds
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Riparian forest buffer restoration and monitoring, forest stewardship planning, education and outreach programs, forest harvest best management practices training and evaluation, invasive species control, and watershed-level planning
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Four project areas: Susquehanna area watersheds (2,125 square miles from Elk River in Cecil County to upper and middle Patuxent in Howard and Montgomery Counties, including Baltimore, Carroll, and Harford Counties); Monocacy area (1,300 square miles in Upper and Lower Monocacy, Double Pipe, Catoctin, Antietam, Conococheague, Licking Creek drainages); Anacostia/West Chesapeake (portions of Prince George's, Montgomery, and Anne Arundel Counties); Town Creek (Allegany County, Maryland and Bedford County, Pennsylvania)

structured_extraction.program_name: Strategic Framing for Climate Change Communication
structured_extraction.program_description: A two-day in-person training program where participants learn about strategic framing as a communication approach to engage audiences in thinking productively about creating or supporting climate change solutions. The program covers strategic framing, values, and solutions-focused messaging to increase participants' ability to clearly and confidently communicate climate change issues. Training is delivered by National Network for Ocean and Climate Change Interpretation (NNOCCI) facilitators from the Maryland Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A two-day in-person training opportunity with instruction provided by National Network for Ocean and Climate Change Interpretation (NNOCCI) facilitators from the Maryland Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve, covering strategic framing, values communication, and solutions-oriented messaging to help participants clearly and confidently communicate climate change issues.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Teachers, community leaders, decision-makers, and individuals and organizations seeking training in climate change communication strategies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Learning strategic framing and communication techniques for climate change messaging, including values-based and solutions-focused approaches
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Climate Resilience office or the Maryland Chesapeake Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve for training availability, registration, and schedule details.

structured_extraction.program_description: An aquatic resources education program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that provides classroom teachers, environmental education centers, and nature centers with hatchery-raised bluegill sunfish, aquarium supplies, teaching materials, and funding support to conduct hands-on fish care and ecology lessons with students from October through May, culminating in a supervised fish release event at an approved site.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources provides aquarium supplies for starter and replacement kits (subject to annual budget and availability on a first-come-first-serve basis), hatchery-raised bluegill sunfish and fish food, a teacher's manual and data sheet, lesson plans and background information, and reimbursement for fish release trip costs including 50 percent of total bus costs (up to 3 buses maximum) and 100 percent of substitute teacher costs (up to 3 substitutes maximum). Participants also receive comprehensive support through the online Fish in the Classroom Aquatic Studies Reporting Form for documenting educational outcomes and classroom fish care activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Classroom teachers, environmental education centers, and nature centers seeking to conduct aquatic resources education with students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Aquarium supplies for classroom fish tanks, hatchery-raised bluegill sunfish and fish food, educational materials including teacher manuals and lesson plans, and reimbursement for transportation (50% of bus costs up to 3 buses) and substitute teacher costs (100% up to 3 substitutes) related to fish release trip events.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Fish pickups are available at multiple locations including Patapsco Valley State Park in Halethorpe (Baltimore County), Gambrill State Park in Frederick (Frederick County), William S. Schmidt Outdoor Education Center in Prince George's County, and Cedarville Fish Hatchery in Brandywine (Prince George's County).
requirements_list: Must be a classroom teacher, environmental education center, or nature center
New participants must attend the mandatory teacher training workshop in September
Returning participants must attend the training workshop every 3 years
Must register annually by May 15th
Must pick up fish and supplies during one of the two designated October pickup days
Must conduct lessons and fish care from October through May
Must release fish at an approved site by June 30th
Must submit reimbursement packages by June 30th with invoices, proof of purchase, and W-9 forms if applicable
Must complete the online ARE reporting form (Fish in the Classroom Aquatic Studies Reporting Form) by July 31st
Must document fish care and maintenance activities using provided recording sheets
Must use equipment responsibly and sign Equipment Responsibilities agreement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online by May 15th using the registration form at the Google Form link provided. New participants and those requiring refresher training must attend the mandatory teacher training workshop (e.g., September 12, 2026 for the 2026–2027 cycle). Pick up bluegill sunfish and aquarium supplies on one of two designated dates in early or mid-October. Conduct lessons and raise fish in the classroom from October through May, documenting fish care using the Bluegill Care Maintenance Record. Organize and conduct a supervised fish release event at an approved site by June 30th. Submit reimbursement documentation (invoices, proof of purchase, and W-9 forms if applicable) by June 30th following the ARE Vendor Invoice Template guidelines. Complete the online Fish in the Classroom Aquatic Studies Reporting Form (ARE reporting) by July 31st to document educational outcomes and student learning.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources offers free fishing gear for loan at various locations throughout the state. This no-cost program is designed to help new anglers and their families build confidence and skills while enjoying Maryland's great outdoors by providing access to fishing equipment at public libraries, state parks, nature centers, and local parks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free loan of fishing gear including rod and reel setup with bobber, split shot sinker, swivel, and hook. Available for individual or group loans depending on site. Policies vary by location regarding number of rods per person, on-site or off-site usage, and loan duration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, families, and groups interested in recreational fishing, including new anglers and anyone wanting to try fishing while camping, hiking, or spending time in parks.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Borrowing fishing equipment for recreational fishing purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at multiple locations throughout Maryland including state parks, public libraries, nature centers, and local parks. Specific locations listed include sites in Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Baltimore County, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Washington, and Worcester counties.
requirements_list: Complete a borrower form
Contact site directly to confirm procedures and availability
Return equipment on agreed return date
Individuals under 16 do not need a fishing license but those 16 and older may need one depending on activity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Find a nearby loaner site from the list of available locations. 2. Complete the Borrower Form online. 3. Contact the chosen site directly to confirm procedures, availability, and policies. 4. Visit the site to check out the fishing gear. 5. Return the equipment on the agreed return date.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tree Planting on Agricultural Lands Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A Keep Maryland Beautiful grant to support tree planting on agricultural lands for environmental and community benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for tree planting on agricultural lands
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural land owners and non-profits
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting on agricultural lands
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: An educational program administered by the Maryland Department of Natural Resources that provides schools with hatchery-raised rainbow trout eggs, fish food, starter kits, and chillers so students can raise trout in classroom aquariums, learn about fish biology and aquatic ecosystems, and participate in fish release events at approved sites. The program offers financial aid as budget allows to classroom teachers, environmental education centers, and nature centers serving grades 3-12, and includes reimbursement for fish release trip costs such as bus transportation and substitute teacher expenses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources provides financial aid for schools participating in the program as the budget allows. New schools receive one starter kit (approximately $700) and one chiller. Returning schools receive one replacement kit (approximately $220). The program also provides hatchery-raised rainbow trout eggs and fish food. Reimbursement for fish release trip costs includes 50 percent of the total cost of buses (maximum of 3 buses) and 100 percent of the total cost for substitutes (maximum of 3 substitutes).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Registration opens January 1st each year. Submit reimbursement packages by June 30th with invoices, proof of purchase, and W-9 forms. Complete and submit the reporting form online by July 31st.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that provides financial, technical, and related assistance to rural volunteer fire departments to enhance wildland fire suppression capabilities, improve firefighter safety, and support wildland fire training. Grants are awarded on a 50/50 cost-share basis with a maximum federal reimbursement of $3,500 per department per year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funds reimburse up to 50 percent of eligible costs after approval and certification of receipt and payment by the fire department. Maximum federal reimbursement is $3,500 per department per year on a 50/50 matching basis. Grants are awarded competitively based on a points system that prioritizes wildland firefighting equipment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural volunteer fire departments serving areas or communities with a population of 10,000 or less. Area fire departments (fire districts, first due areas, etc.) with an aggregate service population greater than 10,000 may be eligible if they serve at least one rural area or community with 10,000 or fewer residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wildland firefighting personal protective equipment (flame-resistant clothing, hard hats, eye protection, leather gloves, hearing protection, chainsaw chaps, fire shelters), power tools (chainsaws, leaf blowers), wildland firefighting equipment (fire hose under 2.5 inches in diameter, nozzles, adapters, bladder bags, wildland gear, chainsaw supplies), wildland fire engine and UTV pumping units (tanks, pumps, hose reels, slip-on units), rehabilitation of wildland firefighting equipment from federal excess programs, fire communications equipment (pagers, portable and mobile radios), off-road ATVs and UTVs, equipment for ATVs and UTVs supporting wildland fire fighting, and wildland firefighting training including National Wildfire Coordinating Group (NWCG) tuition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; available to rural volunteer fire departments throughout Maryland serving rural areas or communities with populations of 10,000 or less based on latest Census data. Area fire departments may serve aggregate populations greater than 10,000 if their service area includes a rural community with population of 10,000 or less.

Applicant must be a volunteer fire department
Area fire departments may be eligible if service area includes a rural community with 10,000 or fewer residents
Equipment must have application to wildland firefighting; equipment solely for structural firefighting, hazardous material response, rescue, or emergency medical services is ineligible
Grants cannot be used for medical, rescue, or HAZMAT equipment, capital construction projects, or vehicle purchases

No capital improvements such as land, building purchases, or construction
Purchases must occur between January 1, 2025 and December 31, 2025 for the 2025 grant cycle
50/50 cost-share match required from the fire department

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides technical planning and design assistance, watershed planning, and programmatic development for protection and restoration projects that improve water quality in the Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, the Maryland portion of the Youghiogheny watershed, and the Maryland Coastal Bays. Planning projects include watershed characterization, surveys, assessments, action plans, and financing plans. Design assistance is available for non-point source best management practices, including living shoreline projects. The program also supports comprehensive watershed protection and restoration activities through two-year milestone support grants. Managed in partnership with the Chesapeake Bay Trust.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants support design assistance, watershed planning, and programmatic development for protection and restoration projects. Eligible activities include watershed characterization, surveys, assessments, action plans, financing plans, best management practice designs, and living shoreline projects, all aimed at improving water quality. The Collaborative provides planning and design grants which are needed before large scale restoration can begin. Over $8.1 million has been awarded to date for 168 planning and design projects throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, non-profit organizations, and local communities undertaking comprehensive watershed protection and restoration activities in the Chesapeake Bay watershed, Youghiogheny watershed, and Maryland Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design assistance, watershed planning, and programmatic development for protection and restoration projects, including watershed characterization, surveys, assessments, action plans, financing plans, non-point source best management practice designs, and living shoreline projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland portion of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, Maryland portion of the Youghiogheny watershed, and the Maryland Coastal Bays.

Applicants must be undertaking comprehensive watershed protection and restoration activities
Jurisdictions should have limited capacity to implement large-scale non-point source restoration and protection efforts on their own
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Communities and organizations interested in undertaking comprehensive watershed protection and restoration activities should fill out the Request for Resources & Services Form and contact Phillip Stafford or Carrie Decker for more information. Visit the Chesapeake Bay Trust website at cbtrust.org for grant information, additional grant details, and a list of preferred contractors. The Collaborative provides coordinated capacity building opportunities to local implementers through its partnership of state agencies, the Chesapeake Bay Trust, University of Maryland Sea Grant Extension Program, University of Maryland Environmental Finance Center, NOAA, and EPA.

structured_extraction.program_description: A five-year pilot program that provides collaborative, science-based funding and technical support to accelerate restoration of the Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic Coastal Bays and their watersheds. The program targets five selected watersheds and combines funding from multiple state agencies to award grants for implementation, operations, and monitoring. It supports a diverse selection of environmental actions including pollution reduction, habitat creation, aquatic resource improvements, equitable public access, carbon sequestration, and public health enhancements. The program also provides technical assistance to Project Sponsors, coordinated state permitting, and ongoing monitoring support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For FY 2026, the program provides Implementation and Operating Grants of up to 50 percent of project costs, with a total of two million dollars per watershed including twenty thousand dollars for operational expenses. Water Quality Monitoring Grants totaling 1.25 million dollars are available, distributed at 250,000 dollars per watershed. Agricultural support is available through existing Maryland Agricultural Cost Share Program and Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation. The State Management Team provides technical assistance including help developing Implementation and Financing Plans, coordinated state permitting, watershed monitoring support, and six annual coordination meetings. Grantees must provide 50 percent outside funding (not from Whole Watershed Fund sources), which may include planning, design, engineering, legal documents such as permits and easements, and maintenance, but not monitoring. Outside funding must be spent after July 1, 2025, with totals documented by end of the five-year program. Funds are distributed to the Project Sponsor quarterly based on reimbursement requests. The program operates over five years with potential for renewal. Established under Maryland Natural Resources Article § 8–2B–01 through 8–2B–03 (Senate Bill 969, Chapter 559).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The original RFP was due December 3, 2024. The next RFP will be released by October 1, 2029.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipal, county, and regional agencies; nonprofit organizations; faith-based groups; homeowners associations; and soil and water conservation districts managing designated watershed projects in Maryland. A single project sponsor must be identified per watershed to administer each project. The five selected watersheds are: Antietam Creek, Baltimore Harbor, Upper Choptank River, Newport Bay, and Severn River.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of environmental restoration and conservation actions including habitat restoration, pollution reduction, stormwater management, riparian forest buffers, wetland restoration, stream restoration, aquatic resource improvements, green infrastructure, shoreline stabilization, agricultural best management practices, septic system improvements, urban tree plantings, public access improvements, community outreach, workforce development, monitoring, and planning/design/engineering work. Outside funding can support planning, design, engineering, legal documents such as permits and easements, and maintenance needs, but not monitoring.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program operates in five selected watersheds during the five-year pilot period: Antietam Creek (Washington County, Maryland and Franklin County, Pennsylvania), Baltimore Harbor (Baltimore City), Upper Choptank River (Dorchester, Talbot, and Delaware), Newport Bay (Wicomico and Worcester Counties, coastal Maryland), and Severn River (Anne Arundel County, Maryland). One watershed must be urban, one suburban, two agricultural, one must adjoin another state, and two must have opportunities to engage overburdened or underserved communities.
requirements_list: Single Project Sponsor identified per watershed to administer projects and coordinate partnerships
Project Sponsor must hold at least four community meetings per year with local government representation
Opportunity for public comment on preliminary designs of each major or large-scale action required
Grantee must provide 50 percent outside funding toward implementation
Outside funding cannot come from any Whole Watershed Fund sources
Outside funding must be spent after July 1, 2025, with totals documented by end of five-year program
Outside funding can include planning, design, engineering, legal documents, and maintenance but not monitoring

Project applicants seeking authorization must provide notice and hold public meetings except under certain circumstances

Stream restoration contractors performing work must be licensed under Maryland Environment Article Title 18, Subtitle 3 or employed by a licensed stream restoration contractor, or be a government employee or property owner performing work on their own property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit proposals in response to a Request for Proposals (RFP). The State Management Team evaluates applications based on criteria including water quality improvement potential, cost-effectiveness, applicant experience, matching funds capability, support for sustainability, environmental justice impacts, innovation, and partnership opportunities. Approved Project Sponsors receive Implementation and Operating Grants and Water Quality Monitoring Grants. Funds are distributed quarterly based on reimbursement requests. The State Management Team meets with Project Sponsors and local government six times annually to review and facilitate project progress. The Department of Environment may authorize projects in accordance with specific requirements and must assess documentation and actions by project applicants prior to authorization. structured_extraction.program_name: Woodland Incentive Program (WIP) and Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP)
structured_extraction.program_description: These programs provide financial and technical assistance to private landowners, agricultural producers, and forest managers to help defray the cost of conservation and forest improvement practices. The Woodland Incentive Program (WIP) is a state program that pays up to 65% of eligible practice costs for tree planting, site preparation, and timber stand improvement on private forestland. The Environmental Quality Incentive Program (EQIP) is a federal program administered in partnership with USDA NRCS that provides cost-share payments (typically 50%, up to 90% for limited resource producers and beginning farmers) for implementing conservation practices including nutrient management, manure management, integrated pest management, irrigation water management, wildlife habitat enhancement, and forestry management on eligible agricultural and non-industrial private forestland. Maryland Forest Service staff act as technical service providers in partnership with USDA NRCS.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Woodland Incentive Program (WIP) pays up to 65% of eligible practice costs through reimbursement. Landowners complete approved practices, pay for goods and services, and submit invoices and checks to the local forester for processing; upon approval, landowners receive a reimbursement check for up to 65% of costs. Approximately $100,000 is distributed annually to 75-100 landowners for management practices on 1,500 to 2,000 acres. The Environmental Quality Incentive Program (EQIP) provides cost-share payments typically at 50% of costs for conservation practices. Limited resource producers and beginning farmers and ranchers may be eligible for cost-shares up to 90%. Sixty percent of EQIP funding is earmarked for livestock production practices including grazing. Both programs also provide technical assistance through Maryland Forest Service staff and NRCS.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private, non-industrial woodland owners, agricultural producers, landowners, and individuals or entities engaged in livestock, agricultural production, or forestry management.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: WIP: Tree planting, site preparation for natural or artificial reforestation, thinning, pruning, prescribed burning, crop tree release, herbicide treatments, and planting of seedlings. EQIP: Nutrient management, manure management, integrated pest management, irrigation water management, wildlife habitat enhancement, and forestry management practices on eligible agricultural and non-industrial private forestland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. WIP eligibility depends on property size and fund availability. EQIP eligible land includes cropland, rangeland, grassland, pasture, and private non-industrial forestland throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: For WIP: Landowner must own at least 5 forest acres but not more than 1,000 acres
For WIP: Forest land must have potential to be harvested for products including logs, timbers, pulpwood, firewood, woodchips, poles, piles, posts and other primary forest products
For WIP: Applicant must not have received Woodland Incentive Program assistance for the same practice in any of the 15 years preceding application
For WIP: Forest stewardship management plan must be written for the property
For WIP: Funds must be allocated prior to beginning any work
For EQIP: Participant must be an agricultural producer or entity engaged in livestock, agricultural production, or forestry management
For EQIP: Land must be eligible cropland, rangeland, grassland, pasture, or private non-industrial forestland
For EQIP: All practices must be implemented in conformance to NRCS standards and specifications
For EQIP: Limited resource producers and beginning farmers and ranchers may qualify for higher cost-share rates up to 90%
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For WIP: Contact your local department forester to discuss and apply for specific practices. If approved, landowner completes the practices and pays for goods and services. Local forester inspects the practice to ensure proper implementation. Upon approval, landowner submits copies of invoices and checks to the forester for processing and receives a reimbursement check for up to 65% of costs. For EQIP: Contact your local department forester or NRCS office. Work with the conservation district and NRCS to develop a conservation plan and submit an application for practices you wish to implement. The State Technical Committee and local work groups identify eligible conservation practices based on local resource concerns.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Corps/Service Year Option Program connects young adults and career-changers with Maryland organizations for a minimum 9-month workforce and community service opportunity. The program operates statewide and is administered by the Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation (DSCI). Organizations (nonprofits, for-profits, government agencies, private schools, and universities) host Members as W-2 employees working 30–40 hours per week earning at least $15 per hour (approximately $27,450 annually). The state reimburses host sites up to $20,000 per year per member for wages, with host sites covering the remaining cost-share of approximately $7,450 per year plus payroll taxes and benefits. Members receive professional development (approximately 10 hours per week reserved for DSCI-led activities), monthly in-person trainings, weekly virtual learning through the BuildWithin Learning Portal, coaching sessions with DSCI Member Success coaches, mentorship, networking, and the opportunity to earn a registered apprenticeship or trade credential. Upon successful completion, members earn a $6,000 completion grant award. The Service Year Option targets recent high school graduates (classes of 2021–2024), GED recipients, and high school completion certificate holders ages 18–24, while Maryland Corps also recruits seasoned individuals ages 18+ seeking career pivots or workforce re-entry. The program builds a lifelong alumni network of community leaders and strengthens Maryland's workforce.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Host Site Partner organizations receive a cost-reimbursement grant of up to $20,000 per year per full-time member to offset member salary and benefits costs. Host sites pay approved member costs upfront, then submit quarterly reimbursement requests for allowable costs. Host sites must cover the remaining cost-share of approximately $7,450 per year plus payroll taxes and benefits. A payroll provider option is available where the provider becomes employer of record and host sites pay bi-weekly. Cost-share waivers may be available through competitive review for organizations unable to meet required cost-sharing (priority consideration for waiver requests by June 1, 2026). Members earn at least $15 per hour (approximately $27,450 annually) for full-time service (30–40 hours per week) for a minimum 9-month placement, plus a $6,000 completion grant award upon successful program completion. Members also receive a biweekly living allowance, professional development training, monthly in-person trainings, weekly virtual learning via the BuildWithin Learning Portal, coaching, mentorship, networking, health coverage and childcare assistance (where eligible), and the opportunity to earn a registered apprenticeship or trade credential. Host sites must provide or facilitate access to basic health insurance (self-only coverage) for members.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 1 (Round 1 deadline: April 1); priority consideration for cost-share waivers by June 1, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based organizations (nonprofits, for-profits, government agencies, private schools, universities) seeking to hire and develop young adults ages 18–24 (Service Year Option) or adults 18+ (Maryland Corps) as full-time employees. Also open to individuals seeking paid service placements, including recent high school graduates (classes of 2021–2024), GED recipients, high school completion certificate holders, career changers, and workforce re-entrants. Individuals ages 17+ may be eligible for certain AmeriCorps-affiliated components.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Host Site Partners use grant funding to help cover member salary and fringe benefits including health insurance. Service placements address community needs in areas such as education, economic opportunity, and community capacity building.

Organization must commit to using DSCI's online Learning Management Platform to assign work and manage Member progress
Host sites must keep clear and accurate financial records
Host sites must submit quarterly reimbursement requests with documentation for allowable costs
Host sites must follow grant guidelines and reporting requirements
Host sites must comply with all terms outlined in grant agreement
Organizations may be required by DSCI to use the DSCI-sponsored payroll provider
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Individuals can apply as a Member, organizations can apply as a Host Site Partner, or individuals can be nominated for membership through DSCI's Application and Matching Portal (app.buildwithin.io) or at serve.maryland.gov. 2. Host Site Partners submit an application including position descriptions for which they want to hire Members. 3. Required webinar attendance after submitting application to reinforce program requirements and milestones. 4. Optional nomination of potential Members to serve at your organization (nominees must not be current employees or relatives). 5. DSCI reviews and accepts applications on a rolling basis and may request clarification. 6. After acceptance and position approval, Host Site Partners use DSCI's Application and Matching Portal to explore potential Members, interview candidates, and extend offers. 7. All Host Site Partners and Members attend required program orientation before service begins. 8. Program launches August/September with Members beginning minimum 9-month service placement. 9. Graduation ceremony held in June annually, with Members' service concluding in June or July depending on start date. Round 1 deadline: April 1; final deadline: May 1. For questions, email applytoserve@maryland.gov or contact Sarah Worley, Recruitment Specialist.

structured_extraction.program_description: A financial assistance program that provides support to AmeriCorps members in Maryland who are facing unexpected emergencies.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Service and Civic Innovation
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial support is available to AmeriCorps members facing unexpected emergencies to help them maintain their service commitment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: AmeriCorps members serving in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To address unexpected emergency financial needs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an AmeriCorps member serving in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Learn more and apply through the Ameraid website at www.ameraid.org/state/MD

structured_extraction.program_description: This program allocates funding on a competitive basis to support the deployment and demonstration of innovative technologies and practices in highway transportation projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive funding to support the deployment and demonstration of innovative technologies and practices in highway transportation projects. The goal is to improve safety, accelerate project delivery, enhance infrastructure performance, and promote sustainability. Eligible activities span all project phases, including planning, financing, design, construction, and operations, and focus on advancing proven innovations with broad application potential.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Highway transportation agencies and project sponsors
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deployment and demonstration of innovative technologies and practices in highway transportation projects across planning, financing, design, construction, and operations phases.
requirements_list: Innovation must be proven and have broad application potential
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted through Grants.gov by May 26, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program supporting the adoption of digital construction management and asset management systems for transportation infrastructure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants for developing and adopting digital construction management systems including 3D scanning, modeling, and integrated data management platforms.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State transportation departments supporting infrastructure modernization and asset management
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Digital platform development, 3D scanning equipment, staff training, data processing and storage, and knowledge transfer for transportation asset management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland state and local transportation agencies eligible.
requirements_list: Project must involve digital infrastructure management
Technology platform adoption required
Staff training and knowledge transfer needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit project applications including system specifications, training plans, and data management protocols to the Federal Highway Administration.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program providing grants for airport facilities and equipment improvements including solar installations, pavement reconstruction, and safety enhancements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants for airport infrastructure improvements including solar power generation, pavement reconstruction, lighting systems, taxiway improvements, and other capital projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Airport operators and authorities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Solar array implementation, pavement reconstruction, runway and taxiway improvements, lighting and navigation aids, terminal modifications, and sustainability initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland airport projects eligible.
requirements_list: Project must improve airport safety or capacity
Detailed engineering and design plans required
Environmental compliance documentation needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit project applications including detailed engineering plans, cost estimates, and environmental compliance documentation to the Federal Aviation Administration.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program funding the replacement and modernization of airport terminal facilities, equipment, and passenger movement systems under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal competitive grants supporting the design and construction of airport terminal improvements including baggage systems, passenger boarding bridges, elevators, escalators, moving walkways, and modernization of terminal infrastructure. Projects must address aging infrastructure, increase passenger capacity and access, improve accessibility for persons with disabilities, enhance energy efficiency, improve airfield safety, or encourage competition. Grant applications are evaluated through a competitive process with consideration given to projects that achieve compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, benefit historically disadvantaged populations, or are part of multi-modal transportation connections.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; submissions accepted per Notice of Funding Opportunity published in Federal Register
structured_extraction.program_audience: Airport sponsors and operators in Maryland seeking to fund terminal facility improvements and modernization projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and construction of terminal facilities, passenger movement systems, baggage handling systems, doors, elevators, escalators, moving walkways, and related passenger infrastructure. Funds may support planning, environmental review, design, and construction phases of eligible projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland airport projects eligible. All Maryland counties eligible to apply. Federal Aviation Administration IIJA competitive grant program open to eligible airport sponsors nationwide, with Maryland airports able to participate.
requirements_list: Airport sponsor must submit completed FAA Form 5100-144 (IIJA Competitive Grant Project Information)
Project must improve passenger experience and terminal functionality
Aging infrastructure must require replacement or modernization or have exceeded its useful life
Detailed design plans, engineering plans, and cost estimates required
Project description limited to 600 characters or less
Total estimated project cost must be provided in whole dollars
Amount of funding requested must be specified in whole dollars
Match funding availability must be identified (Yes or No)
Delivery method must be specified (Design/Bid, Design/Build, CM at Risk, or Other)
Bid or Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) status must be documented
Comprehensive financial plan for entire project required if phased
Project must be on approved Airport Layout Plan (ALP) or provide ALP approval timeline
Environmental determination must be complete or timeline provided
Airspace approval must be complete or identified as not applicable
Forecast enplanements data must be provided from most recently approved forecast
Existing and proposed square footage must be documented
If associated with approved IIJA, AIP, or PFC project, grant numbers and funding amounts must be provided

Project must meet at least one ATP evaluation criterion: increase capacity and passenger access, replace aging infrastructure, achieve ADA compliance and expand accessibility, improve access for historically disadvantaged populations, improve energy efficiency, improve airfield safety through terminal or tower relocation, or encourage actual and potential competition
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete FAA Form 5100-144 (IIJA Competitive Grant Project Information) with all required project details. 2. Gather supporting documentation including detailed terminal designs, engineering plans, cost estimates, Airport Layout Plan approval, environmental determination, and airspace approval if applicable. 3. Do not include Personal Identifiable Information in open text boxes. 4. Save completed form electronically. 5. Submit signed form via email to IIJA.Airports@faa.gov or use the form's Submit button to create an email message with PDF attachment. 6. Include digital signature on the certification page, or if using backup method, sign and date the form. 7. Applications reviewed competitively based on project merit, ATP evaluation criteria, and alignment with IIJA program objectives.

structured_extraction.program_description: This federal program offers competitive grant funding to improve accessibility at public transit stations that are not fully compliant with Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) standards. Eligible activities include planning, design, and construction of elevators, ramps, accessible pathways, platform modifications, pedestrian bridges, vertical circulation systems, and communication systems. Public transit agencies and state or local transportation entities are eligible, with joint applications permitted.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive federal grant funding to improve accessibility at public transit stations. Eligible activities include planning, design, and construction of elevators, ramps, accessible pathways, platform modifications, pedestrian bridges, vertical circulation, ADA-compliant connections between transit modes, and communication systems. Public transit agencies and state or local transportation entities are eligible, with joint applications permitted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public transit agencies and state or local transportation entities, including transit authorities operating rail and bus systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, and construction of station accessibility features including elevators, ramps, accessible pathways, platforms, pedestrian bridges, vertical circulation, communication systems, and ADA-compliant connections between transit modes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland transit stations eligible. Available statewide.
requirements_list: Public transit stations must not be fully ADA-compliant
Joint applications are permitted
Accessibility improvements required
Detailed design and construction plans needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted through the Federal Transit Administration's application portal by the deadline date, including detailed station designs, construction plans, and ADA compliance documentation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Appalachian Regional Initiative for Stronger Economies (ARISE)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program administered through the Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC) that makes competitive funding available for multi-state projects advancing regional economic growth across the Appalachian region, including economic development, transportation infrastructure planning, workforce development, and community capacity building. In Maryland, the program focuses on the Appalachian counties of Allegany, Garrett, and Washington.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive federal grants for multi-state projects that advance regional economic growth across the Appalachian region. Eligible activities include planning and implementation efforts related to infrastructure, workforce development, business growth, community capacity, feasibility assessments, bridge inspections, preliminary engineering, community engagement, and planning for recreation infrastructure and multimodal connectivity — all aligned with ARC priorities. Funding amounts vary based on project scope and county economic distress levels; match rates are calculated using ARC's Match Rate Calculator based on FY2026 County Economic Status (typically 40% match for distressed counties). Full applications are by invitation only following an initial inquiry.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public agencies, Tribes, higher education institutions, and nonprofits working in partnership across at least two states in the Appalachian region; in Maryland, government agencies and regional organizations in Appalachian counties (Allegany, Garrett, and Washington) are eligible. Partnerships must span at least two states within the Appalachian region.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning and implementation efforts related to infrastructure, workforce development, business growth, and community capacity aligned with Appalachian Regional Commission priorities; feasibility assessments, bridge inspections, preliminary engineering, community engagement, and planning for recreation infrastructure and multimodal connectivity. Specific eligible activities include tourism and recreation infrastructure assessment and planning, trail and bridge improvements, visitor amenity enhancements, environmental assessments, and economic impact analysis.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Appalachian region across multiple states; requires partnerships across at least two states within the Appalachian region. In Maryland, eligible counties include Allegany, Garrett, and Washington. Projects must address regional economic development priorities and serve communities experiencing economic distress.
requirements_list: Must be a multi-state project with applicant working in partnership across at least two states
Eligible applicants are public agencies, Tribes, higher education institutions, and nonprofits
Project must be located in Appalachian region with geographic focus on distressed areas
Regional economic development focus required aligned with ARC Strategic Investment Goals
Community engagement and planning component required
Project partnership must include representatives from each participating state
All project partners must acknowledge project summary before application submission
Projects should demonstrate strategic alignment with state and regional Comprehensive Economic Development Strategy (CEDS) goals
Match funding requirement (typically 40% for distressed counties, calculated via ARC Match Rate Calculator)
Projects in distressed areas receive priority consideration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective applicants must first submit a project inquiry for consideration. Upon positive review, full applications are invited on a selective basis. Initial inquiry must include project summary and must be submitted to and acknowledged by all participating states' ARC program managers. Full applications are due May 15, 2026. Applications should include: feasibility studies and assessments, preliminary engineering and design plans, NEPA environmental analysis documentation, community engagement records and documentation, economic impact analysis, partnership agreements and letters of support, and project management/grant administration plans. Applications are submitted to the Appalachian Regional Commission.

structured_extraction.program_name: Better Utilizing Investments to Leverage Development (BUILD) Transportation Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The BUILD (Better Utilizing Investments to Leverage Development) program provides competitive federal grants that support infrastructure projects with significant local or regional impact. These grants replaced the earlier TIGER (Transportation Investment Generating Economic Recovery) program and support projects that expand transportation options, improve freight movement, enhance safety, and leverage regional economic development. Eligible projects include transit facilities, pedestrian bridges, truck parking improvements, rail enhancements, bridge rehabilitation, multi-modal transportation facility reconstruction, highway and bridge projects, port infrastructure investments, and stormwater improvements designed to enhance aquatic habitat.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive federal grant funding for local and regional transportation infrastructure projects. Capital grant requests must be at least $1 million in rural areas and $5 million in urban areas, while planning grants have no minimum award size. The standard Federal cost share may cover up to 80 percent of total project costs. Projects located in Rural areas, Areas of Persistent Poverty, or Historically Disadvantaged Communities are eligible for up to 100 percent Federal funding. There is a $25 million maximum award per project. Approximately $1.5 billion is available in annual guaranteed funding through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), with a 50/50 urban-rural award split. Awards are issued on a competitive basis by the U.S. Department of Transportation. Funds must be obligated by statutory deadlines.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sean Winkler, Senior Policy Advisor; Christy Bernal, Discretionary Grant Manager – Rotation
structured_extraction.program_audience: State transportation agencies, units of local government, public agencies, publicly chartered authorities, special purpose districts or public authorities with transportation functions such as port authorities, Federally recognized Tribal governments, transit agencies, and multi-jurisdictional groups composed of eligible entities. Federal agencies, nonprofits, private entities, and individuals are ineligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, preparation, design work, construction, engineering, feasibility studies, bridge rehabilitation, structural analysis, environmental review, and multi-modal transportation facility reconstruction for transportation infrastructure projects including transit facilities, pedestrian bridges, truck parking improvements, rail enhancements, highway improvements, port infrastructure investments, and stormwater improvements designed to enhance aquatic habitat.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide and U.S. territories. Projects must be located in areas with significant local or regional impact. Projects located in Rural areas, Areas of Persistent Poverty, or Historically Disadvantaged Communities receive enhanced funding eligibility up to 100 percent Federal funding.
requirements_list: Projects must have significant local or regional impact
Project must align with federal transportation priorities and BUILD program goals
Detailed project narratives and engineering plans required
Environmental review and compliance documentation required
Competitive selection process

Eligible project types include highway or bridge projects eligible under Title 23, public transportation projects eligible under 49 U.S.C. Chapter 53, passenger and freight rail projects, port infrastructure investments including inland ports and land ports of entry, surface transportation components of eligible airport projects, projects on Tribal land where title or maintenance responsibility rests with the Federal government, intermodal projects with at least one eligible component, and culvert replacement or stormwater improvements designed to enhance aquatic habitat
Capital grant requests must meet minimum funding thresholds: $1 million in rural areas and $5 million in urban areas; planning grants have no minimum award size
Maximum award of $25 million per project
Projects must comply with federal cost-share requirements and statutory funding obligation deadlines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit detailed project applications including project description, budget, engineering plans, environmental compliance documentation, and project narratives to the U.S. Department of Transportation. Applications must be submitted by the deadline of February 24, 2026. The Secretary of Transportation reviews applications competitively and announces grant winners on the USDOT website. The FY2026 NOFO (Notice of Funding Opportunity) was released on November 26, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program providing grants for modernization, repair, replacement, and improvement of major bridges on the National Bridge Inventory (NBI) in Maryland. The Large Bridge Investment Program (BIP) provides financial assistance to replace, rehabilitate, preserve, or protect bridges, with goals of improving bridge safety and reliability, improving bridge condition (especially those at-risk of falling into poor condition), and leveraging non-federal contributions to advance bridge projects into construction. Supports bridge infrastructure projects statewide, including traffic modernization, multimodal enhancements, safety upgrades, scour protection, seismic protections, bicycle and pedestrian accommodations, and adjacent roadway modifications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants with 80/20 cost-share (federal/local) for bridge projects on the National Bridge Inventory. Large Bridge grants support projects with total cost less than $100 million. Eligible activities include Preliminary Engineering (PE), National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and pre-construction activities, construction (replacement, preservation, reconstruction, rehabilitation), associated work, resiliency measures (scour and seismic protections), bicycle and pedestrian accommodations, and maintenance commitments. Planning grants (approximately $20 million in FY 2026) support feasibility studies, revenue forecasting, and pre-NEPA project development work. Bridge Project grants (approximately $2 billion in FY 2026) support construction and pre-construction activities. Applicants must consider bicycle and pedestrian accommodations and identify a maintenance commitment to the structure.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sean Winkler, Senior Policy Advisor; Christy Bernal, Discretionary Grant Manager – Rotation
structured_extraction.program_audience: States, metropolitan planning organizations, units of local government, special purpose districts with transportation authority, federal land management agencies, tribal governments, and multi-state or multi-jurisdictional combinations of eligible entities responsible for bridge infrastructure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge replacement, rehabilitation, preservation, reconstruction, and associated work; preliminary engineering and NEPA activities; resiliency measures including scour and seismic protections; bicycle and pedestrian accommodations; maintenance planning; adjacent roadway modifications; traffic modernization; and multimodal improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. All bridges on the National Bridge Inventory (NBI) in Maryland are eligible. The program serves urbanized areas and regional transportation corridors.
requirements_list: Bridge must be on the National Bridge Inventory (NBI)
Detailed engineering and design plans required
Environmental review and NEPA permitting necessary
Applicants must consider bicycle and pedestrian accommodations
Applicants must identify a maintenance commitment to the structure
Cost share requirement of 80% federal/20% local match
For projects with total cost less than $100 million (Large Bridge category)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible applicants submit detailed bridge improvement applications through U.S. Department of Transportation to the Federal Highway Administration. Applications must include engineering plans, cost estimates, National Bridge Inventory documentation, multimodal benefit documentation, environmental review status, and maintenance commitment plans. Applicants must demonstrate compliance with federal law and policies. Applications should reference the National Bridge Inventory and include detailed project descriptions, location information, budget documentation, merit criteria addressing state of good repair, safety, mobility, economic vitality, environmental sustainability, and partnership/stewardship. Technical assistance available through MDOT Grants Roadshow and contact representatives.

structured_extraction.program_description: This competitive federal grant program provides funding to support pre-disaster hazard mitigation projects that reduce risk to communities and critical infrastructure from natural hazards. The program also supports flood vulnerability assessments and resilience planning for transportation infrastructure, including flood risk reduction, structural mitigation, and protection of key community lifelines. It prioritizes infrastructure-based solutions that deliver long-term resilience benefits and supports limited capability and capacity building efforts that facilitate implementation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive federal funding to support pre-disaster hazard mitigation projects that reduce risk to communities and critical infrastructure from natural hazards. The program prioritizes infrastructure-based solutions that deliver long-term resilience benefits, including flood risk reduction, structural mitigation, and protection of key community lifelines. Eligible activities include construction projects, flood vulnerability assessments and mapping for transportation facilities, stakeholder engagement, analysis of mitigation options, and limited capability and capacity building efforts that support implementation. The program emphasizes cost-effective, technically feasible projects aligned with approved hazard mitigation plans and demonstrates measurable risk reduction, with a focus on strengthening resilience for vulnerable populations and high-risk areas, including coastal Maryland port facilities and flood-prone transportation infrastructure.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Communities, critical infrastructure owners, state transportation agencies, and port authorities seeking to reduce risks from natural hazards and flooding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-disaster hazard mitigation projects including construction, flood risk reduction, structural mitigation, protection of community lifelines, vulnerability assessments, flood mapping, stakeholder engagement, and analysis of mitigation options for coastal and flood-prone infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide; coastal Maryland port facilities and flood-prone transportation infrastructure are specifically eligible. Baltimore City is a prioritized area.
requirements_list: Projects must be aligned with approved hazard mitigation plans
Projects must demonstrate measurable risk reduction
Focus on strengthening resilience for vulnerable populations and high-risk areas
Project must address flood vulnerability
Vulnerability assessment required
Stakeholder engagement and mitigation options analysis needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted by July 23, 2026 through Grants.gov. Submit vulnerability assessment proposals including facility identification, flood risk analysis, and mitigation strategies to the Federal Emergency Management Agency.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program funding the construction of new transit maintenance and operations facilities to support public transportation system capacity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants for construction of transit maintenance facilities including fleet maintenance shops, parking facilities, vehicle wash bays, and operations support buildings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Transit authorities and public transportation agencies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction of maintenance facilities, fleet parking infrastructure, wash bays, operations support spaces, and related transit facility improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland transit agencies eligible.
requirements_list: Project must increase transit system capacity
Detailed facility design and operational plans required
Environmental compliance documentation needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit project applications including facility designs, operational plans, and capacity improvement documentation to the Federal Transit Administration.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows commuters who carpool, vanpool, bike, walk, or take transit to work to receive a cash payment from their employer in exchange for surrendering their dedicated paid parking space.
