Employers who offer this program can claim a tax credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers who offer Cash in Lieu of Parking to employees who surrender their parking space can claim a Maryland Commuter Tax Credit of up to 50 percent of the cost of providing commuter benefits, with a maximum of $100 per individual employee per month. Employees receive a cash benefit (amount varies by employer) in place of a paid parking space.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers who offer free or subsidized parking to employees, and commuters who use alternative transportation methods such as carpooling, vanpooling, biking, walking, or transit.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash payments to employees who surrender their parking space; employers receive tax credits for offering the program. Can be used to reduce parking demand and achieve corporate sustainability goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Employer must offer free or subsidized parking to employees
Employer must provide a cash allowance to an employee equal to or less than the parking subsidy that would otherwise be paid
Employee must choose to receive cash benefit instead of a parking space
Employee must commute by alternative means (carpool, vanpool, bike, walk, or transit)
Program works best for employers that lease parking, typically implemented at lease renewal
Any employer can implement the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers implement a parking cash out program by offering employees a choice between a parking space or a cash benefit. Employers can then apply for the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit for 50 percent of eligible commuter benefit costs, up to $100 per employee per month. Contact Commuter Choice Maryland for assistance at CommuterChoice@mdot.maryland.gov or 410-865-1100 (Monday-Friday, 8:30 AM - 5:00 PM).

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program supporting the procurement of zero-emission vehicles and equipment and associated charging infrastructure for port operations. Specifically funds equipment electrification and terminal decarbonization to reduce emissions by an estimated 35% compared to 2020 levels.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants from the EPA Clean Ports Program Zero-Emission Deployment Competition for procurement of zero-emission vehicles, equipment, and charging infrastructure to reduce air pollution at port facilities. The Port of Baltimore application requests $145,658,479 in EPA funding with an applicant cost share of $36,414,620 for a total project cost of $182,073,099. Project includes procurement of 213 zero-emission vehicles and equipment: 25 drayage trucks, 188 cargo handling equipment units, 149 electric vehicle supply equipment units, battery energy storage system with microgrid, and electrical infrastructure upgrades. Funds also support emissions inventory development, workforce training, and infrastructure improvements to increase electrical power capacity at terminals. Project period: February 1, 2025 to December 31, 2028. Minimum EPA funding acceptance: $91,962,967.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Port authorities, maritime operators, and port service providers including terminal operators, drayage companies, cargo handling equipment operators, and logistics firms serving the Port of Baltimore
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Zero-emission vehicle and equipment procurement (drayage trucks, cargo handling equipment, terminal tractors, forklifts), charging infrastructure installation (149 EV charging stations), electrical infrastructure upgrades (feeder conductors, duct banks, transformers, switches, power monitoring equipment), battery energy storage systems with microgrids, emissions inventory development, workforce training and development, and community engagement programs to benefit disadvantaged and underserved communities adjacent to the Port of Baltimore.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland port facilities eligible, specifically Port of Baltimore. Project activities distributed across City of Baltimore (37%), Baltimore County (58%), and Anne Arundel County (5%). Port Authority applicants and private sector collaborators at Port of Baltimore marine terminals including Dundalk Marine Terminal, Seagirt Marine Terminal, and Tradepoint Atlantic facility.
requirements_list: Project must demonstrate significant emissions reduction (minimum 35% CO2e reduction compared to baseline)
Zero-emission vehicle and equipment procurement required
Community engagement and workforce planning needed
Applicant must be a Port Authority or eligible port entity
Equipment must be zero-emission technology compliant
Build America, Buy America (BABA) compliance required where possible
Private sector cost-share of minimum 10% of total project cost (Tier B applicants)
Environmental Justice community benefit documentation required
Project must align with Maryland Climate Solutions Now Act (CSNA) goals for 60% GHG reduction by 2031 and net-zero by 2045
Coordination with utility providers required for infrastructure projects
Quarterly reporting and performance monitoring required during project period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit comprehensive project applications to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Clean Ports Program including: project narrative with detailed equipment specifications and quantities, emissions reduction plans with baseline and projected emissions data, electrical infrastructure plans and BGE coordination letters, budget justification and cost estimates for equipment and infrastructure, community engagement and benefits documentation demonstrating support from adjacent disadvantaged communities, workforce development and training plans, partnerships and collaboration letters from all participating entities, risk mitigation strategies, and alignment with state and local climate goals. Applications must include detailed equipment lists specifying number and type of zero-emission vehicles, cargo handling equipment, and charging infrastructure, as well as electrical infrastructure improvement specifications. Applicants must demonstrate partnerships with equipment suppliers, utility companies, and community organizations.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Climate Focused Funding Portal funds transportation projects that provide climate benefits, such as reducing greenhouse gas emissions, improving resilience to climate impacts like flooding and severe storms, or enhancing transportation infrastructure sustainability. The current solicitation focuses on identifying eligible projects to reduce carbon emissions from transportation using federal Carbon Reduction Program funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal Carbon Reduction Program funding for transportation projects with climate benefits. Eligible applicants must provide a non-federal cash match of 20% of the total project cost. Funds can be used only for capital projects, not operating expenses. Projects must meet federal aid requirements. There is no minimum or maximum funding request amount, but the 80/20 non-federal matching requirement applies.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Deron Lovaas (for project ideas and emissions reduction program questions); Allison Breitenother (for application support); Allison Gost (for OneStop portal support)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), local governments, WMATA, and MDOT Modal Administrations (SHA, MPA, MTA, MAA, MVA) with transportation projects that provide climate benefits, including reducing greenhouse gas emissions or improving climate resilience.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects that reduce transportation emissions or improve climate resilience, including but not limited to: fleet electrification and zero-emission vehicles and infrastructure, Transportation Systems Management and Operations (TSMO), Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), congestion mitigation, Vehicle Miles Travelled (VMT) reduction, transportation mode-shift, public transportation services and facilities, bike/pedestrian facilities, efficient street lighting, diesel engine retrofits, port electrification, truck parking technology, connected and automated vehicle (CAV) technologies, transportation demand management, and rail infrastructure and freight rail projects. Operating and maintenance costs are not eligible expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Project location may be specific (county/city) or distributed across region(s). Projects on federal land are eligible with coordination from the federal landowner.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an eligible organization type (MPO, local government, WMATA, or MDOT Modal Administration)
Project must have a defined scope with clearly identified improvements
Project must demonstrate emissions reduction from surface transportation
Project must provide a non-federal cash match of 20% of total project cost (cash match only, no in-kind match)
Matching funds must be from non-federal sources
Project must follow all federal aid requirements
Highway widening/expansion is not an eligible emissions reduction strategy
Projects supporting alternative fuel vehicles must be zero-emission; hybrid vehicles are not eligible
All projects must be capital projects; operating expenses are not eligible
Project must include project location and project limits documentation
Project must include project schedule and milestones documentation
Project must include project cost estimate with cash-flows for all years requesting funding
Project must include source of project cash match documentation
Quantitative emissions reduction calculations are optional but encouraged
If project is listed in STIP/TIP, provide STIP/TIP ID and control number
If project requires right-of-way acquisition, provide status and expected ROW clearance date
Project must explain how it achieves Carbon Reduction Goals from state or agency plans
Project must address equity and potential impacts on disadvantaged communities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must register on the Maryland OneStop Portal at https://onestop.md.gov/. Search for 'Climate Focused Funding' and click the blue 'Apply Now' button to access the application. Complete all required fields in the application, including project components, emissions reduction details, and budget information. Upload all required documentation (project location and limits, project schedule and milestones, project cost estimate, source of cash match, and any supporting documents). Applicants may save draft applications and resume at any time before the deadline. Weekly virtual office hours are available on Wednesdays from 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM during the solicitation window (January 15 - March 26, 2025) on Microsoft Teams for technical assistance and questions. Submit the completed application electronically through OneStop by the deadline. Applications are evaluated using the same process for all eligible applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: CommuterCash is a free mobile app that helps commuters find optimal commuting options and earn cash rewards for logging sustainable trips. Users can explore and log carpool, vanpool, transit, biking, walking, and multimodal travel options during weekday peak hours. Points earned through the app can be redeemed for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits. The program is designed to encourage commuters in Maryland and the Washington, DC area to reduce solo driving and adopt more sustainable commute modes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Commuters earn points by logging eligible work commute trips during peak hours (6:30am-9:30am or 4:00pm-7:00pm on weekdays). Points range from 10 to 100 per trip and are awarded based on the commute mode used, with alternative modes like transit and ridesharing earning higher point values than solo driving. Only one morning trip and one evening trip earn points per day. Points can be redeemed for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits. Up to $10 can be earned after completing 20 trips, with higher tier rewards available up to $90 in value. Maximum earnings are $600 per calendar year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employed commuters traveling to a physical work location within Maryland or into the Washington, DC area who are interested in exploring optimal, sustainable commute options including carpool, vanpool, transit, biking, walking, and multimodal travel.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Points earned can be redeemed for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits. Funds are for rewarding sustainable commute behavior and cannot be used for other purposes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Commuters traveling anywhere within Maryland or into the Washington, DC area (as defined by the Council of Governments regional map) are eligible to participate.
requirements_list: Must be employed and commuting to a physical work location
Telecommuting does not qualify
Trips must be on weekdays (Monday-Friday)
Trips must occur during morning peak times (6:30am-9:30am) or evening peak times (4:00pm-7:00pm)
Only one morning trip and one evening trip earn points per day
Must download the CommuterCash app from Apple App Store or Google Play
Must register and set up a Commuter Connections account
Must use eligible commute modes: carpool, vanpool, transit, biking, walking, or multimodal travel
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the CommuterCash app from the Apple App Store or Google Play. Create and register a Commuter Connections account using your email address. Log your eligible sustainable commute trips in the app during weekday peak hours. Earn points based on your commute mode and patterns. Redeem accumulated points for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits.

structured_extraction.program_name: Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program supporting railroad infrastructure improvements and safety studies including trespassing reduction initiatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants supporting railroad infrastructure improvements including battery electric locomotive procurement, rail connection projects, and trespassing safety studies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Ports, transit authorities, and government agencies involved in rail operations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Locomotive procurement and charging infrastructure, rail connection design and construction, trespassing safety assessments, and implementation of injury reduction programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland rail infrastructure projects eligible.
requirements_list: Project must improve rail infrastructure safety or operations
Detailed engineering and design plans required
Environmental compliance documentation needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit project applications including infrastructure improvement details, cost estimates, and safety benefits documentation to the Federal Railroad Administration.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program supporting the construction, relocation, reconstruction, repair, and modernization of airport control towers at general aviation airports through competitive grants under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive federal grants under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) supporting airport traffic control tower projects. Funding covers planning, environmental, design, and construction phases for new towers, relocation, reconstruction, repair, and improvements to existing towers. Applicants must submit project applications via FAA Form 5100-144 with detailed information on project costs, delivery method, timeline, and how the project impacts the National Airspace System. Matching funds may be required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Airport sponsors and authorities operating general aviation airports, particularly those with aging or non-standard facility conditions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction, design, relocation, reconstruction, repair, and improvements to airport traffic control towers including facility upgrades and technology enhancements. Projects must address operational constraints, nonstandard facility conditions, or aging infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland airport projects eligible under federal FAA Contract Tower Program guidelines.
requirements_list: Existing facility must be at end of useful life or require major modernization
Project must enhance operational safety and efficiency
Detailed engineering and design plans required
Airport sponsor must complete FAA Form 5100-144 for submission
Comprehensive project description limited to 600 characters required
Applicants must describe impact on National Airspace System (NAS)
Environmental determination may be required depending on project stage
Project must be on approved Airport Layout Plan (ALP) or provide timeline for approval
Airspace approval may be required for certain projects
Matching funds required or documented availability
All information must be accurate and applicant authorized to submit on behalf of airport sponsor
Procurement processes must comply with 2 CFR 200
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Complete FAA Form 5100-144 (IIJA Competitive Grant Project Information) with airport and project details. 2) Provide general airport information including airport name, FAA location identifier (LOCID), and point of contact information. 3) Select 'FCT' for Contract Tower Program and indicate project type (new, relocate, reconstruct, repair, or improve). 4) Enter project costs, funding amount requested, delivery method, and timeline (project costs known date, grant execution date, construction start date). 5) Document project stage (planning, environmental, design, or construction), existing and proposed square footage, and tower age. 6) Indicate whether siting study is complete and provide description of impact on National Airspace System (limited to 600 characters). 7) Certify all information is accurate and authorized. 8) Submit completed form via email to IIJA.Airports@faa.gov or use the 'Submit' button which creates an email message with the PDF attached. Digital signatures are supported.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program supporting military installation infrastructure improvements that enhance military readiness and operational capabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants supporting military-related infrastructure including obstruction removal, lighting improvements, and airfield safety enhancements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Military installations and state agencies supporting military operations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Obstruction removal, airfield lighting, wildlife hazard mitigation, environmental compliance, and related military readiness improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland military installations eligible.
requirements_list: Project must support military readiness and operations
Environmental and permitting documentation required
Federal compliance with military standards needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit project applications with military readiness justification and environmental compliance documentation to the U.S. Department of Defense.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program supporting replacement of nonroad diesel-powered equipment with newer technology or zero-emission alternatives to reduce emissions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants for replacement of older diesel-powered nonroad equipment including terminal tractors, forklifts, and other machinery with zero-emission or Tier 4 Final engines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Port operators and companies managing nonroad diesel equipment
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of terminal tractors, forklifts, pumps, air compressors, and other nonroad equipment with zero-emission or Tier 4 Final engine models.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland port and industrial facilities eligible.
requirements_list: Existing equipment must be older diesel-powered models
Equipment replacement or upgrade required
Environmental benefits documentation needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit equipment replacement proposals including inventory lists, specifications, and environmental benefits to the Environmental Protection Agency.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program supporting zero-emission vehicle infrastructure and charging station development to reduce transportation emissions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants for strategic planning and investment in zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicle charging infrastructure along freight corridors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State transportation departments and environmental agencies supporting zero-emission freight development
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Charging infrastructure development, strategic planning for zero-emission freight corridors, and related equipment and facility improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Interstate freight corridors including I-95 corridor in Maryland and neighboring states.
requirements_list: Project must support zero-emission heavy-duty vehicles
Corridor strategy required
Regional coordination with neighboring states needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit comprehensive corridor development plans and infrastructure proposals to the Environmental Protection Agency.

structured_extraction.program_name: FRA Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program providing funding for railroad infrastructure improvements including capacity, accessibility, and reliability enhancements at transit stations, as well as planning, design, and construction of intercity rail improvements including infrastructure replacement and speed enhancements. Supports both transit rail station improvements and intercity passenger rail corridor modernization projects in Maryland. The program funds preliminary engineering and design work to advance shovel-ready rail projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants providing up to 80% of project costs for intercity passenger rail and transit railroad infrastructure improvements. Funding covers preliminary engineering and design work (conceptual design through 30% design level), bridge and tunnel replacement, track and rail infrastructure modernization, signal and electrical system upgrades, station renovation and accessibility enhancements, platform construction, pedestrian bridges, and transit-oriented development support. Non-federal matching share of 20% is required from state, local, or private sources. Example: Brunswick-Rockville Improvements Project requested $12,640,000 federal funding with $3,160,000 non-federal match for total project cost of $15,800,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not specified - rolling basis determined by Federal Railroad Administration NOFO cycles
structured_extraction.program_audience: Transit authorities, state rail authorities, railroad operators, and government agencies responsible for railroad operations and maintenance serving intercity and commuter passengers in Maryland. Eligible applicants include state transit agencies, political subdivisions of the state, and public agencies established by interstate compact.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preliminary engineering, conceptual design (15% design), and final design (30% design) of rail station improvements including new platforms, track modifications, platform construction, pedestrian bridges, accessibility enhancements, bridge and tunnel replacement, track and rail infrastructure modernization, signal and electrical system upgrades, station renovation, transit-oriented development support (parking reconfiguration, bus loop rebuilding, station amenities), and related intercity and commuter rail improvements. Grade-separated pedestrian crossing design and center island platform construction also eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland transit and intercity rail corridors eligible, including Northeast Corridor segments and CSXT right-of-way corridors serving intercity passenger rail routes such as Amtrak's Floridian route. Specific recent projects include Brunswick and Rockville stations on the MARC Brunswick Line in Montgomery County and Frederick County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must improve passenger rail service capacity, reliability, or accessibility
Detailed engineering and design plans required
Environmental compliance documentation needed
Project must improve intercity passenger rail service or commuter rail service
Infrastructure modernization or replacement required to bring assets to state of good repair
Speed and capacity improvements documented
Project must enhance multimodal connections
Safety benefits must be demonstrated including grade crossing information and trespassing injury/fatality prevention
Applicant must be state transit agency, political subdivision of state, or public agency established by interstate compact
20% non-federal matching share required from state, local, or private sources
Project readiness and technical merit must be demonstrated
Benefit-cost analysis required
Railroad agreements (49 U.S.C. 22905-compliant) must be in place or pending prior to construction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit detailed rail improvement proposals to the Federal Railroad Administration during open NOFO periods. Applications must include: project summary with components and lifecycle stage, detailed project description addressing current challenges and proposed solutions, grant funding sources and uses table showing federal and non-federal funding breakdown, applicant eligibility documentation confirming status as state transit agency or eligible public entity, project eligibility criteria demonstration including infrastructure replacement needs and service performance improvements, planning documentation references (state rail plans, regional plans, corridor studies), safety benefit data including grade crossing inventory and incident history, geospatial data with precise decimal degree coordinates, project team organization and past experience documentation, federal reporting and project management procedures, and benefit-cost analysis. Design work proceeds in phases: RFP issuance for design services, bidder selection, conceptual design (15%), and preliminary engineering (30% design) over estimated 56-month project development period.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Fringe Benefit (IRS Section 132 Educational Material)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that lets employers and employees save on taxes by using tax-free dollars for commuting, reducing employees' taxable income. Employers can provide this as a pre-tax benefit, a subsidy, or a combination of both, up to the IRS-set monthly limit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers can choose to cover part or all of an employee's eligible commuting costs, or simply allow employees to set aside pre-tax income to pay for them. Assistance is provided up to the IRS-set monthly limit. When designed alongside the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit, organizations can maximize both federal and state savings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employers and employees seeking to reduce taxes on commuting costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax-free dollars for eligible commuting expenses including transit, carpool/vanpool, biking, and related commuter benefits.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers can design the benefit as a pre-tax benefit, a subsidy, or a combination of both, up to the IRS monthly limit.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program supporting the construction of transportation facilities that provide access to federal public lands including national parks, trails, and wildlife refuges. The program funds projects that improve state and local transportation facilities located on, adjacent to, or providing access to Federal lands for visitors, recreationists and resource users.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants providing 100 percent funding for design, construction engineering, construction, preliminary engineering, environmental documentation, right-of-way acquisition, and planning/technical studies. Projects may include shared-use path construction, pedestrian and bicycle facilities, trail connections, safety enhancements, drainage improvements, and transportation facilities serving federal public lands. Grant amounts and project phases are determined through the project development and MOA process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by funding cycle; submit applications via the Federal Lands Highway website or directly to Efl.planning@dot.gov
structured_extraction.contact_name: Lewis Grimm, PE (FHWA-EFL Planning Team Leader)
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local government agencies, tribal governments, and facility owners or maintainers managing transportation infrastructure near federal public lands. Applicants must own or maintain the facility or provide authorization from the facility owner.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction of shared-use paths, pedestrian crossings, bicycle facilities, trail connections, safety improvements, bridges, culverts, rehabilitation/enhancement projects, preliminary engineering, environmental documentation, right-of-way acquisition, and design services for transportation facilities providing access to federal lands including national parks, monuments, scenic trails, wildlife refuges, and other federally managed areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located on public highways, roads, bridges, trails, or transit systems on, adjacent to, or providing access to federal lands. Maryland projects providing access to federal public lands are eligible. Facilities must have title or maintenance responsibility vested with state, county, city, township, tribal, municipal, or local government.
requirements_list: Project must provide access to or be located on/adjacent to federal lands
Facility must be publicly owned or maintained by state, county, city, township, tribal, municipal, or local government
Applicant must be facility owner or have maintenance responsibility, or provide letter of authorization from facility owner
Project must be consistent with metropolitan, statewide, and/or regional planning processes
Project must be consistent with currently adopted agency plans
Facility title or maintenance responsibility must be vested with eligible government entity
Project must be sponsored/supported by appropriate Federal Land Management Agency (FLMA)
Facility must be ADA-compliant where applicable
Environmental review documentation required (NEPA compliance)
For local delivery, applicant must be certified by State DOT to administer local agency projects
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Applicant assembles project application package using the Eastern Federal Lands (EFL) Access Program Application form (EFL-FM-PLN-03). 2) Application must include project description, detailed cost estimates, maps, photos, and supporting documentation (limit 10 additional pages; letters of support do not count toward page limit). 3) Applicant obtains signature and/or letter of support from appropriate Federal Land Management Agency (FLMA). 4) Complete application package submitted via email to Efl.planning@dot.gov. 5) Programming Decisions Committee (PDC) for the state reviews applications and prioritizes based on weighted selection criteria. 6) Selected projects enter project development phase. 7) Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) executed outlining project delivery method, funding, scope, schedule, and responsibilities. 8) State DOT provides Stewardship and Oversight (S&O). 9) Project phases funded by State DOT following S&O process. Note: Access program funds will not reimburse work performed prior to MOA execution and PR-2 or FMIS obligation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Ferry Programs (Passenger Ferry, Electric or Low-Emitting Ferry Pilot, and Rural Ferry Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: This suite of competitive grant programs provides federal funding to support the improvement, expansion, and sustainability of public ferry services across urban and rural areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant programs that fund capital investments such as acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and modernization of ferry vessels, terminals, and supporting infrastructure, as well as planning efforts and, in rural areas, operating assistance to maintain essential service. Projects are evaluated based on demonstrated need, benefits to service quality and community access, consistency with local and regional priorities, and readiness for implementation, including financial and technical capacity. Additional consideration is given to geographic diversity, safety, accessibility, and support for economic opportunity.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public ferry service operators and communities seeking to improve, expand, and sustain ferry services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital investments for ferry vessels, terminals, and infrastructure; planning efforts; and in rural areas, operating assistance to maintain essential service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Urban and rural areas
requirements_list: Projects must demonstrate need, benefits to service quality and community access
Projects must be consistent with local and regional priorities
Projects must demonstrate readiness for implementation, including financial and technical capacity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted by May 11, 2026 through the federal agency's application portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: Guaranteed Ride Home provides up to six free rides home per year for registered commuters who regularly use sustainable transportation methods. It ensures a reliable way home during personal emergencies for those who bike, walk, carpool, vanpool, or take transit to work. The program is available statewide to all registered commuters committed to sustainable commuting.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to six free rides home per year for eligible registered commuters during personal emergencies, provided at no cost to the commuter.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered commuters who regularly use sustainable transportation methods including biking, walking, carpooling, vanpooling, or transit
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency rides home from work
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide
requirements_list: Must be a registered commuter
Must regularly commute using one of the sustainable methods: biking, walking, carpooling, vanpooling, or transit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Commuter Connections website to create an account and register to participate in the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Innovative Financing and Asset Concession (IFAC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program supporting innovative financing strategies and asset development for transit-oriented development and transit system improvements, including asset scans, feasibility studies, and innovative finance analysis for public transportation infrastructure.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_prioritized_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants of $1,000,000 supporting technical assistance over 24 months. Funding covers professional consulting services and MTA staff labor costs for: (1) asset inventory and scanning of bus-related properties, (2) assessment of development potential, (3) feasibility and economic cost-benefit analysis, (4) innovative financing analysis including public-private partnership (P3) and Transportation Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (TIFIA) options, (5) project oversight and coordination. Grant funds cover $900,000 in consultant services and $100,000 in MTA project oversight. No local match required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State transit authorities, transit agencies (MTA), and government agencies seeking to advance transit-oriented development, improve regional bus networks, and identify innovative financing mechanisms for public transportation infrastructure improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Asset scans and inventory of pipeline projects; assessment of project readiness, capital and operational needs; development potential analysis and preliminary delivery model options; feasibility assessment and economic cost-benefit analysis; innovative financing analysis including P3, TIFIA, and asset concession strategies; preliminary Value for Money analysis; business case development; implementation roadmaps. Examples of eligible improvements include Fifth Bus Division facilities, regional transfer facilities, strategic layover and end-of-line facilities, transit-oriented development supporting bus connections, and bus depot upgrades.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland transit and real estate projects eligible. Priority focus on Baltimore region state, Baltimore City, and Baltimore County-owned properties totaling over 100 assets. Specific example sites include Edison Highway Site (1601 Edison Highway), Lakeland Site (2900 Nieman Ave/2320 Banger St), Kloman Street site (1999 Kloman St), and Klunk Drive Site (3939 Klunk Dr).
requirements_list: Project must focus on innovative financing or transit-oriented development for bus network improvements
State or local government ownership or partnership required
Asset inventory and feasibility analysis required for all sites
Implementation roadmap and financing strategy needed
Project must demonstrate alignment with state and agency-wide planning documents and USDOT strategic goals
Organizational capacity to manage innovative financing arrangements must be demonstrated
Technical and operational feasibility must be assessed
Environmental, permitting, and regulatory considerations must be evaluated
Cost-benefit analysis using FTA and USDOT guidance required
Community engagement and public outreach required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit project applications including detailed scope of work to U.S. Department of Transportation Build America Bureau. Process includes: (1) MTA project initiation and grant agreement finalization with Build America Bureau; (2) Request for Proposals (RFP) or Task Order issuance to potential consulting bidders; (3) Evaluation of proposals and issuance of notice of award; (4) Establishment of working group with MDOT Office of Real Estate and Economic Development, Office of Public Private Partnerships, Office of Project Delivery, and State Highway Administration; (5) Contract negotiation and Notice to Proceed. Subsequent implementation includes five discrete tasks over 24 months with regular working group meetings and stakeholder engagement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant program that supports the development and expansion of bikeway networks across Maryland, including biking and pedestrian programs that support local economies and enhance quality of life through biking and walking. The program supports projects that maximize bicycle access and enhance last-mile connections to work, school, shopping and transit, while prioritizing funding projects that improve safety and access for disadvantaged communities.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for bikeway network development, expansion, Complete Streets safety improvements, and pedestrian program projects. The program supports projects that maximize bicycle access and enhance last-mile connections to work, school, shopping and transit, leveraging past investments in bicycle facilities and complementing existing State, local, and federal programs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Spring application window; awards announced by fall 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, organizations, and agencies developing bikeway infrastructure and pedestrian programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bikeway network development, improvements, Complete Streets safety improvements, and pedestrian program projects that maximize bicycle access and enhance last-mile connections to work, school, shopping and transit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Projects are solicited on an annual basis. Applicants apply in spring. Following a competitive selection process, MDOT will announce Bikeways awards by fall 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program supporting the purchase of low-emission and zero-emission buses to transition public transit fleets to cleaner alternatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants for purchase of diesel-hybrid and zero-emission buses to support transition of public transit fleets to lower-emission alternatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public transit agencies and authorities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of diesel-hybrid buses and zero-emission vehicles including related equipment and charging infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland public transit agencies eligible.
requirements_list: Project must support fleet transition to cleaner technology
Low- or zero-emission vehicle procurement required
Transition plan needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit vehicle purchase proposals including fleet transition plans and environmental benefits documentation to the Federal Transit Administration.

structured_extraction.program_description: A certification program that allows minority business enterprises to qualify for minority business participation goals on state-funded contracts issued by Maryland counties and cities, and for contracts funded by the Maryland Department of Transportation. The program certifies that firms are bonafide minority-owned and controlled businesses operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides certification at no cost that allows minority-owned firms to compete for state-funded contracts and contracts from counties and cities within Maryland. Certification takes several months to complete once a complete application is received. The firm must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessment and Taxation. Applicants must demonstrate they are a bonafide minority business enterprise owned and controlled by individuals who are socially and economically disadvantaged. For MBE certification, the personal net worth cap for disadvantaged owners is $2,192,035 (effective January 1, 2026). Free monthly workshops are available to help applicants prepare applications and navigate the certification process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Minority business enterprises and disadvantaged business enterprises seeking to participate in state and local contracting opportunities in Maryland. Eligible applicants include African American, Alaskan Native, Hispanic, Asian American, Native American, female, and disabled business owners (note: disabled status is not accorded minority status on federally funded projects).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This is a certification program, not a funding program. Certification enables firms to compete for and participate in minority business participation goals on state and local contracts. It qualifies minority-owned businesses to bid on opportunities set-aside for minority business enterprises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland firms or out of state firms applying for MBE certification must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessment and Taxation (SDAT). For out-of-state firms, certification must first be obtained in the applicant's home state before applying for MDOT MBE certification.
requirements_list: Firm must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessment and Taxation (SDAT)
Applicant must submit a complete Minority Business Enterprise Disclosure Affidavit in PDF format
Applicant must complete all sections of the application with no blanks; mark N/A for sections that do not apply with brief explanation
Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Owners (SEDO) must submit a Personal Net Worth (PNW) Statement with all supporting documentation; personal net worth must not exceed $2,192,035 (2026 cap)
All documents must be unredacted and submitted in PDF format
All information must be provided for areas marked N/A with brief explanation of why not applicable
Must provide Statement of Disadvantage signed with wet ink signature for all owners claiming disadvantaged status
Must provide certified Articles of Organization or incorporation from State agency and proof of good standing from SDAT
Must provide documented proof of contributions showing how ownership was acquired
Must provide resumes for all owners, officers, directors, and key employees in detailed chronological order
Must provide proof of U.S. citizenship (passport, permanent resident card, certificate of naturalization, or birth certificate) and government-issued photo ID
Must provide three (3) years of complete personal federal tax returns with authentic wet ink signatures and all schedules
Must provide five (5) years of complete business federal tax returns with authentic wet ink signatures and all schedules
Must provide year-end financial statements for past three (3) years or life of firm if less than three years
Must provide quarterly state unemployment tax wage reports for most recent four (4) quarters and list of employees
Must provide copies of all professional licenses and permits held by business, owners, and employees
Must provide copies of business bank signature authorization or letter from bank official
Must provide copies of all executed and unredacted agreements (lease, loan, distributorship, etc.)
Must provide list of equipment used to provide services for which business is seeking certification
Must provide copies of state-issued vehicle titles/registrations and current vehicle and business insurance policies
Must provide three (3) executed job contracts or invoices with proof of payment
Out-of-state firms must provide copies of home state MBE/WBE certification letters and on-site reports
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download the MBE Only Application (Minority Business Enterprise Disclosure Affidavit) from the MDOT website and review the instructions carefully. 2. Gather all required supporting documents as listed in the MBE Only Document Checklist, including proof of good standing, tax returns, financial statements, resumes, citizenship documentation, and other supporting materials. 3. Complete all sections of the application in PDF format with no blanks; write N/A for sections that do not apply with brief explanation. 4. For all socially and economically disadvantaged owners (51% ownership), complete the Personal Net Worth Statement with all worksheets and supporting financial documentation. 5. Ensure all owners sign documents with wet ink signature and date where required. 6. Notarize the completed application affidavit and Statement of Disadvantage. 7. Compile the complete application package in PDF format with all required supporting documentation organized according to the checklist. 8. Submit the application through the Maryland MBE certification portal online. 9. Attend an interview with the MDOT Minority Business Enterprise Advisory Committee as required. 10. Retain a complete copy of the entire application package for your files. Free monthly workshops are available to help applicants prepare the application and navigate the certification process. Contact OMBE at 410-865-1269 for workshop dates and registration.

structured_extraction.program_description: An internship program designed to introduce Maryland's top college students to careers in Maryland's integrated transportation system. Interns are placed in senior-level assignments during the summer with one of MDOT's agencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Summer internship placements in senior-level assignments within MDOT agencies, providing hands-on experience in transportation careers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland college undergraduate students
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internship work experience and mentorship in transportation industry
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through The Shriver Center partnership program. More information available on the MDOT Fellows Program website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded, competitive, reimbursable grant program administered by the Office of Rail and Intermodal Freight (RIF) of the Secretary's Office at MDOT. The program provides state grant assistance to local jurisdictions, railroads, business and commercial interests, and other key agencies to support railroad corridor preservation, economic development, sustainability, and innovative technologies in freight rail infrastructure. The program makes targeted investments to better leverage existing infrastructure, assets, and funding programs, helping create a pipeline of projects that advance a safe, secure, and resilient multimodal freight network.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grant assistance provided on a reimbursable basis to local jurisdictions, railroads, business and commercial interests, and other key agencies for railroad corridor preservation, economic development, sustainability, and innovative technologies. Projects must have two eligible types: Design projects (for completion of design plans and feasibility assessments, must be completed within 2 years of grant award) or Construction projects (for construction or installation of rail corridor improvements, including sidings/sidetracks, grade crossing improvements, bridges/structures, and drainage improvements; must be completed within 3 years of grant award; design may be funded as a component of a construction award). Applicants must provide a minimum 20% local cash match of the overall project cost; projects providing more than 20% match receive preferred consideration. There is no minimum or maximum funding request amount. Recipients pay for costs first and are then reimbursed by the state. Awards are made through a competitive selection process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, railroads, business and commercial interests, non-profit organizations, Maryland State agencies, and Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs) involved in freight rail.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Railroad corridor preservation, economic development, sustainability, and innovative technologies in freight rail networks. Projects should support one or more focus areas: Expansion of Rail Service or Rail Served Businesses; Safety and Security; System Preservation and Modernization; Environmental Protection and Sensitivity; or Fiscal Responsibility. Projects should align with goals and objectives in the Maryland Transportation Plan, Maryland State Freight Plan, and Maryland State Rail Plan. Not for routine or ongoing maintenance unless utilizing innovative technologies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. All counties are eligible.
requirements_list: Projects must be selected through a competitive process
Applicants must provide a minimum 20% local cash match (cash match required; projects with more than 20% match receive preferred consideration)
Applicants must demonstrate project readiness by uploading the Project Readiness Form and any relevant permit documentation
Projects must align with goals in the Maryland Transportation Plan, Maryland State Freight Plan, and Maryland State Rail Plan
Design projects must be completed within 2 years of grant award
Construction projects must be completed within 3 years of grant award

For Design Projects: Scope of Work/Detailed Project Description, Anticipated Schedule/Duration, Preliminary Cost Estimate, and Agreements (MOU/Local Support Letter/Railroad Support/Cost Sharing or Local Match Agreements) must be submitted

For Construction Projects: Scope of Work/Detailed Project Description, Anticipated Schedule/Duration, Preliminary Cost Estimate, Agreements (MOU/Local Support Letter/Railroad Support/Cost Sharing or Local Match Agreements), Property Certification, Environmental Permitting documentation, Final Contracting/Advertisement Plan, Preliminary Design Plans, and other applicable certifications must be submitted
Applicants must have a OneStop portal account to apply
Applicants must provide cost estimates including cash-flows for all years requesting funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Maryland OneStop Portal (https://onestop.md.gov/). Step-by-step process: 1) Register or login to OneStop Portal account (no fee required); 2) Search for 'Freight Rail Grant Program' on the portal; 3) Review instructions, resources, and links provided; 4) Click 'Apply Now' button to begin application; 5) Complete the application form with project details including project name, sponsor, point of contact, location, project type (Design or Construction), scope of work, cost information, project readiness documentation, and additional details; 6) Upload required documents and supporting materials (cost estimates with cash-flows, Project Readiness Form, permit documentation, maps, scope of work documents); 7) Save draft at any time before deadline by accessing https://onestop.md.gov/dashboard; 8) Sign and submit completed application before deadline. Application resources and guidance documents are available to assist applicants, including Application Questions Form, Resource and Guidance Document, Project Readiness Checklist, FAQ, and OneStop Portal How-To guide. After submission, applications are reviewed and evaluated from May through August, with grant awards announced in September-October. Project selection will be informed by how well projects support progress on prioritized actions and strategies of statewide and local plans.

structured_extraction.program_description: An initiative launched in 2024 that provides funding for local jurisdictions to hire Safe Routes to School coordinators. The coordinators lead SRTS strategies, work with schools, manage programming, and prioritize infrastructure improvements around schools. The program is part of Maryland's Vision Zero initiative and uses the Safe System Approach to improve safety for students traveling to and from school.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Transportation Alternatives Program (TAP) funds are allocated to cover 80% of the salary for an SRTS coordinator hired by eligible local jurisdictions. The local government must cover the remaining 20% of coordinator salary costs. The coordinator position is used to lead local Safe Routes to School strategies, work directly with schools and communities, manage programming, and prioritize infrastructure improvements around schools.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and local governments interested in establishing Safe Routes to School coordination positions. The program serves school communities, families, students, and community members who benefit from safer routes to school.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salary costs for hiring an SRTS coordinator to lead local strategies, work with schools, manage programming, prioritize school infrastructure improvements, conduct walking audits, develop SRTS action plans, engage communities in awareness campaigns, coordinate community events, manage school selection processes, and coordinate funding and resources for pedestrian and bicycle safety improvements around schools.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide in Maryland. As of 2026, four Maryland counties have joined the pilot program to hire coordinators.
requirements_list: Local government must provide 20% salary match
Coordinator position is used to lead SRTS strategies
Coordinator works directly with schools and communities
Coordinator conducts walking audits and develops SRTS action plans for selected schools
Coordinator identifies school champions before implementing SRTS plans

Coordinator engages stakeholders including county department of transportation, local school system, local health department, local planning agency, Maryland Center for School Safety, and law enforcement
Coordinator forms working group with key stakeholders and holds routine meetings (minimum quarterly)
Coordinator may establish a public taskforce for community-wide engagement
Coordinator evaluates school selection based on safety needs, community requests, demographics, voluntary participation, community school designations, Title 1 status, or existing programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local jurisdictions work with Maryland Department of Transportation and Maryland State Highway Administration to apply for the pilot program and coordinate coordinator hiring. Jurisdictions should identify their stakeholder group and determine school selection criteria. An SRTS coordinator, once hired, should assemble key stakeholders, form a working group for routine meetings, select schools based on established criteria, conduct walking audits, identify school champions, develop SRTS action plans, and coordinate community-wide engagement and resource coordination activities.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) offers grants to support tree planting efforts in communities that have been impacted by transportation construction projects, in partnership with the Maryland Urban and Community Forest Committee (MUCFC). The program helps replant trees lost due to transportation infrastructure projects, supports Maryland's Five Million Trees initiative, and advances MDOT's sustainability goals. Eligible areas include communities impacted by the Purple Line construction, urban heat islands, or environmental justice concerns.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $5,000 are available for tree planting projects. Pocket forest projects may request additional funding based on scope. Funds cover tree/plant material, supplies, signage, and maintenance costs (up to 1 year for individual trees, up to 3 years for pocket forests). Up to 5% of the grant may be used for volunteer outreach, signage, or project promotion. Plants should be purchased from state facilities when possible (seedlings $18-50 from state nursery or Tree-Mendous MD Program). Replanting may occur on both public and private property with landowner approval. Final reimbursement requires submission of expenses with bills, receipts, and contracts. Recipients must submit a survivability report one year after completion or future funding opportunities may be impacted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are due February 15 for Spring planting and July 15 for Fall planting. Applications are accepted year-round on a rolling basis for consideration in these planting seasons.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, schools, community/neighborhood associations, community business associations, homeowners associations, business service, youth and civic groups, institutions of higher education, counties, municipalities, forest conservancy district boards, and community members in areas where trees were lost due to transportation construction projects, particularly those experiencing urban heat islands or environmental justice concerns.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tree planting and pocket forest planting projects, including native plant material, supplies, maintenance costs (watering, weeding, mulching for up to 1 year for trees or 3 years for pocket forests), soil amendments and mulch for pocket forests, volunteer outreach, signage, and project promotion (up to 5% of grant).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; projects must be in communities where a state transportation project removed trees (including highways, transit, bridges, tunnels, airports, seaports, park & rides, bike/walking paths, or mass transit projects). Priority is given to projects in areas affected by environmental justice issues, urban heat islands, or communities impacted by the Purple Line construction. Trees can be replanted on both public and private lands with appropriate approvals.
requirements_list: Project must involve replanting trees in areas where removal occurred as part of state transportation facility construction, operation, or maintenance activities
Planted tree species must be native to the area and non-invasive; MDOT preferred plants list should be consulted at https://www.roads.maryland.gov/OED/Preferred_Plant.pdf
Must obtain approval from the county Forestry Board before the application deadline
Projects with matching funds or in-kind support receive preference
Funding cannot be used for required mitigation planting
Replanting may occur on public or private property with landowner approval
All funded projects must be approved by MUCFC and signed by county Forestry Board before project begins
Final report due one month after proposed completion date with project description, number and species of trees planted, photos, itemized expenses with receipts and contracts
Survivability report required one year following completion date; failure to submit impacts future funding eligibility
For pocket forest projects, maintenance plan must cover 3 years; for tree planting projects, 1 year maximum
All signage funded through grant must include MUCFC and MDOT logos
Applicants must be eligible organizations (non-profits, schools, associations, higher education institutions, municipalities, counties, forest conservancy district boards)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted year-round on a rolling basis and reviewed twice annually on or around January 15 for spring planting and July 15 for fall planting. Step 1: Contact your local county Forestry Board for assistance (http://www.marylandforestryboards.org/chairs.cfm). Step 2: Develop your project and obtain Forestry Board approval/signature. Step 3: Submit application form and supporting materials by the deadline, including: project description identifying the specific MDOT transportation facility project that impacted your community, simple site plan and photo of proposed planting site, list of proposed native plants with species and sizes, permit status if applicable, detailed maintenance plan for 1 year (trees) or 3 years (pocket forests) with expected costs and responsible persons, itemized budget showing tree costs, supplies, signage, and maintenance costs, financial information including matching funds/in-kind support, and number of volunteers. Step 4: Mail finalized form to Wanda MacLachlan, MUCFC, 11975 Homewood Road, Ellicott City, MD 21042. Step 5: After funding, complete project and submit final report one month after completion with actual number/species of trees, photos, and all expenses with receipts. Step 6: Submit survivability report one year after completion. For questions, contact Nick Kurtz at nkurtz@mdot.maryland.gov, Allison Gost at allison.gost@maryland.gov, or the Tree Equity Specialist.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Commuter Tax Credit (Commuter Choice Maryland)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state tax credit program administered through the Commuter Choice Maryland initiative that rewards Maryland employers who subsidize their employees' commuting costs. Employers can claim a tax credit equal to 50% of commuter subsidies provided to employees, up to $100 per employee per month. Eligible subsidies include transit passes, vanpool costs, guaranteed ride home programs, telework support, carpool arrangements, active transportation benefits (biking/walking), cash in lieu of parking, and multimodal commuter last mile connections. The program also provides technical support and recognition for employers implementing commuter benefits programs, including planning assistance, employee survey tools, and site assessments. Federal law additionally allows employers to offer employees up to $265 per month as a pre-tax deduction or tax-free subsidy for transit, vanpools, and eligible parking.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers receive a tax credit equal to 50% of commuter subsidies provided to employees, with a maximum of $100 per employee per month. The credit can be taken against state personal income tax, corporate income tax, or insurance premium tax. Non-profit 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) organizations submit Maryland State forms 508CR and MW508. For-profit businesses submit Maryland State Form 500CRW. The credit can also be filed against the Insurance Premium Tax in accordance with COMAR 31.06.04.03. Sole proprietorships, corporations, tax-exempt nonprofit organizations, and pass-through entities such as partnerships, sub-chapter S corporations, limited liability companies and business trusts may also claim the tax credit. Federal law allows employers to offer employees up to $265 per month as a pre-tax deduction or tax-free subsidy for transit, vanpools, and eligible parking, and money spent on transit benefits is exempt from payroll taxes. The program also provides free technical assistance to help employers develop or expand commuter benefits programs, including employee surveys, site assessments, planning tools, and public recognition of employer leadership. If the credit exceeds the state tax liability, the unused credit may not be carried forward to any other tax year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration for the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit should be completed annually; rolling for employer partner program. Income tax credit is available only on an electronically-filed income tax return for the tax year in which the credit is being claimed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland employers, including for-profit businesses and non-profit 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) organizations, that provide or wish to provide commuter benefits to their employees. Also available to government employers and individual commuters. Sole proprietorships, corporations, pass-through entities such as partnerships, sub-chapter S corporations, limited liability companies and business trusts may also claim the tax credit.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To offset the cost of providing commuter subsidies such as public or private mass transit passes, vanpool costs, guaranteed ride home programs, telework support (internet costs, computer equipment, telephone costs, software, supplies, co-working space memberships), carpool arrangements, active transportation benefits (biking/walking, e-scooters - including bicycle maintenance, shared bicycle/scooter membership, bicycling gear such as helmets, hydration packs, spare tubes, patch kits, pumps, tire levers, cycling multitools, bike shoes, gloves, saddle bags, reflective accessories and locks; walking gear including reflective accessories and walking/running shoes), cash in lieu of parking, and multimodal commuter last mile connections (ride hail services for up to five miles). Technical assistance funds support employee surveys, site assessments, and commuter benefits program development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. All commutes must take place on weekdays between 5 a.m. and 7 p.m. Qualified benefits must meet the purpose of transporting employees from their residence or designated meeting place (e.g., Park and Ride Lot) to or from their place of employment in Maryland.
requirements_list: Employer must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Taxation OR be an organization exempt from taxation under § 501(c)(3) or (4) of the Internal Revenue Code
Employer must provide qualified commuter benefits to employees

Qualified benefits include: (1) Public or Private Mass Transit - subsidizing the cost of transit on publicly or privately-owned mass transit systems except taxi services; (2) Vanpool - employer-funded programs with seating capacity of six individual adults with at least three employees being transported together (at least one-half of vehicle adult seating capacity); (3) Guaranteed Ride Home - providing immediate transportation for an employee who participates in commuter benefits and must leave work early for illness or other verifiable emergency; (4) Cash in Lieu of Parking - providing cash allowance equal to the parking subsidy the employer would otherwise pay; (5) Telework - providing telework subsidy to cover prorated costs (internet, computer equipment, telephone, software, supplies, co-working space membership); (6) Carpool - employer-funded program where commute is shared with two or more individuals for more than 80% of the trip, with costs including E-ZPass/toll fees, parking fees, or other carpooling costs, and participating carpoolers registered with Commuter Connections Ridesharing Program; (7) Active Transportation - providing subsidies for bicycle maintenance, shared bicycle/scooter membership, bicycling/walking gear (helmets, hydration packs, bottles with cages, spare tubes, patch kits, pumps, tire levers, cycling multitools, bike shoes, gloves, saddle bags, reflective accessories, locks, walking/running shoes); (8) Multimodal Commuter Last Mile Connection - providing subsidies for ride hail service up to five miles to connect commuter to work or multimodal option
Workplace must be located in Maryland
Credit is limited to 50% of employer contribution, maximum $100 per employee per month
Transit benefits up to $265 per month are pre-tax and exempt from payroll taxes under federal law (as of January 1, 2019)
Employers must register annually to receive the tax credit using the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit Registration Form available at CommuterChoiceMaryland.com
Income tax credit is available only on an electronically-filed income tax return for the tax year in which the credit is being claimed
All commutes must take place on weekdays between 5 a.m. and 7 p.m.
For vanpools: seating capacity must be six individual adults, at least three employees being transported together

For carpools: commute must be shared with two or more individuals for more than 80% of the trip, participating carpoolers must be registered with Commuter Connections Ridesharing Program, reimbursement for maintaining or purchasing a vehicle used for carpooling is not an eligible expense
For multimodal last mile connections: ride hail service can be used for up to five miles of a multimodal commuter trip
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Employers gather necessary business information, types of commuter subsidies provided, and subsidy amounts. 2) Employers complete the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit Registration Form electronically at CommuterChoiceMaryland.com. Employers must re-register annually. 3) Commuter Choice Maryland reviews the application. When approved, the employer receives an email certificate qualifying them for the tax credit. 4) When filing annual taxes, the employer includes the certificate with the appropriate Maryland State tax forms: Form 508CR attached to Form MW508 for 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) organizations, or Form 500CRW for all other Maryland businesses. For tax-exempt organizations claiming credit against state and local taxes withheld, Form MW508CR must be submitted with Form MW508 (Maryland Annual Employer Withholding Reconciliation Report), or if filing electronically, MW508CR must be filed with an amended MW508A. For insurance premium tax claims, documentation must be maintained by the taxpayer and made available to the Insurance Commissioner upon request per COMAR 31.06.04.03; information must be retained for a minimum of three years. 5) Contact Commuter Choice Maryland at (410) 865-1100, Monday-Friday 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., or commuterchoice@mdot.maryland.gov for assistance building, expanding, or promoting commuter benefits programs, or for questions about completing registration and tax forms.

Must have successfully completed one semester of graduate-level courses

Must be able to successfully complete a background check

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Highway Safety Office (MHSO) General Safety Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: A 100% reimbursable grant program that funds behavioral safety projects aimed at improving traffic safety in Maryland. The program focuses on key highway safety priorities including impaired driving prevention, distracted driving prevention, speeding and aggressive driving prevention, occupant protection, and the safety of pedestrians, bicyclists, motorcyclists, young and older drivers. Projects may also support Safe Routes to School initiatives and must use proven NHTSA countermeasures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 100% reimbursable grant program with no required local match. Grants are provided on a reimbursement basis — recipients must spend the money first and then be reimbursed. Funds cover eligible behavioral safety projects and activities in full.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Government agencies, non-profits, colleges, universities, hospitals, schools, communities, and organizations seeking to improve traffic safety behavior in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Behavioral safety pilot projects, safety campaigns, educational materials, outreach projects focused on highway safety priorities including impaired driving, distracted driving, speeding, aggressive driving, occupant protection, pedestrian safety, bicyclist safety, motorcyclist safety, young and older driver safety, and Safe Routes to School initiatives. Must use proven NHTSA countermeasures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must target behavior change through education, engagement, or enforcement
Projects must improve traffic safety in Maryland
The proposed project must address an identified highway safety priority
Projects must relate to Safe Routes to School initiatives where applicable
Must use proven NHTSA countermeasures
The proposal must include strategies, action steps, and measurable outcomes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should first plan their project by considering the safety problem, target population, proposed solution, and evaluation methods. Contact a technical advisor at the Maryland Highway Safety Office for assistance. Applications are submitted through the online 'Grant & Projects for Safety' portal within the Motor Vehicle Administration.
