structured_extraction.program_name: Multimodal Project Discretionary Grant (MPDG) / Infrastructure for Rebuilding America (INFRA)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program supporting major transportation and port infrastructure projects that improve safety, reliability, freight movement, and multimodal connectivity. Projects include bridge rehabilitation, drawbridge improvements, toll modernization, port wharf improvements, and other critical corridor infrastructure enhancements across Maryland. Eligible projects must demonstrate significant transportation benefits, cost-effectiveness, and alignment with federal safety and infrastructure priorities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants supporting major transportation infrastructure projects. Applicants request federal funding as a percentage of total project costs. Example: I-895 Baltimore Harbor Tunnel project requested $80 million in federal funding for a $160 million project (50.9% federal share). Assistance covers design, construction, and reconstruction of roadway infrastructure including bridge replacement, toll system modernization, interchange improvements, pavement rehabilitation, drainage and utility upgrades, intelligent traffic systems, safety improvements, and related transportation infrastructure enhancements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state transportation authorities, including the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA), Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT), and other state agencies responsible for major transportation infrastructure projects. Projects must demonstrate regional significance and support critical transportation corridors in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge rehabilitation, reconstruction, and replacement; toll system modernization and conversion to all-electronic tolling (AET); interchange design and geometric improvements; pavement reconstruction and rehabilitation; drainage system construction; intelligent traffic system deployment; traffic signal installation; over-height vehicle detection systems; safety improvements at grade crossings; utility relocations; traffic barriers and retaining walls; and related major transportation infrastructure enhancements that improve safety, reduce congestion, facilitate freight movement, and enhance regional economic connectivity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland transportation corridor projects are eligible. Projects must be located on or contribute to the National Highway System or support critical regional transportation needs. Priority consideration for projects in Opportunity Zones, Empowerment Zones, Areas of Persistent Poverty, and Environmental Justice communities.
requirements_list: Project must address critical corridor or infrastructure needs with demonstrated transportation challenges
Project must improve safety, mobility, freight movement, or economic connectivity
Project must demonstrate cost-effectiveness with benefit-cost ratio analysis
Detailed engineering and design plans required (minimum 30% design completion)
National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) review and environmental compliance documentation required
Cost estimates and benefit documentation required including safety, economic, and operational benefits
Project must be included in State Transportation Improvement Program (STIP) and regional Transportation Improvement Program (TIP)
Applicants must demonstrate project readiness and timeline for implementation
Environmental Justice community impacts and equity considerations required
Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE) utilization and workforce development commitments required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit comprehensive project applications to the U.S. Department of Transportation including: detailed project description addressing transportation challenges; complete engineering plans and cost estimates; benefit-cost analysis using USDOT-prescribed 7% discount rate; NEPA compliance documentation; evidence of STIP/TIP inclusion; statement of work demonstrating project readiness; timeline for implementation; and documentation of community engagement and equity considerations. Applications must demonstrate alignment with USDOT outcome criteria including safety, state of good repair, economic impacts and freight movement, climate and environmental benefits, equity and quality of life, and innovation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive federal grant program supporting the modernization, upgrade, and operational improvement of port facilities and related intermodal connections. The program funds projects that enhance the movement of goods through ports, improve cargo handling capabilities to accommodate larger vessels, and address safety, efficiency, reliability, and resilience of freight operations. It also supports emissions reduction and electrification infrastructure investments, as well as planning and development-phase activities.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive federal grants supporting port infrastructure upgrades including berth modernization, dredging, fascia walls, crane modifications, concrete pile and cap beam repairs, steel sheet pile toe wall installation, fender systems, and mooring infrastructure to accommodate larger vessels such as Ultra Large Container Vessels (ULCVs). Supports intermodal freight connections, operational improvements, and resilience measures addressing environmental and climate-related risks. Eligible uses include planning and development-phase activities such as feasibility analyses, environmental review, and preliminary engineering, as well as investments in emissions reduction technologies and electrification infrastructure. The Seagirt Marine Terminal Berth I/II Modernization Project example demonstrates typical funding with a Federal contribution of $25 million toward a total project cost of $58.25 million. Projects are evaluated based on ability to address freight mobility needs, deliver measurable economic and operational benefits, align with regional and national freight priorities, and demonstrate readiness, financial commitment, and technical capacity.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Port authorities, government agencies, terminal operators, and port-related entities seeking to improve freight operations and modernize port facilities. Eligible applicants include port administration agencies, terminal operators, and private port-related businesses with capacity to deliver infrastructure improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Port infrastructure upgrades including berth modernization, structural repairs to concrete piles and cap beams, dredging to accommodate larger vessels, fascia wall modifications, crane beam installations, steel sheet pile toe wall installation, fender systems, mooring devices; intermodal freight connections; operational improvements; resilience measures; planning and development activities including feasibility analyses, environmental review, and preliminary engineering; and investments in emissions reduction and electrification infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland port facilities are eligible, with specific relevance to the Port of Baltimore and facilities like Seagirt Marine Terminal. Projects must enhance movement of goods through ports and related intermodal connections and support capacity expansion to handle Ultra Large Container Vessels (ULCVs).
requirements_list: Projects must address freight mobility needs and accommodate larger vessel sizes
Must deliver measurable economic and operational benefits and capacity improvements
Must align with regional and national freight priorities
Must demonstrate readiness, financial commitment, and technical capacity
Project applicant must have established financial commitment (cost-share from non-federal sources)
Environmental compliance and dredging permits required
Engineering plans and preliminary design must be completed or in advanced stages
Projects should target capacity expansion to meet projected demand thresholds
Applicants must demonstrate long-term operational viability and maintenance capability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted through Grants.gov by June 1, 2026. Submissions should include detailed engineering plans, cost estimates, environmental compliance documentation, evidence of financial commitment and cost-share arrangements, and project readiness information. Applications should demonstrate how the project addresses freight mobility constraints, delivers economic benefits, and aligns with regional freight priorities. Sponsoring agencies and operators should coordinate on submissions.

Cybersecurity and operational protocols needed
75% Federal funding requirement with 25% State cost match

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Works and Economic Adjustment Assistance Program

structured_extraction.program_name: Railway-Highway Crossings (Section 130) Program / Railroad Crossing Elimination (RCE)
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program providing funds for the elimination of hazards at public railway-highway crossings and safety improvements at highway-rail grade crossings. Funds are apportioned to each state by formula under Section 130 and prioritized based on safety criteria and available funding. The program also supports feasibility studies for long-term crossing elimination or consolidation, grade separation design and construction, and enhancement of signaling and warning systems at public rail crossings throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants apportioned to Maryland for the elimination of hazards at public railway-highway crossings, grade crossing safety feature enhancements, signaling and warning system upgrades, and feasibility studies for grade separation or crossing elimination and consolidation. Project funding is provided to support preliminary engineering, NEPA re-evaluation, final design, and construction of safety improvements including flashing light signals, automatic roadway gates, bells, and signage at public rail crossings. Projects are prioritized based on safety criteria (including crash history, injury and fatality rates, and HAZMAT exposure) and available funding. Example: The Rosedale Maryland Grade Crossing Improvement Project requested $2,958,969 in federal RCE Program funding (79% of total project cost of $3,758,969) for immediate safety enhancements at four private highway-rail grade crossings and a long-term grade crossing elimination and consolidation study. Safety benefits from enhancements are projected at $17.9 million over 30 years, with potential for $22.1 million in benefits if grade separations and closures are implemented.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not specified; NOFO (Notice of Funding Opportunity) cycles announced periodically
structured_extraction.program_audience: State transportation agencies, public roadway owners, local jurisdictions, railroad operators (CSXT and other freight rail operators), and Baltimore County responsible for railway-highway crossings with documented safety issues, high crash rates, or fatalities and injuries.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Elimination of hazards at public railway-highway crossings; grade crossing safety improvements including installation of flashing light signals, automatic roadway gates, bells, signage, and roadway markings; signaling and warning systems; elimination and consolidation feasibility studies; grade separation design and construction; preliminary engineering and NEPA documentation; final design and construction of safety improvements; project administration and management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All public railway-highway crossings in Maryland. Projects are evaluated and prioritized based on crash history, injury/fatality rates, economic impact, and HAZMAT exposure at specific crossings. Example project locations include private crossings on CSXT's Philadelphia Subdivision in Baltimore County near Rosedale, MD.
requirements_list: Projects must be at public or private railway-highway crossings
Applicant must be a state transportation agency or local jurisdiction with authority over the crossing
Projects prioritized based on safety criteria including documented crash history, injury and fatality rates, and HAZMAT exposure
Crossing must demonstrate high-risk conditions (e.g., crashes above state average, recent fatalities or injuries)
Safety feature enhancement or grade separation study required
Preliminary engineering design and NEPA documentation must be completed or committed to prior to final design and construction phases
49 U.S.C. 22905-compliant Railroad Agreement executed or pending with host railroad operator
Project must be programmed in state or regional planning documents (State Rail Plan, State Freight Plan, TIP, STIP, or Long Range Transportation Plan)
Non-federal match funding must be committed from state, local, or railroad partners
Applicant must demonstrate project readiness including NEPA clearance, environmental permitting status, and timeline for agreement execution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Rail Safety Program Manager (Stacey Beckett) to inquire about current funding opportunities and project eligibility. Monitor the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) website for periodic issuance of Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) announcements for the Railroad Crossing Elimination Program. Submit a competitive application package to FRA that includes: project summary; applicant and project eligibility criteria documentation; detailed project description with safety analysis and proposed improvements; grade crossing information and safety data; evaluation and selection criteria responses (addressing project readiness, technical merit, project benefits, safety analysis, climate/sustainability, equity, workforce development); project implementation and management plan; budget and funding sources; NEPA status or commitment; railroad agreement status; evidence of non-federal match funding commitment; and supporting documentation such as crash data, cost estimates, and engineering plans. Applications are evaluated based on safety benefits (crash reduction, fatality/injury prevention), project readiness (NEPA clearance, agreements executed), technical merit, climate and sustainability benefits, equity considerations, and workforce development potential. Successful applicants receive federal grant funding with project implementation typically occurring over 18-24 months depending on project phase (planning, design, or construction).

structured_extraction.program_description: A suite of incentive programs administered by the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) designed to help Baltimore-area commuters and employers explore sustainable commuting methods including carpool, vanpool, and transit. The program encompasses three main components: (1) Vanpool savings of approximately $500 per month; (2) Carpooler daily incentives of $5 for up to 90 days; (3) CharmPass New Rider Incentive offering free transit passes to first-time MTA transit users in the Greater Baltimore area during select promotional periods; and (4) FareShare Employer Incentive providing up to $3,000 in credits over three consecutive months to employers purchasing transit passes for their employees. Transit passes are valid on Baltimore local transit services including City Bus, Local Bus, Express Bus, Light Rail, Metro Subway, Commuter Bus, and MARC Train. Participating employers are also registered as MDOT Commuter Choice Maryland Employer Partner Program members, gaining access to free resources and recognition.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple incentive types are available: (1) Vanpool participants save approximately $500 per month. (2) Carpoolers earn $5 daily incentives for up to 90 days. (3) New transit riders receive free CharmPass transit passes loaded directly onto their CharmPass mobile app account; passes expire 90 days after receipt and are not redeemable for cash or transferable to other users. Promotional enrollment windows: May 1–8, 2026; June 1–8, 2026; July 1–8, 2026. (4) Employers receive up to $3,000 in credits ($1,000 per month over three continuous months) applied to their CharmPass account to purchase transit passes (City Bus, Local Bus, Express Bus, Light Rail, Metro Subway, Commuter Bus, and MARC Train) for their employees. Employers must enroll by the 15th of the month prior to their starting month and submit purchase orders by the 25th of each month.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: CharmPass New Rider promotional periods: May 1–8, 2026; June 1–8, 2026; July 1–8, 2026 (can sign up for alerts outside promotional periods). FareShare Employer Incentive: ongoing; employers must enroll by the 15th of the month prior to their starting month.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore-area commuters looking for sustainable commuting methods (carpool, vanpool, or transit), first-time MTA transit users in the Greater Baltimore area, and employers with locations or employment centers in the Greater Baltimore area seeking to provide transit benefits to employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Incentives for sustainable commuting via carpool, vanpool, or transit; free transit passes for travel on MTA services (bus, metro, light rail, commuter bus, and MARC) in the Greater Baltimore region; employer credits to purchase transit passes for employees using MTA services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Greater Baltimore area accessible to MTA stations through local transit services, Commuter Bus, and MARC. Service area includes Baltimore City and Baltimore County. Employers must have locations or employment centers in the Greater Baltimore area accessible to MTA stations.
requirements_list: Must be a Baltimore-area commuter
Must use carpool, vanpool, or transit
For CharmPass New Rider: must be a first-time (new) user of the MTA transit system
For CharmPass New Rider: must download the CharmPass mobile application and create an account with email, name, and phone number
For CharmPass New Rider: must select desired type of transit pass
For CharmPass New Rider: account verification occurs within 48 hours, after which transit passes are loaded onto the CharmPass account
For CharmPass New Rider: free transit passes expire after 90 days
CharmPass products are not redeemable for cash or transferable to other users
For CharmPass New Rider: must participate in periodic brief surveys about transit experience
For FareShare Employer: employer must have locations or employment centers in Greater Baltimore area accessible to MTA stations through local transit, Commuter Bus, or MARC
For FareShare Employer: must express interest and contact MTA to set up a meeting
For FareShare Employer: must complete a quick questionnaire to set up an agreement
For FareShare Employer: must enroll by the 15th of the month prior to starting month
For FareShare Employer: must submit next month's transit pass purchase order by the 25th of each month
For FareShare Employer: employees must access CharmPass app and set up an account to use employer-provided passes
For FareShare Employer: must participate in periodic surveys about transit experience
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For CharmPass New Rider: (1) Be a first-time transit user. (2) Sign up through the online form during a promotional enrollment window (May 1–8, June 1–8, or July 1–8, 2026; sign up for alerts outside these windows). (3) Download the CharmPass mobile app and set up an account with email, name, and phone number, selecting the desired transit pass type. (4) Account verification occurs within 48 hours, after which free transit passes are loaded directly onto the CharmPass account. (5) Use passes to travel on MTA transit services. (6) Complete periodic brief surveys about transit experience. For FareShare Employer: (1) Confirm employer eligibility (locations in Greater Baltimore area accessible to MTA transit). (2) Express interest by emailing tso@mdot.maryland.gov or opc.mta@maryland.gov. (3) MTA will set up a meeting to discuss options. (4) Complete a quick questionnaire to set up an agreement. (5) Enroll by the 15th of the month prior to the starting month. (6) MTA verifies the employer account, applies the incentive as a credit, and loads fare products to employees' CharmPass accounts. (7) Employees access CharmPass app and set up accounts to use their passes. (8) Submit monthly purchase orders by the 25th of each month. (9) Participate in periodic surveys about transit experience. For carpool and vanpool programs, visit the respective program pages on the MDOT website to enroll.

structured_extraction.program_name: Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A)
structured_extraction.program_description: This competitive grant program, administered by the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) and supported by the Maryland Department of Transportation, provides funding to support comprehensive efforts aimed at reducing roadway fatalities and serious injuries for all users, including pedestrians, bicyclists, transit riders, and motorists. The program funds development and enhancement of Safety Action Plans, supplemental planning and demonstration initiatives, and implementation of projects and strategies identified through those plans. Implementation grants help build projects and fund operational strategies from an approved Safety Action Plan, including project feasibility, design, and development. Planning grants support creation or update of Safety Action Plans, safety audits, and demonstration activities such as feasibility studies using quick-build strategies, MUTCD engineering studies, pilot programs for behavior or operational activities, and pilot projects utilizing innovative technologies. The program emphasizes data-driven, systemwide approaches grounded in the Safe System Approach, with a focus on improving safety outcomes, advancing equitable investments, and supporting innovative, scalable solutions across communities of varying sizes and capacities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive federal grant funding providing two types of grants with an 80/20% federal/local cost share. Implementation grants construct projects or fund operational strategies identified in an approved Safety Action Plan, including project feasibility, design, and development, and may also fund supplemental planning and demonstration activities as a component of the grant. Planning grants develop or update Safety Action Plans, fund supplemental planning activities including plan updates, topical sub-plans, and road safety audits, and fund demonstration activities that inform Safety Action Plan development through data collection. Eligible demonstration activities include feasibility studies using quick-build strategies (paint, plastic posts, delineators, removable barriers, reallocation of roadway space), MUTCD engineering studies evaluating high-visibility crosswalks and bike lane treatments, pilot programs for behavior or operational activities that include at least one element of the Safe System Approach, and pilot projects utilizing innovative technologies not yet adopted in the community such as speed cameras, variable speed limits, adaptive signal timing, and adaptive lighting. Approximately $1 billion in guaranteed funding is available annually through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Metropolitan planning organizations, political subdivisions of a state (local jurisdictions), Tribal governments, and multijurisdictional combinations of eligible applicants seeking to reduce roadway fatalities and serious injuries for all users including pedestrians, bicyclists, transit riders, and motorists.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development and enhancement of Safety Action Plans, supplemental planning and demonstration initiatives, and implementation of projects and strategies to reduce roadway fatalities and serious injuries. Demonstration activities may include feasibility studies using quick-build strategies (paint, plastic posts, delineators, removable barriers, reallocation of roadway space), MUTCD engineering studies evaluating high-visibility crosswalks and bike lane treatments, pilot programs for behavioral or operational safety activities that include at least one element of the Safe System Approach, and pilot projects utilizing innovative technologies such as speed cameras, variable speed limits, adaptive signal timing, and adaptive lighting.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; all communities of varying sizes and capacities. Jurisdictions proposing projects on state facilities are highly encouraged and required for implementation to receive state concurrence.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's TOD Designation Program provides state recognition of intentional efforts by a local jurisdiction to advance Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) at eligible sites. TOD Designation unlocks opportunities for State support, including MDOT's TOD Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides state recognition and designation status that unlocks eligibility for MDOT's TOD Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund, additional points in competitive application rounds for the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Low Income Housing Tax Credit program, additional points from DGS when evaluating requests for proposals to lease or purchase office or laboratory space, and priority advocacy with MDOT and associate modes in supporting development. Once approved, a State TOD Designation is applicable for 10 years. Upon expiration, jurisdictions can apply to have their Designation extended for an additional 10 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and multicounty agencies with land use and planning authority seeking state recognition and support for Transit-Oriented Development sites
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The designation status enables access to funding for TOD infrastructure and development projects through associated MDOT capital grants and revolving loan funds. Funds support implementation of comprehensive TOD plans including land use development, pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure, housing creation, parking strategies, transit connectivity, green infrastructure, and economic development initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property that is adjacent to the passenger boarding and alighting location of a planned or existing transit station, or any part of which is located within one-half mile of a planned or existing transit station, or property adjacent to a planned or existing transit corridor. Transit corridor is defined as a geographically bound set of two or more contiguous subway, light rail, bus rapid transit or bus transit stations, or a set of two or more contiguous bus transit stations with fixed-route bus service on a roadway dedicated to buses.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction or multicounty agency with land use and planning responsibility

Must develop a deliberate plan or strategy for Transit-Oriented Development addressing nine required categories: land use and development proposal, pedestrian and bicycle connectivity, parking strategy, transit mode connectivity, housing creation and affordability goals, consistency with local and regional plans, green infrastructure, 10-year action plan with community engagement and enabling projects, and economic development strategy
Local legislative body must adopt a resolution in support of State TOD Designation
Plan must maximize the use of transit, walking, and bicycling by residents and employees
For transit corridor designations, jurisdictions must request a pre-application meeting with MDOT before submitting formal application
Applicants should demonstrate comprehensive planning and development vision throughout corridor including both station areas and parcels connecting station areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local jurisdictions develop a deliberate plan or strategy addressing nine required categories (land use, pedestrian/bicycle connectivity, parking, transit modes, housing, plan consistency, green infrastructure, action plan, and economic development) and obtain adoption of a resolution by the local legislative body. The jurisdiction submits a complete application via the online TOD Designation Application Form at https://forms.mdot.maryland.gov/TOD, providing responses to nine application questions and uploading supporting documents for each category. MDOT circulates the plan to MTA, SHA, and Sustainable Growth Subcabinet agencies for feedback. MDOT staff work with the applicant to address any feedback before developing a recommendation to the Sustainable Growth Subcabinet. The Sustainable Growth Subcabinet takes official action to approve or deny applications, issuing a resolution with approval decision and may offer comments on how to improve the TOD project and provide guidance on use of State resources. Once approved, a State TOD Designation is applicable for 10 years; jurisdictions can apply to extend designations for an additional 10 years upon expiration.

structured_extraction.program_name: Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to local jurisdictions and development partners to promote equitable and inclusive development at State-designated transit-oriented development sites across Maryland. The program includes both a capital grant component for public infrastructure and design improvements and a revolving loan fund component to provide gap financing for development projects at the 17 State-designated TOD sites.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The TOD Fund is a $5 million annual statewide competitive program. Local jurisdictions may receive grants for design plans (up to $250,000 with 10% local match) or public infrastructure improvements (up to $750,000 in grant funds with 10% local match plus an additional $250,000 in loans for non-revenue projects; or up to $1,000,000 in loans for revenue-generating infrastructure projects). Development partners applying with a local jurisdiction as co-applicant may receive loans for gap funding (up to $1,000,000). Loans are offered at Treasury interest rates with flexible repayment terms of 3-5 years, depending on use and loan amount. Grants are provided as reimbursement for eligible costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 5 - April 8, 2025 for FY25; additional rounds anticipated
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and development partners working on transit-oriented development projects, including private entities, nonprofit entities, and developers pursuing transit-oriented development projects at State-designated TOD sites
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design plans and planning/design tasks for TOD projects; public infrastructure improvements including transit station parking, station access improvements, strategic parking improvements, station boarding area improvements, bus loop construction, and pedestrian safety improvements; and gap funding for development projects that advance local jurisdiction TOD Designation Plan goals including affordable housing, public infrastructure, or density goals
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must directly benefit a State-designated TOD site as shown on the Maryland Designated TOD Map. Maryland has 17 Designated Transit-Oriented Development sites statewide as of January 2025. Projects must be within one-half mile of the passenger boarding and alighting location of a planned or existing transit station, adjacent to such a station, or adjacent to a planned or existing transit corridor.

For design plans: must include at least one component of site-specific conceptual plans, drawings, renderings, or more advanced design and engineering studies
For public infrastructure: must be owned/operated by public sector or open to public and support a public service or public purpose
For gap funding: applicant must demonstrate need for financial assistance and how project advances TOD Designation Plan goals
Applicant must not be convicted of or under investigation for any criminal activity
Gap funding applicants must not be in default on any outstanding debt
Project site must have appropriate local zoning policy in place by close of application period
Local jurisdiction must commit to implement Complete Streets improvements where practicable

Must promote equitable and inclusive development aligned with one of three core equity and inclusion goals: access to transit for low-income and minority residents; access to transit in areas with affordable housing and diversity of job and educational opportunities; or encouraging development around underdeveloped and underutilized transit stations
Loan applicants must provide three consecutive years of consolidated or certified financial statements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Refer to the Maryland Designated TOD Map and GIS Tool to confirm project eligibility at a State-designated TOD site. 2. Review the NOFO and program webpage for detailed requirements and submission instructions. 3. Attend optional webinar (Webinar #1: February 14, 2025; Webinar #2: March 4, 2025) for clarification. 4. Prepare application including application form, commitment to Complete Streets policy, proof of appropriate zoning, and letters of support. For loan applications, provide three years of financial statements, organizational documents, board roster, IRS Form W-9, documentation of existing loans and liens, and explanation of repayment sources. 5. Submit completed application through the online portal at https://todfundrequest.powerappsportals.us/ by April 8, 2025 at 5 p.m. 6. Applications are reviewed and scored by an interagency review group using evaluation rubric based on project readiness (35 points), project budget and funding (20 points), and equity and inclusion goal attainment (45 points). 7. Award announcements in June 2025. 8. Award agreements signed June-July 2025. 9. Awardees submit updated work plan within 30 days of award and may begin procurement. 10. Reimbursable costs begin after award agreement is finalized. 11. Grantees submit quarterly invoices for reimbursement. Projects must be completed within 3 years or request extension from MDOT. Awardees required to submit quarterly status reports for life of grant award.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitively selected, federally funded reimbursement grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Transportation State Highway Administration. TAP provides funding for transportation alternative projects including pedestrian and bicycle facilities, recreational trails, safe routes to school initiatives, historic transportation building restoration, conversion of abandoned railway corridors to pedestrian trails, and mitigation of highway runoff. The program finances the planning, development, and implementation of projects and activities that improve safety and reduce traffic around schools, as well as broader active transportation infrastructure improvements statewide.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TAP funds award 80% of eligible project costs with a required 20% local match. The program is 80% reimbursable, meaning the funding covers four-fifths of eligible project expenses. Funding supports feasibility studies, design, construction, and safety awareness and program coordination projects. Projects are solicited on an annual basis.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Cheryl Ladota; Britney Jackson; Allison Gost
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, schools, communities, regional transportation authorities, transit agencies, natural resource and public land agencies, school districts, tribal governments, nonprofit organizations (501(c)(3)), and other local and governmental entities with oversight of transportation or recreational trails seeking to improve safety for students traveling to and from school and to develop alternative transportation options including bike and pedestrian infrastructure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Feasibility studies, design projects, construction projects, pedestrian and bicycle facilities, recreational trails, safe routes to school initiatives, historic transportation building restoration, conversion of abandoned railway corridors to pedestrian trails, mitigation of highway runoff, safety awareness and program coordination projects, and other non-traditional transportation improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: 20% local match required
Projects must relate to Safe Routes to School initiatives or other eligible transportation alternatives
Projects must improve safety or reduce traffic around schools (for SRTS projects)

Eligible applicants include local governments, regional transportation authorities, transit agencies, natural resource and public land agencies, school districts and local education agencies, tribal governments, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations, and other local and governmental entities with oversight of transportation or recreational trails
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted to the State Highway Administration's Grants and Programs Management (GPMD) Division through a competitive selection process. Projects are solicited on an annual basis. For the latest updates on funding, visit www.roads.maryland.gov/mdotsha/pages/index.aspx?PageId=144.

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal program supporting the procurement and installation of electric charging ports and ground support equipment to reduce airport emissions. This program funds electric ground support equipment (eGSE) charging infrastructure at commercial service airports to enable the conversion of conventional diesel and gasoline-powered GSE to zero-emission electric equivalents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants covering up to 75% of project costs for procurement and installation of electric charging infrastructure and related electrical system upgrades for airport ground support equipment. For example, the BWI Marshall project includes funding for 250 electric charging ports at an estimated total project cost of $21,675,000 ($14,652,000 for charger procurement and installation at $58,600 per charger, plus $7,023,000 for utility relocations and upgrades to provide approximately 8.3 megawatts of new electrical capacity). Local match requirement is 25% of total eligible project costs. Funding is provided through the FAA Airport Improvement Program (AIP) as part of the Voluntary Airport Low Emission (VALE) Program for commercial service airports. Eligible expenses include purchase and installation of chargers, site preparation, and required utility infrastructure development. Projects must comply with VALE Technical Report Version 7.0 requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 31, 2025 for FAA grant agreement execution and firm selection; May 31, 2027 for project completion
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public airport operators and authorities at commercial service airports, particularly those in EPA-designated nonattainment or maintenance areas for criteria pollutants
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of electric ground support equipment charging ports (chargers), site preparation, preconditioned air unit chargers, ground power unit chargers, related electrical infrastructure, electric utility upgrades and relocations to support charging network capacity. Funding covers infrastructure owned and operated by the airport; airlines purchase and operate the electric GSE vehicles themselves.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Commercial service airports in the United States, with priority for airports located in EPA-designated nonattainment or maintenance areas for criteria pollutants such as ozone, sulfur dioxide (SO2), and particulate matter (PM2.5). Maryland airports eligible; specific focus on BWI Marshall in Anne Arundel County, which is classified as marginal nonattainment for 8-hour ozone, nonattainment for SO2, and maintenance area for PM2.5.
requirements_list: Project must reduce airport emissions from ground support equipment
Airport must be a commercial service airport
Preference for airports in EPA-designated nonattainment or maintenance areas for criteria pollutants including ozone, SO2, or PM2.5
Project must meet Voluntary Airport Low Emission (VALE) Program eligibility criteria C.3.a.3(i) and all provisions of VALE Technical Report Version 7.0
Project must comply with Chapter 6 of VALE Technical Report Version 7.0
Electrical infrastructure must support simultaneous charging capability for all funded charger ports
Project must demonstrate commitment to sustainability and alignment with Federal, state, or local climate goals
All capital costs for eGSE vehicle purchases must be borne by airlines or other operators (not eligible for VALE funding)
Electronic monitoring equipment required to track electric consumption by individual eGSE units for operational cost recovery
No changes to Airport Layout Plan required; NEPA review typically addressed with Categorical Exclusion
Charging infrastructure must be permanently located and operated at the airport, not for public use
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit detailed project application to the FAA Office of Airports including: project narrative describing equipment specifications, installation plans, and environmental benefits; location maps showing airside charger hub locations; emissions reduction calculations using VALE Technical Report Version 7.0 methodology; cost estimates and financial plan with 25% local match commitment; schedule showing preliminary design, engineering, procurement, and installation milestones; regulatory compliance documentation. For BWI Marshall project: preliminary data collection (May-July 2024), design engineering (August 2024-January 2025), procurement (January-May 2025), bid review and FAA grant agreement execution (by May 31, 2025), charger delivery (June 2025-May 2026), electrical enabling work (June 2025-May 2026), charger installation (May 2026-December 2026). Final cost estimates replace preliminary estimates upon receipt of formal bids.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Section 5310 Program - Enhanced Mobility for Seniors and Individuals with Disabilities Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal transit program funded by the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) and administered in Maryland by the Maryland Department of Transportation Maryland Transit Administration (MDOT MTA), with regional coordination provided by bodies such as the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland. The program is designed to improve mobility for older adults and individuals with disabilities by supporting transportation services that go beyond the scope of traditional public transit. It funds capital projects (e.g., accessible vehicles, technology) and operating expenses (e.g., ride-sharing, volunteer driver programs) that address identified transportation gaps in both statewide and rural/underserved areas. Eligible applicants include private nonprofit organizations, state or local government authorities, and public transit agencies that can demonstrate coordination with other transportation and human service providers, financial and managerial capacity, and compliance with FTA guidelines.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Transportation Maryland Transit Administration (MDOT MTA)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual federal funding from the Federal Transit Administration is disbursed to successful applicants. Capital projects are funded at 80% federal and 20% local match; operating projects are funded at 50% federal and 50% local match. Funds may be used for capital expenses such as buses, vans, communication equipment, wheelchair lifts, vehicle maintenance, and computer hardware/software, as well as operating expenses such as accessible taxi services, ride-sharing, vanpooling, voucher programs, and volunteer driver programs. Projects must be consistent with regionally adopted long-range transportation plans and derived from coordinated public transit-human services transportation plans. The program aims to maximize the use of available funds, distribute funds in an equitable and effective manner, promote applications from a broad spectrum of interested agencies, establish criteria for evaluating applications, provide technical assistance to organizations through workshops and administrative assistance, and coordinate Maryland's efforts to provide quality human services transportation services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private nonprofit organizations, state or local government authorities, and public transit agencies that provide transportation services to seniors and individuals with disabilities, including organizations serving Western Maryland region (Garrett, Allegany, Washington Counties and rural parts of Frederick County). The program also serves individuals with disabilities, seniors, and people with low incomes who have unmet, insufficient, or inappropriate transportation needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and operating expenses for transportation services for seniors and individuals with disabilities. Capital: buses, vans, communication equipment, wheelchair lifts, vehicle maintenance, computer hardware/software, accessible vehicles, technology, and mobility management programs. Operating: accessible taxi services, ride-sharing, vanpooling, voucher programs, volunteer driver programs, and nontraditional services that expand or enhance transportation options.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; Western Maryland region (Garrett, Allegany, Washington Counties and rural parts of Frederick County) is served through Tri-County Council for Western Maryland coordination. Projects must address identified transportation gaps in both statewide and rural/underserved areas.
requirements_list: Applicants must provide a cash match of 20% for capital projects and 50% for operating projects.
Services cannot compete with existing public transit or private for-profit providers.
Applicants must follow federal rules, including Title VI of the Civil Rights Act and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).
Project must be derived from coordinated public transit-human services transportation plans.
Project must be consistent with regionally adopted long-range transportation plan.
Project must serve eligible elderly individuals, senior citizens, or people with disabilities.
Applicants must demonstrate coordination with other transportation and human service providers.
Applicants must demonstrate financial and managerial capacity to manage federal funds.
Vehicles or equipment purchased through the program must be maintained in compliance with FTA guidelines.
Projects selected for funding must be included in a locally developed, coordinated public transit-human services transportation plan.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants obtain the application package from the Transportation Association of Maryland (TAM) website and submit completed applications electronically through the MDOT MTA Grant Application Portal (mail or delivery not accepted). In the Western Maryland region, the Tri-County Council for Western Maryland coordinates a local review committee to review, score, and forward Section 5310 applications to MTA for consideration. The application process is competitive, and MDOT MTA conducts the evaluation to ensure applications meet all federal and state requirements.

Upon approval of a discharge upgrade, eligible veterans regain access to all Maryland state veterans benefits including educational benefits, health care, employment assistance, and other services administered by the department.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents or veterans eligible for Maryland state benefits.
requirements_list: Have an other-than-honorable (OTH), General Under Honorable Conditions (GUH), or Uncharacterized (UC) character of service

Discharge characterization resulted from Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI), Military Sexual Trauma (MST), sexual orientation or gender identity, or other criteria established in 38 C.F.R. § 3.12
Believe the discharge characterization was unjust, erroneous, or warrants an upgrade
Submit completed application packet with supporting documentation demonstrating service-connected condition or circumstances warranting discharge review
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Veterans access the fact sheet and application packet from the DVMF website, complete the required forms with supporting documentation, and mail the documents to the Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families DVMF Discharge Review Board at 16 Francis Street, 4th Floor, Annapolis, MD 21401. Free legal assistance is available through the University of Baltimore School of Law Bob Parsons Veterans Advocacy Clinic by emailing dva.army@maryland.gov or contacting the clinic directly. structured_extraction.program_name: Bay Restoration Fund - Wastewater Program (Enhanced Nutrient Removal)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment that provides up to 100 percent state funding for Enhanced Nutrient Removal (ENR) capital projects at wastewater treatment plants in Maryland to reduce nitrogen and phosphorus discharges into the Chesapeake Bay. The program funds upgrades to major and minor wastewater treatment plants with ENR technologies to achieve advanced nutrient removal levels of 3 mg/l total nitrogen and 0.3 mg/l total phosphorus. Eligible projects also include combined sewer overflow abatement, sewer rehabilitation, conveyance system upgrades including pumping stations, sewer extensions to connect homes on septic systems to treatment plants, and nitrogen reduction at shared community septic systems. The program also supports incremental costs of nutrient removal operations and maintenance. Funding is sourced from a $30 per year fee on homes and businesses connected to wastewater treatment plants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 100 percent state grant funds for eligible project costs including planning, design, and construction. Funds are provided on a reimbursable basis after the grantee submits a payment request. Funding applications are accepted December through January annually. Priority is given first to Enhanced Nutrient Removal upgrades at the 67 significant wastewater treatment plants (design flow of 500,000 gallons per day or greater) in Maryland. Once ENR upgrades are complete, starting in fiscal year 2018, funding is allocated to minor wastewater treatment plants for ENR upgrades. Remaining funds are allocated based on project priority ranking to improvements to existing wastewater systems, sewer extensions, and nitrogen reduction projects at shared community septic systems. Upgrades to existing sewerage distribution systems are funded up to $5 million per year through fiscal year 2009. Incremental costs of ENR operations and maintenance are funded up to 10 percent of annual revenue or approximately $6 million per year starting fiscal year 2010.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Publicly owned wastewater treatment plants and local governments managing wastewater treatment plants and sewerage systems that discharge to the Chesapeake Bay, as well as wastewater treatment plant operators and local governmental entities seeking to upgrade treatment infrastructure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, and construction costs for upgrading wastewater treatment plants with Enhanced Nutrient Removal technologies; combined sewer overflow abatement; sewer rehabilitation; conveyance system upgrades including pumping stations; sewer extensions to connect homes on septic systems to treatment plants; nitrogen reduction at shared community septic systems; upgrade of existing sewerage distribution systems; and incremental costs of Enhanced Nutrient Removal operations and maintenance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Priority funding for the 67 publicly owned wastewater treatment plants with design flow of 500,000 gallons per day or greater that discharge to the Chesapeake Bay. Projects must be consistent with county water and sewer plans and Maryland's Priority Places Strategy (Executive Order 01.01.2003.33).

The program approves and ranks BAT systems for removing nitrogen from onsite sewage dispersal systems, provides field verification of systems, and offers Bay Restoration Fund grants for eligible approved technologies that reduce total nitrogen in wastewater. Priority is given to failing systems located in Critical Areas. The BAT Technical Review Committee evaluates and ranks systems based on total nitrogen reduction capability, total cost including operation, maintenance, and electrical consumption, and cost per pound of nitrogen reduction.

Grant funding covers upgrades of existing systems to best available technology for nitrogen removal, or the marginal cost of using best available technology instead of conventional technology. Systems are ranked based on total nitrogen reduction capability, total cost including operation and maintenance and electrical consumption, and cost per pound of nitrogen reduction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and local governments with onsite disposal systems seeking to upgrade to nitrogen removal technology, including property owners installing best available technology systems for onsite sewage dispersal on their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation and operation of approved best available technology systems that remove nitrogen from onsite sewage dispersal systems, including upgrades to existing onsite disposal systems for improved nitrogen removal.

The program also offers low-interest loans to local governments to finance the local cost of implementing BNR facilities and other costs associated with plant upgrades or expansion consistent with Smart Growth criteria.

Small low-income communities may receive up to 75% grant funding for eligible costs. Eligible costs include engineering and pilot studies, design, and construction. Funds are provided on a reimbursable basis after payment requests are made for eligible project costs. The program also provides low-interest loans to local governments to finance the local cost of implementing BNR facilities and other costs associated with plant upgrades or expansion consistent with Smart Growth criteria. The goal is to achieve an annual average effluent concentration of 8 mg/l total nitrogen.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program authorized under the Inflation Reduction Act that provides grants to states, local governments, tribes, and territories for reducing greenhouse gas emissions and other harmful air pollution. The program has two phases: Phase 1 provided noncompetitive planning grants and Phase 2 provides competitive implementation funding. In Maryland, the program is administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment, with the Maryland Energy Administration supporting climate action planning for counties outside certain Metropolitan Statistical Areas through the Local Government Climate Action Support Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides $5 billion in total grants. Phase 1 provided $250 million in noncompetitive planning grants to states, local governments, tribes, and territories. Phase 2 provides approximately $4.6 billion in competitive implementation funds, with competition winners announced in July 2024 and funds awarded in October 2024. Counties outside MSAs also receive direct technical assistance for climate action planning through the Maryland Local Government Climate Action Support Program. Specific award amounts depend on the competition and application.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Josey Schwartz (State of Maryland & Local Support Program), Anna Marshall (Baltimore Metropolitan Statistical Areas), Elizabeth Compitello (Philadelphia Metropolitan Statistical Areas), Jeffrey King (Washington DC Metropolitan Statistical Areas)
structured_extraction.program_audience: States, local governments, tribes, and territories eligible to apply. In Maryland, this includes state government, local governments in Metropolitan Statistical Areas that received planning grants, and counties outside MSAs that are eligible for the Local Government Climate Action Support Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support projects that reduce greenhouse gas emissions and harmful air pollution, as well as climate action planning. Examples include electric vehicle charging infrastructure for commercial medium and heavy-duty vehicles and natural carbon sequestration through forest management and coastal habitat protection and restoration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Phase 1 planning grants were awarded to the State of Maryland and three Maryland Metropolitan Statistical Areas (Baltimore, Philadelphia, and Washington DC regions). Counties outside these MSAs are eligible for support through the Maryland Local Government Climate Action Support Program. Specifically, Western Maryland (Garrett, Allegany, Washington counties), Southern Maryland (Calvert, St. Mary's counties), and Eastern Shore (Kent, Talbot, Caroline, Dorchester, Wicomico, Somerset, Worcester counties) receive direct technical assistance.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Phase 1 planning grants, applications were noncompetitive. For Phase 2 implementation grants, the EPA announced competition winners in July 2024 with funds awarded in October 2024. Interested parties should contact the appropriate regional coordinator. Counties seeking assistance can fill out a form to request support from the Maryland Local Government Climate Action Support Program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program established in 1976 to assist local jurisdictions with implementing capital projects included in comprehensive flood management plans, conducting infrastructure repairs, restoring watersheds, and performing emergency protection work associated with flood events. The program funds comprehensive watershed studies to better understand flood risks and aims to protect local citizens from floodwaters and mitigate future flooding impacts. It also provides financial assistance to help communities purchase, relocate, and elevate houses to reduce flood risk, establish warning systems, and build flood control structures. Matching grants are provided to local governments for projects that increase flood resilience and restore natural floodplain through infrastructure retrofits and emergency preparedness measures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program funds up to 75 percent of the cost of flood mitigation projects when federal funds participate in the cost, with the remaining 25 percent split evenly between the state CFMGP and local governments. When federal funds do not participate, the CFMGP may fund up to 75 percent of the project cost and the local government covers 25 percent. In some configurations, state funds are provided and matched on a 50/50 basis with local government funds (50% state, 50% local). Projects have included acquisition of over 400 flood-prone properties. Grants are typically cost-shared with local governments and federal agencies, and support purchasing, relocating, and elevating houses within floodplains, establishing warning systems, and building flood control structures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal governments in Maryland seeking to improve flood resilience, reduce flood risk, and restore natural floodplain areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects included within comprehensive flood management plans, infrastructure repairs, watershed restoration, emergency protection work associated with flood events, comprehensive watershed studies, infrastructure retrofits, emergency preparedness measures, purchasing/relocating/elevating flood-prone houses, establishing warning systems, and building flood control structures
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties and municipalities are eligible; priority watersheds are designated by MDE in collaboration with the Department of Planning and the Department of Agriculture. Available statewide for communities in floodplain areas.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Counties and municipalities submit applications during the annual solicitation period, typically from December 1 through January 31. After submission, there is approximately 1.5 years until notification that the project was selected, which is made after the Maryland General Assembly approves the state capital budget. Grant awards are made after Maryland Board of Public Works approval. MDE reviews applications and the Legislature authorizes the sale of bonds to generate funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Drinking Water Revolving Loan Fund provides below-market interest rate loans, grants, and loan principal forgiveness to public and private community water systems and other eligible entities to finance projects that ensure safe drinking water and protect Maryland's drinking water supply. Projects can include treatment plant construction and upgrades, source water protection, infrastructure improvements, lead service line replacement, and system consolidation, all aimed at achieving or maintaining compliance with the Federal Safe Drinking Water Act.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Below-market interest rate loans, grants, and loan principal forgiveness are available to eligible public and private community water systems for water treatment plant construction and upgrades, source water protection plan development and implementation, raw water intake and conveyance infrastructure, finished water storage facilities, water distribution system rehabilitation including lead service line replacement, water system consolidation, and planning, design, and construction of eligible drinking water projects. The Maryland Water Infrastructure Financing Administration can also provide financial advisory services to help borrowers determine water rate structures and evaluate the impacts of proposed loans on their financial condition and affordability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private community water systems, local governments, municipalities, non-profits, and other eligible entities in Maryland undertaking drinking water system improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water treatment plant construction and upgrades, source water protection plan development and implementation, raw water intake and conveyance infrastructure, finished water storage facilities, water distribution system rehabilitation including lead service line replacement, water system consolidation, and planning and design for eligible drinking water projects to achieve or maintain compliance with the Federal Safe Drinking Water Act.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Business Telework Assistance Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants to help businesses and organizations expand telework capabilities for their employees by purchasing equipment, software, and technical services needed to develop and implement telework policies. The program supports organizations in establishing or expanding telework programs that conform to best practices established by the Office of Telework Assistance within the Maryland Department of Commerce.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $25,000 to help businesses and organizations purchase hardware, software, and technical services necessary to develop and implement telework policies. Grants vary based on applicant request and demonstrated needs. Eligible costs include hardware, software, or any technical equipment or technical services necessary to implement a telework policy. Preference is given to businesses with under 50 employees. Grant awards are competitive and limited to available funds. The grant cannot be used for previously purchased equipment. Within 1 year after receiving a grant, applicants must submit to the Department a letter describing how the grant funding was used, the telework policy that was implemented, and invoices related to implementation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, January 6, 2023 at 5:00 p.m. for Round 1; if additional funding is available, a second round will open in early 2023. The grant period is currently closed but may reopen in the future.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Existing businesses and organizations in Maryland that are developing or expanding telework policies for their employees. Preference given to businesses with under 50 employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of hardware, software, and technical services to develop and implement telework policies for employees. Eligible purchases include computers, laptops, cameras for video conferencing, software, or any technical equipment or services necessary to implement a telework policy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Applicants must have a physical location in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be in the process of developing a telework policy that conforms to best practices established by the Office of Telework Assistance within the Department of Commerce
Be an existing business or organization in good standing with the State of Maryland
Have a physical location in Maryland
Must be implementing or developing a telework policy
Demonstrate financial need to implement the proposed telework policy
Established Maryland business with operational experience
Must not have previously purchased the equipment with other funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants must complete the Business Telework Assistance Grant Program application form, which requires detailed business information, project description, project budget breakdown, and supporting documentation. Required supporting documents include: detailed sources and uses of funds statement, annual revenues evidenced by financial statement or other financial documentation, project cost documentation, equipment or product specification sheets, IRS Form W-9, Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and an affidavit confirming eligibility requirements. Applications must be submitted by the stated deadline. Funding decisions are based on evaluation criteria including capability of developing a telework policy and operational experience, the number of employees in the business, and the assistance needed. Grant awards are competitive and limited to available funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Clean Diesel Vehicle Initiative (EPA DERA FY2021-2022)

New buses must have 2019 or newer model year engine certified to EPA emissions standards

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Clean Diesel Vehicle Initiative + Baltimore Port Clean Diesel Initiative (EPA DERA FY2023-2024)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to replace older diesel school buses with new electric buses and to replace older drayage trucks at the Port of Baltimore with newer EPA-compliant trucks, as part of the Maryland Clean Vehicle Initiative funded through EPA DERA grants. The program covers up to 45 percent of the electric bus purchase price plus charging infrastructure, and up to half the price of replacement drayage trucks (maximum $35,000).

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide for school bus replacement; Port of Baltimore for drayage truck replacement.
requirements_list: Vehicles being replaced must be older diesel models
New school buses must be electric
New drayage trucks must have MY2017 or newer EPA compliant engine
Owner must provide remaining purchase price not covered by grant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications submitted through EPA DERA grant process administered by MDE.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Local Government Climate Action Support Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of the Environment, in partnership with the University of Maryland's Environmental Finance Center, provides no-cost direct technical assistance to select counties and municipalities across Maryland to support the advancement of greenhouse gas emissions reduction projects, including building decarbonization. The program helps local governments identify high-priority emissions reduction projects and builds capacity for project planning, design, financing, implementation, and grant writing. It specifically serves local governments in areas not covered by Climate Pollution Reduction Grants (CPRG) Metropolitan Statistical Areas planning grants, including Western Maryland, Southern Maryland, and the Eastern Shore.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides no-cost, hands-on technical assistance delivered by the University of Maryland's Environmental Finance Center, including project facilitation, education and training, community outreach and engagement, consultation, grant writing assistance, and direct technical assistance to help navigate resources, tools, and financing mechanisms for greenhouse gas emissions reduction projects, including building decarbonization.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments in Western Maryland (Garrett, Allegany, Washington counties), Southern Maryland (Calvert, St. Mary's counties), and Eastern Shore (Kent, Talbot, Caroline, Dorchester, Wicomico, Somerset, Worcester counties) and their municipalities that are not covered by a CPRG Metropolitan Statistical Areas Planning Grant.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for identifying and planning high-priority greenhouse gas emissions reduction projects with social, ecological, and economic co-benefits, including assistance with building decarbonization, project design, financing, implementation planning, and grant writing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Western Maryland (Garrett, Allegany, Washington counties), Southern Maryland (Calvert, St. Mary's counties), and Eastern Shore (Kent, Talbot, Caroline, Dorchester, Wicomico, Somerset, Worcester counties) — areas not covered by a CPRG Metropolitan Statistical Areas Planning Grant.
requirements_list: Located in an eligible county not covered by a CPRG Metropolitan Statistical Areas planning grant
Must complete a form requesting assistance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested local governments should fill out the assistance request form at https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfeBScF8iiR0wxaw5UOlOeUDxrrN1x31d8BxEGAt8lCo6NiKw/viewform to get started. The University of Maryland Environmental Finance Center will then provide technical support and services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-administered program that provides oversight for the voluntary cleanup of properties contaminated with hazardous substances. The program streamlines the cleanup process while ensuring compliance with existing environmental regulations, and increases certainty for participants through a federal liability agreement with EPA Region III.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides state oversight and technical guidance for voluntary cleanup of contaminated properties. Participants can obtain a No Further Requirements Determination or Certificate of Completion once cleanup is complete. The program also offers a fee waiver for renewable energy siting and development projects that meet eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers with contaminated properties seeking voluntary cleanup; commercial and residential developers; environmental consultants; clean and renewable energy companies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding and technical assistance for the cleanup of properties contaminated with hazardous substances. The program can be used to generate renewable energy on eligible properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Eligible properties in Maryland's VCP fall under a Memorandum of Agreement between MDE and EPA Region III.
requirements_list: Property must be contaminated with hazardous substances
Oil-contaminated sites and sites under active enforcement may be eligible under specified conditions
For renewable energy fee waiver, applicant must certify intention to use the eligible property to generate clean or renewable energy
Applicant must submit VCP application with required attachments
Applicant must post notice at the property that is the subject of the application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed VCP application with required attachments to MDE. For expedited inculpable person approval, submit the Expedited Inculpable Person Form including a completed Inculpable Person Affidavit and $2,000 fee to MDE at 1800 Washington Blvd, Suite 625, Baltimore, Maryland 21230, or email to mde.vcp@maryland.gov. Post public notice at the property. MDE provides oversight and technical guidance through the cleanup process, which includes Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments, Response Action Plans, and cleanup activities. Upon completion, MDE issues either a No Further Requirements Determination or Certificate of Completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) and the Maryland Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MD MEP) partner to place engineering and college students as summer interns at Maryland manufacturing companies. Interns work with company staff to identify process and equipment improvements that save companies money and reduce environmental impact, focusing on energy efficiency, waste reduction, and material use efficiency. The program is funded by the U.S. EPA, MDE, and participating companies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Engineering and college students serve as summer interns at participating Maryland manufacturing companies. The internship program is supported by funding from the U.S. EPA, MDE, and participating companies. Interns work to identify process and equipment improvements for energy efficiency, waste reduction, and material use efficiency, helping companies reduce costs and environmental impact.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internship placements for engineering and college students to conduct process and equipment improvement projects that reduce costs and environmental impact through energy efficiency, waste reduction, and material use efficiency
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Participating company must be a manufacturing facility located in Maryland
Student must be an engineering or college student

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Department of the Environment awards CO2 offset allowances for projects that demonstrate real, additional, verifiable, enforceable and permanent avoidance of CO2 emissions or reduction of atmospheric CO2 levels. Projects may be located in any participating RGGI state or other approved jurisdiction.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

Project types include landfill methane capture and destruction, reduction or avoidance of CO2 emissions from natural gas or oil end-use combustion through energy efficiency, avoided methane emissions from agricultural manure management, reduction in sulfur hexafluoride emissions, and carbon sequestration through reforestation, improved forest management, or avoided conversion.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects must demonstrate real, additional, verifiable, enforceable and permanent avoidance of CO2 emissions or reduction of atmospheric CO2 levels through landfill methane capture, energy efficiency improvements, agricultural methane reduction, SF6 emissions reduction, or carbon sequestration activities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects may be located in any participating RGGI state or other approved jurisdiction
requirements_list: Project must demonstrate real, additional, verifiable, enforceable and permanent avoidance of CO2 emissions or reduction of atmospheric CO2 levels
Consistency application must be submitted to MDE within six months of commencing the offset project (one year for carbon sequestration projects)
Projects must comply with specific standards under COMAR 26.09.03
