structured_extraction.program_name: Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) Fee Waiver for Clean and Renewable Energy Siting and Development
structured_extraction.program_description: A fee waiver program for Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP) applicants who want to locate clean or renewable energy projects on Brownfield sites (degraded or contaminated lands). Applicants can receive a waiver of the standard VCP application fee when they certify their intention to use an eligible property to generate clean or renewable energy. The program also provides liability protection after remediation of Brownfield sites and, in participating jurisdictions, Brownfield tax incentives. Fee waiver criteria were established through regulations adopted on November 23, 2021, with applications accepted beginning January 1, 2022.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Application fee waiver for the Voluntary Cleanup Program. The standard VCP application fee is $10,000 for new projects or $2,000 for a subsequent application if there is an active VCP application in progress. This waiver eliminates that fee for clean or renewable energy development projects on Brownfield sites. The waiver is granted based on criteria established through regulations adopted on November 23, 2021. The VCP program also provides liability protection after remediation of Brownfield sites and, in participating jurisdictions, Brownfield tax incentives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial and residential developers, environmental consultants, and clean and renewable energy companies interested in cleaning up contaminated Brownfield properties for clean or renewable energy projects, including solar, wind, geothermal, or biomass generation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The fee waiver applies to the application cost for the Voluntary Cleanup Program when redeveloping Brownfield sites for clean or renewable energy generation, such as solar, wind, geothermal, or biomass projects, eliminating the need to pay the standard VCP application fee.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland; Brownfield tax incentives available in participating jurisdictions.
requirements_list: Applicant must certify intention to use an eligible property to generate clean or renewable energy
Property must be a Brownfield site (degraded or contaminated land) eligible under the Voluntary Cleanup Program
Project must involve clean or renewable energy generation
Applicant must meet criteria established in regulations adopted November 23, 2021
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a VCP Fee Waiver Application along with their Voluntary Cleanup Program application, certifying their intention to use the property for clean or renewable energy development. The program supports both point source pollution prevention projects run by public entities and local governments, and nonpoint source pollution prevention projects run by public and private entities, consistent with the Federal Clean Water Act and Maryland Bay Restoration Fund Act.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

Financial advisory services are also available through the Water Infrastructure Financing Administration to assist applicants in determining affordable user rate structures and modeling the fiscal impact of the proposed loan on financial capacity.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.

Nonpoint source pollution prevention projects are available to public and private entities

structured_extraction.program_description: Federal Clean Water Act Section 319(h) grants administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment to reduce or eliminate water quality impairments associated with nonpoint source pollution. The program provides financial assistance for implementing best management practices and outreach initiatives, as well as planning, design, construction, monitoring, and analysis of projects that improve water quality and habitat in Maryland watersheds. A Request for Proposals is released each year, with priority given to projects in EPA-accepted watershed plans that address impairments on Maryland's 303(d) List of Impaired Waters.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal Clean Water Act Section 319(h) grant funds are provided as reimbursement-style grants in Maryland. Recipients must fund projects first and then seek reimbursement from MDE. Funds can support planning, design, construction, monitoring, and analysis of projects that reduce pollutant loads and improve water quality in impaired watersheds listed on Maryland's 303(d) List, particularly those with approved Total Maximum Daily Loads (TMDLs). A Request for Proposals is released each year in Spring, with a Summer submission deadline. The FFY26 RFP is now closed, with selections expected in November 2025; the FFY27 RFP opens July 1, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FFY26 RFP now closed; FFY27 RFP opens July 1, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal agencies, Soil Conservation Districts, State agencies, State institutions of higher learning, private firms, and nonprofit organizations seeking to improve water quality in Maryland watersheds through nonpoint source pollution reduction.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning, design, construction, monitoring, and analysis of projects that reduce or eliminate water quality impairments associated with nonpoint source pollution, including implementation of best management practices and outreach initiatives. Primary focus is on implementation projects that result in quantifiable or measurable improvements in water quality and habitat, including pollutant load reductions for impairments addressed in TMDLs or identified in the 303(d) List.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, with priority for projects located in one of Maryland's EPA-accepted watershed plans. Eligible watersheds include Aaron Run, Antietam Creek, Assawoman Bay, Casselman River, Corsica River, Lower Jones Falls, Middle Gwynns Falls, Lower Monocacy River, Sassafras River, Spring Branch, Tidal Back River, Upper Back River, Upper Choptank River, and Upper Jennings Run.
requirements_list: Projects must reduce or eliminate water quality impairments listed in Maryland's List of Impaired Waters (303(d) List)
Typically, implementation projects involving in-the-ground construction require EPA acceptance of a watershed plan as prerequisite
Applicants must demonstrate capacity in grant management and funding, as this is a reimbursement-style grant requiring upfront funding
Justification of capacity must be included in the proposal
Projects must result in quantifiable or measurable improvements in water quality and habitat
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A Request for Proposals is released each Spring, with submissions typically due in Summer. Interested entities submit proposals during the published RFP period. The FFY26 RFP has closed with selections to be made in November 2025. The FFY27 RFP will open on July 1, 2026. MDE reviews proposals and may request additional documentation to ensure project completion capacity.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that accelerates investment and supports site readiness as a direct pathway to economic competitiveness by providing financial support to defray costs of site characterization and site improvements, plus collaborative marketing support, to grow the inventory of shovel-ready sites across Maryland for industrial and commercial development. The program was created through an Executive Order of the Governor of Maryland on December 19, 2024, and was funded by the Maryland General Assembly at $3.5 million for FY2026.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers three types of support: (1) Site Characterization Grants providing up to $10,000 to assess site readiness and develop a shared understanding of site needs, with match requirement eliminated effective January 1, 2026; (2) Site Improvement Grants supporting infrastructure development and environmental remediation with no maximum funding limit based on project needs and funds availability, with a 3:1 total cash match from all sources expected for competitive applications, with preference for higher match scenarios; and (3) Collaborative Marketing Support assisting with site marketing through the MBRSP Sites Dashboard and related deliverables. Site Improvement Grants may be used for due diligence (geotechnical engineering, final site engineering and design, grading plans, rail studies, traffic impact studies), environmental/brownfields clean-up (remediation, demolition), site improvements (clearing, grading, flood mitigation, drainage, signage, landscaping), utility improvements (extensions, upgrades, redundancy, utility easement/right-of-way acquisition), and transportation improvements (internal roadways, pedestrian access, rail spurs and access improvements).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis with priority cycle in May; applicants submitting complete applications in May will be notified by July 1; applicants submitting June 1 or later will be notified within 60 days of submission
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public sector entities (counties, municipalities, and authorities) and private sector entities that own and/or have development rights to eligible sites, as well as developers and communities seeking to prepare sites for business development and economic growth.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Site characterization and assessment; infrastructure upgrades; environmental remediation; site development improvements; marketing of shovel-ready sites; due diligence studies; geotechnical engineering; final site engineering and design; grading plans; rail studies; traffic impact studies; brownfields remediation; demolition; clearing and grading; flood mitigation; drainage improvements; signage; landscaping; utility extensions and upgrades; internal roadways; pedestrian access; rail spurs and access improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties; eligible sites must be greenfields, brownfields, or redevelopment sites in pre-development phase; minimum of 5 acres; intended for solely industrial or commercial purposes (horizontal mixed-use allowable if industrial/commercial portion meets all criteria); intended to be occupied primarily by private sector companies in life sciences, information technology, aerospace, defense, computational biology, quantum computing, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, or position, navigation, and timing industries; jurisdiction-specific industries of focus may be eligible if applicant provides evidence of coordinated local strategy; tourism and agricultural farmland are not eligible; sites must not be restricted from further development.
requirements_list: Site must be a minimum of 5 acres
Site must be greenfield, brownfield, or redevelopment site in pre-development phase
Site intended for solely industrial or commercial purposes (horizontal mixed-use allowable if industrial/commercial portion meets all criteria)

Site intended to be occupied primarily by private sector companies in life sciences, information technology, aerospace, defense, computational biology, quantum computing, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, or position, navigation, and timing industries, or jurisdiction-specific industries with documented local strategy
Site must not be restricted from further development by local, state, or federal statute, judicial ruling, or standing agreement
Applicant must own and/or have development rights to the land
Applicant must agree to conditions outlined in MBRSP Program Guidelines
For private sector applicants: must have letter of support from county and, if applicable, municipality
For private sector applicants: must allow access to the site
For private sector applicants: must demonstrate commitment to future or continued site improvement
For private sector applicants: must demonstrate commitment to utilizing site for business growth in high-value-added sectors
For Site Improvement Grants: 3:1 total cash match from all sources expected for competitive applications, with preference for higher match scenarios
For private sector Site Improvement Grant applicants: must provide significant portion of total cash match
For private sector Site Improvement Grant applicants: must agree to reasonable post-improvement price per acre developed in coordination with MBRSP prior to application approval
For private sector Site Improvement Grant applicants: must agree to financial clawback provisions if site is used for purpose outside MBRSP Program Guidelines
For Site Characterization Grants: proof of property ownership or legal agreement to develop the site
For Site Characterization Grants: evidence of local match (eliminated effective January 1, 2026)
For Site Improvement Grants: detailed site improvement plan including scope of work and detailed budget
For Site Improvement Grants: evidence of financial commitment for required local match
For Site Improvement Grants: copy of all existing due diligence reports and studies related to site
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed MBRSP application form (Site Characterization Grant Application or Site Improvement Grant Application) along with supporting documents to sites@medco-corp.com. Include project name, applying organization name, and grant category in email title. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with a priority cycle in May. For Site Characterization Grant finalists, a remote visit will be arranged including PowerPoint presentation about the site and high-level discussion about potential uses. For Site Improvement Grant finalists, an in-person site visit will be arranged including sit-down discussion with PowerPoint presentation and site tour. Applicants submitting complete applications in May will be notified of outcome no later than July 1 of that calendar year. Applicants submitting June 1 or later will be notified within 60 days of submission. Upon award notification, MEDCO, applicant, and holder of title or option to purchase will jointly execute Grant Agreement. For Site Characterization Grants, MEDCO will contract directly with agreed-upon third-party site development professional(s) and invoice applicant for reimbursement of their match portion. For Site Improvement Grants, funding will be disbursed upon completion of work and submission of expense documentation. Following completion of Scope of Work, project leaders must submit quarterly status questionnaire each January 1 and July 1 for three (3) calendar years.

structured_extraction.program_description: Following a Presidentially declared disaster, the Individuals and Households Program provides grants to eligible households who experience difficulties after the disaster. When households are denied low-interest loans from the Small Business Administration and their homeowners or flood insurance does not provide sufficient coverage, the IHP may provide Housing Assistance and/or Other Needs Assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants in two forms: Housing Assistance (for temporary housing, repair of disaster-damaged homes, replacement of disaster-damaged homes, or semi-permanent or permanent housing construction, up to the IHP maximum) and Other Needs Assistance (for medical and dental expenses, funeral and burial costs, repair or replacement of clothing and household items, specialized tools or protective clothing, educational materials, clean-up items, fuel for primary heat source, vehicle repair or transportation costs, moving and storage expenses, and other necessary expenses or serious needs).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and households experiencing difficulties following a Presidentially declared disaster.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing repairs and replacement, temporary housing, semi-permanent or permanent housing construction, medical and dental expenses, funeral and burial costs, clothing replacement, household items, educational materials, clean-up supplies, fuel, vehicle repair or transportation, moving and storage expenses, and other necessary disaster-related expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in areas of Maryland following a Presidentially declared disaster. Special flood insurance requirements may apply if a home is located in a Special Flood Hazard Area.
requirements_list: Household must have been denied a low-interest loan from the Small Business Administration
Homeowners or flood insurance must not provide sufficient coverage
Home must meet safe and sanitary living conditions after repairs
If home is in a Special Flood Hazard Area, homeowner must comply with flood insurance purchase requirements and local flood codes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Households apply for assistance following a Presidentially declared disaster. The program evaluates eligibility based on SBA loan denial and insurance coverage limitations.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership program that provides cybersecurity assistance to K-12 schools throughout Maryland to enhance resilience, protect student and staff data, and support mitigation and recovery from cyber incidents. Services include cybersecurity assessments, emergency planning, training, and ongoing support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides technical assistance in planning, implementation, and support areas. Planning assistance includes cybersecurity maturity assessment, current plan assessment, resource allocation analysis, and training program setup. Implementation assistance includes remediation recommendations, response plan development, disaster recovery and continuity of operations support, and training exercises. Ongoing support includes funding notifications and continuous access to a network of resources and advice.
structured_extraction.program_audience: K-12 schools and school systems throughout Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cybersecurity planning, implementation, training, disaster recovery planning, incident response, and resilience building for educational institutions
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland schools and school systems
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools interested in receiving assistance should use the online form to request support in one or more of the support areas offered by the initiative. Contact the MDEM or DoIT teams for questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to support facility hardening and other physical security enhancements and activities to nonprofit organizations that are at high risk of terrorist attack. The program helps pay for security improvements to buildings and other safety activities to protect against potential threats.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers project grants to nonprofit organizations to fund security upgrades such as facility hardening and other physical security enhancements and activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations at high risk of terrorist attacks.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for facility hardening and other physical security enhancements and activities, including physical security improvements and threat mitigation.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Public Assistance Program provides supplemental financial assistance to State and local governments and certain private non-profit organizations for response and recovery activities after a Presidentially-declared disaster. It provides Federal grant assistance for the repair, replacement or restoration of disaster-damaged, publicly owned and uninsured facilities at a 75% Federal/25% applicant grant share formula, helping to alleviate the financial burden on affected entities following a federally-declared disaster.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant assistance provided at a 75% Federal/25% applicant grant share formula for repair, replacement or restoration of disaster-damaged, publicly owned and uninsured facilities. The federal government covers 75% of the cost, and the applicant must cover the remaining 25%. Assistance is delivered as a formula grant and direct payment for specified use.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Nora Lagola, State Public Assistance Officer
structured_extraction.program_audience: State and local governments, municipalities/towns, regional entities, state colleges, and certain private non-profit organizations affected by a Presidentially-declared disaster.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repair, replacement or restoration of disaster-damaged, publicly owned and uninsured facilities; response and recovery activities following a Presidentially-declared disaster.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide for Maryland counties affected by a Presidentially-declared disaster.
requirements_list: State, local government, or certain private non-profit organization status
A disaster must be officially declared by the President
Facility damage must result from a Presidentially-declared disaster
Facilities must be publicly owned and uninsured
Applicants must provide a 25% cost share
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants are encouraged to create accounts on the FEMA Grants Portal before a disaster. After a Presidential Disaster Declaration, the Public Assistance process is completed through the FEMA Grants Portal. Contact information, insurance, and necessary documentation can be added and updated during the application process. Applications are generally due within 90 days after the disaster declaration.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides revolving loan fund financing for hazard mitigation projects, though specific terms, amounts, and repayment details are not described on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, businesses, and organizations seeking funding for hazard mitigation and resilience projects in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding for mitigation projects that help reduce the potential negative effects of natural and human-caused hazards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can request information on applying for a mitigation grant through a web form. Detailed application procedures are available on the Resilient Maryland Revolving Loan Fund dedicated page.

structured_extraction.program_name: State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program (SLCGP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program that helps states, local governments, rural areas, and territories address cybersecurity risks and threats to information systems. The program provides strategic investments to enhance the cybersecurity posture of government agencies and bolster the protection of critical infrastructure and essential public services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program is a reimbursement-based grant that provides funds for approved cybersecurity projects. Subrecipients submit reimbursement requests for project-related expenses with documentation showing proof of purchase and proof of payment. Funding is awarded to the pass-through entity (MDEM) upon signature of the subrecipient subaward agreement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis for FY2023 second-round applications; all FY2023 projects must be completed by September 30, 2027
structured_extraction.program_audience: State agencies and local governments in Maryland seeking to strengthen cybersecurity and address cybersecurity risks
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cybersecurity projects and activities approved by the Maryland State Cybersecurity Planning Committee that align with the state's cybersecurity priorities and enhance the cybersecurity posture of government agencies
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland state agencies and local governments, as well as rural areas and territories. Funding is managed by MDEM as the state's lead agency.
requirements_list: Must register for the Cyber Hygiene (CyHy) service provided by CISA
Must complete the Nationwide Cybersecurity Review (NCSR) annually
Must submit quarterly status reports with financial and programmatic information until project completion
Must have a fully executed Subrecipient Agreement (SRA) contract in place before starting the project

Must follow all federal and state compliance requirements including proper reporting and documentation

If approved, funds are awarded upon signature of the subrecipient subaward agreement. Applicants must submit a Letter of Intent to Accept or Reject Funding within 30 days of approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program supports nonprofit and community-based organizations in conducting outreach across Maryland to educate homeowners and tenants about the benefits of building electrification paired with energy efficiency and renewable energy upgrades. The program emphasizes cost-effective solutions for low- to moderate-income households to reduce energy burdens, lower utility bills, improve home health and safety, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Outreach must include in-person engagement with residents and may include online resources, phone and email advising, print materials, and hands-on demonstrations.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants ranging from a minimum of $50,000 to a maximum of $125,000 per award. A total of $250,000 is anticipated to be available for Fiscal Year 2026. Partial awards may be issued. Funding is provided directly to the individual identified on the application form, who may then provide subgrants or stipends to other organizations or community groups working within Maryland. Grants funds may be used for direct expenses including material/equipment purchase costs of electric appliances for demonstration purposes, print collateral and media materials, other outreach supplies, community event or meeting rentals, food and supplies, online promotions, staffing expenditures, and subgrants or stipends for partner organizations. Administrative/indirect costs may be requested at negotiated rates or at least 10% of modified total direct costs under OMB Uniform Guidance. Grant period is 24 months beginning with the effective date of the executed grant agreement. Grant funds are paid in arrears over the course of the grant period for the performance of eligible, approved activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and community-based organizations classified as 501(c)(3) that conduct outreach to educate low- to moderate-income households about residential electrification, energy efficiency, and renewable energy solutions. These organizations serve as trusted community messengers to communicate benefits of electrification to the communities they serve, particularly overburdened and underserved communities as defined by Maryland statute.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Organizations use funding to conduct outreach and education activities about building electrification benefits, emphasizing how to pair electrification measures with energy efficiency upgrades and renewable energy solutions to maximize savings for low- to moderate-income households and overburdened communities. Eligible activities include educating on: the benefits of electrification (health, safety, environmental and climate benefits, enhanced performance and ease of use, potential financial savings); electrification equipment and appliances (electric heat pumps for space heating and cooling, electric heat pump water heaters, electric stoves/cooktops/ranges, electric heat pump clothes dryers, and responsible pre-electrification measures); incentives and rebates (how residents can combine federal, state, local, and utility incentives); and connecting residents with available incentives and rebates for electrification, energy efficiency, and renewable energy measures. Activities may include assessing household needs, identifying applicable incentive or assistance programs, screening for program eligibility across multiple programs, assisting with application submission and required documents, and providing support services such as language interpretation or disability access.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland. Applicants must specify the communities and regions they intend to serve from five state region options: Western Region (GREEN), Central Region (ORANGE), Eastern Region (BLUE), Southern Region (PINK), and Baltimore City Region (RED). All outreach efforts must prioritize communities designated as overburdened as defined in Maryland statute (Code of Maryland, Environment Article §1-701). Applicants may use the Maryland Department of the Environment MDEnviroScreenTool to identify these communities. Region selections do not indicate that the applicant is proposing outreach across the entirety of all selected regions; rather, it provides a general indication of focus. To enhance geographic diversity, MEA may consider an applicant's area(s) of geographic focus when determining a grant award decision.
requirements_list: Applicant must be classified as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Applicant must be registered to do business in Maryland and provide Evidence of Good Standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Applicant must provide a complete application including all required application documents
Applicant must specify the regions they intend to serve from the provided region designations
The applicant's proposed outreach efforts must include the required in-person component and focus on the subject matter specified in the FOA

Applicant must commit to tracking required quantitative outcome metrics: number of individuals provided with in-person outreach and education, number of in-person outreach events held, and number of individuals screened for rebates/incentives
Outreach must focus on low- to moderate-income households
Activities must emphasize pairing electrification with energy efficiency and renewable energy upgrades
Outreach must educate single-family and multi-family dwelling owners and tenants
Minimum grant request is $50,000
Maximum grant request is $125,000
Residential homes, businesses, and units of government are not eligible

Ineligible activities include: contracting work of any kind including appliance installations and removals, managing home electrification installation projects, outreach efforts targeting only business owners or HVAC installers, and outreach efforts promoting use of fossil-fuel powered appliances
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted using the Application Jotform (online application required; PDF version available on program webpage) by December 31, 2025. Full program details are provided in the Funding Opportunity Announcement document. The application package must include: (1) Narrative (no more than 10 pages) providing comprehensive overview addressing Minimum Eligibility Requirements and Competitive Evaluation Criteria including project design and approach, historic success with education and outreach programming, track record as trusted community partner, experience serving overburdened communities, and combination of outreach channels; (2) Budget attachment (Excel or PDF) detailing budget items; (3) IRS Form W-9 for the applicant organization with name and address matching application form; (4) Evidence of Good Standing from SDAT indicating the organization is in good standing with Maryland. Optional application documents include letters of support (two or more preferred) from project partners. The evaluation process includes three review steps: (1) Program Manager Eligibility Review for compliance with Minimum Eligibility Requirements, (2) Evaluation Team Member Individual Review scoring each complete application on Competitive Evaluation Criteria worth up to 18 points total (Qualifications & Experience 0-4 points, Project Feasibility 0-4 points, Justification & Quantitative Metrics 0-4 points, Budget and Return on Investment 0-4 points, Letters of Support 0-2 points), and (3) Evaluation Team Group Review with final score determined by averaging individual scores. Grants recommended in order of highest final score to lowest eligible final score until available funding is exhausted. Applicant may NOT disclose sensitive or confidential information without prior approval. Timeline: FOA issued September 18, 2025; Application deadline December 31, 2025; Grant agreements signed and executed estimated March/April 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: BG&E Home Performance with ENERGY STAR Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Baltimore Gas & Electric subsidizes the cost of a comprehensive home energy audit and provides rebates and incentives for energy efficiency improvements specific to the home. The program covers air and duct sealing, insulation, windows and doors, smart thermostats, heat pump water heaters, and heating and cooling upgrades. After the audit, customers receive a detailed list of recommended upgrades and can apply for BGE rebates calculated based on improvement type and estimated energy savings.

After the audit is completed, customers receive a detailed list of applicable upgrades and improvements. BGE provides rebates to help cover the cost of improvements, calculated based on improvement type and estimated energy savings. Eligible improvements include air and duct sealing, insulation, windows and doors, smart thermostats, heat pump water heaters, and heating and cooling upgrades.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Burning Wood and Pellet Stove Rebate Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides rebates to Maryland homeowners to purchase and install eligible clean burning wood or pellet stoves at their primary residence, helping them invest in clean energy by displacing electric, non-natural gas fossil fuel heating systems, or old wood or pellet stoves. The program concluded after fiscal year 2024 and is no longer accepting applications.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Wood burning stoves meeting EPA certification and emissions/efficiency requirements receive a $500 rebate. Pellet burning stoves meeting EPA certification and emissions/efficiency requirements receive a $700 rebate. Wood stoves must emit no more than 3.0 grams of particulate matter per hour and have an EPA-published Higher Heating Value efficiency rating of at least 75%. Pellet stoves must emit no more than 2.0 grams of particulate matter per hour and have an EPA-published Higher Heating Value efficiency rating of at least 75%. The program had an anticipated total budget of $200,000 available from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund. Rebates were issued on a first-come, first-served basis until funding was exhausted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 31, 2024 (program concluded, no longer accepting applications). All eligible stoves must have been purchased by December 1, 2023, and all systems installed with applications received or postmarked by March 31, 2024.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners seeking to install clean burning wood or pellet stoves at their primary residence. Applicants must own a residential property located in Maryland that serves as their primary residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and installation of eligible clean burning wood or pellet stoves to replace electric, non-natural gas fossil fuel heating systems, or old wood or pellet stoves. Stoves must be new (not used or second-hand).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, non-competitive, first-come, first-served basis. All Maryland counties eligible.
requirements_list: Applicant must be the owner of a residential property located in Maryland
Property must be the applicant's primary residence at time of application
Home must not be owned by an irrevocable trust (properties in revocable trusts with grantor as primary resident are eligible)
Stove must be EPA-certified based on EPA Certified Wood Stove Database

Pellet stove must emit no more than 2.0 grams of particulate matter per hour

Stove must be new, not purchased used or obtained second-hand
Installation must be at primary place of residence
Stove must displace electric, non-natural gas fossil fuel heating systems, or old wood or pellet stove
One rebate per technology per property only (wood and pellet stoves considered same technology)
Installation must show proof of passed final inspection if permit required by county or local jurisdiction
Stove and installation costs must be paid in full with supporting documentation
Photographic documentation of installed system must be provided
Application must be complete, signed, and dated by homeowner applicant with federal tax identification number
Application must be received by MEA within twelve months of stove installation

Maryland-authorized contractor must be used for installation (must be incorporated or registered to do business in Maryland, possess all required licenses and certifications, be in good standing with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation)
Contractor must be National Fireplace Institute (NFI) certified (strongly encouraged)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Homeowner purchases an eligible clean burning wood or pellet stove and arranges installation by a Maryland-authorized contractor. 2) Homeowner obtains final inspection documentation from the county or local permitting authority if required. 3) Homeowner pays the stove and installation costs in full. 4) Homeowner takes photographs of the installed system. 5) Homeowner completes the rebate application form (available at https://energy.maryland.gov/residential/Pages/incentives/woodstoves.aspx) and gathers all required supporting documents including: signed and dated application, final inspection documentation, payment documentation (zero-balance invoice), photographic documentation, property ownership and primary residency documentation (SDAT Real Property database screenshot or copy), and completed IRS Form W9. 6) Homeowner mails the complete application and all supporting documents to: Maryland Energy Administration, Attn: Clean Burning Wood and Pellet Stove Program, 1800 Washington Blvd. Suite 755, Baltimore, MD 21230. Alternatively, applicants can request electronic submission via encrypted email through Virtru by emailing CERP.MEA@Maryland.gov with first name, last name, zip code, and email address. 7) MEA reviews application for completeness upon receipt. 8) Complete applications are reviewed for compliance with program criteria. 9) If found eligible, application is submitted for approval and payment. 10) Applicants can track application status using the Weekly Status Report on the program website. 11) Applications are handled on a first-come, first-served basis. Note: Applications are no longer being accepted as of March 31, 2024; this program has concluded.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration's Commercial and Canopy Solar Program (CCSP) provides grant funding to support solar energy installations on commercial properties, including rooftop-mounted solar systems, ground-mounted solar systems, and solar canopies over parking or bodies of water. The program serves low-to-moderate income and overburdened communities and helps Maryland's businesses, nonprofits, and organizations increase access to solar energy technologies to meet clean energy, energy affordability, and greenhouse gas reduction goals. Funding for solar canopies was previously offered as a standalone Solar Canopy and Dual Use Technology Grant Program (FY25) and is now incorporated into this program.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding calculated using a formula based on Area of Interest, solar PV installation type, and system capacity. For Area of Interest 1 (Equitable Commercial and Canopy Solar): non-canopy systems receive $2,000 per kilowatt DC or 90% of total project cost (whichever is lower); canopy systems receive $2,500 per kilowatt DC or 90% of total project cost (whichever is lower). For third-party owned systems: non-canopy $750 per kilowatt DC; canopy $1,000 per kilowatt DC. For Area of Interest 2 (Commercial Solar for Sustainability): non-canopy systems receive $1,700 per kilowatt DC or 75% of total project cost (whichever is lower); canopy systems receive $2,125 per kilowatt DC or 75% of total project cost (whichever is lower). For third-party owned systems: non-canopy $750 per kilowatt DC; canopy $1,000 per kilowatt DC. If a single application includes both canopy and non-canopy arrays, grant calculation is the sum of canopy capacity at the canopy rate and non-canopy capacity at the non-canopy rate. Maximum grant award is $500,000 per property owner. For applicant-owned systems, funding may be used to subsidize costs of enabling electrical upgrades, equipment, installation, commissioning, and interconnection. For third-party owned systems, funding may be used as an upfront payment to buy-down the rate of a Solar PV Lease or Power Purchase Agreement (PPA). Grant funding may not be used to make monthly payments on a PPA or Solar PV Lease. Total program budget for FY26 is $13,000,000 anticipated from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund Clean Energy Jobs Act Alternative Compliance Payments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits, businesses, and other organizations registered to operate in Maryland. Area of Interest 1 (Equitable Commercial and Canopy Solar): Maryland businesses and other organizations that have been designated as or are actively in the process of being designated as a nonprofit organization, Small Business Enterprise (SBE), or are small Veteran-Owned businesses that own or operate eligible facilities. Area of Interest 2 (Commercial Solar for Sustainability): other Maryland businesses and organizations that own or operate eligible facilities. Both tracks serve low-to-moderate income communities located in a census tract with an average median income at or below 80% of the average median income for the State, or overburdened or underserved communities. Eligible facility types include multi-family dwellings, LMI-serving 501(c)(3) nonprofits, hospitals and medical facilities, home offices, owner-occupied agricultural businesses, commercial properties occupied by retail businesses, business offices, warehouses, and hotels.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Solar energy installations on commercial properties, including rooftop-mounted solar systems, ground-mounted solar systems, and solar canopies over parking or bodies of water. Solar PV systems purchased by applicants and third-party owned solar energy systems are eligible. Solar canopy systems must meet EV-ready standards. Funding covers development and installation costs. Maximum eligible system capacity is 200% of average annual usage based on the latest 12 months of utility bills. Aggregate net metering is permitted for LMI-serving 501(c)(3) nonprofit facilities only. Other grid-tied solar PV configurations may be reviewed on a case-by-case basis. Community solar systems, local government projects, higher education projects, public school projects, agrivoltaic projects, and projects greater than 2 MW-DC are ineligible and should apply to other MEA programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - serves all of Maryland on a non-competitive, first-come, first-served basis. All project facilities must be geographically located within the State of Maryland and in a community classified as low-to-moderate income or overburdened, following definitions and boundaries established under State Government Article §9–20B–05(i)(1). Prioritizes census tracts with average median income at or below 80% of the state average median income, and overburdened or underserved communities. Eligible census tracts can be identified using the Census Tracts and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) Alternative Compliance Payment page, including a searchable list of eligible census tracts.
requirements_list: Applicants must be registered to operate in Maryland and have an established Employer Identification Number (EIN) or Tax Identification Number (TIN)
For Area of Interest 1: must be designated as or actively in process of being designated as a nonprofit organization, Small Business Enterprise (SBE), or Veteran-Owned business
For Area of Interest 2: must own or operate eligible facilities as specified in the program guidelines
Parking facilities with solar canopies must be EV ready and meet EV-ready standards per Appendix A
Maximum grant award is $500,000 per property owner
For Area of Interest 1 (Equitable Solar Access track): located in census tract with average median income at or below 80% of state average median income, OR overburdened or underserved community
Installation must be at a Maryland business, nonprofit, or organization
Project must be on property either owned or leased by the applicant; applicants must provide documentation of ownership or lease
Applicant and any contractor must be in Good Standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (DAT)
Up to 5% of project expenses incurred prior to grant agreement execution are eligible for reimbursement; expenses greater than 5% of total project cost cannot be reimbursed
Applicants cannot receive another grant for the same project if previously funded under this program
Applicant must be able to enter into a formal grant agreement with MEA
Project must be completed, including all milestones and required reporting documents, by no later than four (4) years from grant agreement signing
Installation must not result in an adverse finding to historical significance per Maryland Historic Trust review
A North American Board of Certified Energy Practitioners (NABCEP) certified PV Installation Professional or PV Design Specialist must be directly involved with design or construction
Applicant must contribute funding toward total project cost (cost match required)
For third-party owned systems: Solar PV Lease or Power Purchase Agreement must guarantee 20% electricity cost savings throughout the life of the agreement

For multi-family buildings: tenant rent will not be increased solely based on solar PV system installation for a period of two (2) years; property owner must notify tenants and provide Tenant Synopsis Form

For LMI-serving 501(c)(3) nonprofits: energy bill savings must be realized by the nonprofit; facility must be owned or long-term leased; for individual net metered facilities, facility must be in LMI/overburdened community or more than 50% of beneficiaries must live in such community; for aggregated net metering, all facilities must be in eligible geography or more than 50% of beneficiaries in eligible community

For hospitals and medical facilities: energy bill savings must be realized by medical provider; facility must be owned or long-term leased; more than 50% of patients must live in LMI/overburdened community
For home offices: energy bill savings must be realized by owner who lives in LMI/overburdened community
For owner-occupied agricultural businesses: farm must be in LMI/overburdened community and energy bill savings must be realized by owner who lives in such community

For commercial properties (retail, office, warehouse, hotel): property must be in LMI/overburdened community and funded measures must enable community resiliency during power outages or severe weather
MSAP Recipients: owner-occupied businesses that received funding under the Maryland Solar Access Program are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through a JotForm portal. Applicants must provide a complete application form signed by an authorized representative. Required documents include: (1) Complete and signed FY26 MEA application form; (2) For Area of Interest 1 only, evidence of applicant status (SBE certification, Veteran-Owned documentation, or 501(c)(3) IRS letter); (3) Signed attestation certifying project facility meets eligible facility designations; (4) Complete and signed IRS Form W-9; (5) Good Standing documentation with Maryland DAT; (6) Evidence of facility control (property deed, DAT Real Property Search results, or signed Property Owner's Permission Letter for leased facilities); (7) Complete and accurate FY26 Commercial and Canopy Solar Program Budget Workbook; (8) Documentation of 12 continuous months of electric utility consumption data and percentage of onsite load offset; (9) Comprehensive solar PV system information including system size in kW-DC, location details, solar production estimate from PVWatts or similar program, one-line diagram, and for canopies, EV-Ready documentation; (10) Facility site map showing solar PV system location. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. As of March 30, 2026, the application portal is closed to new applications due to funding depletion. MEA is reviewing the existing queue and converting eligible projects from requested to reserved status. Check back for updates on program status; the portal may reopen if funding remains.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commercial, Industrial, and Agricultural Grant Program (CI&A)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration's Commercial, Industrial, and Agricultural Grant Program provides competitive grants to commercial, industrial, agricultural, and non-profit enterprises undertaking deep energy retrofits and cost-effective energy efficiency upgrades. Eligible projects include existing buildings, major renovations, and new construction that exceed minimum code and performance standards and achieve at least 20 percent energy savings. Benefits may include operational expense savings, emissions reductions, health and safety compliance, and productivity enhancements.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides competitive grants from a total budget of up to $8.4 million. For facilities where over 50% of clients are from low-income populations, grants may cover 100% of project costs. For all other projects, grants cover less than 100% of costs. Applicants may also apply for a separate loan to finance the remaining project balance. Electric panel upgrades are an eligible measure. Projects must achieve at least 20% energy savings and exceed minimum code and performance standards.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and operators of commercial, industrial, agricultural, data center, and non-profit facilities located in Maryland, including corporations, LLPs, LLCs, and GPs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency and conservation upgrades, electrification, onsite renewable energy measures, and deep energy retrofit projects for existing buildings, major renovations, and new construction. Projects must result in energy performance exceeding minimum codes or standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must own or operate facilities located in Maryland (statewide).
requirements_list: Projects must be above minimum code and performance standards
Projects must achieve at least 20 percent energy savings
Multifamily residential buildings must contain five or more units
To qualify for 100% project cost coverage, the facility must demonstrate that over 50% of its clientele are from low-income populations
Building uses must be commercial, industrial, data center, agricultural, or non-profit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This is a competitive grant program. Applicants must submit a complete proposal by the deadline electronically when possible. Staff will confirm receipt within one to two business days via email. The Maryland Energy Administration scores applications based on the quality of documentation and the project's environmental benefits. The agency awards grants in rank order until program funds are fully allocated. An informational webinar was held on November 20, 2024 to provide best practices, project eligibility criteria, and application guidance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) Grant Program increases access to affordable and reliable electric vehicle charging networks and reduces transportation greenhouse gas emissions throughout Maryland, with a particular emphasis on low- and moderate-income, overburdened, and underserved communities. The program provides competitive grants through two areas of interest: Area of Interest 1 supports local governments in funding feasibility and planning studies for future EVSE development, and Area of Interest 2 supports applicants in offsetting costs of Level 2 or Level 3 EVSE installations, including Direct Current Fast Charging (DCFC) systems. The program aims to expand equitable access to EV charging infrastructure for businesses, nonprofits, and state and local governments across Maryland.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers competitive grants through two areas of interest. Area of Interest 1 (EV Infrastructure Planning) provides funding to help local governments (counties and municipalities) offset feasibility and planning study costs for future EVSE development, with an anticipated budget of $500,000. Award amounts for AOI1 are calculated using a formula based on applicant entity type and planning project type, ranging from $40,000 to $150,000 per applicant, with reimbursements made in arrears for eligible expenses with supporting documentation. Area of Interest 2 (EVSE Installations) provides funding to help applicants offset costs of Level 2 or Level 3 EVSE installations, including Direct Current Fast Charging systems, with an anticipated budget of $9,000,000, divided into $5 million for Public and Community Oriented Properties and $4 million for Multifamily Housing properties. Per-port incentive amounts range from $5,600 to $150,000 for Owner Operated systems and $5,600 to $120,000 for Third Party Owner Operator systems, depending on power level. Maximum grant amounts per applicant range from $750,000 to $1,000,000 depending on entity type. Grant funds are disbursed as reimbursements in arrears and limited to eligible expenses with supporting evidence such as receipts and invoices. Total anticipated program funding for FY 2026 is $10 million.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 27, 2026 at 3:00 PM EST (AOI2); February 25, 2026 at 3:00 PM EST (AOI1)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, nonprofits, and state and local governments seeking to develop or install electric vehicle charging infrastructure in Maryland, particularly in low- and moderate-income, overburdened, and underserved communities. AOI1 is limited to local governmental entities (counties and municipalities). AOI2 is open to businesses, nonprofits, higher education institutions, local education agencies, and units of municipal or county governments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Area of Interest 1 (EV Infrastructure Planning) funds can be used for community-level and/or site-level EV infrastructure planning activities including feasibility studies, EV readiness plans, engineering analyses, site assessments, and preliminary budgeting for future EVSE installations in or accessible to low- and moderate-income, overburdened, and underserved communities. Area of Interest 2 (EVSE Installations) funds can be used to offset costs of Level 2 or Level 3 EVSE installations including chargers, cables, connectors, pedestals, utility and electrical upgrades, construction/site preparation, engineering/design, permitting costs, warranty, network-related costs, ADA compliance costs, signage, and site lighting (if not already in place) at public, community-oriented, or multifamily housing properties (5+ units) in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: State-wide throughout Maryland, with emphasis on low- and moderate-income, overburdened, and underserved communities. Overburdened communities are defined as any census tract where at least three environmental health indicators are above the 75th percentile statewide, in accordance with Maryland's Climate Solutions Now Act of 2022. Applicants can use the MDEnviroscreen Tool to identify overburdened census tracts. Preference is given to projects over 50 miles from currently available charging stations as indicated in the Alternative Fuels Data Center.
requirements_list: Infrastructure must be in or accessible to low- and moderate-income, overburdened, and underserved communities
Eligible applicants may apply to one or both areas of interest
Applicants must refer to the relevant Funding Opportunity Announcement for specific eligibility requirements, project requirements, and evaluation criteria
AOI1 applicants must be local governmental entities (counties, municipalities, or Baltimore City)

AOI2 applicants must be registered and in good standing with Maryland SDAT (if business/nonprofit), or be accredited higher education institutions, local education agencies, or municipal/county government units
AOI2 projects must result in minimum of two Level 2 or Level 3 charging ports per site
All EVSE equipment must be new (not repurposed or refurbished)
All EVSE must carry minimum 5-year warranty
All networked EVSE must use OCPP 1.6 or newer
EVSE ports must maintain 97% uptime
All equipment must be repaired within 15 business days of issue identification
Projects must be completed within 24 months of grant agreement execution
Grantees must maintain operations and reporting for minimum 5 years post-commissioning for AOI2
Infrastructure projects must be located in Maryland within applicant jurisdiction
AOI1 projects must be completed within 2 years of grant agreement execution
Multiple environmental and design considerations must be addressed including accessibility, pedestrian safety, parking adequacy, and ADA compliance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible applicants may apply to one or both areas of interest through an online JotForm portal. Area of Interest 1 applications use the JotForm application for EV Infrastructure Planning (https://form.jotform.com/transportationmea/fy26-C-EVSE-AOI1-applications), and Area of Interest 2 applications use the JotForm application for EVSE Installations (https://form.jotform.com/transportationmea/FY26-C-EVSE-AOI2-Installations). Applications must include all required documents as specified in the Funding Opportunity Announcement, including project narratives, IRS W-9 forms, budget workbooks, and supporting documentation. For AOI1, local governments must submit applications directly, and the project narrative should not exceed 7 pages. For AOI2, property owners or third-party organizations may apply, project narratives should not exceed 10 pages, and applicants must provide project design documents and equipment specification sheets. Applications are reviewed through a three-step process: (1) Program Manager Eligibility Review to verify minimum eligibility requirements; (2) Individual Evaluation Team Member Review scoring applications according to established criteria; and (3) Group Review by the Evaluation Team to finalize scores and make grant recommendations ranked in descending order by score until funding is exhausted or all eligible applications are funded. Grant application rankings may be adjusted to ensure geographic diversity. Applications should be submitted electronically; staff confirm receipt of electronic applications within one to two business days via email. Applicants will be notified of selection decisions with an expected notification date in Summer 2026. Partial grants are possible depending on the number and quality of applications received and available funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Solar Low-to-Moderate Income Power Purchase Agreement Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to Community Solar Subscriber Organizations to offset costs associated with Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs), enabling clean energy to be offered to low-to-moderate income (LMI), overburdened, and underserved households at lower cost. In FY26, the program focuses specifically on low-income households. Grants help subscriber organizations offer lower subscription rates to low-income households and increase their participation in community solar programs through two Areas of Interest: AOI-1 for projects with at least 15% low-income subscription, and AOI-2 for 100% low-income projects sited on landfills or brownfields.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Approximately $17 million in total funding from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) using Solar Alternative Compliance Payment funding. Initial funding allocation is $5 million for AOI-1 (projects requiring at least 15% low-income subscription with minimum 25% cost savings) and $12 million for AOI-2 (100% low-income projects on landfills/brownfields). AOI-1 grants are capped at $1,000,000 per project. AOI-2 projects are funded at $2,000/kW-dc, capped at $6,000,000 plus interconnection incentives (MEA pays 75% of actual interconnection wiring costs after the first $1,000,000, with maximum interconnection incentive of $3,000,000). Minimum grant amount is $50,000. Funding offsets costs associated with Power Purchase Agreements to enable subscriber organizations to offer lower subscription rates and clean energy to low-income households. Milestone payments are made as authorized by the Grant Agreement, with remaining funds distributed after project produces creditable power.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Solar Subscriber Organizations (Maryland PSC-approved) seeking to provide affordable solar energy to low-income households. Applicants must be registered to do business in Maryland and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. Residents do not receive funds directly from the Maryland Energy Administration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding is used to offset costs associated with Power Purchase Agreements for community solar projects. Funds cannot be used to verify income for subscribers or for project costs incurred prior to grant agreement execution. Funds support installation and operation of solar photovoltaic arrays under the Maryland Community Solar Program, enabling community solar projects to offer clean energy to low-income households at lower cost with lower subscription rates.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide competitive program available throughout Maryland. Project sites and benefiting locations must be within Maryland. The Evaluation Team may adjust rankings to ensure at least one project is available to low-income subscribers in each utility service territory.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Community Solar Subscriber Organization registered with the Maryland Public Service Commission (PSC)
Applicant must be registered to do business in Maryland and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (DAT)
Applicant must have an established Employer Identification Number (EIN/TIN) at time of application
Project site and benefiting locations must be within Maryland
Authority to Operate in Maryland: applicant and contractors must be legally authorized to do business in Maryland
Good Standing requirement: applicant and contractors must provide proof of Good Standing with Maryland DAT
Prior Recipients Restriction: applicants previously funded for the same project cannot receive another grant for that project
Completion Deadline: projects must complete by no later than May 30, 2030
NABCEP Certification Requirement: at least one NABCEP PV Installation Professional (PVIP) or PV Design Specialist (PVDS) must be employed and involved in electrical and mechanical design
Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) Model: subscription must be structured with little to no upfront cost to subscriber, with subscribers paying on $/kWh basis
Contract Terms Guarantee: grantee must provide guarantees that agreed terms will not be changed in manner disadvantaging low-income subscribers over 20-year period
Project Operational Status: project must produce creditable power by date specified in grant
Participation in Maryland PSC Community Solar Program: project must be part of permanent Community Solar Program with subscriber number issued by Maryland PSC, complying with COMAR 20.62
Technical and National Testing Requirements: system must meet IEEE 1547 and National Electric Code (NEC) standards; all components must be listed/labeled by recognized national testing laboratory
Solar Renewable Energy Credits (SRECs): projects must register for and receive SRECs, with verification of successful registration with PSC and PJM Interconnection
Prior Expenses Restriction: funds cannot be used for costs incurred prior to grant agreement execution unless MEA agrees in writing
Ability to Enter Grant Agreement: awarded applicants must enter formal grant agreement with MEA before receiving funds
Count of Subscribers Requirement: grantee must provide count of low-income subscribers with Completion Report by specified date, including detailed explanation of income certification
Maryland Historic Trust Review: review must determine no adverse impact to project site or historical district
AOI-1 Specific Requirement: project must guarantee at least 15% of energy output subscribed to low-income subscribers with minimum 25% cost savings from utility's CSEGS credit rate

AOI-2 Specific Requirements: project must provide at least 50% of energy generated at no cost to designated low-income subscribers, remaining energy subscribed with 25% cost savings; project must be sited on Maryland landfill, rubble-fill, or brownfield site suitable for community solar system
80% Workers Requirement: at least 80% of workers on project must reside within 50 miles of project site per State Government Article §9-20B-05 (SEIF requirement)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Review the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) and all program requirements. Step 2: Prepare required application documents including completed Application Worksheet with Incentive Calculation tab, IRS Form W-9, Good Standing documentation from Maryland DAT, site plan, Google Earth map, energy production estimate, project timeline, utility rate history, evidence of site control, guarantee of savings, and applicable checklists. Step 3: Submit complete Application Package electronically when possible by 3:00 P.M. ET on December 23, 2025. MEA staff will confirm receipt within one to two business days via email. Step 4: Program Manager Eligibility Review - MEA Program Manager reviews application for compliance with Minimum Eligibility Requirements. Applications not meeting requirements are rejected and applicant is notified. Step 5: Evaluation Team Individual Review - Each Evaluation Team member reviews and scores application according to Evaluation Criteria (primary criterion is Greenhouse Gas reduction per dollar of grant funding, with additional favorable criteria including total benefit to subscribers, building rooftops in cities/towns, energy storage pairing, waste landfill/VCP land use, and public education). AOI-1 and AOI-2 applications are scored separately. Step 6: Evaluation Team Group Review - Team convenes to review findings and scores; individual members may modify scores based on new information; final score is average of individual scores. Step 7: Grant Recommendations - Grants recommended in order of highest to lowest eligible score until funding exhausted. Partial grants possible if insufficient funds available for full project funding. Step 8: Upon selection, grantee must enter formal grant agreement with MEA. Upon receipt of commitment letter (if applicable) or signed grant agreement, MEA encumbers funds. Step 9: Grantee completes project installation and notifies MEA when system is operational (all permits closed, inspections passed, commissioning completed, permission to operate received from utility). Step 10: MEA and Subscriber Organization conduct site visit and recalculate final grant amount based on actual capacity and percentage of energy to low-income subscribers. Step 11: Grantee submits Final Invoice and Completion Report with supporting documentation. MEA processes payment request upon receipt of complete and accurate invoice and report.
