structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide competitive grant program that provides funding to eligible public school districts and bus vendors to purchase and lease new electric school buses for student transportation, with a focus on expanding access to funding for overburdened and low to moderate income communities.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants covering up to 120% of the incremental cost of eligible electric school buses, plus funding for charging infrastructure and associated costs. Maximum award is $2,000,000 per grantee, which may increase to $2,500,000 depending on income qualifications and school district size. Up to $4.9 million is available in Fiscal Year 2026. Eligible charging installation costs are now covered proportionally to charger costs to support expansion of EV charging capacity. Charging infrastructure incentives are capped at 30% of total project funding request. Associated costs include: (1) Project Start-up for LEAs - up to $200,000 per application for planning and fleet analysis; (2) Project Start-up for vendors - up to $25,000 per vendor (maximum 4 vendors per school district); (3) School District Technician Training - up to $7,200 to certify six technicians in maintaining and repairing high voltage battery and electrical systems. Funding is distributed as cost-reimbursement only; applicants must have financial capability to cover expenses upfront and seek reimbursement from MEA. Reimbursement occurs monthly upon submission and approval of invoices within 45 days after the end of each month.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public local education agencies and fleets or private school bus vendors operating on behalf of local education agencies that transport students for school or school-related programming.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of new electric school buses for routine transportation of students, charging infrastructure installation, and associated costs including project start-up expenses for EVSE and facility planning, and school district technician training for maintaining and repairing electric school bus systems. Retrofit or repowered vehicles are not eligible, and vehicles previously funded by another Maryland State grant are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available to all Maryland public school districts and eligible bus vendors.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public local education agency or a fleet/private school bus vendor operating on behalf of a local education agency
Vehicle must be purchased new (retrofits or repowered vehicles are not eligible)
Vehicle must be used for routine transportation of students for school or school-related programming or activities
Vehicle cannot have been funded in whole or in part by another Maryland State grant
Combined MEA and other state incentives (including federal) cannot exceed the total funding request or project cost
Requested vehicles must be domiciled within the State of Maryland for a minimum of three years
Applicants must agree to operate awarded vehicles according to the Grant Program General Provisions specified by the Maryland Energy Administration

Private school bus vendors and non-profit applicants representing a school district must demonstrate current registration and good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Non-profit applicants not directly operating the vehicles shall provide evidence of a contractual agreement with an LEA at the time of application
Requested vehicles must be appropriately insured and authorized for use in the State of Maryland
Applicants must consent to share vehicle usage data with MEA for a minimum of three years, including VINs, license plate numbers, bus routes, and other pertinent data
Vehicle owners are obligated to notify MEA in advance of any intention to sell or relocate awarded vehicles outside Maryland; repayment of received funding is required if vehicles are relocated

Replacement component: if the new electric school bus will replace an older diesel school bus, applicant must state the Model Year (MY) of the replaced bus (must be MY 2013 or older diesel buses or oldest buses in fleet, whichever is feasible)

Buses previously funded through MEA's Clean Fuels Incentive Program (CFIP), Alternative Fuel Infrastructure Program (AFIP), or Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Grant Program (MHD ZEV Grant Program) are not eligible for this program
Retroactive funding will not be provided; vehicles must not be ordered and/or purchased prior to execution of the grant agreement or commitment letter
If combined funding from MEA and other sources exceeds the total project costs, excess funds must be returned to MEA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through the Jotform application form by December 26, 2025 at 3:00 PM ET. All application materials and instructions are provided in the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) document. Complete application package must include: (1) Completed, signed Jotform application form with Sections A-E; (2) Attachment A (ESB Summary Table) and Attachment B (EVSE Summary Table) saved as Excel files using specified naming conventions; (3) Supporting documentation including vendor technical specifications, vehicle lease documentation (if applicable), completed IRS Form W-9, site host letter of commitment (if applicable), and proposed EVSE equipment and installation quotes/estimates (if applicable). Technical advising is available for free. One-on-one meetings or calls are available by contacting the program manager at transportation.mea@maryland.gov or natalie.buscemi@maryland.gov. Confirmation of receipt will be sent within two business days. If confirmation is not received within this timeframe, applicant must contact MEA to confirm successful transmission. Applications are evaluated by a review team of at least three qualified energy professionals using a 100-point scoring rubric based on: Application Quality (10 points), Project Cost and Funding Request (15 points), Emission Reductions Benefits (30 points), Project Planning/Schedule (30 points), Project Communication and Partnerships (10 points), and Project Equity (5 points). Projects are ranked highest to lowest with priority given to schools in overburdened and low-to-moderate income communities. Award recommendations are finalized by the MEA Agency Director or designee.

structured_extraction.program_name: Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) Rebate Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides rebates to reduce the financial burden of acquiring and installing electric vehicle charging stations and to increase EV adoption in support of the state's EV deployment and greenhouse gas reduction goals. It supports both residential and commercial installations statewide, with a total FY2026 budget of $2.5 million. Residential rebates are initially allocated 60% ($1.5 million) and commercial rebates 40% ($1.0 million). After April 1, 2026, initial allocation limits are removed and all eligible applications are processed in order received.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This is a reimbursement program where applicants must provide their own funding upfront. Rebates are issued on a first-come, first-served basis as funds are available to complete and eligible applications. Residential rebates cover 50% of eligible EVSE acquisition and installation costs, capped at $700 per charger. Commercial rebates cover 50% of eligible costs, capped at $5,000 per charger, with a maximum aggregate award of $125,000 per entity in FY2026. Level 1 EVSE purchased on or after October 1, 2023 are no longer eligible (except when upgraded to Level 2). The FY2026 program has $2.5 million in total funding ($1.5 million initially for residential, $1.0 million initially for commercial). After April 1, 2026, initial allocation limits are removed and all eligible applications are processed in the order received. Eligible costs include site design, charger equipment, installation labor, permitting, site preparation, utility connection upgrades, signage, and operation equipment. Ineligible costs include electricity fuel, ongoing maintenance, taxes, shipping, and credit card fees. Applicants cannot receive awards for Level 1 EVSE purchased after October 1, 2023, used equipment, or equipment replacing previously incentivized EVSE.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1, 2026 at 3:00 PM EST, or until budgeted FY2026 funding is exhausted, whichever comes first. Application must be received within 6 months of EVSE installation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, businesses, non-profits, and government organizations seeking to install electric vehicle charging stations. Eligible residential applicants include individuals purchasing EVSE for private use at their home and individuals with legal rental licenses purchasing for residential properties they own and lease. Eligible commercial applicants include employers providing EVSE to employees, companies supporting fleet electric vehicles, incorporated non-profit entities in good standing with SDAT, units of state or local government, and owners/property managers of multi-unit developments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and installation of qualified electric vehicle supply equipment (charging stations). Eligible costs include site design, charger equipment, installation labor, permitting, site preparation, utility connection upgrades, signage, and equipment necessary to implement and operate the EVSE. Subscription-based project costs are also eligible. Gift cards may be listed as cash expenditures for rebate reimbursement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. EVSE must be installed on property located in Maryland and must be used for charging on-road motor vehicles propelled by electricity. MEA is investigating options to provide additional benefits for EVSE installations in multi-unit developments within low-to-moderate-income, overburdened, and underserved communities.
requirements_list: Applicants must acquire and install qualified EV supply equipment
Level 1 EVSE purchased on or after October 1, 2023 are not eligible, unless upgraded to Level 2 charging capability
Multi-unit developments (MUDs) are eligible

Applicants must provide an IRS Form W-9 with name matching income tax return format; residential applicants required, commercial applicants required if first-time applicants or if mailing address changed
Applicants must comply with MEA's current data collection protocols as detailed in the Funding Opportunity Announcement
Equipment must be electric vehicle charging equipment
Installation must be completed and paid in full before application submission
Equipment must be safety certified by a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory (NRTL) identified by OSHA
Equipment must be purchased new; used EVSE is ineligible
For installations with labor costs, EVSE must be installed by a Maryland-licensed, professional electrical contractor; self-installation requires proof of Maryland electrical license
EVSE may be networked or non-networked
EVSE may be publicly or privately accessible
EVSE may be hard-wired or plug-in
Residential applicants limited to one rebate per individual per address
Application must be submitted within 6 months of EVSE installation
Commercial applicants must be registered and in good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Commercial applicants cannot receive more than $125,000 in aggregate FY2026 funding
Applicant must have right to install EVSE at property or have obtained property owner/landlord consent
Installation must comply with all local and state zoning, building, historic preservation, and applicable codes
Applicant must have obtained all necessary regulatory approvals, permits, variances, and licenses including Maryland Historical Trust approval if applicable
Commercial applicants must register publicly available EVSE with Plugshare and US Department of Energy's Alternative Fuel Data Center (AFDC)
Applicant must not be in default on financial obligations to the State or MEA
Regulated utilities and federal government units are ineligible
A single charger cannot receive multiple rebates even if owned by different people or relocated
MEA may withhold rebate funds to satisfy outstanding tax or financial obligations to the State or federal government
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted electronically through the MyMEA Portal at https://mea.maryland.gov/evse-program-details. Applicants must first create an account using their full legal name (no middle initials). Residential applicants select the residential program option and commercial applicants select the commercial option (or authorized third-party representative). Applications must be submitted within 6 months of EVSE installation and payment in full. Required application documents include: paid invoice or receipt for EVSE charger showing items purchased, price, date, and applicant name/address; paid invoice or receipt for installation showing price, date, installation address, and clear description of work performed (descriptive invoices required); photograph of installed EVSE (for NEMA 14-50 outlet installations, photo must show EVSE plugged into outlet); and completed IRS W-9 Form with name matching income tax return format and identical mailing address and taxpayer ID to application. Incomplete applications are deemed ineligible until all necessary supporting documents are provided. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis and processing begins only after MEA receives all necessary documents, not from the initial submission date. Rebates are issued as funds are available; issuance cannot be assured once FY2026 budget is exhausted. Applicants can track application status through the portal and receive update emails. For questions about applications and status, contact evse.mea@maryland.gov. For general program questions, contact Natalie Buscemi at transportation.mea@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: EmPOWER Maryland is a statewide energy efficiency program established by the EmPOWER Maryland Energy Efficiency Act of 2008. Maryland's largest electric and gas utilities offer incentives to help households and businesses save energy and money, including free or discounted energy audits, weatherization services, and efficient appliances. The program promotes energy efficiency to help reduce per capita electricity usage and peak demand, saving Marylanders money. A 2024 law (House Bill 864) requires utilities to develop comprehensive energy efficiency and conservation plans to achieve greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets through energy efficiency, conservation, demand response, and beneficial electrification programs. A 2024 law also requires utilities to add incentives for switching from fossil fuel heating and appliances to electric alternatives. Low-income customers can receive installation of energy conservation measures at zero out-of-pocket cost through the Low Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP) administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD).
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Utilities offer a variety of incentives including free or discounted energy audits, weatherization assistance, and rebates or discounts on efficient appliances. Low-income customers can receive installation of energy conservation measures at zero out-of-pocket cost through the Low Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP) administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). Under House Bill 864 (effective 2024-2025), utilities must develop comprehensive plans achieving greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets through energy efficiency, conservation, demand response, and beneficial electrification programs. A 2024 law requires utilities to add incentives for switching from fossil fuel heating and appliances to electric alternatives. Utilities provide full cost recovery through surcharge line items on customer bills. For 2025 and 2026, electric companies must achieve at least 2.25% annual electricity savings; starting in 2027, at least 2.5% annually. At least 80% of greenhouse gas emissions reductions must come from behind-the-meter programs. The Department of Housing and Community Development procures or provides energy efficiency, conservation, demand response, and beneficial electrification programs for low- and moderate-income individuals, with contractors required to pay at least 150% of state minimum wage, provide career advancement training, afford collective bargaining rights, provide paid leave, comply with wage and hour laws, and offer health insurance and retirement benefits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; no specific deadline. Electric companies and gas companies must submit plans on or before January 1, 2025, and on or before January 1 every 3 years thereafter starting in 2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland households and businesses served by participating investor-owned utilities, including Baltimore Gas & Electric (BGE), Potomac Edison Company (PE), Delmarva Power & Light (Delmarva), Potomac Electric Power Company (PEPCO), Washington Gas Light Company (WGL), Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative, Inc. (SMECO), and Choptank Electric Cooperative. Low-income customers qualifying for DHCD low-income assistance programs can receive zero-cost energy efficiency and conservation measures.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy audits, weatherization, and efficient appliances to reduce energy use and costs. Funds support energy efficiency improvements, beneficial electrification (switching from fossil fuel heating and appliances to electric alternatives), demand response programs, and conservation measures. For low-income households, funding covers health and safety upgrades, weatherization, energy efficiency, and general maintenance through a whole-home approach coordinating multiple funding sources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to customers of participating Maryland utilities, including service territories of Baltimore Gas & Electric (BGE), Potomac Edison Company (PE), Delmarva Power & Light (Delmarva), Potomac Electric Power Company (PEPCO), Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative, Inc. (SMECO), Washington Gas Light Company (WGL), and Choptank Electric Cooperative. Programs administered by utilities and the Department of Housing and Community Development serve all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Must be a customer of a participating EmPOWER Maryland utility
Low-income customers must qualify for the Department of Housing and Community Development's low-income assistance programs to receive zero-cost installation of energy conservation measures
For low-income residential properties, household income must be below 250% of the federal poverty level or meet eligibility criteria approved by the Public Service Commission

Contractors performing work under DHCD programs must meet job requirements including paying at least 150% of state minimum wage, providing career advancement training, affording collective bargaining rights, providing paid leave, complying with federal and state wage and hour laws, offering health insurance with monthly premiums not exceeding 8.5% of employee net monthly earnings, and offering retirement benefits
Thermal insulating materials used in programs must not contain formaldehyde intentionally added or present at greater than 0.1% by weight
For weatherization of leased or rented residences, benefits must accrue primarily to low-income tenants; rent cannot be increased and tenants cannot be evicted as a result of weatherization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your utility provider directly to learn about available programs and incentives. Each utility administers its own EmPOWER portfolio. Submit applications electronically when possible; staff will confirm receipt within one to two business days via email. Low-income customers should visit the DHCD Low Income Energy Efficiency Program (LIEEP) page or contact DHCD for information on zero-cost assistance. For questions, contact the Maryland Energy Administration at DLInfo_MEA@maryland.gov or call 410-537-4000 or 1-800-72-ENERGY. Utilities must develop plans achieving greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets as established by the Public Service Commission, with plans submitted on or before January 1, 2025, and subsequently on or before January 1 every 3 years starting in 2027.

structured_extraction.program_name: Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grants (EECBG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded competitive grant program administered by the Maryland Energy Administration that provides subgrants to county and local governments to support energy planning and strategy development, decarbonization strategy development, energy audits and feasibility studies, and expansion or revision of existing energy plans. The program helps communities transition to a low-carbon, climate-resilient economy through planning activities that provide comprehensive community approaches to addressing the State's clean energy and climate goals, while improving community health, well-being, and economic development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive subgrants with awards anticipated to range between $100,000 and $350,000; however, larger awards are possible for exceptional proposals. Total anticipated funding allocation of up to $1,462,617 for all proposals. Funding is distributed through regional allocations: Central region $210,230, Eastern region $650,210, Southern region $188,457, and Western region $413,720. Matching funds are not required. Partial awards may be made depending on the number and quality of applications received. Grant period extends to approximately December 2, 2026, with possible extensions for good cause upon request and MEA approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Incorporated cities, towns, and counties in Maryland that were not eligible to receive EECBG funding directly from the U.S. Department of Energy under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act of 2021. The ten largest counties (Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Carroll, Charles, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, and St. Mary's) and Baltimore City were eligible for direct DOE funding and are ineligible for MEA's allocation. Other incorporated units of local government seeking energy efficiency improvements are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy planning and strategy development, energy-focused decarbonization strategy development including considerations for future renewable energy or electrification deployment, energy audits and feasibility studies, and expansion or revision of existing energy plans and strategies. Projects must be planning activities only; capital expenditures and new construction are not eligible. Projects involving fossil-fuel or other combustion technologies that produce greenhouse gas emissions are typically not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Counties and incorporated units of local government in Maryland with regional allocations ensuring equitable access. Central region includes Montgomery, Carroll, Howard, Baltimore, Harford, and Cecil counties. Eastern region includes Kent, Queen Anne's, Talbot, Caroline, Dorchester, Wicomico, Somerset, and Worcester counties. Southern region includes Charles, Prince George's, Anne Arundel, Calvert, and St. Mary's counties. Western region includes Garrett, Allegany, Washington, and Frederick counties. Funds may be redistributed between regions if insufficient eligible applications are received from a particular region.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an incorporated city, town, or county in Maryland that did not receive direct EECBG funding from DOE
Applicant must submit a complete application by the December 12, 2025 deadline at 3 p.m.
Proposed project must align with eligible activities: energy planning, decarbonization strategy development, energy audits, feasibility studies, or expansion of existing energy plans
Project must be a planning activity only; capital expenditures and new construction are ineligible
Projects strictly for research and development without direct application to energy conservation are ineligible
Initiatives that have been completed prior to grant award announcement are ineligible
Projects including fossil-fuel or other combustion technologies producing greenhouse gas emissions are typically ineligible
Double-dipping or overlapping funding for the same expenses is not permitted
Applicant must provide a W-9 form with the application matching the organization name and business address
Applicant must provide written authorization from the applicant's governing body
Applicant must submit a detailed project budget by line item with overall requested funding amount
Application must include project narrative and value proposition (250 words max)
Application must address assurance of longevity and project maintenance over time (250 words max)
Application must demonstrate alignment with existing state policies including BEPS, Maryland's Climate Pollution Reduction Plan, and Renewable Portfolio Standard (250 words max)
Application must describe collaboration with other organizations, agencies, or stakeholders (250 words max)
Stacking with compatible federal, state, and local incentives is encouraged but double-dipping is prohibited
If selected, grantee must receive electronic payments through the State of Maryland's Comptroller's Office
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a complete EECBG Grant Program application form (PDF version available on MEA website) by December 12, 2025 at 3 p.m. 2. Application must include: government name and address (matching W-9), authorized signatory information, application point of contact, project narrative and value proposition, assurance of longevity, alignment with state initiatives, collaboration details, detailed line-item budget, W-9 form, and written authorization from governing body. 3. Submit all materials electronically unless opted out of electronic communications. 4. Applications are reviewed in three stages: (a) Program Manager conducts eligibility review against Section 2 criteria; ineligible applications are rejected; (b) Evaluation Team members individually review and score eligible applications using evaluation criteria (Value Proposition 0-4 points, Longevity and Continuity 0-3 points, Alignment with existing policies 0-3 points, Collaboration 0-3 points, maximum 13 points); (c) Evaluation Team convenes for group review, finalizes scores, and recommends awards. 5. Highest-scoring proposals are selected for awards subject to funding availability and regional allocations. 6. Partial awards may be offered if sufficient funds are not available for full project funding. 7. Selected applicants execute grant agreement with MEA (anticipated by January 21, 2026) and must return fully executed agreement within 10 business days.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Resilient Infrastructure for Sustainable Energy (RISE) Program provides grants to help fund improvements to Maryland's electricity and related power infrastructure. The program aims to strengthen the electric grid and build resilience against threats including severe weather, tropical storms, hurricanes, extreme temperatures, winter storms, cyberattacks, physical attacks, and aging components. The program is federally funded through Section 40101(d) of the federal Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (Bipartisan Infrastructure Law).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides competitive grants with a total program budget of approximately $15,000,000, of which approximately $13,000,000 is federally funded. Funds are available to Maryland electricity infrastructure operators, fuel suppliers, and other utility industry stakeholders. Grant amounts vary by applicant size: AOI 1 (Large Applicants - those selling more than 4,000,000 MWh annually) receive grants not expected to exceed $3,000,000 with a mandatory 100% cost-match. AOI 2 (Small Applicants - those selling 4,000,000 or less MWh annually) receive grants not expected to exceed $3,000,000 with a mandatory one-third (1/3) cost-match. Partial grants may be awarded depending on application volume and available funding. Each selected applicant must meet federal requirements in addition to Maryland requirements. Grantees must comply with federal funding reporting and funding requirements as conditions of receiving payment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland electricity infrastructure operators, fuel suppliers, electricity grid operators, electricity storage operators, electricity generators, transmission owners and operators, distribution providers, and other related utility industry stakeholders
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support improvements to Maryland's electricity and related power infrastructure with a focus on enhancing the resilience and reliability of the electricity grid through non-generation measures. Allowable activities include: weatherization technologies and equipment; fire-resistant technologies and fire prevention systems; monitoring and control technologies; undergrounding of electrical equipment; utility pole management; relocation or reconductoring of power lines with advanced conductors; vegetation and fuel-load management; non-generation distributed energy resources including microgrids and battery-storage subcomponents for enhancing system adaptive capacity during disruptive events; adaptive protection technologies; advanced modeling technologies; hardening of power lines, facilities, and substations; and replacement of old overhead conductors and underground cables. Prohibited uses include construction of new electric generating facilities, construction of large-scale battery-storage facilities not used for enhancing system adaptive capacity during disruptive events, and cybersecurity measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. All project sites must be located within the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be legally authorized to transact business in Maryland with an established Employer Identification Number (EIN) at time of application
Applicant must be in Good Standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (DAT) with proof provided via Business Entity Search screenshot/PDF or Certificate of Good Standing
Project site(s) must be located within the State of Maryland
Each grantee must meet certain federal requirements including NEPA review, Davis-Bacon Act compliance, and Build America, Buy America Act compliance before grant agreement execution
Applicant must contribute a cost-match based on AOI: 100% for AOI 1 (Large Applicants) or one-third (1/3) for AOI 2 (Small Applicants)

Project must include a Project Planning Committee composed of community, governmental, utility, and other relevant stakeholders; applicant must demonstrate good faith effort to engage local electric utility even if declined
Any contractor, developer, vendor, or third-party organization with executed contract must be in Good Standing with DAT with written evidence provided
Maryland RISE Program funds cannot be used for project costs incurred prior to execution of grant agreement with MEA
Prior projects that include same scope of work covered under previous or existing MEA grant will only be considered case-by-case with appropriate justification
Maryland RISE Program funds can only be used for eligible activities as listed; funds cannot be used for prohibited activities
If solar PV or battery storage technologies are considered, at least one NABCEP PV Installation Professional or PV Design Specialist must be employed and involved in electrical and mechanical design
Applicant must be able to enter into a grant agreement with MEA prior to receiving funds
Any project funded must be completed no later than June 30, 2028, assuming grant agreement execution by June 15, 2025
Municipal, county, or state entity applicants must attest to compliance with State Finance and Procurement Article requirements; MEA provides funds directly to government entity grantee only
Maryland Historic Trust review must be completed before grant funds are disbursed; adverse impact findings must be mitigated or avoided before disbursement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a complete application package by 3:00 P.M. ET on Tuesday, January 21, 2025, to GridResilience.MEA@Maryland.gov. The application package must include: (1) completed and signed FY25 Maryland RISE Application Form; (2) project proposal not exceeding ten (10) pages; (3) completed FY25 Maryland RISE Project Budget Workbook; (4) complete, accurate, and up-to-date IRS Form W9; and (5) Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation Good Standing documentation. Applications are evaluated through a four-step review process: (1) Program Manager Eligibility Review verifies compliance with Minimum Eligibility Requirements; applications not meeting requirements are rejected; (2) Evaluation Team Member Individual Review where each team member scores applications according to Evaluation Criteria; (3) Evaluation Team Group Review where team members convene to review findings and finalize scores, with final score determined by averaging individual member scores; (4) DOE Clearance where recommended projects are submitted to the U.S. Department of Energy for required approval before grant issuance. MEA will notify selected applicants and execute grant agreements; non-selected applicants will also be informed. Only highest-scoring proposals meeting Minimum Eligibility Requirements are considered for funding subject to program availability. MEA does not anticipate funding projects scoring fewer than sixteen (16) points out of twenty-seven (27) possible points. Partial grants may be offered if insufficient funds remain for full project funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Higher Education Clean Energy Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive statewide grant program administered by the Maryland Energy Administration that supports Maryland's accredited colleges and universities in adopting on-site renewable energy technologies, integrating strategic energy planning into operations and academic curricula, and advancing workforce development in the renewable energy sector. The program funds solar installations, sustainability planning, clean energy curriculum development, and workforce training to create sustainable campuses that serve as learning environments and hubs for renewable energy education and job creation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding totaling $8,000,000 from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF). Maximum funding caps are: $1,000,000 for solar installation activities per application (up to $2,500/kW for applicant-purchased systems or $600/kW for third-party owned systems), $145,000 for campus clean energy master planning per applicant (mandatory for first-time grantees), $145,000 for clean energy sector course development per applicant, and $25,000 for student internships per applicant (up to $5,000 per intern, maximum 5 interns). Applicants may submit one or more applications. Grant administration costs up to 15% of total awarded funds are allowable. Expected period of performance: 36-39 months from grant agreement execution.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's accredited two and four year colleges and universities (Institutions of Higher Education)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Solar system installations (roof-mounted, ground-mounted, or canopies over parking areas), strategic energy planning and campus sustainability planning, clean energy curriculum development and workforce training, student internships in the renewable energy and sustainability sectors, campus clean energy master plan development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all of Maryland. For additional compliance fee-funded awards, limited to community colleges located in census-tracts with median income at or below 80% of state median income, or in overburdened or underserved communities.

For solar installations: applicants must leverage federal incentive programs or provide compelling reason for waiver

First-time applicants must develop a Campus Clean Energy Master Plan (mandatory, up to $145,000)
First-time applicants can only apply for CCEMP and course development funding in first application only

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit applications through the electronic application portal on the Maryland Energy Administration website. Applicants complete and submit a Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) response with required minimum documentation including: authorization letter, IRS Form W-9, system diagrams, site maps, prospective construction schedule, solar energy calculator outputs, electrical schematics, cost savings analysis, comprehensive project budget with leveraged federal/state/local funding identified, and for first-time grantees, CCEMP narrative and schedule. Applications are evaluated competitively by a review team including MEA staff and external experts in energy, construction, and capital development. Primary evaluation metric is energy generation (kWh) per dollar of MEA grant funding (kWh/$). Applications are ranked based on multiple weighted criteria including cost-effective climate impact, community engagement plan, existing solar energy courses, minority serving institution status, scope justification, student internship utilization, course development pursuit, past performance with MEA, and environmental justice considerations. One grant per eligible applicant receives priority; additional awards made if funds remain. Geographic diversity is considered after overall scoring.

structured_extraction.program_name: Inflation Reduction Act Home Energy Rebates Program (HERO & HEAR)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration administers two rebate programs created under the federal Inflation Reduction Act to help homeowners and low-to-moderate income households with energy improvements. The programs include the Home Efficiency Rebates Opportunity (HERO) program, which supports qualifying whole-home energy efficiency upgrades that reduce energy use by at least 20%, and the Home Electrification & Appliance Rebates (HEAR) program, which funds electrification upgrades to single-family and multi-family homes. Both programs focus on low-and-moderate income beneficiaries and include components developed in partnership with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. The HERO program has received conditional approval from the U.S. Department of Energy and is awaiting final approval before launching.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates for energy efficiency and electrification upgrades to single-family and multi-family homes, focused on low-and-moderate income beneficiaries, through the HERO and HEAR programs. HERO provides rebates for qualifying whole-home energy efficiency upgrades that achieve at least a 20% reduction in energy use. HEAR provides rebates for home electrification and appliance upgrades, specifically for replacing fossil fuel appliances (e.g., fuel oil, natural gas) with electric alternatives such as heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, and other qualifying equipment. Rebates can be worth up to $8,000 for low and moderate income households. HEAR rebates cannot be used for electric-to-electric appliance replacements; all appliance replacements must involve fossil fuel to electric conversions. Retroactive rebates are not available for HEAR projects that have already been completed.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency and electrification upgrades to single-family and multi-family homes, including qualifying whole-home energy efficiency improvements that reduce energy consumption by at least 20%, heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, and other qualifying clean energy equipment and appliances. Electrification includes replacing fossil fuel-powered systems and appliances with electric alternatives, such as switching from a gas furnace to an electric heat pump or replacing a gas water heater with an electric one.

structured_extraction.program_name: Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program administered by the Maryland Energy Administration that provides low-interest financing for cost-effective energy efficiency and conservation projects for eligible borrowers' facilities and operations. The program helps Maryland nonprofits, businesses, local governments, and state agencies reduce energy consumption, lower energy costs, and decrease greenhouse gas emissions. It prioritizes comprehensive projects with multiple measures to maximize energy savings and supports a wide range of sectors including commercial, agricultural, manufacturing, and government facilities.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: First-come, first-served loans for energy efficiency projects available in two categories: (1) Microloans: $10,000-$50,000 at 3% interest, up to 10 years, with simple payback by no later than 50% of project cost-effectiveness; (2) Traditional Loans: $50,001-$500,000 at 2% interest, up to 18 years, with simple payback not exceeding project cost-effectiveness. For State agencies and DGS: up to $2,000,000 at 0% interest plus 1% administrative fee, up to 18 years. All borrowers require personal guarantees. Microloans may not require collateral but require personal guarantee(s). Traditional loans require fully-secured liens on equipment and possibly property. FY26 total funding: $4,281,842. First 90 days (July 1 - October 31, 2025): $2,140,921 reserved for nonprofits and $2,140,921 for state governmental bodies. Restrictions lift November 1, 2025. Application fee: $250 for businesses, nonprofits, and local governments (state agencies exempt, instead pay 1% administrative fee on loan balance).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland non-profit organizations, local governments, Maryland businesses, state agencies, commercial building owners, agricultural building owners and operators, and State of Maryland governmental bodies including departments, colleges, and universities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy conservation measures and improvements in eligible facilities that reduce energy consumption and cost, including: LED lighting and controls; heat pump replacements from fossil fuels; HVAC electrification alternatives; building envelope measures (insulation, air sealing); chiller replacements; building management systems and automation; hot water, chilled water, and steam system management; variable frequency drives; process-specific equipment; combined heat and power for manufacturing and critical infrastructure where electrification alternatives unavailable. Funds may also cover ancillary costs including technical assessments, studies, plans and specifications, start-up, architectural and engineering services, equipment procurement, licenses, materials, construction, rehabilitation, modification, and installation of necessary machinery and equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Projects must be located within the State of Maryland and installed at facilities owned or leased by the applicant for at least the duration until the loan is fully repaid.
requirements_list: Eligible borrower must be a Maryland non-profit organization, local government, Maryland business, or state agency with legal authority to transact business in Maryland
Business located within a residence is not eligible
Non-governmental borrowers must be in Good Standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Project must be cost-effective with energy cost savings to be achieved before consideration of rebates or incentives
Project must demonstrate accurate and complete 12 consecutive months of baseline energy usage under normal conditions
Energy savings claims must use vetted sources such as Mid-Atlantic Technical Resource Manual or energy modeling software
Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis subject to funding availability
For facility retrofits, 12 months of utility bills and completed EmPOWER rebate applications required
For incremental improvements, baseline energy consumption estimation documentation required
Facility must be owned or leased by applicant; if leased, explicit written permission from owner required and owner acknowledgment that applicant will own installed equipment
Project must not adversely affect historical significance if on historic property
For businesses and nonprofits requesting microloans, applicants must demonstrate adequate financial resources to collateralize the loan

All required documentation must be submitted including IRS Form W9, articles of incorporation/organization, bylaws/operating agreements, Certificate of Good Standing, financial statements (3 years), board roster, goods/services summary, utility bills or baseline documentation

Security requirements may include personal guarantees, security agreements on equipment with UCC-1 filings, liens on real property, legal counsel opinion letters, or other collateral as determined by MEA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the online application portal with separate applications available for businesses/nonprofits/local governments and for state agencies. Step 1: Program Manager reviews application package for completeness and compliance with minimum evaluation criteria. Step 2: Technical analysis by outside vendor evaluates ECM specifications, energy savings assumptions, and project feasibility. Step 3: Financial viability and creditworthiness review assesses repayment ability, financial risk, and appropriate security instruments. MEA staff confirms receipt within 1-2 business days via email. Applications are evaluated on first-come, first-served basis based on date MEA receives complete application. Loan review process may take several months to allow third-party reviews sufficient time. Upon final Request for Disbursement, borrower must provide evidence of project completion. Disbursements made directly to borrower by check from Comptroller of Maryland upon presentation of invoices or proof of payment for Eligible Project Costs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Government Energy Modernization (L-GEM) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland Energy Administration that supports local governments in Maryland to engage in sustainable, long-term clean energy and energy efficiency projects. The program provides incentives for local governments to undertake decarbonization planning, energy efficiency, clean energy, and electrification projects—including geothermal systems, solar, and landfill-gas-to-energy installations—leading to reduced energy usage and greenhouse gas emissions, increased cost savings, and robust clean energy and economic development. For FY26, the program offers over $64 million in one-time funding to accelerate adoption of clean energy, replacing the Maryland Smart Energy Communities (MSEC) program. Funding is divided into four areas of interest (AOI): AOI1 provides non-competitive formula block grants for counties and Baltimore City; AOI2, AOI3, and AOI4 provide competitive merit-based grants for municipalities and counties for planning, implementation, and electrification projects respectively.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time $64 million in grant funding for FY26, divided into four Areas of Interest: AOI1 provides approximately $50 million in non-competitive formula block grants for counties and Baltimore City for planning and implementation of energy efficiency and renewable energy projects, available over 36 months; AOI2 provides approximately $3 million in competitive merit-based grants for municipalities and counties for planning activities (feasibility studies, energy audits, strategy development, energy planning), with awards up to $300,000 and 90% reimbursement rate; AOI3 provides approximately $7 million in competitive grants for implementation of energy efficiency and renewable energy projects (excluding electrification), up to $1,000,000 per application; AOI4 provides $4 million in competitive grants for electrification projects replacing fossil fuel systems. AOI1 recipients receive secured funding upfront for flexible use over the 36-month period. AOI2, AOI3, and AOI4 provide merit-based awards following competitive review. Cost shares vary: AOI1 requires 5-10% cost share based on county per capita income; AOI2 requires 10% cost share; AOI3 and AOI4 vary by project type. Programs operate on a reimbursement basis for most projects, except third-party-owned solar systems which are funded at $1,000/kW-DC without standard cost share requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Incorporated towns, cities, and counties of Maryland, including county and municipal governments and Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning activities including feasibility studies, energy audits, energy planning, and strategy development; renewable energy projects such as solar, geothermal, and landfill-gas-to-energy installations; energy efficiency projects including building envelope measures like weatherization and insulation, and efficient equipment and appliance upgrades like air source heat pumps and LEDs; and electrification projects to replace fossil fuel systems with electric systems across local government portfolios of public facilities. Funding may also support building automation systems, retrocommissioning, and energy storage when paired with renewable energy generation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Only incorporated towns, cities, and counties of Maryland may apply. Statewide program. Projects must be located at government-owned or leased buildings or facilities in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an incorporated town, city, or county in Maryland
Applicants must be county or municipal governments
Counties and Baltimore City are eligible for AOI1 (non-competitive block grant); municipalities are not eligible for AOI1
Municipalities are eligible for AOI2 (planning grants), AOI3 (implementation excluding electrification), and AOI4 (electrification projects)
Counties that apply for AOI1 are not eligible to apply for AOI2 or AOI3 but may apply for AOI4
AOI1 applications require formula-based funding structure and counties must request a minimum of $500,000
AOI2, AOI3, and AOI4 applications are evaluated on merit based on alignment with program goals and priorities
Implementation projects in AOI3 may not include electrification
Applications must be submitted by the grantee; third parties may not submit on behalf of the grantee
Signatory authority required from an officer with authority to commit the grantee (e.g., Chair of Board, President, CFO, General Manager)
IRS Form W-9 must be submitted with application; name and mailing address must match organization records
Applicants must identify staff responsible for overseeing activities after award period ends
For AOI1, counties must provide comprehensive narrative outlining vision for 36-month grant period, including project types, anticipated timelines, target buildings/systems, and expected outcomes
For AOI2 and AOI3, budget documentation using MEA's budget template is required
Equipment must not be purchased or installed before grant agreement execution

Cost share requirements: AOI1 ranges from 5-10% based on county per capita income ($68,500 threshold); AOI2 requires 10% cost share; AOI3 and AOI4 vary by project type; third-party-owned solar exempt from standard cost share with per-kW-DC funding instead
Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) benchmarking compliance required; applicants must provide Unique Building Identifiers (UBIDs) of covered buildings
Communities must identify energy code version enforced and provide documentation; 2018 International Energy Conservation Code (IECC) recommended

For rented or leased buildings: letter of concurrence from property owner required stating permission and commitment to maintain improvements for equipment life; payback period must be shorter than remaining lease term
Projects on government-owned or leased facilities only; subgrants to public agencies permitted if projects align with program goals
No funding for fossil fuel or combustion technologies except basic health and safety repairs with technical analysis; cost alone is not valid justification
No funding for projects already started in calendar 2025; no payments or financial commitments before grant agreement execution
Planning and design activities may be completed in advance but construction cannot begin until grant agreement signed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications submitted through online electronic application forms (separate for each AOI). Applicants submit by 5:00 P.M. ET on December 5, 2025. For AOI1: Submit comprehensive narrative with project overview, funding request, and supporting documents via JotForm at https://form.jotform.com/marylandenergy/FY26-L-GEM-AOI1. After application deadline, MEA reviews all applications and determines funding allocations. Grant agreements anticipated to be finalized by Summer 2026. Once executed, counties must submit separate project-specific forms on rolling basis for MEA approval prior to implementation. Upon project completion, submit invoice and final report for fund release. Optional one-on-one meetings available with program manager. For AOI2 and AOI3: Submit completed application via JotForm with narrative addressing specific competitive criteria, budget documentation using MEA template, and supporting materials. Applications reviewed by evaluation team for eligibility and competitive scoring. Partial awards may be considered if insufficient funds for full project. Grantees must receive electronic ACH/Direct Deposit payments from State of Maryland; Form X-10 submitted to Comptroller's Office. MEA staff available to review draft applications prior to submission though turnaround not guaranteed. Environmental Finance Center provides free grant writing support for select counties, primarily rural jurisdictions. Throughout grant performance, provide quarterly progress reports, detailed invoices, and upon completion, final close-out report and invoice.

structured_extraction.program_name: MEA's Decarbonizing Public Schools Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Decarbonizing Public Schools Program helps Local Education Agencies (LEAs) and school districts develop capacity and advance strategies for promoting clean and efficient energy use within their portfolio of current and future K-12 schools and support facilities. The program prepares LEAs to expand their capacity to manage energy data and reduce energy use and greenhouse gas emissions while designing for future high-performance schools. It provides incentives through both formula and competitive funding approaches, covering areas such as energy management capacity building, energy efficiency upgrades, solar installations, and net zero energy school design.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides approximately $36 million in total funding from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund ($1.5M for AOI 1, $15M for AOI 2, $11M for AOI 3, and $8.5M for AOI 4), Climate Action Plan and Alternative Compliance Program. Funding is offered through both formula and competitive approaches. AOI 1 (Capacity Building): $75,000 base plus $3,000 x scaling factor for energy data management support, or $70,000 base plus $3,000 x scaling factor for strategic capital planning. AOI 2 (Energy Efficiency): Minimum $50,000 per application, maximum $3,000,000; MEA reimburses up to 75% of activity costs. AOI 3 (Solar): $50,000-$1,000,000 per application; $3,000/kW for LEA-owned systems (cap $1,000,000), $750/kW for 3rd-party solar canopies (cap $1,000,000), $500/kW for 3rd-party rooftop systems (cap $1,000,000), up to $50,000 for planning/technical studies. AOI 4 (Net Zero Energy Schools): Average $1-$3 million per application. Applicants may apply for funding to support one or multiple areas of interest (AOIs) for either their entire school district, a significantly sized multi-facility subset, or individual school facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs), also known as school districts, in Maryland operating K-12 schools and support facilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used for energy data management capacity building, energy use reduction, greenhouse gas emissions reduction, net zero energy design considerations for public school portfolio planning, solar installations on schools (roof-mounted, ground-mounted, or solar canopies), energy efficiency upgrades within K-12 schools and support facilities, electrification updates to mechanical systems, building envelope improvements, building controls integration, lighting upgrades, and incremental costs of new construction designed to improve efficiency above current energy code requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Some funding areas of interest may prioritize projects in eligible census tracts designated as overburdened or with income at 80% or below the median income for the State. AOI 3 (Solar on Schools) eligibility is restricted to schools in qualifying census tracts. Schools serving qualifying census tracts but not physically located in them may qualify if at least 50% plus one of enrolled students come from qualifying census tracts.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local Education Agency (LEA) or school district
Project must involve K-12 schools or support facilities
Applications must be submitted by the LEA; third-parties may not submit on behalf of the LEA

Application must be signed by an LEA officer with authority to commit the applicant to execute the grant's requirements (e.g., Chair of the Board of Education, Chief Financial Officer, General Manager)
An LEA staff person must be identified who will be responsible for overseeing continuation of activities after the award's period of performance
Applicants may apply for funding to support one or multiple areas of interest (AOIs)
For AOI 1 Category 1: Open to all LEAs; FY26 funding prioritizes LEAs starting energy data management process
For AOI 1 Category 2: Applicant must demonstrate that it has already incorporated energy data collection and analysis into facility management and capital planning efforts

For AOI 2: Minimum funding request per application is $50,000; maximum is $3,000,000; MEA reimburses up to 75% of total activity costs; applicants expected to leverage remaining 25% through federal, local, and state incentives and budgets
For AOI 2: Applications must include engineering calculations demonstrating expected energy and cost savings annually and over technology lifetime
For AOI 3: Must be located in qualifying census tract (overburdened or 80% or below median state income); minimum $50,000 per application; maximum $1,000,000

For AOI 3: Must submit technical reports including site evaluations, solar potential assessments, and preliminary engineering studies; detailed system diagram, site map, electrical schematic, and construction schedule; output from recognized Solar Energy Calculator showing expected energy production
For AOI 3: Applicants encouraged to submit single comprehensive proposal rather than multiple smaller proposals
For AOI 4: Funding available for design, construction, and post-occupancy commissioning of Net Zero Energy Schools

Applicants may submit multiple applications across different AOIs but are generally limited to one award per category/AOI initially; additional awards possible only if remaining budget exists after initial awards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit the FY26 Decarbonizing Public Schools Program Application through an online form (https://form.jotform.com/251605585653159) or PDF version via email to Schools.MEA@Maryland.gov. Applications must be received by November 21, 2025, at 3:00 PM EST. For AOI 1 and AOI 2, applicants should submit a project budget using the MEA Schools Decarbonization Program Budget template. For AOI 2, applications must include detailed project budgets, site location information (names, addresses, grade levels, square footage), and engineering calculations. For AOI 3, applicants must submit budget showing full cost and requested funding, technical feasibility reports, system design details, and energy production calculations. The program uses both formula (AOI 1) and competitive evaluation with consideration of need. Applications will be reviewed by a team that may include individuals from MEA, IAC, and other entities with experience in energy, construction, and capital development. The review process follows a structured, multi-stage approach: (1) program manager reviews each application for eligibility and minimum criteria compliance; (2) evaluation team members independently score applications based on competitive criteria; (3) evaluation team compiles scores, finalizes overall scores, ranks applications, and makes funding recommendations. Period of performance varies by AOI: AOI 1 is 18-21 months; AOI 2 is 24-27 months; AOI 3 is 36-39 months; AOI 4 is 72-75 months. Extensions for good cause may be requested and must be justified with written documentation explaining the need, granted at MEA's sole discretion.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) Procurement & Technical Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) provides procurement and technical assistance services to help non-state building owners and organizations across Maryland develop and implement clean energy and decarbonization projects. MCEC offers a suite of technical services designed to accelerate decarbonization project development and execution, including decarbonization planning and energy performance contracting project development and implementation.

Assistance supports non-state building owners and organizations seeking to implement clean energy and decarbonization initiatives.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Energy Administration Geothermal Rebate Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) provides rebates to Maryland residents for installing geothermal heating and cooling systems on eligible residential properties. Single-family detached homes and single-family townhomes are eligible; multi-family properties are not eligible. Rebates of $3,000 are awarded on a non-competitive, first-come, first-served basis for complete and eligible applications, subject to available budget of $150,000 from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Non-competitive rebates of $3,000 are awarded for the installation of a new geothermal heating and cooling system (GHC system) on an eligible Maryland residential property. The GHC system must be electrically-powered, ground-source, serve as the primary heating and cooling system, and include the installation of new ground loops or wells. The system must exceed 1.00 refrigerant ton (approximately 12,000 BTU/hr or 3.51 kW) in size. Rebates are awarded on a first-come, first-served basis to eligible applicants with complete applications, subject to available budget. Partial rebates are not awarded. Funding is limited to $150,000; applications are accepted subject to available funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, February 27, 2026 or until the budget is exhausted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who own or lease single-family detached homes or single-family townhomes in Maryland and wish to install geothermal heating and cooling systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of new geothermal heating and cooling systems in eligible residential properties. The system must be electrically-powered, ground-source heat pump inclusive of necessary HVAC equipment and ground loops, pond loops, or vertically-drilled wells, and serve as the primary heating and cooling system.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Eligible properties include single-family detached homes and single-family townhomes located in Maryland. Multi-family properties are not eligible. Properties within historic areas or recorded in Maryland's Cultural Resource Information System (MEDUSA) may require pre-coordination with the Maryland Historical Trust.
requirements_list: Property must be located in Maryland
Property must be a single-family detached home or a single-family townhome
Multi-family properties are not eligible
Applicant must be a Maryland resident
Applicant must own the property OR have an active residential lease with explicit written and notarized permission from the property owner to install the system
Installation contractor must be incorporated or registered to do business in Maryland and possess all required licenses and certifications
GHC system must be electrically-powered ground-source heat pump serving as primary heating and cooling system
GHC system must include installation of new ground loops or wells (replacement systems using existing ground loops or wells do not qualify)
GHC system must exceed 1.00 refrigerant ton (approximately 12,000 BTU/hr or 3.51 kW) in size
GHC system must be fully installed, operational, and have received all necessary permits and inspections
GHC system must be paid-in-full at time of application
Applications must be submitted within 12 months of system installation
Applications must be complete and accurate with all required supporting documents
Applicant must provide taxpayer identification number or social security number
Property must not have an adverse impact on historical significance as determined by Maryland Historical Trust
Property cannot have previously received a geothermal rebate through prior MEA Residential Clean Energy Rebate Program (R-CERP) or Commercial Clean Energy Rebate Program (C-CERP)
Only one rebate per installation address; no rebates for second GHC systems or increased capacity of existing systems
Applicant must sign application (installation contractors may not sign on behalf of applicants)
Rebates are awarded on first-come, first-served basis subject to available funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Carefully review the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) for all program requirements and instructions. 2. Submit application details electronically through the MEA online JotForm application portal at https://form.jotform.com/meachpy/geo-resi. 3. Request a secure Virtru encrypted email from MEA by emailing geothermal.mea@maryland.gov. 4. Complete and sign the FY26 Geothermal Rebate Program Signature Sheet and obtain an IRS W-9 form. 5. Submit the signed signature sheet and W-9 form via the secure encrypted email (DO NOT submit social security information through JotForm or unencrypted email). 6. MEA reviews applications for completeness, accuracy, and eligibility in the order received. If an application is incomplete, the applicant has 14 calendar days to submit missing information or the application will be canceled. 7. Eligible applications proceed to historic preservation review by MEA and potentially the Maryland Historical Trust. 8. Upon approval and passing all reviews, the application is submitted for financial processing in Maryland's payment system while funding remains available. Applications are processed and converted from 'funds requested' to 'funds reserved' status on a first-come, first-served basis.
