structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Energy Administration Resilient Maryland Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Resilient Maryland Program provides funding for Maryland communities and organizations to offset the costs of planning, designing, and constructing microgrids, resilient facility power systems, and resiliency hubs. The program supports development and installation of distributed energy resources for critical and community uses, including solar photovoltaic systems, battery energy storage systems, and combined heat and power systems. Funding is available for preconstruction planning and feasibility analysis as well as system installation, with a focus on Maryland communities, businesses, and critical infrastructure seeking reliable, clean, and affordable energy solutions. The program is designed to enhance resilience and reliability for community members by reducing reliance on utility-supplied power, lowering greenhouse gas emissions, and safeguarding vital services against outages.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant program providing up to $13,000,000 total funding from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) split across three Areas of Interest: AOI 1 Preconstruction Planning ($500,000) for feasibility analysis, preliminary engineering design, financial proforma, greenhouse gas impact assessment, and implementation barriers analysis for microgrids, resiliency hubs, and resilient facility power systems; AOI 2 Microgrids ($4,500,000) for equipment purchase and installation of microgrids, resilient facility power systems, and resiliency hubs serving community-scale resilience; AOI 3 Resiliency Hubs ($8,000,000) for solar photovoltaic and battery energy storage systems in low-to-moderate income or overburdened communities. Grant amounts vary by AOI and project type: AOI 1 minimum $50,000 with maximums of $125,000 for microgrids, $15,000 per hub (up to 10 hubs), or $50,000 for resilient facility power systems, covering 100% of costs for nonprofits/governments and 50% for for-profits. AOI 2 minimum $100,000 with maximums of $1,500,000 for microgrids, $1,000,000 for resilient facility power systems, $300,000 for combined heat and power, or $2,000 per kWDC of solar and $2,000 per kWh of battery storage for resiliency hubs, covering 95% for nonprofits/governments and 50% for for-profits. AOI 3 minimum $100,000 maximum $2,000,000 calculated at $5,000 per kWDC of solar capacity plus battery storage, covering 95% for nonprofits/governments and 50% for for-profits.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Emma Stoney (AOI 1 and AOI 2 Projects); David Comis (AOI 3 Projects)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland organizations, businesses, communities, critical infrastructure entities, and government agencies seeking to develop and install distributed energy resources, microgrids, and resiliency hubs. Eligible applicants include local governments, units of state government, nonprofit entities, and for-profit businesses legally authorized to operate in Maryland. The program is not open to residential applicants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to offset feasibility analysis, planning, equipment, and installation costs for microgrids, resilient facility power systems, resiliency hubs, solar photovoltaic systems, battery energy storage systems, and combined heat and power systems. AOI 1 funds support five key planning deliverables: feasibility analysis, preliminary engineering and project design, project financial proforma, greenhouse gas impact analysis, and implementation barriers analysis. AOI 2 and AOI 3 funds support equipment purchase, installation, and system commissioning. Ineligible uses include acquisition of land, buildings, or real property; routine operation, maintenance, or repairs of existing infrastructure; projects focused solely on renewable energy capacity expansion without resilience considerations; energy storage systems for residential customers; fossil fuel or combustion technologies that produce greenhouse gas emissions (except basic health and safety repairs); and expenses already funded by other MEA grant programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; available throughout Maryland. For AOI 3 projects, the facility must be located within a community classified as low-to-moderate income (LMI) or overburdened as defined in State Government Article §9–20B–05(i)(1), and the majority of households served must be LMI as defined in State Gov't Art. § 9-2014 (2022). Eligible census tracts are available on MEA's website. Applicants must affirm that more than 50 percent of residents within walkable distance (approximately half mile radius) to the Resiliency Hub meet the definition of LMI at 80 percent of statewide median income.
requirements_list: Eligible entities must be legally authorized to operate in Maryland and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Applicants must provide a Certificate of Status from the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation and an IRS Form W-9 demonstrating an established Employer Identification Number (EIN)
The project site(s) and benefiting location(s) must be located within the State of Maryland

Projects must be on property either owned or leased by the applicant with documentation of ownership or lease; leased property requires a letter of concurrence from the property owner permitting installation and ensuring upgrades remain operational
Applicants must demonstrate ability to enter into a formal grant agreement with MEA before receiving any grant funds
Grant funds cannot be used for expenses incurred prior to grant agreement execution unless MEA agrees in writing
Any project funded must be completed including all milestones and required reporting by December 31, 2030 (assumes grant agreement execution by July 1, 2026)
AOI 1 projects must focus on preconstruction planning and feasibility analysis with five required deliverables; construction, equipment purchase, and site infrastructure costs are ineligible
AOI 2 projects must construct microgrids, resilient facility power systems, or resiliency hubs for critical purposes; funding restricted to equipment purchase, installation, and commissioning

AOI 3 projects must construct solar photovoltaic and battery energy storage systems for resiliency hubs in LMI or overburdened communities; funding strictly limited to projects deploying both solar PV and battery energy storage systems
AOI 3 projects must demonstrate 50 percent probability of sustaining critical loads for 72-hour period, operational minimum 14 hours per day
AOI 3 projects require resiliency hubs to remain open to surrounding community during power outages for minimum 5 years without discrimination or restriction
AOI 3 projects must provide emergency heating and cooling, refrigeration for temperature-sensitive medications, outlets or power sources for charging devices, and ventilation and emergency lighting

AOI 3 projects require labor attestations that installation contractors pay at least 150% of state minimum wage, afford collective bargaining rights, provide paid leave, maintain unemployment insurance and workers compensation, comply with wage laws, and offer employer health insurance with premiums not exceeding 8.5% of net monthly earnings
All projects must include formation of a Project Planning Committee with representatives from community, local government, utility, and other relevant stakeholders
Applicants must demonstrate engagement with local electric utility or provide evidence of attempted outreach if utility declines participation
Applicants must include letters of support from stakeholder groups represented on the Project Planning Committee
All applications require complete online submission through jotform portal with all forms signed by the applicant
For AOI 2 and AOI 3 projects: completed signature form with building owner, building operator, and system owner signatures required
Applicants must provide cost match as required by AOI and project type (see assistance_description for specific percentages)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the online Resilient Maryland Application portal using a jotform. The process includes: (1) Complete the online application data form with all required information; (2) Complete the Project Proposal (maximum 11 pages including 1-page executive summary) addressing evaluation criteria including applicant overview and relevant experience, project planning committee identification, technologies selected, value proposition, energy challenges, emissions reductions, project scope, project partners, and organizational/project team experience; (3) Complete the Budget Workbook detailing project costs, funding sources, and cost-sharing amounts; (4) For AOI 2 and AOI 3 projects, complete the Signature Form with signatures from building owner, building operator, and system owner affirming consent to installation and compliance with program requirements; (5) Provide Certificate of Status from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation; (6) Provide IRS Form W-9 showing Employer Identification Number; (7) Provide documentation of property ownership or lease agreement; (8) For leased property, provide property owner's letter of concurrence; (9) For AOI 3 projects, provide attestation of labor requirements compliance. All applications are screened for completeness and minimum eligibility requirements. Applications meeting minimum eligibility are competitively evaluated using criteria including application completeness, organizational and project team experience (15 points), project justification and community benefits (20 points), project scope and resiliency design (20 points), financial planning and budget detail (15 points), planning quality and risk mitigation (15 points), stakeholder engagement and support, equity and climate considerations, and implementation readiness. Grants are recommended from highest to lowest final score until funding is exhausted.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Energy Storage Income Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: An income tax credit program for residential and commercial taxpayers who have installed an energy storage system on their residential or commercial property in Maryland. The program awarded tax credit certificates on a first-come, first-served basis, with MEA authorized to award a total of $750,000 in tax credit certificates during a given tax year. Current state law authorizes MEA to offer the program through tax year 2024. The most recent application window was for Tax Year 2024, with a deadline of January 15, 2025.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit certificates awarded to eligible residential and commercial taxpayers on a first-come, first-served basis. The program authorized MEA to award a total of $750,000 in tax credit certificates during a given tax year. Tax credits are calculated as the lower amount of: 30% of total installed costs of the energy storage system, or $5,000 for residential properties, or $150,000 for commercial properties. Reserved allocations: $450,000 for residential taxpayers (purchased systems) and $300,000 for commercial taxpayers (purchased and leased systems). Tax credits are applied to Maryland State Income Tax Liability, are non-refundable, and any unused amount may not be carried over to future tax years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 15, 2025, at 3:00 P.M. EST for Tax Year 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial taxpayers who have installed an energy storage system on their property in Maryland between January 1, 2024, and December 31, 2024. This includes property owners, individuals, and corporations that own or pay for installation of energy storage systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of a qualified energy storage system on residential or commercial property in Maryland. Eligible systems must store electrical energy, mechanical energy, chemical energy (including electrochemical), or thermal energy that was once electrical energy. Mobile energy storage systems, electric vehicles, recreational camping equipment, and electric hot water heaters (except those in demand response programs) are ineligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Installation of an energy storage system on residential or commercial property in Maryland completed during Tax Year 2024 (January 1, 2024 - December 31, 2024)
Eligible applicants must be residential or commercial taxpayers who own or pay for the energy storage system installation
Energy storage system must be fully installed, pass all necessary permit inspections, and be paid in full
System must be certified by a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory (NRTL) listed on the US Department of Labor's OSHA NRTL Program
System must be installed by a licensed professional and comply with all applicable building, fire codes, and local utility interconnection requirements
Systems receiving MEA grant funding from another program are ineligible
Commercial taxpayers limited to one energy storage tax credit certificate in Tax Year 2024
Residential taxpayers limited to one energy storage tax credit certificate regardless of tax year
Energy storage tax credit certificates limited to one per property address regardless of tax year
For systems installed in Tax Year 2023 but with final inspection approval received in Tax Year 2024, MEA will consider the system completed in Tax Year 2024 and eligible for Tax Year 2024 tax credit
If system does not require permit and inspection, applicant must provide documentation that county or authority having jurisdiction does not require permit or waived requirement
Applicants must certify under penalty of perjury that all information provided is complete, accurate, and true
Applicants must submit any missing documents within 14 days of MEA's notification or by January 20, 2025, at 3:00 P.M. EST, whichever is earlier
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application electronically via JotForm portal available on the Program webpage, or request a paper application by December 31, 2024 at 3:00 P.M. EST via email to energystorage.mea@maryland.gov. Paper applications must be received by first-class mail by the application deadline. If an energy storage installation company is submitting the application on behalf of the property owner, a completed Authorized Applicant Signature Form signed by both the property owner and installation company representative must be included. Applications are reviewed on a rolling, first-come, first-served basis. Required supporting documents include: proof of real property ownership (MEA reviews SDAT records); zero-balance itemized invoice showing all costs with breakdown of energy storage vs. renewable energy costs if applicable; all required permit numbers and proof of final inspection approval or documentation of permit/inspection waiver; equipment certifications from NRTL; equipment cut sheets, specification sheets, or system brochure; photographs of fully installed and commissioned system; and Authorized Applicant Signature Form if applicable. Applicants must submit any missing documents within 14 days of MEA notification. Taxpayers must file Maryland income tax return electronically and complete Business Tax Credit Form 500CR with binary attachment or PDF of tax credit certification from MEA. If one Reserved Tax Credit Allocation is oversubscribed, eligible applicants will be placed on waitlist queue; MEA removes Reserved Allocations on July 1, 2024, and waitlisted applicants are issued certificates in order received.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Ground Source Heat Pump Advantage Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program administered by the Maryland Energy Administration that provides per-unit installation incentives to residential builders, developers, housing authorities, and eligible business entities that install ground source (geothermal) heat pump systems in qualifying new construction residential developments. The program aims to lower upfront costs and support market transformation with an emphasis on affordable housing in low-to-moderate income and overburdened communities. It also assists eligible homeowners installing ground source heat pumps in new construction homes to improve energy efficiency and reduce heating and cooling costs.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEA provides a $12,000 per GSHP installation incentive to residential builders, developers, housing authorities, or other business entities that install GSHP systems in qualifying new construction residential developments. A total of $2,000,000 is anticipated to be available for FY26. MEA anticipates funding between one and three proposals with a focus on GSHP deployments at scale. Grant funds will be paid in arrears over a 48-month grant period tied to demonstrated project progress and completion of approved milestones. MEA may retain up to 25% of the total awarded grant amount until all incentivized GSHP systems are fully installed, commissioned, and operational. Final funding amounts may vary based on the number and quality of applications received and MEA's available resources. Administrative costs and reimbursable indirect costs combined cannot exceed 15% of the total grant amount.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential builders, developers, housing authorities, and eligible business entities installing ground source heat pump systems in new construction residential developments located in low-to-moderate income and overburdened communities, as well as nonprofit organizations and business entities partnering with eligible builders, developers, or housing authorities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of ground source (geothermal) heat pump systems in qualifying new construction residential developments. Systems must be entirely electric with no fossil fuel systems or appliances, serve as the primary heating and cooling system for each unit, and be located in single-family detached homes or attached townhomes within qualifying census tracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Developments must be located in low-to-moderate income (LMI) and/or overburdened census tracts as defined in Chapter 98 of the 2023 Laws of Maryland (HB550). A map of qualifying census tracts is available on the Maryland Energy Administration website. The MDEnviroScreen tool may also be used to identify overburdened communities.
requirements_list: Projects must meet a minimum deployment scale of at least 15 GSHP installations
Developments must be located in low-to-moderate income (LMI) and/or overburdened census tracts as defined in HB550
GSHP installations must be in new construction residential developments in single-family detached homes or attached townhomes
Incentivized units must be entirely electric with no fossil fuel systems or appliances
Systems must be electrically powered ground source heat pumps inclusive of all necessary HVAC equipment and ground loops
Systems must be the primary heating and cooling system for each unit (backup electric resistance heating is permitted)
Systems must be fully installed, have received all required permits, passed all inspections, and be fully operational
All participating developments must be designed, permitted, and constructed in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local building, zoning, and land use codes
Residents must be provided with system training and written documentation covering system operations, maintenance, and warranty information
Final eligibility for the full per-unit incentive is contingent upon completion of system commissioning and submission of required documentation
If using geothermal system leasing models, homeowners must receive clear written disclosures describing the ownership and financing structure
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted using the online Jotform application portal at https://form.jotform.com/marylandenergy/MDGAP (Jotform is required; non-Jotform applications should be submitted to Ryan Trauley at geothermal.mea@maryland.gov). Applications must be received by March 15, 2026 at 3:00 PM EST. Complete applications must include: (1) a Narrative (maximum 15 pages) addressing Minimum Eligibility Requirements and Competitive Evaluation Criteria; (2) a Budget attachment in Excel or PDF format detailing all budget items; (3) IRS Form W-9 with organization name and address matching the application form; (4) Evidence of Good Standing from Maryland SDAT; and (5) Letters of Support from project partners (at least two recommended). The evaluation process includes three steps: (1) Program Manager Eligibility Review based on Minimum Eligibility Requirements; (2) Team Member Individual Review scoring each complete application according to Competitive Evaluation Criteria; and (3) Team Group Review and Award Recommendation. Grant agreements are anticipated to be executed in June 2026. Applicants should verify eligibility using the census tract map on the Maryland Energy Administration website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Offshore Wind Supply Chain Investment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides non-competitive funding to support new or existing businesses entering or expanding in the offshore wind supply chain in Maryland. The program awards grants on a first-come, first-served basis across two areas of interest: capital expenditures and industry event attendance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Non-competitive grant funding available in two areas of interest. Area of Interest 1 (Capital Expenditures) provides up to $1,750,000 in funding, with MEA awarding up to 50 percent of total project costs not to exceed $400,000 per applicant. Applicants must contribute at least 50 percent of total project costs as matching funds. Eligible expenses include relocation costs, new construction, renovations, and purchase and installation of equipment. Area of Interest 2 (Industry Events) provides up to $250,000 in funding, with one-time reimbursements up to $5,000 per applicant per fiscal year for attending eligible offshore wind and marine technology industry events. Eligible expenses include event registration fees, exhibition fees, scheduled travel costs, and lodging costs. Total program funding is up to $2,000,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 15, 2025 at 5:00 P.M. EST or until all program funding has been awarded, whichever occurs first
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, government and public institutions, and emerging businesses seeking to enter or expand in the offshore wind supply chain. Emerging businesses must be at least 51 percent owned and controlled by individuals with a personal net worth not exceeding $6,500,000 as adjusted for inflation. MEA highly encourages applications from new or existing emerging businesses, including minority, woman, and veteran owned emerging businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Area of Interest 1 (Capital Expenditures): relocation costs, new construction of real property, renovations to existing real property, and purchase and installation of new or manufacturer certified or third-party licensed refurbished equipment. Grant funds may not be used for purchase of new or existing real property (though matching funds may cover this) or relocation costs for employees. Area of Interest 2 (Industry Events): event registration fees, exhibition fees, scheduled travel costs (economy airfare only, up to 6 months in advance), baggage fees, ground transportation, and lodging based on GSA/Department of State per diem rates. Food and beverages are ineligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Applicants willing to relocate or expand into Maryland are eligible contingent upon receiving a grant award. Proposed projects must hold the potential to benefit the state and local communities through job opportunities and commitments to promoting diversity, inclusion, and equity in their business operations. Proposed projects should be designed to serve the larger U.S. offshore wind market and related industries.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit organization, government or public institution, or an emerging business

Emerging businesses must be at least 51 percent owned and controlled by individuals certified to have a personal net worth not exceeding $6,500,000 as adjusted for inflation according to the Consumer Price Index
For Area of Interest 1: applicant must have a completed Market Entry Report detailing capital expenditure needs and business strategy to engage in Maryland's offshore wind supply chain
Applicant must be interested in entering the offshore wind industry or expanding in Maryland's offshore wind supply chain
Applicant must provide a Certificate of Status from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) showing good standing
Applicant must provide business ownership documentation demonstrating at least 51 percent ownership and control (for business applicants)
Applicant must provide Personal Net Worth Attestation confirming emerging business status (for business applicants)
Applicant must provide IRS Form W-9 with name and address matching application submission
For Area of Interest 1: applicant must provide proof of matching funds (at least 50 percent of total project costs)
For Area of Interest 1: applicant must provide project specification sheets and equipment certifications (NRTL certifications if applicable)
For Area of Interest 1: applicant must provide letters of support from all project partners detailing their commitments
For Area of Interest 2: application must be submitted at least 90 days prior to event attendance
For Area of Interest 2: applicant must provide event description and summary of eligible costs with supporting invoices
Applications must be submitted through the online Jotform application portal
All required application documents must be included in the submission; administratively incomplete applications will not be considered
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed application package through the online Jotform portal specific to your Area of Interest. For Area of Interest 1 (Capital Expenditures), applicants must submit: (1) Project Narrative (no more than 10 pages) addressing applicant overview, project scope, needs assessment, project timeline, list of project partners, and sustainability statement; (2) Market Entry Report detailing goals, target sales, product/service description, target market, major action items and timeline, strategy, and budget; (3) Budget Narrative including total project budget breakdown, return on investment calculation, and proof of funds; (4) Certificate of Status from SDAT; (5) Business ownership documents; (6) Personal Net Worth Attestation; (7) IRS Form W-9; (8) Equipment specification sheets; (9) NRTL certifications if applicable; and (10) Letters of support from project partners. For Area of Interest 2 (Industry Events), applicants must submit at least 90 days prior to event: (1) Event description (1 page) explaining significance and relevance; (2) Summary of costs with supporting invoices; (3) Certificate of Status; (4) Business ownership documentation; (5) Personal Net Worth Attestation; and (6) IRS Form W-9. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and bi-monthly. Applicants will receive notice of approval or denial within 90 days of submission. For Area of Interest 1, applications are evaluated on project scope, market entry report, needs assessment, feasibility, sustainability, economic development opportunity, budget and return on investment, and community support. Award payments for Area of Interest 2 are issued after the event and may take 8-12 weeks.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Offshore Wind Workforce Training and Education Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant funding program administered by the Maryland Energy Administration that supports workforce training centers and academic institutions to develop or expand offshore wind education and training programs. The program is split into two areas of interest: AOI 1 for Industry Education (developing or expanding general offshore wind education programs at any education level) and AOI 2 for Workforce Training (developing or expanding offshore wind workforce certification-based training programs). The program prepares individuals for careers in the offshore wind industry and related sectors including skilled trades, manufacturing, transportation, and logistics.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding of up to $3,000,000 total for Fiscal Year 2025, split between two areas of interest. AOI 1 (Industry Education) provides up to $1,500,000 to develop or expand offshore wind education programs at any education level. AOI 2 (Workforce Training) provides up to $1,500,000 to support development or expansion of offshore wind workforce certification-based training programs. Individual project awards are capped at $500,000 (75% of total project costs), with applicants required to contribute at least 25% matching funds or in-kind services. Funds offset capital and operating expenditures including relocation costs, renovations, equipment purchase and installation, labor and personnel, permitting and inspections, and administrative expenses. For FY26, MEA is partnering with the Maryland Department of Labor's EARN Maryland Program to fund projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 3:00 P.M. ET, Friday, December 13, 2024 (FY25); November 29, 2024 first-come, first-serve (FY25 via Program Overview); September 26, 2025 (FY26 via EARN Maryland)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, academic institutions, government entities, and emerging businesses (for AOI 2) seeking to develop or expand offshore wind education and workforce training programs, including workforce training centers. For FY25, AOI 1 is open to nonprofit organizations and academic institutions. AOI 2 is open to new or existing workforce training centers owned or operated by emerging businesses, nonprofit organizations, governmental entities, and academic institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and operating expenditures associated with developing or expanding offshore wind education and training programs, including: general offshore wind education at any education level; technical trade skills training; safety standards training for employment in the offshore wind industry; supportive services for trainees; expanding training capacity for skilled workers in related sectors such as manufacturing, transportation, and logistics; equipment purchase and installation; renovations; relocation costs; permitting and inspections; labor and personnel; and administrative expenses. AOI 2 applicants must also include a graduate placement plan for connecting graduates with employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Programs must prepare individuals for careers in the offshore wind industry in Maryland and the larger U.S. offshore wind market. Applicants may be located anywhere in Maryland and serve students statewide or regionally.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization or academic institution (AOI 1) or nonprofit organization, government entity, academic institution, or emerging business operating/planning to operate a workforce training center (AOI 2)
Proposed projects must provide general offshore wind education or certification-based training for employment within the offshore wind industry
Projects must address technical trade skills and/or safety standards
AOI 2 applicants must operate or plan to operate a workforce training center and develop or expand a certification-based training program for offshore wind employment
AOI 2 applicants must provide a sample graduate placement plan for connecting graduates with employment
All application materials listed in the respective AOI Funding Opportunity Announcement must be included
Applications must be submitted through the online Jotform application portal (FY25) or the EARN Maryland application process (FY26)

MEA strongly encourages applications from emerging businesses, minority-owned emerging businesses, members of historically disenfranchised groups, formerly incarcerated individuals, and people with disabilities

For business applicants: must meet the Maryland definition of an 'Emerging Business' (at least 51% owned and controlled by individual(s) with personal net worth not exceeding $6,500,000 as adjusted annually for inflation)
Applicants must provide Certificate of Status from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Business applicants must provide business ownership documents and personal net worth attestation
Applicants must provide IRS Form W-9
Applicants must provide letters of support from project partners detailing commitments
Applications must include comprehensive project narrative (maximum 10 pages) addressing all evaluation criteria
All application materials must be administratively complete to be considered
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must review the applicable Area of Interest (AOI) Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) and complete the corresponding application through the online Jotform portal for FY25. The application package must include: (1) Project Narrative (maximum 10 pages) covering Applicant Overview, Project Scope Statement, Needs Assessment, Project Work Plan, and List of Project Partners; (2) Budget Narrative with total project budget breakdown; (3) Certificate of Status from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation; (4) Business Ownership Documents (for business applicants); (5) Personal Net Worth Attestation (for business applicants); (6) IRS Form W-9; and (7) Letters of Support from project partners. For FY26, applicants should visit the EARN Maryland Summer 2025 Solicitation for Implementation Grant Proposals webpage. Applications are evaluated competitively based on Project Scope, Project Work Plan, Feasibility, Needs Assessment, Budget and Available Resources, and Partnerships. Notice of approval or denial is provided within 90 days of the application deadline. MEA will not consider administratively incomplete applications. Partial awards are possible; if insufficient funds exist to fully fund a project, applicants may accept partial funding or decline the offer.

structured_extraction.program_description: Help low-to-moderate income Maryland residents install solar photovoltaic systems to power their homes with clean, affordable, and sustainable energy.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to help income-eligible households install solar photovoltaic systems on their homes through participation with program-approved contractors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible households who contract with a solar photovoltaic vendor from the program's participating contractor list.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of solar photovoltaic systems on residential homes.
requirements_list: Household must be income-eligible for the low-to-moderate income designation
Must contract with a program-approved solar photovoltaic vendor

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to Maryland counties and municipalities to offset costs associated with implementing the free-to-use U.S. National Renewable Energy Laboratory SolarAPP+ solar permitting software for their communities, as required by the 2024 Brighter Tomorrow Act. Funded through federal State Energy Program Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act formulaic award funds, the program is noncompetitive and awards grants on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Noncompetitive, first-come, first-served grants totaling $3,900,000 in federal funding from the State Energy Program Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act formulaic award. Grant awards are calculated formulaically with a base incentive of $10,000 and a scale factor of $0.95 per household serviced by the applying jurisdiction. Individual grants are not expected to exceed $100,000. MEA may consider a higher individual grant if an application demonstrates need with sufficient justification and program funding is available after all other eligible applications have been funded. Partial grants are possible depending on the number of complete and eligible applications received. Funds help pay for staff time related to training, development of procedures or integration with current processes, fee adjustments, and information technology (IT) resources specific to the implementation of SolarAPP+ permitting software.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 3:00 P.M. ET, February 25, 2026, or until funding is exhausted, whichever comes first
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties and municipalities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff time related to training, development of procedures or integration with current processes, fee adjustments, and information technology (IT) resources specific to the implementation of SolarAPP+ permitting software. Funding cannot be used for any staff time or other expenses unrelated to SolarAPP+ implementation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties and municipalities statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland county or municipality

Any contractor that the applicant will work with must be legally authorized to do business in the State of Maryland and must have an established Employer Identification Number (EIN) at the time of application
Project site(s) and location(s) that will benefit from the project must be located within the State of Maryland
The applicant and any contractor must be in Good Standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (DAT), with proof provided at application
Program funds cannot be used for project costs incurred prior to execution of a grant agreement with MEA
If an applicant has previously received Program funding for the same project, they cannot receive another Program grant for the same project
Applicants awarded a grant must enter into a formal grant agreement with MEA before receiving any grant funds
Any project funded must complete all milestones and required reporting documents by no later than July 1, 2027 (assumes grant agreement execution by July 1, 2026)
Maryland counties or municipalities must attest to compliance with State Finance and Procurement Article sections 14-416 and 17-303 (as applicable)
Grantees will be expected to meet certain federal requirements as a condition of receiving funds
Must adopt automated solar permitting software as required by the 2024 Brighter Tomorrow Act

Applicants must provide an overview of their current residential solar permitting requirements and procedures, including permitting volume, adoption rates, timelines, staff time and resource use, and inspection outcomes
Applicants must specify the type of SolarAPP+ integration desired (standalone or integrated model)

Applicants must provide a detailed description of anticipated staff hours broken out by staff category and all-in hourly rate, including training time, procedure development time, fee adjustment time, and IT resource time
Applicants must provide a complete cost breakdown with each line item and associated cost for which MEA funding is requested
Applicants must submit a complete, accurate, and signed IRS Form W9
Good Standing documentation from Maryland DAT must be submitted with the application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through the online MEA SolarAPP+ Implementation Grant Program Application Portal by 3:00 P.M. ET on February 25, 2026. Applicants who cannot use the portal must contact MEA by February 1, 2026, at SolarAPP.MEA@Maryland.gov to request an exception. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis and evaluated for completeness and eligibility according to minimum eligibility requirements. An application missing information or documentation will be placed on standby and the applicant will have fourteen (14) calendar days to submit the missing information before rejection. Each complete and eligible application is evaluated noncompetitively by MEA staff. An application that passes evaluation is recommended for funding and the applicant is notified. Applicants with grant requests exceeding $100,000 will have their request considered by an MEA evaluation panel, subject to funding availability. Full grants are made for approved projects until funds are exhausted. If insufficient funds remain to fully fund a project, the applicant may accept partial funding or decline, allowing MEA to offer partial funding to the next qualified applicant. Upon award, grantees must enter a formal grant agreement with MEA and set up electronic payments through the State of Maryland Comptroller's Office by submitting Form X-10. Grantees must comply with all reporting requirements specified in the grant agreement.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland's Residential Clean Energy Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant/rebate program operated by the Maryland Energy Administration that provides financial assistance to Maryland homeowners for the installation of clean energy systems at their primary residences, including solar photovoltaic systems, solar water heating systems, and geothermal heating and cooling systems. Grants are distributed until funds are depleted and funding may run out quickly.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $1,000 in rebates/grants for clean energy systems installed at primary residences in Maryland. Grants are provided for solar photovoltaic systems, solar water heating systems, and geothermal heating and cooling systems. Funds are distributed until depleted, and funding may run out quickly.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners installing clean energy systems at their primary residences
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of solar photovoltaic systems, solar water heating systems, and geothermal heating and cooling systems at primary residences
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: System must be installed at a primary residence in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit applications electronically when possible. Staff will confirm receipt within one to two business days via email. Contact the Maryland Energy Administration for updated information on grant availability and application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to help businesses, nonprofit organizations, individuals, state agencies, local governments, public and private schools, and community colleges install mechanical insulation on commercial, industrial, or agricultural properties to improve energy efficiency. The program enables energy-saving improvements to large-scale thermal distribution networks by reducing energy waste in facilities across Maryland. Mechanical insulation includes insulation materials, facings, and accessory products used for thermal requirements for mechanical piping and equipment in hot and cold applications, and heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning applications.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to offset the cost of installing mechanical insulation on commercial, industrial, or agricultural properties to enable energy-saving improvements to large-scale thermal distribution networks. Grant funds may be used to defray costs documented by invoices for project design, feasibility analysis, material acquisition, installation, and post-installation commissioning. An individual grant award may not exceed the lesser of: (1) 30% of the total amount of qualified project expenses paid or incurred by the applicant, or (2) $20,000. MEA will consider only applications indicating a total project cost valued at no less than $10,000. The total value of program award disbursements per entity is capped at $100,000. Multiple applications representing distinct projects can be submitted by a single entity. Grant proceeds are issued in arrears to awardees that submit invoices demonstrating successful project completion. Total funding available is $400,000. Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis until funding is fully awarded or until December 17, 2025 at 3:00 P.M., whichever occurs first.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis until funding is fully awarded or until 3:00 p.m. on Wednesday, December 17, 2025, whichever is first
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, nonprofit organizations, Maryland business entities, state agencies, local governments, public and private schools, and community colleges seeking to install mechanical insulation on commercial, industrial, or agricultural properties in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of mechanical insulation (materials, facings, and accessory products) on commercial, industrial, or agricultural properties for energy efficiency improvements to large-scale thermal distribution networks. Eligible costs include project design, feasibility analysis, material acquisition, installation, and post-installation commissioning. Non-eligible costs include administrative costs related to procurement management and any remediation and repair costs for hardware to which mechanical insulation is to be applied. Costs must be net project costs not already covered by other incentives, cost-effective with anticipated simple payback of no more than 15 years, not included in a scope for which a purchase order or contract was issued prior to application filing, and not subject to concurrent funding from other MEA grant sources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available across all Maryland counties. Grant-eligible facilities must be located in the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an individual, non-profit organization, Maryland business entity, state agency, local government, public or private school, or community college
Property/facility must be located in Maryland
Non-governmental applicants must be in Good Standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Property must be commercial, industrial, or agricultural
Scope of work must be for mechanical insulation installation only, excluding all other hardware that would be installed concurrently
Proposed scope of work must demonstrate that resulting performance measures will exceed ASHRAE Technical Committee (TC) 1.8 performance criteria
Applicant must provide documentation quantifying the project's estimated energy-saving potential prepared by a competent engineering professional
Applicant must demonstrate annual energy consumption before and after insulation improvement
Applicant must provide recent 12-month billing history for all fossil fuel and electricity accounts relevant to the thermal system
Total project cost must be valued at no less than $10,000
Applicant must submit IRS Form W-9 with matching applicant name
Applicant name on application and W-9 form must match
If applicable, applicant must provide SDAT Certificate of Good Standing or Business Entity Search entry for non-governmental applicants
Applicant must provide proof of facility location in Maryland
Applicant must demonstrate capital investment commitment for all total project costs remaining after accounting for rebates, incentives, and FY26 program funding
Applicant must provide completed utility rebate or incentive applications if applicable

Mechanical insulation may not satisfy only cosmetic purposes; must satisfy energy conservation, operating cost reductions, process control, noise abatement, environmental impact minimization, or workplace comfort and safety objectives
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Read the FY26 Mechanical Insulation Grant Program Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) thoroughly. 2. Complete the FY26 Mechanical Insulation Application form in full. 3. Gather all required documentation including: proof of applicant eligibility, scope of work documentation, project location and facility information, thermal system description with schematic illustration, description of mechanical insulation components to be installed itemized by type/material/configuration/quantity, documentation of total-project energy performance improvement with calculations, insulation manufacturer's cut sheets or product descriptions, summary of leveraged funding sources, utility rebate applications, 12-month energy billing history, IRS Form W-9, and SDAT Good Standing documentation (if applicable). 4. Use the 3E Plus online calculator (strongly encouraged) to calculate energy savings and performance measures meeting ASHRAE standards. 5. Submit complete application package via email to insulation.mea@maryland.gov in PDF format. 6. Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis. Qualified projects are awarded in order received. 7. If application is incomplete, MEA will provide opportunity to update for completeness within 7 business days. Application will then be reviewed based on date complete application is received, not the incomplete submission date. 8. If selected, grant proceeds are issued in arrears upon submission of invoices demonstrating successful project completion. Earlier submissions are encouraged for better chances of funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration offers grants to help fleet companies, organizations, communities, and commercial or industrial entities purchase qualifying zero-emission vehicles and heavy equipment for commercial or industrial use. The program aims to accelerate the adoption of zero-emission vehicles in medium and heavy-duty applications, thereby reducing greenhouse gas emissions and promoting cleaner transportation solutions. Grants cover up to 75% of the incremental cost of eligible newly manufactured zero-emission medium-duty or heavy-duty fleet vehicles and qualified heavy equipment property. Separate funding pools are available for on-road vehicles and off-road equipment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants cover up to 75% of the incremental cost (difference between zero-emission vehicle price and equivalent petroleum-fueled vehicle price) of eligible newly manufactured zero-emission vehicles and heavy equipment property. Up to $10 million is available in Fiscal Year 2026, divided into two separate funding pools: $8 million for on-road vehicles (Area of Interest 1) and $2 million for off-road equipment (Area of Interest 2). For AOI 1, the maximum grant per applicant is $2.5 million; for AOI 2, the maximum is $375,000 per applicant. Grants are paid in arrears after vehicle purchase and delivery. Reimbursement is processed through Jotform links after project completion. Projects must be completed and reimbursement materials submitted within 24 months of the grant agreement effective date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Fleet companies, organizations, communities, commercial and industrial entities, local governments, non-profit organizations, agricultural entities, fleet operators, airports, higher education institutions, and K-12 schools in Maryland. Eligible applicants must be persons (individuals, partnerships, firms, associations, corporations, or other entities) or units of local government.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of newly manufactured zero-emission medium-duty or heavy-duty fleet vehicles (Class 3-8, GVWR over 10,000 lbs) for on-road commercial or industrial use, or qualified zero-emission heavy equipment property for off-road use. Eligible equipment includes construction, earthmoving, or industrial heavy equipment such as excavators, forklifts, terminal tractors, skid steer loaders, wheel loaders, and riding mowers. Equipment must be mobile and not use an internal combustion engine. Battery electric vehicles (BEV) or hydrogen fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEV) are eligible. For emergency vehicles associated with life safety, Range Extended Electric Vehicles (REEV) are also eligible. Vehicle supply equipment (charging infrastructure) is not eligible under this program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Vehicles must be domiciled in Maryland and registered to the applicant. Vehicles shall be domiciled and primarily operated within the State for no less than three (3) years from the vehicle delivery date. If a grantee redeployes out of state, sells, or takes a vehicle out of service before the end of the three-year period, the grantee may be required to repay the grant.
requirements_list: Applicants must be a person (individual, partnership, firm, association, corporation, or other entity) or a unit of local government in Maryland
Applicants must have at least three (3) vehicles in their existing fleet, or in their fleet after purchase of the ZEV vehicles being submitted for consideration under the MHD ZEV Program
These fleet vehicles must be domiciled at a non-residential place of business
Applicants may only include vehicles directly owned or leased by the applicant
Vehicles and equipment must be newly manufactured zero-emission models (not retrofitted or repowered)
Vehicles must be medium-duty or heavy-duty for on-road fleet use (Class 3-8, GVWR more than 10,000 lbs), or qualified heavy equipment for off-road use (also more than 10,000 lbs)
Vehicles and equipment must be for commercial or industrial use, not personal or individual use
Vehicles being purchased for resale are ineligible
Personal passenger vehicles, parallel plug-in hybrid electric vehicles, neighborhood electric vehicles (NEVs), and low-speed vehicles (LSVs) are ineligible
Repowered vehicles (used vehicles with replaced engines/drivetrains) are ineligible
Applications must conform with program requirements and definitions outlined in §9–2011 of Md. Code, State Government article
Applicants must be in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation

Applicants are ineligible for program funding for vehicles that have previously been awarded or are expecting to be awarded funding through the State's VW Environmental Mitigation Trust Fund program or other State funding programs

If an applicant receives an award from a federal program or non-State program for the same vehicle and also receives a MHD ZEV award, the amount of the MHD ZEV award shall not exceed the applicant's contribution to the project
Purchase orders must be dated after the effective date of the Grant Agreement (unless MEA agrees otherwise in writing)
Vehicles must be registered in Maryland to the applicant
Vehicles shall be domiciled and primarily operated within the State for no less than three (3) years from vehicle delivery
If the vehicle is hosted at a site owned by another entity, MEA will require a signed letter of commitment from the site host

Vehicles are not required to replace an existing conventional vehicle in the applicant's fleet; however, vehicles associated with replacement or retirement of existing gas/diesel vehicles will be viewed more favorably during review
See the FY26 MHD ZEV Grant Program Funding Opportunity Announcement for full eligibility details
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the program requirements and eligibility criteria in the FY26 MHD ZEV Grant Program Funding Opportunity Announcement. 2. Register for access to the MyMEA online application portal at https://energy.maryland.gov/transportation/Pages/MediumandHeavyDutyGrant.aspx. 3. Complete the following required application sections through the portal: Project Narrative, General Information, Zero Emission Vehicle Summary Table, Attachment Checklist, and Applicant Signature. 4. Prepare and upload required attachments as separate files (do not combine into one file): vendor documentation of technical specifications for ZEVs and petroleum-equivalent vehicles; vehicle lease documentation (if leasing); letter of commitment from site host (if applicable); completed IRS Form W-9 with taxpayer identification number (submit via encrypted means if using SSN). For purchased vehicles, provide vendor quotes for both ZEV and comparable petroleum-fueled vehicle showing purchase price and specifications. For leased vehicles, provide lease documentation clearly specifying lease term duration and payment frequency/amount. 5. Submit the complete application through the MyMEA Portal by the deadline: November 20, 2025 at 3:00 PM ET. Applications submitted after this deadline will not be accepted. 6. If selected for award, applicant must be willing and able to enter into a Grant Agreement with MEA. The applicant name and federal tax identification number on the IRS W-9 must match the grantee name on the grant agreement. 7. Upon grant agreement execution, MEA sets up electronic payments through the State of Maryland's Comptroller's Office. 8. After vehicle purchase and delivery, submit quarterly operations reports for three years, including vehicle miles traveled, energy use, project bids, VINs, license plate numbers, and other data as required by MEA. 9. Provide progress updates to MEA as requested prior to vehicle delivery. 10. Submit all reimbursement materials through Jotform links after vehicle delivery. Projects must be completed and all reporting/reimbursement materials submitted within 24 months of the grant agreement effective date.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides competitive grants to non-profit organizations and local government entities to implement energy efficiency, electrification, and solar photovoltaic upgrades to single-family and multi-family residential buildings that benefit low-and-moderate income Maryland residents. This program combines the former Energy Efficiency Equity Program and Solar Energy Equity Program, offering funding under two areas of interest: AOI 1 (Energy Efficiency Projects) with an anticipated budget of $17,246,905, and AOI 2 (Solar Energy Projects) with an anticipated budget of $8,000,000. Starting in FY26, nonprofit organizations seeking funding to upgrade low-and-moderate income-serving commercial facilities should refer to the Commercial and Industrial Grant Program instead.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants awarded to non-profit organizations and local governments for energy efficiency, electrification, and solar photovoltaic upgrades in residential buildings serving low-and-moderate income Maryland residents. AOI 1 (Energy Efficiency Projects) provides up to $21,000 per residence for weatherization and electrification measures, with a minimum award of $105,000 per region and up to $400,000 for first-time grant recipients. AOI 2 (Solar Energy Projects) provides $30,000-$1,500,000 per award for solar PV systems (3-15 kW capacity) with two implementation categories: Category 1 (Direct Ownership) where homeowners own panels outright, or Category 2 (Zero Cost Power Purchase Agreement) where the grantee owns the system and provides power to homeowner at no charge through a 20-year prepaid agreement. Grantees can claim up to 15% of total grant amount for grant administration and indirect costs combined. All projects must be completed by September 1, 2028, with invoices and reports submitted by October 1, 2028. Grant period is two years from effective date of grant agreement. MEA reimburses grantees in arrears for actual costs incurred after receiving required invoicing and documentation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and local government entities serving low-and-moderate income Maryland residents in single-family and multi-family residential buildings. Residents do not receive funds directly from the Maryland Energy Administration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements, electrification, and solar photovoltaic upgrades to single-family and multi-family homes that benefit income-qualifying (low-to-moderate income) residents. Eligible activities include weatherization measures, electrification of appliances and HVAC/domestic water heating systems, solar PV systems, enabling repairs, energy audits, permitting, inspections, and project-related workforce training (up to $6,000 per award for BPI or NABCEP PVIP certifications).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. AOI1 is competitive regionally with allocations based on number of low-to-moderate income households per region. AOI2 is competitive statewide with consideration for geographic diversity in award determinations.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit organization incorporated in Maryland or a local government entity (city, county, or municipality)
Projects must benefit residential buildings (single-family or multi-family)
Residents must be income-qualifying (low-to-moderate income), defined as 80% of state median income with specific household income limits provided
Projects must generate significant reductions in residential energy usage

For AOI1: Energy measures must be cost-effective with simple payback of 18 years or less (cumulative average over grant cycle). Energy audit by BPI-certified auditor required except for Limited Upgrade projects (1-2 measures only) or New Construction/Substantial Rehab projects. All health and safety testing must be conducted per BPI Standards.

For AOI2: Solar PV systems must be 3-15 kW capacity, sized to provide 95% or less of projected annual electrical needs. Dwelling units must be owner-occupied primary residences for single-family or multifamily buildings up to 4 units (at least one owner-occupied). Multifamily units must have independent electrical meters. Weatherization work by BPI-certified individual required within last 5 years or within 6 months of installation. NABCEP-certified PV Installation Professional must be involved in design or construction.
Solar PV systems that have already received funding from Maryland Solar Access Program (MSAP) are not eligible
Commercial buildings and commercial spaces in mixed-use buildings are not eligible

For AOI2 Category 1 (Direct Ownership): Grantee responsible for design, installation, and commissioning; homeowners own panels and retain solar renewable energy credits (RECs); Consumer Protection Plan must be provided to residents

For AOI2 Category 2 (Zero Cost PPA): Grantee owns system and provides power at no charge through 20-year prepaid PPA; Grantee must consult tax professional and apply for federal Solar Investment Tax Credit and Low-Income Communities Bonus Credit; Grantee responsible for system insurance and maintenance paid from Reserve Account; Contingency plan required to protect residents in event of grantee insolvency or inability to fulfill obligations

structured_extraction.program_name: Residential and Commercial Energy Storage Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Residential and Commercial Energy Storage (RCES) Program provides grants to support the deployment of energy storage systems for both residential and commercial customers across Maryland. The program aims to enhance grid reliability, increase energy resilience, and accelerate the adoption of clean energy technologies statewide. Grants are funded through the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) via Regional Renewable Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI) proceeds and awarded on a first come, first served basis. The RCES Program was established in statute and replaces the prior Maryland Energy Storage Income Tax Credit Program that sunset at the end of 2024.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to eligible projects on a first come, first served basis. Total program budget is $2,000,000 available from RGGI-RE proceeds through the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) for Fiscal Year 2026. Grants support the installation of qualifying battery energy storage systems (BESS). Grant awards are calculated as the lower amount of: 30 percent of the total installed costs of the BESS, $5,000 for a BESS installed on a residential property, or $150,000 for a BESS installed on a commercial property. As of April 6, 2026, 100% of funding has been requested and 90% has been reserved for approved projects. Partial grants are possible depending on the number of eligible applications received and funds available. A valid, signed BESS installation contract must be in place before application submission. No installation work can begin until after the Reservation Certificate is issued. Applicants have 180 days from the Reservation Certificate effective date to complete installation and submit the Completion Certificate.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 5, 2026, or until all program funding is exhausted, whichever comes first
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial property owners, third-party owners of energy storage systems, and non-profit organizations in Maryland seeking to install battery energy storage systems that are grid-connected.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of qualifying battery energy storage systems (BESS) on residential or commercial properties. A battery energy storage system means a system used to store electrical energy, or mechanical, chemical, or thermal energy that was once electrical energy, for use as electrical energy at a later date or in a process that offsets electricity use at peak times. The system must be grid-connected, meaning there is a physical linkage between the energy storage system and the utility grid.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to applicants across all Maryland counties.

Commercial applicants and third-party owners must provide evidence of Good Standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (DAT)

No installation work can begin until after the Reservation Certificate is issued by MEA

Applications with missing or incomplete information will be placed on standby and applicants will have 14 calendar days to submit missing documentation; applications not completed within 14 days will be rejected
All participating businesses and contractors must comply with all applicable Environmental Standards

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process consists of two steps submitted through the MyMEA Portal. Step 1 - Reserve Grant Funds: Applicants must create a MyMEA account and submit a complete application package with all required supporting documents including complete application data, executed BESS installation contract, and any required authorization forms. MEA will review the application for eligibility and, subject to funding availability, issue a Reservation Certificate confirming reserved grant funds. Step 1 review notification takes up to 45 days. Staff will confirm receipt of applications within one to two business days via email. The Reservation Certificate is considered effective after it has been signed and dated by MEA. The reservation of funds expires 180 days after Step 1 approval unless an extension is formally approved. Step 2 - Complete Installation and Claim Funds: Within 180 days of the effective date of the Reservation Certificate, applicants must submit a Completion Certificate through the MyMEA Portal indicating BESS installation is complete. The Completion Certificate must include completion certificate data, executed BESS agreement, utility interconnection agreement and permission to operate, proof that BESS is paid-in-full (if owned by applicant) or financing agreement documentation (if financed), complete IRS Form W-9, and good standing documentation (for commercial applicants). Upon receipt, MEA will review the Completion Certificate to confirm eligibility. Eligible projects will be awarded grant funding by processing payment of the reserved grant funds. If an application is missing information, the applicant will be notified and given 14 calendar days to provide the missing documentation; if not received, the application will be rejected but the applicant may reapply subject to funding availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants for the design and installation of solar photovoltaic energy-generating systems on homes of Marylanders that experience low-to-moderate income, or are in overburdened or underserved communities. Homes must have already completed energy efficiency and weatherization upgrades through MEA's Energy Efficiency Equity Grant Program or through DHCD's Weatherization Assistance Program or EmPOWER Maryland Limited Income Energy Efficiency Program. The program is administered by the Maryland Energy Administration and is competitive, with funding available statewide across different Areas of Interest.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding provides up to 100% reimbursement of solar photovoltaic system design and installation costs, with a maximum of $25,000 per home inclusive of all direct and indirect costs. Up to $5,000 of the per-home $25,000 allowance may be used for roof repairs or mold remediation necessary for safe and successful solar installation. Up to $10,000,000 total funding is expected to be available across different Areas of Interest. Grantees may receive up to a maximum total individual grant of $1,500,000. Applicants can apply for one of two Areas of Interest: AOI 1 (Direct Ownership, where the homeowner owns the system outright) or AOI 2 (Zero-Cost Power Purchase Agreement, where the grantee owns the system and provides power free of charge under a 20-year prepaid lease). Reimbursement is provided in arrears after the system obtains permission to operate from the local electric utility and passes all required permitting inspections. Partial grants are possible; MEA will fully fund each eligible application in order received, subject to funding availability.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit complete application package electronically to SolarEquity.MEA@Maryland.gov by the deadline. Required documents include: (1) completed and signed FY25 MEA SEE Program Application Form, (2) project narrative (maximum 5 pages) describing project scope, participating homes, county/municipality location, number of homes, estimated system capacity, and how the project meets evaluation criteria, (3) completed IRS Form W9, (4) for nonprofits: proof of incorporation and nonprofit status, (5) for third-party contractors: Maryland DAT Good Standing documentation. The application is competitive. MEA will assemble a Grant Review Team of at least 3 qualified program managers and energy specialists who will conduct individual reviews using evaluation criteria (Community Benefits, Greenhouse Gas Reductions per MEA Dollar, Cost-Effectiveness, Selection of Contractors, and New/Existing Applicant bonus points), then meet to discuss reviews and reach consensus on funding recommendations. Each eligible application will be fully funded in order received, subject to funding availability. Applicants may receive partial grants if insufficient funding remains.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration provides technical assistance to state and local government entities to help them evaluate potential solar project sites. This includes solar site surveys and preliminary development work to help government entities make informed decisions about solar energy projects, including location, use, and budgeting. Technical assistance is provided free-of-charge through the Maryland Environmental Service (MES) for solar site assessments on government-owned or controlled buildings and previously disturbed land, and may include limited technical assistance for microgrid sizing and design, detailed support for specific engineering problems, data analytics services, and solar project reviews or owner representative services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEA provides technical assistance at no cost, coordinating with the Maryland Environmental Service (MES) or other technical service providers selected by MES and MEA. The program has an anticipated budget of up to $860,000 in technical assistance. Technical services are normally expected to be less than $10,000 for an individual building, though MEA is particularly interested in larger scale projects evaluating solar feasibility across 5 to 20 buildings within a local government's portfolio. The program is non-competitive and operates on a first-come, first-served basis. MEA may adjust applications for technical assistance if requests exceed the scope of allowable assistance under the Program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: N/A. The program remains open until funding is expended. Applications submitted before 3:00 p.m. on Friday, March 13, 2026, are likely to be funded before the end of the fiscal year.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application spreadsheet along with required documents (cover letter, site map, evidence of property control, and IRS Form W-9) electronically to MEA via email at msec.mea@maryland.gov. If specifically authorized by MEA, supporting documents may be mailed to: Maryland Energy Administration, Attn: Solar Technical Assistance Program, 1800 Washington Blvd., Suite 755, Baltimore, MD 21230. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. A review team selected by the MEA Program Manager will evaluate applications and supporting documents against minimum criteria including project readiness and commitment. Approved applications are forwarded to Maryland Environmental Service to assign to a Technical Assistance provider and receive a quote. structured_extraction.program_name: U.S. Department of Agriculture Rural Development Rural Energy for America Program (REAP) for Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency
structured_extraction.program_description: The USDA Rural Energy for America Program (REAP) provides guaranteed loan financing and grant funding to agricultural producers and rural small businesses to purchase or install renewable energy systems or make energy efficiency improvements. REAP has two main components: (1) Renewable Energy Systems and Energy Efficiency Improvement Assistance providing grants and guaranteed loans for purchasing and installing renewable energy systems (wind, solar, renewable biomass including anaerobic digesters, small hydro-electric, ocean, geothermal, or hydrogen derived from renewable resources) and making energy efficiency improvements, and (2) Energy Audit and Renewable Energy Development Assistance Grants available to government entities, institutions of higher education, rural electric cooperatives, and public power entities. The program helps rural farms and small businesses cut costs, save energy, and strengthen operations by covering up to 25% of eligible project costs through matching grants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Renewable Energy Systems and Energy Efficiency Improvement Assistance: Grants and guaranteed loans to agricultural producers and rural small businesses. Grants range from $2,500 to $500,000 for renewable energy systems and $1,500 to $250,000 for energy efficiency improvements, with maximum grant portion not exceeding 25% of total eligible project costs. Guaranteed loans range from $5,000 to $25 million with guarantee fee of 1% of the guaranteed portion and annual renewal fee of 0.25% of the guaranteed portion. Combined grant and guaranteed loan funding will not exceed 75% of eligible project costs. Energy Audit and Renewable Energy Development Assistance Grants: Available to government units, educational institutions, rural electric cooperatives, and public power entities to establish programs assisting agricultural producers and rural small businesses with energy evaluations. Maximum aggregate amount of energy audit and renewable energy development assistance grants awarded to any one recipient cannot exceed $100,000 per fiscal year. Recipients conducting energy audits must require the agricultural producer or rural small business to pay at least 25% of the audit cost.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on ongoing basis with specific deadline windows varying by project type and funding amount. For FY 2015: Renewable energy system and energy efficiency improvement grants requesting $20,000 or less (competing for set aside): April 30, 2015. Grants requesting $20,000 or less or over $20,000 (unrestricted): April 30, 2015 or June 30, 2015. Guaranteed loan-only applications: Continuous application cycle with monthly competitions on the first business day of each month. Energy audit and renewable energy development assistance grants: February 12, 2015.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers who earn at least 51% of income from farming or ranching, privately owned for-profit small businesses located in rural areas or towns with populations of 50,000 or less. For Energy Audit and Renewable Energy Development Assistance Grants: units of State, Tribal, or local government; instrumentalities of State, Tribal, or local government; institutions of higher education; rural electric cooperatives; public power entities; and councils serving agricultural producers and rural small businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase or installation of renewable energy systems (wind, solar, renewable biomass including anaerobic digesters, small hydro-electric, ocean, geothermal, or hydrogen derived from renewable resources) or energy efficiency improvements to reduce energy costs and consumption at agricultural or rural business facilities. For Energy Audit grants: conducting energy audits and developing renewable energy development assistance programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rural areas of the United States, including towns with populations of 50,000 or less. Rural Development State Offices administer the program with state-specific allocations. Applicants' proposed projects must be located in the state where they submit applications to the Rural Development Energy Coordinator.
requirements_list: Earn at least 51% of income from farming or ranching (for agricultural producers), OR operate a privately owned for-profit small business
Located in a rural area or town with a population of 50,000 or less
