Want to install a system that generates renewable energy or reduces energy costs
The project's technology must be readily available for purchase and commercially proven
Applicant must be eligible applicant type per 7 CFR 4280.109, 4280.110, and 4280.112
Unless exempt, applicant must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to submitting application
Applicant must provide DUNS number in application
Maintain active SAM registration with current information during active federal award period
For combined grant and guaranteed loan requests: comply with requirements in 7 CFR 4280.165
For guaranteed loan applicants: lenders and borrowers must meet eligibility requirements in 7 CFR 4280.125 and 4280.127
For renewable energy system and energy efficiency improvement projects: meet requirements in 7 CFR 4280.113 and 4280.128

For energy audit and renewable energy development assistance grants: applicant must be unit of State, Tribal, or local government; instrumentality of State, Tribal, or local government; institution of higher education; rural electric cooperative; public power entity; or council as defined in 16 U.S.C. 3451
For energy audit grants: require agricultural producer or rural small business to pay at least 25% of audit cost
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit complete applications in accordance with Notice and 7 CFR part 4280, subpart B. Grant applications may be submitted as hard copy to the appropriate Rural Development Energy Coordinator or electronically via Grants.gov. Applicants submitting electronically must download application package, complete it offline, then upload and submit via Grants.gov. Guaranteed loan-only and combination grant/guaranteed loan applications must be submitted as hard copy to the appropriate Rural Development Energy Coordinator. Grant applications with total project costs of $80,000 or less must provide information per 7 CFR 4280.119; $200,000 or less but more than $80,000 per 7 CFR 4280.118; greater than $200,000 per 7 CFR 4280.117. Guaranteed loan applications must provide information per 7 CFR 4280.137. Combined grant and guaranteed loan applications must provide information per 7 CFR 4280.165(c). Energy audit/renewable energy development assistance applications must provide information per 7 CFR 4280.190. All applications must include environmental review documents per 7 CFR part 1940, subpart G. Applications are reviewed and scored for eligibility, applicant and project qualifications, and technical evaluation as applicable. Contact the applicable USDA Rural Development Energy Coordinator for your State for application materials and assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: World Resources Institute Local and State Clean Energy Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: WRI provides technical assistance and support at the state, local and tribal level to help public agencies and communities in the U.S. advance their clean energy and equity goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance and support for advancing clean energy and equity goals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public agencies and communities in the U.S.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance for clean energy and equity initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nationwide.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant recognizes an individual representing a Maryland land trust for outstanding leadership, partnership and innovation in a conservation project or organization development. The grant is awarded annually to support local land trust programming.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Environmental Trust (part of Keep Maryland Beautiful Grant Program)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $5,000 awarded annually to an individual representing a Maryland land trust. Funding is awarded to the land trust on behalf of the individual. The award recognizes outstanding leadership, partnership, and innovation in conservation projects or organizational development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals representing Maryland land trusts who have demonstrated outstanding leadership in land conservation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To support local land trust programming and recognize outstanding leadership in conservation projects or organizational development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Individual must represent a Maryland land trust
Individual must demonstrate outstanding leadership, partnership, and/or innovation in a conservation project or organizational development
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Click the application link provided to apply through the Keep Maryland Beautiful grants portal at cbtrust.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship designed to assist and encourage transfer students from Maryland community colleges to attend a 4-year institution within the state and complete their bachelor's degrees in a timely manner. Established in 2014, the scholarship is specifically targeted for transfer students and provides financial support based on academic merit and financial need. Students must be enrolled in an eligible accredited Maryland postsecondary institution. A waiting list is maintained each year due to demand exceeding available funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Recipients are eligible for $1,000 annually ($500 per term) towards tuition and mandatory fees. Recipients enrolling in science, teaching, engineering, computer science, mathematics, or nursing programs are eligible for $2,000 annually ($1,000 per term). The scholarship may be used towards tuition and mandatory fees at the 4-year Maryland institution the student has transferred to. The scholarship can be renewed for up to 3 years or six terms of study, whichever is longer. Renewal recipients must complete the FAFSA each year and maintain a minimum 2.5 cumulative GPA at their 4-year institution. Renewing recipients do not need to submit a new application and their scholarship will be automatically renewed as long as they meet the criteria and their 4-year institution certifies them. Awards are contingent on the availability of funds. The 2+2 Transfer Scholarship is a need-based scholarship with a Student Aid Index (SAI) cap of $10,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: For 2026-2027: Application opens January 15, 2026. Deadline to submit application and FAFSA: October 15, 2026. Deadline to submit requested documentation: November 15, 2026. Deadline to submit proof of associate's degree: February 15, 2027. For 2025-2026: Application opened in early March 2025. Deadline to submit application and FAFSA: December 31, 2025. Deadline to submit requested documentation: January 31, 2026. Deadline to submit proof of associate's degree: March 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Higher Education Commission, Office of Student Financial Aid
structured_extraction.program_audience: Transfer students from Maryland community colleges who are planning to complete a bachelor's degree at a 4-year Maryland public or private nonprofit institution. Applicants must be Maryland residents with demonstrated financial need. Undocumented students are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees at a 4-year Maryland public or private nonprofit higher education institution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be residents of Maryland attending a Maryland community college and transferring to a Maryland public or private nonprofit 4-year higher education institution.
requirements_list: Be a resident of Maryland
Not be an undocumented student
Submit a 2+2 Transfer Scholarship application via the MHEC One-App in MDCAPS by October 15, 2026 (for 2026-2027) or December 31, 2025 (for 2025-2026)
File the applicable year's Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) by October 15, 2026 (or December 31, 2025 for 2025-2026)
Students ineligible to file FAFSA cannot apply

Be attending a Maryland community college with plans to finish an associate's degree by December 2026 OR have completed an associate's degree from a Maryland community college in the 2025-2026 academic year or later

For 2026-2027: Have graduated or will graduate with associate's degree in Fall 2025, Spring 2026, or Summer 2026 and transfer to 4-year institution in Fall 2026 for full-year award, OR will graduate in Fall 2026 and transfer in Spring 2027 for Spring-only award
Applicants who completed associate's degree must transfer to 4-year institution as a full-time, degree-seeking undergraduate student
Have maintained a minimum cumulative 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale while at a Maryland community college
Cannot have received a bachelor's degree or associate's degree prior to the eligible transfer window
Have demonstrated financial need with a Student Aid Index (SAI) not over $10,000
Submit all required documentation by the listed deadlines
Submit community college transcript with current cumulative GPA by November 15, 2026 (for 2026-2027) or January 31, 2026 (for 2025-2026)
Submit proof of associate's degree via final community college transcript showing degree conferment date by February 15, 2027 (for 2026-2027) or March 15, 2026 (for 2025-2026)
Submit proof of Selective Service registration for applicable students by February 15, 2027 (for 2026-2027) or March 15, 2026 (for 2025-2026)
Priority given to those pursuing workforce shortage fields of study such as teaching and STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit the 2+2 Transfer Scholarship application through the MHEC One-App on MDCAPS (https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us/) by the applicable deadline (October 15, 2026 for 2026-2027; December 31, 2025 for 2025-2026). 2. File the applicable year's FAFSA by the same deadline. 3. Submit the student's most recent community college transcript with current cumulative GPA by November 15, 2026 (2026-2027) or January 31, 2026 (2025-2026). 4. Applications and documentation are reviewed on a rolling basis. Awarding occurs on a rolling basis beginning in late spring, after an applicant has submitted all requested documents and MHEC staff review them. On average, this takes 4-5 weeks. 5. You will receive an email notification from MDCAPS or you can check your application status in MDCAPS. You will have two weeks from the time the email notification is sent to accept or reject the award in MDCAPS. If no response is received after two weeks, the award offer is cancelled. 6. Once conditionally awarded, submit proof of associate's degree via final community college transcript showing degree conferment date by February 15, 2027 (2026-2027) or March 15, 2026 (2025-2026). 7. Submit proof of Selective Service registration (if applicable) by the same deadline. 8. Only after MHEC staff have reviewed and approved the student's proof of associate's degree and proof of Selective Service Registration (if applicable), can the institution certify the student and request payment. 9. Awards are certified and paid out once all requirements are met. The timeline between accepting an award and it being paid to the institution varies greatly depending on the actions of the student and institutional certification processes. Institutions tend to certify students after their Census Date each semester. Once an institution receives payment, they have their own internal processes for the award to be applied to the student's account. 10. A waiting list is maintained each year due to demand exceeding available funding. Appeal options are available for students deemed ineligible.

structured_extraction.program_description: Competitive scholarship program covering full college tuition and fees, providing a monthly non-taxable allowance, and leading to a commission in the U.S. Air Force.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Full college tuition coverage, laboratory fees, textbook and incidental fees covered. Non-taxable $100 monthly allowance during the school year. Minimum four-year active duty service obligation required.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than December 1 of senior year
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school graduates age 17 to 25 who are U.S. citizens
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, laboratory fees, textbooks, and incidental fees
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Student's choice of over 500 colleges and universities throughout the country
requirements_list: High school graduate
Age 17 to 25
U.S. citizen
SAT or ACT scores
Minimum GPA requirement
Favorable class standing
Successful interview
Pass physical aptitude test
Minimum four-year active duty service obligation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply during junior year of high school or no later than December 1 of senior year. Awards based on SAT or ACT scores, GPA, class standing, interview, and physical aptitude test.

structured_extraction.program_description: Competitive scholarship program providing tuition coverage, fees, books, and a tax-free subsistence allowance, leading to a commission in the U.S. Army.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tuition, laboratory fees, and standard amount for textbooks, classroom supplies, and equipment covered. Tax-free subsistence of up to $1,500 each school year. Scholarship winners obligated to military service: either 2 to 4 years active duty followed by service in Army National Guard or Army Reserve, or 8 years in Army National Guard or Army Reserve.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school graduates age 17 to 21 who are U.S. citizens
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, laboratory fees, textbooks, classroom supplies, and equipment
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Four-year scholarship recipients must attend Army ROTC host institutions; two and three-year recipients may attend any college offering Army ROTC
requirements_list: High school graduate
Age 17 to 21
U.S. citizen
SAT or ACT scores
High school academic review
Successful interview
Pass physical aptitude exam
Military service obligation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply during junior year in high school. Awards based on SAT or ACT and high school academic review, interview, and physical aptitude exam.

structured_extraction.program_name: Charles W. Riley Firefighter and Ambulance and Rescue Squad Member Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Charles W. Riley Firefighter and Ambulance and Rescue Squad Member Scholarship Program encourages active career or volunteer members of fire-fighting, ambulance, and rescue organizations serving Maryland communities to pursue credited courses leading to a degree in fire service technology, emergency medical technology, fire service management, or public safety administration with a minor or concentration in fire service technology or fire service management. The program provides financial assistance to help these individuals pursue higher education in fields that support employment in organized fire departments, ambulance services, and rescue squads throughout the state of Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An annual award of at least 50 percent of the student's actual annual tuition and mandatory fees at an eligible institution. The award may not exceed the annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate student at a 4-year public institution within the University System of Maryland, other than the University of Maryland Global Campus (UMGC) and the University of Maryland, Baltimore (UMB). Recipients may receive the award for up to 5 years of full-time study or 8 years of part-time study. Applicants not selected are placed on a waitlist pending funding availability. Awards are subject to the availability of funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application for the 2025-2026 academic year is now open and will close on April 1, 2026. The application for the upcoming 2026-2027 academic year will become available on January 15, 2026, and will close on October 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Higher Education Commission Office of Student Financial Assistance
structured_extraction.program_audience: Actively engaged career or volunteer firefighters, ambulance members, and rescue squad members in Maryland who are pursuing higher education in fire service technology, emergency medical technology, fire service management, or public safety administration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Annual tuition and mandatory fees at eligible institutions in Maryland for credited courses leading to a degree in fire service technology, emergency medical technology, fire service management, or public safety administration with a minor or concentration in fire service technology or fire service management.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Applicants must be residents of Maryland. If applicant is a dependent student, parent must also be a Maryland resident. Applicants must be members of fire-fighting, ambulance, and rescue organizations serving Maryland communities.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident; if a dependent student, parent must also be a Maryland resident

Actively engaged as either a volunteer member within a county or municipality operating a Length of Service Award Program (LOSAP) with at least 50 LOSAP points recorded in the tax year prior to the award year with points earned in at least two different categories, OR a volunteer member within a county or municipality not operating LOSAP with at least 50 points recorded under the county or municipality point system in the tax year prior to the award year with points earned in at least two different categories, OR a career member who has worked a minimum of 1,000 hours as part of a fire, ambulance, or rescue squad in the tax year prior to the award year
Accepted for admission or enrolled at an eligible institution in Maryland each semester as a full-time (12+ credits per semester) or part-time (6-11 credits per semester) undergraduate

Pursuing a credited course leading to a degree in fire service technology, emergency medical technology, fire service management, or public safety administration with a minor or concentration in fire service technology or fire service management
Maintain a minimum 2.5 GPA for renewal awards (no GPA requirement for initial applicants)
Meet Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) requirements of the institution
Maintain drug-free status for the full term of the award
Submit Riley Application through MDCAPS
Submit Riley Service Verification Form completed by the institution
Submit Riley Fire Official Acceptance Letter or comparable documentation (initial applicants only)
Submit Riley Fire LOSAP or documentation of points earned from county or municipality (required for active volunteers)
For initial applicants, electronically sign Riley Fire Promissory Note and Riley Fire Employment Obligation Agreement in MDCAPS prior to receiving payment
Audited courses cannot be used to reach minimum credit hours required for full-time or part-time status
Total dollar amount of all State awards may not exceed cost of attendance or $28,000, whichever is less
MHEC One App and required documentation must be submitted by the applicable deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us. 2. Upload all required documents by the application deadline (July 1 or April 15, depending on year). 3. Required documents vary by applicant type: Initial volunteer applicants must submit Riley Service Verification Form, LOSAP or equivalent points documentation, and official letter of acceptance. Initial career applicants must submit Riley Service Verification Form and official letter of acceptance. Renewal applicants must submit Riley Service Verification Form and LOSAP or points documentation (if volunteer). 4. At the beginning of each semester, the institution will be asked to certify eligibility; payment will be processed approximately four weeks after certification is returned to OSFA. 5. For initial applicants, must electronically sign Riley Fire Promissory Note and Riley Fire Employment Obligation Agreement in MDCAPS before receiving payment. 6. Eligible renewal applicants receive priority over initial applicants. Within each group, applicants are ranked and awarded on a first-come, first-served basis according to submission date of completed online application. 7. Applicants not selected are placed on a waitlist and must reapply in subsequent years. Late applications and supporting documents will be accepted only if funds are available after all eligible on-time applicants are awarded.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that supports Maryland's college access and completion goals by providing financial support and fostering collaboration between high-need local education agencies and higher education institutions. The program raises the academic preparedness of economically and environmentally disadvantaged students in grades 6-12 so they can attend, persist, and succeed in college. It funds activities that encourage students to aim higher, study harder, and take courses required for college admission, and provides student support services, comprehensive mentoring, financial aid counseling, and academic preparation activities in English/Language Arts and mathematics.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grants awarded to accredited Maryland public or independent two- or four-year higher education institutions, or partnerships between a lead higher education institution and a non-profit organization, to support college preparation and intervention programs for eligible students. Up to $150,000 per project for the FY 2025 funding cycle. Awards support academic services to students (enrichment, remediation, tutoring, research opportunities, individualized academic support in mathematics and English/language arts), student and family financial aid advising services (FAFSA assistance, financial literacy, college and career awareness), and student and family academic planning and career counseling (college/career counseling, academic planning, leadership development for parents). Grant period: August 5, 2025 through August 4, 2026. 50% of the total grant award is disbursed at the beginning of the project period, and the remaining 50% is disbursed upon receipt and processing of the interim report.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland middle and high school students in grades 6-12 who are economically and environmentally disadvantaged, served through partnerships between accredited Maryland public or independent two- or four-year higher education institutions (and non-profit partners) and local education agencies in eligible counties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial support to raise the level of academic preparedness of economically and environmentally disadvantaged students to enable them to attend, persist, and succeed in college, including: (A) Academic services to students such as enrichment, remediation, tutoring, research opportunities, and individualized academic support with a strong preference for mathematics, English/language arts, or cross-disciplinary work; (B) Student and family financial aid advising services including information on FAFSA, financial literacy, college and career awareness, and leadership development activities; (C) Student and family academic planning and career counseling including college and career counseling, academic planning, workshops on high school graduation requirements, college benefits, college preparation, college visits, career exploration activities, and paid/volunteer internships.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Caroline County, Dorchester County, Prince George's County, Somerset County, and Wicomico County. The program focuses on high-need GEAR UP districts and similar designated service regions. High-need LEAs meet three-quarters of the following eligibility criteria: (1) ≥44.4% or higher free and reduced meals (FARM) in feeder middle schools; (2) ≥39.6% or higher FARM in feeder high schools; (3) FARM cohort graduation rate less than 77.93%; (4) College remediation rates of recent high school graduates by place of residence greater than 32.7%.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an accredited Maryland public or independent two- or four-year institution of higher education
Partnerships between a lead higher education institution and a non-profit organization are eligible to apply
Must partner with a Local Education Authority (LEA) in an eligible county
Must serve low-income and economically and environmentally disadvantaged students in grades 6-12
Target population must be Maryland middle and high school students from the designated service regions
Successful projects must demonstrate cooperative planning between the IHE, LEA Coordinator, school district central office representatives, and school principals
Projects providing academic services must show need using LEA academic test measures and demonstrate project success by academic pre- and post-testing of participants
Projects providing student/family services must provide evidence of project success by comparing percent of gain from pre- and post-survey results from both students and parents
Project objectives and expected outcomes must be SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, and Time Sensitive)
Evaluation plan must be integrated into project design and implementation, not conducted after completion
Institutions may hold multiple grants and may apply for new grants
Grantees are strongly encouraged to conduct at least some activities on their campus
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a complete proposal including: (1) Proposal cover sheet; (2) Abstract (250 words or less describing project services); (3) Table of contents; (4) Proposal narrative (maximum 15 pages, not including cover sheet, abstract, budget, budget narrative, cooperative planning agreements, résumés, or appendices) addressing: Needs Assessment (10 points), Project Objectives and Outcomes (15 points), Management Plan (15 points), Plan of Operation (25 points), and Project Evaluation (20 points); (5) Budget and cost-effectiveness (15 points) using provided Excel format with budget summary and narrative; (6) Statement of Assurances signed by appropriate organizational representative (President or Vice President for IHEs, CEO or Superintendent for school districts); (7) Cooperative Planning Agreement signed by lead institution, school district superintendent/CEO, LEA coordinator, high school principal(s), and other partners. All proposals must be typed in 12-point Times New Roman, Arial, or similar font, single-spaced, on 8.5x11-inch pages with one-inch margins and numbered pages (narrative pages only). Electronic copy of proposal and Excel budget document must be submitted to Anthony Reiner at Anthony.Reiner@maryland.gov by 4:00 p.m. on July 25, 2025. A copy of the abstract must be submitted as a Microsoft Word document. Proposals are evaluated by a review panel using the stated criteria. Award notifications are provided via email by August 5, 2025. Grantees must submit an interim report by January 10, 2026, and a final report by November 4, 2026 (revised final report deadline from September 30, 2026 per RFP). Second payment of grant funds is contingent upon acceptance of the interim report by MHEC.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community College Tuition Waiver for Students with Disabilities Receiving SSI or SSDI
structured_extraction.program_description: A tuition waiver program that eliminates or reduces tuition costs for eligible students with disabilities who receive Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) benefits while enrolled in degree, certificate, or continuing education programs at Maryland community colleges. Students may receive up to 12 credits per semester tuition-free if enrolled in degree or certificate programs designed to lead to employment, or up to 6 credits for other credit coursework. The waiver applies to the tuition balance remaining after any grants and scholarships are applied and does not cover other costs such as books and fees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tuition waiver covering up to 12 credits per semester for degree or certificate programs designed to lead to employment, or up to 6 credits for other coursework at Maryland community colleges. The waiver applies to the balance remaining after grants and scholarships are applied. A course must have at least 10 enrolled students for the waiver to apply. Students are responsible for all other costs such as books and fees. The waiver must be requested every time the student enrolls and requires an annual FAFSA filing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1 each year for State aid consideration; file FAFSA between January 1 and March 1
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) benefits who are enrolled or planning to enroll at Maryland community colleges.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition costs at Maryland community colleges for degree or certificate programs designed to lead to employment, and continuing education instruction designed to lead to employment, including life skills instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland community colleges statewide.
requirements_list: Must be receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) benefits
Must provide proof from the Social Security Administration (SSA) of receiving SSI or SSDI benefits
Must complete and file the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at www.fafsa.gov
Must file FAFSA between January 1 and March 1 each year for State aid consideration
Must enroll in a degree, certificate program, or continuing education instruction designed to lead to employment
Course must have at least 10 enrolled students
Must request the waiver every time you enroll
Must file an annual FAFSA to renew the waiver
Contact your financial aid office to apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and file the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at www.fafsa.gov between January 1 and March 1 each year for State aid consideration. Contact the financial aid office of the community college you plan to attend to have the waiver activated. Provide proof from the Social Security Administration of receiving SSI or SSDI benefits. Request the waiver every time you enroll and file an annual FAFSA to renew.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Cybersecurity Public Service Scholarship Program, administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC), supports students pursuing education in cybersecurity-related degree or certificate programs identified by the Secretary of Higher Education as directly relevant to cybersecurity. Recipients receive scholarship funds to help pay for tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board. After graduation, recipients must fulfill a service obligation by working in cybersecurity roles for eligible government entities or educational institutions in Maryland, including local education agencies, public high schools, community colleges, or state/county/city government. The program also extends to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8 and are pursuing cybersecurity education at eligible Maryland public or private institutions. The award converts to a loan if the recipient fails to complete an approved cybersecurity program or fails to meet the service obligation requirement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The annual scholarship award amount is prescribed by MHEC and may be used for tuition and mandatory fees, room and board, and education expenses as defined by MHEC. Full-time students may renew the award for up to two additional years (maximum 3 years of full-time study); part-time students may renew for up to five additional years (maximum 6 years of part-time study), provided they continue to meet eligibility requirements including maintaining a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0, satisfactory academic progress, continued enrollment in an approved cybersecurity program, and continued eligibility for in-state tuition. For part-time students, the award is prorated based on part-time status. The award converts to a loan payable to the state if the recipient fails to complete an approved cybersecurity program or fails to fulfill the service obligation. Recipients must work one year for each year they received the scholarship in a cybersecurity field for an eligible employer (local education agency, public high school, community college, state/county/city government) or teach cybersecurity in a public high school or community college.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application for the 2026-2027 academic year becomes available January 15, 2026 and closes October 15, 2026. A separate deadline of July 1 applies for required documentation submission. For the 2025-2026 academic year, April 1, 2026 deadline applies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time or part-time students currently enrolled at public or private non-profit institutions in Maryland who are within three years of graduation from an approved credit-bearing degree or certificate program in cybersecurity. Also available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who meet in-state tuition eligibility requirements under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8 and are pursuing cybersecurity education at eligible Maryland public or private institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees; room and board; education expenses as defined by MHEC related to cybersecurity studies at eligible Maryland institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Students must be enrolled at public or private non-profit institutions in Maryland. Recipients must work in the cybersecurity field in Maryland to fulfill the service obligation. Also available to students attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions who qualify under in-state tuition provisions.
requirements_list: Cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 at the time of application
Enrolled full-time or part-time at a public or private non-profit institution in Maryland
Enrolled in an approved credit-bearing cybersecurity degree or certificate program directly relevant to cybersecurity
Completed at least 25 percent of total credit requirements toward approved degree or certificate at time of application
Within three years of graduation from an approved program
Not received Federal Cyber Corps Scholarships for Service award
Sign agreement to work in cybersecurity field for eligible government entity or educational institution in Maryland for specified period (one year for each year of scholarship received)
Maintain satisfactory academic progress and 3.0 GPA for renewal
For renewal: continue to be eligible for in-state tuition
For renewal: continue to enroll as full-time or part-time student
For renewal: part-time students must complete at least 6 semester hours per semester
For qualified children of undocumented immigrants: must be a qualified child of undocumented immigrants
For qualified children of undocumented immigrants: must meet in-state tuition eligibility requirements under §15–106.8 of the MD Education Article
For qualified children of undocumented immigrants: file taxes using prior-prior-year tax information
Males aged 18-25 must register with Selective Service System and provide proof
If dependent, must provide parental information and have one parent sign the application
Must apply through the MHEC One App in the Maryland College Aid Processing (MDCAPS) portal
May not falsify or conceal a material fact in connection with application
Pledge to remain drug-free for full term of award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us using the MHEC One App. Required documents include an official or unofficial college transcript confirming enrollment status and an Institutional Verification Form completed by the institution confirming enrollment in an approved cybersecurity program. All documents must be submitted online through the applicant's MDCAPS account by the application closing date. At the beginning of each semester, the institution will be asked to certify that the recipient meets award requirements. When the institution completes certification and returns it to OSFA, the award is processed for payment, typically within approximately four weeks. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. For qualified children of undocumented immigrants, the application opens at the same time as the FAFSA each year. Awarding occurs in the summer and eligible applicants are notified by email. Applicants must accept their award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks of notification or the award will be canceled. Contact your institution's financial aid office for questions about payment status.

structured_extraction.program_name: Delegate Howard P. Rawlings Guaranteed Access (GA) Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A need-based grant program that provides financial assistance to eligible low-income Maryland students enrolled at Maryland postsecondary institutions for educational expenses. Part of the Howard P. Rawlings Educational Excellence Awards program, it guarantees access to higher education for students with the greatest financial need. The grant covers up to 100% of a student's calculated adjusted financial need for their first 2 academic years of enrollment. It is also available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15-106.8. The grant is renewable for up to 3 additional years (4 years total) if renewal requirements are met.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Need-based grant covering up to 100% of a student's calculated adjusted financial need for the first 2 academic years of enrollment, or up to the maximum award amount, whichever is lower. Previous award years' maximum amounts have ranged from $18,000-$22,100; the 2026-2027 maximum will be determined in Spring 2026. The minimum award is $400 per year. Award amounts are calculated based on cost of attendance at the institution, the student's living situation (on campus, off campus, or with parent), and the amount of financial need. The grant is renewable for up to 3 additional years (4 years total) if renewal requirements are met. For renewal after at least 2 years of receiving any combination of Delegate Howard P. Rawlings Educational Excellence Awards (GA, EA, or CB-EAG), students must complete 30 credits annually for full award or 24-29 credits for prorated award. Awarding begins the first week of April 2026 and continues until funds are exhausted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1, 2026 for FAFSA or MHEC One-App submission; August 1, 2026 for documentation deadline
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Higher Education Commission Office of Student Financial Assistance
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible first-time and renewal undergraduate students from low-income families seeking to attend Maryland public and private postsecondary institutions. Also available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15-106.8. Students must be under age 26 at time of first receiving the grant (born after July 1, 2000 for 2026-2027 award year), have completed high school or obtained a GED, and plan to enroll full-time as degree-seeking undergraduate students at eligible Maryland two-year or four-year institutions. As of the 2026-2027 academic year, eligible college students pursuing their first undergraduate degree who have not previously received an Educational Assistance Award (GA, EA, or CB-EAG) can be considered for the GA.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses including tuition, fees, and other costs of attendance for full-time undergraduate degree-seeking students at eligible Maryland postsecondary institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be eligible for in-state tuition in Maryland and must attend an eligible two-year or four-year Maryland public or private postsecondary institution. A Maryland university or college must be listed on the student's FAFSA or MHEC One-App by the consideration deadline. Students must begin college within 6 years of completing high school or obtaining a GED.
requirements_list: Be eligible for in-state tuition in Maryland
File the 2026-2027 FAFSA or MHEC One-App by March 1, 2026
Have a Maryland university or college listed on FAFSA or MHEC One-App by March 1, 2026

Meet initial income requirements: annual total family income at or below 130% of federal poverty guidelines for the 2024 tax year (new applicants); renewal applicants must be at or below 150% of federal poverty guidelines or remain eligible for the federal Pell Grant
Be accepted for admission and plan to enroll in a regular undergraduate program at an eligible two-year or four-year Maryland institution
Enroll as a full-time degree-seeking undergraduate student (12 credits per semester minimum)
Have completed high school or obtained a GED with a passing score of 145 per module
Begin college within 6 years of completing high school or obtaining a GED
Be under age 26 at time of first receiving the GA grant (must be born after July 1, 2000 for the 2026-2027 award year)
Cannot have previously received an Educational Assistance Grant or Campus-Based Educational Assistance Grant
Cannot have previously received a bachelor's degree prior to the start of the 2026-2027 academic year
Submit any required documentation by August 1, 2026
Maintain satisfactory academic progress standards of the enrolled institution
For renewal after at least 2 years: complete 30 credits annually for full award or 24-29 credits for prorated award
For renewal: remain eligible for in-state tuition and enroll as a full-time degree-seeking undergraduate student at an eligible Maryland institution
If a qualified child of undocumented immigrants: meet non-resident exemption requirements under §15-106.8 of the Maryland Education Article
If a qualified child of undocumented immigrants: file taxes using prior-prior-year tax information
Male applicants ages 18-25 must register with the Selective Service System and provide proof of registration
If dependent and filing MHEC One-App: must provide parental information and have one parent sign the application
Cannot be in default on a Federal Title IV student loan
May not use audited courses to reach the minimum 12 credit hours required for full-time status
Drug-free pledge required for the full term of the award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students submit the 2026-2027 FAFSA (for U.S. citizens and eligible non-citizens) or MHEC One-App (for undocumented students) by March 1, 2026 through the MDCAPS system at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us/MDCAPS/login.aspx. U.S. citizens and eligible non-citizens should complete FAFSA at https://studentaid.ed.gov/sa/fafsa. There is no separate GA Grant application. MDCAPS will automatically consider students who meet basic eligibility requirements. Students may be asked to submit documentation if they meet certain circumstances (GED recipient, independent student status, dependent MHEC One-App filer, male MHEC One-App filer age 18 or older, FAFSA filer missing family size, or randomly selected for financial verification). Required documentation must be submitted online through the student's MDCAPS account by August 1, 2026. Documentation is reviewed on a rolling basis and takes an average of 4-5 weeks. Awarding begins the first week of April 2026 and continues on a rolling basis until funds are exhausted. MHEC notifies applicants of awards via email from MDCAPS. Students may also log into MDCAPS and check 'Check Your Application Status' from their dashboard to view current status. Students must accept their award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks of email notification or the award will be canceled. MHEC reserves the right to not reinstate any cancelled awards. Qualified children of undocumented immigrants must apply through the MHEC One App in the MDCAPS portal; notifications for these applicants are sent in late April. Awards are disbursed after an institution certifies the student, usually starting in September for Fall term and February for Spring term after enrollment is finalized. After certification, an institution initiates the payment request process each term. It can take 4-6 weeks after an institution has requested payment for the institution to receive it. Once an institution receives payment, they have their own internal processes and procedures for an award to be applied to a student account.

structured_extraction.program_name: Douglas J.J. Peters Veterans of Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Douglas J.J. Peters Veterans of Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Program provides financial assistance to United States armed forces personnel who served in the Afghanistan or Iraq Conflicts on or after October 24, 2001 (Afghanistan) or March 19, 2003 (Iraq), and their eligible family members (son, daughter, stepson, stepdaughter, or spouse) who are current high school seniors or full-time or part-time, degree-seeking undergraduate students enrolled in an eligible accredited Maryland postsecondary institution. The program is administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission and awards annual scholarships that may not exceed 50% of the annual tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board of a resident undergraduate at the highest-cost four-year public institution in the University System of Maryland (excluding University of Maryland Global Campus and University of Maryland, Baltimore).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship awards that may not exceed 50% of the annual tuition and mandatory fees and room and board of a resident undergraduate at the highest-cost four-year public institution in the University System of Maryland (excluding University of Maryland Global Campus and University of Maryland, Baltimore). Award amounts for the 2026-2027 academic year: up to $9,189 for on-campus housing, up to $5,186 for students living with parents, or up to $5,756 for off-campus housing. Awards supplement federal education benefits and may be used for tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at eligible Maryland institutions. Renewal awards are available for up to 4 years of full-time enrollment (12+ credits per semester) or 8 years of part-time enrollment (6-11 credits per semester). Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with renewal students receiving first priority, followed by eligible veterans who receive priority over dependents or spouses. All awards are subject to the availability of funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 15, 2026 for the 2026-2027 academic year; applications open January 15, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: United States armed forces personnel who served in Afghanistan or contiguous airspace on or after October 24, 2001, or in Iraq or contiguous waters or airspace on or after March 19, 2003, including active duty members, veterans, reserve component members, and Maryland National Guard members. Also eligible are spouses, sons, daughters, stepsons, and stepdaughters of qualifying service members. Applicants must be Maryland residents (including active military stationed in Maryland whose home of residency is Maryland) accepted for admission to or enrolled in an undergraduate program or 2-year terminal certificate program at an eligible Maryland postsecondary institution. Eligible family members include current high school seniors and full-time or part-time degree-seeking undergraduate students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses including tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at eligible Maryland postsecondary institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents or active members of the United States armed forces stationed in Maryland whose home of residency is Maryland. Students must be enrolled in a regular undergraduate program or a 2-year terminal certificate program with coursework acceptable for transfer credit toward an accredited baccalaureate program at an eligible Maryland postsecondary institution.
requirements_list: Must be a member of the Uniformed Services of the United States who served in Afghanistan or contiguous airspace on or after October 24, 2001, or in Iraq or contiguous waters or airspace on or after March 19, 2003; OR be a son, daughter, stepson, stepdaughter, or spouse of such a service member
Must be a Maryland resident, or an active member of the U.S. armed forces stationed in Maryland whose home of residency is Maryland

Must be accepted for admission or enrolled in a regular undergraduate program or 2-year terminal certificate program with coursework acceptable for transfer credit toward an accredited baccalaureate program at an eligible Maryland institution
Must be enrolled as full-time (12+ credits per semester) or part-time (6-11 credits per semester) undergraduate student
Audited courses cannot be used to reach the minimum credit hours required for full-time or part-time status

Must submit required military documentation: DD-214 (Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty) documenting service in Afghanistan or Iraq for veterans; current official military orders for active duty members; marriage certificate and military orders for spouses; birth certificate and military orders for children/stepchildren
If filing FAFSA or MHEC One-App, must complete by March 1 of the applicable award year
Must accept award within six weeks of notification date or award will be cancelled
For renewal: must continue enrollment in eligible program, maintain Maryland residency, and maintain satisfactory academic progress toward degree and institutional standards
For renewal: must maintain at least a 2.5 cumulative grade point average on a 4.0 scale
For renewal: if filing FAFSA or MHEC One-App, must be completed by March 1; renewal students do not need to reapply if they continue to meet renewal requirements
Total financial assistance including state aid and veterans educational benefits may not exceed cost of attendance as determined by the institution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis from January 15, 2026 through October 15, 2026 for the 2026-2027 academic year. Submit the online application through the MHEC One-App on the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us/. All required documentation must be submitted online through the applicant's MDCAPS account via secure upload (select 'Electronic File Upload' from the homepage). Required documents vary by applicant type: veterans and reserve/National Guard members must submit DD-214 (Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty) documenting service in Afghanistan or Iraq; active duty members must submit current official military orders; spouses must submit marriage certificate and military orders documentation; children/stepchildren must submit birth certificate and military orders documentation. FAFSA or MHEC One-App are not required to determine eligibility, but if completed must be submitted by March 1 or applicant becomes ineligible. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with priority given to renewal applicants (who do not need to reapply or resubmit documents if they continue to meet renewal requirements), then veterans over dependents or spouses, then ranked by application completion date. Award notifications are sent via email; applicants must login to MDCAPS to accept their award by the established timeframe to prevent cancellation. Payment to institutions begins approximately 4-8 weeks after institution certification of enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: EARN Maryland provides funding for free training in a variety of industries including cybersecurity, information technology, healthcare, and construction. The program operates statewide and offers multiple training programs that students may enroll in.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: EARN provides free training funding in cybersecurity, information technology, healthcare, and construction. The program operates statewide with different training program partnerships available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers and students looking to enter or transition into new careers, particularly those impacted by school closures or seeking workforce training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free training in cybersecurity, information technology, healthcare, and construction industries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students may enroll in EARN programs through partnerships. For more information on EARN, including a list of current program partnerships, visit the DLLR website.

structured_extraction.program_name: ENOUGH (Engaging Neighborhoods, Organizations, Unions, Governments, and Households) Initiative
structured_extraction.program_description: A state-led, place-based strategy to address concentrated child poverty in Maryland through targeted grants and technical support to eligible communities. The initiative funds solutions developed by communities with lived experience of poverty to tackle deeply rooted challenges. Grantees work with community partners to develop Neighborhood Action Plans that reduce childhood poverty by increasing investments in high-poverty areas and improving economic mobility. Grantees also establish Community Voice Committees to identify resident needs and create systems for lasting change. The Governor's Office for Children, Maryland agencies, and a network of local, state, and national organizations partner with applicants and grantees to understand, develop, and implement community-focused solutions to end child poverty.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $20 million statewide investment in FY2025 providing competitive grants across three tracks and technical support to eligible communities. Track 1: Partnership Development provides up to 10 awards of approximately $65,000 each to build capacity for addressing root causes of poverty. Track 2: Plan Development provides up to 7 awards of approximately $300,000 each to conduct community asset mapping, needs assessments, and develop neighborhood action plans. Track 3: Implementation provides up to 3 awards of up to $5,000,000 based on community size (prorated at 50% for first cycle) with eligibility for four annual funding cycles; in subsequent years, Implementation grantees receive up to $10,000,000 based on community size. All grantees receive robust technical assistance including resource hubs with expert trainings, data dashboards, hands-on support from local and national experts, and assistance identifying and applying for additional funding streams.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Notice of Intent to Apply Due for All Tracks: July 19, 2024; Full Application Deadline for Track 2 and Track 3: September 20, 2024; Full Application Deadline for Track 1: November 1, 2024; FY2025 ENOUGH Grant Estimated Start Date: Winter 2025
structured_extraction.contact_name: Governor's Office for Children ENOUGH Support Team
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible communities throughout Maryland with high levels of child poverty, including community organizations, neighborhoods, local governments, and nonprofit organizations, driven by residents' lived experience and expertise to address concentrated child poverty. Specific eligible communities must have at least one U.S. Census tract where more than 30% of children are living in poverty and be served by a community school with a concentration of poverty level of at least 80%.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing and implementing community-focused solutions to address concentrated child poverty and its root causes, including building partnership capacity, developing Neighborhood Action Plans, conducting community asset mapping and needs assessments, increasing investments in high-poverty areas, improving economic mobility, creating Community Voice Committees, and implementing systems for change across education, health, workforce, housing, public safety and community development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible communities throughout Maryland with high levels of child poverty. Eligible communities must have at least one U.S. Census tract where more than 30% of children are living in poverty AND be served by a community school with a concentration of poverty level of at least 80%. An interactive map and list of eligible communities across Maryland is available at https://bit.ly/ENOUGHMap. In Frederick County, the program is focused on the Route 40 corridor (Golden Mile) community on the west side of the City of Frederick, including areas served by Hillcrest and Waverley Elementary Schools.
requirements_list: Communities must have at least one U.S. Census tract where more than 30% of children are living in poverty
Communities must be served by a community school with a concentration of poverty level of at least 80%
Must establish an established set of core partnerships including at least one community-based non-profit organization, one local government entity, and one local public school
Must designate a Lead Partner known as the Community Quarterback to serve as lead applicant and coordinate across partner organizations
Focus on communities with high levels of child poverty
Work with community partners to develop a Neighborhood Action Plan
Prioritize community voice in creating systems for change
Solutions must be driven by residents' lived experience and expertise
Track 2 and Track 3 applicants must have a robust partnership structure with organizations centered on community voice and expertise in ENOUGH pillars with established governance structure
Track 3 applicants must have completed a community needs assessment and developed a neighborhood action plan ready for implementation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible communities should review the interactive map at https://bit.ly/ENOUGHMap to confirm eligibility. To receive the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and other updates, email the Governor's Office for Children ENOUGH Support Team at ENOUGH@maryland.gov with subject line 'ENOUGH NOFO.' Communities must submit a Notice of Intent to Apply by July 19, 2024. Pre-application technical assistance is available July-September 2024. Full applications for Track 2 and Track 3 are due September 20, 2024, and for Track 1 by November 1, 2024. FY2025 ENOUGH Grant funding is estimated to begin Winter 2025. Communities should determine which track aligns with their level of readiness and can progress through tracks over time.

structured_extraction.program_name: Educational Assistance Grant / Campus Based Educational Assistance Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: State financial aid grants available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8 and attend eligible Maryland public or private institutions. The program includes two grant types: the Educational Assistance Grant (awarded by MHEC, with notifications in late April) and the Campus Based Educational Assistance Grant (awarded through the student's institution, with notifications in the summer). Both grants are administered through the Maryland Higher Education Commission and applied for via the MHEC One App (Maryland State Financial Aid Application - MSFAA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State financial aid grants for qualified undocumented students attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions. The Educational Assistance Grant is part of the Howard P. Rawlings Educational Excellence Award Program and is awarded by MHEC with notifications by late April. The Campus Based Educational Assistance Grant is awarded through the student's institution with notifications in the summer. Award amounts vary based on financial need and enrollment status. Students must accept their award online through the MDCAPS portal within 2 weeks of notification or the award will be canceled. Dependent students must provide parental financial information; independent students report only their own information (and spouse's if married). Prior-prior-year tax information (two years before the award year) is used for eligibility determination.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1 for Educational Assistance Grant and Guaranteed Access Grant; after March 1 for Campus Based Educational Assistance Grant. Exact deadline dates vary by program year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8, including DACA students, who attend eligible Maryland public or private institutions. Ineligible to receive federal aid through the FAFSA.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial aid for educational expenses (tuition, fees, room and board, books, supplies) at eligible Maryland public or private institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions statewide. Students must have filed Maryland income tax returns meeting specific residency and continuity requirements.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified child of undocumented immigrants
Must be eligible for in-state tuition under §15–106.8 of the MD Education Article
Must not be a U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen with an Alien Registration number
Must not be an international student on a student visa
Must be ineligible to receive federal aid (FAFSA)
Must attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution

Must file Maryland income tax returns: either 3 consecutive years while attending secondary school plus years between secondary school and community college registration, OR all years while enrolled at community college plus years between community college and senior institution registration
Must file taxes using prior-prior-year tax information (two years before the award year)
Males aged 18–25 must register with the Selective Service System and provide proof of registration
If dependent, must provide parental information and have one parent sign the Parent Signature Page
Must apply through the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) via the Maryland College Aid Processing (MDCAPS) portal
Must create MDCAPS account and complete MSFAA Eligibility Wizard
If dependent, Parent Signature Page must be submitted to MHEC for application to be valid; failure to submit disqualifies applicant from consideration
Must accept award online through MDCAPS portal within 2 weeks of notification or award will be canceled
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Create a Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) account at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us. If you are an undocumented student without a Social Security Number, enter zeroes. Activate your account via email link. 2) Complete the MSFAA Eligibility Wizard by answering questions to confirm you are eligible: Are you a U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen (answer no)? Do you or your parent have SSN/ITIN (answer yes if you filed tax returns)? Did you/your parent file Maryland income tax returns per residency requirements? Have you completed FAFSA (answer no). 3) Upon confirmation of MSFAA eligibility, gather required documents: your and parent's income information (bank statements, W-2, pay stub, or prior-prior-year federal income tax return), Social Security card or ITIN, additional financial information (child support statements, TANF, real estate, investment, business/farm information). 4) Complete the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) with the following sections: Student Demographic Data (name, SSN/ITIN, date of birth, address, email, marital status, citizenship, state of residence, driver's license, parent's education, high school completion, degree type); Student Income and Tax Data (tax return status, filing status, AGI, taxes paid, exemptions, earnings, assets, untaxed income); Dependency Information (answer 14 yes/no questions to determine if dependent or independent); Household information; Parent Information (if dependent); and School Selection (add up to 10 institutions). 5) Review all information and terms and conditions, then submit the application. 6) Receive confirmation page showing dependency status. If dependent, download and have parent complete and sign Parent Signature Page and submit to MHEC Office of Student Financial Assistance. 7) If eligible for Educational Assistance Grant, MHEC notifies applicants by late April. If eligible for Campus Based Educational Assistance Grant, institution notifies applicant via email in summer. 8) Accept award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks of notification. OSFA will contact applicants by email if additional documentation is required to verify eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program and Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program (also known in conjunction with the Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship Program) provides student financial assistance to certain Maryland residents due to their eligible military or public safety service, or due to their eligible family or marital relationship to such an individual. This includes veterans, dependents and surviving spouses of U.S. Armed Forces members who died or were disabled due to military service, victims of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks and their families, POW/MIA of the Vietnam Conflict and their families, public safety employees and volunteers who were disabled in the line of duty, and dependents and surviving spouses of public safety employees or school employees who died or were disabled in the line of duty. The program supports eligible students attending institutions of higher learning within Maryland at the undergraduate, graduate, professional, certificate, or private career school level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Renewable scholarship awards up to a maximum of $14,086 for the 2026-2027 academic year (up to $13,689 for 2025-2026) and a minimum of $3,000 or the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of the institution attended, whichever is less. The award amount cannot exceed the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate at the highest-cost four-year public institution in the University System of Maryland (excluding University of Maryland University College and University of Maryland, Baltimore). Awards are automatically renewed annually for eligible students who continue to meet eligibility requirements. Students may hold awards for up to five years of full-time study (12 or more credits per semester) or eight years of part-time study (6-11 credits per semester), or a combination of both. No more than 15 scholarships may be awarded annually to veterans with a service-connected disability of 25% or greater. All awards are subject to the availability of funds. The institution is required to fund eligible students and is then reimbursed by the State.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are enrolled full-time or part-time in undergraduate, graduate, or professional programs at eligible institutions, or in 2-year terminal certificate programs with coursework acceptable for transfer credit to accredited baccalaureate programs, or in private career schools. Applicants must be at least 16 years old and meet specific military or public safety service-related eligibility conditions. Eligible individuals include veterans with qualifying service-connected disabilities, dependents and surviving spouses of U.S. Armed Forces members, victims of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks and their families, POW/MIA of the Vietnam Conflict and their families, public safety employees and volunteers disabled in the line of duty, and dependents and surviving spouses of public safety employees or school employees killed or 100% disabled in the line of duty.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses including tuition and mandatory fees at eligible institutions for undergraduate, graduate, professional, 2-year terminal certificate, or private career school programs. May not be used in conjunction with other financial assistance that would cause the student to exceed their cost of attendance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents at the time of application, with exceptions for certain dependents, stepchildren, and surviving spouses of state or local public safety employees killed or 100% disabled in the line of duty, disabled public safety employees, and their eligible dependents and spouses. If a dependent, their parents must also be Maryland residents at the time of application, except for public safety employee dependents and spouses.
requirements_list: Must be enrolled in a regular undergraduate, graduate, or professional program at an eligible institution at full-time (12+ credits per semester) or part-time (6-11 credits per semester) enrollment, OR enrolled in a 2-year terminal certificate program with course work acceptable for transfer credit at an accredited baccalaureate program, OR enrolled in a private career school
Must be at least 16 years old
Must be a Maryland resident at the time of application (with exceptions for certain public safety employee dependents and spouses); if dependent, parents must also be Maryland residents

Son, daughter, or stepchild of a United States Armed Forces member who died as a result of military service after December 7, 1941, or who suffered a service-connected 100% permanent disability from military service after December 7, 1942
Surviving spouse (who has not remarried) of a United States Armed Forces member who suffered a service-connected 100% permanent disability from military service
Veteran with a service-connected disability of 25% or greater who has exhausted or is no longer eligible for federal veterans' educational benefits

Son, daughter, stepchild, or surviving spouse of a victim of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks who died as a result of the attacks on the World Trade Center, Pentagon, or United Airlines Flight 93

Prisoner of war or missing in action from the Vietnam Conflict (declared on or after January 1, 1960), or their son, daughter, or stepchild (born prior to or while parent was POW/MIA), and was a Maryland resident when declared a prisoner of war or missing in action

Son, daughter, stepchild, or surviving spouse (who has not remarried) of a state or local public safety employee (career or volunteer fire department member, ambulance or rescue squad member, law enforcement officer, correctional officer, or Maryland National Guard member) who died or was 100% disabled in the line of duty
State or local public safety employee or volunteer who was 100% disabled in the line of duty

Son, daughter, stepchild, or surviving spouse (who has not remarried) of a school employee who died or sustained an injury rendering them 100% disabled as a result of an act of violence in the line of duty
Application must be submitted to the institution's financial aid office by July 15 of each year
FAFSA is not required but may be completed if student wishes to apply for need-based state awards
Awards subject to availability of funds; no award is guaranteed
As a condition of receiving a Maryland State scholarship or grant, pledge to remain drug-free for the full term of the award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New and renewal applicants should contact their institution's financial aid office for application instructions and eligibility verification documentation requirements. Students should NOT submit applications or supplemental documentation directly to the Maryland Higher Education Commission. All required documentation must be submitted directly to the institution's financial aid office by July 15 of each year. Renewal awardees are not required to reapply each year if they continue to meet eligibility requirements. The institution awards all eligible students and is then reimbursed by the State. Students can inquire about application status with their institution's financial aid department.

structured_extraction.program_description: An initiative to reduce inequities in college completion by providing coaching, financial support, and other community resources to bolster access to higher education and build a more educated workforce for students pursuing postsecondary degrees or credentials at Maryland community colleges. The program supports students of color and students from low-income families, and provides both student-facing and institutional supports including data analytics, targeted advising, and continuous improvement resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three community colleges receive $125,000 each in funding. The program provides comprehensive student supports including coaching, financial support, community resources, regular targeted advising, and data analytics to track student retention and degree completion. Both the Maryland Higher Education Commission and MDRC provide support and training to participating colleges to launch and continuously improve the initiative.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Donna Thomas, Interim Vice President, Student Affairs (Baltimore City Community College); Crystal Smith, Dean of Student Success and Advisement (Prince George's Community College); Paul Fields, Director of Advising and Title III (Wor-Wic Community College)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students of color and students from low-income families pursuing postsecondary degrees or credentials at participating Maryland community colleges.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Student coaching, advising, financial support, and community resources to support college completion and economic mobility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Three Maryland community colleges: Baltimore City Community College, Prince George's Community College, and Wor-Wic Community College.
requirements_list: Program eligibility requirements vary by college
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the participating college directly for information about program eligibility requirements and application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides tuition assistance to students who are dependents or surviving spouses of fallen transportation workers. Eligible students may be enrolled in undergraduate, graduate, professional, or private career school programs at eligible Maryland institutions. Awards are renewable for up to five years of full-time study or eight years of part-time study, or a combination thereof.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides tuition assistance awards to eligible students. The award amount may not exceed the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate at a 4-year public institution within the University System of Maryland (other than University of Maryland University College and University of Maryland, Baltimore), with the highest annual expenses for a full-time resident undergraduate, and must be no less than the lesser of $3,000 or the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident at the institution the recipient attends. Awards are renewable on an annual basis for up to 5 years of full-time study or 8 years of part-time study, or a combination thereof. The scholarship may be used for tuition and mandatory fees at any eligible institution of postsecondary education. Award amounts may not reflect subsequent tuition and fee increases made throughout the academic year. Awards are subject to the availability of funds. If the institution notifies OSFA that the recipient is receiving other financial assistance that causes them to exceed their financial need or the cost of attendance, State financial aid may be reduced or cancelled.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students who are dependents or surviving spouses of fallen transportation workers and are enrolled in eligible higher education programs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees at eligible institutions of postsecondary education, including undergraduate, graduate, professional, or private career school programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland. Students must be enrolled at an eligible institution in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be the child, stepchild, or surviving spouse of a fallen transportation worker (whose occupation is in the construction, rehabilitation, or operation of a transportation facility or project in the State, and who died on or after January 1, 2022, as a result of an accident occurring while performing job duties necessary for the construction, maintenance, rehabilitation, or operation of a transportation facility or project in the State)
Be at least 16 years old

Be accepted for admission or enrolled in a regular undergraduate, graduate, or professional program at an institution of postsecondary education: Full-time (12+ credits per semester) or part-time (6-11 credits per semester) undergraduate; Full-time (9+ credits per semester) or part-time (6-8 credits per semester) graduate student; or professional program
Be enrolled in a 2-year terminal certificate program in which the coursework is acceptable for transfer credit for an accredited baccalaureate program in an eligible institution; or
Be enrolled in a private career school
For renewal: Recipients must continue to meet all eligibility requirements and be enrolled on at least a part-time basis in an eligible Maryland postsecondary institution
Application must be submitted through the student's financial aid office by July 15 of each year
As a condition of receiving the award, pledge to remain drug free for the full term of the award
