structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New and renewal applicants should work through their institution's financial aid office to apply. Applicants should contact their institution's financial aid office for application instructions and submit applications by July 15 of each year. All documentation should be submitted directly to the institution, not to the Maryland Higher Education Commission. The institution is required to fund all eligible students and then request reimbursement from the State.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports Maryland's GEAR UP goals to increase the number of economically disadvantaged students who intend to pursue postsecondary education. The program provides summer enrichment, skill-building, and inclusive programming to secondary GEAR UP students while educating students and their families about postsecondary education and college financing options.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $45,000 may be requested by the institution in their proposal. The grant period is from June 15, 2018 to August 15, 2019.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited Maryland public or not for profit independent two-year or four-year institutions of higher education that partner with Local Education Agencies to serve economically disadvantaged secondary students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports summer enrichment, skill-building, and inclusive programming including application workshops, counseling and advising, comprehensive mentoring, self-discovery and career exploration workshops, project leadership and management, ideation and innovation sessions, communication effectiveness workshops, and cross-cultural leadership and diversity workshops.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Service regions include Baltimore City, Dorchester County, and Wicomico County.
requirements_list: Must be an accredited Maryland public or not for profit independent two-year or four-year institution of higher education
Must partner with a local education agency
Must select required funded activities
Must include a completed and signed Cooperative Agreement by the submission deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application from the GEAR UP webpage at mhec.maryland.gov/institutions_training/Pages/GEARUP.aspx. Submit both electronic and hard copies of the proposal to Kendall E. Cook at the Maryland Higher Education Commission by the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that provides financial aid to students who participated in GEAR UP activities at designated sites in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties during the grant period (2014-2020) and are now pursuing undergraduate education at accredited institutions. Awards are made after federal Pell Grants, state aid, and other public or private aid (excluding loans and work-study) have been applied.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards up to $15,000 for fall and spring semesters of the 2023-2024 academic year and up to $10,000 for summer 2023. Award amounts vary based on student financial need and cannot exceed the cost of attendance. Awards are made after federal Pell Grant, state aid, and other public or private aid (excluding loans and work-study) have been applied. Processing and disbursement occur after the drop/add period at the institution.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FAFSA must be filed before March 1 each year; GEAR UP Scholarship Application due July 1, 2023 for Summer 2023; Fall 2023/Spring 2024 application deadline not specified
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland high school graduates who participated in GEAR UP activities at designated GEAR UP sites in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties during the grant period (2014-2020) and are pursuing undergraduate education at accredited institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Undergraduate education expenses at accredited two- or four-year institutions of higher education, private career schools, or state/regional accredited trade schools/certificate programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents according to their institution's state residency policy and must have participated in GEAR UP activities at GEAR UP sites specifically located in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties during the grant period (2014-2020).
requirements_list: Participated in GEAR UP activities at GEAR UP sites in Baltimore City, Dorchester, or Wicomico Counties during the grant period (2014-2020)
Maryland resident according to the institution's state residency policy

Enrolled or accepted for enrollment in a program of undergraduate instruction at an accredited two- or four-year institution of higher education, private career school, or state/regional accredited trade school/certificate program
High school diploma or recognized equivalent
Less than 22 years old at the time of first scholarship award
Maintain satisfactory academic progress in accordance with the standards of the institution
Completed FAFSA before March 1 each year
Completed GEAR UP Scholarship Application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at www.fafsa.gov before March 1 each year. Complete and submit the GEAR UP Scholarship Application, available online as a Google Form. Applications are processed and verified following the drop/add period at the institution. Awards are made after the drop/add period. Eligible students are notified via the email address listed on their application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Governor's Emergency Education Relief (GEER) Fund for Maryland Community Colleges
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program providing emergency assistance to educational entities impacted by COVID-19. In Maryland, $10 million of GEER funding was allocated to the state's 16 community colleges to expand workforce development programs and continuing professional education leading to government or industry certification or licensure, with particular focus on individuals who lost employment due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission's Office of Grants Management, grant awards to individual institutions ranged from $250,000 to $1,480,602.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $10,000,000 total in federal grant funds distributed to Maryland's 16 community colleges for workforce development and professional education courses. Grant awards varied by institution, ranging from $250,000 to $1,480,602. Funds may be used for direct aid to students, materials and supplies, equipment, curriculum development, salaries and wages, professional development and technical training, student recruitment and marketing, technology training, and certification examination and licensure fees or vouchers for programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland community colleges and their students, particularly individuals impacted by COVID-19 job loss, seeking workforce development and continuing professional education leading to government or industry certification or licensure.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry certification or licensure; direct aid to students; materials, supplies, and equipment; curriculum development; salaries and wages; professional development and technical training; student recruitment, marketing, and advertising; technology training; certification examination and licensure fees or vouchers for programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — distributed among all 16 Maryland community colleges serving all counties.
requirements_list: Community college status
Focus on workforce development courses and continuing professional education
Courses must lead to government or industry certification or licensure
Particular focus on individuals impacted by COVID-19 through loss of employment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications processed through the Maryland Higher Education Commission's Office of Grants Management. Specific application procedures are not detailed on the program page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Governor's Emergency Education Relief Fund II (GEER II)
structured_extraction.program_description: A supplemental grant program funded through the U.S. Department of Education to provide emergency assistance to local education agencies, institutions of higher education, and other educational entities affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. In Maryland, funds support community colleges and private nonprofit colleges and universities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Governor Hogan allocated $10 million total from the GEER II Fund to Maryland higher education institutions. Community colleges received $7.4 million to provide workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry-required certification or licensure, particularly for individuals impacted by COVID-19 through job loss. Private nonprofit colleges and universities received $2.6 million to support institutional costs resulting from COVID-19. Specific grant amounts were distributed to individual institutions as listed in the program tables.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community colleges, private nonprofit colleges and universities, and other educational entities in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Workforce development courses and continuing professional education leading to government or industry-required certification or licensure; institutional costs resulting from COVID-19
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: Scholarship and living expense grants for graduate nursing faculty students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarships and living expense grants for graduate nursing faculty with separate deadlines for each semester.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education and living expenses
requirements_list: Be a graduate nursing faculty student

structured_extraction.program_description: The Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program, administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC), provides financial assistance to degree-seeking graduate and professional students who are Maryland residents enrolled in eligible programs at designated Maryland institutions. Eligible fields of study include dentistry, law, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, social work, and veterinary medicine. Awards are merit-based and ranked according to demonstrated financial need as shown on the FAFSA. Funds may not be available for all eligible students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards ranging from a minimum of $1,000 per year to a maximum of $5,000 per year. Students may receive awards for a maximum of eight semesters (four years) provided they maintain enrollment in an eligible program, meet satisfactory academic progress standards set by their institution, file a FAFSA each year, and continue to demonstrate financial need. Awards are ranked based on demonstrated financial need as shown on the FAFSA. Funds may not be available for all eligible students.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Contact the financial aid office of the school you will attend for their deadlines; deadline is determined by each individual institution
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident degree-seeking graduate and professional students demonstrating financial need, enrolled part-time or full-time in eligible programs at designated institutions including: University of Maryland, Baltimore (UMB) Schools of Medicine, Dentistry, Law, Pharmacy, or Social Work; University of Baltimore School of Law; The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine; The Virginia-Maryland Regional College of Veterinary Medicine; or certain Maryland institutions offering a master's degree in nursing or social work or a first professional degree in pharmacy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial assistance for educational expenses for eligible degree-seeking graduate and professional programs in dentistry, law, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, social work, and veterinary medicine.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents. Students must attend one of the following eligible institutions: University of Maryland, Baltimore (UMB) Schools of Medicine, Dentistry, Law, Pharmacy, or Social Work; University of Baltimore School of Law; The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine; The Virginia-Maryland Regional College of Veterinary Medicine; or certain Maryland institutions offering a master's degree in nursing or social work or a first professional degree in pharmacy.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must demonstrate financial need as shown on the FAFSA
Must be enrolled as a degree-seeking student, either part-time or full-time
Must attend one of the eligible institutions listed
Must be enrolled in an eligible program: dentistry, law, medicine, nursing, pharmacy, social work, or veterinary medicine
Must file FAFSA annually
Must maintain satisfactory academic progress standards of the institution
For renewal: must remain enrolled in an eligible program
For renewal: must maintain satisfactory academic progress
For renewal: must file a FAFSA each year
For renewal: must demonstrate continued financial need
May receive awards for a maximum of eight semesters
Application deadline is determined by each individual institution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and file the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at studentaid.gov. Contact the financial aid office of the institution you will attend and ask to be considered for a Graduate and Professional Scholarship. The institution determines eligibility for awards and renewals, and applicants are ranked based on financial need as demonstrated on the FAFSA. Contact the financial aid office of your school for their specific application deadlines.

structured_extraction.program_name: Howard P. Rawlings Campus-Based Educational Assistance Grant (CBEAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A need-based financial aid program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that provides grants to full-time undergraduate students who were not considered for the Howard P. Rawlings Educational Assistance Grant because they did not file the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) or Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) by the Maryland state deadline of March 1st. The program is state-funded and allocates money to participating two-year and four-year Maryland colleges and universities each academic year, which then select and award qualified students from their allocated CBEAG funds. Awards are offered at the discretion of the institution for students who file FAFSA on or after March 1st.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students attending four-year institutions receive a grant equal to 40% of OSFA adjusted financial need. Students attending community colleges receive a grant equal to 60% of OSFA adjusted financial need. The minimum annual award is $400 and the maximum award is $3,000. Award amounts may be less than the minimum if funds are exhausted. The total dollar amount of all state awards may not exceed the student's cost of attendance as determined by the institution or $28,000, whichever is less. Award amounts and terms are ultimately determined by the institution.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FAFSA or MSFAA filed March 1 or later (offered at school's discretion)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time degree-seeking undergraduate students who are Maryland residents (and whose parents are Maryland residents if the student is a dependent), attend two-year or four-year Maryland colleges or universities, and who filed the FAFSA or MSFAA after the March 1st state deadline and were therefore not considered for the Howard P. Rawlings Educational Assistance Grant.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Need-based financial aid for undergraduate education expenses, including cost of attendance as defined by the student's college or university financial aid office.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants and their parents (if dependent) must be Maryland residents. Students must enroll at a two-year or four-year Maryland college or university.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident (and parents must be Maryland residents if the applicant is a dependent student)
Must enroll at a two-year or four-year Maryland college or university
Must be a full-time (12 or more credits per semester) degree-seeking undergraduate student
Must have filed the FAFSA or MSFAA after the March 1st state deadline
Must be eligible to receive the federal Pell Grant
Audited courses cannot be used to reach the minimum credit hours required for full-time status
Total of all state awards cannot exceed the cost of attendance as determined by the school or $28,000, whichever is less
Cannot hold the award concurrently with the Guaranteed Access Grant, Part-Time Grant, or Educational Assistance Grant
Must be qualified for CBEAG award as determined by the participating institution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must contact their college or university's financial aid office to apply. Each institution's financial aid office selects and awards qualified students from the CBEAG allocation provided to that institution. Schools review FAFSA applications dated March 1 or later and award grants at their discretion.

structured_extraction.program_name: Howard P. Rawlings Educational Excellence Awards (EEA) Program – Educational Assistance (EA) Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's largest need-based financial assistance program, administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission, that provides scholarships and grants to help students attend Maryland postsecondary institutions. The program is comprised of two components: the Educational Assistance (EA) Grant, which provides need-based awards of up to $3,000 annually for up to four years to eligible full-time undergraduate students; and the Guaranteed Access (GA) Grant, which covers 100% of demonstrated financial need with a maximum award of up to $20,200 annually. For the 2023-2024 academic year, more than 43,000 students received awards totaling over $100 million. The program is designed to reduce student debt and help students with the greatest financial need afford postsecondary education in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Educational Assistance (EA) Grant provides need-based awards with a maximum annual award of $3,000 and a minimum annual award of $400. Award amounts are calculated based on the cost of attendance at the institution, the student's living situation (on campus, off campus, or with parent), and the amount of financial need as determined by the OSFA-calculated adjusted financial need formula: Cost of Attendance (adjusted by regional cost of living adjustment) minus Student Aid Index minus certain state awards minus federal Pell Grant. Students may receive an award for up to four years for bachelor's degree programs or up to two years for associate degree programs, with renewal for additional years contingent on availability of funds and meeting satisfactory academic progress standards. The Guaranteed Access (GA) Grant covers up to 100% of a student's demonstrated financial need with a maximum award of up to $20,200 annually. Both EA and GA are part of the larger Educational Excellence Awards and students can only receive one or the other, not both. After receiving an EA award, a student cannot be reconsidered for the GA regardless of changes in financial circumstances. Students who have received the award for at least two years must complete 30 credits annually for the full award amount, or 24-29 credits for a prorated award amount, or less than 24 credits results in ineligibility for renewal. All awarding is contingent on availability of funds. For the 2023-2024 academic year, more than 3,600 students received the Guaranteed Access grant and more than 39,600 students received the Educational Assistance grant, with total awards exceeding $100 million.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1, 2026 for FAFSA or MHEC One-App submission; August 1, 2026 for documentation deadline
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Higher Education Commission, Office of Student Financial Aid
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school seniors and full-time degree-seeking undergraduate students (12 credits or more per semester) enrolled at eligible two-year or four-year Maryland postsecondary institutions who are eligible for in-state tuition and demonstrate financial need. U.S. citizens, eligible non-citizens, and undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition may apply. Deaf or hearing-impaired students may use the grant at out-of-state institutions if the institution makes special provisions for deaf and hearing-impaired students not available at Maryland institutions or if the student is enrolled in a program with a reciprocal agreement in the Academic Common Market.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses for postsecondary education, including tuition and fees, to help cover the cost of attendance at Maryland postsecondary institutions and reduce student debt.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to Maryland residents and students eligible for in-state tuition in Maryland. Students must have a Maryland university or college listed on their FAFSA or MHEC One-App by the March 1 deadline. The grant may be used at an out-of-state institution only if the recipient is deaf or hearing-impaired and the institution makes special provisions not available at Maryland institutions, or if the student is enrolled in a program with a reciprocal agreement in the Academic Common Market.
requirements_list: Be eligible for in-state tuition in Maryland, as determined by the institution
File the 2026-2027 FAFSA or MHEC One-App by March 1, 2026
Have a Maryland university or college listed on FAFSA or MHEC One-App by March 1

Demonstrate financial need using the OSFA-calculated adjusted financial need formula (cost of attendance adjusted by regional cost of living adjustment minus Student Aid Index minus certain state awards minus federal Pell Grant)
Be a currently enrolled high school senior OR currently enrolled at an eligible two-year or four-year Maryland institution as a full-time (12 credits/semester) degree-seeking undergraduate student
Cannot have previously received a bachelor's degree prior to the start of the applicable academic year
Submit any required documentation (such as parent signature page, proof of Selective Service registration, or family size verification form) by August 1, 2026 if requested
Cannot be in default on a Federal Title IV student loan
May not use audited courses to reach the minimum credit hours required for full-time status
For renewal: remain eligible for in-state tuition, continue to demonstrate financial need, and maintain satisfactory academic progress standards of the enrolled institution

For renewal after receiving the award for at least two years: complete 30 credits annually for full award amount or 24-29 credits for prorated award amount; completing less than 24 credits results in ineligibility for renewal
Must be continuously enrolled as full-time, degree-seeking undergraduate student to renew (cannot take a break from college)
Must accept award within the allotted timeframe or award will be canceled
Pledge to remain drug free for the full term of the award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students must file a 2026-2027 FAFSA or MHEC One-App by March 1, 2026 through the MHEC One-App system at mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us. There is no separate application for the Educational Assistance Grant; MDCAPS will automatically consider students who meet basic eligibility requirements. Some students may be asked to submit additional documentation (such as a parent signature page, proof of Selective Service registration, or family size verification form) online through their MDCAPS account by August 1, 2026. To accept an award, students must log into MDCAPS, create a user ID and password, and activate their account via email. It is critical to accept or decline the award as soon as notified; if MHEC receives no response within a few weeks, the award offer will be canceled and may not be reinstated. Students will receive email notifications from MDCAPS and can check their application status through their MDCAPS dashboard. Awards are disbursed after the institution certifies the student, usually starting in September for the Fall term and February for the Spring term. After institution certification and payment request, it can take 4-6 weeks for payment to reach the institution. Once the institution receives payment, they have their own internal processes for crediting the award to a student account. Awarding is anticipated to begin in Summer 2026 and will continue until all funds are exhausted. Awards are made in multiple rounds throughout the year, with subsequent rounds announced during summer months.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program that provides funding to Maryland public institutions of higher education and regional higher education centers to support efforts to address food insecurity among students on Maryland campuses. Eligible institutions must be designated as a hunger-free campus and pledge a 25% matching contribution. FY 2026 awards total $150,000, with grants ranging from $10,000 to $22,000 per institution. The grant period runs from October 15, 2025 through June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) awards grant funding to Maryland public institutions of higher education or regional higher education centers that have been designated as a hunger-free campus and pledge a 25% matching contribution. Institutions must provide in-kind or matching funds equal to at least 25% of the total grant funds requested. FY 2026 awards total $150,000. Grant recipients may use funds flexibly to implement program goals, including supporting emergency assistance, hiring staff to manage initiatives, and funding operational activities. The grant period runs from October 15, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Grantees must submit an interim report by March 3, 2026 and a final report by September 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland public institutions of higher education and regional higher education centers designated as hunger-free campuses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports efforts to address food insecurity among students on Maryland campuses through flexible use including: addressing student hunger; leveraging sustainable solutions to meet basic food needs on campus; raising awareness of services offered on campus that address basic food needs; building strategic partnerships at local, state, and national levels to address food insecurity among students; supporting emergency assistance; hiring staff to manage related initiatives; and funding operational activities related to the program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland public institutions of higher education and regional higher education centers statewide. Applicants targeting communities with highest rates of concentrated child poverty in each county, particularly those eligible under the Governor's Office for Children's ENOUGH Grant Program, will receive priority consideration.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland public institution of higher education or regional higher education center

Must be designated as a hunger-free campus meeting specific criteria including having an established hunger task force that meets at least 3 times per academic year and sets at least 2 goals with action plans
Must have a designated staff member responsible for assisting students in enrolling in SNAP or connecting students with available outreach partners
Must have a designated staff member responsible for informing students participating in federal work-study programs that they are eligible for SNAP
Must participate in an awareness day campaign activity and plan at least one campus awareness event during National Hunger and Homelessness Awareness Week
Must provide at least one food pantry on campus or enable students in need to receive food through a separate, stigma-free arrangement
Must provide options for students to utilize SNAP benefits at campus retailers or provide information on off-campus retailers that accept SNAP (for 4-year institutions and regional centers)
Must develop and maintain a meal-sharing program allowing students to donate unused meal plan credits (for 4-year institutions and regional centers)
Must conduct a standardized annual student survey on hunger and submit results to MHEC
Must submit an annual report detailing efforts to address student hunger to MHEC
Must pledge a 25% matching contribution (in-kind or cash) to be used to implement the goals of the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Institutions submit electronic PDF applications to Anthony Reiner at Anthony.Reiner@Maryland.gov by the deadline of October 6, 2025 at 4:00 PM. Applications must include a cover sheet (Appendix A), table of contents, grant narrative (maximum 10 single-spaced pages addressing campus hunger task force, SNAP enrollment efforts, SNAP eligibility notification, SNAP options at campus stores, National Hunger and Homelessness Awareness Week participation, campus food pantry, meal plan donation program, student hunger survey, and needs assessment), budget summary (Appendix B), budget narrative, and statement of assurances (Appendix C). All application components must use the provided forms and be submitted together. MHEC reviews applications and notifies award recipients via email by October 15, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Inmate Training and Job Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program that provides funds to eligible institutions of higher education to deliver educational and vocational training opportunities for inmates incarcerated at Maryland correctional institutions. The program targets inmates in the twelve months before their release from incarceration, with the goal of expanding and improving higher education pathways for incarcerated individuals. Eligible institutions include Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, and University of Maryland Eastern Shore.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grants provided to eligible institutions of higher education to establish pilot programs offering educational and vocational training opportunities for inmates in Maryland correctional institutions during the twelve months before their release. Implementation grants of up to $25,000 are awarded to support a six-month implementation period (August 8, 2025 through February 2026). Continuation grants beyond the implementation period are available on a pro-rata basis according to program enrollment data reported by December 15, 2025. Allowable costs include personnel compensation, mentor stipends, supplies, equipment, consultant and contractual services, and travel expenses directly related to grant activities. Indirect costs up to 8% may be charged. The overall grant period runs from August 8, 2025 through June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible institutions of higher education (Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Eastern Shore) authorized to submit proposals for the Inmate Training and Job Pilot Program to provide training to incarcerated individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funding supports educational and vocational training opportunities for inmates in correctional institutions during the twelve months preceding their release from incarceration. Allowable costs include: compensation of employees for time devoted to grant activities; stipends for mentors; supplies, equipment, and services in support of grant activities; consultants and contracts specifically for the purpose of the grant; travel expenses incurred specifically to carry out grant activities; and indirect costs up to 8%. Unallowable costs include supplanting existing services, capital improvements, and costs incurred prior to grant approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Program serves inmates incarcerated at Maryland correctional institutions including Eastern Correctional Institution (Westover), Jessup Correctional Institution (Jessup), Maryland Correctional Institution–Jessup (Jessup), Maryland Correctional Institution–Women (Jessup), Dorsey Run Correctional Facility (Jessup), Patuxent Institution (Jessup), Baltimore City Correctional Facility (Baltimore), Central Maryland Correctional Facility (Sykesville), Maryland Correctional Institution Hagerstown (Hagerstown), Maryland Correctional Training Center (Hagerstown), Roxbury Correctional Institution (Hagerstown), Western Correctional Institution (Cumberland), and North Branch Correctional Institution (Cumberland). Eligible institutions include Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, and University of Maryland Eastern Shore.
requirements_list: Applicant must be one of the four eligible higher education institutions (Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Eastern Shore)
Training must target inmates in the twelve months before release from Maryland correctional institutions
Proposals must be submitted by July 25, 2025 by 4:00 p.m. in PDF format to Anthony Reiner at Anthony.Reiner@Maryland.gov
Program must provide meaningful, credit-bearing coursework that contributes to graduation requirements or leads to an industry-recognized certificate or license
Program must provide coursework through suitable format (in-person, virtual, hybrid) considering incarceration limitations
Program must provide structured support services including academic counseling, mentoring, tutoring, and support for participants with disabilities
Institutions must develop individualized plans for each participant that identify academic and career goals, degree or credential pathway, required coursework, and support services
Institutions must designate a pilot program director responsible for inmate participation and coursework oversight
Program must identify at least three (3) students serving as mentors (must be 18+ years old, enrolled at institution, in junior or senior year, receive course credit and stipend)
Programs must collect and report programmatic data regularly including participant enrollment, course completion, post-confinement employment, continuing education, and certification/licensure
Post-confinement data must be collected for two (2) years following participant release
Implementation proposals must have goals, objectives, and outcomes for the six-month implementation period
Continuation grants require successful enrollment of participants by December 15, 2025 to qualify for continued funding beyond implementation period
Budget must be reasonable, allowable, allocable, and necessary; costs deemed excessive will be removed and budget adjusted
Indirect costs cannot exceed 8% of total direct costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible institutions must submit complete proposals by July 25, 2025 at 4:00 p.m. Proposals must be submitted in PDF format to Anthony Reiner at Anthony.Reiner@Maryland.gov. An abstract must be submitted as a separate Microsoft Word document. Initial Review: Proposals are reviewed for formatting and completeness; incorrectly formatted or incomplete proposals may be rejected, with opportunity to correct non-material issues. Review Panel Evaluation: A review panel with expertise in higher education, labor and workforce development, and criminal justice evaluates proposals according to specified criteria (Proposal Narrative 70%, Budget and Budget Narrative 20%, Overall Approach and Feasibility 10%) and individually awards points. Collective Review: The panel meets to discuss each proposal and requests for additional information or programmatic changes, and makes funding recommendations. Request for Additional Information: Applicants are notified of any requests for additional information or programmatic changes. Funding Recommendation Approval: Panel recommendations are submitted to the Secretary of Higher Education (or designee) for final approval. Grant Award: Award letters and notices of grant awards are issued for funded proposals. Award notifications will be issued by email prior to midnight on August 8, 2025. The grant period begins August 8, 2025. Interim reports are due December 15, 2025, and final reports are due September 30, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Jack F. Tolbert Memorial Student Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Jack F. Tolbert Memorial Student Grant Program provides financial assistance to full-time students attending approved private career schools in Maryland. Administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission, the program awards up to $500 per academic year to eligible Maryland resident students enrolled at least 18 clock hours per week. The award may be renewed one time if the student continues to meet enrollment and residency requirements. Funds may not be available to award all eligible students, and awards are made by the schools on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The award amount of a Tolbert Grant may be up to $500 per academic year. Funds may not be available to award all eligible students. The award may be renewed one time if the applicant continues enrollment at an approved Maryland private career school, maintains enrollment of at least 18 clock hours per week, and files the FAFSA. Awards are made by the schools independently on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 15, 2026 for the 2025-2026 academic year; FAFSA by March 1 preferred; rolling deadline applies
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time students attending approved private career schools in Maryland who are Maryland residents, or dependent students whose parent is a Maryland resident, enrolled for at least 18 clock hours per week in any major.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial assistance for tuition and education expenses at approved private career schools in Maryland. All majors are eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents only. If the applicant is a dependent student, the parent must also be a Maryland resident. Students must be attending approved private career schools in Maryland.
requirements_list: Enrolled at an approved Maryland private career school
Enrolled for at least 18 clock hours per week
Must be a Maryland resident, or if a dependent student, the parent must be a Maryland resident
Must complete and file the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA); FAFSA by March 1 preferred
Must submit an application for the Tolbert Grant Program at the financial aid office of the private career school
For renewal: continue enrollment at an approved Maryland private career school, maintain at least 18 clock hours per week, and file the FAFSA
Contact institution for Tolbert Grant application information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply at the financial aid office of their private career school. Complete and file the FAFSA (by March 1 if possible) and submit an application for the Tolbert Grant Program at the school's financial aid office. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Schools determine eligibility and make awards independently.

structured_extraction.program_name: Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP) attracts qualified individuals to fields of employment in government and the nonprofit sector, particularly those with critical manpower shortages in the state and lower salaries than in the private sector, by providing state assistance in the repayment of educational loans. The program specifically serves individuals working in eligible public service fields who serve Maryland's low-income or underserved residents, including teachers, nurses, school nurses, mental health professionals, lawyers, social workers, speech pathologists, physical and occupational therapists, licensed clinical counselors, veterinary practitioners and technicians, and other specified professions. Annual loan repayment assistance is provided based on total educational debt, with recipients locked into a three-year award tier with guaranteed eligibility for renewal each year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides annual loan repayment assistance based on total educational debt. Recipients are locked into a three-year award tier with guaranteed eligibility for renewal each year. Awards are paid in one lump sum via check issued to the recipient's home address. Annual payments range from $1,500 to $10,000 depending on total debt tier: $15,000 or below receives $1,500 annually; $15,001–$40,000 receives $3,000 annually; $40,001–$75,000 receives $6,000 annually; $75,001 and over receives $10,000 annually (up to $30,000 overall limit). Recipients must deposit the check and make payment to their lender within 120 days, then submit proof of payment. Payments continue as long as recipients remain eligible and submit required documentation by the annual deadline. Renewal recipients are prioritized, followed by priority applicants, then non-priority applicants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 15, 2026 (2025-2026 award year); October 15, 2026 (2026-2027 award year). Applications open September 17, 2025 for 2025-2026 and January 15, 2026 for 2026-2027.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals employed full-time in Maryland in eligible public service fields including teachers (all subject areas, including those in Title I schools), nurses, nurse faculty, school nurses, mental health professionals (public school employees providing school mental health services), lawyers (providing legal services to low-income residents), social workers, speech pathologists, physical and occupational therapists, licensed clinical counselors (in high-need geographic areas), and veterinary practitioners/technicians who have graduated from Maryland institutions (or possess appropriate state certification) and are serving low-income or underserved residents in government and nonprofit sectors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational loan repayment assistance for borrowers employed in eligible public service fields in government and nonprofit sectors serving low-income or underserved populations in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be employed full-time in the state of Maryland. Maryland residents and individuals serving in Maryland are eligible. Licensed clinical counselors must work in a high-need geographic area of the state.
requirements_list: Must work in a listed eligible field (critical profession)
Must have graduated from a Maryland institution (except lawyers; teachers who have not graduated from a Maryland institution must have a resident teacher certificate from MSDE)
Must be employed full-time in the state of Maryland in government, local government, or nonprofit organization
Loans cannot be Parent Plus loans and cannot be in default; all qualified educational student loans (including consolidated loans and loans in deferment/grace status) may be included

Income limits apply: Single applicants cannot exceed $75,000 (or $100,000 for nurse faculty); married applicants cannot exceed $150,000 (or $185,000 for nurse faculty); if married and both salaries count, individual salary cannot exceed single limit and combined cannot exceed married limit

For veterinary practitioners: must have provided services as state employee for at least 5 years OR volunteered minimum 100 hours per year for 3+ years at eligible animal shelter; for veterinary technicians: same requirements apply

Nancy Grasmick Teacher applicants must teach in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Math subjects OR teach in school where at least 75% of students are in free meal program for 2 years, AND have received highest performance evaluation rating for most recent year
Nancy Grasmick School Nurse applicants must be licensed registered nurse in public school, employed by county school system or local health department for school health services for at least 2 years

Nancy Grasmick Mental Health Professional applicants must be public school employee certificated under Title 6, Subtitle 4 of Education Article, employed in local school system providing mental health services, and worked in Maryland for past 2 years
Urban Teacher Center (UTC) applicants must be in 2nd year of program and possess Maryland Resident-Teaching Certificate; UTC applicants are not eligible for lock-in award
Must not have outstanding state service obligations from other Maryland scholarships at time of application; prior obligations must be completed before application year
Janet L. Hoffman LARP application must be completed through MDCAPS and all required documentation must be submitted by applicable deadline

Required documentation includes: signed Maryland state income tax return (or federal if Maryland not filed, or IRS non-filing letter); lender verification form showing all educational loans; employment verification form; address verification documentation (driver's license, MVA change of address, or residential lease); institutional certification form or college transcript; W-9 form
Mid-Year Employment Verification must be completed within 21 days of award notification or award will be cancelled
Must accept award online through MDCAPS by deadline specified in award notification or award will be forfeited
Must submit proof of payment to lender within 120 days of receiving award check
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us. For 2025-2026 award year, applications open September 17, 2025 and are due by March 15, 2026 (postmarked by March 15 accepted as on-time). For 2026-2027 award year, applications open January 15, 2026 and are due by October 15, 2026. Upon submission, applicants receive a task list checklist of required documents. All required documents must be submitted via Secure Upload through MDCAPS (faxed or emailed documents not accepted). Documents include signed state/federal income tax return, lender verification, employment verification, address verification, and institutional certification/transcript. Applications are grouped by employment field and within each field by renewal status (renewals awarded first, then priority applicants, then non-priority). If awarded, applicant receives email notification and must accept award online through MDCAPS by specified deadline. Mid-Year Employment Verification must be completed within 21 days of award. Upon employment verification, award check is issued to recipient's home address. Recipient must deposit check and pay lender within 120 days, then submit proof of payment to lender. Final employment verification is completed after June 30 to verify service obligation completion. New applicants and required documentation are due by deadline noted above; current recipients seeking renewal must submit renewal documentation and verification forms by same deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship Program provides financial assistance to eligible children and surviving spouses of school employees who either died or sustained an injury that rendered the school employee 100 percent disabled, as a victim in an act of violence occurring in the line of duty. Administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission, the program offers renewable scholarships to support postsecondary educational expenses at eligible institutions statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides renewable scholarships that may be used for tuition and mandatory fees at any eligible Maryland postsecondary institution. Awards cannot exceed the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate at the highest-cost four-year public institution in the University System of Maryland (excluding University of Maryland University College and University of Maryland, Baltimore). The minimum award is the lesser of $3,000 or the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees at the recipient's institution. For the 2025-2026 academic year, the maximum award is $13,689. For the 2026-2027 academic year, the maximum award is $14,086. Awards are automatically renewed annually for eligible students. Students may hold awards for up to five years of full-time study (12 or more credits per semester) or eight years of part-time study (6-11 credits per semester), or a combination of both. Awards are not guaranteed and are subject to the availability of funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 15 of each year; July 15, 2025 for the 2025-2026 academic year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible children and surviving spouses of school employees who died in the line of duty or sustained an injury in the line of duty that rendered the school employee 100 percent disabled as a result of an act of violence. Applicants must be at least 16 years old, Maryland residents, and enrolled full-time or part-time in eligible educational programs at Maryland postsecondary institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees for undergraduate, graduate, or professional programs; 2-year terminal certificate programs with coursework acceptable for transfer credit at an accredited baccalaureate program; or private career school enrollment at eligible institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents at the time of application. Maryland residents, and if a dependent, parents must also be Maryland residents. Eligible children and surviving spouses of school employees are not required to be Maryland residents at the time of application or at the time of the disabling or fatal event.
requirements_list: Must be the son, daughter, stepchild, or surviving spouse (who has not remarried) of a school employee who either died in the line of duty or sustained an injury in the line of duty that rendered the school employee 100 percent disabled as a result of an act of violence
Must be at least 16 years old
Must be a Maryland resident at the time of application (exceptions apply for certain eligible applicants)

Must be enrolled full-time (12 or more credits per semester) or part-time (6-11 credits per semester) in a regular undergraduate program, OR enrolled full-time (9 or more credits per semester) or part-time (6-8 credits per semester) in a graduate or professional program, OR enrolled in a 2-year terminal certificate program with coursework acceptable for transfer credit at an accredited baccalaureate program, OR enrolled in a private career school at an eligible Maryland postsecondary institution
Awards are subject to the availability of funds
If total financial assistance exceeds cost of attendance, award may be reduced or cancelled
As a condition of receiving the award, pledge to remain drug-free for the full term of the award
Renewal awards are not automatic; recipients must continue to meet all eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New and renewal applicants should contact their institution's financial aid office for application instructions and to submit applications. The application and processes are conducted by the student's institution. Students should not submit applications or supplemental documentation directly to the Maryland Higher Education Commission. Applicants must submit all required documentation to their institution's financial aid office by July 15 of each year for the upcoming academic year. New applications and all required documents must be received by the institution no later than the deadline. The institution's financial aid office will award all eligible students, and the institution is then reimbursed by the state for funds expended. Renewal awardees are not required to reapply each year; however, institutions will notify eligible students of renewal status. To find out the status of your application or award, contact your institution's financial aid department.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state financial aid scholarship available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8. The program provides financial aid to eligible students attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions, with awarding occurring in the summer and eligible applicants notified by email.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State financial aid scholarship for qualified children of undocumented immigrants attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions. Eligible programs include: Educational Assistance Grant, Guaranteed Access Grant, Campus-Based Educational Assistance Grant, Part Time Grant, Delegate Scholarship, Senatorial Scholarship, Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship, and Richard W. Collins III Leadership with Honor Scholarship. Undocumented students may also apply for the Cybersecurity Public Service Scholarship Program. Awarding occurs in the summer and eligible applicants are notified by email. Students must accept their award online through the MDCAPS portal within 2 weeks of notification or the award will be canceled.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by program; March 1 deadline for Educational Assistance Grant and Guaranteed Access Grant programs; varies for other state financial aid programs
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified children of undocumented immigrants who meet the non-resident exemption requirements under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8, are eligible for in-state tuition, and attend eligible Maryland public or private institutions. Students must be ineligible to receive federal aid through the FAFSA.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses at eligible Maryland public or private institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified child of undocumented immigrants
Must meet in-state tuition eligibility requirements (non-resident exemption) under §15–106.8 of the MD Education Article
Must attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution
Must be ineligible to receive federal aid using the FAFSA
Must file taxes using prior-prior-year tax information (e.g., 2021 tax information for 2023-24 award year)
Males aged 18–25 must register with the Selective Service System and provide proof of registration
If dependent, must provide parental information and have one parent sign the application
Must apply through the MHEC One App in the Maryland College Aid Processing (MDCAPS) portal
Must complete the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) Eligibility Wizard to confirm eligibility
Dependent students must submit a signed Parent Signature Page for the application to be considered valid
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the MSFAA Eligibility Wizard through the Maryland College Aid Processing (MDCAPS) portal to confirm eligibility. Create an MDCAPS account by visiting https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us and clicking 'Create a Student Login'. Answer questions to determine eligibility (U.S. citizenship status, SSN/ITIN availability, Maryland tax filing history, FAFSA completion). If eligible, complete the full Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) including: student demographic data, income and tax data from two prior years, dependency status questions, household information, school selection (up to 10 institutions), and agree to terms and conditions. Submit the application by the established deadline for the specific grant or scholarship program. Dependent students must download and submit a signed Parent Signature Page from the Confirmation Page. After submission, the Office of Student Financial Assistance (OSFA) reviews the application and contacts applicants via email for any additional documentation required. Awarding occurs in the summer and eligible applicants are notified by email. Students must accept or decline their award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks of notification or the award will be canceled.

structured_extraction.program_name: MHEC One App for Undocumented Students
structured_extraction.program_description: An application system that allows qualified children of undocumented immigrants to apply for various Maryland State financial aid grants and scholarships. Eligible applicants complete the application through the Maryland College Aid Processing Portal (MDCAPS). The Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) is available online to applicants who are ineligible to receive federal aid using the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified children of undocumented immigrants who meet the non-resident exemption requirements under Maryland Education Article §15-106.8 can apply for various state financial aid grants and scholarships including: Educational Assistance Grant, Guaranteed Access Grant, Campus Based Educational Assistance Grant, Part Time Grant, Delegate Scholarship, Senatorial Scholarship, Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship, Near Completer Grant, Cybersecurity Public Service Scholarship Award, and Richard W. Collins III Leadership with Honor Scholarship. Applicants may also apply for the Cybersecurity Public Service Scholarship Program by completing that specific application separately. Applicants must attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution. The personally identifiable information provided on the MSFAA is confidential and used solely to determine eligibility for state financial aid.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Deadlines vary by specific scholarship or grant program. For example, the Educational Assistance Grant and Guaranteed Access Grant require completion by March 1, while the Campus Based Educational Assistance Grant application can be completed after March 1. See MHEC website at https://mhec.state.md.us/preparing/Pages/FinancialAid/descriptions.aspx for individual program deadlines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15-106.8 and attend eligible Maryland public or private institutions. Undocumented students, including DACA students, who are ineligible for federal financial aid may use this application.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State financial aid grants and scholarships for college attendance at eligible Maryland public or private institutions
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution
requirements_list: Applicant must be a qualified child of undocumented immigrants
Applicant must meet the non-resident exemption requirements under §15-106.8 of the MD Education Article
Applicant must attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution

Applicant or parent/legal guardian must have filed a Maryland income tax return each year for 3 years while applicant attended a public or nonpublic secondary school in Maryland, and for each year between secondary school graduation and community college registration, OR filed a Maryland income tax return each year while enrolled at a community college in the State and for each year between graduation or achievement of 60 credits and registration at a public senior higher education institution
Prior-prior-year tax filing information is required (for example, 2021 tax information for the 2023-2024 cycle); must provide bank statements, W-2 or pay stub and/or federal income tax return
Male applicants between ages 18 and 25 must register with Selective Service System and provide proof of registration
Dependent students under age 24 must provide parental information and have one parent sign the Parent Signature Page
Social Security Number is not required but applicant must meet non-resident exemption requirements; applicants without SSN or ITIN may enter zeroes
U.S. Citizens or eligible non-citizens with an Alien Registration number should complete the FAFSA instead
International students studying in the U.S. on a student visa are NOT eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Create an MDCAPS account at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us by entering demographic information, email address, and creating a username and password. Undocumented students without a Social Security Number should enter zeroes. Activate the account via email link. 2. Complete the MSFAA Eligibility Wizard to confirm the MSFAA is the correct application by answering questions about citizenship status, SSN/ITIN, Maryland tax return filing history, and FAFSA completion. 3. Complete the MSFAA application by gathering required documents (prior-prior-year tax returns, income information, bank statements, SSN or ITIN if available, and parent information if dependent). Enter demographic data, student income and tax data, dependency information, household information, and parent information (if dependent). Add up to 10 institutions you plan to attend. 4. Review and agree to terms and conditions, then submit the application. 5. Download and obtain parent signature on the Parent Signature Page if classified as a dependent student; failure to submit this page will disqualify applicant from consideration. 6. MHEC will review the application and notify applicants by email if additional documentation is required. After submission, applicants can check application status through MDCAPS and view outstanding tasks. For the state's largest need-based aid programs (Educational Assistance Grant and Guaranteed Access Grant), notification of awards occurs by late April, with other awards notified in summer. Applicants must accept their award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks of notification or the award will be canceled.

structured_extraction.program_description: A last-dollar scholarship administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that covers any remaining tuition and mandatory fee expenses after federal or state financial aid has been applied for eligible students enrolling at Maryland community colleges. Students can receive up to $5,000 per academic year to help pay for community college education. The scholarship is available to Maryland high school graduates or GED recipients eligible for in-state tuition who enroll full-time or part-time in credit-bearing vocational certificates, certificates, associate degree programs, sequences of credit or non-credit courses leading to licensure or certification, or registered apprenticeship programs. The program also serves qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15-106.8 and attend Maryland community colleges.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A last-dollar scholarship providing up to $5,000 per academic year (or actual tuition and mandatory fees after federal and state financial aid, whichever is less) to cover remaining tuition and mandatory fee expenses at Maryland community colleges after federal or state financial aid has been applied. The minimum award is $100 annually ($50 per semester). Funds are awarded directly to the institution. The scholarship is available for credit-bearing vocational certificates, certificates, associate degree programs, sequences of credit or non-credit courses leading to licensure or certification, or registered apprenticeship programs. Renewal recipients must continue to meet income requirements, maintain a 2.5 cumulative community college GPA if in a credit-bearing program, and make satisfactory academic progress. Awards are contingent upon available State funding. Renewal applicants are prioritized over initial applicants; initial applicants are prioritized based upon greatest demonstrated need. Payment to the institution occurs approximately four weeks after the institution certifies at the beginning of each semester that the recipient meets award requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1, 2026 for academic year 2025-2026 (FAFSA or MHEC One App and all required documentation); rolling deadline for Continuing Education applicants each academic year (2023-2024 academic year deadline by September 15, 2023)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland high school graduates or GED recipients who are eligible for in-state tuition and planning to enroll or currently enrolled full-time or part-time at a Maryland community college, as well as qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15-106.8 and attend Maryland community colleges. Also serves continuing education applicants enrolling in sequences of credit or non-credit courses leading to licensure or certification or registered apprenticeship programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To cover remaining tuition and mandatory fee expenses after federal or state financial aid has been applied, for credit-bearing vocational certificates, certificates, associate degree programs, sequences of credit or non-credit courses leading to licensure or certification, or registered apprenticeship programs at Maryland community colleges. Does not cover other costs such as books, room, and board.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties. Students must attend the community college located in their county or region of residence. Regional community colleges include Wor-Wic Community College, Chesapeake College, and College of Southern Maryland. If the local community college does not offer the student's chosen program, they may attend any other Maryland community college that offers it. Students may also use the scholarship to attend a community college with on-campus residential facilities.
requirements_list: Maryland high school graduate or GED recipient (with no minimum passing score required)
Eligible for in-state tuition as determined by the community college in accordance with Title 15 of the Education Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland
Planning to enroll or currently enrolled full-time or part-time at a Maryland community college

Enroll in a credit-bearing vocational certificate, certificate, or associate degree program; OR a sequence of credit or non-credit courses leading to licensure or certification; OR a registered apprenticeship program
High school seniors must have earned an unweighted cumulative 2.3 GPA at the end of first semester of senior year or by end of senior year
Community college applicants must document cumulative GPA of at least 2.5 from previous or current community college enrollment, OR high school unweighted cumulative GPA of at least 2.3
GED applicants must submit a copy of their examination
Applicants who graduated from high school five or more years before applying are exempt from submitting a high school transcript to document GPA requirement
Homeschool applicants must provide documentation confirming earned unweighted cumulative high school GPA of at least 2.3

Adjusted gross income not exceeding $100,000 for single applicants or single-parent households, or $150,000 for married applicants or two-parent households (based on 2021 tax year for 2023-2024 academic year)
Submit FAFSA or MSFAA by April 1 (or April 15 as stated in some materials) annually
Submit required documentation to institution by established deadline
Applicants enrolled in credit-bearing programs must enroll in at least 6 credits per semester
For non-credit continuing education applicants: must enroll in at least two courses per term of their sequence
Maintain at least 2.5 cumulative community college GPA if enrolled in credit-bearing program
Make satisfactory academic progress toward degree or certificate
Continue to meet adjusted gross income requirements annually
For continuing education applicants: must pass all courses taken in each term and enroll in next available courses offered at the community college for the sequence
For non-credit continuing education applicants: complete the Promise Non-Credit Application through MDCAPS
Qualified children of undocumented immigrants must meet non-resident exemption requirements under §15-106.8 of the MD Education Article
Male applicants aged 18-25 must register with the Selective Service System and provide proof of registration
If dependent, must provide parental information and have one parent sign the application
Must file taxes using prior-prior-year tax information (for MHEC One App applicants)
May not have earned a bachelor's degree or an associate degree
May not have received other educational grants or scholarships that cover full cost of attendance at community colleges
Remain drug free for the full term of the award (Drug Free Pledge requirement)
Not dually enrolled in high school and community college at time of application (dually enrolled students may apply after high school graduation)
If selected for FAFSA Verification, must complete verification with financial aid office
Must accept award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks or award will be canceled
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit either the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) or MSFAA (Maryland State Financial Aid Application) by April 1 (or April 15 per FAQ) annually. The MSFAA is for students ineligible to submit FAFSA, including qualified children of undocumented immigrants and those meeting non-resident exemption requirements under §15-106.8 of the MD Education Article. Contact your local community college to verify in-state tuition eligibility and program enrollment. For non-credit continuing education applicants, also complete the Promise Non-Credit Application online through the MDCAPS portal. Submit required documentation directly to your institution (not through MDCAPS), including high school transcript with GPA (official or unofficial), GED examination copy if applicable, income documentation, and proof of Selective Service registration if applicable (males 18-25). High schools may alternatively upload cumulative GPA through MDCAPS GPA Upload tool. The MSFAA and FAFSA open at the same time each year. After submission, applicants are considered for various state financial aid programs. Initial awarding occurs in mid-August to mid-September and eligible applicants are notified by email using the email address on their MDCAPS account. Applicants must accept their award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks or the award will be canceled. Applicants can monitor application status in their MDCAPS account under "Check Application Status." Document drop-off events are held across Maryland; documents may also be submitted by mail or in-person drop box delivery. If selected for FAFSA Verification, applicant must complete this with the school financial aid office before being awarded. At the beginning of each semester, the institution certifies that the recipient meets requirements and requests funds; payment is made approximately four weeks after certification.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Dent-Care Loan Assistance Repayment Program (MDC-LARP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A student loan assistance repayment program for dentists and dental hygienists who treat Maryland's most vulnerable populations. The program is designed to increase access to oral health care services for Maryland Medical Assistance Program (MMAP) recipients by increasing the number of dentists and dental hygienists treating this population. Eligible dentists may receive up to $50,000 per year for each year of obligated service for up to 3 years (maximum $150,000), while eligible dental hygienists may receive up to $10,000 per year for up to 2 years (maximum $20,000). Funds are used to assist with repayment of outstanding student loan debt.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible dentists may receive up to $50,000 per year for each year of obligated service for up to a maximum of 3 years of service (total maximum $150,000). Eligible dental hygienists may receive up to $10,000 per year for each year of obligated service for up to a maximum of 2 years of service (total maximum $20,000). Funds are used to assist with repayment of outstanding student loan debt. Repayment amounts and terms are determined by the Maryland Department of Health.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Practicing dentists and dental hygienists in Maryland who treat Maryland Medical Assistance Program (MMAP) recipients, including dental professionals with outstanding educational loans seeking loan repayment assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of outstanding student loan debt incurred for dental or dental hygiene education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be practicing in Maryland and serving Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients in Maryland. Maryland residents and dental professionals serving in Maryland are eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a practicing dentist or dental hygienist in Maryland who graduated from an accredited dental or dental hygiene school in Maryland
Must have a valid unrestricted license to practice dentistry in Maryland
Must be employed full-time or part-time as a dentist or dental hygienist in Maryland providing care to MMAP recipients
Must have at least 30 percent of patient population as MMAP recipients
Must be currently paying off outstanding student loan debt
Cannot be in default on a loan or have an incomplete service obligation
Work in dental care
Contact Maryland Department of Health for application and deadline information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and file an MDC-LARP application available through the Maryland Department of Health. Contact MDH for information regarding required documentation needed to complete an application. Submit all required materials promptly to ensure timely processing. Application deadline is July 31, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland GEAR UP Workforce Employability and Leadership Skills Program (WELSP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program centered on career exploration and educational planning that promotes self-efficacy, supports leadership curricula, connects youth to professional sectors, and builds transferable skills required to secure and sustain employment. The program trains students to understand their core values, sharpen soft skills, set achievable goals, and develop leadership capacities through career and job exploration. It includes in-school soft skill and leadership workshops, career exploration counseling, summer programs, workplace readiness training, and youth employment opportunities, while educating students and families about postsecondary education benefits and college financing options.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $90,000 per institution provided to accredited public or not-for-profit independent two- or four-year institutions of higher education in partnership with local education agencies. Grantees must provide a 25% match contribution (cash and/or in-kind). Grant awards are disbursed in two payments: 50% upon award notification and 50% after the interim report is received and approved. Funds support in-school soft skill and leadership workshops, career exploration counseling, summer programs, workplace readiness training, and youth employment initiatives, as well as educational outreach to students and families about postsecondary education and college financing options.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: November 13, 2020 (FY 2021 cycle); specific deadlines vary by fiscal year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Economically disadvantaged students in Maryland GEAR UP school districts in Baltimore City, Dorchester, and Wicomico counties, served through accredited public or not-for-profit independent two- or four-year institutions of higher education in partnership with local education agencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: In-school soft skill and leadership workshops (communication, collaboration, self-management, advocacy), in-school leadership workshops (cross-cultural leadership, creative innovation and project management, commitment and responsibility), career and job exploration counseling, summer programs with focus on self-discovery and career exploration, STEM experiential learning, branding and entrepreneurship, workplace readiness training, youth employment opportunities and initiatives, and educational materials and outreach to students and families about postsecondary education benefits and college financing options.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program serves Maryland GEAR UP school districts in Baltimore City, Dorchester, and Wicomico counties. Five or more awards are anticipated.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an accredited public or not-for-profit independent two- or four-year institution of higher education (IHE)
Applicant must partner with a local education agency (LEA)
Grantees must provide matching contribution equal to at least 25% of total direct funds requested (cash and/or in-kind contributions)

Two or more of the following activities are required: in-school/virtual soft skills workshops, in-school/virtual leadership workshops, career and job exploration counseling, summer programs, or workplace readiness training and youth employment
Proposals must show evidence of collaborative planning between the primary IHE and the LEA
Indirect costs charged to the grant cannot exceed 8%
Records must be maintained for three years after grant ends
Quarterly Time & Effort reports required to document effort toward meeting GEAR UP matching requirements
All publications and media announcements must acknowledge MHEC support with specific disclaimer language
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Institutions submit proposals to a competitive Request for Proposals (RFP) process, typically issued annually.
