Submission requires an unbound original proposal and five copies to MHEC, electronic copy via email, and abstract as Microsoft Word document. Proposals must include cover sheet, abstract (250 words or less), table of contents, and proposal narrative (maximum 15 pages) covering needs assessment, project objectives and outcomes, management plan, plan of operation, project evaluation, and budget with cost-effectiveness analysis. Proposal narrative is scored on: Needs Assessment (10 points), Project Objectives and Outcomes (15 points), Management Plan (15 points), Plan of Operation (25 points), Project Evaluation (20 points), and Budget and Cost Effectiveness (15 points). Selected grantees receive notice of award and project start date notification.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Higher Education Outreach and College Access Program (MD-HEOCAP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state grant program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that provides funds to eligible nonprofit organizations to increase college and career awareness, promote college access, and support college completion for low-income Maryland high school students through statewide outreach efforts. The program creates matching fund opportunities for nonprofit organizations to expand their outreach efforts and provides funding to established community organizations for targeted outreach to encourage low-income students to enroll in and complete college.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $100,000 are awarded on a competitive basis to eligible 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations for a twelve (12) month grant period (October 16, 2025 through June 30, 2026). Grant funds support statewide outreach efforts that encourage low-income Maryland high school students to attend and complete college. Nonprofits are required to provide one-to-one matching funds equal to the total grant funds requested. For example, if an organization requests $20,000 in grant funds, they must provide $20,000 in matching funds. Eligible costs include personnel, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, supplies, consultant and contractual services, and other justified costs. Indirect costs may not exceed 8% of total direct costs. Grants are disbursed in two payments: 50% upon award (November 2025) and 50% upon receipt and approval of the interim report (March 23, 2026). Selected organizations must submit interim reports (due March 16, 2026) and final reports (due September 30, 2026) documenting their activities and outcomes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations located in Maryland that have been in existence for five or more consecutive years and work with low-income high school students to increase college access and completion.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Outreach activities, college access activities, communication, and services designed to encourage and support low-income Maryland high school students to enroll in and complete college programs. Eligible costs include personnel, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, supplies, consultant and contractual services, and other justified costs directly related to project activities and services. Indirect costs may not exceed 8%.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible organizations must be located in Maryland. Applicants targeting communities with the highest rates of concentrated child poverty in each county will receive priority, including communities eligible under the Governor's Office for Children's Engaging Neighborhoods, Organizations, Unions, Governments and Households (ENOUGH) Grant Program. In counties without eligible ENOUGH communities, applicants may target communities where the rate of child poverty is the highest for that respective county.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Must have been in existence for five or more consecutive years
Must be located in Maryland
Must have established partnerships with a local school system and/or higher education institution
Must provide college access activities, communication, and services with a proven track record of success
Must offer services to enhance and increase college access and completion for low-income Maryland high school students
Must provide one-to-one matching funds equal to the total grant funds requested

Must address mandated project goals: Goal 1 - Students will demonstrate greater awareness of postsecondary opportunities and college admission requirements through surveys and/or pre- and post-assessments; Goal 2 - Students will demonstrate greater awareness of the FAFSA and financial aid through surveys and/or pre- and post-assessments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit grant applications in response to the Request for Proposals (RFP) process. Proposals must be submitted electronically in PDF format to Anthony Reiner at Anthony.Reiner@Maryland.gov by 4:00 PM on October 6, 2025, with a copy of the abstract submitted as a Microsoft Word document. The review process includes: (1) Initial Review for formatting and completeness, with opportunity to correct non-material issues; (2) Review Panel Evaluation where panel members score proposals according to established criteria; (3) Request for Additional Information/Project Changes as needed; (4) Funding Recommendation Approval by the Secretary of Higher Education; and (5) Grant Award notification. Award notifications are issued via email by October 15, 2025. Selected organizations carry out their projects during the grant period (October 16, 2025 through June 30, 2026) and submit an interim report by March 16, 2026 and a final report by September 30, 2026 documenting their activities and outcomes. Proposals must not exceed 15 single-spaced pages (excluding cover sheet, abstract, budget, assurances, résumés, and appendices) and must include: cover sheet, abstract, table of contents, proposal narrative addressing needs assessment, organizational capacity, project goals/objectives/outcomes, operations plan, management plan, and project evaluation, budget summary, budget narrative, and statement of assurances.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland John R. Justice Grant Student Loan Repayment Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal funded program that provides loan repayment assistance for state and federal Maryland public defenders and prosecutors. Recipients must agree to remain employed as public defenders or prosecutors for a minimum of three years and sign a service obligation agreement. If the recipient fails to fulfill the three-year service obligation, they must repay the full grant award.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides loan repayment assistance to help eligible prosecutors and public defenders pay down outstanding balances on qualified education loans, including Federal Stafford loans, Graduate PLUS loans, Federal Family Education Loan Program (FFELP) loans, Federal Perkins loans, William D. Ford Federal Direct Loans, and Federal Direct Consolidation loans. The annual allocation of program funds is equally distributed between prosecutors and public defenders, with each appellate court district receiving an equal share of funds. Recipients are ranked by their loan debt to adjusted gross income (AGI) ratio within their appellate court district, with cost of living factors applied for applicants with identical ratios. Annual repayment benefits cannot exceed $10,000 per calendar year with an aggregate maximum of $60,000. Repayment amounts are subject to federal and state tax regulations and are taxable income to the recipient. Recipients must commit to a three-year service obligation as a condition of receiving the grant. Applicants who fail to fulfill the three-year service obligation must repay the full grant award. Awards are subject to the availability of funding and U.S. Department of Justice approval of the signed service obligation agreement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland state and federal public defenders and prosecutors who are licensed attorneys employed full-time as employees of the state of Maryland, units of local government (including tribal government) who provide legal representation to indigent persons in criminal or juvenile delinquency cases, or work for a nonprofit organization under contract providing such representation, or are employed as full-time federal defender attorneys under Section 9(g) of section 3006A of Title 18, United States Code. Note: The 2021-2022 application cycle is specific to Maryland state and federal public defenders; applications are not accepted from state prosecutors during this cycle.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of outstanding balances on qualified education loans, including Federal Stafford loans, Graduate PLUS loans, Federal Family Education Loan Program (FFELP) loans, Federal Perkins loans, William D. Ford Federal Direct Loans, and Federal Direct Consolidation loans. Ineligible loans include loans made to parents of dependent students (Parent PLUS loans) and consolidation loans used to repay parent loans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be employed in Maryland or as federal defenders operating under Section 9(g) of section 3006A of Title 18, United States Code. Applicants are identified and ranked by their county of employment within appellate court districts.
requirements_list: Must be a U.S. Citizen or eligible non-citizen

Must have an outstanding balance due on a qualified education loan (Federal Stafford loans, Graduate PLUS loans, FFELP loans, Federal Perkins loans, William D. Ford Federal Direct Loans, or Federal Direct Consolidation loans)
Must be an attorney continually licensed to practice law in Maryland

Must be a full-time employee of the state of Maryland or unit of local government (including tribal government) who provides legal representation to indigent persons in criminal or juvenile delinquency cases including supervision, education or training of other persons providing such representation, or a full-time employee of a nonprofit organization under contract with the state or unit of local government who devotes substantially all employment to providing such representation, or employed as a full-time federal defender attorney under Section 9(g) of section 3006A of Title 18, United States Code
Must not be in default on a federal guaranteed educational loan
Must not owe a refund on any scholarship or grant program administered by MHEC's Office of Student Financial Assistance
Must sign a three-year service obligation agreement and remain employed for a minimum of three years
Prior-year Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) must equal or be less than $60,000 if single, or $130,000 if married
Must have a minimum of $40,000 total eligible student loan debt (income and loan debt limits may be adjusted if insufficient applicants are received)
Must not receive benefits under another program that provides loan repayment/forgiveness assistance for eligible educational loans (applicants without such benefits receive priority)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a complete application packet postmarked by the deadline to Priscilla Moore at the Maryland Higher Education Commission. Required documents include: (1) completed and signed 2021-2022 John R. Justice Grant Program Application; (2) completed Employment Verification form with employer completion; (3) Lender Verification form for each loan or recent account statements indicating loan type; (4) photocopy of signed 2020 Federal income tax return and 2021 W-2s (or IRS non-filing verification if taxes were not required); (5) Service Agreement (Appendix A for initial applicants, Appendix B for 2nd or 3rd year participants, or Appendix C for those seeking additional benefits after completing initial 3-year obligation). Awardees will be notified by midnight on the specified award date. Recipients are selected based on loan debt to AGI ratio and cost of living factors within appellate court districts. Applicants should contact Priscilla Moore at priscilla.moore@maryland.gov with questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Legislative Scholarships (Delegate Scholarship and Senatorial Scholarship)
structured_extraction.program_description: Scholarships awarded by members of the Maryland General Assembly — both State Delegates and State Senators — directly to constituents in their legislative districts to help Maryland residents afford postsecondary education. The Delegate Scholarship and Senatorial Scholarship are offered to Maryland residents who plan to pursue a postsecondary credential full-time or part-time at a two-year or four-year Maryland college, university, or private career school. The scholarships support undergraduate students, graduate students, high school seniors, private career school enrollees, undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition, and students in community college certificate or license programs. Awards are available regardless of family income, institution choice, or enrollment status (full-time or part-time). Nearly $12 million in total scholarships was administered to 16,879 students in the 2020-2021 academic year, with Delegates awarding $6,708,972 to 9,166 students and Senators awarding $5,382,227 to 7,713 students. Delegate Scholarship awards are not automatically renewable; students must reapply each year. Senatorial Scholarships are automatically renewed for up to three additional years (or until degree completion, whichever comes first) if enrollment and academic progress requirements are maintained; a fifth year of funding is available for full-time students who exhaust funds. If a Senatorial Scholarship is used for undergraduate study, students must reapply to their Senator to renew for graduate study.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Delegate Scholarship: minimum annual award of $200 for the 2026-2027 academic year; maximum amount not yet determined; awards are not automatically renewable and students must apply with their State Delegate annually. Senatorial Scholarship: minimum annual award of $400 for the 2026-2027 academic year; maximum amount not yet determined; automatically renewed for up to three additional years or until degree completion (whichever occurs first) as long as the award remains active and eligibility requirements are met; a fifth year of funding is available for full-time students who have exhausted funds. Students may hold either scholarship alongside all other state awards, provided the total dollar amount of all state scholarship awards does not exceed the student's cost of attendance as determined by their Financial Aid Office. Funds may not be available to award all eligible students. Awards are administered through OSFA (Office of Student Financial Assistance) when requested by the legislator, or directly by the legislator's office. Audited courses cannot be used to reach minimum credit hour requirements. Prior approval from OSFA and/or the legislator is required to change from full-time to part-time enrollment. As a condition of receiving the award, students pledge to remain drug-free for the full term of the award.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Deadline varies by delegate or senator; FAFSA (or MHEC One-App if ineligible for federal aid) must be completed by March 1 if delegate or senator requests OSFA administration; awarding ends in late March; unique major application for out-of-state programs opens March 15 and closes July 1; Fall appeals for less than 6 credits enrollment open July 1, 2026 and close December 15, 2026; Spring appeals open October 1, 2026 and close April 15, 2027
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Higher Education Commission, Office of Student Financial Assistance
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who are current high school seniors, current or prospective full-time or part-time degree-seeking undergraduate students, current or prospective full-time or part-time degree-seeking graduate students, private career school enrollees, undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition, or individuals currently or recently (within the last two years) enrolled in a community college certificate or license program. Available to all students regardless of family income, postsecondary institution choice, or full-time or part-time attendance status.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses including tuition and fees at two-year or four-year Maryland colleges, universities, or private career schools. May also be used at out-of-state institutions under specified circumstances: if the student's major is not available at any Maryland institution and the legislator agrees; if the student is on active duty with the U.S. Military and domiciled in Maryland; or if the student is disabled and studying at an institution outside Maryland that offers special provisions for disabled students not available in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents. Must be eligible for in-state tuition. Scholarships are primarily for use at Maryland institutions. Out-of-state use is permitted if the student's major has been approved by the Maryland Higher Education Commission as unique (not available at any Maryland institution) and the legislator agrees, if the applicant is on active duty with the U.S. Military and domiciled in Maryland, or if the student is disabled and studying at an institution outside Maryland that offers special provisions for disabled students not available in Maryland. Administered through Maryland Delegates and Senators representing the 47 legislative election districts.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident and eligible for in-state tuition
Must plan to pursue a postsecondary credential full-time (12+ credits undergraduate or 9+ credits graduate per semester) or part-time (6-11 credits undergraduate or 6-8 credits graduate per semester)
Must be a constituent of the Maryland Delegate or Senator awarding the scholarship

Must attend a two-year or four-year Maryland college, university, or private career school (with out-of-state exceptions for approved unique majors, active military duty, or disability accommodations)

Must be in at least one eligible category: current high school senior, current or prospective full-time or part-time degree-seeking undergraduate student, current or prospective full-time or part-time degree-seeking graduate student, private career school enrollee, undocumented student eligible for in-state tuition, or currently or recently (within last two years) enrolled in a community college certificate or license program
Audited courses cannot be used to reach minimum credit hour requirements
If OSFA administers the award, must complete FAFSA or MHEC One-App (One-Application) by March 1; if legislator makes own awards, contact legislator for instructions
If eligible for in-state tuition but ineligible for federal aid, must file the MHEC One-App (One-Application) instead of FAFSA
For Delegate Scholarship: Must reapply annually with your State Delegate; awards are not automatically renewable

For Senatorial Scholarship renewal: must continue as full-time or part-time degree-seeking student and maintain satisfactory academic progress; award will automatically renew for up to three years or until degree completion (whichever occurs first); if used for undergraduate study, must reapply to Senator for graduate study renewal
Must have prior approval from OSFA and/or legislator to change from full-time to part-time enrollment
Pledge to remain drug-free for the full term of the award
Total dollar amount of all state scholarship awards may not exceed cost of attendance as determined by school's financial aid office

Students enrolled in less than 6 credits per semester may appeal if disabled; disability appeals require medical documentation from physician, specialist, psychologist, psychiatrist, or other licensed clinical practitioner confirming disability status and impact on ability to maintain half-time course load, plus documentation of course schedule
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students should contact their local State Delegate or State Senator for instructions on how to apply and for the applicable deadline specific to their legislator. If the legislator requests that OSFA administer awards to students, students must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) by March 1, and OSFA will administer awards. Students eligible for in-state tuition but ineligible for federal aid must file the MHEC One-App online instead of the FAFSA. For Delegate Scholarships, students must call or write to their legislator if the Delegate makes his/her own awards. For out-of-state unique major exceptions (major not available at any Maryland institution), students must complete and submit the online Unique Major Application between March 15 and July 1. At the beginning of each semester, the institution will be asked to certify that the student meets the requirements of the award. When the institution completes the certification and requests funds from OSFA, the award will be processed for payment approximately four weeks after certification. Students enrolled in less than 6 credits may submit a disability appeal: Fall appeals open July 1 and close December 15; Spring appeals open October 1 and close April 15. Appeals must be submitted through the 2026-27 MHEC Grant and Scholarship Appeal Request Form with all required documentation; OSFA will review and make a determination within 45 business days. Awarding ends in late March. Required documentation must be submitted directly to the Delegate's or Senator's office or through OSFA as applicable.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Foster Care Recipients (MLARP Foster Care)
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides state assistance in the repayment of educational loans owed by foster care recipients who are employed by the state, or by a county or municipality of the state, and who received a graduate or undergraduate degree from an institution of higher education in Maryland. Eligible recipients must have been placed in out-of-home foster care for at least three years and must remain employed in state, county, or local government for a minimum period following award. Award amounts are equal to the lesser of 10% of total educational loan debt or $5,000 per year, and are automatically renewable annually for up to three years upon timely submission of required documentation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Award amount is equal to the lesser of 10% of the applicant's total educational loan debt or $5,000 per year, whichever is less. Awards are automatically renewed annually for up to three years if required documentation (employment verification, lender verification, and Maryland state income tax return or equivalent) is submitted by the deadline each year. Assistance is provided as loan repayment support for educational loans from university, government, or commercial sources. Consolidated loans and loans in deferment or grace period status qualify, but Parent PLUS loans and loans in default do not. Recipients must sign and return an employment obligation agreement agreeing to remain employed by the State or a county or municipality of the State for at least 1 year after the expiration of the term of the award.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are available each year starting January 15th. The application and all supporting documents must be received by the Office of Student Financial Assistance (not postdated) by October 15th to be considered on-time. For the 2026-2027 academic year, the deadline is October 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Former foster care recipients who were placed in out-of-home foster care by the state or a unit of state government's department of social services for at least three years, who have received an undergraduate or graduate degree from a Maryland institution of higher education, and who are employed at least part-time (20 hours per week) in state, county, or local government in Maryland with outstanding educational loans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of educational loans (undergraduate or graduate) obtained from university, government, or commercial sources for degrees earned at Maryland institutions of higher education. Loans must not be in default. Consolidated loans and loans in deferment or grace period status qualify, but Parent PLUS loans do not.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents who were placed in out-of-home foster care by the state or a unit of state government's department of social services for at least three years and who are currently employed in state, county, or local government in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident
Must have been placed in out-of-home foster care by the state or unit of state government's department of social services for 3 years or more
Must have earned an undergraduate or graduate degree from a college in Maryland
Must be employed at least part-time (20 hours per week) in state, county, or local government
Must have educational loans from a university, government, or commercial source
May not be in default on any loan
Must not be currently fulfilling a state service obligation from other Maryland scholarships (prior service obligations must be completed first)
Must sign and return an employment obligation agreement to remain employed for at least one year after award expiration
Must complete the MLARP Foster Care paper application
Must submit all required documentation by the application deadline (October 15th annually)
Must submit a signed Maryland state income tax return (or Federal tax return with notation of no Maryland return filed, or IRS Letter 1077)
Must submit employment verification form completed by employer
Must submit institutional certification or official transcript verifying degree and graduation date
Must submit lender verification form for each loan
Must report any changes in employment status throughout the service/award years
Must not falsify or conceal a material fact in the application
Must pledge to remain drug free for the full term of the award
Applicant must have foster care experience verified by court order or local department of social services documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the MLARP Foster Care paper application available on the MHEC website and submit all supplemental documentation through a Google Form application. Required documentation includes: (1) Employment Verification Form completed by employer showing job title, employment status (full-time, part-time, or contractual), dates of employment, and salary information; (2) Institutional Certification Form or official transcript from the Maryland college listing degree received and graduation date; (3) Lender Verification Form for each educational loan showing loan type, outstanding balance, and current loan status; (4) Proof of foster care placement (copy of court order stating commitment to local department of social services custody for 3 years or more); and (5) Signed Maryland state income tax return or equivalent (Federal tax return with notation if no Maryland return filed, or IRS Letter 1077 if no returns filed). All documents must be uploaded to the application or emailed to careerbased.mhec@maryland.gov and received by the deadline (October 15th annually). Renewal applicants must resubmit required documentation by the annual deadline each year. Applications are available starting January 15th each year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Police Officers and Probation Agents (MLARP Police Officers)
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides state assistance in the repayment of educational loans to individuals working as police officers or probation agents in Maryland law enforcement and correctional agencies. Awards are based on the applicant's annual salary and total loan debt, and recipients may receive renewal awards for up to three years. The program is administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission and is available statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards provide direct repayment of educational loan debt. The award amount is calculated by multiplying the applicant's annual salary by a percentage based on total loan debt: 10% for debt below $15,000; 20% for debt between $15,000–$40,000; 30% for debt between $40,000–$75,000; and 40% for debt over $75,000. The payment amount cannot exceed the total debt. Recipients receive a 3-year lock-in award with set award amounts for each year, and may renew for an additional 2 years (up to 5 years total) as long as they remain eligible. One-time, 1-year only awards are also available and equal the yearly payment for the applicant's debt range. Applicants are ranked by graduation date (most recent first), then application completion date (earliest first), then income (lowest first).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 15, 2026 for the 2025-2026 academic year; October 15, 2026 for the 2026-2027 application
structured_extraction.program_audience: Police officers and probation agents employed in Maryland law enforcement and correctional agencies who hold graduate, professional, or undergraduate degrees from Maryland public colleges or universities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repayment of educational loans (graduate, professional, or undergraduate degree loans in criminal law, criminology, or criminal justice) for individuals working as police officers or probation agents in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Applicants must be working for eligible law enforcement or probation agencies serving the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Received a graduate, professional, or undergraduate degree in criminal law, criminology, or criminal justice from a public college or university in Maryland
Currently working as a police officer or probation agent for at least 2 years at an eligible agency
Police officer must be authorized to enforce general criminal laws and be a member of an eligible law enforcement agency

Probation agent must serve as a parole and probation agent, supervisor (supervising a caseload with no employees reporting to them), or regional administrator for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
Annual gross salary cannot exceed $85,000; if married, combined salaries cannot exceed $170,000
Must remain employed as a police officer or probation agent at an eligible law enforcement agency throughout the application cycle
Must submit Maryland signed income tax return (2024 for 2025-2026 application; 2025 for 2026-2027 application)
Must submit employment verification form
Must submit lender verification form
Must submit institutional certification form documenting degree completion in criminal law, criminology, or criminal justice from a Maryland public college or university
After award: must sign Master Promissory Note (MPN) through Student Portal
After award: must sign Employment Obligation Agreement (EOA) through Student Portal
After award: must submit LARP Documentation of Address Verification
After award: must submit W9 Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an online application through the MHEC One App in the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us. All required documentation must be submitted to MHEC by secure upload online through the applicant's MDCAPS account by the closing date. Applicants will have an 'incomplete' status until all documentation is submitted; once all documents are received, status changes to 'Qualified' and the Program Administrator verifies eligibility. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis for awarding throughout the application period and after. Recipients receive payment via check mailed to the address provided on the application. All awards are subject to availability of funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Police Officer and Probation Agent Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship awarded to current police officers or probation agents, or individuals planning to become police officers or probation agents, who are enrolled in academic programs that further their career in law enforcement. Recipients must commit to working as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland for at least five years during the eight-year period after graduation. The program is administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission and is available at Maryland public senior institutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An annual scholarship award equal to 50% of the equivalent annual tuition and mandatory fees of a resident undergraduate student at the eligible Maryland public senior institution. Recipients must sign a promissory note and service obligation agreement committing to work as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland for at least five years during the eight-year period after graduation. If the student fails to satisfy degree requirements or perform the service obligation, the award will convert into a loan payable to the state. Payment to the institution will be made approximately four weeks after the institution completes the certification that the student meets the requirements of the award.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application for the 2025-2026 academic year will close April 1, 2026. The application for the upcoming 2026-2027 academic year will become available on January 15, 2026 and will close October 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Higher Education Commission Office of Student Financial Assistance
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current police officers or probation agents, or individuals planning to become police officers or probation agents, who are Maryland residents or have graduated from a Maryland high school and are accepted for admission or currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a Maryland public senior institution.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees for undergraduate or graduate academic programs that further the recipient's career in law enforcement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents or have graduated from a Maryland high school. The scholarship is available at Maryland public senior institutions. Recipients must work as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland for at least five years during the eight-year period after graduation.
requirements_list: Must be a current police officer or probation agent, or an individual planning to become a police officer or probation agent
Accepted for admission or currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a Maryland public senior institution
Must be a Maryland resident or have graduated from a Maryland high school
Enrolled full-time or part-time pursuing a course of study or program that furthers the recipient's career in law enforcement
Current police officers must be authorized to enforce general criminal laws of the state and be a member of an approved law enforcement agency as defined in Public Safety Article §3–201
Probation agents must be serving as a parole and probation agent, supervisor, or regional administrator for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services in the State
Must sign and return a promissory note and service obligation agreement
Must work as a police officer or probation agent in Maryland for no less than five years during the eight-year period after graduation
If graduated from a Maryland high school but not a Maryland resident, must submit a copy of final high school transcript
Documentation from the institution confirming enrollment in a program that furthers career in law enforcement must be submitted
Must pledge to remain drug-free for the full term of the award

To renew the award, must continue to be a Maryland resident, maintain satisfactory academic progress, maintain a minimum 3.0 GPA, and continue enrollment as a full-time or part-time student in a degree program that furthers intent to become a police officer or probation agent
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit an online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) using the MHEC One App by the established deadline. Required documentation includes: documentation confirming current employment as a police officer (if applicable); a copy of the final high school transcript if the applicant graduated from a Maryland high school but is not a Maryland resident; and documentation from the institution confirming enrollment in a program that will further their career in law enforcement. Award recipients must sign and return a promissory note and service obligation agreement. At the beginning of each semester, the institution will certify that the student meets the requirements of the award. When certification is completed and returned to OSFA, the award will be processed for payment to the institution, which will be made approximately four weeks after certification. Contact your institution's financial aid office for questions about payment status.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Teacher Quality and Diversity Competitive Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides competitive grants to teacher preparation programs at Maryland institutions of higher education to help students from groups historically underrepresented in the teaching profession achieve teacher preparation and certification requirements. It supports the development of highly qualified teachers and leaders from diverse backgrounds, including African Americans, American Indians/Alaska Natives, Hispanics/Latinos, individuals from low-income backgrounds, first-generation college students, and individuals with disabilities. The program encourages alternative accelerated pathways into teaching, consortium-based proposals, comprehensive standards-aligned programming with mentoring, transcript analysis pathways for licensure, and targeted interventions supporting male-identifying students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual funding of $1,000,000 is available through two tracks: (1) Individual track awards between $50,000–$150,000 per institution, and (2) Consortium track awards between $250,000–$500,000 for proposals involving multiple institutions of higher education and school systems. Grants support teacher preparation programs at accredited Maryland institutions of higher education. Funds may be used for salaries of staff directly involved in the project, equipment, materials, supplies, development and administration of competency-based curricula and assessments, student success services such as academic advising, certification exam preparation, faculty or teacher mentor stipends, and evaluation-related costs. Funds cannot be used for student financial aid grants, scholarships, or stipends. 100% of the total grant award will be disbursed at the beginning of the project period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited institutions of higher education in Maryland, with priority given to historically black colleges and universities and Hispanic-serving institutions with a track record of preparing diverse and high-quality teachers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support teacher preparation and certification programs for students from historically underrepresented groups in the teaching profession. Eligible uses include: salaries of staff directly involved in the project; equipment, materials, and supplies; development and administration of competency-based curricula and assessments, including designing curriculum frameworks and creating assessments that award credit based on demonstrated proficiency; alternative accelerated pathways into teaching that leverage subject-matter expertise and prior professional experience, including credit for prior learning; consortium-based proposals to strengthen transfer pathways from community colleges to baccalaureate institutions; comprehensive standards-aligned programming with extensive mentoring; cohesive course sequences for licensure through transcript analysis pathways; student success services such as academic advising and certification exam preparation; faculty or teacher mentor stipends; targeted interventions supporting male-identifying students; and evaluation-related costs including data collection and analysis. Funds cannot be used for student financial aid grants, scholarships, or stipends.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must be located at accredited institutions of higher education in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicants must be accredited institutions of higher education in Maryland
Proposals must demonstrate a sustainable plan for continuation beyond the grant period
Programs must serve students from groups historically underrepresented in the teaching profession
Priority given to historically black colleges and universities and Hispanic-serving institutions with a track record of preparing diverse and high-quality teachers
Proposals may emphasize alternative accelerated pathways into teaching that leverage subject-matter expertise and prior professional experience
Consortium-based proposals encouraged to strengthen transfer pathways from community colleges to baccalaureate institutions
Programming must meet State requirements and provide extensive mentoring
Proposals may include a cohesive sequence of courses for licensure through a transcript analysis pathway
Targeted interventions to support male-identifying students encouraged
Proposals must include all requisite forms: Cover Sheet, Application, Budget, Funding Opportunity Award Letter, Assurances, and Letters of Support
Proposal narrative limited to maximum of ten (10) single-spaced pages (excluding cover sheet, abstract, budget, assurances, résumés, or appendices)
Pages must have one-inch margins and be in 12-point Times New Roman or Arial font
Proposal pages must be 8 ½ x 11 inches in size

For consortium grants, must identify a lead institution with fiscal and administrative responsibility, include at least one other Maryland institution of higher education, include at least one local education agency partner to support candidate placement and mentoring, and describe each partner's role, governance structure, and how decision-making will be shared
Consortium grants must include letters of support signed by the President of each participating institution
Proposals must demonstrate alignment with regional teacher workforce needs and shortage areas (STEM, special education, bilingual education)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Request for Proposals was issued September 25, 2025. Applicants must submit all required application materials including a cover sheet (signed by the institution's President), abstract, proposal narrative, budget summary, budget narrative, statement of assurances, and letters of support from partner local education agencies (and participating institutions for consortium proposals). Applications must be submitted by email to anthony.reiner@maryland.gov by 4:00 p.m. on October 30, 2025. An electronic copy of the grant proposal in PDF format must be submitted to Elena Quiroz-Livanis at elena.quiroz@maryland.gov, and a copy of the abstract must be submitted as a Microsoft Word document. A panel of qualified reviewers will read and score each proposal according to evaluation criteria. The review panel convenes to discuss proposals and funding recommendations, which are submitted to the Secretary of Higher Education for final funding decisions. Award notifications will be made by email no later than November 28, 2025. Grant period runs from December 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026, with an interim report due March 31, 2026 and a final report due August 31, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Tuition Waiver for Unaccompanied Homeless Youth
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Tuition Waiver for Homeless Youth provides financial assistance to homeless youth who are enrolled as candidates for an associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate at a Maryland public institution of higher education. The waiver exempts eligible students from paying tuition and mandatory fees, covering tuition, registration fees, and all fees required as a condition of enrollment for both credit-bearing and non-credit-bearing courses across fall, winter, spring, and summer semesters. The waiver does not cover room, board, books, or transportation. Students remain exempt from paying tuition and fees for up to ten years after first enrolling or until they earn a bachelor's degree, whichever comes first.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students verified as homeless youth are exempt from paying tuition, registration fees, and all mandatory fees required as a condition of enrollment at any Maryland public institution of higher education. The waiver covers these fees for fall, winter, spring, and summer semesters for both credit-bearing and noncredit courses. Students remain exempt for up to ten years after first enrolling or until earning a bachelor's degree, whichever occurs first. The waiver can be renewed for up to an additional four years or until the bachelor's degree is awarded, whichever occurs first. Room, board, books, and transportation are not covered. Scholarships or grants awarded to a waiver recipient cannot be applied to tuition since it is already waived. The amount of the waiver varies by institution.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeless youth who are unaccompanied and living in unstable housing, as defined by the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act, who are enrolled or planning to enroll at a Maryland public institution of higher education as candidates for an associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate. Students must be enrolled on or before reaching age 25.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, registration fees, and all mandatory fees required as a condition of enrollment at Maryland public institutions of higher education for students pursuing associate degrees, bachelor's degrees, or vocational certificates (both credit-bearing and non-credit-bearing programs). Does not cover room, board, books, or transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at all Maryland public institutions of higher education. Youth must have had a consistent presence in Maryland for at least one year before enrollment, documented by school, employment, or other records. Eligibility information is provided to Maryland public colleges and universities by the Maryland Department of Human Services.
requirements_list: Must be verified as a homeless child or youth as defined by the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act
Verification must occur at any time during the 24 months immediately preceding enrollment or while enrolled in a public institution of higher education
Must be enrolled as a candidate for an associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate at a Maryland public institution of higher education
Must have had a consistent presence in Maryland for at least one year before enrollment, documented by school, employment, or other records
Must complete and file the FAFSA or MHEC One-App each year
Must be enrolled on or before reaching age 25
Must be enrolled full-time or part-time while earning an associate, bachelor's, or vocational certificate at a Maryland public institution of higher education
Must remain enrolled in an eligible program to renew the award
All academic majors are eligible, including credit-bearing and non-credit-bearing vocational certificate programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the financial aid office at the Maryland public institution you plan to attend to apply for the tuition waiver. Homeless status must be verified by a director or designee of an emergency or transitional shelter, street outreach program, homeless youth drop-in center, or other program serving those experiencing homelessness; a school district homeless liaison; a director or designee of a project supported by a federal TRIO or GEAR UP program grant; or a financial aid administrator. Eligibility information is provided to Maryland public colleges and universities by the Maryland Department of Human Services. Eligible applicants are encouraged to complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa or the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) via the MHEC One App. Students must file the FAFSA or MHEC One-App each year to renew the waiver. Undocumented applicants should consult directly with the financial aid office at the institution.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state financial aid grant available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8 and are near completing their degree at eligible Maryland public or private institutions. The grant provides financial aid to help these students complete their college education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State financial aid grant for qualified undocumented students who are near completing their degree at eligible Maryland public or private institutions. The grant amount varies based on student need and institutional funding. Awarding occurs in the summer and eligible applicants are notified by email. Students must accept their award online through their MDCAPS portal within 2 weeks of notification or the award will be canceled. To qualify for the Near Completer Grant, students must apply through the MSFAA application, which must be submitted by the established deadline for this specific program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by program; see state financial aid grant and scholarship program deadlines on MHEC website
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified children of undocumented immigrants who meet the non-resident exemption requirements under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8, are eligible for in-state tuition, attend eligible Maryland public or private institutions, and are near completion of their degree program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial aid for educational expenses at eligible Maryland public or private institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified child of undocumented immigrants
Must meet in-state tuition eligibility requirements (non-resident exemption) under §15–106.8 of the MD Education Article
Must attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution
Must be near completion of degree program
Must file taxes using prior-prior-year tax information (e.g., use 2021 tax information for 2023-2024 MSFAA)
Males aged 18-25 must register with Selective Service System and provide proof of registration
If dependent, must provide parental information and have one parent sign the application
Must apply through the MSFAA (Maryland State Financial Aid Application) in the Maryland College Aid Processing (MDCAPS) portal
If classified as dependent student, parent must complete and submit the Parent Signature Page for the application to be valid

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Create an MDCAPS account at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us and log in. Step 2: Complete the MSFAA Eligibility Wizard to confirm you are eligible for the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (not the FAFSA). Step 3: Complete the MSFAA application by providing student demographic data, income and tax information (from two prior years), dependency information, household information, and school selection. Step 4: For dependent students, have a parent complete and sign the Parent Signature Page. Step 5: Submit the application by the established deadline for the Near Completer Grant program. Step 6: After submission, OSFA will review your application and may request additional documentation. Step 7: Upon approval, eligible applicants will be notified by email in the summer. Step 8: Accept your award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks of notification or the award will be canceled. Contact the Office of Student Financial Assistance at osfamail.mhec@maryland.gov or 410-767-3300 with questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Next Generation Scholars of Maryland (NGS) Program - FY 2026
structured_extraction.program_description: A college access program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that supports low-income, first-generation students in high-poverty school systems. The program provides cohort-based mentoring, college guidance, and college preparation services to students identified as early as 7th grade (grades 7-12) and supports them through high school graduation and into their first year of college. Grants are awarded to nonprofit organizations to continue delivering these services in eligible school districts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: FY 2026 grants totaling $5,000,000 will be awarded to approximately 11-15 nonprofit organizations to provide guidance, mentoring, and college preparation services to cohort students in grades 7-12 in eligible school districts. Funds support services including: guidance and college preparation, mentoring and one-on-one counseling, career interest assessments, financial aid literacy assistance, high school graduation planning, summer work or internship opportunities, visits to college campuses and workplaces, intensive summer bridge programs for students entering postsecondary education, and support for matriculation and graduation from institutions of higher education. Students must pre-qualify for the Guaranteed Access Grant. Services extend through high school graduation and the first year of college. Approved uses include: salaries, stipends, paid student internships, student transportation, materials and supplies, travel, equipment, and other costs approved by MHEC. Funds may not be used for supplanting existing program funds, capital improvements, purchase of gift cards, or costs incurred prior to grant approval. Grant period: July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Proposals are due no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT on July 1, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations that provide college access programs to low-income, first-generation students in high-poverty school districts in one or more of the eligible school systems. Applicants must have been previously awarded a grant under the Next Generation Scholars Program or be providing services in the specified eligible school districts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports guidance services, mentoring, and college preparation activities for cohort-based groups of students identified as early as 7th grade (grades 7-12), through high school graduation and into their first year of college. Students must pre-qualify for the Guaranteed Access Grant. Specific approved uses include salaries, stipends, paid student internships, student transportation, materials and supplies, travel, equipment, and other costs approved by MHEC. Activities must include high school graduation planning, summer work or internship opportunities, financial aid literacy assistance, career interest assessments, mentorship and one-on-one counseling, visits to college campuses and workplaces, intensive summer bridge programs, and support for matriculation and graduation from institutions of higher education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Nonprofit organizations must support students in one or more of the following school systems: Allegany County Public Schools, Baltimore City Public Schools, Caroline County Public Schools, Dorchester County Public Schools, Kent County Public Schools, Prince George's County Public Schools, Somerset County Public Schools, or Wicomico County Public Schools.

structured_extraction.program_name: Nurse Educator Doctoral Grants for Practice and Dissertation Research (NEDG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that supports nursing faculty pursuing and completing doctoral degrees while reducing their student loan debt. The program aims to increase the number of doctoral-prepared nurse faculty in Maryland to meet the critical need for highly educated nurses to teach future generations and conduct nursing research. Eligible nursing faculty employed at Maryland nursing programs are nominated annually by deans and directors of participating institutions. Recent awards totaled $293,914 distributed among seven nursing faculty members.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards ranging from $5,000 to $60,000 (most commonly $12,800 to $60,000) per recipient to support nursing faculty in expediting completion of their terminal doctoral degree and reducing existing student loan debt. Recent awards totaled $293,914 distributed among seven nursing faculty members. Eligible nursing faculty employed at Maryland nursing programs are nominated by deans and directors of nursing programs at Maryland universities and community colleges.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nursing faculty members employed full-time at nursing programs at Maryland universities and community colleges who are pursuing or completing a doctoral degree in nursing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expediting completion of a terminal doctoral degree, supporting practice and dissertation research, and reducing existing student loan debt.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; nursing faculty must be employed at one of the participating Maryland nursing programs across six Maryland universities and six Maryland community colleges.
requirements_list: Must be a nursing faculty member employed at an eligible Maryland nursing program (university or community college)
Must be pursuing or completing a terminal doctoral degree
Must be nominated by the Dean or Director of the nursing program
Participating institution must be a Maryland community college or Maryland university with a nursing program
Candidates must be recognized and nominated annually
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Deans and Directors of Nursing Programs at participating Maryland universities and community colleges recognize and nominate eligible nursing faculty for these awards. The nomination and award process occurs annually, with new nominations due every September.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Nurse Support Program II (NSP II) is a multi-year program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) and funded by an allocation of up to 0.1 percent of regulated gross hospital revenue through the Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC). The program is designed to increase the number of nurses in Maryland by expanding the academic capacity of nursing education programs at Maryland institutions of higher education. NSP II addresses the nursing shortage by supporting nursing faculty development, doctoral education, nurse educator training, and innovative nursing education initiatives. The program operates through two primary mechanisms: (1) Competitive Institutional Grants that fund nursing schools in expanding capacity through shared resources, innovative educational design, new program development, and clinical training opportunities; and (2) Statewide Initiatives including the New Nurse Faculty Fellowships (NNFF), the Nurse Educator Doctoral Grants for Practice and Dissertation Research (NEDG), the Hal and Jo Cohen Graduate Nursing Faculty Scholarship (GNF), and the Academic Nurse Educator Certification (ANEC) program. The program provides up to $90 million over five years ($18 million per year beginning in fiscal year 2021), with FY23 awards totaling $4,101,847 across thirteen proposals at twelve institutions, and FY24 awards totaling $5.8 million to nine nursing programs. Fifteen community colleges and thirteen universities across all geographic regions of Maryland participate in NSP II-funded initiatives. The program is rooted in findings from the Maryland Nursing Program Capacity Study, which identified critical unmet demand for nurses in Maryland and the capacity of higher education institutions to expand nursing enrollments with sufficient resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: NSP II provides up to $90 million in funding over five years ($18 million per year beginning in fiscal year 2021) through two mechanisms: (1) Competitive Institutional Grants—including one-year resource grants, multi-year implementation grants, and planning grants—that support nursing schools in expanding capacity through shared resources and innovative education design. Award size depends on the project's ability to impact the nursing shortage, the depth and breadth of the initiative, and budget feasibility. FY23 awards totaled $4,101,847 distributed among thirteen grant proposals at twelve institutions; FY24 awards totaled $5.8 million to nine nursing programs (six universities and three community colleges). Funding is allocated based on demonstrated institutional capacity to increase nursing enrollments, quality of partnerships, strategic alignment with state and national nursing education goals, innovation, and feasibility of proposed initiatives. (2) Statewide Initiatives including: the New Nurse Faculty Fellowships (NNFF) providing funding for newly hired nursing faculty to support research and teaching; the Nurse Educator Doctoral Grants for Practice and Dissertation Research (NEDG) providing graduate degree tuition support and financial assistance for nurses pursuing doctoral degrees; the Hal and Jo Cohen Graduate Nursing Faculty Scholarship (GNF) supporting graduate nursing faculty; and the Academic Nurse Educator Certification (ANEC) program supporting nurse educator certification. Additionally, the Maryland Student Loan Repayment Tax Credit is referenced as a supplementary form of assistance available to nurses. The program was designed based on survey findings indicating that Maryland's 24 nursing deans and directors were willing to expand enrollments if resources were available, with institutions reporting they could enroll an additional 1,245-1,299 nursing students with adequate funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland higher education institutions (universities and community colleges) with nursing programs, nursing faculty seeking doctoral credentials or educator development, hospital-based nurses and professional development specialists, graduate nursing students, and nurses seeking to advance their education and careers across all geographic regions of Maryland. Particular emphasis on programs serving geographically underserved nursing students, particularly in western Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support: expanding nursing program enrollment and developing new cohorts; planning and establishing new nursing degree and certificate programs (including PhD programs); building nurse-managed health centers; developing entry-to-practice programs; nursing faculty development, retention, and recruitment; graduate degree tuition support for nurses and nursing educators; course release time for faculty pursuing terminal degrees; nurse educator certification and professional development; leadership development programs; clinical simulation equipment and training; acquiring exam software and testing resources for licensure exam preparation; website and program expansion; innovative initiatives to reduce barriers to nursing education; addressing obstacles to expanding enrollments such as faculty shortages, limited clinical sites, and facility constraints; and increasing the proportion of highly-educated nurses in Maryland's workforce.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available to all Maryland institutions of higher education. Fifteen community colleges and thirteen universities across all geographic regions and types of programs participate. The program emphasizes support for programs serving geographically underserved nursing students, particularly in western Maryland. Graduate nursing programs are offered at only six institutions in Maryland, with four located in the Baltimore metropolitan area, one in Prince George's County, and one in Wicomico County. NSP II supports efforts to increase access to graduate nursing programs through expanded online instruction and use of Regional Higher Education Centers (RHEC) to offer programs in underserved areas.
