structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Competitive Institutional Grants: Institutions submit competitive proposals during each fiscal year's application cycle. Proposals are evaluated by an eight- to nine-member review panel based on alignment with statewide and national nursing education goals, innovation, depth and breadth of initiative, budget feasibility, and demonstrated impact on nursing capacity. The review panel recommends proposals for funding, which are then approved by the Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC). For Statewide Initiative components—including Nurse Faculty Programs for New Nurse Faculty, Nurse Educator Doctoral Grants for Practice and Dissertation Research, Cohen Scholars, and Academic Nurse Educator Grants—applicants should visit www.nursesupport.org for specific application procedures and deadlines. Each statewide initiative has its own application process and timeline managed through the nursesupport.org portal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Nurse Support Program II (NSP II) - New Nursing Faculty Fellowship (NNFF)
structured_extraction.program_description: The New Nursing Faculty Fellowship (NNFF), part of the Nurse Support Program II (NSP II), is an ongoing fellowship program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that provides financial support to recruit, retain, and assist in the development of new nurse faculty members at Maryland universities and community colleges. The program aims to increase the state's academic capacity to educate nurses, support the nursing workforce, and encourage the recruitment and retention of nursing faculty from underrepresented groups, including racial and ethnic minorities and men. New recipients receive $20,000 disbursed over three years ($10,000 in year one and $5,000 in each of years two and three), contingent on continued full-time employment in good standing. Previously awarded faculty members receive ongoing annual disbursements based on continued full-time employment. The program has been in operation since 2005 and is funded through the Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: New nursing faculty recipients receive $20,000 total over three years: $10,000 in the first year and $5,000 in each of the following two years, provided the faculty member remains employed full-time in good standing at a participating Maryland nursing program. Previously awarded faculty members receive ongoing annual disbursements of $5,000 per year based on continued full-time employment in good standing. Awards are made to faculty members at participating Maryland universities and community colleges.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nursing faculty members at Maryland universities and community colleges who are nominated by the Deans and Directors of Nursing Programs at participating institutions, including both newly nominated faculty and previously awarded faculty maintaining continued full-time employment in good standing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for nursing faculty development, recruitment, and retention at participating Maryland higher education institutions, including competitive compensation to equip nursing faculty with tools to meet healthcare demands and support faculty with doctoral degrees to teach future generations of nurses and conduct research.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at participating Maryland nursing programs, including nine universities and nine community colleges: Bowie State University, Johns Hopkins University, Morgan State University, Notre Dame of Maryland University, Salisbury University, Stevenson University, Towson University, University of Maryland Baltimore, Washington Adventist University, Allegany College of Maryland, Anne Arundel Community College, Chesapeake College, Community College of Baltimore County, Frederick Community College, Harford Community College, Montgomery College, Prince George's Community College, and Wor-Wic Community College.
requirements_list: Must be a nursing faculty member at a participating Maryland college, university, or community college
Must be nominated by the Dean or Director of the Nursing Program at their institution
Must be employed full-time at a Maryland nursing program
Must maintain full-time employment in good standing to continue receiving payments in subsequent years
For ongoing recipients, continued full-time employment in good standing at a Maryland nursing program is required for annual disbursements
Program prioritizes faculty from underrepresented groups in nursing, including racial and ethnic minorities and men
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Deans and Directors of Nursing Programs at eligible Maryland universities and community colleges nominate qualified nursing faculty members annually. Nominations are due every August. New recipients are selected and receive their first disbursement following the nomination and selection process. Awards are approved for funding by the administrator for the Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC). The program has operated annually since 2005, with faculty evaluated for continued eligibility based on maintained full-time employment status.

structured_extraction.program_name: Nurse Support Program II - Academic Nurse Educator Certification (ANEC) Award
structured_extraction.program_description: The Academic Nurse Educator Certification (ANEC) Award provides $5,000 financial incentives to full-time nurse faculty at Maryland higher education institutions who have achieved and maintained the National League for Nursing Certified Nurse Educator (CNE) credential. The program is part of Nurse Support Program II and is designed to support professional development and continuing education activities that help faculty maintain their CNE credential and demonstrate excellence in academic nursing education. Eligible activities include continuing education, CNE examination fees, licensing and certification maintenance, and professional organization dues. Recipients are nominated by deans and directors of nursing programs at eligible Maryland community colleges and universities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each eligible full-time nurse faculty member receives a $5,000 award to support professional development activities including continuing education, CNE examination fees, professional certifications and licensing maintenance, credential maintenance requirements, and professional organization dues associated with achieving and maintaining the National League for Nursing's Certified Nurse Educator (CNE) credential. Recipients are nominated by deans and directors of nursing programs at their institutions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 15, 2020 (for a prior cycle; check program website for current deadlines)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time nurse faculty at Maryland higher education institutions (community colleges and four-year colleges/universities) who have achieved or are maintaining their National League for Nursing Certified Nurse Educator (CNE) credential.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development activities including continuing education, CNE examination fees, continuing education requirements to maintain credentials, professional certifications and licensing maintenance, and professional organization dues.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland at participating higher education institutions, including community colleges and universities such as Baltimore City Community College, Carroll Community College, Community College of Baltimore County, College of Southern Maryland, Frostburg State University, Harford Community College, Johns Hopkins University, Notre Dame of Maryland University, Prince George's Community College, Salisbury University, Stevenson University, Towson University, and University of Maryland, Baltimore.
requirements_list: Must be full-time nurse faculty at a participating Maryland higher education institution
Must have achieved and be maintaining the National League for Nursing's Certified Nurse Educator (CNE) credential
Must be nominated by the dean or director of their nursing program at their institution
Must demonstrate excellence as an academic nurse educator
Faculty must have completed or renewed their CNE credential during the specified academic years for the relevant award cycle
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Nominations come directly from deans and directors of nursing programs at eligible Maryland higher education institutions. The program administrator reviews nominations and selects recipients based on their achievement and maintenance of the NLN Certified Nurse Educator (CNE) credential and demonstrated excellence as academic nurse educators.

structured_extraction.program_name: One Step Away Grant Program (Complete College Maryland)
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive, state-funded grant program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that supports accredited public and nonprofit independent two- and four-year institutions in their efforts to identify, re-engage, re-enroll, and graduate near-completer students. Near-completers are students who have earned 75 percent or more of the credits required toward an associate or bachelor's degree, or who may have enough credits for a degree, but have stopped out or dropped out for 12 or more consecutive months without obtaining a degree. The program provides institutions with funds to offer financial assistance, tutoring, customized degree plans, and dedicated One Step Away advisors to help near-completers complete their degrees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $60,000 per institution are awarded on a competitive basis to accredited Maryland public and nonprofit independent two- and four-year institutions. The grant period runs from August 5, 2025 through August 31, 2026. Institutions must provide in-kind or matching funds equal to at least one-third of the total project cost. Matching funds can be provided as cash or in-kind contributions such as staff time dedicated to the project, with up to 8% of the total project cost allowed as indirect costs in-kind match. Funds support a range of activities including: degree audit infrastructure and software enhancements; individualized or templated degree completion plans; enhancement or redesign of degree programs (such as flexible general studies majors); establishment of a dedicated concierge or near-completer counselor position; faculty and staff professional development; marketing and outreach; and student financial support such as emergency grants, tuition discounts, book vouchers, fee waivers, prior learning assessment portfolio funding, transportation vouchers, and childcare support. Students receiving more than $2,000 in financial support per semester must demonstrate need through FAFSA completion or Pell eligibility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Accredited Maryland public and nonprofit independent two-year and four-year associate and bachelor's degree-granting colleges and universities seeking to identify, re-engage, re-enroll, and graduate near-completer students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to identify, contact, re-enroll, and graduate near-completer students. Specific fundable activities include degree audit infrastructure and software; degree completion plans; flexible or redesigned degree programs; dedicated concierge or near-completer counselor positions; faculty and staff professional development; marketing and outreach; and student financial support including emergency grants, tuition discounts, book vouchers, fee waivers, prior learning assessment funding, transportation vouchers, and childcare support. OSA is not solely a financial aid program and does not provide a sustainable source of financial aid due to its short-term nature.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland institutions only. All accredited Maryland public and nonprofit independent two- and four-year institutions granting associate or bachelor's degrees are eligible.
requirements_list: Institution must be accredited
Institution must be public or nonprofit independent
Institution must be a two-year or four-year college or university
Institution must grant associate or bachelor's degrees
Institution must be located in Maryland
Institution must provide in-kind or matching funds equal to at least one-third of the total project cost
Near-completer students must have earned 75 percent or more of credits required for an associate or bachelor's degree, or have enough credits for a degree but have not been awarded it
Near-completer students must have stopped out or dropped out for at least 12 consecutive months without obtaining a degree
Near-completer students must be in good academic standing
Applicants must develop a needs assessment using institution-specific data on the near-completer population
Applicants must address at least three of the six grant program objectives
Applicants must demonstrate how proposed activities support re-enrollment and degree completion
Applicants must provide a management plan with essential personnel roles, organizational structure, timelines, and milestones
Applicants must provide an operations plan describing activity implementation strategies, timelines, recruitment and retention plans
Applicants must provide a project evaluation plan linked to objectives and outcomes
Applicants must commit to data reporting requirements throughout and after the grant period
Project directors and staff must have sufficient time to conduct the project efficiently and on schedule
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Institutions apply through a competitive Request for Proposal (RFP) process. Applications must include: (1) a cover sheet using the provided form, (2) an abstract of 250 words or less as a Microsoft Word document, (3) resumes for all essential personnel, and (4) a narrative of maximum 15 pages addressing Needs Assessment (10 points), Project Objectives and Projected Outcomes (10 points), Management Plan (15 points), Operations Plan (30 points), and Project Evaluation (20 points), plus a Budget Summary and Budget Narrative (15 points). Applications must follow specific formatting requirements: 8.5 by 11-inch pages, Arial/Times New Roman/Calibri font, 12-point for text (10-point for tables), single-spaced with one-inch margins. Electronic applications must be emailed to Anthony.Reiner@maryland.gov by 4:00 p.m. on July 25, 2025. Award notifications will be sent via email by August 5, 2025. The grant period runs August 5, 2025 to August 31, 2026, with the first 50% payment in August 2025 and remaining funds released in January 2026. Institutions must submit a One Step Away Student List to MHEC by August 15, 2025 for MVA address matching, with updated lists returned by August 25, 2025. Initial contact with near-completer students must be made by September 2, 2025. Interim reports are due December 23, 2025, and final narrative, data, and financial reports are due November 30, 2026. Technical assistance available from Anthony Reiner.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state financial aid grant available to qualified children of undocumented immigrants who are eligible for in-state tuition under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8 and are attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions on a part-time basis. The program provides financial assistance to support part-time college attendance for this population of students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State financial aid grant for qualified children of undocumented immigrants attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions on a part-time basis. The amount and specific terms of the award are determined based on financial need and eligibility. Students are considered for the Part-Time Grant after submitting the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA). The applicant's institution will notify them if they have been awarded this grant. Students must accept their award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks of notification or the award will be canceled.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by academic year; the MSFAA application deadline is typically aligned with the specific state grant program deadlines. For the 2023-2024 academic year, the deadline for certain programs like the Educational Assistance Grant and Guaranteed Access Grant is March 1, while the Campus-Based Educational Assistance Grant can be completed after March 1.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified children of undocumented immigrants who meet the non-resident exemption requirements under Maryland Education Article §15–106.8 and are eligible for in-state tuition at eligible Maryland public or private institutions, enrolled on a part-time basis.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial aid for educational expenses related to part-time college attendance at eligible Maryland public or private institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students attending eligible Maryland public or private institutions throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Be a qualified child of undocumented immigrants eligible for in-state tuition under §15-106.8 of the MD Education Article
Meet the non-resident exemption requirements
Attend an eligible Maryland public or private institution on a part-time basis
Be ineligible to receive federal aid (such as FAFSA)
File taxes using prior-prior-year tax information (e.g., 2021 tax information for the 2023-2024 award year)
If male between ages 18 and 25, register with Selective Service System and provide proof of registration
If dependent, must provide parental information and have one parent sign the Parent Signature Page
Complete the MSFAA (Maryland State Financial Aid Application) through the Maryland College Aid Processing (MDCAPS) portal
Submit the MSFAA by the established deadline for the specific grant or scholarship program being applied for
For dependent students, parent must submit signed Parent Signature Page to the Office of Student Financial Assistance for the application to be valid
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Create an MDCAPS account at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us if you do not already have one. 2. Complete the MSFAA Eligibility Wizard to confirm you are eligible to complete the MSFAA (you should not be a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen with an Alien Registration number). 3. Complete the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) through MDCAPS, which opens each year at the same time the FAFSA opens. The MSFAA requires submission of: student demographic data, income and tax information from two prior years, dependency status information, household information, parent information (if dependent), and school selection. 4. Submit the MSFAA by the established deadline for the specific grant program you are applying for. 5. If you are a dependent student, download the Parent Signature Page from the confirmation page and have your parent complete and sign it, then submit it to the Office of Student Financial Assistance. 6. After submission, the OSFA will review your application and may contact you for any additional documentation required. 7. If awarded the Part-Time Grant, your institution will notify you. You must accept the award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks of notification or the award will be canceled.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Part-Time Grant Program provides funds to Maryland public and independent colleges and universities based on the number of undergraduate part-time students with demonstrated financial need who are enrolled in degree-granting programs at specific institutions. Funds are distributed to institutions, which select and award recipients. The program also supports students dually enrolled in a Maryland high school and an institution of higher education. Award amounts vary based on financial need as determined by the FAFSA or Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA/MHEC One App).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Need-based grants ranging from a minimum of $200 to a maximum of $2,000 per academic year. Funds are distributed by the state to participating Maryland public and independent colleges and universities based on the number of eligible part-time undergraduate students with demonstrated financial need. Institutions then select and award recipients. Award amounts depend on financial need as determined by FAFSA or Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA/MHEC One App) and availability of funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1 (FAFSA or MHEC One App). Contact your institution for any additional institution-specific deadlines.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Part-time, degree-seeking undergraduate students enrolled at a Maryland two-year or four-year college or university, and students dually enrolled in a Maryland high school and an institution of higher education, who demonstrate financial need and are Maryland residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses for part-time undergraduate study in degree-granting programs at Maryland public and independent colleges and universities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants and their parents (if dependent) must be Maryland residents. Enrollment must be at a two-year or four-year Maryland public or independent college or university.
requirements_list: Must be enrolled part-time (3-11 credits per semester) as a degree-seeking undergraduate student at a two-year or four-year Maryland college or university
Must be a Maryland resident (applicant and parents if dependent)
Must demonstrate financial need as determined by FAFSA or Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA/MHEC One App)
Must complete and file FAFSA or MHEC One App by March 1 (or institution-specific deadline)
Must maintain satisfactory academic progress to renew award
Must file FAFSA or MHEC One App each year to renew
May receive the Part-Time Grant for a maximum of eight years total
Eligibility and award selection determined by the institution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and file the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) or submit the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA/MHEC One App) online through MDCAPS by March 1. It is strongly suggested to file as soon as possible. Contact the financial aid office of your institution to apply and to check for any additional institution-specific deadlines. Recipients are selected and awarded by the institution.

structured_extraction.program_name: Richard W. Collins III Leadership with Honor Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This scholarship program promotes the state's interests in educating diverse student bodies and achieving diversity in Reserve Officer Training Corps (ROTC) programs by providing financial assistance to eligible minority students and students from groups historically underrepresented in ROTC. The program supports current or prospective undergraduate and graduate students, including undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition, who are enrolled in ROTC programs at designated Maryland Historically Black Colleges and Universities. The program prioritizes recipients with demonstrated financial need and awards renewable scholarships not to exceed the recipient's education expenses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual renewable scholarship awards not to exceed the recipient's education expenses. Minimum award of $500 per semester and $1,000 per academic year. Recipients with demonstrated financial need are prioritized. Awards are renewable for up to three additional years if the recipient continues to meet eligibility and enrollment requirements and maintains satisfactory academic progress toward a degree as defined by the institution. Awards are subject to the availability of funds and may be adjusted or canceled if total financial assistance (including state aid and Veterans Educational Benefits) exceeds cost of attendance. Payment is made to the institution approximately four weeks after institutional certification is completed and returned to OSFA.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: For 2026-2027: Applications open January 15, 2026 through October 15, 2026. FAFSA or MHEC One App due by July 15, 2026. Richard Collins application with all required documentation due by October 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current or prospective full-time and part-time undergraduate and graduate degree-seeking students who are minority students or members of groups historically underrepresented in ROTC programs, including undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition, enrolled at Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, or University of Maryland Eastern Shore and participating in a ROTC program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education expenses including tuition, fees, and other costs associated with degree-seeking study at eligible institutions for students enrolled in ROTC programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Students must be enrolled full-time or part-time at one of four designated Maryland institutions: Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, or University of Maryland Eastern Shore. Students must be determined eligible for in-state tuition by their institution.
requirements_list: Must be a current or prospective full-time or part-time degree-seeking undergraduate or graduate student in a certificate, undergraduate, graduate certificate, or graduate degree program, or an undocumented student eligible for in-state tuition
Must be identified by the institution as a minority student or member of another group historically underrepresented in ROTC programs
Must be enrolled full-time (12+ credits) or part-time (6-11 credits) at Bowie State University, Coppin State University, Morgan State University, or University of Maryland Eastern Shore
Must be a current member of a ROTC program at the institution
Must be determined eligible for in-state tuition by the institution
Must not falsify or conceal material facts in connection with the application
Must submit Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) or MHEC One App (for undocumented students) by July 15
Must submit institutional certification form completed by the institution confirming ROTC program membership
Must maintain satisfactory academic progress toward a degree and meet the institution's standards for renewal
Must pledge to remain drug-free for the full term of the award
Must maintain the satisfactory academic progress standards of the institution
If dependent, must provide parental information and have one parent sign and submit the Parent Signature Page
Males aged 18-25 must register with Selective Service System and provide proof of registration
All required documents must be submitted by the closing date (October 15)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Create an MDCAPS account at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us. 2. Submit the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) online at https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa or the MHEC One App (for undocumented students) through MDCAPS by July 15. 3. Complete the online Richard Collins III Leadership with Honor Scholarship application through MDCAPS by October 15. 4. Upload the institutional certification form completed by your institution and documentation confirming ROTC program membership to your MDCAPS account using secure upload. 5. If you are a dependent student, download and have your parent(s) complete and submit the Parent Signature Page to MHEC at the Office of Student Financial Assistance by the closing date. 6. Check your Award Status in MDCAPS for application status updates. 7. If awarded, you will be notified by email and must accept your award online through MDCAPS within 2 weeks of notification or the award will be canceled. 8. At the beginning of each semester, your institution will certify you meet the requirements and your award will be processed for payment approximately four weeks after certification is returned to OSFA.

structured_extraction.program_name: Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A recurring tax credit program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission that provides financial relief to Maryland residents burdened by student loan debt. The program allocates up to $18 million in tax credits annually to eligible applicants who have incurred undergraduate and/or graduate student loan debt, whether they attended in-state or out-of-state institutions. Tax credits are applied to the recipient's Maryland state income tax return. Recipients must use the full amount of the tax credit toward payment of eligible student loans and provide proof of doing so, or return the credit. Maryland State employees with student loan debt receive priority consideration. Credit amounts vary by year and institution type (e.g., in-state vs. out-of-state attendees).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to $18 million in tax credits annually to Maryland residents. Credits are applied directly to the recipient's Maryland state income tax return. Credit amounts vary by year and institution type: in recent years, residents who attended in-state institutions received $1,000 each, while those who attended out-of-state institutions received $813–$883 each. Recipients must use the full tax credit amount to pay eligible student loans and must provide proof of payment within two years, or return the credit. Applications are accepted between July 1 and September 15 each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with student loan debt who file Maryland state income taxes. Eligible applicants must have attended either Maryland or out-of-state institutions. Maryland State employees with student loan debt receive priority consideration.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit must be used to pay off existing eligible student loan debt. Recipients must prove the full amount of the tax credit was applied toward their outstanding student loan balance within two years of receipt.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Maryland residents statewide. Applicants must maintain Maryland residency for the applicable tax year and file Maryland state income taxes.
requirements_list: Claim and maintain Maryland residency for the applicable tax year
File Maryland state income taxes for the applicable tax year
Have initially incurred at least $20,000 in undergraduate and/or graduate student loan debt
Have at least $5,000 in outstanding student loan debt at the time of applying for the tax credit
Currently make payments on student loans
Complete and submit an application to the Maryland Higher Education Commission by September 15 of the applicable year
Submit all required graduate and/or undergraduate student loan information, including Maryland income tax information and college transcripts
Agree to pay the complete tax credit received into outstanding loan balance within two years and provide a record of the payment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted between July 1 and September 15 each year. Applicants should visit the Maryland Higher Education Commission website at https://mhec.maryland.gov/preparing/pages/studentloandebtrelieftaxcredit.aspx to access the application. Complete the application with all required student loan information, Maryland income tax information, and college transcripts, and submit to the Maryland Higher Education Commission by the September 15 deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Teaching Fellows for Maryland Scholarship provides financial assistance to students pursuing undergraduate or graduate degrees leading to a Maryland professional teacher's certificate. Recipients must commit to working as public school or public prekindergarten teachers in Maryland upon completion of their studies, either in high-needs schools (as identified by the Maryland State Department of Education) or in grade levels or content areas where there is a shortage of qualified educators, or in schools where at least 50% of students are eligible for free or reduced-price meals (FRPM). The program supports aspiring teachers, career changers, and teaching assistants with at least two years of experience at Maryland public schools or public prekindergarten programs. Awards cover tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board, with a service obligation attached. Over $1.9 million in total awards has been distributed to 106 students.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: At Maryland public senior higher education institutions, the scholarship covers 100% of annual tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board for resident undergraduate or graduate students. At Maryland private nonprofit institutions, the award is the lesser of: (1) 100% of annual tuition and mandatory fees at the University of Maryland College Park plus 100% of room and board at the institution, or (2) 50% of annual tuition and mandatory fees at the institution plus 100% of room and board. Private nonprofit institutions must provide a matching scholarship equal to the State award for tuition and fees only (not required for room and board). Students with off-campus or with-parent housing receive a housing allowance based on room and board costs provided by their institution. Recipients may renew the award for up to three additional years (four years for five-year degree programs) if they maintain full-time or part-time enrollment and satisfactory academic progress. At the beginning of each semester, the recipient's institution certifies that the student meets award requirements, and payment is processed approximately four weeks after certification. Undergraduate recipients must fulfill a service obligation of one year for each year of scholarship received; graduate recipients must fulfill two years of service for each year of scholarship received (minimum two years total in qualifying positions). Service obligation begins one year after degree completion and must be fulfilled at schools where at least 50% of students are eligible for free or reduced-price meals, or in a high-needs school or shortage grade level/content area. Recipients must submit an Annual Service Questionnaire on an annual basis to verify employment history until the service obligation is fulfilled. Over $1.9 million in total awards has been distributed to 106 students.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application for the 2026-2027 academic year will become available on January 15, 2026, and will close on October 15, 2026. A December 1 deadline also applies per some program materials.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Higher Education Commission Office of Student Financial Assistance
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school seniors, undergraduate students, graduate students, college graduates, career changers, and teaching assistants with at least 2 years of experience at Maryland public schools or public prekindergarten programs who are enrolled or planning to enroll at an eligible institution in an undergraduate or graduate program leading to a Maryland professional teacher's certificate and who commit to teaching in Maryland public schools or public prekindergarten programs in high-needs areas, shortage fields, or schools where at least 50% of students are eligible for free or reduced-price meals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board (or a housing allowance for off-campus/parental housing) for undergraduate or graduate studies leading to a Maryland professional teacher's certificate at eligible Maryland institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. State residency is no longer required for applicants. Recipients must commit to working as a public school or public prekindergarten teacher in Maryland upon completion of studies, in a high-needs school as identified by the Maryland State Department of Education or in a grade level or content area with a shortage of qualified educators. If no qualifying positions are available, recipients may teach in any public school or public prekindergarten program in Maryland. Students must attend an eligible Maryland institution.

All applicants must submit an Institutional Certification Form completed by their institution
Must sign and return a promissory note agreeing to fulfill the service obligation
