Graduate recipients must fulfill a service obligation of two years for each year of scholarship received; minimum 2 years total
Recipients must maintain satisfactory academic progress and institutional standards for renewal awards
Service obligation must be fulfilled at schools where at least 50% of students are eligible for free or reduced-price meals, or in a high-needs school or shortage grade level/content area
Recipients must become professionally certified to teach in Maryland within 2 years after completing degree program
Recipients are required to begin employment in Maryland one year after degree completion
Recipients must verify employment history on an annual basis by submitting an Annual Service Questionnaire until service obligation is fulfilled
If recipient does not complete degree, recipient must repay scholarship with interest
Recipients must remain drug-free for the full term of the award; unlawful use of drugs and alcohol may endanger enrollment and financial aid
Individuals may not falsify or conceal material facts in application; subject to criminal prosecution if they do
Office of Student Financial Assistance must be notified in writing of address and/or telephone number changes
If recipient holds this scholarship with any other award requiring a service obligation, recipient must perform service in consecutive years
Awards are subject to availability of funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) using the MHEC One App. Required documents include appropriate transcripts (high school transcript after first semester of senior year for high school applicants, or college/final high school transcript for current post-secondary students), a typed essay of at least 600 words detailing exceptional dedication to or aptitude for teaching, and an Institutional Certification Form completed by the institution. Teaching assistants must submit a Teaching Assistant Employer Verification Form in lieu of a transcript. All required documents must be submitted through the applicant's MDCAPS account by the closing date. Recipients must sign a promissory note for the service obligation. At the beginning of each semester, the recipient's institution will be asked to certify that the student meets the requirements of the award. When the institution completes the certification and returns it to the Office of Student Financial Assistance, the award will be processed for payment, occurring approximately four weeks after certification. Award is contingent on availability of funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Title IX Campus Sexual Assault Proceedings - Attorney Reimbursement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: MHEC reimburses attorney fees and certain costs for legal representation of students in Title IX campus sexual assault proceedings at Maryland higher education institutions. The program covers attorneys on the MHEC Attorney List as well as non-list attorneys, and provides reimbursement at a set hourly rate up to a maximum number of hours per case, along with travel cost reimbursement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Attorneys representing students in Title IX proceedings may receive reimbursement at a rate of $120 per hour (as of FY 2025), billed in increments of 6 minutes or less, up to a maximum of 20 hours per case. For MHEC list attorneys, any representation beyond 20 hours must be provided pro bono (without charge). For non-list attorneys, the student is responsible for all fees beyond 20 hours. MHEC list attorneys must charge fees equivalent to those paid under civil legal services programs administered by the Maryland legal services corporation (currently $100 per hour), and must certify they have not and will not charge clients any costs and fees in excess of this reduced fee rate. Travel costs including mileage (at $0.70 per mile for FY 2025), tolls, public transit, and parking are reimbursable up to $200 per case. Reimbursement is subject to availability of appropriated funds. Payment requests must be submitted within 60 days of termination of representation, and allow at least 60 days for processing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: All payment requests should be submitted within 60 days of termination of representation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Attorneys providing legal representation to students involved in Title IX campus sexual assault proceedings at Maryland higher education institutions. Attorneys do not need to be on the MHEC Attorney List to request payment. Students at Maryland higher education institutions participating in Title IX proceedings also benefit from this program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Attorney fees for legal representation in Title IX proceedings only. Travel costs including mileage, tolls, public transit, and parking. Reimbursement does not cover office expenses such as copies, postage, or secretarial/paralegal time.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland higher education institutions. Students must be participating in Title IX proceedings at a Maryland higher education institution.
requirements_list: Legal services must be provided on or after August 1, 2019
Representation must be for Title IX proceedings only — no payment for civil, criminal, or non-Title IX student disciplinary proceedings
Attorney fees capped at $120 per hour, billed in increments of 6 minutes or less
Maximum allowable limit of 20 hours per case

For MHEC list attorneys: must charge fees equivalent to those paid under civil legal services programs administered by the Maryland legal services corporation under Human Services Article, Title 11, Annotated Code of Maryland (currently $100 per hour) and must certify they have not and will not charge clients any costs and fees in excess of this reduced fee rate; representation beyond 20 hours must be provided pro bono
For non-list attorneys: student is responsible for all fees beyond 20 hours
Travel cost reimbursement limited to $200 per case
Submission deadline is within 60 days of termination of representation

Attorney must submit Payment Request Form, Additional Information Form, Retainer/Representation Agreement, Detailed Billing Statement, Student Certification Form (completed by student), and first notice of proceedings from institution
Travel cost reimbursement requests must include receipts
Submissions must include federal employer identification number (FEIN)
Reimbursement subject to availability of appropriated funds
Attorney must complete form indicating MHEC Attorney List status, services provided, and hours requested
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Attorney obtains student signature on the Student Certification Form (student must authorize representation for payment and confirm receipt of services). 2. Attorney completes the Payment Request Form (including MHEC Attorney List status, representation dates, services provided, and hours requested). 3. Attorney completes the Additional Information Form (including attorney information, proceeding details, and representation information). 4. Attorney submits payment request to TitleIXproceedings.MHEC@maryland.gov within 60 days of termination of representation in a single PDF document containing: (a) Payment Request Form, (b) Additional Information Form, (c) copy of retainer/representation agreement (may be redacted), (d) detailed billing statement (may be redacted), (e) Cost Reimbursement Form if applicable with receipts, (f) Student Certification Form signed by student, and (g) copy of first notice of proceedings provided to student by college/university under Md. Code Ann., Educ. § 11-601(d)(3)(iv) or § 11-601(d)(4)(i). 5. MHEC processes request (allow at least 60 days for processing). 6. MHEC list attorneys must certify in writing that they have not and will not charge clients any costs and fees in excess of the reduced fee rate ($100 per hour).

structured_extraction.program_name: Tuition Reduction for Non-Resident Nursing Students
structured_extraction.program_description: A tuition reduction program that helps out-of-state students enrolled in nursing programs at public colleges and universities in Maryland pay the same tuition as Maryland residents. The assistance covers the difference between non-resident and resident tuition rates (the tuition differential), effectively allowing non-resident students to pay in-state tuition rates. Awards are renewable for additional years provided students maintain satisfactory academic progress and remain enrolled in an eligible nursing program. Recipients must fulfill a service obligation as a full-time nurse in a hospital or related institution or repay the scholarship with interest.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The annual award amount is the tuition differential — the difference between the amount of tuition paid by an out-of-state student and the amount paid by an in-state student at the same institution, in the same nursing program, for the identical number of credit hours. The institution adjusts tuition charges so that the student pays in-state tuition rates. Awards are renewable for up to three additional years at four-year institutions or one additional year at two-year institutions, provided the student maintains satisfactory academic progress and remains enrolled in an eligible nursing program. Full-time enrollment is defined as 12 or more credits per semester; part-time enrollment is 6-11 credits per semester. Audited courses cannot be used to meet minimum credit hour requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application for the 2025-2026 academic year closes on April 1, 2026. The application for the 2026-2027 academic year becomes available January 15, 2026 and closes October 15, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-resident students enrolled in nursing programs at two-year or four-year public institutions in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition reduction to bring non-resident students' tuition rates to the same level as Maryland resident students in nursing programs at public institutions in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to non-residents of Maryland attending two-year or four-year public institutions in Maryland. Recipients must work as full-time nurses in a hospital or related institution (which includes organized institutions, environments or homes that provide domiciliary, personal, or nursing care for two or more unrelated individuals) for four years (if from a four-year institution) or two years (if from a two-year institution), or repay the scholarship with interest.
requirements_list: Be a resident of a state other than Maryland
Be enrolled each semester as a degree-seeking full-time (12+ credits per semester) or part-time (6-11 credits per semester) undergraduate
Be accepted into and remain enrolled in a nursing program leading to a degree in nursing at a Maryland community college or four-year public institution
Audited courses cannot be used to reach minimum credit hour requirements
Maintain satisfactory academic progress standards as defined by the institution
Remain enrolled in an eligible nursing program
Pledge to remain drug-free for the full term of the assistance

Sign and return a promissory note agreeing to serve as a full-time nurse (35 hours or more per week) in a Maryland hospital or related institution for four years (if attending a four-year institution) or two years (if attending a two-year institution), or repay the scholarship with interest
Begin service within six months of graduation
If holding this scholarship with another award requiring a service obligation, service must be performed in consecutive years
If failing to meet any eligibility requirement, the award will be canceled
If failing to remain eligible for the program, must still fulfill the obligations of the promissory note or the assistance must be repaid with interest
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) using the MHEC One App. Once an application is approved by the Office of Student Financial Assistance (OSFA), the applicant and their institution are informed in writing. The institution is responsible for making the adjustment in tuition charges and for reporting to OSFA the amount of assistance for each student annually.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tuition Waiver for Foster Care Recipients
structured_extraction.program_description: A financial assistance program that waives tuition and mandatory fees for eligible foster care youth and former foster care youth pursuing higher education at Maryland public institutions. The waiver covers enrollment in associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate programs at any Maryland public college or university. Administered jointly by the Maryland Higher Education Commission and the Maryland Department of Human Services, the program supports individuals who have experienced out-of-home placement and are seeking to continue their education before age 25.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The waiver exempts eligible individuals from paying tuition and mandatory fees (including registration fees and other mandatory fees required for enrollment) at any Maryland public institution of higher education. The amount varies by institution based on their tuition rates. The waiver does not cover room, board, books, or transportation. Scholarships or grants awarded to a foster care recipient may not be applied to tuition, as it is already waived. Eligibility is determined in part through the FAFSA application process, and funds may be provided on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 1st annually (FAFSA priority deadline); contact financial aid office for institution-specific deadlines
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals under the age of 25 who are current or former foster care recipients who have been placed in out-of-home placement by the Maryland Department of Human Services and are enrolled or planning to enroll full-time or part-time in an associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate program at a Maryland public college or university.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and mandatory fees (including registration fees and other mandatory enrollment fees) at Maryland public institutions of higher education for associate degree, bachelor's degree, or vocational certificate programs. Does not cover room, board, books, or transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland only. Applicants must have resided in an out-of-home placement in Maryland at specific trigger points (high school graduation, GED completion, 18th birthday, or other specified conditions involving the Maryland foster care system). Program is available at all Maryland public colleges and universities statewide.
requirements_list: Must be under age 25 at the time of enrollment
Must be enrolled full-time or part-time in an associate, bachelor's, or vocational certificate program at a Maryland public institution of higher education on or before reaching age 25
Must have been placed in out-of-home placement by the Maryland Department of Human Services

Must meet one of the following residency/placement conditions: (1) Resided in out-of-home placement in Maryland at the time of high school graduation or GED completion; (2) Resided in out-of-home placement in Maryland at the time of 18th birthday; (3) Resided in out-of-home placement on 13th birthday and was placed into guardianship or adopted out of out-of-home placement after 13th birthday; or (4) Resided in out-of-home placement in Maryland for at least 1 year on or after 13th birthday and returned to live with parents after placement ended
Younger siblings of eligible foster care recipients may qualify if concurrently placed into guardianship or adopted by the same guardianship or adoptive family
Must file the FAFSA (https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa) or the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) via the MHEC One App by the March 1st priority deadline
Undocumented applicants should consult with the financial aid office at the Maryland public institution they plan to attend
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa or the Maryland State Financial Aid Application (MSFAA) via the MHEC One App at http://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us/ by the March 1st priority deadline. 2. Contact the financial aid office at the Maryland public institution you are currently attending or plan to attend. Eligibility information is provided to Maryland public colleges and universities by the Maryland Department of Human Services. 3. You may also contact your caseworker or the Independent Living Coordinator at your local department of social services for assistance. 4. Undocumented applicants should consult with the financial aid office at the Maryland public institution they plan to attend.

structured_extraction.program_name: Tuition Waiver for Maryland National Guard
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides tuition assistance to individuals serving in the Maryland National Guard.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tuition waiver for National Guard members attending educational institutions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland National Guard members.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition for education and training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be serving in the Maryland National Guard

structured_extraction.program_description: An incentive program that awards $50,000 college scholarships to encourage young people aged 12-17 to get vaccinated against COVID-19. Winners receive scholarships covering full tuition and fees at Maryland public universities, distributed through Maryland529 college savings plans, selected through random drawings. The program awarded a total of $1 million across twenty winners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Twenty winners each receive a $50,000 scholarship totaling $1 million in awards, distributed through Maryland529 programs. For winners ages 12-14, the award is distributed as a 4-Year Maryland Prepaid College Trust Account funded with $50,000. For winners ages 15-17, a Maryland College Investment Plan contribution of $50,000 is awarded. The scholarship covers full tuition and fees at a public, in-state institution of higher education. Winners are selected through random drawings: two winners per week for eight weeks beginning July 12, plus four winners on Labor Day (September 6), using the same random number generator used for the $2 Million VaxCash Promotion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents aged 12 to 17 years old who have been or will be vaccinated against COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full tuition and fees at a public, in-state Maryland institution of higher education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must both live and be vaccinated in Maryland. The city or county of winners will be published, though winners may otherwise remain anonymous.
requirements_list: Must be between 12 and 17 years old
Must live in Maryland
Must be vaccinated against COVID-19 in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible youth who are vaccinated in Maryland are automatically entered. Random drawings are held beginning July 12, selecting two winners per week for eight weeks. On Labor Day (September 6), four additional winners are selected. Winners are chosen using the same random number generator used for the $2 Million VaxCash Promotion. Winners may remain anonymous, though their city or county will be published.

structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program that provides financial assistance to students enrolling in approved non-credit certificate programs at participating Maryland Community Colleges. The program supports workforce development pathways that lead to apprenticeships, employment, licensure, or job skill enhancement. Awards may be renewed for an additional developmental sequence and can be combined with other state grants or scholarships provided the total does not exceed the student's total cost of attendance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A maximum annual award of $2,000 per student to pay for tuition, mandatory fees, and associated costs of attendance at a participating Maryland Community College. Funds cannot exceed the student's unmet costs after other grants or scholarships are applied. The award may be renewed for an additional developmental sequence. The scholarship may be combined with other state grants or scholarships as long as the total does not exceed the student's total cost of attendance, and cannot duplicate costs already covered by another grant, scholarship, or employer.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Contact your college financial aid office for application deadlines
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students who are Maryland residents, Maryland high school graduates, or active duty U.S. Military members stationed in, residing in, or domiciled in Maryland, who are enrolling in an approved non-credit Workforce Development Sequence at a participating Maryland Community College.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, mandatory fees, and associated costs of attendance at a participating Maryland Community College for non-credit workforce development sequence programs related to job preparation, registered apprenticeships, licensure, certification, or job skill enhancement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide at participating Maryland Community Colleges. Applicants must be Maryland residents, Maryland high school graduates, or active duty U.S. Military members stationed in, residing in, or domiciled in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident or Maryland high school graduate, OR an active duty U.S. Military member stationed in, residing in, or domiciled in Maryland
Must enroll in an eligible Workforce Development Sequence at a participating Maryland Community College
Courses must be non-credited and related to job preparation, registered apprenticeship, licensure or certification, or job skill enhancement
Program must lead to apprenticeships, employment, licensure, or job skill enhancement
Individual college may have additional eligibility criteria
Contact your college financial aid office to apply and obtain deadline information
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must contact their college financial aid office to apply and obtain application deadline information. Award recipients may be eligible to receive the award for an additional developmental sequence by contacting their financial aid office.

structured_extraction.program_name: Workforce Shortage Student Assistance Grant Program (WSSAG)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Workforce Shortage Student Assistance Grant Program provides financial assistance to Maryland residents who are degree-seeking students planning to work in specific career fields with workforce shortages upon graduation. Eligible fields include child care, human services, teaching, nursing, physical and occupational therapy, social work, and public service. Students must commit to working in Maryland in their chosen field after graduation to fulfill a service obligation. Awards are available to full-time and part-time students enrolled at two-year or four-year Maryland colleges and universities, and are renewable for up to five years provided eligibility requirements are maintained.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants based on institution type and enrollment status: $2,000 per year for full-time community college students (12+ credits per semester) or $1,000 per year for part-time community college students (6-11 credits per semester). For four-year institutions: $4,000 per year for full-time students (undergraduate 12+ credits per semester or graduate 9+ credits per semester) or $2,000 per year for part-time students (undergraduate 6-11 credits per semester or graduate 6-8 credits per semester). Awards are automatically renewed for up to a maximum of five years as long as the student continues to meet all eligibility requirements. The total dollar amount of all State awards may not exceed the student's cost of attendance (as determined by the school's financial aid office) or $28,000, whichever is less. Recipients must fulfill a service obligation of one year for each year of scholarship received if working full-time (35+ hours per week), or two years for each year received if working part-time (at least 20 hours per week) in Maryland. Service obligation must begin within one year of degree completion and cannot be fulfilled prior to completion. If the service obligation is not met, the grant must be repaid with interest.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application and all supporting documents must be received by July 1 to be considered on-time. FAFSA (optional but recommended) by June 1. For the 2025-2026 academic year, applications are due by April 1, 2026. For the 2026-2027 academic year, applications are due by October 15, 2026. Applications available each year starting in mid-April through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland resident students who are degree-seeking, enrolled full-time or part-time at two-year or four-year Maryland colleges or universities, pursuing majors in eligible workforce shortage fields including child care, human services, teaching, nursing, physical and occupational therapy, social work, and public service, and planning to work in those fields in Maryland after graduation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and educational expenses for degree programs in eligible workforce shortage fields, including child care, human services, teaching, nursing, physical and occupational therapy, social work, and public service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must be a Maryland resident. If a dependent student, the parent must also be a Maryland resident. Student must enroll at a Maryland two-year or four-year college or university and must work in Maryland in their chosen field to satisfy the service obligation.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident; if dependent, parent must also be Maryland resident
Enroll as a full-time or part-time degree-seeking undergraduate or graduate student at a two-year or four-year Maryland college or university

For undergraduates: full-time requires 12+ credits per semester; part-time requires 6-11 credits per semester; may enroll for less than 6 credits in a semester but must earn at least 12 credit hours per academic year including summer term

For graduate students: full-time requires 9+ credits per semester; part-time requires 6-8 credits per semester; may enroll for less than 6 credits in a semester but must earn at least 9 credit hours per academic year including summer term
Audited courses cannot be used to reach minimum credit hour requirements for full-time or part-time status

Enroll in an eligible major leading to employment in an eligible workforce shortage field (child care, human services, teaching, nursing, physical and occupational therapy, social work, public service)
Maintain satisfactory academic progress standards of the institution
Have a cumulative unweighted GPA (will be recalculated to 4.0 scale if necessary)
File the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) for need-based ranking (optional but recommended; influences award order and must be filed by July 1 for consideration)
Nursing and physical or occupational therapy students must include an acceptance letter from their department
Submit official or unofficial transcripts from all institutions attended, including the student's full name, institution name or letterhead, and GPA
Sign and return a promissory note agreeing to fulfill service obligation within one year of degree completion
Begin employment in the eligible field within one year of completing the degree

Fulfill service obligation: one year for each year of scholarship received if working full-time (35+ hours per week), or two years for each year received if working part-time (at least 20 hours per week)

Not have previously received a scholarship under MHEC's former programs (Child Care Provider; Developmental Disabilities, Mental Health, Child Welfare, and Juvenile Justice Workforce Tuition Assistance Program) or not be currently receiving those awards
May receive other State scholarship awards, but total dollar amount of all State awards cannot exceed cost of attendance or $28,000, whichever is less
Pledge to remain drug-free for the full term of the award
Not falsify or conceal material facts in connection with the application (subject to criminal prosecution if violated)
Notify the Office of Student Financial Assistance in writing of any address and/or telephone number changes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available each year through the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS) starting in mid-April. Apply online at https://mdcaps.mhec.state.md.us via the MHEC One App. Create a user ID and password, and activate your account using the activation link sent via email. File the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at www.fafsa.gov by June 1 (optional but recommended, as it influences award order based on financial need). Submit the WSSAG application and all required documentation through MDCAPS by uploading documents through your account using the Electronic File Upload tool by July 1 to be considered on-time. Faxed documents are not acceptable. Nursing and physical/occupational therapy students must include acceptance letters from their departments. Submit official or unofficial transcripts from all institutions. At the beginning of each semester, your institution will certify that you meet the requirements; payment will be processed and made approximately four weeks after certification. Students are ranked first by Grade Point Average (GPA) within the following ranges (3.8-4.0, 3.6-3.79, 3.4-3.59, 3.0-3.39, 2.9 and below), and then by financial need within each GPA range. If awarded, you will be notified by email with an award offer and must login to MDCAPS to accept your award within three weeks of notification and submit the online promissory note. Awards are subject to availability of funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funding opportunities for State, County, and Local law enforcement agencies to support traffic safety initiatives including overtime enforcement, equipment, and training focused on highway safety priorities such as impaired driving prevention, distracted driving prevention, speeding and aggressive driving prevention, occupant protection, and pedestrian and bicyclist safety.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided as reimbursement only, with funds disbursed after expenses are incurred. Funding is available for officer overtime for enforcement patrols, training, and equipment. Five emphasis areas receive funding: Aggressive Driving (overtime for enforcement patrols, training, and equipment); Distracted Driving (overtime for enforcement patrols and training); Impaired Driving (overtime for saturation patrols and checkpoints, training, and equipment); Occupant Protection (overtime for enforcement patrols, training, and equipment); and Pedestrian/Bicycle Safety (overtime for enforcement patrols, training, and equipment).
structured_extraction.program_audience: State, County, and Local law enforcement agencies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Officer overtime for enforcement patrols, training, and equipment. Funding may be used for year-round enforcement strategies targeting the five emphasis areas: aggressive driving, distracted driving, impaired driving, occupant protection, and pedestrian and bicyclist safety. Operations must be data-driven and targeted based on crash and citation data.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; available to State, County, and Local law enforcement agencies throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Operations must be data-driven
Target locations must be based on crash and citation data
Expenses must be incurred before funds are disbursed (reimbursement only)

Projects must focus on one or more of Maryland's highway safety priorities: impaired driving prevention, distracted driving prevention, speeding and aggressive driving prevention, occupant protection, and pedestrian and bicyclist safety
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants are encouraged to develop proposals for enforcement initiatives focusing on Maryland's highway safety priorities. Applications are submitted through the Grants & Projects for Safety (GPS) system. Log in to the GPS portal at https://gps.mva.maryland.gov/Web/Default to submit applications.

structured_extraction.program_name: African American Heritage Preservation Program Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides capital grants to assist in the preservation of buildings, sites, and communities significant to African American history and culture in Maryland. Jointly administered by the Maryland Historical Trust and the Maryland Commission on African American History and Culture, funding supports preservation, restoration, rehabilitation, and interpretation of historic properties with African American heritage connections. Eligible applicants include nonprofit organizations, local governments, businesses, and individuals.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Capital grants up to $250,000 per project. No match is required. The program typically has an annual budget of $5 million for grants. Funds support preservation or acquisition of buildings, sites, or structures significant to African American history; restoration or rehabilitation of historic sites; development of new facilities to interpret or celebrate African American history; stabilization of endangered properties; and development of plans, specifications, and architectural or engineering services directly related to pre-construction work. Funds cannot pay for routine maintenance, fundraising expenses, research, exhibits, or work that has already started or been completed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, businesses, and individuals interested in preserving buildings, sites, and communities significant to African American history and culture in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preservation or acquisition of buildings, sites, or structures significant to African American history; restoration or rehabilitation of historic sites; development of new facilities to interpret or celebrate African American history; stabilization of endangered properties; development of plans, specifications, and architectural, engineering, or other special services directly related to pre-construction work. Funds cannot pay for routine maintenance, fundraising expenses, research, exhibits, or work that has already started or been completed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must be located in Maryland
Project must demonstrate a clear, direct connection to African American history, culture, or heritage
Property owner permission must be provided as part of the application
Projects must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties
Property or proposed use must have an association with African American heritage and should benefit the public to be competitive
For religious properties: grants can generally only fund structural or exterior work, not interior worship spaces or elements bearing religious imagery
For cemeteries: applicant must demonstrate clear property ownership
Work that is already underway or completed is not eligible for funding
If the property is listed or eligible for the National Register, the owner must convey a term preservation easement to the Maryland Historical Trust
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review grant guidelines and sample materials. Confirm applicant and project eligibility. Attend pre-application workshop or webinar. Prepare required attachments including cost estimates, photographs, letters of support, and proof of ownership or site control. Submit completed application through the grants portal before the deadline of July 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM. The agency typically announces decisions by December each year.

structured_extraction.program_description: Annual funding for historic preservation projects and programs carried out by local governments that participate in the Certified Local Government Program. Grants help communities strengthen preservation programs, document historic resources, and promote education and outreach.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund commissioner and staff training as well as non-capital projects. Commissioner and staff training grants are non-competitive up to an amount specified in grant guidelines each year. Project grants are competitive. Maximum grant request for projects is $25,000. No match requirement, but a 15% match is encouraged. Funding comes from the Maryland Historical Trust's Historic Preservation Fund allocation from the National Park Service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Local Government Program participants. Only CLGs are eligible to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commissioner and staff training, historic property surveys, National Register of Historic Places nominations, design guidelines for historic districts, training for local preservation commission members, preservation plans or planning studies, and public education and outreach about preservation topics.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all Certified Local Governments in Maryland statewide, subject to available federal funding.
requirements_list: Must be a Certified Local Government participating in the CLG Program
Projects must be non-capital projects that support local preservation efforts or commissioner and staff training
Maximum grant request for projects: $25,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review grant guidelines emailed to CLG contacts when the application round opens. Confirm project eligibility and consult with MHT staff as needed. Submit a completed application through the MHT grants portal before the posted deadline. Applications open early February with a deadline at the end of February.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Rehabilitation Tax Credits for Historic Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program administered jointly by the Maryland Historical Trust (serving as the State Historic Preservation Office) and the National Park Service. The program provides a 20% federal income tax credit on qualified rehabilitation expenditures for income-producing historic buildings certified as qualified historic structures. There is no cap on the amount of the federal credit. The program aims to incentivize investment in historic buildings, create jobs, and revitalize communities.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A federal income tax credit equal to 20% of qualified rehabilitation expenditures for eligible income-producing historic properties. There is no cap on the amount of the federal credit. The rehabilitation project must be substantial, defined as a minimum of $5,000 or the adjusted basis of the building, whichever is greater. Projects typically must be completed within a 24-month period. The Maryland Historical Trust assists with site visits, project advice, and makes certification recommendations to the National Park Service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, private investors, businesses, non-profits, and individuals who own income-producing historic buildings listed in or eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of certified historic structures and income-producing historic buildings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties listed in the National Register of Historic Places or eligible for listing; nationwide program available for eligible income-producing properties anywhere in Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be listed in or eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places
Property must be determined by the National Park Service to be a certified historic structure
Property must be income-producing
Rehabilitation project must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
Rehabilitation project must be substantial, with a minimum of $5,000 or the adjusted basis of the building, whichever is greater
Rehabilitation project typically must be completed within a 24-month period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the application from the National Park Service website, complete it with details about your rehabilitation project, and submit the Historic Preservation Certification Application electronically using current forms. First submit to the Maryland Historical Trust, which reviews it, assists with site visits and project advice, and forwards it to the National Park Service for final approval and certification.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding for the preservation of Maryland's historic properties and sites. Supports important and urgently needed preservation projects that benefit the public, including acquiring historic properties, stabilizing and rehabilitating them, and developing pre-construction plans and specifications. Grants of up to $100,000 are available to nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and individuals for capital projects that promote acquisition, rehabilitation, restoration, or predevelopment of historic properties. Energy projects as part of acquisition or rehabilitation are also eligible.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $100,000 per project. The program typically has about $600,000 available for grants each year. A 1:1 cash match is required for all applicants other than nonprofit organizations. If a property receives grant funding, a historic preservation easement on the property must be conveyed to the Maryland Historical Trust. Energy projects as part of acquisition or rehabilitation are eligible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March (FY26 grant round anticipated to open February 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, local governments, businesses, and individuals seeking to preserve historic properties listed in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquiring historic properties such as buildings, bridges, and other qualifying structures and sites; stabilizing, rehabilitating, or restoring historic properties; developing plans, specifications, and architectural or engineering services for pre-construction work; energy projects as part of acquisition or rehabilitation. Funds cannot be used for routine maintenance, fundraising expenses, research, exhibits, or work already started or completed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Projects must be for properties listed in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places.
requirements_list: Property must be listed in or determined eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places, either individually or as part of a historic district
Property owner permission must be provided as part of the grant application
Projects must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties
1:1 cash match required for all applicants other than nonprofits
Nonprofit and local government applicants may fund pre-construction planning; other applicants may not
Religious properties can generally only fund structural or exterior work, not interior worship spaces or elements bearing religious imagery
Cemeteries may qualify but applicant must demonstrate clear property ownership
If property receives grant funding, a historic preservation easement must be conveyed to MHT
Work that is already in progress or completed is not eligible for funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review current grant guidelines and sample materials. 2. Confirm applicant and project eligibility. 3. Attend pre-application workshop or webinar. 4. Prepare required attachments including cost estimates, photographs, letters of support, and proof of ownership or site control. 5. Submit completed application through the grants portal before the posted deadline. Applications are usually available in February and due in mid-March. The agency makes decisions by July each year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Historic Preservation Loan Program for Capital Projects
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides loan assistance to nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and individuals for the acquisition, rehabilitation, refinancing, or predevelopment costs of historic properties that cannot access traditional financing. Energy projects as part of an acquisition or rehabilitation/restoration are eligible expenditures. Certain qualified nonprofit organizations are also eligible for nonrepayable fund transfers (similar to grants) beginning in FY 2024.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with terms up to two years for pre-development projects and up to twenty years for other projects. Interest rates for businesses and individuals are set at 1/8 percent higher than the most recent State general obligation bonds. Loan amount depends on available funds, borrower's ability to repay, and property value, typically not exceeding 80% of appraised value. Qualified nonprofit organizations may also receive nonrepayable fund transfers for acquiring properties for resale, restoring properties, or providing loans to other organizations and individuals. Energy projects as part of acquisition or rehabilitation are eligible expenditures.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually. Contact program administrator. The FY25 application submission period is now closed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and individuals who own or want to acquire eligible historic properties and cannot access traditional or commercial financing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, refinancing, rehabilitation, and predevelopment costs (studies, plans, architectural services) for historic properties. Nonrepayable transfers for qualified nonprofits may be used to acquire properties for resale, restore properties, or provide loans to other organizations and individuals. Energy projects are eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for historic properties located anywhere in the state.
requirements_list: Applicant must be unable to access traditional or commercial financing
Project must involve a historic property (acquisition, rehabilitation, refinancing, or predevelopment)
The assisted property must be listed on or eligible for listing on the National Register of Historic Places
A preservation easement on the assisted property must be given to the Maryland Historical Trust for loan projects
Business and individual applicants must demonstrate they could not obtain private financing
The project must show a public benefit to be competitive
A fee of $1,000 or 10% of the loan amount, whichever is less, is required
Project must meet Secretary of Interior Standards for Rehabilitation
Homeowner-occupied homes are generally not competitive unless they are exceptionally historically significant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact program staff to discuss your project's eligibility. Next, review the program guidelines and applications. There are different applications for loans and nonrepayable transfers. The process from submitting the application to settlement usually takes six to nine months. Applications are accepted annually; contact the program administrator for current cycle details.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funds research, survey, documentation, planning, and education projects related to Maryland's historic, architectural, archaeological, and cultural resources. These grants do not support preservation-related activities that involve building construction or major rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants may request up to $75,000 in funding. Local governments must provide a 1:1 match (cash or in-kind). Funds are awarded through a competitive process.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Heather Barrett and Matthew McKnight, PhD
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and local governments conducting research, documentation, and education projects related to Maryland's historic, architectural, archaeological, and cultural resources
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Research, survey, documentation, planning, and education projects related to historic buildings, archaeological sites, cultural resources, National Register nominations, collection improvements, emergency planning, educational materials, oral history documentation, and preservation plans or feasibility studies. Cannot be used for building acquisition, major construction, full rehabilitation, fundraising events, or general administrative costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all of Maryland
requirements_list: Nonprofit organizations or local governments are eligible
Local governments must provide a 1:1 match (cash or in-kind)
Applicants may request up to $75,000 in funding
Work cannot have begun prior to grant approval
Projects must demonstrate public value, readiness to proceed, and support statewide preservation goals
Ineligible projects include building acquisition, major construction, or full rehabilitation
Ineligible projects include those focusing mainly on fundraising, social or promotional events, or general administrative costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review grant guidelines. Attend a virtual workshop. Submit an Intent to Apply form when the round opens. Prepare full application package including project description, budget, timeline, and explanation of the significance of the historic or cultural resources and need for the project. Submit completed application through the grants portal before the posted deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Heritage Areas Program provides technical and financial assistance to protect and enhance heritage resources within Maryland's 13 certified heritage areas. The program offers annual management grants to certified heritage area management entities, project grants for heritage-related initiatives, loans for capital projects, and tax credits for rehabilitation of historic structures. The goal is to improve quality of life for residents and maximize economic development through heritage tourism.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers annual management grants to the 13 certified heritage area management organizations for management activities, marketing, and mini-grants distributed to local organizations. Project grants are available up to $50,000 (non-capital) and $100,000 (capital), both requiring a one-to-one match. Loans can cover up to 50% of a project's total cost based on financial need and may be used for acquisition, development, rehabilitation, restoration, leasehold improvements, and purchasing equipment, furnishings, or inventory. A tax credit of up to 20% is available for eligible rehabilitation costs of qualifying historic structures. Refinancing is not eligible for loans.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually; contact program administrator. The FY26 grant round is now closed. The FY27 grant round will open in December 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations, government agencies, individuals, and businesses with projects located within Maryland's 13 certified heritage areas, as well as heritage area management entities certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heritage area management, marketing, and mini-grants to local organizations; capital and non-capital heritage projects including acquisition of property or rights to use property, construction, repair, restoration, rehabilitation, leasehold improvements, purchasing equipment, furnishings, or inventory, planning, exhibits, signage, and educational programs or events.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the boundaries of one of Maryland's 13 certified heritage areas, covering all 23 Maryland counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Project must be located within a certified heritage area
All grants require a one-to-one matching contribution from the grantee
Loans require the project to create or improve place-based heritage resources
Refinancing is not eligible as part of the loan project cost
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Heritage Areas Program staff for more information and to begin the application process. Grant rounds open annually, typically in December. Loan regulations and additional details are available in the program's loan regulations document.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Heritage Areas Program Emergency Grants
structured_extraction.program_description: Emergency grant applications are considered from eligible applicants outside of the regular grant cycle when sudden or emergency needs are caused by unexpected events. These grants support urgent heritage-related projects that cannot wait for the regular funding round.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency grants awarded on a case-by-case basis to eligible applicants for urgent heritage-related projects caused by unexpected events. Specific funding amounts are not stated on this page.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications considered outside of the regular grant cycle on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, local governments, and state or federal agencies with urgent heritage-related projects within Maryland's certified heritage areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heritage-related projects or experiences that the public can visit and enjoy, triggered by sudden or emergency needs caused by unexpected events.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must take place within the boundaries of one or more certified Maryland heritage areas.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, a local government, or a state or federal agency.
Project must be located within the boundaries of one or more certified heritage areas.
Applicant must discuss the project with the executive director of the heritage area where the project will take place before applying.
The need must not have been known during the last grant cycle.
Applicant must explain why the project cannot wait until the next regular round or demonstrate that something new has happened since the last round making the activity urgent.
Project must support the program's goal of creating or improving heritage-related places or experiences that the public can visit and enjoy.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Before applying, discuss the project with the executive director of the heritage area where the project will take place. Submit an emergency grant application demonstrating that the need was not known during the last grant cycle and explaining why the project cannot wait for the next round or what new circumstance has made it urgent.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit (Competitive Commercial)
structured_extraction.program_description: The state's largest and most competitive preservation incentive program that provides a state income tax credit equal to up to 20% of the qualified capital costs expended in the rehabilitation of eligible income-producing historic properties. The program is administered by the Maryland Historical Trust and awards credits on a competitive basis for commercial rehabilitation projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a state income tax credit for up to 20% of eligible rehabilitation costs, capped at $5 million per project. Credits are awarded competitively. Eligible expenses must exceed the greater of the structure's adjusted basis value or $25,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually; will be updated when FY2026 application is posted
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dana Marks Halpert, Carey L. Jones, or Kate Jaffe
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of historic, income-producing properties and commercial property developers in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital costs related to the rehabilitation of a historic structure, including repairs or alterations that preserve the building's significant features while making it usable.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. The property must be a certified historic structure — listed on the National Register of Historic Places, a contributing resource in a historic district, or located in a Certified Heritage Area.
requirements_list: Eligible expenses must exceed the greater of the structure's adjusted basis value or $25,000.
The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) must review and approve the project before work begins.
The project must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.
Projects awarded $1 million or more in tax credits must meet state corporate diversity requirements.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit all forms electronically. First, contact MHT Tax Credit staff to set up a Microsoft Teams channel. The application has three parts: Part 1 certifies the building is historic. Part 2 describes the proposed project to certify it meets program requirements. Part 3 certifies that the completed work meets the requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Encourages investment in historic neighborhoods and helps Marylanders preserve their homes for future generations by providing state income tax credits to homeowners who rehabilitate eligible historic buildings. The credit equals 20% of qualified capital costs expended in the rehabilitation, capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period, with a minimum project expenditure of $5,000.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners can receive a state income tax credit equal to 20% of qualified capital costs expended on the rehabilitation of an eligible historic residential property. The credit is capped at $50,000 in a 24-month period. Projects must have a minimum of $5,000 in eligible expenses.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dana Marks Halpert, Carey L. Jones, or Kate Jaffe
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners who live in their single-family historic home as a primary or secondary residence in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation and preservation of historic homes. Eligible expenses include: roof repair or replacement, chimney repair, window restoration, new storm doors or windows, masonry repointing, floor refinishing, structural repairs, and plumbing, electrical, and mechanical systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The home must be a certified historic structure — either listed in the National Register of Historic Places, a contributing resource within a National Register Historic District, or a locally designated structure that the Maryland Historical Trust determines is eligible for the National Register. Program is available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a single-family, owner-occupied residence.

Projects must have a minimum of $5,000 in eligible expenses.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, read the application instructions and contact tax credit staff for guidance. Second, download and complete the three-part application. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit (Small Commercial)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps strengthen Maryland's communities and encourages local economic growth by providing state income tax credits for small commercial projects that rehabilitate historic buildings. The credit equals 20% of the approved rehabilitation costs for projects with total expenses under $500,000, capped at $50,000 within a 24-month period. The program has a yearly funding cap of $2 million.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a state income tax credit equal to 20% of qualified rehabilitation costs. Total project expenses cannot exceed $500,000. The credit is capped at $50,000 within a 24-month period. Projects must have at least $5,000 in eligible expenses to qualify. Projects in Opportunity Zones may receive additional credits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, on a first-come, first-served basis until the program cap is reached for the current fiscal year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of certified historic structures used to produce income, including developers who plan to sell a rehabilitated property to a homeowner, and small commercial property owners in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for projects that repair or alter a historic structure for a modern use while preserving its significant features. Eligible work includes roof and chimney repair, window restoration, structural repairs, and updating plumbing, electrical, and mechanical systems. Funds cannot be used for landscaping, new construction, appliances, or tool purchases.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. To be eligible, a building must be a certified historic structure — listed on the National Register of Historic Places, a contributing resource in a National Register Historic District, a designated local historic structure, or located within a certified heritage area.
requirements_list: The building must be a certified historic structure.
The building must be primarily income-producing, rehabilitated to be sold to a homeowner, or a targeted agricultural or post-WWII building.
Total qualified rehabilitation expenses must not exceed $500,000.
Projects must have a minimum of $5,000 in eligible expenses.
All project work must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation.
The Maryland Historical Trust must review and approve all aspects of the project before work begins.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact program staff early in the planning process. The application has three parts. Part 1 certifies that the building is a historic structure. Part 2 certifies that the proposed project meets program requirements. Part 3 certifies that the completed project meets program requirements. Applicants must submit all parts for approval before starting work.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state income tax credit program that provides financial incentives for owners of certified historic properties to rehabilitate historically significant structures. The program offers tax credits of up to 20% of qualified rehabilitation expenditures (capital costs) on certified heritage structures, including energy improvements. Three credit types are available: a homeowner credit, a small commercial building credit, and a major rehabilitation credit. The program also provides credits of up to 20% of eligible rehabilitation costs for qualifying historic properties and buildings within Maryland Heritage Areas. Eligible properties include those individually listed or contributing to historic districts listed in the National Register of Historic Places, buildings eligible for but not yet listed on the National Register, non-historic buildings certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority as contributing to the heritage area, and locally designated historic properties. The program is designed to encourage preservation and restoration of historically significant buildings statewide and is administered primarily by the Maryland Historical Trust.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland state income tax credit equal to 20% of qualified capital costs (rehabilitation expenditures) expended in the rehabilitation of a certified heritage structure. Three credit types are available: a homeowner credit, a small commercial building credit, and a major rehabilitation credit. Energy improvements are eligible expenditures. For properties within Maryland Heritage Areas, an additional tax credit of up to 20% of eligible rehabilitation costs is available. Rehabilitation work must be completed within a 24-month period and meet a minimum cost threshold of $5,000 for owner-occupied residential projects, or the greater of the adjusted basis of the structure or $5,000 for all other projects. Eligible costs include plumbing, HVAC, and electrical system upgrades; kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation; architectural and engineering fees; and restoration of historically significant landscape features. Ineligible costs include financing charges, building permit fees, new construction (e.g., patios and decks), and non-historic structures. Projects may be phased, with each phase meeting the cost threshold separately. State tax credits may also be combined with county tax credits where applicable. Applicants must apply before any renovations are started.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners, individuals, for-profit entities, and non-profits interested in rehabilitating certified historic or heritage structures in Maryland, including owners of primary residences, secondary residences, small commercial buildings, or major commercial properties listed on or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places, locally designated historic properties, or buildings certified as contributing to Maryland Heritage Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified rehabilitation capital costs for certified historic or heritage structures, including structural repairs, plumbing, HVAC, and electrical system upgrades, kitchen and bathroom rehabilitation, architectural and engineering fees, restoration of historically significant landscape features, and energy improvements. Ineligible costs include financing charges, building permit fees, new construction such as patios and decks, and non-historic structures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland program available for properties listed on or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places, locally designated historic properties, or buildings certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority as contributing to the importance of a heritage area. Properties within Maryland Heritage Areas may be eligible for additional heritage area tax credits.
requirements_list: Property must be a certified historic structure or certified heritage structure

Property must be individually listed or contributing to historic districts listed in the National Register of Historic Places, OR eligible for but not officially listed on the National Register, OR locally designated as a historic property, OR certified by the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority as contributing to the importance of the heritage area
Rehabilitation work must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
Application must be submitted before any renovations are started
Rehabilitation must be completed within a 24-month period
Minimum cost threshold of $5,000 for owner-occupied residential projects, or the greater of adjusted basis of the structure or $5,000 for all other projects
Expenditures must qualify as qualified rehabilitation capital costs
Work must be documented with before and after rehabilitation photographs
MHT approval of rehabilitation plans is preferred before work begins
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Historical Trust to determine property eligibility. Obtain nomination forms or contact your local planning office to confirm whether your property contributes to the significance of a National Register or local historic district. Submit rehabilitation plans to MHT for approval before beginning work to ensure compliance with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation. Complete both federal and state tax credit application forms if applicable, fully completing the federal form and at least the first sheet of each part of the state form. Provide before and after rehabilitation photographs as documentation. MHT will review the project for adherence to the Standards and determine tax credit eligibility. Contact MHT at 410-514-7644, 410-514-7625, or 410-514-7620, or visit https://mht.maryland.gov/Pages/funding/tax-credits.aspx for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Each of Maryland's 13 heritage areas may offer mini-grants for heritage-related non-capital projects such as educational programming or planning efforts under $5,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Mini-grants for non-capital heritage-related projects such as educational programming or planning efforts. Individual heritage areas determine their own mini-grant programs and amounts are typically under $5,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations, agencies, nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and individuals operating within Maryland's heritage areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heritage-related non-capital projects including educational programming and planning efforts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Each mini-grant is specific to one of Maryland's 13 heritage areas. Applicants should visit the individual heritage area websites for specific eligibility.
requirements_list: Project must be located within a specific heritage area
Project must be heritage-related
Project must be non-capital in nature
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the individual heritage area websites to learn more about mini-grant availability and application processes for each specific area.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Museum Assistance Program offers funding and technical assistance to support Maryland museums and institutional collections. The program helps historical and cultural museums strengthen operations, build professional capacity, and improve long-term sustainability. It supports institutions in interpreting Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, and history of science and technology, while promoting tourism, public education, and professional museum practice.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In Fiscal Year 2026, the program provides grants totaling $285,000 statewide. Applicants may request up to $20,000 in funding, with grants typically between $10,000 to $15,000. No match is required. Grants support everyday museum operations including staff salaries, staff or volunteer training, office and administrative costs such as insurance, reporting and accounting, environmental monitoring such as pest management or humidity control, and security and safety systems. Capital projects such as construction, restoration, or building repairs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and local governments that manage or operate museums in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports everyday museum operations such as staff salaries, training for staff or volunteers, office and administrative costs including insurance, reporting and accounting, environmental monitoring such as pest management or humidity control, and security and safety systems. Capital projects such as construction, restoration, or building repairs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Grants are available statewide to museums throughout Maryland. Museums must interpret Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, or history of science and technology.
requirements_list: Nonprofit applicants must manage a museum that has been open and operating for at least three years
Nonprofit applicants must be in good standing with the state and be tax-exempt or have applied for tax-exempt status
Local government applicants must operate a museum that has been open and operating for at least three years
Applicants must not be museums operated in whole or in part by the state or federal government
Applicants must have a museum that collects, preserves, and interprets objects and materials for the public
Applicants must interpret Maryland's cultural heritage, history, natural history, or history of science and technology
If an applicant runs more than one museum, each museum seeking funding requires a separate application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the current grant guidelines. 2. Confirm project eligibility and applicant type. 3. Prepare required attachments such as cost estimates, photographs, and proof of ownership or site control. 4. Submit a completed application through the grants portal before the posted deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: This competitive program funds projects that protect historic maritime resources and increase public awareness of the nation's maritime heritage. Projects must demonstrate clear public benefit and include a public education component.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides $380,192 in total funding. Applicants may request between $10,000 and $100,000 per project. Projects must have total costs between $20,000 and $200,000 and require a 1 to 1 non-federal match.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tribal governments, state governments, local governments, and nonprofit organizations working on maritime heritage projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports identification of historic maritime resources including archaeological sites; repair, rehabilitation, stabilization, maintenance, or limited reconstruction of historic maritime buildings, structures, vessels, and sites; and improvements that increase public access to maritime resources. All projects must include a public education component. Grant funds cannot support work that has already started or been completed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; projects must follow the Secretary of the Interior's Standards and Guidelines for Archeology and Historic Preservation and, where applicable, the Standards for Historic Vessel Preservation Projects.
requirements_list: Projects must demonstrate clear public benefit
Projects must include a public education component

Projects must support at least one eligible activity: identification of historic maritime resources, repair or rehabilitation of historic maritime buildings or vessels, or improvements that increase public access to maritime resources
Projects must have total costs between $20,000 and $200,000
A 1 to 1 non-federal match is required
Grant funds cannot support work that has already started or been completed
Projects must follow the Secretary of the Interior's Standards and Guidelines for Archeology and Historic Preservation and the Standards for Historic Vessel Preservation Projects where applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review the grant guidelines and manual for detailed requirements. Confirm applicant and project eligibility. Prepare a complete application including scope of work, budget, and required documentation. Submit the completed application through the grants portal before the posted deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credits available for homeowners as well as commercial and small commercial historic preservation projects.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits for homeowners and commercial projects related to historic preservation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, commercial businesses, and small commercial projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Historic preservation projects for residential and commercial properties

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Mortgage Program helps families achieve homeownership by offering competitive loan options, down payment assistance, tax credits, and low-interest loans to make buying a home more affordable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers down payment assistance, tax credits, and low-interest loans to help eligible homebuyers purchase homes across Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible first-time homebuyers and families seeking to achieve homeownership in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance, closing costs, and financing for home purchase.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should find a lender through the MMP lender directory, complete homebuyer education, obtain lender pre-approval, and work with a realtor to purchase a home.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration Excise Tax Credit for Plug-In Electric Vehicle Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's excise tax credit program providing $3,000 in tax relief for qualifying zero-emission plug-in electric vehicles (EVs) or fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs) purchased in the state. The program is administered in coordination with the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration and is subject to available funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $3,000 excise tax credit applied at the point of vehicle purchase for qualifying zero-emission plug-in electric vehicles or fuel cell electric vehicles, subject to available state funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals purchasing qualifying zero-emission plug-in electric or fuel cell electric vehicles in Maryland.
