structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of qualifying zero-emission plug-in electric vehicles or fuel cell electric vehicles.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - Maryland
requirements_list: Vehicle must be a qualifying zero-emission plug-in electric vehicle or fuel cell electric vehicle
Credit is based on available funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) for information on applying for the excise tax credit for plug-in electric or fuel cell electric vehicles.

structured_extraction.program_description: A designation program that offers Maryland counties and municipalities tax incentives and other tools to encourage activity and investment in specific geographic areas where arts are part of an economic development strategy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Districts receive tax incentives and other tools to encourage arts and entertainment activity and investment in designated geographic areas. The program provides designation status and associated tax credits for businesses and activities within the designated district.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal governments in Maryland seeking to designate geographic areas as Arts and Entertainment Districts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax incentives and designation status to encourage arts and entertainment activity and economic development in designated geographic areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Districts must be located within designated Priority Funding Areas. Applicants must be a county or municipal government in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be a county or municipal government in Maryland
Select a geographic area with significant level of arts activity, entertainment venues, and/or arts business
Include arts and entertainment in the area's economic development strategy
Communicate with all municipalities and counties involved in the proposed district
Obtain agreement with all impacted governments concerning tax credits associated with the designation
Complete an Intent to Apply form online 90 days before the application deadline
Submit a complete application as specified in A&E District Designation Guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete an Intent to Apply form 90 days before choosing either the April 1st or October 1st deadline. A formal application is then submitted following A&E District Designation Guidelines. Applications are reviewed for completeness and adherence to regulations by MSAC staff, then reviewed by the A&E Districts Advisory Committee which includes representation from the departments of Commerce, Housing and Community Development, Transportation, and Planning, as well as current A&E District managers. Final decision is made by the Maryland Secretary of Commerce.

structured_extraction.program_description: Annual operating grants that support activities, programs, and projects in Arts & Entertainment (A&E) Districts throughout Maryland. Appointed management entities of designated A&E Districts may apply for Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) operating support funds to advance district priorities. The program offers two application tracks: an on-year application (in the fifth fiscal year post-designation) requiring comprehensive program details, and an off-year application (all other years) with shorter requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual operating grants provided to appointed management entities of designated A&E Districts. Applicants submit either an on-year application (in the fifth fiscal year post-designation with complete program details, goals, objectives, strategies, outcomes, revised management and marketing plans, and a proposed budget) or an off-year application (in all other years including redesignation years, with shorter requirements outlining the proposed budget and any needed updates). The A&E Districts Advisory Committee reviews on-year applications and recommends funding, while MSAC staff reviews off-year applications. All funding recommendations require approval from the MSAC Council and the Secretary of Commerce. Payment is processed within 6–8 weeks after grant agreement execution. Grantees must submit a final report at project completion and a brief report at the end of each fiscal year. Funds support district activities, programs, and projects as outlined in the management entity's proposed budget and district priorities, including general promotion of the district, event/festival production and management, business attraction, providing support services for local artists, providing arts-related support services for businesses, public art project management, promoting available real estate, managing partnerships/collaborations, facilitating coordination with overlapping designation programs, and other general activities including fundraising, board management, and advocacy.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Appointed management entities of designated Arts & Entertainment Districts in Maryland that are nonprofit 501(c)(3) organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for district activities, programs, and projects as outlined in the management entity's proposed budget and district priorities, including general promotion of the district, event/festival production and management, business attraction, providing support services for local artists, providing arts-related support services for businesses, public art project management, promoting available real estate, managing partnerships/collaborations, facilitating coordination with overlapping designation programs, and other general activities including fundraising, board management, and advocacy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to designated A&E Districts throughout Maryland. Applicants must have a current contract or memorandum of understanding with a county or municipality to manage a designated A&E District. The A&E District's designation is the responsibility of the local government approved by the Secretary of Commerce for designation.
requirements_list: Be the appointed management entity of a designated A&E District in Maryland
Be a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization
Complete a signed letter of agreement between the county or municipality holding the designation and the management entity
Have a current contract or memorandum of understanding with a county or municipality to manage a designated A&E District

Maintain a Board of Directors or Advisory Board of at least five (5) individuals to oversee and/or advise on A&E District activities, composed of community members representing the diversity of populations in the district and its surrounding communities as well as various constituencies (artists, arts organizations, businesses, etc.)
Employ at least one person at a minimum of 15 hours per week whose job responsibilities include coordinating A&E District activities
Submit application annually (either on-year or off-year form depending on fiscal year post-designation)
Submit a final report at project completion
Submit a brief report at the end of each fiscal year
Maintain a website or website page that publicizes the A&E District as well as its tax credits and other incentives, opportunities, and events, with links to MSAC's site
Maintain a distribution list of local constituents
Send regular communications (email, social media, and/or print, etc.) promoting A&E District and MSAC opportunities
Maintain a current profile page on MSAC's website
Notify MSAC at least two months ahead of deadlines of available local grant opportunities relevant to artists
Provide MSAC with ongoing updates of local needs and concerns through scheduled reports and additional communications
Arrange at least one site visit per year for MSAC to meet with A&E District leadership, board, and/or constituents
Adhere to all grantmaking, crediting, and reporting requirements as communicated by MSAC
Maintain programs, events, projects, communication tools, vendors, and resources that are responsive to identified needs of the community and equitably benefit all district constituents
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The management entity for an A&E District must submit one application form annually, along with a signed Letter of Agreement between the local government and the management entity. On-year applications (fifth fiscal year post-designation) include a complete application with updated goals, objectives, strategies, outcomes, revised management and marketing plans, and a proposed budget. Off-year applications (all other years including redesignation years) are shorter and outline the proposed budget and any needed updates. The A&E Districts Advisory Committee reviews on-year applications, provides feedback, and recommends funding. MSAC staff reviews off-year applications. All funding recommendations require final approval from the MSAC Council and the Secretary of Commerce. A signed Letter of Agreement that clarifies the role and expectations of the A&E District and agreements between the county or municipality(ies) holding A&E District designation and the management entity is required in order for the management entity to apply to MSAC for A&E District General Operating Support.

structured_extraction.program_name: Admissions & Amusement Tax Exemption for Arts & Entertainment Districts
structured_extraction.program_description: Local governments in Arts & Entertainment Districts may exempt from the admissions and amusement tax the gross receipts from any admissions or amusement charges imposed by an arts and entertainment enterprise or a qualifying residing artist operating in an Arts & Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Arts and entertainment enterprises and qualifying residing artists may be exempt from paying admissions and amusement tax on gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges in Arts & Entertainment Districts. Eligibility and application procedures vary by local government.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Arts and entertainment enterprises and qualifying residing artists conducting business in Arts & Entertainment Districts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Applies to gross receipts from admissions or amusement charges
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must operate within one of Maryland's 29 designated Arts & Entertainment Districts
requirements_list: Be an arts and entertainment enterprise or a qualifying residing artist
Conduct business in an Arts & Entertainment District
Charge admissions or amusement fees
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Comptroller's Office to learn more about the Admissions and Amusement tax or contact your local government administering the specific Arts & Entertainment District. Each local government determines the process for claiming exemptions.

structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time grant that provides financial support to fully developed and ready-to-implement public art initiatives in Maryland that celebrate America's 250th anniversary (semiquincentennial). The program funds projects aligned with the national America250 initiative commemorating the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding supports eligible public art projects including conservation and promotion of existing works or creation and installation of new works. Awarded funding may be used for administrative fees (up to 15% of total request), artist fees and labor for Maryland-based artists and fabricators, materials (artwork, base, lighting, landscaping), contracted services and equipment rental, studio or space rental to fabricate and assemble the artwork, signage or plaques to identify the artwork, and dedication event expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based nonprofit organizations with IRS-designated 501(c)3 status, units of state or local government, and colleges or universities located in Maryland that want to create or support public art initiatives celebrating America's semiquincentennial.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Administrative fees (up to 15% of total request), artist fees and labor for Maryland-based artists and fabricators, materials including artwork, base, lighting, and landscaping, contracted services and equipment rental, studio or space rental for fabrication and assembly, signage or plaques to identify artwork, and dedication event expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Maryland. The artist, artisan, studio, or team must be based in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be Maryland-based and one of: nonprofit organization with IRS 501(c)3 status, unit of state or local government, or college or university in Maryland
Project must be a fully developed public art initiative ready for immediate implementation
Artwork concept must be finalized
All required permits and site permissions must be acquired
Project must be entering initial stages of implementation with ability to complete and fully install by June 30, 2026
Artwork must be either an architectural enhancement of artistic significance or an installation of artwork
Eligible mediums include murals, tile mosaics, paintings, sculptures
Artwork must fit within MSAC's definition of Public Art
Project must be located in Maryland
Artist, artisan, studio, or team must be based in Maryland
Final report must be submitted by September 1, 2026
Public art project must be clear, specific, aligned with submitted drawings, and communicate a vision aligned with America250 goals
Public art initiative must be site-responsive and engage the site and/or community around the America 250 celebration
Lead artist, fabrication team, and proposed artwork must demonstrate artistic excellence and artistic merit
Artist's prior experience must demonstrate ability to deliver safe and durable artwork built for public environment within required timeframe
Timeline of public art project must be realistic and feasible for completion within required timeframe
Budget must be financially realistic and able to be completed within required timeframe
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit an online application by logging into or creating an account on SmartSimple, the grants management platform. Applications must be completed and submitted electronically, including use of an electronic signature. Technical support is available during regular office hours. Lost, misdirected, or late applications are the applicant's responsibility. Applicants must meet all revision deadlines after submission as specified in writing, or the application will be withdrawn. Applications are reviewed by a team of MSAC staff and representatives from the Maryland250 Commission based on criteria required by the National Endowment for the Arts. Scoring rubric evaluates: clarity and alignment with America250 goals, site-responsiveness and community engagement, artistic excellence and merit, feasibility and realistic timeline, and financial soundness. All grantees must file a final report in SmartSimple by September 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A qualified residing artist who lives in Maryland and sells artistic work in any of the 29 Arts & Entertainment Districts throughout the state is eligible for an income tax subtraction modification on income derived from their in-district sales. This means qualifying artists do not pay state or local income tax on income derived from artistic work created and sold within an Arts & Entertainment District, though federal income tax still applies. For performing artists, this includes income from performances in a district. For all qualified residing artists, this includes internet sales originating in a district. One-member Limited Liability Companies may also be eligible if the single member is a qualifying resident artist. This incentive is available statewide across all of Maryland's designated Arts & Entertainment Districts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualifying resident artists subtract qualifying Arts & Entertainment District income from their Maryland state income tax filing before state and local income taxes are calculated, resulting in zero state and local income tax on that income (federal income tax still applies). This is an income tax subtraction modification — not a tax credit — on income derived from in-district sales and performances. For performing artists, this includes income from performances in a district. For all qualified artists, this includes internet sales originating in a district. There is no limit to the amount of qualifying income that can be subtracted. One-member LLCs may be eligible if the single member is a qualifying resident artist. Artists file a completed Form 502AE with their annual state tax return to claim the modification.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline; tax benefit is claimed on annual tax return
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified residing artists (individuals or single-member LLCs) who live in Maryland, own or rent residential real property in Maryland, and create and sell or perform artistic work within one of Maryland's designated Arts & Entertainment Districts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: State and local income tax exemption on income derived from the sale or performance of artistic work created within an Arts & Entertainment District, including internet sales originating in a district.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must own or rent residential real property in Maryland and conduct a business and create or perform artistic work within one of Maryland's 29 designated Arts & Entertainment Districts. The program is available statewide wherever a designated Arts & Entertainment District exists.
requirements_list: Own or rent residential real property in Maryland
Conduct a business in an Arts & Entertainment District
Derive income from the sale or performance of artistic work created within an Arts & Entertainment District
Artistic work must be created, written, composed, or executed by the individual alone or with others

Work must fall into eligible categories including books, plays, musical compositions, paintings, photographs, sculptures, crafts, film, dance, jewelry, clothing, functional art, storytelling, digital media, or other listed artistic forms
Must be a qualifying resident artist as defined by statute
File Maryland State Tax Form 502AE with state income tax return
One-member Limited Liability Companies may be eligible if the single member is a qualifying resident artist
Income must be derived from in-district sales or performances
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Artists claim the income tax subtraction modification by filing a completed Form 502AE with their annual Maryland state income tax return. The subtraction is claimed before state and local income taxes are calculated. Retain receipts, books, accounts, and other documentation proving the income qualifies for the incentive. Forms are available at marylandtaxes.gov. Questions can be directed to the Maryland Comptroller's Office Tax Help at taxhelp@comp.state.md.us. Additional eligibility information and a directory of Arts & Entertainment Districts is available on the Maryland State Arts Council website.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Arts Capital Grant program provides Maryland-based non-profit arts organizations with direct access to state capital funding for projects that improve or produce a complete, usable, and accessible arts facility. Funds can support expanding, producing, renovating, or making major repairs to a facility or its infrastructure. The program allocates $3,000,000 per year for six years (fiscal years 2024–2029).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State capital grants ranging from $50,000 to $500,000 distributed to eligible non-profit arts organizations for capital projects that improve or produce a complete, usable, and accessible arts facility. The program allocates $3,000,000 per year for six years (fiscal years 2024–2029). Previous grantees cannot have received $500,000 in Arts Capital funds within a five-year period. Grants are distributed through a competitive process with applications reviewed by a statewide panel.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based 501(c)(3) non-profit arts organizations that own or lease a physical property in the state, have annual operating budgets below $3,000,000, and are open to the public providing arts-based cultural education or experiences.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects that improve or produce a complete, usable, and accessible arts facility, including expanding, producing, renovating, or making major repairs to a facility or its infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be based in Maryland and the project facility must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization
Must be Maryland-based
Must operate a physical property in Maryland that is either leased or owned
Annual operating budget must be below $3,000,000
Must either participate in MSAC's Grants for Organizations or County Arts Development programs, or be open to the public and provide arts-based cultural education or experiences
Must provide proof of property ownership or a lease agreement with at least five years remaining at the time of application
Previous grantees must have completed their prior projects and submitted final reports before re-applying
Cannot have received $500,000 in Arts Capital funds within a five-year period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First-time applicants should contact program staff before applying. All organizations apply through the SmartSimple online system. Applications are reviewed by a statewide panel. The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) will notify all applicants of their decision electronically.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Arts in Education Grant provides funds to Teaching Artists on the Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) Teaching Artist Roster to support arts education engagements at Maryland-based nonprofit organizations, schools, and other government entities. This grant strengthens and promotes lifelong learning in the arts across Maryland by enabling teaching artists to lead arts learning activities in school and community settings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers project grants up to a maximum of $6,000 (final amount depends on the applicant's request) to teaching artists on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster to implement arts education programs in Maryland schools, libraries, community centers, detention centers, and other nonprofit or government locations. Individual lead artists may receive a maximum of $21,000 in grant awards for FY 2026; teaching artist organizations may receive a maximum of $84,000 in grant awards for FY 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis between July 2025 and January 2026. The application deadlines are: September 5, 2025, November 5, 2025, January 5, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Teaching artists on the Maryland State Arts Council's (MSAC) Teaching Artist Roster who collaborate with Maryland schools, nonprofit organizations, or government entities, as well as school and community organizations seeking arts education programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support teaching artists to implement arts education programs in Maryland schools, libraries, community centers, detention centers, and other nonprofit or government locations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland
requirements_list: The teaching artist must be on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster.
The collaborating school or community site must be a 501(c)3 nonprofit, a unit of government, or a college/university in Maryland.
The collaborating site must have operated for at least one full fiscal year with ongoing arts activities.
A school or community site may participate in up to two grants per fiscal year.
Individual lead artists may receive a maximum of $21,000 in grant awards for FY 2026.
Teaching artist organizations may receive a maximum of $84,000 in grant awards for FY 2026.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, the teaching artist and the school or organization agree to collaborate on services, timelines, and fees. Second, the school or organization identifies a coordinator for the project. Third, the teaching artist or their affiliated organization starts and submits the application online using SmartSimple. A panel then reviews applications, and the applicant receives a notification the following month.

structured_extraction.program_description: The state's Percent-for-Art program that brings new, permanent artworks to state-owned buildings. For all new or renovated state-owned buildings, part of the construction budget is reserved for public art. MSAC manages each commission project, from artist selection through installation, and the completed artworks join the State's public art collection.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For all new or renovated state buildings meeting eligibility criteria (greater than 15,000 square feet of occupiable space and greater than 50% of capital project budget funded by the State), 0.05% of the estimated construction cost (sometimes referred to as the "Public Art Premium") is reserved to commission or purchase site-specific original artwork through a contractual agreement with an artist. Artists who receive a commission contract directly with the unit of State Government responsible for the project and work directly with the project design team. The 2026-2028 Public Artist Roster will serve as the primary method of artist selection for Artwork Commission projects with budgets ranging from $50,000 to $1,500,000. Artists can expect to be committed to a project for approximately two to five years, depending on the scale and timeframe of the construction project. Artists selected through the roster are expected to create site-responsive work, integrate artwork with building architecture or landscape, and engage with the community or public audience as part of the concept development and design process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 30, 2025 for the 2026-2028 Public Artist Roster. Applications accepted annually on a rolling basis through the Public Artist Roster or through open Calls for Artists (Request for Qualifications) issued for specific projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Independent artists and artist-led teams, studios, or collectives who are residents of the United States and its territories interested in creating permanent public artworks for state-owned buildings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commission or purchase of site-specific original artwork for state-owned buildings that is integrated into the construction or renovation project and accessible to the public. Artwork must be permanent, responsive to the specific site and community, architecturally integrated with the building design or landscape, and engage with the local community or public audience.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be residents of the United States or US Territory. Artwork commissions are for state-owned buildings in Maryland. Roster is open to artists and artist-led teams from across the United States.
requirements_list: Must be an independent artist, artist-led team, studio, or collective
Must reside in the United States or US Territory
Must produce or present unique and original artwork
Must be the lead artist whose original work is included in the roster application
Must be 18 years of age or older
May submit only one application
Must not be directly affiliated with or a subsidiary of a larger arts organization, commercial company, or program that exists as part of a larger institution or entity
Must not be enrolled in any matriculated high school, undergraduate, or graduate degree program as of July 1, 2025
Must demonstrate a unique vision or perspective
Must show an authentic relationship to subject matter
Must demonstrate ability to create site-responsive work engaging a site and/or community
Must demonstrate command of materials and/or skill in technique (applicant must meet 3 of 4 eligibility criteria)
Must be willing to work closely with a design team to integrate artwork into building architecture or landscape
Must be interested in translating work into resilient or durable materials suitable for public environments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Artists apply by joining the Maryland Public Artist Roster or responding to open Calls for Artists when issued. For the 2026-2028 Public Artist Roster: Artists complete a one-time application in SmartSimple that includes contact information, residency status, a one-sentence summary using a provided template, up to 10 artwork samples (8 images and 2 videos with required metadata), a biographical statement (250-word limit) describing experience with public art and commissioned projects, an artist statement (250-word limit) describing their practice, selection of minimum budget category or "no minimum budget required," description of community engagement experience (250-word limit), and metadata for each artwork sample. Applications are reviewed by a panel of independent panelists from across the U.S. for eligibility based on whether applicants meet 3 of 4 criteria: communicating a unique vision or perspective, demonstrating authentic relationship to subject matter, showing ability to create site-responsive work engaging a site and/or community, and demonstrating command of materials and/or skill in technique. For Artist Selection Committees, a diverse pool of artist candidates (60-100 per project) is drawn from the Public Artist Roster. An Artist Selection Committee composed of arts professionals, representatives from the user agency and primary building occupant, the project's lead design architect, and representatives from the Maryland Public Art Commission and MSAC Public Art Program staff reviews semi-finalist artists (4-6 per opportunity) and selects artists for commissions. Alternatively, artists may respond to single project "Calls for Artists" issued as Requests for Qualifications (RFQ) or RFQ plus proposal for specific projects.

structured_extraction.program_description: The County Arts Development (CAD) grant program supports Maryland's county arts agencies, extending the service of the Maryland State Arts Council. These grants help county arts agencies connect with artists, arts organizations, and local communities, providing equitable financial and technical support to artists, arts organizations, and arts programs within their jurisdictions. The program also encourages local arts activities and provides fair funding for the arts at the county level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This program provides formula-based grants to support county arts agencies across Maryland's 24 jurisdictions to help them meet their goals of providing equitable funding for local arts and supporting artists, arts organizations, and arts programs. It also offers technical assistance to help applicants with their plans and operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County arts agencies designated as official government offices or non-profit organizations in each of Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support the operations of county arts agencies, including their own grant-making activities, local arts activities, equitable and accessible financial and technical support to artists and arts organizations, diverse programming, creative expression, and lifelong learning throughout Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is open to the officially designated arts agency or council for each of Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be a local agency or nonprofit designated by the jurisdiction's government as the official arts agency or council.
Submit an application annually, which will be either a detailed three-year plan ('On-Year') or a shorter update ('Off-Year').
Grantees must submit interim and annual final reports detailing the use of funds.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Designated county arts agencies submit one of two types of applications each year. Every three years, an agency submits an 'On-Year' application with a detailed three-year plan. MSAC staff and a review panel review a draft and provide feedback. The agency revises the plan and submits it for final Council approval. In the two years between, the agency submits a simpler 'Off-Year' application. This application notes any changes to the three-year plan and includes required financial reports.

structured_extraction.program_name: Creativity Grants for General Operating Support
structured_extraction.program_description: Strengthens the vitality and sustainability of small organizations to maintain a strong and stable arts infrastructure in Maryland. This program provides grants to support the general operations of small arts organizations, helping them maintain a strong and stable arts community across the state. Available to organizations only, not independent artists.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants of up to $4,000 for general operating support to cover an organization's overall operations for an entire season or fiscal year. Technical assistance and information are also available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling. MSAC is currently accepting applications for the FY2026 application cycle.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small arts organizations in Maryland, including 501(c)3 nonprofits, local government units, and colleges or universities. Independent artists are not eligible for this specific grant.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General operating support to fund an organization's overall operations for an entire season or fiscal year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The organization must be incorporated in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit in operation for at least one year, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college/university.
Must produce or present arts programs, services, or projects that are available to the public.
Cannot be a current participant in the Grants for Organizations (GFO), County Arts Development (CAD), or Arts & Entertainment District (A&E) programs.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit their application through the SmartSimple online portal. A panel reviews applications monthly. The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) notifies applicants of their status. If approved, the grantee receives a grant agreement to process payment, which can take up to 90 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Arts Council's Creativity Grants for Projects strengthen the vitality and sustainability of artists and small organizations and provide opportunities to serve the growing needs of relevant arts projects and collaborations within Maryland communities. The program offers two grant types: a Planning & Development grant that supports early-stage research and development for a proposed arts project, and an Implementation grant that supports the execution and delivery of a specific arts project, event, or program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants ranging from $1,000 to $4,000 to support artists and small organizations. Two grant types are available: (1) Planning & Development grants support early research and development for a proposed arts project, including research, concept development, and feasibility studies; (2) Implementation grants support carrying out and delivering a specific arts project, event, or program. Upon award approval, 100 percent of the award amount is paid, with payment processed within 6-8 weeks after execution of the grant agreement. For awarded activities, initial payment may take up to 90 days. Funded activities must occur within the application timeframe (July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis from July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026 with a monthly review process. Applications submitted by the last day of each month are reviewed by a panel in the following month, with notifications following early the following month.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Emily Sollenberger Dobbins and Laura Weiss
structured_extraction.program_audience: Independent artists and Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit arts organizations in operation for one year or more, units of Maryland local government, and Maryland colleges, universities, and schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used for two main purposes: Planning & Development grants support the early stages of a proposed arts project including research, development, concept refinement, and feasibility studies; Implementation grants support carrying out and executing a specific arts project, event, or program to occur within the application timeframe. Expenses must align with the proposed activities and timeline outlined in the application.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. Projects must serve Maryland communities or be executed by Maryland-based applicants.
requirements_list: Must be an independent artist, a Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit organization in operation for at least one year, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college, university, or school.
Organizations applying through fiscal sponsorships can be funded if the Fiscal Agency and the Organization operate within a Model A sponsorship.
Applicants must identify a specific event, activity, or project to occur within the application timeframe (July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026).

Organizations that receive funding through general operating programs (Grants for Organizations, County Arts Agencies, Arts & Entertainment Districts, Folklife Network, or Creativity Grant for General Operating) are not eligible for project-based support.
An applicant is only eligible for one Creativity Grant per fiscal year.

Planning & Development applications must include: clear description of planning/development process with overarching goals, details of creative process, and goals for future community engagement and impact; detailed timeline with specific activities and tasks for the planning phase; detailed budget with all planned expenses and anticipated income beyond the MSAC request.

Implementation applications must include: clear description of proposed arts activity with specific logistical details of execution; description of plans for community engagement, goals, intended impact, and geographic area served; detailed timeline including planning, promotional efforts, expenditure of funds, implementation, execution, and evaluation; overall budget with projected expenses, income sources beyond MSAC request, and how MSAC funding will be used.
Meet specific eligibility requirements detailed in the FY 2026 Grant Guidelines.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through the SmartSimple portal on a rolling basis from July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026. Applications submitted by the last day of each month are reviewed by a panel in the following month, with notifications sent early the following month. The review panel is composed of members of the public statewide representing a range of arts discipline expertise who electronically review and score all applications according to established review criteria and scoring rubrics. For Planning & Development grants, applications are scored on description of the planning/development process and goals (0-36 points), detailed timeline for the planning phase (0-12 points), and detailed budget with expenses and income (0-12 points). For Implementation grants, applications are scored on description of the proposed activity and community engagement plans (0-36 points), detailed project timeline (0-12 points), and overall project budget (0-12 points). Applicants are notified of grant status as soon as possible after panel review. Award decisions are final and not subject to appeal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that funds a mentor artist and apprentice artist to work together for one year to support living cultural traditions. The mentor artist passes down their knowledge of traditional arts to the apprentice artist.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funding to support a one-year mentorship where a mentor artist teaches traditional arts to an apprentice artist. Expenses must total at least $5,000, which may include teaching materials, travel, and compensation for mentor and/or apprentice artists' time. Upon execution of the grant agreement, payment is processed for receipt in 6-8 weeks. Grantees must submit a final report at project completion and brief reports at the end of each fiscal year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are traditional/folk artists in Maryland (apprentices) and experienced mentor artists from the United States or U.S. territories.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports the mentorship relationship between mentor and apprentice artists during a one-year period of traditional arts education and knowledge transfer. Funds may be used for teaching materials, travel, and compensation for mentor and/or apprentice artists' time.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Apprentice artists must be Maryland residents. Mentor artists must be residents of the United States or a U.S. territory. If the mentor artist resides out of state, the apprentice must demonstrate that the desired skillset is unavailable in Maryland.
requirements_list: Mentor artist must be a U.S. resident or U.S. territory resident
Mentor artist must demonstrate vital contributions to a particular living cultural tradition in Maryland
Mentor artist must demonstrate expertise through skill set and public/community recognition as a tradition bearer
Apprentice artist must be a Maryland resident
Apprentice artist must demonstrate prior experience, basic skill level, and commitment to long-term learning in a particular traditional art
Apprentice artist must demonstrate preparedness through a progressive trajectory of past accomplishments
Apprentice artists under 18 must provide parent/guardian contact information and e-signature acknowledging permission to participate
Proposed apprenticeship expenses must total at least $5,000
Applicants must describe the form of folklife, its cultural history and culture of origin, and the current community participating in the tradition
Applicants must demonstrate how the apprenticeship would contribute to the cultural, practical, and artistic value of the tradition
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit complete narrative information answering prompts about the form of folklife (name, description, cultural history and culture of origin, and current community participation), mentor and apprentice expertise and skill sets, any official or unofficial recognitions received, how the apprenticeship contributes to the tradition's continued vitality, biographical information for both mentor and apprentice, and a detailed work plan including types of activities taught, materials needed, dates and locations of training, and itemized expenses totaling at least $5,000. Applicants may submit supplemental written and audiovisual materials. Applicants may upload audio or video recordings of narrative answers instead of written submissions. Applications are evaluated on five criteria: traditional nature of the folklife form, expertise of the mentor artist, preparedness of the apprentice artist, potential impact on the tradition's vitality, and feasibility of the work plan. Detailed information is provided in the Grant Guidelines and Application Scoring Rubric.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Grants for Artists program provides funds to support working or living expenses for artists in Maryland. The program aims to provide holistic support rather than focusing solely on particular product or project-based needs. A primary goal is to strengthen the creative workforce, which is a vital part of Maryland's economy and culture.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support the working and living expenses of Maryland artists, providing holistic support rather than focusing solely on particular product or project-based needs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Working artists in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To support working and living expenses of artists.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: See program guidelines for details about eligibility, application submission, and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: General operating support provided to nonprofit and tax-exempt organizations, as well as units of government, that produce or present ongoing arts programming that is open to the public. In FY 2025, MSAC awarded GFO grants to 309 arts organizations and programs across the State, totaling $18,136,157.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: General operating support grants to arts organizations and programs. In FY 2025, 309 organizations received awards totaling $18,136,157. Starting FY 2027, organizations will complete applications annually and participate in conversations with a GFO program director and one site visit by a public panelist as part of a four-year application cycle. Grant amounts and specific terms vary by organization based on program budget, operations, and artistic activities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Intent to Apply form by September 15th annually; GFO application by Saturday, November 15
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and tax-exempt organizations, and units of government that produce or present ongoing arts programming open to the public
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General operating support for arts organizations and programs, including salaries, facility costs, equipment, artistic materials, and other expenses necessary for ongoing arts programming.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Organizations must establish that the majority of the arts activities they produce and present take place in Maryland and that most of the arts organization's or program's annual expenditures are devoted to activities that occur within the State of Maryland. Organizations must be incorporated in Maryland as a nonprofit or have significant physical presence in Maryland.
requirements_list: Produce or present the arts to the public through ongoing arts programming
Have 501(c)3 tax-exempt status from the U.S. Internal Revenue Service at the time of application, except for units of local government and colleges and universities
Be incorporated in Maryland as a nonprofit or have significant physical presence in Maryland
Have operated as an arts organization or arts program for one full fiscal year and be able to submit a financial statement for the most recently completed fiscal year at the time of application
Establish that the majority of the arts activities produced and presented take place in Maryland
Ensure that most of the arts organization's or program's annual expenditures are devoted to activities within the State of Maryland
Be governed by a legally-liable board of directors acting under a mission statement and budget specific to the organization
Submit an Intent to Apply form if the organization is a new applicant or did not receive a GFO grant in the most recent funding cycle
Demonstrate ongoing and substantial arts programming that is open to the public
Maintain current insurance coverage appropriate to the organization's operations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: New applicants and those who did not receive a GFO grant in the most recent funding cycle must submit an Intent to Apply form by September 15 annually. After eligibility is determined, organizations complete a GFO application by November 15. Applications are submitted through SmartSimple. Grant agreement forms are prepared and emailed after July 1 to those awarded funding. Forms must be signed and all reporting requirements met before grant funds are disbursed. Funds are generally distributed in full after the Grant Agreement Form and required reports are submitted. Award recipients must file a final report in SmartSimple by the deadlines specified in communications from MSAC. Organizations participate in a four-year cycle beginning FY 2027, with annual application completion and program director conversations plus one public panelist site visit per cycle.

structured_extraction.program_name: Grants for Organizations (GFO) - New Applicants Intent to Apply
structured_extraction.program_description: An initial application process for organizations new to the Grants for Organizations program. New organizations must submit an Intent to Apply form to determine eligibility before proceeding to a full application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Organizations submit an Intent to Apply form to determine eligibility for grant funding. Eligible organizations then proceed to complete a standard application for consideration in the next funding cycle. This program supports general operating expenses for arts organizations in eligible disciplines including Dance, Literary Arts, Music, Public Art, Theatre, Arts Services, Folk & Traditional Arts, Multi-disciplinary, and Visual Arts/Media.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Intent to Apply deadline: September 15th annually; standard application deadline: November 15th
structured_extraction.program_audience: Arts organizations new to the Grants for Organizations program who did not receive FY 2026 GFO funding but wish to be considered for the next funding cycle
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General operating support for eligible arts disciplines including Dance, Literary Arts, Music, Public Art, Theatre, Arts Services, Folk & Traditional Arts, Multi-disciplinary, and Visual Arts/Media
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Organization must be new to the GFO program
Organization must not have received FY 2026 GFO funding
Must submit Intent to Apply form by September 15th annually
Eligible organizations must then complete a standard application by November 15th
Organization must be a Maryland-based non-profit arts organization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Submit an Intent to Apply form by September 15th to determine eligibility. Step 2: Eligible organizations receive notification of their eligibility status. Step 3: Submit a standard application by November 15th as a current GFO applicant would. Application assistance is available through guidelines documents and webinar slides provided by MSAC.

structured_extraction.program_description: A juried list of Maryland-based professional performing artists with a demonstrated history of successful touring engagements. MSAC uses the roster to promote collaboration between Maryland touring artists and presenters to increase touring opportunities for Maryland professional performing artists.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Artists accepted to the roster are promoted through MSAC's Arts Directory with linked profiles to increase visibility and touring engagement opportunities with Maryland presenters. Accepted artists receive instructions for setting up an Arts Directory profile for direct contact with venue presenters. There are no direct financial assistance or funding awards. Roster status must be renewed once every three years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026 on rolling basis with review every other month
structured_extraction.contact_name: Laura Weiss and Emily Sollenberger Dobbins
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based professional performing artists in disciplines including dance, literary arts, music, public art, theater, folk and traditional arts, multi-disciplinary work, and visual arts and media.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Roster placement provides promotional opportunities and increased touring engagement visibility through the Arts Directory. Artists are promoted to presenters seeking touring performers. There are no direct financial assistance or funding awards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents or have their company's primary place of business located in Maryland. If a group, at least 50% of members must be Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident and 18 years old or older
If a group, all members must be 18 or older and at least 50% must be Maryland residents
If a group or company, the primary place of business must be located in Maryland
College and university-based performers must perform regularly off-campus for professional fees
Must be able to demonstrate a successful history of professional touring engagements within the past three years
Must provide clear and concise artist/company description suitable for venue marketing materials
Must describe artistic goals, qualifications, and experience with how touring aligns with those goals
Must provide brief biographical information about key members demonstrating experience and training
Must describe tour management, programming development, and preparation practices
Must specify basic space and technical requirements for performances
Must submit three work samples that clearly demonstrate artistic quality
Must provide a list of touring engagements from the past three years demonstrating capacity for expansion
Must provide a standard performance contract that is clear and detailed
Must provide examples of promotional materials representing the artist/company experience
Must meet all eligibility requirements outlined in the program guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis from July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026 with reviews conducted every other month. Applicants submit applications through SmartSimple, including all required work samples and supporting materials. A panel of jurors representing various disciplines reviews and scores applications electronically using a detailed rubric assessing artist description, artistic goals and qualifications, tour management practices, technical requirements, and supplemental materials quality. Applicants are notified of roster status via SmartSimple following each review period. New roster members receive instructions for setting up an Arts Directory profile. Arts Services Program Directors are available to review draft applications prior to submission (allow at least 6 weeks processing time). Declined applicants can request feedback from reviewers (allow at least 6 weeks processing time).

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to eligible Maryland nonprofit organizations to subsidize the presentation costs of artists listed on the Maryland Performing Artists Touring Roster. Grants range from $500 to $5,000 and support statewide access to performing arts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $500 to $5,000 to subsidize presentation costs for performers on the Maryland Performing Artists Touring Roster. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis every other month.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland nonprofit organizations, local governments, and arts programs at colleges or universities that present performing artists.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support the costs of presenting artists from the Maryland Performing Artists Touring Roster.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to eligible Maryland nonprofit organizations statewide.
requirements_list: Must present an artist from the Maryland Performing Artists Touring Roster.
Fiscal sponsorships must operate under a 'Model A' agreement.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, select an artist from the Touring Roster and contact them to negotiate performance details and fees. Then, complete and submit the application in the SmartSimple online portal. A panel reviews applications every other month. The agency notifies applicants of their status after the review. Approved applicants receive a grant agreement to process payment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Folklife Network grants fund organizations serving as regional folklife centers in Maryland. Regional folklife centers support activities that identify, document, support, or present the living cultural traditions of Maryland's diverse communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Folklife Network grants provide funding to regional folklife centers to support activities that identify, document, support, or present the living cultural traditions of Maryland's diverse communities. Grants are approximately $85,000. Upon execution of grant agreement, payment is processed for receipt in 6 to 8 weeks. Grantees are required to submit a final report at the completion of the funded project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations serving as regional folklife centers in Maryland, including non-profits, universities, museums, and arts organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Activities that identify, document, support, or present the living cultural traditions of Maryland's diverse communities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide through designated regional folklife centers
requirements_list: Applicant must be an organization serving as a regional folklife center in Maryland
Final report required at completion of funded project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application according to MSAC guidelines. See Grant Guidelines for detailed information on application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: Recognition program that honors long-term achievement in traditional arts. Each year six winners are selected from nominations in three categories: Person/People, Place, or Tradition. Each awardee receives a grant to use at their discretion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each award includes a $10,000 grant that recipients may use at their discretion. Payment is processed for receipt within 6-8 weeks after grant agreement execution. Nominations are evaluated on three main criteria: identification of a form of folklife with its cultural history and community of origin; the nominee's connection and importance to that cultural community; and the nominee's sustained engagement with the folklife over a substantial period of time. Scoring is based on a rubric with ratings of Excellent (17-20 points), Good (13-16 points), Fair (9-12 points), or Poor (8 or fewer points) for each criterion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People, places, and traditions located in Maryland that demonstrate long-term achievement in traditional arts and folklife. Nominators may reside anywhere.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Awardees may use grant funds at their discretion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible nominees must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Nominees must demonstrate long-term achievement in traditional arts and folklife
People, places, and traditions may receive the award only once
Awards are not given posthumously
Self-nominations are accepted

Eligible categories include performance, creative practice, research, documentation, presentation, entrepreneurship, artistry, or community leadership for Person/People category; gathering points for community fellowship or sites for traditional practice for Place category; long-term practices that have connected communities to traditional arts for Tradition category
Nomination must clearly identify a living cultural tradition strongly connected to a cultural community of origin over a generational period of practice
Nominee must demonstrate importance to the current community participating in the form of folklife
Nominee must show sustained engagement with the form of folklife extending over a substantial period of time

For Person/People nominations, evidence of individual sustained engagement is required; for Place nominations, evidence of functioning as a community gathering place is required; for Tradition nominations, evidence of the traditional practice's sustained role is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a nomination via MSAC's online grants management system SmartSimple. Nominators must create a profile in one of several categories (such as Independent Artist or County Arts Council). Complete nominations include answers to prompts about the cultural history and community of origin of the form of folklife, the current community participating in the folklife, evidence of the nominee's importance to that community, and evidence of the nominee's sustained engagement with the folklife. Nominators should provide specific details addressing the scoring rubric criteria on identification of folklife, connection to cultural community, and sustained engagement. Optional supplemental materials may be included. Contact the State Folklorist for draft review assistance before submission.

structured_extraction.program_description: A national arts education program that encourages high school students to study and recite great poetry. Students develop public speaking skills, build confidence, and learn about literary history and contemporary life through participation in local, regional, and state competitions, with top performers advancing to national finals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides competitive opportunities for high school students to recite poetry for judges. Monetary prizes are awarded to students placing 1st, 2nd, and 3rd at regional and state competitions. At the state level, the winner receives $200 and an all-expenses-paid trip with an adult chaperone to Washington, DC for the National Finals, with their school or organization receiving $500 for poetry materials. One runner-up receives $100 and their school/organization receives $200 for poetry materials. At the national finals, a total of $50,000 in awards and school stipends is distributed annually, including a $20,000 award for the National Champion. Students advancing to regional and state competitions receive coaching from Poetry Coaches prior to competition.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Local competitions must be hosted by Friday, January 16, 2026. Regional competitions occur in February 2026. State competition is March 7, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All high school students in Maryland, including traditional high school students, homeschooled students, and students in after-school programs or community organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program supports student participation in poetry recitation competitions and provides prizes for winners. Schools and organizations can use funds and materials to implement Poetry Out Loud at their institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland program with regional competition locations in Baltimore-central region (Towson), West-central region (Frederick), and South-central region (Oxon Hill). Schools and community organizations throughout Maryland may host local competitions.
requirements_list: Must be a high school student
Students select three poems from the Poetry Anthology to recite
All poems for 2025-26 are in the public domain
Winners from local competitions advance to regional competitions
Top three or four students from each regional competition advance to state competition
Winners determined solely by judges' scores based on Poetry Out Loud Evaluation Criteria
Students must provide titles and authors of poems and recitation order in advance to contest coordinator
Students may not change poem selections or order once submitted
Students must announce the poem title and author before reciting
Students must recite from memory
Epigraphs included with poems in the anthology should be recited
Stanza numbers and dedications are optional
Translated poems must include the translator's name
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and community organizations register with their state Poetry Out Loud coordinator by visiting PoetryOutLoud.org 'State Contacts' section. Registered schools or organizations host local competitions by January 16, 2026. Winners advance to regional competitions held in February 2026 in designated regions (Towson, Frederick, Oxon Hill). Regional winners advance to state competition on March 7, 2026. Independent or homeschooled students may register directly for regional competitions. All advancing students receive coaching from Poetry Coaches prior to competition. State winners advance to National Finals in Washington, DC. Students explore the online anthology of over 1,200 poems, select three poems to memorize, study and discuss the poems to understand their meaning, practice recitations with feedback, and then compete in local, regional, and state contests.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that encourages and supports relevant professional development opportunities for artists and arts organizations throughout Maryland. The program provides grants to help artists and arts organizations grow and learn, supporting long-term financial success through training, conferences, workshops, and other professional development activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding of up to $2,000 to support professional development opportunities such as training programs, conferences, workshops, and other learning experiences for artists and arts organizations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis from September 2, 2025 through March 31, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual artists and arts organizations in Maryland, including nonprofits, local government units, and colleges/universities/schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development activities such as training programs, conferences, workshops, and other learning opportunities that support growth for artists and arts organizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout the state of Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicants must be either an independent artist, a Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit in operation for at least one year, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college/university/school.
Applicants must identify a specific professional development opportunity that will take place during the application period.
Nonprofits must meet certain grant income requirements.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted through the Smart Simple online portal on a rolling basis from September 2, 2025, through March 31, 2026. A panel reviews applications submitted by the last day of each month during the following month. The agency then sends notifications. If approved, applicants will receive a grant agreement to process the payment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Incentive for Arts & Entertainment Districts
structured_extraction.program_description: Property owners of manufacturing, commercial, or industrial properties located in Arts & Entertainment Districts are eligible for a local property tax credit based on the difference between pre- and post-renovation assessments when the property has been wholly or partially renovated for use by qualified residing artists or arts and entertainment enterprises.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners receive a local property tax credit calculated based on the difference between the pre-renovation and post-renovation assessments of their property. The amount and duration of the tax credit, as well as the application process, is determined by the local government administering each individual Arts & Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: District manager contacts vary by district
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of manufacturing, commercial, or industrial property in Arts & Entertainment Districts
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property renovation costs for renovation of property for use by qualified residing artists or arts and entertainment enterprises
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located within one of Maryland's 29 designated Arts & Entertainment Districts
requirements_list: Own manufacturing, commercial, or industrial property in an Arts & Entertainment District
Complete substantial or partial renovation of the property
Renovate property for use by qualified residing artists or arts and entertainment enterprises
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the district manager for the specific Arts & Entertainment District where your property is located to inquire about available incentives and the application process. Each local government determines its own application requirements and timeline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Art Across Maryland - Conservation Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to organizations to conserve and preserve existing public artworks in Maryland. It offers two tracks: a Conservation Planning Grant (up to $10,000) supporting planning efforts such as collection inventories, digitization of records, community outreach, and assessments; and a Conservation Implementation Grant (up to $30,000) supporting the direct conservation of permanent public artworks where the project is fully developed with an identified project team and approval from artwork and site owners.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two grant tracks are available: (1) Conservation Planning Grant awards up to $10,000 to support artwork conservation planning including project administration, consultancy fees, community engagement, collection management services and technology, local survey work, inventory file digitization, artwork database creation, and collection management software purchase or lease. (2) Conservation Implementation Grant awards up to $30,000 to support the conservation of permanent public artwork including relocation, cleaning, structural repairs, site improvements, signage, and project management fees not to exceed 10% of the grant request. Eligible implementation activities include cleaning, waxing, coating, and painting by professional service providers; replacement or addition of components for structural integrity; landscape site improvements such as drainage and plant maintenance; lighting and electrical work for accessibility and energy efficiency; conservation of existing or creation of new identification and interpretive signage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) status, Maryland-based fiscal sponsors with Model A sponsorship agreements, units of government with arts program capacity, colleges and universities in Maryland, and pre-K through 12 schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning track: administrative fees related to project management and planning, consultant fees (professional conservators, artists, structural engineers, materials specialists, historians, and preservationists), community engagement including public meetings and community education, local survey work, inventory file digitization, artwork database creation, and collection management software purchase or lease. Implementation track: relocating public artwork within or to Maryland to increase public access and long-term preservation, conservation and maintenance activities such as cleaning, waxing, coating, and painting by professional service providers, replacement or addition of components for structural integrity, landscape site improvements such as drainage and plant maintenance, lighting and electrical work for accessibility and energy efficiency, conservation of existing or creation of new identification and interpretive signage, and organization administration or project management fee not to exceed 10 percent of the grant request.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The final location of the artwork to be conserved must be in Maryland. Applicants must be Maryland-based organizations.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit with IRS 501(c)(3) status based in Maryland, a Maryland-based fiscal sponsor with Model A sponsorship agreement, a unit of government, a college or university in Maryland, or a pre-K through 12 school
The artwork must be considered public art as defined by MSAC
The final location of the artwork must be in Maryland
The artwork must be publicly accessible
Artwork must comply with local jurisdiction regulations, permissions, and permitting requirements
The conservation project (Implementation track) must be fully developed with identified project team
Written support and approval from artwork and site owners must be in place (Implementation track)
Applicants may only submit one PAAM grant application per fiscal year
Grantees receiving Project Grants in the prior fiscal year are not eligible to apply for PAAM Project Grants in the subsequent fiscal year
Indirect costs cannot exceed 10 percent of the total grant request
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations apply via the secure online grants application software SmartSimple at marylandarts.smartsimple.com. Applicants must log in or create a free account. All applications must be completed and submitted by electronic means, including electronic signatures. Technical support is available during regular office hours at (410) 767-6555. Applicants must meet all revision deadlines after submission or the application will be withdrawn. Applications are evaluated using published rubrics for each grant track (Planning and Implementation).

structured_extraction.program_name: Public Art Across Maryland New Artworks Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to support the planning, creation, and installation of new local public art projects in Maryland. The program offers two grant types: Planning Grants for independent artists or organizations working with communities to plan and develop public art project proposals, and Project Grants for organizations working with identified artists to fabricate and install new public artwork developed through a community engagement process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two types of grants are offered: Planning Grants provide up to $10,000 to support independent artists or organizations creating public art proposals with communities. Eligible Planning Grant expenses include community engagement and outreach activities, artist fees and honorariums for proposal design, consultant services, facility and equipment rentals, online application software fees, and artwork proposal design and development including digital renderings, shop drawings, design and engineering reviews, and permit applications. Project Grants provide up to $30,000 to organizations to support fabrication and installation of new public artwork. Eligible Project Grant expenses include artist fees, contracted services such as studio assistants, fabricators, contractors, and installers, equipment and space rentals for fabrication and installation, artwork materials and tools, plaques and interpretive signage, transportation of artwork to site, insurance and permitting fees, and organization administration and project management fees not to exceed 10 percent of the total grant request, and artwork dedication expenses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY2026 New Artworks grant applications will be accepted from September 8 through December 12, 2025. Final reports for Project Grants funded in FY2025 are due September 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Independent artists who are Maryland residents and are not enrolled in a high school, undergraduate, or graduate degree program, or nonprofit organizations with 501(c)3 status, fiscal sponsors, government units, colleges, universities, and schools based in Maryland interested in planning, creating, or installing new public art projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planning Grant: community engagement and outreach activities, artist fees and honorariums for proposal design, consultant services, facility and equipment rentals, online application software, artwork proposal design and development including digital renderings, shop drawings, design and engineering reviews, and permit applications. Project Grant: artist fees, contracted services such as studio assistants, fabricators, contractors, and installers, equipment and space rentals for fabrication and installation, artwork materials and tools, plaques and interpretive signage, transportation of artwork to site, insurance and permitting fees, organization administration and project management fees (up to 10 percent of grant request), and artwork dedication expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Independent artists must be Maryland residents owning or renting residential property in Maryland for at least six months before application submission. Organizations must be based in Maryland. Artwork must be sited in Maryland in locations accessible to the public such as parks, trails, plazas, sidewalks, community centers, libraries, schools, and local government buildings.
requirements_list: Independent artists must be Maryland residents owning or renting residential property in Maryland for at least six months before application submission
Independent artists must be 18 years of age or older
Independent artists must not be enrolled in any matriculated high school, undergraduate, or graduate degree program at the time of application
Independent artists must be the lead artist whose original work is included in the proposed activities
Organizations must be nonprofit with 501(c)3 status, Maryland-based fiscal sponsor, unit of government, college, university, or school based in Maryland
For collaborative artist groups, at least 50 percent must be Maryland residents
Applicants may only submit one PAAM grant application per fiscal year
Artwork must be public art as defined by MSAC
Artwork must be designed by a Maryland artist
Artwork must be new, original, and specifically designed for the PAAM program
For Project Grants, artist must be fully identified at time of application
