For Project Grants, artwork must be fully designed at time of application
For Project Grants, applicant must have proof of permission to install artwork at proposed site at time of application
For Project Grants, artwork must have been developed through a community engagement process
Artwork must be publicly accessible
Artwork must comply with local jurisdiction regulations, permissions, and permitting requirements
Grantees receiving Project Grants in prior fiscal year are not eligible to apply for any PAAM Project Grant in subsequent fiscal year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply through the secure online grants application software SmartSimple. To apply: (1) Create a free account at marylandarts.smartsimple.com; (2) Complete application with all required information, project narrative, budget, and supporting materials such as artwork renderings, site plans, letters of support, proof of site permission (for Project Grants), and evidence of community engagement (for Project Grants); (3) Submit application electronically with an electronic signature by the deadline; (4) Meet all revision deadlines after submission if requested by program staff. Applications are evaluated using published rubrics that assess project quality, community engagement, artistic merit, feasibility, and alignment with program goals. Applicants will be notified of funding decisions following the review period. Grantees receiving Project Grants must submit final reports by September 30, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Special Request Grants support arts organizations and programs with needs that fall outside the eligibility of established MSAC grant programs. The program funds three types of activities: pilot or one-time projects, innovative projects addressing stated constituent needs, and capacity-building efforts for Maryland's arts sector. It also supports special arts activities that are not part of an organization's regular budget and represent a departure from regular activities but align with MSAC's goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants ranging from $2,000 to $25,000 to support arts activities outside an organization's regular budget.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Arts organizations and programs, including other organizations with dedicated arts programs, whose needs fall outside the eligibility of established MSAC grant programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pilot or one-time arts projects, innovative projects addressing constituent needs, and capacity-building efforts for arts organizations; also funds arts activities that are outside of an organization's regular budget and different from its usual activities.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an Arts Organization or an organization with a dedicated Arts Program.
Grantees must submit a final report after the project is complete.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A panel evaluates applications electronically. The panel uses criteria from the grant guidelines to score each application. Panelists assign points and provide written comments for each question.

structured_extraction.program_name: 2022 Equipment Assistance Grants for National School Lunch Program (NSLP) Operator
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant provides funds for National School Lunch Program operators to purchase equipment that serves healthier school meals, improves food safety, and expands access to school meals. Equipment requests may include new equipment, renovation of equipment, or replacement of equipment. Individual items must have a value greater than $1,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants totaling $954,126 in 2022 funding to purchase equipment valued at greater than $1,000 per item to support school meal operations. Equipment may be new, renovated, or replacement items. Grant operates in two phases: Phase 1 (October 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024) and Phase 2 reallocation (July 1, 2024 through September 30, 2024). Awards are made within 30 days of the application deadline.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, February 1, 2023. No later than 5:00 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: National School Lunch Program operators in Maryland schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of equipment (new, renovated, or replacement) to serve healthier school meals, improve food safety, and expand access to school meals. Each item must cost more than $1,000.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All schools in Maryland participating in the National School Lunch Program
requirements_list: Equipment items must have a value greater than $1,000
All individual items requested must have a value greater than $1,000
Costs incurred prior to grant approval may not be funded through the award
Applicant must be a National School Lunch Program operator
Priority given to high-needs schools where 50 percent or more of enrolled students are eligible for free or reduced-price meals
Priority given to schools that have not previously received an NSLP Equipment Grant

Grantee must comply with state and federal statutes and regulations including Civil Rights Act of 1964, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 34, Elementary and Secondary Education Act, Education Department General Administrative Regulations (EDGAR), General Education Provisions Act (GEPA), and Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)

Grantee shall retain all records of financial transactions and accounts relating to the grant for a period of five years or longer if required by federal regulation
Entities expending federal funds of $750,000 or more in a single fiscal year must have an annual financial and compliance audit in accordance with 2 CFR Subpart F 200.500 et. seq.
Grantee must receive prior written approval from MSDE Program Monitor before implementing programmatic changes
Grantee must receive prior written approval from MSDE Program Monitor for any budgetary realignment of $1,000 or 15% of total object, program or category of expenditure, whichever is greater
Budget realignments must be submitted at least 45 days prior to the end of the grant period
Requests for grant extension must be submitted at least 45 days prior to the end of the grant period
If receiving a Phase 1 award, all spending must be completed and final report submitted no later than June 30, 2024
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants access the application and Grant Information Guide (GIG) released on December 26, 2022 on the MSDE Grants webpage. The GIG provides an overview of all details and serves as a guide for completing the grant application. Completed applications must include Goals, Measurable Outcomes and Evidence of Impact, Plan of Operation, Key Personnel, and Project Timeline. Submit the completed application by February 1, 2023 at 5:00 p.m. EST. Awards are made within 30 days of the application deadline with Notices of Grant Award (NOGAs) to follow. Two virtual customer service support sessions were available on January 9, 2023 and January 18, 2023 to review requirements and answer questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: 21st Century Community Learning Centers (21st CCLC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Funds community learning centers that provide students with academic enrichment opportunities and additional services to complement their regular school program. Centers offer literacy instruction and related educational development programs for families of participating students. Programs target students and families from schools eligible for Title I schoolwide programs or schools serving high percentages of low-income students. The program is officially known as the Nita M. Lowey 21st Century Community Learning Centers Maryland Out-of-School Time Programs for the Future (MD OST PFTF).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grants awarded through a competitive application process for a three-year period (36 months total). Grants are level-funded at 100% of the original award for all three years, contingent on funding availability and satisfactory performance. Total funds available: $22.6 million (FY25). MSDE uses 93% of received funds to support out-of-school time programs. Grant amounts may be reduced based on grantee inability to meet goals and performance measures, including failure to serve at least 85% of proposed participant levels, or based on fiscal or programmatic concerns. Grantees must attend bi-monthly networking meetings providing technical assistance from Maryland State Department of Education personnel, peer-to-peer technical assistance, and resources selected by coordinators based on grantee needs. Grant funds must be expended in the grant year awarded; MSDE does not allow carryover into following grant years.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Reginald Burke, Executive Director, Office of Federal Programs, Division of Student Support and Federal Programs
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies, schools, faith-based organizations, community-based organizations, institutions of higher education, for-profit corporations, and consortiums serving students and families from Title I schools or schools with high percentages of low-income students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic enrichment opportunities, literacy instruction, related educational development programs, complementary services to support student academics and family engagement. Allowable expenses include: intervention strategies and evidence-based curriculum; salaries and fringe benefits for staff; professional development and trainings; consultants and evaluators; classroom materials and supplies; remedial and academic enrichment programs; core academic subject instruction; arts and music education; entrepreneurial education and college/career readiness programs; tutoring and mentoring; programs for limited English proficient students; recreational activities; technology education; expanded library services; drug and violence prevention programs; counseling; and character education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all Maryland counties. Services must be provided to students and families who primarily attend schools eligible for Title I schoolwide programs, Title I schools serving at least 40% students from low-income families, high schools with graduation rates less than 67%, or other schools determined by the LEA to need intervention and support. Private school students must have comparable opportunities for participation.
requirements_list: Services must target students and families from Title I eligible schools or schools serving high percentages (at least 40%) of low-income students
Grantees must attend bi-monthly networking meetings and required out-of-school (OST) national and regional conferences, MSDE grantee meetings and trainings
Must provide families with literacy instruction and related educational development programs

Eligible applicants include local education agencies, interagency/interdepartmental organizations, community and faith-based organizations, private or public organizations, institutions of higher education, and consortiums of two or more eligible entities

School year programs must provide no less than 12 hours of programming per week (weekdays and/or Saturdays) for 25 weeks OR no less than 4 hours on Saturdays only for 25 weeks, with at least 4 hours of academic programming per week for 25 weeks OR at least 1 hour of academic programming per Saturday for 25 weeks
Summer only programs must provide no less than 80 hours total with at least 32 hours of onsite academic and enrichment programming on the calendar
School year and summer programs must meet school year requirements AND provide no less than 80 hours for summer with at least 32 hours onsite academic and enrichment programming
Must demonstrate adequate progress toward achieving all measurable objectives
Must meet or exceed 85% of the proposed level of students served as indicated in the original application or most recent Grant Renewal Application
Must submit required documentation timely including monitoring components, corrective actions, monthly reimbursement reports, and detailed local narrative evaluation reports
Must maintain and submit Government Performance and Results Act (GPRA) data to U.S. Department of Education by established deadlines
Must participate fully in statewide evaluation activities
Must comply with all applicable state statutory and regulatory requirements

Must provide evidence of compliance with federal, state, and local fire, health, zoning codes, and safety standards; non-LEA subrecipients in non-public school facilities must submit copies of all required licenses, certifications, Use and Occupancy (U&O) permits, and current Fire Inspection reports per operating site
Must provide description of comparable opportunities for public and private school students and evidence of consultation with private school officials
Must describe efforts to provide timely notice of intent to apply and dissemination of information
Programming must align with Maryland College and Career Readiness Standards
Programs should address at least one Maryland Leads Strategy, Maryland Strategic Plan, or Blueprint for Maryland's Future priority area
Academic enrichment programs must be based on evidence-based research meeting Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA) criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit renewal applications through a Qualtrics application portal by the deadline. The renewal application requires submission of performance data for the previous year and a renewal proposal for the upcoming year. Applicants must include exhibits covering Performance Goals and Indicators, Management Plan, Partner Plan, and Evaluation Plan. Customer service support sessions are offered to assist applicants. Applications are reviewed competitively. Upon submission, MSDE reviews the Grant Renewal Application and performance data including start-up reports, Critical Elements Monitoring, timely invoice submissions, and number of amendments. Approved subgrantees for subsequent year funding receive a risk assessment level (1-5) reflected on the Notification of Grant Award (NOGA). Final documents must be uploaded to the Critical Elements Monitoring folder by the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: Assists job seekers with Autism with self-determination and employment readiness skills through small group, interactive learning sessions.

Offered in-person in your community, at DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) campus in Baltimore, and online.

structured_extraction.program_name: Accreditation Support Fund (Maryland Program Accreditation and National Accreditation)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Accreditation Support Fund, administered by the Maryland State Department of Education, provides financial assistance to licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers, and school-age only programs to help cover the costs associated with obtaining and maintaining accreditation. The fund has two components: (1) National Accreditation Support, which covers required application fees for national accreditation (initial application, renewal application, and annual update fees) charged by recognized national accrediting organizations; and (2) Maryland Program Accreditation Support, which covers the cost of instructional materials needed to pursue Maryland Program Accreditation. Accredited programs may also use funds to purchase instructional materials for their early learning programs. The program is part of Maryland EXCELS and aims to improve the quality of early childhood and school-age child care programs statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides two types of support: (1) National Accreditation Support covers required application fees for national accreditation with recognized organizations (American Montessori Society, NAEYC, NAFCC, Cognia Early Learning Accreditation, and others), including initial applications, renewal applications, and annual update fees. Funding cannot exceed the fee charged by the accrediting organization. Awards are paid directly to the accrediting organization on the applicant's behalf. (2) Maryland Program Accreditation Support provides reimbursement for non-consumable instructional materials associated with pursuing or maintaining Maryland Program Accreditation. Maximum reimbursement is $2,500 for programs serving 100 or fewer children, or $3,000 for programs serving more than 100 children per accreditation cycle. Eligible materials include curricula, classroom technology, outdoor play equipment, science and sensory materials, books, and literacy activities. Funds cannot be used for facility improvements, association membership fees, staff training, consumable items (paint, crayons, markers, glue, paper), or costs already paid through another funding source. Purchases must have been made within 12 months before the application date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers, school-age only programs, and public pre-K programs in Maryland that are pursuing or maintaining Maryland Program Accreditation or national accreditation, and participating in Maryland EXCELS.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: (1) National Accreditation: required application fees for national accreditation including initial applications, renewal applications, and annual update fees with recognized accrediting organizations. (2) Maryland Program Accreditation: non-consumable instructional materials including curricula, classroom technology, outdoor play equipment, science and sensory materials, books and literacy activities, and other learning materials. Cannot be used for facility improvements, association membership fees, staff training, consumable items, or costs paid through another funding source.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide—available to all licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers, school-age only programs, and public pre-K programs in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center, registered family child care provider, school-age only program, or public pre-K program

Must be pursuing or maintaining Maryland Program Accreditation or national accreditation with a recognized accrediting organization (NAFCC, NAEYC, Cognia Early Learning Accreditation, AMS, AMI/USA, AIMS, AWSNA, COA/ASA, Lumen Accreditation, Maryland Accreditation, MSA-CESS, NAC, or NECPA)
Program must be participating in Maryland EXCELS
For National Accreditation: must have completed application submitted to accrediting organization and completed Accreditation Work Plan
For Maryland Accreditation: must have completed Initial Self-Appraisal or current Maryland Accreditation status
Cannot use funds for facility improvements, association membership fees, or staff training
Cannot use funds for consumable items (paint, crayons, markers, glue, paper)
Cannot use funds for costs that are paid through another funding source
Cannot use funds for costs greater than the fee charged by the accreditation organization (National Accreditation only)
Purchases for reimbursement must have been made within 12 months before the application date (Maryland Accreditation only)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For National Accreditation Support: (1) Gather required documents: copy of completed NAFCC or national accrediting organization application, completed Accreditation Work Plan detailing steps and due dates to achieve accreditation, copy of accrediting organization's fee page, proof of membership in accrediting organization, and copy of current accreditation certificate if currently accredited; (2) Submit the Application for National Accreditation Support through the Maryland One Stop portal at onestop.md.gov. For Maryland Program Accreditation Support: (1) Gather receipts for learning materials purchased during the accreditation process or accredited status (within 12 months of application); (2) Complete the Infants and Toddlers Classroom Learning Materials Checklist and/or Preschool and School-Age Classroom Learning Materials Checklist with information matching receipts; (3) Submit the Application for Maryland Accreditation Support through the Maryland One Stop portal. For both programs: Applications will be reviewed within 30 days of submission. MSDE Accreditation Manager or Accreditation Specialist will notify applicants via email and OneStop of application status. If documentation is missing or incorrect, MSDE will request revisions. If approved, payment for National Accreditation is paid directly to the accrediting organization; for Maryland Accreditation, reimbursement is processed for payment. Programs may also contact Quality Assurance Specialists for guidance and support. Video tutorials are available to guide applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 90-minute annual training update required for all child care staff and family child care providers. The training covers health, safety, and nutrition topics and qualifies for 1.5 continuing education hours toward Core of Knowledge requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training update that must be completed by all child care staff and family child care providers by December 31, 2025. Newly approved family child care providers and staff hired from October to December 2025 must complete the training by March 31, 2026. The training consists of multiple modules covering health, safety, and nutrition topics. Upon successful completion of all topics and the Final Review Activity with a score of 80% or higher, participants unlock and receive a Certificate of Completion that must be downloaded and saved. Participants can complete the training one section at a time, as the system remembers where they left off.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Must be completed by December 31, 2025. Newly approved providers and staff hired October-December 2025 must complete by March 31, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All child care staff and family child care providers in Maryland. Also recommended for child care substitutes and volunteers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This is a training program with no financial assistance component.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through online access via Canvas.
requirements_list: Must be a child care staff member or family child care provider
Must complete the 90-minute training consisting of multiple modules
Must access training online at https://msde.instructure.com/login/canvas using valid email address and password credentials
Must achieve a score of 80% or higher on the Final Review Activity
Must download and save the Certificate of Completion
Newly approved providers and those hired October-December 2025 have an extended deadline of March 31, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Access the training by going to https://msde.instructure.com/login/canvas. Log in with your email address and password. From the welcome page, click the Educator Resources button, then click Early Childhood Modules, then click the Basic Health and Safety Annual Update 2025 button. Select Introduction to Basic Health and Safety to start. Complete the Introduction module first, which will unlock the other training topics. Complete each topic in any order, using the EXIT COURSE button before leaving each section. The system will remember your progress. Once all topics are complete, the Final Review module becomes available. Complete the Final Review with a score of 80% or higher to unlock the Certificate of Completion module. Download and save your Certificate of Completion and email it to your licensing specialist.

structured_extraction.program_description: Registered apprenticeship program that provides high-quality career-connected learning for students, combining paid on-the-job training with related technical instruction. Students gain work experience while in school in a variety of industries and can participate during the school day, after school, over the summer, or on weekends.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students receive 450 hours of paid on-the-job training and 144 hours of related technical instruction. Apprenticeship placements and schedules are set by the employer and student to meet individual needs, with flexibility to participate during school day, after school, over the summer, or on weekends.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in Maryland public schools and adult apprentices interested in career-connected learning opportunities across various industries.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid on-the-job training and related technical instruction in approved apprenticeship positions. Adult apprentice programs can help with college tuition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland, delivered in partnership with local school districts.
requirements_list: Approved by the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council
Consists of 450 hours of paid on-the-job training
Consists of 144 hours of related technical instruction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students and families should talk to their school's apprenticeship or career-connected learning coordinator to explore opportunities, eligibility, and scheduling. The coordinator will help match students with employers based on their career interests and availability. Employers can partner with a Maryland Department of Labor Navigator to learn how to register positions and host student apprentices.

structured_extraction.program_description: DORS Rehabilitation Technology Services provides customized assessments and training to help individuals with disabilities find and learn to use assistive technology to support their employment and educational goals. Services include assessment, equipment provision, training, and ongoing technical support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS provides customized assessments for individuals with disabilities to determine appropriate assistive technology. The program offers a range of equipment including desktop or portable video magnifiers, note-taking devices, specialized software (voice recognition, screen reading, reading and writing assistance), and mobile devices or apps for organization and time management. Training is provided on equipment use and includes classes on specific software such as JAWS screen reading software and ZoomText magnification and screen reading software, as well as specialized classes based on individual needs. Assessments and training can be held at the Work and Training Center in Baltimore or in the individual's community. Ongoing technical support is available to individuals and groups.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: Contact your DORS Counselor or local office for more information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers and students with disabilities who are DORS consumers and have an employment or educational goal
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistive technology equipment and software; training and technical support on use of assistive technology
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; services available at Work and Training Center in Baltimore or in the individual's community
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer
Must have an employment or educational goal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals should contact their DORS Counselor or local DORS office. Alternatively, individuals can request DORS services via QR code. Staff will conduct a customized assessment to identify appropriate assistive technology and provide training and technical support.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 12-week training course that prepares individuals with disabilities to work in entry-level automotive detailing jobs, covering both classroom instruction and hands-on experience in exterior and interior vehicle cleaning, polishing, waxing, and maintenance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 12-week training program delivered in classroom and hands-on formats at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore. The program includes videos, lectures, product demonstrations, and extensive practical experience. Participants learn customer service skills, interior and exterior cleaning techniques, equipment operation and safety (including orbital dual action buffers, power washers, and drill brushes), chemical handling and solution mixing, use of clay bars, removing minor defects and scratches, and advanced detailing techniques such as compounding and waxing. Training covers the quality hands-on work required by high-end detail shops or dealerships. Industry professionals serve as guest instructors.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: Maryland DORS Counselor or local office; services can be requested via QR code available on the program materials
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities seeking entry-level employment in automotive detailing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job training in automotive detailing techniques and customer service for entry-level work in detail shops and dealerships.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Training is provided at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore.
requirements_list: Valid driver's license with no more than two points
3rd grade or higher reading comprehension level and basic math skills
Ability to lift 50 pounds
Ability to squat, stoop and kneel
Certain criminal backgrounds may disqualify an individual from the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office for more information or to request DORS Services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 16-week training course that prepares job seekers with disabilities to work in the automotive industry as entry-level general service technicians. Students learn vehicle maintenance and repair tasks including lubrication, tire service, battery replacement, tune-ups, brake repair, and vehicle inspections using modern automotive equipment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 16-week in-person training program provided at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in northeast Baltimore. The program includes instruction in customer service, shop safety, automotive maintenance and repair, and hands-on training with equipment such as tire balancing machines, 4-wheel alignment lifts, and hand tools. Training covers lubrication and fluid changes, tire changing and balancing, battery testing and replacement, tune-ups, vehicle inspections, and brake repair.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities seeking entry-level automotive general service technician positions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in automotive maintenance, repair, customer service, and shop safety skills using state-of-the-art equipment and facilities at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center

3rd grade reading level

No disqualifying criminal background

structured_extraction.program_description: A free online training course that meets state and federal requirements of the Child Care and Development Block Grant (CCDBG). All child care staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for the care and safety of children in a licensed child care program must complete this training. The course covers health, safety, and nutrition topics and typically takes 3 hours to complete across four modules.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training course delivered through the MSDE Canvas learning management system at https://msde.instructure.com. Participants must complete all four modules (Introduction, and three additional topic modules) in order and a Final Review and Survey to receive a certificate of completion. The course must be completed within the designated training period for each monthly cohort (typically 21 days). Participants must score a minimum of 80% on the Final Review and Survey to receive a certificate. Each account receives two attempts to pass the Final Assessment. If a participant scores below 80% on the first attempt, they may retake the Final Review and Survey one additional time before the course ends. If an account has completed any course sections and scored below 80%, the participant will not be allowed to register for the online course again; the grade stands as final. Only registrants who have not completed any course sections may register for a future course. Participants do not need to complete the entire training in one sitting; they can stop and return without starting over by clicking EXIT COURSE and logging back in later. Face-to-face training is also available through approved trainers at a cost set by the trainer or training organization. New employees have 90 days after hire to complete the course to be in compliance.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens and closes on a monthly basis. May cohort registration opens April 13 at 9:00 am and closes April 23 at 12:00 pm. Training must be completed by May 22.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers, staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for the care and safety of children in licensed child care programs in Maryland. New employees must complete within 90 days of hire.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This training program does not provide financial assistance. It is an educational/training requirement for maintaining a child care license or registration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Online training is available to all providers. Face-to-face training through approved trainers is available in various locations.
requirements_list: Must be a child care provider, staff member, substitute, or adult responsible for care and safety of children in a licensed child care program
New employees must complete within 90 days after hire to be in compliance
Must have a valid email address to register
Each registrant is only allowed one email address; there can only be one name associated with one email address
Must complete all four modules in order (Introduction must be completed first; other modules unlock after Introduction is complete)
Must complete the Final Review and Survey
Must score a minimum of 80% on the Final Review and Survey to receive a certificate
Each account receives two attempts to pass the Final Assessment
If you score below 80% on the first attempt, you may retake once; if you score below 80% overall, you cannot register for the online course again
Must complete training before the course end date (accounts expire at end of each session)
Must have technical skills including using a mouse, typing, using email, viewing videos, navigating the internet, and printing from a browser (or arrange face-to-face training)
Must use EXIT COURSE button when leaving the training to ensure progress is saved
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Check the Basic Health and Safety Training web page for monthly registration dates. 2. Register online during the designated one-week registration period each month using the registration form. 3. A confirmation email will be sent with login instructions. 4. Go to https://msde.instructure.com/login/canvas and type your email address as the username. 5. Type the password you created in the Password window. 6. Select Introduction to Basic Health and Safety first; other modules are locked until Introduction is complete. 7. Complete all four modules in any order after the Introduction (as you complete each topic, a green check mark appears). 8. Once all topics are complete, the Final Review module will be available. 9. Take the Final Review and Survey in one sitting. 10. Submit the survey to receive an immediate score. 11. If you score 80% or higher, your Certificate of Completion appears in the Modules section. 12. Print and save your certificate before the course ends (MSDE does not have or save copies of certificates). 13. If you score below 80%, you have one additional attempt to retake the Final Review and Survey before the course ends. 14. You do not need to complete the entire training in one sitting; you can log back in and continue from where you left off, but always use the EXIT COURSE button when leaving. 15. For questions or issues, email healthandsafetyocc.msde@maryland.gov with your full name and email address. Email inquiries will be addressed in the order received.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides scholarship awards to eligible students who qualify for free or reduced-price school meals to attend participating nonpublic schools in Maryland. Priority is given to students who received BOOST scholarships in the previous year and their siblings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards to students for tuition at participating nonpublic schools. Award amounts are determined by the BOOST Advisory Board based on total funding available, household income, student academic level, and financial assistance provided by the school. The award is capped at the tuition owed to the school after accounting for any school discounts and cannot exceed the family's tuition responsibility. Estimated award amounts are around 2,500 scholarships from approximately $9,000,000 in funding for the 2026-2027 school year. Scholarship checks are sent to the school and must be signed by the parent/guardian to be deposited to the student's tuition account. Funds can only be used for tuition and required fees for enrollment, not transportation or meals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 8, 2026, no later than 11:59 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.contact_name: Allison Sanborn, Program Manager; James Clark, Administrative Support
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in kindergarten through 12th grade whose families qualify for free or reduced-price school meals and who are enrolled or accepted at participating nonpublic schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and required fees for enrollment at participating nonpublic schools for students in kindergarten through 12th grade. Funds cannot be used for transportation or meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties where participating nonpublic schools are located. As of March 2026, 178 nonpublic schools across 19 jurisdictions participate in the program.
requirements_list: Student must qualify for free and reduced-price meals (FARMs) based on household income verification
Student must be enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school for the 2026-2027 school year
Student must be entering grades kindergarten through 12th grade for the 2026-2027 school year (Pre-K students are not eligible)
Parent/guardian must complete online BOOST Scholarship application through Submittable portal
Parent/guardian must upload 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns for income and household size verification
Parent/guardian must provide child's full name as it appears on birth certificate
Parent/guardian must indicate whether child received BOOST award last year or is sibling of BOOST recipient
Parent/guardian must identify the nonpublic school the child will attend and current school enrollment status
Parent/guardian must indicate if child has learning disability and receives special education services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through the Submittable portal from March 9 through May 8, 2026. Parents/guardians complete the application and upload their 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns for income and household size verification. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and completeness on a rolling basis and are not first-come-first-serve. After May 8, all application data is compiled and ranked by household income as a percentage of federal poverty level. The BOOST Advisory Board convenes in June/July 2026 to determine base award amounts and additional awards for special education students. Parents/guardians are notified of award eligibility by August 2026. Those offered awards must accept or decline by the deadline in their notification. Participating schools confirm student enrollment and submit required documentation. Scholarship checks are distributed to schools between September and December 2026. As parents decline awards, MSDE continues to offer scholarships to the next eligible applicants on the waiting list, with no new awards offered after December 11, 2026. Customer service support sessions and weekly virtual office hours are available for parents during the application period.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF)
structured_extraction.program_description: A tuition assistance and professional development program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that helps child care providers in Maryland pay for college education to earn degrees in early childhood education, child development, elementary education, or special education. Scholarship/tuition payments are made directly to accredited participating colleges and universities, not reimbursed to participants. The program also supports broader professional development and training opportunities for child care providers participating in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program at Level Two or higher.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tuition assistance provided by direct payment to participating accredited colleges and universities in Maryland. Awards may be used for tuition, fees, and required textbooks toward completion of a college degree in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education. Funds cannot be used to pay for costs previously incurred prior to the award. Recipients must maintain employment as a child care provider at least 10 hours per week while participating. Funds are awarded for one school year at a time with annual review of academic performance. The fund does not reimburse participants; payments go directly to the institution. Upon completion of the degree or withdrawal from the fund, recipients must fulfill a service commitment requirement: two years for associate degree, four years for bachelor's degree, or 2.5 years for master's degree (or one month per college credit completed). Recipients must work at least 20 hours per week in an approved child care facility during the service commitment period or repay the full amount paid on their behalf.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First-time applications are due by March 1. Continuation applications (including transfers to four-year colleges) are due by June 30.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and staff who work in licensed child care centers or are registered family child care providers in Maryland, work at least 10 hours per week, and are participating in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program at Level Two or higher.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, fees, and required textbooks for associate or bachelor's degrees in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education at accredited participating Maryland colleges and universities. Funds can only be used toward the completion of a college degree in an approved field and cannot be used to pay for costs previously incurred prior to award approval.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Must work in a licensed child care center or be a registered family child care provider in Maryland. Must maintain employment in Maryland while participating in the program and agree to work in child care in Maryland for at least 20 hours per week after completing the degree or withdrawing from the fund.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Get accepted into a CCCPDF participating college or university of your choice. Step 2: Schedule an appointment with the CCCPDF Coordinator at that college to which you have been accepted and complete the application process. Step 3: Submit a completed CCCPDF application with all required documentation (signed and dated application, proof of at least one year child care experience, signed letter from current employer or current family child care license, documentation of participation in Maryland Child Care Credential Program at Level Two or higher, letter of acceptance with declared major from the participating college, and professional development plan) through the college Coordinator. The Coordinator must review the application checklist for completion and sign it before submission to MSDE. First-time applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. MSDE notifies applicants by letter of fund approval or denial. Funds are distributed directly to the college or university.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Pandemic Relief Fund provides grants to licensed child care centers and registered family child care providers to help meet increased operating costs and provide financial relief during the COVID-19 pandemic. Funded through the Coronavirus Response and Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act of 2021, this program made $60 million available statewide to support child care programs affected by the pandemic.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $2,400 to $60,000 depending on the licensed capacity of the child care facility. Funds must be used for increased operational costs and pandemic relief and recovery for child care operations related to the COVID-19 pandemic. All grant funds must be spent by December 31, 2021. Recipients must maintain financial documentation for 5 years and may be subject to random audits. Funds are subject to offset for state of Maryland tax debts, but such captured funds are automatically released the following day. Federal tax debts must be resolved directly with the IRS. Recipients will receive a 1099-G form for reporting purposes if the grant amount exceeds $600.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and registered family child care providers in Maryland that are operating as of March 3, 2021
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Increased operational costs and pandemic relief and recovery for child care operations related to the COVID-19 pandemic. Funds must be spent by December 31, 2021.

If multiple locations exist, separate applications required for each licensed location

Provider ID required for application; do not submit social security number

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Quality Incentive Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Quality Incentive Grant Program supports child care providers in improving the professionalism and quality of their programs and initiatives that enhance children's school readiness. Funds help providers acquire training, education, supplies, materials, and equipment to create stimulating learning environments aligned with early childhood development standards. Grants are awarded quarterly based on facility size, enabling child care centers and family child care homes across Maryland to implement knowledge gained through professional development and enhance the overall quality of care for children.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded quarterly (in January, April, July, and October) based on facility size. Providers with fewer than 10 children may receive up to $1,000. Facilities with up to 29 children may receive up to $1,500. Facilities with more than 30 children may receive up to $2,500. Child care providers are eligible for a grant award once every three years. Funds can be used to purchase supplies, materials, and equipment that improve or enhance quality of care, as well as support training and education activities that implement knowledge gained through professional development.

The program guide lists eligible and non-eligible expenses.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Scholarship (CCS) Program, administered by the Maryland State Department of Education, helps eligible Maryland families pay for high-quality child care and early education programs. The program serves over 45,000 children as of 2025 and provides payment scholarships to cover part of child care costs for children under 13, or individuals aged 13-19 with qualifying disabilities. Families receive either a temporary 60-day scholarship (issued within three business days via the Fast Track process) or a full 52-week scholarship. Families are responsible for paying a State-assigned co-payment and any amount above the scholarship rate directly to their provider. Families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) have a $0 co-payment. The program also supports families experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, and fosters quality child care and coordination among early childhood development and afterschool programs. As of May 1, 2025, the program temporarily stopped issuing scholarships to new families due to budget constraints; families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are exempt from the enrollment freeze. Existing enrollees continue to receive support, and applications are still accepted and placed on a Frozen Status List (waitlist) pending available funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible families receive payment scholarships from CCS Central 2 that cover part of their child care costs. Scholarship amounts range based on family income and the number of children enrolled; amounts decrease for families with more than one child receiving a scholarship. The co-payment (amount the family must pay) ranges from $0 to $3 per week. There are three types of scholarships: (1) Temporary 60-day scholarships issued within three business days via the Fast Track process to help with immediate child care costs while the full application is processed; (2) Full 52-week formal scholarships for care at Maryland registered family homes or licensed child care centers; and (3) Informal scholarships for relative care or non-relative care in the child's home. Families receiving TCA or SSI have a $0 co-payment. Family income must be below the Initial Income Scale for new applications (ranging from $76,117 for a family of 2 to $167,904 for a family of 12) or the Continuation Income Scale for existing scholarship holders (ranging from $86,266 for a family of 2 to $190,292 for a family of 12). Families who qualify but cannot be awarded due to limited funding are placed on a Frozen Status List. Families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are not subject to the enrollment freeze. Existing families continue receiving scholarships as long as they remain qualified and submit renewal forms on time. Scholarships can be used for before and after school child care as well as early childhood and school-age care programs. Child care providers receive advance payments processed on the 1st and 15th of each month. Advance payment calculations occur on the last Friday of each month for the upcoming advance payment if the provider submits all required forms at least 5 days before the last Friday of the month. Providers receiving payment by direct deposit can anticipate payment from the Maryland State Comptroller's Office within 7 days after completion of payment processing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Starting May 1, 2025, the program temporarily stopped issuing scholarships to new families due to budget constraints. As of April 14, 2026, the program is not accepting new applications. Applications are still accepted on an ongoing basis and placed on a waitlist (Frozen Status List) pending available funding. Fast Track applications are processed within 3 business days. Full applications are determined within 30 calendar days from date of submission or within 5 business days of receipt of all required documentation.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible Maryland resident families who are working, in an approved training program, or attending school, and have children younger than 13 or individuals aged 13-19 with qualifying disabilities. For families where both parents live in the same household, both parents must meet all eligibility requirements. Child care providers (formal and informal) serving scholarship recipients are also part of the program.

Scholarships can be used for before and after school child care as well as early childhood and school-age care programs.

Child must be immunized to Maryland state standards or documentation supporting exemption from immunization must be provided

Must register in the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal at family.childcareportals.org

For Fast Track application: submit proof of employment or enrollment in training/school on company/school letterhead, proof of residency (utility bill, lease, mortgage statement, or Maryland driver's license with matching address), and proof of income (most recent 4 weeks of consecutive pay stubs for weekly/bi-weekly/semi-monthly employment, or 1 most recent paystub for annual employment)

For full 52-week scholarship: provide most recent four consecutive weeks of pay stubs, proof of identity for all household members, proof of approved activity, proof of all other income (alimony, armed services pay, social security, SSI, self-employment, TCA, tips/commission, unemployment benefits, veterans assistance, workers compensation), proof of address within 15 days of Fast Track approval, and documentation of other benefits (SNAP, TCA, WAG, GBI, housing assistance)

Existing scholarship holders must complete recertification on time to continue receiving benefits

Low-income family status (for Child Care and Development Fund component)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Create an account on the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal at family.childcareportals.org by clicking 'Register for a New Account' and verifying your email with a verification code sent to your inbox. Step 2: Click 'Start a New Scholarship Application' on the Application Dashboard. Step 3: For Fast Track (one-time only option for new customers): Complete and submit the short online Fast Track scholarship application with three required documents: proof of employment or enrollment in training/school on company/school letterhead, proof of residency (utility bill, lease, mortgage statement, or Maryland driver's license), and proof of income (most recent 4 weeks of pay stubs representing consecutive wages, or tax documentation for self-employed applicants). All applicants must provide the most recent 30 days of continuous income for standard employment or most recent 90 days for self-employment. Step 4: The Fast Track application is processed within 3 business days by CCS Central 2. Step 5: If eligible, a temporary 60-day scholarship is issued within 3 business days via Fast Track to help with child care costs while the full application is processed. Step 6: Within 15 days of Fast Track approval, submit a Full Scholarship Application with additional documentation: most recent four consecutive weeks of pay stubs, proof of identity for all household members (driver's license, passport, or government-issued ID for adults; birth certificate for children), proof of address on utility bill/lease/mortgage statement matching application address, proof of approved activity schedule on employer or school letterhead, proof of all other income, proof of citizenship or qualified alien status for all children (birth certificate or Head Start enrollment documentation), documentation of other benefits (SNAP, WIC, TCA, WAG, GBI, housing assistance eligibility statements), and any other applicable documentation (migrant worker verification, homelessness verification, emancipation documentation, child support documentation, informal provider relationship documentation, immunization records or exemption documentation). Step 7: Full Scholarship Application is determined within 30 calendar days from submission or within 5 business days of receipt of all required documentation. If approved, a full 52-week scholarship is issued. Step 8: Families who qualify but cannot be awarded due to limited funding (enrollment freeze) are placed on a Frozen Status List and will receive scholarships once funding becomes available. Families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are exempt from the enrollment freeze. Step 9: Select a child care provider once scholarship is issued. Participating quality early childhood and school-age programs can be located through the Maryland EXCELS directory at https://findaprogram.marylandexcels.org/. Step 10: For existing scholarship holders, submit a Redetermination Application 45 days before the end of the current eligibility period to renew benefits. Step 11: Families may submit Interim Change Requests to report changes in circumstances such as changes in income, activity, child care needs, or household composition. Step 12: Language interpretation services are available. For questions not addressed by the portal, submit questions through the Provider/Family Inquiry Link on money4childcare.com or contact CCS Central 2 at 1-877-227-0125.

structured_extraction.program_description: A payment system where the Maryland State Department of Education pays child care providers in advance based on enrollment rather than retroactively based on attendance. Payments are made monthly (split into two payments per month on the 1st and 15th) based on the number of children with active scholarships on a provider's roster as of the last Saturday of the previous month.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Child care providers receive advance monthly payments based on enrollment of children with active Child Care Scholarship vouchers. Payments are processed on the 1st and 15th of each month by MSDE, with funds typically received by providers on the 6th and 21st (or shortly thereafter, depending on the provider's bank). Each month's payment is divided into two equal amounts. Payments are calculated based on a daily rate to account for varying numbers of days in each month. Advance payments cover up to 60 days of child absences per calendar year; absences beyond 60 days (without a medical waiver) result in an overpayment that must be recovered. Payments are reconciled monthly through a True-Up process (now shortened to one month after changes occur) that adjusts for changes in scholarship enrollment, license status, Maryland EXCELS status, voucher end dates, and other eligibility changes. The True-Up process looks back three months for adjustments. Payments may include Maryland EXCELS Tier payments based on provider quality rating. For Registered Family Home Providers who are Service Employees International Union (SEIU) members, union dues and COPE are deducted from advance payments. Registration fees and union dues are reconciled separately during True-Up periods. Informal providers are not paid for absences and holidays; overpayments are established when absences are reported.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/Ongoing - no application deadline; automatic enrollment for providers already participating in Child Care Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 877-227-0125 or 855-435-7410 (after hours); extended hours: Tuesday-Thursday 5pm-9pm, Saturday 9am-12pm
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers, regulated family child care providers, and informal child care providers that participate in the Child Care Scholarship Program and have children with active scholarships.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payments cover the cost of child care services provided to children with active Child Care Scholarship vouchers. Funds are used by providers for operating expenses related to serving scholarship-eligible children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland for all eligible providers participating in the Child Care Scholarship Program.
requirements_list: Provider must be enrolled in the Child Care Scholarship Program
Provider must have active child care scholarships for enrolled children
Children must appear on the provider's invoice (registered with active receipted vouchers) by the last Saturday of the previous calendar month to be included in that month's advance payment
Providers must maintain current Maryland EXCELS participation status; if EXCELS participation expires mid-month, payments do not include days after expiration unless participation is renewed
Providers must have a valid license (for licensed and regulated providers) or be in good standing (for informal providers)
Providers must submit invoices within 15 calendar days of the end of the service period to receive timely and accurate payments
Providers must submit signed invoices confirming service period and attendance information (though attendance no longer affects payment amounts)
Informal child care providers must submit documentation online through the Child Care Provider Portal
Attendance/Invoice Reports are still required within 60 days of the end of the service period; failure to submit results in assumed 60-day absence and payment recoupment
Providers with children whose absences exceed 60 days in a calendar year (without a medical waiver) will have an overpayment established for excess absence days
Customers (families) must validate attendance within 15 calendar days of receiving alerts to do so
Providers must upload relevant Sign-In/Sign-Out sheets within 10 business days of receiving an attendance dispute notification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Licensed providers and regulated family child care providers who already participate in the Child Care Scholarship Program are automatically enrolled in the Advance Payments system; no separate application is required. Informal child care providers must be registered in the Child Care Provider Portal to submit documentation. Providers submit enrollment information and invoices through the Child Care Provider Portal. MSDE processes advance payments on the 1st and 15th of each month based on active scholarship enrollment. Providers receive individual notification emails at the start of each month detailing payment calculations, enrollment used, base amounts, adjustments for mid-month voucher changes, and offsets for scholarship terminations. Invoice Detail Reports are provided through the Child Care Provider Portal showing detailed payment breakdowns. Families submit scholarship applications through the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal. The portal supports both full applications and fast-track applications (presumptive eligibility). Once a scholarship is issued and family selects a provider, the voucher is assigned to that provider, and advance payments begin the following month. Disputes regarding payments or attendance can be submitted through the portal or by contacting CCS Central 2.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The CACFP provides nutritionally balanced meals and snacks that contribute to the wellness, healthy growth, and development of young children, and the health and wellness of older adults and people with chronic disabilities. The program reimburses childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, emergency shelters, and adult day care facilities with federally-funded dollars for meals and snacks that comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns. Meals incorporate healthy foods such as vegetables, fruits, and whole grains while limiting added sugar exposure. The program serves children including infants, adults over 60, and people living with a disability. Over 300 agencies across Maryland participate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CACFP reimburses child and adult care agencies with federally-funded dollars for meals and snacks that comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns. CACFP sponsors receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their CACFP meal reimbursements. Children 18 years and younger in emergency shelters are automatically eligible for free meals with no application forms required. Funds are used to offset meal and supplement costs to public, private nonprofit, or proprietary centers licensed to provide non-residential childcare and adult daycare services. Providers manage financial claims through the Maryland Accountability and Reporting System (MARS). The annual maximum reimbursement for a child or adult care center serving 25 free-eligible participants breakfast, lunch and a snack 5 days per week is available. The annual maximum reimbursement for a family child care home serving 6 Tier I participants breakfast, lunch and a snack 5 days per week is available. Participating centers may earn Core of Knowledge hours and increase their EXCELS rating level.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, emergency shelters, and adult day care facilities serving children including infants, adults over 60, and adults living with a disability. Includes public, private non-profit, and for-profit centers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Meals and snacks that meet USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns served at participating childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, emergency shelters, and adult day care facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Over 300 agencies across Maryland participate in the CACFP. Family Child Care Providers participate through specific sponsoring organizations serving different regions of the state: Cecil County Government serves Cecil, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, and Kent County; Frederick County Community Action Agency serves Frederick and Carroll Counties; Montgomery County Public Schools serves Montgomery County; Prince George's County Public Schools serves Prince George's County; and The Planning Council serves all counties. Program is available statewide.
requirements_list: Must be licensed to provide non-residential child or adult care services
Meals and snacks must comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns
Participating sites must be registered childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, emergency shelters, or adult day care facilities
Must serve eligible populations including children (including infants), adults over 60, or adults living with a disability
Program serves low-income families and their children
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. An interested child or adult care center calls MSDE at (410) 767-0199 to begin the CACFP Interest Process. 2. The interested center completes the CACFP Interest Survey and Budget Worksheet. 3. MSDE determines the center's eligibility to participate in the CACFP. 4. The center must complete CACFP Basics Training and a three-part online application. 5. MSDE completes a pre-approval visit. 6. MSDE approves the center to participate in the CACFP and the center can begin to claim reimbursement for meals served. For Family Child Care Providers, contact one of the sponsoring agencies listed, which provide training, technical assistance, and monitor compliance with CACFP regulations.
