structured_extraction.program_description: A federally mandated program that requires local education agencies identified as having significant disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or discipline to reserve 15 percent of their special education funding to implement comprehensive, proactive, and responsive actions addressing root causes of overidentification. The program includes providing educational and behavioral evaluations, services, support with evidence-based literacy instruction, professional development, and systemic organizational change efforts to reduce racial and ethnic disparities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local education agencies identified as having significant disproportionality must reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds to implement comprehensive coordinated early intervening services. Funds support: (1) Educational and behavioral evaluations and services, including evidence-based literacy instruction; (2) Professional development and training for teachers and staff to deliver scientifically-based academic and behavioral interventions; (3) Coaching and mentoring services; (4) Extended contracts or extended hours for staff delivering interventions; (5) Progress monitoring and data analysis; (6) Systemic organizational change efforts; (7) Building leadership capacity and developing stakeholder implementation teams; (8) Instructional materials and software exclusively for intervention services; (9) Computing devices for delivery of interventions; (10) Substitute teacher salaries to enable professional development participation; (11) Travel costs for professional development and CCEIS activities. Funds cannot be used for: core curriculum, universal screening, student transportation, furniture, office equipment, rent/occupancy costs, special education eligibility evaluations, or services intended exclusively for students with disabilities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Plans submitted according to state calendar; Interim Report #1 due January 31; Interim Report #2 due January 31; Grant Amendment Requests due August 15; Final Report due November 30
structured_extraction.contact_name: Gary W. Richardson, MBA (Branch Chief); Demetria White (Interagency Specialist)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies (public school districts and charter schools) in Maryland that have been identified by the state as having significant disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or discipline for one or more racial or ethnic groups over two or more consecutive years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support: providing educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and evidence-based literacy instruction; professional development and training for personnel capacity-building; coaching and consultation; evidence-based academic and behavioral interventions (Tier 2 and Tier 3) for students without disabilities needing additional support; progress monitoring systems; data analysis and root cause identification; building leadership capacity; developing stakeholder implementation teams; comprehensive evaluation systems; systemic organizational change; review and revision of policies and procedures; instructional materials and software exclusively for intervention delivery; computing devices for intervention delivery; extended staff contracts/hours; and staff travel for professional development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; applies to all local education agencies in Maryland that meet the criteria for significant disproportionality (at least one subgroup with risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years).
requirements_list: Local education agency must be identified by the state as having significant disproportionality in one or more of: identification of children with disabilities by race or ethnicity, placement in particular educational settings by race or ethnicity, or incidence, duration, or type of disciplinary actions by race or ethnicity
LEA must have one or more subgroups evidencing a risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years (unless the risk ratio declines by a defined amount from one year to the next)
LEA must reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds for CCEIS activities

LEA must develop a comprehensive CCEIS Plan addressing root cause factors using an approved self-assessment tool (IDEA Data Center Equity Rubric, Safe and Supportive Learning Guide, or Center on School Turnaround Program Review Tool)

LEA must establish a local implementation team and diverse stakeholder group including internal and external partners, school administrators, general and special education staff, parents/community members, and school/student support representatives
LEA must conduct self-assessment and data review to identify root cause factors
LEA must identify schools or regions most significantly disproportionate based on multiple data points

For each area of identified significant disproportionality, LEA must address: review and/or adjustments to policies, procedures, and practices (required annually); identification of academic and/or behavioral interventions; and professional learning for personnel capacity-building
LEA must implement proactive and responsive planned response actions aligned with projected expenditures
LEA must establish measurable outcomes with goals and interim benchmarks including expected completion dates and data sources
LEA must evaluate plan outcomes with emphasis on teacher/staff fidelity of implementation and measurable student outcomes
LEA must maintain proper time and effort records when special education staff are funded to deliver Tier 2/3 interventions
LEA must not supplant state, local, or other federal funds with CCEIS reserved funds
LEA must submit required fiscal documents: MSDE Grant Budget C-1-25, Budget Detail Forms, and supporting documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Identify whether LEA meets significant disproportionality criteria based on state letter. Step 2: Form a local implementation team including special education directors, general education coordinators, school administrators, teachers, parents, and community members. Step 3: Conduct self-assessment using one of three approved tools: IDEA Data Center Equity/Inclusion/Opportunity Rubric, Addressing the Root Causes of Disparities in School Discipline guide, or Assessing and Improving Special Education Program Review Tool. Step 4: Complete comprehensive data analysis examining identification, placement, and disciplinary removal patterns by race/ethnicity across multiple years and schools; review policies, procedures, and practices for consistency and equity; analyze program implementation fidelity. Step 5: Identify root causes of disproportionality within districts' control (e.g., access to evidence-based instruction, barriers to identification, inconsistent procedures, implicit bias, inadequate diagnostic screening). Step 6: Develop Planned Response Actions (PRAs) for each identified area of disproportionality addressing: policy/procedure review and adjustment, academic/behavioral interventions, and professional learning. Step 7: Complete SFY 2025 CCEIS Plan template including reserved funds allocation, categories of analysis, root cause narrative, PRAs with measurable goals and interim benchmarks, data collection methods, and budget detail. Step 8: Obtain required signatures from local director of special education, chief academic officer, finance officer, and superintendent. Step 9: Submit plan to MSDE for review by DEI/SES Equity Specialist, Programmatic Liaison, and Fiscal Liaison. Step 10: Receive feedback and submit amendments as needed. Step 11: Submit Interim Progress Reports #1 and #2 with cumulative variance reports and PRA progress monitoring data. Step 12: Submit Final Progress Report and Final Financial Report by November 30. Step 13: Submit Grant Amendment Requests by August 15 if changes needed during fiscal year.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides counseling on post-secondary education opportunities to Pre-ETS students with Autism, exposing them to apprenticeships, job training, direct job placement, college, and other options. Part of the Pre-Employment Autism Support (PEAS) initiative.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pre-ETS students with Autism participate in classroom and other activities that introduce them to education, training and employment options available after high school, including apprenticeships, career training, job placement, and college. Students participate in college tours. The program also includes instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training to help develop the soft skills needed to get and keep a job.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) students with a documented diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder who are currently enrolled in high school, post-high school education program, or recognized educational program like trade school.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Counseling and guidance on post-secondary education and training opportunities, including college tours, career exploration, self-advocacy instruction, and social skills training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Offered at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center in Maryland
requirements_list: Documented diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder
Eligible for Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS)

Currently enrolled in high school (including home school or alternative secondary education program), post-high school education program such as college, or another recognized educational program like trade school
At least 14 years old but less than 22 years old
Has an Individualized Education Program (IEP), 504 plan, or medical records that document disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local office for more information or request DORS Services via QR code to enroll in Pre-ETS and the Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Consultation and support services to help people with disabilities explore, access, and participate in registered apprenticeship programs across Maryland. Services include assessments, academic instruction, exploration of apprenticeship opportunities, and ongoing support throughout the apprenticeship journey.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS provides free consultation and support services including apprenticeship coordination, academic assessment and instruction, apprenticeship exploration, and ongoing support for job seekers with disabilities pursuing registered apprenticeships. Services help individuals identify opportunities, prepare for applications, and succeed in apprenticeship programs. Registered apprenticeships are paid jobs where apprentices work on the job while receiving training from skilled craftspeople and related classroom instruction, earning according to a progressive pay scale.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders with disabilities interested in pursuing registered apprenticeships
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services include apprenticeship coordination, academic assessment, classroom instruction preparation, and support throughout the apprenticeship program enrollment and participation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout the state of Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer (individual with a disability receiving DORS services)
Interest in exploring or participating in registered apprenticeship programs
Be 18 years of age
Have a high school diploma (by means of high school graduation, GED, or NEDP)
Have transportation
Be drug free
Be physically able to perform required tasks
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Apprenticeship Coordinator to discuss your interests and receive an initial consultation. Visit occupations.mdapprenticeship.com to see available apprenticeship occupations. Call (410) 767-2246 or email info@mdapprenticeship.com to connect with an apprenticeship navigator. DORS will provide an appropriate mix of services based on your needs, which may include assessments, academic instruction, exploration activities, and ongoing support. Apply directly to the program sponsor or employer.

structured_extraction.program_name: Food Is Safe Here (FISH) Initiative - Food Safety Training for School Nutrition Professionals (ServSafe)
structured_extraction.program_description: An ongoing program of food safety training options and resources for school food service personnel in Maryland who participate in federally funded Child Nutrition Programs. This includes ServSafe Food Handler and Food Manager Training and review sessions utilizing the National Restaurant Association's ServSafe curricula and certification exam for school nutrition professionals. Certified ServSafe Instructors from local education agencies can teach ServSafe Manager classes and order materials at no cost, and Certified Proctors can order answer sheets and administer exams at no cost.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An ongoing program providing food safety training options and resources for school food service personnel in Maryland participating in federally funded Child Nutrition Programs. Includes ServSafe Food Handler and Food Manager Training and review sessions using the National Restaurant Association's ServSafe curricula and certification exam. Certified ServSafe Instructors from local education agencies can teach ServSafe Manager classes and order materials at no cost. Certified Proctors can order answer sheets and administer exams at no cost. An online form is available to order training materials, with orders required four weeks in advance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School nutrition managers, supervisors, directors, and other school nutrition professionals, as well as school food service personnel in Maryland participating in federally funded Child Nutrition Programs, who are required to receive food safety training
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Food safety training and certification in ServSafe standards, as well as food safety training options and resources for school food service personnel
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Participation in federally funded Child Nutrition Programs
Must submit online order form at least four weeks in advance of scheduled training dates
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online order form at least four weeks in advance of scheduled training dates. Training dates must be scheduled before ordering materials. Contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs for available food safety training options and resources. Orders can be placed using the online form provided.

structured_extraction.program_description: A workforce training program that prepares job seekers with disabilities for jobs in the food service industry, including cafeterias, restaurants, and food stores. The training includes seven weeks of classroom instruction and hands-on cafeteria experience, followed by a seven-week internship at a local business.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Seven weeks of classroom instruction at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) in northeast Baltimore in partnership with the Community College of Baltimore County, and hands-on experience in the WTC cafeteria, followed by a seven-week internship at a local business. Training covers food handling and preparation skills, kitchen safety and equipment operation, reading and following recipes, food portions and nutrition, weighing and measuring foods, customer service skills, point of sale skills and register operation, and ServSafe® principles.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities seeking workforce training in food services who can meet the physical and cognitive requirements of the job.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in food service skills, safety, and customer service, culminating in paid or unpaid internship experience in cafeterias, restaurants, and food stores.

Must be able to stoop, bend, and stretch
Must be able to be considerate and work well with others
Must be able to communicate effectively
Must be able to follow two-step instructions
Must be able to lift and carry 30 pound food containers and trays
Must be able to stand for long periods of time

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides free fresh fruits and vegetables to children at eligible Maryland elementary schools during the school day, promoting nutrition education and encouraging healthier eating habits. The program also enables Maryland schools to receive weekly deliveries of fresh fruits and vegetables from a Maryland-based produce company through USDA DOD Fresh allocations, with an emphasis on locally available products. Funding is also available to eligible residential child care institutions to encourage children to consume more fresh fruits and vegetables.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides direct payments and subsidies to eligible elementary schools and residential child care institutions to purchase and provide free fresh fruits and vegetables to students during the school day. Schools may also allocate USDA Foods funds to receive weekly deliveries of fresh produce from a Maryland-based produce company. Currently operates at 196 elementary schools across the state.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible Maryland elementary schools, residential child care institutions, and children enrolled in those schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and provision of free fresh fruits and vegetables to students during the school day; nutrition education about the fruits and vegetables served
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: 196 elementary schools and eligible residential child care institutions throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an elementary school or eligible residential child care institution
Must meet program requirements for nutrition education
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools apply through the Maryland State Department of Education to participate in the program. Applications are accepted annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that teaches people with vision loss who are age 55 and older how to become independent in their homes and communities. It provides training and support services to help older individuals with vision loss develop independent living skills, including safe cooking techniques, managing personal care and household tasks, orientation and mobility instruction, Braille instruction, and assistive technology training. DORS teachers and specialists are located throughout Maryland to deliver these services statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: In-home training and support services to help older individuals with vision loss develop independent living skills. Services may include training in managing personal care and household tasks, labeling and organizing personal care items clothing appliances and medications, safe cooking techniques, orientation and mobility training, Braille instruction, assistive technology use, referral to community peer support groups and other services, and introduction to community resources that enhance daily living such as NFB-NEWSLINE and resources at the Maryland State Library for the Blind and Print Disabled. ILOB rehabilitation specialists come to the home to provide assessment and training, working as a team with ophthalmologists, low vision professionals and community partners to provide personalized service.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals age 55 and older whose primary disability is vision loss or blindness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Independent living skills training including safe cooking, personal care and household management, Braille instruction, assistive technology, orientation and mobility instruction, community referrals, and introduction to community resources to help older individuals with vision loss maintain or achieve independence in their homes and communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-wide. DORS teachers and specialists are located throughout Maryland, including rural counties. Regional offices serve: Baltimore area (Baltimore City, Baltimore, Cecil, Howard, and Harford Counties); Wheaton area (Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Garrett, Montgomery, and Washington Counties); Annapolis area (Anne Arundel, Calvert, Caroline, Charles, Dorchester, Kent, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico and Worcester Counties).
requirements_list: Individual must be age 55 or older
Individual must have vision loss or blindness as their primary disability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office for Blindness & Vision Services or one of the regional offices. Call the main office at 410-554-9277, email obvs.dors@maryland.gov, or call the regional office serving your area. You will be contacted to set up an intake meeting with a DORS counselor or teacher who will gather information and determine eligibility. ILOB rehabilitation specialists will come to your home to provide assessment and training.

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Support Services (IECMHSS) Program Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This program improves the ability of staff, programs, and families to prevent, identify, treat, and reduce the impact of social, emotional, and other mental health problems among children birth through 5 years old. It provides both child and family support as well as classroom and program improvements through mental health consultation, training, coaching, and mentoring. The program also supports positive mental and behavioral health practices for young children who have developmental, social, emotional, or behavioral issues, providing referrals and services for children, families, teachers, and caregivers to build the capacity of early care and education providers and family members to promote healthy social-emotional development. Grants are awarded to non-profit and public agencies to deliver these services statewide across Maryland's 12 child care licensing regions. The program began in 2002 as a pilot in Baltimore City and the Eastern Shore and expanded statewide in 2006.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants to non-profit and public agencies to deliver infant and early childhood mental health support services statewide. Funding supports mental health consultation services, staff training, coaching, and mentoring to build confidence and competence in dealing with challenging behaviors. Consultants work with teachers to improve classroom environments, work with families, and refer children needing more intensive mental health services to appropriate support and clinical programs. Services are delivered through 12 statewide child care licensing regions. Applicants must operate 12 months per year except for federal holidays.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and public agencies licensed to do business within Maryland that provide infant and early childhood mental health services, as well as child care programs, early childhood providers, teachers, families, and children birth through 5 years old.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports positive mental and behavioral health practices, mental health consultation services, referrals and services for children with developmental, social, emotional or behavioral issues, staff training, coaching, and mentoring for early care and education providers and family members, and referrals to intensive mental health services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across all 12 child care licensing regions in Maryland. Applicants must be licensed to do business within the State of Maryland. The program began in 2002 as a pilot in Baltimore City and the Eastern Shore, and expanded statewide in 2006.
requirements_list: Non-profit or public agency status
Licensed to do business in Maryland
Proven capacity to provide Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Services
Operate 12 months per year except for federal holidays
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete the Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Support Services Program Application form and submit it by the deadline. Customer service support sessions are offered to provide an overview of the program, requirements, and proposal guidelines. Additional details are available through the Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Grant Opportunity page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Judy Center Early Learning Hubs (Judith P. Hoyer Early Care and Education Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Judy Center Early Learning Hubs are comprehensive family engagement centers located in elementary schools across Maryland, serving families with children from prenatal stages through age 5 (and through kindergarten). Using a multigenerational approach, Judy Centers empower families to prepare children for success in school by providing child development support and family support services. Centers are located in Title I school districts and provide or connect families with local community partners for a wide range of services including developmental screenings, family learning activities and engagement, parenting classes and workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based family and child playgroups, referrals for services and supports, early intervention identification, evidence-based home visiting, and case management with service coordination with community partners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Judy Centers are grant-funded programs administered by the Maryland State Department of Education, operating at 86 sites across Maryland as of FY2024. Services are provided directly by the centers or through referrals to local community partners and include: developmental screenings, family learning activities and engagement, parenting classes and training workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based family and child playgroups, referrals for services and supports, early intervention identification, evidence-based home visiting, case management with families, and service coordination with community partners. In FY2024, Judy Center Early Learning Hubs provided services to 17,681 children from birth to kindergarten age and 14,750 families. Services are provided directly to families rather than as direct financial assistance to recipients. Full-day/full-year services are defined as not less than seven hours or more than 12 hours per day, with year-round operation. Judy Centers provide meals during school day, school breaks, weekends, and after-school hours. Professional learning is offered to partners to address needs and trends in the early childhood community. All early care and education programs in partnership with the Judy Center must be accredited or pursuing accreditation.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager; Nancy Garcia, Judy Center Specialist (Spanish language assistance)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children from prenatal stages through age 5 (and through kindergarten) who live within the school zone where a Judy Center is located, particularly in Title I elementary school districts across Maryland. The program serves families from historically underserved communities and those with high needs in designated Title I school zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program provides services directly to families rather than funding to applicants. Services include developmental screenings, family learning activities and engagement, parenting education and workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based family and child playgroups, referrals for services and supports, early intervention identification, evidence-based home visiting, case management and service coordination with community partners, health-related services including referrals for dental, vision, and hearing screenings, mental health assessments, and physical growth and nutritional assessments, full-day/full-year care coordination, and meals during school day, breaks, weekends, and after-school hours.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Judy Centers are located in elementary schools across Maryland, primarily in Title I school districts. As of FY2024, 86 Judy Center sites operate across all 24 Maryland jurisdictions (23 counties and Baltimore City), ensuring representation in all regions. Eligible families must live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located. Children residing in the zone will attend Pre-K and Kindergarten at that school. The program is expanding according to The Blueprint for Maryland's Future legislation passed in 2021, with plans to expand by nine centers annually until 2025, then 18 sites annually from 2026-2030.
requirements_list: Families must live within the school zone where the Judy Center is located
Children must be from prenatal stages through age 5 to access family support services (continuing through kindergarten)
Children will attend Pre-K and Kindergarten at the school where the Judy Center is located
Program is located in Title I school districts and serves underserved families with high needs

Families must engage with the Judy Center at least 12 times during the fiscal year to be counted as served, or be enrolled in formal partner programs such as Kindergarten, Prekindergarten, Early Head Start, Head Start, Patty Centers, family child care providers, or child care centers
Children with disabilities and their families are fully included in all services as part of IEP and IFSP requirements
All families have access to comprehensive services including health-related referrals, adult education connections, and workforce development opportunities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families interested in Judy Center services should contact their local Judy Center Early Learning Hub directly. A map and contact information for each Judy Center, including coordinator names, phone numbers, and email addresses, can be found at https://marylandfamiliesengage.org/judy-center-hubs-map/ or through the Maryland Judy Centers website at marylandjudycenters.org. Individual Judy Center coordinators for each of the 86 sites are listed in the Judy Center Contact List. Families do not submit formal applications; instead, they engage directly with center coordinators who conduct outreach, family engagement, and service coordination. The Judy Center staff assists and links families in connecting to services and resources through case management to ensure the family is supported in meeting their specific needs. Services are coordinated through partnership Steering Committees that meet at least six times annually.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education to support the expansion of Judy Center Early Learning Hubs — comprehensive family engagement and early childhood support centers located in elementary schools across Maryland. The program provides funding to expand early learning hub programs and services statewide, with the Fiscal Year 2026 application now available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support the expansion of Judy Center Early Learning Hub programs and services. Specific grant amounts and terms are referenced as available in the application materials. The Fiscal Year 2026 application is now available.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager; Nancy Garcia, Judy Center Specialist (Spanish assistance)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elementary schools, school districts, and school systems seeking to expand Judy Center Early Learning Hub programs and services in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expansion of Judy Center Early Learning Hub programs and services, including early childhood support and family engagement services located in elementary schools across Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Available to elementary schools and school systems across all Maryland counties seeking to expand Judy Center Early Learning Hub programs.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Judy Center Expansion Grant Application for Fiscal Year 2026 is now available. Interested applicants should submit the application and may contact Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager, at kaymi.plank@maryland.gov or 410.767.0675 for application details and instructions. Spanish-language assistance is available by contacting Nancy Garcia, Judy Center Specialist, at nancy.garcia1@maryland.gov or 410-767-0785.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants supporting library partnerships as part of the PDG B-5 grant activities to build local capacity for early childhood services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to support library partnerships as part of early childhood local capacity building initiatives funded through PDG B-5.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Libraries and local organizations partnering on early childhood services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Library partnerships for early childhood services coordination
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide

structured_extraction.program_name: Licensing Compliance Grant for Family Child Care Providers (LCGFCCP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that helps registered family child care providers offset costs of opening their child care programs and achieving or maintaining compliance with family child care regulations. The program reimburses eligible providers for expenses such as safety supplies, training fees, background checks, medical examination fees, small household repairs, and other costs necessary to meet registration and regulatory requirements. Providers must meet income eligibility requirements, with annual household income not exceeding 60% of Maryland's State Median Income for their family size.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants of up to $1,000 for eligible expenses incurred to achieve or maintain compliance with family child care regulations. Reimbursement is provided in the form of a grant award. Earlier program iterations referenced reimbursements of up to $500; the current program cap is up to $1,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers whose annual household income does not exceed 60% of Maryland's State Median Income for their family size.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible expenses include safety supplies, provider medical examination fees, criminal background check fees, small household repairs in approved child care areas, approved child care training course fees, expenses related to local water, sewer, fire, and health requirements, program materials and equipment, and other costs identified as necessary for completion of the registration process and achieving or maintaining compliance with family child care regulations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; available to all registered family child care providers throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider
Annual household income must not exceed 60% of Maryland's current State Median Income for the applicant's family size
Expenses must be incurred to achieve or maintain compliance with family child care regulations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are processed in accordance with regulations set forth at COMAR 13A.14.07, which specifies eligibility requirements, application procedures, and the method by which awards are made. More information about the application process is available on the program webpage.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Early Childhood Advisory Council System Improvement Grant FY26
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program to support the operations and activities of Local Early Childhood Advisory Councils (LECACs/ECACs) across Maryland counties. LECACs work to establish school readiness benchmarks, conduct needs assessments of early childhood programs, develop action plans to increase participation in early childhood programs, and coordinate early childhood initiatives locally. The program also supports service delivery coordination at the local level through Quality Improvement Grants funded through PDG B-5 resources, helping local ECACs coordinate early childhood services at the community level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded through PDG B-5 resources to support Local Early Childhood Advisory Councils (LECACs/ECACs) in coordinating early childhood services at the community level, supporting LECAC operations, establishing school readiness benchmarks, conducting needs assessments, and developing action plans to increase program participation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Early Childhood Advisory Councils (LECACs/ECACs) in Maryland counties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting LECAC operations, establishing school readiness benchmarks, conducting needs assessments of early childhood programs, developing action plans to increase program participation, coordinating early childhood initiatives locally, and supporting service delivery coordination at the local level.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties with an established Local Early Childhood Advisory Council; available statewide through local ECACs.
requirements_list: Must be a Local ECAC to apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local ECACs submit applications through the MSDE Grants website. Specific application procedures are also referenced on the Local ECACs page at the Early Childhood Maryland Public Schools site.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Accreditation is a voluntary quality recognition program for licensed child care centers and public pre-kindergarten programs to demonstrate their commitment to providing high-quality early childhood and school-age learning. Programs work through a 24-month process using Maryland Accreditation Standards, self-appraisal with input from staff and families, program improvement planning, optional technical assistance, and validation visits to earn accreditation status valid for five years. Upon earning accreditation, programs become eligible for Accreditation Support Funds, higher Maryland EXCELS quality rating payments, and participation in the Military Child Care in Your Neighborhood PLUS program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Programs receive optional technical assistance through virtual sessions for Program Administration and Home and Community Partnerships, and onsite visits for Program Operation. Upon accreditation, programs become eligible for Accreditation Support Funds to purchase instructional materials, higher Maryland EXCELS quality rating payments, and eligibility for Military Child Care in Your Neighborhood PLUS program participation. Accreditation is awarded for five years. Accredited programs that earned accreditation beginning January 1, 2022 through April 30, 2024 receive an extension equal to five years from the date of award. Programs awarded accreditation on or after May 1, 2024 receive five-year status. During the five-year cycle, accredited programs submit Annual Updates for the first three years (containing Annual Update Form, Classroom and Staff Information, Program Improvement Plan, and Staff Qualification Form), with submissions accepted up to 60 days before the Annual Update due date. In years four and five, programs begin re-accreditation 24 months before expiration.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; programs can begin orientation and register within 12 months of completion. Re-accreditation begins 24 months before accreditation expiration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and public pre-kindergarten programs seeking to demonstrate commitment to high-quality early childhood and school-age education services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The accreditation process itself is not directly funded, but accredited programs gain access to Accreditation Support Funds that can be used to purchase instructional materials for early learning programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available to all Maryland licensed child care centers and public pre-kindergarten programs across all counties.
requirements_list: Program must be a licensed child care center or public pre-K program
Family Child Care programs are not currently eligible
Program must complete self-paced orientation
Program must meet Maryland Accreditation Standards for either early childhood or school age programs
Program must conduct self-appraisal with staff and family input
Program must develop and implement a Program Improvement Plan
Program must complete a Final Self-Appraisal
Program must undergo a Validation Visit

Early Childhood Educators (for licensed child care/Head Start) must have at least an Associate's degree in Early Childhood Education/Child Development or related field and hold a Maryland Child Care Credential level 5 or higher, Administrator Credential level 2 or higher, or State of Maryland teaching certificate in early childhood, or Bachelor's degree in Early Childhood Education or related field

Public School classroom educators must have a State of Maryland Teaching Certificate in early childhood education or be pursuing residency through the Maryland Approved Alternative Preparation Program
Assistant Teachers (for licensed child care/Head Start) must have a high school diploma and Maryland Child Care Credential level 2 or higher, CDA Certificate, or 90 hours certification

Public School Assistant Teachers/Paraprofessionals must have a high school diploma awarded on or before July 1, 2027, or CDA credential, or Associate degree or higher, or served as a Teaching Assistant in a publicly funded prekindergarten classroom for minimum 5 years at least 20 hours per week and 180 days per year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First step is completing the self-paced Maryland Accreditation Orientation. Programs then follow a 24-month accreditation process: Year One includes forming a Self-Appraisal Team, completing Initial Self-Appraisals with staff and family input, submitting required documentation and comments in each indicator, developing a Program Improvement Plan, applying for Maryland Accreditation Support Funds, and requesting or declining optional Technical Assistance (virtual sessions for Program Administration and Home and Community Partnerships, or onsite visits for Program Operation). Within 12 months of finishing orientation, programs register online and click 'begin' in their binder. Year Two includes completing a Final Self-Appraisal with required documentation, requesting a Validation Visit at least 90 days before accreditation expiration, hosting the Validation Visit at least 30 days before expiration, uploading comments, evidence, and pictures within 3 days of binder re-opening in response to validator's ratings, and receiving the Accreditation Decision from MSDE (receipt date becomes the anniversary date). After accreditation is awarded, programs submit Annual Updates for the first three years (due dates determined by accreditation expiration date, with submission windows from March 1 to April 30 of the update years). Programs enter years four and five of the accreditation cycle during which no Annual Updates are submitted; instead, re-accreditation begins 24 months before expiration by completing the Maryland Accreditation Orientation again and selecting 'Begin Maryland Accreditation' to open a new binder.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind (MBEPB)
structured_extraction.program_description: Program authorized by the Federally mandated Randolph-Sheppard Act that prepares individuals whose primary disability is vision loss to operate successful retail concession and food service operations in federal, military, DOD, and state of Maryland facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Training and support services to help individuals who are blind or have significant vision loss develop the skills and knowledge to own and operate vending operations, food service, and retail concession businesses in federal and state facilities. The three-phase program includes: (1) an eight-week New Manager Training course conducted by BEP staff at DORS' Workforce & Technology Center in Northeast Baltimore; (2) formal food service training with certified instructors and chefs, including National Restaurant Association certification in food service sanitation; and (3) on-the-job training consisting of three to six months of extended internship at various BEP facilities under an experienced manager. Assistance also includes counseling, case management, and access to assistive technologies such as laptop computers with adaptive software, digital talking cash registers, talking bill identifiers, scales, thermometers, and Braille note takers.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals whose primary disability is vision loss or blindness who are interested in operating their own business in the form of a vending operation, food service, or retail concession in federal, military, DOD, or state facilities. OBVS can also assist legally blind individuals over age 55 who have independent living, but not employment, goals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business training, food service certification, assistive technology, counseling, case management, and support services to prepare individuals to own and operate vending, food service, or retail concession businesses in public facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-wide. Vending operations are located in federal, military, DOD, and state of Maryland facilities, including state office buildings in Annapolis and Baltimore, National Institutes of Health, Internal Revenue Service, U.S. Food & Drug Administration, Motor Vehicle Administration, Social Security Administration, US Coast Guard, and Fort George G. Meade.
requirements_list: Individual must be legally blind U.S. citizen
Individual must have at minimum a high school diploma or GED equivalent
Individual must have an aptitude for business management
Individual must have practical skills and meet the legal criteria for operating a business supported by federal law
Individual must be referred by a DORS OBVS counselor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, request DORS services by visiting dors.maryland.gov and selecting Request DORS Services. The form can be completed by the job seeker, a family member, a medical provider, a social worker, or other interested party. You will be contacted to set up an intake meeting where a DORS counselor will gather information and provide details regarding your eligibility for DORS services. If you already have a DORS counselor, ask your counselor about BEP directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary professional development system that recognizes and rewards child care professionals (staff and administrators) who exceed state licensing requirements. Participants advance through credential levels by taking approved training, gaining work experience, and participating in professional activities. Child care staff progress through seven credential levels while administrators advance through four levels. The program reviews and processes applications for training vouchers and training reimbursement to cover pre-service training, conferences, and college coursework.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants earn achievement bonuses upon achieving credential levels: Staff Credential Level 2 receives $200 (one time), Level 3 receives $300 (one time), Level 4 receives $500 (one time), Level 4+ receives $600 (annually), Level 5 receives $750 (annually), and Level 6 receives $1,000 (annually). Administrator Credential Level 1 receives $600 (one time), Level 2 receives $750 (annually), Level 3 receives $1,000 (annually), and Level 4 receives $1,500 (annually). Participants with Credential Level 2 or higher are eligible for $400 per year in training vouchers and reimbursements (as funds are available) to cover pre-service training, conferences, and college coursework. All participants can receive tuition assistance for enrolling in approved college or university programs through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications open periodically; rolling admissions for renewals
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers, operators, directors, teachers, assistants, and aides in licensed child care centers and Letter of Compliance programs in Maryland who exceed state licensing requirements and work directly with children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development including Core of Knowledge (COK) training in child development, curriculum, health/safety/nutrition, special needs, professionalism, and community issues; pre-service training; work experience in child care settings; participation in Professional Activity Units (PAUs) such as professional association membership, accreditation work, peer mentoring, conference attendance and presentations, and college coursework leading to Associate's, Bachelor's, or Master's degrees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; available to all child care professionals in Maryland working in licensed child care centers, registered family child care homes, or Letter of Compliance programs.
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider, operator, director, or staff member (teacher, assistant teacher, or aide) in a licensed child care center or Letter of Compliance program in Maryland
Must work directly with children on a daily basis
Must exceed state licensing requirements
Cannot have been sanctioned by the Office of Child Care
Cannot be a substitute or volunteer in a child care program
Must complete Core of Knowledge (COK) training in six key areas: child development, curriculum, health/safety/nutrition, special needs, professionalism, and community issues
Must complete continued training applicable to credential level
Must participate in Professional Activity Units (PAUs) related to the child care profession
Must continue working in a registered or licensed child care program for at least one year after acceptance
Credentials are issued for a 12-month period and may be renewed if you continue working in a registered or licensed child care program
Program is voluntary
Training may be taken from OCC-approved trainers, colleges, or universities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants complete a professional development plan aligned with their target credential level. They obtain Core of Knowledge (COK) training from approved trainers, colleges, or universities in the six required topic areas. Participants gain work experience in direct child care settings and accumulate Professional Activity Units (PAUs) through activities such as joining professional associations, presenting trainings, mentoring, attending conferences, or pursuing college coursework. Documentation of completed activities is submitted to the Credentialing Program. For renewals, participants must submit proof of continued training, PAUs, and employment. Applications for training vouchers and training reimbursement are submitted separately through the Office of Early Learning and Instruction. Requests for PAU approval of activities not on the standard matrix are reviewed within 60 days and notification is sent via email.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Child Care Resource Network (MCCRN) Technical Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: MCCRN provides technical assistance to help child care providers start, expand, and operate facilities. Services include support with licensing and compliance, behavioral issues, special needs, credential and program accreditation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance is provided to child care centers, family child care providers, Head Start programs, nursery schools, cooperatives, drop-in centers, playgroups, community and non-profit organizations, community groups, employers, and public agencies. Services cover licensing and compliance issues, behavioral issues, children with special needs, and credential and program accreditation support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Existing and potential center-based and family child care providers, Head Start programs, nursery schools, cooperatives, drop-in centers, playgroups, community and non-profit organizations, community groups, employers, and public agencies committed to expanding child care resources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance with starting, expanding, and operating a child care facility; licensing and compliance; behavioral issues; children with special needs; and achieving credential and program accreditation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Child Care Resource Network for technical assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Quality Rating and Improvement System (QRIS) that awards child care and early education programs quality ratings from 1 to 5 based on meeting standards in areas like developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement. Participating providers receive a road map, guidance from a regional Quality Assurance Specialist, training, and incentives to improve their practices. The goal is to increase the number of high-quality early childhood and school-age care programs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Providers receive a road map for quality improvement, training opportunities, guidance from a regional Quality Assurance Specialist, and incentives to improve their practices. The process involves uploading evidence of meeting Maryland EXCELS Standards into an online system, which is then reviewed by staff who provide ratings for each standard area and an overall quality rating. Providers can improve their ratings by continuing to meet and exceed standards. Quality Assurance Specialists are available by region to assist with increasing quality ratings and to provide information about available training, work groups, and resources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers, early education programs, and school-age program providers who want to improve the quality of services they provide to families and children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support and training to improve the quality of child care and early education services in areas including developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement. Incentives are provided to support quality improvement efforts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Regional Quality Assurance Specialists serve specific county areas including Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Cecil & Harford, Carroll & Howard, Montgomery, Allegany, Frederick, Garrett & Washington, The Eastern Shore, Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's, and Prince George's.
requirements_list: Must operate an early childhood or school-age child care program
Must be committed to providing high-quality care and education that exceeds basic licensing requirements
Meet Maryland EXCELS Standards in areas including developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement
Participate in the quality rating process by uploading evidence of meeting standards
Work with a regional Quality Assurance Specialist
Commitment to quality improvement
Ability to document and upload evidence of meeting standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers sign up to participate through the Maryland EXCELS website. Once enrolled, they work with a regional Quality Assurance Specialist to create and upload evidence of meeting Maryland EXCELS Standards into an online system. Evidence is reviewed by Maryland EXCELS staff who assign ratings for each standard area and an overall quality rating. Providers can then improve their ratings by continuing to meet and exceed standards. Regional Quality Assurance Specialists are available to provide assistance and guidance throughout the process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education distributes bonuses to child care programs participating in Maryland EXCELS. Programs receive bonuses ranging from $1,000 to $13,500 based on the type of program, quality rating, and capacity. Bonuses are awarded when programs publish a quality rating for the first time or re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Child care programs receive one-time bonus payments ranging from $1,000 to $13,500. Bonuses are determined by program type (child care center, family child care, or large family home), quality rating level (1-5), and capacity. For Child Care Centers with capacity 1-50, bonuses range from $1,000 (rating 1) to $4,500 (rating 5); capacity 51-100 range from $1,000 to $9,000; capacity 100+ range from $1,000 to $13,500. For Family Child Care, bonuses range from $1,000 (rating 1) to $4,300 (rating 5). For Large Family Homes, bonuses range from $1,000 (rating 1) to $4,500 (rating 5). Programs receive bonuses when they publish a first-time quality rating or re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5 during the eligible period. Bonuses are typically processed within 60 days of the date the quality rating is published and are paid by check or direct deposit. Programs may spend bonuses at their discretion.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Vickie DiSanto, Meghan Leach-Gwynn, L'Ornya Bowie
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care programs participating in Maryland EXCELS including child care centers, family child care providers, and large family homes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bonuses may be spent at the discretion of the program for purposes such as purchasing learning materials, furniture, hiring staff, salary increases, or other program improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all eligible child care programs participating in Maryland EXCELS.
requirements_list: Must be participating in Maryland EXCELS
Must be in compliance with all Maryland EXCELS regulations
Must participate in scheduled Continuous Quality Improvement visits
Must publish a first-time quality rating or re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5 between July 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application or forms are required. If eligible, programs automatically receive the bonus payment by check or direct deposit within 60 days of the date the quality rating is published. Programs can check the status of payment on the General Accounting Division (GAD) website. Contact a Quality Assurance Specialist for assistance with increasing your quality rating and to learn more about available training, work groups, and resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: A reimbursement incentive program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that rewards child care providers for offering high-quality services to families using the Child Care Scholarship program. Programs that achieve Maryland EXCELS Quality Ratings of levels 3, 4, or 5 receive increased reimbursement payments ranging from 10% to 44% above base rates, based on the child's age, type of care, and the program's quality rating level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Programs receive increased reimbursement payments ranging from 10% to 44% above base rates. The increase percentage depends on the program's Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating (Level 3, 4, or 5), the age of the child served (under 2 years or 2 years and over), and the type of care provided. Family child care homes receive increases of 10% to 29% depending on rating level and child age. Child care centers receive increases of 10% to 44% depending on rating level and child age. Payments are processed through the standard invoicing system and reflected on the Invoice Detail Report as 'EXCELS' payments for each eligible child.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care programs (both family child care homes and child care centers) participating in the Child Care Scholarship program that have achieved Maryland EXCELS Quality Ratings of Level 3, 4, or 5 and serve families using the Child Care Scholarship program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Increased reimbursement for providing high-quality child care services to families using the Child Care Scholarship program. The increased reimbursement can be used for any purpose related to operating the child care program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide to all Maryland child care providers participating in Maryland EXCELS.
requirements_list: Program must be actively participating in Maryland EXCELS
Program must participate in the Child Care Scholarship program
Program must achieve and maintain a Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating of Level 3, 4, or 5
Program must serve children whose families are using the Child Care Scholarship program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Programs participating in the Child Care Scholarship program automatically receive Maryland EXCELS Payments once they achieve a quality rating of Level 3 or higher. No separate application is required; the increased reimbursement payments are automatically applied to invoices for eligible children and shown separately as 'EXCELS' on the Invoice Detail Report.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Families may borrow hearing aids for up to one year. The program also provides access to videos and other materials to support language development. All resources are provided at no cost to eligible families.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Zella Shabasson, Au.D. and Dr. Paige Bradford
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland families with children diagnosed as deaf or hard of hearing from birth to age 21 who have not yet graduated from high school.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hearing aids for trial or temporary use; educational videos and materials about language and communication methods for deaf and hard of hearing children.

Child diagnosed by an audiologist or other medical professional as deaf or hard of hearing
Child age birth to 21 and has not yet graduated from high school

For hearing aids: do not have insurance coverage for hearing aids, are experiencing delays or difficulties acquiring or replacing hearing aids, and/or need a hearing aid trial before purchasing personal aids or receiving a cochlear implant

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Infants & Toddlers Program (MITP) Consolidated Local Implementation Grant (CLIG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant mechanism through which local jurisdictions receive federal and state funds to implement local early intervention programs for infants and toddlers with disabilities and developmental delays, in compliance with federal and state regulations, policies, and procedures. The program supports the creation and operation of local systems of early intervention services across all Maryland jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local jurisdictions receive federal and state funds (formula and project grants) through their designated Local Lead Agency to support local early intervention programs for infants and toddlers with disabilities and developmental delays. Funds support the creation and operation of local early intervention services in compliance with federal Part C regulations and state policies. Grant funding is provided through multiple funding streams including Part C, Part B 611, Part B 619, state general funds, supplemental discretionary funds, Blueprint for Maryland's Future funds, American Rescue Plan funds, and extended IFSP grants.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Daniele Redivo, Glenn Graymen, Nancy Vorobey
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions with designated Local Lead Agencies implementing Local Infants & Toddlers Programs (LITPs) and partner agencies, including local governments and non-profit organizations that provide services to infants and toddlers with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting local early intervention programs for infants and toddlers in compliance with federal and state regulations, policies, and procedures, including the creation and operation of local early intervention services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties through their Local Lead Agencies.
requirements_list: Local Infants & Toddlers Program (LITP) must have a designated Local Lead Agency
Local Lead Agency aggregates information from LITP partner agencies
Must comply with federal Part C regulations and state policies and procedures
Must submit required applications, budget submissions, reports, and assurances by specified deadlines
All submissions must be uploaded to the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website using correct file naming conventions and submission procedures
Grantees must send email notification to designated fiscal grants liaison after uploading documents to ensure timely processing
Only authorized individuals with assigned Entity Code and log-on credentials may access the MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local Lead Agencies complete grant applications using provided forms and templates, including the SFY 2026 CLIG Application, budget submissions workbook, linking funds to program improvement chart, recipient assurances, federal certifications, GEPA Section 427, and state systemic improvement plan template. All submissions must be uploaded to the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website (MMSFTW) at https://msde.sftp.md.gov/ using the correct file naming convention format: FileCode_EntityID_SFY_GrantNameCode_APP.pdf (e.g., INTG_LLA02_2025_CLIG_APP.pdf for county applications). For amendments and reports, use: FileCode_EntityID_SFY_GrantNameCode_GrantNumber_TypeCode.pdf. Files should be uploaded to the ToMSDE folder, and grantees should save a screenshot of the upload timestamp as proof of submission. Email notification of submission must be sent to the designated fiscal grants liaison with the document name(s). Documents received in the FromMSDE folder are subject to deletion 30 days from posting date and should be immediately downloaded and saved locally.

Currently, 581 schools participate in the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides state funding to supplement federal meal reimbursements, ensuring all children in participating schools receive a nutritious breakfast at the start of each school day. Meals are consumed in the classroom. Currently, 581 schools participate in the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children in participating schools located in economically disadvantaged areas throughout Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing nutritious breakfast meals served in the classroom to students at the start of each school day

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (Autism Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid waiver program that provides community-based, long-term, person-centered therapeutic services and support to eligible children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder to enable home and community living as an alternative to institutional care. Through this program, students and families receive respite care, environmental accessibility adaptations, family training and consultation, supported adult life planning, intensive individual support services in the home and community, therapeutic integration services, service coordination, and in some cases residential habilitation. Families join a registry to access available waiver slots, which are filled on a first-come, first-served basis as they become available through attrition. The program is statewide with over 60 provider agencies, and is administered through local education agencies with oversight by the Maryland Department of Health and Maryland State Department of Education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Autism Waiver provides Medicaid coverage for community-based services including Intensive Individual Support Services (one-on-one assistance for self-help, socialization, communication, daily living, functional living, behavior management, and adaptive skills), Therapeutic Integration (regular or intensive structured programs during after-school hours, weekends, and non-school days), Respite Care (short-term supervision and assistance with activities of daily living), Environmental Accessibility Adaptations (funding for physical home modifications), Family Consultation (individualized consultation and training), Adult Life Planning (family-centered support accessing adult community services), and Residential Habilitation (community-based residential placement with goal of returning child to home). Participants also receive Service Coordination/targeted case management and full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and mental health services. No fees are charged to families. Waiver slots are filled on a first-come, first-served basis as they become available through attrition. To maintain eligibility, participants must use at least one participant-focused Autism Waiver service per month.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - families contact the AW Registry to be eligible to apply when a vacancy occurs; program may be at capacity at any given time; 45-day deadline to accept invitation, establish contact, complete technical eligibility checklist, and submit financial application after receiving application letter from Maryland Department of Health
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and youth ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old with Autism Spectrum Disorder who meet institutional level of care requirements and financial eligibility criteria. Also serves families of eligible children. Must reside in Maryland and have an active IEP or IFSP with qualifying hours of special education services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based therapeutic services and supports for children and youth with autism including: adult life planning, environmental accessibility adaptations, family consultation and training, intensive individual support services, residential habilitation, respite care, therapeutic integration services, service coordination/targeted case management, and full Medical Assistance benefits (health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and mental health services).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents only. Statewide program with over 60 provider agencies. Administered locally through county offices and local education agencies. For additional information contact Maryland State Department of Education at 1-800-535-0182, TTY (410) 333-6442, or Maryland Department of Health at 410-767-5220.
requirements_list: Be a resident of Maryland
Be ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old
Have a current educational classification of Autism or a clinical diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (within the last 3 years by a qualified diagnostician)

Receive early intervention or special education services identified through an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) for ages 1-5, an Individual Education Program (IEP) in an early childhood or Kindergarten setting for ages 3-5, or an IEP with 15 hours or more of special education and related services and/or 1:1 adult supports per week for first grade through high school exit

Meet eligibility requirements for an Intermediate Care Facility for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICF-IID) institutional level of care and choose to receive Autism Waiver services as an alternative
Be able to be served and safely maintained in the home and community with Autism Waiver services

Meet financial eligibility for Medical Assistance with monthly income not exceeding 300% of Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits and countable assets not exceeding $2,000 or $2,500 (depending on eligibility category)
Must be eligible for the Maryland Home and Community Based Services Waiver for Children
Choose the Autism Waiver as the waiver that best meets the child's needs

Military Exception: Dependents of US Military Service members invited to apply to the AW while the family is out of the state for military services shall be offered an opportunity to apply upon request when they return to Maryland and meet all technical eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact the Autism Waiver Registry Helpline at 1-866-417-3480 to have the child's name added to the waitlist. Provide: child's name, date of birth, address, county of residence, and contact information. Parents must confirm ASD diagnosis and that child has an IFSP or IEP with at least 15 hours of special education/related services per week. 2. MDH vendor conducts initial screening during intake call based on parent self-report. 3. MSDE verifies technical eligibility criteria: resident of Maryland, under age 21, Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis, IFSP or IEP with 15 hours of special education/health-related services. 4. If technically eligible, name is added to Registry and letter is sent to family. 5. Family is placed on AW Waitlist in chronological order from time name was placed on Registry. 6. When a waiver slot becomes available, parents receive an application letter from MDH. 7. Family contacts local education agency (LEA) or early intervention program to speak with AW contact and begin eligibility determination process. 8. Family works with child's assigned Service Coordinator to complete financial eligibility application within 45 days from date of MDH application letter. 9. Family contributes to Level of Care assessment process (to be signed by Maryland licensed psychologist or certified school psychologist employed by LEA). 10. Family attends multidisciplinary team meeting to develop Plan of Care. 11. Family receives notification of eligibility from the State. If eligible, letter includes start date to begin AW services. 12. To maintain eligibility, participant must use at least one participant-focused Autism Waiver service per month. For more information, contact Maryland State Department of Education at 1-800-535-0182, TTY (410) 333-6442, or Maryland Department of Health at 410-767-5220.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pre-service training course required for individuals seeking to acquire a Child Care Center License or a Family Child Care Registration in Maryland. The training covers medication administration theory and practice, including special needs support services such as individualized medical management, treatment plans, procedure skills competency support (Type 1 Diabetes, Seizure, Tube Feeding, Urinary Catheter, Oxygen Mask/Cannula), and Spanish-language instruction where available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A six-hour classroom training course (6 Hours Health, Safety, Nutrition) with theory and practice components covering medication administration. Participants receive a certificate upon completion after passing content and skill tests. Training is provided by licensed Maryland Registered Nurses (RN) who have completed Medication Administration Trainer training and are approved by the Nurse Consultant in the Office of Child Care's Licensing Branch. Training is available during day and/or evening hours depending on the trainer. Special Needs Support Services and Spanish-language instruction are available through select trainers. Trainers establish their own fee structures, payment methods, refund policies, cancellation policies, and no-show rescheduling policies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking to acquire a Child Care Center License or a Family Child Care Registration in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in medication administration for child care providers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - training available in all Maryland counties through approved trainers
requirements_list: Must be seeking a Child Care Center License or Family Child Care Registration
Must be able to complete a six-hour classroom training course
Must pass content and skill tests to receive certificate
Valid Maryland Registered Nurse license required for trainers (MBON-RN)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Nurse Consultant or locate an approved trainer from the Medication Administration Trainer List. Each trainer manages their own registration process, scheduling, and enrollment. Trainers provide information on how to register for classes, available hours (day and/or evening), fees, payment methods, cancellation policies, and no-show rescheduling policies. Participants must complete the six-hour training course and pass both content and skill tests to receive a certificate.
