structured_extraction.program_description: The National School Lunch Program provides nutritionally balanced, low-cost, or free lunches to children each school day. Schools receive federal reimbursement for meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards. The program serves over 900,000 students daily across all 24 Maryland public school systems and 22 participating non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions. The program also helps reduce food insecurity and supports student health and academic readiness.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive federal reimbursement for meals that meet USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans. Students from eligible families receive free or reduced-price lunches. Children from families with incomes at or below 130 percent of the federal poverty level are eligible for free meals (Annual income limits by household size range from $18,954 for a household of 1 to $65,728 for a household of 8, with $6,682 for each additional family member). Households with incomes between 130 and 185 percent of the federal poverty level are eligible for reduced-price meals (Annual income limits by household size range from $26,973 for a household of 1 to $93,536 for a household of 8, with $9,509 for each additional family member) but receive free meals due to state funding under the Maryland Cares for Kids Act. Categorical eligibility applies to children participating in certain federal assistance programs, those experiencing homelessness, migrants, runaways, foster children, and those enrolled in Head Start or Even Start. Direct certification is available for children receiving Medicaid. All foods sold in schools must meet Maryland Nutrition Standards for All Foods Sold in School, including the USDA Smart Snacks standards, with specific requirements for calories, sodium, fat, sugar content, and beverage standards that vary by grade level (elementary, middle, high school). These standards apply to all foods and beverages sold on campus from 12:01 am through 30 minutes after the end of the school day, including cafeteria a la carte items, vending machines, school stores, and fundraising activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: K-12 students in Maryland public schools and participating non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions; administered through schools and institutions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Provision of nutritionally balanced school lunches and snacks meeting USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans; funds help offset the cost of producing meals for students; support for healthy foods and beverages in compliance with Maryland Nutrition Standards for All Foods Sold in School
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all 24 Maryland public school systems and 22 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions across the state
requirements_list: Must attend a participating public or non-profit private school or residential childcare institution

Must meet income eligibility guidelines (130% of federal poverty level for free meals; 130-185% of federal poverty level for reduced-price meals) or qualify through categorical eligibility, direct certification, or participation in Maryland Meals for Achievement or Community Eligibility Provision
Schools must meet USDA nutrition guidelines and Dietary Guidelines for Americans
All foods sold in schools must meet Maryland Nutrition Standards for All Foods Sold in School, including Smart Snacks standards for calories, sodium, fat, and sugar content
Beverage standards must comply with state and federal regulations, with soda and caffeine prohibited during school hours and 30 minutes after school day ends
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families apply directly to their Local Education Agency's school nutrition office for free or reduced-price meal eligibility. Schools determine categorical eligibility and direct certification based on participation in federal assistance programs or Medicaid enrollment. For income determination, household income is compared to published Income Eligibility Guidelines; if a household has multiple income sources at different frequencies, all income must be annualized. Students attending Community Eligibility Provision schools or Maryland Meals for Achievement schools receive meals at no charge without individual application. Schools apply through their school system or institution; the program is administered by the Maryland State Department of Education.

structured_extraction.program_description: The State aid program that reimburses the cost of tuition for students with disabilities who are placed in nonpublic special education schools through their Individualized Education Program (IEP). The state pays its share of the cost in accordance with Maryland law.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program calculates and provides state aid to reimburse a portion of the tuition costs for students placed in nonpublic special education schools. The state's share is determined according to Education Article §8-415 of the Annotated Code of Maryland. Students in nonpublic placements are included in the September 30th enrollment count with a code 09 indicator and are reimbursed through the tuition reimbursement process rather than through Foundation calculations. Reimbursement covers Standard Educational and Related Services, Extended School Year Services, and IEP Residential Services as specified in the student's IEP. Related services include audiology, counseling, medical services, occupational therapy, orientation and mobility, parent counseling and training, physical therapy, psychological services, recreation, rehabilitation counseling, school health services, social work services, speech-language pathology, one-to-one classroom aide, intensive behavior modification, and extended day services. A cost sheet must accompany each application to confirm the annual rate of charges for approved services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted within specified timelines: ESY or entry dates in July/August submit by September 30; entry dates September 1-June 2 submit within 30 calendar days of entry date; entry dates June 3-30 submit by July 7; discharge applications within 30 days of discharge date; service revision applications within 30 days of revision date.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sheila F. Philip, JD; Jeffrey Miller
structured_extraction.program_audience: School districts and local education agencies placing students with disabilities in nonpublic special education schools. Applies to both MSDE-approved day/residential programs and individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state special education programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition costs for students placed in nonpublic day or residential special education programs approved by the Maryland Department of Education. Funds support standard educational and related services, extended school year services, residential services, and related services including but not limited to audiology, counseling, medical services, occupational therapy, physical therapy, psychological services, school health services, social work services, and speech-language pathology services as specified in the student's IEP.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. All Maryland counties and local school systems are eligible. Program also covers out-of-state special education programs for individual placements when deemed necessary by IEP teams.
requirements_list: Student must have an Individualized Education Program (IEP) indicating placement in a nonpublic special education school
The nonpublic school must be approved by the Maryland Department of Education (for approved day/residential programs) or placement must be justified for non-approved or out-of-state programs
Student must be included in the September 30th enrollment count
IEP must have been developed in accordance with federal and State laws and approved by the student's parent, guardian, or parent surrogate
A review of measurable annual goals, including benchmarks or short-term objectives, must have been completed in accordance with federal and State laws
The requested day or residential placement must be able to provide an appropriate educational program in the least restrictive environment

For individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state programs: must submit IEP team minutes supporting placement, letter from the service providing school stating they can implement FAPE in the least restrictive environment, and copy of any mediated or due process agreement/decision

For residential placements: must identify lead agency and funding source (such as Autism Waiver, Core Service Agency, DDA, DHMH, DJS, DSS, Home Circumstance, LSS, MSDE, Medical Assistance, Parent Placement, or Private Insurance)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: School districts submit applications for either MSDE-approved day and residential programs or for individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state programs. Applications must include student information, IEP placement information, requested reimbursement for IEP services (including standard educational services, extended school year services, residential services, and related services), and verification/assurance by the LEA Special Education Supervisor/Director or designee. An approved cost sheet must accompany each application to confirm annual charges. For individual placements, additional supporting documentation must be submitted including IEP team minutes, a letter from the school stating they can implement FAPE in the least restrictive environment, and agreements/decisions for mediated or due process cases. Applications must be typed or printed legibly and submitted according to specified timelines based on entry, discharge, or revision dates. Applications submitted late must include written notice and expected submission date. MSDE may audit and investigate application contents and supporting documentation; discrepancies or noncompliance may result in refunds of State funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Outdoor Nature-Based Child Care License Pilot Program

The program also supports grant funding for outdoor child care pilot initiatives, enabling providers to develop and implement nature-based early education programs statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a new licensing pathway that allows child care providers to operate in outdoor, nature-based settings in Maryland, as well as grant funding to support the development and implementation of outdoor nature-based child care pilot programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and organizations seeking to operate outdoor nature-based child care and early education programs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating outdoor nature-based child care and early education programs, including program development and implementation in outdoor settings.

structured_extraction.program_description: Educational support services for people with Autism in collaboration with community colleges throughout Maryland. Provides adjustment to college life, career guidance, employment and communication skills training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Educational support services including adjustment to college life, assessment services, career guidance and counseling, career exploration activities, employment and communication skills training, and individual and group sessions at participating community colleges. Students enroll in credit/certificate classes and register with the Disability Support Services (DSS) office at their college. The DORS Pathways coordinator works with students, families, DORS counselors, DSS staff, and faculty.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with a documented diagnosis of Autism attending participating community colleges in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College education and career development support through Disability Support Services at community colleges.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at Anne Arundel Community College, Community College of Baltimore County, Howard Community College, Prince George's Community College, College of Southern Maryland, and Montgomery College.
requirements_list: Have a documented diagnosis of Autism
Have a DORS Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that supports college as part of the employment plan
Register with the Disability Support Services (DSS) program at the college
Attend weekly group sessions and schedule classes around this standing appointment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local DORS office or DORS Counselor to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that supports college as part of the employment plan. Enroll in credit/certificate classes at a participating community college and register with the Disability Support Services (DSS) office. Participate in weekly group sessions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Patty Centers/Family Support Center Network (Family Support Centers)
structured_extraction.program_description: A network of 24 centers in 14 Maryland counties offering free, comprehensive educational and health-related services to parents and children ages birth through three. Services include infant and toddler care assessment while parents are on-site, parent education classes, adult education and family literacy programs, job readiness training, health education with agency referrals, home visits, peer support networks, and coordination between agencies to connect families to community resources. Additional services are available through referral for families statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free educational and health-related services including infant and toddler care assessment while parents are on site, parent education classes, adult education and family literacy programs, job readiness training, health education with agency referrals, home visits for some services, peer support networks, and coordination between agencies to connect families to community resources. On-site support and referrals to families are also provided.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents and children ages birth through three in participating Maryland counties, as well as families statewide through referral services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services are designed to promote optimal child development, help adults develop effective parenting skills and pursue school or employment goals, create supportive parent networks in local communities, and connect families to community resources and agencies. Family support services target parents and children birth through age three.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Primarily available in 14 Maryland counties (Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Caroline, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, Talbot, and Washington) with 24 Patty Center locations. Early Head Start programs are located in Southern Anne Arundel County, seven communities in Baltimore City, Caroline County, Cecil County, Dorchester County, and Talbot County. Referral services are available statewide.
requirements_list: Must have a child ages birth through three
Must be able to access a Patty Center location in your county
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local Patty Center or visit the Maryland Family Network website to find your nearest center and learn about enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training to Pre-ETS students with Autism, focusing on soft skills needed to obtain and maintain employment. Includes activities introducing students to education, training and employment options after high school, such as apprenticeships, career training, job placement, and college, including college tours.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Classroom and other activities providing instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training to help Pre-ETS students with Autism develop soft skills needed to obtain and maintain employment. Includes participation in Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities (CPSEO) activities that introduce students to education, training and employment options available after high school, including apprenticeships, career training, job placement, college, and college tours.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) students with a documented diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in self-advocacy and social skills to support employment readiness. Counseling on post-secondary education opportunities including apprenticeships, career training, job placement, and college exploration.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Offered at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center in Maryland
requirements_list: Currently enrolled in high school (including home school or alternative secondary education program), post-high school education program (such as college), or another recognized educational program like a trade school
At least 14 years old but less than 22 years old
Has an Individualized Education Program (IEP), 504 plan, or medical records that document disability
Documented diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office for more information or request DORS services. Eligible students can enroll in Pre-ETS and the Pre-Employment Autism Support program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Pre-ETS are five specific services designed to help students with disabilities identify their career interests and enhance their awareness of the world of work. The services include job exploration counseling, instruction in self-advocacy, counseling on post-secondary education opportunities, workplace readiness training, and work-based learning experiences. These services are generally short term and cover introductory topics emphasizing exploration and preparation for employment and post-secondary education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Five specific services provided at no cost to students and families. Services include: (1) Job Exploration Counseling - explore skills, interests and career opportunities through interest inventories, labor market information, and sessions about in-demand occupations; (2) Instruction in Self-Advocacy - learn strategies for effective communication and understand rights and responsibilities through sessions with instructors about knowing your rights, self-awareness, problem solving, and effective communication (such as the Youth Leadership Forum); (3) Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities - gain awareness of career pathways and training options available after high school, guidance on choosing the right type, and how to access disability supports; (4) Workplace Readiness Training - learn knowledge, skills and abilities valued by employers including how to interact with supervisors and coworkers, strategies to get to work on time, and appropriate dress and behavior on the job; and (5) Work-Based Learning Experiences - participate in work opportunities outside traditional school settings, such as work experiences at local participating employers. Specific services vary based on individual needs and opportunities in the local area.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jessica Markum, Staff Specialist for Students and Transitioning Youth; Muttasim Fadl, Employment Services Specialist for Students with Blindness or Vision Impairments; MSDE Division of Rehabilitation Services Headquarters
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities who are at least 14 years old and no more than 21 years old, are enrolled in a secondary school (including home school or other alternative secondary education program), post-secondary education program, or other recognized educational program and have not graduated or withdrawn, and have a documented disability such as an Individualized Education Program (IEP), 504 plan, or medical documentation of a disability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to help students explore career interests, develop self-advocacy skills, learn about post-secondary education options, develop workplace readiness skills, and gain work-based learning experiences to prepare for transition from school to post-school life and employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services available statewide through local DORS offices throughout Maryland. Services are also available virtually. DORS is located in more than 20 offices around Maryland.
requirements_list: At least 14 years old and less than 22 years old

Enrolled in a secondary school (including home school or other alternative secondary education program), post-secondary education program, or other recognized educational program and has not graduated or withdrawn
Have a documented disability (on an IEP or 504 plan, or have medical documentation of a disability)
Complete the Request DORS Services form
Provide Social Security Number
Provide documentation of disability
Provide proof of school enrollment
Provide proof of age
Sign and date the Pre-ETS Consent to Participate form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Request DORS Services by going to dors.maryland.gov and selecting 'Request DORS Services.' The form can be completed by anyone - the student, parent, family member, medical provider, teacher, or school staff. Include an email address as DORS communicates through the secure SARA system. You can also call your local DORS office for assistance with the form over the phone. Find your local DORS office by going to dors.maryland.gov and clicking 'Find my Local DORS Office.' Step 2: Allow approximately 10 business days for a DORS representative to contact you via text message and email through SARA to schedule a virtual or in-person intake meeting. Step 3: Provide additional information including Social Security Number, disability documentation, proof of school enrollment, and proof of age. Sign the Pre-ETS Consent to Participate form and submit all information through the secure SARA system. Step 4: After qualification, a counselor from the local DORS office will meet with the student and family to plan their Pre-ETS services. During this meeting, the student will discuss career interests, service needs and available transition services. Information on the website is available in multiple languages.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education that provides funding to local education agencies and qualified private providers to deliver high-quality full-day prekindergarten and school readiness services to three- and four-year-old children from families earning at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level. The program aims to expand access to full-day pre-kindergarten education throughout Maryland at no cost to eligible families, in alignment with The Blueprint for Maryland's Future.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding awarded to local school systems and qualified private providers to administer high-quality full-day prekindergarten programming and school readiness services. Estimated average grant amount of $400,000 per award, with approximately 50 grants available from total funding of $26,644,000. Funding calculated at $19,950 per full-day slot for three- and four-year-old children. Grant period runs July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, with a minimum instructional year of 180 days. Grant funds support staffing (commensurate salaries for teachers with P-3 certification aligned to local education agency salary schedules; minimum salaries for teachers without P-3 certification per Lead Teacher Salary Schedule; assistant teachers must meet Blueprint requirements), operations, classroom materials and supplies, technology costs (not to exceed 10% of total request), facility rental/mortgage costs (reasonably allocated, not to exceed available funds), accreditation/Maryland EXCELS rating maintenance costs, screening and intervention services, program evaluation and monitoring (not to exceed 5%), indirect costs (not to exceed 15% for nonprofits, 10% for other grantees as amended March 6, 2026), at least one meal per day meeting CACFP requirements, academic field trips, and approved professional learning activities for instructional staff. Funds may not be used for supplanting existing program funds, capital improvements, costs prior to grant approval, or transportation except field trips. All grant requirements must be met and lead teachers hired by July 1, 2026 before invoices or advance payment requests can be processed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, March 11, 2026. No later than 5:00 pm EDT. (Amended on March 6, 2026)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dr. Nykia Washington, Prekindergarten and Mixed Delivery Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies (school systems), Head Start programs, and qualified private child care providers (center-based and family child care programs) who will deliver prekindergarten services to three- and four-year-old children from families earning at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports the administration and delivery of high-quality prekindergarten and school readiness services, including salaries and benefits for qualified teaching and assistant staff; equipment, materials, and supplies for classrooms including MSDE-approved curriculum resources aligned to Maryland Early Learning Standards; reasonable rental/mortgage and utility costs; technology costs (up to 10%); costs for maintaining Maryland EXCELS ratings or accreditation; screening and intervention services; evaluation and monitoring costs (up to 5%); indirect costs (up to 15% for nonprofits, 10% for other grantees); meals meeting CACFP standards; academic field trips; and approved professional development for instructional staff totaling at least 20 hours addressing school readiness, Maryland Early Learning Standards, science of reading, early mathematics, social foundations, High Quality Instructional Materials, and CLASS assessment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must hold a valid license or registration as a child care provider or local school system (if applicable)
Must currently meet Maryland EXCELS rating requirement (Level 3 or higher for private providers; Level 4 or higher for public providers)
Must be a Head Start program or qualified vendor as defined in COMAR 13a.06.02 (if private provider)
Families served must have household incomes at or below 300% of Federal Poverty Level
Must provide high-quality prekindergarten programming in alignment with The Blueprint for Maryland's Future
Programs must meet Maryland EXCELS quality standards
Must deliver programming targeting children and families with household incomes up to 300% of Federal Poverty Level

Lead teachers must meet Blueprint requirements: hold bachelor's degree in early childhood education or related field from accredited institution; OR hold bachelor's degree in ECE from foreign institution verified as comparable; OR hold bachelor's degree in any field; OR have 10+ years documented ECE experience (20 hours/week, 180 days/year minimum) as of July 1, 2024. Lead teachers not holding P-3 certification must achieve minimum CLASS scores: Emotional Support 5.00, Classroom Organization 5.00, Instructional Support 3.00
Lead teachers with P-3 certification must be paid commensurate with local education agency salary schedules in respective counties
Lead teachers without P-3 certification must be paid at minimum salary per Lead Teacher Salary Schedule

Assistant teachers in classrooms with 10+ students must meet Blueprint requirements: hold high school diploma and by July 1, 2027 (private providers) or 2027-2028 school year (public providers) earn Child Development Associate with preschool designation or associate degree in ECE; OR have 15+ years (private) or 5+ years (public) documented ECE experience (20 hours/week, 180 days/year minimum) as of July 1, 2024

For Montessori programs: teachers must hold bachelor's degree and Montessori credential from AMI, AMS, or MACTE-accredited program; student-to-personnel ratios not to exceed 10:1 (max 20 students under age 5) or 14:1 (max 28 students if some age 5+)
Programs must verify Maryland EXCELS published level and provide plan to maintain or achieve level 5 by identified deadline
Must include qualified individual with bachelor's degree or higher in ECE or related field with ECE experience as Key Personnel responsible for instructional oversight

Applications must include description of income verification and family documentation collection and secure on-site maintenance based on FY26 Federal Poverty Levels, including procedures for identifying and appropriately serving students with disabilities, students experiencing homelessness, and multilingual learners as part of eligibility and enrollment process
Must include SMART goals addressing standards alignment, instructional practice, quality improvement, and child outcomes
Must demonstrate community need for high-quality Pre-K through needs assessment or market analysis
Must describe how implementation leads to desired goals and outcomes, strengthening school readiness and improving child outcomes
Must include family engagement strategies
Must provide description of professional learning activities (20 total hours) for instructional staff supporting school readiness and alignment with Maryland Early Learning Standards
Must include plan to build long-term sustainability and community/business partnerships
Private providers must pass license check confirming valid child care license
Head Start programs only: must submit letter of support from Head Start-funded grantee if applicant is not the funded grantee
All grant requirements must be met prior to start of grant year (July 1, 2026)
Lead teachers must be hired by July 1, 2026 to avoid disruption in grant funds

Upon grant award, LEAs must submit signed Memorandum of Understanding between MSDE, the LEA, and any private providers outlining roles, responsibilities, and plans for serving children with disabilities, multilingual learners, students experiencing homelessness, parental preference, centralized enrollment, payment processing, administrative costs, racial/socioeconomic integration, and disproportionate concentration avoidance by September 30, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit applications electronically through Qualtrics online form by 5:00 p.m. EDT on March 11, 2026. Eligibility screening questions determine pathway to full application or modified short form. All new applicants and existing grantees without track record of success must complete full application in entirety. Existing grantees with track record of success (maintained qualified lead teacher, minimum Maryland EXCELS Level 3+, compliance with reporting/fiscal guidelines, no corrective action plan, 85%+ seat fill rate by December 31, 2025) may submit modified short form. Full application consists of 10 sections: Program Eligibility/Maryland EXCELS, Evidence of Need/Market Analysis, Measurable Goals, Program Quality and Curriculum, Plan of Operation, Staffing/Key Personnel/Management, Project Timeline/Implementation, Collaboration and Sustainability, Fiscal Systems and Controls, and Budget/Budget Narrative. Modified short form includes only required sections with reduced scoring (minimum 45 points vs. 80 for full application). Applicants can complete application in multiple sittings on same device/browser with progress saved locally. Application must not be altered or omitted sections. All required appendices must be uploaded within Qualtrics system. Applicants have opportunity to review answers and download responses as PDF before final submission. Paper application available for reference only. MSDE offered customer service support sessions January and February 2026 and open office hours in February 2026 to answer questions about application and process. Grant Information Guide, application worksheet, and tips for completing application available online. Timely submission encouraged to increase likelihood of award.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project SELECT (Student Education, Lunchroom Environment, and Culinary Training)
structured_extraction.program_description: A USDA Team Nutrition training grant implemented from 2016 through 2019 that targeted middle schools to increase student selection and consumption of vegetables and fruits, and improve student knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors about nutrition through culinary training, food service operations improvements, and family engagement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The grant provided training and technical assistance in culinary and food service operations, Smarter Lunchrooms strategies, food tasting events, and nutrition education. A family engagement wellness toolkit was also developed to support wellness policy implementation involving families and parents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Middle schools in targeted school systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Culinary and food service training, Smarter Lunchrooms strategies, food tasting events, nutrition education, and family wellness toolkit development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Five targeted school systems: Allegany, Baltimore City, Montgomery, Prince George's, and Wicomico counties
requirements_list: Middle school location
Participation in one of five targeted school systems
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This was a time-limited grant program implemented from 2016 through 2019. The program is no longer accepting applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: The School Breakfast Program provides nutritious breakfasts to students in participating public and non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions, helping ensure children are ready to learn and reducing food insecurity. Federal reimbursement helps schools offer meals that meet USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans. Students from low-income families may qualify for free or reduced-price breakfast based on family income eligibility, including families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance and/or food stamp benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive federal reimbursement dollars for nutritious breakfasts served to students that comply with USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans. Free and reduced-price meals are available to children from families with incomes at or below 130-185% of the poverty level, or students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance and/or food stamp benefits. All 24 Maryland public school systems, 17 non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions participate, serving over 898,000 students daily. Funds help offset the costs of producing meals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in Maryland public schools, non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions, as well as the schools and institutions serving them
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchasing and serving nutritious breakfast meals that meet USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans; funds help offset costs of producing meals
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland public school systems, 17 non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions across the state
requirements_list: Meals must comply with USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans
Participating schools must follow federal reimbursement procedures
Schools must be public or non-profit private
Students from families with incomes at or below 130-185% of the poverty level qualify for free or reduced-price meals
Students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance and/or food stamp benefits are eligible for free meals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools apply through their school system or institution and participate through state and federal nutrition program coordination administered by the Maryland State Department of Education. Individual students may apply for free or reduced-price meals through their school district based on family income eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides milk to children in schools, childcare centers, and eligible camps that do not participate in other federal child nutrition meal programs. The program encourages the consumption of fluid milk by children in public and private nonprofit schools, summer camps, and other eligible nonprofit sites, and provides reimbursements to offset the cost of milk served to children.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses schools and institutions for milk served to children. Eligible institutions include public and private nonprofit schools, childcare centers, and camps that do not participate in other federal child nutrition programs. Schools with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs without access to meal programs may also participate. Funds are used to offset the cost of the half-pint of milk served to children.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children in public and private nonprofit schools, childcare centers, and eligible camps; institutions serving milk to children that do not participate in other federal child nutrition meal programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for milk served to children; funds must be used to offset the cost of milk provided to children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland schools, childcare centers, and eligible camps statewide.
requirements_list: Institution must not participate in other federal child nutrition meal programs
Schools with half-day pre-K and kindergarten programs without meal program access may participate
Eligible sites include public and private nonprofit schools, summer camps, and other eligible nonprofit sites
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Institutions apply annually to participate and receive reimbursement for milk provided to children.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education provides annual grants to qualified non-profit organizations that offer enriching educational programs to Maryland students. These programs provide learning experiences that align with the State's educational priorities and cannot be replicated in classrooms. The programs emphasize experiential learning and one-on-one support, including free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, and tutoring. Pre- and post-visit classroom activities and professional development for teachers are also funded.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants of approximately $6,706,449 are available for FY 2027, with an estimated 60-65 grants to be awarded. Funds support direct services to students and teachers including: salaries, wages, and stipends for direct service; supplies and materials to implement educational programs; outreach, engagement, informational, and marketing tools; equipment necessary for direct service; and contractual expenses. Funds must be used within the fiscal year for which they are granted. Funds cannot be used for construction, capital improvements, transportation of students, utilities, operating costs, or food.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, June 13, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations that provide enriching educational programs directly to Maryland school groups and students. Organizations must provide direct service to Maryland students and teachers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salaries, wages, and stipends for direct service to students and educators; supplies and materials to implement educational programs; outreach, engagement, informational, and marketing tools to expand reach; equipment necessary for direct service to students and teachers; and contractual expenses. Funds are to provide direct services to students and teachers and must be used within the fiscal year for which they are granted.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. For fiscal year 2027, funding is available for organizations serving Maryland students statewide. Currently, 57 organizations are in the SAI program, and in fiscal year 2024, approximately 440,000 Maryland students and teachers were served through this program.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization in good standing
Must be based in the State and incorporated or registered under the laws of Maryland
Must be exempt from federal income tax under §501(c)(3), (4), or (6) of the Internal Revenue Code
Must be current in payment of all tax obligations to the State or any unit or subdivision of the State
Must provide direct service to Maryland students and teachers
Must provide enriching educational programs to Maryland students
Programs must align with the State's curricular and educational priorities
Programs must provide learning experiences that cannot be replicated in the classroom
Must emphasize experiential learning and one-on-one support services
Must submit a Fiscal Impact Statement describing the educational program, amount of funds requested, populations served, educational goals and objectives, and anticipated outcomes
Must submit proof of 501(c)(3) nonprofit status
Must provide names of independent governing board members
Must submit a copy of most recent independent annual audit or internally generated financial statement
Must provide evidence of active liability insurance coverage
Must submit detailed operating budget indicating less than 50% of budget comes from state grants (except Baltimore Zoo), with all sources of income and expenditures specified

Must provide evidence of direct service to Maryland school groups or individuals with disabilities, including data on age levels and projected numbers of students and teachers to be served statewide and by jurisdiction
Must provide plans to align educational programs with MSDE's educational and curricular priorities
No more than 20% of participants served may come from nonpublic or homeschools
Must demonstrate program goals that are specific, measurable, ambitious yet attainable, realistic, and time-bound
Must provide evaluation methods for program goals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application window opens on Thursday, May 1, 2025. Applicants must download the electronic SAI application from the MSDE SAI webpage, complete all sections and attachments, and save as one PDF file. The complete application must be submitted by email to sai.applications@maryland.gov by 5:00 p.m. EDT on Friday, June 13, 2025. MSDE reviews applications on a rolling basis. A review committee at MSDE evaluates all submissions using a standardized scoring rubric. For any application sections scored as Level 1 (Does Not Meet Criteria), written feedback is provided and an opportunity to revise and resubmit is offered. Results are communicated to the State Superintendent in July, then provided to the State Board of Education for review in August. Final approval for awards is determined in legislation as authorized by the budget bill for fiscal year 2027. MSDE holds virtual customer service support sessions (May 5 and May 23, 2025) to help applicants understand program requirements and walk through the application process. Applicants should review the Grant Information Guide and application materials before submitting.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive vocational rehabilitation services that help students with disabilities obtain meaningful employment and prepare for a successful career. Includes Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) and VR Employment Services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students with disabilities receive Pre-ETS services plus a broad range of vocational rehabilitation services to obtain or prepare for meaningful employment. Pre-ETS may cover job exploration counseling, counseling on opportunities for enrollment in comprehensive transition or post-secondary education programs, work-based learning experiences, workplace readiness training, and self-advocacy through activities, lessons, and workshops. Students with the most significant disabilities receive VR Employment Services with an individualized plan of services to support them in obtaining competitive integrated employment. Those without the most significant disabilities are placed on a waiting list and served as resources become available. DORS reviews available documentation and arranges assessments as necessary to determine eligibility.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities who are enrolled in secondary school (including home school or alternative secondary education program), post-secondary education, or another recognized educational program, are at least 14 years old but less than age 22, have a disability documented with an IEP, 504 plan, or medical record, and seek employment preparation and meaningful employment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Vocational rehabilitation services to help students obtain or prepare for meaningful employment, including job exploration counseling, work-based learning experiences, workplace readiness training, and self-advocacy activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. DORS has a counselor assigned to every public high school in Maryland.
requirements_list: Enrolled in secondary school (including home school or alternative secondary education program), post-secondary education program, or another recognized educational program and has not graduated or withdrawn
At least 14 years old but less than age 22
Has a disability documented with an Individualized Education Program (IEP), 504 plan, or medical record
Eligible for services based on DORS assessment and determination of eligibility
Students with most significant disabilities receive VR Employment Services first; others are placed on waiting list and served as resources become available
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools with parent or guardian consent can complete the online Request DORS Services form to refer the student, or families can complete the form themselves. Schools should share documentation such as IEP, 504 plan, and/or psychological assessment with the DORS liaison as appropriate. DORS counselors review available documentation and arrange assessments as necessary. DORS transition counselors discuss both Pre-ETS and VR Employment Services programs with students and families. If eligible and can be served based on significance of disability, the student completes an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) with their DORS counselor, which may be developed with family or school personnel. Once the IPE is approved, Student Employment Services begin. Those without the most significant disabilities are placed on the waiting list; those on the waiting list the longest are served first.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded, state-administered program that provides free healthy meals to children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income and economically disadvantaged areas during the summer months when school is not in session. The program merges summer activity and enrichment programs with federal meal reimbursement to help children stay healthy and well-nourished while out of school. Two program models are available: SUN Meals, which provides meals and activities at a site location, and SUN Meals To-Go, which provides multi-day meal boxes for pickup (registration required). In Baltimore City, the program is administered through the Department of Housing and Community Development, offering free nutritious breakfasts and lunches at designated meal serving sites.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses providers who serve free healthy meals to children and teens in low-income areas during summer months. Each meal meets one-third of the minimum daily nutritional requirements as devised by the USDA. Meals are prepared by a food service management company and delivered daily to site locations. Breakfast consists of cold cereal or bread/bread alternate, fruit juice, and milk. Two program models are available: SUN Meals, which provides meals and activities at a site location, and SUN Meals To-Go, which provides multi-day meal boxes for pickup (registration required). In Baltimore City, free nutritious breakfasts and lunches are provided to eligible children ages 18 and younger at designated meal serving sites. The program operates Monday through Friday from June 17 through August 22 (dates pending verification of Baltimore City Schools' calendar).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income and economically disadvantaged areas; organizations wishing to become meal sites or meal serving sites, including non-profits and government entities throughout Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for providing free nutritious meals (breakfasts and lunches) to eligible children and teens during summer months when school is not in session, to reduce food insecurity year-round
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties. Low-income and economically disadvantaged areas within each county are eligible. Baltimore City has a separate application process administered through the Department of Housing and Community Development. Eligibility is determined by geographic location.
requirements_list: Participants must be 18 years or under
Must be in economically disadvantaged or low-income areas
Meals must meet one-third of the minimum daily nutritional requirements as devised by the USDA
Meals must be provided during summer months when school is not in session
For SUN Meals To-Go sites, registration is required to receive meals
Site must be located in the jurisdiction of the sponsoring organization (e.g., Baltimore City only for Baltimore City sites)
Site must plan to receive meals for a minimum of two weeks
Site must serve a minimum of 10 eligible youth ages 18 or younger
Youth workers ages 18 or younger are considered eligible youth
Private homes and public school buildings are not eligible to receive meals
Sites requesting breakfast must have adequate refrigeration to store perishables overnight
Refrigeration is also required for perishable lunch components if the meal is not served within one hour of delivery
Sites are subject to pre-operational inspection and must be approved by staff
Site supervisor and at least one alternate must attend mandatory 3-hour training session
Sites must agree to serve all meals in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply to participate as a SUN Meals site statewide, contact the sponsoring organization for your county. Each county has a designated sponsoring organization (primarily county public schools or, in Baltimore City, the Department of Housing). In Baltimore City, organizations interested in becoming meal serving sites may apply by downloading the application form (2026_SFSP_Site_Application.pdf). Completed applications should be submitted to the program office. The site supervisor and at least one alternate must attend a mandatory 3-hour training session. Sites are subject to pre-operational inspection and staff approval before beginning to serve meals. Eligibility is determined by geographic location.

structured_extraction.program_description: Required annual training for participating agencies providing updates on USDA regulations, guidance, and professional development for the Summer Food Service Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Required annual training for participating Summer Food Service Program agencies providing updates on USDA regulations and guidance and professional development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agencies participating in the Summer Food Service Program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training on SFSP regulations, guidance, and professional development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Participation in Summer Food Service Program required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs for dates and locations of required annual training.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program or Seamless Summer Option to support staff training, recipe tasting events, and development of high-quality standardized recipes using local agricultural products for Maryland schools. The program aims to build state capacity to create appealing recipes that align with student preferences and are realistic for schools to implement. MSDE partners with chefs from Prince George's Community College's Department of Wellness, Culinary Arts, and Hospitality, Maryland SNAP-Ed, and the Maryland Department of Agriculture to develop four standardized recipes (Vegetable Side Dish, Chicken or Fish Bowl, Vegetarian Bowl, and Entrée Salad) and gather student feedback through taste tests to refine them.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSDE provides grant funding to Local Education Agencies for the grant period May 1, 2022 – September 30, 2023. Funding supports: (1) Salaries/wages to hire substitute school nutrition staff to allow staff to attend training; (2) Stipends for staff time to attend training activities outside of normal work hours; (3) Food and nutrition equipment and smallware costs (total equipment value cannot exceed 5% of LEA subgrant total); (4) Food costs for grant-related training and taste tests (food expenditures cannot exceed 20% of LEA subgrant total, and must comply with Buy American Provision); (5) Consumable costs for grant-related training and taste tests for each school. MSDE anticipates awarding ten (10) grants, with additional grants possible if funds are available. Funding cannot be used for child nutrition program costs outside grant scope, purchasing meals/snacks for training participants, foods for reimbursable meals, foods as incentives/prizes, foods for home preparation, foods unrelated to standardized recipes, prizes or incentive items, gardening tools/materials, or clothing items.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than 5:00 pm EST on April 22, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022 that are in good standing and willing to commit participation of up to three schools.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salaries/wages for substitute school nutrition staff to allow attendance at training; stipends for staff time attending training outside normal work hours; food and nutrition equipment and smallware (crinkle cutters, peelers, food processors, knives, roasting pans, utensils); food costs for training and taste tests; consumable costs for training and taste tests. Training and nutrition education resources related to recipes will be developed by Maryland SNAP-Ed for school nutrition staff and teachers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland schools participating in the National School Lunch Program or Seamless Summer Option. Priority consideration given to schools located in rural zones as defined by USDA map (one point per school, max 3 points per LEA) and schools located in Internal Revenue Service (IRS) designated Qualified Opportunity Zones (one point per school, max 3 points per LEA).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local Education Agency (LEA)
Applicant must be participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during 2021-2022 and be in good standing
LEA must commit participation of up to three schools; if more than one school selected, at least two schools must serve different grade levels (certain exceptions may be approved)
All selected schools must be enrolled as Team Nutrition Schools and registered prior to application submission
LEA must designate a Grant Coordinator to serve as primary liaison with MSDE and grant partners, manage subgrant funds, and ensure grant activities are implemented at all participating schools
LEA and participating schools must commit to prepare at least one chef-designed recipe and host two or more student taste tests per recipe between Spring 2022 - Spring 2023
Schools must serve at least one final recipe in a reimbursable meal by end of grant period
Grant Coordinator must participate in periodic virtual meetings with grant partners
Grant Coordinator must submit quarterly reports on utilization of subgrant funds
Grant Coordinator must facilitate logistics for all training and recipe tasting events
Grant Coordinator must manage collection of data from recipe tasting events using provided templates
School nutrition staff must attend required training events hosted by MSDE and/or grant partners
Schools must use provided nutrition education resources to implement nutrition education for local products used in recipes
Grant Coordinator must secure photographs, data, and success stories for MSDE quarterly progress reports to USDA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested LEAs should complete the following steps: (1) Identify and register up to three participating schools that participate in NSLP or SSO and are registered as Team Nutrition Schools; (2) Complete a School Agreement Form for each participating school, requiring signatures from School Principal, Kitchen Manager, and a third school staff member (such as School Health Council member, Title 1 Coordinator, or Community Coordinator); (3) Complete the Team Nutrition Grant Application Form including all required components: school listing, recipe selection (schools can choose to test one, two, three, or all four recipes - Vegetable Side Dish, Chicken or Fish Bowl, Vegetarian Bowl, Entrée Salad), budget narrative, and school agreements; (4) Complete the Team Nutrition Budget Form (Excel file); (5) Obtain required signatures on LEA Agreement Form from Superintendent, Food and Nutrition Services Director, and LEA Grant Coordinator; (6) Submit completed application (saved as PDF), signed assurances page, signed agreement forms, and budget file to NutritionTraining.MSDE@maryland.gov by April 22, 2022 at 5:00 pm EST. MSDE will review applications for eligibility and completeness, score applications using selection criteria (Free and Reduced-Price enrollment percentage, rural zone location, Opportunity Zone location), and notify LEAs of award status by April 29, 2022.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that connects people with disabilities who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) with the Department of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) or community Employment Networks to help them achieve and maintain employment. Participants develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) and receive services including training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, job coaching, benefits counseling, and ongoing support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive free vocational rehabilitation services including job training, career counseling, job placement, job coaching, and benefits planning. The program is free and voluntary with no costs to participants. Services are coordinated to help individuals achieve employment goals and maintain work. If a participant's Ticket is 'In Use' with DORS and they are making good progress, Social Security will not conduct a Continuing Disability Review (provided they reply to any letters from Social Security). Work incentives are built into the program to help participants try working without immediately losing benefits, earn more money, keep health insurance, and get cash benefits back if they have to stop working due to disability. Medicare can be kept for at least 93 months after earning more. Medicaid can be maintained through various work incentive programs, including the Employed Individuals with Disabilities (EID) program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) and are between 18 and 64 years old.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services are used to help participants develop employment skills, find jobs with health benefits and earnings greater than their SSDI or SSI check, and maintain employment. Participants can also receive benefits planning assistance to understand work incentives and how work affects their benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
Must be between 18 and 64 years old
Must sign an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) with DORS or assign Ticket to DORS for the Ticket to become 'In Use'
Must work toward employment and educational goals to meet SSA's Timely Progress requirements
Must reply to any letters sent by Social Security
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals with SSDI or SSI between ages 18-64 can contact DORS to assign their Ticket to Work to the agency. DORS will work with the individual to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) based on the kind of job they want. Services will be coordinated to help reach employment goals. If already using the Ticket with an Employment Network, DORS will coordinate with that provider to ensure services are aligned. After obtaining employment and the DORS case closes, the Ticket will no longer be 'In Use' with DORS, and Social Security will send a letter explaining options for reassigning the Ticket if additional help is needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides eligible child care providers up to $400 each year to cover the cost of professional training, including approved core of knowledge training, pre-service training, conference registration, and approved college coursework.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $400 per year provided through two pathways: training vouchers (advance funding issued before training occurs for pre-service training, conferences, and approved college coursework) and training reimbursements (reimbursement issued after training completion for approved core of knowledge training, pre-service training, conferences, and approved college coursework). Applicants will receive notification of approval or denial via email within 30 days of application submission.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Beginning December 29, 2025 applications will be accepted. For training vouchers, application must be submitted at least 60 days before the conference or pre-service training. For training reimbursements, application must be submitted within 180 days of training completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers who hold a Maryland Child Care Credential at Level 2 or higher, or who held such a credential that expired between July 1, 2024 and August 30, 2025.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Approved core of knowledge training (minimum 2 clock hours), pre-service training, registration at statewide and national child care conferences, and approved college coursework in child development, early childhood materials and methods, special education, administration and management of child care programs, infants and toddlers, school-age children, health and safety and nutrition, and language and literacy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; available to child care providers throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must hold a Maryland Child Care Credential at Level 2 or higher
Alternatively, held a Level 2 or higher credential that expired between July 1, 2024 and August 30, 2025
Training must have been approved by MSDE according to COMAR 13A.14.09
For training reimbursements, training must have taken place less than 181 days before the application date
For training vouchers, application must be submitted at least 60 days before training/conference
For training reimbursements, application must be submitted within 180 days of training completion
Must submit documentation of successful completion (transcript, grade slip, or certificate of successful completion)
Training fees and association membership fees are not eligible
CDA credential or CDA renewal fees are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must register for an individual account on the Maryland OneStop platform and submit a completed application with required documentation. For training vouchers, submit at least 60 days before training. For training reimbursements, submit within 180 days of training completion. Applicants will receive notification of approval or denial via email within 30 days of application submission. If approved, applicants download their training voucher from the Maryland OneStop portal, sign it, and forward it to the trainer/training organization to complete training registration. After training completion, recipients must log into the Maryland OneStop portal, navigate to the Verification of Training Completion section, and upload their certificate of successful completion. Trainers submit the voucher to MSDE for payment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Transition Services for Students with Disabilities
structured_extraction.program_description: Activities that prepare students with disabilities to transition from school to post-school life, including employment, education, and independent living.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Services and activities that prepare students with disabilities, including those who are blind or have vision loss, to move from school to post-school life. Services include career guidance, assistive technology, training, independent living skills, orientation and mobility instruction, and job placement support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities, including those who are blind or have vision loss, preparing to transition from school to post-school activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transition planning, career exploration, assistive technology, training, independent living skills instruction, and other services to prepare students for post-school employment, education, and community living.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-wide. DORS counselors and teachers are located throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Student must have a disability
Student must be in school or transitioning from school
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Request DORS Services form or contact your local DORS office. You will be contacted to set up an intake meeting with a DORS counselor who will gather information and determine eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program supports domestic nutrition programs and American agricultural producers by purchasing 100 percent American-grown and produced foods for use in schools participating in the National School Lunch Program. Schools reduce food expenses by an average of twenty percent and can choose from over two hundred domestically grown fruits, vegetables, grains, poultry, dairy, and meat products. Child and Adult Care Food Program sponsors receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their meal reimbursements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive domestically produced foods through a catalog selection system with over two hundred products including fruits, vegetables, grains, poultry, dairy, and meat. The program reduces average school food expenses by twenty percent. Child and Adult Care Food Program sponsors receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their meal reimbursements. Schools participating in the National School Lunch Program automatically receive support through this food distribution program. Schools order products from the USDA Foods catalog and receive shipments of American-grown and produced commodities for use in meal preparation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland public schools and institutions participating in the National School Lunch Program and federal nutrition programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of 100 percent American-grown and produced fruits, vegetables, grains, poultry, dairy, and meat products for school meal programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland schools participating in the National School Lunch Program
requirements_list: School must participate in the National School Lunch Program
School must be willing to incorporate USDA Foods into meal planning and preparation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) automatically receive support through this food distribution program. Schools select from the USDA Foods catalog to order available commodities. Orders are placed through the state agency and products are delivered to school food service facilities for use in meal preparation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Virtual mentoring and support service for individuals on the autism spectrum attending college. Helps students transition into and navigate college while developing self-advocacy and social skills.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Remote mentoring program providing weekly online individual sessions with DORS Autism Services staff and weekly VCAMP online group sessions. Helps students on the autism spectrum transition from high school to college or from two-year to four-year college, develop self-advocacy and social skills, learn about campus supports such as Disability Support Services (DSS) and academic tutoring, improve time management and organizational skills, and develop appropriate grooming and hygiene skills for success in the college environment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals on the autism spectrum who are DORS participants attending in-state or out-of-state two- or four-year colleges and not participating in the in-person Pathways program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Virtual mentoring and support services for college transition, navigation, self-advocacy development, social skills improvement, time management, organizational skills, and grooming and hygiene skills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to DORS participants attending either in-state or out-of-state two- or four-year colleges where the in-person DORS Pathways program is not available
requirements_list: Be a DORS participant on the autism spectrum
Have a documented diagnosis on the autism spectrum
Have an approved Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that includes college
Work towards an industry-recognized college degree or certification from a two-year or four-year college where the in-person DORS Pathways program is not available
Commit to weekly online sessions with DORS Autism Services staff
Attend weekly VCAMP online group sessions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local office to request DORS Services and enroll in VCAMP. DORS will determine eligibility and enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that reimburses businesses for employee wages while they train qualified job seekers from the Department of Rehabilitation Services. Businesses can participate in short-term training (one month) or long-term training (up to four months).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term on-the-job training provides up to 100% salary reimbursement for one month. Long-term on-the-job training provides gradually decreasing wage reimbursement over up to four months as the employee becomes more skilled and independent. Businesses must provide a written authorization or preauthorized credit card from a DORS representative before providing services. Payment is the responsibility of DORS, and invoices are typically processed within approximately 30 days of receipt.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Brian Haas, Vendor Coordinator or DORS Business Services Representative
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses seeking to hire and train qualified job seekers from DORS.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wage reimbursement for employees undergoing on-the-job training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Services available through six regional DORS offices and the Office for Blindness & Vision Services.
requirements_list: Must hire a qualified DORS job seeker
Must complete the DORS Provider/Vendor Application form
Must become an approved DORS provider/vendor
Must obtain written authorization or preauthorized credit card from a DORS representative before providing services
Must provide invoices containing bill-to DORS office information, remit-to address, Federal Tax ID, invoice date, description of services rendered, and cost
Federal Tax ID number required (IRS Form W-9)
Approval timeline: applicant will be contacted by DORS administration within 30 days of application submission
Approval may be authorized until expiration date of supporting license/certificate; providers must reapply with current credentials to remain approved
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the DORS Provider/Vendor Application form. 2. Attach required supporting documentation including IRS Form W-9 and relevant licenses/certifications. 3. Submit application and all required information to: Director, DORS Business Support Services, 2301 Argonne Drive, Baltimore, MD 21218-1696. 4. Contact your regional DORS office or Brian Haas, Vendor Coordinator at 410-554-9505 or Vendor.dors@maryland.gov for assistance. 5. DORS will contact applicant within 30 days of receiving complete application. 6. Upon approval, obtain written authorization from DORS representative before providing services to trainees.

structured_extraction.program_description: A two-part training program for individuals with disabilities who have little or no work experience or who have been out of the workforce for an extended period. The program develops workplace skills through classroom sessions and community-based activities at the DORS WTC campus in Baltimore.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers two six-week courses that may be taken together or as stand-alone programs. Work Readiness 1 includes career exploration, soft skills development, financial management, organizational skills, self-determination and awareness, interpersonal skills and teamwork, workplace preparation and communication, and job retention through videos, lectures, guest speakers, worksite tours, and job shadowing. Work Readiness 2 focuses on customer service, workplace ethics, conflict management, resume writing, job descriptions, mock interviews, and managing your online footprint through guest speakers, job shadowing, and volunteer work experiences at community worksites.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students or job seekers with disabilities who have little or no work experience or have been out of the workforce for an extended period and are seeking competitive employment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and skill development for workplace readiness, including soft skills, career exploration, financial management, and real-world work experience through volunteering and community worksites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is delivered at DORS WTC campus in Baltimore.
requirements_list: Must have a disability
Must have little or no work experience or have been out of the workforce for an extended period
Must be able to function in a classroom setting and fully participate in all individual and group activities (Work Readiness 1)
Must demonstrate capability and desire to participate in competitive employment (Work Readiness 2)
Must be able to spend half of each day volunteering at a community worksite with drop-in support only (Work Readiness 2)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Consumers may contact their DORS Counselor or local office to enroll. Work Readiness 1 and 2 may be taken together or as stand-alone programs through the Workforce Training Center.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program created to assist Maryland's rural and agricultural businesses impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The program funds technology-empowered initiatives that help rural and agricultural businesses recover, rebuild, and pivot from economic crisis. It encourages collaboration between rural businesses, research institutions, and industry partners. Examples include developing innovative products or novel applications of existing technology.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $200,000 per project for a period of one year. Funds are disbursed in two tranches: 50% upon closing and the remaining 50% upon completion of a mid-term activity report. Companies receiving awards must provide quarterly updates on fund usage, project status, and economic impact for five years following the award date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland rural and agricultural businesses impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic seeking technology-empowered solutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technology-empowered initiatives to help rural and agricultural businesses recover, rebuild, and pivot from economic crisis, including development of innovative products or novel applications of existing technology.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland rural areas, defined as all counties except Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Howard County, Anne Arundel County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland Qualified Business in good standing with the MD Department of Assessments & Taxation
Must have principal business operations located in Maryland with at least 50% of workforce working in the State

Must be headquartered in or collaborate with a business in a Rural Area of Maryland (all counties except Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Howard County, Anne Arundel County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County)
Must collaborate with a Maryland research university, entrepreneurial organization, or related industry partner
Must have fewer than 100 members of workforce
