Must propose a tech-empowered and sustainable solution with measurable economic development impact
Must not be engaged in retail sales, real estate development, insurance, banking, lending, or professional services by accountants, attorneys, or physicians
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications submitted through TEDCO's online application portal at https://www.tedcomd.com/agriculture-and-rural-rebuild-arr-challenge prior to May 14, 2021. Applications reviewed within 30 days of submission. Review process comprises three stages: Compliance Review (eligibility verification), Detailed Review (TEDCO staff review with possible virtual interview), and Final Decision (forwarded to Executive Director/CEO). Applicants notified of decisions and approved applicants have up to 90 days to execute funding agreement and complete closing. Applicants must submit a grant proposal not exceeding 7 pages with 1-inch margins and 12-point Arial font including: complete work description, collaborative effort statement, sustainability plan and impact statement, funding request with budget summary, and expected outcomes with performance metrics and timeline.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides TEDCO portfolio companies with AWS credits and access to cloud services, including compute, storage, databases, machine learning, artificial intelligence, data lakes and analytics, and Internet of Things technologies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Startups that have raised Series A or lower and are not already part of Activate may receive $25,000 in AWS credits valid for two years, with eligibility for additional credits later. Credits can be used for eligible AWS services and support from infrastructure technologies like compute, storage, and databases, to emerging technologies such as machine learning and artificial intelligence, data lakes and analytics, and Internet of Things.
structured_extraction.program_audience: TEDCO portfolio companies that have raised Series A or lower funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible AWS services including infrastructure technologies (compute, storage, databases) and emerging technologies (machine learning, artificial intelligence, data lakes, analytics, Internet of Things).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: TEDCO portfolio companies in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a TEDCO portfolio company
Must have raised Series A or lower
Must not already be part of AWS Activate
Must contact Graham Dodge to obtain TEDCO's Organization ID
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit https://aws.amazon.com/startups/credits#packages and contact Graham Dodge (gdodge@tedcomd.com) to get TEDCO's Organization ID, which is required to submit the application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Amazon Web Services AI Pitch Competition-In Person
structured_extraction.program_description: A pitch competition showcasing AI-focused organizations and early-stage AI concepts. Handpicked participating teams present challenges or concepts to a panel of AWS industry experts and receive real-time feedback and guidance. Up to 10 finalists compete for up to $50,000 in AWS and PREDICTif services to support their AI initiatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $50,000 in AWS and PREDICTif services provided to finalists. Services include technical support and cloud resources to help bring AI initiatives to life.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations with AI-focused innovations or early-stage AI concepts, from fully formed initiatives to ideas needing technical support
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: AWS and PREDICTif services to develop and implement AI solutions and concepts
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based organizations
requirements_list: Must register for attendance
Attendance limited to 110 people
Up to 10 teams selected to pitch as finalists
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants register for the event and click the link provided (https://www.marylandsbdc.org/locations/corridor-region/pitch-competition) for pitching application details. Finalists are selected and present to a panel of AWS industry experts.

structured_extraction.program_description: Building Resources for Investment, Development, and Growth in Entrepreneurship - an eight-week cohort-based program designed to support Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual entrepreneurs. The program equips participants with technical knowledge, resources, and personalized guidance to access debt and equity capital through workshops, one-on-one mentoring, and applied learning activities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An eight-week hybrid program (in-person and virtual via Zoom) that includes three hours per week of expert-led workshops on business and capital readiness topics, one to two hours per week of one-on-one mentoring from subject-matter experts, and applied assignments where participants draft loan applications, strengthen investor materials, and revise financial projections.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual entrepreneurs, with a focus on women business leaders navigating Maryland's entrepreneurial innovation ecosystem.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides knowledge and resources for accessing debt and equity capital, improving financial literacy, strategic planning, and investor readiness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Be a Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individual entrepreneur
Complete the application form
Selected applicants will be notified following the review process
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested entrepreneurs complete an application form. Selected applicants are notified following review and provided with next steps regarding enrollment and program onboarding.

structured_extraction.program_description: The BII Pilot Program supports an equitable innovation and entrepreneurial ecosystem in higher education institutions throughout the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson Metropolitan Statistical Area. It seeks to advance technology toward commercialization of products or services and bolster support systems for entrepreneurs developing technology-based ventures through two main grant tracks: Technology Advancement and Entrepreneurship Commercialization, Programming, and Infrastructure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technology Advancement grants provide up to $50,000 to full-time faculty members, students, or student principal investigators at eligible institutions to support commercialization of new or existing technology. Joint applications from two or more universities can receive up to $75,000. Technology-based startups collaborating with faculty, students, or staff can also apply. Entrepreneurship Commercialization, Programming and Infrastructure grants provide up to $50,000 to staff or faculty operating entrepreneurship programs at eligible institutions. Duration is up to 9 months for Technology Advancement and up to 12 months for Entrepreneurship Commercialization.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Indication of Interest (IOI) Close: Wednesday, April 15th, 2026. RFAs Close: Wednesday, May 20th, 2026, at 11:59pm ET.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Faculty, students, and technology-based startups at eligible institutions in the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson Metropolitan Statistical Area. Staff and faculty operating entrepreneurship and commercialization programs at eligible institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants support commercialization of new or existing technology, creation or enhancement of entrepreneurship programs, commercialization infrastructure for technology-based ventures, and support for start-up creation or entrepreneurship development at eligible universities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Institutions must be located in or serve the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson Metropolitan Statistical Area. Eligible institutions include Anne Arundel Community College, Baltimore City Community College, Carroll Community College, Chesapeake College, Community College of Baltimore County, Coppin State University, Goucher College, Harford Community College, Howard Community College, Johns Hopkins University, Loyola University Maryland, Maryland Institute College of Art, McDaniel College, Morgan State University, Notre Dame of Maryland University, St. John's College, Stevenson University, Towson University, University of Baltimore, University of Maryland Baltimore, and University of Maryland Baltimore County.
requirements_list: Applicants must be from eligible institutions that have opted into the BII program
Institutions must formally join the initiative as collaborators to submit proposals
Full-time faculty at MII-Qualifying Universities cannot serve as lead applicants for Technology Advancement Grants
Applicants must engage with an onsite Project Lead at least one month (30 days) before application submission
Applications must include a current, dated letter of approval from an onsite Project Lead
For Technology Advancement: applicants must be full-time faculty, students, student principal investigators, or technology-based startups collaborating with institution staff
For Entrepreneurship Commercialization: applicants must be staff or faculty operating entrepreneurship or commercialization programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications follow a two-step process. First, applicants submit an Indication of Interest (IOI) form. BII staff review the IOI to verify eligibility and invite selected applicants to submit a full application within approximately two weeks. Applicants must meet with an onsite Project Lead before submitting the IOI and again before submitting the full application. The full application is submitted through a portal after receiving an invitation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Business Resource Information, Development, and Guidance Ecosystem (BRIDGE) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program created by TEDCO to provide legal, accounting, and financial advisory services to Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI)-owned businesses and Very Small Businesses (VSBs) with fewer than 10 employees. BRIDGE helps these businesses access capital and federal funding opportunities by offering business assessments, individualized roadmaps, financial literacy training, credit repair coaching, accounting system setup, legal services through university clinics, federal proposal development training, and short-term executive advisory engagements. Services are delivered through SBDCs, CDFIs, university law clinics, and loaned executives across Maryland, Delaware, Virginia, and Washington D.C.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: BRIDGE offers no-cost technical assistance including business assessments, individualized roadmaps, financial literacy training, credit repair coaching, accounting system setup, legal services through university clinics, federal proposal development training, and short-term executive advisory engagements. Services are delivered through SBDCs, CDFIs, university law clinics, and loaned executives. The program is designed to prepare businesses for access to capital including State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) funds and federal funding from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, CHIPS and Science Act, Inflation Reduction Act, and SBIR/STTR programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals (SEDI)-owned businesses and Very Small Businesses (VSBs) with fewer than 10 employees in Maryland, Delaware, Virginia, and Washington D.C.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance for business development including financial planning, capital readiness preparation, federal proposal development, legal services, accounting system setup, credit repair, and executive coaching.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland, Delaware, Virginia, and Washington D.C.
requirements_list: Business must be SEDI-owned or a Very Small Business (VSB) with fewer than 10 employees
Businesses seeking services to prepare for capital access or federal funding opportunities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at https://tedco.tfaforms.net/184. Attend virtual BRIDGE Program Open Forum held monthly on the third Thursday at 10:00 AM to learn more about the program and ask questions. Upon application, BRIDGE Advisors conduct a BRIDGE Assessment diagnostic and create an individualized roadmap guiding the business to specific legal, accounting, and financial technical assistance services.

structured_extraction.program_description: Concept Capital is TEDCO's initiative to bridge the early-stage funding gap for underrepresented entrepreneurs across Maryland. The program provides flexible funding and specialized support to founders, with a focus on socially and economically disadvantaged and rural-based founders.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Convertible notes ranging from $25,000 to $50,000 with founder-friendly terms including zero interest, zero discount, and negotiable valuation caps. Eligible founders also receive one-on-one mentoring and advisory services, advanced software for performance tracking and investment-readiness, and tailored guidance to achieve critical venture milestones. In addition to funding, entrepreneurs receive mentorship and advisory services to help them prepare for future venture capital investment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Underrepresented entrepreneurs across Maryland, including socially and economically disadvantaged individuals, minority founders, disabled founders, female founders, and rural-based founders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early-stage funding for technology-driven businesses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based business with principal office in Maryland and 51% or more of workforce in-state. Founder or business must be located in a rural or disadvantaged community.
requirements_list: Maryland-based business (principal office in Maryland with 51%+ workforce in-state)
Technology-driven business (non-retail focus)
Founded within the last 7 years
Founder or business located in a rural or disadvantaged community, or a socially and economically disadvantaged individual (SEDI), including minority, disabled, or female founders
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications will reopen in 2027. The specific application process steps are not detailed on this page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A global startup program that helps developers create, launch, and scale their startups by providing cloud infrastructure credits, technical training, mentorship, priority support, networking opportunities, and marketing assistance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides up to $1,000 worth of DigitalOcean cloud credits valid for 12 months, technical training and mentorship, priority support through DigitalOcean's Customer Success teams, access to a dedicated Slack community, marketing help and promotions, and invitations to exclusive networking events. Verified startups receive credits within 15 days of application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and startup founders seeking to create, launch, and scale their startups.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cloud infrastructure deployment and scaling, including compute, storage, databases, and emerging technologies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Global program; Maryland startups eligible through TEDCO.
requirements_list: Must create a DigitalOcean team account with official email address
Must add a valid payment method
Must use same email address to apply
Must mention TEDCO when prompted for accelerator/incubator/VC name
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Create a DigitalOcean team account with official email, add valid payment method. Step 2: Apply via Hatch application link (do.co/hatch-application), mention TEDCO as accelerator/incubator/VC. Verified startups receive credits within 15 days.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that support infrastructure and workforce development initiatives to strengthen Maryland's innovation economy, foster economic opportunity for all residents, and accelerate growth of emerging and advanced industries. The fund aims to position Maryland as a leading global and inclusive innovation economy by 2040.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Infrastructure Awards provide up to $1,000,000 per project (higher amounts may be considered) for projects lasting 12 to 36 months depending on project scope and readiness. Workforce Awards provide up to $250,000 per project (higher amounts may be considered) for projects lasting 12 to 24 months depending on project scope and readiness. Approximately $3 million is anticipated for Infrastructure Awards (1-3 expected awards) and approximately $2 million for Workforce Awards (8-10 expected awards). Matching funds are required: a preferred 1:1 cash match from private sector, federal sources, or other sources is encouraged. For Infrastructure projects, higher matching ratios receive more favorable consideration. For Workforce projects, lower matches will be considered, especially for projects demonstrating strong partnerships and community impact. In-kind contributions are welcomed but will not be evaluated as equivalent to cash match. TEDCO does not accept indirect costs as part of the budget.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public entities, nonprofit organizations, private entities, public-private partnerships, and higher education institutions working on infrastructure and workforce development initiatives. Projects must intend to have a physical presence in Maryland for at least 5 years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure and workforce development initiatives that support Maryland's economic competitiveness, foster economic opportunity, and accelerate growth of emerging and advanced industries. Funds must be used in the State of Maryland. Infrastructure projects support building or expanding physical infrastructure for innovation economy, especially in high-impact sectors such as advanced manufacturing, advanced laboratory, and advanced technology. Workforce development funds support educational programs, degree and non-degree programs, certifications, training, and exposure to career pathways in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics (STEAM) for all ages, with emphasis on middle and high-skilled job training and focus on including individuals from underserved communities. Funds cannot be used for scholarships or salary increases associated with transitioning part-time employees to full-time roles.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Projects must be based in Maryland, benefit Maryland's innovation economy and workforce, and be consistent with goals included in the Equitech Growth Commission's Strategic plan.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public entity, nonprofit organization, private entity, public-private partnership, or institution of higher education
Applicant must intend to have a physical presence in Maryland for at least 5 years
Awardees must be in good standing with the State of Maryland at the time of the award and remain in good standing throughout the term of the funded project
Projects must be consistent with the Equitech Growth Commission Strategic plan and address critical infrastructure or workforce development needs
Projects must secure matching funds as specified: 1:1 cash match preferred from private sector, federal sources, or other sources
Matching funds must be unencumbered and dedicated solely to the proposed project, verified through Letters of Commitment
For Workforce projects, must have focus on including individuals from underserved communities and addressing barriers to participation for underrepresented populations

Project proposals must include: problem statement, proposed solution and project activities, goals and objectives, project timeline with chronological milestones and associated metrics, diversity and inclusion plan, alignment with EGF Purpose, metrics and impact assessment, budget and justification with separate columns for EGF funds and matching funds, and letters of commitment for cash matching funds

Priority industry types include: entrepreneurship development, STEM education, advanced manufacturing, cybersecurity and IT industry workforce development, advanced technology, and advanced laboratory space

Additional areas of consideration include: environmental and energy technology, aerospace and defense, smart agriculture and food technology, healthcare, life sciences and bioinformatics, autonomous systems and robotics, FinTech, creative industries and digital media, and logistics and supply chain innovation
Projects must meet eligibility requirements in Compliance Review or will be automatically rejected
Applications with inadequate or missing materials will be automatically rejected in Screening Review
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Equitech Growth Fund RFA (Request for Applications) document at https://www.tedcomd.com/funding/cultivate-maryland/ for detailed requirements and evaluation criteria. 2. Register and attend optional informational webinars (April 16, June 11, or July 23, 2026). 3. Submit a complete application through the online Jotform at https://tedco.jotform.com/260855899774077 by August 7, 2026 at 5:00 pm. 4. Application must include: Application Information (organization name, address, type, project details, contact info, project summary of 500 words maximum, funding requested, matching funds committed), Project Proposal (5 pages maximum, 11pt font or larger, 1 inch margins, single-spaced) with project description, diversity and inclusion plan, alignment with EGF purpose, metrics and impact assessment, completed Budget and Justification Worksheet (Exhibit A) with separate columns for EGF and matching funds, and Letters of Commitment verifying unencumbered cash matching funds are available and committed. 5. Letters of Commitment should be addressed to: Equitech Growth Fund Program Manager, TEDCO, 10960 Grantchester Way, Suite 120, Columbia, MD 21044. 6. Applicants will receive email confirmation of submission. 7. Applications undergo Compliance Review (eligibility check), Screening Review (completeness check), Detailed Review (scored by TEDCO staff and external reviewers on alignment with EGF goals, project viability and feasibility, economic impact and job creation, capacity to leverage matching funds, community engagement and inclusivity, and metrics and impact measurement), and Due Diligence Process (verification of assumptions, budget review, virtual meetings if needed). 8. Each criterion scored 1-5 (5=Excellent, 4=Very Good, 3=Good, 2=Fair, 1=Low). Multiple reviewers score applications; applicants receive average score. 9. Finalists may be required to attend virtual interview near week of September 7, 2026. 10. TEDCO staff submit recommendations to CEO for Final Decision. 11. All applicants notified of outcome. Upon approval, submit closing documents: Application Form, Project Proposal, Key Milestones, Key Metrics, Budget, Spending Plan and Disbursement Request, Letter of Commitment for Cash Matching Funds, Project Location Lease, Certificate of Good Standing for State of Maryland, Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws or Operating Agreement, and Board Resolution for Signing Authority. 12. Upon successful closing, awardee receives funds via wire transfer based on agreed timelines and milestones. Full payment disbursed upon completion of award agreement. 13. Awardees must submit interim and final progress reports every 4-6 months during the project, and annual impact reports for five years following project completion describing how project met goals and overall economic impact. Contact equitechgrowth@tedcomd.com for questions or clarifications. Questions regarding the RFA must be submitted by July 24 at 5:00 PM ET; answers posted by July 31.

structured_extraction.program_name: Federal Labs Leveraging Innovation to Products (FLLIP) Pilot Program

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers education, expert guidance, targeted matchmaking with federal laboratories, comprehensive technical assistance including market research and patent strategy, and support for developing formal relationships with federal lab partners.

Users get access to templates, automation tools, collaboration features, a patents dashboard, and customer support. Services currently focus on patents and include trademark services for up to two trademarks. Each user receives up to two hours of practical, hands-on support and a 30-minute onboarding session from the IPGen team.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free one-year subscription to IPGen's IP management software platform. Included services: machine learning and automation tools for IP processes; templates; private collaboration and messaging features; community forum access; status tracking; patents dashboard; and customer support. Each subscriber receives a 30-minute onboarding session and up to two hours of hands-on practical support from the IPGen team (available in 30-minute increments). The platform helps entrepreneurs effectively manage and protect their IP, streamline IP processes, reduce risks, and enhance the value of their intellectual property.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based entrepreneurs and startup businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The platform assists with intellectual property management throughout the full IP lifecycle, including searching, drafting, and prosecution of patents and trademarks. It enables startups to streamline IP processes, reduce risks, and enhance the value of their intellectual property, providing a strong foundation for future business growth.

structured_extraction.program_description: DefTech is a membership-based entrepreneurial resource and program that connects Maryland businesses, entrepreneurs, and DoD lab personnel to federal laboratories for product development, testing, intellectual property licensing, and commercialization services. The center helps businesses search for patents from defense research labs in Maryland, connects them with product development resources through DoD Research Labs, and guides them through the licensing process. Member companies receive professional support services including access to technical experts, intellectual property due diligence, business support, research tools, and connections with the Federal Lab Education Accelerator (FLEX) program for market and technology assessments. The center provides information, networking, education, and mentoring to facilitate the technology transfer process for technologies developed at National Security Agency/Fort Meade and other Department of Defense labs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DefTech provides proprietary business services to member companies at no cost for the initial 30 companies in the first program year (program cost waived due to funding from DoD Office of Local Community Cooperation, Maryland Department of Commerce, and TEDCO). Services include: DefTech Academy and Certification courses on technology transfer and government-related contracting; pre-lab engagement training; proprietary monthly distribution of federal funding notices and industry engagement opportunities; private meetings with federal labs for DefTech members only; monthly virtual office hours with DefTech Advisors to assist companies working with federal labs; information services to help navigate the Technology Transfer (T2) process with DoD research laboratories; networking opportunities to connect with T2 staff, scientists, engineers, and service providers; education covering technology transfer topics including market-oriented product development, intellectual property and patent law, and customer discovery; and one-on-one mentoring and technical assistance for clients interested in licensing technology from DoD labs, including identifying relevant intellectual property, market analysis, and commercialization planning. Free consulting services also include searching for available patents from defense research labs in Maryland and guidance through the licensing process.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland companies, entrepreneurs, and individuals developing or interested in developing commercial products and services using federal laboratory intellectual property, equipment, facilities, and expertise. Includes technology companies seeking to establish a presence in Maryland, scientists and engineers working at DoD research labs, and non-traditional defense contractors. Focus on high technology and bio innovation sectors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services support business creation, growth, and operations through access to federal laboratory resources, technology transfer expertise, intellectual property licensing opportunities, product development support, market assessment assistance, patent searching, and commercialization planning for defense and commercial technologies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. The DefTech Center partners with DoD laboratories located in Maryland including National Security Agency/Fort Meade, U.S. Army Medical Research and Materiel Command, U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command labs (Army Research Laboratory, C5ISR, Chemical Biological Center), and Aberdeen Proving Ground.
requirements_list: Company or individual must be developing or interested in developing commercial products and services using federal laboratory intellectual property, equipment, facilities, or expertise
Membership is highly competitive with limited membership each year
Primary focus on high technology and bio innovation sectors
Applicants may be admitted as members for preliminary training if they need additional knowledge and resources before federal lab engagement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an online application which is reviewed by a DefTech Advisor for initial screening. Accepted applicants are placed into one of two categories: (1) Resource-ready for immediate federal engagement and commencement of DefTech services, or (2) Preliminary training followed by commencement of DefTech services. Graduate companies are eligible for alumni membership. Interested parties may also contact the DefTech Center directly — reach Jill Porter, Business Development Director, at [email protected] or 410-222-7410.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides equity investment in Maryland-based startup companies that have licensed technology from a qualifying research university within the past year, supporting the commercial launch and early development of university-based innovations. The program supports start-ups within Johns Hopkins University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Baltimore, University of Maryland Baltimore County (UMBC), University of Maryland College Park, Frostburg State University, and Bowie State University.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $300,000 in equity investment for commercial launch and early development activities over a 9-month funded project. Investment is provided through one of two mechanisms determined by the MII Board of Directors: (1) Five-year convertible promissory note with 8% annual interest that may convert to equity if the company receives $500,000 or more in outside investment or undergoes an acquisition, OR (2) Revenue-based reimbursable grant requiring the company to pay back 3% of quarterly revenues for 10 years following the award date or until repayment equals twice the total amount disbursed, whichever comes first. Disbursement is milestone-based: initial payment upon closing, with subsequent payments upon successful completion of project milestones. Funding must be used for eligible expenses incurred during the 9-month funding period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 5:00pm on the 15th day (or first business day thereafter) of each submission month. 2026 deadlines: January 15, April 15, July 15, October 15
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based startup companies that have licensed technology from a qualifying university (Johns Hopkins University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Baltimore, University of Maryland Baltimore County, University of Maryland College Park, Frostburg State University, or Bowie State University) within the past 12 months.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commercial launch, early development, and related commercialization activities for university-licensed technologies. Eligible expenses must support the proposed 9-month project to achieve technical and commercial milestones that increase the company's value proposition for product launch, customer acquisition, and follow-on investment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Company must be Maryland-based with principal place of business in Maryland. At least 50% of the company's employees (FTE) must reside or work in Maryland, the 'nerve center' of the company's business must be in Maryland, and the company must lease or own a facility in Maryland from which it conducts business. Technology must have been licensed from a qualifying Maryland research university within 12 months of proposal submission.
requirements_list: Company must be Maryland-based and meet the MII Principal Place of Business definition (at least 50% of employees reside/work in Maryland, nerve center of business in Maryland, must lease or own a Maryland facility)
Company must have no more than pre-seed level dilutive funding totaling less than $1,000,000

Technology must be licensed from a qualifying university (Johns Hopkins University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Baltimore, University of Maryland Baltimore County, University of Maryland College Park, Frostburg State University, Bowie State University)

License must have been executed no more than 12 months prior to applying for a Program award (if technology has not yet been licensed, fully executed license agreement required within 90 days of notification of MII award)
Company must be dependent on licensed technology for commencement of its operations
Technology must have appropriate intellectual property protection
Must engage with a Site Miner at least 30 days before application submission
Application must include a dated letter of approval signed by a Site Miner confirming prior engagement of at least 30 days
Must obtain a unique TEDCO ID number before applying
Application must include current signed letter from the Qualifying University's Technology Transfer Office indicating approval and certifying Technology disclosure reference number and IP status
Company cannot have pre-seed dilutive funding of $1,000,000 or more
Cannot accept any investment greater than $250,000 without offering TEDCO the opportunity to participate on a pari-passu basis
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Register with TEDCO and obtain a unique TEDCO ID number specific to the company. 2) Meet with a Site Miner (designated by the Qualifying University) at least 30 days before application submission to receive valuable input and feedback on the proposal. 3) Draft a complete application consisting of: General Application Information (entered directly into online portal including TEDCO ID, project title, budget, abstract, university name, Site Miner engagement confirmation, and other required fields); and Full Application (single PDF file not exceeding 15 pages with specific formatting requirements including 1-inch margins, 12-point minimum font). 4) Full Application must include: Cover Page (1 page), Company Formation Proposal (5 pages) addressing Technology Description/Status/IP, Market Analysis/Competition, Commercialization Pathway/Go-to-Market Strategy/Risk Assessment, and Project Milestones/Detailed Budget; Executive Summary (2 pages); and Supplemental Materials including signed letters from Technology Transfer Office and Site Miner (both dated within 30 days of submission), Economic and Societal Impact Statement, and optional support letters. 5) Submit complete application through MII online portal by 5:00pm on the 15th day (or first business day thereafter) of submission months (January, April, July, or October). 6) Applications are evaluated by a review committee on technical merit, commercial potential, and alignment with program goals. 7) CEO is required to present the application to the review committee. 8) Successful applicants will have an award agreement executed. 9) During the funded project (up to 9 months), company must submit milestone reports and financial reports, with funding disbursed based on successful milestone completion. 10) After project completion, company must submit a final report within 30 days and continue quarterly financial reporting and annual reports on commercialization progress for up to 10 years (depending on investment structure).

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by TEDCO under the Maryland Innovation Initiative (MII) that funds research projects to validate technology and assess market potential for innovative technologies from Maryland research universities. The program supports full-time faculty in advancing university-discovered technologies toward commercialization through proof-of-principle studies, technology validation, and market assessment activities. It helps transition promising discoveries from academic institutions to commercial development, funding both technology development reports and commercialization planning. A pilot Technology Validation Program component specifically targets faculty at Bowie State University and Frostburg State University with a streamlined $50,000 grant structure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers two grant tracks: (1) Standard Technology Assessment: Up to $130,000 per grant for sole applicants to conduct technology validation and market assessment over 9 months. Joint applications from two or more qualifying universities can receive up to $180,000 for commercialization of technologies existing at multiple universities or activities at multiple sites. Awards include two major deliverables: a Technology Validation report (5-page final report) and a Commercialization Plan (separate document). The Commercialization Plan budget is separate from the Technology Assessment budget with up to $15,000 allocated. Within the Commercialization Plan budget, applicants may spend up to $5,000 on I-Corps programs and up to $4,500 on company formation costs or university start-up attorney costs. (2) Technology Validation Program (Pilot for Bowie State and Frostburg State Universities): $50,000 grant structured as two components to be completed within 6 months: Technology Development Report (up to $40,000) for proof-of-principle studies to validate technology for commercial application and advance it to generate strong IP or attract licensees, and Market Assessment (up to $10,000) to support market analysis and development of a commercialization plan. Up to $4,000 of the Technology Development budget may be allocated for intellectual property protection expenses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling submissions for Technology Validation Program (pilot). Standard Technology Assessment submissions: 5:00pm on the 15th day (or first business day thereafter) of each submission month. 2026 deadlines: January 15, April 15, July 15, October 15
structured_extraction.contact_name: Silvia Goncalves; Abi Kulshreshtha, PhD; Griffin St Louis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Full-time faculty members at qualifying universities: Johns Hopkins University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Baltimore, University of Maryland Baltimore County, University of Maryland College Park, Frostburg State University, and Bowie State University. The pilot Technology Validation Program specifically targets full-time faculty at Bowie State University and Frostburg State University.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technology validation, market assessment, and commercialization activities for university-discovered technologies with commercial potential. Funds can be used to conduct proof-of-principle studies to validate a technology's commercial use, advance technology to generate strong intellectual property, attract potential licensees, conduct market analysis, develop commercialization plans, support I-Corps customer discovery programs, and pay for company formation costs or university start-up attorney costs for licensing agreements. Technology Development funds support costs for materials, supplies, personnel, fringe benefits, and other direct costs. Commercialization Plan funds may support market research, contracting with industry experts, engaging interim CEOs, developing regulatory and reimbursement strategies, and I-Corps participation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Technologies must be owned by or disclosed to a qualifying Maryland research university with appropriate intellectual property protection. Standard program eligible universities: Johns Hopkins University, Morgan State University, University of Maryland Baltimore, University of Maryland Baltimore County, and University of Maryland College Park. The pilot Technology Validation Program is limited to full-time faculty at Bowie State University and Frostburg State University.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a full-time faculty member at a qualifying university
Technology must be owned by a qualifying university or disclosed to the university's technology transfer office
Appropriate intellectual property protection must exist for the technology (patent, patent application, copyright, trademark, or other form of intellectual property)

Applicant must complete TEDCO registration and obtain a TEDCO ID before submitting the MII application

Project must be completed within the specified grant period (9 months for standard Technology Assessment; 6 months for the Technology Validation Program pilot)
Technology Development Report and Market Assessment components must both be completed (Technology Validation Program pilot)

Technology Transfer Office must provide a signed letter confirming disclosure of technology and indicating whether they have or will secure appropriate intellectual property protection (Technology Validation Program pilot)
Site Miner letters must be dated within one month (30 days) of application submission date (Standard Technology Assessment)
Full Application must not exceed 15 pages total, or submission will be rejected without consideration (Standard Technology Assessment)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Standard Technology Assessment: (1) Register with TEDCO to obtain a unique TEDCO ID by visiting https://tedco.tfaforms.net/74. (2) Engage with a Site Miner (assigned by the qualifying university) at least 30 days before submitting application to discuss MII program requirements and review draft application. (3) Complete online General Application Information including DEI information, project title (15 words max), proposed duration (9 months or less), PI profile information, indication if new or revised, Qualifying University name(s), MII Phase, non-proprietary abstract (300 words max), total budget requested, technology disclosure reference number, IP status, technology type/category, and confirmations that letters from technology transfer office and Site Miner are included and that research/grants administration approval is obtained. (4) Draft Full Application (single PDF, single-sided, 1-inch margins, 12-point font minimum, not exceeding 15 pages total) including Cover Page (1 page with project title, Qualifying University name(s), PI name, funding amount requested), Technology Validation Proposal (5 pages scoring section covering: Technology Description and Status/IP including problem statement, solution statement, technology description with supporting data, IP description and landscape analysis; Market Analysis and Competition including value proposition, market segmentation, market size (TAM/SAM/SOM), market trends, and competitive analysis; Commercialization Pathway and Risk Assessment; Project Milestones with timeline and measurable outcomes; Detailed Budget and Justification), Commercialization Plan Proposal (1 page describing scope of work to validate commercial hypothesis and build on market analysis to form complete Commercialization Plan as deliverable), and Supplemental Materials (Economic and Societal Impact Statement, signed Technology Transfer Office letter, signed Site Miner letter dated within 30 days, optional support letters, references, and optional resubmission response to reviewer comments not exceeding 1 page). (5) Submit complete application by 5:00pm on submission deadline (15th or first business day thereafter of January, April, July, or October). Applications submitted after 5:00pm are rejected. (6) Applications undergo Compliance Review to verify minimum requirements are met. Applications not meeting requirements are rejected. (7) Applications receiving favorable compliance review are assigned to multiple reviewers for preliminary scoring. (8) Applications with strong preliminary scores are invited to MII Review Committee meeting for discussion and final scoring by committee members. (9) MII Review Committee provides final score based on average of scores from committee members. (10) Applications are reviewed by MII Board of Directors approximately 75 days (about 2.5 months) after submission for final approval. Site Miners receive access to reviewer comments, final scores, and recommendations with adequate time to help applicants prepare resubmission if needed. Technology Validation Program Pilot (Bowie State and Frostburg State): (1) Obtain TEDCO ID number from https://tedco.tfaforms.net/74. (2) Submit General Application Information via email to Griffin St Louis including TEDCO ID, project title, PI name and contact information, Eligible University, technology source/contact person responsible for commercialization, non-proprietary abstract, and keywords. (3) Identify necessary internal approvals and resources including staff/students prior to submission; work with university entrepreneurship centers and business school students for Market Assessment. (4) Draft Full Proposal (PDF format, maximum 5 pages one-sided, 1-inch margins, 12-point font, numbered pages) including Abstract (non-proprietary), Description of the Technology (general description with novelty and commercial applications, problem and importance, why better than competing approaches, detailed description with survey of competing approaches, preliminary data or convincing evidence), Intellectual Property (description with disclosure reference number, patent/application serial numbers and filing dates, strategy for strengthening IP), Project Plan and Milestones (specific aims, detailed work description, quantitative endpoints, final milestone demonstrating technology for specific market application), Market Assessment (plan to develop Commercialization Plan as final deliverable, approach to draft document outlining product development and distribution steps, purpose to identify and resolve high-risk business model portions), Project Team (list of personnel with background and proposed contribution), Budget and Budget Justification (detailed budget classified as Personnel/Fringe Benefits, Materials & Supplies, Other Direct Costs itemized; justification with total hours, cost/hour, and fringe benefits; travel costs only if critical; no indirect costs allowed; up to $4,000 may be allocated by technology transfer office for IP protection expenses), and References & Support Letters (appendix not counted toward 5-page limit). (5) Submit Full Proposal as email attachment to Program Manager. Applications may be submitted at any time before 06/01/2024. (6) MII conducts Compliance Review ensuring applications meet basic requirements; non-compliant applications rejected without further review. (7) MII conducts internal Technical Review by individuals with technical and commercial experience under confidentiality; reviewers comprehensively evaluate translational potential, design appropriateness, innovation, commercial application, and commercialization potential; reviewers provide recommendation and for rejected applications provide concerns to applicant. (8) MII Board of Directors makes final award decision. Full review process takes no more than 30 days. (9) If awarded, award letter sent with funding agreement to applicant, grants/contracts office, and technology transfer office. If rejected, notification includes Review Committee comments and independent technical review if available. (10) Applicant has 30 days to sign agreement and return to MII; if not signed and returned within 30 days, proposal becomes inactive and applicant must reapply.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides financial and technical assistance to eligible entities seeking help with establishing new makerspaces, expanding existing makerspaces, or developing programming for makerspaces throughout Maryland. It supports the growth of a statewide community of makerspaces that provide entrepreneurs, learners, and community members with access to tools, technologies, and knowledge to support their growth and development, expand workforce training opportunities, and enable the creation of assistive technologies and physical goods. In 2025, nearly $785,000 was awarded to 14 organizations across the state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program awards grants in three types: Type A (Establish a New Makerspace): up to $100,000 per year for up to three years for a maximum of $300,000; applicants may also request up to $25,000 for one year to conduct a feasibility study (requires 1:1 cash match). Type B (Expand an Existing Makerspace): up to $100,000 for one year. Type C (Develop Programming for a Makerspace): up to $25,000 for one year. Type B and C require 1:1 matching funds or in-kind contributions. In 2025, nearly $785,000 was awarded in total to 14 organizations statewide. Funds can be used for the establishment of a new makerspace, the expansion of a makerspace, or the development of programming for a makerspace, including facility costs, utility costs, tools, technology, 3D printers, design software, training, marketing, internship opportunities, community events, and technical education opportunities. A 1:1 matching requirement applies; matching funds may come from donors or the applicant organization itself, and in-kind matches are acceptable, including donated materials, tools, space, or volunteer time. In-kind matches are permitted except for Type A feasibility study funding, which requires 1:1 cash match. Technical Assistance of up to ten (10) hours is available and will be provided by Open Works located in Baltimore City to address specific needs in the establishment, expansion, or operation of a makerspace.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, agencies or instrumentalities designated by local governments, nonprofit entities, and makerspace organizations interested in establishing, expanding, or developing programming for makerspaces in Maryland. Also serves entrepreneurs, community members, and workforce development participants interested in tools, technology, and assistive technologies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishment of a new makerspace, expansion of an existing makerspace, or development of makerspace programming. Funding can support facility costs including utility costs, tools, equipment, technology, 3D printers, design software, training for software usage, marketing, internship opportunities, community events, technical education opportunities, real estate purchase, renovations, planning, and operations. Funds also support the creation and provision of low-tech assistive devices to Maryland residents.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. Makerspace facilities must be located in Maryland and open and accessible to the general public. Makerspaces that serve a specific K-12 school, university, or otherwise pre-defined community are ineligible unless they also devote at least 50% of their operating hours to public programming or services.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government, an agency or instrumentality designated by a local government, or a nonprofit entity

Makerspace must be defined as a community space that provides access to tools, technology, and knowledge for learners and entrepreneurs, results in prototyping or creation of physical goods, and supports technical education opportunities for personal growth, workforce training, and early-stage business ventures
Applicant must be operating or seeking to operate a makerspace in Maryland

Makerspace facilities receiving assistance must be open and accessible to the general public; makerspaces serving a specific K-12 school, university, or pre-defined community must devote at least 50% of operating hours to public programming or services
Applicant must provide a Letter of Intent from the entity providing matching funds, documenting the amount of matching funds or in-kind contributions

Applicant must provide matching funds or in-kind contributions equal to at least 100% of the grant amount requested (1:1 match); in-kind contributions include real costs incurred by the applicant for the proposed project and must be approved by TEDCO; in-kind matches are not permitted for Type A feasibility study funding, which requires 1:1 cash match

Entities receiving Financial Assistance must agree to provide six-month project status reports (submitted at the end of December and end of June each calendar year) for the duration of the funded project, including financial reports (Income Statement and Balance Sheet), milestone reports (1-2 pages), and project reports (brief commentary/analysis)

Entities receiving Financial or Technical Assistance must participate in quarterly meetings of the Maryland Makerspace Network to discuss data collection standards, reciprocity standards, safety and operational best practices, formal establishment of a member-driven association, co-op opportunities for insurance and purchasing, and other relevant network matters

Type A applicants seeking funding up to $100,000 per year must have completed a successful feasibility study and must show evidence of additional financial support and a sustainability plan extending beyond the initial five-year period from the date of award

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a complete online application through TEDCO's website by the deadline of May 15, 2026 at 5 pm ET. The application requires: entity name and type, main point of contact, makerspace location information, Letter(s) of Intent from organizations providing matching funds (cash or in-kind) showing the amount, and up to 500-word responses to additional questions. All uploaded files must be formatted as PDF. TEDCO recommends preparing responses in MSWord or text editor and copying into the form to avoid technical issues and retain a copy. One review cycle per year is conducted for Financial Assistance. Technical Assistance requests can be made at any time after the award selection process is completed via a separate online application. The full review process takes up to 60 days from the application deadline. Stage One (Eligibility Review) evaluates whether the applicant has adhered to all RFA requirements, format compliance, valid LOIs, and matching fund commitments. Stage Two (Preliminary Review) includes in-depth review by a TEDCO committee evaluating project type and funding amount, project description and innovation level, project timeline and milestones, data collection and impact measurement plans, use of funds, applicant county, and organizational expertise and partnerships. Strongest applicants advance to Stage Three. Stage Three (Meeting with Review Committee Members) requires selected applicants to present their plan and answer questions in an in-person or virtual meeting at TEDCO's option; applicants may be asked to provide a facility tour. Presentations must address the problem being solved, proposed solution breakdown, innovation or uniqueness compared to similar solutions, marketing/roll-out strategy, project timeline and budget breakdown, matching fund sources and sustainability ability, impact measurement and data gathering strategies, and relevant organizational and team experience. Stage Four (Final Decision) involves TEDCO's CEO reviewing all committee recommendations for final decision. Rejected applicants are notified via email and may request a follow-up meeting to understand areas for improvement in future submissions. Questions should be emailed to mmip@tedcomd.com or jferguson@tedcomd.com; all questions and answers are posted on the Program webpage. Payments to awardees are made via wire transfer to the applicant's bank after completion of grant-related paperwork.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the MSCRF website at www.mscrf.org/funding-opportunities. For eligibility requirements and application procedures, visit MSCRF funding opportunities. All applicants must secure IRB approval or exemption determination before grant disbursement. Applicants must also obtain any required IACUC approval. Grant agreements are executed between TEDCO and the grantee institution, with the Principal Investigator identified in the agreement. Annual and final reports are filed electronically through the TEDCO Funds System at www.tedcofunds.org. Grantees must provide annual funding letters requesting continuation of funding for the following year.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Stem Cell Research Fund Validation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grant funding to validate stem cell research findings and support the development of promising stem cell technologies toward pre-clinical applications. The program promotes State-funded stem cell research and cures through financial assistance to public and private entities within the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State-funded grants provided to public and private entities in Maryland to promote human stem cell research and medical treatments. Grants are disbursed according to an approved project budget for eligible project costs. Disbursement may occur in multiple installments (initial payment, and potentially year 1 and year 2 payments) contingent upon continued compliance with grant terms, satisfactory report reviews, and absence of default. All grant proceeds must be used solely for eligible project costs as specified in the approved project budget and application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Researchers and institutions conducting stem cell research, including universities, nonprofit research institutions, and companies located in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Human stem cell research and development of stem cell-based medical treatments and technologies. Grant proceeds must be used solely for eligible project costs as set forth in the approved project budget. Adjustments within budget categories or between categories (up to 10% of the category) may be made without amendment if consistent with the grant purpose.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based public and private entities, including constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland and Maryland corporations
requirements_list: Grantee must obtain IRB (Institutional Review Board) approval for the project or a determination that the project is exempt from IRB approval within six months of the effective date
Grantee must obtain any required IACUC (Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee) approval for the project before disbursement of any grant proceeds
Grantee must use grant funds only for eligible project costs as specified in the approved project budget
Grantee must comply with all applicable Laws and the State's policy concerning drug and alcohol free workplaces
Grantee must comply with all laws prohibiting discrimination in employment and operations
Grantee must maintain detailed project records in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles for three years after discharge of all duties
Grantee must complete the project by the completion date specified in the agreement
Grantee must use best scientific efforts to accomplish the aims described in the approved application
Principal Investigator identity cannot be changed without advance written consent of TEDCO
Grantee must file annual reports (except for final year) no later than 30 days before the anniversary of the effective date
Grantee must file a final report within 45 days after the end of the grant term
Grantee must cause the Principal Investigator to present at an annual in-state symposium during each year of the grant term and the year immediately following
Grantee must share final results of the project and any cell lines initially developed with other fund grantees upon reasonable written request, subject to confidentiality agreements
Grantee must maintain existence and remain in good standing
Grantee must indemnify TEDCO and the Maryland Stem Cell Research Fund from claims and expenses arising from the project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the MSCRF website at https://www.mscrf.org/funding-opportunities. The application must include a detailed project description, project budget, and the identity of the Principal Investigator. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and scientific merit. Upon approval, a grant agreement is executed specifying the grant amount, project scope, completion date, and all terms and conditions. Before disbursement of any grant proceeds, the grantee must provide evidence of IRB approval (or exemption determination) and any required IACUC approval. Grant funds are then disbursed according to the payment schedule outlined in the grant agreement, contingent upon continued compliance with all grant terms and satisfactory performance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded program administered by UMBC and supported by the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) that helps Maryland retain top technology talent by increasing the number of paid technical internships offered across the state. The program provides financial assistance to technology-based businesses and state and local agencies to hire more paid technical interns, supporting workforce development and keeping skilled graduates in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers financial assistance to technology-based businesses, state agencies, and local agencies to support the hiring of more paid technical interns, helping offset the cost of internship compensation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Technology-based businesses, state agencies, and local agencies in Maryland seeking to hire paid technical interns.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding to support the hiring of paid technical interns at technology-based businesses and state and local agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
requirements_list: Must be a technology-based business, state agency, or local agency
Must be seeking to hire paid technical interns
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the MTIP website at https://mtip.umbc.edu/ for application instructions and links to career centers for individual institutions. Alternatively, contact Jen Spencer Heilman, Program Director of Workforce Initiatives with the Maryland Technology Internship Program, for more information on opportunities and application.

structured_extraction.program_description: Connects Maryland business owners with the state's top entrepreneurs and experts to provide guidance and support for business growth.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland business owners and entrepreneurs

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Open Institute for Black Women Entrepreneur Excellence (Howard County Pilot Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: A 10-month hybrid leadership development program for Black women entrepreneurs in Howard County that builds critical skills to foster resilience and creates a community of peer advisors. The program combines in-person and virtual sessions held monthly at the Maryland Innovation Center in Columbia, Maryland, covering leadership, communication, real-world perspectives, and business development planning.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants pay a $250 registration fee to cover assessments in the prerequisite session. Upon program completion, $200 of the fee is refunded. The program consists of 10 months of hybrid in-person and virtual training sessions covering leadership, communication, real-world business perspectives, and development planning. Entrepreneurs outside Howard County may be considered based on available slots.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Black women entrepreneurs who are founders, co-founders, or CEOs of businesses at pre-seed to growth stage (maximum pre-series A) based in Howard County, though applicants from outside Howard County may be considered based on available slots
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program participation provides training in leadership, communication, real-world business perspectives, and strategic business development planning through a 10-month structured curriculum
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is designed for Howard County-based business owners, though entrepreneurs located outside of Howard County will be considered based on available slots. In-person sessions are held at the Maryland Innovation Center in Columbia, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a founder, co-founder, or CEO
Company must be at minimum pre-seed to growth stage
Company must be at maximum pre-series A stage
Participant can miss no more than two sessions to graduate from the course
Participant must pay $250 registration fee (with $200 refund upon completion)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply to the program. Upon acceptance, participants pay a $250 registration fee and attend the 10-month hybrid program consisting of monthly in-person and virtual sessions. Sessions begin at 4:30pm and include prerequisite preparation, introductory sessions, leadership and communication workshops, real-world perspectives, and business development planning.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's pitch program that allows startups to present their company and business idea to receive constructive feedback and guidance from experienced business professionals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Startups present their pitch and receive feedback from seasoned professionals to help refine their business concept and strategy.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Startups seeking feedback on their business concept and pitch
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable - this is a technical assistance program

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that assists start-up and small technology-based businesses in rural areas of Maryland with mentoring, technical assistance, and business consulting at no cost to help companies advance to the next level of success.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Regional mentors provide professional ongoing mentoring, consulting services, and technical management assistance at no cost. Assistance includes business model and strategy development, market and competitive analysis, funding opportunities and introductions, financial analysis, business plan or grant review, intellectual property guidance, prototype development, and manufacturing problem solving. Companies that receive mentoring services for at least 90 days are eligible to apply for up to $25,000 in pre-seed funding.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Regional mentors: Justin Ferguson (Southern Region), Karen Zuccardi (Frederick County), Graham Dodge (Carroll and Northern Baltimore Counties), Ardon Hall (Allegany County), Sarah Myers (Garrett County), Jeremy Perando (Garrett County), Laurie Brewer (Washington County), Samuel Shoge (Upper Shore Region), Bill Bernard (Lower Shore Region)
structured_extraction.contact_email: jferguson@tedcomd.com, kzuccardi@tedcomd.com, gdodge@tedcomd.com, mathmassness@gmail.com, sarah@dcabfun.com, jperando@xologies.com, lauriebrewer@glowupconsult.com, sshoge@tedcomd.com, bbernard@tedcomd.com
structured_extraction.program_audience: Start-up and small technology-based businesses in rural Maryland with fewer than 16 employees and annual revenues of $1 million or less.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical and business assistance for new technology development or utilizing technology to create new or expand existing business. Pre-seed funding can be used for business advancement and growth.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rural Maryland as defined by the Rural Maryland Council, including Allegany, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties.
requirements_list: Must be involved in developing new technologies or products or utilizing technology to create or expand business
Must have fewer than 16 employees
Annual revenues $1 million or less
Must be in good standing with Maryland Department of Taxation & Assessments
For pre-seed funding: must have received mentoring services for at least 90 days

Companies receiving mentoring for at least 90 days can apply for pre-seed funding. Applicants should familiarize themselves with TEDCO investment legislation regulations before applying.
