structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive program that provides matching funds to small businesses that have received federal Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) or Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) awards. The program aims to strengthen SBIR/STTR awards, promote commercialization of research by small businesses, facilitate technology transfer from universities and federal labs, and encourage small businesses—including economically disadvantaged ones—to pursue federal SBIR/STTR funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For Phase I SBIR/STTR awards, TEDCO grants an award equal to the lesser of 25% of the Phase I award or $25,000. For Phase II SBIR/STTR awards, TEDCO grants an award equal to the lesser of 25% of the Phase II award or $75,000. The full amount of awarded funds is provided through ACH transfer upon successful completion of the closing process and execution of a non-negotiable grant agreement. TEDCO plans to issue awards on a quarterly basis, anticipating 4-6 Phase I Matching awards and 2-3 Phase II Matching awards each quarter, subject to funding availability.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Quarterly deadlines: March 30 (5:00 pm ET), June 30 (5:00 pm ET), September 30 (5:00 pm ET), December 31 (5:00 pm ET). If a deadline falls on a weekend or Maryland State holiday, the deadline is the first non-holiday weekday following the specified date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, including economically disadvantaged small businesses, that have received SBIR or STTR awards from the federal government. Maryland-based companies with less than 250 employees that have received or will receive federal SBIR/STTR awards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Matching funds to complement federal SBIR/STTR awards; to support commercialization of research, technology transfer, and economic development in Maryland. Funds may be used for technical tasks, equipment purchase, marketing activities, hiring, IP protection, and other business operations in Maryland.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based companies. Over half of the applicant's workforce must work at and from a physical location in Maryland. The applicant's principal business operations must be conducted from a physical location in Maryland. Award recipients must agree to use funds primarily to support business operations in Maryland or, in the case of start-up businesses, to establish and support business operations in Maryland.
requirements_list: Company must have received an SBIR or STTR award within six months immediately preceding the date of submission of a Program application to TEDCO (award date determined by Notice of Award from government agency)
Company must have more than half of its workforce working at and from a physical location in Maryland
Company must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Company's principal business operations must be conducted from a physical location in Maryland
Company must employ fewer than 250 employees
Company must not be primarily engaged in retail sales, real estate development, insurance, banking, lending, or provision of professional services by accountants, attorneys, or physicians
Company must not have received a prior award under the Program in the current fiscal year
Company must have received fewer than 3 awards under the Program in total
Company must be a technology or life sciences company
Company must be primarily US-owned

Applicant must agree to execute a securities repurchase agreement or equivalent commitment requiring return of award funds with accrued interest and fees if the company does not maintain Qualified Business status for at least 2 years after receiving a Program award
Applicant must agree to return the award if the applicant fails to fulfill the eligibility and maintenance requirements of the Program
Applications must be submitted online through TEDCO's application portal at https://www.tedcomd.com/sbirsttr-matching-funds
Applications received by other means (email, mail) or after the Application Cycle Deadline will not be considered
Applicants must submit a screenshot of Maryland Good Standing certificate
Applicants must submit winning SBIR/STTR proposal, SBIR/STTR award letter, and Use of Matching Funds Justification document (max 2 pages, 11-point font, 1-inch margins, PDF format recommended)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted during four quarterly cycles per year: January 1 - March 30, April 1 - June 30, July 1 - September 30, and October 1 - December 31 (5:00 pm ET deadlines). All applications must be submitted online through TEDCO's application portal. First-time applicants must complete TEDCO registration and obtain a TEDCO ID, which involves submitting general company details, business addresses, company overview, and demographic data. The application includes three components: (1) General Applicant Information (company details, basic qualifications, ownership/demographics, intellectual property, employment data, funding history); (2) Proposal and Award Information (copy of winning SBIR/STTR proposal and award letter); and (3) Use of Matching Funds Justification (2-page document explaining use of funds strategy and potential impacts including technology description, commercialization/technology transfer promotion, public health relevance, job creation potential, economic impact, rural/distressed area impact, and community representation). Applicants receive automated email confirmation upon submission. The review process consists of four stages: (1) Compliance Review to verify eligibility requirements (45 days); (2) Detailed Review where TEDCO staff score applications on general criteria and make recommendations; (3) Due Diligence Process including site visits, presentations, interviews, and validation of claims; and (4) Final Decision by TEDCO's CEO based on application, reviewer scores, diversity criteria, likelihood of job creation and economic development, and available funding. Applicants may be required to attend an in-person interview at TEDCO's Columbia Office (10960 Grantchester Way, Suite 120, Columbia, MD 21046). Upon approval, applicants have up to 30 days to execute the non-negotiable grant agreement. Full award funds are transferred via ACH upon closing. Awardees must submit economic impact reports annually for 5 years following the award, including information about revenues, employees, follow-on funding, and similar economic impact data.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive training program administered by TEDCO that selects up to 25 Maryland life science and technology businesses to receive expert guidance on developing competitive Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) proposals to win federal grants and contracts. The program provides expert guidance in proposal writing, business planning, commercialization, and pitch development to help companies secure up to $305,000 in non-dilutive Phase I funding. Graduates have collectively received over $29 million in SBIR and STTR Phase I and II funding from agencies including NSF, NIH, NASA, the Air Force, and USDA.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers two parts for up to 25 selected companies. Part I focuses on foundational skills in business planning, commercialization, and pitch writing through 2 live workshops and hands-on learning opportunities including pitch development, business model advice, and access to collaborative SharePoint portals. Part II provides 6 additional workshops for companies with approved NSF pitches, focusing on proposal quality enhancement and submission readiness. Participants receive comprehensive training materials, guidance on federal registration requirements (SAM.gov and Research.gov), access to market research tools, and expert feedback on proposals. Successful companies can access up to $305,000 in Phase I non-dilutive federal funding for research and development of innovative technologies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses and Maryland companies in life science and technology sectors seeking Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) funding, across all 24 counties and Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides training and guidance to help businesses prepare proposals for federal SBIR/STTR grants and contracts. The program itself does not directly provide funding, but successful companies can access up to $305,000 in Phase I non-dilutive funding for research and development of innovative technologies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland's 24 counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be a small business in life science or technology sector
Must have a compelling innovation to commercialize
Must register with SAM.gov and Research.gov federal databases
Must apply and be selected as one of up to 25 participants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested businesses apply through the TEDCO online application form to be selected as one of up to 25 participants. Selected participants join a cohort-based program starting with Part I workshops on business planning, commercialization, and pitch writing. Top performers advance to Part II with additional specialized proposal-writing workshops. Participants receive comprehensive training materials, federal registration support, market research tools, and expert feedback on their proposals throughout the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The SBIR/STTR Technical Assistance program helps Maryland technology and life sciences companies build expertise needed to access federal Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) funding. The program provides workshops, training sessions, and individual proposal reviews to help small businesses navigate SBIR/STTR program requirements, understand available resources, and develop strong proposals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a two-part approach: Part 1 includes workshops covering federal SBIR/STTR program overviews, agency-specific processes (DoD, NIH, DoE), and practical training on identifying the right topics, writing technical proposals, preparing commercialization plans, and developing budgets. Part 2 provides two rounds of individual proposal reviews by technical and business experts to enhance proposal quality. The program also includes guest presentations from industry experts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland small businesses with limited experience securing federal SBIR/STTR investments who have not previously been awarded SBIR/STTR funding
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide direct funding; it provides training and technical assistance to help businesses access federal SBIR/STTR funding from agencies including the Department of Defense, National Institutes of Health, and Department of Energy.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland small businesses
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland small business
Must not have previously been awarded an SBIR/STTR grant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the online application portal (Apply Now link provided). TEDCO will work with participants to schedule individual proposal reviews.

structured_extraction.program_name: Social Impact Funds (Pre-Seed Builder and Inclusion)
structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's Social Impact Funds comprise two equity investment programs — the Pre-Seed Builder Fund and the Inclusion Fund — designed to support technology startups from all industries that are founded or owned by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals. The Pre-Seed Builder Fund targets pre-seed stage startups where at least 50% of founders demonstrate economic disadvantage, providing initial investments typically of $100,000 via convertible notes with capacity up to $750,000. The Inclusion Fund addresses the gap between pre-seed and seed financing for early-stage technology startups that are often overlooked by traditional financing sources, requiring at least 30% ownership by individuals who have demonstrated social and economic disadvantage. Both funds provide not only capital but also hands-on executive support, peer-to-peer mentorship, and networking opportunities to help companies reach sustainability, create jobs in Maryland, and attract follow-on financing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Pre-Seed Builder Fund typically invests initial amounts of $100,000 via convertible notes or equity, with capacity to invest up to $750,000 on a single deployment. The Inclusion Fund also invests up to $750,000 per deployment in early-stage technology startups via convertible notes or equity. Both funds may require a minimum 1:1 private capital match for some investments (seed stage investments range from $200,000 to $500,000). All funded companies receive hands-on and educational executive support, peer-to-peer mentorship and collaboration, and networking opportunities. Investment decisions are made at TEDCO's discretion based on evaluation of the company's merits and various investment criteria. Companies that do not receive funding may reapply no sooner than 6 months after the initial application if significant commercial progress is made.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-seed and early-stage technology startups from all industries based in Maryland, with at least one full-time employee and more than half the workforce based in Maryland. The Pre-Seed Builder Fund requires at least 50% of founders to demonstrate economic disadvantage; the Inclusion Fund requires at least 30% ownership by individuals who have demonstrated social and economic disadvantage. Companies must have less than 251 employees and equity raised to date less than $15,000,000.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General business growth and development, including reaching sustainability, creating jobs in Maryland, and becoming attractive candidates for follow-on financing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Principal place of business must be in Maryland. More than half of the workforce must be based in Maryland. Companies must commit to Maryland through a five-year claw-back agreement.

At least one full-time employee

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are assessed on an ongoing basis and must be submitted online through TEDCO's Social Impact Funds application portal at tedcomd.com. After submission, applicants should email investments@tedcomd.com to confirm receipt. Applications received through other means such as email or mail will not be considered. If a company does not receive funding, they are encouraged to reapply no sooner than 6 months after the initial application if significant commercial progress is made. Upon approval, TEDCO commences additional due diligence and applicants' legal representatives work with TEDCO's lawyers to draft investment documents and confirm eligibility information.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's evergreen venture capital funds invest in and support early-stage technology-based businesses in Maryland, from pre-seed to pre-venture capital funding stages. The program provides equity investments to help entrepreneurs launch and grow their companies. Additionally, TEDCO operates a Limited Partnership program designed to fund early-stage venture capital funds focused on investing in Maryland, structured to meet SSBCI guidelines.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Equity investments of $500,000 to $1,500,000 per deal (with potential for up to $2,000,000), provided as convertible notes or equity. A minimum 1:1 private capital match is required. TEDCO aims to be a meaningful participant in or catalyst to rounds and typically invests as the first institutional investor or in the first institutional round, with preference to follow-on in early-stage rounds. Additionally, TEDCO offers limited partnership equity investments in early-stage venture capital funds with standard limited partnership terms and fees structured to meet SSBCI guidelines. Fund managers have significant operating and venture experience and work to make entrepreneurs successful.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - applications reviewed on a continuous basis (rolling basis)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Katherine Hill Ritchie, Senior Director, Venture Funds

Maryland-based companies with more than half the workforce working from a physical location in Maryland, headquarters in Maryland, fewer than 251 employees, and equity raised to date less than $30,000,000 (excluding TEDCO and grant funding). Also open to early-stage venture capital funds focused on investing in Maryland. The fund considers deals outside the region and may refer them to other co-investors.

TEDCO also invests in the larger regional tech community and considers companies outside Maryland if sufficiently compelling. Maryland focus is required for Limited Partnership investments.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit their application online through TEDCO's application portal at https://tedco.tfaforms.net/f/vftedcoapplication. structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's Seed Investment Funds are designed to assist seed-stage businesses showing promise of becoming venture fundable companies or that can achieve sustainability through customer revenue, follow-on funding, or other forms of corporate venture. The program supports early-stage entrepreneurs building exceptional companies in Maryland across technology sectors including cybersecurity/information technology, life sciences, and general technology commercialization. The program is supported in part by Maryland's State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) funding, which helps expand investment capacity. Four fund types are available: Cybersecurity Investment Fund, Life Sciences Investment Fund, Technology Commercialization Fund, and Gap Investment Fund.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: TEDCO makes seed-stage equity investments through convertible debt and equity instruments with check sizes ranging from $100,000 to $500,000. Four fund types are available with specific requirements: (1) Cybersecurity Investment Fund - invests in cybersecurity and information technology companies; (2) Life Sciences Investment Fund - invests in companies with an FDA pathway; (3) Technology Commercialization Fund - invests broadly in early-stage technology companies (100% deployed for FY25); (4) Gap Investment Fund - invests broadly in early-stage technology companies and requires dollar-for-dollar matching funds from non-governmental sources with proceeds used for new hires in Maryland. A minimum 1:1 private capital match is required for the Gap Fund. For Technology Commercialization, Cybersecurity, and Life Sciences Funds, companies must not have raised more than $2,500,000 in dilutive funding. For the Gap Fund, the limit is $5,000,000 in dilutive funding. The program is supported in part by Maryland's SSBCI funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - applications assessed on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage seed-stage technology entrepreneurs and companies in Maryland, including those in cybersecurity, life sciences, and tech commercialization. Applicants welcome from all industries but must be technology-based companies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Seed stage investing for company development and growth toward venture funding or revenue sustainability, covering cybersecurity/information technology, life sciences, general tech commercialization, and gap funding. Gap Fund proceeds must be used for new hires in Maryland.

Principal place of business and headquarters must be in Maryland. Companies must be committed to Maryland and willing to sign a five-year claw-back agreement.

Technology Commercialization Fund: No more than 15 employees, has not raised more than $2,500,000 in dilutive funding
Cybersecurity Investment Fund: No more than 15 employees, has not raised more than $2,500,000 in dilutive funding, focused on information technology and network security
Life Sciences Investment Fund: No more than 15 employees, has not raised more than $2,500,000 in dilutive funding, companies in process of developing FDA-approved products for human health

Gap Investment Fund: No more than 30 employees, has not raised more than $5,000,000 in dilutive funding, requires dollar-for-dollar match from non-governmental sources, proceeds must be used for new Maryland hires
Cannot invest in sole proprietorships, retail sales, real estate development, insurance/banking/lending, or professional accounting/law/medical services
TEDCO cannot invest if business no longer meets Maryland-based business requirements (except in rare circumstances where substantial economic impact is demonstrated)
Applications must be submitted online through TEDCO's application portal
Applicants should familiarize themselves with TEDCO investment regulations (TEDCO Statute, InvestMaryland Program Statute, and COMAR)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application online through the Seed Funds application portal at tedcomd.com/seed-funds. Applications are assessed on a rolling basis. After submission, applicants may email seed@tedcomd.com to confirm receipt. Applications received through other means such as email or mail will not be considered. If TEDCO determines the company is eligible but chooses not to invest, the company is encouraged to reapply no sooner than 6 months after the initial application if significant commercial progress is made. Meeting basic requirements does not guarantee funding; TEDCO's investment team will evaluate the merits of the investment based on various criteria. If approved for investment, TEDCO commences additional diligence and applicants' lawyers will work with TEDCO's lawyers (from the Office of the Attorney General) to draft investment documents and confirm eligibility information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows federal agencies to provide funding to Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) Phase I and Phase II awardees to enhance their project's commercialization potential. The program focuses on overcoming technical challenges, optimizing commercialization strategies, and minimizing risks associated with bringing innovative products or processes to market. TEDCO experts assist Maryland-based small businesses with technology assessment, market analysis, business model development, commercial road mapping, investment readiness, and IP and regulatory affairs support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Phase I offers up to $6,500 per award, which may be in addition to the award amount depending on the federal agency. Phase II provides up to $50,000 per project, with the funding approach varying by agency—either as part of the award budget or in addition to it. Funding can be used to help with business strategy, operations, product sales, IP protection, market research, market validation, regulatory planning, and manufacturing plans. TEDCO experts assist with technology assessment, market analysis and strategy, business model development, commercial road mapping, investment readiness assessment, and IP and regulatory affairs support.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland companies that are SBIR/STTR Phase I and Phase II awardees from federal agencies, with fewer than 250 employees, CEO and 50% of the company located in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical and business assistance including technology assessment, market analysis and strategy, business model development, commercial road mapping, investment readiness assessment, IP and regulatory affairs support, overcoming technical challenges, solving technical problems during projects, minimizing technical risks, and commercializing SBIR/STTR products or processes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland company with fewer than 250 employees with CEO and 50% of the company located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Maryland company with fewer than 250 employees
CEO and 50% of the company are in Maryland
Company must be a recipient of SBIR/STTR Phase I or Phase II funding from a federal agency
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested parties should apply early in the SBIR/STTR funding cycle through the online form. TEDCO performs an initial assessment and schedules conversations to identify specific technical and business needs. TEDCO works with the applicant and an expert to develop a Statement of Work (SOW) that outlines specific TABA support services. Monthly check-ins monitor progress and address emerging needs. A comprehensive evaluation is conducted at the conclusion of the support period.

structured_extraction.program_description: TEDCO's program that assists small technology-based startups located in urban Maryland areas through mentoring, guidance, and targeted projects designed to help them grow and succeed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides mentoring and targeted project support to help small technology-based startups in urban areas develop and expand.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small technology-based startups in urban Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business development, mentoring, and targeted growth projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Urban areas of Maryland
requirements_list: Located in urban Maryland
Technology-based business

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland ABLE accounts provide a way to help individuals with disabilities save money and pay for qualified disability-related expenses without jeopardizing state or federal means-tested benefits such as SSI or Medicaid.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: ABLE accounts allow individuals with disabilities to save money and pay for qualified disability-related expenses without affecting state or federal means-tested benefits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified disability-related expenses
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Individual must have a disability

structured_extraction.program_name: ALERT / Alcohol Law Education Regulatory Training
structured_extraction.program_description: ALERT is designed to educate Montgomery County servers, sellers, managers and owners of alcohol beverage establishments in alcohol beverage regulatory compliance. Participants learn how to develop responsible alcohol policies, review issues identified by County and State enforcement agencies, and have an opportunity to meet and network with peers and county officials. Training is available in English and Spanish, with PowerPoint presentations available in multiple languages including Amharic, Chinese, French, Korean, and Vietnamese.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training held from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM on the 2nd and 4th Monday of every month (except holidays). No cost to attend. Registration is required in advance as space is limited. Training covers alcohol beverage regulatory compliance, responsible alcohol policies, enforcement issues, alcohol's effects on the body, responsible beverage service, Maryland alcohol rules and regulations, inspections, underage alcohol use and ID verification, and Board of License Commissioners hearing procedures. Presentations are available in multiple languages including English, Spanish, Amharic, Chinese, French, Korean, and Vietnamese. Attendees receive a letter of attendance upon completion, provided they join by 10:15 AM and remain through the training session.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - sessions held monthly on 2nd and 4th Monday
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County servers, sellers, managers, and owners of alcohol beverage establishments
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational training in alcohol beverage regulatory compliance, responsible alcohol policies, enforcement issues identified by County and State enforcement agencies, alcohol's physiological effects, responsible service techniques, Maryland alcohol law, inspection procedures, underage drinking prevention, ID verification methods, and Board of License Commissioners hearing procedures
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a server, seller, manager, or owner of an alcohol beverage establishment in Montgomery County
Must register online in advance as space is limited
Attendees must join the meeting by 10:15 AM or will not be admitted and will not receive a letter of attendance
Attendees should sign in 10 minutes early to allow time for technical troubleshooting

Training covers 8 parts: ALERT purpose and agency overview, alcohol's effects on the body, responsible beverage service, Maryland alcohol rules and regulations, inspections, underage alcohol use and IDs, course evaluation, and Board of License Commissioners hearing procedures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register online through the provided Zoom registration links (available in English and Spanish). Space is limited so early registration is encouraged. Attendees should sign in at least 10 minutes before the scheduled 10:00 AM start time. Training is held entirely online via Zoom. A letter of attendance is issued to those who join by 10:15 AM and remain through completion of the training. Registration links are provided for each monthly session on the 2nd and 4th Monday.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans provided to minority- and women-owned small businesses to support growth and development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Minority- and women-owned small businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business growth and operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be minority- or women-owned

structured_extraction.program_description: Property owners or lessees in Montgomery County Parking Lot Districts can apply for an exemption from paying an annual property-value-based (Ad Valorem) tax if they meet minimum parking space requirements defined in County zoning code. The exemption allows property owners to avoid the tax that would otherwise fund the public parking lot district program.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners or lessees who provide the minimum number of parking spaces required by Article 59-6 of the County Zoning Code can apply for exemption from paying the annual Ad Valorem tax assessed on their property value within a Parking Lot District. The exemption eliminates the obligation to pay the annual property-value-based tax that funds the public parking lot district program. Alternatively, property owners in a Parking Lot District may provide fewer parking spaces than required after making other adjustments and make payment under Chapter 60 instead of seeking a full exemption.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and lessees in Montgomery County Parking Lot Districts (Bethesda, Silver Spring, Wheaton, and Montgomery Hills) who meet or can meet minimum parking space requirements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exemption from annual Ad Valorem tax payment on property value within designated Parking Lot Districts
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in the four Montgomery County Parking Lot Districts: Bethesda, Silver Spring, Wheaton, and Montgomery Hills. Silver Spring District covers area in the Thirteenth Election District; Bethesda District covers area in the Seventh Election District; Wheaton and Montgomery Hills Districts have specific geographic boundaries defined in Chapter 60 of Montgomery County Code.
requirements_list: Property must be located within one of the four designated Parking Lot Districts: Bethesda, Silver Spring, Wheaton, or Montgomery Hills
Property owner or lessee must provide the minimum number of parking spaces as defined in Article 59-6 of the County Zoning Code (based on property use and square footage)
Application must be submitted on or before April 1 each year

All required supplemental documents must be submitted with a fully executed application to qualify for review, including: completed cover sheet, application form, list of all tenants located on property with square footage, site plan of complete property, and detailed plans of all parking spaces
Property owner or lessee must certify that information provided in application is true and accurate
If application is rejected, it may not be resubmitted until the following fiscal year application deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners or lessees must submit a completed exemption application package to the Department of Transportation, Division of Parking Management by April 1 each year. The application package must include: (1) completed cover sheet with property name, account number, main point of contact information, and preferred communication method; (2) fully completed Application for Exemption from Parking Lot District Tax form with property details, owner information, parking space information, property usage information, and certification; (3) list of all tenants located on the property including square footage of each (Exhibit A if applicable); (4) site plan of complete property; and (5) detailed plans of all parking spaces. Applications should be submitted to: Department of Transportation, Division of Parking Management, Management Services & Property Development, 100 Edison Park Drive, 4th Floor, Gaithersburg, Maryland 20878. Applications may be submitted by mail (Attn: Jeremy Souders), fax (240-777-8730), or email (Jeremy.souders@montgomerycountymd.gov). All required supplemental documents must accompany the application or it will be rejected in its entirety and application materials will not be returned to the petitioner.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Affordable Housing Opportunity Fund (AHOF) provides short-term financing to developers to acquire properties at risk of losing affordability. Administered by the National Housing Trust Community Development Fund (NHTCDF) in partnership with Montgomery County DHCA, the fund offers three-year loans to help developers bid competitively to maintain affordability and preserve housing for current renters at affordable rents. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as initial loans are repaid and the fund is replenished.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides short-term, three-year loans from a dedicated pool of $14 million in revolving County funds, matched at least 3:1 with private lending. The AHOF offers advantageous terms, standardized processing and pricing to support competing on cost of capital and timely execution. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as initial loans are repaid and the fund is replenished. The National Housing Trust Community Development Fund (NHTCDF) coordinates applications from developers and arranges private capital to combine with Montgomery County funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Affordable housing developers (for-profit and non-profit) seeking to acquire properties at risk of losing affordability in order to preserve housing and protect tenants from displacement in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition of properties at risk of loss of affordability to preserve housing and maintain tenant occupancy at affordable rents. Funds provide sufficient time to position the property for longer-term affordability financing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Developer must have plans for refinancing that will ensure long-term affordability and repay the AHOF funding
Property must be at risk of loss of affordability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Developers access the Term Sheet, FAQ, and application process information on the NHTCDF webpage. 2) Applications are submitted to NHTCDF (National Housing Trust Community Development Fund), which manages the AHOF. 3) NHTCDF underwriter reviews the application and provides a recommendation to DHCA. 4) DHCA Director reviews the recommendation and determines whether to accept, modify, request additional information, or reject. 5) Final approval is evidenced by a conditional commitment letter detailing terms and conditions. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis as initial loans are repaid and the fund is replenished.

structured_extraction.program_description: A matching grant and cost-share program created through a partnership between Montgomery County Office of Agriculture (OAG) and Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) that provides reimbursement assistance to farmers and agricultural entrepreneurs for business projects essential to the improvement or expansion of agricultural enterprises. Eligible projects include deer fencing, agricultural wells, vertical racks for microgreens, farm equipment and tools, hydroponics equipment, aquaponics equipment, refrigeration, irrigation pond repair, greenhouses, composting equipment, cultivation equipment, irrigation systems, and other farm mechanization or infrastructure. The program supports both new and existing agricultural enterprises including table crop farmers, vineyards, commodity farmers, vertical farmers, horticulture businesses, and other non-traditional types of agriculture.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides matching grant cost-share assistance through MARBIDCO and ACRE. MARBIDCO and OAG each contribute up to half of the total project cost, not to exceed $6,000 combined ($3,000 per agency). For projects totaling more than $20,000, an additional $1,000 in ACRE funding may be available. The farmer/agricultural business owner must invest at least half of the total project cost. Maximum lifetime assistance per agricultural operation is $15,000 (MARBIDCO funding). Agricultural enterprises may apply up to twice per fiscal year for different projects. Funding is a reimbursement program requiring original receipts and proof of full payment before reimbursement is issued. Total County funding available per fiscal year is $25,000 for all Montgomery County projects combined.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified Montgomery County-based agricultural entrepreneurs and farmers seeking to improve, expand, and increase the profitability of their agricultural enterprises through capital improvements, infrastructure projects, and equipment purchases. Both new and existing agricultural enterprises are eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Agricultural business infrastructure projects and equipment purchases including but not limited to deer fencing, agricultural wells, vertical racks for microgreens, farm equipment and tools, hydroponics equipment, aquaponics equipment, refrigeration, irrigation pond repair, greenhouses, composting equipment, cultivation equipment, irrigation systems, and other farm infrastructure and mechanization that will enable future revenue and/or employment growth of the enterprise.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Applicant must be headquartered in Montgomery County. Eligibility also depends on property characteristics such as restrictive covenants, easements, size, assessment, and regulatory suitability/compliance of the property.
requirements_list: Applicant must be registered as a business and in good standing with the MD Department of Assessment and Taxation
Applicant must be headquartered in Montgomery County
For sole proprietors not registered with the State of Maryland, must provide a copy of their Schedule F (Form 1040) as proof of operating a legitimate agricultural business
Applicant must apply and receive approval from both OAG and MARBIDCO before making any purchases or beginning any phase of the project
Business owner must invest at least half of the total project cost

Project must enhance the overall agricultural economy by contributing to startup or expansion of an agricultural enterprise in Montgomery County, or be associated with infrastructure improvement or equipment purchase that will enable future revenue and/or employment growth
Property must meet program requirements including consideration of restrictive covenants, easements, size, and assessment
Lifetime maximum of $15,000 per agricultural operation (MARBIDCO funding)
Maximum of $3,000 per project from ACRE (up to $1,000 additional available for projects totaling more than $20,000)
Applicant must provide original receipts and proof of full payment upon project completion
Agricultural enterprise may apply up to twice per fiscal year for different projects
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Interested agricultural enterprises submit a completed application to the Montgomery County Office of Agriculture with the following information: applicant contact information, project description, project type, total project cost, estimated employment data related to the project, and a formal written estimate of the total project cost. Step 2: The Office of Agriculture reviews the application and has sole discretion to accept or deny the application based on property characteristics (restrictive covenants/easements, property size, assessment, regulatory suitability/compliance), potential for agricultural economic development, and program intent. If the project appears to fit within MARBIDCO's economic development profile and criteria, OAG submits the application with a cover letter to MARBIDCO for consideration. Step 3: If approved by the MARBIDCO Review Committee, the applicant is notified and may begin the project. OAG and MARBIDCO enter into an agreement to provide cost-shared grant funding. Step 4: Upon project completion, the applicant notifies OAG and provides paid receipts showing the total project cost has been paid in full. The agreed-upon grant amount is reimbursed to the applicant. Project data reporting may be required.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Research and development, innovation, and technology commercialization.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Annual Sidewalk Program provides for the installation of multiple minor sidewalk projects each year that fill missing links in existing sidewalk networks. Part of Montgomery County's ongoing Pedestrian Safety Program, it aims to provide safer access for people with disabilities and improve pedestrian access to schools and nearby public transportation or public facilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program installs sidewalks and ADA-compliant pedestrian infrastructure. Projects originate from resident and association requests, which undergo rigorous field investigation to determine feasibility. Requested locations are prioritized based on criteria to ensure fair and equitable project selection across all residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents and associations seeking sidewalk installation or ADA improvements
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of sidewalks and ADA-compliant pedestrian infrastructure to fill missing links in existing sidewalk networks, provide safer access for people with disabilities, and improve pedestrian access to schools and public transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents and associations submit requests for sidewalk and ADA installation. Each request undergoes a rigorous field investigation to determine feasibility. Requested locations are prioritized to ensure fair and equitable project selection.

structured_extraction.program_name: Arts and Entertainment District Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit for owners of manufacturing, commercial, or industrial buildings located in Arts and Entertainment Districts in Montgomery County that are wholly or partially renovated for use by a qualifying resident artist or arts and entertainment enterprise. The credit applies for 10 years and is based on growth in property assessments after renovation, providing meaningful tax relief to incentivize building renovation and arts-focused economic development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A real property tax credit based on growth in property assessments for renovated buildings in Arts and Entertainment Districts. The base-year assessment is the assessment before renovation. For properties not in Enterprise Zones, the credit is: Years 1-5 (80% of assessment increase), Year 6 (70%), Year 7 (60%), Year 8 (50%), Year 9 (40%), Year 10 (30%), then expires. For properties also in Enterprise Zones, an additional 20% is added to the Enterprise Zone credit. The credit runs for a total of 10 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners renovating manufacturing, commercial, or industrial buildings in Arts and Entertainment Districts in Montgomery County for use by qualifying resident artists or arts and entertainment enterprises.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces property tax liability for renovated buildings used by qualifying resident artists or arts and entertainment enterprises.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Arts and Entertainment Districts in Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Building must be a manufacturing, commercial, or industrial property
Building must be located in an Arts and Entertainment District
Building must be wholly or partially renovated for use by a qualifying resident artist or arts and entertainment enterprise
Must continue qualifying use throughout the 10-year credit period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Department of Finance at (240) 777-8931 to apply.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prenatal care coordination, education, screening, transportation, and provision of supplies and equipment for pregnant women and newborns including portable cribs, diapers, car seats, and other incentives.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for qualified brownfield sites that undergo voluntary cleanup or corrective action plans. The credit covers increased property tax liability resulting from assessment increases after cleanup. Additional credit is available for sites in Enterprise Zones or Neighborhood Business Development areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit equal to 50 percent of increased property tax liability for 5 years following revaluation after cleanup. An additional 20 percent credit is available if the site is in an Enterprise Zone or a County-designated neighborhood in the Neighborhood Business Development Program. Credit is forfeited if the recipient withdraws from the voluntary cleanup program or the Maryland Department of Environment withdraws approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners of qualified brownfield sites undergoing voluntary cleanup or corrective action
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces property tax liability for brownfield sites
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Qualified brownfield site
Completion of voluntary cleanup or corrective action plan approved by Maryland Department of Environment
Continued participation in voluntary cleanup program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Department of Finance; credit is applied based on Maryland Department of Environment approvals

structured_extraction.program_description: A farmland preservation initiative that permanently extinguishes residential development rights, including associated septic capacity, to protect Montgomery County's Agricultural Reserve and reduce land fragmentation.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides financial compensation for permanently extinguishing residential development rights through easement placement on the property. The County calculates offers using the BLT Valuation Formula, which includes a Base Value (minimum price set annually by the County Executive), Added Value (based on property characteristics), and a Maximum Value (highest price allowed by the County). Offers cannot exceed the Maximum Value established by the County Executive. Funding is limited and subject to annual budget allocations. If funds are insufficient, some eligible applications may not be accepted during a purchase period. Property owners receive permanent protection of their agricultural land from future residential, commercial, and industrial development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with property in the Agricultural Reserve (AR Zone) in Montgomery County who wish to preserve farmland and prevent residential development. Applicants can be individuals, businesses, LLCs, trusts, or other legal entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide funding for farm operations; rather, it provides financial compensation for permanently extinguishing residential development rights on the property through an easement. Landowners receive payment based on the BLT Valuation Formula.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Property must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR Zone) in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be in the Agricultural Reserve (AR Zone)
Minimum 50 acres, or smaller if contiguous to protected land
At least 50% of land must be USDA Soil Classes I, II, or III
Must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
Must have sewage disposal area(s) approved on a final well and septic plan
Must obtain a Well and Septic Approval Letter from the Department of Permitting Services (DPS)
Applications must include the Well and Septic Approval Letter before they are reviewed
The total number of approved septic areas and the number of approved septic areas to terminate must be clearly identified
Properties with existing TDR easements must disclose how many TDRs remain
Participation is voluntary and acceptance is not guaranteed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Request a Well and Septic Approval Letter from the Department of Permitting Services (DPS) by emailing Heidi.Benham@montgomerycountymd.gov. 2. Complete the official BLT Easement Application Form with all required documentation, including the updated Well & Septic Approval Letter. 3. Submit the completed application packet by February 13, 2026 via email to Mike Weyand at Michael.Weyand@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov. 4. The Office of Agriculture reviews applications for completeness and eligibility (February-March). 5. Eligible applications are forwarded to the Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board (APAB) for ranking based on objective criteria (size, soil quality, land tenure) and additional factors aligned with program goals (March-April). 6. The County determines available funding and prioritizes ranked applications (May-July). 7. Formal offers are made to selected landowners (May-July). 8. Title searches and legal documentation are completed, easements are recorded in land records, and payments are issued to landowners (August-November). 9. Properties are monitored at least biannually for compliance. Landowners without an updated Soil Conservation Plan must implement one within one year of settlement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Call-N-Ride provides subsidized taxi trips to low-income older adults (age 63 and older) and individuals with disabilities (age 18 to 62) who are Montgomery County residents. The program helps participants travel to medical and personal appointments within Montgomery County, with special exceptions for approved medical facilities in designated service areas outside the county. Participants receive subsidies on a sliding fee scale based on household size and income. Additionally, participants with current MetroAccess identification cards can access the Same Day Access Program offer, receiving $60 in value on their Call-n-Ride swipe card when they pay $30, with no income requirement for that specific offer. Participating taxi companies include Action Taxi, Anytime Taxi, and Regency Taxi/Barwood Taxi.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive subsidies on a sliding fee scale based on household size and income. Subsidy assistance ranges from $5.25 to $30.00 per $60 value, or $10.50 to $60.00 per $120 value, depending on income level. For example, a single-person household with income up to $15,856 per year pays $5.25 for vouchers worth $60 per month. Additionally, participants with current MetroAccess identification cards can receive $60 in value on their swipe card when they pay $30 (no income requirement for this Same Day Access offer). All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, with special exceptions for approved medical facilities in designated service areas.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who are low-income older adults age 63 and older, or persons with disabilities age 18 to 62. Same Day Access Program is also available to individuals with current MetroAccess identification cards regardless of income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to medical and personal appointments, as well as any purpose within Montgomery County. Trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, with approved exceptions for transportation to approved medical facilities in designated service areas outside the county.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, Maryland. Special exceptions allow transportation to approved medical facilities in Designated Service Areas outside the county.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County, Maryland resident
Must be low-income (income limits apply based on household size)
Must be either an older adult age 63 and older, or a person with disabilities age 18 to 62
All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County
For Same Day Access Program offer: must have a current MetroAccess identification card (no income requirement for this specific offer)
For disability certification (ages 18 to 64): must submit CNR Disability Certification Form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the CNR Application Form and submit it via fax, email, or mail to the Call-n-Ride office at cnrorder@montgomerycountymd.gov or call 301-948-5409. For applicants ages 18 to 64 with disabilities, also submit the CNR Disability Certification Form. Provide income documentation to verify eligibility and income levels. You may also contact Connect-A-Ride at 301-738-3252 for application assistance. Recertification is required periodically using the CNR Recertification Form.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Program of General Caregiver Support Services (PGCSS) provides resources, education and support to caregivers of Veterans. Caregivers who enroll have access to education and training, including courses at local VA medical centers, support services, and VA home and community-based care. The Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers (PCAFC) offers enhanced clinical support for Family Caregivers of eligible Veterans with monthly stipends, health care insurance through CHAMPVA, mental health counseling, beneficiary travel benefits, and respite care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides education and training courses at local VA medical centers, support services, and access to VA home and community-based care for caregivers of Veterans. Primary Family Caregivers under PCAFC may receive: a monthly stipend paid directly to the caregiver; access to health care insurance through CHAMPVA if you do not already have health insurance; mental health counseling; certain beneficiary travel benefits when traveling with the Veteran to appointments; and at least 30 days of respite care per year for the Veteran. Secondary Family Caregivers may receive mental health counseling related to care of the Veteran and certain beneficiary travel benefits when traveling with the Veteran to appointments.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 1-855-260-3274 (Toll Free National Caregiver Support Line); 202-745-8000 x 55926 (DC VA Medical Center); 410-605-7000 x 54143 (Baltimore VA Medical Center)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Caregivers of Veterans, including spouses/partners, parents, siblings, children, family members, friends, and battle buddies. The veteran does not need to have a service-connected condition and may have served during any era.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Education, training, support services, and VA home and community-based care for caregivers. For eligible Primary Family Caregivers, funds also include monthly stipends, health care insurance coverage, mental health counseling, beneficiary travel benefits, and respite care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide and in all Maryland counties through local VA Medical Centers.
requirements_list: Individual must be a caregiver of a Veteran
For PGCSS: Veteran does not need to have a service-connected condition
For PGCSS: Veteran may have served during any era
For PCAFC: Veteran must have sustained or aggravated a serious injury or illness in the line of duty in the active military, naval or air service during any service era
Veterans can designate one (1) Primary Family Caregiver and up to two (2) Secondary Family Caregivers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Caregivers who enroll in PGCSS have access to program benefits. Contact the VA National Caregiver Support Line at 1-855-260-3274 (Toll Free) to speak with licensed social workers who can answer questions, listen to concerns, and directly link you to the Caregiver Support Coordinator at your local VA Medical Center. Each Caregiver Support Coordinator can locate assistance tailored to your unique situation. For direct services, call the Washington DC VA Medical Center and ask for the Caregiver Support Coordinator in the Social Work Department.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County offers licensed child care center space in public buildings for qualified operators to expand affordable and high-quality child care options. The program provides facility options across 29 dedicated county public facilities, including specific locations at UpCounty Regional Services Center in Germantown (licensed for 68 children) and Shady Grove Life Sciences Center in Rockville (licensed for 42 children). Selected operators lease the space from the county and provide child care services to infants, toddlers, preschoolers, and school-age children, with priority given to underserved communities. Programs must meet high-quality standards including accreditation and achieving levels 3-5 in Maryland EXCELS.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county provides access to licensed child care facility space in public buildings across 29 dedicated county facilities. Operators lease the space at a rate of $11.35 per square foot per year, which includes utilities (except phone and internet), janitorial services, building and grounds maintenance, snow and trash removal, and pest control. Lease terms are seven years with options to renew for one four-year period and one three-year period. Programs must operate from at least 6:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday-Friday, year-round. Programs receive ongoing support and monitoring and must meet high-quality standards including accreditation and achieving levels 3-5 in Maryland EXCELS. The program will actively seek and enroll 20% of their program with subsidy payment families.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers and operators seeking to establish or expand child care services in Montgomery County public facilities, with priority for underserved communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lease of child care facility space in public buildings to operate licensed, subsidized child care programs serving infants, toddlers, preschoolers, and school-age children, with support for meeting quality standards and accreditation. Operators must accommodate children of Montgomery County Government employees with priority placement, serve families participating in State and County child care subsidy programs (minimum 20% enrollment), accommodate children with special needs and English Language Learners, provide part-time and occasional care options, and establish community participation activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, with priority for underserved communities. Specific known locations include UpCounty Regional Services Center at 12900 Middlebrook Road, Germantown, MD (licensed for 68 children) and Shady Grove Life Sciences Center at 14910 Broschart Road, Rockville, MD (licensed for 42 children), among 29 total dedicated public facilities countywide.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit two complete applications (Parts A-J with attachments) in a spiral or notebook bound binder no larger than 1-inch to Tamieka Thomasson at 1401 Rockville Pike Suite 200, Rockville, MD 20852 by 4:00 p.m. on November 15, 2019 through a competitive bid process. Applications scoring 85 or above out of 110 in Parts A-F advance to the external selection committee, which scores the full application (Parts A-J). structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Water Montgomery Watershed Restoration and Outreach Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County grant program that promotes initiatives and projects to reduce pollutants and improve water quality in local streams and waterways through public engagement, education, and community-based restoration. The program funds public outreach and stewardship projects, community-based restoration water quality implementation projects, litter reduction initiatives, and water quality monitoring programs that educate and engage residents in watershed improvement while achieving measurable impacts and sustainable behavior change. Specific project types include tree planting, rain gardens, trash cleanup, and public education initiatives that keep rivers and streams healthy.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $100,000 are offered to support community-based restoration projects, litter reduction initiatives, public outreach and stewardship efforts, and water quality monitoring projects. structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible projects include community-based restoration (designs for construction-ready in-the-ground projects demonstrating runoff reduction and local water quality improvement on nonprofit-owned property), litter reduction projects in the Anacostia watershed and countywide, public outreach and stewardship to educate and engage residents, water quality monitoring projects that build resident knowledge and monitoring skills, tree planting, rain gardens, trash cleanup, and public education initiatives that maintain healthy rivers and streams.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program for homeowner and condominium associations experiencing financial hardship to address immediate health or safety repairs in common areas, such as failing water supply lines, elevators, fire suppression systems, stormwater drainage, facades, balconies, sidewalks, pathways, and parking lots. The program provides financial assistance for critical common area improvements in residential communities to address health, safety, or occupancy risks.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans are provided up to a maximum of $500,000, repayable over up to 15 years with no interest charged. A 1% loan commitment fee is required at closing on the total approved loan amount. Loans are secured by a pledge of current and future association assets and require a promissory note and loan agreement. DHCA's loan will be subordinate to all other loans for the project. No real estate lien is required. Funding is released as progress payments based on invoices. The association must contribute a minimum of 20% of total project costs from its own funds.

Eligible projects must be based on professional inspections and/or government citations.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Block Grant Program provides federal funding administered by Montgomery County to develop viable communities by supporting activities that provide decent housing and suitable living environments, expand economic opportunities for low and moderate income persons, and fund neighborhood revitalization, economic development, and improved community facilities and services. The program funds nonprofit organizations providing public service activities such as eviction prevention, employment, youth development, education, health care, mental health services, crime prevention, welfare, housing-related supportive services, and recreation for low and moderate-income Montgomery County residents. CDBG funds are also used for affordable housing acquisition, preservation, and rehabilitation, as well as broader community development activities. Montgomery County received approximately five million dollars in CDBG funds in fiscal year 2026 (July 2025 - June 2026).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CDBG awards are grants to eligible nonprofit organizations and local governments. For public services grants for County Fiscal Year 2027, the maximum grant amount is $45,000 per organization. In FY26, $660,000 was allocated to nineteen nonprofit organizations providing services to lower-income County residents; similar funding is anticipated for FY27, pending HUD determination in early 2026. For housing-related activities, at least 51% of units assisted must be income-certified at or below 80% AMI at occupancy or financing, and Davis Bacon wage rates apply for all rehabilitation work if more than eight units are included. Each CDBG-funded activity must serve no less than 70 percent low- and moderate-income (LMI) persons. Construction projects are not eligible for the public services grant component. Grantees may lease (not purchase) capital equipment with CDBG funds. Entertainment-related expenses and direct income payments to individuals are ineligible; however, payments made to third parties on behalf of service recipients for basic services (food, shelter, rent, mortgage, utilities) cannot exceed three consecutive months. Political activities are ineligible. Funds will not be available until July 1, 2026, or after.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations that serve low and moderate-income Montgomery County residents; governmental and quasi-governmental agencies, including County agencies (strongly encouraged to apply in partnership with a nonprofit); and organizations or developers acquiring or rehabilitating affordable housing in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Public service activities including eviction prevention, housing-related supportive services, employment, crime prevention, positive youth development, health care, education, mental health services, welfare, and recreation; affordable housing acquisition, preservation, and rehabilitation; neighborhood revitalization; economic development; and improved community facilities and services. Construction projects and land acquisition are not eligible for public services grants. Equipment purchases are ineligible; only equipment leasing is permitted. Entertainment-related expenses and direct income payments to individuals are ineligible. Income payments to third parties on behalf of service recipients for basic services cannot exceed three consecutive months.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Excludes the Town of Barnesville, Chevy Chase View, Chevy Chase Village, Village of Chevy Chase (Section 3), Town of Laytonsville, and Village of Martin's Additions. The Cities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park operate their own CDBG programs and should be contacted directly for activities within city limits or principally serving city residents. Applicants must directly serve Montgomery County residents.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open August 11, 2025, for County Fiscal Year 2027 (July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027) funding. Applicants must submit a complete fillable Adobe PDF application form by email to cdbg@montgomerycountymd.gov no later than 4:00 p.m. on Friday, September 19, 2025. Only complete applications received by the deadline will be considered for review; applicants will be notified if applications are missing minor information (such as federal identification numbers) and given seven days to provide such information, but unanswered questions or missing budgets/attachments do not qualify as minor omissions. Applications submitted after the deadline will only be considered if addressing an emergency or unique one-time opportunity, at the Director's discretion. DHCA staff screens applications for completeness and eligibility and sends confirmation emails by September 22, 2025. Staff completes eligibility review by September 26, 2025. The Community Development Advisory Committee (CDAC), composed of County residents appointed by the County Executive, reviews eligible applications. CDAC holds a public hearing on October 7, 2025 (tentative) to solicit community input on priority needs. CDAC members meet with applicants in October-November to discuss applications and answer questions. CDAC makes funding recommendations to the County Executive by January. Applicants are notified in writing of the County Executive's recommendations in March. The County Executive submits recommendations to the County Council in March/April, and the Council holds hearings on the budget. The County Council makes final funding decisions in late May as part of the approved budget. Staff and grantees finalize contract language and requirements July-September 2026. Grantees receive Notice to Proceed and begin delivering services with a twelve-month spending period beginning with Notice to Proceed. Funds will not be available until July 1, 2026, or after.

structured_extraction.program_name: Cost Sharing Capital Grants Program (Montgomery County)
structured_extraction.program_description: A recurring grant program administered by Montgomery County that solicits applications from qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations seeking to implement capital projects in Montgomery County. The program operates through a cost-sharing model in which the applicant organization contributes a portion of the project cost. Grants support capital projects that provide access to resources, direct services, historical preservation, cultural enrichment, infrastructure and facility improvements, equipment acquisition, and other benefits to Montgomery County residents. The program has operated across multiple fiscal years (FY24, FY25, FY26, FY27) and uses a two-stage application process (for FY24) or single-stage process (for FY25 and later cycles). The program prioritizes projects with commitment to underserved populations, readiness for immediate implementation, and organizational ownership or long-term commitment to the asset being improved.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant program providing capital funding for infrastructure, equipment, and facility improvements, with required cost-sharing from the applicant organization. FY24: Two-stage application process with awards ranging from $25,000 to $1,000,000 depending on funding category (Arts Facility State Match: $25,000-$750,000; Small Arts: $25,000-$100,000; Non-Arts State Match: $25,000-$1,000,000; Small Non-Arts: $25,000-$100,000). FY25: Single-stage application for organizations with existing State capital awards; minimum $50,000, maximum $1,000,000 with $350,000 annual maximum per fiscal year. Multi-year awards up to three years possible pending satisfactory performance and continued appropriation. FY24 awards provided on cost-reimbursable basis; FY25 anticipated to provide 30% upfront payment with remainder cost-reimbursable. Capital expenses defined as $5,000 or more in one-time costs for purchase or improvement of a single fixed asset.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY24: Tuesday, March 19, 2024 at 3:00 PM (closed); FY25: Thursday, March 20, 2025 at 1:00 PM; FY27 cycle anticipated to launch in April 2026 immediately after State of Maryland FY27 budget passage
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ali Hoy, Program Manager II (FY25); Olga Kravets, Outgoing Grants Program Manager (FY24)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations seeking to implement capital projects in Montgomery County that provide access to resources, direct services, historical preservation, cultural enrichment, infrastructure improvements, or other benefits to Montgomery County residents. FY25 requires organizations to have already secured a Maryland State capital award (State Bond Bill or other Maryland State capital funding) for the same capital project.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects including: purchase of land or buildings; construction of new buildings; improvements to land (e.g., turf, bleachers); expansions or add-ons to existing facilities; renovation and upgrades to existing facilities; renewal of assets to preserve historical buildings and sites; purchase of major equipment ($5,000+). NOT eligible: operating costs (rent, leases, salaries, utilities, staff benefits, supplies, minor equipment under $5,000, maintenance); indirect costs; loans or mortgage payments on existing properties; lobbying; expenses incurred prior to grant award; costs that supplant other funding sources.

requirements_list: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization status (or collaboration with at least one entity having this status)
Registered and in Good Standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Capital project must be or planned to be located in Montgomery County

One application per organization per cycle
For FY25: Must have existing Maryland State capital award (State Bond Bill or other forms of Maryland State capital funding) for the same capital project
For FY25: Organizations currently pursuing but who have not yet secured Maryland State capital funding are not eligible
Cost-sharing contribution required from applicant organization

For projects involving rented or leased space: must demonstrate long-term commitment (5+ years minimum) to be competitive; short-term rental/lease (less than 5 years) or lack of property selection reduces competitiveness
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: FY24: Two-stage application process. Applications submitted through SM Apply online platform at https://mcmdgrants.smapply.org. Stages include Project Scope of Work, Project Budget with Budget Narrative, Project Work Plan/Timeline, Performance Plan, Project Leadership Summary, and Memorandum of Understanding (for collaboratives). Stage 1 submissions followed by Stage 2 submissions. Award notification expected roughly 2 months after deadline via email. FY25: Single-stage application process. Applications submitted through Euna Grants (eCivis) platform at https://portal.ecivis.com. Applicants must: (1) create account on eCivis portal; (2) select FY25 Cost Sharing Capital Grants Program from OGM homepage; (3) complete application including Funding Category Consideration, Lead Applicant Information, Applicant Background, Project Scope of Work, Project Budget and Budget Narrative, Project Work Plan/Timeline, and Performance Plan Tasks. Information sessions held prior to each application cycle. Incomplete applications or those submitted after deadline will not be considered. Independent Review Committee scores proposals using Confidence Rating system based on weighted criteria. Final award decisions made by County based on Committee recommendations and other relevant factors including applicant's past performance on County awards. Award notification expected roughly 2 months after deadline.
