structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides technical and financial support to property and business owners to improve the exteriors of older commercial properties. Property and business owners are reimbursed up to 50% of eligible costs for design and construction of approved facade improvement projects. Improvements may include new facade renovation and treatments, building and pylon signage, LED lighting, streetscape elements, landscape installation, art and mural installation, and other exterior amenities. Participants must maintain improvements for a negotiated term through a facade easement agreement with the county. The program is available countywide in Montgomery County and targets buildings that are 10 or more years old or do not meet current commercial standards.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible property and business owners are reimbursed up to 50% of the total eligible project costs, up to $500,000. County reimbursement amounts above $500,000 may be available at the discretion of the DHCA Director on a per-project basis, based on the availability of program funds and evaluation of the overall scope of improvements as related to the program's goals. Easement terms are negotiated based on total project costs: $150,000-$300,000 requires a three (3) year easement term from recordation; $300,001-$700,000 requires a five (5) year easement term from recordation; $700,001-$1,000,000 requires a seven (7) year easement term from recordation with lien subordination required if applicable. Participants must maintain improvements throughout the easement term via a facade easement agreement with the county. Program participants may repurchase the easement prior to the end of the easement term using a specified formula.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Due to current funding limitations, projects will not be reviewed for full submission and approval until July 1, 2025, at the earliest
structured_extraction.program_audience: County property and business owners interested in making improvements to the exterior of commercial properties that are 10 or more years old or do not meet current commercial standards. Properties must be commercial or mixed-use buildings with a retail component and four or fewer stories tall.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Design and construction costs for facade improvements including demolition of existing facade, new facade renovation and treatments, building and pylon signage with lighting, cleaning and painting of building exterior, installing new windows and doors, canopies and awnings, exterior site lighting, exterior electrical work, parking lot and sidewalk repaving, landscape plant material installation, parking lot reconfiguration and restriping, dumpster enclosures, convenience features including benches and outdoor seating, and new or refurbished murals and permanent public art. All approved projects must provide for installation of new facade materials (not including paint) on at least 50% of the main face of the building. Site improvement expenses cannot exceed 15% of the building facade improvement costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available countywide in Montgomery County, Maryland. Projects are eligible throughout the County, with priority consideration given to projects located in program priority areas (Glenmont, Hillandale, Layhill, Long Branch, Montgomery Village, or Wheaton) and/or in an Equity Focus Area within the County, and/or mixed-use projects (but not exclusively used for or converted to housing), and/or projects with significant first floor retail.

Project must achieve the program's objective to provide significant improvements to the facade and improve the overall physical appearance of the building as determined by the Architectural Review Committee
All approved projects must provide for installation of new facade materials (not including paint) on at least 50% (excluding window and door areas) of the main face or front of the building
Site improvement expenses cannot exceed 15% of the building facade improvement costs
Participants must maintain improvements for a negotiated term via facade easement agreement with the county
Property owner must sign and execute all documentation for agreements and easements
If property is located within a historic district and/or on the historical register, participants must obtain approval of the Historic Preservation Commission
Participants must obtain all necessary permits from the Department of Permitting Services

Participants must provide property Tax ID number, certificate of insurance naming Montgomery County as an additional insured, resolution from Board/Managing Member if applicable, letter from construction contractor with start and completion dates, and current title report
Participants must submit all invoices and receipts for eligible project costs within forty-five (45) days of project completion
Participants must register in the County's Central Vendor Registration System (CVRS) to receive payment
Participants must allow DHCA periodic inspections during the easement term to ensure proper maintenance
Noted damage or unapproved alterations must be remedied within timeframe provided in written notice from DHCA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Interested property and business owners must complete a Program Interest Form available at www.montgomerycountymd.gov/DHCA/community/neighborhood/facade.html. Program Interest Forms are accepted on an ongoing basis and reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis. 2. DHCA staff will follow-up via email verifying receipt of all Interest Forms. 3. Proposed projects meeting program participation requirements will be emailed requesting submittal of project concept designs and materials including existing building photos, concept design drawings of all sides of the building to be improved, concept design plans for site improvements if applicable, material samples and color selections, detailed line-item cost estimates, and estimated architectural and engineering service fees. 4. The applicant and/or their architectural and engineering firm may mail, hand deliver, or email materials to DHCA staff who will schedule a date to present the proposed project to the Architectural Review Committee (in-person or via TEAMS/ZOOM) for feedback and recommendations. 5. The Committee will make a recommendation to the DHCA Director to either approve the project with or without contingencies or disapprove it. Applicants are notified via email. 6. The DHCA Director has absolute and sole discretion on whether to approve the project for funding (decision is final). 7. A Program Offer Letter will be provided detailing the project funding amount offered (in the form of an easement purchase) and correlating easement terms. This letter must be signed by the property owner and returned within ten (10) business days. 8. Program participant must provide additional documentation including Tax ID, insurance certificate, Board resolution if applicable, contractor letter, and current title report. 9. A public notice for projects with easement terms of five (5) or more years invites written comment with a deadline of no more than 30 days. Notice is sent to property owners within 500 feet and disseminated via DHCA website, site posting, online community news/social media, emails, newsletters, and community listservs. 10. At conclusion of public notice period, DHCA emails Notice to Proceed. 11. Design and construction should be completed within reasonable timeframe based on project scope. 12. Participant submits all invoices and receipts within forty-five (45) days of project completion. 13. DHCA issues reimbursement check within thirty (30) days after which DHCA records the easement. 14. DHCA conducts periodic inspections during easement term to ensure maintenance compliance. Contact Kristina Ellis at Kristina.Ellis@montgomerycountymd.gov for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Design for Life (DFL) Property Tax Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary property tax incentive program administered by Montgomery County that encourages development of housing options accommodating a wider range of accessibility needs. The program provides property tax credits and Development Impact Tax for Schools credits to homeowners, builders, and developers who construct or modify residential properties to meet Design for Life accessibility standards. It offers three tiers of incentives: (1) Accessibility Features credit for individual accessibility improvements to existing homes; (2) Level I (VISITable) credit for homes meeting basic visitability accessibility standards; and (3) Level II (LIVEable) credit for homes meeting higher livability accessibility standards. The program aims to increase the stock of visitable and livable housing in Montgomery County, help County residents remain in their homes as physical needs change, encourage businesses to provide accessible housing, and increase the marketability of accessible properties. It applies to both new construction and renovation of single-family attached and detached homes, townhouses, duplexes, and condominium units. A school impact tax credit may also be available for new construction projects meeting Level I or Level II standards.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides three tiers of property tax credits: (1) Accessibility Features Property Tax Credit: 50% of eligible costs up to $2,500 (less any other subsidies) for individual accessibility features costing over $500, incurred within 12 months of application. Maximum $2,000 can be applied in any single tax year, with excess carrying over to future years. Annual limit on all such credits is $100,000 per program year. (2) Level I (VISITable) Property Tax Credit: up to $3,000 total (less other subsidies, including school impact tax credits), with a maximum of $2,000 applied per tax year and excess carrying over to future years. Applies to new or existing single-family homes, townhomes, and duplexes meeting Level I standards. Annual limit on all such credits is $500,000 per program year. (3) Level II (LIVEable) Property Tax Credit: up to $10,000 total (less other subsidies, including school impact tax credits), with a maximum of $2,000 applied per tax year and excess carrying over to future years. Applies to new or existing single-family homes, townhomes, and duplexes meeting Level II standards. Annual limit on all such credits is $500,000 per program year. Additionally, a Development Impact Tax for School Improvements credit is available for new single-family residences meeting Level I or Level II standards, ranging from $500 to $2,000 per residence depending on the percentage of residences in the project meeting the standard: 5% of units = $500/Level I house; 10% = $1,000; 25% = $1,500; 30% = $2,000 (applies only where there is no bonus density for DFL units). All credits run with the property upon transfer of title and excess credits carry over to future tax years. The tax credit is assessed by the Department of Finance and applied as a line item deduction on the property tax bill. Condominium units require a commercial building permit rather than residential permit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, builders, and developers in Montgomery County who construct or modify residential properties to meet accessibility standards, including first-time homebuyers, young families, active adults, persons living with temporary or permanent impairments, and home care facility owners. Eligible properties include single-family detached or attached dwelling units, townhouses, duplexes, and condominium units that are the owner's principal residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of permanent accessibility features in residential dwellings, including: (1) no-step entrances; (2) ramps; (3) wider doorways (32-inch nominal clear width); (4) elevators or lifts; (5) stair glides; (6) chair lifts; (7) accessible bathrooms (including walk-in or roll-in showers or tubs); (8) accessible kitchens; (9) grab bars; (10) lever door handles; (11) chair height toilets; (12) relocation of switches and electrical outlets/thermostats; (13) closet renovations for accessibility; (14) sensory impairment accommodations (alternative sensory alarms); and (15) other improvements meeting Level I (VISITable) or Level II (LIVEable) accessibility standards. Eligible costs include reasonable installation costs and required permit or inspection fees. For Level I, required features include: at least one no-step entrance, connected accessible route to a place to visit on entry level, usable powder room or bathroom on entry level, and 32-inch nominal clear width interior door. For Level II, all Level I features plus: accessible circulation path connecting entrance to kitchen, accessible bedroom, and full bathroom with walk-in or roll-in shower or tub.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Applies to new construction and renovation of residential properties throughout the county. Property owners in the City of Rockville or City of Gaithersburg must also submit a signed affidavit from their respective city verifying that all necessary inspections have been completed and that accessibility features have been installed according to permit.
requirements_list: Property must be the owner's principal residence as indicated on the real property tax bill
Property must be a new or existing residential dwelling: single-family detached or attached dwelling unit, townhouse, duplex, or condominium unit
Installations must be permanent
For Accessibility Features credit: eligible costs must be incurred within 12 months prior to application; costs must exceed $500; costs must be documented by contracts, receipts, or invoices

For Level I (VISITable) standard: must include at least one no-step entrance, connected accessible route to a place to visit on entry level, usable powder room or bathroom on entry level, and 32-inch nominal clear width interior door

For Level II (LIVEable) standard: must include all Level I features plus accessible circulation path connecting entrance to kitchen, accessible bedroom, and full bathroom with walk-in or roll-in shower or tub
For Level I and Level II credits: all required accessibility feature modifications must be completed prior to final approved inspection
A building permit must be obtained before work begins

DFL Application Box must be checked when applying for residential or commercial permit online; if applying on paper, submit Building Permit Supplemental Design for Life Application with architectural and/or engineering plans
For condominium units, a commercial building permit rather than residential permit is required
Only one application for tax credits per property during a single tax year
Costs must be paid by the applicant/property owner
For Development Impact Tax for Schools credit: owner must enter into an Impact Tax Credit Certification Agreement before building permits are issued
For school impact tax credit: project must meet Level I or Level II Accessibility standards and be new home construction

Before a buyer signs a contract for a new single-family residence, the seller must disclose that a property tax credit may be available and provide general information about eligible improvements and estimated costs
For properties in Rockville or Gaithersburg, submit signed city affidavit verifying inspections and compliance
Final building code inspection and Design for Life final inspection must be passed before applying for the tax credit
Applicant must not have received other subsidies for the same property modifications (affidavit required)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process is two-part. PART 1 - Building Permit: Apply for and receive a building permit before work begins. Apply online through the Montgomery County eServices portal (check the DFL Application Box on the residential or commercial permit application) or submit paper documents in person at the Montgomery County Department of Permitting Services, 2425 Reedie Drive, 7th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902. If applying on paper, submit the Building Permit Supplemental Design for Life Application along with architectural and/or engineering plans documenting the DFL renovations. For projects seeking a Development Impact Tax for Schools credit, also submit a separate School Impact Tax Credit Certification Agreement before permits are issued. PART 2 - Tax Credit Application: After all work is completed, pass both the final building code inspection and the Design for Life final inspection. Then submit a completed Application for Design for Life Tax Credits (available as a PDF form) with supporting documentation including: a copy of the building permit, cost documentation (contracts, receipts, or invoices), copies of applications and receipts for any other subsidies received, and an affidavit stating that neither the previous owner nor the applicant has received other subsidies for the property modifications. Applicants in Rockville or Gaithersburg must also submit signed city affidavits. Submit completed application to DPS.DesignforLife@montgomerycountymd.gov or in person at the Department of Permitting Services, 2425 Reedie Drive, 7th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902. DPS certifies that requirements are met and forwards certification to the Department of Finance. The Department of Finance assesses the appropriate tax credit amount, notifies the applicant, and applies the credit as a line item on the next property tax bill. Upon acceptance of your permit application, you will receive an email invitation to upload electronic plans and supporting documents through the ProjectDox (ePlans) system. All drawings must be uploaded to the DRAWINGS folder and all supporting documentation to the DOCUMENTS folder. Files must be PDF format, no more than 20 characters in the file name, with no special characters. A 3" x 4" area must be reserved at the top center of all drawings for the DPS electronic approval stamp. Drawings should be minimum 24" x 36" size and must be to scale with graphic scale clearly indicated.

structured_extraction.program_name: Design for Life - Level I (VISITable) Accessibility Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for homeowners and builders/developers who construct or renovate single-family homes to meet Level I (VISITable) accessibility standards in Montgomery County. VISITable homes include design elements such as a no-step entrance, connected accessible route to a place to visit on the entry level, usable powder room or bathroom, and 32-inch nominal clear width interior doors to accommodate people with disabilities and improve accessibility for all residents. The credit runs with the property and applies to qualifying expenditures exceeding $500 incurred within 12 months of application.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners receive a property tax credit of up to $3,000 less other subsidies and school impact tax credits, applied to the property tax bill. The maximum credit applied in any tax year is $2,000, with excess credit carrying over to subsequent years. The credit runs with the property. Applies to expenditures exceeding $500 incurred within 12 months of application. For builders or developers, school impact tax credits are available against development impact taxes depending on the percentage of homes meeting Level I standards: $500 per Level I house if 5% of project homes are VISITable; $1,000 per Level I house if 10% are VISITable; $1,500 per Level I house if 25% are VISITable; and $2,000 per Level I house if 30% are VISITable (applies only where there is no bonus density for Design for Life units). Property tax credits for Level I are up to $3,000 less other subsidies including school impact tax credits. Annual limit on property tax credits allocated for all homeowners is $500,000; annual limit for individual accessibility features is $100,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing - applications accepted at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners who own and live in an attached or detached single-family dwelling unit as their primary residence in Montgomery County, and builders or developers constructing single-family homes that meet Level I (VISITable) accessibility standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction or renovation costs to make a single-family home meet Level I (VISITable) accessibility standards, which require at least one no-step entrance, a connected accessible route to a place to visit on the entry level, a usable powder room or bathroom, and a 32-inch nominal clear width interior door. Expenditures must exceed $500 and be incurred within 12 months of application.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, including the jurisdictions of Montgomery County Department of Permitting Services, City of Gaithersburg, and City of Rockville.
requirements_list: Own and live in the home as primary residence (for homeowners)
Expenditures must exceed $500
Expenditures must be incurred within 12 months of application
Property must be an attached or detached single-family dwelling unit

Must meet all four Level I (VISITable) design elements: (1) at least one no-step entrance located at any entry door connected to an accessible route to a place to visit on the entry level; (2) a usable powder room or bathroom; (3) a 32-inch nominal clear width interior door; and (4) an accessible circulation path at least 36 inches wide
Powder room or bathroom must have clear space of 2'6" by 4'0" to position a wheelchair or mobility aid
Building permit must be issued and work completed and certified by Department of Permitting Services (final building inspection must be completed before applying)
Eligible costs must be documented by contracts, receipts, or invoices demonstrating the cost or amount of money spent on purchase and installation, including any required permit or inspection fees
Builders or developers must work with the County to establish impact tax credit certification agreements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: After a building permit is issued and work is completed and certified by the Department of Permitting Services, homeowners submit the Design for Life Application for Tax Credit form (attached with the application). The final building inspection must be completed before applying for the tax credit. The application must include contracts, receipts, or invoices documenting eligible costs exceeding $500. The property tax credit is applied to the property tax bill in amounts up to $2,000 per tax year, with any balance carrying over to following years. Builders or developers work with the County to establish impact tax credit certification agreements and must submit the required documentation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Design for Life - Level II (LIVEable) Accessibility Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for homeowners and builders/developers who construct or renovate single-family homes to meet Level II (LIVEable) accessibility standards in Montgomery County. LIVEable homes include comprehensive accessibility design elements—such as no-step entrance, accessible kitchen, bedroom, and bathroom with walk-in or roll-in shower, and accessible circulation path throughout—that allow people with disabilities to fully live in and move throughout the home. Homeowners receive a property tax credit based on qualifying expenditures, while builders or developers may receive credits against school impact taxes based on the percentage of homes in a project meeting LIVEable standards.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners receive a property tax credit of up to $10,000 for Level II (LIVEable) standards, less other subsidies and school impact tax credits. The credit applies to qualifying expenditures exceeding $500 incurred within 12 months of application. The maximum credit applied in any tax year is $2,000, with excess credit carrying over to following years. For example, a homeowner spending $15,000 receives a $10,000 tax credit applied at $2,000 per year for 5 successive years. The tax credit runs with the property. Homeowners can also receive property tax credits for individual accessibility features at 50% of eligible costs (up to $2,500 per year) if not claiming Level I or Level II standards. Builders or developers receive school impact tax credits (not property tax credits) for Level I or Level II homes based on project participation: $500 per Level I house if 5% of project homes are LIVEable, $1,000 per Level I house if 10% are LIVEable, $1,500 per Level I house if 25% are LIVEable, and $2,000 per Level I house if 30% are LIVEable (applies only where there is no bonus density for Design for Life units). Property tax credits are available for eligible costs documented by contracts, receipts, or invoices.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners who own and live in an attached or detached single-family dwelling unit as their primary residence in Montgomery County, and builders or developers constructing single-family homes that meet LIVEable accessibility standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction or renovation costs to make a single-family home meet Level II (LIVEable) accessibility standards. The eight required design elements are: (1) a no-step entrance, (2) an accessible route to a place to visit on entry level, (3) a usable powder room or bathroom, (4) a 32-inch interior doorway, (5) an accessible circulation path for wheelchairs throughout, (6) an accessible kitchen, (7) an accessible bedroom, and (8) an accessibility-enhanced full bathroom with walk-in or roll-in shower. Qualifying expenditures must exceed $500 and be incurred within 12 months of application. Costs may include permit or inspection fees. Individual accessibility features can also qualify for separate property tax credits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, including jurisdictions within the County's permitting authority and cities of Gaithersburg and Rockville.
requirements_list: Own and live in the home as primary residence (for homeowners)
Expenditures must exceed $500
Expenditures must be incurred within 12 months of application
Property must be an attached or detached single-family dwelling unit (including townhouses and duplexes)

Home must meet all eight Level II (LIVEable) design elements: no-step entrance, accessible route to visit space, usable powder room or bathroom, 32-inch interior doorway, accessible circulation path, accessible kitchen, at least one accessible bedroom, and accessibility-enhanced bathroom with walk-in or roll-in shower
Building permit must be issued and work completed and certified by Department of Permitting Services
Final building inspection must be completed before applying
Homeowners must submit Design for Life Application for Tax Credit form after final inspection
Eligible costs must be documented by contracts, receipts, or invoices demonstrating purchase and installation costs
Homeowner must provide complete list of features and costs for each feature with application
Owner's principal residence must be designated as such on property's real property tax bill
Builders or developers must work with the County to establish impact tax credit certification agreements
If receiving any subsidy from governmental, quasi-governmental, or non-profit entity, must provide documentation and the subsidy amount will be deducted from credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: After a building permit is issued and work is completed and certified by the Department of Permitting Services with final building inspection completed, homeowners submit the Design for Life Application for Tax Credit form to the Department of Permitting Services (or designee). The application must include: (1) property owner information, (2) property location and building permit number, (3) detailed listing of all qualifying features with costs, (4) documentation of eligible costs (contracts, receipts, invoices), and (5) disclosure of any subsidies received. The Department of Permitting Services reviews and certifies eligibility through an affidavit process. The property tax credit is then applied to the property tax bill in amounts up to $2,000 per tax year, with any balance carrying over to following years until fully applied. For builders or developers, certification agreements must be established with the County prior to construction to qualify for school impact tax credits. Applications are processed on a rolling basis. The annual program limit for all property tax credit applications is $500,000 for Level I and Level II standards.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program to solve drainage problems where there is no storm drain system or the existing system is failing or is inadequate. The program addresses requests for assistance to correct drainage problems where runoff water originates from the public right-of-way.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Division of Transportation Engineering receives and addresses requests for assistance to correct drainage problems. After receiving a request, staff investigate the nature and cause of the problem, determine if it qualifies as a drainage assistance project, calculate watershed size and surface water flow characteristics, verify affected properties and damage extent, review existing drainage systems, determine if a spot solution or comprehensive capital improvement project is needed, and notify the requestor of action being taken. For maintenance of existing storm drain systems (such as clearing debris from inlets, storm drain pipes, drainage channels, or reconstruction of roadside curbs), contact MC-DOT's Division of Highway Services at 240-777-6000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents and property owners experiencing drainage problems where runoff originates from the public right-of-way.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Addressing drainage problems and improving drainage systems where there is no storm drain system or the existing system is failing or is inadequate. Funding may support spot solutions or comprehensive capital improvement projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Requests must involve drainage issues associated with surface runoff from roads and other property owned and maintained by Montgomery County. For drainage problems where water runoff originates from private property and flows onto private property, applicants should contact other referral agencies.
requirements_list: Drainage problem must be where runoff water originates from the public right-of-way
Existing storm drain system must be failing, inadequate, or absent

Request must include: location of drainage problem, brief description of problem and where water originates and where it goes (photographs are helpful), requestor's name, home address, and telephone number
Permission must be granted authorizing a site visit by County staff on property, if applicable
Availability to meet County staff at the site during site visit, if necessary
Community or Homeowner Association name and representative contact information, if applicable
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A request for assistance can be initiated by completing the Drainage Request Form, telephone call, email, fax, or letter to the Design Section of the Division of Transportation Engineering at 100 Edison Park Drive, 4th floor, Gaithersburg, Maryland 20878. Fax: 240-777-7277. A County staff member knowledgeable in surface runoff issues will review the request in a timely manner. After review is completed, the requestor receives an explanation of the review findings and proposed action. The evaluation process includes: investigation of the nature and cause of the problem; determination of whether it should be included as a DAR Project or referred to another agency; calculation of watershed size and water flow characteristics; verification of affected properties and damage extent; review of existing drainage systems; determination of whether a spot solution or comprehensive Capital Improvement Project (CIP) is needed; determination of availability of right-of-way or easements; and notification to residents of action being taken.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program to address maintenance needs on existing storm drain systems, including clearing debris from inlets and pipes, re-establishing eroded or silted drainage channels, addressing water ponding on roads, and reconstructing roadside curbs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County maintenance and repairs for existing storm drain systems, including clearing debris from inlets and storm drain pipes, re-establishing drainage channels that have eroded or silted over time, addressing water ponding on roads such as puddles and potholes, and reconstructing roadside curbs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents and property owners with drainage concerns on existing storm drain systems requiring maintenance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Maintenance and repairs of existing storm drain systems including debris removal, channel re-establishment, road ponding solutions, and curb reconstruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Program applies to existing storm drain systems maintained by Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Drainage concern must be on existing storm drain systems where maintenance is needed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Division of Transportation Engineering by email at mcdot.highway@montgomerycountymd.gov to report drainage system maintenance issues.

structured_extraction.program_name: Early Head Start Birth to Five Community Based Model
structured_extraction.program_description: A full-year, full-day early childhood program serving infants, toddlers, and preschoolers through a network of registered family child care homes and licensed center-based programs. Participating programs receive funding and comprehensive support services including staff training, technical assistance, coaching, and family engagement services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Registered family child care homes and licensed center-based programs with a minimum of Level 3 EXCELS rating receive $17,965 per child annually (monthly payments of $1,497) for providing 1,380 annual hours (9 hours daily) of Early Head Start services to eligible families. Programs receive comprehensive wrap-around services including training, technical assistance, coaching support, family engagement services, health services, administrative support, and education supplies and equipment. Minimum enrollment slots: 2 for family child care providers, 4 for childcare centers. Families must meet 100% Federal Poverty Level income eligibility and receive free services with no co-pay allowed.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications available November 1st through November 15th. Application closes November 14, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed childcare centers and registered family child care homes serving infants, toddlers, and preschoolers (ages birth to 3) in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Program funds support full-day early childhood care and education services, staff professional development, technical assistance, family engagement services, health services, administrative support, and education supplies and equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Montgomery County. Income-eligible families with children birth to three years old living in Montgomery County may apply, space permitting.
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care home or licensed center-based program licensed through Maryland State Department of Education
Must be registered and published as Level 3 in Maryland EXCELS
Must have attended one of the orientation sessions in October to be considered
Childcare centers require minimum of two teachers with Infant & Toddler CDA credential
Family child care providers require minimum of FCCP CDA credential
Must be responsible for the early childhood education component of the program
Must provide families with option to access Maryland State Childcare Scholarship and County Working Parents' Assistance (WPA) programs for extended day options
Must fully participate in comprehensive services including site visits, parent engagement, and coaching
Must provide county review access to last MSDE-OCC inspection report
Must submit two letters of recommendation from current or past parents
Childcare programs with multiple locations must submit separate application for each location
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Childcare providers must attend an orientation session in October. Applications open November 1st and are available through November 15th through an online form posted on the Montgomery County Community Action Agency website. Programs that attended orientation sessions are eligible to apply. Families apply directly with Montgomery County and receive a list of participating childcare programs to select from. Program services begin Winter 2026 (January).

structured_extraction.program_name: Economic Development Fund Grant & Loan Program (EDFGLP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A discretionary strategic attraction and retention program administered by Montgomery County that provides financial assistance (grants and loans) to private employers who retain jobs or stimulate new job creation in Montgomery County. The program targets projects in focused industry sectors that generate significant economic development impact, such as job growth or retention and capital expenditure. Priority is given to high technology companies, manufacturing companies, businesses located in urban revitalization areas, and other private employers providing the greatest public benefits. A sub-program also provides financial assistance specifically to small businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and loans are provided to private employers and small businesses in Montgomery County. Typical assistance ranges from $5,000 to $100,000, with higher amounts possible for large projects. Small businesses may receive up to $125,000. Project awards stipulate conditions for disbursement and minimum performance measures, and include clawback provisions to recapture funds if a business fails to achieve expected economic output.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private employers and small businesses in Montgomery County seeking to retain or create jobs or generate significant economic development impact.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job creation and retention activities, capital expenditure, and other projects that generate significant economic development impact in targeted industry sectors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, with priority for businesses located in urban revitalization areas.
requirements_list: Must be a private employer in Montgomery County
Must retain jobs or create new jobs, or generate significant economic development impact such as job growth or retention and capital expenditure
Project must be in a targeted industry sector
Must demonstrate projected employment growth and capital investment, or other positive economic impacts
Must provide financial history and projections including balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements
Must demonstrate sound background of the company and its management
Must have a favorable present and future market outlook for the business
Must meet minimum performance measures stipulated in the project award
Priority given to cases creating significant employment growth within 1 to 3 years
Priority given to projects resulting in significant capital investment
Priority given to projects that materially improve the County's economy
Priority given to projects that complement state and private sector funding programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Montgomery County Business Portal. Applications are evaluated using established evaluation criteria and priority criteria to arrive at a funding decision. Awards include conditions for disbursement and clawback provisions if minimum performance measures are not met.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program from the City of Gaithersburg for larger businesses wanting to relocate or expand within the City of Gaithersburg.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding provided by the City of Gaithersburg for larger businesses relocating or expanding within city limits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Large businesses relocating or expanding in Gaithersburg.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business relocation and expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Gaithersburg, Montgomery County, Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County offers tax-exempt financing through the issuance of Economic Development Revenue Bonds (EDRB) or Industrial Revenue Bonds to non-profit organizations and selected for-profit businesses seeking to locate or expand operations within the County. The County participates in both the Maryland Industrial Development Financing Authority (MIDFA) and Economic Development Revenue Bond (EDRB) programs to support economic development projects. The County issues bonds to finance qualifying projects, and the borrower repays the bonds through project revenues. Neither the full faith and credit nor the taxing power of Montgomery County is pledged to the payment of principal, interest, or other costs.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt financing through the issuance of Economic Development Revenue Bonds (EDRB) or Industrial Revenue Bonds. Neither the full faith and credit nor the taxing power of Montgomery County is pledged to the payment of principal, interest, or other costs. Applicants pay a non-refundable application fee of $5,000 at the time of filing, an annual administrative fee of 10 basis points (0.10%) on the original issue amount due at closing and annually thereafter while bonds are outstanding, and bear all legal and administrative costs incurred by the County during review and pursuit of the financing agreement. The County reviews the application, holds a TEFRA public hearing, and the County Council votes on approval. The typical process takes approximately 6 weeks or longer depending on the County Council's agenda.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and selected for-profit businesses seeking to locate or expand operations in Montgomery County, Maryland, requiring tax-exempt financing for economic development projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax-exempt financing for economic development projects including construction and acquisition of facilities, land purchases, building rehabilitation, equipment acquisition, facility development, expansion, and relocation projects. For non-profits: projects that advance their charitable mission (medical, educational, charitable endeavors). For for-profits: small manufacturing facilities, solid waste disposal facilities, low-income housing projects, and projects with positive economic and fiscal impact. Associated costs such as architectural, engineering, financing, and legal fees are also eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. The project must be located in Montgomery County. Special consideration given to businesses located or to be located in areas designated for urban revitalization or strategically targeted growth.
requirements_list: Provide detailed background information on the organization or business including description, products/services, and three years of financial statements (audited preferred)
Submit letter of good standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
If non-profit, provide IRS Determination Letter prior to bond closing
Non-profit organizations must be tax-exempt entities qualified under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code

Provide complete project description including purpose, amount and term of financing requested, financing structure, facilities description, site location and map, itemized project costs, equipment description and costs, and status of other government approvals
Projects must be non-speculative in nature, developed for a specific occupant
Projects must comply with federally mandated tax legislation restricting use of tax-exempt financing
Underwriter must provide a letter stating the project has been reviewed for financial aspects and deemed financially feasible
Schools must hold a Certificate of Approval from the State Board of Education, or if affiliated with a church, have a determination of exemption from the State Board of Education
Medical or health service organizations must be properly licensed by the County, State, and/or Federal government as applicable
Religious organizations must obtain a letter of preliminary advice from the County's bond counsel regarding compliance with separation of church and state requirements
For-profit applicants and their landlords must pay County property taxes and be current on all property taxes and amounts due to the County and State of Maryland
Disclose any legal issues involving the project

Provide employment information including current employment in Montgomery County and Washington Metropolitan Area, breakdown by occupational category with average salaries, and five-year projections of new employment by occupational category
Provide statement of projected tax benefits, new employment opportunities, willingness to participate in County employment-training programs, and other economic and community benefits
Projects should demonstrate positive economic and fiscal impact on the County
Pay non-refundable application fee of $5,000 at filing (check made payable to Montgomery County)
Pay annual administrative fee of 10 basis points on original issue amount, due at closing and annually thereafter while bonds are outstanding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Borrower completes application and submits to the Montgomery County Department of Finance with a $5,000 non-refundable application fee (check made payable to Montgomery County) and all required materials, including IRS Determination Letter for non-profits, financial feasibility letter from underwriter, licensing documentation, letters of good standing, and any other required certifications. A copy is also submitted to County bond counsel. 2. Department of Finance reviews the application and requests a Letter of Intent from the borrower. County bond counsel drafts a County Council Resolution for acceptance. 3. Department of Finance holds a TEFRA (Tax Equity and Fiscal Responsibility Act) public hearing. After the hearing, the Department forwards its recommendation to the County Executive along with the Letter of Intent and Resolution. 4. If the County Executive accepts the Letter of Intent and Resolution, it is forwarded to the County Council for action. 5. County Council votes on the Resolution. The typical process takes approximately 6 weeks or longer depending on the County Council's agenda.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program from the City of Gaithersburg for businesses moving to or expanding within the City that have been in operation for two or more years. Provides matching grants for capital improvements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants provided by the City of Gaithersburg for capital improvements of businesses relocating or expanding within city limits.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in Gaithersburg with at least two years of operating history.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements and business expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Gaithersburg, Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be located in City of Gaithersburg
Business must have been in operation for two or more years

structured_extraction.program_name: Electric Leaf Blower Rebate Program (Incentive Program for Electric Leaf Removal Equipment)
structured_extraction.program_description: A time-limited rebate program administered by Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection to encourage residents and leaf removal businesses to transition from gasoline- or fuel-powered leaf blowers to electric equipment. Residents receive a $100 rebate per electric leaf blower purchase. Revenue qualifying businesses (less than $250,000 annual revenue or 5 or fewer employees) receive rebates up to $1,500 per 12-month period. Non-revenue qualifying businesses ($250,000 or more annual revenue or 6 or more employees) receive rebates up to $1,000 per 12-month period. The program runs through December 31, 2026, with no sunset date specified.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residents receive a $100 rebate per purchase (limited to one rebate per 12-month period). Revenue qualifying leaf removal businesses receive rebates up to $1,500 per 12-month period. Non-revenue qualifying leaf removal businesses receive rebates up to $1,000 per 12-month period. Rebates are limited to the cost of the eligible equipment listed in the application and are subject to availability of funds. Pre-approval from the Director is required prior to equipment purchase.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted by December 31, 2026; Comment deadline for regulation was January 31, 2024; Effective Date April 2, 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents and leaf removal businesses seeking to replace gasoline- or fuel-powered leaf removal equipment with electric models.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of electric leaf removal equipment including handheld, backpack, or walk-behind devices; battery-powered and corded leaf blowers; leaf vacuums; and batteries and chargers required to power such equipment.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot project created to help Montgomery County residents transition from fossil fuels (oil, gas, and propane) in their homes by providing a one-stop option for electrification. The program offers energy audits, electrification assessments, and direct financial incentives at the point of sale for replacing gas and oil appliances with electric alternatives. Electrify MC aims to help residents fully electrify their homes, including heating, cooling, hot water, cooking, and laundry appliances, while connecting them to additional utility rebates and weatherization resources through EmPOWER Maryland programs.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residents receive direct incentives applied at the point of sale for electrification work. Incentives range from $100 to $2,500 depending on the appliance: $250 for electric dryer installation, $500 for electric stove or heat pump water heater installation, $1,000 to $2,500 for heat pump heating systems (depending on type and efficiency tier), $200 for whole-house surge protector, $100 for single-appliance surge protector, $165 for natural gas line capping permit, and $500 for oil tank removal. Additional incentives are available through EmPOWER Maryland utility programs for insulation and weatherization work.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who own individually metered residences and want to transition from fossil fuels to electric heating, cooling, hot water, and cooking appliances.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support electrification of residential heating and cooling systems (heat pumps), water heaters, stoves, and dryers. Also covers electrical circuit installation, surge protectors, natural gas line capping, and oil tank removal when replacing fossil-fueled appliances.

Utilities must be individually metered

Electric appliances must meet minimum efficiency standards (CEE Tier 1 or ENERGY STAR where specified)
For heat pumps, fossil fuel heating cannot be retained (except where noted)
For mini-split heat pumps, must provide 50% or more of total heating load
All combustion appliances must be removed from kitchen when installing electric range/cooktop
Incentives cannot be received retroactively for work already completed
Residents must be enrolled in the program and sign the Montgomery County Electrify Everything Pledge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Electrify MC Help Desk by phone (301-830-5767) or email (electrifymc@elysianenergy.com). Sign up through the online form to receive a phone call and email from the Electrify MC team. Schedule an energy audit (part of EmPOWER Maryland program, costs $100). Complete audit and electrification assessment. Choose electrification options with Elysian Energy. Have work completed through Elysian Energy. Receive direct incentives at point of sale and utility rebates in 6-8 weeks.

structured_extraction.program_name: Emerging Business Improvement Districts Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A recurring annual grant program administered by Montgomery County that supports the development and establishment of Business Improvement Districts (BIDs) or Urban District Corporations (UDCs) in emerging commercial areas of Montgomery County. The program promotes economic development and community revitalization by providing funding for BID/UDC creation, planning, marketing, outreach, and related activities. The program has been offered in multiple fiscal years (FY23, FY24, FY25, FY26) and is expected to continue on an annual basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support the creation and development of Business Improvement Districts (BIDs) or Urban District Corporations (UDCs) in emerging commercial areas of Montgomery County. FY26: $300,000 total available funding with awards between $100,000 and $300,000 for up to 12 months, with possibility for renewal for up to three total years contingent on satisfactory performance and funds availability. FY25: $414,600 total available funding with awards between $100,000 and $300,000 for up to 12 months. Applicants may submit multi-year proposals (up to three years total). Eligible operating expenses include: administrative expenses for program managers and support staff, community or business outreach, expenses for determining the most beneficial commercial district management entity, implementation of neighborhood economic development activities, and neighborhood place making and place management. Ineligible expenses include: capital expenses ($5,000 or more for fixed assets), prior obligations, debts, fines, penalties, lobbying, and supplanting funds from other sources. Indirect costs up to 15% permitted (or organization's federal NICRA rate if applicable). Award notification letters typically released approximately one month after application deadline.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Monday, March 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM (FY26); Thursday, May 15, 2025, at 11:59 PM (FY25)
structured_extraction.contact_name: TJ Dant (Community Projects Manager, Community Engagement Cluster); Ali Hoy (Office of Grants Management)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations working towards becoming a Business Improvement District (BID) or Urban District Corporation (UDC). Direct target population includes organizations establishing BIDs/UDCs. Indirect target populations include businesses, organizations, and residents of Montgomery County benefiting from BID/UDC activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds support ongoing operational costs for Business Improvement District or Urban District Corporation development, including: administrative expenses for program managers and support staff; community and business outreach; expenses incurred in determining the most beneficial commercial district management entity; implementation of neighborhood economic development activities; neighborhood place making and place management; personnel costs; fringe benefits; travel; supplies; contractual services; and other project-related costs. All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and exclusively for Montgomery County residents, provided free of charge, and open to all residents regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, age, sex, marital status, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, family responsibility, genetic status, presence of children, or source of income.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County commercial areas. All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and be exclusively for Montgomery County residents. The organization's principal place of business must be located in Montgomery County; if a national or regional organization, must have a location in Montgomery County through which it provides related services.

Organization must be currently registered and in Good Standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Organization's principal place of business must be located in Montgomery County
All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County for Montgomery County residents only
Current Montgomery County contract or grant award winners must be in performance compliance and current on all reporting obligations with substantial progress towards award goals
Applicants may submit only one application per organization per NOFO

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register and create an account with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) Business Express and verify Good Standing status. 2. Register with Montgomery County Central Vendor Registration System (CVRS). 3. Create a profile on the Euna (eCivis) Grants online application platform at https://portal.ecivis.com/#/login. 4. Review the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and program resources. 5. Attend optional Information Session (virtual via MS Teams) to ask questions and receive guidance on application completion (FY26: February 9, 2026, 3:00-4:00 PM; FY25: April 21, 2025, 3:00-4:00 PM). 6. Access the FY26 (or applicable year) EBID Grant Program Solicitation page and click Apply button through the Euna portal. 7. Complete all application tasks in the online platform: Applicant Information (organization details, IRS 990 or exemption explanation), Applicant Background (optional race/ethnicity demographic data for leadership), Project Strategy (project title, overview, target zip codes, funding request amounts, narrative responses to 10 strategy questions), Project Work Plan/Timeline (objectives, activities, implementation timeline, staffing details), Memorandum of Understanding (if collaborative), Performance History and Performance Plan (milestones, KPIs, metrics), and Budget Tool with Budget Narrative (detailed Year 1 budget using pre-built form with eligible expense categories plus multi-year budget projections if applicable). 8. Submit complete application through the online platform before deadline (FY26: Monday, March 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM; FY25: Thursday, May 15, 2025 at 11:59 PM). 9. Applications undergo three-stage review: (a) OGM Administrative Review assessing organizational and Montgomery County eligibility conditions; (b) Programmatic Eligibility Review by Community Engagement Cluster assessing proposal eligibility; (c) Subject Matter Expert (SME) Review by qualified panel scoring proposals against weighted criteria. 10. Award notification letters released approximately one month after deadline. Successful applicants receive Grant Agreement with total amount awarded, funding restrictions, requirements, and payment terms.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Energy-Efficient Buildings Property Tax Credit is a two-tiered incentive program offering property tax credits for both new and existing energy-efficient commercial and multi-family buildings. For existing buildings, owners can receive up to 100% property tax credit against County taxes for two years following major energy efficiency improvements. The Tier 1 credit is calculated by subtracting the baseline ENERGY STAR score from the improved ENERGY STAR score and multiplied by a tier multiplier (1.0 to 2.5). The Tier 2 credit provides an additional 25% for LEED O+M Gold or BREEAM In-Use Excellent, or 50% for LEED O+M Platinum or BREEAM In-Use Outstanding. For newly constructed buildings, owners can receive up to 100% property tax credit against County taxes for four years (five years for Living Building Certification) for constructing buildings that exceed current building code requirements by at least 10%. The Tier 1 new construction credit ranges from 5–100% annually based on the percentage above code, multiplied by a credit factor (0.5–2.0). The Tier 2 new construction credit is 25% for LEED Gold, NGBS Gold, PHIUS+/Passive House, or BREEAM-NC Excellent, or 75% for LBC Petal Certification, LEED Platinum, NGBS Emerald, BREEAM-NC Outstanding, or Living Building Certification. Buildings located in Equity Emphasis Areas receive an additional 10% credit. Combined credits cannot exceed 100% per year.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to 100% property tax credit against Montgomery County taxes. For existing buildings: 2-year credit calculated by subtracting baseline ENERGY STAR score from improved score and multiplying by a tier multiplier (1.0–2.5); additional 25% credit for LEED O+M Gold or BREEAM In-Use Excellent, or 50% for LEED O+M Platinum or BREEAM In-Use Outstanding; buildings may apply up to 3 times total. For newly constructed buildings: 4-year credit (5 years for Living Building Certification) with no annual cap; Tier 1 credit of 5–100% annually based on percentage above code (10–20% above = 5–10%; 21–30% = 21–30%; 31–40% = 46.5–60%; above 40% = 82–100%); Tier 2 credit of 25% for LEED Gold, NGBS Gold, PHIUS+/Passive House, or BREEAM-NC Excellent, or 75% for LBC Petal Certification, LEED Platinum, NGBS Emerald, BREEAM-NC Outstanding, or Living Building Certification. Buildings in Equity Emphasis Areas receive an additional 10% credit. Combined credits cannot exceed 100% per year. A maximum of $5 million is allocated annually for property tax credits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; for existing buildings, improved ENERGY STAR score must be issued within 12 months of application; for new buildings, application must be submitted within 1 year of receiving use and occupancy permit
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of existing and newly constructed commercial and multi-family residential buildings with at least 10,000 square feet of gross floor area in Montgomery County, including developers seeking to reduce property tax liability through energy efficiency improvements or new energy-efficient construction.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces property tax liability for energy efficiency improvements to existing commercial and multi-family buildings, or for constructing new commercial and multi-family buildings that exceed current building code energy requirements. Credits apply directly against Montgomery County property taxes owed.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Buildings located in MWCOG Equity Emphasis Areas receive an additional 10% credit on top of the base credit amounts.

Building must be commercial or multi-family residential
At least 10,000 square feet of gross floor area
For existing buildings: received a Certificate of Occupancy from the Department of Permitting Services
For existing buildings: achieved at least 50% occupancy rate for at least 12 consecutive months
For existing buildings Tier 1: set a 12-month baseline in ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and demonstrated measurable reduction in energy use consistent with Montgomery County Code Section 52-103A

For existing buildings Tier 1: baseline and improved ENERGY STAR Scores must not be more than 6 calendar years apart
For existing buildings Tier 1: baseline ENERGY STAR Score 12-month period must not begin earlier than August 26, 2018
For existing buildings Tier 1: improved ENERGY STAR 12-month score cannot be issued more than 12 months before application date
For existing buildings Tier 1: ENERGY STAR Data Verification Checklists must be verified by a licensed Professional Engineer (PE) or Registered Architect (RA) in good standing
For existing buildings Tier 2: received LEED O+M, BREEAM In-Use, or equivalent certification
For existing buildings: documentation must include finalized Department of Permitting Services permit and vendor installation invoices

Existing buildings are eligible for a maximum of 3 applications (one initial and two reapplications); for reapplications, baseline ENERGY STAR score cannot be older than previous application's baseline score

For newly constructed buildings: certification from Department of Permitting Services within the last 12 months showing minimum 10% energy efficiency performance above current Building Code requirements
For newly constructed buildings: energy performance must be demonstrated by performance pathway validated by a DPS-stamped energy model
For newly constructed buildings: buildings that demonstrated code compliance via prescriptive pathway are not eligible
For newly constructed buildings: building has not previously received this credit
For newly constructed buildings Tier 2: received LEED, NGBS, PHIUS+/Passive House, BREEAM-NC, LBC Petal, or Living Building certification (obtained within 2 years of use and occupancy permit)
Building must meet energy efficiency standards consistent with applicable Montgomery County Code requirements

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For existing buildings: (1) Set a 12-month baseline using ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager; (2) Document energy conservation actions and installations with finalized Department of Permitting Services permit and vendor invoices; (3) Measure improved performance using Portfolio Manager; (4) Have ENERGY STAR Data Verification Checklists verified by a licensed Professional Engineer (PE) or Registered Architect (RA); (5) Submit application through the online SeamlessDocs portal. Existing building owners may reapply up to two additional times after the initial application. For Tier 2 existing buildings, obtain LEED O+M, BREEAM USA In-Use, or equivalent certification and include with submission. For newly constructed buildings: (1) Obtain Department of Permitting Services certification showing at least 10% energy efficiency above current Building Code requirements using the performance pathway with a DPS-stamped energy model; (2) For Tier 2, obtain LEED, NGBS, BREEAM-NC, or equivalent certification; (3) Submit application through the online SeamlessDocs portal within 1 year of receiving a use and occupancy permit. Applications are submitted through the County's seamless online application portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A ten-year real property tax credit for businesses that locate or expand in designated Enterprise Zones in Montgomery County, including downtown Silver Spring, Wheaton, Gaithersburg (Olde Towne), Takoma Park, and Long Branch. The credit is available only for nonresidential properties and is based on growth in property assessment after new construction or refurbishment. The credit percentage decreases over the 10-year period. The State of Maryland also provides a complementary income tax credit for qualifying new employees working in the zone.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Ten-year credit against real property taxes for nonresidential properties in designated Enterprise Zones, based on the increase in assessment compared to the base-year assessment (established before new construction or refurbishment). Credit schedule: Years 1–5 = 80% credit on taxes from assessment increase; Year 6 = 70%; Year 7 = 60%; Year 8 = 50%; Year 9 = 40%; Year 10 = 30%; then expires. Personal property is not included. The State also provides a credit against State income taxes for each employee working 25+ hours per week with 50%+ work time in the Zone: $3,000 first year and $2,000 second year for economically disadvantaged employees, or a $1,000 one-time credit for other employees.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Michael Parent (County credit); Peter McGinnity (Wheaton and Takoma Park/Long Branch administrators); Tom Lonergan (Gaithersburg)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses locating or expanding in designated Enterprise Zones in Montgomery County seeking to develop nonresidential properties through new construction or refurbishing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces real property tax liability resulting from increased property assessments due to new construction or property improvements within a designated Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available only for nonresidential properties within designated Enterprise Zones in Montgomery County, including downtown Silver Spring, Wheaton, Gaithersburg (Olde Towne), Takoma Park, and Long Branch.

Gaithersburg's Olde Towne Enterprise Zone is administered by the City of Gaithersburg (Tom Lonergan). For County credit inquiries, contact Michael Parent in the Department of Finance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A recurring grant program administered by Montgomery County that provides subsidized child care seats to make quality early childhood education and care more affordable and accessible for families in Montgomery County. The program has been offered in multiple fiscal years (FY24, FY25, FY27) and provides financial assistance to eligible child care providers to support subsidized seats for low- and moderate-income families. Program materials are available in both English and Spanish.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding provided to child care providers to support subsidized seats for infants and toddlers (age 6 weeks through 3 years). FY27 total pool: $2,075,059. Minimum award: $206,960 for centers and letter of compliance programs; $51,740 for family child care and large family child care programs. Funding covers full-day seat expenses at $25,870 per child per year ($6,467.50 quarterly). Centers and letter of compliance must apply for minimum 8 seats; family and large family child care must apply for minimum 2 seats. Funds cover all tuition expenses with no co-pay or additional costs to families. Multi-year proposals (3 years) accepted but funding beyond first 12 months contingent on performance and Council appropriations.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ali Hoy, Program Manager II (OGM) and Liran Laor, Program Manager II (DHHS Early Childhood Services)

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Full-day subsidized child care seats for infants and toddlers (age 6 weeks through 3 years); tuition and seat expenses; professional development for staff (up to 12 hours per year); program implementation and quality improvement

structured_extraction.program_description: Medical reimbursement program for active MCFRS volunteers who require follow-up medical testing recommended by Fire Rescue Occupational Medical Section (FROMS) when they have no health insurance or their insurance will not cover the costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County reimburses eligible volunteers up to $5,000 over the course of the collective bargaining agreement for follow-up medical testing costs when the volunteer has no health insurance or their insurance will not cover such costs. Reimbursement covers the cost of specialist testing recommended by FROMS. Reimbursement is processed within 10 business days of submission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active volunteers who are members of a local fire rescue department (LFRD) and have completed at least six months of service, and who require follow-up medical testing as determined by FROMS.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Follow-up medical testing and specialist services recommended by Fire Rescue Occupational Medical Section (FROMS) based on conditions discovered during annual physicals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an active volunteer member of an LFRD who has completed at least six months of service

Follow-up testing must be required by MCFRS based on conditions discovered during annual physical provided by FROMS
Volunteer must have no health insurance or insurance that does not cover the follow-up testing
Volunteer must attest to lack of insurance coverage and provide documentation establishing lack of coverage
Must utilize the services of the provider recommended by FROMS, if any
Reimbursement cannot exceed $5,000 over the course of the agreement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the following documents to michael.kelley@montgomerycountymd.gov and CC satchel.kornfeld@montgomerycountymd.gov: (1) a document from FROMS stating that a specialist is needed, (2) copy of medical invoice or statement showing amount and proof of payment, and (3) a statement from the member attesting that the amount paid is not covered by insurance or that they have no insurance. Allow up to 10 business days for processing.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY23 Nonprofit Technical Assistance and Management Support Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports nonprofit organizations through technical assistance and management support services to strengthen organizational capacity and effectiveness. The program provides unrestricted funds to enhance core capacity, infrastructure, and support functions that result in improved overall performance of organizations and their programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unrestricted grant funding to support nonprofit organizations through technical assistance and management support. FY23 awards provided $5,244.00 per organization. Award amounts typically range from a minimum of $5,000 to a maximum of $75,000, with up to $10,000 allowable for capital expenses. Funds are distributed as a full upfront payment (100% of award amount) upon execution of the grant agreement, with a 12-month spending period. Operating expenses may include leadership development, back-office support, audits, insurance, advocacy, fundraising, consulting services, staff training, and IT licenses. Capital expenses (limited to $10,000) may include computers, equipment, furniture, and minor facility improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations in Montgomery County serving or advocating for underserved communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Unrestricted funds for enhancing organizational core capacity, infrastructure, and support functions. Eligible uses include leadership and organizational development, back-office support functions (human resources, accounting, IT support), independent audits, liability insurance, advocacy and outreach activities, fundraising, professional memberships, IT licenses and software, consulting services for finance/legal/IT/HR/data analysis/program design/fundraising, staff training and tuition, and capital expenses for equipment and facilities (up to $10,000). Funds cannot be used for new or expanded programs, lobbying, pre-award expenses, or to supplant other funding sources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County. All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County. For national or regional organizations, principal place of business or a location must be in Montgomery County and funds must support Montgomery County staff/operations only.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY23 Strengthening Support to Migrant and Asylum-Seeking Residents Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports organizations providing services and support to migrant and asylum-seeking residents of Montgomery County. The program aims to support and strengthen culturally and linguistically proficient services to bolster service delivery to new Montgomery County migrant populations by providing grants to small and emerging organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding from a total pool of $200,000. Award sizes vary with at least two awards. The minimum grant award that will be considered for any applicant is $50,000 and the maximum grant award considered will be $100,000. The grant will be awarded for up to one year (12-month performance period). All grant agreements must be finalized by June 30, 2023. Funds are provided on a reimbursement or fixed schedule basis after sufficient documentation is submitted to the administering County agency. Funds must be spent after the contract is finalized and a Notice to Proceed is secured.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ali Hoy, Outgoing Grants Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and emerging nonprofit organizations (annual budget within $250,000-$500,000) in Montgomery County providing direct services to recently arrived migrant and asylum-seeking individuals and families
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Culturally and linguistically proficient direct service delivery to migrants and their families; training for provider organizations that will strengthen the organization's capability to respond to needs for services. Specifically, support for: obtaining stable housing, immigration-related legal support, and employment supports. Funding cannot be used for lobbying, expenses made prior to grant award, to supplant funds from other grant sources, or to provide services that wholly occur outside of Montgomery County.

Eligible capital expenses include accessible transportation services, purchase or retrofit of wheelchair accessible vehicles, purchase of traditional sedans for target populations, and purchase of vehicles for food access and other safety net services. County funding cannot be used to supplant other funding for already planned services. Funds must be spent after the contract is finalized and a Notice to Proceed is secured.
