The initial performance period is 12 months, with the possibility of multi-year funding up to three years contingent on satisfactory program performance and future Council appropriations. Indirect costs are permitted at a maximum rate of 15%. Operating expenses are covered, including staff salaries, contract trainers, materials and supplies, liability insurance, transportation costs, entrance or usage fees, rent or lease costs for space, minor equipment or electronics, software licenses or services, tuition or training/course fees, and other expenses required to implement the proposed project. structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports community organizations and nonprofit initiatives serving residents of Montgomery County. The program provides funding for unique, innovative programs to cover special community needs not otherwise addressed by other County funding or efforts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for community organizations and nonprofit initiatives. FY24 funding totals $5.75 million. Applicants may request funding between $50,000 and $375,000. The performance period is January 1, 2024 to December 31, 2024. Applicants may submit multi-year funding proposals of up to three (3) years, with funding beyond the first 12 months contingent on satisfactory project performance and future Council appropriations. Programs may include workforce development, job training, vocational services, internships, case management, academic development programs, after-school educational activities, tutoring, college preparation, STEM training, substance abuse prevention and treatment, wellness, leadership development, mentoring, social programs, accessible sports programs, advocacy, civic engagement, community coalition building, and basic needs support for vulnerable populations. Up to 10% of total project value may be used for capital expenses. Indirect costs may be included using the applicant's federal Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA) if available, or up to 15% if not. Funds cannot be used for lobbying, expenses incurred prior to grant award, replacing other funding sources, or services wholly occurring outside Montgomery County.

Organizations must be registered and in Good Standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT).

Projects may fund community improvement initiatives, organizational operations, community-serving programs, and innovative approaches to address community needs not otherwise addressed by County funding. Eligible expenses include program staffing, direct services, operational costs, and up to 10% for capital expenses required for project implementation.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY24 Community Projects Fund Grant Program

The program provides $1 million in one-time funding across four quarters with at least $250,000 available in each cycle.

Award amounts range from $5,000 to $25,000 minimum per application. At least $250,000 is available in each quarterly cycle. Q2 also includes an additional $100,000 from the Department of Health and Human Services for the Fentanyl Use, Overdose, and Death Reduction Grant Program with four $25,000 awards available for up to one year performance periods. Funds support new initiatives, project expansions, or combinations thereof but cannot be used to expand existing County-funded programs or supplant other funding sources.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit complete applications online through SM Apply platform at https://mcmdgrants.smapply.org/. Applicants must create an account, select the FY24 Community Projects Fund Grants Program, and complete all application tasks. Application tasks include: Applicant Information (Reusable Task with organization details and supporting documents), Applicant Background (Reusable Task for demographic data), Project Strategy (1-page narrative addressing target population, community needs, organizational capabilities, funding impact, and partnership details if applicable), Project Budget (itemized costs in MS Excel format), Budget Narrative/Justification (1-page explanation of expenditures and cost-share sources), Project Work Plan/Timeline (1-page implementation schedule with objectives, activities, timeline, and responsible staff), Performance Plan (1-page outline of success measurement and outcome metrics), and Optional Supporting Documents. All documents should be submitted as PDFs except budgets (MS Excel). Information sessions are held prior to each deadline to provide guidance. Applications must be complete and submitted by deadline; incomplete or late applications will not be accepted. An independent Review Committee scores applications based on five criteria: Project Goals and Grant Program Priorities (20 points), Sound Fiscal Management and Budget (15 points), Organizational Capability and Relevant Experience (35 points), Performance Plan (10 points), and Soundness of Overall Proposal (20 points). Award notifications released approximately one month after deadline via email.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports transportation and mobility initiatives that improve access to services and opportunities for residents of Montgomery County, specifically targeting disabled individuals, seniors, individuals with limited incomes, and other vulnerable populations in underserved communities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding totaling $800,000 ($640,000 for capital expenses and $160,000 for operating expenses) distributed through approximately 8-10 awards ranging from $20,000 to $105,000. Capital expenses are limited to $65,000 maximum per applicant and operating expenses to $40,000 maximum per applicant. Eligible capital expenses include purchase or retrofit of wheelchair accessible vehicles, multi-passenger vans, or adaptable vehicles. Eligible operating expenses include vehicle maintenance, fuel, insurance, salaries/stipends for transportation providers, and ride-hailing gift cards. Awards are cost reimbursable with payments made within 30 calendar days of receipt and approval of financial reports. Grant duration is 12 months with estimated start date of March 1, 2024.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations providing transportation, public health, and community benefit services to disabled individuals, seniors 63 years and older, individuals with limited incomes aged 18-62, and other vulnerable populations in Montgomery County, particularly in underserved communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation services and improvements including: purchase or retrofit of wheelchair accessible vehicles; purchase of multi-passenger vans; vehicle maintenance, fuel, insurance and operational fees; salaries and stipends for transportation providers; ride-hailing service gift cards (Uber, Lyft); and programs that increase access to transportation for target populations in underserved communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County OR be exclusively for Montgomery County residents if activities occur outside the County. For example, transporting a senior from Silver Spring to a medical appointment in Baltimore is eligible, but transportation services occurring wholly outside Montgomery County are not eligible.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted through the Montgomery County Office of Grants Management online grants application portal (https://mcmdgrants.smapply.org/). Applicants must create an SM Apply account and select the FY24 Enhanced Mobility Grants Program to access the application. The application consists of the following tasks: (1) Applicant Information - organization legal name, SDAT ID, Tax ID, CVRS ID, mission statement, contact information, grant/financial management practices, data collection practices, and uploads of IRS tax exempt determination letter, most recent 990 form, current board list, and optional audit reports; (2) Applicant Background - optional racial and ethnic information on organizational leadership; (3) Project Narrative - project title, overview, location, target populations served, service/project description, alignment with funding priorities, target population demographics, language capacity, proposed outcomes, and organizational capacity (2 page limit); (4) Outreach Plan - methods for reaching target audience, key messages, media support, and engagement tracking (1 page limit); (5) Project Budget - itemized capital and operating expenses in MS Excel format with supporting documentation; (6) Budget Narrative/Justification - explanation of proposed expenditures, cost calculations, experience with cost reimbursable awards, impact of funding reductions, and information on regional work/other funding sources (1 page limit); (7) Project Work Plan/Timeline - program objectives, activities, implementation timeline, and responsible staff over 12-month period (1 page limit); (8) Performance Plan - metrics including total trips provided and individuals served with collection methods and targets (1 page limit); (9) Optional Supporting Documents. An information session was held November 20, 2023. Award notification letters expected approximately one month after deadline. Applications received after the deadline will be disqualified. Applicants needing ADA accommodations should contact Office of Grants Management.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that supports outreach and enrollment assistance for SNAP and other nutrition benefits programs to increase participation among eligible residents, specifically targeting Montgomery County families with children ages zero (0) to five (5) who are eligible but not yet enrolled in SNAP benefits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding ranging from $20,000 to $100,000 (with final award amounts potentially lower than $20,000). Total funding available: $200,000. Performance period: March 15, 2024 through March 15, 2025 (12 months). Funds support SNAP outreach and enrollment assistance including dedicated staff, training and technical assistance for partners, creation of outreach materials, and other related operating expenses. Eligible activities include: training community partners on SNAP eligibility and enrollment processes; creating and distributing information resources (digital or hard copy materials); direct outreach to and engagement with residents; and support of SNAP and nutrition assistance applications that are new, in progress, or in recertification.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by Montgomery County that awards funding to community-based nonprofit organizations to implement innovative approaches to reach and provide enrollment support to Montgomery County families who are eligible but not actively enrolled in SNAP and other federal and state-level nutrition benefits programs, including WIC, SUN Bucks, Free and Reduced Price Meals, and WIC/Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Programs. The program operates on a multi-year cycle with potential renewal for up to three years (through May 31, 2028) pending successful performance outcomes and grant administration compliance.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding ranging from $50,000 to $150,000 for innovative outreach and enrollment assistance approaches. Year one (FY25) awarded approximately $304,000–$306,000 in total funding to six state-designated SNAP Community-Based Organizations for the performance period June 1, 2025–May 31, 2026. Year two and beyond provides renewal funding (up to $300,000 total) to grantees that maintain compliance and achieve successful performance outcomes, with potential for additional one-year renewal periods through May 31, 2028. Funds support staffing, program expenses, outreach events, enrollment assistance, training, referral coordination, transportation, and operating costs. Applicants without a federal Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA) may include up to 15% for indirect costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: State-designated SNAP Community-Based nonprofit organizations in Montgomery County with primary service area in Montgomery County, working to reach families with children eligible for SNAP and other nutrition benefits programs. Year two and subsequent funding is available to prior-year grantees that have maintained compliance and achieved successful performance outcomes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Implementation of innovative outreach approaches, enrollment support, benefits navigation, nutrition education, trainings, capacity building, referral coordination, and administrative support to connect Montgomery County residents (particularly families with children) eligible for but not actively enrolled in SNAP, WIC, SUN Bucks, Free and Reduced Price Meals, WIC/Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Programs, MC Groceries Program, and other food and non-food income supports. Eligible expenses include staffing and fringe costs, outreach events, transportation, training, resource development, room rentals, and indirect administrative costs.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Community Food Assistance (CFA) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides direct funding to food assistance provider organizations and food recovery organizations to address food insecurity in Montgomery County. The program supports the purchase and distribution of shelf-stable food, fresh food, and prepared meals to residents experiencing food insecurity, as well as food recovery operations including recovering, handling, and redistributing surplus food. Organizations must deliver regularly scheduled, no-cost food services to Montgomery County residents at County-based sites at least once per month, and must have been providing such services for a minimum of one year. The program also funds capacity building for the County's network of community partners and prioritizes underresourced ZIP codes, home delivery models, services to immigrant and unhoused residents, and high-performing returning grantees. Recipients are expected to collectively recover and redistribute more than 10 million pounds of food annually. In FY25, $3,699,500 was awarded across 49 organizations; in FY26, $3.5 million is allocated for community-based food distribution and $428,202 was awarded to six organizations for food recovery services. The program also includes a $1.9 million Special Appropriation expansion distributed to 53 nonprofit providers.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct cash grants to nonprofit food assistance provider organizations and food recovery organizations. FY26 funding allocation: $3.5 million for community-based food distribution grants to multiple organizations, $428,202 awarded to six food recovery organizations (comprised of $290,785 in renewable FY26 CFA funding and $137,417 from FY26 Special Appropriation passed November 18, 2025), and $1.9 million in expanded grants distributed to 53 nonprofit providers through Special Appropriation. Award amounts range from $5,000 to $300,000, with final awards potentially lower than $5,000. Grants support: direct food purchases through retailers, wholesalers, distributors, and producers; pre-packed produce boxes; Staples Program credits through Manna Food Center and Capital Area Food Bank; operational costs (staffed, supplies, location, transportation, indirect expenses) capped at 15% of total requested budget. Organizations may also receive credits to order produce, shelf-stable products, and nutritious food items through bulk-food purchasing partnerships. Organizations receiving awards of $49,999 or less receive single up-front payment; awards of $50,000+ distributed in two installments (half at start, half after successful performance during first two quarters). Priority given to underresourced ZIP codes, home delivery models, services to immigrant and unhoused residents, food recovery operations, high-performing returning grantees, organizations supporting local food economy through purchasing from County farms and DMV businesses owned by underserved communities, participant choice models, organizations leveraging additional resources, and those committing to edible food diversion assessments and peer learning participation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY26 community-based food distribution grant program launched July 2025 (anticipated early August 2025); new food recovery grant applications expected fall 2026; rolling/ongoing program with regular annual cycles
structured_extraction.contact_name: Heather Bruskin; Catherine Nardi (Program Manager, OFSR)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit food assistance provider organizations and food recovery organizations serving Montgomery County residents experiencing food insecurity, including those operating food pantries, prepared meal programs, home delivery services, and food recovery/redistribution operations. Target populations: Montgomery County households in underserved communities experiencing or at risk of experiencing food insecurity, including approximately 110,000 children living in households with incomes below self-sufficiency standards (below 400% of Federal Poverty Line).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase and distribution of shelf-stable food, fresh food, and prepared meals to Montgomery County residents experiencing food insecurity; food recovery operations including recovering, handling, and redistributing surplus food; capacity building for community partners; food distribution through pantries, prepared meals, and home delivery; services to specific populations including immigrants and unhoused individuals; wholesale or retail food sourcing; bulk-food purchasing through partnerships with Manna Food Center and Capital Area Food Bank; staffing for food assistance programs; supplies including boxes, bags, PPE, packaging; location costs (rent, utilities); transportation (gas, rental); indirect operational expenses (accounting, IT). Allowable programming models include: choice pantry model offering variety of culturally relevant healthy shelf-stable and fresh food items (fruits, vegetables, dairy, meat, eggs); pre-packed box/bag distribution with healthy locally sourced produce; delivery and distribution of nutritious medically and/or preference-tailored prepared meals. Grant funding CANNOT be used for: gift cards, capital expenses (one-time purchases of infrastructure/equipment), purchases already made, purchases or activities unnecessary to accomplish grant purposes, prior obligations/fines, debts and penalties, lobbying expenses, alcoholic beverages, or supplanting (replacing) other funds.

Organizations must have principal place of business in Montgomery County; if national or regional organization, must have location in Montgomery County through which related services are provided.

Priority for organizations operating participant choice model for food access
Priority for organizations leveraging additional resources (in-kind contributions, organizational investment, non-county public dollars, secured outside grants)
Priority for organizations committing to participate in Edible Food Diversion assessment with Montgomery County Department of Environmental Protection
Priority for organizations committing to regular participation in Food Assistance Provider peer learning circle (approximately 2 hours per month)
Priority for organizations demonstrating cultural competency and strong understanding of community food access needs
For award of $20,001+, must provide unduplicated household data or performance plan to collect and track unduplicated data by end of grant period

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications submitted through online Montgomery County Office of Grants Management Grants Application Platform (https://mcmdgrants.smapply.org and program page https://mcmdgrants.smapply.org/prog/FY25CFA). Applicants must create SMApply account, select FY26 Community Food Assistance Program, and complete comprehensive application. FY26 community-based food distribution grants launched July 2025 with anticipated early August 2025 launch. Application includes: Applicant Information (legal name, SDAT ID, tax ID, CVRS Vendor ID, mission, contact info, grant/financial management practices, data management practices); required document uploads (IRS Tax Exempt Determination Letter, most recent 990 Form or exemption explanation, current NICRA if applicable, board list with names/affiliation/contact, public copy of most recent independent audit or financial review, optional recent organizational reports); Applicant Background (optional for post-award analysis); Food Security Program Overview (current budget, previous fiscal year budget to actuals, service formats, food types, frequency, ZIP codes served, average households served monthly, cultural/medical diet accommodation, distribution day/time/location, eligibility criteria); Project Strategy (project title, detailed 100-word project overview, grant request amounts itemized by funding category, current board-approved budget upload, food assistance services start date, total average individual services delivered per month, additional ZIP codes with capacity, capacity for unduplicated data collection, program commitments with checkboxes including Edible Food Diversion assessment participation and peer learning circle participation, detailed 250-word narrative on service delivery logistics including participant outreach/recruitment, food sourcing strategy, tailoring to preferences/dietary needs, nutritional guidelines, external benefits/referrals, 250-word narrative on underserved populations/communities to be supported and outreach strategies, 100-word goals for coming year compared to prior year including anticipated operational changes, 100-word description of resources informing program development, 250-word narrative on relationship with demographic/geographic community and how community insight informs planning, 100-word description of cultural/linguistic/technical proficiency capability, 250-word explanation of unique organizational strengths and partner collaborations, narrative on organizational/program alignment with OFSR values, optional 250-word long-term goals narrative, optional 100-word description of resources needed outside grant); Program Budget (MS Excel format using required Budget Template showing itemized expenses for food sourcing and operational costs, other revenues including in-kind resources and leveraged funding, with detailed justification on second template tab), and Budget Narrative (500-word narrative on expenditure purpose and cost calculations, 250-word description of project impact if funding reduced, 500-word narrative on budget alignment with current service levels and cost efficiency strategies, 250-word narrative if services outside Montgomery County describing how to ensure exclusive benefit to County residents); Performance Plan (2-page PDF outlining measurement, data collection, and metric tracking). Applications requiring ADA accommodation should contact OGM. Incomplete applications not accepted. Review Committee composed of neutral qualified individuals from Montgomery County and broader community scores applications based on stated criteria and submits funding recommendations. Final awards decided by County based on scores and other factors. Award notification letters released via email approximately one month after deadline. For successful applicants, Grant Agreement contains total awarded amount, funding restrictions, programmatic/administrative/policy requirements, reporting requirements, payment terms. All awardees required to submit monthly Service Data Reports (12 total) and Quarterly Narrative and Financial Reports (4 total) through OFSR online reporting platform (https://bit.ly/FY26_CFA) following specified schedule (reports due by 30th or end of month following end of quarter). Reporting metrics vary by award amount: awards $20,000 or less require basic duplicated household counts, direct food purchase tracking, operational cost documentation; awards $20,001-$49,999 require unduplicated household data by ZIP code; awards $50,000-$100,000 require demographic breakdown by ZIP code/household size plus food distribution amounts by type; awards $100,001+ require most detailed reporting including demographics by age (children, seniors). Food recovery grantees submit additional metrics on recovered food pounds, recovery runs with details, DMV sourcing percentages, and in-kind resource values. All grantees conduct annual satisfaction surveys and provide documentation photos/materials for OFSR communications.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY26 Food Recovery Network Coordination Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by Montgomery County that supports the design, implementation, and ongoing coordination of a centralized Montgomery County Food Recovery Network. The program funds organizations to rescue and redistribute excess food from farms, retailers, and food service establishments to people facing food insecurity. It is designed to improve efficiency, streamline operations, and boost resource sharing within the local Food Recovery Network by convening food recovery organizations, facilitating data and resource sharing, and identifying opportunities for collaboration and efficiency across programs. Historically, the program has awarded funds (e.g., $30,000) to entities such as the Montgomery County Food Council to serve as the primary coordinating organization for the County's Food Recovery Collaborative, strengthening partnerships across the County's food system. The FY26 program will fund one eligible nonprofit organization with a single grant of $125,000 to design, implement, and coordinate a centralized network of food recovery organizations, including all FRNI and CFA food recovery grantees.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A single grant for a total of $125,000 will be made available to fund one award to an eligible nonprofit organization. The grant has a 12-month performance period from on/about September 30, 2025 through September 30, 2026. Grant funding supports the design, implementation, and ongoing coordination of a centralized Montgomery County Food Recovery Network. Eligible uses include: staffing and coordinator positions; design and implementation of a centralized network; organizing convenings and regular community of practice gatherings with food recovery partners; facilitating data and resource sharing through technology platforms for logistics coordination and communication; identifying opportunities for collaboration and efficiency; providing technical assistance and training to network members on operational topics such as food safety, organics waste management, and relationship management; recruiting and retaining new food recovery donor partners; developing strategies to address logistical challenges including pick-up, storage, and redistribution coordination; leveraging existing partnerships and structures to increase resources; identifying cost-savings opportunities through collective purchasing and discount negotiation; and developing and distributing educational and communications materials for diverse audiences including food donors, network members, and food assistance recipients. Budget requests should focus on operational costs such as staffing, print/communications materials, and technology investments. Capital costs (infrastructure, equipment) are not eligible. Indirect costs up to 15% are permitted. Grant funding cannot be used for prior obligations, fines, debts, penalties, lobbying, alcoholic beverages, or supplanting other funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible nonprofit organizations capable of coordinating and managing a food recovery network that: demonstrate experience in coordinating community partners; have working knowledge of the food recovery landscape in the DMV region; do not directly distribute recovered food; and are registered and in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). Organizations must have their principal place of business located in Montgomery County or, if a national or regional organization, must have a location in Montgomery County through which they provide related services. Examples of eligible applicants include the Montgomery County Food Council and other food recovery coordination organizations seeking to improve coordination, collaboration, and distribution capacity across Montgomery County's food recovery network.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Coordination and management of the Food Recovery Network, including: design and implementation of a centralized network; identifying and engaging food recovery network member organizations; establishing consensus-based formal network member agreements; organizing regular community of practice gatherings and other communication pathways; providing regular technical assistance and training on operational topics (food safety, organics waste management, communications, relationship management); implementing and utilizing technology platforms for logistics coordination, communication, and resource sharing; supporting network member compliance with data collection and reporting requirements; administering formal and informal feedback loops with network members; designing and implementing strategies to address logistical challenges including pick-up, storage, and redistribution coordination; developing equitable and efficient systems for sharing infrastructure and resources; recruiting and retaining new food recovery donor partners including institutions, commercial-scale producers, and specialty food sources; developing strategies to increase shared-use cold storage, refrigerated vehicles, and dry-storage space; leveraging existing local, statewide, regional, and national food recovery partnerships; increasing non-County funding and in-kind resources; identifying cost-savings opportunities through collective purchasing and competitive pricing research; developing and distributing educational and communications materials for food donors, network organizations, and food assistance recipients on food safety, donation guidelines, storage of potentially hazardous foods, and community benefits of recovered food.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Create an account and log into the Euna (eCivis) Portal at https://portal.ecivis.com/#/login. 2. Access the FY27 CSP Grant Program Solicitation Page at https://gn.ecivis.com/GO/gn_redir/T/4iv2ovv23l69 and click the 'Apply' button. 3. Complete all required application tasks: (A) Applicant Information with contact information for two different people; (B) Applicant Background including optional demographic data; (C) Proposal PDF with narrative responses addressing background/justification, organizational capacity, financial capacity, project plan, coordination/integration, engagement with schools/families/communities, measurable outcomes, and prior grant performance (for current providers); (D) Implementation Timeline using the FY26 CHRC Grant Program Activities Template (Excel) detailing all funded activities with timeline, frequency, target served, outcome, and intended impact; (E) Budget using the Euna Grants Budget Tool with line items and narrative explanation (8,000 characters max) for each cost; (F) Ignore the Goals Tool. 4. Submit completed application by January 6, 2026 at 11:59 PM through the online portal. 5. Applications undergo three review stages: OGM Administrative Review (Montgomery County Eligibility Conditions), Programmatic Eligibility Review by HHS, and Subject Matter Expert (SME) Review using a Confidence Rating system. Reviewers score against weighted criteria totaling 100 points. 6. OGM will contact applicants with brief window (usually two business days) to resolve minor errors. Major issues or Montgomery County Eligibility Condition issues generally cannot be remedied. 7. Upon selection, grant agreements are drafted (March-April 2026) and executed by May-June 2026, with service delivery beginning July 1, 2026. Applicants can attend information sessions on November 25, 2025 (3:00-4:30 PM) or December 18, 2025 (12:30-2:00 PM) for additional guidance. Technical support is available from OGM (grants@montgomerycountymd.gov, 240-773-3384) for platform issues and from Sara Rose (sara.rose@montgomerycountymd.gov, 240-777-1400) for programmatic questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: FareShare is a commuter benefits matching program administered by Montgomery County that encourages private employers to provide transit and vanpool subsidies to their employees. The county reimburses employers for contributions above a minimum threshold of $25 per employee per month, up to the federal maximum of $325 per month (as of January 1, 2025), helping reduce traffic congestion, support clean air goals, and save employees money on their commute. The program is designed to help employers test and establish sustainable commuter benefit programs, with a maximum reimbursement of $40,000 per year to any single employer. Employees receive enhanced transit and vanpool benefits on a tax-free basis and do not need to live in Montgomery County to participate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County reimburses employers for transit subsidy contributions to employees above a minimum $25 per employee per month, up to a maximum of $325 per employee per month (as of January 1, 2025). County reimbursement is up to $300 less the $25 required employer contribution per employee per month, with a maximum of $40,000 in reimbursement per year to any single employer. Employees receive transit subsidies up to $325 per month on a tax-free basis. Employers are also eligible for a Maryland State tax credit of 50% of their contribution, up to a maximum of $100 per employee per month. This program is intended to help employers with start-up costs and to incorporate commuter benefits costs into their budgeting, not to provide ongoing County subsidy indefinitely. FareShare is offered on a first-come, first-served basis and is contingent upon availability of funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private employers (for-profit and non-profit) in Montgomery County that want to provide transit and vanpool benefits to employees, and their employees. Employees do not have to live in Montgomery County to participate as long as their employer is located in Montgomery County. Public sector employers and employees are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employee transit and vanpool commuting costs, provided as tax-free direct benefits. Employers can offer benefits to help with employee commuting expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Employers must be located in Montgomery County, Maryland. Employees must work for an employer in Montgomery County but may live anywhere. Public sector employers and employees are not eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a private (non-public) employer in Montgomery County
Non-profit employers are eligible; public sector employers are not eligible
Employer must offer a transit benefit to employees
Minimum $25 contribution per employee per month required to receive county reimbursement
Total benefit provided to any employee cannot exceed their actual commuting cost
Maximum county reimbursement is $40,000 per year to any single employer
Maximum benefit offered per employee per month is $325 (as of January 1, 2025)
Employer must participate in the FareShare Program for employees to receive benefits
Employers encouraged to set maximum subsidy at a level their organization can sustain after county match ends
Public sector employees are ineligible
Employers must conduct a pre-program survey of employees at the worksite prior to implementation of the FareShare program
Employers are expected to participate in subsequent Commuter Surveys every other year to evaluate impact on employee commuting choice
Employers must use best efforts to achieve a survey response rate acceptable to the County
Program is contingent upon availability of funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers interested in joining FareShare should contact Commuter Services at 240-773-BWTW (2989) or mcdot.CommuterServices@montgomerycountymd.gov. If the employer does not currently offer a direct transit/vanpool benefit, Commuter Services will assist them in starting a commuter benefits program. MCDOT marketing specialists will visit the employer's office free of charge to help set up a customized commuting benefits program. Employers complete the FareShare Employer Enrollment Form and submit it along with the Montgomery County Employer Worksheet Invoice and the WMATA SmartBenefits Order Confirmation Form to the Commuter Services representative for processing and reimbursement from the County. Employees can ask their employer to download the FareShare brochure or contact MCDOT directly at 240-773-2989 or mcdot.CommuterServices@montgomerycountymd.gov.

structured_extraction.program_name: Fentanyl Use, Overdose, and Death Reduction (FUODR) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A recurring grant program administered by Montgomery County's Department of Health and Human Services that aims to reduce the number of persons using, overdosing, and dying from fentanyl in Montgomery County, Maryland. The program supports initiatives and organizations addressing fentanyl-related overdoses and deaths through prevention, harm reduction, treatment, and recovery support services. Funded through Opioid Abatement Funds, the program has awarded grants in FY24, FY25, and anticipates launching FY26 funding in April 2026.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Department of Health and Human Services allocates Opioid Abatement Funds for this program. For FY25, $100,000 has been allocated with up to 2 one-time awards ranging from a minimum of $50,000 to a maximum of $100,000 per award. Grant funding supports programs addressing fentanyl overdose prevention, harm reduction, treatment, and recovery support services. Applicants may submit multiple applications per organization, however only one award per organization may be awarded. The grant award period is up to one year, with implementation starting no earlier than June 1, 2025. Grant funds cannot be used for direct transfer to participants, capital expenditures exceeding $5,000, lobbying, or to supplant other funding sources.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations with Federal 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status (or 501(c)(6) commercial nonprofits) offering substance use services, harm reduction, and overdose prevention in Montgomery County. Organizations must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) with principal place of business in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prevention education activities (in-person or virtual), harm reduction services, naloxone distribution, treatment programs, recovery support, tuition support for after-school and camp programs, youth outreach programs, parent and caregiver workshops, community events, stipends for peer support and community service workers, online outreach and social media campaigns, educational workshops and presentations, public awareness campaigns, and small incentives to participate in drug-free programs (gift cards, rewards, certificates). Funds cannot be used for direct cash transfers to participants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and be exclusively for Montgomery County residents. Organizations serving most highly impacted populations in zip codes 20910, 20860, 20912, 20877, and 20842 will be prioritized, though countywide activities are eligible.

All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and be exclusively for Montgomery County residents
Current Montgomery County contract or grant award winners must be in performance compliance and current on all reporting obligations

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Create an account on the Euna Grants (eCivis) application platform at https://portal.ecivis.com/#/login. 2. Access the FY25 FUODR grant program page at https://gn.ecivis.com/GO/gn_redir/T/1svsfn9d4deku and click the Apply button. 3. Complete all required application tasks: Applicant Information Form (organization details and supporting documents), Applicant Background (organizational demographics), Project Strategy (project overview, zip codes, and narrative responses to 8 strategy questions), Funding Request and Financial Form (budget details and financial management practices), Project Work Plan/Timeline (12-month implementation schedule with objectives, activities, timeline, and responsible staff), Performance Plan (milestones, KPIs, data collection methods, and evaluation approach), and Budget Tool with detailed Budget Narrative. 4. Submit completed application through the online portal by the deadline. 5. Attend optional Information Session on Friday April 18, 2025, from 2:30-3:30 PM for detailed guidance. 6. Organizations receiving awards will be notified via email approximately one to two months after the deadline. 7. Award recipients must provide two reports during implementation (progress report midway through and final report) including success stories, challenges, lessons learned, zip code data, KPI metrics, participant demographics, qualitative evaluation data, participant testimonials, and budget reconciliation. Site visits may occur with 48-hour notice.

structured_extraction.program_name: Fiscal Year 2022 Community Services Grants Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services provides grants to community organizations for health and human services. This program supports nonprofits and community groups delivering services in the county. The Community Services Grants program provides one-time only grants to non-profit organizations serving Montgomery County residents for approved equipment and other capital purchases.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $10,000 per organization to support health and human service projects. Grants are one-time only and provide reimbursement to funded organizations for approved equipment and other capital purchases including capital improvements and their associated delivery and setup costs. Funded projects and expenditures must occur between July 1, 2021 and June 30, 2022. Grants are distributed via reimbursement upon receipt of proof of payment and required documentation verifying the purchase of approved items. Only one application per organization per grant period is permitted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and agencies incorporated under 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code providing health and human services activities in Montgomery County. Organizations that have not received funding for the last three years will be given priority.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements, equipment, technology improvements, and goods for health and human services programs. Funds must be used for approved equipment and other capital purchases. Vehicles, salaries, conferences, training costs not related to equipment purchases, funds to apply to deficits and losses in other funding sources, personnel expenses, and non-local travel are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Grants will be awarded for projects implemented in Montgomery County only. Organizations must operate in and provide direct service to residents of Montgomery County. Organizations may have headquarters and/or administrative offices outside of Montgomery County so long as they demonstrate that client populations to be served reside in Montgomery County.

Applicant must offer health and human services activities consistent with stated outcomes

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be typed and submitted on the appropriate forms with all required attachments. All applications must be sent electronically on or before April 7, 2021 to Community.ServicesGrants@montgomerycountymd.gov. Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant without consideration. Applications will be subject to an initial acceptance review for completeness, legibility, clarity, compliance with guidelines, and fiscal accuracy. A Grants Review Panel including public and private representatives will review applications based on evaluation criteria. The Review Panel will present recommendations to the Montgomery County Executive, who determines final approval based on availability of funds. Final determination of awards is subject to County Council approval during its annual review of the FY22 budget. Grant applications will be reviewed and grants announced by July 1, 2021. Awardees will be required to submit an organizational invoice with documentation confirming payment and receipt of approved items, acknowledge Montgomery County in all publicity and promotional materials, submit a project completion summary within 30 days of project completion, and assure items will be used solely for the stated purpose for up to two years following the award.

structured_extraction.program_name: Food Aggregation Grant Program (FY26 Resilient Infrastructure – Local Food Aggregation Grant)
structured_extraction.program_description: A multi-year, single-award grant program administered by Montgomery County that supports the aggregation, distribution, and marketing of food grown by regional and County-based farmers to wholesale and institutional markets. The program aims to increase the supply of locally-sourced and fresh food available to residents and organizations in Montgomery County by funding the establishment and operation of a food aggregation facility, including build-out costs and distribution infrastructure. The program awards one successful applicant through a two-stage application process: Stage One assesses eligibility for grant funding and Stage Two assesses program alignment and viability of success.
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Year One: $550,000 total ($250,000 flexible grant funding for operational activities + $300,000 capital grant funds for facility construction/retrofitting, structured as reimbursable payments). Requires minimum 50% matching funds ($275,000), with no more than 20% in-kind ($55,000). Year Two: $500,000 (40% grant funding/$200,000 + 60% County food purchases/$300,000), contingent on compliance and performance. Years Three-Four: $300,000 annually (100% County committed food purchases). All funding contingent on appropriation, compliance with reporting requirements, and achievement of annual milestone objectives.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: In fiscal year 2026 (July 2025 - June 2026), Montgomery County received approximately $2 million in HOME funds. Funds are loaned to non-profit and for-profit developers for affordable housing activities including acquisition, rehabilitation, new construction, and tenant-based rental assistance. The maximum per-unit subsidy is published annually by HUD. Rental units must have 90% at or below 60% AMI, with 20% at or below 50% AMI if more than five units. Homeownership projects assist persons earning up to 80% AMI. Funds are tied to individual units and monitored based on construction type: rehabilitation/acquisition of less than $15,000 per unit (5 years), $15,000-$40,000 (10 years), or more than $40,000 (15 years); new construction (20 years). Longer affordability periods of 30-40 years may apply for the life of the HOME loan. An annual maximum subsidy per unit applies. Davis-Bacon wage rates apply for projects with 12 or more units. A subsidy layering review is required if other federal funds are included in the project. Loan terms typically include 0-3% interest rates with options for monthly amortization, deferred payments, or cash flow-based repayment. Projects must comply with income and rent limits, annual tenant certification, occupancy deadlines (6 months for lease-up, 18 months for full occupancy), and other affordability requirements.

HOME funds may not be used for operating costs, organizational costs, or non-residential accessory structures.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Developer submits application to the Department of Housing and Community Affairs (DHCA) with information needed for normal development project. The application is straightforward and part of a rolling application process with no deadlines. Staff reviews application and analyzes requests. The Housing Loan Review Committee (HLRC), comprised of private citizens and designated county staff knowledgeable in affordable housing development, finance, and management, reviews the application and meets with the applicant to determine if request meets threshold criteria and funding guidelines. The HLRC makes recommendations to the Director of DHCA. The Director of DHCA reviews recommendations, determines which requests will be funded, and sets the conditions and terms of the loan based on project needs. Upon approval, developer receives funding via low-interest or cash flow loans, available at closing or as needed. All proposals must be consistent with threshold criteria and funding guidelines in the County's Consolidated Plan. During underwriting review, DHCA evaluates cost reasonableness, market demand, developer capacity, and commitment of other funding sources. Factors considered include: compliance with HOME mission and guidelines, public purpose serving low-income population, neighborhood need, physical improvement needs, project design compatibility, land use and zoning, community support, financial feasibility, leveraging, cost reasonableness, market feasibility, readiness to proceed, availability of support services, and development team capacity.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Families with children meeting age and income requirements receive enrollment in a full-day Head Start/PreK program at no cost. Children receive approximately 9 hours daily of early childhood education, meals, snacks, health screenings, and family support services during the school year. The county establishes a monthly payment process with participating childcare providers on behalf of enrolled families. Parents may also use publicly funded child care subsidies such as Working Parents Assistance or Purchase of Care to help pay for before and after school child care, or privately pay for extended hours.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration begins March 2nd for school year 2026-2027
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children ages three or four years old by September 1st whose family income is at or below 100% of the federal poverty level, residing in Montgomery County. Children in foster care are automatically eligible regardless of income. Priority is given to three-year-olds transitioning from Early Head Start programs (CentroNia, Reginald S. Lourie Center, or Sheppard Pratt Family Services, Inc.).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Early childhood education and care services, classroom instruction, meals and snacks, health screenings and services, nutrition support, mental health services, social skills development, disability services, and family support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Montgomery County, Maryland. Families must reside in Montgomery County. Special registration sites are available in March throughout the county.

Family must reside in Montgomery County
Children must be 3 or 4 years old by September 1st of the calendar year
Priority given to children transitioning from Early Head Start programs (CentroNia, Reginald S. Lourie Center, or Sheppard Pratt Family Services, Inc.)
Three year old program has limited spaces and locations available
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Registration for the 2026-2027 school year begins March 2nd. New families to Montgomery County Public Schools can create an account at the MCPS enrollment portal. Existing MCPS parents can log into ParentVUE. Special registration sites are available in March throughout the county. Parents interested in registering may also call MCPS Early Childhood Programs and Services at 301-230-0676; MCPS will advise on required documents. After acceptance into the Community Action program, families receive a list of participating childcare programs to select from; families are encouraged to contact and visit programs before selecting. Families enroll directly with their chosen childcare program and notify the county of their selection; the county then contacts the provider to confirm enrollment and establish the monthly payment process. Call 240-740-4530 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healing Art: Climate Resilience Through Art
structured_extraction.program_description: A six-month artist-in-residence project inviting community-based artists and arts collectives to create sustainability-themed visual artwork for the Department of Health and Human Services building. Selected artists will engage with staff and community participants through hands-on art-making activities and workshops, with the resulting artwork displayed inside the DHHS building at 1301 Piccard Drive in Rockville. The project aims to strengthen community ties in the face of climate hazards, build social support and facilitate healing, promote environmental ethics, and foster a sense of agency among DHHS clients.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: All-inclusive honorarium stipend of $18,000 to the selected artist or team. This covers all artist fees, fabrication and production costs, art-making materials, meeting costs, documentation, transportation, general liability insurance, and other costs associated with the residency project. Up to four finalists are selected from submissions and each receives a $500 honorarium for developing their proposal and presenting to the selection panel. The project will run for a maximum of 6 months with an expected completion date in June 2024.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based artists and arts collectives living in Montgomery County who are at least 18 years old and not enrolled as full-time students. Artists in historically underrepresented communities including Black, Indigenous, Native American, Latinx, Chicanx, Arab, MENASA, Asian, Pacific Islander, socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals, differently abled individuals, and LGBTQIA+ constituents are highly encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Artist fees, fabrication and production costs, art-making materials, meeting costs, documentation, transportation, general liability insurance, and other costs associated with creating environmental-themed visual artwork and conducting community workshops. Artists may work in any visual media (e.g., mural, mosaic, collage, etc.) that engages with collective staff and constituents at the facility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must reside in Montgomery County, Maryland with a verifiable mailing address in Montgomery County. The artwork will be displayed at 1301 Piccard Drive in Rockville, Maryland. All engagements and workshops will be hosted onsite at 1301 Piccard Drive.
requirements_list: Reside in Montgomery County, MD with a verifiable mailing address in Montgomery County (P.O. boxes not accepted)
Be at least 18 years old
Not be enrolled as a full-time student
Be a practicing artist with demonstrated history of creating work
Be able to provide a Social Security Number (SSN) or Individual Tax Identification Number (ITIN) prior to undertaking activities
Carry general liability insurance for the duration of the project
Interest and demonstrated track record in community engagement
Familiarity with materials, supplies and processes typical in creating installations with similar budgets
Experience presenting work to the public through public art, public installation, or thematic exhibition
Experience working in collaborative situations with project stakeholders, artists, arts administrators, curators and producers
Ability to complete work within required timeframes
Clarity of project proposal and conceptual approach
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Phase One - RFQ Submission (by November 6, 2023): Submit an online application including artist name and contact information, CV or resume (up to 2 pages as MS Word or PDF), current artist statement, short narrative responses to three specific questions about artistic interest, community involvement experience, and teaching artist experience, and up to 10 images of past completed work with descriptions. Images must be submitted as individual JPEG files (maximum 300 dpi, no larger than 1024 x 768 pixels) with file names formatted as ArtistLastName###.jpg. Image list must be submitted as a DOC file. A community-based selection panel will review submissions and invite up to four finalists. Phase Two - Finalist Proposals (November 2023 - January 2024): Selected finalists have six weeks to prepare proposals for community workshops and final artwork design. Finalists receive a $500 honorarium and tour the facility during this period. Finalists present proposals to the selection panel via Zoom in January 2024. One artist or team is selected to receive the residency contract and begin work in January 2024, with all activities completed by June 2024. Optional: Artists can attend an informational Zoom session (October 26, 3:00-4:00pm) or schedule a guided tour of the facility (available until October 27, limited to 15 people per tour). For assistance, contact PublicArt@creativemoco.com.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy, Efficient, Electrified, Climate-Adapted Pilot (HEECAP) Homes Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: HEECAP Homes is a grant program administered by Montgomery County designed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, provide gap funding for health and safety repairs, and offer climate adaptations for low- and moderate-income homes in Montgomery County. The program supports a comprehensive approach to fixing homes, electrifying them to improve indoor air quality, and enhancing durability and climate resilience. Funding is competitively awarded to community partner organizations (primarily 501(c)(3) nonprofits) to implement strategies including home electrification, HVAC improvements, asbestos and radon remediation, electrical modernization, roof repairs, window replacements, solar battery storage, extreme heat measures, flooding measures, and other climate resilience enhancements for eligible households. The program has been offered in multiple fiscal years (including FY24, FY25, and FY26), with both Montgomery County Government and Maryland DHCD funding available. FY26 includes approximately $1.5 million in total funding ($1 million MCG + $500,000 DHCD).
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides competitively awarded grant funding to 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations to implement comprehensive home retrofits for low- and moderate-income households. FY26 MCG funding offers a maximum of $1,000,000 available (for approximately 2-5 awards), with individual awards ranging from $100,000-$400,000. FY26 DHCD funding offers $500,000 (for approximately 2-3 awards), with individual awards ranging from $100,000-$300,000. MCG grants may fund both capital and operating costs; DHCD grants fund capital costs only (no indirect costs permitted). The grant performance period is 12 months (June 3, 2026-June 2, 2027, with possibility of renewal). Funds are provided on a tranche-funded basis upon submission and approval of quarterly programmatic and financial reports. Eligible uses include: electrification of heating/cooling systems and water heaters with ENERGY STAR-certified heat pumps; asbestos testing and removal; window/door repair or replacement; roof repair/replacement; electrical panel upgrades and electrical modernization; solar battery storage; chimney repair/removal; extreme heat measures; flooding measures (sump pumps, drainage); interior finish repairs for water/mold damage; dehumidifiers; radon mitigation; flood insurance procurement; and training/capacity building (MCG only). Ineligible uses include weatherization/insulation, fossil-fuel appliances, gut rehabilitation, consumable items, and projects outside Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jeremy Good (Technical Questions); Gregory Weissman (Administrative Questions)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofits registered as 501(c)(3) organizations that are currently working with low- and moderate-income (LMI) residents to improve household energy efficiency. Target beneficiaries are low- to moderate-income homeowners and residents in Montgomery County (households with income at or below 80% of Area Median Income for Montgomery County).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health and safety repairs, electrification of heating and water heating systems, HVAC improvements, electrical panel upgrades and modernization, asbestos and radon remediation, window and roof repairs, solar battery storage systems, chimney repair/removal, extreme heat adaptation measures, flooding mitigation and prevention measures (sump pumps, drainage), interior finish repairs to remediate water or mold damage, dehumidifiers, flood insurance procurement, and staff training/capacity building (MCG only). Funds cannot be used for weatherization/insulation, fossil-fuel appliance installation, gut rehabilitation, projects outside Montgomery County, cosmetic improvements, or consumable items.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All eligible projects must be located in Montgomery County, Maryland. Activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and exclusively for Montgomery County residents. DHCD-funded projects must be within the boundaries of DHCD's Sustainable Communities.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Competitive selection process. Step 1: Create an account in the Euna (eCivis) online grants portal at https://portal.ecivis.com/#/login. Step 2: Access the appropriate FY26 HEECAP Grant Program solicitation page (MCG or DHCD-funded) and click 'Apply'. Step 3: Complete all required application tasks including: Applicant Information Form (organization legal name, SDAT ID, Federal Tax ID, SDAT standing confirmation, Maryland Charities Database status, website, most recent IRS 990 form or exemption explanation, organization point-of-contact information, legally authorized signatory information, and board chair information); Applicant Background Task (optional); Licenses, Policies and Procedures; Project Strategy (9-part narrative covering target population, income verification, climate/health needs, organizational capacity, quality assurance, cultural/linguistic proficiency, positive outcomes, pilot scalability, and collaboration details if applicable); Project Staffing Plan (PDF with staff assignments and percentage of time); Project Work Plan/Timeline (PDF); Performance Plan and Performance History (PDF with KPIs); Optional Supporting Documentation; and Project Budget Supporting Information with Euna Budget Tool and detailed Budget Narrative. Step 4: Submit complete application through online portal by Wednesday, April 22, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST. Applications received after the deadline will be disqualified. Step 5: OGM conducts Administrative Review to verify Montgomery County Eligibility Conditions and application completeness. Minor errors may be corrected within 2 business days; major issues result in disqualification. Step 6: DEP recruits independent Subject Matter Expert (SME) Review Committee composed of qualified individuals from Montgomery County Government and possibly broader community, selected for experience in grant subject matter, grants administration, project management, and/or racial equity and social justice analysis. Review Committee scores proposals based on published criteria and submits recommendations. Step 7: Final decisions made by County based on scores and other relevant factors including expert opinion and updated priorities. Step 8: Award notification letters expected approximately one month after deadline via email. Grant Agreement will contain total award amount, funding restrictions, programmatic/administrative/policy requirements, reporting requirements, and payment terms. Step 9: Successful grantees required to attend initial kick-off/compliance orientation meeting (attendance triggers initial percentage of total award). Grantees then paid based on submission and approval of quarterly programmatic and financial reports. MCG reports are quarterly; DHCD reports due September 1, 2026, December 1, 2026, March 1, 2027, and final report June 15, 2027. Monthly check-ins with County staff required. County reserves right to conduct site visits with resident approval.

It helps people with personal care, chores, and activities of daily living to support independence and allow them to remain in their own homes. The program aims to prevent or reduce time spent in institutions and to prevent or address abuse, neglect, self-neglect, or exploitation.

Depending on household income and family size, individuals may be required to contribute toward the hourly cost of the aide service on a sliding-scale basis. The fee is paid to the Department of Social Services. Weekly service hours are established through an assessment based on individual need and available funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Computer Telecommuting Incentive Personal Property Business Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A personal property tax credit program for employers in Montgomery County who purchase new home computers or laptops to establish new off-site employee workstations for telecommuting. The credit equals up to 50 percent of the cost of each personal computer, with an annual maximum credit of $2,000 per business. Computers must have been purchased after December 31, 2005. The program has an annual funding cap—$100,000 in 2006, $175,000 in 2007, $250,000 in 2008, with subsequent years set by the County Council—and credits are granted on a first-come, first-served basis. Employees using the computers must work from home at least 78 days per calendar year (approximately 1.5 days per week) and must certify that the computers are used for business purposes.

Annual program funding caps: $100,000 (2006), $175,000 (2007), $250,000 (2008), with subsequent years set by the County Council. Credits are granted in order of application receipt (first-come, first-served). Computers must be purchased after December 31, 2005. Employees must certify that computers are used for business purposes and that they work from home at least 78 days per year (or 1.5 days per week).

Applications are processed first-come, first-served up to the annual program funding limit. Credits are applied to the year of purchase or the following tax year.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Fire and Rescue Service provides complimentary home safety visits to residents. A trained representative checks smoke alarms for proper operation, replaces outdated or non-working alarms, changes backup batteries as needed, identifies home fire hazards, helps develop escape plans, and provides fire safety education. The program targets high-risk individuals including older adults, seniors, and people with mobility, vision, hearing, or other disabilities.

The program provides battery-only smoke alarms with 10-year sealed, tamper-resistant batteries and silence/hush buttons. Hardwired smoke alarms may not be replaced with battery-only units. Specialized alarms for deaf or hearing impaired individuals are available. Program does not include installation or replacement of hardwired smoke alarms.

Renters eligible but landlords responsible for alarm installation and replacement.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state and local tax credit program that limits the annual increase in taxable assessment for owner-occupied principal residential properties to a fixed percentage — 10 percent per year for most of Montgomery County and statewide, or 5 percent in the Town of Kensington. Homeowners pay no property tax on assessment increases above this limit, spreading assessment growth over a longer period and providing relief during periods of rapid property value increases. This credit does not apply in the first year following purchase of a home. Administered by the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), a one-time application is required.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: A credit applied against property tax on the portion of annual reassessment exceeding the fixed percentage limit — 10% for most municipalities in Montgomery County and the State of Maryland, or 5% in the Town of Kensington. The homeowner pays no property tax on assessment increases above this limit. The credit stabilizes tax payments by spreading assessment growth over a longer period. Not applicable in the first year following the purchase of a new home. Property owners must file a one-time application with SDAT; applications must be on file by May 1, 2026 to ensure the County Income Tax Offset Credit appears on future tax bills beginning July 1, 2026.
