structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check if you already have a Homestead Application on file by visiting the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) property search website and searching your property. Look for 'Homestead Application Status' to see if it shows 'Approved', 'Application Received', or 'No Application'. Step 2: If no application is on file, find your Real Property Account Number from your SDAT letter or the property search results. Then apply either online through the Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application page at onestop.md.gov or by mail using the paper application form at https://dat.maryland.gov/realproperty/Documents/Homestead_application.pdf. You only need to apply once; you do not need to reapply every year. Applications must be on file by May 1, 2026 to ensure the County Income Tax Offset Credit appears on future tax bills beginning July 1, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rental assistance for very low and extremely low-income households, the elderly, and persons with disabilities. Provides a rent subsidy so that recipients pay no more than 40% of their total household income on housing.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rent subsidy that limits housing costs to no more than 40% of total household income. Available through tenant-based vouchers usable at any home, apartment, or private market residence meeting safety standards and rent reasonableness requirements, or project-based vouchers assigned to specific buildings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Very low and extremely low-income households, elderly individuals, and persons with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance to make housing more affordable.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Housing Path Portal online application system for all HOC rental programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rental assistance program that helps low-income families, the elderly, and persons with disabilities afford decent and safe housing. Vouchers can be used at any residence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental assistance vouchers that can be used at any residence to help make housing affordable.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families, elderly individuals, and persons with disabilities in Rockville.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance at any residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Rockville

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Stabilization Services - Emergency Eviction Prevention
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides case management and limited financial grants to Montgomery County residents at risk of homelessness or eviction. The program offers emergency financial assistance, needs assessment, and case management to help households keep their current housing, obtain new housing, prevent utility shut-off, restore disconnected utility services, and receive burial assistance. Eviction prevention grants are available to eligible households that have received a court judgment for eviction, a put-out notice from a landlord, or a red and white notice from the Sheriff's Office. The program also addresses prevention of foreclosure and utility disconnection for eligible households experiencing housing emergencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Limited financial grants and case management services are provided to eligible households. Eviction prevention grants are given as emergency financial assistance to prevent eviction. The program also offers utility assistance (to prevent shut-off or restore disconnected services), burial assistance grants, and support for obtaining new housing including security deposit and first month's rent assistance. Specific grant amounts are not publicly stated.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - no deadline specified. Apply at any time when experiencing a housing emergency.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents at risk of homelessness or facing eviction. Priority is given to those with court judgments for eviction, put-out notices from landlords, or red and white notices from the Sheriff's Office. Individuals and families experiencing housing emergencies are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency financial assistance to prevent eviction, keep current housing, obtain new housing, prevent utility shut-off, restore disconnected utility services, burial assistance, and prevention of foreclosure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents only. Residents of the City of Gaithersburg, City of Rockville, or City of Takoma Park may be eligible for support through their respective municipality.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Household income must be at or below 60% of the area median income (AMI)
Must not have received an eviction prevention grant in the past 12 months
Must have a court summons, judgment, red and white notice from the Sheriff's Office related to an eviction, or a landlord-issued put-out notice
Must provide photo identification for all adults in the household
Must provide last 30 days of bank and financial statements for all accounts
Must provide last 30 days of income documentation for all adults
Must provide proof of expenses (utilities, phone, car, childcare, rent, or mortgage)
Must provide emergency court or legal documentation related to eviction
Must provide current rental ledger for eviction prevention cases
Must provide welcome letter and lease for security deposit and first month's rent assistance
Must sign release of information form authorizing HSS to contact third parties
Must meet program guidelines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit one of three offices in person to apply: Germantown Office (12900 Middlebrook Road, 2nd floor, Germantown, MD 20874), Rockville Office (1301 Piccard Drive, 2nd floor, Rockville, MD 20850), or Silver Spring Office (8818 Georgia Avenue, Silver Spring, MD 20910). Bring all required documentation at the time of application. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with sign-in for in-person assistance available until 4:30 p.m. Alternatively, call 311 (or 240-777-0311 from outside Montgomery County) to request a phone interview. For assistance, contact HSS Customer Service at HSS@montgomerycountymd.gov or call 311.

structured_extraction.program_name: Housing at Metrorail Stations Act: WMATA Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT)
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax abatement program that exempts all Montgomery County real property taxes for 15 years for high-rise residential developments built on WMATA-leased property at Metrorail stations throughout Montgomery County. To qualify, developments must include at least 50% rental housing with at least 25% of units reserved as moderately priced dwelling units (MPDUs) for households earning no more than 50% of area median income. The program also requires prevailing wage compliance, local worker hiring, and regular reporting to the County. The WMATA PILOT is administered under a covenant that runs with the land for 15 years from the date the qualifying development receives a use and occupancy permit for residential units.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% abatement of all County real property taxes for a period of 15 years for qualifying high-rise residential developments on WMATA-leased property at Metrorail stations. The tax abatement does not include exemption for any tax levied under an applicable special taxing area law. Developments must include at least 50% of leasable square footage as high-rise residential apartment units (more than 8 stories above ground) with at least 25% of units reserved as MPDUs for households earning at or below 50% of area median income. At least 25% of construction workers must be Montgomery County residents. Developers must ensure contractors and subcontractors have no three or more final, non-appealable penalties of $5,000 or more in the prior three years for violations of applicable wage and hour laws, including prevailing wage and Maryland wage and hour laws. Developers must execute a covenant running with the land for 15 years from the date of use and occupancy permit. The covenant may be included as part of the MPDU covenant under Chapter 25A of the County Code. Developers must provide quarterly certified payroll reports during construction listing employee identifier, initials, salary/hourly rate, and zip code of residence. Developers must provide annual compliance certifications including rent rolls, household income certifications, and financial audits. Developers must permit examination of books and records by the County and retain records for five years after covenant expiration. Failure to comply requires immediate repayment of all taxes that would have been due plus interest and penalties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and property owners proposing high-rise residential projects on WMATA-leased property at Metrorail stations in Montgomery County, including both for-profit and non-profit developers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax abatement on all County real property taxes for qualifying high-rise residential developments at Metrorail stations, covering the full 15-year covenant period.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, specifically on properties owned by WMATA at Metrorail stations where land is leased from WMATA to the developer.
requirements_list: Developer must be a business entity in good standing with the State of Maryland
Developer must lease land from WMATA at a Metro station
At least 50% of the leasable square footage of the project must consist of high-rise residential apartment units (more than 8 stories above ground)
Land on which the project is located must be at a Metro station on land leased from WMATA

At least 25% of rental units must be moderately priced dwelling units (MPDUs) reserved for households with incomes at or below 50% of area median income, as required under Chapter 25A of the County Code
At least 25% of workers constructing the qualifying project must be Montgomery County residents

Contractors or subcontractors must not have three or more final, non-appealable penalties of $5,000 or more in the prior three years for violations of applicable wage and hour laws, including prevailing wage law and applicable Maryland wage and hour laws
Developer must execute a covenant running with the land for 15 years from the date of use and occupancy permit
Quarterly certified payroll reports required during construction listing employee identifier, initials, salary/hourly rate, and zip code of residence
Annual compliance certifications required during the 15-year covenant period including rent rolls, household income certifications, and financial audits
Developer must notify the Director of any addition, sale, transfer, assignment, or other termination of the property as a qualifying development at least 30 days prior to the effective date
Developer must permit County examination of books and records during normal business hours and retain records for five years after covenant expiration
Failure to comply requires immediate repayment of all taxes, interest, and penalties that would have been due
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Developers seeking a WMATA PILOT must enter into a PILOT Agreement with the County. Developers should contact the Department of Finance to initiate the process. During construction, developers must submit quarterly certified payroll reports on a calendar quarter basis listing all contractors and subcontractors' employees with identifier number, initials, annual salary or hourly rate, and zip code of residence, certified by the general contractor. Following issuance of the use and occupancy permit, developers must submit annual compliance certifications by January 31 of each year to the Montgomery County Department of Finance, Director, 101 Monroe Street, 15th Floor, Rockville, Maryland 20850, certifying that at least 50% of leasable square footage consists of high-rise residential apartment units and at least 25% of MPDUs are maintained for households at or below 50% of area median income. Supporting documentation must include rent rolls, household income certifications, and financial audits.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides one-time financial assistance up to $25,000 and/or technical assistance to financially healthy small businesses in designated areas of Montgomery County that are adversely impacted by a redevelopment project initiated by the County, on County-owned property, or of a County facility. Designated areas include Silver Spring, Bethesda, and Clarksburg related to specific County-related projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time financial assistance up to a maximum of $25,000 and/or technical assistance provided to financially healthy small businesses adversely impacted by County-initiated redevelopment projects, projects on County-owned property, or County facility projects. Grants are given on a one-time basis. Current designated areas receiving assistance include Silver Spring (Studio Plaza Project area), Bethesda (Bethesda Metro Station South Entrance CIP Project area), and Clarksburg (Clarksburg Square Road Extension Project area).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Financially healthy small businesses in designated areas of Silver Spring, Bethesda, and Clarksburg adversely impacted by County-initiated or County-facility redevelopment projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To provide one-time financial assistance and technical support to help sustain business operations and viability during impacts from County redevelopment projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated geographic areas in Silver Spring (Studio Plaza Project area), Bethesda (Bethesda Metro Station South Entrance CIP Project area), and Clarksburg (Clarksburg Square Road Extension Project area) related to specific County-related redevelopment projects.
requirements_list: Business must be financially healthy
Business must be located in a designated area (Silver Spring, Bethesda, or Clarksburg)
Business must be currently experiencing adverse impact due to redevelopment projects in designated areas
Business must be adversely impacted by a redevelopment project initiated by the County, on County-owned property, or of a County facility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Montgomery County Business Portal. The Division of Fiscal Management within the Department of Finance administers the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Income Tax Offset Credit (ITOC) program grants county residents who own and live in their residential property a $692 annual tax credit applied to their county income taxes. The credit is automatic once a Homestead Tax Credit application is approved and on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and continues automatically in future years without needing to reapply.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A $692 annual tax credit applied to Montgomery County income tax bills. The credit is automatic once a Homestead Tax Credit application is approved and on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. It applies in the year the application is processed and continues automatically in future years without needing to reapply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who own and live in the residential property they own as their primary residence.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The $692 credit is applied as a reduction to Montgomery County income tax liability, effectively reducing the property owner's county tax bill.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Applicants must be county residents and property owners who live in the property they own as their primary residence.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must own the residential property where you live
Must live in the property as your primary residence
Must have a Homestead Tax Credit application on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation by May 1st
Application must be filed with the State of Maryland, not Montgomery County
Application must be in 'Approved' or 'Application Received' status at SDAT
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Check if you already have a Homestead Tax Credit application on file by visiting the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) website at https://sdat.dat.maryland.gov/RealProperty/ and searching your property. If your homestead application status shows 'Approved' or 'Application Received,' you do not need to apply. Step 2: If no application is on file, obtain your Real Property Account Number from your SDAT letter or the property search results. Step 3: File a one-time Homestead Tax Credit Eligibility Application either online through the SDAT website or by mailing a paper form. Once submitted and processed, the credit automatically applies to your county income tax bill and continues in all future years without needing to reapply. Applications are available in multiple languages including Amharic, Chinese, French, Korean, Spanish, and Vietnamese.

structured_extraction.program_name: Income Tax Offset Tax Credit (ITOC) Reinstatement (Appeal/Restoration)
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for owner-occupied residential properties in Montgomery County. Property owners who previously received this credit but lost it due to not having a current Homestead Tax Credit application on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation can apply for reinstatement.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Income Tax Offset Tax Credit (labeled as County Property Tax Credit on the property tax bill) is a credit applied to property taxes for owner-occupied residential properties. The credit is automatically applied to future years once an approved Homestead Tax Credit application is on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Under Maryland law, a person can have only one property listed as their principal residence. The Income Tax Offset Credit is available only for properties that are the property owner's principal residence.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of residential properties in Montgomery County who previously received the Income Tax Offset Tax Credit but lost it due to not having a current Homestead Tax Credit application on file.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit for owner-occupied residential properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Property must be owner-occupied residential property and serve as the applicant's principal residence.
requirements_list: Property must be owner-occupied residential property
Property must be the applicant's principal residence
Property owner must have an approved Homestead Tax Credit application on file with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation as of May 1, 2023
Applicant must certify that they own the property and occupy it as their principal residence

Required attachments for reinstatement application: copy of electric bill from the last 2 months with same address as property showing applicant's name as the party being billed; AND at least one of the following: current valid driver's license, first page of most recent Maryland income tax return showing owner's address, or first page of most recent federal income tax return showing owner's address
Address on identity documents must match the property address
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners can apply for reinstatement either online using the ITOC Reinstatement Online Application or by mail. For mail applications, download the application form, print it, and mail it with required attachments to the Department of Finance, Division of Treasury, Excise Tax Unit, Attn: ITOC Reinstatement Application, 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, Maryland 20850. Incomplete applications will not be processed. Applicants must include their printed name, property address, phone number, email address, mailing address, proof of principal residence with the date applicant began living at the address, and their signature certifying ownership and occupancy of the property.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid program that provides community-based services and supports planning to enable older adults and individuals with disabilities to live in their own homes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Medicaid-funded program providing personal assistance services, supports planning (case management), nurse monitoring, personal emergency response systems, environmental assessments, and accessibility adaptations based on assessed individual need.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Older adults and individuals with disabilities who need assistance with activities of daily living and qualify for Medicaid.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal care assistance, nurse monitoring, medical supplies, personal emergency response systems, environmental assessments, accessibility adaptations, and medical day care services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must qualify for community Medicaid or a Medicaid waiver
Must need help with activities of daily living such as bathing, grooming, and dressing
Must meet the program's medical level of care
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals should call the Aging and Disability Resource Unit (ADRU) at 240-777-3000 to apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Individuals 65 and Above and Retired Military Services Members Tax Credit (Bill 42-16)
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for Montgomery County residents aged 65 or older who either have owned and lived in their home for at least 40 consecutive years or are retired from the U.S. Armed Forces, military reserves, National Guard, uniformed corps of the Public Health Service, or uniformed corps of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. Surviving spouses of military retirees who did not remarry are also eligible, provided the military retiree was at least 65 years old at the time of death and retired from eligible service. The credit equals 20% of Montgomery County property taxes on the owner-occupied dwelling and is granted for 7 consecutive years.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 20% credit on Montgomery County property taxes applied to owner-occupied dwellings. The credit is granted for 7 consecutive years and is not available after that period. For applicants 65 or older who have owned and lived in the same dwelling for at least 40 consecutive years, the property assessment must not exceed $700,000 at the time of application. For military retirees 65 or older, the property assessment must not exceed $550,000. For surviving spouses of military retirees, the property assessment must not exceed $550,000. The tax credit appears as a line item deduction on the property tax bill issued in July.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals 65 years of age and above who own and occupy their home in Montgomery County and have either owned and lived in the dwelling for at least 40 consecutive years or are retired from the U.S. armed forces or uniformed services. Surviving spouses of military retirees who did not remarry are also eligible, provided the military retiree was at least 65 and retired from eligible service at time of death.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: County property tax reduction on owner-occupied dwellings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Must be 65 years of age or older (birthday on or before June 30, 1961 for tax year beginning July 1, 2026)
Must own and occupy the dwelling
For 40+ year owners: deed must be dated June 30, 1986 or earlier
For 40+ year owners: property assessment must not exceed $700,000 at time of application

For military retirees: must be retired from the U.S. Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines, Coast Guard, National Guard, military reserves, or uniformed corps of the Public Health Service or National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) (not just a veteran)
For military retirees: property assessment must not exceed $550,000 at time of application
Must be on the deed for the property
For surviving spouses: surviving spouse must be at least 65 years old
For surviving spouses: Military Retiree must have been at least 65 years old at time of death and retired from eligible service
For surviving spouses: must not have remarried after the military retiree's death
For surviving spouses: must provide death certificate, signed affidavit that surviving spouse did not remarry, and proof of military retirement (DD-214 form showing RETIRED or Retired Military ID)
For surviving spouses: proof of age must be provided via Driver's License or Certificate of Live Birth
For properties titled in a trust: must submit an Affidavit Re Trust Ownership
Must provide proof of age via Driver's License or Certificate of Live Birth; applications without this documentation will not be processed
For 40+ year owners: must provide copy of original deed; applications without deed will not be processed
For military retirees: must provide copy of Retired Military ID; applications without this documentation will not be processed
Application must be received by April 1 deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the appropriate Tax Credit Application form: (1) Standard Application for individuals 65+ or military retirees, or (2) Surviving Spouse Application for surviving spouses of military retirees. Gather required documentation including proof of age (Driver's License or Certificate of Live Birth), deed (for 40+ year owners), military retirement documentation such as DD-214 form showing RETIRED status or Retired Military ID (for military retirees), death certificate (for surviving spouses), affidavit certifying the surviving spouse did not remarry (for surviving spouses), and Affidavit Re Trust Ownership if property is titled in a trust. Mail the completed application and all required documents to the Department of Finance, Division of Treasury, Attn: Bill 42-16 Tax Credit, 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, Maryland 20850. Incomplete applications will not be processed. Approved applications submitted by April 1 will be processed on the property tax bill issued in July. You can verify your approved credit by reviewing your bill online at https://apps.montgomerycountymd.gov/realpropertytax or by calling MC311 at 311 (or 240-777-0311 from outside the county).

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Consultation Support Services
structured_extraction.program_description: Free consultation services to support healthy social and emotional development for infants and young children birth to age 5 enrolled in licensed child care programs. Consultants work with parents and child care staff to develop strategies to help children form secure relationships, regulate emotions, and learn in their child care setting and at home.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free mental health consultation services provided by consultants who observe children in their child care setting, gather information through conversation with parents and child care staff, and develop strategies to support the child's social and emotional development. Families receive resources and referrals, and assessment information may be shared with other professionals such as pediatricians, occupational therapists, and speech therapists as requested.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents and child care providers of children birth to age 5 enrolled in licensed child care programs in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services include observation and consultation to develop strategies supporting the child's social and emotional development, healthy relationship formation, emotion regulation, and learning readiness in child care and home settings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Child must be birth to 5 years old
Child must be enrolled in a licensed child care program
Services are not provided in before and/or after school programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call Montgomery County Child Care Support Services at 240-777-4769 (extension GROW) to apply. No documents are required to bring.

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant at Risk Home Visiting Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A home visiting program that provides public health nursing services to new mothers and babies who are at risk due to factors such as teen pregnancy, lack of prenatal care, substance use, mental health issues, intimate partner violence, unstable housing, previous infant death, preterm birth, very low birthweight, or other serious risk circumstances.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Public health nurses conduct home visits to provide comprehensive maternal-infant assessment, education, and support services. Services include maternal medical follow-up, infant medical follow-up, home visiting and case management, breastfeeding support, safe sleep education, immunization support, smoking cessation, mental health support, substance use referrals, IPV services, and family planning/reproductive health planning. Services are provided at no cost to participants.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Montgomery County Public Health Services - Maternal-Child Health Program
structured_extraction.contact_phone: Silver Spring Health Center: 240-777-3054; Germantown Health Center: 240-777-4648
structured_extraction.program_audience: New mothers and infants meeting risk criteria in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home visiting services, public health nursing support, maternal-infant assessment, health education, and referrals to support services for at-risk mothers and infants
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Age less than 18 years
Age 40 years or older
Lack of prenatal care or late entry into prenatal care
Substance use or misuse (alcohol or illegal drugs)
Mental or behavioral health concerns or history of depression
Intimate partner violence or history of abuse/violence
Unstable housing or homelessness
Previous infant death
Previous preterm birth or preterm labor
Very low birthweight (less than 1500 grams)
Small for gestational age
Gestational age less than 34 weeks at birth
Very low Apgar score (less than 4 at 5 minutes)
Birth defect or syndrome
Congenital infection
Positive toxicology screen
Metabolic disorder or neurological condition
Anemia, asthma, chronic hypertension, diabetes, or other medical conditions
Gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, or sexually transmitted infection
Lack of social or emotional support
Maternal-infant attachment or parenting deficit
Smoking or tobacco use
CPS case involving family
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Maryland Postpartum Infant and Maternal Referral Form. Submit the completed form by facsimile (FAX), encrypted email, or other secure means to the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services - Maternal-Child Health Program at Silver Spring Health Center (Fax: 240-777-3054) or Germantown Health Center (Fax: 240-777-4648). After a referral is received, a public health nurse will contact the family to establish home visiting services. Patient authorization is not required to submit this form as permitted under HIPAA regulations for public health authorities.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland program providing tax credits to potential investors in early-stage companies, with the goal of increasing the number of companies developing innovative technologies in Maryland, increasing overall investments in current and emerging technology sectors, and increasing the number of individual investors actively investing in Maryland technology companies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits for individual investors in early-stage technology companies to stimulate innovation investment across Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual investors in early-stage technology companies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Investment in early-stage innovative technology companies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Introduction to Managing in a Union Setting
structured_extraction.program_description: A mandatory training course for all County managers and supervisors that covers how labor relations work in Montgomery County Government, the role of the Office of Labor Relations and management, discipline and terminations, and the grievance process.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Mandatory training course that must be completed within the first year of employment or promotion for all County managers and supervisors. Course covers labor relations fundamentals, management and employee rights, union rights, discipline and terminations, and the grievance process. Delivered via webinar with enrollment through the AccessMCG ePortal or Extranet Portal. Employees with MCG Computer Network login enroll through AccessMCG ePortal (Employee Self-Service > MCG HR Employee Self-Service > Learner Home). Contractors, volunteers, and interns with MCG login access through AccessMCG ePortal (Learning Services for Contractors and Volunteers). Community partners, retirees, and others without MCG login set up a profile in AccessMCG Extranet Portal and request approval to access Learning Areas. Registration closes 24 hours in advance of class. Webinar link will be sent via Outlook email prior to class. Email confirmation sent within 24 hours of enrollment with detailed information. Reminder sent 7 days before scheduled class.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Montgomery County managers and supervisors
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in labor relations, management rights, employee rights, union rights, discipline, terminations, and grievance processes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a County manager or supervisor
Must complete within first year of employment or promotion
MCG Computer Network login or AccessMCG Extranet Portal access required for enrollment
Employees must access through AccessMCG ePortal using MCG Network credentials
Contractors and volunteers with MCG login access through Learning Services for Contractors and Volunteers
Community partners, retirees, and others without MCG login must create AccessMCG Extranet Portal profile and request approval to access Learning Areas (can take up to 48 hours for approval)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Enrollment process depends on user type: (1) MCG Employees: Log into AccessMCG ePortal at https://eportal.montgomerycountymd.gov with MCG Network credentials, navigate to Employee Self-Service > MCG HR Employee Self-Service > Learner Home, search for class by keyword, click Enroll, review enrollment details, and click Apply. (2) Contractors/Volunteers with MCG login: Access https://eportal.montgomerycountymd.gov, select Learning Services for Contractors and Volunteers, click through to County Learning Area, navigate to MCG OLM for Contractors and Volunteers > Learner Access > Learning > Learner Home, then search and enroll. (3) Community Partners/Retirees/Others without MCG login: First set up profile at AccessMCG Extranet Portal with email, department/organization, and secure password (8+ characters with number, letter, symbol). Complete security questions and wait ~1 hour for confirmation. Then log back into Extranet Portal, select Learning Services, request approval for desired Learning Areas (wait up to 48 hours for Catalog Administrator approval), then access MCG External Learner Self-Service to search and enroll in classes. Registration closes 24 hours before class. Confirmation email sent within 24 hours with class details. Reminder sent 7 days before class date.

structured_extraction.program_description: A residential electrician training program through the Joint Apprenticeship and Training Committee of Local Union 26 IBEW. Upon acceptance, trainees are placed with a signatory contractor and work toward becoming a licensed electrician.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Paid apprenticeship program requiring completion of 10,000 hours of job training (approximately 2,000 hours per year), 8 modules, and 10 classes. Pay increases as trainees progress through the program. Trainees may be accepted as apprentices during the process. Application fee is $50. Computer-mediated learning courses require a $150 subscription fee for 12 months of access to the PTSI system.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking residential electrician training. No GED or high school diploma required. Participants must have access to a computer and WiFi for online coursework.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Residential electrician apprenticeship training combining on-the-job experience with classroom instruction and computer-mediated learning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program based in Washington, DC near Springdale with the main Local Union 26 location. Training is with signatory contractors of Local Union 26 IBEW.
requirements_list: No GED or diploma required
Must pass $50 application fee
Access to computer and WiFi required
Must complete 10,000 hours of job training
Must fulfill 8 modules
Must take 10 classes
$150 subscription fee for 12 months of CML course access
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application online through the JATC 26 residential trainee application portal. Pay a $50 application fee. Accepted individuals sign an agreement and are placed with a signatory contractor of Local Union 26 IBEW. Complete the required 10,000 hours of job training, 8 modules, and 10 classes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Keeping it SAFE: Under Twenty-One Alcohol Prevention Coalition Student Video Contest
structured_extraction.program_description: A public service message video competition for student teams from Montgomery County public and private middle schools, high schools, and faith-based or service-based organizations. Teams of two or more students create 30-second videos about the risks and dangers of underage alcohol use, covering topics such as peer pressure, future impacts, and social media's influence on underage alcohol consumption. Winning entries receive cash prizes awarded to their affiliated schools or organizations, and all participating students earn 5 SSL (Student Service Learning) hours. The contest is administered by Montgomery County and is held annually, with prizes awarded at a reception in early May.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cash prizes awarded to winning student teams' schools or organizations. High school prizes: 1st place $1,000, 2nd place $500, 3rd place $350, Honorable Mention $100. Middle school prizes: 1st place $500, 2nd place $300, 3rd place $250, Honorable Mention $100. The video receiving the most online 'likes' receives an additional $150 prize. Prizes are awarded at a reception in early May. Checks are payable to schools or organizations only. All participating students also earn 5 Service Learning (SSL) hours.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Student teams of two or more students enrolled in Montgomery County public or private middle schools and high schools, or in faith-based or service-based organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creation of a 30-second public service message video about underage alcohol use risks on one of three topics: standing your ground against peer pressure to drink, how underage alcohol consumption affects your future, or social media's impact on underage alcohol consumption. Cash prizes are awarded to affiliated schools or organizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to students enrolled in Montgomery County public or private schools or in faith-based or service-based organizations. Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Teams must have at least two or more students
Students must be enrolled in Montgomery County public or private schools or in faith-based or service-based organizations
Video must be exactly 30 seconds in length (slates and credits cannot be overlaid onto the PSA or included in the 30-second message allotment; entries over 30 seconds will be disqualified)
Video must address one of three specified topics about underage alcohol use risks (not anti-drunk driving messages)

Video should not include copyrighted images, music, or materials without permission (including materials from magazines, books, DVDs, websites, films, YouTube, music, commercials, etc.; documented permission must be included if using copyrighted materials)
No clothing, language, or music which glorifies alcohol, drugs, sex, violence, or gang-related paraphernalia
Do not feature branded products; cover, distort, or make your own labels
Video must be submitted in 16x9 aspect ratio in 720p or higher definition
Video must be submitted via a public shared file link (e.g., Dropbox, Google Drive); TikToks and YouTube links are not allowed; YouTube Shorts must be submitted via a public shared drive
Speak slowly and clearly so all words are understood
Background music or sounds should not interfere with spoken dialogue
Screen text, size, and display must be readable
List sources of information on the reflection page
Each participating student must submit a signed consent and release form
Entries must be submitted via the online application form before the deadline
Winning entries may be used by KIS for public information purposes and submitted to media outlets
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Fill out the online application form and provide a link to your video entry submitted via a public shared file link (e.g., Dropbox, Google Drive). Submit a signed consent and release form for each participating student. Submit all materials through the online application portal by the deadline of March 31, 2026 by 4:00 PM. Students whose teams follow the contest guidelines and submit video documents prior to the contest deadline will receive 5 SSL hours. Prizes are awarded at a reception in early May. Checks are payable to schools or organizations only.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial incentives and risk mitigation support to landlords who partner with Montgomery County's Services to End and Prevent Homelessness (SEPH) to house individuals experiencing homelessness. Landlords receive incentive payments, claim reimbursement for property damage and unpaid rent losses, and access to supported tenants and networking opportunities.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides incentive payments to landlords who participate. New landlords receive a one-time sign-on bonus of $500, and referred landlords receive $250. Landlords can submit claims for reimbursement related to property damage beyond normal wear and tear, unpaid rent, and vacancy losses. The annual limit of financial coverage per participating tenant is $5,000. The lifetime limit of financial coverage per participating tenant is $10,000. This limit may include any combination of financial losses associated with property damages, unpaid rent, or vacancy losses. Landlords must first attempt to collect financial losses from the tenant. If the tenant does not make payment arrangements within 10 business days, the Claim Form can be submitted for reimbursement consideration. For unpaid rent claims, security deposits and other available financial resources must be applied first. For property damage claims, the landlord must use DHCA OLTA 'What is Ordinary Wear and Tear?' guidelines. Claims for unpaid rent can only be filed at the end of the lease term. Property damage claims can be filed during the lease term or within 45 days of tenant vacating. LRMF will consider minimum reimbursements of $100. If a landlord files a claim with their insurance, they must disclose and submit a copy of the insurance claim payout information; LRMF will consider paying the difference between the financial loss and insurance payment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed and registered Montgomery County landlords who are willing to rent to individuals referred through eligible Montgomery County SEPH housing programs (SHaRP, Rapid Rehousing, Housing Initiative Program, or eligible Permanent Supportive Housing programs).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to cover property damage claims (for damages beyond normal wear and tear), unpaid rent losses, and vacancy losses. Incentive payments are provided to new landlords ($500 sign-on bonus) and referred landlords ($250). Funds cannot be used for ordinary wear and tear, replacement of structural elements, major appliances, or HVAC systems unless damage is due to tenant negligence or abuse.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Tenants must be leasing a unit in Montgomery County and participating in one of the eligible housing programs (SHaRP, Rapid Rehousing, Housing Initiative Program, or eligible Permanent Supportive Housing programs that provide ongoing case management services). Fair Market Rent standards provided by HUD apply.
requirements_list: Landlord must be a licensed and registered property owner in Montgomery County
Landlord must sign the Landlord Risk Mitigation Fund Program Agreement
Landlord must provide a copy of the lease agreement
Property must meet inspection requirements and comply with county rental codes/laws
Property must be in clean, habitable, and sanitary condition, free of rodents and vermin, and in complete compliance with all applicable laws before tenant move-in
Landlord must agree to program terms and conditions
Landlord must complete and submit all required documentation within 15 calendar days of lease signing
Landlord must maintain valid contact information with SEPH or LRMF team
Landlord must participate in pre move-in inspection completed by SEPH designated housing service provider or housing locator
Tenant must initially occupy the unit on or after March 1, 2024 (or between 7/1/2020 and 9/15/2023 for previously enrolled participants)
Rent must be under Fair Market Rent standards provided by HUD
Shared housing leases and room rentals are permitted if unit meets county rental codes and rent is under fair market rate
Landlord must attempt to collect financial losses from tenant before submitting claim
For unpaid rent claims, security deposits and other available financial resources must be applied first
Landlord must first contact the tenant directly, then contact tenant's housing service provider for conflict resolution before considering eviction
Landlord must participate in mitigation efforts with housing service provider or OLTA prior to starting eviction process
Landlord must notify program immediately if tenant breaches lease without proper notice
Landlord must follow lease agreement terms in accordance with federal, state, and local law
Damages must be assessed and verified by SEPH designated housing service provider or housing locator
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landlords should contact the LRMF team at LRMF@montgomerycountymd.gov to register and express interest in the program. After partnership is established, the process involves: (1) Signing the Landlord Risk Mitigation Fund Program Agreement and submitting a copy of the lease agreement; (2) Completing a pre move-in inspection with a SEPH designated housing service provider or housing locator (free of cost) who will take pictures/videos and complete a detailed inspection report form prior to tenant occupancy; (3) Submitting all required documentation within 15 calendar days of lease signing to LRMF@montgomerycountymd.gov; (4) If property damage occurs or rent is unpaid, landlord must first attempt to collect from the tenant directly and within 10 business days; (5) Landlord submits the Landlord Risk Mitigation Claim Form with all required supporting documentation to LRMF@montgomerycountymd.gov. For unpaid rent, required documentation includes notice to vacate, letter sent to tenant in effort to recover, current tenant rent payment ledger, security deposit application verification, and insurance claim information if applicable. For property damage, required documentation includes notice to vacate, letters sent to tenant, receipts/invoices for repairs with itemized charges and estimates, security deposit application verification, insurance claim information if applicable, and detailed description of damage beyond normal wear and tear. Claims are reviewed on a case-by-case basis. Payment is contingent upon approved claim amount to the extent of available funds in the program.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead for Impact Leadership Development Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An interactive peer leadership development program designed to help professionals working in homelessness services strengthen their leadership skills, gain confidence, and create meaningful change in Montgomery County. Participants engage in group workshops, one-on-one coaching, peer circles, and develop a leadership project over six months.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program includes a virtual orientation (April 30, 12-1pm), four in-person group sessions (May 21, June 18, September 17, October 15, 10am-2pm or 10am-3pm ET), two virtual sessions (July 16 and August 13, 10am-1pm ET), three one-on-one virtual coaching sessions, monthly small group peer meetings, monthly pre-work with recorded video lessons and reflection exercises, and a 360-degree leadership profile assessment. Participants develop a leadership project to translate their vision into action. Total time commitment is estimated at 2 to 4 hours per week over six months. The application requires 60-90 minutes to complete and includes both written and video components.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Professionals and leaders deeply committed to ending homelessness in Montgomery County who work for nonprofit organizations, government agencies, or the private sector within the continuum of care system.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This is a training and leadership development program, not a direct funding program. Participants develop and advance a leadership project that translates their vision for the county into action.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to leaders working in Montgomery County's continuum of care and those committed to ending homelessness in the county.
requirements_list: Deeply committed to ending homelessness in Montgomery County

Willing and able to attend all scheduled sessions throughout the six-month program (virtual orientation April 30, in-person sessions May 21, June 18, September 17, October 15, and virtual sessions July 16 and August 13)
Ready to step into or deepen leadership role
Ability to commit 2 to 4 hours per week for the program duration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete a Google Form application with personal information and written responses to five questions about professional background, motivation for social services work, current contributions to ending homelessness, leadership strengths and challenges, and scheduling conflicts. Applicants also submit video responses to three questions about their decision to apply, a recent leadership demonstration, and what they would contribute to the learning community. The complete application (written and video) must be submitted by 5PM on April 8th. The selection committee will review applications and notify participants of acceptance by April 20th. Selected participants will attend a virtual orientation on April 30th.

structured_extraction.program_description: A housing-focused coalition that connects income-qualified seniors and people with disabilities to home repairs, accessibility modifications, and social support services. The coalition provides health and safety improvements, accessibility features, weatherization upgrades, handyman services, and community connections.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The coalition provides in-kind services including installation of accessibility features (grab bars, handrails, ramps, lever handles, walk-in showers), health and safety repairs (roof replacement, electrical and plumbing improvements, flooring), handyman services for minor repairs, weatherization and energy efficiency upgrades (appliance replacement, insulation, air sealing, HVAC and water heater replacements), and yard work services. A free one-year membership to Silver Spring Village is available for eligible Silver Spring residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-qualified homeowners who are older adults or people with disabilities living in the 20910 and 20912 zip codes (Silver Spring Village and Village of Takoma Park areas).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home repairs, accessibility modifications, energy efficiency upgrades, and weatherization improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Currently operates in zip codes 20910 and 20912 as a pilot program within the Silver Spring Village and Village of Takoma Park service areas. Expansion is planned for the future.
requirements_list: Income qualified
Homeowner status
Older adult or person with disabilities
Resident of Silver Spring Village or Village of Takoma Park service area (zip codes 20910 and 20912)
Services may vary by individual and eligibility varies by service type
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested residents in zip codes 20910 and 20912 can access the coalition through any of its member organizations including Habitat for Humanity Metro Maryland, Rebuilding Together Montgomery County, Village of Takoma Park, Silver Spring Village, Montgomery College, or Village Coordinator at Montgomery County Aging and Disability Services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A recurring grant program administered by Montgomery County that supports community organizations and projects that serve as beacons of excellence and innovation in their neighborhoods and communities. The program provides funding to nonprofits demonstrating exemplary community impact and improvement efforts. The FY27 Lighthouse Grant Program specifically supports socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals and families navigating challenges related to immigration status, providing comprehensive services including centralized intake and needs assessment, navigation to critical services such as housing, healthcare, education, immigration legal services, intensive case management, and strong outreach to diverse immigrant populations across the County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding for community organizations serving as umbrella (lead) organizations to deliver comprehensive services to support socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals and families navigating immigration-related challenges. FY27 provides one award of $3,993,574 to one umbrella organization (pending County Council appropriation). FY26 awarded $3,504,636.00. Funds are released in stages: 25% at project launch, 25% after December 1st, 25% after March 1st, 20% after June 1st, and remaining 5% after final reports accepted. The award period is typically 12 months (July 1 to June 30) with a potential one-time no-cost extension to October 1. Eligible expenses include personnel salaries, fringe benefits, direct client assistance (rental assistance, vehicle expenses, documentation fees), emergency support, travel, equipment ($10,000+), supplies, contractual services, formalized partner costs, construction, and indirect charges up to 15% of direct costs. Organizations with approved federal NICRA rates above 15% may charge that rate instead.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ali Hoy, Program Manager II (OGM); Remi Aromire, Program Manager II (HHS Lighthouse Initiative)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and community organizations based in or serving Montgomery County residents, particularly those with experience serving socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals and families navigating immigration-related challenges. Applicants must demonstrate capacity to serve as an umbrella (lead) organization managing formalized partnerships with other community-based organizations and delivering comprehensive, culturally and linguistically responsive services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel, fringe benefits, direct client assistance (short-term rental assistance, vehicle-related expenses, documentation fees, emergency support), travel, document fees for required documentation, equipment, supplies, contractual services, formalized partner support, construction, and indirect charges. Services must be provided free of charge to Montgomery County residents and include centralized intake and needs assessment systems, navigation to housing, healthcare, education, immigration legal services, intensive case management, emergency support for family stabilization, capacity-building support to partner organizations, robust outreach to diverse immigrant populations, and immigration legal services including legal orientations and consultations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County. Organization's principal place of business must be located in Montgomery County; if a national or regional organization, it must have a location in Montgomery County through which it provides related services. All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and/or be exclusively for Montgomery County residents.
requirements_list: Organization must be currently registered and in Good Standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Organization must have a 'Current' standing with the Maryland Secretary of State OneStop – Charities Public Registry
Organization's principal place of business must be located in Montgomery County (or have established location in county if national/regional)
All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County exclusively for Montgomery County residents
Services must be provided free of charge with no donations requested and no use of County resources for fundraising
Services must not be provided in promotion of a particular religion, political party, or with requirement of service/program attendance

Services must be open and available to all Montgomery County residents regardless of race, color, religious creed, ancestry, national origin, age, sex, marital status, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, family responsibility, genetic status, presence of children, or source of income
Current Montgomery County contract/grant award winners must be current on all reporting obligations with substantial progress toward goals

Proposed expenses must be for new activity, expansion of existing activities, or combination; cannot fund prior obligations, debts, fines, penalties, lobbying, alcoholic beverages, or supplanting other funds
Organizations must demonstrate prior experience working with priority populations (socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals and families navigating immigration status challenges)
Minimum of three (3) years of experience managing multisector collaborations and/or coordinating community-based programs serving priority populations with cultural competency
Must establish formalized partnerships with other community-based organizations and provide letters of commitment (LOC)
Must demonstrate strong track record of coalition building, administrative and fiscal management, service delivery, community collaboration, and organizational capacity building
Must develop comprehensive intake and needs assessment system accurately identifying needs of individuals and families in priority populations
Must provide navigation and guidance to connect individuals and families to local systems (housing, healthcare, education, immigration legal services)
Must provide emergency support to address urgent needs and reach stabilization
Must provide intensive case management services for long-term integration and self-sufficiency
Must establish and engage community advisory board composed of community members and service providers
Must provide capacity-building support to partner organizations including training, technical assistance, and organizational development
Must develop and implement robust outreach strategy for diverse immigrant populations across the County
Must provide immigration legal services including legal orientations and individual legal consultations

Must operate case management system with schema and codebook tracking demographic characteristics, uniquely identifying clients/families over time, tracking activities/assessments/referrals, and associating individuals/households with activities
Must provide culturally and linguistically responsive services
Must address needs of diverse priority populations including Central/South American, African, Caribbean, Middle Eastern, and Asian diaspora communities
Must implement proactive stabilization and preparedness supports including guardianship planning, estate and asset preparedness, and documentation readiness planning

Must submit comprehensive Outreach Plan to HHS within thirty (30) days of award execution detailing geographic coverage strategy, targeted engagement approaches, outreach activities, language access strategy, and capacity to respond to surge demand
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Create an account on the Euna Grants (eCivis) platform at https://portal.ecivis.com/#/login. 2. While logged in, access the FY27 Lighthouse Grant Program page and click the 'Apply' button. 3. Review the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) document containing detailed application requirements, scoring criteria, and program details. 4. Optionally attend an MS Teams Live Online Grant Program Information Session (Friday, April 3, 2026, from 12:00 PM - 1:00 PM focused on grant partnerships and platform demonstration, or Friday, April 10, 2026, from 1:00 PM - 2:00 PM focused on grant program details and FAQs). 5. Identify and establish formalized partnerships with local community-based organizations; obtain letters of commitment from partner organizations. 6. Optionally complete the FY27 Lighthouse Grant Program Partnership Interest Form to connect with interested community-based organizations. 7. Complete all required application tasks including organizational information, project narrative, community advisory board plan, formalized partnerships documentation, cultural competency and language access plans, intake and needs assessment system description, outreach strategy, case management system documentation, monitoring and evaluation plan, budget narrative and budget tool, and all certifications and assurances. 8. Ensure organization records match across SDAT, Montgomery County Vendor Registration System (CVRS), and application. 9. Submit completed application through the online platform by the submission deadline (Wednesday, May 13, 2026, at 11:59 PM). 10. Applications that are incomplete, do not meet legal requirements, or are submitted after the deadline will not be accepted. 11. Award notification letters expected approximately one month after application deadline via email and grants management platform.

structured_extraction.program_description: A school-based program that provides integrated social services, behavioral health services, community education, and health services to children and families at select elementary and middle schools in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free mental health services (including diagnostic evaluations, child and family therapy, classroom observations, school and provider consultations, and group counseling), social services (family needs assessments, family care management, referrals to services, and concrete assistance), community education services (workshops, health fairs, parenting classes), and expanded health services through School-Based Health Centers. Services are offered at no cost to families; students with Medicaid receive mental health services with Medicaid billed directly.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and families with a child enrolled at a school where Linkages to Learning is offered, with priority given to schools with the highest percentage of students who have qualified for Free and Reduced-Priced Meals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Family needs assessments, family care management, mental health treatment, therapy, counseling, community education, parenting classes, and expanded health services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at select elementary and middle schools in Montgomery County with the highest percentage of students who have qualified for Free and Reduced-Priced Meals.
requirements_list: Child must be enrolled at a school where Linkages to Learning is offered
For expanded health services through School-Based Health Centers, parents or guardians must complete an enrollment packet
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Clients are usually referred through their school counselor or school staff, though families may self-refer. For Family Care Management and Child/Family Mental Health Services, staff conduct intake paperwork at the first appointment. Community Education Services require no application. For expanded health services, parents or guardians complete an enrollment packet with assistance available at the School-Based Health Center.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Local Small Business Reserve Program (LSBRP) ensures that Montgomery County Government departments award at least 25 percent of their procurements for goods, services, and construction to registered and certified local small businesses. The program helps county departments identify solicitations appropriate for LSBRP competition and gives local small vendors an equal opportunity to compete for county contracts on equal footing with similarly-sized businesses. All informal solicitations are required to be reserved under LSBRP. The program also includes a Veteran-Owned Business Preference, whereby businesses certified as VOSB or SDVOSB receive an additional 5 percent evaluation point preference starting January 2, 2025. Eligible entities include retailers, construction and trades companies, wholesalers, service firms, and non-profit organizations based in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Registered and certified local small businesses receive procurement set-asides, with Montgomery County agencies required to award at least 25 percent of their contracts to eligible businesses. All informal solicitations are reserved under LSBRP. Vendors register through the County Vendor Registration System (CVRS) at no cost and compete for county contracts in goods, services, and construction. Veteran-owned businesses certified as VOSB or SDVOSB receive an additional 5 percent evaluation point preference starting January 2, 2025. The program is available for contracts with Montgomery County Government, Montgomery College, Montgomery County Public Schools, and the Housing Opportunities Commission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County-based independently-owned small businesses including retailers, construction and trades companies, wholesalers, service firms, and non-profit organizations that meet size, revenue, and location requirements, as well as veteran-owned small businesses interested in contracting with Montgomery County Government, Montgomery College, Montgomery County Public Schools, or the Housing Opportunities Commission.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to county government procurement contracts for goods, services, and construction awarded by Montgomery County Government and associated county entities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have its principal place of business in Montgomery County, defined as either having physical business location(s) only in Montgomery County, or having physical business locations both in and outside the county where the county-based location(s) accounts for over 50 percent of the business's total employees or gross sales.
requirements_list: Business must be independently owned; brokers and subsidiary businesses are not eligible
Federal tax number or W-9 in the name of the business is required
Principal place of business must be in Montgomery County

Meet employee and sales thresholds by business type: Retail (maximum 30 employees OR prior 3-year average sales of $5,000,000 or less), Wholesale (maximum 30 employees OR prior 3-year average sales of $5,000,000 or less), Services (maximum 100 employees OR prior 3-year average sales of $10,000,000 or less), Construction (maximum 50 employees OR prior 3-year average sales of $14,000,000 or less), Manufacturing (maximum 40 employees OR prior 3-year average sales of $14,000,000 or less)
Must register and obtain LSBRP certification through the County Vendor Registration System (CVRS)

For Veteran-Owned Business Preference: must obtain VOSB or SDVOSB certification from the U.S. Small Business Administration or U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and upload the certification to CVRS profile
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register and apply for LSBRP certification through the County Vendor Registration System (CVRS) at https://azex32.montgomerycountymd.gov/cvrs/ at no financial cost. Vendors create and maintain their registrations on this web-based system. For Veteran-Owned Business Preference Program participation, obtain VOSB or SDVOSB certification from the U.S. Small Business Administration or U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, then upload the certification to your CVRS profile. DBRC staff meet regularly with county department and agency staff to identify LSBRP procurement opportunities and solicit bids from registered vendors. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with no specific deadline.
attachment_urls: https://montgomerycountymd.gov/pro/resources/files/reports/FY24 Local Small Business Reserve Program Annual Report_council.pdf

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Union 5 Plumbers and Gasfitters Apprenticeship
structured_extraction.program_description: A 5-year paid training program for individuals seeking to become licensed plumbers and gasfitters. Pay increases by 5 percent every 6 months. Upon graduation, participants can work as plumbers in other areas of the country or relocate when employment opportunities arise.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 5-year paid apprenticeship program with 5 percent pay increases every 6 months. Applications for the 2025-2026 school year are accepted online only. All required documents must be on file to receive an exam date. Applicants must pass an entrance exam.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals aged 17 and older at time of application (must be 18 to start the program). High school diploma or GED required. Candidates must pass an entrance exam.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in plumbing and gasfitting trades with paid employment components.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program located in Lanham, Maryland (5000 Forbes Blvd.). Training provides credentials recognized nationally.
requirements_list: GED or high school diploma required
Must be 17 or older when applying, 18 or older when starting
Must pass entrance exam
All required documents must be on file to receive exam date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted online only. Applicants click 'Apply Now' on the left side under Home > Application > Apply Now. All required documents must be submitted before receiving an exam date.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps low-income families and older adults in Montgomery County access home internet service at an affordable rate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-income families and older adults may qualify to receive home internet access for as little as $9.95 per month through available providers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families and older adults in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home internet access
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Low-income household status or older adult age
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit website for details on available providers and how to get help determining eligibility and applying for the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The MC Groceries Program is a food assistance initiative administered by Montgomery County that helps families access fresh and shelf-stable food items through a convenient online shopping experience. Eligible households receive monthly grocery benefits in the form of Instacart Fresh Funds codes, which can be used to purchase groceries from over 20 retailers available through Instacart for home delivery or in-store pickup. The program targets households with children under 18 who do not qualify for SNAP benefits due to income or citizenship restrictions and are experiencing food insecurity. Enrollment expansion aims to serve up to 700 families, and program benefits are expected to be available from July 15, 2026, to July 15, 2027.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households receive $100 in monthly benefits for each child under age 18 (up to a maximum of $400 per month per household). Benefits are provided as Instacart Fresh Funds credits redeemable through the Instacart online platform and mobile app, restricted to nutritious food and non-alcoholic beverage items similar to SNAP restrictions, including fresh or frozen produce, seafood, dairy, eggs, meat and meat alternatives, bakery, deli, and pantry staples. All eligible items are marked with a Fresh Funds icon. Funds are automatically loaded on the participant's Instacart account on the 15th of each month or the following business day and can be used for home delivery or in-store pickup from participating Instacart retailers. Non-eligible items and amounts exceeding the Fresh Funds balance will be charged to the backup payment method. Driver tips, delivery fees, and service fees can be covered with Fresh Funds benefits. A household with one eligible child receives $100/month, two children $200/month, three children $300/month, and four or more children $400/month. Unspent funds do not roll over to the next month.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program benefits expected to be available from July 15, 2026, to July 15, 2027
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 301-818-3614 or 240-777-4141; Instacart Senior Support: 1-844-981-3433 (8 a.m. - 11 p.m. ET daily)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Households with at least one child under age 18 residing in Montgomery County who do not qualify for SNAP benefits due to income or citizenship restrictions and have post-tax household income below 400% of the Federal Poverty Level.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of fresh and shelf-stable food items and nutritious non-alcoholic beverages through the Instacart online shopping platform, available for home delivery or in-store pickup from participating retailers. Eligible items include fresh or frozen produce, seafood, dairy, eggs, meat and meat alternatives, bakery, deli, and pantry staples similar to SNAP-eligible items.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must reside in Montgomery County, Maryland throughout the program year. Deliveries must be made to the address provided during enrollment. Over 20 retailers are available through Instacart in the Montgomery County area.
requirements_list: Reside in Montgomery County throughout the program
Have at least one child under age 18 who does not receive SNAP benefits
Household post-tax income below 400% of the Federal Poverty Level (approximately $132,000/year for a 4-person household)
Have access to a backup electronic payment method such as debit card, credit card, Google Pay, Apple Pay, PayPal, or Klarna
Able to navigate an English-only platform
Willing to participate in a mid-year check-in and pre/post-program surveys
Upload proof of income such as recent pay stubs or employer letter
Provide valid photo identity document for parent or guardian (driver's license, Maryland ID card, or passport)
Provide proof of address such as lease, landlord letter, driver's license, or utility bills with current address
Provide government-issued proof of identity for all children (birth certificate or school documents)
Household does not have an active SNAP case
Meet household income eligibility requirements
Create an Instacart Fresh Funds account
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact a Nutrition Benefits Navigator to complete an eligibility pre-screening. 2. If eligible, the Navigator will assist with completing a waitlist form. 3. As openings become available, individuals on the waitlist will be notified and asked to complete an application with required documentation including proof of income, valid photo ID, proof of address, and government-issued proof of identity for all children. 4.
