structured_extraction.program_name: Make Office Vacancy Extinct (MOVE) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Make Office Vacancy Extinct (MOVE) Grant Program is a sub-program of the Economic Development Fund established to support rental costs incurred when eligible new or existing businesses locate, relocate, or expand in Montgomery County. The program provides one-time financial assistance to businesses signing their first commercial office lease (Inaugural Commercial Lease) or expanding their existing office space by at least 500 square feet (Expanded Commercial Lease) in Montgomery County. The program is designed to attract new businesses to the County, reduce vacant Class A and B office or flex space, and support local economic development. Retail, restaurant, and independent financial or insurance agent/broker establishments are not eligible.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers tiered grants based on the size of the leased office space, calculated per eligible square foot with maximum award limitations: businesses leasing less than 7,500 square feet receive $8.00 per square foot up to $60,000 maximum; for leases between 7,501 and 10,000 square feet, the grant is $10.00 per square foot up to $100,000 maximum; for leases over 10,000 square feet, the grant is $12.50 per square foot up to $150,000 maximum. Strategic Industries receive $15.00 per square foot up to $150,000 maximum. The overall maximum grant award is $150,000. For Inaugural Commercial Leases, Eligible Square Feet equals the total square footage of the leased premises. For Expanded Commercial Leases, Eligible Square Feet equals the total square footage in the new/expanded lease minus the square footage of the previous lease. Grants are disbursed after verification of lease and occupancy. Awards are subject to availability of funds and are distributed first-come, first-served based on the date of receipt of a Completed Application. A Business is limited to one MOVE Program award per County Fiscal Year (July 1 through June 30). A Business and its Subsidiaries are limited to three MOVE Program awards total. If the calculated award exceeds remaining available appropriated funds in a County Fiscal Year, the awardee receives an award based on available appropriation, with additional funding provided if subsequently appropriated.

Office Space includes real estate locations in buildings leased and occupied by a business for a commercial purpose that is not for retail or restaurant, with the exception that craft alcohol production companies such as breweries, cideries, distilleries, and wineries whose primary use of space is production are eligible despite their retail operations.

The lease term must be 36 months (3 years) or longer

Leased space must be classified as Office Space (a real estate location leased and occupied by a business for commercial purpose not for retail or restaurant, with exceptions for craft alcohol production facilities)
Business must be in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Submit signed Articles of Incorporation or equivalent document
Submit a utility bill or equivalent document generated by a party other than the Business or landlord for the leased premises with the same physical address as the leased premises
Submit a complete business plan that clearly identifies the type and purpose of the business
Complete Application must be submitted within 180 days of the lease execution date
Retail, restaurant, and independent financial or insurance agent/broker businesses are not eligible
Leased premises must be labeled as Office Space by Third-Party Software, have a real property address, and not be a mobile trailer or other similar non-permanent structure
Business cannot execute the lease with its Subsidiary
Sole proprietor cannot primarily sell products or services underwritten by a third party
Awardee must remain in the County for a minimum of 36 months post-award
Awardee must maintain the Eligible Square Feet for 36 months post-award

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Review program criteria and eligibility requirements to ensure qualification. Gather all required supporting documentation including: executed lease, signed Articles of Incorporation or equivalent, utility bill or equivalent proof of occupancy with matching address, and a comprehensive business plan. Submit the complete application online through the County's online portal (time-stamped by system) within 180 days of lease execution date. Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis. A program manager designated by the Director of Finance will conduct a site visit to verify occupancy before the County disburses grant funds. The Director of Finance makes final determination on all applications. Applicants will receive formal notification of award status, including reasons for denial if applicable. Awardees receive a conditional grant award letter stipulating the process to receive funds and post-award requirements. Businesses may remedy any incomplete or out of compliance eligibility requirements; for first-come, first-served purposes, the Completed Application date is based on when the Business rectifies all deficiencies.

Non-profit entities organized to promote the interests of persons with a disability may qualify if they demonstrate on a contract-by-contract basis that at least 51% of the persons used to perform services or manufacture goods are persons with disabilities

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Certified MFD businesses must obtain certification from one of the recognized certifying agencies (MDOT, SBA, WBENC, MSDC, Capital Region MSDC, or City of Baltimore MWBOO). Once certified, businesses can explore contracting opportunities with Montgomery County through the program's outreach activities, workshops, and forums. The Performance Plan requires County approval before contract execution. During contract performance, MFD subcontractors submit monthly MFD Reports of Payments Received (Form PMMD-97) to the Program Manager. Prime contractors must submit documentation of compliance with the Performance Plan before receiving final payment. Waiver requests may be submitted to the MFD Program Manager if appropriate circumstances exist.

structured_extraction.program_description: An inclusionary zoning program administered by Montgomery County that requires a percentage of housing units in residential developments to be made available for low- and moderate-income households at affordable prices or rental rates. The program helps distribute low and moderate-income households throughout the county's growth areas and expands the inventory of affordable housing. It operates as both a homeownership and rental program: first-time homebuyers with moderate income can purchase newly constructed or resale MPDU homes at significantly below-market prices subject to a 30-year control period (or 10 years for units first purchased before April 1, 2005), and income-eligible households can rent affordable units in apartment communities throughout the county. Developers in qualifying residential developments are required to set aside 12.5–15% of units as MPDUs. After the purchase control period expires, owners may sell at market price but must share 50% of excess profit above the MPDU resale value with Montgomery County. Montgomery County's MPDU program was the first successfully implemented inclusionary zoning program in the country, established in 1974, and has produced more than 17,800 affordable units since inception.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For homeownership: First-time homebuyers purchase MPDU homes at affordable prices below market value. For-sale MPDU units are priced according to Executive Regulation 21-22 based on construction costs, with base unit structure costs ranging by unit type (e.g., single-family detached base cost $127,100, townhouse base cost $109,725-$116,270). Homes are subject to a 30-year control period (or 10-year for some resale homes first purchased before April 1, 2005) during which the owner must occupy as primary residence, cannot refinance above the controlled resale price, and can only sell through the MPDU program at the MPDU-calculated maximum resale price (based on original purchase price, inflation, documented improvements, real estate commission, and transfer taxes) to certified MPDU program participants. After the control period expires, the owner may sell at market price but must pay 50% of excess profit to Montgomery County and into the Housing Initiative Fund. Refinancing or obtaining a home equity line of credit during the control period requires MPDU office notification and documentation. The Housing Opportunities Commission may purchase up to one-third of units produced. For rentals: Affordable rental units are available in apartment communities throughout the county. For new garden apartment tenants, maximum income is 65% of Area Median Income (AMI); for new high-rise apartment tenants (5 stories or more), maximum income is 70% AMI; for renewing tenants, maximum income can be up to 130% of the new tenant maximum. Income limits and rent amounts are recalculated annually. Rental income limits as of April 11, 2025: garden apartments range from $74,500 for 1-person household to $123,500 for 6-person household; high-rise apartments range from $80,500 for 1-person household to $133,000 for 6-person household. MPDU rents are set by Executive Regulation and recalculated annually. Rent can increase only once per 12 months and cannot exceed the Voluntary Rent Guideline. Application fees capped at $25. No amenities fees or surface parking fees allowed for MPDU tenants. Other rental assistance programs may be used to help pay MPDU rent. Developers are required to make 12.5–15% of units available as MPDUs (higher percentage in planning areas where at least 45% of census tracts have a median household income of at least 150% of the countywide median). Control periods are 30 years for for-sale units and 99 years for rental units.
structured_extraction.contact_name: MPDU Office Staff; Greater Washington Urban League (GWUL) for orientation and homebuyer classes
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time homebuyers and renters with household incomes up to 70% of the Washington Metro Area Median Income for purchase units; rental income limits are 65% AMI for garden apartments and 70% AMI for high-rise apartments for new tenants. Priority is given to people who live or work in Montgomery County, but applicants do not need to live in the county to apply for purchase units. Renewing rental tenants may have income up to 130% of the new tenant maximum. Households must include appropriate household size for property bedroom count.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase or rental of moderately priced housing units in residential developments in Montgomery County. For purchase, funds must be used for the MPDU property purchase and household size must be appropriate to the property size. For rental, units must serve as the tenant's primary residence and cannot be sublet. Property must remain owner-occupied as primary residence during control period for purchase units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicable to residential and mixed-use developments of 20 or more units in Montgomery County. The program applies countywide, with higher MPDU requirements (15%) in planning areas where at least 45% of census tracts have a median household income of at least 150% of the countywide median household income. Rental units are available throughout Montgomery County; note that the cities of Rockville and Gaithersburg have separate MPDU policies. Alternative Location and Alternative Payment Agreements may direct MPDU funding to HOC sites or other designated locations in some cases.
requirements_list: Income must not exceed 70% of the Washington Metro Area Median Income for purchase units (approximately $79,500 for family of two or $99,500 for family of four based on 2025 rates)
First-time homebuyer requirement applies for purchase units: applicant and all household members must not currently own a home and must not have owned a home anywhere in the past five years
Minimum annual household income of $40,000 for purchase applicants
Maximum annual household income based on household size for purchase (ranging from $80,500 for 1-person household to $133,000 for 6-person household as of April 11, 2025)
Mortgage pre-qualification letter for at least $150,000 from a licensed mortgage lender issued within the last three months
Ability to demonstrate you can afford the mortgage loan, utilities, and fees
Federal tax return from most recent filing year for all adult wage earners; if no tax return filed, verification of non-filing must be provided
Household size appropriate to MPDU property size (bedroom count)
Complete three free online training courses in order: MPDU Orientation Seminar (2.5 hours), First-Time Homebuyer Class (8 hours HUD-certified), and Application Tutorial
Pass post-tests with 80% or higher score for each class
Submit completed application with supporting documents via MPDU Application Portal
Provide government identification for all adult household members
Provide First-Time Homebuyer Certificate from a HUD-approved housing counselor issued within the past two years
Provide two most recent pay stubs (or four if paid weekly) for every wage earner, or complete Verification of Income form if unable to provide pay stubs
Provide proof of residence if current taxes do not show current address
For self-employed individuals, provide notarized Year-To-Date summary of income and expenses from the current year
For retired individuals, provide proof of pension income and/or social security benefits statement
Provide documentation of all other sources of income such as Social Security Income, child support, or alimony
Owner occupancy required during the control period for purchase units
Single-family MPDUs must have at least 2 bedrooms
Bedroom ratio in rental developments must match market-rate units
If purchasing during control period, must work with MPDU-trained realtor and lenders familiar with MPDU requirements
If refinancing or obtaining home equity line of credit during control period, must notify MPDU office and follow specific documentation procedures
If selling during control period, must offer to County and Housing Opportunities Commission first, then to certified MPDU program participants through random selection drawing
Property must remain subject to MPDU covenants and maximum resale price restrictions during control period

For rentals: Household gross annual income must be between minimum amount (varies by property) and maximum amount based on household size and development type (65% AMI for garden apartments, 70% AMI for high-rise apartments for new tenants; up to 130% AMI for renewing tenants)
Credit rating must be acceptable to apartment community management for rental
Applicant and all rental household members must not have owned any residential property during the previous 5 years and must have never owned an MPDU
MPDU rental unit must be primary residence and cannot be sublet
Number of bedrooms eligible based on household size for rental: 1 person gets 1 bedroom; 2 people get 1 or 2 bedrooms; 3-4 people get 2 or 3 bedrooms; 5+ people get 3 or more bedrooms
MPDU certificates valid for one year; income must be recertified annually
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: FOR PURCHASE: Step 1: Submit pre-screening intake form to Greater Washington Urban League (GWUL) to register for MPDU Orientation Seminar (2.5 hours, virtual, offered second and fourth Thursdays monthly). Step 2: Attend and pass MPDU Orientation Seminar post-test (80% or higher). Step 3: Register for and attend First-Time Homebuyer Class (8 hours, virtual, HUD-certified, offered second Saturday of month). Step 4: Pass First-Time Homebuyer Class post-test (80% or higher). Step 5: Receive email from MPDU office with instructions to complete online Application Tutorial. Step 6: Complete Classes Validation Form by entering first name, last name, email, and Orientation ID. Create user account through AccessMCG Extranet. Step 7: Access MPDU Application Portal to take Application Tutorial (must pass with 80% or better). Step 8: Submit completed application form and supporting documents through MPDU Application Portal. Step 9: MPDU staff reviews application (30-day processing time, longer if documents missing). Step 10: If eligible, applicant receives Certificate of Eligibility in mail within three weeks of approval. Step 11: Certificate holder can participate in random selection drawings for available MPDU properties. Step 12: Upon selection, applicant works with MPDU-trained realtor and familiar lender to complete purchase. FOR RESALE DURING CONTROL PERIOD: (1) Request MPDU Maximum Resale Price from MPDU office (response within 21 days). (2) Complete and return MPDU Marketing Form. (3) Offer to County and Housing Opportunities Commission (right of first refusal). (4) If not purchased, offer to certified MPDU program participants through random selection drawing with MPDU-trained realtor. (5) If no certified participants interested, request written permission to sell to general public. (6) Upon sales contract ratification, realtor provides required documents to MPDU office within 14 days. FOR REFINANCE/HELOC DURING CONTROL PERIOD: (1) Request current MPDU Maximum Resale Price. (2) Receive letter with refinance/HELOC value. (3) Send letter to lender. (4) After closing, email settlement details to MPDU office. (5) MPDU office sends official letter to lender and settlement company. (6) Lender and title company ensure MPDU covenants appear on deed. (7) MPDU office records Notice of Sale and Refinance. FOR SALE AFTER CONTROL PERIOD EXPIRES: (1) Send completed Shared Profit Calculation Request Form and Calculation of Improvements Credit Request Form (if applicable) and copy of signed sales contract to MPDU office (allow 21 days). (2) MPDU office calculates shared profit and sends to owner, realtor, and settlement agent. (3) Settlement company sends shared profit payment check to Montgomery County and into Housing Initiative Fund. (4) County terminates MPDU covenants once paid. FOR RENTALS: Tenants apply directly to individual MPDU apartment communities of their choice, not to DHCA. Step 1: Review list of apartment communities with MPDU units on DHCA website. Step 2: Identify properties of interest. Step 3: Contact one or more apartment communities to apply. The apartment community management provides the application form, verifies income and credit history, and determines eligibility. Property managers recertify income and household size annually, with notice sent 90 days before lease expiration.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery Cares - Medical Care for Uninsured Adults
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery Cares is a group of community-based health care providers and county clinics that offers comprehensive medical and dental care to uninsured, low-income adults in Montgomery County. Services include doctor and nurse visits, preventive check-ups, sick visits, prescription medications, laboratory tests, x-ray imaging, specialist referrals, and oral/dental health care. The program also includes an Adult Dental Program for residents ages 19 to 59. Services are provided on a sliding fee scale based on income and are available to those not eligible for state and federal programs such as Medicaid, Medicare, or employer-sponsored coverage.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery Cares health centers and county clinics provide medical and dental care services to eligible uninsured adults on a sliding fee scale based on income. Services include preventive check-ups, sick visits, prescription medications, laboratory tests, x-ray imaging, specialist referrals, and dental care. There are no fees or payments for the program itself, though individual health centers may set their own fees for specific services. The program also offers prescription assistance to enrolled patients. The Adult Dental Program provides dental services to low-income adults ages 19 to 59 with income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level. Applicants can apply through the Safety-Net Programs Application form (available in English and Spanish) or online through the Community Connect Portal for the Adult Dental Program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Uninsured adults age 18 or older who are residents of Montgomery County with income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Level, and who are not enrolled in health insurance including Medicaid, Medicare, commercial insurance, or employer-sponsored coverage. The Adult Dental Program is specifically for residents ages 19 to 59. Also available to uninsured and low-income families not eligible for state and federal programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical care services including preventive check-ups, sick visits, prescription medications, laboratory tests, x-ray imaging, specialist referrals, dental care, and prescription assistance for uninsured adults.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at multiple health centers and county clinics throughout Montgomery County. Applicants must be residents of Montgomery County and must provide proof of residency.

Must be uninsured or not eligible for health insurance (Medicaid, Medicare, commercial insurance, or employer-sponsored coverage)
Must be a Montgomery County resident

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 311 or 240-777-0311 for information about a Montgomery Cares health center near you. Applicants have two options: (1) Call the health center of your choice to enroll and bring proof of income and proof of Montgomery County residency to your first appointment; or (2) Complete the Safety-Net Programs Application (available in English and Spanish) and email to OESS.MoCo@montgomerycountymd.gov. The application form collects information about household members, employment income, unearned income, and other benefits received. For the Adult Dental Program, applicants can apply online starting January 1st, 2025 using the Community Connect Portal.

Eligible residents can receive one Chromebook by scheduling an appointment at a local Montgomery County library. U.S. citizenship is not required to participate.

structured_extraction.program_description: The County purchases agricultural land preservation easements to conserve farmland and prevent future commercial, residential, or industrial development. The program uses a formula-based system to determine easement value.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases agricultural easements on eligible farmland. Easement values are determined using a formula based on farm size, soil quality, road frontage, and farm location rather than appraisals. The program places a permanent easement on the property to prevent future development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of agricultural land in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To purchase development rights on farmland through agricultural easements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Farms must be located in the Agricultural Reserve (AR), Rural Cluster Zone (RC), Rural Zone (RZ), or other zones determined by the County's Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board to possess significant agricultural value.
requirements_list: Farm must be located in Agricultural Reserve, Rural Cluster Zone, Rural Zone, or other zones with significant agricultural value
Minimum property size of 50 acres, or 10 acres or more of cropland adjacent to other protected land
One Transferable Development Right for every 25 acres of land must be retained with the property prior to easement application
At least 50 percent of the land must meet USDA Soil Classification Standards I-III or Woodland Classifications 1 and 2
Land must lie outside water and sewer categories 1, 2, and 3
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners interested in participating should contact the office for specific information about their property. Applications are typically processed within 6 to 12 months.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) Financing
structured_extraction.program_description: Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) is an innovative financing program administered by the Montgomery County Green Bank that helps qualifying commercial property owners fund building improvements. Private capital providers offer lower-cost, long-term flexible financing covering up to 100 percent of eligible property improvements, with no upfront cost. Repayment is made through annual or semi-annual surcharges on the property tax bill for up to 20 years. The financing stays with the property if it is sold, and the new owner continues paying the surcharge until the loan is fully paid. Eligible improvements include energy efficiency upgrades, renewable energy installations, climate resiliency and adaptation upgrades, water conservation upgrades, and environmental health and safety improvements. Financing may be used for planned renovations, completed renovations within the last 12 months, or new construction projects.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Private capital providers offer lower-cost, long-term flexible financing covering up to 100 percent of eligible property improvements with no upfront cost. Repayment is structured as annual or semi-annual surcharges on the property tax bill for up to 20 years. The loan remains with the property through ownership changes, allowing new owners to assume the repayment obligation upon sale. The Green Bank also serves as a small C-PACE capital provider for transactions of $2.5 million or less to help stimulate market activity and close gaps for smaller projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing program - applications accepted at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial building owners and operators in Montgomery County seeking financing for energy efficiency, renewable energy, climate resiliency, water conservation, or environmental health and safety improvements to their properties, including building owners, capital providers, and contractors. The program particularly targets minority-owned businesses and low-income and disadvantaged community (LIDAC) property owners and developers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency upgrades, renewable energy installations, climate resiliency and adaptation upgrades, water conservation upgrades, and environmental health and safety improvements. Financing can be used for planned renovations, completed renovations that occurred within the last 12 months, or new construction projects. Projects must comply with Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. The program applies only to commercial properties, not residential properties.
requirements_list: Property must be a qualifying commercial property located in Montgomery County
Improvements must be for energy efficiency, renewable energy, climate resiliency, climate adaptation, water conservation, environmental health and safety upgrades, or related eligible purposes
For existing buildings, renovations must be planned or must have been completed within the last 12 months
Property must comply with Montgomery County Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) requirements or be pursuing BEPS compliance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Building owners, capital providers, and contractors interested in the program should contact the Montgomery County Green Bank to learn more and to apply for financing. The Green Bank provides technical assistance through its Technical Assistance Program to help building owners assess their property and identify C-PACE-eligible building upgrades. Applicants may also contact the Department of Finance to determine property eligibility. The Green Bank offers one-on-one technical assistance, participation in industry events and webinars, and direct coordination with senior lenders and project sponsors to address structural, legal, and underwriting considerations specific to C-PACE.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Council Summer Fellows Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A paid ten-week summer fellowship for graduate students to gain real-world local government experience. Participants work on policy analyses, research projects, and ongoing initiatives while developing skills in public policy and local government administration. Fellows also write a self-selected independent research paper and present their findings to the County Council.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive an $8,000 stipend for the ten-week program running from June 1, 2026 through August 7, 2026. The program is full-time (Monday-Friday, 40 hours/week) with hybrid schedule possible with supervisor approval. Fellows work directly with decision makers including elected officials and senior management staff on policy analysis, research, and ongoing projects. The program includes weekly meetings with Councilmembers to learn about the policymaking process and weekly field trips to explore the County. Fellows develop skills in writing, quantitative and qualitative research, project management, data analysis, implementation review, process development, public speaking, and presentations. Housing and transportation costs are not covered by the program and relocation to the region for the summer is at the applicant's expense.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Stage 1 application available from November 17, 2025 to January 9, 2026. Stage 2 deadline: late January 2026. Applicants notified by end of March 2026.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Naeem Mia, Pamela Dunn, Logan Anbinder, Nicole Rodríguez-Hernández
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current graduate-level students (Masters or PhD programs) in policy-related fields including public policy, public administration, public affairs, public health, planning, law, or related disciplines who will have completed their first year of study by summer 2026.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants conduct self-selected independent research projects and work on policy analyses focused on topics such as educational equity, racial equity and social justice, pay and wage analysis, senior care, criminal justice, food security, transportation, environment, affordable housing, county growth policies, health and human services, and public safety. Near the end of the program, Fellows present their policy recommendations to the full County Council during a live Council session. Councilmembers have used the policy analyses and recommendations from these reports to directly impact local and state legislation and policy decisions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must live in the Washington, D.C. region during the fellowship period. Telework agreements may be discussed on an individual basis with supervisors, though in-person hours are still expected. Program is located in Montgomery County, Maryland. Many County office buildings are a 10-minute walk from either the Rockville Metro Station or the Wheaton Metro Station. Other placements may be elsewhere in the County, accessible by bus or car. Relocation to the region for the summer is at the applicant's expense.
requirements_list: Be a current graduate-level student (Masters or PhD)
Cannot have graduated before the program start date of June 1, 2026
Must have completed at least the first year of graduate study by the program start date
Still be in their degree program as of summer 2026 (i.e. have not graduated)
Study public policy, public administration/affairs, public health, planning, law, or related fields
Maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale
Live in the Washington, D.C. region during the fellowship period
Demonstrate enthusiasm to learn about local government
Show innovative ideas and approaches to policy problems
Embody strong interpersonal skills and collaborative mindsets
Be eager to make a real impact on Montgomery County residents and businesses
Desire opportunity for skill development
All levels of work experience and backgrounds are invited to apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application consists of three stages. Stage 1: All prospective Fellows must submit requested preliminary information at the Council Summer Fellows website (tinyurl.com/MoCoSummerFellows). The Stage 1 application will be available from November 17, 2025 to January 9, 2026. Stage 2: Selected applicants from Stage 1 will receive a Stage 2 application via email. Applicants selected for Stage 2 must submit: two reference letters (at least one from a graduate professor/supervisor is preferred), first semester graduate school transcript when available, a writing sample of 5-10 pages, and responses to four short answer prompts regarding interest in the program, applicable skills/attributes, a policy analysis approach to a selected topic from a pre-determined list, and an example of a work/school assignment that could be of interest to a local government. Stage 2 deadline is late January 2026. Stage 3: Selected applicants participate in an interview with tentative interview dates in February 2026. Applicants selected for the program will be notified by the end of March 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County-funded initiative to promote a broad range of housing opportunities for residents. The fund supports multifamily housing development and rehabilitation projects in Montgomery County, including construction or acquisition of affordable housing units, purchase and rehabilitation of existing rental units that would otherwise be removed from the affordable housing supply, and development of housing or mixed-use developments that include affordable housing units. The program is administered under specific county regulations and guidelines governing eligibility, income and rent limits, and annual tenant certification requirements. Since 1989, DHCA has provided flexible financing as loans to for-profit and nonprofit affordable housing developers.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: County funding for multifamily housing development and rehabilitation projects provided primarily as non-recourse, secured loans with flexible terms. Funds may be used to construct or acquire affordable housing units, buy and rehabilitate existing rental units at risk of losing affordability, and assist in developing housing or mixed-use developments that include affordable housing units. Up to $28.0 million from Fiscal Year 2021 HIF funding was available beginning July 1, 2020. Loan terms are negotiated based on project needs; the interest rate is generally 3% but can vary depending on project purpose and financing. Loan repayments can amortize monthly, be deferred for a period of time, or be based on a property's annual available cash flow. Loans are subject to annual monitoring fees. Projects must maintain affordability for the greater of 30 years or the term of the Program Loan. Large projects are defined as projects with 10 or more county-funded units with $500,000 or more in county funds. Developers requesting county funds for projects with less than 10 county-funded units or less than $500,000 may use the small project application.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Experienced affordable housing developers, for-profit and nonprofit organizations, property owners/managers, and organizations seeking to promote affordable housing opportunities in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Multifamily housing development and rehabilitation; construction or acquisition of affordable housing units; purchase and rehabilitation of existing rental units at risk of losing affordability; development of housing or mixed-use developments with affordable housing components; limited pre-development costs in unique situations; capital purposes including new construction, acquisition, and acquisition/rehabilitation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Multifamily housing projects
Affordable housing focus with units serving households at or below 70% AMI
Compliance with income and rent limits
Annual tenant certification
Experienced affordable housing developers with demonstrated capacity in affordable housing development

Completed Program Application (Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development 202 Application for projects requesting more than $500,000; DHCA Small Project Application for less than $500,000)
Acceptable evidence of site control (deed, long-term lease with term at least six months longer than proposed Program loan and senior loan terms, or purchase contract with feasible closing date)
For new construction projects: sites must be currently zoned for intended use or developer must have feasible plan to obtain necessary zoning
No debarment or outstanding taxes with County
No outstanding DHCA obligations on other projects
Financial feasibility demonstrated through pro-forma analysis over 20 years, debt service coverage of 1.0, loan-to-value ratio generally not exceeding 100%
Appraisal ordered by first mortgage lender or DHCA reviewed before loan approval
Preference for projects with cash equity contribution from applicant's owner/sponsor/parent company
Preference for projects with at least 50% of developer's fee deferred for Low Income Housing Tax Credit projects
Projects must meet County's right of first refusal requirements under County Code Chapters 11A, 11C, and 53A
Readiness to proceed with ability to close within 12 months of funding commitment (or 12 months from tax credit award)
Projects should leverage other funding sources with target 3:1 leverage ratio
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on a rolling, continuous basis with no fixed deadline. Experienced rental housing developers submit either a small project application (for projects with less than 10 county-funded units or less than $500,000 in county funds) or a large project application (for projects with 10 or more county-funded units with $500,000 or more in county funds). Applicants are encouraged to discuss project proposals with DHCA staff for eligibility and feasibility prior to submission. Applications must be submitted by email to DHCA.Housing@montgomerycountymd.gov and include loan request summary forms, financial forms, cost estimates, and tenant housing reports for occupied rental housing. Upon receipt, DHCA staff will send an email receipt to the applicant. Applicants should provide complete, thorough applications; if DHCA requires clarification or additional information, the applicant must submit such material in a timely manner. Applications requesting Program funding are reviewed by a Selection Advisory Committee (SAC) appointed by the DHCA Director. The SAC reviews applications and makes a recommendation to the DHCA Director on whether a project should be considered for funding. The Director has sole discretion to determine whether to use Program funds for a project. After the Director's decision, the applicant receives notification about whether their project will be funded. The County may withdraw an appropriation of Program funding at any time prior to closing.

structured_extraction.program_description: A public campaign financing program that provides matching funds to eligible candidates running for Montgomery County elective offices (County Executive, Council-at-Large, and District Council). The program aims to encourage greater voter participation in County elections, increase opportunities for more residents to run for office, and reduce the influence of large contributions from businesses, political action groups, and other large organizations. Candidates must meet certification requirements by collecting qualifying contributions from Montgomery County residents. In the 2018 election cycle, 23 candidates received approximately $5.25 million in matching public funds total. In the 2022 election cycle, 20 candidates received approximately $3.7 million in matching public funds total.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides public matching funds to certified candidates based on qualifying contributions collected from Montgomery County residents. For County Executive, the maximum public contribution is $870,170 per election with matching ratios of 7 to 1 for the first $50 of qualifying contributions, 4 to 1 for $51-$100, and 2 to 1 for $101-$150, with $0 matching for contributions of $151-$500. For Council-at-Large, the maximum is $290,060 with matching ratios of 5 to 1 for the first $50, 3 to 1 for $51-$100, and 2 to 1 for $101-$150, with $0 matching for contributions of $151-$500. For District Council, the maximum is $145,030 with the same matching ratios as Council-at-Large. Qualifying contributions must be at least $5 but no more than $500. Matching contributions are determined based on the formula for the respective office. Public funds are distributed via direct deposit (ACH) to the candidate's publicly funded campaign account during the distribution period (365 days before the primary election through 30 days after the general election). In the 2018 election cycle, 23 candidates received approximately $5.25 million in matching public funds total. In the 2022 election cycle, 20 candidates received approximately $3.7 million in matching public funds total.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 26, 2026 (Certificate of Candidacy); April 15, 2026 (Notice of Intent and public financing committee registration); May 9, 2026 (Qualifying Period closes)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maurice Valentine (PEF Liaison) and David Crow (Fiscal Projects Manager)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Candidates running for Montgomery County elective offices, including County Executive, Council-at-Large, and District Council positions. Candidates must be Montgomery County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Campaign financing for candidates running for Montgomery County elective office. Allowable uses are limited to expenses directly related to election campaign activities incurred during the specific time period for either the primary or general election. Prohibited uses include personal expenses, paying for personal endorsements, paying late filing fees, and contributions to other candidates or political organizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Candidates must be Montgomery County residents. Qualifying contributions must be collected from Montgomery County residents with residential addresses in Montgomery County (no P.O. boxes). Only contributions from County residents are matched with public funds.
requirements_list: Candidate must be a Montgomery County resident
Candidate must be running for an eligible County elective office (County Executive, At-Large Councilmember, or District Councilmember)
Submit Certificate of Candidacy to Montgomery County Board of Elections by February 26, 2026
Register public campaign financing committee with Maryland Campaign Reporting Information System (MDCRIS) by April 15, 2026; Notice of Intent is generated automatically during registration
File Notice of Intent to Qualify with the State Board of Elections by April 15, 2026
Open a publicly funded campaign account with a bank prior to receiving public funds
Collect required number of qualifying contributions during the qualifying period (January 1, 2023 through May 9, 2026)
For County Executive: collect 500 qualifying contributions with $40,000 aggregate minimum
For Council-at-Large: collect 250 qualifying contributions with $20,000 aggregate minimum
For District Council: collect 125 qualifying contributions with $10,000 aggregate minimum
Qualifying contributions must be $5 or more but no more than $500 per contributor

Contribution receipts must include candidate full name, contributor name, contributor residential address in Montgomery County (no P.O. box), contribution amount, date of contribution, and contributor signature (or digital signature using a method approved by the Board)
Submit receipts for qualifying contributions with a summary sheet to the Board during the qualifying period or the receipt submission period
Submit campaign finance report including each qualifying contribution received, each expenditure made, and all receipts associated with each contribution and expenditure
Be certified by the Maryland State Board of Elections
Election must be contested (more candidates than positions available)
Only individual contributions are eligible; contributions from organizations, businesses, and political action committees are not allowed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Submit Certificate of Candidacy in person at Montgomery County Board of Elections by February 26, 2026. Step 2: Register your public campaign financing committee with MDCRIS at https://campaignfinance.maryland.gov by April 15, 2026; your Notice of Intent is generated automatically. During registration, provide committee name, candidate information (name, address, date of birth, email, phone, fax), chairperson information, treasurer information, and bank account information. Step 3: Open a publicly funded campaign account with a bank using the Statement of Organization generated from MDCRIS and an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the Internal Revenue Service. Update the bank account number in MDCRIS once opened. Step 4: Collect the required number of qualifying contributions from Montgomery County residents during the qualifying period (January 1, 2023 through May 9, 2026). Ensure each contribution is documented on a receipt that includes the candidate's full name, contributor's name and residential address in Montgomery County, contribution amount, date, and contributor's signature. Step 5: Submit receipts for qualifying contributions with a summary sheet to the Maryland State Board of Elections either in person or electronically via the Board's platform. Receipts can be submitted during the qualifying period or the receipt submission period (June 23, 2025 through June 23, 2026 for primary or November 3, 2026 for general election). Submissions may be made with regularly scheduled campaign finance reports or on the first and third Tuesday of each month. Step 6: The Maryland State Board of Elections will verify that you have met the certification requirements (required number and aggregate amount of qualifying contributions). Step 7: Once certified by the Board, public matching funds will be calculated based on the matching formula for your office and distributed via direct deposit (ACH) to your publicly funded campaign account during the distribution period (June 23, 2025 through December 3, 2026). Step 8: File campaign finance reports detailing all contributions and expenditures. Candidates work with the Montgomery County Office of Consumer Protection (PEF Liaison) for operational and logistical questions. Once approved by the state, the Department of Finance administers finances and disburses matching funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Recreation's Financial Aid Program (Rec Assist)
structured_extraction.program_description: Rec Assist is a financial assistance program administered by the Montgomery County Department of Recreation that helps eligible county residents who receive public assistance afford recreation programs, classes, memberships, and activities. The program reduces the cost of program and membership fees for qualifying families and individuals, making recreational opportunities more accessible. Eligible applicants receive $400 per family member placed on their recreation account to apply toward a variety of Recreation programming, including out-of-school time programs such as yoga, summer camps, swim lessons, sports, art, dance, and swim passes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible applicants receive $400 per family member placed on their recreation account. Funds subsidize activity and membership fees for Montgomery County Recreation programs. A minimum 20 percent co-payment per activity or membership is required at time of registration. Funds can only be applied to activities costing $25 or more; they cannot be used for activities under $25, facility rentals, gift cards, daily pool admissions, supplemental fees (including security deposits, withdrawal fees, materials fees, late pick-up fees), or merchandise. Funds are available for 12 months (January 1 – December 31, 2026) or until depleted, whichever comes first, on a first-come, first-served basis. Once the Rec Assist fund is depleted, participants must pay full price for all registrations, even if they still have Rec Assist dollars on their account.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications for 2026 are accepted from December 8, 2025 through November 30, 2026; funds valid through December 31, 2026 or until fund is depleted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who receive public assistance and their eligible family members, including families who receive FARMS (Free and Reduced Meal Services), TCA (Temporary Cash Assistance), SSI (Supplemental Social Security Income), Housing Assistance from a Shelter, SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program), Maryland Medicaid, Care for Kids, Maryland Energy Assistance, WIC, or Heat and Eat (H-EAT). Students attending Montgomery County Public Schools participating in Community Eligibility Provision also qualify.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for Montgomery County Recreation classes and programs including yoga, summer camps, swim lessons, sports, art, dance, and swim passes. Funds can only be applied to activities costing $25 or more. Applicants may purchase one swim punch pass per eligible family member per year with Rec Assist funds. Cannot be used for activities under $25, sports team league fees, facility rentals, recreation gift cards, daily pool admissions, supplemental fees (security deposits, withdrawal fees, materials fees, late pick-up fees), aquatic merchandise, previous account balances, or adjustments to previous registrations.

Alternatively, applicants may download the application form and mail it to Montgomery County Recreation, Attention: Rec Assist, 2425 Reedie Drive, 10th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902, or walk it in to the Department of Recreation's Customer Service office (Monday-Friday, 8:30 a.m. - 4:30 p.m., located at 2425 Reedie Drive, 10th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902). Applications without required documentation will not be processed. Notification of application status will be sent via email within 10 business days of receipt. Eligible applicants will have $400 per family member placed on their recreation account within 10 business days of approval. Applications are available in English, Spanish, Amharic, Chinese, French, Korean, and Vietnamese.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Senior Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A Montgomery County property tax credit available to homeowners age 65 or older whose home is their principal residence. The credit is calculated as 50 percent of the combined State Homeowners' Tax Credit and County Supplement, and is applied to the owner-occupied residential property tax bill. The credit may be based on the State Homeowners' Tax Credit, a County Supplement, or both combined, depending on individual eligibility. The program is designed to reduce the property tax burden for qualifying senior residents.

The credit is applied to the owner-occupied residential property tax bill. The credit may be based on the State Homeowners' Tax Credit, the County Supplement, or both combined, depending on which components the applicant qualifies for. The exact credit amount varies based on individual circumstances and eligibility for state and county components.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Senior Property Tax Deferral Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows qualifying seniors age 65 and older with family income below approximately $80,000 to defer the amount by which their current Montgomery County property tax exceeds their previous county property tax. The deferred taxes do not accrue interest during the deferral period but become a lien on the property and must be repaid when the property is sold, the owner moves, or other specified conditions occur. There is no deferral for state taxes, municipal taxes, water quality fees, solid waste fees, or other county charges.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program allows eligible seniors to defer payment of the amount by which their current county property tax exceeds their previous county property tax. The deferred taxes do not accrue interest during the deferral period and become a lien on the property. There is no deferral for state taxes, municipal taxes, water quality fees, solid waste fees, or other county charges. The deferred amount reduces the property tax burden for the current tax year only, and the accumulated deferred taxes cannot exceed 50% of the assessed value of the property. Deferred taxes must be repaid when the property is sold, the owner moves, the property becomes subject to tax sale, the use of the property changes, or other specified conditions occur. The County records the lien in the land records of Montgomery County and notifies all mortgagees and beneficiaries under any deed of trust. A homeowner may end a deferral at any time by giving written notice to the Director of Finance and paying the deferred tax.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior citizens (at least 65 years old) who own their principal residence in Montgomery County, have resided there for at least five consecutive years, and whose combined household income did not exceed $80,000 in the previous calendar year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Deferral of the increase in the Montgomery County property tax portion of the annual property tax bill, reducing the current year property tax burden for eligible seniors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The property must be located in Montgomery County, Maryland and must be the applicant's principal residence. The eligible property is limited to the real property on which the residence is located and the curtilage as determined by the Supervisor of Assessments, and any adjacent unimproved land on the same lot or parcel that is not assessed on the basis of agricultural use.
requirements_list: At least one applicant must be at least 65 years old
The property must be the applicants' principal residence
At least one applicant must have resided in the dwelling as their principal residence for five consecutive years and must continue to occupy the property as their principal residence

Combined gross income of all individuals who actually reside in the dwelling must not have exceeded $80,000 in the previous calendar year (excluding dependents and those paying reasonable fixed charges for rent or room and board)
The accumulated deferred taxes cannot exceed 50% of the assessed value of the property
Applicant must sign a Tax Deferral and Lien Agreement
Applicant must be a homeowner
Applicant must provide proof of age (copy of birth certificate, driver's license, or other proof of age)
If applicant filed a federal income tax return, a photocopy of the completed federal return including all accompanying schedules and other forms must be submitted
Property cannot be used for farming, business, or rental purposes (or if partially used, the percentage for residential use must be specified)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available in printed form at the Division of Treasury (27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, MD 20850) or as an electronic PDF. Applicants must complete the application form and the Tax Deferral and Lien Agreement form and submit both along with proof of age, a copy of the federal income tax return (if filed), and any required schedules or documentation to Treasury by September 1st of each year. Applications should be mailed to: Montgomery County Maryland Department of Finance, Division of Treasury, ATTN: Tax Deferral, 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, MD 20850. For the property tax year beginning July 1st, pay the full 1st installment in a timely manner to avoid interest charges. Once approved, the deferral will be applied toward the 2nd installment or refunded if the bill has been paid in full. The County will file a lien on the property at the expense of the property owner and notify mortgage companies and beneficiaries under any deed of trust. Incomplete applications will be returned and must be completed and resubmitted. Additional documentation or verification may be requested in individual cases.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Supplemental Homeowners' Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides additional County property tax credits for homeowners who qualify for the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit. The credit is based on a homeowner's household income compared to their property tax bill, calculated on a progressive scale based on combined gross income levels. Homeowners age 60 and older receive an additional 50% matching tax credit from Montgomery County. For the July 1, 2026 tax billing year, the combined income eligibility limit is $76,620, with a net worth limit of $255,400 (excluding principal residence and qualified retirement savings), and an assessed value threshold of $383,100. The credit percentage ranges from 0% to 8% depending on income level, with maximum annual adjustments based on the Consumer Price Index. For taxpayers age 70 or older, retroactive applications may be submitted for up to 3 prior years.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible homeowners receive a tax credit applied against General County and Special Service Area real property taxes. The credit amount is calculated based on a progressive scale according to combined gross income levels, ranging from 0% to 8% depending on income level. For the July 1, 2026 tax billing year, the combined income eligibility limit is $76,620 and the assessed value threshold is $383,100. Maximum annual adjustments are based on the Consumer Price Index. Homeowners age 60 and older who qualify receive an additional 50% matching tax credit from Montgomery County in addition to the state tax credit. The average combined credit with the Senior Property Tax Credit was $1,276 last year. No separate county application is required — approval for the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit automatically qualifies eligible applicants for the County Supplement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1st for that tax year; taxpayers age 70 and older may submit retroactive applications at any time for the current and 3 prior levy years
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners of all ages who qualify for the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit and reside in Montgomery County, with enhanced benefits for homeowners age 60 and older and retroactive filing provisions for those age 70 and older
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credits applied against County General and Special Service Area real property taxes, reducing the homeowner's county property tax bill
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must qualify for the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit
Must be a homeowner with owner-occupied principal residence
Household combined gross income must not exceed the annual limit (currently $76,620 for July 1, 2026 tax year)
Net worth must not exceed the annual limit (currently $255,400 for July 1, 2026), excluding principal residence and qualified retirement savings
Property assessed value must not exceed the annual threshold (currently $383,100 for July 1, 2026)
Homeowners age 60 and older receive an additional 50% matching tax credit
Taxpayers age 70 and older may submit retroactive applications for up to 3 prior levy years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete and submit the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit application to the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) by October 1st, either online at onestop.md.gov or via paper application. There is no separate application for the County Supplement — approval for the State credit automatically makes the applicant eligible for the County Supplement. Taxpayers age 70 and older may submit retroactive applications at any time for the current and 3 prior levy years. For assistance, contact 311 (240-777-0311), (800) 944-7403, or 410-767-5900.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Transfer of Development Rights Program (TDR)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows landowners in the Agricultural Reserve to sell development rights to designated growth areas elsewhere in the County. When development rights are sold, a TDR easement is placed on the property that permanently restricts development to a maximum of 1 unit per 25 acres.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners create Transferable Development Rights from their Agricultural Reserve land and sell them to designated receiving areas in growth zones. This generates private funds while placing a permanent easement on the property restricting development. To date, over 52,000 acres have been preserved through the TDR program with $117 million in private funds generated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of agricultural land in the Agricultural Reserve
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Landowners recapture lost equity from zoning changes by selling development rights to growth areas
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Agricultural Reserve property designated for the program. Development rights can be transferred to designated receiving areas elsewhere in the County.
requirements_list: Property must be located in the Agricultural Reserve
Property must be zoned to allow TDR creation

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Utility Assistance Program / Weatherization Program / Home Energy Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides help with past due utility bills for heating and electricity, as well as ongoing benefits, for residents at risk of service disconnection. Also assists low-income households with home energy costs through weatherization improvements to reduce long-term energy expenses. The program combines direct financial utility assistance with technical weatherization services.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance to help pay past due heating and electricity bills, with ongoing benefit options available for eligible residents. Also includes home energy assistance and weatherization improvements to help low-income households reduce energy costs. Applications can be completed online through MyDHR or submitted on paper.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents struggling with utility bills or at risk of service disconnection, particularly low-income households.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Heating and electricity bill assistance; home energy assistance; weatherization improvements to reduce energy costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Low income
Meet program eligibility criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications can be completed online through MyDHR, submitted on paper at 1301 Piccard Drive 4th floor Rockville, or dropped off at document drop boxes at housing stabilization offices. Phone appointments can be requested by calling 240-777-4450. Contact the program directly if at risk of shut off.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County Working Families Income Supplement (Refundable Earned Income Credit)
structured_extraction.program_description: A local tax credit program offered by Montgomery County that provides a 56% match of the State Refundable Earned Income Credit (EITC) for eligible low-income working residents of Montgomery County. To receive this credit, residents must file a Maryland tax return. Eligible ITIN filers may also receive this supplement. Residents with at least one dependent who qualify for the federal Earned Income Credit and the Maryland Earned Income Credit automatically receive a refund check from the Maryland Office of the Comptroller, funded by Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Montgomery County matches the State Refundable Earned Income Credit at 56%. Eligible residents receive a separate check from the Comptroller paid for by Montgomery County. ITIN filers are eligible. Checks are mailed on the following schedule: end of July for returns filed through June, end of October for returns filed July through September, and end of January for returns filed through December.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income working residents of Montgomery County who are eligible for the Maryland EITC, including ITIN filers and those with at least one dependent
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied to income tax liability or issued as a refund check
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must be a Montgomery County resident and file taxes as such for the year in which the Refundable Earned Income Credit is claimed
requirements_list: Must have earned income in the tax year
Must be eligible for the federal Earned Income Credit
Must claim the Maryland Earned Income Credit
Must have at least one dependent (for the refundable credit check)
Must be eligible for the State Refundable Earned Income Credit
Must have filed as a Montgomery County resident for the tax year
Must file a Maryland tax return
ITIN filers are eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents file their Maryland income tax return claiming the Maryland Earned Income Credit and the local supplement. The Maryland Office of the Comptroller verifies eligibility based on the information provided in the tax return. Eligible residents automatically receive the Montgomery County Refundable Earned Income Credit check without filing a separate application.

structured_extraction.program_name: Montgomery County's Pet Waste Management Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The program helps homeowner associations reduce bacteria levels in local rivers and streams by installing and maintaining pet waste stations in common areas. The Department of Environmental Protection collaborates with HOAs to provide onsite evaluation, outreach materials, pet waste stations, and maintenance support for up to one year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible homeowner associations receive onsite evaluation, outreach materials, pet waste stations (number determined based on the extent of the issue), and maintenance of the stations for up to one year at no cost. After one year, the HOA can decide to adopt the stations by taking over maintenance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowner associations and condominium associations in Montgomery County that do not currently have a pet waste management program and are interested in installing pet waste stations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation and maintenance of pet waste stations in common areas managed by homeowner associations to manage pet waste and reduce bacteria contamination in local waterways.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Located in Montgomery County. One exception: HOAs located in a municipality such as City of Rockville, City of Gaithersburg, and City of Takoma Park are not eligible.
requirements_list: Located in Montgomery County (with exceptions for certain municipalities)
Currently do not have a pet waste management program
Interested in having a pet waste management program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested HOA or condominium associations should send an email to AskDep@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov or call customer service at 311 (240-777-0311) to express interest and ask questions or concerns.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $25,000 zero-interest loans are granted to qualifying first-time home buyers. Up to $1.0 million is reserved specifically for County and MCPS employees under this program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time home buyers who are employees of Montgomery County Government or Montgomery County Public Schools (MCPS).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for home purchases.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time home buyer
Must be an employee of Montgomery County Government or Montgomery County Public Schools

Services include home visiting, prenatal and postpartum care coordination, health education, preparation for delivery and infant care, and referrals to community resources. Does not require immigration status. Formerly known as the Maternity Partnership Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free nurse case management, care coordination, community health worker services, home visiting, prenatal and postpartum care coordination, prenatal classes, health education, and referrals to community resources. Services are provided in the home or at health centers. Formerly known as the Maternity Partnership Program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income, uninsured, or Medicaid-enrolled pregnant women and recently postpartum mothers living in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prenatal care services, nurse case management, care coordination, home visiting services, prenatal and postpartum education, health education, and referrals to community resources
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents only
requirements_list: Must be pregnant or recently postpartum
Must be low-income, uninsured, or enrolled in Medicaid
Must live in Montgomery County
No immigration status requirement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No formal application required. Women can contact the Local Health Department directly to enroll. Contact Silver Spring Health Center at 240-777-3160 or Germantown Health Center at 240-777-3380. Women will be assessed and provided nurse case management or assigned to a Community Health Worker.
