structured_extraction.program_description: Gap financing for multifamily rental housing developments with more than four units. The program supports experienced rental housing developers with projects that comply with development and applicant requirements and meet preferred criteria to increase or preserve affordable rental housing.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Gap financing provided through a conditional commitment letter detailing terms and conditions of DHCA's participation in the project. The amount of financing is determined during staff review based on appropriate financing needs, existing requests, and priority considerations. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and processed in the year funding is required.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Manager of the Multifamily Section and Chief of Housing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Experienced rental housing developers with multifamily rental housing projects of more than four units seeking gap financing to increase or preserve affordable rental housing in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap financing for multifamily rental housing development and redevelopment projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must have more than four units
Applicant must be an experienced rental housing developer
Project must comply with development and applicant requirements
Project must meet one or more of the County and DHCA preferred criteria to increase or preserve affordable rental housing
Project must complete Intake or Inquiry form to begin
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Complete an Intake or Inquiry form. 2) DHCA staff contacts applicant to provide next steps and discusses project proposals for eligibility and feasibility. 3) Meeting with Manager of Multifamily Section and Chief of Housing to discuss the proposal. 4) Staff review of project, considering appropriate financing amount, existing requests, and priority considerations. 5) Quarterly updates provided as project plans evolve. 6) Developer obtains general support letter from DHCA if needed. 7) Developer finalizes development plan including land use approvals, entitlements, and financing. 8) Final application submission to Multifamily team for underwriting. 9) Project presented to DHCA Selection Advisory Committee (SAC) for review and recommendation. 10) DHCA Director reviews SAC recommendation and determines approval. 11) Final approval evidenced by conditional commitment letter.

structured_extraction.program_description: The My Turn Program provides support, funding, and programmatic and financial assistance to families with children ages 3 to 18 who have developmental disabilities and are not yet connected with State of Maryland resources. Services include outreach, assistance with summer camp placements, and funding for recreational community activities such as swimming and horseback riding. The program helps children with developmental disabilities participate in community-based activities and summer camp experiences. Therapeutic services such as occupational therapy, physical therapy, and speech therapy are not covered.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides funding for one recreational activity or summer camp session at a time. Funding covers community-based recreational activities such as swimming and horseback riding, as well as summer camp experiences and placements. Outreach and other programmatic and financial assistance are also provided to eligible families. Therapeutic services such as occupational therapy, physical therapy, and speech therapy are not covered.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Recreational activities: July to January; Summer camp requests: February to first week of July
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children ages 3 to 18 who have developmental disabilities and are not yet connected with State of Maryland resources, residing in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding for recreational community activities such as swimming and horseback riding, summer camp experiences and placements, outreach, and other programmatic and financial assistance for children with developmental disabilities. Therapeutic services are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland residents only.
requirements_list: Child must be ages 3 to 18 years old
Child must have a developmental disability as defined by Maryland Developmental Disability Administration (DDA)
Must be a Montgomery County resident
Family must not yet be connected with State of Maryland resources
Child must have a physical or mental condition other than a sole diagnosis of mental illness requiring individually planned and coordinated services
Condition must be likely to continue indefinitely
Condition must be manifested before age 22
Condition must result in inability to live independently
Must bring documentation pertaining to child's developmental disability including school records, Individualized Education Plan (IEP), and psychological evaluations
Only one funding request can be submitted at a time
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 240-777-1216 to schedule an interview with a My Turn Program staff member. Bring all documentation pertaining to the child's developmental disability, including school records, IEP, and psychological evaluations.

structured_extraction.program_description: A national discount program providing Montgomery County residents with free prescription discount cards and low-fee dental and health discount programs to help save money on prescription drugs, dental care, vision services, hearing aids, and other health-related expenses. The program offers savings on eyeglass frames, lenses, exams, accessories, contact lenses, laser vision services, hearing aids, diabetic supplies, and a wide range of dental procedures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers three components: (1) Montgomery RX (Prescription Discount Program) - free prescription discount cards saving an average of 24% off the retail price of prescription medicines, good at over 68,000 retail pharmacies nationwide with discounts available for county residents and their pets; (2) Dental Discount program - low-fee enrollment ($6.95 monthly individual, $8.95 monthly family, $69 annual individual, or $79 annual family) providing 15% to 50% discounts at over 110,000 dental providers nationwide covering check-ups, cleanings, fillings, crowns, x-rays, root canals and more, with no deductibles or benefit maximums; (3) Health Discount program - low-fee enrollment ($6.95 monthly individual, $8.95 monthly family, $69 annual individual, or $79 annual family) providing 15% to 75% discounts at a national network of providers including 35% off eyeglass frames and related vision services, 35% off hearing aids with complimentary screenings, discounts on diabetic supplies, prepaid lab work, and 15% off Lasik and PRK services through the U.S. Laser Network. This is NOT insurance.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 1-877-321-2652 for prescription discounts; 1-877-573-2395 for dental and health discounts; 1-800-364-6331 for assistance processing pharmacy claims
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents of all ages and income levels
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Prescription medications with average savings of 24%, dental care including check-ups, cleanings, fillings, crowns, x-rays, and root canals; vision services including eyeglass frames, lenses, exams, accessories, contact lenses, and Lasik/PRK surgery; hearing aids and complimentary screenings; diabetic supplies; and prepaid lab work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Prescription discounts are valid at over 68,000 retail pharmacies nationwide. Dental discounts available at over 110,000 providers nationwide. Health discounts available at a national network of providers.
requirements_list: Resident of Montgomery County
This is NOT insurance
Discounts only available at participating pharmacies and providers
Member must pay entire cost less applicable discount
Savings may vary by drug/service and by pharmacy/provider
Prescription claims not eligible for reimbursement through Medicaid, Medicare, or other government programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the Prescription Discount Program (Montgomery RX): Pick up a free card at all Montgomery County libraries, regional service centers, or senior centers. Alternatively, download and print your own card from the program website at www.nacorx.org or call toll-free 1-877-321-2652. Present the card to your pharmacist who will activate it. For Dental and Health Discount programs: Enroll by selecting your preferred plan and paying the applicable monthly or annual fee online at www.nacohealth.org, or call the toll-free number 1-877-573-2395 to learn more and enroll. The plan includes a 30-day cancellation provision.

structured_extraction.program_name: Neighborhood Events Matching Funds (NEMF) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered through Montgomery County's Regional Service Offices that provides matching funds to neighborhood organizations, block groups, tenant associations, and civic clubs to hold community events and activities that promote engagement, capacity building, networking, and stimulate the local economy. The program supports neighborhood events and educational community gatherings across five regional service areas in Montgomery County, encouraging community involvement and local economic growth.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $1,000 per applicant per funding cycle (July 1 – June 30) are provided on a matching basis (dollar-for-dollar, 1:1 match) with cash or in-kind donations from the applicant to help cover expenses for community events. Matches can be made through volunteer hours, work/effort by members, donations of services or materials, or cash donations. Funding is distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. For the funding cycle July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026, events must take place within that period. First-time applicants receive priority consideration.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; applications processed on a first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.contact_name: Regional Service Offices: Thomas C. Dant (Bethesda/Chevy Chase), Ayanna King (East County), Talia Beaulieu-Hains (Mid-County), Nahom Tekle (Silver Spring), Jake Adler (UpCounty)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local neighborhood organizations, block groups, tenant associations, and civic clubs that are active and in good standing in Montgomery County, across five regional service areas: Bethesda-Chevy Chase, East County, Mid-County, Silver Spring, and UpCounty.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Event and activity expenses for neighborhood gatherings and educational community events that are open to residents and create sustainable and lasting positive impacts for the neighborhood. Eligible expenses may include food, paper products, printing, equipment rental, and other items necessary to host the event.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, administered through five Regional Service Offices: Bethesda-Chevy Chase, East County, Mid-County, Silver Spring, and UpCounty. Applicants should determine their region using the GIS tool at https://gis3.montgomerycountymd.gov/AboutMyAddress/AboutMyAddress.html.
requirements_list: Organization must be a neighborhood organization, block group, tenant association, or civic club
Organization must be active and in good standing
Eligible activities must be open to all residents (unless applicant provides explanation for restrictions)
Activities must create sustainable and lasting impacts for the neighborhood
All events must comply with Montgomery County Law
Applicants must provide proof of payment (receipts) for expenditures from the eligible activity
Grant funds must be matched dollar for dollar (1:1) with cash or in-kind donations (volunteer hours, donated services, donated materials, or cash)
Maximum funding of $1,000 per applicant per funding cycle (July 1 – June 30)
Applicant group must be registered in the County Central Vendor System (https://azex32.montgomerycountymd.gov/cvrs)
A final report must be submitted after the event
First-time applicants receive priority for funding consideration
The group must agree to program rules and conditions of the grant prior to payment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit an online application through SeamlessDocs (https://montgomerycountymd.seamlessdocs.com/ng/fa/2p14wq9mrqer) or download a PDF form from your Regional Service Office. 2. Complete the application form including applicant information, event details, estimated expenses, and matching funds pledge. 3. Submit the completed application to your corresponding Regional Service Office (contact information provided on form). 4. The Regional Service Office will review the application to determine if the event qualifies, typically taking 1-2 weeks. 5. If approved, you will receive a notice with the grant amount (up to $1,000). 6. Register your group in the County Central Vendor System if not already registered. 7. Provide receipts and documentation of expenses and matching donations. 8. Host your event and submit a final report after completion. 9. Payment is issued after all post-event requirements are met. For PDF versions or applications in different languages, contact your Regional Service Office directly.

structured_extraction.program_description: A training, mentorship, and technical assistance program that helps new and beginning farmers develop viable agricultural businesses in Montgomery County. The program provides classroom and equipment training, business consulting, mentoring from experienced farmers, and connects applicants with available farmland through local landowners in the Agricultural Reserve. Participants receive training in marketing, business planning, accounting, sustainable farm practices, and more, while also gaining access to shared equipment through the Montgomery Soil Conservation District.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants receive classroom training held once a week in the evenings from January through March, covering topics such as customer validation, marketing, business planning, soils and composting, agritourism, value-added products, equipment and infrastructure, farm accounting and taxes, food safety, organic certification, season extension techniques, and integrated pest management. Equipment training is provided as weather permits. Business consulting services are also available through UMD Extension. The program also provides mentoring from experienced farmers (mentors provide advice and counseling for a minimum of one year) and matches participants with private landowners in the Agricultural Reserve for long-term leased sites. Participants have access to shared equipment through the Montgomery Soil Conservation District to reduce startup costs. Please note that the New Farmer Program is not fully active due to budgetary and staffing reductions primarily affecting the mentorship and land matching components; however, training and other available assistance continue to be provided.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are submitted during sign up periods; applicants will be advised of their status in December
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and beginning farmers interested in starting or expanding agricultural or horticultural businesses in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and technical assistance for developing farm business plans and starting agricultural operations; mentorship from experienced farmers; land matching services connecting farmers with private landowners in the Agricultural Reserve; access to shared farm equipment through the Montgomery Soil Conservation District to reduce startup costs; business consulting through UMD Extension
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, with land matching focused on the Montgomery County Agricultural Reserve
requirements_list: Minimum 1-3 years of farm experience
Thoughtful enterprise concept demonstrating good market opportunity
Work history and references
Agriculture or horticulture training will support future business plans
Personal capacity to take risk and resources to cover living expenses
Awareness of sustainable farming principles
Must be a new farmer seeking to establish an agricultural enterprise in Montgomery County
Must live in or plan to live in Montgomery County; must have access to transportation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a New Farmer Program Application to the Montgomery County Office of Agriculture during sign-up periods. The Office of Agriculture and UMD Extension advisors review the application and contact applicants to provide assistance where needed. Ratings for the mentorship aspect of the program (when available) are based on specified criteria: thoughtful enterprise concept demonstrating good market opportunity, years of farm experience, work history and references, how agriculture/horticulture training will support future business plans, personal capacity to take risk with resources to cover living expenses, and awareness of sustainable farming principles. Highest-rated applicants are invited for interviews. Applicants are notified of their status in December. Accepted participants then work with landowners to negotiate and sign lease or contract agreements for farmland (Montgomery County will not be a party to the lease agreement), are matched with an experienced mentor, and gain access to business planning and technical resources.

structured_extraction.program_name: New Jobs Tax Credit (including Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit)
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program for businesses that expand their physical space and hire new employees in Montgomery County. The program includes two tiers: the regular New Jobs Tax Credit (6-year credit) for businesses that expand by at least 5,000 square feet and create at least 25 new permanent full-time jobs within 24 months; and the Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit (24-year credit) for very large expansion projects in qualified industries that meet substantially higher thresholds for space, jobs, and wages. Both credits are based on increased property tax assessments from the expansion, and companion State tax credits are also available.
list_of_eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Regular New Jobs Tax Credit: A 6-year credit against real and personal property taxes based on increased assessments from expansion. Credit rates: Years 1-2: 52%; Years 3-4: 39%; Years 5-6: 26%. Enhanced New Jobs Tax Credit: A 24-year credit at 58.5% of additional local tax liability for all 24 years. State tax credits also apply: Regular credit — 28% (years 1-2), 21% (years 3-4), 14% (years 5-6); Enhanced credit — 31.5% for each of 24 years. State credits apply against corporate or personal income taxes, financial institutions franchise tax, or insurance premiums tax, and can be carried forward up to five years. Both credits are subject to recapture if job and space requirements are not maintained for three years. Businesses must not previously occupy the new or expanded premises to qualify.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Business must notify County before expansion begins; 6 years to create/fill jobs and acquire space
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jennifer E. Barrett, Director or Michael Parent
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses seeking to locate, maintain, or expand operations in Montgomery County. Businesses already resident in the County or moving from outside Maryland are eligible. Businesses moving from other Maryland counties or Baltimore City are not eligible. Retailers are not eligible for the regular credit. The Enhanced credit targets large companies in qualified industries.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Credits are applied against real and personal property taxes (and State income/franchise/insurance taxes) to reduce tax liability resulting from business expansion involving increased space and new employees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Montgomery County. Businesses already in Montgomery County or relocating from outside Maryland are eligible. Businesses moving from another Maryland county or Baltimore City are not eligible. New or expanded premises must not have been previously occupied to qualify.
requirements_list: Regular Credit: Increase space by at least 5,000 square feet and create at least 25 new permanent full-time employees within a 24-month period
Notify the County before expanding space and staff
Businesses already resident in the County or moving from outside Maryland are eligible; businesses moving from other Maryland counties or Baltimore City are not eligible
Retailers are not eligible for the regular New Jobs Tax Credit
New or expanded premises must not have been previously occupied

Enhanced Credit — must be in a qualified industry (manufacturing, mining, transportation, communications, agriculture, forestry, fishing, research/development/testing, biotechnology, computer programming/data processing/computer services, central financial/real estate/insurance services, central administrative offices or company headquarters, public utility, warehousing, or business services)

Enhanced Credit — must meet at least one of three thresholds: (1) increase space by 250,000+ sq ft and create 1,250+ new permanent full-time jobs, with all employees earning 150%+ of federal minimum wage; (2) increase space by 250,000+ sq ft, create 500+ new permanent full-time jobs (if already have 2,500+ existing positions), with all employees earning 150%+ federal minimum wage; or (3) expend $150M+ to increase space by 700,000+ sq ft, create 500+ new permanent full-time jobs (if already have 1,100+ existing positions), pay all employees 150%+ federal minimum wage and provide subsidized health care
Complete required space acquisition and job creation within six years of notification
Credits subject to recapture if job and space requirements are not maintained for three years
Business must demonstrate it pays individual or corporation income tax, financial institution franchise tax, or insurance premiums tax
No other tax credit or exemption can be given for the same new or expanded premises during the same taxable year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses must submit a notification letter to the Montgomery County Department of Finance (Jennifer E. Barrett, Director, 101 Monroe Street, 15th Floor, Rockville, Maryland 20850) stating intent to seek the credit before expanding space and staff. The notification should include current business location and employee count, planned expansion details (square footage and employee count), and target completion date. Submit quarterly filing documentation (Maryland withholding taxes or unemployment insurance taxes) and a copy of lease or space documentation. Submit the New Jobs Tax Credit Application form, which requires business information, property details, number of new permanent full-time positions, tax payment information, and documentation verifying payroll records and employee time sheets. The business then has six years to acquire the new space and hire the required employees. Once requirements are met, notify the County Department of Finance to begin receiving the credit. Applicants must provide documentation to verify information for the taxable year the credit is sought and for the three taxable years following the last year in which a tax credit was granted.

structured_extraction.program_description: This recurring grant program, administered by Montgomery County's Office of Emergency Management and Homeland Security, provides funding to nonprofit community service providers, places of worship, religious organizations, and other faith-based institutions in Montgomery County to improve their preparedness and security. Organizations at higher risk of hate crimes or violence can request funding to support costs related to security personnel, training, planning, and security equipment and infrastructure. The program has operated across multiple fiscal years (FY24, FY25, FY26) and aims to ensure residents feel safe when gathering to worship and celebrate community.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Office of Emergency Management and Homeland Security offers up to $1.2 million in grants per fiscal year for FY26. Organizations at higher risk of hate crimes or violence can request up to $15,000 per facility (reduced from $20,000 in FY24) to support costs related to security personnel, planning, training, security assessments, security drills, or security equipment such as cameras and fususCORE devices. Organizations with multiple facilities may submit up to five separate applications (one per facility). The grant period is 12 months upon execution of a grant agreement. Eligible uses include hiring or augmenting security personnel, paying for security assessments or plans, conducting security training, developing and executing security drills, and purchasing new security cameras or fususCORE devices to share camera feeds with Montgomery County Police. Ineligible expenses include equipment purchases (except security cameras and fususCORE), facility upgrades, supplies, pre-contract expenses, security camera monitoring services, and fususCORE subscription services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Tuesday, November 4, 2025, at 11:59 PM (Extended from original date of Tuesday, October 28, 2025)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ali Hoy (Program Manager II, Office of Grants Management) and Ehsan Bahador (Emergency Management Specialist, OEMHS)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit community service providers, places of worship, religious organizations, and faith-based institutions in Montgomery County that have experienced or are at higher risk of hate crimes and violence. structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Security personnel, training, planning, security assessments, security drills, security equipment (cameras, fususCORE devices to share camera feeds with police), and other safety improvements to protect against hate crimes and violence. Funds cannot be used for equipment purchases (except cameras and fususCORE), facility upgrades, supplies, expenses incurred before contract execution, security camera monitoring services, or fususCORE subscription services.

requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization with Federal 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status or a religious organization meeting 501(c)(3) requirements
Must be experiencing threats or hate crimes, or be at significant risk of hate crimes based on work, community, and/or known threats to similar organizations or communities nationally
Must be currently registered and in Good Standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Must be registered as a vendor with Montgomery County (organizations not already vendors must register before submitting application)
All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County

Proposed expenses must be for a new activity, expansion of existing activities, or combination of both; cannot supplant other funding
For-profit businesses are not eligible
Organizations with multiple facilities must submit separate applications for each facility, with a limit of five (5) applications per organization
Must provide documentation of hate crimes or threats (police reports demonstrating prior hate or bias-related incidents)
Must provide at least two quotes or proposals from vendors for each eligible expense included in the budget
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Office of Grants Management's Euna Grants (eCivis) online platform. The process includes three stages of review: (1) Administrative review by OGM to assess Montgomery County eligibility conditions and application completeness; (2) Programmatic eligibility review by OEMHS to ensure proposals meet program requirements; (3) Subject Matter Expert review by a review committee composed of neutral, qualified individuals from Montgomery County Government and possibly the broader community, selected for their experience in the program's subject area, grants administration, project management, and ability to analyze programs through a racial equity and social justice lens. Applicants must complete the following tasks: Lead Applicant Information (legal name, SDAT ID, Federal TIN, board list, IRS 990 form or exemption explanation), Lead Applicant Background (optional demographic data for racial equity analysis), Application Questions (project title, funding request, cost-shares, total project cost, organization need, use of funds, benefit estimate, current security funding, security assessment status, training participation, reduced funding impact, county location assurance), Required Supporting Document Uploads (police reports demonstrating need and at least two vendor quotes for each expense), and Budget Tool with Budget Narrative. An optional information session is held via Microsoft Teams. Award notification letters are expected in January 2026. Grantees must submit semi-annual and final activity and financial reports showing authorized activities and expenses. Program opens for applications Tuesday, September 30, 2025. Information session: Wednesday, October 1, 2025, 7:00-8:00 PM via MS Teams. Deadline extended to Tuesday, November 4, 2025, 11:59 PM.

structured_extraction.program_name: Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) Exemption
structured_extraction.program_description: The PILOT Program provides County and State real property tax abatements to support affordable housing development and preservation in Montgomery County. The County negotiates an exemption from County real and special area property taxes in exchange for a property owner's commitment to provide affordable housing to low-income residents. There are two tracks: (1) By-Right PILOTs, established by Bill 26-21 (effective March 28, 2022), which are automatically granted to projects owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County or non-profit developers where at least 50% of units are reserved for households earning 60% or less of Area Median Income for at least 15 years — these abate 100% of County real property taxes; and (2) Standard PILOTs, which are negotiated on a case-by-case basis for for-profit or non-profit rental housing projects, lowering or eliminating County real property taxes for a negotiated period tied to the affordability commitment. All PILOTs are administered under a Regulatory Agreement recorded in land records, and are overseen by the Department of Housing and Community Affairs and the Department of Finance. Property owners or managers must pay an annual monitoring fee of $40 per unit per year and file annual financial reports and compliance certificates.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The PILOT program provides County real property and special area tax abatements for qualifying affordable rental housing projects. There are two tracks: (1) By-Right PILOT: 100% abatement of all County real property taxes for at least 15 years, automatically granted to projects owned or controlled by the Housing Opportunities Commission of Montgomery County or non-profit developers where at least 50% of units are reserved for households earning 60% or less of Area Median Income. The PILOT is administered under a Regulatory Agreement recorded in land records and may be transferable under certain conditions. (2) Standard PILOT: Negotiated abatement that lowers or eliminates County real property taxes for a period tied to the affordability commitment. Tax abatement is typically calculated per affordable rental unit based on the average County homeowner tax credit (adjusted annually) as authorized under Maryland Tax-Property Code Section 9-104. Standard PILOTs are not transferable. For non-HOC properties, the County Council sets maximum annual funding limits for a 10-year period. All property owners/managers must pay an annual monitoring fee of $40 per unit per year, due by September 30th, and file annual financial reports and compliance certificates.

Legal description of the property
Project description including total number of units and number of affordable units
Documentation demonstrating affordability of units such as rent rolls or LIHTC Covenants
For Standard PILOT: project financial pro forma including evidence of financial commitments for total project costs and financial need for the PILOT
For Standard PILOT: demonstrate site control equivalent to fee simple title, 99-year lease, or option to purchase with no contingencies except financing
Rent levels must be limited according to applicable regulations
Property owners/managers must file annual financial reports and compliance certificates
Annual monitoring fee of $40 per unit per year, due by September 30th
Must comply with PILOT regulations and meet requirements of Maryland law governing PILOTs
County Council approval required for non-HOC properties under Standard PILOT track
Any other information or documentation reasonably required by the County to determine applicant eligibility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit required information electronically to DHCA.Multifamily@MontgomeryCountyMD.gov or by mail to Department of Housing and Community Affairs, 1401 Rockville Pike, 4th Floor, Attn: PILOT Request, Rockville, MD 20852. For By-Right PILOTs, the County reviews documentation to confirm eligibility and executes a Regulatory Agreement recorded in land records. For Standard PILOTs, the County analyzes the request to define the level of PILOT required using financial information provided by the property owner; terms are negotiated between the property owner and the County; County Council approval is required for non-HOC properties. The Department of Finance calculates property tax abatement amounts and credits them against County property taxes on annual tax bills. The Asset Management team ensures ongoing compliance with affordability terms.

structured_extraction.program_name: Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) & Housing Initiative Program (HIP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Initiative Program (HIP) is a permanent supportive housing program for Montgomery County residents experiencing homelessness. Participants pay 30% of their adjusted gross income directly to the landlord, with the program covering the remaining 70% of rent via check or direct deposit. The program includes monthly case management and supportive services to help participants remain stably housed.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HIP covers application fees and security deposits (up to 2 months rental amount). Participants pay 30% of adjusted gross income directly to the landlord; HIP covers the remaining 70% of rent via check or direct deposit. Participants receive a utility allowance to assist with utility costs. Ongoing supportive services include monthly case management and in-home visits tailored to participant needs. The subsidy is permanent as long as participants qualify and remain eligible, requiring annual renewals in the first year and bi-annual renewals thereafter.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents experiencing homelessness or residing in shelter placement, and their landlords. Participants must have combined adjusted monthly household income not exceeding 30% of area median income and household assets not exceeding $10,000. Participants must be included in at least one special population category.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Permanent supportive housing with application fees, security deposits, rent subsidies (70% of monthly rent), utility allowances, case management, and supportive services to maintain stable housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be Montgomery County resident
Must be homeless or residing in shelter placement
Combined adjusted monthly household income must not exceed 30% of area median income
Household assets must not exceed $10,000

Must be included in at least one special population: sensory, cognitive or mobile impairment; developmental disability or chronic mental disorder; co-occurring disability; chronic substance abuse; elderly person in need of independent or supportive housing; or homeless status
All participants are referred through the Montgomery County Coordinated Entry System (CES) and assessed for Permanent Supportive Housing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: All HIP participants are referred from the Montgomery County Coordinated Entry System (CES) and are assessed for Permanent Supportive Housing eligibility. Interested landlords can contact HIP@montgomerycountymd.gov to express interest in partnering with the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A recurring annual grant program administered by Montgomery County that supports place-based initiatives and organizations working to improve specific neighborhoods and communities through comprehensive, coordinated strategies aligned with the Main Street Approach. The program has been offered across multiple fiscal years (FY23–FY26), providing funding to nonprofit organizations implementing neighborhood-level improvement efforts and commercial corridor revitalization in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant program providing funding ranging from $50,000 to $200,000 per award for up to 12 months of project implementation. FY26 awards total $450,000 distributed among 2-5 awards, with at least $200,000 designated for programs serving the Silver Spring Regional Services Center area and at least $50,000 (contingent on State award) for Damascus Main Street Area. Multi-year funding proposals accepted for up to three years total, with funding beyond the first 12 months contingent on satisfactory performance and appropriation of funds. Funds are tranche-funded (quarterly or semi-annual payments based on grant monitor approval of programmatic and financial reports). Eligible operating expenses include administrative costs, staff salaries and benefits, community and business outreach, implementation of economic development activities, and place-based management. Indirect costs up to 15% or applicant's federal NICRA rate allowed. Capital expenses (defined as $5,000 or more for fixed assets), lobbying, supplanting other funding sources, and prior obligations are ineligible.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Cornelius Kuteesa, Community Projects Manager II, CEC; Ali Hoy, Program Manager II, OGM
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations implementing place-based strategies to improve specific neighborhoods and commercial corridors in Montgomery County through economic growth, revitalization, and community engagement aligned with the Main Street Approach.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community development, neighborhood improvement, coordinated services, place-based management strategies, commercial corridor revitalization, retention and attraction of neighborhood-serving retail and small businesses, unification of commercial corridors through events, promotion, marketing, maintenance, and diverse stakeholder engagement. Activities must fall into two main categories: provision of assistance to commercial areas to retain, expand, and attract neighborhood-serving retail and other small businesses, and unification and strengthening of commercial corridors through events, promotion, marketing, maintenance, and diverse stakeholder engagements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County commercial corridors and economic development areas. Priority funding areas include the Silver Spring Regional Services Center area (minimum $200,000) and Damascus Main Street Area (minimum $50,000 contingent on State award). All activities and expenditures must occur in Montgomery County or be exclusively for Montgomery County residents.
requirements_list: Organization must have federal 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) tax-exempt status or be a collaboration with at least one entity having this status
Organization must be currently registered and in Good Standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Principal place of business must be located in Montgomery County; if national or regional organization, must have Montgomery County location providing related services
All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and exclusively for Montgomery County residents
Applicants may submit only one application per organization under this NOFO
Proposed expenses must be for new activity, expansion of existing activities, or combination of both; County funding cannot supplant other funding for already planned activities
Organization must have active engagement with stakeholders including broad-based community support from both public and private sectors
Organization must have well-defined vision and mission statements relevant to community conditions and equity principles
Organization must have operational board and/or committees staffed by volunteers aligned with Main Street Four Point Approach
Grant Monitor(s) shall have ability to serve as ex officio member of Grantee organization's Board of Directors at Grantor's discretion
Current Montgomery County contract or grant award winners must be in performance compliance and current on all reporting obligations with substantial progress toward award goals
Organization must verify status with SDAT prior to application review and maintain Good Standing throughout grant period
Organization must register with Montgomery County Central Vendor Registration System (CVRS) if awarded to receive payments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Register and create a profile on the Euna (eCivis) online application platform at https://portal.ecivis.com. Step 2: Verify organization is registered and in Good Standing with Maryland State Department of Assessment and Taxation (SDAT) at https://egov.maryland.gov/BusinessExpress/EntitySearch. Step 3: Register with Montgomery County Central Vendor Registration System (CVRS). Step 4: Access the FY26 PBM Grant Program Solicitation Page at https://gn.ecivis.com/GO/gn_redir/T/h7m493ns9moj and click "Apply" button. Step 5: Complete all application tasks including Applicant Information, Applicant Background, Project Strategy, Project Staffing Plan, Project Work Plan/Timeline, Performance Plan, Budget Tool, and Goals Tool. Step 6: Attend optional virtual Information Session (January 22, 2026, 1:00-2:00 PM) for guidance. Step 7: Submit complete application through Euna platform by Monday, March 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM. Application Review Process: OGM conducts administrative review assessing Organization and Montgomery County Eligibility Conditions; CEC conducts Proposal and Organization Eligibility Review; SME Review Committee composed of neutral, qualified individuals scores proposals using Confidence Rating System (100 possible points) based on Alignment with Funding Priorities (30 points), Management and Programmatic/Operational Capacity (30 points), Feasibility of Design and Approach (25 points), and Racial Equity and Cultural Proficiency (15 points); Final award decisions made approximately one month after deadline based on scores, reconciliation of funding across categories, and other factors including applicant performance history.

structured_extraction.program_description: FEMA makes federal funds available to state, local, tribal and territorial governments to plan for and implement sustainable, cost-effective measures designed to reduce the risk to individuals and property from future natural hazards, while also reducing reliance on federal funding from future disasters. The program is part of FEMA's Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) programs, which include Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC), Flood Mitigation Assistance (FMA), Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP), and HMGP Post Fire.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal grant funding administered through the Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) program to implement sustainable, cost-effective mitigation measures before disasters occur. Funding can support capability and capacity building activities (hazard mitigation planning, codes and standards, technical assistance), hazard mitigation projects (property acquisition, structure elevation, mitigation reconstruction, floodproofing, wildfire mitigation, retrofitting, warning systems, and other eligible activities), and management costs. For most HMA programs, eligible sub-applicants must provide a 25% non-federal cost share (federal share up to 75%). Small impoverished communities may be eligible for up to 90% federal share under BRIC. Flood Mitigation Assistance (FMA) and severe repetitive loss (SRL) properties may be eligible for up to 100% federal share. Repetitive loss (RL) properties may be eligible for up to 90% federal share. FEMA provides 100% federal funding for subrecipient management costs for BRIC program activities. Projects cannot be started or completed before the kick-off meeting with MDEM. All eligible activities must be included in the applicant's Scope of Work prior to the close of the application period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application timeframe varies based on Notices of Funding Opportunities (NOFO) announcement from federal government; Notices of Interest received after August of each year will be kept in repository for next cycle
structured_extraction.program_audience: State, local, tribal and territorial governments seeking to reduce risk from future natural hazards. Sub-applicants may include state agencies, local governments, Indian tribal governments, special governmental districts, and private nonprofits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sustainable, cost-effective measures designed to reduce risk to individuals and property from future natural hazards. Eligible uses include: (1) Capability and Capacity Building activities such as hazard mitigation planning, planning-related activities, advance assistance, project scoping, technical assistance, partnerships, and codes and standards; (2) Hazard Mitigation Projects including property acquisition and demolition, mitigation reconstruction, structure elevation, stabilization, flood risk reduction, floodproofing, tsunami vertical evacuation, safe rooms, wildfire mitigation, retrofitting, secondary power sources, warning systems, and aquifer recharge/storage/recovery; and (3) Management costs to support execution and completion of projects (limited to 5% of total cost estimate).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland and other eligible jurisdictions. The program is administered at the federal level by FEMA and at the state level by Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM). Local applications are coordinated through Montgomery County Office of Emergency Management and Homeland Security (OEMHS).
requirements_list: Sub-applicant must be a state agency, local government, Indian tribal government, special governmental district, or private nonprofit organization
Sub-applicant is responsible for non-federal cost share (typically 25% minimum; higher percentages may apply depending on program and project type)
Sub-applicant must not use federal funds for non-federal cost share
Project must be aligned with and included in applicant's FEMA-approved Hazard Mitigation Plan (HMP) in compliance with 44 CFR Part 201
Projects cannot be started or completed prior to kick-off meeting with MDEM
Measures must be sustainable and cost-effective with a benefit-cost ratio demonstrating cost-effectiveness
For flood-related projects under FMA: community must be registered in and in good standing with National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP); property must have an active NFIP policy
Subapplication must include detailed Scope of Work, Schedule, and Budget
Environmental and Historic Preservation review and documentation required
All activities must be identified in Scope of Work prior to close of application period
Applicant must comply with federal requirements including non-discrimination, accessibility, procurement standards, Build America Buy America Act, and conflict of interest provisions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: (1) Submission begins with Notice of Interest (NOI) submitted to Montgomery County Office of Emergency Management and Homeland Security (OEMHS) in August each year. (2) OEMHS reviews NOIs for basic applicability to FEMA Hazard Mitigation Assistance programs (BRIC, FMA, HMGP). (3) OEMHS submits recommended NOIs to Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM). (4) Upon State recommendation and approval, OEMHS provides technical assistance to applicants. (5) OEMHS submits recommended sub-applications to FEMA through MDEM. (6) FEMA evaluates applications for eligibility, feasibility, effectiveness, and cost-effectiveness. (7) MDEM disburses grant awards to awarded sub-applicants. (8) Fillable NOI and sub-application forms are provided by OEMHS. Applicants should refer to FEMA's HMA Program and Policy Guide for detailed requirements on Scope of Work, budget documentation, cost-effectiveness analysis, environmental and historic preservation documentation, and all assurances and certifications.
attachment_urls: https://www.montgomerycountymd.gov/OEMHS/Resources/Files/Hazard Mitigation Assistance Program and Policy Guide (2024).pdf

structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program administered by Montgomery County that provides financial incentives for residents, businesses, and non-profit organizations to install private security cameras on their properties. The program aims to deter and solve crime by increasing video surveillance in the community. Homeowners can receive up to $250 per camera installed at their residence, while businesses and non-profit organizations can receive rebates for up to five cameras, totaling up to $1,250. Camera footage is not shared with police unless the owner voluntarily integrates their camera through MoCoConnect. The program began accepting applications on November 15, 2023, and has been expanded from specific high-crime priority areas (including the 4th Police District Wheaton-Glenmont area and the 6th District Gaithersburg/Montgomery Village area) to cover more communities around downtown business centers and, ultimately, the entire county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residents/homeowners can receive up to $250 in reimbursement per security camera installed at their home. Businesses and non-profit organizations can receive up to $1,250 in reimbursement for up to 5 cameras ($250 per camera). The program has been expanded to cover more communities around downtown business centers and the entire county.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners or tenants of residential, business, or nonprofit properties in Montgomery County, particularly those in areas experiencing high crime rates including the 4th Police District (Wheaton-Glenmont) and 6th District (Gaithersburg/Montgomery Village).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of private security cameras at residential properties, businesses, and non-profit organizations within Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available countywide in Montgomery County, Maryland. Originally targeted eligible priority areas with high crime rates in specific police districts (4th District Wheaton-Glenmont, 6th District Gaithersburg/Montgomery Village). The program has since been expanded to include more communities around downtown business centers and ultimately the entire county.
requirements_list: Applicant must be owner or tenant of the property
Property must be used as a residence, business, or nonprofit organization
Property must be located in an eligible area within Montgomery County
Home ownership or tenancy in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can learn more about the program, check their eligibility, and complete an application at montgomerycountymd.gov/pol/howdoI/security-camera-rebate.html. For additional information, contact Sgt. Ijeoma Enendu at 240-773-5581 or ijeoma.enendu@montgomerycountymd.gov, or call the Montgomery County Police Department at 240-773-5700.

structured_extraction.program_description: A zoning program that allows affordable housing (rental and for-sale) to be developed in commercial and industrial zones in Montgomery County where residential uses are not normally permitted. Housing is designed and priced to be affordable to households earning 75 percent of county median income, adjusted for family size.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program permits developers to build residential housing (both rental and for-sale) in certain commercial and industrial zones through a special exception approval process. Base residential density is six units per acre; this can increase to 21.5 units per acre if at least 35 percent of units are affordable to households at or below county median income. For-sale affordable units are controlled for ten years; rental units are controlled for twenty years. Sales prices must not exceed 175 percent of comparable Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit prices. Rental rates are set at 75 percent of area-wide median income for a four-person family, adjusted for family size, with maximum rents not exceeding 30 percent of calculated gross household income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers seeking to build residential housing in commercial and industrial zones in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are used to develop affordable housing units (both rental and for-sale) in commercial and industrial zones. Single-family dwelling units must have at least two or more bedrooms. Multi-family efficiency and one-bedroom units are permitted subject to ratio requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program applies to specific commercial and industrial zones in Montgomery County: C-1 (Convenience Commercial), C-2 (General Commercial), C-3 (Highway Commercial), C-4 (Limited Commercial), O-M (Office Building, Moderate Intensity), I-1 (Light Industrial), I-3 (Technology and Business Park), and I-4 (Low Intensity, Light Industrial). No more than 25 percent of land zoned for commercial and industrial use in each master plan area can be used for multifamily housing.
requirements_list: Developer must apply for and receive approval of a Special Exception from the Montgomery County Board of Appeals
Developer must execute a written agreement with the Director of DHCA before a building permit is issued
Agreement must contain subdivision name, marketing name, and a construction staging plan sequencing affordable units with or before other dwelling units
Developer must record the productivity housing agreement in County Land Records
Copy of recorded agreement must be provided to the County
Copy of executed agreement must be submitted to Department of Permitting Services with first building permit application
Single-family PHUs must have at least two or more bedrooms
Multi-family efficiency and one-bedroom unit ratios must not exceed the ratio of market-rate efficiency and one-bedroom units to total market-rate units
For subdivisions with both single-family and multi-family dwellings, specific rental unit ratios must be maintained
Maximum sales prices must not exceed 175 percent of comparable Moderately Priced Dwelling Unit sale price
PHU rental rates based on 75 percent of area-wide median income for four-person family, adjusted for family size
Maximum rents including tenant-paid utilities must not exceed 30 percent of calculated gross household income
Sold PHUs must be occupied by owner as primary residence during control period
Rental units may not be sublet without developer permission and Department approval of income-qualified household
During control period, PHU may not be resold or refinanced for amount greater than determined by DHCA
After control period expires, owner may sell on open market but must pay one-half of excess profit to Housing Initiative Fund
For-sale units controlled for ten years; rental units controlled for twenty years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Developer applies for Special Exception, which must be approved by the Board of Appeals per zoning ordinance Section G-2.36.2. 2. Developer executes written agreement with DHCA Director before building permit is issued; agreement must include subdivision name, marketing name, and construction staging plan for affordable housing units. 3. Developer records productivity housing agreement in County Land Records and provides copy to County. Agreement is released from Land Records once all required PHU covenants are recorded. 4. Copy of executed agreement is submitted to Department of Permitting Services with first building permit application. DPS will not issue building permits unless PHUs are part of the approved staging plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rental assistance program where vouchers are tied to specific units in designated buildings or developments. Residents must live in the assigned building or development to receive assistance. The program is administered in Montgomery County, including through the Housing Opportunities Commission (HOC) and the City of Rockville Housing and Community Development, providing subsidized rental assistance to eligible low-income households.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Vouchers tied to specific units in designated developments and buildings provide rental assistance to eligible low-income households. Residents must reside in the designated building or development to receive the subsidy.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households and residents seeking rental assistance in specific designated buildings or developments in Montgomery County, including the City of Rockville.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance in specific designated buildings or developments.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply through the Housing Path Portal online application system for all HOC rental programs. For City of Rockville units, contact Rockville Housing Enterprises.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit for Public Safety Officers
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit applied to Montgomery County property tax for eligible public safety officers, emergency communications specialists, deputy sheriffs, correctional officers, and active volunteer firefighters and rescue personnel who are the legal owners of and occupy their principal residence in Montgomery County. The credit is the lesser of $2,500 or the amount of County property tax due on the property, applied annually upon successful application.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An annual property tax credit of up to $2,500 or the amount of County property tax due on an owner-occupied principal residence, whichever is less. Applicants must reapply annually by April 1 of the year prior to the tax levy year for which the credit is sought.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 annually of the year prior to the Tax Levy Year that the credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active public safety officers (including full-time sworn police officers, firefighters, emergency medical technicians), public safety communications specialists, deputy sheriffs, correctional officers, and active volunteer firefighters and rescue personnel employed by Montgomery County, M-NCPPC, WSSC, WSTC, County municipalities, or the Department of Health and Human Services Crisis Center, who own and occupy a principal residence in Montgomery County. Also includes full-time County employees assigned to the Department of Health and Human Services Crisis Center responsible for providing emergency response services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credit applied to Montgomery County property tax on the owner-occupied principal residence.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicant must be the legal owner of and occupy a property in Montgomery County as their principal residence.
requirements_list: Must be an active public safety officer (full-time sworn police officer, firefighter, emergency medical technician, or correctional officer), public safety communications specialist, deputy sheriff, correctional officer, or active volunteer firefighter or rescue personnel

Must be employed by Montgomery County, M-NCPPC, WSSC, WSTC, a County municipality, or the Department of Health and Human Services Crisis Center, or be an active volunteer for a local fire and rescue department
Must be the legal owner of an owner-occupied property in Montgomery County
Property must be the applicant's principal residence
Must apply annually by April 1 of the year prior to the tax levy year for which the credit is sought
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an online application by April 1 of the year prior to the tax levy year for which the credit is sought. Separate application forms are available for different employer categories: active County employees, fire rescue volunteers, M-NCPPC officers, WSSC officers, and various municipality officers. An automatic confirmation email is sent to the email address provided upon submission. Applicants who do not receive confirmation within 24 hours should contact MC311.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit against county property tax for qualified disabled veterans or their qualified surviving spouses. The credit amount depends on the veteran's service-connected disability rating.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A tax credit equal to 50% of the county property tax for veterans with a service-connected disability of 75% or more, or 25% of the county property tax for veterans with a service-connected disability between 50% and 74%. The disabled veteran's federal adjusted gross income must not exceed $100,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 before the tax year for which credit is sought
structured_extraction.program_audience: Disabled veterans with a service-connected disability rating of 50% or higher who are discharged under honorable conditions, and qualified surviving spouses of disabled veterans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The credit reduces county property tax liability for the applicant's principal residence in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a disabled veteran with a permanent service-connected disability rating of at least 50% (reasonably certain to continue for the life of the veteran), or a 100% service-connected disability for a non-permanent disability
Must have been discharged under honorable conditions from active service in the U.S. Armed Forces as defined in 38 U.S.C. Section 101
Must own property in Montgomery County that serves as principal residence
Property must be occupied by no more than 2 families
Federal adjusted gross income must not exceed $100,000 for the immediately preceding taxable year
Cannot qualify for a Property Tax Exemption under Section 7-208 of the Tax Property Article of the Maryland Code
Must submit application on or before April 1 before the tax year for which credit is sought
Must include copy of discharge papers (DD-214) indicating honorable discharge
Must include certification of disability from U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs indicating percentage of disability
Must include copy of Federal Income Tax Return from immediately preceding taxable year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete and submit the Property Tax Credit – Disabled Veterans application form along with required documentation to the Montgomery County Division of Treasury. Required documents include: (1) DD-214 discharge form indicating honorable discharge, (2) Certification of disability from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs showing disability percentage, and (3) Copy of Federal Income Tax Return from the immediately preceding taxable year. All three required documents must be submitted or the application will not be processed. Submit to Division of Treasury, 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, Maryland 20850.

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit – Local Income Tax Offset
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit available to owner-occupied residential properties to offset increases in county income tax revenues from a county income tax rate exceeding 2.6 percent. The County establishes the credit amount by Resolution. This credit is only available to owners of owner-occupied residential properties as determined by SDAT.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit against the county tax imposed on owner-occupied residential property. The credit offsets increases in county income tax revenues resulting from county income tax rates above 2.6 percent. The amount of the credit is established by County Resolution.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of owner-occupied residential properties (principal residences)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces county property taxes for owner-occupied residential dwellings
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Owner-occupied residential property (principal residence)
As determined by SDAT
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Department of Finance for details on credit amount and application process

structured_extraction.program_name: Property Tax Credit – Nonprofit Swim Clubs
structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for nonprofit swim clubs in Montgomery County that use their facilities exclusively to provide recreational outlets for local communities. The club must provide documentation of nonprofit status and certify that facilities are used solely for community recreation. The credit applies against general county taxes and special service area taxes, reducing the club's annual property tax liability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit against County Taxes (General County Tax and Special Service Area Taxes) for nonprofit swim clubs in Montgomery County. The credit reduces the club's annual property tax liability. The credit must be applied for annually by May 1 preceding the taxable year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 1 preceding the taxable year (e.g., May 1 for Levy Year the same calendar year)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit swim clubs serving local communities in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces property tax liability for nonprofit swim club properties; credit applies to general county taxes and special service area taxes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be organized as a nonprofit organization
Must operate a swim club
Facilities must be used exclusively for community recreational purposes
Must provide copy of Articles of Incorporation
Must provide current Certificate of Good Standing from State of Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must certify under oath that the property is a nonprofit swim club using facilities exclusively to provide recreational outlet for local community
Application must be filed with Treasury Division by May 1 preceding the taxable year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit required documentation annually to the Treasury Division by May 1 preceding the taxable year. In the first year of application, and in any subsequent years if there has been a change, the swim club must provide copies of Articles of Incorporation and a current Certificate of Good Standing from the State of Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. The applicant must certify under oath and affirmation that the property is a nonprofit swim club using facilities exclusively to provide a recreational outlet for a local community.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for owner-occupied residential properties with installed solar or geothermal devices. The program was suspended effective November 8, 2011. Tax credits are not being granted for applications received after November 8, 2012.

Program is no longer accepting applications after November 8, 2012.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides bystanders with knowledge, skills, and tools to address life-threatening injuries before medical professionals arrive. The program deploys trauma care kits in public spaces such as schools and government buildings and offers training to help residents respond effectively in emergencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides in-person training sessions for residents and government employees on how to administer trauma care, instructional videos demonstrating techniques for using trauma kit equipment, a mobile application available for Apple and Android devices with step-by-step instructions, and printed instructional materials. Trauma care kits containing tourniquets (C-A-T), compression dressings, gauze, chest seals (HyFin), survival blankets, and other medical supplies are deployed in Montgomery County government facilities, Montgomery County Public Schools, and Montgomery College locations. Training covers major bleeding control on limbs, direct pressure for bleeding wounds, wound packing for neck/armpit/groin wounds, chest seal application for chest/abdomen/back wounds, and shock prevention techniques.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Montgomery County, Montgomery County government employees, Montgomery County Public Schools employees, and Montgomery College staff
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training on trauma care techniques and provision of trauma care kits for use in emergency situations involving severe bleeding, penetrating trauma, or hypothermia. Kits are deployed to administer tourniquets, compression dressings, gauze packing, chest seals, and survival blankets.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Currently limited to Montgomery County Government facilities, Montgomery County Public Schools, and Montgomery College. The program serves Montgomery and Prince George's Counties through deployment of trauma care kits and training resources.
requirements_list: Assistance must be provided voluntarily
Helper must act in good faith with honest intentions
Actions must not be grossly negligent or intentionally harmful
Training requests are dependent upon resource availability
Helper must ensure their own safety before offering assistance
Helper should protect themselves from blood-borne infections by wearing gloves if available
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents and Montgomery County Government employees can request in-person Public Access Trauma Care training by clicking a form link on the program webpage. Montgomery County Government Departments can contact OEMHS to request a PATC kit evaluation or kit replacement if their facility does not have a kit or if an existing kit is missing, damaged, or has been used. Training and kit requests are subject to resource availability. Additional information and training resources are available at publicaccesstraumacare.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: A conditional grant program that provides financial assistance through the Economic Development Fund to local for-profit small businesses and non-profit organizations in Montgomery County experiencing significant adverse impact due to a communicable disease outbreak that resulted in a Federal, State, or County Public Health Emergency order restricting business operations. The program was established during the COVID-19 pandemic to support public health emergency response efforts and assist eligible businesses and workers in maintaining continued operations during public health emergency restrictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Conditional grant program administered through the Economic Development Fund providing financial assistance to eligible small businesses and non-profit organizations impacted by public health emergency orders. Assistance consists of grants or conditional grants where conditional grants remain as grants upon satisfactory adherence to terms, otherwise becoming repayable. Maximum assistance of $10,000 based on actual lost revenue calculated as the difference between Average Historical Revenue and Adjusted Revenue (adjusted for deferred rent or reduced payroll expenses). Additional assistance up to $2,500 available for technology equipment and software to facilitate employee teleworking. County Council appropriated $25,000,000 to fund the program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses and non-profit organizations in Montgomery County with 100 or fewer full-time equivalent employees experiencing significant adverse impact from a public health emergency order restricting business operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Continued operation of businesses and organizations during public health emergency restrictions, including support for purchasing technology equipment and software to facilitate employee teleworking. Funds cannot be used for expenses already reimbursed by COVID-19 related Federal or State assistance programs, insurance reimbursements, or wages paid to employees during periods of unemployment insurance eligibility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Business must have its principal place of business in the County.
requirements_list: Must be a privately owned local for-profit business or non-profit organization
Must have principal place of business in Montgomery County
Must be in existence and in Good Standing with the State of Maryland at time of application (registration with SDAT sufficient for sole proprietorships and general partnerships)
Must employ 100 or fewer full-time or full-time equivalent employees

Must demonstrate Significant Financial Loss (adjusted revenue loss of 50% or greater) for a financial period caused directly or indirectly by the Public Health Emergency when compared to equal duration period prior to emergency
Must provide documentation such as federal income tax returns and Profit and Loss Statements demonstrating revenue prior to and after Public Health Emergency
All grants or conditional grants are subject to appropriation and availability of funds
Grant recipients must enter into a grant agreement with the County including audit rights, reporting obligations, and certification under penalty of perjury
Funds used for expenses reimbursed by other COVID-19 assistance programs must be repaid
Funds cannot reimburse business for losses covered by insurance policies
Funds cannot reimburse wages for employees eligible for unemployment insurance benefits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must provide documentation including federal income tax returns and Profit and Loss Statements demonstrating revenue for financial period prior to Public Health Emergency and corresponding documentation showing significant revenue loss. Revenue loss is calculated by determining Annual Historical Average from pre-emergency financial statements, calculating Monthly Historical Average, determining actual revenue during Public Health Emergency period, adjusting for deferred rent or reduced payroll expenses, and confirming revenue loss of 50% or greater. All applicants must apply online. Applications are evaluated based on established criteria and an award process defined in Executive Regulation 9-20. Written comments on the program were submitted by August 31, 2020 to the Department of Finance. Grant recipients must enter into a grant agreement with the County covering audit rights, reporting obligations, and certification requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to small businesses affected by Purple Line construction to help compensate for the impact on their operations and nearby neighborhoods.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To compensate for the impact of Purple Line construction on business operations

Located in or affected by Purple Line construction area

structured_extraction.program_description: A free technical assistance program that helps licensed child care centers, letter of compliance programs, and registered family child care homes improve quality through expert coaching, group sessions, peer mentoring, and multilingual support. The program guides providers in reaching higher quality levels, obtaining accreditation, and improving business operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free technical assistance including expert coaching, group training sessions, peer mentoring, and multilingual support to help child care providers improve quality. Reimbursement is available for accreditation materials and NAFCC membership fees. Services are offered both onsite and virtually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers, letter of compliance programs, and registered family child care providers in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Quality improvement activities including accreditation materials, NAFCC membership, business coaching, and professional development for early care practitioners
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
