Programs operating in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Quality Enhancement program to work with a Quality Enhancement Coordinator who will develop and implement an individualized action plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: A low-cost internet service program providing affordable broadband access to eligible low-income households in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly internet service at $9.95 per month plus Maryland state tax. No installation or equipment fees. Broadband speeds up to 250 Mbps. Includes TiVo Stream 4K and a $100 gift card available for $29.99 as a separate offering.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households in Montgomery County who participate in qualifying assistance programs (Medicaid, Public Housing, SNAP, WIC, TANF, NSLP, Headstart, SSI, Veteran's Administration Pension, LIHEAP, or Pell Grant).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Discounted home internet access.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Limited service area in Silver Spring, Chevy Chase, and Gaithersburg, Montgomery County. Cannot have had RCN service in the past 60 days.

Have not had RCN service in the past 60 days
Cannot be a current internet customer of Comcast, RCN, or Verizon
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Sign up by visiting https://www.rcn.com/internet-first/ or calling 800-746-4726.

structured_extraction.program_name: Racial Equity & Social Justice Initiative Trainings
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive training program for Montgomery County government employees focused on understanding and advancing racial equity and social justice. The program offers multiple training modules covering topics like racial equity in government, structural racism, racial healing, inclusive language, biases, empathy, and heart leadership. Employees are required to complete 8 hours of racial equity and social justice training each fiscal year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free training programs for county employees available as self-guided classes and instructor-led sessions via Zoom or in-person. Core offerings include mandatory trainings (Advancing Racial Equity: The Role of Government - 4 hours, offered monthly except August from 10:00 am – 2:00 pm; Understanding Structural Racism in Montgomery County - 3 hours classroom time plus 1 hour reflection form for 4 hours total credit, offered from 10:00 am – 1:00 pm with prerequisite of Advancing Racial Equity training). Optional trainings include Racial Healing Circles (1.5 hours, in-person in HR training room), Inclusive Language 101 (2 hours), Heart Leadership (2 hours), Biases/Empathy/Inclusion training (2 hours), ORESJ self-guided training (2 hours), Unconscious Bias Self-Paced class, Lunch & Learn programs (1 hour each), and other department-approved trainings. Most trainings except Racial Healing Circles, Lunch & Learns, and special programs are available as self-guided modules. Registration is completed through the AccessMCG ePortal Employee Self Service/Learner Home.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing enrollment; space is limited per session
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County government employees. The program is designed for all staff to build understanding of racial equity and social justice issues.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and professional development in racial equity, structural racism, inclusive language, leadership, and related topics to support employees in advancing equity in their departments and communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County government employees only.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County government employee
8 hours of racial equity and social justice training required each fiscal year

Two mandatory classes must be taken every other fiscal year starting July 2024: 'Advancing Racial Equity: The Role of Government' (prerequisite) and 'Understanding Structural Racism in Montgomery County' (both must be taken within the same fiscal year)
Completion of reflection form for 'Understanding Structural Racism' course to receive 4 hours of credit
Advancing Racial Equity: The Role of Government is a prerequisite for 'Understanding Structural Racism in Montgomery County'
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employees interested in participating in training offerings should enroll through the AccessMCG ePortal by selecting Employee Self Service, then Learner Home, and searching for the class by keyword ('equity' for Advancing Racial Equity, 'Understanding Structural Racism' for the structural racism course, 'racial healing circle' for Racial Healing Circles, or 'Women' for Women's History Month Lunch & Learn). Trainings are held via Zoom unless otherwise noted. Questions about training offerings should be directed to Jeanette Rojas at the provided email address. Check the ORESJ website and AccessMCG ePortal/Oracle for current training information and schedules. Space is limited per session, so early enrollment is recommended.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program where Montgomery County Public Schools high school horticulture and environmental science classes receive plants, pots, soil, and guidance to grow native plants in their greenhouses during the second semester. Students propagate native plants for watershed restoration projects, return a portion to the Department of Environmental Protection, and use the remaining plants for native plant sales or other environmental projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides plants, pots, soil, and guidance at no charge to participating schools. Montgomery County Parks' Pope Farm greenhouse grows seeds of native plants harvested from nature. These seeds are germinated and grown in trays, then seedlings are separated and grown in small plug trays. The plug trays are given to schools along with potting soil and 1-quart pots. Schools transfer plugs to 1-quart pots in their greenhouses during the second semester where plants mature. Participating schools return at least 33% of the plants produced to RainScapes by mid-spring (usually before Spring Break but no later than the first week in May) for use in stormwater management and watershed restoration projects throughout the county. Schools can use the remaining plants for native plant sales, community-based environmental projects, or as part of green job education in the horticulture curriculum.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 30th for the following academic year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County Public Schools high school horticulture and AP environmental science programs with greenhouse access
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Plants, pots, soil, and supplies for native plant propagation in school greenhouses for watershed restoration, stormwater management, native plant sales, and environmental education projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County Public Schools only
requirements_list: Must be a high school horticulture and/or AP environmental studies program in Montgomery County Public Schools
Must have greenhouse access
Must return at least 33% of plants produced to RainScapes by mid-spring (usually before Spring Break but no later than the first week in May)
Must complete one-page assessment survey of the project
Participation is by invitation based on previous participation or by request from a teacher by March 30th
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Teachers request participation by emailing rainscapes.application@montgomerycountymd.gov by March 30th for the following academic year. Participation is by invitation based on previous participation or teacher request. After acceptance into the program, schools collect materials (plug trays, potting soil, and 1-quart pots) from Pope Farm Greenhouses at a pickup date provided after application approval. Schools transfer plugs to 1-quart pots and maintain plants in their greenhouses during the second semester. RainScapes staff pick up plants from schools in spring, usually before Spring Break but no later than the first week in May.

structured_extraction.program_name: RainScapes Rewards Rebate - Permeable Pavement Retrofit
structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program that provides financial incentives to property owners in Montgomery County who install permeable pavement. Permeable pavement allows stormwater to seep into the ground while maintaining a durable surface for cars and people, with specially engineered layers underneath that clean and soak in stormwater. The program is designed to reduce stormwater runoff and enhance the local environment.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebate of $14 per square foot for permeable pavement installation. Maximum rebate: Residential - $7,500; Commercial/Institutional - $20,000. Minimum project size: Residential - 100 square feet; Commercial/Institutional - 200 square feet. Rebates are awarded on a first come, first served basis. Projects must be installed within six months of the approval letter. Rebate payments are issued by the Montgomery County Department of Finance after project passes final inspection and receipts and property owner agreement are submitted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not specified; currently closed to applications
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County property owners who want to install permeable pavement for stormwater management. Properties must be located within Montgomery County but outside of the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of permeable interlocking concrete pavers (PICP) to replace existing impervious surfaces like driveways, walkways, patios, and parking areas. Runoff from roofs and other adjacent impervious surfaces may also be directed to the permeable pavement if the contributing impervious area does not exceed five times the permeable pavement area.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, excluding the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park. Projects must be on private property and cannot be built in the County's right-of-way. Properties must be located outside the municipalities that collect the Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) separately.
requirements_list: 100 square foot minimum project size for residential; 200 square feet for commercial/institutional
Project must be on private property, not in County's right-of-way
Project must replace existing impervious surface (driveway, walkway, patio, parking area)
Soil must pass a perc test (percolation test within 0-36 hours); if over 36 hours, an underdrain is required
Driveway slope should not exceed 5% and must slope away from the house
Waterproof liner required within 10 feet of house foundation (basement/crawl space) and 5 feet from a slab
Maintain 10-foot setback from house foundation with positive drainage away from foundation
Maintain 5-foot setback from sanitary sewer or water mains; never install over water, sewer, or gas mains
Maintain 100-foot setback from any water supply well
Maintain 50-foot setback from any septic system component
Do not disturb more than 25% of critical root zone for trees with 8 inches or greater diameter at breast height (DBH)
Projects within close proximity of large canopy trees approved on case-by-case basis
Does not redirect existing flow of water to a paved surface or neighbor's property
Does not back up water onto neighbor's property
Residential: Installed by certified ICPI contractor with PICP training or experienced contractor with portfolio of 5 permeable paver projects
Commercial/Institutional: Installed by contractor with PICP Specialist designation
Contractor must have attended PICP training course through ICPI (Interlocking Concrete Paver Institute) or submit portfolio showing at least 5 permeable projects
Proof of Right of Way permit if storing construction materials or equipment in County's right-of-way
Installation must follow RainScapes Permeable Paver Manual or PICP specifications
Cannot be installed on slopes greater than 10%; slopes between 5%-10% must be terraced with flow barriers
Aggregates must be washed natural stone; recycled construction materials not allowed
Projects must be installed within six months of approval letter date
Project cannot be used to fulfill county-required stormwater permit; only new projects considered
Residential permeable pavement should be sized for 1.0 to 2.5 inches of rain capture; minimum for rebate is 1.0 inch
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Review the RainScapes website and design manual for permeable pavement projects. 2) Complete the online RainScapes rebate application. 3) Submit application through the online system. Applicants should receive confirmation email from RainScapes@montgomerycountymd.gov upon successful submission. 4) If application contains all necessary information, the Department of Environmental Protection will contact applicant to schedule a mandatory preliminary inspection before project installation can begin. 5) Submit supporting documents specific to permeable pavement rebate (contractor credentials, Right of Way permit if applicable, site assessment, perc test results). 6) Once preliminary inspection is passed and supporting documents are approved, applicant receives an application response letter with approval details and rebate funding level, plus a property owner agreement. 7) Installation can begin after receiving approval letter; project must be completed within six months of approval date. 8) After installation, contact Department of Environmental Protection to schedule a final inspection. 9) At final inspection, applicant may receive list of necessary adjustments; photo document completion of any adjustments and email to RainScapes@montgomerycountymd.gov. A second final inspection may be necessary. 10) Submit itemized receipts (with sales tax subtracted), electronically-signed property owner agreement, and any adjustment documentation. 11) Rebate is processed for payment by Montgomery County Department of Finance after project passes final inspection and all required documents are submitted. Applicants can check status of current application through the online system.

structured_extraction.program_description: A cost-share rebate program administered by Montgomery County that provides financial incentives for property owners to install stormwater management features on their land. The program helps residential, commercial, institutional, HOA, school, and community properties reduce stormwater runoff and pollution flowing into storm drains and streams. Eligible project types include rain gardens, conservation landscapes, water harvesting systems (rain barrels and cisterns), green roofs, permeable pavement, and pavement removal. The program also offers workshops and training to help residents implement these projects. Specific rebate rates vary by project type: rain gardens ($10/sq ft, minimum 75 sq ft), conservation landscapes ($5/sq ft without ponding or $6/sq ft with 3 inches of ponding, minimum 250 sq ft for ponding), green roofs ($9/sq ft, minimum 100 sq ft), pavement removal ($3–$7/sq ft depending on replacement material), rain barrels ($1/gallon, max $250), and cisterns ($1/gallon, max $500 residential or $2,000 commercial/institutional). Maximum lifetime rebates are $7,500 for residential properties and $20,000 for commercial, HOA, multifamily, or institutional properties per parcel. Properties within the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park are served by separate municipal rebate programs. The program is accepted on a first-come, first-served basis when the application period is open, and rebate checks are issued within 8–12 weeks after final inspection.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cost-share rebates are provided to offset the costs of installing eligible on-site stormwater management retrofit projects. Rebate rates by project type: Rain Gardens — $10 per square foot (minimum 75 sq ft); Conservation Landscapes — $5/sq ft without ponding or $6/sq ft with 3 inches of ponding (minimum 250 sq ft for ponding projects); Green Roofs — $9 per square foot (minimum 100 sq ft); Pavement Removal — $3–$7 per square foot depending on replacement type; Rain Barrels — $1 per gallon of capacity (maximum $250 per property); Cisterns — $1 per gallon of capacity (maximum $500 for residential, $2,000 for commercial/institutional, with exceptions considered case-by-case). Overall maximum lifetime rebates: $7,500 for residential properties; $20,000 for commercial, HOA, multifamily, or institutional properties per parcel (by tax ID). Rebate amounts are based on approved receipts (excluding sales tax) up to the specified maximum. Eligible expenses include plants, materials (mulch, compost), hardware, equipment rental, design fees, and labor directly related to the project. Rebate checks are issued within 8–12 weeks after final inspection. For community/HOA/congregational properties, the maximum is $20,000 per parcel. Water collected in rain barrels or cisterns is for non-potable, exterior uses only; the County does not currently permit hooking these devices into a home's sewer system for interior uses such as toilet flushing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a first come, first served basis; rebate application period is currently closed. Ongoing program with no fixed deadline — applications accepted at any time subject to fund availability when open.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Montgomery County outside the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park, including individual homeowners, residential properties, commercial properties, institutions, schools, homeowner associations, communities, community pools, congregations, private schools, and contractors. Each of those municipalities operates its own separate RainScapes rebate program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of stormwater management features including: rain gardens that capture and filter stormwater runoff from roofs, driveways, and other hard surfaces; conservation landscapes that replace lawn or invasive plants with native plants and improved soil; water harvesting systems including rain barrels and cisterns that attach to roof downspouts to collect and store rainwater for reuse; green roofs that hold special soil and plants to treat stormwater runoff and conserve energy; permeable pavement; and pavement removal with replacement by natural surfaces such as rain gardens, conservation landscaping, or lawn. Also supports workshops and training on stormwater management and native plantings. Eligible expenses include plants, mulch, compost, hardware, equipment rental, design fees, and labor directly related to the project.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland, excluding the municipalities of Rockville, Gaithersburg, and Takoma Park (which each operate their own separate RainScapes rebate programs). Properties must pay the Montgomery County Water Quality Protection Charge to be eligible. Rain gardens and stormwater gardens must be located on private property and not in the County's right-of-way (area between sidewalk and street). For ponding gardens, the garden must be at least 10 feet downhill from building foundations and at least 5 feet away from built slabs like garages, patios, driveways, and sidewalks. Gardens cannot be placed over utilities (water, gas, electric), requiring minimum offsets of 36 inches for gas and 18 inches for other utilities.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the RainScapes website and project-specific design manuals and requirements documentation. Read the application process document. 2. Define your property concerns and goals and select an eligible project type. 3. Find your Property Tax ID and submit a project application through the online RainScapes Rewards portal, uploading any existing plans or site images. For rain barrels, no preliminary inspection is required. 4. Within 2–4 weeks, a planner will be assigned and will conduct a mandatory site assessment of your property (not required for rain barrels). 5. Work with your planner to develop a project plan that meets all requirements, including planting plans (for planted projects), site design documents, and HOA approval if applicable. Submit required plan documents to your planner within 3 months of receiving the site assessment report. 6. Once the plan is approved, you will receive an official project approval letter with approval details and rebate funding level, along with a Property Owner Agreement. Installation can begin after receiving the approval letter. Call Miss Utility (811) before digging. 7. Install your project within 6 months of plan approval, ensuring all work meets minimum standards for your project type. Install in appropriate weather conditions using proper sediment control procedures. 8. Contact the Department of Environmental Protection to schedule a final inspection (typically virtual, including measurements and photos). 9. At final inspection, you may receive a list of necessary changes or adjustments to make before rebate can be issued. Complete any adjustments and photo-document them, then email to RainScapes@montgomerycountymd.gov. Depending on the number of adjustments, a second final inspection may be necessary. 10. Submit all supporting documents at the end: copies of itemized receipts (with sales tax subtracted), electronically-signed Property Owner Agreement, and any other project-specific documentation. 11. Your rebate will be processed for payment after your project passes final inspection and you have submitted your receipts and Property Owner Agreement. The rebate check will be issued by the Montgomery County Department of Finance within 8–12 weeks of final inspection approval. 12. Optionally apply for a Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) credit on your property tax bill through the WQPC website. Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis when the program is open. Ongoing program with no fixed deadline—applications accepted at any time subject to fund availability when open.

structured_extraction.program_description: Offers time-limited flexible housing subsidy for up to 24 months along with support services. The subsidy decreases every three months as tenant income increases. Participants are expected to transition to paying full rent upon discharge from the program. Checks are paid directly to the landlord.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Time-limited flexible housing subsidy for up to 24 months that decreases every three months as tenant income increases. Assistance includes security deposit coverage (up to double the monthly rental amount) and financial services support. Landlords receive monthly subsidy payments covering a portion of rent, with tenants paying the remaining portion directly to landlord. Payments made via check by mail or direct deposit/ACH. Upon program exit after 24 months, tenants are connected to the Rental Assistance Program and other eligible support services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents exiting homelessness, their landlords, and case managers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing subsidy including security deposits and rental payment support, plus financial services and case management support for up to 24 months
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Participants must be Montgomery County residents exiting homelessness
Tenants must recertify income regularly with assistance from Case Manager
Tenant rental contribution must remain affordable based on current net income
Participants must work with assigned Case Manager throughout program
Program serves tenants who qualify for support services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landlords should contact Elizabeth.Driggers@montgomerycountymd.gov to express interest in partnering with the RRH program. Someone will contact landlords to discuss partnership opportunities and available incentives. Tenants work with assigned Case Managers who handle all program questions, income recertification, and ongoing support throughout the 24-month period.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit for landlords who provide reduced rent to elderly (age 65+) or disabled tenants who meet income and asset eligibility requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rental Agreements preserve and maintain affordable housing by restricting a certain number of units in multifamily projects to income and rent limits. In return for these restrictions, the County pays a per-unit subsidy to the property owner. The subsidy is calculated as the difference between the stipulated affordable rent and the average market rate rent for a comparable unit.

list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing

Rental agreements typically arise from expiring MPDU agreements, Right of First Refusal opportunities, or affordable housing development and preservation projects. Rent increases on subsidized units must follow the County's Voluntary Rent Guideline. An annual monitoring fee of $40 per unit per year is required, due by September 30th.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Per-unit subsidy payments to compensate for restricting units to income and affordable rent limits

Pay annual monitoring fee of $40 per unit per year by September 30th

structured_extraction.program_description: The Montgomery County Rental Assistance Program (RAP) provides monthly housing subsidies to help eligible low-income residents pay their rent. Payments range from $100 to $503 per month and are sent directly to the participant by 2-party check (made out jointly to the head of household and the landlord, rental agent, management authority, or primary leaseholder). The program is referral-based and also includes the Handicapped Rental Assistance component, which helps low-income disabled individuals with rental expenses in licensed care facilities. Benefit amounts are set by county regulation, with minimum and maximum amounts established therein. The program serves residents exiting homelessness as well as other low-income families and individuals who meet eligibility criteria such as age, income, disability, or need.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly housing subsidy ranging from $100 to $503 per month paid directly to participants. Benefits are calculated as either 40% of combined monthly gross income for households of three members or fewer, or 35% of combined monthly gross income for households with four or more members. Payments are made by monthly checks payable jointly to the head of household and the landlord, rental agent, management authority, or primary leaseholder (or as a single payee check to the landlord at recipient's written request). Rental costs are subject to limitations including not exceeding 120% of average suitable-sized unit costs in Montgomery County. Benefits are designed to renew annually if the tenant's income and rental amount remain within program limits. Includes support for licensed care facility rental costs for disabled individuals. Benefit amounts are set by county regulation with defined minimum ($100) and maximum ($400) levels.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families, disabled individuals, and residents exiting homelessness or at risk of becoming homeless in Montgomery County needing help paying rent, as well as their landlords
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment of monthly rental costs and expenses in licensed care facilities for eligible low-income individuals and families. Cannot include garage, pet, pool, housekeeping, food, health aide services, or other such fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must be experiencing homelessness or at risk of becoming homeless, OR have a disability, OR be age 55 or above
Must meet income eligibility requirements (40% of combined monthly gross income for households of three members or fewer; 35% for households with four or more members)
Referral required to access program
Rental unit cannot be owned by a relative of the tenant or by a relative who lives in the home
Rental costs cannot exceed 120% of average suitable-sized unit costs in Montgomery County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Referral-based program. Prospective applicants must be referred to the program and meet current eligibility requirements. Tenants are assigned an eligibility worker to assist in the application and renewal process. Benefits are designed to renew annually; all tenants receive recertification packets several months before benefits expire. Contact the Montgomery County Department of Health and Human Services at (240) 777-4940 or RAP@montgomerycountymd.gov for more information or to be referred to the program. Landlords must register with the Montgomery County Client Vendor Registration System (CVRS) to receive payments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Resident and Community Gardening Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A recurring grant program administered by Montgomery County that supports resident and community gardening projects to increase the volume of fresh, edible food available to residents experiencing food insecurity. The program expands the capacity of eligible organizations to provide residents with access to yard, patio, and community gardening supplies, space, and education, while also increasing food production, improving green spaces, and building community in Montgomery County neighborhoods. The program has been funded in FY23, FY24, and FY26, with appropriations ranging from $100,000 to $210,000 per cycle.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding is awarded on an annual or recurring cycle through the FY26 Resident and Community Gardening Grant Program. For FY26, $200,000 in total grant funding is available. Individual awards are expected to range from $25,000 to $100,000, with final award amounts potentially lower than $100,000. The initial grant performance period is seventeen (17) months (anticipated June 30, 2026 to November 1, 2027), with the opportunity for renewal for one additional year (12 months) contingent on performance, continued need, and availability of funds. For the initial grant period, applicants must provide a minimum 25% match (up to 10% in-kind). If renewed, applicants may be funded at 25% of the initial grant award and must meet an increased match requirement of 75% (not including in-kind). Example: An FY26 Award of $60,000 would require $15,000 match (up to $6,000 in-kind); if renewed, the award would be $15,000 maximum and require an $11,250 match. Funds support resident and community gardening projects that measurably increase the volume of fresh, edible food available to Montgomery County residents experiencing food insecurity. Historically, $210,559 was awarded to seven grantees in a prior cycle (FY24).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible Federal 501(c)(3) tax-exempt nonprofit organizations or collaborations between two or more organizations where at least one holds 501(c)(3) status, located in or serving Montgomery County residents. The program targets organizations seeking to support resident and community gardening initiatives that expand food production capacity and increase food security for Montgomery County residents experiencing food insecurity. Organizations must be registered and in Good Standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and current with the Maryland Secretary of State OneStop - Charities Public Registry.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure investments such as raised beds, greenhouses, electrical hookups, water access, and other systems supporting land use viability; tools and supplies including equipment, seeds, soil, and gardening materials needed to plant, cultivate, and harvest edible crops; community resources and materials for trainings and community events; staffing and operational costs for program management; costs associated with delivering education and print materials. Projects may support community food production for distribution to residents experiencing food insecurity, population-specific food production with nutrition and agriculture education, and production of culturally relevant foods and agrarian practices. Grant funding cannot be used for lobbying, alcoholic beverages, pet food, prior obligations or debts, or activities that wholly occur outside Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. The organization's principal place of business must be located in Montgomery County; if a national or regional organization, it must have a location in Montgomery County through which it provides related services. All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and/or be exclusively for Montgomery County residents. Any services or activities taking place outside of Montgomery County must be exclusively benefiting Montgomery County residents.
requirements_list: The organization must be a Federal 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status organization or a collaboration between two or more organizations with this status
The organization must be currently registered and in Good Standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
The organization must have a 'Current' standing with the Maryland Secretary of State OneStop – Charities Public Registry

The organization's principal place of business must be located in Montgomery County; if a national or regional organization, it must have a location in Montgomery County through which it provides related services
All activities and expenditures under this grant program must be provided in Montgomery County and/or be exclusively for Montgomery County residents

All activities funded through this grant must be provided free of charge (no donations or fundraising permitted using County resources), not provided in promotion of a particular religion or political party, and be open and available to all Montgomery County residents regardless of race, color, religious creed, ancestry, national origin, age, sex, marital status, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, family responsibility, genetic status, presence of children, or source of income

Current Montgomery County contract or grant award winners must be current on all reporting obligations for other awards and those reports must reflect substantial progress towards the goals of their awards

Proposed expenses must be for a new activity, expansion of existing activities, or a combination of both; grant funding cannot be used for any purchase already made, purchases or activities unnecessary to accomplish grant purposes, prior obligations or fines, debts and penalties, lobbying expenses, alcoholic beverages, pet food, or supplanting other funds
Applicants may only submit one application
Projects must demonstrate three or more years of experience in community garden-based food production (for priority funding)
Projects must demonstrate annual production of 1,000+ pounds of edible crops (for priority funding)
Projects must increase square footage and/or enhance use of secured community gardening property by a minimum of 25% during the initial one-year program period (for priority funding)

Must demonstrate actionable plans to produce substantial quantities of edible, nutrient-dense crops suitable for household consumption with minimum projection of 1,000 pounds of food grown/harvested during grant period (for priority funding)
Must prioritize production of crops aligned with community dietary patterns and cultural food preferences
Must distribute food to County residents either directly or through established food access partners such as food hubs, pantries, schools, or community markets
Must present a defined plan for utilizing grant funds to expand existing programming and realistic plans to sustain operations long-term beyond the grant period (for priority funding)
Must develop project implementation plan and budget proposal that allocates grant funds at approximately $10-$20 per square foot of new gardening area (for priority funding)
Must outline staffing, volunteer, and/or workforce development strategies that demonstrate sufficient relevant expertise and ensure continuity of programming (for priority funding)

Must demonstrate established or emerging partnerships within Montgomery County, including with institutional, government, and/or community-based organizations with shared use agreements for land and/or grant-funded infrastructure (for priority funding)

Must outline strategies to diversify operational funding sources with secured sources of external funding comprising at least 25% of the total project budget (up to 10% can be in-kind) for priority funding consideration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply through the Euna (eCivis) Online Grants Application Platform by registering and creating an application profile. The application includes multiple required tasks: Applicant Information Form (organization legal name, SDAT ID, Federal Tax ID, confirmation of current SDAT and Charities Database status, IRS 990 Form or exemption explanation, contact information); Applicant Background Task (demographic and staffing data not visible to Review Committees); Project Strategy Task (project title, overview, funding request, total project cost, zip codes served, and strategy narrative addressing program service delivery, food types and quantities, educational supports, language capacity, community impact, and partnerships); Project Budget Task (detailed itemized expenses including staffing, program costs, indirect costs, and revenues/cost-shares); Budget Narrative/Justification (purpose and calculation of expenses, funding reduction impact, alignment with current programs); Project Staffing Plan (optional but recommended if requesting staff funding); Project Work Plan/Timeline (implementation schedule over 17-month performance period); Performance Plan (tracking and evaluation methods with required Key Performance Indicators); and optional Performance History and supporting documents. An FY26 Resident and Community Gardening Grant Information Session was held on Tuesday, April 14th, 2026 at 11:00 AM EST via MS Teams Live (recording available). Applications must be submitted through the online platform no later than May 6, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST. Incomplete applications, applications not meeting legal requirements, or those submitted after the deadline will not be accepted. The Office of Food Systems Resilience will conduct administrative review, programmatic eligibility review, and subject matter expert review. Review Committees composed of neutral, qualified individuals will score proposals and submit recommendations. Award notification letters are expected approximately three weeks after the application deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Residential Real Property Tax Deferral – General
structured_extraction.program_description: A program allowing eligible homeowners to defer payment of county property taxes on residential real property used as their principal residence. The deferred amount is limited to the increase in county taxes over the prior year's bill, covering General County and Special Service Area real property taxes. Eligible homeowners must have annual household gross income not exceeding $120,000 and must have owned and occupied the home as their principal residence for at least 5 years. Interest accrues on deferred amounts at a rate set annually by the County (not to exceed the prime lending rate, approximately 3%). The accumulated deferred taxes and interest cannot exceed 50% of the property's full cash value. Deferred taxes and accrued interest become due upon sale or transfer of title.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Homeowners may defer the amount by which their county property taxes exceed the prior year's county taxes. This includes General County and Special Service Area real property taxes. Interest accrues annually at a rate set by the county not to exceed the prime lending rate (approximately 3%). The accumulated deferred taxes and interest cannot exceed 50% of the property's full cash value. When the property is sold or title is transferred, all deferred taxes and accrued interest become due.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners with gross household income not exceeding $120,000 whose principal residence is in Montgomery County and who have owned and occupied the dwelling for at least 5 years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Allows deferral of county property tax payments on the homeowner's principal residence, covering the amount by which current year taxes exceed the prior year's taxes.

Property must be residential real property
Deferred taxes and accrued interest cannot exceed 50% of the property's full cash value
Deferred taxes and interest become due upon sale or transfer of title

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides short-term temporary relief to the primary unpaid full-time live-in caregiver who is providing full-time care to frail elderly adults, functionally disabled adults (including those with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias), children with challenging behaviors, children and adults with developmental disabilities, and children with severe medical conditions. Care is provided by trained, certified care workers in the family's home, adult medical day programs, or in an approved respite care facility. Respite may be provided for a few hours, a day, a weekend, or sometimes longer. A subsidy may be provided to pay a Respite Care Provider, though respite is not an entitlement and subsidy availability is subject to limited funding.

Respite is not an entitlement and eligibility for a subsidy does not guarantee funds for each respite occasion requested due to limited funding. Respite staff work with the family to locate an appropriate provider for direct services.

Families are notified when the application is received. Processing takes up to 30 business days. Once approved, the primary caregiver participates in an orientation and respite staff work with the family to locate an appropriate provider.

structured_extraction.program_description: The SafeKeep Program provides temporary care of owned pets while their owners are unable to care for them due to illness, homelessness, or other emergencies. Space is limited, and pets must meet medical and behavioral criteria to be considered for foster placement.

Pets may be placed in approved foster homes, a partner boarding facility, or at the Montgomery County Animal Services and Adoption Center. Spay and neuter procedures are provided by OAS if the pet is not already altered. Length of stay is limited to a maximum of thirty days.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Pet owners in Montgomery County who are unable to care for their pets due to illness, homelessness, or other emergencies and who are working with a social worker, case manager, or allied agency.

Owner must plan to take their pet home within thirty days
Pet must be used to living indoors
Pet must be overall healthy and either not require medication or currently taking medicine that maintains their health
Pet must be friendly towards strangers
Owner must be willing to have their pet spayed or neutered
Pets must successfully complete a full intake with OAS staff, including heartworm or FELV/FIV testing if not already up to date on required vaccinations
Dogs with a bite history are not eligible
Dogs aggressive to people are not eligible
Dogs aggressive to other dogs that may pose a safety risk to staff are not eligible
All dogs must undergo a behavior evaluation to qualify for foster placement
All species of pets are eligible provided they meet behavioral and health criteria

structured_extraction.program_name: Same Day Access (SDA) Program (MetroAccess-based taxi subsidy)
structured_extraction.program_description: Same Day Access (SDA) is a subsidized transportation program administered by Montgomery County for certified MetroAccess participants who reside in Montgomery County. It provides affordable curbside paratransit and taxi transportation services for people with disabilities who have difficulty using fixed-route buses or rail. Participants receive a $60 value on their Call-n-Ride swipe card when they pay $30 once a month, with no income requirement. The program is designed to give eligible residents with disabilities access to flexible, on-demand transportation for medical appointments, personal errands, and other trips within the county.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants who have current MetroAccess identification cards receive a $60 value on their Call-n-Ride swipe card when they pay $30.00 once a month. This benefit is provided to all eligible MetroAccess participants regardless of income. Participants can only make one payment per month. The maximum balance that can be accumulated on the card is $360 (payment plus subsidy). If a remaining balance exists at the end of the month, it rolls over to the following month. The subsidy covers taxi fares at meter rates set by Montgomery County, with an initial charge of $4.00, $2.00 per mile travel cost, $1.00 per extra passenger, and $1.00 for personal service (loading items). The maximum trip limit is $60.00 per one-way trip including tip. Participants may add tips up to 15% of the taxi fare. The subsidy supports curbside paratransit and taxi transportation for trips that begin and end in Montgomery County, with approved exceptions for medical facilities in designated service areas outside the county (including Washington D.C., Baltimore, Prince George's County, Howard County, and Northern Virginia). Pre-authorization is required for trips exceeding the $60.00 limit to approved medical facilities outside Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who have current MetroAccess identification cards and disabilities that prevent them from using fixed-route bus or rail service.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidized taxi and paratransit transportation for medical appointments, personal errands, and other trips that begin and end in Montgomery County, with special exceptions for transportation to approved medical facilities in designated service areas outside the county (Washington D.C., Baltimore, Prince George's County, Howard County, and Northern Virginia). All trips must be dispatched through participating taxicab companies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All trips must begin and end in Montgomery County, Maryland. Special exceptions allow transportation to approved medical facilities in designated Designated Service Areas (DSA) outside the county, including locations in Washington D.C., Baltimore, Prince George's County, Howard County, and Northern Virginia. Pre-authorization is required for trips to approved medical facilities outside Montgomery County. Transportation to approved medical facilities in the region is available upon pre-authorization by calling Call-n-Ride at 301-948-5409, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. PO Boxes are not acceptable as proof of residence.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident (with proof of current residence within the last six months; PO Box not acceptable)
Must have a current MetroAccess identification card
Must be certified as eligible by MetroAccess
Must have a disability that prevents use of fixed-route bus or rail
No income requirement

Must provide proof of Montgomery County residence such as: recent Social Security/Supplemental Security Income (SSI) Statement, Utility Bill (Gas, Electric, Water, Cable, Home Telephone, Cell Phone, Home Security), IRS W-2, Property Tax Bill, Homeowner's/Auto/Renter's Insurance Bill, Monthly Mortgage Statement, or Residential Rental/Lease Agreement
Must submit photocopy of current Metro Access identification card (required for participation)
Must submit photocopy of government-issued photo identification (required)
Recent wallet/passport size photograph recommended but not required for swipe card
SDA swipe card will become inactive upon expiration of Metro Access ID card; recertification required with renewed Metro Access ID copy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the SDA Application Form in its entirety, printing clearly and completely. 2. Submit required documentation with the application: photocopy of current Metro Access identification card, proof of Montgomery County residence (from documents issued within last six months), and photocopy of government-issued photo identification. A wallet-size photograph is recommended but not required. 3. Submit application materials via fax to 240-556-0999, email to cnrorder@montgomerycountymd.gov, or mail/hand-deliver to Call-n-Ride, 101 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Rockville, MD 20850. 4. Upon approval, receive welcome packet with CNR swipe card and membership information. 5. Call a participating taxicab company to schedule trips, identifying yourself as a CNR participant and providing your name, CNR swipe card number, pick-up and destination addresses, and pick-up time. 6. Present CNR swipe card to driver at beginning and end of trip. Participants without photograph on card must also provide valid photo ID. 7. Upon arrival, approve meter amount and may add tip up to 15%. Driver will swipe card to process payment and print receipts. 8. Sign both receipts (driver keeps one, you keep one for six months). 9. For recertification: Submit SDA Recertification Form with updated Metro Access ID photocopy and proof of current residence within 30 days of receiving recertification letter, or swipe card will become inactive. 10. For questions or assistance applying, contact Call-n-Ride at 301-948-5409 (Monday-Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.) or email cnrorder@montgomerycountymd.gov. You may also call Connect-A-Ride at 301-738-3252 for help applying. Translation services available by dialing 866-998-0338, Account #15071, PIN #6101.

structured_extraction.program_description: A dental program operated through Montgomery County Public Schools providing preventive dental services to students at select schools during school hours on school premises. Services include screenings, exams, cleanings, fluoride treatments, sealants, and Silver Diamine Fluoride (SDF) treatment for tooth decay. Registration forms are available in English and Spanish.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free dental services on school premises during normal school hours, including dental screenings and exams, cleanings, fluoride varnish applications (2-4 times per year), dental sealants on permanent back molars, and Silver Diamine Fluoride (SDF) treatment to stop tooth decay (applied every 3, 6, or 12 months as needed). No payment is required; however, Medicaid may help cover costs and the Health Department will seek reimbursement from Medicaid if the child has dental coverage through Medicaid. Services are provided by County Health Department dental professionals at participating schools.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students at select Montgomery County Public Schools who need preventive dental care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Preventive dental services including screenings and exams, cleanings, fluoride varnish treatments, dental sealants on permanent molars, and Silver Diamine Fluoride (SDF) treatment for tooth decay, provided on school premises during school hours.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Select schools throughout Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Student enrollment at a participating school
Parent or legal guardian completion and submission of the School-Based Dental Program Registration Packet
Completion of Minor Consent form for dental treatment
Medical history form must be completed
Acknowledgment of HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices
No allergies to silver (if SDF treatment is planned)
No painful sores or raw areas in mouth or gums (if SDF treatment is planned)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Parents or guardians must complete the School-Based Dental Program Registration Packet, which includes an Informed Consent and Medical History Form. The form collects child information, medical history (including asthma, diabetes, TB, ADHD, AIDS/HIV, epilepsy, bleeding problems, hepatitis, emotional disorders, and latex allergies), current medications, and dental insurance information (Medicaid, private dental insurance, or uninsured status). Parents must also complete and sign the Minor Consent form for dental treatment, which outlines treatment procedures, behavior management techniques, and potential risks. An Attestation of Parentage or Legal Guardianship form must be completed to verify parental or legal guardian status. A Client HIPAA Acknowledgement and Designation Disclosure Form must be signed acknowledging receipt of the Notice of Privacy Practices. If Silver Diamine Fluoride treatment is planned, a separate Informed Consent for SDF must be completed. All completed forms should be returned to the child's school. Registration forms are available in English and Spanish. Parents should contact the Dental Kids program at the phone number or email provided for more information or questions.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program, administered by Montgomery County's Office of Food Systems Resilience in partnership with the Office of Grants Management, supports projects that address critical gaps in healthy food access for children and families by implementing innovative approaches to providing food assistance co-located at Montgomery County Public School (MCPS) sites. The program funds new initiatives and the expansion of existing projects — including food pantries, pre-packed snack bags, grocery gift cards, and prepared meals — at MCPS school sites. In FY24, 8 organizations received $480,452; in FY25, 11 organizations received $1,250,274; and in FY26, 13 organizations received $2,303,775 (including $300,000 in new budget funds) across 99+ school sites, serving an estimated 50,000 students and their families. The FY26 cycle launched in summer 2025.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding is awarded annually to non-profit organizations and other eligible entities to support school-based food assistance programs co-located at MCPS school sites. Applicants may request a minimum of $40,000 and maximum of $300,000; final award amounts may be lower than $40,000. In FY26, 13 organizations received a total of $2,303,775 (including $300,000 in new budget funds) to serve 99+ school sites and an estimated 50,000 students. In FY25, 11 organizations received $1,250,274, and in FY24, 8 organizations received $480,452. Funding supports food purchases, staffing costs, operational expenses including infrastructure (refrigeration, storage, shelving), and indirect costs up to 15% (or established NICRA rate). Grants are typically 10-month performance periods from approximately August 15 through June 30. The FY26 cycle launched in summer 2025 with a prior application deadline of July 14, 2025.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY26: Applications Closed 7/14/25; FY25: Friday, July 26, 2024 at 12:00 PM (closed)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Heather Bruskin; Catherine Nardi (Program Manager, OFSR); Ali Hoy (Program Manager II, OGM)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations, for-profit entities, and other eligible organizations based in Montgomery County that are experienced food assistance providers seeking to establish, expand, or maintain food assistance programs at Montgomery County Public School sites to serve students and their families experiencing or at-risk of experiencing food insecurity.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support projects that address food insecurity for children and families through school-based initiatives such as food pantries (choice pantry model), pre-packed snack bags, pre-packed boxes/bags with shelf-stable and/or fresh foods, grocery gift cards, prepared meals, meal service expansion, nutrition education, and food purchasing at MCPS school sites. Allowable expenses include food purchases, staffing and fringe costs, operational costs, infrastructure (refrigeration, storage, shelving), transportation, data collection and reporting, and indirect costs. Funds cannot be used for lobbying, expenses made prior to grant award, supplanting other funds, or services wholly occurring outside Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County Public Schools sites in Montgomery County, Maryland. The FY26 program targets approximately 80–99 MCPS school sites serving more than 50,000 children. All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and/or exclusively for Montgomery County residents. Awardees are matched with one or multiple specific school(s) following the grant review period based on alignment of individual school's needs with providers' current programs, experience, and capacity.

Organizations must have provided food assistance services over the past calendar year in at least one MCPS site, demonstrated through email documentation, formal contract/MOU, or signed letter of support from school administrator
Organizations must be currently registered and in Good Standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Organization's principal place of business must be located in Montgomery County; if national/regional organization, must have location in Montgomery County providing related services
All activities and expenditures must be provided in Montgomery County and/or exclusively for Montgomery County residents
Proposed project must not exclude any potential beneficiaries based on race, ethnicity, gender, or other protected class
Current Montgomery County contract or grant award winners must be current on all reporting obligations and reports must reflect substantial progress toward goals
Organizations must be able to establish and maintain a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with assigned school partner(s)
Organizations must maintain regular communication with school-based point(s) of contact
Organizations must develop program models for successful services at schools
Programs must address food resource needs identified by school personnel
Projects must be implemented at a Montgomery County Public School site
Attend a participating MCPS school site (for individual beneficiaries)
Lead applicants may only submit one application per cycle
Proposed expenses must be for new activity, expansion of existing activities, or combination of both; cannot supplant existing funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations apply through the Montgomery County SM Apply online grants application platform (https://mcmdgrants.smapply.org) by completing all required application tasks including Applicant Information, Applicant Background, Project Strategy Narrative (3 pages max), Project Budget (MS Excel), Budget Narrative/Justification (2 pages max), Project Staffing Plan (2 pages max), Project Work Plan/Timeline (1 page max), and Performance Plan (2 pages max). Applications must include supporting documentation such as IRS Tax Exempt Determination Letter for nonprofits, most recent IRS 990 Form or explanation of exemption, current board list, independent audit report or financial review, and proof of prior MCPS partnership. An independent Review Committee composed of neutral qualified individuals from Montgomery County Government and community members reviews and scores applications based on criteria outlined in the NOFO. Final decisions made by County based on scores and other relevant factors. Award notification letters are released via email approximately one month after application deadline. Successful applicants receive a Grant Agreement specifying total award amount, funding restrictions, programmatic/administrative/policy requirements, reporting requirements, and payment terms. Once awarded, grantees must submit mid-cycle (5-month) and end-cycle (10-month) programmatic and financial reports including participation metrics, service delivery details, budgetary information, and narrative feedback through the OFSR online reporting platform. Applications administered by the Office of Food Systems Resilience in partnership with the Office of Grants Management.

This option applies only to owner-occupied residential property and became mandatory for all eligible real property owners starting in tax year 2000.

Property must be located in Montgomery County
Mailing address must match the premise address
If escrowing taxes with lender, must notify lender by May 1st of intent to pay annually

structured_extraction.program_description: A subsidy program that helps eligible seniors aged 62 and older afford assisted living group home care in licensed assisted living facilities located in Montgomery County. The program limits facility charges and provides monthly subsidies up to $1,056 to help cover the cost of care, making assisted living more accessible for qualified older residents who meet income and asset requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Monthly subsidy payment of up to $1,056 per month. The subsidy limits the total amount an assisted living facility may charge a subsidy participant to no more than $3,300 per month for the care rate. Applicants may qualify for partial subsidies based on their calculated monthly payment. The subsidy helps make care more affordable, though it typically does not cover the full cost of care. Assisted living facilities must be state and county licensed and agree to participate in the subsidy program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents aged 62 or older who require 24-hour supervision, meet income and asset limits, and need assisted living care in a licensed facility in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To help pay for assisted living group home care and services in licensed assisted living facilities participating in the program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be Maryland residents. The program is administered by Montgomery County and serves facilities located within Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland resident
Must be 62 years or older
Must require 24-hour supervision as documented by a nurse from the Department of Health and Human Services
Income no more than $4,350 for an individual (as of July 14, 2023)
Assets no more than $20,064 for an individual (as of July 14, 2023)
For a couple, income is looked at individually with no more than $20,064 in assets combined
Qualify for subsidy based on program criteria
Reside in a licensed assisted living facility participating in the subsidy program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Senior Assisted Living Subsidy program at 240-777-1138 to request an application. Submit a completed application, photo ID, and proof of income, assets, benefits, and medical expenses. A nurse from the Department of Health and Human Services will perform an on-site assessment at no cost to determine eligibility. Applications are reviewed and processed on a first-come, first-served basis when all steps are complete, subject to funding availability. Facilities must be state and county licensed and agree to participate in the subsidy program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County's Senior Nutrition Program provides hot congregate meals at lunchtime for seniors and other eligible individuals at multiple senior program locations throughout the county. The program is funded under Public Law 109-365, the Older Americans Act (OAA) and is offered in partnership with the Department of Health and Human Services, Aging and Disability Services. For seniors ages 60 and over, a voluntary donation is requested (recommended $3 per meal); for those under 60, the full price of the meal is required. Advanced registration is required at least one week in advance. The program also offers boxes of seven frozen meals for weekly pickup at senior centers, and provides information about home-delivered meals (Meals on Wheels) for seniors who cannot cook or travel to congregate meal sites. Spouses of any age of active participants, disabled adult children living with active participants, SNP volunteers (two hours per month), and individuals with disabilities under age 60 living in buildings where a nutrition site is located may also be eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Hot congregate meals provided at lunchtime at 13 senior program and community recreation locations throughout Montgomery County. Most locations serve Monday through Friday at 12:00 PM, with some variations (some locations at 11:30 AM; some locations on specific days such as Tuesday/Friday or Monday/Thursday; Benjamin Gaither Center serves Tuesday-Thursday; Montgomery Village Foundation at Stedwick Community Center serves Monday-Thursday). For seniors ages 60 and over, a voluntary donation is requested with a recommended amount of $3 per meal (donations can be made in cash, check, or credit card). For those under 60, the full price of the meal is required. Donations of any amount are accepted; no change is provided but donors can contribute for multiple days at once. Additionally, boxes of seven frozen meals are available weekly for pickup at Senior Centers. Information and referrals are provided for home-delivered meals (Meals on Wheels) for those unable to attend congregate sites. Advanced registration is required at least one week in advance; some centers offer stand-by or waiting list options for last-minute availability if extra meals are available (stand-by list available only for registered participants at the specific center). All meals include milk or yogurt and 100% fruit juice. Hot, cold, and vegetarian meal options are available. Monthly menus are available in Chinese, English, French, Korean, Spanish, or Vietnamese. Meals are prepared and served by Nutrition Site Managers at each location. Weather-related closures may occur when Montgomery County Schools have delayed openings or closures; meals prepared for closure days are frozen and served the following open day.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Senior Nutrition Site Managers (individual center staff)
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 240-777-4925 (Senior Programs Team general line); 240-777-3810 (HHS Aging and Disability Services); or individual senior center phone numbers
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors ages 60 and over (donation basis), spouses of active participants (any age), disabled adult children living with active participants, SNP volunteers (any age, two hours per month), individuals with disabilities under age 60 living in buildings where a nutrition site is located, and individuals under 60 at full meal price. Program is available at 13 senior program and community recreation locations around Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nutrition support through hot congregate meals at lunchtime at senior centers and community recreation centers, weekly frozen meal boxes for pickup, and referrals to home-delivered meals (Meals on Wheels). Meals meet nutritional standards and provide socialization opportunities and access to supportive services throughout the county.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at 13 locations throughout Montgomery County, Maryland: Benjamin Gaither Center (Gaithersburg), Damascus Community Center (Damascus), East County Community Center (Silver Spring), Germantown Community Center (Germantown), Holiday Park Senior Center (Wheaton), Long Branch Community Center (Silver Spring), Margaret Schweinhaut Senior Center (Silver Spring), Montgomery Village Foundation at Stedwick Community Center (Montgomery Village), North Potomac Community Center (Rockville), Rockville Senior Center (Rockville), Silver Spring Recreation & Aquatic Center (Silver Spring), Wheaton Community Center (Silver Spring), and White Oak Community Center (Silver Spring).
requirements_list: Age 60 and over for donation-based participation (those under 60 may participate at full meal price)
Spouses of any age of active participants are eligible
Disabled adult children living with active participants are eligible
SNP volunteers (of any age) for minimum two hours per month are eligible
Individuals with disabilities under age 60 living with a parent or grandparent who is an already registered participant are eligible
Individuals with disabilities under age 60 living in a building where a nutrition site is located are eligible
Valid Maryland ID may be required
Annual registration required; SNP registration form must be completed and submitted to the Nutrition Site Manager at preferred meal location
Participants receive an SNP meal card to be used for each meal transaction; card can be used at any meal location in Montgomery County
Advanced registration required at least one week in advance by calling the specific center to reserve meals
Reservations must be made at the specific center where the meal will be consumed; one meal per location per day maximum
Meal reservation/cancellation deadline is 10:00 AM on: Wednesday for Monday meals, Thursday for Tuesday meals, Friday for Wednesday meals, Monday for Thursday meals, Tuesday for Friday meals

No-show policy: cancellations made the day of the meal are considered no-shows; two no-shows within a two-week period (1st-15th or 16th-end of month) result in loss of advance reservation privileges for the next two-week period; accumulated no-shows can lead to temporary or permanent removal from program

Stand-by list available only for registered participants without advance reservations or who have lost advance reservation privileges; must be present in person at the center to be added to stand-by list for that day only
Call the center to determine number of meals available and reservation procedures

Behavior expectations: participants must abide by SNP rules and regulations, maintain courteous and respectful conduct, comply with meal ordering and cancellation timelines, no bullying or harassment, no disruptive behavior, no removal of perishable food items from dining areas (nonperishable items like whole fruit, bread, sealed fruit cups permitted)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the SNP registration form (available in multiple languages: Chinese, English, French, Korean, Spanish, Vietnamese) and submit to the Nutrition Site Manager at your preferred meal location. 2. Registration must be completed annually. 3. Upon registration, participants receive an SNP meal card to be used for each meal transaction; the card can be used at any meal location in Montgomery County. 4. To reserve a congregate meal: Contact the Nutrition Site Manager at your desired center by phone or email at least one week in advance. 5. Complete a monthly reservation menu selecting your preferred meal type (hot, cold, or vegetarian option). 6. Submit the monthly reservation form to the Nutrition Site Manager. 7. Observe reservation/cancellation deadlines: Wednesday (for Monday meals), Thursday (for Tuesday meals), Friday (for Wednesday meals), Monday (for Thursday meals), Tuesday (for Friday meals) by 10:00 AM. 8. Arrive at the designated location at the scheduled mealtime. 9. Make your voluntary donation (recommended $3) or pay the full meal price if required. 10. For stand-by meals: If you do not have an advance reservation or have lost reservation privileges, you may speak to the Nutrition Site Manager about being added to the stand-by list on that day only; you must be present in person at the center. 11. For frozen meal pickup: Contact the nearest Senior Center for enrollment information and weekly meal pickup details. 12. For home-delivered meals: Request information and referrals from the Nutrition Site Manager for Meals on Wheels providers in your area.

The program was created by Montgomery County Council under Bill 6-12 in April 2012.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance up to $125,000 and/or technical assistance provided periodically over the duration of the County-related project to small businesses that are financially healthy but adversely impacted by redevelopment. Businesses may receive more than one disbursement, with the maximum total assistance amount being $125,000 throughout the entire project period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Financially healthy small businesses in identified geographic areas adversely impacted by County-funded redevelopment projects, projects on County-owned property, or County facility projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business operations and viability maintenance during County-related redevelopment periods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Identified geographic areas within Montgomery County affected by County-funded redevelopment projects, projects on County-owned property, or County facility projects. The current focus is the Wheaton Revitalization Project.
requirements_list: Business must be financially healthy
Business must be located in an identified geographic area
Business must be adversely impacted by a County-funded redevelopment project, a redevelopment project located on County-owned property, or a County facility project
Business must meet eligibility requirements and criteria described in Executive Regulation 24-12AM
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Division of Fiscal Management for application details and to determine eligibility. Assistance is provided periodically over the duration of the County-related project. Applications are reviewed based on Executive Regulation 24-12AM criteria.

structured_extraction.program_description: A collaboration between Montgomery County and community banks to promote job growth through small business lending. The County invests $50 million in participating community banks, which commit an equal amount of lending, resulting in $100 million in loans to local small businesses to support job creation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County deposits $50 million in participating community banks that are headquartered in Montgomery County, have assets greater than $200 million and no more than $10 billion, and meet safety and soundness standards. Each participating bank commits an equal amount of lending. The banks must originate loans within 12 calendar months of the County's commitment to make a deposit. All funds deposited are covered by FDIC insurance. The result is $100 million in total lending to local small businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses in Montgomery County and community banks headquartered in the County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business loans to support job creation and growth
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County. Participating banks must be headquartered in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Banks must be headquartered in Montgomery County
Banks must have assets greater than $200 million and no more than $10 billion
Banks must meet safety and soundness standards established by the County
Loans must be originated within 12 calendar months of the County's commitment to make a deposit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Community banks apply to participate in the program. The County evaluates participating banks based on headquarters location, asset size, and safety and soundness criteria. Once approved, banks receive County deposits and commit to matching lending.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps Montgomery County residents who need support to live independently in their community or secure institutional care when appropriate. The program provides information and referral services to connect people with other agencies, crisis intervention services for people going through difficult life changes, and ongoing case management to help adults maintain independence.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides no-cost assessment and case management services to financially eligible participants. Services include information and referral (connecting adults to other agencies), crisis intervention (up to 60 days of intensive help during a crisis or life change), and case management (comprehensive assessment and individualized service planning to help adults live independently in the community). Financially eligible participants receive these services at no charge. Information and Referral Services and Crisis Intervention Services are available regardless of income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County residents who need case management, crisis intervention, or information and referral services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides case management services, information and referral to other agencies, and crisis intervention support to help adults maintain independence or secure appropriate institutional care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County residents only. Applicants must live in the community.
requirements_list: Must be a Montgomery County resident
Must live in the community
Must be in need of services

For Continuing Case Management Services: income may not exceed 80 percent of State Median Income based on family size, and liquid assets may not exceed $19,999 for one individual plus $3,000 for each additional family member
Information and Referral Services and Crisis Intervention Services are available regardless of income
Must agree to receive and engage in services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Aging and Disability Resource Unit at 240-777-3000 to apply. No documents are required to bring.
