structured_extraction.program_name: Speak Up, Save a Life Video Contest
structured_extraction.program_description: An annual video competition for middle and high school students in Montgomery County that challenges teenagers to create original videos promoting awareness about the dangers of illicit opioids, fentanyl, and overdose risk. Winners receive cash prizes ranging from $1,000 to $5,000.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cash prizes awarded to winning video entries: first place receives $5,000, second place receives $3,000, third place and fan favorite winners each receive $1,000, and an additional $5,000 is split among honorable mention winners. Participating Montgomery County Public Schools (MCPS) students also earn 10 service learning hours.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in grades 6 through 12 living in or attending school in Montgomery County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are awarded as prizes for creating an original video that promotes awareness about opioids, fentanyl, and overdose dangers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to all 6th through 12th grade students living in or attending school in Montgomery County.
requirements_list: Must be a 6th to 12th grade student living in or attending school in Montgomery County
Video must be 50-70 seconds in length
Video must have a title
Video must be in English or Spanish

Video must address at least one topic: statistics or factual information about opioids/fentanyl, impact of peer pressure or mental health issues, examples of healthy choices to avoid illegal drugs, or bystander intervention
Video must include the visual link knowtherisksmc.org or the QR code and logo as a resource
Video may not include copyrighted music, audio, video clips, characters, logos, or protected material unless it is open source music or composed and performed by students in the group
Video may not include illegal items, inappropriate language, needles or syringes, violent or graphic overdose scenes, or general violence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students submit their video entries through the Video Contest Registration Page (Google Form). The contest opens on October 9 and entries are due by the stated deadline. Winners are selected and announced at an awards ceremony.

structured_extraction.program_description: A temporary food service license for events lasting no more than 30 consecutive days at a fixed location where food or drink is prepared, served, or sold using mobile, permanent, or temporary structures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county issues a temporary food service license that permits food or drink preparation, serving, or sale at events lasting no more than 30 consecutive days (licenses issued for maximum of 14 consecutive days per license). Fees vary by organization type and food category: For-Profit organizations pay $70 for potentially hazardous or open food (including samples), $40 for commercially prepackaged non-potentially hazardous food (first license), and $35 for additional licenses at the same event. Non-Profit organizations (with 501c(3), 504c, 507c, or 510c documentation) pay $30 for potentially hazardous or open food and $15 for non-potentially hazardous food. A $30 late fee applies for applications received less than 3 business days prior to an event. The application process includes review and inspection before the event begins. The license is mailed to the applicant or issued at the time of inspection. Approval typically takes 10-14 business days.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: At least two working days prior to the event (applications received less than 3 business days prior incur a $30 late fee)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anyone who plans to sell or give away food at a temporary event in Montgomery County, except for those selling only fresh produce or live crustaceans.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Authorization to prepare, serve, or sell food or drink at a temporary event lasting no more than 30 consecutive days at a fixed location using mobile, permanent, or temporary structures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Event must be at a fixed location
Event duration cannot exceed 30 consecutive days
Application must be submitted at least two working days before the event starts (an additional $30 fee applies for applications filed less than three working days prior)
Applicant must submit application with attachments and appropriate fee
Non-profits must provide 501c(3), 504c, 507c, or 510c documentation
Inspection may be conducted at the event prior to operating
Exception: fresh produce or live crustaceans do not require a license
Food for a temporary event may not be prepared or stored at home
Cold food must be kept at 41°F or below and frozen food at 0°F or below
No bare hand contact with ready-to-eat food; plastic gloves or clean, sanitized utensils must be used
All water and ice must come from an approved source
Hand washing station with tempered running water (minimum 100°F) must be provided and operational before food preparation begins
All storage, food handling, preparation, cooking, and serving must be conducted under an approved overhead cover, tent, canopy, or tarp
No person who is ill or has an open wound is allowed to work with the food operation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the application, attachments, and appropriate fee online through the CivicGov platform, by PDF via email, by mail, or by fax at least two working days prior to the event. Mail applications to: Licensure & Regulatory Services, 2425 Reedie Drive, 9th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902. Fax to: 240-777-3088 or 240-777-3088. Incomplete applications will be returned. The application and attachments will be reviewed, and an inspection may be conducted at the event if warranted. The license will be mailed to the applicant or issued at the time of inspection. Approval typically takes 10-14 business days. A $30 late fee applies for applications received less than 3 business days prior to the event. Credit card payments (Visa or MasterCard only) are accepted.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows property owners to transfer stormwater facilities into the County's Stormwater Facility Maintenance Program. Once transferred, Montgomery County becomes responsible for structural maintenance of the facility, such as leaks, stone replacement, and replacing concrete and pipes. Property owners remain responsible for non-structural maintenance such as trash removal, grass cutting, and landscaping.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County assumes responsibility for structural maintenance of the stormwater facility, including repairs for leaks, stone replacement, and replacing concrete and pipes. This relieves the property owner of these maintenance costs. Property owners retain ownership of the facility and continue to be responsible for non-structural maintenance such as trash removal, grass cutting, and landscaping.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; applications accepted on a rolling basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners and homeowners' associations who own stormwater facilities, particularly those with facilities located on HOA or common areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The assistance covers structural maintenance of stormwater facilities, including repair of leaks, replacement of stone, and replacement of concrete and pipes. Non-structural maintenance such as trash removal, grass cutting, and landscaping remains the responsibility of the property owner.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Residential facilities located on HOA or common areas in Montgomery County are eligible for transfer. Storm drains are not part of the Stormwater Facility Maintenance Program and may not be transferred.
requirements_list: Facility must have an approved final inspection
Facility must be in proper working condition as determined by DEP
Property owner must provide deed showing transfer from developer to property owner or HOA
Property owner must provide stormwater easement and covenants documentation (existing or new)
Property owner must provide information on stormwater facility type and facility number
Property owner must provide property location and property parcel numbers (tax account numbers)
Property owner must provide most recent tax bill
All documents must be completed, signed, and notarized
For facilities without existing easement or covenant, applicant may request DEP assistance in providing easement metes and bounds (Exhibit A) and graphic depiction (Exhibit B)
Condominium owners must contact DEP prior to submission as additional documents are required
Applicants should consider hiring an attorney to assist with document preparation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The transfer process has three stages. Stage 1: Gather required documents including deed, stormwater easement and covenants documentation, facility information, property location, property parcel numbers, and most recent tax bill. Contact DEP at SWMF.Transfer@montgomerycountymd.gov or 311 before submitting to ensure all necessary documents are prepared. Stage 2: Complete the Stormwater Facility Maintenance Transfer Application form and all supporting transaction documents (grants of easement, declaration of covenants, or covenant amendments). Sign and notarize all documents but do not execute them until DEP approves the drafts. Submit the application and supporting documents for legal review by DEP and Montgomery County Office of the County Attorney. After legal review and certification, the County Attorney returns documents to DEP for submission to County Administrative Officer for signature. DEP then returns fully executed documents to applicant. Stage 3: Record all signed and approved documents with County Land Records. Notify DEP when documents have been recorded. Official approval letter and letter indicating Montgomery County becomes responsible for structural maintenance are sent after DEP receives notification of recording. Timeline varies based on application completeness, document submission, and number of applications being processed.

Also available for businesses with at least 25 employees that operate on-site licensed child care centers. The credit is available to property owners and taxpayers who own or operate qualifying day care facilities in Montgomery County.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Day care providers, property owners, and employers operating child care facilities in Montgomery County

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland
requirements_list: Improvement used exclusively for day care services

Credit is limited to the lesser of $3,000 or the amount of general county and special area taxes attributable to the improvement

requirements_list: Surviving spouse has not remarried

Deceased officer/worker was domiciled in Maryland at time of death

structured_extraction.program_description: A workforce development program that employs high school students in public sector and nonprofit jobs throughout Montgomery County. Participants receive mentorship from career professionals, job readiness training, skill-building workshops, and meaningful work experience while earning pay.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants are seasonal/temporary employees of Montgomery County Recreation paid at minimum wage of $16.70/hr. They work between 200 to 350 hours (varying by grade level: 9th grade 350 hours, 10th grade 300 hours, 11th-12th grade 200 hours each) at assigned host organizations. They receive on-the-job training, complete three coaching sessions, attend 30 hours of workforce development training, develop and implement a capstone project, and earn a certificate of completion and letter of reference. Host sites provide structured work opportunities, onsite training and coaching, supervision, mentorship, and practical experiences to develop job-ready skills.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Spring/Summer: Jan. 2 - March 30; Fall/Winter: Aug. 1 - Nov. 30
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County high school students who are at least 15 years old and residents of Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support teen wages for employment in public sector and nonprofit positions. Teens gain work experience in fields such as recreation, communications, finance, human resources, special events, and other skilled trade positions through structured on-the-job training, coaching, and classroom instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland. Applicants must be Montgomery County residents.
requirements_list: Be a Montgomery County resident
Be a high school student
Be at least 15 years old
Have availability to work the full program duration at the assigned placement
Attend a mandatory TeenWorks employment information session
Complete the employment application
Have parent/guardian consent to be employed in the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an interest form by the seasonal deadline. Attend a mandatory TeenWorks employment information session to learn about the program and requirements. Complete the employment application through the government jobs portal. The TeenWorks program will match participants based on interest assessment responses, considering interests, skills, career goals, and host organization requirements. Participate in an interview with the TeenWorks team. Upon selection, complete a parent/apprentice agreement form and attend a placement meeting with the partnering organization.

structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County Government offers tuition assistance funds to eligible employees to support their educational pursuits and career development. The program provides reimbursement for tuition and compulsory fees for courses, certificates, degrees, and training that are directly related to the employee's current job functions or career ladder within the County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides tuition assistance reimbursements to Montgomery County Government employees with merit system status on a first-come, first-served basis. Funding is available each fiscal year beginning July 1st. FY26 maximum awards: FOP full-time $1,730.00, FOP part-time $865.00; IAFF full-time $1,830.00, IAFF part-time $915.00; MCGEO and other bargaining units have varying amounts. Tuition assistance covers tuition and compulsory fees (matriculation, registration, laboratory fees, library services) but does not cover books, supplies, exam fees, or other incidental expenses. Probationary employees may apply but must pay upfront and receive reimbursement after course completion and upon achieving merit system status. Reimbursements can be sent to employees electronically or by paper check. The program is taxable income under current federal law. Employees must remain employed by the County for one to two years after completing a funded course (varies by bargaining unit) or reimburse a prorated amount of the assistance received.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First-come, first-served until fiscal year funding is obligated. FY26 application opens July 1, 2026 at 9 am. Applications must be submitted at least three to four weeks prior to course registration and within the fiscal year (July 1 through June 30).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Montgomery County Government employees with merit system status, including probationary employees. Eligibility varies by union/bargaining agreement (FOP, IAFF, MCGEO, UNREP, MCVFRA).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and compulsory fees for education or training to obtain a certificate, associate degree, baccalaureate degree, or graduate degree. Training must be directly related to either the employee's current County job functions or career ladder in the same job series or profession, or a field of study that will prepare the employee to make a career change within the County. Courses must be taken at accredited institutions as recognized by the United States Department of Education or Higher Education Accreditation Commission.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County Government employees only.
requirements_list: Must have merit system status with Montgomery County Government
Probationary (permanent full-time or part-time) employees may apply but must pay tuition upfront and receive reimbursement after course completion and upon achieving merit system status
Eligibility and funding amounts vary by union/bargaining agreement (FOP, IAFF, MCGEO, UNREP, MCVFRA)
Training must be directly related to current job functions, career ladder within the County, or a field of study enabling career change within the County
Courses must be taken at accredited colleges or universities recognized by the United States Department of Education or Higher Education Accreditation Commission
Course must be completed with a passing grade or documented course completion certificate
For FOP employees: must remain employed for two years after course completion or reimburse prorated amount
For IAFF employees: must remain employed for one year after course completion or reimburse prorated amount
Courses must have a start date within the current fiscal year
Final grade notice or course completion certificate must be submitted to OHR upon completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employees log into the Montgomery County Government online portal using their County USERID and password, navigate to the Tuition Assistance Program application, and submit their application. Applications must be submitted at least three to four weeks prior to actual course registration. Once approved, employees receive an authorization letter from OHR addressed to the school. The letter serves as a contract authorizing the school to bill the County directly for tuition fees. Employees must attach either an approved leave request signed by their supervisor or an approved work schedule with flex-time adjustment if taking the course during normal work hours. Processing time is typically 7-14 days. Upon course completion, employees must submit the original grade notice or course completion certificate to the OHR training staff. Future tuition assistance requests will not be processed until grades or certificates from prior courses have been received. Tuition assistance is available on a first-come, first-served basis until fiscal year funding is exhausted.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit program for residential properties used for urban agriculture in Montgomery County. Owners receive an 80% credit on county property taxes for up to 10 years (two 5-year periods). Properties must be between half an acre and 3 acres, zoned residential, and located within 1,000 feet of a Metro Station Policy Area. Owners must generate more than $5,000 in gross annual income from selling agricultural products grown or raised on the property, or donate more than $5,000 of such products to a qualifying charitable organization.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The credit equals 80% of the County property tax on the eligible property for each tax year. The credit is available for 5 tax years and may be renewed for another 5 tax years, for a maximum total of 10 years of tax credits. The credit is calculated and issued on a revised tax bill after the initial July bill, appearing as a line item deduction. The credit terminates if the property owner does not earn more than $5,000 in gross income from the property in any given tax year, or if the property ceases to be used for urban agricultural purposes. If the property is no longer used for agricultural purposes during the term of the credit, the owner becomes liable for all property taxes that would have been due if the credit had not been granted for any year the property was not used for agricultural purposes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 (before the tax year that begins July 1); for 2017 taxes only, applications accepted until September 1, 2017
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of residential properties used for urban agriculture within Montgomery County, including individual property owners and urban agricultural enterprises
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit reduces the property owner's annual county property tax bill for properties used for urban agricultural activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be within 1,000 feet of one of ten Metro Station Policy Areas: Bethesda Central Business District, Friendship Heights, Glenmont, Grosvenor, Rockville Town Center, Shady Grove, Silver Spring Central Business District, Twinbrook, Wheaton Central Business District, or White Flint. All eligible properties must be in Montgomery County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Property must be between 1/2 acre and 3 acres in size
Property must be zoned residential

Property must be used solely for urban agricultural purposes (cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers, ornamental plants; limited keeping of fowl or bees; or aquaculture), except an individual may also reside on the property

Owner must receive more than $5,000 in gross income each year from the sale of agricultural products grown or raised on the property (or donate more than $5,000 of agricultural products to a charitable organization registered with the Maryland Secretary of State)
Property must be within 1,000 feet of a Metro Station Policy Area
Application must be submitted on or before April 1 before the tax year for which the credit is sought
Property owner must apply annually to continue the credit
Multiple contiguous subdivision lots under common ownership may be combined to satisfy minimum lot size requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners must submit an application on or before April 1 before the tax year for which the credit is sought. Applications are made to the Montgomery County Office of Agriculture on a form containing the information required by the Office of Agriculture. An online application is available, or a paper version can be obtained from the Department of Finance, Division of Treasury at 27 Courthouse Square, Suite 200, Rockville, Maryland 20850. The Montgomery County Office of Agriculture certifies each property for the tax credit annually and makes a recommendation to the Director of Finance, who determines taxpayer eligibility. The tax credit is calculated and issued on a revised tax bill after the initial July bill, appearing as a line item deduction. To renew the credit, the property owner must apply no later than 90 days before the expiration of the initial 5-year term. A taxpayer may appeal a final decision by the Director denying or terminating the credit to the Maryland Tax Court within 30 days after receiving notice of denial or termination.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three service tiers available after discount: $19.99 per month (200 Mbps download/upload with Discovery+ for 3 months), $39.99 per month (400 Mbps download/upload with Discovery+ for 6 months), or $59.99 per month (Gigabit download/upload with Discovery+ for 12 months), all plus Maryland state tax. Equipment fees of $15 per month apply after the third month. Additional $10 discount available if combined with a $70 per month wireless phone plan. Disney+ is free for the first 12 months ($6.99 thereafter).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income households and seniors in Montgomery County who participate in qualifying assistance programs or have household income below 135% of federal poverty rate.

requirements_list: Participate in qualifying assistance programs (Medicaid, Public Housing, SNAP, Veteran's Administration Pension, VA Survivor's Benefit) or have household income below specified thresholds

structured_extraction.program_name: Volunteer Income Tax Assistance Partnership (VITA) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Free tax preparation and filing assistance for low- and moderate-income Montgomery County residents. IRS-certified volunteer tax preparers prepare and electronically file federal and state income tax returns at no cost, and help taxpayers claim special credits including the federal Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC, maximum $8,046), Maryland Earned Income Tax Credit, and the Montgomery County Working Families Income Supplement. The program also assists with ITIN (Individual Taxpayer Identification Number) applications and renewals, promotes financial education, banking and asset building, and provides referrals to public and community resources. The program served over 2,000 households in a recent year, obtaining a total net of $8.6 million in tax credits. Volunteers are trained and IRS-certified to serve as tax preparers, programmers, receptionists, quality reviewers, and site coordinators — no prior experience is required to volunteer.

Services include preparation and e-filing of federal and state income tax returns, assistance claiming the federal EITC (maximum $8,046), Maryland EITC, and Montgomery County Working Families Income Supplement, ITIN application and renewal assistance, and referrals to community resources. Appointments are available in-person at multiple Montgomery County locations (Casey Community Center in Gaithersburg at 810 S Frederick Ave; TESS Community Action Center in Silver Spring at 8703 Flower Ave; Community Action Agency in Rockville at 1401 Rockville Pike, Suite 320; and WorkSource Montgomery in Wheaton at 11510 Georgia Avenue, 3rd Floor) as well as virtual appointments on Fridays. Walk-in appointments are available Tuesday through Thursday, 2–4 pm in Rockville on a first-come, first-served basis. Tax season appointments run January 20 through April 9, 2026; amended returns and prior year returns may be served June through November. Specific appointment hours vary by location: Mondays 2 pm–8 pm (Casey Community Center); Tuesdays 2 pm–8 pm (TESS) or 11 am–5 pm (Community Action Agency); Wednesdays 12 pm–8 pm (Community Action Agency); Thursdays 11 am–5 pm (WorkSource Montgomery and Community Action Agency); Fridays 11 am–5 pm (virtual appointments).

structured_extraction.program_name: Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) Credit Reduction Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows residential, agricultural, multi-family, non-residential property owners, homeowner associations, and nonprofit organizations in Montgomery County to reduce their annual Water Quality Protection Charge (WQPC) by installing and maintaining on-site stormwater management practices such as rain gardens, green roofs, permeable pavement, rain barrels, cisterns, stormwater ponds, conservation landscaping, dry wells, and grass swales. Property owners may receive credits of up to 60% or 80% depending on the type and extent of stormwater management practices installed. Property owners may also request a hardship reduction or appeal the charge.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Single-family residential (SFR) properties can receive a credit of up to 80% of their annual WQPC based on the volume of water treated by stormwater management practices. The credit is calculated by comparing the total volume of water captured by all practices on the property to the Environmental Site Design Volume (ESDv) required for the property: Percent Credit = (Total Volume Captured / ESDv) × 80%. Non-residential and multi-family residential (NR/MFR) properties can receive credits of up to 60% or 80% depending on the extent of stormwater treatment. For NR/MFR properties, the credit is based on the volume of stormwater treatment provided by each practice. If design data is available, applicants can input the design volume into the NR/MFR Credit Calculator. If no design data is available, the calculator automatically calculates an assumed treatment volume. Credits are applied as a reduction to the annual WQPC charge on the property tax bill according to: WQPC Credit = Percent Credit × WQPC Charge on Bill (before credit). Credits must be renewed every 3 years. Property owners may also request a hardship reduction of the charge or file an appeal. Off-site stormwater treatment may qualify for additional credits.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 311 (in County) or 240-777-0311, 711 for MD Relay TTY
structured_extraction.program_audience: All property owners in Montgomery County, including residential, agricultural, multi-family, non-residential properties, homeowner associations, and nonprofit organizations who have or wish to install and maintain stormwater management practices such as rain gardens, green roofs, permeable pavement, rain barrels, cisterns, stormwater ponds, conservation landscaping, dry wells, and grass swales.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The Water Quality Protection Charge funds Clean Water Montgomery initiatives including stream restoration, stream monitoring, storm drain cleaning and maintenance, stormwater management practice inspection, water quality and wildlife habitat protection, and flood prevention activities. Credits are applied to reduce the annual WQPC charge for properties with registered stormwater management practices.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County, Maryland only. Stormwater management practices must be registered with the County.
requirements_list: Must be a property owner in Montgomery County
Must have a stormwater management practice on the property to qualify for the credit reduction
Stormwater management practices must be registered with Montgomery County
Must maintain practices in accordance with Department of Environmental Protection maintenance requirements
Credits must be renewed every 3 years
Application must be submitted by September 30
Different application processes exist for residential and agricultural properties, multi-family and non-residential properties, and nonprofit organizations
Applicants must provide Account ID (8-digit number from property tax bill), owner name, property address, mailing address if different, telephone number, and email address

For multi-family and non-residential properties: engineer certified plans including total impervious area, year of installation, facility size and units, and impervious area treated by the stormwater management system are required
A photograph of the stormwater management system is required for multi-family and non-residential properties
For condo properties, only one application is needed from the condo association if the practice applies to all owners
A site visit may be required to verify the stormwater management practice
Stormwater management practices must be properly installed and maintained according to MDE Stormwater Design Manual specifications
Single-family residential practices must comply with maintenance requirements in Montgomery County Code Section 19-28
For SFR properties, applicants must complete an Inspections and Maintenance Checklist confirming practices are functioning per maintenance requirements
Underground practices such as dry wells must have above-ground components such as observation pipes or downspout pipes visible for verification

Properties with permitted stormwater management practices through Department of Permitting Services or RainScapes projects generally do not need to submit design information if technical plans are filed with County
Privately installed practices may be required to submit specific design information for County to establish credit amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners choose their property type (Residential & Agricultural, Multi-Family & Non-Residential, or Nonprofit Organizations) and complete the corresponding charge reduction application using WQPC forms available at the online portal. Applications are due September 30. For SFR properties: The SFR credit application prepopulates initial application information including parcel area, impervious area and other WQPC information once a property tax account is selected. Applicants select types of stormwater management practices present on property from list of eligible practices. Applicants then complete the Inspections and Maintenance Checklist, confirming practices are functioning per maintenance requirements. After completing inspection information and contact information, applicants access the SFR Credit Calculator where they input size and/or number of stormwater management systems and any date information. The calculator computes volume of water treated by practices based on assumptions typical for each practice within County context. The calculator then accumulates total volume treated by all practices and prorates the WQPC credit up to 80%. For NR/MFR properties: Applicants submit engineer certified plans including total impervious area, year of installation, facility size and units, and impervious area treated by stormwater system. If design data is available, applicants input design volume into NR/MFR Credit Calculator. If no design data is available, calculator automatically calculates assumed treatment volume. Photographs of stormwater management systems are required. A site visit may be required to verify the stormwater management practice. The Department reviews registration and calculates credit based on volume of water captured. For all property types: Approximately 3 years later, applicants must renew credits by re-submitting application. For questions, call MC311 at 311 or 240-777-0311, email AskDEP@montgomerycountymd.gov, or create a service request on County website.

structured_extraction.program_name: SBIR/STTR Matching Grant Program (Small Business Innovation Research and Small Business Technology Transfer Matching Grant Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: Montgomery County offers matching grants to help small businesses conducting research in biotechnology, medicine, or life sciences advance their technologies toward commercialization. The program provides non-dilutive funding to companies that have received federal SBIR or STTR awards. The program includes three phases: Phase 0 to help companies obtain technical assistance before applying for their first SBIR/STTR award (up to $5,000 reimbursement); Phase 1 for companies that have received their first or second Phase 1 federal award (up to $25,000 match); and Phase 2 for companies that have received multiple Phase 1 awards and up to one prior Phase 2 award (up to $50,000 match). At least 51% of research and development must be conducted in Montgomery County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Phase 0 grants provide up to $5,000 reimbursement of qualified reimbursable expenses (technical assistance costs) associated with applying for a first SBIR/STTR award. The Phase 1 application must be submitted to the relevant Federal department or agency for Phase 0 applicants to be reimbursed, with a limit of two Phase 0 grants per company to pursue Phase 1 awards. Phase 1 grants provide 25% matching funds up to a maximum of $25,000 for companies that have received a federal SBIR/STTR Phase 1 award. Phase 2 grants provide 25% matching funds up to a maximum of $50,000 for companies that have received a federal SBIR/STTR Phase 2 award. For both Phase 1 and Phase 2 grants, up to 50% of the matching grant amount may be used for reimbursement of business expenditures attributable to technical assistance, investment assistance, or commercialization assistance expenses; the remaining funds may be used for other business research-related expenses. All matching grant funds must be used for purposes related to the company's SBIR or STTR grant. Applicants cannot use matching grant funds for expenditures reimbursed by other federal, state, or county funding sources. All Phase 0 and Phase 1 or Phase 2 matching grants awarded are subject to annual appropriation and availability of funds for the Program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, first-come-first-served basis with two application periods per calendar year: February 15 and August 11 (applications begin at 9:00 a.m. EST)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with a maximum of 20 employees conducting research in biotechnology, medicine, or life sciences in Montgomery County that have applied for or received federal SBIR or STTR Phase 1 or Phase 2 awards (or are preparing to apply for their first Phase 1 award in the case of Phase 0).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Phase 0: reimbursement of qualified reimbursable expenses (technical assistance costs) for writing SBIR/STTR Phase 1 applications. Phase 1 and Phase 2: up to 50% of matching grant for reimbursement of technical assistance, investment assistance, or commercialization assistance expenses; remaining 50% for other business research-related expenses related to advancing the technology toward commercialization. Funds must be used for purposes related to the company's SBIR or STTR grant and cannot be used for expenditures reimbursed by other federal, state, or county funding sources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Company must conduct at least 51 percent of research and development operations in Montgomery County, Maryland. This requirement must be maintained for a minimum of two years from the date of disbursement of the County's conditional matching grant.
requirements_list: Must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Must have a maximum of 20 employees at the time of application

Phase 0: Business must have retained technical assistance after December 27, 2022, submitted a SBIR/STTR Phase 1 proposal, been in operation for 5 years or less, received no prior SBIR/STTR awards (0), and have qualified reimbursable technical assistance expenses

Phase 1: Business must have been awarded an SBIR/STTR Phase 1 grant in the current fiscal year (as of July 1, 2022), been in operation for 5 years or less, and received a maximum of 2 Phase 1 and zero Phase 2 awards in prior years

Phase 2: Business must have been awarded an SBIR/STTR Phase 2 grant in the current fiscal year (as of July 1, 2022), been in operation for 7 years or less, and received a maximum of 4 Phase 1 and 1 Phase 2 award in prior years
Research must be in medicine, biotechnology, or life sciences
At least 51% of research and development must be conducted in Montgomery County
Company must have been awarded an SBIR or STTR Phase 1 or Phase 2 federal grant (for Phase 1 and Phase 2 applicants)
Awardees must use the County's matching grant for purposes related to their SBIR or STTR grant
Awardees must continue to conduct at least 51% of research and development operations within Montgomery County for a minimum of two years from the date of disbursement

Awardees must submit an annual report to the County certified by an officer or director, including: expenditures of County matching grant funds, proof of occupancy in Montgomery County (lease payment or property tax bill), copy of progress reports required by the SBIR/STTR grantor, and high-level summary of company information (leadership team, contact information, employee count, funding received, research focus and progress)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses apply through an online portal on the Montgomery County Business Center website (www.MontgomeryCountyMD.gov) on a first-come, first-served basis. Applications are accepted during two application periods per calendar year beginning February 15 at 9:00 a.m. EST and August 11 at 9:00 a.m. EST. Applications must be complete and submitted online; they are automatically date and time stamped in order of submission. Phase 0 applicants must submit documentation of retained technical assistance after December 27, 2022, evidence of SBIR/STTR Phase 1 proposal submission, and documentation of related qualified reimbursable expenses. Phase 1 and Phase 2 applicants must submit their matching grant applications after receiving notification of their federal SBIR/STTR Phase 1 or Phase 2 award in the current fiscal year (as of July 1, 2022), along with documentation of expenses for eligible technical, investment, or commercialization assistance and a proposed budget for how they plan to use the County's conditional grant funds. Award recipients will be sent a formal letter offering County funds as a conditional grant with specified performance conditions that must be satisfied to convert the conditional grant to a permanent grant. Program funds are allocated as follows per application period: 20% for Phase 0 grants, 40% for Phase 1 grants, and 40% for Phase 2 grants; however, funds may be reallocated among phases based on applicant demand and the Director's discretion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A property tax credit against real property tax for the portion of property leased, occupied, and used by a religious group or organization exclusively for public religious worship, educational purposes, or office space necessary to support or maintain public religious worship or educational purposes. The religious group or organization must qualify for property tax exemption and hold verifiable tax-exempt nonprofit status from the IRS. Available in Montgomery County and Prince George's County, Maryland, with each county having its own application process and deadlines.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit against county real property tax for the portion of commercial-zone real property leased, occupied, and used exclusively by a qualifying religious group or organization for public religious worship, educational purposes, or office space necessary to support these purposes. The property owner is contractually obligated to reduce the amount of taxes for which the religious group is otherwise contractually liable by the amount of the tax credit. In Montgomery County, the credit is claimed through the Division of Treasury. In Prince George's County, the credit is claimed with the Supervisor of Assessments and Taxation. Credits are available on an annual basis; the property owner and tenant must reapply each tax year the property qualifies and the lease remains in effect.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduces property tax liability for the portion of leased real property used exclusively by religious organizations for worship, education, or necessary office space supporting these purposes.

Prince George's County: Application must be submitted to the Supervisor of Assessments and Taxation no later than September 1 of the tax year for which the credit is being requested. Upon termination of the lease or cessation of possession by the tenant, the owner must notify the Supervisor of Assessments and Taxation (or equivalent authority in Montgomery County) within 30 days. structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive federal grant program administered by FEMA that provides funding to states, local communities, federally recognized tribes, territories, and individual homeowners for projects that reduce or eliminate the risk of repetitive flood damage to buildings insured by the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP). In Maryland, MDEM (Maryland Department of Emergency Management) administers the program at the state level. In Montgomery County, the Office of Emergency Management and Homeland Security (OEMHS) coordinates sub-applications on behalf of local governments and agencies. In St. Mary's County, the Department of Emergency Services applies on behalf of interested homeowners to receive funding from FEMA through MDEM.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal competitive grant covering up to 75% of eligible project costs for structures with repetitive loss (RL) properties, up to 90% for structures with severe repetitive loss (SRL) properties, and up to 100% for severe repetitive loss properties. Eligible activities include property acquisition and demolition, structure elevation, mitigation reconstruction, floodproofing of historic residential structures, localized and non-localized flood risk reduction, structural and non-structural retrofitting, infrastructure retrofit, and other cost-effective hazard mitigation measures. Sub-applicants and homeowners must provide the remaining cost share (minimum 25% for standard projects) through non-federal sources; federal funds may not be used for this cost share. For homeowners, the non-federal cost share must be placed in an escrow account upon project approval. FEMA selects recipients based on project ranking, project eligibility, cost-effectiveness (calculated using benefit-cost analysis), and consistency with applicable County Hazard Mitigation Plans. The application is offered annually with specific due dates communicated each year based on fund availability from FEMA via Notices of Funding Opportunities (NOFO). FMA tends to prioritize repetitive loss (RL) and severe repetitive loss (SRL) projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual; specific due dates communicated each year based on fund availability from FEMA via Notices of Funding Opportunities (NOFO). Montgomery County Notice of Interest (NOI) submissions typically begin in August.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ehsan Bahador (Montgomery County); St. Mary's County Emergency Management staff
structured_extraction.program_audience: States, local governments, tribal governments, state and tribal agencies, and individual homeowners with buildings or homes insured by the National Flood Insurance Program that are at high risk for or have experienced repetitive flood damage. Communities must be registered in the NFIP and in good standing with the program. In Montgomery County, eligible sub-applicants are local or tribal governments or agencies. In St. Mary's County, eligible applicants are homeowners located within a flood zone.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that reduce or eliminate the risk of repetitive flood damage to NFIP-insured buildings and homes through cost-effective mitigation measures aligned with the applicable County Hazard Mitigation Plan. Eligible activities include: property acquisition and demolition, structure elevation, mitigation reconstruction, floodproofing of historic residential structures, generator/emergency power backup, localized and non-localized flood risk reduction, structural retrofitting, non-structural retrofitting, wind retrofit, infrastructure retrofit, soil stabilization, and other approved mitigation activities that address flood hazards and reduce community disaster risk.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Montgomery County and St. Mary's County, Maryland. Homes and buildings must be located within a flood zone (Special Flood Hazard Area preferred), actively insured through the NFIP, and the community must be in good standing with the National Flood Insurance Program.
requirements_list: Community must be registered with the NFIP (National Flood Insurance Program)
Community must be in good standing with the NFIP
Property must have an active NFIP policy
Home or building must be located within a flood zone
Property must have experienced repetitive flood damage or be at high risk for flood damage
Sub-applicant must be a local government, tribal government, state agency, or tribal agency (Montgomery County)
Sub-applicant is responsible for providing non-federal cost share (minimum 25% for standard projects; lower percentages may apply for RL or SRL properties)
Sub-applicant/homeowner must not use federal funds for the non-federal cost share
Homeowner must be willing and able to commit to providing their cost share in an escrow account upon project approval (St. Mary's County)
Project must be aligned with County Hazard Mitigation Plan
Project must be cost-effective with a benefit-cost ratio greater than 1.0
Project must address repetitive flood damage to National Flood Insurance Program insured buildings
Elevation Certificate required
Copy of NFIP Declaration required
Documentation of previous losses due to flooding (if applicable)
FEMA-approved Hazard Mitigation Plan required for the benefitting entity
Environmental and historic preservation review and documentation
Compliance with federal flood risk management standards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Montgomery County Process: Applicants submit a Notice of Interest (NOI) to OEMHS, typically beginning in August. The NOI form requests information about the sub-applicant, project location, activity type, mitigation plan compliance, cost estimates, funding sources, and project partnerships. OEMHS reviews NOIs for basic applicability and alignment with HMA program requirements. Upon State recommendation and approval, OEMHS provides technical assistance to develop complete sub-applications and submits recommended sub-applications to FEMA through MDEM. A Project Scoping Subapplication including scope of work, schedule, budget, cost-effectiveness documentation, and environmental review is required. MDEM disburses grant awards to awarded sub-applicants. St. Mary's County Process: Homeowners contact Emergency Management staff at EMA@stmaryscountymd.gov with all required documents (Elevation Certificate, NFIP Declaration, documentation of previous losses) and state interest in applying for FMA grant funding. Staff will assess eligibility, connect with applicants regarding the next available application cycle, work with applicants to obtain project proposals and additional documentation, and submit the application on the applicant's behalf. The process may take several months; approval may take approximately one year, and funding release may take an additional year after approval. All applicants must demonstrate that projects are included in an approved local hazard mitigation plan and provide documentation of cost-effectiveness through benefit-cost analysis or pre-calculated benefits.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides tax-exempt bond financing and generates 4% Federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits for multifamily rental housing projects. Supports new construction, adaptive reuse of non-residential buildings, and preservation of existing housing units for low-to-moderate income individuals, families, and seniors.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_prioritized_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bond financing paired with 4% Federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC). HAPGC finances projects rated AA or higher by major rating agencies (Standard & Poor's, Moody's) with credit enhancement, or unrated transactions privately placed with major institutional investors. Financing terms include: Loan-to-Value ratios acceptable to credit enhancement providers; Debt Service Coverage of generally 1.15x; Reserve requirements including Debt Service Reserve (3-6 months), Operating/Lease-Up Reserve (3-6 months), and Reserve for Replacement. Secondary financing (soft debt) may be permitted with HAPGC approval. HAPGC Fees: $5,000 non-refundable application fee; 15 basis points (.15%) Inducement Resolution fee (credited toward financing fee); 25 basis points (.25%) Commitment fee (credited toward financing fee); 100 basis points (1%) financing fee at closing; annual servicing fee of 25 basis points (.25%) of original bond amount. Borrower responsible for Bond Counsel, Bond Underwriting, Trustee, Rating Agency, and other third-party fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Private for-profit and not-for-profit developers and owners developing multifamily rental housing projects for low-to-moderate income individuals, families, and seniors in Prince George's County. Rental housing developments must include at least 20% of apartments leased to residents earning no more than 50% of AMI or 40% of units leased to residents earning no more than 60% of AMI with rents not exceeding 30% of tenants' adjusted gross income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and permanent financing for new construction, substantial rehabilitation, and adaptive reuse of non-residential buildings for multifamily rental housing. Financing supports development of higher density, multifamily housing in transit-oriented, mixed-use communities and projects in Inner Beltway Communities, Regional Transit Districts, Opportunity Zones, and Designated Development Areas.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, including urban, suburban, and rural areas. Priority given to projects located in: Inner Beltway Communities (incorporated and unincorporated areas between the District of Columbia and Interstate 495); Regional Transit Districts (areas around Metro stops at Largo Town Center, New Carrollton, Prince George's Plaza, Branch Avenue, and Suitland); Opportunity Zones (projects in census tracts designated as Opportunity Zones); Designated Development Areas (areas designated by the County for future development); and projects that preserve existing affordable housing.

Either new construction or substantial rehabilitation

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit complete application package including Form 202, Form 203, resumes, financial documents, site information, environmental reports, and $5,000 non-refundable application fee. 2. HAPGC Credit Underwriting team reviews and underwrites application to determine project feasibility, creditworthiness, and desirability. 3. Underwriting team submits Credit Memo to HAPGC Credit Committee with recommendations. 4. Credit Committee reviews and approves (or declines) financing request and submits recommendations to Development and Finance Sub-Committee of HAPGC Board. 5. Sub-Committee approves financing request and directs staff to prepare Inducement Resolution (allows recouping of certain development costs at closing but is not a financing commitment). 6. HAPGC Board of Commissioners approves Inducement Resolution; borrower pays 15 basis points (.15%) Inducement Resolution fee. 7. HAPGC prepares Resolution for Prince George's County Council approval; County Council authorizes financing and evidences local support. 8. TEFRA public hearing held (required by IRS Code Section 103). 9. Upon Inducement Resolution approval, HAPGC staff works with Sponsor and development team to fulfill bond issuance requirements; borrower pays 25 basis points (.25%) Commitment fee upon execution of Commitment Letter. 10. Loan Commitment phase: review and approval of updated proforma, appraisal, credit reports, environmental reports, title/survey, management plan, and construction plans/specifications. 11. Executive Director issues Commitment Letter describing financing nature, requirements, and any credit enhancement. 12. Bond Closing: For public offering, Official Statement prepared for competitive bid or negotiated sale; for private placement, Private Placement Memorandum prepared. 13. Mortgage Loan Closing: Executed with Sponsor, credit enhancement provider, tax credit purchaser; borrower pays 100 basis points (1%) financing fee. 14. Execute Regulatory Agreement and Land Use Agreement recorded in land records. 15. Construction monitoring, income certifications, cost certification, and compliance reporting throughout construction and permanent financing term.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Alternative Compliance Program is an elective partnership between Prince George's County and qualified tax-exempt faith-based organizations or other 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations to improve water quality by treating and reducing polluted stormwater runoff. Participating organizations may qualify for a reduction in a portion of their Clean Water Act Fee by agreeing to implement one or more of three available stormwater management options: providing easements for stormwater management installations, participating in outreach and education activities, or implementing green care and good housekeeping practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Organizations may qualify for a reduction in a portion of their Clean Water Act Fee. Option 1 provides a 50% fee reduction for impervious area (subject to triennial maintenance inspections) if the property owner provides a temporary right-of-entry and easement for the County to install stormwater best management practices. Options 2 and 3 each provide a 25% fee reduction if the property owner participates in outreach and education activities or implements green care and good housekeeping practices. An administrative fee of $20.58 per tax account per year still applies and cannot be waived.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Stormwater Management Division, Department of the Environment
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tax-exempt faith-based organizations and other 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The fee reduction applies toward the Clean Water Act Fee on the property. Organizations must use funds or resources to install and maintain stormwater best management practices, participate in education and outreach campaigns, or implement green care and good housekeeping practices on their property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Organization must be a tax-exempt faith-based organization or other 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization
Property owner must agree to one or more of the three program options
Option 1 participants must sign a Maintenance Agreement and continuously maintain installed best management practices, which are subject to triennial inspection by the Department of the Environment

Option 2 participants must engage in education and outreach activities and may host County representatives for annual activities such as rain check rebate programs, recycling events, trash pick-up events, or tree planting

Option 3 participants must use certified landscaping companies for lawn care or commit to good housekeeping practices including at least 3 activities such as water conservation, maintaining healthy vegetation, keeping sites clean, pollution prevention, proper hazardous material disposal, and reducing fertilizer and pesticide use
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Select the option(s) to participate in and complete the application form, then digitally sign and submit it online via PDF to the Department of the Environment at the Stormwater Management Division address. Step 2: Meet with the County's agent to develop an alternative compliance plan and finalize which options are feasible. Step 3: Submit the written alternative compliance plan to the Department of the Environment for review and approval of the fee credit amount.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing free native trees and shrubs for schools to plant and maintain on school grounds in Prince George's County. The program educates students about the value of native trees, empowers them to enhance their community, and provides funds to support planting projects in schoolyards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program is free to participating schools and provides free native trees and shrubs plus funds to support planting projects on school grounds in Prince George's County. DoE provides technical and design assistance with selecting tree planting locations on the school campus, purchasing and arranging delivery of materials and trees, and developing a tree planting plan and post-planting maintenance schedule.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools in Prince George's County interested in planting and maintaining native trees on school grounds
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Planting native trees and shrubs on school grounds, related planting project costs, and maintenance of planted trees for two years after planting
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
requirements_list: Submit an Intent to Apply Form
Schedule a consultation with the Program Coordinator
Submit a Program Application
Develop a tree planting plan for campus
Create a post-planting maintenance plan covering two years after planting
Plant trees during spring or fall only (not summer)
Obtain approval from school principal and facility manager
Project organizer must commit to two-year maintenance plan
Request marking of utility lines by MISS Utility
Complete the PGCPS Request for Building Alterations and Improvements form
Maintenance tasks include watering trees every 7 days during dry periods, weeding and mulching up to two times per year, and pruning
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools must submit an Intent to Apply Form to the Department of the Environment's Sustainable Initiatives Division, Attn: Carole Barth, 1801 McCormick Drive, Suite 500, Largo, Maryland 20774. Upon receipt, the Program Coordinator will contact the school to schedule a required consultation. During the consultation, the coordinator provides information on completing the Program Application, developing a tree planting plan for the campus, and creating a post-planting maintenance plan. The school then submits the Program Application. Project organizers must inform and obtain support of the school principal and facility manager, reach out to teachers and staff to avoid conflicts, involve groups like the school's Green Team, recruit staff or volunteers for planting, and develop a maintenance plan specifying who will care for plants year-round for 2 years after planting.

structured_extraction.program_name: Artificial Intelligence for Small Business with the University of Maryland
structured_extraction.program_description: A hybrid training initiative tailored for small business owners to leverage artificial intelligence for business growth. The program combines an online AI certificate course facilitated by University of Maryland Robert H. Smith School of Business professors with immersive in-person bootcamp sessions. Participants learn AI-driven business models, practical AI tool application, strategic AI implementation, and receive personalized coaching and mentorship from AI experts to enhance profitability and competitiveness. The program is funded through ARPA Grant Funding and accepts a cohort of up to 50 companies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free training program consisting of an online artificial intelligence certificate course facilitated by University of Maryland professors, followed by half-day intensive in-person bootcamp sessions. Boot camp topics include AI for Customer Relationship Management, Operational Efficiency with AI, and Data-Driven Decision Making with AI. Participants receive personalized coaching and industry mentorship throughout the program. Program is funded through ARPA Grant Funding and accepts a total of 50 companies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small established, second-stage businesses and small business owners seeking to harness artificial intelligence to innovate products, streamline operations, enhance customer experience, and grow their businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and mentorship in artificial intelligence integration, including online coursework, bootcamp instruction, personalized coaching, and mentorship. Participants gain hands-on experience with AI tools and platforms for business model adaptation, operational optimization, customer engagement strategies, and investment roadmaps for AI scaling.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
requirements_list: Must be a small established business
Must be in a second-stage of business development
Total of 50 companies will be selected
Applicants are not guaranteed enrollment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through the provided online form. Cohort acceptance notifications are provided on a specified date. Selected participants then complete the online certificate course followed by the in-person bootcamp sessions.

structured_extraction.program_name: BGE Electric Vehicle Charging Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate and incentive program that helps offset the cost of adopting electric vehicles and installing electric vehicle charging stations for residential and multifamily properties in Maryland. The program provides rebates for Level 2 smart chargers and DC fast chargers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residential customers can receive rebates and incentives up to $300 for adopting an electric vehicle and installing a charger. Multifamily property managers, owners, and homeowners associations may be eligible to receive incentives up to $25,000 for installing Level 2 smart chargers or DC fast chargers on their properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residential and multifamily property owners, property managers, and homeowners associations who are BGE customers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of Level 2 smart chargers and DC fast chargers for electric vehicles
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County and Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a BGE customer
Residential or multifamily property
Must install eligible Level 2 smart charger or DC fast charger
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Use the BGE resource page to receive rebates and incentives and receive information on finding and comparing available electric vehicles and charger stations

structured_extraction.program_description: A state program that provides financial assistance to local governments in areas designated for growth due to military base realignment and closure (BRAC 2005). The program helps manage increased residential population in well-defined zones, supports public infrastructure improvements related to military base expansion, and coordinates state resources for businesses and local governments in these zones.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local governments in designated BRAC Zones receive payment of 100% of state real property tax increment on qualified properties and payment equal to 50% of the local jurisdiction's real property tax increment on qualified properties. These funds can be used to pay back bonds, including Tax Increment Financing bonds, issued for infrastructure improvements. Projects can also receive priority consideration for financing assistance from various state agencies. Benefits are available for 10 years from the time the first project in the zone is designated as a qualified property.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Economic Development Corporation - Business Development Specialist
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and businesses located in designated BRAC Zones
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Infrastructure improvements and repayment of bonds, including Tax Increment Financing bonds, issued for infrastructure improvements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated BRAC Zones in Prince George's County, Maryland, in areas designated for growth to accommodate military base expansion
requirements_list: Property must be located in a designated BRAC Zone
Property must be qualified to receive the tax increment benefits
Infrastructure improvements must be the focus of bond issuance and fund use
Benefits available for 10 years from the time the first project in the zone is designated as a qualified property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist for application details and to determine eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: A community-based initiative that helps youth in Prince George's County who are referred by the Department of Juvenile Services. structured_extraction.program_name: Business English Essentials: Communicate To Elevate
structured_extraction.program_description: A 7-week workshop series designed for non-native English-speaking entrepreneurs to strengthen their business communication skills and grow their business. The program focuses on real business vocabulary, professional communication, and confidence-building through live interactive lessons and networking opportunities with business coaches and peers. The program concludes with a Business Speed Coaching Event featuring one-on-one expert sessions with industry leaders. It is offered as part of Prince George's County's Latino Business Services and Grow Prince George's Training Programs initiatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A free 7-week intensive workshop series covering key English terminology used in business, professional communication skills, and confidence-building through live interactive lessons. Participants build confidence in speaking with customers, lenders, and partners, gain networking opportunities with business coaches and peers, and conclude with a Business Speed Coaching Event featuring one-on-one expert sessions with industry leaders. The program does not distribute funds directly to participants; assistance is delivered as training and coaching services. Participants must complete an application providing personal information, business details, demographic information for reporting purposes, and ownership details including UEI number registration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-native English-speaking entrepreneurs and business owners in Prince George's County who are ready to strengthen their communication skills and grow their business.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants gain training in business English terminology, professional communication skills, confidence-building, and networking opportunities with business coaches and peers. The program does not distribute funds directly to participants; assistance is delivered as training and coaching services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a non-native English speaker
Must be an entrepreneur or business owner
Must be interested in improving business communication skills
Must provide full name, cell phone number, and email address
Must provide business address (street, city, state, zipcode)
Must provide demographic information including disability status, age (55+), household composition, and income level

The application requires participant information (name, contact details, business address), personal details for reporting purposes (disability status, age, household type, income level, race/ethnicity), ownership information (UEI number, job creation plans, employee background), and position title. Selected participants are notified February 5–6, 2026, and the program commences February 11, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to Prince George's County-based hotels, motels, private RV parks, and bed & breakfasts to support long-term sustainability and resiliency for business operations affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. Grants help cover COVID-19 safety measures, payroll, supplies, rent, fixed debt payments, and other critical operating costs for properties that experienced at least 25% financial losses due to the pandemic.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $190,339.98 per property. Each property receives $951.70 per room (not to exceed $95,169.99) plus a pro-rata share of remaining funds. Maximum grant per property is $190,339.98.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit hotels, motels, private RV parks, and bed & breakfasts in Prince George's County that have been financially affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personal protection equipment (PPE), payroll, supplies, rent, fixed debt payments, and other business-critical cash operating costs related to COVID-19 impacts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be physically located in Prince George's County and must be open for business to the public for accommodations no later than March 31, 2021.
requirements_list: Applicant must be physically located in Prince George's County
Business must be a hotel, motel, private RV park, or bed & breakfast
Must be financially sound and debt-free with the State of Maryland (not under bankruptcy or litigation)
Must not be delinquent on any taxes, fees, or other charges owed to Prince George's County
Must have incurred financial losses of at least 25% directly or indirectly caused by the COVID-19 pandemic
Must be a for-profit entity (corporations, partnerships, cooperatives, or sole proprietors eligible)
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Must be open for business to the public for accommodations no later than March 31, 2021
Primary function of business must be providing overnight accommodations
Must confirm business status is 'Active' and in 'Good Standing' with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an online application through the application portal by selecting 'New Application'. Retain your application number for future reference. You can save and continue your application using your application ID number if unable to complete in one session. Attach all required documentation items (completed form, evidence of good standing, voided check, articles of incorporation/organization/formation, and W-9) within the application portal. Before submitting, confirm that your business is 'Active' and in 'Good Standing' by using SDAT's free search tool at businessexpress.maryland.gov. If your business is not in good standing, follow the Good Standing Checklist provided to resolve any issues, which may include filing Annual Reports, paying penalties, ensuring an active Resident Agent, resolving any holds from state agencies, or obtaining necessary clearance letters and tax certificates. Submit your completed application. Once submitted, no changes or additional documents can be added. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Recipients will be notified via email of grant awards.

Eligible residents purchase coupon books that can be used to pay for rides with participating cab companies when Metrobus, Metrorail, and Call-A-Bus are not available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible seniors and persons with disabilities may purchase up to fourteen $20 coupon books in a six-month period at $10 per book. Each $20 coupon book is sold for $10, providing a 50 percent discount. Residents mail a completed application form with a check or money order for $10 per coupon book to the Office of Transportation along with proof of age and/or disability.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase coupon books to pay for taxi rides with participating cab companies
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County only
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County resident
Must be age 60 or older, or a person with a disability
Must provide proof of age and/or disability, such as a driver's license, Metro Senior or Metro Disability Card, or MetroAccess card
May purchase up to fourteen $20 coupon books in a six-month period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply online at the provided URL or use a printable application form. To order coupon books by mail, applicants complete the application form, enclose $10 per $20 coupon book as a check or money order payable to Prince George's County, include proof of age and/or disability, and mail everything to the Office of Transportation at 9400 Peppercorn Place, Suite 320, Largo, MD 20774. For questions, call 301-499-8603 or Maryland Relay 800-735-2258.

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fund (Bay Restoration Funds)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant and disbursement program that provides funds from the State's Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fund to help property owners reduce nitrogen pollution from septic tanks or connect to public sewer systems. The program supports installation of Best Available Technology (BAT) nitrogen-reducing septic tank systems as an alternative to or in place of connecting to the public sewer system. The goal is to improve water quality and restore the health of the Chesapeake Bay ecosystem within the Bay watershed.

Applications are submitted and processed through the Momentum portal (momentumhome.princegeorgescountymd.gov).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners and property owners in Prince George's County with septic systems or wells who want to reduce nitrogen pollution and improve water quality in the Chesapeake Bay watershed
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of Best Available Technology (BAT) nitrogen-reducing septic tank systems or connection to public sewer systems
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must have an onsite septic system or well in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted and processed through the Momentum portal (momentumhome.princegeorgescountymd.gov).
