structured_extraction.program_description: A Prince George's County program that provides support services to help families address health conditions influenced by the home environment. Services include case management for children with elevated blood lead levels, environmental assessments, educational programs about lead exposure prevention, and up to six home visits for children diagnosed with asthma to help manage triggers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides case management support for children with elevated blood lead levels, home environmental assessments to identify lead hazards, educational programs on lead exposure prevention and safe lead paint reduction practices, telephone consultations for guidance on asthma triggers and indoor air quality, and up to six home visits to families with children diagnosed with asthma to help manage the condition. Items for home asthma trigger control may also be provided. Services are provided at no cost to eligible families.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children with elevated blood lead levels and children under 19 with asthma who have Medicaid or are eligible for Medicaid. Primary caregivers of these children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reducing environmental lead hazards and asthma triggers in the home through assessments, consultations, education, and provision of items to control asthma triggers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Child must have an elevated blood lead level confirmed by health testing (for lead component)
Child must be under 19 years old with asthma diagnosis (for asthma component)
Child must have Medicaid or be eligible for Medicaid (for asthma home visits)
Child must have been exposed to lead or living conditions that place them at risk
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For children with elevated blood lead levels, the Health Department receives reports from the state and contacts families directly. For asthma program participation, eligible families should contact the program. If a child tests positive for elevated blood lead, caregivers should call 301-883-7538 for case management assistance.

structured_extraction.program_name: Clean Energy Program - Energy Efficiency Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program administered by Prince George's County that provides supplemental funding to help residential homeowners in designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) offset the costs of energy efficiency improvements and retrofitting measures for their homes. The program provides up to $7,500 in grant funds for energy efficiency measures, including air sealing, insulation, HVAC upgrades, water heater improvements, and renewable energy adoption (solar PV and solar water heater). The program works in combination with Pepco and Washington Gas incentives and EmPOWER Maryland programs (Home Performance with ENERGY STAR and Low Income Energy Efficiency Program) to reduce energy costs and carbon emissions while addressing energy inequality and barriers to access. Solar installation grants of up to $10,000 are also available for rooftop photovoltaic systems. The program uses a holistic approach to energy efficiency and supports both market-rate and low-income residents in designated ERC areas.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $6,250 for natural gas incentives or up to $7,500 maximum (including $5,000 for electric incentives and $2,500 for natural gas incentives). Of the maximum $7,500 grant award, up to $5,000 can be allocated toward electric incentives (Pepco) and up to $2,500 toward natural gas incentives (Washington Gas). Up to 50-60% of the total grant award ($3,750) can be allocated toward air sealing and insulation, excluding ancillary equipment. Energy audit costs are reimbursed as part of the grant; low-income homeowners receive discounted energy audits, while market-rate residents may pay $100 upfront (discounted from $400), which is reimbursed as part of the $6,250-$7,500 grant. Solar installation grants provide up to $10,000 for rooftop solar photovoltaic systems with a minimum system size of 2.0 kW, paid upon receipt of invoice after grant prequalification. Funds are available in addition to applicable Pepco and Washington Gas utility incentives. Program operates on a first-come, first-served basis. Note: As of February 2024, the program is no longer funding electric incentives due to funding availability; all-electric homes do not qualify.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Department of the Environment, Sustainable Energy
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential homeowners in Prince George's County who reside within one of the nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) and are customers of Pepco and/or Washington Gas. Eligible property types include single-family homes, townhouses, and individually metered condominiums built before March 23, 2016. Both market-rate and low-income residents are served.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements including air sealing, insulation, HVAC upgrades, water heater improvements, weatherization, and other measures recommended by a home energy assessment. Also covers renewable energy adoption (rooftop solar PV and solar water heaters), professional services to address barriers to efficiency adoption, energy audit costs, and ENERGY STAR certified appliances (for condominiums).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must live within one of nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) in Prince George's County: Bladensburg–East Riverdale, Forestville, Hillcrest Heights–Marlow Heights, Kentland–Palmer Park, Oxon Hill–Glassmanor, Silver Hill, Suitland–Coral Hills, Langley Park, and Woodlawn–West Lanham. Eligibility can be verified using the ERC Address Locator tool at https://bit.ly/3aZStLH.
requirements_list: Must be a Prince George's County resident
Must be a Pepco and/or Washington Gas utility customer
Must provide proof of utility customer status from bills dated within the last 3 months
Must live in a single-family home, townhouse, or condominium that is individually metered
Building must have been built before March 23, 2016
Must reside in one of the nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERC); eligibility verified via the ERC Address Locator
Must apply to the applicable EmPOWER Maryland incentive program (Home Performance with ENERGY STAR for market-rate applicants or Low Income Energy Efficiency Program for income-qualified applicants)
Must receive a comprehensive home energy assessment from a BPI-certified building professional
For gas incentives: energy audit must demonstrate at least 10% energy savings without direct install measures; for combined gas and electric incentives: minimum 15% energy savings required
For electric-only incentives: minimum 10% energy savings required
All contractors must be registered as a vendor with Prince George's County Contract Administration and Procurement Division
If subcontracting, must provide proof of subcontractor license and signed contract between contractor and subcontractor
For solar grants: minimum system size of 2.0 kW; must be a rooftop installation
Health and safety measures must be remedied before energy efficiency work begins
Condominiums are not eligible for home performance and solar grants (only Quick Home Energy Check-up and Appliance Rebate Program available for ENERGY STAR certified appliances)

For LIEEP (Low Income Energy Efficiency Program): household income must be below specified limits based on family size (ranging from $66,250 for 1 person to $126,400 for 8 people, plus $12,850 per additional person)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Confirm eligibility by using the ERC Address Locator tool (https://bit.ly/3aZStLH) to verify residence in a designated Energy Resiliency Community. 2. Select a pre-approved contractor from the program's approved list; contractor must be registered as a Prince George's County vendor. 3. Have a comprehensive home energy audit conducted by a BPI-certified professional, who will provide a prioritized list of recommended measures (PLOM). 4. Homeowner selects measures and signs the contractor's proposal. 5. Apply to the applicable EmPOWER Maryland incentive program (Home Performance with ENERGY STAR for market-rate or Low Income Energy Efficiency Program for low-income applicants). 6. Submit prequalification documents to Department of Environment, Sustainable Energy, including: recent utility bills (within 3 months), home energy assessment report, proof of EmPOWER Maryland application, IRS Form W-9, Affidavit of Income (for income-qualified applicants), and Terms and Conditions Agreement. 7. Prequalification approval issued within 15 business days of complete application receipt. 8. Contractor completes approved work within 90 days of prequalification approval (one-time extension possible, not to exceed 6 months total). 9. Contractor submits final invoice and HPwES Reservation of Funds email and test-out form. 10. Final approval and site visit occur within 10 business days of invoice receipt. 11. Grant funds disbursed upon project completion for efficiency improvements, or upon receipt of invoice for solar grants after prequalification. Office of Finance approves invoices within 30 business days of payment request.

structured_extraction.program_description: Community spaces equipped with resources like backup power, cooling or heating, and food storage to help residents prepare, respond, and recover during climate disruptions and extreme weather events.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and technical support are available for community-based organizations to develop resilience hub projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing resilience hub projects equipped with backup power, cooling or heating, food storage, and information resources
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations can apply for a Resilience Hub grant; specific application procedures are not detailed on this page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Commercial Property Improvement Program (CPIP) provides grant incentives to retail shopping center owners and main street retail space owners in Prince George's County to make exterior and major building systems improvements. The goal is to boost the economic performance of obsolete and underperforming retail centers by enhancing their appearance, marketability, competitiveness, and overall retail experience for county residents. Eligible improvements include exterior facade enhancements, placemaking, lighting, and major building systems upgrades. The program prioritizes retail centers located in strong trade areas with high visibility.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from a minimum of $50,000 to a maximum of $350,000, covering up to 50% of approved construction costs. Applicants must provide a matching 50% contribution. The minimum grant of $50,000 corresponds to $100,000 in total project costs, and the maximum grant of $350,000 corresponds to $700,000 or more in total project costs. Reimbursement occurs as costs are incurred and documented for construction. Architectural design and permit costs are reimbursed only after construction is completed. Construction must begin within 90 days of grant approval and be completed within 180 days of approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Retail shopping center owners, retail center owners, and main street retail space owners in Prince George's County, particularly those with obsolete or underperforming retail centers in strong trade areas with high visibility.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Exterior facade enhancements, placemaking, lighting, major building systems improvements, and other exterior improvements for retail centers and main street storefronts. Architectural design and permit costs are also eligible for reimbursement after construction completion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Priority given to retail centers and spaces located in strong trade areas with high visibility.
requirements_list: Applicants must provide a 50% matching contribution for the total project cost
Minimum grant is $50,000 for $100,000 in total project costs
Maximum grant is $350,000 for $700,000 or more in total project costs
Commercial space must be retail use; places of worship and non-retail uses are not eligible
Shopping center owners who received CPIP funding in 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, or 2023 are not eligible
Construction must begin within 90 days after grant approval
Construction must be completed within 180 days after grant approval

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program administered by Prince George's County that helps local jurisdictions implement community development initiatives focused on providing decent housing, creating suitable living environments, and expanding economic opportunities for low- and moderate-income persons. The program develops viable urban communities by supporting affordable housing, neighborhood enhancement, public services, and community infrastructure improvements.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development awards annual grants to Prince George's County, which competitively offers grants to municipalities and non-profit organizations. Funds support community facilities and infrastructure development, affordable housing acquisition or preservation, neighborhood enhancement, and public services targeted at low- and moderate-income communities. Eligible uses include housing acquisition and rehabilitation, demolition, direct assistance to micro and small for-profit businesses to create or retain jobs, street improvements and sidewalks, health facilities, job development, youth services, senior programs, health services, public facilities and infrastructure improvements, and public services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not currently accepting applications for Program Year 52 (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027). Proposal application packets typically available in October.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipalities, local government agencies, and non-profit organizations in Prince George's County seeking to develop viable urban communities and improve conditions for low- and moderate-income residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable housing acquisition and rehabilitation, demolition, direct assistance to micro and small for-profit businesses to create or retain jobs, street improvements and sidewalks, health facilities, job development, youth services, senior programs, health services, public facilities and infrastructure improvements, and public services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Applicant agencies should ideally be located in Prince George's County.

Individual persons are not eligible

At least 51% of persons or households receiving the service must be low- and moderate-income, OR project beneficiaries must live in a low- and moderate-income area (census tract or block group) as determined by HUD, OR the project addresses a slum or blighted condition or meets an urgent need
Project must support community development
Focus on housing, living environment, or economic development
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Proposal application packets are available in October. A Proposal Advisory Group reviews proposals. The County Executive makes recommendations to the County Council. The County Council holds public hearings in April and adopts the Annual Action Plan by early May. The County submits the adopted Annual Action Plan to HUD by May of each year. Projects are implemented beginning July 1.

structured_extraction.program_description: A volunteer training program that teaches citizens basic disaster preparedness, emergency response, and rescue skills to help their communities survive and recover from disasters and emergencies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides 22 hours of basic training covering disaster preparedness, fire safety and utility control, disaster medical operations, light search and rescue operations, disaster psychology, CERT organization, and terrorism awareness. Advanced training is also available in areas including National Incident Management Systems, emergency shelter management, CPR/AED, crowd control, amateur radio, animal rescue assistance, and equipment operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual citizens and volunteers of all ages (both adults and teens) who want to prepare themselves and their communities to respond to disasters and emergencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in emergency response skills including disaster preparedness, fire safety, medical operations, search and rescue, and other emergency management competencies.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals interested in CERT training must complete the CERT Interest Form available at the program website or through the provided link. Submissions are reviewed on a rolling basis, and applicants will be contacted with information about upcoming training sessions.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Impact Grant Program, administered by the Redevelopment Authority of Prince George's County, provides small capital grants to civic and neighborhood associations and community-based organizations to help implement innovative projects within Prince George's County. Eligible projects must focus on neighborhood beautification or environment and natural resources sustainability. Grants support capital expenses such as equipment and materials purchases, but cannot be used for operations, program costs, salaries, or personnel. The program aims to strengthen communities and build organizational capacity in priority areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Redevelopment Authority of Prince George's County awards capital grants up to $50,000 per organization. A total of $250,000 is available per fiscal year, with $100,000 designated for projects in National Capital Strategic Economic Development Areas (sustainable communities' boundaries inside the Beltway as approved by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development) and $150,000 for county-wide projects. Grants must be used for capital purposes only, including purchase of equipment and materials for community-based projects in two eligible categories: (1) Neighborhood Beautification (streetscaping, street furniture, pedestrian enhancements, recreational improvements, signage, banners, wayfinding systems, commercial façade improvements, internal and external improvements to commercial buildings used by the public, permanent public art installations) or (2) Environment and Natural Resources and Sustainability (park and stream restoration, urban agriculture, tree canopy replenishment, green roofs, low impact development, stormwater management, preservation of historic landmarks, structures and sites). Grants are disbursed on a reimbursable basis with a one-year performance period from the date of execution of the CIG Grant Agreement. Funds cannot be used for operating costs, program costs, salaries, stipends, or personnel expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Civic and neighborhood associations, community-based organizations, homeowners associations (HOAs), and houses of worship incorporated as 501(c)(3) nonprofits located within Prince George's County and in good standing with the State of Maryland. Prince George's County government and affiliated entities are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital expenses only, including purchase of equipment and materials for neighborhood beautification projects (streetscaping, street furniture, pedestrian enhancements, recreational improvements, signage, banners, wayfinding systems, commercial façade improvements, internal and external improvements to commercial buildings used by the public, permanent public art installations) or environment and natural resources sustainability projects (restoration of parks, streams and open space, urban agriculture, tree canopy replenishment, green roofs, low impact development, stormwater management, preservation of historic landmarks, structures and sites). Funds cannot be used for operations, program costs, salaries, stipends, or personnel.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants and projects must be located within Prince George's County, Maryland. Organizations located in municipalities must have their projects located within the municipality boundaries. Projects may be eligible for priority funding if located within National Capital Strategic Economic Development Areas (sustainable communities' boundaries inside the Beltway as approved by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development).

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit one original and three copies of the Community Impact Grant Program Application (Exhibit A) along with all required supporting documentation by mail or hand delivery. Applications must be postmarked by or received by May 18, 2026, by 5:00 PM EST. Email applications are not accepted. Mail to: Andrea Anderson, Redevelopment Authority, 9200 Basil Court, Suite 504, Largo, MD 20774. A Proposal Analysis Group (PAG) will evaluate all completed applications received by the deadline in accordance with established criteria including: physical impact and enhancement of community (30 points), applicant's track record of completed grant projects (20 points), demonstrated community and municipal support (20 points), readiness and likelihood of project implementation (20 points), leverage of additional funds and in-kind contributions (10 points), and economic inclusion through subcontracting with eligible Prince George's County-based small businesses, county-based businesses, county-located businesses, and minority business enterprises (10 points preference). Minimum 75 points required to qualify; maximum 110 points possible. Applications will be evaluated for completeness; incomplete applications or those submitted after deadline will not be accepted. Redevelopment Authority staff will conduct site visits if needed and may request additional information. Applicants recommended for approval may be required to make formal project presentations. RDA will provide award recommendations to Office of County Executive for final approval. Upon approval, applicants will enter into a CIG Grant Agreement. Questions should be submitted via email to Andrea Anderson by May 8, 2026, by 5:00 PM EST. Responses to questions will be posted on the RDA website. Pre-application meeting held April 21, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A discretionary grant program offered by the Office of the County Executive to qualified nonprofit organizations in Prince George's County. Grants fund eligible non-profit organizations that provide services or activities in Prince George's County, supporting projects aligned with County strategic priorities and serving underserved populations across diverse geographic areas. Awards are evaluated based on criteria including value added to the identified community, overall program costs, organizational stability, adequacy of other funding sources, organization mission and goals, statement of need, project description, sustainability relative to amount requested, evidence of partnerships, and investment in communities served.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Discretionary grants up to $100,000 per award (FY 2026). Previous awards have ranged from $1,000 to $125,000. Total award amount is disbursed in one payment via electronic deposit (ACH preferred). Award funding depends on factors including community value added, program costs, organizational stability, existing funding sources, organization mission and goals, statement of need, project description, sustainability relative to amount requested, evidence of partnerships, and investment in communities served. All award recipients must submit a final financial expenditure report and final programmatic summary report upon completion of the grant period.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application and required supporting documentation to the Office of Management and Budget. Only complete proposals are forwarded to the Executive Review Panel for review and funding consideration. Executive Review Panel convenes to review proposals and make award recommendations. structured_extraction.program_name: County Right of First Refusal Program: Multifamily Rental Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: The County Right of First Refusal Program expands the availability of affordable rental housing by giving Prince George's County the first opportunity to purchase multifamily rental properties with 20 or more dwelling units before they are sold to other buyers. The program preserves naturally affordable housing and expands housing options for low- to moderate-income households. The County may exercise its right to purchase such properties directly or assign its purchase rights to a third party (a ROFR Developer). The program operates under Prince George's County Code Section 13-1110 et seq. and aims to prevent displacement and preserve affordable housing for moderate and low-income households.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County exercises its right of first refusal to purchase multifamily rental properties consisting of 20 or more dwelling units, or may assign its purchase rights to a third party (ROFR Developer). Property owners must provide written notice to the Director of Housing and Community Development after entering into a bona fide contract of sale. The County then has the opportunity to purchase the property or negotiate an exception agreement before the sale closes. An exception to the County's right of first refusal can only be approved by execution of a Written Agreement between the County and the prospective buyer prior to entering into a bona fide contract of sale. The County also offers the ROFR Preservation Fund, which provides subordinate loans of up to $3,000,000 at 0% interest for acquisition and rehabilitation of properties under the ROFR Program. Loans have terms up to 40 years with no repayment due prior to December 31, 2026. The County may also approve PILOTs (Payment in Lieu of Taxes) to reduce real estate taxes. Properties receiving funding must establish affordability restrictions for a minimum of 30 years, with rent and income restrictions recorded in the Land Records of Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jonathan R. Butler, Director; Ashley P. Johnson-Hare, Deputy Director; Pamela A. Wilson, Chief, Housing Development Division; Karan Stewart
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and prospective buyers of multifamily rental properties with 20 or more units in Prince George's County, as well as real estate developers, non-profit housing organizations, and the Prince George's County government. Eligible participants in the ROFR Developer Roster are pre-qualified entities with interest and capacity to assume the County's acquisition rights.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and preservation of multifamily rental properties as affordable rental housing for low- to moderate-income households. Property owners must notify the County when selling multifamily rental facilities; the County may exercise its right to purchase the property to preserve it as affordable rental housing. ROFR Preservation Fund proceeds must be used for acquisition, rehabilitation, and other typical transaction costs of properties acquired under the ROFR Program. Properties must establish income and rent restrictions on an agreed-upon percentage of units for at least 30 years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program applies to all areas of Prince George's County as of October 6, 2015. For properties located within County municipalities, the approval of the municipality is required prior to purchase of a property under the ROFR Program. For transactions within a municipality, the ROFR Code requires that the municipality be provided with a 180-day period in which to approve or disapprove the County's ROFR actions to purchase a property in the municipality. Properties receiving ROFR Preservation Fund loans whose source of capital includes ARPA funds must be located within the boundaries of a Qualified Census Tract (QCT) in Prince George's County. Properties receiving ROFR Preservation Fund loans whose source of capital is solely Maryland DHCD funds may be located anywhere within Prince George's County.

The County has the right to purchase the property or assign its rights to purchase to a third party within timeframes specified in County Code Section 13-1110 et seq.

An exception to the County's right of first refusal can only be approved by execution of a Written Agreement between the County and the prospective buyer prior to entering into a bona fide contract of sale
For ROFR Preservation Fund loans: Borrower must be approved by the Department as an eligible participant in the ROFR Program

For ROFR Preservation Fund loans: Property must comply with Diversity and Equity Policy for Publicly Subsidized Development Projects if undergoing significant renovation or development

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Property owners seeking to sell a multifamily rental facility with 20 or more units must submit written notice to the Director of Housing and Community Development after entering into a contract of sale. The County evaluates the property and exercises its right of first refusal by issuing an RFP to the ROFR Developer Roster, or negotiates an exception agreement with the prospective buyer. If the County exercises ROFR, it may directly purchase the property or assign its rights to a qualified ROFR Developer. If an exception is requested and approved, a Written Agreement is executed establishing affordability restrictions. For ROFR Preservation Fund loans, the Department conducts underwriting based on the submitted loan application and supporting documentation including due diligence reports from the Senior Lender(s). The Department requires reliance letters for Environmental Report(s), Capital Needs Assessment, and Property Appraisal. Once approved, loan documents (Loan Agreement, Deed of Trust, Promissory Note, Affordability Agreement, Subordination Agreement, and Intercreditor Agreement) are executed. Offers and inquiries should be submitted electronically by email to designated staff members. Contact the Department of Housing and Community Development, New Development and Preservation Division for additional program details and procedures. Phone: 301-883-6511.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Economic Development Incentive (EDI) Fund provides financial assistance to support economic development in Prince George's County through expansion of the commercial tax base, job retention and attraction, support for small and local businesses, promotion of development and redevelopment opportunities, transit-oriented development, and growth of key industry sectors. The $50 million fund stimulates job growth, retains current jobs and businesses, and attracts new businesses to Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The EDI Fund provides $50 million in financial assistance including conditional and conventional loans and grants. Approximately 65% of committed funds revolve back into the fund for future investment. A $1 million set-aside supports small businesses in obtaining lines of credit from traditional banks. Funding is available for land and building acquisitions, building construction and improvement, equipment acquisition, and working capital. Annual appropriations range from $7 million to $11 million per year. Interest rates are set on a case-by-case basis depending on credit and personal history, generally at competitive market rates or slightly lower. An application fee of 1% of the loan amount is required: for loans up to $1,000,000, the upfront fee is $2,500; for loans of $1,000,000 and above, the upfront fee is $5,000 with the balance due at closing. The prime rate for Prince George's County is 4%. The review process takes approximately 90 days.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Download an application from the website, fill out an online application at https://edif.princegeorgescountymd.gov/, or pick one up from the office. Step 2: Complete all required sections and gather necessary prequalification documents including application fee, signed application, personal financial statements, confidentiality agreement, credit report, business plan, and incorporation documents. Step 3: Submit the application by mail, online, or in person at the office. A business development specialist will contact you after review. You can track your application progress online at the EDI Fund portal. If your application meets basic requirements, additional documents including financial statements, cash flow analysis, tax information, and resumes will be required. Applications are reviewed for consistency with statutory goals, and independent review of credit and financial soundness is conducted. The review process takes approximately 90 days. Contact the EDC's Financial Services Program Manager for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Prince George's County program that provides emergency rental assistance to eligible tenants and landlords to prevent eviction and address housing insecurity. The program helps tenants below 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI) who are having difficulty paying rent due to financial hardship arising from the COVID-19 pandemic. Assistance is available both through tenant-initiated applications and landlord-initiated applications on behalf of eligible tenants. Funds are paid directly to landlords to cover current or back rent. Priority is given to households at or below 50% AMI. The program targets rental units in designated Qualified Census Tracts (QCTs) meeting risk factors related to housing stress, social factors, and pandemic effects. The program provides up to 18 months of cumulative rental assistance per household.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct rental assistance payments made to landlords on behalf of eligible tenants to cover current or back rent and prevent eviction. Maximum of 18 months of cumulative assistance per household. Tenants must have household income at or below 80% of Area Median Income (AMI), with priority for households at or below 50% AMI. For applicants at 30% AMI and below, no court documents are required. For applicants between 31%-50% AMI, a court summons is required. For applicants between 51%-80% AMI, a court judgment is required. Households above 50% AMI must have an eviction notice, active Warrant for Possession, court summons, court judgment, Warrant of Restitution, or must be facing eviction due to delinquent rent. All applicants must show financial hardship directly or indirectly due to COVID-19 and must have past due rent or utilities (housing instability requirement). The amount of assistance is determined by the county after application review, subject to available funding. Landlords applying on behalf of tenants must sign a Rental Assistance Agreement and tenants must sign an affidavit accepting the final assistance amount before payment is issued.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tenants in Prince George's County with household income below 80% of Area Median Income who are experiencing difficulty paying rent or facing eviction due to financial hardship caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as landlords or property owners with eligible tenants in Prince George's County rental units who wish to apply on behalf of those tenants.

For landlord applications, properties must be located in Qualified Census Tracts (QCT) as defined by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, meeting risk factors such as housing stress, social factors, and pandemic effects.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, tenants or landlords must call the ERAP Hotline at (301) 883-6504 and press option 9 to receive an access code. The portal is currently closed and access codes are required to complete an application. Applicants access the online portal at erentalassistance.princegeorgescountymd.gov using their access code and submit required documentation including residency verification, income verification (tax forms, W-2, 1099, paystubs, or bank statements for calendar year 2020 and current month; self-certification letter acceptable as last resort), proof of rental status (signed lease or Landlord Attestation), and evidence of financial hardship and housing instability (written attestation, unemployment documentation, past due rent/utility bills, or eviction notices). For landlord applications, landlords must also submit landlord information (name, address, SSN/Tax ID, property deed, W-9 form, EFT/ACH enrollment form) and rent ledger. After submission, DHCD screens applications to determine prioritization. Landlord applications prioritize most vulnerable census tracts. Tenant applications prioritize based on AMI level and court documentation level (judgments and scheduled evictions for 51%-80% AMI; court summons for 31%-50% AMI; no court documents needed for 30% AMI and below). Applications are assigned to reviewers who conduct review and quality control checks. Approved applications receive finance and DHCD approval before being sent to County Finance for payment processing. DHCD contacts applicants by email regarding any discrepancies or missing information. Approved applicants receive a notice of award indicating the dollar value of approved assistance. Landlords must sign a Rental Assistance Agreement and tenants must sign an affidavit, both indicating acceptance of the final assistance amount, before payment is issued to the landlord.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state and local incentive program offering tax credits to encourage the expansion of existing businesses and attraction of new business activity and jobs within designated Enterprise Zone areas in Prince George's County. The program encompasses approximately 8,492 acres and provides benefits for private sector investment, facility renovation and rehabilitation, new business locations, existing business expansions, and new job creation. Enhanced benefits are available in designated Enterprise Zone Focus Areas where economic distress is greater.
structured_extraction.assistance_description:
Two tiers of tax credits are available depending on whether the business is located in a standard Enterprise Zone or an Enterprise Zone Focus Area.

State Income Tax Credits:
- Standard Enterprise Zone: $1,000 one-time credit per new employee, or $6,000 per economically disadvantaged employee spread over 3 years ($3,000 year 1, $2,000 year 2, $1,000 year 3)
- Enterprise Zone Focus Area (enhanced): $1,500 one-time credit per new employee, or $9,000 per economically disadvantaged employee spread over 3 years ($4,500 year 1, $3,000 year 2, $1,500 year 3). Must be employed for at least 12 months to claim the larger Focus Area credit.

Local Real Property Tax Credits:
- Standard Enterprise Zone: 80% of eligible assessment for years 1-5, declining by 10% annually for years 6-10 (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%)
- Enterprise Zone Focus Area (enhanced): 80% of eligible assessment for all 10 years on real property expansion, renovation, or capital improvement

Local Personal Property Tax Credit (Focus Areas only):
- 80% of eligible assessment for all 10 years on new investments in personal property

Accelerated County Permitting Process also available.

Credits may be carried forward for up to five years if insufficient tax liability to use all credits in the year earned. Can be combined with Maryland Job Creation Tax Credit and other state income tax credits without affecting federal income tax credit eligibility.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Must be certified by December 31 to receive property tax credits beginning July 1 of the following year
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses seeking to expand, relocate, or invest within Prince Oeorge's County's designated Enterprise Zone areas, including both standard zones and Focus Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits to offset the cost of state income taxes on new hires, local real property taxes on property improvements and capital investments, and local personal property taxes on new personal property investments within the Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Enterprise Zone areas within Prince Oeorge's County, encompassing approximately 8,492 acres. Enhanced benefits are available in designated Enterprise Zone Focus Areas where economic distress is greater.

Employees must have been hired after the business was located in the Enterprise Zone or after the zone was designated

For economically disadvantaged employee credits, employees must meet economically disadvantaged criteria (family income 70% or less of Bureau of Labor Statistics Lower Living Standard) and receive certification from Maryland Job Service
For personal property tax credit, business must make new investments in personal property (Focus Areas only)
For real property tax credit, business must engage in real property expansion, renovation, or capital improvement
Qualified property must not be used for residential purposes (mixed-use properties must allocate eligible assessment to nonresidential portion)
Qualified property must be used in a trade or business (vacant land generally ineligible unless required for use with building, such as parking)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview:
1. Contact the Prince Oeorge's County Enterprise Zone Administrator at 301-583-4650 to speak with a Business Development Specialist or contact Andre Plummer at applummer@co.pg.md.us
2. Obtain the Enterprise Zone Certification Application from the Economic Development Corporation
3. Complete the application form with business, property, and employment information
4. Submit the application to the Prince Oeorge's County Economic Development Corporation, 1801 McCormick Drive, Suite 350, Largo, MD 20774, attention Andre Plummer, Financial Services Program Manager
5. The Enterprise Zone Administrator reviews the application to determine if the property is located in the Enterprise Zone
6. If eligible, a certification letter is issued allowing the business to take advantage of Enterprise Zone incentives
7. For state income tax credits, submit Maryland Tax Form 500CR with your state income tax return, including Maryland Job Service certification of eligibility for economically disadvantaged employees if applicable
8. For property tax credits, the Enterprise Zone Administrator certifies the property to the Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), which determines the base and eligible assessment values and tracks the eligible assessment for the 10-year period
9. For applications seeking property tax credits effective July 1 of the following year, certification must be completed by December 31 of the preceding calendar year
10. Once new construction, expansion, or rehabilitation is completed, notify the Economic Development Corporation to request SDAT reassessment

structured_extraction.program_description: A public campaign financing program that provides matching funds to candidates for elected office in Prince George's County. The program promotes broader access to elected office and reduces the influence of large donations in local government by enabling candidates to run on the strength of their ideas supported by small donations from ordinary people.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Candidates who meet eligibility requirements and raise qualifying contributions receive matching funds from the Fair Election Fund. Qualifying contributions must be between $1 and $250 per donor during the 4-year election cycle, made by Prince George's County residents, and received after filing Notice of Intent but no later than the general election. The matching formula provides public contributions to certified candidates during the Distribution Period (365 calendar days before the primary election through 15 calendar days after the general election). Maximum public contributions are set based on the elective office. Certified candidates may receive multiple distributions during the election cycle.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 9pm on the last Tuesday in February of the election year (for 2026 election: February 24, 2026)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Prince George's County who are candidates for County Executive, At-Large County Councilmember, or District Councilmember in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Campaign financing for candidates running for County Executive, At-Large County Councilmember, or District Councilmember in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Candidates must be Prince George's County residents to participate.
requirements_list: Candidate must be a Prince George's County resident
Candidate must be running for one of the covered offices: County Executive, At-Large County Councilmember, or District Councilmember
Must register a public financing committee in MDCRIS by 9pm on the last Tuesday in February of the election year
Must file Notice of Intent to Qualify with the State Board of Elections
Must open a citizen funded campaign account with a bank

Must collect minimum qualifying contributions based on office sought: County Executive requires 40 contributions totaling $2,000; At-Large County Councilmember requires 30 contributions totaling $1,500; District Councilmember requires 20 contributions totaling $1,000
All qualifying contributions must be from Prince George's County residents
Individual contributions limited to maximum $250 per donor per 4-year election cycle
Cash contributions limited to maximum $100 per individual per 4-year election cycle
Contributions must be $1 or more to qualify for matching
Cannot accept contributions from organizations, PACs, corporations, labor organizations, or political parties
Cannot accept anonymous contributions
Cannot accept loans except from the candidate or candidate's spouse
Candidate and spouse may contribute/loan up to $6,000 each but these do not qualify for matching or count toward certification requirement
Must submit receipts for all qualifying contributions with contributor name, residential address, date, and signature
Must close or make inactive any other campaign finance accounts during the period seeking public funds
Must file campaign finance reports through MDCRIS
Must file Certificate of Candidacy with the State Board
Must comply with all regulations governing use of Fair Election Fund contributions
Submissions of receipts for matching must be by 11:59 PM on the date of the primary or general election
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register a public financing committee in the Maryland Campaign Reporting Information System (MDCRIS) at https://campaignfinance.maryland.gov by 9pm on the last Tuesday in February of the election year. During registration, provide election type, election year, office type, office sought, jurisdiction, party affiliation, committee name, candidate information, chairperson information, treasurer information, and publicly funded campaign account information. MDCRIS will generate a Notice of Intent and Statement of Organization. 2. File the Notice of Intent to Qualify with the State Board of Elections (generated automatically at MDCRIS registration). 3. Open a citizen funded campaign account with a bank. An Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS is required—file Form SS-4 with the IRS. Banks will accept the processed Statement of Organization as proof of authority. Update the account number in MDCRIS once opened. 4. Collect qualifying contributions from Prince George's County residents. Each contribution must be $1-$250 per donor per election cycle, acknowledged with a receipt containing contributor name, residential address, date, and contributor signature or approved digital signature. Receipts must be maintained and submitted to the State Board. 5. Submit all required documents to the State Board through MDCRIS for certification, including: receipts for required number of qualifying contributions and aggregate dollar amount, a signed declaration agreeing to follow Fair Election Fund regulations, a campaign finance report listing each qualifying contribution and expenditure with receipts, and a Certificate of Candidacy. 6. The State Board will certify the candidate within 10 business days of receiving complete documentation. An applicant may submit one application; if denied, one updated resubmission is allowed before the end of the Qualifying Period. 7. Once certified, the Prince George's County Office of Finance will disburse public contributions during the Distribution Period (365 calendar days before primary election through 15 calendar days after general election). 8. Submit contribution receipts for matching by 11:59 PM on the date of the primary or general election. For questions, contact the State Board of Elections.

structured_extraction.program_name: HIV/AIDS Program (HAP) / Ryan White Comprehensive AIDS Resources Emergency (CARE) Act
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive federal and county program that provides high quality HIV/AIDS healthcare and support services to medically under-served individuals and families affected by HIV/AIDS. It functions as a payer of last resort, funding treatment when no other resources are available. Services include medical care, case management, dental care, nutrition counseling, substance abuse counseling, mental health services, emergency financial assistance, health insurance premium assistance, and referrals for housing and utility assistance. Free HIV counseling and testing services are also available to the general public, along with a PrEP program for those who are HIV-negative.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HIV-positive clients receive low-cost and free medical services based on their financial status, including comprehensive health assessments, medical treatment plans, specialized clinic care, case management with emergency financial assistance, transportation assistance to appointments, medication assistance, dental services, nutrition counseling, substance abuse counseling, and mental health services. Additional support services include early intervention services, health insurance premium and cost sharing assistance, medical nutrition therapy, outpatient ambulatory services, and outreach services. HIV testing services are free to the public. Services are available to uninsured and under-insured eligible residents, with the program functioning as a payer of last resort when no other resources are available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Maryland living in Prince George's, Montgomery, Charles, Calvert, or Frederick County who are HIV positive and uninsured or underinsured. Full comprehensive services are available for Prince George's County residents. Individuals living outside Prince George's County may access limited services including dental, outpatient ambulatory services, and mental health and substance abuse services. Free HIV counseling and testing services are available to the general public. Those without HIV can access the PrEP program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Medical care and treatment for HIV and AIDS, including physician and nurse services, diagnostic testing, medications, dental services, nutrition guidance, counseling for substance abuse and mental health, emergency financial assistance, health insurance premium and cost-sharing assistance, transportation to medical appointments, early intervention services, outpatient ambulatory services, outreach services, case management coordination, and referrals for housing and utility assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Full comprehensive services are available to residents of Prince George's, Montgomery, Charles, Calvert, and Frederick County in Maryland. Individuals living outside Prince George's County may access limited services including dental, outpatient ambulatory services, and mental health and substance abuse services.

Must meet income guidelines

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals can contact the program by phone at 301-583-3150 or (301)883-7879 to schedule an appointment or obtain more information about eligibility. structured_extraction.program_description: A federal entitlement program administered by Prince George's County that provides funds to expand the supply of decent, affordable housing for low and very low-income families. The program supports nonprofit and for-profit developers to produce, construct, and rehabilitate housing, helps first-time homebuyers purchase homes, assists with acquiring or improving group homes for special populations, and supports Community Housing Development Organizations in creating housing opportunities for households of limited income. It also provides gap financing for real estate developers to build affordable multi-family housing developments for families and individuals with income below 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI). Additionally, HOME-ARP funding is available for homeless populations through the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance is provided to eligible projects and beneficiaries in the form of subordinate loans and grants. For multifamily rental projects, HOME financing is available as a subordinate loan with the following terms: (1) HOME Loan Amount: Up to $2,500,000 with exceptions at Director's discretion; (2) Interest Rate: 2% simple interest during permanent loan period, 0% during construction; (3) Term: Generally coterminous with senior loan with 40-year amortization from beginning of permanent loan period; (4) Collateral: Subordinate lien Deed of Trust recorded in Prince George's County land records; (5) Legal Fee: $55,000 due at closing for HOME Loans, $50,000 for HOME-ARP Loans; (6) Annual Payments: Due by April 30 unless alternative date agreed upon; (7) Prepayment: Allowed without penalty if borrower complies with affordability and rental requirements and is not in default. HOME-ARP Loans for homeless populations have similar terms with loan amounts limited to 100% of Total Development Costs plus up to $45,000 per HOME-ARP Assisted Unit for Operating Cost Assistance Reserve. Prince George's County receives approximately $3.5 million annually from HUD appropriation based on formula considering housing supply inadequacy, poverty incidence, fiscal distress, and other factors.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit developers, for-profit developers, real estate developers, first-time homebuyers, Community Housing Development Organizations, and special populations needing group homes in Prince George's County. HOME-ARP funds specifically target homeless populations referred through the County's Continuum of Care Coordinated Entry Policy.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and rehabilitation of affordable housing units, producing and rehabilitating housing, assisting first-time homebuyers to purchase homes, acquiring or improving group homes for special populations, supporting Community Housing Development Organizations in creating housing opportunities for low and very low-income households, providing gap financing for building affordable multi-family housing developments, acquisition costs, professional fees, and project reserves. For HOME-ARP specifically: construction expenses, acquisition costs, professional fees, and operating cost assistance reserves for homeless housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Projects are prioritized if located within one mile of the Blue Line transit Corridor, within one mile of the Purple Line transit Corridor, within one mile of existing and planned Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) Metro Stations throughout the County, in conformance with housing priorities in Prince George's County's 2035 Adopted General Plan, mixed-use mixed-income developments, or with sustainable design and green standards.
requirements_list: Projects must comply with Federal lead-based paint regulations of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1992

Minimum affordability period must be incorporated into each project based on the type of eligible activity (minimum 15 years for rehabilitation, 20 years for new construction, at least 40 years for affordability agreements)
Beneficiaries must be low or very low-income households

For HOME Loans: HOME units must be affordable to households with incomes at or below 60% of Area Median Income (AMI), with at least 20% of all HOME units affordable to households at or below 50% of AMI

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted throughout the fiscal year on a rolling basis on a project-by-project basis. The application and underwriting process includes: (1) Submit application with project plan, market assessment, sources and uses statement, operating pro forma, and development team information; (2) DHCD conducts preliminary underwriting analysis evaluating project budget, financing, development schedule, developer capacity and experience, market demand, and compliance with subsidy layering guidelines; (3) All financial stakeholders must execute legally binding written agreements; (4) DHCD reviews and approves Diversity and Equity Plan and Section 3 Plan; (5) Project undergoes initial closing or construction start underwriting review; (6) DHCD executes written agreements including Commitment and Program Agreement, Regulatory Agreement, Declaration of Covenants, Deed of Trust, Deed of Trust Note, Building Loan Agreement, and PILOT Agreement as applicable; (7) Financial assistance amounts are determined individually for each project throughout the fiscal year based on underwriting analysis; (8) Borrower must submit annual documentation to demonstrate compliance with affordability requirements and financing reporting. Contact the New Development and Preservation Division at 301-883-5540 or KAStewart@co.pg.md.us for application procedures and guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_name: High Technology Facilities Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A real property tax credit that encourages growth and development of existing and new high-technology facilities in Prince George's County. The credit applies to manufacturing, fabrication, assembling, and research and development facilities in high technology industry clusters that locate or expand in the county and meet specified qualifications.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credit against county property taxes for qualifying high technology facilities that construct or expand buildings. The credit is phased over five years on the increased assessed value: 100% in year one, 80% in year two, 60% in year three, 40% in year four, and 20% in year five. A business entity must be primarily involved in high technology manufacturing, fabrication, assembling, or research and development; construct or expand a building of at least 5,000 square feet; invest at least $500,000 in construction or expansion; and create at least 10 new permanent full-time positions within the facility within three years. The credit application must be submitted by October 1 of the tax year the property becomes eligible.

structured_extraction.program_audience: High-technology businesses and developers primarily involved in high technology manufacturing, fabrication, assembling, or research and development in technology industry clusters including biotechnology and biomedical, information technology and services, high tech machinery and instruments, defense and aerospace, energy and chemicals, and high technology research. Also includes businesses entering lease agreements with high-technology governmental agencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit against Prince George's County real property taxes for construction, expansion, or improvements to high technology facilities. Funds must be used for construction or expansion of buildings of at least 5,000 square feet in the county.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. The facility must be located in the county and meet all specified qualifications.
requirements_list: Must be primarily involved in high technology manufacturing, fabrication, assembling, or research and development as defined by 33 U.S. Standard Industrial Classification codes

Business must be primarily involved with applications of engineering, life sciences, computer sciences, research and development, or production of materials, parts, or equipment used in such applications
Must construct, expand, or cause to be constructed or expanded a building within the county with at least 5,000 square feet of gross floor area to be occupied by the business entity
Must invest at least $500,000 in construction or expansion of the building
Must create at least 10 new permanent full-time positions for the business entity located within the building within three years
Relocation of existing positions from elsewhere in the county or reclassification of preexisting positions does not count as new positions
Application must be submitted by October 1 of the tax year in which the property becomes eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The business entity or building owner must complete an application and include the following information: legal description of the property, written description of the business activity, floor plans and documentation demonstrating construction or expansion of the gross floor area, documentation of the minimum investment of at least $500,000, a properly issued valid Use and Occupancy permit, and any other information the Director of Finance requires. The EDC will market the program, assist with applications, and provide information to applicants and the Director of Finance. structured_extraction.program_name: Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS (HOPWA)
structured_extraction.program_description: HOPWA funds address the specific needs of persons living with HIV/AIDS and their families. The program provides housing services and information through regional grantees serving the Washington D.C. Eligible Metropolitan Area. Funds support rental and emergency assistance through a voucher system to individuals and families with AIDS, as well as housing counseling and housing information through the Metropolitan Housing Access Program (MHAP).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HOPWA funds are distributed by HUD using a statutory formula based on AIDS statistics from the Center for Disease Control and Prevention. Three quarters of HOPWA formula funding is awarded to qualified states and Metropolitan areas with the highest number of AIDS cases. One quarter of the formula funding is awarded to Metropolitan areas that have a higher than average per capita incidence of AIDS. A voucher system provides rental and emergency assistance to individuals and families with AIDS. Services also include housing counseling and housing information through the Metropolitan Housing Access Program (MHAP).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Persons living with HIV/AIDS and their families in the Washington D.C. Eligible Metropolitan Area, including Prince George's County, Calvert County, and Charles County, needing rental, emergency, and housing assistance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded home improvement program administered by Prince George's County that provides financial assistance to eligible homeowners and non-profit organizations for housing rehabilitation and repairs. The program includes two main tracks: (1) HRAP, which offers home loans of up to $60,000 at 0% interest with no monthly payment for health and safety home repairs; and (2) the Homeowner Preservation Program (HOPP), which provides grants of up to $50,000 for households under 50% of area median income (or up to $30,000 for other eligible households) for health, safety, energy efficiency, and accessibility repairs. Together, these programs help low-income homeowners upgrade deteriorated dwellings to meet contemporary minimum property standards and eliminate housing code violations.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant supports Prince George's County-based micro businesses with up to $2,500 to enhance their technological capabilities. The funds can be used for low-cost marketing efforts, remote processing, equipment for credit card processing, social media marketing, and other technology-related improvements. The program received funding from the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) through the Coronavirus State Fiscal Recovery Fund (CSFRF) and Coronavirus Local Fiscal Recovery Fund (CLFRF).

Eligible uses include low-cost marketing efforts, remote processing equipment, credit card processing equipment, social media marketing efforts, and other technology-related improvements. Grants are distributed from a total allocation of $100,000. Grants will not be approved and awarded on a rolling basis; all applications will be reviewed once received. Grant funds may be reported as taxable income, and IRS 1099 Forms will be issued to each grant recipient.

Must have a physical location within Prince George's County

structured_extraction.program_name: Municipal Corporations Leased Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit against property tax imposed on real property for that portion leased, occupied, and used exclusively by a municipal corporation that meets specified conditions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credit against property tax for that portion of real property that is leased, occupied, and used exclusively by a municipal corporation. The property owner is contractually obligated to reduce the amount of taxes for which the municipal corporation is otherwise contractually liable by the amount of the tax credit. The credit is applied to the property tax bill of the property owner for the tax year in which the lease is in effect.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1 prior to the tax year for which the credit is being requested
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners who lease space to municipal corporations in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit against property tax for the portion of real property leased to qualifying municipal corporations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Portion of property must be leased, occupied, and used exclusively by the municipal corporation
Credit does not apply when the municipal corporation subleases the property, uses the property for any profit-making purpose, or no longer occupies the property
Municipal corporation must be contractually liable to the owner for property taxes
Property owner must be contractually obligated to reduce taxes by the amount of the tax credit
Both property owner and municipal corporation lessee must sign the application under oath
A copy of the executed lease between property owner and lessee must be submitted with application
Owner must notify Supervisor of Assessments and Taxation within 30 days of lease termination or cessation of occupancy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application must be submitted to the Supervisor of Assessments and Taxation no later than April 1 prior to the tax year for which the credit is being requested. Application must be signed under oath by both the property owner and the municipal corporation that is or will become the lessee. A copy of the executed lease between the property owner and the lessee must be submitted with the application. Upon termination of the lease or cessation of possession by the tenant, the owner must notify the Supervisor of Assessments and Taxation within 30 days of such event.

structured_extraction.program_name: Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) 2026 for Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_description: Funding for owners and developers to support affordable multifamily rental housing development and preservation projects in Prince George's County. The program seeks to advance the County's goal of producing and preserving approximately 10,000 affordable housing units by 2030 through strategic investments that promote community stability, economic mobility, and equitable development.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides multiple funding sources for acquisition, rehabilitation, or new construction of affordable multifamily rental housing: (1) HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) or County Housing Investment Trust Fund (HITF) loans up to $2,500,000 per project, offered as subordinate debt and gap financing for projects seeking Low Income Housing Tax Credits (9% or 4% LIHTC); (2) Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) providing tax relief up to $600 per affordable unit per year, reviewed on a project-by-project basis based on financial viability; (3) DHCD determines the appropriate funding source(s) for each project based on resource availability and policy priorities. All projects must comply with the County's Diversity and Equity Policy for Publicly Subsidized Development Projects, including local hiring, minority business enterprise participation, and supplier diversity goals.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Experienced, mission-aligned owners and developers seeking to develop affordable multifamily rental housing in Prince George's County, particularly those seeking Low Income Housing Tax Credits and projects near transit corridors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, rehabilitation, or new construction of affordable multifamily rental housing. Projects must demonstrate a financing gap and need for additional county funding sources. Projects must have secured necessary financing and be in a position to progress towards closing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Projects receiving HOME funds must meet federal Neighborhood and Site Selection standards (24 CFR Part 92 Section 202). Highest priority given to projects within one mile of any WMATA Metrorail Station.
requirements_list: Comply with County Diversity and Equity Policy for Publicly Subsidized Development Projects (Section 10-335 of Prince George's County Code)
Comply with federal Section 3 rules (24 CFR 135), including: minimum 25% of total labor hours by Section 3 workers, minimum 5% by Targeted Section 3 workers
At least 30% of Development Costs for Construction paid to County-Based Small Businesses (CBSB) and/or Locally-Owned Businesses (LOB), including at least 20% of design costs
Use Best Efforts to achieve at least 25% of Development Costs for Construction paid to County-Based Minority Business Enterprises (CMBE)
General Contractor Team must include one or more CMBE and/or LOB businesses
At least 25% of construction work hours performed by County Residents, including at least 20% of specialty trade work hours by County Residents
If requesting PILOT, must submit completed PILOT Analysis Workbook with application
Demonstrate financial viability and gap in financing requiring County subsidy
For time-sensitive projects outside NOFA timeframe: project must have secured financing and be positioned to progress towards closing
Meet all applicable Federal, State of Maryland, and Prince George's County program regulations and requirements

Primary real estate service providers (listing agents, appraisers, closing agents, settlement/title companies) must have principal place of business in Prince George's County for residential ownership projects
Maintain Good Standing status with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
