structured_extraction.program_name: Pathway to Purchase Home Buyer Assistance Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A first-time homebuyer assistance program administered by Prince George's County that provides down payment and closing cost assistance to eligible first-time homebuyers to purchase for-sale, foreclosed, or owner-occupied short-sale residential properties in the County. The program facilitates homeownership through an approved network of participating lenders, housing counseling agencies, and title companies, offering favorable loan terms and financial assistance to qualified borrowers who meet income and other eligibility requirements. Funded by the Federal HOME Investment Partnership Program (HOME) pursuant to 24 CFR Part 92.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides up to $50,000 in down payment and closing cost assistance to eligible first-time home buyers through an approved network of participating lenders. The P2P Loan is structured at 0% interest with deferred payment. Purchaser must pay back the loan according to the Recapture Chart based on length of time the property is retained as primary residence within a 10-year affordability period: Less than 1 year = 100% of loan due; 1-2 years = 90%; 2-3 years = 80%; 3-4 years = 70%; 4-5 years = 60%; 5-6 years = 50%; 6-7 years = 40%; 7-8 years = 30%; 8-9 years = 20%; 9-10 years = 10%; 10 years or more = 0% (loan forgiven). In the event of default, the outstanding balance will accrue an annual interest rate of 5.75%. Assistance covers down payment and closing costs for the purchase of for-sale, foreclosed, or owner-occupied short-sale residential properties in Prince George's County. Maximum purchase price limits for resales is $448,000 and for new construction is $485,000 (as of June 2025).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing program with no defined application deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: First-time home buyers in Prince George's County who meet income and other eligibility requirements and are seeking to purchase residential properties. Applicants must have gross annual household income not exceeding 80% of the area median income (AMI) for Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and closing cost assistance for purchasing for-sale, foreclosed, or owner-occupied short-sale residential properties in Prince George's County. Assistance can also be used for mortgage principal reduction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to buyers purchasing homes in all zip codes within Prince George's County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a first-time home buyer (not owned residential real estate anywhere during the three years immediately preceding the application date)

Must meet program income limits: Household of 1 up to $91,800; 2 up to $104,900; 3 up to $118,000; 4 up to $131,100; 5 up to $141,600; 6 up to $152,100; 7 up to $162,600; 8 up to $173,100 (as of June 2025)
Gross annual household income must not exceed 80% of area median income (AMI) for Prince George's County
Maximum Housing (front-end) monthly Debt to Income Ratio of 35%; maximum total (back-end) monthly DTI ratio of 47%
Must have an eligible ratified Contract of Sale on a residential property located in Prince George's County
Property must be for-sale, foreclosed, owner-occupied short-sale residential property, new construction, townhouse, or condominium in the County
Property must pass Housing Quality Standards (HQS) inspection conducted by American Property Consultants, Inc. (APC)
Must work with a Certified Participating Lender
Must complete 8-hour housing counseling through a HUD-certified housing counseling agency (online classes acceptable)
Must obtain title insurance from approved title companies
Must complete required borrower and seller affidavits and disclosures
Subject to lead disclosure requirements (Federal Lead-Based Paint Law; Title X Section 1018)
Must agree to live in the home as primary residence for the entire 10-year loan term
Must be at least 18 years of age
Must be creditworthy and able to qualify for a first mortgage with a Certified Participating Lender
First mortgage must be a fully amortized, fixed rate mortgage (FHA or Conventional; no adjustable rate or balloon payment mortgages)
No minimum cash contribution required from borrower
Borrower is prohibited from receiving money back at settlement
Must have at least 21 business days remaining on final sales contract (not including federal holidays) or an executed amendment extending the contract
For short sales, amendment must be signed by the short sale bank, not the seller
All household members 18 years and above income must be counted toward household income limit
Co-Borrower (Relative/Parent) must also be first-time homebuyer and meet all eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact a PATHWAY TO PURCHASE Program Certified Participating Lender and get pre-approved for a first mortgage only. 2. Contact a real estate agent to identify properties in Prince George's County. 3. Attend an in-classroom 8-hour housing counseling course provided by a HUD-Certified Housing Counseling Agency (online courses accepted). 4. Familiarize yourself with Housing Quality Standards Move-in Inspection Checklist and Requirements. 5. Work with a real estate agent to place a contract on a residential property that can pass HQS inspection with at least 60 days for settlement. 6. When contract is successfully negotiated and ratified, contact the Participating Lender who pre-approved you so they can submit your file to underwriting. The Participating Lender must obtain conditional approval for the first trust loan before submitting the application to PATHWAY TO PURCHASE PROGRAM. 7. Schedule or request HQS Inspection with APC at www.hudpass.com (initial inspection fee of $139 payable by buyer; $65 follow-up fee for completed repairs on failed inspections; $139 no-show/no-access/turned-off utilities penalty fee). 8. Work with lender and real estate agent to complete loan package and address underwriting issues necessary to receive approval for first mortgage and submittal of PATHWAY TO PURCHASE application. 9. P2P Applications can only be submitted by a Certified Participating Lender. All required application intake documents on the P2P submission checklist must be submitted with an application—only complete applications will be accepted; incomplete packages will be returned immediately to the lender. 10. P2P requires 21-business days (not including Federal Holidays) to process and close an application after all documents on the Application Checklist are received. P2P operates on the Federal Government Closing schedule. Files submitted to P2P with no activity for 30 days will be returned to Lender. 11. The submittal of an application by a Certified Participating Lender does not guarantee funding; applications are approved and funded on a first come, first ready basis. Do not attempt to submit an application with less than 21 business days remaining on the contract, as it will not be accepted. Contact K. K. Jones at kkjones@co.pg.md.us or 301-883-6511 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Pathways to Financial Management for Business / Grow Prince George's Strategic Training - Finance Bootcamp
structured_extraction.program_description: A financial management training initiative offered by Prince George's County that includes a six-part series of financial management seminars and a Finance Bootcamp. The seminar series educates and empowers small business owners to successfully manage the financial aspects of their business, covering essential components of small business financial planning and management with experts in banking, innovative financing, and small business development. The Finance Bootcamp strengthens participants' financial management capabilities, enhances business performance, and helps navigate certifications and government contracts, covering financial statement analysis, performance dashboards using QuickBooks Online, compliance, certification requirements, and government contract financing, led by experienced CPA Jeff Wilson, II. Both programs serve Prince George's County small business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Pathways program consists of six seminar sessions covering financial management topics. Participants can attend in-person sessions or access live stream sessions by purchasing tickets. The series concludes with a FREE lender matchmaking event where graduates meet one-on-one with lenders and can apply for financing on-site. The Finance Bootcamp is a free training program held on Wednesdays, 2:30-4:30pm, covering financial statement analysis, performance dashboards using QuickBooks Online, compliance, certification requirements, and government contract financing strategies. Lenders and finance resources provide counseling and onsite loan application support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs in Prince George's County seeking financial management education, access to capital, and guidance on certifications and government contracts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and education in financial planning and management, financial statement analysis, performance dashboards, compliance, certification requirements, and government contract navigation; access to lenders for business financing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For the Pathways seminar series, participants can register for individual sessions or purchase the entire series; in-person and live stream tickets are available, and video recordings of past sessions can be purchased. The series concludes with a free lender matchmaking event where graduates can meet with lenders and apply for financing. For the Finance Bootcamp, apply to join a cohort through the application link provided at https://www.pgcedc.com/gpg-trainings.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program offered by Prince George's Federal Credit Union that allows members to temporarily skip loan payments during financial hardship, such as during a federal government shutdown.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Qualified borrowers can skip up to 2 months of payments on existing loans without penalty. The program excludes real estate loans, mobile home loans, and revolving loans including credit cards.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Programs will discontinue the day the shutdown ends
structured_extraction.program_audience: Members of Prince George's Federal Credit Union who hold qualifying loans and are experiencing financial hardship due to federal government shutdowns.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary relief from monthly loan payment obligations to help manage finances during periods of reduced income or employment disruption.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to members of Prince George's Federal Credit Union.
requirements_list: Must be a member of Prince George's Federal Credit Union
Must have a qualified loan (excludes real estate loans, mobile home loans, and revolving loans including credit cards)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Members should contact Prince George's Federal Credit Union at 301.627.2666, email Inquiries@PrinceGeorgesCFCU.org, or visit any branch location to request a payment deferral on their existing loan.

structured_extraction.program_description: An agreement from the county to abate property taxes and instead charge a negotiated payment. The payment can range from zero to the full amount of taxes due or more. In some cases, taxes are deferred rather than abated.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A negotiated agreement that abates or defers property taxes in exchange for a different payment amount, which can range from zero to the full tax amount or more. Can serve as an alternative to tax increment financing.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses seeking property tax relief in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax abatement or deferral through negotiated payment arrangements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Financial Services Program Manager to negotiate a PILOT agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free training program that prepares residents to become certified peer recovery specialists. The curriculum consists of five approved courses totaling 50 hours covering ethics, advocacy, recovery and wellness, mentoring and education, and harm reduction for peer recovery specialists.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free five-course curriculum approved by the Maryland Addiction & Behavioral-Health Professionals Certification Board. Each session includes one to three in-person days with 50 hours total. Participants must attend all five courses within two years to receive certification.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County residents age 18 and older who have at least 2 years of recovery from a substance use or co-occurring disorder, or have successfully completed reentry.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification to become a peer recovery specialist.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Open to Prince George's County residents.

Must be age 18 or older
Must have at least 2 years of recovery from a substance use or co-occurring disorder, or have successfully completed reentry
Must attend all five courses within two years to receive certification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register for the next available training session through the online registration form. Contact PeerTrainings@co.pg.md.us if you have questions or would like to be notified about the next training.

structured_extraction.program_name: Pepco Electric Vehicle Charging Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program that helps offset the cost of installing electric vehicle charging stations for residential and multifamily properties in Maryland. The program provides rebates for Level 2 smart chargers and covers installation costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Residential customers who install an eligible Level 2 smart charger at their single-family home after July 1, 2019 receive up to $300 rebates. Multifamily property managers, owners, and homeowners associations can receive up to $25,000 in rebates on qualified charging equipment installation of Level 2 smart chargers and a 100% discount on installation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides $5,000 to Prince George's County-based personal services businesses to help them establish or expand online sales capabilities and improve their digital presence and technology infrastructure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each eligible business receives a $5,000 grant. Funds can be used to reimburse expenses incurred after March 9, 2020 for establishing or expanding online sales capabilities, including website development and enhancements, targeted marketing, establishing e-commerce functionality, app integration, appointment scheduling software enhancements, and purchasing personal computers and related equipment. General infrastructure improvements such as plumbing, electrical work, or general interior repairs/improvements are not eligible. Grant funds are reported as taxable income and IRS 1099 Forms will be issued to each grant recipient.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Personal services business owners in Prince George's County with fewer than 20 employees. Businesses can operate as sole proprietorships, partnerships, limited liability companies (LLCs), or corporations. A physical brick and mortar location in Prince George's County is not required.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Website development and enhancements, targeted marketing, establishing e-commerce functionality, app integration, appointment scheduling software enhancements, personal computers, and other equipment or services related to online or e-commerce capabilities for businesses. Expenses incurred after March 9, 2020 are eligible. General infrastructure improvements such as plumbing, electrical work, or general interior repairs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must have a physical location or operate in Prince George's County, Maryland. Physical brick and mortar location is not required; many personal service businesses operate as independent contractors or provide services on location.
requirements_list: Business must be in the eligible personal services sector (NAICS codes 8121, 8122, 8123, 81210, 541940, 812930)
Business must have been established prior to March 9, 2020
Business must be registered and in good standing with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Business must currently be in operation
Business must have no more than 20 total employees excluding the owner (includes contracted/1099 employees)
Business entity must be Limited Liability Company (LLC), Partnership, Corporation, or Sole Proprietorship
Sole proprietors must provide trade registration documents, business EIN Number, or a statement of non-registration
Applicants who did not receive a COVID-19 Business Relief Grant or Loan from the Maryland Department of Commerce are prioritized
Businesses that received Prince George's County Business Relief Initiative Grant in 2020 are still eligible to apply
If owning multiple personal service businesses, each location must have a separate federal tax ID and address
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must verify their business is active and in good standing using SDAT's online search, then complete an online application portal. Required documents include a completed online application form, Employment Verification Form, Evidence of Good Standing (screenshot or photo from SDAT), a voided check, and organization documents (Operating Agreement for LLC, Partnership Agreement for partnerships, Bylaws for corporations, or tax return documentation for sole proprietors). All applications are reviewed after the deadline and grants are not approved on a rolling basis. Grant recipients are notified by email and must sign a Grant Agreement with non-negotiable terms. Funds will be electronically deposited through ACH bank payment by December 1, 2021.

structured_extraction.program_description: PreventionLink is a free health and healthcare transformation program administered by Prince George's County that serves two audiences: (1) residents of southern Maryland living with or at risk for chronic diseases such as diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol, providing peer-supported online and in-person programs led by lifestyle coaches, certified health educators, and community health workers; and (2) primary care practices in Prince George's, Charles, Calvert, and St. Mary's counties, offering technical assistance, care coordination, community health worker support, and access to self-management programs through a bi-directional electronic referral system to improve health outcomes for patients with or at risk for diabetes, hypertension, or heart disease.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For residents: Free enrollment in peer-supported online and in-person health programs including lifestyle coaching, certified health education, and community health worker support to prevent or manage chronic diseases. For primary care practices: Technical assistance including care plan development, workflow optimization, risk stratification implementation, practice coaching through on-site visits or virtual calls, community health worker support, access to a community of practice that meets quarterly, educational sessions and webinars, and bi-directional electronic referral system integration for tracking patient participation in self-management programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: (1) Residents of southern Maryland (particularly Prince George's County) living with or at risk of chronic diseases such as diabetes, high blood pressure, or high cholesterol; and (2) Primary care practices operating in Prince George's, Charles, Calvert, or St. Mary's counties that use an Electronic Health Record System and connect to the Chesapeake Regional Information System for our Patients (CRISP).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: For residents: Program participation includes health coaching, education, and support to prevent or manage chronic diseases through lifestyle coaching, certified health education, and community health worker assistance. For providers: Technical assistance, care coordination, community health worker services, and access to chronic disease prevention and management programs; providers use the assistance to develop care plans, implement team-based care models, conduct small tests of change, and identify and refer patients to evidence-based self-management and community resources.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Resident services are free for residents of southern Maryland with focus on Prince George's County. Primary care practice services are available to practices operating in Prince George's, Charles, Calvert, or St. Mary's counties.
requirements_list: Referral from a physician or completion of an interest form (for resident participants)
Commitment to attend and participate in all program sessions (for resident participants)
Eligibility determination by program staff (for resident participants)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For residents: Step 1: Request a referral from your physician, or fill out an interest form if you don't have a primary care doctor. Step 2: Your doctor determines eligibility and refers you to the appropriate PreventionLink program, or program staff reviews your form to determine eligibility. Step 3: PreventionLink connects you with lifestyle coaches, certified health educators, and community health workers. For primary care providers: Submit an interest form online at https://www.princegeorgescountymd.gov/form/preventionlink-participant-interest, call PreventionLink at (301)-883-7220, or email PreventionLink@co.pg.md.us. Applicants must agree to enroll in the program, meet all eligibility requirements including EHR use and CRISP connection, and sign required agreements including a Business Associate Agreement, Data Exchange Agreement, Memorandum of Understanding, and Commitment Form.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County - Solar Energy Grant (Solar PV Grant)
structured_extraction.program_description: A county grant program that provides financial assistance to help Prince George's County residents afford rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) system installation. The program is designed to be coupled with state energy incentives and follows successful implementation of energy-efficiency measures. It offers higher grants for residents in designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs) and standard grants for other county residents. The program aims to help grant recipients achieve at least 10% energy savings and makes solar energy more affordable and accessible by connecting residents with vetted solar installers and available grant opportunities. Eligible costs include all parts, components, and accessory equipment necessary to operate and/or install the system, plus reasonable facilitation measures such as tree trimming (up to 20% of grant for ancillary costs). The program is administered in partnership with the Maryland Clean Energy Center and is available to residents who are Pepco and/or Washington Gas customers.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For Pepco customers in an Energy Resiliency Community (ERC) with homeowner-owned systems: grant of up to $10,000 (income-qualified applicants below 60% of median income may receive up to 100% of costs up to $10,000; market-rate applicants receive up to $5,000). For all other homeowner-owned systems outside an ERC or non-Pepco customers: grant of up to $5,000. For third-party owned systems (leases or PPAs): ineligible for this grant. Solar power outlet installation: up to $2,000 available as an add-on. Up to 20% of the grant may be spent on ancillary costs and reasonable measures to facilitate installation such as tree trimming, service panel upgrades, roof repairs, and mold remediation. Funds are distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. Solar PV systems must be at least 2 kW DC and designed to produce at least 800 kWh per year per installed kW. Grant payment is issued as reimbursement after all requested documents have been submitted and approved.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis from November 10, 2025, to February 27, 2026. The deadline may be extended, but awards are limited, so early submission is strongly encouraged.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Department of Environment (DoE), Climate and Energy Division, Sustainable Energy
structured_extraction.program_audience: Single-family homeowners in Prince George's County who are Pepco and/or Washington Gas customers, have not previously received a Solar Energy Grant from the county, and wish to install a rooftop solar photovoltaic system. Priority and higher grant amounts are available to residents within the nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs): Bladensburg - East Riverdale; Forestville; Hillcrest Heights - Marlow Heights; Kentland - Palmer Park; Oxon Hill – Glassmanor; Silver Hill; Suitland - Coral Hills; and Woodlawn – Lanham. Self-installers are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of new rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on single-family residences, including all parts, components, and accessory equipment necessary to operate and/or install the system; solar power outlet purchase and installation; and reasonable measures to facilitate system installation such as tree trimming, service panel upgrades, roof repairs, and mold remediation (up to 20% of grant for ancillary costs). Systems must be at least 2 kW DC and designed to meet minimum benefit requirements of producing at least 800 kWh per year per installed kW.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Applicants must be county residents living in single-family residences or dwelling units within townhouses in which they own the roof. Higher grant amounts (up to $10,000) are available to Pepco customers residing in one of nine designated Energy Resiliency Communities (ERCs): Bladensburg - East Riverdale; Forestville; Hillcrest Heights - Marlow Heights; Kentland - Palmer Park; Oxon Hill – Glassmanor; Silver Hill; Suitland - Coral Hills; and Woodlawn – Lanham. All other Prince George's County homeowners are eligible for the standard grant amount (up to $5,000). Use the ERC Address Locator at http://bit.ly/ERClocator to confirm eligibility.
requirements_list: Be a Prince George's County resident who has not previously received a Solar Energy Grant from Prince George's County
Live in a single-family residence as proven by the MD SDAT Real Property Data Search, which may include a dwelling unit within a townhouse in which you own the roof
Not already own a rooftop solar system; the grant is exclusively for new solar PV system installations
Own the solar photovoltaic system through a cash purchase, loan, or financing (third-party/lease arrangements are ineligible)
Must be a Pepco and/or Washington Gas customer
Must reside in a designated Energy Resiliency Community (ERC) and be a Pepco customer to qualify for the $10,000 ERC grant
Have successfully implemented energy-efficiency measures prior to applying for the solar grant (recommended for all applicants)
Project must achieve at least 10% energy savings
Solar PV system must be at least 2 kW DC and designed to produce at least 800 kWh per year per installed kW
Work with a solar contractor that is registered as a Prince George's County vendor with the Office of Procurement
Solar contractor must hold a valid Maryland Home Improvement Commission (MHIC) license and employ a master electrician with appropriate licensure
Solar contractor must have at least one person who is NABCEP PV Installation Professional (PVIP) Certified and involved in design and installation
Site supervisor must have completed at least 40 hours of solar PV technical and safety course training
Solar contractor must be listed on the Maryland Energy Administration's (MEA) Maryland Solar Access Program (MSAP) Participating Contractor List
Solar contractor must comply with MEA's Consumer Protection Policy for the MSAP
All major system components must be new and meet current applicable federal, state, and local regulations
Submit solar photovoltaic grant application with signed Grant Award Terms and Conditions Agreement and signed Affidavit of Income
Submit final invoice using county template, recent (within 3 months) electricity bill as PDF, and IRS Form W-9
Provide contractor qualifications including NABCEP PVIP certification proof and personnel credentials
Submit detailed solar PV analysis with system design, yearly estimated output, energy savings projections, payback period, inverter and module specs, roof condition and shading report
Submit pre-installation photos per county Photo Documentation Guide
Submit signed contract between homeowner and contractor with itemized quote including scope of work that meets all MEA MSAP Consumer Protection Policy and MHIC Contract Requirements
Submit proof of executed financing contract if applicable (e.g., loan agreement)
Receive a Prequalification Notice from DoE before installing solar
Contractor must provide a Standard Customer Agreement that includes consumer protection requirements and MHIC contract requirements
Contractor must provide a Quality Assurance Plan describing how they ensure quality workmanship and safety on each project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1 - Scan for Eligibility: Confirm you meet basic requirements including being a Prince George's County resident, living in a single-family residence, not already owning a rooftop solar system, owning the system through cash purchase or financing (not third-party lease), and being a Pepco and/or Washington Gas customer. Use the ERC Address Locator (http://bit.ly/ERClocator) to determine if you qualify for the higher ERC grant amount. Step 2 - Obtain Financial Assistance: Determine your eligible grant amount based on location (ERC or non-ERC) and utility provider. Consider additional state incentives like the Maryland Solar Access Program. Step 3 - Look for an Eligible Solar Contractor: Select a solar contractor from the Maryland Solar Access Program's Participating Contractor List. Verify the contractor is registered as a Prince George's County vendor, holds a valid MHIC license, has NABCEP PVIP certification, and complies with MEA MSAP requirements. Obtain solar quotes and ensure contractor meets all eligibility requirements. Step 4 - Apply for Prequalification (Before Installation): Working with your selected contractor, compile and submit required documents by email to CleanE@co.pg.md.us or by hand delivery/mail to: Prince George's County Department of the Environment (DoE), Sustainable Energy, 1801 McCormick Drive, Suite 500, Largo, MD 20774. Required documents include: (1) completed Solar PV Grant Application with signed Grant Award Terms and Conditions Agreement and Affidavit of Income; (2) final invoice using county template; (3) recent (within 3 months) electricity bill as PDF; (4) IRS Form W-9; (5) contractor qualifications including NABCEP PVIP certification; (6) detailed solar PV analysis with system design, yearly estimated output, energy savings, payback period, roof condition and shading report; (7) pre-installation photos per county Photo Documentation Guide; (8) signed homeowner-contractor agreement with itemized quote meeting all MEA MSAP and MHIC requirements; (9) proof of financing if applicable. Alternatively, if the contractor has received MSAP Reservation of Funds confirmation, submit MSAP documents instead (Reservation of Funds confirmation, executed Solar PV Agreement, signed MSAP Customer Disclosure Form, signed MSAP Authorization Form). All signatures must be handwritten or digital; typed names are not accepted. Prequalification approval typically occurs within approximately 30 business days of receipt of a complete application. Systems installed prior to receiving a Prequalification Notice do not qualify for this grant. Step 5 - Receive Grant Funds (After Installation): After installation is complete, working with your contractor, submit: (1) final invoice if equipment changed (with job completion date); (2) utility's Permission to Operate letter and interconnection agreement; (3) proof of all necessary permits and official inspection sticker from third-party residential solar inspector participating in DPIE's Third Party Residential Solar System Inspection Program; (4) close-out documents including commissioning checklist, owner's manual, warranty proof, and as-built drawings; (5) installation photos per county photo documentation guide; (6) proof of system registration with Maryland Public Service Commission (PSC); (7) proof of one month of solar generation (utility bill) and completed feedback survey; (8) Authorization for Electronic Funds Disbursement form for direct payments if applicable. Grant payment is issued as reimbursement only after all properly submitted documents have been received and approved. Installation must occur within 6 months of receiving prequalification approval; extensions may be granted for circumstances outside applicant's control with written justification. Final approval of installation and site visit by DoE staff is expected within 15 business days of receipt of invoice. Payment approval by DoE Office of Finance is intended within 30 to 60 business days. It is recommended homeowners conduct a whole-house energy audit before installing solar to maximize energy savings. For energy efficiency grant incentives and assistance, check the county's Energy Efficiency Grant program and Empower Maryland. If ineligible for rooftop solar, consider subscribing to a community solar program. Contact DoE Sustainable Energy at CleanE@co.pg.md.us or 301-883-5810 for additional details.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Alternative Energy/Energy Conservation (Solar & Geothermal) Residential Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides a property tax credit to residential property owners in Prince George's County who install solar energy or geothermal energy devices on their properties. The credit applies to residential structures utilizing solar or geothermal systems and is administered locally by Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property tax credit for residential structures in Prince George's County that install and utilize solar energy or geothermal energy devices. The credit amount is determined based on the installation cost of the alternative energy system. Application and proof of claim, including documentation of installation, must be filed with the Director of Finance. The credit is applied against the property's annual tax assessment.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Prince George's County Director of Finance
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners in Prince George's County who install solar energy or geothermal energy devices on their properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of solar energy or geothermal energy devices on residential structures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County only.
requirements_list: Residential structure must be located in Prince George's County
Residential structure must utilize solar energy or geothermal energy devices
Installation must be completed and operational
Applicant must own the residential property
Application and proof of claim must be filed with the Director of Finance
Documentation of system installation costs required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must file an application and proof of claim with the Prince George's County Director of Finance. Documentation of the solar or geothermal system installation, including installation costs and system specifications, must be submitted with the application. The credit is claimed on the property tax return for the tax year following installation.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County COVID-19 Business Recovery Initiative (Formerly Relief Fund)
structured_extraction.program_description: A public-private partnership that provided loans and grants to small businesses in Prince George's County whose operations were interrupted due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The initiative helped small, local, and minority-owned enterprises retain their pre-pandemic workforce and sustain operations, offering working capital assistance of up to $100,000 per business and a total program funding pool of up to $20 million.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $100,000 per business to support cash operating expenses including payroll, suppliers, rent, fixed debt payments, and other business-critical operating costs, covering up to 6 months of verified payroll and operating expenses. The overall program had a funding pool of up to $20 million. Loans were also available as part of the broader public-private partnership initiative.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small, local, and minority-owned for-profit businesses in Prince George's County facing economic hardship due to COVID-19 interruptions, including sole proprietors and 1099 applicants as of May 15, 2020.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Cash operating expenses including payroll, suppliers, rent, fixed debt payments, and other business-critical cash operating costs for up to 6 months of verified expenses, as well as workforce retention and sustaining operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have a principal business office or location physically located in Prince George's County and must maintain their operations in the County.

Meet U.S. Small Business Administration definition of a small business
Not a new business venture
For-profit business entity
Must retain jobs and commit to hiring County residents for future vacancies
Must maintain operations in the County
Commit to best efforts to have 35% County-based business participation in any future construction work
Must provide evidence that application has been submitted to U.S. SBA and State of Maryland if available
As of May 15 2020 sole proprietors and 1099 applicants are accepted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete an online application and submit required documentation including tax returns, income statements, payroll records, employment certification, evidence of business disruption, and personal financial statements for owners with 20% or more ownership interest.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Child Care Provider Recovery Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funded by $2 million in CARES Act funding to help licensed child care centers and registered family child care homes in Prince George's County that closed or had difficulty reopening due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Grant funds supported reopening costs including personal protective equipment (PPE), payroll, supplies, rent, fixed debt payments, and other critical business operating costs. Of the total $2 million, $1.4 million was targeted to licensed child care centers and $600,000 to registered family child care homes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $20,000 for licensed child care centers and up to $3,000 for registered family child care homes. Funds supported reopening expenses including personal protective equipment (PPE), payroll, supplies, rent, fixed debt payments, and other critical business operating costs. Funds cannot be used for bonuses, incentives, or expansion. Total funding appropriated was $2 million in CARES Act funds, with $1.4 million targeted to licensed child care centers and $600,000 targeted to registered family child care homes. Funds were distributed electronically via ACH bank payment upon award and signing of Grant Agreement.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and registered family child care homes (including large family child care homes) in Prince George's County that closed or had difficulty reopening due to COVID-19.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reopening expenses including personal protective equipment (PPE), payroll, supplies, rent, fixed debt payments, and other critical business operating costs. Funds cannot be used for bonuses, incentives, or expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County only. Centers must be located in the County.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center or registered family child care home (including large family child care homes) located in Prince George's County
Must be currently closed or recently reopened after July 30, 2020
Must serve children from birth to age five years

Recipients were required to submit quarterly reports and a final report on fund usage. Contact Prince George's County Economic Development Corporation for more information.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Climate-Smart Local Producers Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A pilot program funded by the USDA Partnerships for Climate-Smart Commodities program that supports farmers and producers—particularly those in underserved communities, including people of color, women, and minority-owned operations—to implement climate-smart practices in organic farming. The program aims to reduce barriers to farm ownership and operation, support the implementation of climate-smart and organic farming practices on existing and new farms, develop a marketing strategy that emphasizes eating locally and climate-smart practices, measure greenhouse gas reductions from farming practices, and contribute to the availability of healthy food throughout Prince George's County.

list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a $3,250,000 competitive grant from the USDA Partnerships for Climate-Smart Commodities program. Funding supports farmers and producers in implementing climate-smart and organic farming practices, including Fruit, Vegetables, Specialty Crops and a variety of other crops. Assistance includes reducing barriers to farm ownership and operation on existing and new farms, increasing access to healthy food throughout the county, and measuring greenhouse gas reductions from farming practices. Emphasis is placed on beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged farmers, veteran farmers, limited resource farmers, women farmers, minority-owned farm operations, and producers growing specialty crops in underserved communities.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports implementation of climate-smart and organic farming practices on existing and new farms, marketing of locally grown products emphasizing climate-smart practices and woman and minority-owned farms, reducing barriers to farm ownership and operation, measuring greenhouse gas reductions, and increasing access to healthy food throughout the County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland, with specific focus on underserved communities within the county.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Rain Check Rebate Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A rebate program administered by Prince George's County in partnership with the Chesapeake Bay Trust that provides financial incentives to homeowners, businesses, nonprofits, and other property owners to install approved Best Management Practices (BMPs) that improve stormwater runoff quality, reduce runoff quantity, and enhance local streams and rivers. Eligible practices include cisterns, conservation landscaping, green roofs, pavement removal, permeable pavement, rain barrels, rain gardens, and urban tree canopy (including trees up to $150 per tree). The program also offers up to a 100% reduction in the Clean Water Act Fee (Impervious Area Fee component) for property owners who install qualifying BMPs. Annual rebate funds are limited and awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. The program supports climate resilience by reducing local flooding and improving water quality in the Chesapeake Bay watershed.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rebates are awarded based on the type of stormwater management practice installed. Residential properties receive up to a $6,000 lifetime rebate ceiling. Commercial properties, homeowner associations, condominium associations, civic associations, multi-family dwellings, nonprofits, and not-for-profit organizations receive up to a $20,000 lifetime rebate ceiling. Specific rebate amounts by practice: cisterns ($2 per gallon stored), conservation landscaping ($5 per square foot), green roofs ($10–$20 per square foot), pavement removal ($6 per square foot), permeable pavement ($12 per square foot), rain barrels ($2 per gallon stored), rain gardens ($10 per square foot), and urban tree canopy ($150 per tree). Rebate amounts cannot exceed the total project cost. Additionally, property owners who install approved BMPs may receive up to a 100% reduction in their Clean Water Act Fee (Impervious Area Fee component). Fee reduction credits are valid for three years and require reapplication for renewal. All rebates are awarded first-come, first-served with limited annual funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/ongoing program; applications accepted year-round until annual funding is exhausted
structured_extraction.contact_name: Prince George's County Department of the Environment
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential property owners, commercial property owners, homeowner associations, condominium associations, civic associations, multi-family dwelling owners, nonprofit and not-for-profit organizations, and other property owners in Prince GeorgéOs County seeking to install stormwater management practices or reduce their Clean Water Act Fee.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of approved stormwater management Best Management Practices (BMPs) including cisterns, conservation landscaping, green roofs, pavement removal, permeable pavement, rain barrels, rain gardens, and urban tree canopy (trees). Funds may also support off-site BMP installation. Projects must reduce stormwater runoff quantity or improve stormwater quality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Properties within the municipal limits of the City of Bowie are excluded. Residents of Cheverly, University Park, and College Park are ineligible for urban tree canopy rebates (those municipalities have their own tree rebate programs) but may participate in all other rebate categories (cistern, green roof, pavement removal, permeable pavement, rain barrel, and rain garden).

Property must be located in Prince George's County
Property must not be located within the City of Bowie municipal limits
Applicants in municipalities with their own stormwater rebate programs (Cheverly, University Park, College Park) are ineligible for urban tree canopy rebates but eligible for other practices
Projects must be completed within 12 months of receiving pre-approval from Chesapeake Bay Trust (CBT); for rain barrels, receipt or invoice must be submitted within 12 months of application
Chesapeake Bay Trust must inspect the completed project and confirm it complies with the original approved application and County best practice guidelines
Application for fee reduction credits must be approved within 12 months of project completion date
Department of the Environment must be granted access for inspection and field verification of BMPs
BMPs must be functioning correctly and maintained in good condition to receive and retain Clean Water Act Fee reduction credits
Fee reduction credits are valid for three years and require reapplication for renewal
If property is part of a Homeowners Association, applicant must provide HOA approval documentation
Projects involving permit requirements for new building construction, additions, or renovations are not eligible
All applicants must sign a property owner agreement; commercial or public project applicants must also sign an operations and maintenance agreement
Rebate amounts cannot exceed the total project cost
Projects must comply with County stormwater management guidelines and best practice standards for each BMP type
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply through the Chesapeake Bay Trust (CBT) website. CBT staff assist with questions, review and process applications, and conduct pre- and post-inspections. Most applications require CBT pre-approval before project implementation begins. Rain barrel projects do not require pre-approval but receipts or invoices must be submitted within 12 months of application. All invoices and receipts must be submitted to CBT for review and approval. For Clean Water Act Fee reduction credits for existing BMPs, property owners should contact the Department of the Environment to request inspection and verification. A Fee Lookup Tool is available to estimate fee reductions based on various BMP scenarios. Contact the Department of Environment at 301-883-5810 for additional information. Rebates are awarded first-come, first-served with limited annual funding. Applications are accepted throughout the year on a rolling basis until annual funding is depleted.

structured_extraction.program_name: Prince George's County Stormwater Stewardship Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that funds on-the-ground restoration and program activities to improve communities and water quality while engaging Prince George's County residents in the restoration and protection of local waterways. The program also supports community-wide climate resilience projects and addresses local flooding through focused outreach, community engagement, and installation of green infrastructure practices. Eligible activities include water quality improvement, citizen awareness and engagement, technical assistance to churches, tree planting, environmental education, trash reduction in the Anacostia, and installation of small to medium-scale green infrastructure practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants fund on-the-ground restoration and program activities that improve water quality and community engagement. Since program inception, 112 grants have been awarded for a total of $8.7 million. Projects must be implemented in Prince George's County. Matching funds and in-kind services are not required but are considered favorably in the review process. Annual funding varies by fiscal year, with recent years ranging from $585,429 to $2,051,010 in total dollars granted.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Tax-exempt and 501(c) nonprofit organizations, municipalities, faith-based organizations, educational institutions, community associations, civic groups, homeowners, and businesses in Prince George's County, as well as community organizations and residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Water quality improvement projects, citizen awareness and engagement initiatives, technical assistance to churches, tree planting, environmental education programs, trash reduction efforts in the Anacostia watershed, community outreach and engagement, and installation of small to medium-scale green infrastructure practices to address stormwater management and local flooding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must be implemented in Prince George's County, Maryland. Pilot projects have been conducted in areas such as Tantallon in Fort Washington.
requirements_list: Must be a qualified tax-exempt or 501(c) nonprofit organization, municipality, faith-based organization, educational institution, community association, civic group, homeowner, or business
Project must be implemented in Prince George's County

Applications are evaluated on likelihood of project success, cost-effectiveness and appropriate budget items, consistency with request for proposal, sustainability, justification and need, appropriate partners demonstrating support, and demonstration value and transferability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process is competitive and managed by Chesapeake Bay Trust, a state agency established by the Maryland General Assembly in 1985. Funding partners and an external Technical Review Committee evaluate all applications. Proposals are reviewed and scored by at least three external peer reviewers composed of experts in their fields. All applicants are offered the opportunity to receive reviewer feedback. For more information, visit https://cbtrust.org/ or https://cbtrust.org/prince-georges-stormwater-stewardship-2/ to view a complete list of grant awardees.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Project Based Voucher (PBV) Program provides affordable rental housing assistance to low-income households at specific multifamily properties throughout Prince George's County. Unlike tenant-based vouchers, PBV assistance is attached to designated units at approved properties — if a family moves out of a PBV unit, the rental assistance remains with that unit rather than following the household. The program is administered locally by the Housing Authority of Prince George's County (HAPGC) under federal housing assistance guidelines.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental assistance funds attached to specific units at designated multifamily properties throughout Prince George's County. PBV assistance helps eligible households pay a portion of rent at approved private properties, with the amount of assistance varying based on household income, family size, and unit size. Households cannot participate in any other federally funded housing subsidy program while leasing a PBV unit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Waitlist currently closed. Previous application period was Monday, March 16, 2026, at 12:01 a.m. to Tuesday, March 17, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. EST

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Assistance is only available at specific PBV properties located throughout Prince George's County, including Fort Washington, Capitol Heights, Upper Marlboro, Lanham, Glenarden, Bladensburg, Riverdale, Hyattsville, District Heights, and Clinton.
requirements_list: Household income must meet program income limits
Family size must be appropriate for available unit size
Cannot participate in any other federally funded housing subsidy program
Must pass landlord screening process
Must meet HAPGC program eligibility requirements
Must complete eligibility verification
Must provide required documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted during open application periods through an online portal. Applicants are randomly selected through a lottery process. Selected applicants are notified by email and mail and receive instructions to complete eligibility verification and provide required documentation. Applicants are notified of waitlist status within 45 days after the application closes. Once a rental unit becomes available, selected households are referred to a PBV unit to begin the property's application and screening process. After the landlord approves the application, it is sent to HAPGC for final program eligibility review.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project Based Voucher Accessibility Waiting List
structured_extraction.program_description: A separate waiting list for current participants, residents, and applicants of the Housing Authority of Prince George's County programs who need accessible housing units that meet their accessibility needs related to a disability.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Placement on a dedicated waiting list for accessible housing units. The program provides assistance to individuals with disabilities who are current participants of the Housing Choice Voucher Program, Public Housing Program, Project Based Voucher Program, or Moderate Rehabilitation Program, or who are current applicants on Housing Authority waiting lists. Applicants submit a preliminary application to the 504 Coordinator. Applications are accepted in paper form only and are dated and time stamped to establish priority placement on the waiting list. Priority is determined by four tiers: (1) Current residents and participants needing accessible units with at least one family member using a wheelchair or scooter; (2) Current residents and participants needing accessible units without wheelchair/scooter users; (3) Applicants needing accessible units with at least one family member using a wheelchair or scooter; (4) Applicants needing accessible units without wheelchair/scooter users. Within each tier, priority is based on application date. If accepted, participants must relinquish any current tenant-based voucher, moderate rehabilitation unit, or public housing unit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No deadline; applications accepted at any time
structured_extraction.program_audience: Current participants of Housing Choice Voucher Program, Public Housing Program, Project Based Voucher Program, or Moderate Rehabilitation Program; current residents of Public Housing; or current applicants on Housing Authority waiting lists who have a disability and need accessible housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to accessible housing units, including rentals in privately owned and managed properties. Rental cost is typically 30% of household adjusted gross income. Applicants can request specific unit accommodations such as wheelchair accessibility, modifications for persons who are blind or deaf, extra bedrooms for live-in attendants, single-level units, accessible bathrooms, and other disability-related modifications.

requirements_list: Must be current participant of HAPGC Housing Choice Voucher Program, OR current resident of HAPGC Public Housing Program, OR current participant of HAPGC Project Based Voucher Program, OR current participant of HAPGC Moderate Rehabilitation Program, OR current applicant on HAPGC waiting lists
Must have a disability requiring accessible housing accommodations
Only Head of Household or application holder (for those on waiting lists) is eligible to apply; other household members cannot apply separately

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed PBVAWL preliminary application in person or by mail to the 504 Coordinator at the Housing Authority of Prince George's County office located at 9200 Basil Court, Room 500, Largo, MD 20774. Applications are available at the HAPGC office at 9200 Basil Court, Suite 107, Largo, MD 20774, or online at ha.mypgc.us. All applications are accepted in paper form only. Applicants may request reasonable accommodations to complete the application, including auxiliary aids, services, materials in alternative formats, or assistance with paperwork.

Must own residential property in Prince George's County

structured_extraction.program_description: This program forgives the remaining balance on Direct Loans for employees of government or not-for-profit organizations after they have made 120 qualifying monthly payments under an accepted repayment plan while working full-time for an eligible employer.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program forgives the remaining balance on Direct Loans after the borrower has made 120 qualifying monthly payments under an accepted repayment plan while employed full-time by an eligible government or not-for-profit employer. The borrower must have Direct Loans or consolidate other federal student loans into a Direct Loan, and must repay under an income-driven repayment plan (SAVE, PAYE, IBR, or ICR) or a 10-year Standard Repayment Plan. The amount forgiven will be the principal and interest that was due on eligible Direct Loans when the final qualifying payment was made. Payments need not be consecutive, and employment need not be consecutive. Only eligible payments made on or after October 1, 2007, can become a qualifying payment for PSLF. FFEL Program, Perkins Loan Program, or other student loans are not eligible unless consolidated into a Direct Loan.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Employees of federal, state, local, or tribal government agencies and qualifying not-for-profit organizations who have federal student loans and are seeking loan forgiveness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This program provides loan forgiveness on Direct Loans only; funds are not disbursed to applicants but rather the loan balance is forgiven after 120 qualifying payments are made.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to employees of U.S. federal, state, local, or tribal government and qualifying not-for-profit organizations anywhere in the United States.
requirements_list: Be employed by a U.S. federal, state, local, or tribal government or qualifying not-for-profit organization (including U.S. military service), or serve in an AmeriCorps or Peace Corps position
Work full-time for that agency or organization, meaning at least an average of 30 hours per week
Have Direct Loans or consolidate other federal student loans (FFEL, Perkins) into a Direct Loan
Repay loans under an eligible repayment plan: Income-Driven Repayment plan (SAVE, PAYE, IBR, or ICR) or a 10-year Standard Repayment Plan
Make a total of 120 qualifying monthly payments (payments need not be consecutive) on or after October 1, 2007
Be a direct employee (receiving a W-2) of the qualifying employer or employed under a contract in a position that cannot be filled by direct employees under applicable state law
Have Direct Loans that are not in default
Be employed full-time by a qualifying employer at the time of application for forgiveness
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Public Service Loan Forgiveness & Temporary Expanded PSLF Certification & Application form using the PSLF Help Tool at StudentAid.gov/pslf or manually. The PSLF Help Tool allows you to search the PSLF Employer Database to verify employer eligibility, prepare and electronically sign the form, and request electronic signature from your employer. For manual submission, download the form, complete all sections, sign it, have your employer complete and sign Section 5A (Employer Certification), and submit to the U.S. Department of Education via mail to P.O. Box 300010, Greenville, TX 75403, fax to 540-212-2415, or online upload at StudentAid.gov. Certify your employment annually and whenever you change employers or employment status. The Department may contact your employer to verify employment before granting forgiveness.

One contract covers homemaking services for consumers in the Southern area of the County, and one contract covers the Northern area of the County.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Provision of homemaking and home health personal care services including personal care, light housekeeping, grocery shopping, meal planning and preparation, assistance with dressing, bathing, hair washing, bed making, therapeutic exercise, and assistance with walker and medical equipment.

All employees must be bonded
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available for pick-up Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. from the Prince George's County Department of Family Services, Harriett Hunter Building, 6420 Allentown Road, Camp Springs, Maryland 20748. A pre-bid conference will be held on Thursday, August 24, 2017 at 9:00 a.m. Attendance is strongly encouraged.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing temporary relief care services for eligible individuals and families needing respite care support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Respite Care Program provides temporary relief care services for eligible caregivers and individuals. Services may include in-home respite care assistance or facility-based respite care options to provide temporary relief to primary caregivers. The program offers trained respite care workers to supervise and care for individuals, allowing primary caregivers to take a break from their caregiving responsibilities.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Prince George's County Department of Social Services
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and families needing temporary respite care services, including caregivers of elderly individuals, individuals with disabilities, and children requiring supervised care.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Temporary relief care services provided by trained respite care workers, including in-home respite care and facility-based respite care options.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Prince George's County
Must meet income eligibility requirements
Must complete Respite Care Program Application form
Primary caregiver must be identified
Individual requiring respite care must meet service eligibility criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed Respite Care Program Application to Prince George's County Department of Social Services. Application should include demographic information, caregiver details, individual needing care information, and service needs assessment. Contact the department for current application status and available services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provided financial assistance to Prince George's County restaurants and food service establishments to help them recover from the COVID-19 pandemic. Grants supported long-term sustainability and resiliency, COVID-19 safety measures, and operation at reduced capacity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $25,000 provided to support COVID-related costs including working capital (rent, payroll, job training), purchase of equipment and services to expand outdoor dining (tents, heaters, warmers, carts), capital or leasehold improvements such as HVAC system upgrades to improve air quality, interior improvements to support social distancing (sneeze guards, protective shields, transaction windows, tables/chairs), technology and marketing to support carryout and delivery, purchase of PPE and disposable food containers and utensils, sanitization services, and operating expenses such as rent, payroll, inventory, insurance, and utilities. Applicants must identify intended use of funds by completing an expense chart. Grant funds are reported as taxable income and IRS 1099 Forms are issued to grant recipients.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit restaurants, food trucks, catering establishments, and licensed farm stands in Prince George's County that were negatively impacted by COVID-19 and meet the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) definition of a small business. Sole proprietors, 1099s, and independent contractors are eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital including rent, payroll, and job training; purchase of equipment and services to expand outdoor dining such as tents, heaters, warmers, and carts; capital or leasehold improvements such as HVAC system upgrades to improve air quality; interior improvements to support social distancing such as sneeze guards, protective shields, transaction windows, tables/chairs; technology and marketing to support carryout and delivery; purchase of personal protective equipment (PPE) and disposable food containers and utensils; sanitization services; and operating expenses including rent, payroll, inventory, insurance, and utilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have a physical location in Prince George's County, Maryland and demonstrate a principal business office or location physically located in Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Physical location must be in Prince George's County
Must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Not be in bankruptcy or litigation
Have incurred financial losses caused directly or indirectly by the COVID-19 public health emergency
Must be a for-profit entity including corporations, partnerships, cooperatives, and sole proprietors
Sole proprietors, 1099s, and independent contractors are eligible
Must meet U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) definition of a small business
Primary function of the business must be food service
Must have a physical location evidenced by a Food Service Facility License/Permit
Food trucks and catering companies are eligible if they have a physical location
Restaurants currently closed must commit to reopening within 30 days of receipt of funds
Franchises must be independently owned and operated
Can own and apply for multiple restaurant locations with separate addresses and food service licenses/permits
Complete online application required
Evidence of Good Standing required
Food Service License or Permit required
Copy of voided check required
Articles of Incorporation, Organization, or Formation required
Operating Agreement (with all amendments) required for Limited Liability Companies
Partnership Agreement (with all amendments) required for partnerships
Bylaws (with all amendments) required for corporations
Sole proprietors must provide trade registration documents or business EIN Number (Federal Tax ID Number) to substantiate business status
Expenses identified should be consistent with eligible use of funds and equal the grant amount requested
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submitted a complete online application with evidence of good standing, food service license or permit, copy of voided check, and articles of incorporation or formation. Sole proprietors must provide trade registration documents or business EIN Number (Federal Tax ID Number). Applicants identified intended use of funds by completing an expense chart. Applications were reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis and grants were awarded on a rolling basis. Recipients were notified by email, and upon notification, recipients had to sign a Grant Agreement with non-negotiable terms and submit required documents. Funds were electronically deposited through ACH bank payment within 14 days of completing the Grant Agreement. Recipients were required to certify that all information was accurate.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps people aged 55 years and older put their skills and experience to work in their communities through volunteer work. Volunteers choose how much time they want to serve, from a few hours to up to 20 hours each week in various roles focused on helping individuals achieve healthy futures.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Mileage reimbursement up to $30 per month, orientation and on-the-job training, and secondary accidental and personal liability insurance. Volunteers can serve from a few hours to up to 20 hours per week.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People aged 55 years and older who are willing to help people of all ages and ethnicities and serve in Prince George's County communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Volunteer work in nursing homes, assisted living facilities, hospitals, non-profit services, hospice care, health insurance assistance, helping seniors remain in their homes, and transportation services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be at least 55 years old
Must be willing to help people of all ages and ethnicities
Must be willing to serve in Prince George's County communities
Must be willing to use their gifts and talents to help others
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Download the RSVP Registration Form and submit it to enroll in the program. Contact the Aging & Disabilities Services Division at 301-265-8450 for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: Used to finance the construction of a manufacturing or commercial facility for a private user. The county receives bond authorization from the State of Maryland to issue non-housing industrial development revenue bonds for authorized projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Non-housing industrial development revenue bonds issued by the county to finance construction of manufacturing or commercial facilities. Authorized projects include manufacturing facilities with a total project cost of less than $10 million.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction of manufacturing or commercial facilities.
