requirements_list: Manufacturing facilities must have a total project cost of less than $10 million
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Financial Services Program Manager to discuss bond financing options and eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Revitalization Tax Credit (Redevelopment and Revitalization Tax Credit)
structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that encourages redevelopment and investment in existing communities of Prince George's County by providing relief from county real property taxes on the incremental assessed value created by qualified improvements to real property. The credit is available for eligible improvements located within designated Revitalization Tax Credit Districts (including inner-beltway census tracts where median household income does not exceed the County's median) and phases in over multiple years at varying rates depending on whether improvements are residential or non-residential. Eligible improvements include construction, reconstruction, extension, or new development of non-residential and residential structures requiring a county building permit.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Non-residential properties receive a 100% tax credit on the incremental county property tax value in year 1, declining to 80% in year 2, 60% in year 3, 40% in year 4, and 20% in year 5. Residential properties receive 100% in year 1, 66% in year 2, and 33% in year 3, with a maximum of $200,000 in eligible improvements per dwelling unit. The credit applies to county property taxes on the increased assessment resulting from qualified improvements. Application must be filed with the Director of Finance no later than October 1 of the tax year the property becomes eligible, along with proof of a use and occupancy permit and a legal description of the property.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: October 1 of the tax year the property becomes eligible
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and developers making qualified improvements to residential or non-residential real property in designated Revitalization Tax Credit Districts within Prince George's County, including inner-beltway census tracts where median household income does not exceed the County's median. County Council approval is required for developments of ten or more single-family dwellings and for multifamily units.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax relief against county property taxes on the incremental value created by qualified real property improvements, including construction, reconstruction, extension, or new development of non-residential and residential structures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Improvements must be located within a designated Revitalization Tax Credit District established by the County Council, including census tracts inside the Beltway where the median household income does not exceed the County's median household income. Districts are selected based on factors including median household income, residential density, land use, economic factors, and unemployment rates.
requirements_list: Property must be located within a designated Revitalization Tax Credit District in Prince George's County
Improvements must be qualified real property improvements that increase assessed value and require a county building permit

Eligible improvements include: construction, reconstruction, or extension of non-residential structures; reconstruction or extension of existing residential structures; construction or reconstruction of new single-family residential structures on lots where a structure was razed or demolished within the prior 5 years or on vacant lots between adjacent single-family residential structures; and new construction in developments of less than 10 single-family dwellings
For residential developments of ten or more single-family dwellings and for multifamily units, County Council approval is required
Maximum eligible residential improvements are capped at $200,000 per dwelling unit
Application must be made under oath using the form provided by the Director of Finance and filed no later than October 1 of the tax year the property becomes eligible
Application must include a legal description of the property and proof of a properly issued use and occupancy permit applicable to the eligible improvements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application must be made under oath using an application provided by the Director of Finance and filed with the Director no later than October 1 of the tax year the property becomes eligible. The application must provide a legal description of the property, proof of a properly issued use and occupancy permit applicable to the eligible improvements, and such other information as the Director may require. Contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 to speak with a Business Development Specialist, or contact the Office of Finance, Treasury Division at 301-952-4030, or the EDC Financial Services Program Manager Andre Plummer at applummer@co.pg.md.us / 301-583-4650 for additional guidance.

structured_extraction.program_description: A commercial real estate and equipment loan program available to established business owners seeking to purchase owner-occupied commercial real estate. Loans are guaranteed by the U.S. Small Business Administration.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SBA-guaranteed loans for established business owners to purchase or finance owner-occupied commercial real estate, construction, machinery and equipment. Loan terms are 20 years for real estate and 10 years for machinery and equipment. Typically a 10 to 20 percent cash down payment is required with personal guaranties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Established business owners seeking to acquire or finance fixed assets such as commercial real estate, machinery and equipment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Commercial real estate acquisition, construction, machinery and equipment financing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
requirements_list: Business must be more established
Personal guaranties typically required
10 to 20 percent cash down payment typically required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Financial Services Program Manager to inquire about SBA 504 loan availability and application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Free confidential business mentoring and advice provided by working and retired executives and business owners. SCORE offers start-up guidance for new businesses, business plan templates, access to free business tools and templates, and training workshops and webinars.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free confidential business mentoring and advice from experienced business counselors. Services include start-up guidance, business plan templates, access to free business tools and templates, and training workshops and webinars.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small business owners and entrepreneurs, including those starting new businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mentoring, business planning, and training services

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call 301-583-4650 to make an appointment with a SCORE mentor at the EDC.

structured_extraction.program_name: School Facilities Surcharge Exemption for Studio and Efficiency Apartments Near Transit
structured_extraction.program_description: An exemption program that eliminates the school facilities surcharge fee entirely for studio and efficiency apartment units in designated areas near public transit in Prince George's County. The program is designed to encourage affordable housing development near public transit and in approved transit overlay zones by relieving developers and builders from the surcharge otherwise assessed on new residential construction permits.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Studio apartments and efficiency apartments are fully exempt from the school facilities surcharge fee. Without this exemption, the surcharge would otherwise be $15,489 per unit outside the Capital Beltway or $9,035 per unit inside the Capital Beltway or abutting a WMATA mass transit rail station, as of Fiscal Year 2015. The exemption applies to dwelling units classified as studios or efficiency apartments in qualifying locations, eliminating the fee assessed on new residential construction permits for those units.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and builders creating studio and efficiency apartment units in Prince George's County near public transit or in approved Transit District Overlay Zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The surcharge exemption is a fee abatement that eliminates the school facilities surcharge assessed on new residential construction permits for qualifying studio and efficiency apartment units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Studio and efficiency apartment units located within one-quarter mile of a metro station, within an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ), or in other limited circumstances as determined by the county.
requirements_list: Dwelling unit must be classified as a studio apartment or efficiency apartment
Property must be located within one-quarter mile of a metro station, within an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ), or meet other limited circumstances as determined by the county
Building permit must be issued for new residential construction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 to speak with a Business Development Specialist for more information about eligibility and the application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: School Facilities Surcharge Reductions for Multifamily Housing Near Transit
structured_extraction.program_description: A reduction program that lowers the school facilities surcharge fee by 50% for multifamily residential properties located near public transit in Prince George's County. Eligible areas include properties within one quarter mile of a metro station, the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ). The program is designed to incentivize transit-oriented development by reducing the cost burden of the school facilities surcharge on new residential construction and redevelopment.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The school facilities surcharge for multifamily residential properties is reduced by 50%. Outside the Capital Beltway, the surcharge is reduced from $15,489 per unit to $7,745 per unit. Inside the Capital Beltway or for buildings within a basic or conceptual site plan abutting an existing or planned WMATA mass transit rail station, the surcharge is reduced from $9,035 per unit to $4,518 per unit (rates as of Fiscal Year 2021). The reduction applies to new residential construction for which a building permit is issued, as well as qualifying redevelopments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and builders creating multifamily residential properties near public transit in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The surcharge reduction is a fee abatement that applies to the school facilities surcharge assessed on new residential construction permits and qualifying redevelopments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Multifamily properties located within one-quarter mile of a metro station, within the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or within an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ) in Prince George's County.
requirements_list: Property must contain multifamily residential units
Property must be located within one-quarter mile of a metro station, within the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or within an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ)
Building permit must be issued for new residential construction
Property must be a multifamily residential development or redevelopment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 to speak with a Business Development Specialist for more information about eligibility and the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County offers reductions and exemptions on school facilities surcharge fees for eligible residential developments, as required by Maryland State Law and ordinances enacted by the Prince George's County Council. The school facilities surcharge is a fee applied to new residential developments or redevelopments to cover anticipated increases in public educational services required to accommodate residents brought by new development. Qualifying developments can receive a 50% reduction in the surcharge or a full exemption depending on location and housing type. Surcharge amounts are annually adjusted based on the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multifamily residential properties within ¼ mile of a metro station, in the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or in an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ) receive a 50% reduction in school facilities surcharge fees. Studio apartments and efficiency apartments in properties within ¼ mile of a metro, in an approved TDOZ, or in other limited circumstances are fully exempted from the school facilities surcharge. Surcharge fees are subject to annual adjustments based on the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers of new residential developments or redevelopments in Prince George's County, as well as businesses and organizations subject to school facilities surcharge fees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Surcharge reductions and exemptions apply to school facilities surcharge fees charged on new residential units, providing surcharge relief rather than funding for specific uses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland. Reductions apply to multifamily properties within ¼ mile of a metro station, in the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or in an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ). Exemptions apply to studio and efficiency apartments within ¼ mile of a metro, in an approved TDOZ, or in other limited circumstances. Different surcharge amounts apply for properties inside versus outside the Capital Beltway or abutting WMATA mass transit rail stations.
requirements_list: For reductions: multifamily residential property located within ¼ mile of a metro station, in the Bowie MARC Station Community Center Designation Area, or in an approved Transit District Overlay Zone (TDOZ)
For exemptions: studio apartment or efficiency apartment in a property located within ¼ mile of a metro, in an approved TDOZ, or in other limited circumstances
Property must be a new residential development or redevelopment subject to school facilities surcharge
Surcharge fees are adjusted annually according to the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Economic Development Corporation at 301-583-4650 and ask to speak with a Business Development Specialist, or contact the EDC's Financial Services Program Manager, Andre Plummer, at applummer@co.pg.md.us or 301-583-5067 for details about eligibility, reductions, and exemptions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Assisted Living Subsidy Program (Prince George's County)
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides financial assistance to low-income older adults who need help paying for placement in an assisted living facility. This enables them to live in the community instead of a nursing facility. The assisted living facility offers congregate meals, housekeeping, personal services, and 24-hour supervision.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding for placement costs in assisted living facilities for eligible low-income older adults.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income older adults age 62 and older who are Prince George's County residents and meet income and asset limits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To pay for placement in an assisted living facility that provides housing, meals, housekeeping, personal services, and 24-hour supervision.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County residents only.
requirements_list: Be at least 62 years old
Be a Prince George's County resident
Meet income guidelines not to exceed $4,350 per month (individual)
Meet asset guidelines not to exceed $20,064 (individual) or $24,400 (couple)

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Community Service Employment Program (SCSEP/Title V)
structured_extraction.program_description: A work-based training program providing part-time employment opportunities at local community service agencies for older residents of Prince George's County who are unemployed and have poor employment prospects. The program offers personal and job-related counseling, job training, job referral services, and supportive services to help participants find employment. SCSEP providers also educate employers about the benefits of hiring older workers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Part-time work-based training opportunities at local community service agencies. The program provides paid employment for senior interns while offering personal counseling, job training, job referral services, and other supportive services to help participants secure employment in the community.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Prince George's County Department of Family Services, Aging & Disabilities Services Division
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unemployed residents of Prince George's County who are at least 55 years old, have poor employment prospects, and meet income eligibility requirements. Veterans and their eligible spouses are encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Participants receive part-time paid employment while receiving job training and supportive services including personal and job-related counseling, job training, and job referral assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County residents only.
requirements_list: Be a resident of Prince George's County
Be at least 55 years of age
Be legally eligible to work in the U.S.
Be unemployed with poor employment prospects
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Qualified individuals may apply regardless of employment history or educational level. Accepted individuals participate in part-time work-based training at a host agency while receiving supportive services and counseling to help secure employment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Nutrition Program - Congregate Meal Component
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that serves hot nutritious meals to seniors at various congregate settings such as senior centers, religious facilities, senior housing, and community centers. Participants may receive transportation to local nutrition sites and have access to recreational and educational programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides subsidized hot nutritious meals at congregate sites, with optional transportation provided to eligible seniors. Each meal meets at least one-third of the Recommended Dietary Allowances for older adults and follows the Dietary Guidelines for Americans. Participants also have access to recreational and educational programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents who are at least 60 years of age, or spouses aged 60 and older of program participants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidized meal programs and related nutrition services at congregate sites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Be a Prince George's County resident
Be at least 60 years of age, or have a spouse that is 60 years of age and attends the Senior Nutrition Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the senior center or congregate nutrition site of your choice to make reservations. Site-specific contact information is listed above for each location.

structured_extraction.program_name: Senior Nutrition Program - Home-Delivered Meal Component
structured_extraction.program_description: A meal delivery program that provides hot meals to homebound older adults in Prince George's County. Meals are delivered to the recipient's door five days a week. Each meal meets at least one-third of the Recommended Dietary Allowances for older adults and follows the Dietary Guidelines for Americans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides prepared, nutritious hot meals delivered five days per week to the home of eligible homebound seniors. The intent is to help residents remain in their own home.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Prince George's County residents who are at least 60 years of age and homebound, or spouses aged 60 and older of program participants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Subsidized meal delivery to homebound seniors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Be a Prince George's County resident
Be at least 60 years of age, or have a spouse that is 60 years of age and attends the Senior Nutrition Program
Be homebound
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Aging & Disabilities Services Division at 301-265-8450 for enrollment information and to arrange meal delivery through one of the Meals-on-Wheels program locations.

structured_extraction.program_description: A guaranteed revolving loan fund available to established businesses with at least 3 to 5 years of profitable operating history. The program assists emerging growth companies seeking to expand into new markets or overcome expansion challenges.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Guaranteed revolving loans for established businesses seeking general working capital, leasehold improvements, inventory, equipment purchases (not rolling stock), and human capital increases for business expansion. Businesses must have at least 3 to 5 years of profitable operating history.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Established businesses seeking financing to expand their operations into new markets.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General working capital, leasehold improvements, inventory, equipment purchases, and human capital increases for business expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County
requirements_list: Business must be established
At least 3 to 5 years of profitable operating history required

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial support for solar and energy efficiency upgrades to reduce energy costs and emissions.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Solar energy installation and energy efficiency upgrades
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County

structured_extraction.program_description: Free spay and neuter surgeries for pets of county residents in low-income communities. Funding is provided through a grant from the Maryland Department of Agriculture.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free spay and neuter surgical services to individuals who cannot afford them. Services are provided through a grant from the Maryland Department of Agriculture. A numbered voucher is issued to the applicant for use at Spay Spot. The service must be used within 30 days of authorization or the voucher becomes null and void. Funding availability may vary as monies do not come from the County's General fund.

Application must be filled out correctly

structured_extraction.program_description: A cohort-based training program designed for entrepreneurs, small business owners, and individuals thinking about starting or growing their business in Prince George's County. Participants receive structured guidance and tools covering business plan and brand identity development, startup legal and tax obligations, financial literacy and funding strategies, target customer identification, go-to-market strategy development, and key resources for sustaining long-term operations. The program concludes with a Business Speed Coaching Event featuring one-on-one expert sessions with industry leaders, as well as Q&A interest sessions and ongoing support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A structured cohort-based training series covering business planning and brand identity development, startup legal and tax obligations, financial literacy and funding strategies, target customer identification, and go-to-market strategy development. The program also provides key resources guidance for sustaining long-term operations and concludes with a Business Speed Coaching Event featuring one-on-one expert sessions with industry leaders. Q&A interest sessions are available prior to cohort selection, and ongoing support is provided throughout. No direct financial assistance is provided to participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Entrepreneurs, small business owners, and individuals thinking about starting or growing a business in Prince George's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and business support services including business planning, brand identity, legal and tax guidance, financial literacy, funding strategies, market research, go-to-market strategy, and long-term operational support. Funds are not directly distributed to participants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Prince George's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be thinking about starting or growing a business
Must be interested in launching or growing a business in Prince George's County
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an application through the Jotform link provided. Q&A interest sessions are available prior to cohort selection. structured_extraction.program_description: A summer employment program administered by Prince George's County that connects young people ages 14–24 with enriching and constructive paid work experiences in community organizations, private sector companies, and government agencies throughout Prince George's County. Participants gain meaningful work experience, develop job skills, receive job readiness training, explore diverse careers, network with industry leaders, and earn income. The program is funded in part through a U.S. Department of Labor – Employment and Training Administration grant and runs for approximately 6 weeks. Host organizations serve as worksites for youth participants, with the County providing financial support for participant wages and related services including transportation subsidies and technology access to bridge the digital divide. Youth can participate in various training and career exploration programs tailored to their age group.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Youth ages 14–24 receive summer employment with wages paid through the program. Hourly participants ages 16-17 earn $13.00/hour with maximum 32 hours per week; ages 18-24 earn $15.00/hour with maximum 40 hours per week. All hourly pay includes FICA tax withholding. For stipend-based training programs, participants receive one-time stipend payments: ages 14-15 receive $300, ages 16-17 receive $400, and ages 18-24 receive $500 upon completion of 75% of required coursework. The program runs approximately 6 weeks (2025 program: July 1 - August 8; 2026 program: July 6 - August 14), with multiple pay dates during and after the program period. Payments are made via direct deposit or by check mailed to home address. The program is funded in part through a U.S. Department of Labor – Employment and Training Administration grant. The County also provides subsidies that may cover transportation costs and technology access to bridge the digital divide. Host employers hire young people directly or serve as designated worksites, with the County providing financial support for participant wages and related services. Appropriate agreements (Referral Agreement for corporate partners or Memorandum of Understanding for nonprofit and government partners) are established with host organizations. Business partners may also provide sponsorships: Capstone Sponsorships fund program curriculum, workforce training and transportation costs; Student Sponsorships fund individual students' full employment at nonprofit locations at levels including Fulfilling the Promise Partner ($5,000 per youth ages 16-22), Prince George's Pride Partner ($3,500 per youth ages 14-15), and Transportation Partner ($1,500 for transportation support).

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wages earned through summer employment in community organizations, private sector companies, and government agencies. Funds also support transportation subsidies, technology access, and employment opportunities for youth participants. Program funding supports curriculum, workforce training, job readiness training, professional development, career exploration activities, and networking opportunities.

Must meet eligibility requirements to be entered into random lottery selection

Organizations must complete the annual SYEP Partner Participation Survey by January 30

Host organizations must provide Certificate of Insurance with minimum $1,000,000 Commercial General Liability (including sexual abuse and child molestation coverage), $1,000,000 Commercial Auto Liability, and Maryland Statutory Workers' Compensation and Employers' Liability coverage
Organizations must submit IRS Form W-9
Organizations must have a Personnel Policy addressing Sexual Harassment and Workplace Disturbances
For nonprofits: Prince George's County Government must be listed as additional insured on General Liability policy

Selected participants must complete onboarding documentation including W-4, MW507 (for hourly participants), I-9 Eligibility to Work Verification (in-person), Work Permit for Minors (ages 14-17), Workplace Harassment Avoidance Training video and acknowledgment, Code of Conduct Acknowledgement Form, and Direct Deposit Form or US Bank Card Acknowledgement by program start date or position will be forfeited
Participants must report to work on time, sign in with supervisor, and make themselves visible during working hours
For stipend-based programs, participants must maintain visual identification on virtual platforms using legal first and last name
For stipend programs, completion of 75% of required coursework including all assignments and projects is required to receive stipend payment
Stipend participants must have all absences approved in advance by supervisor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For youth applicants, follow a 6-step process: 1) Select the SYEP application based on your age group (14-15, 16-17, or 18-24); 2) Create a NEOGOV username and password; 3) Complete all screens on the application; 4) Certify the information is accurate; 5) Submit by March 31, 2026 at 11:59 pm; 6) Receive email confirmation of submission. Applicants ages 18-24 should attach a resume and supporting documents (licenses, awards, certificates). Eligible candidates are entered into a random lottery, and employment offers are extended to randomly selected youth until all positions are filled. Selected candidates receive eligibility notices April 1-11, with selection, placement, and job offers April 21 - June 30. Host sites may request former participants with exemplary performance. Onboarding for selected participants occurs April 21 - June 30 (or applicable dates for 2026 program). For organizations interested in becoming host employers or sponsors, email SYEPPartners@co.pg.md.us to make an inquiry. Prospective partners must complete the annual SYEP Partner Participation Survey by January 30. Once selected, appropriate agreements (Referral Agreement for corporate partners or Memorandum of Understanding for nonprofit and government partners) will be prepared and partners must provide required documentation including Certificate of Insurance, IRS Form W-9, and Personnel Policy. The program provides partner information sessions monthly throughout the year. Youth participants should set up a professional email address, gather personal information (Social Security Card, photo ID, birth certificate), open or prepare a bank account for direct deposit, identify job/career interests, set up a professional voicemail greeting, and prepare a resume (for ages 18+) before applying.

structured_extraction.program_description: Tax Increment Financing (TIF) is a mechanism that helps fund public improvements related to economic development, such as parking facilities, roadways, stormwater management, and other public infrastructure within designated districts. When a development or redevelopment project creates additional tax revenues, the county can issue bonds to pay for public improvements and finance those bonds through the incremental increase in revenue that the project will generate. The county delineates a project area and declares a base year; tax revenues from assessed value above the base year attributable to the new project are remitted to a special fund and used to pay debt service for identified improvements.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county issues bonds to pay for public improvements such as roads, parking, and stormwater management. These bonds are financed through the incremental increase in tax revenue that the development project generates. The county delineates a project area and declares a base year. Tax revenues from assessed value above the base year that is attributable to the new project are remitted to a special fund and used to pay debt service for identified improvements. Projects within pre-designated TIF Districts have increased certainty of approval, though exact terms must be negotiated with the county.

structured_extraction.program_description: Prince George's County provides funds to civic, neighborhood, community and homeowner organizations, local municipalities and libraries for planting native trees and shrubs in public or common areas. The program supports park and playground plantings, memorial and street tree plantings, and stream reforestation projects throughout Prince George's County, while providing a hands-on opportunity for residents to learn how to properly plant and care for trees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Community-based projects (civic, neighborhood, community and homeowner associations and libraries) receive up to $5,000 per project, and municipalities receive up to $10,000 per project. The program requires a 50 percent match (cash or in-kind contribution). Funds are disbursed to the applicant after project completion on a reimbursement basis. Eligible expenditures include plant material, tree protectors, gator bags, site preparation costs (soil amendment and invasive plant removal), planting costs, protective fencing and mulch. Costs per plant including soil amendment, gator bags and other expenditures cannot exceed $150 for a 5 foot tall/5 gallon tree. Volunteer time can be used as an in-kind match at a rate of $25 per hour. Applications are accepted on a continuous basis.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: WesBanco offers relief loans up to $5,000 with no payments for up to 90 days (45 days in PA) for federal employees affected by government shutdowns. The loan has an 18-month repayment period with an Annual Percentage Rate (APR) of 7.00% as of October 2, 2025. The monthly payment for the maximum loan amount at the maximum term with 90 days to first payment would be $296.71. There are no loan fees or closing fees. Approval is subject to WesBanco's standard underwriting.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Federal employees in Prince George's County and other areas served by WesBanco who are experiencing financial challenges due to a federal government shutdown.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial relief during periods of reduced income or employment disruption caused by federal government shutdowns.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available at all WesBanco locations, with specific availability varying by state (90 days to first payment in most states, 45 days maximum in PA).
requirements_list: Must be a federal employee
Must have been financially affected by the government shutdown
Subject to WesBanco's standard underwriting approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications for the Federal Relief Loan are being taken over the phone or in-person at all WesBanco locations. Contact WesBanco at 800-905-9043 to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A temporary and permanent employment program for young adults ages 18 to 24 who previously participated in the Summer Youth Enrichment Program. The program offers entry-level positions in Prince George's County government agencies to retain talented youth, fill staffing gaps, and develop a pipeline of career-ready professionals. The program provides exposure to job and career opportunities within Prince George's County Government that may lead to permanent positions and long-term careers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides temporary and permanent employment opportunities for youth ages 18 to 24 in entry-level government positions across eight career pathway disciplines: Budget Management and Finance, Community and Customer Relations, Environmental Services, Government Operations, Health and Human Services, Infrastructure and Development, Information Technology, and Public Safety. Interns work full-time or part-time (typically 40 hours per week) in Prince George's County government agencies for 6-month job assignments at an hourly rate of $18.00 per hour. The program is funded through a U.S. Department of Labor Community Projects Grant of $3,000,000 with a performance period of June 1, 2024 to May 31, 2027, projected to fund 20 interns in 2024, 37 in 2025, and 25 in 2026. Interns participate in monthly cohort and individual check-ins, professional development training, mentorship from agency staff, capstone project development, quarterly performance reviews, and have the opportunity to transition to permanent County employment upon successful completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young adults ages 18 to 24 who are residents of Prince George's County and previously participated in the Summer Youth Enrichment Program (SYEP), and who are transitioning from high school or college into employment
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Employment in entry-level government positions within Prince George's County agencies across multiple career pathways including budget management, community relations, environmental services, government operations, health and human services, infrastructure and development, information technology, and public safety. Interns gain real-world work experience, develop professional skills, receive mentorship, participate in professional development training, and work on capstone projects that address real County issues.

Must have a driver's license for certain positions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible participants complete and submit the Youth@Work Internship Program application through the government jobs portal at governmentjobs.com between August 26, 2025 and September 9, 2025. Applicants must attach a resume and complete a short summary explaining their reason for wanting to participate in the program. All instructions must be followed carefully and all required information must be included before submission. Applications will be screened by hiring managers. Selected candidates will be contacted and interviewed by agency representatives between September 17 and October 3, 2025. Not all applicants will be granted an interview, and interviews do not guarantee selection. Hiring managers will select and onboard candidates who are approved for positions. Selected candidates must attend orientation including New Employee Orientation Program (NEOP) and Youth@Work Internship Program orientation before reporting to their work assignment on October 21, 2025. Two interested youth information sessions are available on August 20, 2025 and September 3, 2025 to learn more about the program.

The program is coupled with state energy incentives and follows successful completion of energy-efficiency measures. Eligible costs include any parts, components, or accessory equipment necessary to operate and/or install the device.

structured_extraction.program_name: CatalystQ – The Catalyst for Minority Business Excellence in Queen Anne's County
structured_extraction.program_description: CatalystQ is Queen Anne's County's minority business accelerator program designed to help minority entrepreneurs start, grow, and succeed by addressing key barriers including access to capital, business knowledge, legal and regulatory compliance, and professional networking. The program was launched in 2023 as a pilot program supporting five minority entrepreneurs and has been expanded with renewed funding to serve 5-10 participants. The program provides selected minority-owned businesses with an intensive experience including hands-on coaching, mentorship, micro-grants for strategic growth initiatives, and connections to professional service providers. Participants receive guidance on business planning, marketing, networking with financial and professional services providers, and strategic growth. The program includes regular in-person sessions, one-on-one support from experienced professionals, access to Small Business Development Center consultants, accountants, lawyers, and other subject matter experts. Graduates receive certificates of completion and continuing education credits.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each of the 5-10 selected minority-owned businesses receives a micro-grant for strategic growth initiatives aligned with their needs (mini-grants are restricted and cannot be used for working capital or equipment purchases), plus hands-on business coaching and mentorship. The program is an intensive 3-6 month experience including regular in-person sessions, mentoring, and one-on-one support from experienced professionals. Technical assistance areas include: Accounting & Bookkeeping (required), Legal Advice & Services (required), Marketing/Communications/Branding/Public Relations (required), Strategic & Business Planning (required), Human Resources & Payroll Services (required), Access to Capital & Banking Education (required), and optional services such as Customer Data & User Experience Analytics, IT, Website Development, Business Funding Pitch & Grant Writing, Supply Chain & Procurement, E-Commerce, and Innovation/Technology Adoption. Entrepreneur support services include: Entrepreneurship and Business Start-Up Training (required), Mentorship Programming and Networking Opportunities (required), workshops on critical business topics, assistance registering a business, training on licensing processes, DEDI Directory/MBE certification preparedness, business readiness for government contracting, and translation services. Participants receive access to mentors, Small Business Development Center consultants, accountants, lawyers, and other subject matter experts. Program facility is provided by the county. Graduates receive certificates of completion and continuing education credits. Total funding is up to $100,000 to support program delivery through at least December 2025, with program continuation anticipated beyond that date.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: RFP Submission Deadline: August 4, 2025 (for service providers/contractors); Business application deadline: September 12, 2025, with applications due by 5pm
structured_extraction.program_audience: Minority entrepreneurs and minority-owned small businesses (particularly underrepresented and early-stage entrepreneurs) operating in or based in Queen Anne's County, Maryland, who are interested in scaling their ventures, developing their businesses, joining a network of minority entrepreneurs, and addressing barriers to business growth. Service providers and qualified organizations seeking to deliver the program are also welcome to submit proposals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Micro-grants for strategic growth initiatives aligned with the business's mission (grants are restricted and cannot be used for working capital or equipment purchases); business planning, marketing collateral creation, and establishing professional relationships with local banks, accountants, insurance providers, and attorneys; access to capital, business knowledge, legal and regulatory compliance, and networking support; technical assistance in accounting, bookkeeping, legal services, marketing, communications, branding, strategic planning, human resources, payroll, IT, website development, business funding/grant writing, supply chain and procurement, e-commerce, and innovation; entrepreneur support services including training, mentorship, networking, business registration assistance, licensing support, and government contracting readiness.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Queen Anne's County, Maryland only. Businesses must be based in or operating in Queen Anne's County to be eligible. The program specifically targets minority entrepreneurs and underrepresented small business owners in Queen Anne's County.

QACETD leads all outreach, promotion, and participant selection. Selected participants are notified on September 15th, and the program begins in September 2025 (after Labor Day) with regular in-person sessions thereafter. Selected participants attend regular sessions, participate in mentoring, and receive one-on-one support from the contractor and professional service providers. FOR SERVICE PROVIDERS/CONTRACTORS: RFP Submission Process: Qualified entities including non-profit organizations, for-profit entities, trade associations, institutions of higher education, and co-working space operators are invited to submit proposals. Submit proposals via mail with one original and one digital version (PDF) on a flash drive by August 4, 2025 to: Queen Anne's County Economic & Tourism Development, 425 Piney Narrows Road, Chester, MD 21619. Questions should be directed via email to Heather Tinelli at htinelli@qac.org by July 25, 2025; responses will be posted on July 28, 2025. Proposals selected for interviews will be notified by August 8, 2025. Contract award and project planning begins August 15, 2025 with program start anticipated for early September 2025. Reporting will be required on program outcomes, participant progress, and financial expenditures as specified in the contract. Billing frequency and retainer details will be determined with the selected vendor based on workplan and deliverables. Change orders may be considered post-award to adjust timeline and content based on participant needs.

structured_extraction.program_description: A work-based learning program that builds and maintains career pathways between Maryland job-seekers and Maryland businesses through a nationally recognized registered apprenticeship and training program. Participants receive on-the-job training and related classroom instruction through an approved employer in eligible career track occupations related to in-demand industries including manufacturing, science, technology, engineering and math (STEM). Participants complete 450 hours of paid employment and 141 hours of related instruction, with opportunities to advance within the business upon completion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible employers hire youth apprentices and provide paid on-the-job training and related classroom instruction in eligible career track occupations. The program requires 450 hours of paid employment with the approved business and 141 hours of related instruction, creating an 'earn and learn' opportunity. Employers must be approved by the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council (MATC). An apprenticeship navigator from the Maryland Department of Labor works with the employer to develop and navigate the program. Upon completion, employers offer opportunities for advancement within the business. The program is designed to reduce turnover costs, increase job satisfaction, and increase employee productivity while developing a pipeline of highly skilled workers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school students seeking work-based learning experiences in eligible career tracks and employers in manufacturing, STEM, and traditional apprenticeship industries looking to develop a trained workforce and plan for employee succession.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid on-the-job training and related classroom instruction for youth participants in eligible career track occupations, including skill development in manufacturing, STEM, and traditional apprenticeships.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in Queen Anne's County and Kent County, Maryland. Employers must be located in close proximity to local school systems selected to participate in the Apprenticeship Maryland Program.
requirements_list: Business must be approved by the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council (MATC)
Youth must be approved and enrolled through participating high school systems
Eligible employer must have an apprentice position available for a high school student in one of the eligible career tracks
Youth must complete 450 hours of paid employment with the approved business
Youth must complete 141 hours of related instruction
Employer must have expected future entry-level job openings in eligible career track occupations
Employer must provide paid compensation to create an 'earn and learn' opportunity
Employer must offer opportunities for advancement within the business following completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers begin by contacting the Youth Apprenticeship Navigator or Queen Anne's County Career Technology Liaison. Step 1: Complete a brief online Eligible Employer Application through the Maryland Department of Integrated Technology portal at https://www.doit.state.md.us/selectsurvey/EligibleEmployer#. This initial application goes directly to Bob Zimberoff, the Youth Apprenticeship Navigator, who will contact the employer. Step 2: The Youth Apprenticeship team works with the employer to complete the full application. Step 3: The application is submitted to the Maryland Labor Secretary for review. Step 4: If initially approved, the Secretary forwards the application to the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council (MATC) for consideration and final approval. Step 5: MATC conducts an expedited review in consultation with MD Labor's Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning, who notify the Secretary of the decision. Step 6: Employer receives final determination of eligibility. Step 7: Join the Apprenticeship Maryland Program and begin developing your apprenticeship pipeline.

structured_extraction.program_description: Established by Queen Anne's County Commissioners, the Economic Development Incentive Fund (EDIF) provides financial assistance to support the growth of existing businesses and attract or enhance businesses that complement Queen Anne's County's major industry sectors. The fund offers loans, conditional loans (which can convert to grants when job creation targets are met), and grants to businesses starting, expanding, or relocating to Queen Anne's County. Strong consideration is given to businesses in Advanced Manufacturing, Agriculture and Seafood, Technology, and Hospitality and Tourism industries. Projects must demonstrate significant economic impact consistent with the County's development goals, such as job creation and retention, increased production, and potential for niche markets.
structured_extraction.agency: Queen Anne's County Economic Development Incentive Fund Commission
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund offers $1.1 million in cash incentives through conventional commercial loans and conditional loans. Conditional loans can convert to grants when job creation requirements are met or exceeded. Assistance is typically available in amounts up to $50,000 for equipment acquisition and workforce development. Additionally, $240,000 is allocated specifically for workforce development support. Funding requests are reviewed at the discretion of the EDIF Commission, with disbursement authorized by the County Commissioners as program funding is available. Applicants may request assistance for various business purposes including equipment acquisition, working capital, real estate acquisition or improvement, and workforce development.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications may be submitted online through the SeamlessDocs online application portal at https://qacmd.seamlessdocs.com/f/qacedifapplication or by downloading and completing the paper application form and mailing it in. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Fund (MAERDAF)
structured_extraction.program_description: MAERDAF provides grants to rural-serving nonprofit organizations and community colleges that promote statewide and regional planning, economic and community development, and agricultural and forestry education. The program aims to increase the overall capacity of these organizations and community colleges to meet rural development challenges and help them establish new public and private partnerships for leveraging non-state sources of funding. Rural community colleges that support small and agricultural businesses through enhanced training and technical assistance are also eligible. Combined heat and power is an eligible expense.

In FY2014, $167,000 total was dispersed among nine awardees with grants ranging from $5,650 to $25,000. Priority is given to applicants that have secured matching funds from non-state sources, though matching is not required. Federal funds are considered matching funds. Projects must serve more than one rural county.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to help foster growth in Wicomico County's emerging and existing agriculture and resource-based industries. It is a partnership between Salisbury-Wicomico Economic Development (SWED), Wicomico County, PNC Bank, and the Maryland Agricultural & Resource Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO). The program provides financial assistance to for-profit agricultural and resource-based businesses through a cost-share model where applicants must contribute at least 50% of project costs.
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Targeted grant amounts are typically $2,500 or less per applicant, matched equally by MARBIDCO on a cost-share basis. Applicants must contribute at least 50% of total project costs. MARBIDCO cannot invest more than the local government (SWED) share. Special caps apply: Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) matching grants capped at $5,000; deer fences and farm operation solar systems or generators capped at $3,000. Maximum of $25,000 in total grants per government jurisdiction per fiscal year. Grants are provided on a reimbursement basis after project completion and receipt of eligible receipts. Funds are one-time payments. Minority-owned, women-owned, disabled-owned and veteran-owned businesses are encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit existing and emerging agricultural and resource-based businesses headquartered and located in Wicomico County, Maryland. Minority-owned, women-owned, disabled-owned and veteran-owned businesses are encouraged to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible uses include: agri-tourism (new or expansion of current initiatives); agricultural business diversification (new or expansion of current initiatives); deer fencing (specifications determined by MARBIDCO); equipment and facilities that assist Wicomico County's farming, forestry, or seafood industries; production, packaging, processing, or marketing of agricultural products that grow in soil or water. Ineligible uses include operating expenses in the ordinary course of operations, personal expenses, refinancing, loan payoffs, and vehicles.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be headquartered and located in Wicomico County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must be for-profit
Business must be existing or emerging
Business must be headquartered and located in Wicomico County, Maryland
Business must be registered and in Good Standing with the State of Maryland
Business must be in Good Standing with Wicomico County, Maryland

Project must assist Wicomico County's farming, forestry, or seafood industries (including agritourism) or facilitate production of foodstuffs or other goods that grow in soil or water, or involve packaging, processing, or marketing of such products
Applicant must make a financial contribution of at least 50% of project cost
Business must currently be in operation
Applicant must be in compliance with federal, state and local laws and remain in compliance
Businesses engaged in illegal activity per local, state or federal regulations are excluded
Publicly-traded firms are ineligible
Only one entity (including related entities) may apply for funds in any given year
Locally-owned franchises of national chains are eligible if locally owned and controlled and meeting all other criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact SWED at 410-749-1251 to discuss your project. 2. Submit a completed application along with a W-9 form to info@swed.org. 3. SWED reviews the application to determine if it fits within MARBIDCO's program criteria. 4. If eligible, SWED submits the application along with a cover letter requesting consideration to MARBIDCO. 5. MARBIDCO makes the final approval decision at its sole discretion. 6. If approved, the applicant is notified and may begin the project. 7. Upon project completion, the applicant notifies SWED and provides receipts for eligible expenses. 8. SWED reviews documentation and issues reimbursement check for the agreed-upon grant amount. Grant funds are provided on a reimbursement basis only after all documentation and receipts have been received.

structured_extraction.program_name: SBA Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) - Francis Scott Key Bridge Collapse
structured_extraction.program_description: The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) provides low-interest, long-term Economic Injury Disaster Loans to help small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small aquaculture businesses, and private nonprofit organizations overcome temporary loss of revenue and meet working capital needs resulting from the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse. Loans up to $2 million are available to cover normal operating expenses such as fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills that cannot be paid because of the disruption caused by the disaster.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest, fixed-rate disaster loans up to $2 million to help small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small aquaculture businesses, and private nonprofit organizations overcome temporary loss of revenue. Interest rates are 4% for businesses and small agricultural cooperatives, and 3.25% for private nonprofit organizations, with terms up to 30 years. Interest does not accrue until 12 months from the date of first disbursement, and repayment begins 12 months from the date of first disbursement. Funds can be used to pay normal operating expenses including fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills that cannot be paid because of the disruption caused by the bridge collapse. The actual loan amount is limited to the economic injury determined by SBA, less business interruption insurance and other recoveries. SBA may waive the $2 million statutory limit if a business is a major source of employment. Eligibility is based on the financial impact of the disaster only, not on actual property damage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small aquaculture businesses, and private nonprofit organizations impacted by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse in Maryland and contiguous counties in Delaware, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and the District of Columbia.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Normal operating expenses such as fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills that cannot be paid because of the disruption caused by the disaster; working capital needs during the disaster recovery period. Loans cannot be used to refinance long-term debts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties (Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Baltimore City, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, Worcester); contiguous counties in Delaware (Kent, New Castle, Sussex); District of Columbia; contiguous Pennsylvania counties (Fulton, Franklin, Adams, York, Bedford, Fayette, Lancaster, Somerset, Chester); contiguous Virginia counties (Arlington, Alexandria, Loudoun, Accomack, Fairfax); and contiguous West Virginia counties (Morgan, Berkeley, Jefferson, Hampshire, Mineral, Grant, Preston).
requirements_list: Must be a small business, small agricultural cooperative, small business engaged in aquaculture, or most private nonprofit organization
Must have experienced economic injury or temporary loss of revenue caused by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse
Eligibility is based on the financial impact of the disaster only, not on any actual property damage
Business must have been affected by the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse
Must have acceptable credit history and demonstrate ability to repay the loan
Must be a small business without the financial ability to offset the adverse impact without hardship
Previous SBA loan borrowers must have complied with the terms of previous SBA loans, including maintaining required flood insurance and/or hazard insurance
Borrowers whose damaged or collateral property is located in a special flood hazard area must purchase and maintain flood insurance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants may apply online using the MySBA Loan Portal at https://lending.sba.gov or through sba.gov/disaster. Applications can also be completed in person at SBA Business Recovery Centers. Two centers are available in Baltimore County: (1) CareFirst Engagement Center, 1501 South Clinton Street, Baltimore, MD 21224, and (2) Dundalk Renaissance Center, 11 Center Place, Suite 201, Dundalk, MD 21222. Both centers opened Monday, April 1, 2024 with initial hours 1 p.m. to 6 p.m. Regular hours are Monday–Friday 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. (Closed Sundays). Customer Service Representatives assist with completing applications, accepting documents, and providing status updates. For additional information, call SBA's Customer Service Center at (800) 659-2955 or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov. For people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides low-income and income-eligible households with monthly financial assistance toward broadband internet and mobile services. Through participating providers such as Comcast Xfinity, eligible households receive a monthly credit toward their internet and mobile service bills, helping them afford reliable connectivity. Qualified households on Tribal lands receive an enhanced benefit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible low-income households receive a monthly credit of up to $30 toward Internet and Xfinity mobile services from participating providers. Qualified households located within Tribal lands receive up to $75 per month. The benefit is applied directly to the household's broadband service bill through a participating internet service provider. Internet Essentials offers two service tiers: Internet Essentials at 50/10 Mbps ($9.95/month before ACP credit, $0 after credit) and Internet Essentials Plus at 100/10 Mbps ($29.95/month before ACP credit, $0 after credit). Both include equipment rental fees. Xfinity Mobile unlimited service is available at $45 per line per month, or $24.95/month for Internet Essentials with one Xfinity Mobile Unlimited line when ACP is applied. If a customer has both Internet and Xfinity Mobile service, the ACP benefit is first applied to the Internet portion, with any remaining balance applied to Xfinity Mobile services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income and income-eligible households in Somerset County who qualify for federal benefit programs and are seeking affordable broadband and mobile internet service. Must be 18 years of age or older and meet certain eligibility criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Monthly support toward broadband internet service and mobile service bills from participating internet service providers, including Comcast Xfinity. Can be used for high-speed internet service ranging from 50 Mbps to 100 Mbps depending on service tier selected.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Somerset County, Maryland, including qualifying Tribal lands, with service available through participating providers in the area. Service is limited to areas where Comcast Internet service is available.
requirements_list: Recipient of National School Lunch Program benefits
SNAP recipient
Medicaid recipient
Federal Public Housing Assistance recipient
Lifeline program recipient
Federal Pell Grants recipient
WIC recipient
Other eligible federal benefit program recipients
Household must live in an area where Comcast Internet service is available
Must be 18 years of age or older
Have not had Comcast Internet service within the last 90 days (waived if enrolling in ACP with Comcast)
No outstanding debt to Comcast that is less than one year old (waived if enrolling in ACP with Comcast or through June 30, 2022 for Internet Essentials applicants not enrolling in ACP)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process has three main steps: Step 1 - Check ACP eligibility by completing the National Verifier form at acpbenefit.org or by calling 833-511-0311. Save the National Verifier Application ID. Step 2 - Apply for Internet Essentials at InternetEssentials.com or call 1-855-8-INTERNET (1-855-846-8376). The online application can be completed from a mobile device and is available in multiple languages including English, Spanish, Chinese Traditional, Chinese Simplified, Russian, Somali, and Arabic. Applicants can verify identity using a Social Security number, Alternate ID, or text messaging verification. After approval, equipment will be delivered within 7-10 business days. Step 3 - Complete the Xfinity ACP enrollment form at Xfinity.com/acp using the National Verifier Application ID to receive the ACP credit. Expect a status update within 48 hours of applying for ACP. Existing Xfinity or Internet Essentials customers can apply for ACP by completing Steps 1 and 3 only. Application status can be checked by visiting InternetEssentials.com and clicking 'Application Status.'

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Stretch Program for Difficult to Serve Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial assistance to help unserved and underserved Maryland households access high-speed, affordable internet, particularly those in areas with geographic challenges, long driveways, or distance from existing broadband infrastructure that discourage internet service providers from delivering service. The program includes specific assistance for properties with difficult-to-access locations such as long driveways in Somerset County, and extends statewide to all Maryland jurisdictions through partnerships with local governments and internet service providers. The program aims to bridge the digital divide and foster digital equity by delivering high-speed broadband service with minimum speeds of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provide funding to extend broadband service to unserved and underserved properties. The Difficult to Serve - Long Driveway Grant specifically assists properties that are challenging to reach. In the first round, $19.6 million in Fiscal Year 2024 awards were distributed to help approximately 2,400 unserved Maryland households access high-speed internet. Grant amounts range from a minimum of $500,000 to a maximum of $9,000,000 per eligible project. Applicants must provide a cash match of at least 5% of actual capital construction costs. Funds are provided to local jurisdictions and internet service providers to close broadband infrastructure gaps. Eligible uses include: installation or extension of fiber optic facilities, installation of end user facilities including wiring and wireless access points, and educational and technical assistance outreach to support adoption. Free broadband service via WiFi connectivity must be extended through all common areas of housing communities with minimum speeds of 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload. Non-capital administrative costs are capped at 1% of total project costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications due December 15, 2023; Awards anticipated February 2024; Projects must be completed by June 30, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Unserved and underserved Maryland households and covered populations including: individuals living in households with income less than or equal to 150% of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers (English learners and those with low literacy levels), and individuals who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups. Also includes local jurisdictions (county and municipal) and public housing authorities that own and maintain public housing for low- and moderate-income households. Somerset County property owners with internet speeds below 25 Mbps are specifically targeted.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Broadband infrastructure installation and extension including: extension of fiber optic facilities to publicly owned housing structures, installation of interior wiring to individual units within publicly owned housing, installation of wireless access points in public and common areas to provide free internet service, electronic equipment necessary for distribution of broadband service, minor building modifications necessary for final distribution of broadband service, network engineering and design services, all broadband networking equipment (hardware and software), low voltage contracting work, installation and provisioning labor costs, taxes and shipping costs directly related to broadband network equipment. Also covers educational support and technical assistance including ACP registration assistance and broadband adoption outreach.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland jurisdictions are eligible. In the first round, 18 jurisdictions received awards and every jurisdiction that applied received funds. Priority focus on publicly owned housing developments identified as having a need for broadband investment, particularly those lacking access to connections that reliably meet or exceed minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds (or 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload if scalable to symmetrical speeds). Somerset County properties that are currently unserved or underserved with internet speeds below 25 Mbps are specifically eligible.
requirements_list: Property must be unserved (without access to high-speed internet) or underserved (below 25 Mbps)
Property must be in a difficult-to-serve area due to geographic challenges or distance from broadband infrastructure
Applicant must be a local jurisdiction (county or municipal) or public housing authority that owns and maintains publicly supported housing for low- and moderate-income households
Projects must be able to provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds measured at each dwelling unit
Applicant must agree to maintain and secure project equipment and technology and acquire necessary hardware warranty and service agreements for at least 5 years after project completion
Applicant must provide a minimum cash match of 5% of actual capital construction costs
Applicants must include community engagement costs as part of grant applications to provide ACP registration assistance and/or educational assistance
All equipment purchased must be new and non-depreciated
Free broadband service via WiFi must be provided through all common areas of housing communities
Wireless access points must be installed in public and common areas providing free internet service to residents who cannot afford wired service or cannot subscribe due to past billing issues
Projects must include open access wired network infrastructure designed to facilitate accessibility for all service providers
Internal wiring infrastructure must be designed for open access use
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local jurisdictions apply in partnership with Internet Service Providers by submitting a complete electronic PDF application to osb.md@maryland.gov. Required application components include: completed application form, project summary with executive summary describing the public housing location and how it was chosen, statement of experience demonstrating applicant's capability and past network deployments, detailed network design including technology type and speed capabilities, community profile with demographic data and engagement strategies, subscriber cost information if applicable, discussion of potential barriers, partners and local engagement plan, implementation schedule with major milestones and risks, and detailed line item budget on the Capital Budget form. Applications are reviewed for completeness and eligibility. Awards are made based on scoring criteria evaluating project description, community need, organizational capacity, partnerships, budget reasonableness, schedule feasibility, and sustainability. Scoring is on a maximum of 40 points, with awards made high to low score as funding permits.

structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County offers a property tax incentive program to stimulate and encourage investment in commercial real property located in designated challenged areas. When commercial property owners invest at least 10% of the assessed value (minimum $25,000) in renovations, rehabilitation, and upgrades, the program freezes property taxes for 7 to 10 years depending on investment level. The program targets areas including the Lexington Park Development District, Charlotte Hall Town Center, and the Town of Leonardtown Downtown area.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property taxes are held constant (frozen) for either 7 or 10 years depending on the investment level. If investment is 10–15% of the property's assessed value, taxes are frozen for 7 years. If investment is 16% or more of assessed value, taxes are frozen for 10 years. The total value of assessment reduction may not exceed 25% of the property's assessed valuation at the time of award. After the incentive period ends, the property owner pays taxes based on the current rate and assessed value. The minimum investment is $25,000 and must be at least 10% of the assessed value.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners in St. Mary's County located in designated challenged areas including the Lexington Park Development District, Charlotte Hall Town Center, and the Town of Leonardtown Downtown area, seeking to invest in property improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovations, rehabilitation, and upgrades of commercial real property, including: exterior improvements to building façades, exterior painting and cleaning, structural improvements, structure-mounted signage, canopies, shutters and awnings, screening of utility and storage enclosures, enhanced exterior lighting, replacement or enhancement of streetscape amenities such as walkways, landscaping, bike racks and lighting, sidewalks, and new construction that enhances the building or property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties must be located in designated challenged areas within St. Mary's County, including the Lexington Park Development District (primary targeted area), Charlotte Hall Town Center, or the Town of Leonardtown Downtown area. Projects must be in alignment with the Lexington Park Development District Master Plan and St. Mary's County Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance.
requirements_list: Must be a commercial property owner
Property located in a designated challenged area (Lexington Park Development District, Charlotte Hall Town Center, or Town of Leonardtown Downtown area)

Minimum total investment of $25,000
Total value of assessment reduction may not exceed 25% of the property's assessed valuation at time of award
Eligible investments must be a one-time investment occurring within a 12-month period
Project must involve renovations, rehabilitation, or upgrades to commercial real property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Property Tax Challenge application form (available online at the St. Mary's County website) with project details, investment amount, property information, and economic benefit description. The application is a first formal step toward county consideration. Award of an incentive is subject to approval by the Commissioners of St. Mary's County. Completion of the application does not guarantee approval.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Housing subsidies to help pay rental costs for individuals requiring assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals requiring assistance with rental costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact The Housing Authority, St. Mary's County, Maryland to learn more about the program.
