structured_extraction.program_description: Helps seniors live with dignity and in the comfort of their own homes at lower cost than care at a nursing facility. Eligible individuals receive a comprehensive assessment of their needs performed by a registered nurse, case management to secure and coordinate services, and access to a limited pool of gap-filling monies to help fund services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides case management services and financial assistance for eligible seniors. Case management and assessments are performed by a registered nurse. Assistance includes gap-filling monies to help fund: durable medical equipment, emergency response systems, loaned equipment, incontinent supplies, nutritional supplies, financial assistance for prescriptions, and other services. Funding is limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis subject to a waiting list.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Seniors age 65 or older who are current residents of St. Mary's County, meet income and asset requirements, are severely or moderately disabled as determined by nursing assessment, and are at risk of nursing home placement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Case management, durable medical equipment, emergency response systems, loaned equipment, incontinent supplies, nutritional supplies, prescriptions, and other gap-filling services to support seniors remaining in their homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County only. Applicants must be current residents of St. Mary's County.
requirements_list: Age 65 or older
Current resident of St. Mary's County
Meet income and asset guidelines
Severely or moderately disabled as determined by nursing assessment tool
At risk of entering a nursing facility as determined by nursing assessment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the St. Mary's County Department of Aging & Human Services Maryland Access Point (MAP) at 301-475-4200, ext. 1057 to inquire about the program or request a referral. Upon contact, individuals are screened to determine eligibility. Those appearing eligible will be contacted by a Local Health Department nurse to schedule an in-home assessment. The assessment is presented to the Senior Care Steering Committee team to determine if the client meets eligibility criteria and to develop a plan of care. The plan outlines current services and needed services, then is forwarded to a case manager for implementation. Each Senior Care client is assigned a case manager responsible for implementing the care plan and monitoring status. A waiting list for Senior Care may apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides older adults with door-to-door transportation to medical appointments, social engagements, shopping, and other destinations using volunteer drivers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides door-to-door transportation service using volunteer drivers in personal vehicles. Riders are charged suggested donations based on distance: $10 for trips less than 15 miles, $15 for 15-30 miles, $20 for 31-50 miles, and $50 for outlying destinations (Annapolis, Baltimore, Washington D.C.). Service is limited to 4 trips per month per rider. Riders must request trips at least 3 business days in advance for in-county destinations and 5 business days for out-of-county medical-only destinations. Transportation requests are not guaranteed and can only be accommodated if a driver is available. The program is funded through a grant from the Maryland Transit Administration and the Commissioners of St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Adults age 60 and older who are St. Mary's County residents with low to moderate income, unable to use public transportation, and lacking reliable transportation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation to medical appointments, social engagements, shopping, and other destinations within and outside the county (out-of-county trips limited to medical purposes).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to St. Mary's County residents age 60 and older. Out-of-county trips are limited to medical-only destinations (Annapolis, Baltimore, Washington D.C.).
requirements_list: Be 60 years of age or older
Be a St. Mary's County resident
Have a low to moderate income not exceeding $5,216 per month for an individual or $7,050 for a couple
Have cognitive awareness and the ability to ambulate using a cane or walker (wheelchairs cannot be accommodated)
Lack access to reasonable, affordable transportation
Must use other forms of public transportation when available and when appropriate
Complete the Senior Rides Application Form
Sign release/waiver form
Be ready at time of pickup
Be prepared to pay all tolls, parking, or other fees incurred on the trip (suggested donations based on distance)
Wear seatbelt
Be courteous
Transportation to procedures requiring anesthesia and/or excessive wait times will be considered at the time of request
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Senior Rides Application Form, which can be completed by phone, in-person, or mail. Provide information including date of birth, street address, emergency contact, income verification, and any mobility aids or disabilities. Sign the required Ridership Release/Waiver form. Once accepted into the program, riders request transportation at least 3 business days in advance for in-county trips or 5 business days for out-of-county medical trips.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Shore Erosion Control Program provides technical and financial assistance to public and private property owners dealing with shore erosion problems. The program helps prevent sediment loss, reduce pollution, protect and restore tidal marshes, and protect structures and improvements along shorelines. It supports both structural projects (though structural assistance for private property was terminated in 1996 and reinstated in 2002) and vegetative or non-structural projects like living shorelines.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching grants are available: 45/55 matching grants for private landowners (private pays 45%, program pays 55%) and 75/25 grants for eligible public land protection projects (public pays 75%, program pays 25%). The program also provides technical assistance for project design and management. Future maintenance is the responsibility of property owners. For living shoreline projects specifically, the program covers funding, design, and construction assistance. Annual benefit charges are levied as a special assessment on participating properties following project completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private property owners experiencing shore erosion problems in St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Shore erosion control projects including vegetative buffers, fringe tidal marshes, living shorelines, and protection of structures and improvements along shorelines
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County and other areas along the Chesapeake and coastal bays in Maryland
requirements_list: Property owner must have shore erosion problems
For living shorelines, property must have shoreline exposure
Property owners must submit a Letter of Interest (petition) indicating proposed district boundaries
At least 75% of property owners must return a Confirming Petition in support of the district to proceed
District assumes responsibility for all costs incurred after establishment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Property owners submit a Letter of Interest (petition) to create a Shore Erosion Control District, indicating district boundaries. 2. The Letter of Interest is forwarded to DNR Shore Erosion Control for consideration. 3. DNR prepares a Need & Feasibility Report including proposed work and preliminary cost estimates. 4. The County conducts an informational meeting with district property owners to review the Report. 5. The County provides a Confirming Petition to each owner detailing estimated costs and project terms. If 75% of Confirming Petitions are returned in support, the process continues. 6. A Public Hearing is conducted to establish the District by ordinance. The County countersigns applications and executes a loan agreement with the State. 7. Complete construction plans and cost estimates are prepared by DNR or consultant. 8. A Public Hearing is held by the Board of County Commissioners to present final plans and specifications. The Board determines whether to proceed. 9. Construction is advertised for bid. 10. An escrow account is established if owner cash contributions are required. 11. Construction is awarded and completed. 12. Following construction, a Public Hearing is held to fix and levy annual assessment charges, which will be paid as a special benefit assessment.

structured_extraction.program_description: Organization that supports farms and the future of agriculture in the Southern Maryland region through farmland preservation, support for regional farmers, and resources to help consumers find local farms.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Agricultural support services including farmland preservation, farmer assistance, and market development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Farmers and agricultural businesses in Southern Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Farmland preservation and agricultural development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's, Calvert, and Charles Counties

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary's County FIRE/EMS Scholarship Program Year 2025-2026
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program for active members of St. Mary's County Volunteer Fire Departments, Rescue Squads, and Advanced Life Support Units interested in pursuing extended education in fire and emergency medical services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual scholarship awards to cover tuition and course materials for post-secondary education leading to a certificate, diploma, or other evidence of qualification. Reimbursement is the lesser of the scholarship awarded or the total cost of tuition and course materials. Maximum of 36 credit hours per year. Total funding is spread amongst eligible applicants based on number of credit hours planned, cost per credit hour, and application completeness. Effective date coincides with the first day of the fiscal year (July 1, 2025).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Active members of St. Mary's County Volunteer Fire Departments, Rescue Squads, and Advanced Life Support Units pursuing extended education in fire and emergency medical services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition, course materials, and fees for post-secondary education courses leading to certificates, diplomas, or other evidence of qualification from recognized post-secondary educational facilities in fire and EMS fields. Coursework must fall within the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County. Active members must be from a St. Mary's County Volunteer Fire Department, Rescue Squad, or Advanced Life Support Unit.
requirements_list: Must be an active member of a St. Mary's County Volunteer Fire Department, Rescue Squad, or Advanced Life Support Unit
Must have met minimum program requirements for the previous calendar year in the Length of Service Award Program (LOSAP) for VFD, VRS, or ALS
Must be recommended by the President or Chief of the applicant's department
Must submit completed application on or before 31 August 2025
Must submit completed and signed Scholarship Agreement (Agreement No. ESB26)
Must submit completed IRS W-9 form
Must submit copy of acceptance letter into post-secondary education institution (not required if follow-on application from previous year applicant)
Must submit copy of acceptance into clinical portion of studies if applicable
All documents must contain original signatures in blue ink or digitally encrypted date-stamped electronic signatures
No faxed copies accepted
Upon registration: must provide registration receipt and bookstore receipts indicating tuition and course material costs
Upon course completion: must provide institution's grade report showing satisfactory completion with minimum 2.0 grade on 4.0 scale
Upon completion of yearly LOSAP paperwork: must provide document signed by President, Chief, or authorized designee verifying LOSAP requirements met
Must repay St. Mary's County if reimbursed by another Maryland State award program for amounts exceeding total tuition and book costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Obtain application materials from St. Mary's County Emergency Services. 2. Complete the application form ensuring all items are answered and all required attachments are included. 3. Complete the Scholarship Agreement (Agreement No. ESB26) by entering your name on the first page and signing and printing your name on the second page with the date. Leave all other fields blank. 4. Prepare completed IRS W-9 form. 5. Obtain and copy acceptance letter into post-secondary education institution (not required if follow-on applicant). 6. If applicable, obtain and copy acceptance into clinical portion of studies. 7. Submit all documents to: St. Mary's County Emergency Services, Attention: Angel Clem, P.O. Box 653, Leonardtown, MD 20650-0653. 8. Ensure receipt by 31 August 2025. 9. Emergency Services Board reviews and makes recommendations to Commissioners of St. Mary's County for approval. 10. Upon award, submit registration receipt and bookstore receipts within one month of enrollment. 11. Upon course completion, submit grade report within two weeks. 12. Upon completion of yearly LOSAP paperwork, submit LOSAP verification document. 13. County processes scholarship payment request. 14. Applicants must resubmit valid application for each school year the scholarship is requested for renewal consideration. Notification of scholarship status anticipated on or about 30 October 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary's County Façade and Streetscape Improvement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that reimburses commercial property and business owners for a portion of expenses incurred when rehabilitating buildings, storefronts, and streetscapes in designated revitalization areas. The program aims to create positive visual impact, stimulate private investment, improve safety, and complement community revitalization efforts in the historic commercial core of Lexington Park and Charlotte Hall.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses 50 percent of eligible project costs, with a maximum reimbursement of $6,000 per project. The grant is limited to one application per address per calendar year. Minimum project cost is $1,000 to qualify for a $500 reimbursement. Projects must be completed within six (6) months from the date stated in the executed Grant Agreement. Grant funds are issued on a reimbursement basis via direct deposit after project completion and approval. If final project costs are less than estimated, reimbursement is 50% of the lower cost. If final project costs exceed estimates, the grant amount remains as initially approved and cannot increase.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners and tenants with written authorization from the property owner located in designated revitalization areas (Lexington Park Downtown and Great Mills Corridor, and Charlotte Hall Sustainable Communities designation) in St. Mary's County. Eligible properties must be non-residential, mixed-use, industrial or office uses, or vacant and zoned in Commercial, Mixed-use, Industrial or Office Districts. Home occupation businesses are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Facade repairs and streetscape improvements visible from a public right-of-way or shared parking facility, including: cleaning and repair of building exteriors, masonry cleaning and repointing, exterior paint or finishes, replacement of deteriorated windows, doors, siding and framing, restoration of exterior architectural details for historic buildings, installation or repair of ordinance-compliant signage and exterior lighting, removal/repair/installation of awnings/canopies/shutters, removal of roll-down security gates, ADA-compliant exterior and site accessibility improvements, and landscaping improvements on or adjacent to the premises visible from the public right-of-way.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the Façade and Streetscape Grant Area in Lexington Park (as delineated in the Lexington Park Master Plan as the Downtown and Great Mills Corridor) and the Charlotte Hall footprint of the Sustainable Communities designation. Only work on facades visible from a public right-of-way or a shared parking facility are eligible for grant funding.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the designated Façade and Streetscape Grant Area in Lexington Park or Charlotte Hall
Proposed work must align with eligible reimbursement projects as outlined in Program Guidelines
Applicants must obtain cost estimates from licensed and insured contractors
Work must be on facades visible from a public right-of-way or shared parking facility
Minimum project cost of $1,000 to qualify for minimum $500 reimbursement
Reimbursement is 50 percent of project cost with a maximum of $6,000
Limited to one application per address per calendar year
Applications must be complete and accurate; incomplete applications may result in ineligibility
Property owner written permission is required if application is submitted by a tenant/business owner
Must be for non-residential, mixed-use, industrial, office uses, or vacant properties zoned Commercial, Mixed-use, Industrial or Office Districts
Home occupation businesses are not eligible
Work completed prior to approval and Letter of Commitment is not eligible for funding
Project must be completed within six (6) months from the date stated in the executed Grant Agreement
Applicant is responsible for obtaining all required building permits and site plans
Projects must comply with Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation if building is on St. Mary's County inventory of Historic Structures
Any building code compliance violations must be corrected as part of the proposed improvement work
Changes to scope of work must be pre-approved by the Review Committee
Applicant must maintain the property and improvements after completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Verify the property is located within the Façade and Streetscape Grant Area using the provided Lexington Park map and Charlotte Hall Sustainable Communities designation. 2. Confirm the proposed work aligns with eligible reimbursement projects by reviewing the Program Guidelines. 3. Obtain cost estimates from licensed and insured contractors. 4. Identify the requested reimbursement amount (50 percent of project cost, maximum $6,000, minimum qualifying project $1,000). 5. Gather all required documents as listed in the sample application. 6. Submit a complete application through the online form. Note: Applications cannot be saved and must be completed in one session. 7. A Review Committee will review the application and coordinate approval from state authorities (including Maryland Historical Trust if applicable). 8. If approved, receive a Letter of Commitment specifying the grant amount and any conditions of approval. 9. Complete the project within six (6) months from the date in the Grant Agreement. 10. Submit a Project Completion Report including photos of completed work and proof of payment. 11. DED staff will review the report and conduct a site visit. 12. Upon verification of consistency with approved work, reimbursement request is submitted to DHCD. 13. Once DHCD approves and transmits funding, direct deposit reimbursement is processed. For questions, contact Lee Greely by email or phone.

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary's County Senior Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County provides a property tax credit for senior citizens of limited income on their dwelling.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A property tax credit applied to the dwelling tax bill for qualifying senior citizens.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Senior citizens age 70 and older with limited income
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax bill reduction
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County
requirements_list: Age 70 or older as of July 1 of the tax year in which application is submitted
Household taxable net income equal to or less than $80,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available at all senior activity centers.

structured_extraction.program_description: A transportation program for elderly people and persons with disabilities in Maryland who are not close enough to public transportation routes. The program provides general-purpose door-to-door transportation and encourages efficient coordination of transportation services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State grant funding (between $130,000 to $175,000 per year with required local match) provides door-to-door transportation service via wheelchair accessible buses or county cars. Fares are $3.00 one-way or $6.00 for a round trip with discounts available for seniors. Extra stops beyond the one included stop per round trip are charged at $3.00 per additional stop. Service operates Monday through Friday in five zones throughout St. Mary's County to serve elderly and disabled residents. One attendant may accompany riders free of charge; additional attendants or companions require payment of $3.00 each. Payment (cash, check, or SSTAP tickets) is required at pickup time with exact change; drivers do not make change. Cancellations made the day before are accepted at no cost. Drivers provide curb-to-curb or door-to-door service (if requested in advance) and can assist passengers but do not enter homes, shop, or assist with shopping. All vehicles are wheelchair accessible with platform lifts accommodating wheelchairs, walkers, crutches, and those with difficulty climbing steps (capacity 600 pounds).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elderly people and persons with disabilities in St. Mary's County who lack sufficient access to public transportation routes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Door-to-door transportation to medical appointments (prioritized on a first-come, first-served basis), senior nutritional centers, shopping, social engagements, and other destinations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in St. Mary's County in five service zones: Zone 1 (Charlotte Hall, Golden Beach, Helen, Chaptico, Budds Creek, Wicomico, Clements), Zone 2 (Oakville, Loveville, Hollywood, Leonardtown, Avenue, Compton, Mechanicsville), Zone 3 (California, Lexington Park, Great Mills), Zone 4 (Piney Point, Ridge, Park Hall, Callaway, St. Inigoes), and Thursday service to all zones. Service operates Monday through Friday. ADA Paratransit service is available within ¾ mile of existing STS public transportation routes.
requirements_list: Must be elderly or a person with a disability
Must lack sufficient access to public transportation routes or meet ADA paratransit eligibility criteria

For ADA paratransit eligibility: (1) person who uses regular public transportation and needs a wheelchair accessible vehicle; (2) person unable to board, ride or disembark without assistance beyond driver assistance; (3) person with impairments preventing travel to public transportation stops; or (4) certified by transportation provider
Must complete paratransit application to qualify for SSTAP
Must present proof of age for senior discount fares
Appointments scheduled between 10:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m.
Appointments can be scheduled up to 30 days in advance
Weekly recurring appointments permitted but require weekly confirmation
Pickup locations must have wheelchair ramp or assistant, with accessible driveway and safe turnaround
Riders must be ready at scheduled time and return at designated time
Exact change payment required at pickup; drivers do not make change
One stop per round trip included; additional stops charged at $3.00 each
Passengers may carry only packages they can physically carry
Service animals only permitted animals on buses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Transportation Division at (301) 863-8400 extension 1120 or 1121 in the morning or during office hours (Monday-Saturday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.) to confirm eligibility, discuss SSTAP enrollment, and schedule appointments. Provide your name, telephone number, location, destination, date, and appointment time. Seniors need to present proof of age to receive discount fares. Special identification cards are available from the STS Transit office at 44829 St. Andrews Church Road, California, Maryland 20619. For ADA Paratransit: application forms will be mailed upon request; returned applications evaluated within 21 days; applicant notified of results within 5 days. Eligible persons receive identification card valid in other transit areas. Re-certification required every 2 years. If eligibility is denied, applicant can appeal to the Human Relations Committee within 60 days; decision made within 30 days. Cancellations accepted without cost if made the day before.

structured_extraction.program_name: U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Programs and Services for Businesses
structured_extraction.program_description: USDA provides funding opportunities for rural small businesses through loans, loan guarantees and grants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal loans, loan guarantees, and grants for rural small businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural small businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business operations and growth
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Rural areas; Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County offers incentives to citizens who volunteer at fire departments and rescue squads, including college scholarship programs, length of service awards, dependent care reimbursement, and Maryland State tax incentives after three years of service. Free training is provided for those wanting to become certified firefighters or EMTs. The program also includes a Fire and EMS Cadet Program for high school juniors and seniors partnered with the St. Mary's County Board of Education and Maryland Fire and Rescue Institute (MFRI).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers multiple incentives including free training and certifications (Firefighter, EMT, and Paramedic), Maryland income tax deductions, college scholarship programs, length of service award programs, and dependent care reimbursement. Training is provided at no cost by instructors from the Maryland Fire and Rescue Institute (MFRI) through the University of Maryland. College credits can be earned by successfully completing many of the courses offered. High school students in the Fire and EMS Cadet Program can earn Firefighter 1, Vehicle Machinery and Extrication, Hazardous Materials Operations, Firefighter 2, Rescue Technician Site Operations, and Emergency Medical Technician certifications.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Citizens interested in volunteering with St. Mary's County fire departments and rescue squads, including high school juniors and seniors for the Fire and EMS Cadet Program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Free training and certifications, incentive awards, scholarships, dependent care reimbursement, and tax benefits for volunteer firefighters and EMTs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must volunteer at a fire department or rescue squad in St. Mary's County
Must complete free training to become a certified firefighter or EMT
Tax incentive and other benefits require minimum requirements to be met
All organizations require Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) training and an orientation (pre-basic) course to get started
Active membership requires being 18 years old or older
Junior membership available for ages 16-17
Cadet membership available for ages 13-15
High school students in Cadet Program must maintain at least a C average (2.0 GPA)
Students must be a member of a volunteer fire department or rescue squad to participate in the Cadet Program
Tax incentive requires three years of service
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Emergency Services Recruitment & Retention Coordinator at 301-475-4200 ext. 2114 or fireemsrecruitment@stmaryscountymd.com for information about volunteering and eligibility for incentives. For applications and additional information, visit the websites of individual fire departments and rescue squads in St. Mary's County or contact a Membership Committee Member for full details on incentive programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Waterway Improvement Program provides grants and loans for marking channels and harbors, clearing debris from waterways, dredging channels, and constructing jetties and marine facilities that benefit the boating public. Projects improve water access, navigation, anchorage, and recreational opportunities on waterways. The program is administered through the establishment of special taxing districts in St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three funding mechanisms are available through the Maryland Waterway Improvement Fund: (1) 100% grants for projects that significantly benefit the general boating public by providing accessibility to sheltered water bodies, suitable anchorage conditions, relieving congestion, or providing water access for fueling, repair, and storage; (2) 50/50 matching grants where the State reimburses 50% of project costs and the remaining amount is recovered through district assessment; (3) Interest-free long-term loans for eligible projects. The maximum allocated by the State per year per project is $25,000. For loans and matching grants, county and resident costs are repaid through the established taxing district over a period not to exceed 25 years or the estimated service life of the improvement, whichever is less. The benefit charge constitutes a lien upon the property and shall be paid annually with county taxes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in St. Mary's County whose real property abuts a natural or artificial body of water and who seek waterway improvements that benefit the boating public
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Marking channels and harbors, clearing waterway debris, dredging channels, and constructing jetties and marine facilities. For dredging projects, property owners must identify and provide an adequate spoil disposal site.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Real property abutting a natural or artificial body of water within St. Mary's County waterways
requirements_list: Project must be eligible as described in Natural Resources Article Section 8-707 of the Annotated Code of Maryland
For 100% grants, project must provide accessibility to sheltered water bodies, suitable anchorage, improved access, or relief of waterway congestion
A petition from at least 75% of benefited property owners is required to initiate formal need and feasibility review
All co-owners of a property must sign the petition (authorized officer of a corporation may sign on behalf of corporate owner)

The value of the benefit derived from the project must meet or exceed the costs of the project to demonstrate no substantial, unreasonable, or unpalatable disproportionality between the amount assessed and the value that accrues to the land
Property owners must define the limits of the proposed Waterway Improvement District and prepare a Letter of Interest with a list and boundary map of properties to be included

After project completion, the County and Maryland Department of Natural Resources are not obligated or responsible for any future maintenance costs; future maintenance is the responsibility of the District
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Affected property owners define the district limits and prepare a Letter of Interest signed by at least 75% of properties within the proposed boundary, including a list and boundary map. 2. The County refers the Letter of Interest to the Maryland Department of Natural Resources for a Need and Feasibility Report. 3. If supported by the report, the County holds a Public Informational Meeting to present findings, estimated costs, and funding options. 4. Property owners submit a Petition (must be signed by 75% of benefited properties) that sets forth the district purpose, enumerates properties to be included, identifies the chosen assessment method, and provides approximate costs. The Petition must include an affidavit concerning property ownership. County staff must approve the Petition. 5. The Board of County Commissioners holds a Public Hearing and may establish the District by Ordinance. 6. County (in-house staff or consultant) prepares plans and specifications and obtains necessary permits. 7. The project is advertised and bid for construction. 8. A Public Informational Meeting is held to discuss design and construction costs. If bids exceed the budgeted amount, a Public Hearing must be held to amend the District budget. 9. The construction contract is executed. 10. After construction is complete, the County executes a Waterway Improvement Fund Loan Agreement with DNR and requests reimbursement. 11. A Public Hearing is held to fix the assessment (Levy Ordinance). 12. The Board of County Commissioners fixes and levies the benefit charge against each lot in the District, to be paid annually with county taxes. A person adversely affected by the establishment of a District may appeal to the Circuit Court of Maryland for St. Mary's County within 30 days of the Ordinance effective date.

structured_extraction.program_name: New and Expanding Business (NEXB) Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County offers a tax credit incentive to businesses that create at least ten full-time jobs locally. The program helps companies in targeted industries, specific locations, or underserved areas within the county. Businesses receive real and personal property tax credits for up to ten years, scaled to the number of jobs created, with a maximum benefit of $100,000.
structured_extraction.agency: St. Mary's County Department of Economic Development / Commissioners of St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses that create 10–15 new jobs receive $5,000 per year for 5 years (total $25,000). Businesses that create 16–25 jobs receive $8,000 per year for 8 years (total $64,000). Businesses that create 26 or more jobs receive $10,000 per year for 10 years (total $100,000). The credit applies to real and personal property taxes. An additional 50% reduction on county property taxes is provided for new capital investments for the duration of the credit period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and expanding businesses locating in or already operating in St. Mary's County that create at least 10 new full-time jobs, particularly those in targeted industries or underserved areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit can be applied to real and personal property tax obligations. Businesses must create new jobs and may receive additional credit for new capital investments in targeted or underserved industries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: St. Mary's County, including the Lexington Park Development District, Leonardtown Development District, Town of Leonardtown, and designated town centers.
requirements_list: Business must be in a targeted industry (Defense, Cyber Security, Aerospace and Aviation, Unmanned and Autonomous Systems, Manufacturing, Agriculture, Aquaculture, Value-Added Agriculture Products) OR locate in the County and hire at least 10 full-time employees OR be a retail, local service, or tourism-related business in a targeted investment area OR provide a service/product in an underserved area or fill a service gap
Business must create a minimum of 10 new full-time jobs locally (full-time job equivalence accepted)
Jobs must be new to St. Mary's County, not relocated from another St. Mary's County location
Business must reach the 10-job minimum within three years; credit begins only in the year the firm reaches 10 employees
Full-time job equivalence is accepted
Only taxable capital investments are eligible for the additional property tax credit
Must be a private venture
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an application to the Department of Economic Development, which can provide assistance at (301) 475-4200 ext. 71400. DED reviews the application and the Director recommends applicants for approval. Recommended requests are forwarded to the Commissioners of St. Mary's County for consideration. If approved, the applicant signs a contract outlining benefits and obligations, which is then presented to the Commissioners for final approval. For applications in the Town of Leonardtown, the Leonardtown Town Manager provides a recommendation. Submitting an application does not guarantee an award.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-supported program that provides funding to replace conventional septic tanks with nitrogen-reducing units or to connect existing dwellings to public sewer where public sewer is available.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to replace conventional septic tanks with nitrogen-reducing units or to fund sewer connections for existing dwellings where public sewer is available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners in Talbot County with existing dwellings that have septic systems or that are near available public sewer.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replacement of conventional septic tanks with nitrogen-reducing units or funding for sewer connections to existing dwellings.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Talbot County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Sanitary District Officer or visit the Bay Restoration Septic Fund program page for application details and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) - Talbot County
structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Block Grant program provides federal funding to support community development projects that benefit low- and moderate-income persons in Talbot County. Funds can be used for renovation and rehabilitation of facilities serving vulnerable populations, including food pantries, shelters, mental health centers, and other community services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Talbot County receives Community Development Block Grant funds from the federal government through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Recent awards include $75,000 to Neighborhood Service Center and $75,000 to St. Michaels Community Center (CV-1-11 COVID funding, must be spent by June 30, 2026). Funds can be used for services, staffing, food supplies, shelter improvements, appliances, equipment, and food bank facility improvements. The county administers grants to non-profit and government organizations for renovation, rehabilitation, and operational support of facilities serving low- and moderate-income residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and government agencies serving low- and moderate-income residents in Talbot County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services, staffing, food supplies, shelter improvements, appliances, equipment, food bank facility improvements, building renovation and rehabilitation for community facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Talbot County, Maryland only.
requirements_list: Funds must benefit low- and moderate-income persons
Only active subrecipients eligible for amendments
All funds must be spent by designated deadlines
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Talbot County Council holds public hearings to consider Community Development Block Grant applications and amendments. The county submits applications to DHCD for approval. Interested organizations should contact the Grants Administrator.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Repair and Reinvestment Fund supports community-based initiatives that benefit disproportionately impacted and low-income communities. The fund is supported by revenue from Maryland's adult-use cannabis tax and is designed to reinvest in communities that have experienced disproportionate impacts from past cannabis enforcement and related social and economic disparities. CRRF is grounded in a restorative justice approach to public investment and aims to repair harm and reinvest in community strength.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two grant pathways are available for the inaugural funding round (5/1/26 – 6/30/27): Pathway 1 - Small Community Grants ($10,000 maximum award; $50,000 total available) support targeted, time-limited, or transactional efforts including direct services, short-term interventions, community engagement, planning activities, and capacity-building efforts. Pathway 2 - Community Impact Grants (minimum $25,000 award; $150,000 total available) support comprehensive and transformational strategies including multi-component initiatives, strong collaborations, and approaches with clearly articulated outcomes. Ineligible uses: law enforcement agencies/activities and supplanting existing local government programs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 3/27/26 by 11:59pm via submission link (Notification of Intent due 3/6/26)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit organizations serving or benefiting disproportionately impacted and low-income communities in Talbot County. Funds must benefit Talbot County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To support community-based initiatives addressing harms from disparate cannabis law enforcement, including: community-based services and supports (early childhood education, afterschool programs, behavioral health, family support, housing stability, transportation, reentry and legal supports); economic opportunity and workforce development (workforce training, job readiness, community-based economic initiatives); and strategies that strengthen individual, family, and community well-being, expand access to services and resources, build community capacity and leadership, and contribute to long-term sustainable community change.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Talbot County, Maryland. The disproportionately impacted area identified by the Maryland Office of Social Equity is Easton (ZIP code 21601). Funding may be awarded to programs or strategies located elsewhere in Talbot County when applicants can demonstrate that the proposed work addresses similar harms and benefits communities experiencing intersecting disproportionate impact and low-income challenges.
requirements_list: Serve or benefit disproportionately impacted and/or low-income communities in Talbot County
Be a nonprofit or for-profit organization (individuals not eligible)
Demonstrate ability to successfully carry out the proposed project within the grant period
Use awarded funds to support projects that benefit Talbot County residents
Clearly describe the community or population served and how the proposed work benefits low-income and/or disproportionately impacted communities
Provide succinct, well-reasoned responses with supporting materials when directly relevant
Submit complete application and signed budget by deadline
For funded organizations: provide W-9, most recent audit or IRS Form 990, evidence of good standing with Maryland, job descriptions for positions supported by CRRF funds
Maintain background checks for staff/volunteers working with children and youth
Comply with applicable state and federal laws and regulations
Maintain sound financial management and internal controls
Commit to data collection and reporting requirements proportional to award size
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Review the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and eligibility requirements. 2. Attend the pre-application meeting on 2/10/26 at 10am via Zoom (optional but recommended) to learn about program expectations and ask questions. 3. Complete and submit the Notification of Intent to Apply form by 3/6/26. 4. Complete the application form and signed budget form with detailed cost calculations. 5. Submit complete application and budget via the submission link by 3/27/26 at 11:59pm. 6. Applications will be reviewed by a TFN Board committee using a scoring rubric emphasizing CRRF alignment and community connection. 7. Funded applicants must enter into a grant agreement with Talbot Family Network and provide required documentation. 8. Small Community Grant grantees submit mid-year and year-end reports; Community Impact Grant grantees submit quarterly reports.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY 2025 Opioid Restitution Fund Community Micro Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A one-time grant program that provides funding to non-profit organizations for initiatives addressing the opioid crisis, including school education campaigns, overdose prevention, substance use treatment, and crisis response systems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: One-time grants ranging from $1,000 to $20,000 to be used by June 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The portal for this round of funding has now closed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations with active 501(c)3 status and in good financial standing located in Talbot County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: School education campaigns to prevent opioid use, evidence-based overdose prevention and substance use treatment, crisis response systems, safe stations, and stabilization centers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Talbot County.
requirements_list: Non-profit organizations must have active 501(c)3 status
Organizations must be in good financial standing
Submit a formal letter of interest identifying the amount of funding being requested
Provide justification and identify who will benefit from the funds
Illustrate the scope of work
Provide a summary of how the proposed funding will be used to address identified objectives
Describe how the grant funds will quantify the project's success
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Non-profit organizations must submit a formal letter of interest to the Talbot County Council for consideration of Community Opioid Restitution funding. The letter must include the requested funding amount, justification, scope of work, summary of fund usage, and success metrics.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pool of federal and state funding that makes loans to small businesses to create and save jobs in western Maryland. Borrowers repay loans and the money returns to the fund to make additional loans, creating an ongoing financial tool.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $10,000 to $500,000. Interest rates are prime plus 1 percent with a 5 percent floor. Terms are up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets. Application fee is $250 (non-refundable) for loans over $25,000, or $25 for loans between $10,000-$25,000. Loan origination fee is 1.5 percent at closing for loans over $25,000, or $0 for loans between $10,000-$25,000. Collateral required includes Deeds of Trust, Machinery and Equipment liens, Personal Guarantees, and Key Man Life Insurance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit small businesses located in Garrett, Allegany, or Washington County seeking to create or expand their operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business acquisition, commercial real estate acquisition, building improvements, equipment purchase, leasehold improvements, business start-up costs, and working capital. Not eligible for real estate speculation or projects that do not create or retain permanent jobs, and projects that otherwise qualify for financing through traditional lenders or other programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to businesses located in Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties in western Maryland.
requirements_list: For-profit corporations, non-profit organizations, partnerships, or sole proprietorship located in eligible counties
Project must create or retain a minimum of one job for each $30,000 of RLF funds requested
Repayment capacity and financial strength demonstrated
Industry and management experience
Established since 1980
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit Western Maryland Revolving Loan Fund Inquiry Form and Personal Financial Statement Form. Lenders use standard underwriting practices evaluating repayment capacity, financial strength of company and guarantors, industry and management experience, and collateral protection.

structured_extraction.program_description: A pool of federal and state money that makes loans to small businesses to create and save jobs in western Maryland. The program provides gap financing to small businesses seeking to locate or expand in Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties. Borrowers repay loans and the money returns to the fund to make additional loans, creating an ongoing revolving financing source. The program operates by participating with banks and other lenders, as applicable.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loan amounts range from $10,000 to $500,000. Maximum loan terms are 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets (e.g., buildings or equipment). Interest rates are tied to the prime interest rate at prime plus 1 percent, with a floor of five percent. An application fee of $250 (non-refundable) is required for loans over $25,000, and $25 for loans between $10,000–$25,000. Approved borrowers are assessed a 1.5% loan origination fee at closing, with no origination fees for loans between $10,000–$25,000. The project must create or retain a minimum of one job for each $30,000 of RLF funds requested.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Ms. Chris Funk, Business Development Loan Officer, Tri-County Council for Western Maryland
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses — including for-profit corporations, non-profit organizations, partnerships, and sole proprietorships — seeking to locate or expand in Garrett, Allegany, or Washington counties in western Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business acquisition, commercial real estate acquisition, building improvements, equipment purchase, leasehold improvements, business start-up costs, and working capital. Ineligible uses include real estate for speculation, projects that do not create or retain permanent jobs, and projects that qualify for financing through traditional lenders or other programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties in western Maryland (Appalachian region).
requirements_list: Eligible entities include for-profit corporations, non-profit organizations, partnerships, or sole proprietorships located in Garrett, Allegany, or Washington County
The project must create or retain a minimum of one job for each $30,000 of RLF funds requested
An application fee of $250 (non-refundable) is required for loans over $25,000; $25 for loans between $10,000–$25,000
A 1.5% loan origination fee is charged at closing (waived for loans between $10,000–$25,000)
Collateral required includes Deeds of Trust, Machinery and Equipment liens, Personal Guarantees, and Key Man Life Insurance
Standard underwriting practices apply; factors include repayment capacity, financial strength of company and guarantors, industry and management experience, and collateral protection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit an inquiry form and personal financial statement. A non-refundable application fee is required for loan processing. The lender uses standard underwriting practices to evaluate the application. Loan applications are accepted on a continual basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Small Business Administration (SBA) federal program that helps small businesses located in Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZones) in urban and rural communities gain preferential access to federal procurement opportunities and contracts. Certified businesses can access set-aside awards, sole source awards, price evaluation preferences, and subcontracting opportunities. The program operates in designated HUBZone areas including all of Garrett County and designated areas in the City of Hagerstown and surrounding Washington County region.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HUBZone certification provides preferential status for federal contracting. Benefits include access to 3% of all federal prime contract dollars targeted to HUBZone businesses, set-aside awards (contracts reserved exclusively for HUBZone firms), sole source awards (contracts awarded directly to a single HUBZone firm without competition), a 10% price evaluation preference in full and open contract competitions (allows HUBZone firms to be more competitive on price), and subcontracting opportunities. In Fiscal Year 2022, HUBZone contracting government-wide was valued at $16.3 billion. The program does not directly provide funds but gives certified businesses preferential status to compete for and win federal government contracts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses located in designated HUBZone areas seeking federal contracting opportunities, including businesses in Garrett County and the City of Hagerstown/Washington County region.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Access to federal government contracts and procurement opportunities, including set-aside awards, sole source awards, and subcontracting opportunities. Funds can be used for any business purpose related to performing federal contracts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All of Garrett County has been designated as a Historically Underutilized Business Zone. Designated HUBZone areas also exist in the City of Hagerstown and the surrounding Washington County region. Businesses must have their principal office located in a designated HUBZone area and meet all other eligibility criteria. The Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department provides local resources and guidance for businesses seeking HUBZone certification.
requirements_list: Be a small business as defined by the SBA Size Standards (typically 500 or fewer employees depending on industry)
Principal office located in a designated HUBZone
At least 35% of employees must reside in a HUBZone

Be at least 51% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens, a Community Development Corporation, an agricultural cooperative, an Alaska Native corporation, a Native Hawaiian organization, or an Indian tribe
Must meet SBA eligibility criteria for HUBZone certification
No delinquent federal taxes or loans
Cannot have been debarred or suspended from federal contracting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses must be certified by the SBA before participating in the HUBZone program. Step 1: Determine eligibility using the SBA HUBZone eligibility workbook tool to organize and present information related to principal office location and employee residency. Step 2: Create a login and account on the SBA's online HUBZone application portal. Step 3: Complete and submit the certification application with required documentation. Step 4: The SBA reviews the application and determines eligibility within approximately 15 business days. Step 5: Upon approval, the business is added to the HUBZone registry and can begin bidding on contracts. Annual recertification is required to maintain certification status, and program examinations are conducted at least every three years. Businesses in Hagerstown and Washington County may also contact the City of Hagerstown Planning & Economic Development Department for additional local guidance and resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) provides low-interest federal disaster loans to help small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small businesses engaged in aquaculture, and most private nonprofit organizations recover from economic losses caused by declared disasters including flooding and drought. Loans are available to eligible entities that have suffered substantial economic injury, even if no physical damage was sustained. Funds can be used for working capital needs such as fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills not paid due to the disaster. Multiple disaster declarations have made this program available across various Maryland counties.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest federal disaster loans up to $2 million with interest rates as low as 4% for small businesses and 3.625% for private nonprofits. Loan terms can be up to 30 years, determined on a case-by-case basis based on each applicant's financial condition and ability to repay. Interest does not accrue and payments are not due until 12 months from the date of the first loan disbursement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 23, 2026 (flood disaster, PA-20019); February 2, 2026 with a 60-day grace period (drought disaster); July 1, 2024 (prior drought declaration #20069, closed)
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 1-800-659-2955 (1-800-877-8339 for the deaf and hard-of-hearing; dial 7-1-1 for telecommunications relay services)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, small businesses engaged in aquaculture, and most private nonprofit organizations located in SBA-declared disaster areas in Maryland that have suffered substantial economic injury from flooding or drought. Agricultural producers, farmers, and ranchers are generally not eligible except for small aquaculture enterprises.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital needs caused by the declared disaster, including fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills not paid due to the disaster. Covers economic injury costs resulting from flooding or drought conditions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in multiple Maryland counties depending on the applicable disaster declaration: Allegany County (flood disaster PA-20019); Baltimore, Carroll, Cecil, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, and Washington counties (drought disaster, March 15, 2025 declaration); Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, Howard, Montgomery, and Washington counties (prior drought declaration #20069). Also available in contiguous counties in Pennsylvania and Virginia under applicable declarations.
requirements_list: Must be a small business, small agricultural cooperative, small business engaged in aquaculture, or most private nonprofit organization
Must be located in a disaster-declared county
Must have suffered substantial economic injury from the applicable disaster (flooding or drought)
May apply even if no physical damage was suffered
Not an agricultural producer, farmer, or rancher (except small aquaculture enterprises) for drought-related declarations
Financial losses must be directly related to the applicable disaster declaration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online at sba.gov/disaster or download loan applications from the SBA website. Completed paper applications can be mailed to: U.S. Small Business Administration, Processing and Disbursement Center, 14925 Kingsport Road, Fort Worth, TX 76155. For assistance, contact SBA's Customer Service Center at 1-800-659-2955 or email DisasterCustomerService@sba.gov. For the deaf, hard-of-hearing, or those with a speech disability, call 1-800-877-8339 or dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services. Reference the applicable disaster number (PA-20019 for the Allegany County flood disaster; relevant drought declaration numbers as applicable).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Industrial Partnerships (MIPS) program promotes the development and commercialization of products and processes through industry and university research partnerships. It provides funding, matched by participating companies, to help Maryland companies leverage the facilities, resources, and expertise within Maryland's public universities to create new products and opportunities. The program enables both small and large companies to collaborate with researchers from any of the 13 University System of Maryland institutions to further their research and development efforts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Matching funds (grants of $100,000 or more) awarded on a competitive basis to help Maryland companies pay for university-based research. Companies must provide matching funds. Projects are initiated by companies and conducted with researchers from any of the 13 University System of Maryland institutions. In addition to funding, companies gain access to university facilities, resources, and expertise.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small and large Maryland companies seeking to develop and commercialize new products and processes through research partnerships with University System of Maryland institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: University research for the development and commercialization of new products and processes, including access to university facilities, resources, and expertise.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-based companies; program is available statewide across all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Maryland-based company
Joint proposal with researcher from a University System of Maryland institution
Local business must provide matching funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Projects are initiated by companies and submitted as joint proposals with university researchers on a competitive basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fund for investing in promising early-stage companies associated with the University System of Maryland (USM). Maryland-based companies that are affiliated with USM institutions and seeking equity financing or convertible debt financing may apply. The fund supports company growth and development across a range of industries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Equity or convertible debt financing for early-stage companies associated with the University System of Maryland. Investment funding is provided to support company growth and operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage Maryland-based companies affiliated with University System of Maryland institutions seeking equity or convertible debt financing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Company growth, development, and operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Company must be affiliated with the University System of Maryland
Company must be Maryland-based
Company must be seeking equity financing or debt financing convertible into equity

structured_extraction.program_name: Upper Shore Workforce Investment Board Incumbent Worker Training Fund (IWT)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps businesses in Kent and Queen Anne's counties pay for training for their current employees. The training should help workers improve their skills, get new career opportunities, or earn higher wages. All training must result in a credential that confirms completion. Applicants must not be contractual employees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses businesses for training costs. A company can receive a maximum of $5,000. The targeted training rate is $1,500 per individual, though this amount is negotiable.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in Kent and Queen Anne's counties that want to train their current, non-contractual employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training expenses that result in a credential confirming completion. This includes classroom training for new skills and certifications, on-the-job training, in-house training programs, and training from outside providers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to businesses located in Kent and Queen Anne's counties.
requirements_list: Applicants must have a plan to train current, non-contractual employees.
All trainings must result in a credential that confirms completion.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply using the application form provided on the program webpage, or contact Debbie Bowden at envistrallc@gmail.com for more information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides financial assistance to agricultural operations in Washington County to support innovation and equipment purchases that enhance farm productivity and modernization.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funding to support agricultural innovation and equipment purchases. Specific award amounts and terms are not detailed on this page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural operations and farmers in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Agricultural innovation and equipment purchases to enhance farm operations and productivity
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Details about the application process are available on the program's dedicated page.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that encourages landowners to enter into a ten-year agreement restricting their land from development. In return, participants receive protection from nuisance complaints through the Right to Farm Ordinance, become eligible to sell Development Rights Easements through the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Program (MALPP), and receive a property tax credit.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners voluntarily restrict their agricultural land from development for a minimum of ten years. In exchange, they receive nuisance complaint protections under the Right to Farm Ordinance, county property tax credits for farmland, farm buildings, and a partial tax credit for the home. They also become eligible to apply to sell Development Rights Easements through the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF). Tax credits are provided for the farmland, farm buildings, and partial credit for the home.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County with eligible farmland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Property tax credits for farmland, farm buildings, and partial home tax credits. Eligibility to apply for permanent agricultural preservation easement sales through MALPF.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Land must be outside water and sewer service areas and outside of growth areas.
requirements_list: Land must be a minimum of 50 acres stand-alone or 20 acres if contiguous to other districts
Land must have a minimum of 50% soil classified as Class I, II, or III
Land must be outside water and sewer service areas
Land must be outside growth areas
Land must be eligible agricultural property
Landowner must voluntarily enroll in the program
Agreement restricts land from development for minimum ten years
Land must remain in agricultural use for at least ten years from the date the agreement is recorded
Land may not be developed or subdivided for industrial, commercial, or residential use except as permitted by County regulations
Soil erosion and water quality practices must be implemented according to an approved soil conservation plan
Agreement must be notarized and recorded in County land records
All titled landowners must sign the agreement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners contact the Land Preservation Office in the Department of Planning & Zoning at 240-313-2430 or askplanning@washco-md.net. They complete an Agricultural District Intake Form providing information about the property, acreage, soils, and farming operation. The County reviews the application for eligibility. Once approved, landowners sign a notarized Agricultural Preservation District Agreement with the County's Land Preservation Office. The agreement is then recorded in the County land records. The ten-year restriction period begins upon recording of the agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides incentives and financing options for agricultural businesses and operations in Washington County, including loans for equipment and land purchases, grants for value-added producers, farmland acquisition assistance, and access to USDA funding opportunities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple financing and grant programs available: Maryland Resource-Based Industry Financing Fund offers low-interest loans (2.25% initially) up to $250,000-$750,000 for equipment, land, and processing; Rural Business Equipment and Working Capital Loan Fund offers loans at 5.25% up to $100,000; Maryland Vineyard/Hops/Orchard Fruit Planting Loan Fund at 4.50% up to $100,000; Forestry Equipment Loan Fund at 4.75% up to $150,000; Rural Business Energy Efficiency Improvement Loan Fund at 4.50% for $2,500-$30,000; Maryland Urban Agriculture Commercial Lending Incentive Grant up to $10,000; Maryland Value Added Producer Grant-Capital Assets Option $2,500-$10,000; Next Generation Farmland Acquisition Program for down-payment assistance; USDA Farmers Market Promotion Program $50,000-$500,000 with 25% match; USDA Local Food Promotion Program $25,000-$500,000 with 25% match; USDA Rural Development Grants $10,000-$500,000; USDA Value Added Producer Grants $75,000-$250,000; Regional Food System Partnership Program $100,000-$1,000,000 with 25% match; Community Food Projects $35,000-$400,000 with 100% match; Rural Energy for America Program for renewable energy and efficiency; Maryland Agriculture Water Quality Cost Share Program covering up to 87.5% of BMP installation costs; Maryland Agricultural Education and Rural Development Assistance Fund up to $40,000.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by program; MVAPG-CAO and USDA VAPG offered annually; Community Food Projects available in April with June deadline
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural businesses, beginning farmers, forest products businesses, rural small businesses, food processors, and agricultural cooperatives in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition, equipment purchases, working capital, building construction, energy efficiency improvements, facility expansion, value-added product development, farmland conservation easements, and agricultural best management practices for water quality
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County; some programs serve rural areas as defined by USDA (areas outside cities with 50,000+ population)
requirements_list: Operate or establish an agricultural business or related rural enterprise

For MVAPG-CAO: must be crop producer, agricultural cooperative, seafood/livestock processor, or timber products processor in business minimum 2 years; hemp fiber processors eligible if in business before June 30, 2020
For value-added programs: product must meet value-added definition through physical state change, differentiated production/marketing, product segregation, or biomass energy benefits
For USDA programs: typically require 25% match funding; some programs require 100% match
For Next Gen Program: must be beginning farmer purchasing farmland with conservation easement
For MUACLIG: requires participation of commercial bank, Farm Credit Association, or FSA in project financing
For MVAPG-USDA Option: must be eligible under USDA VAPG Program and receive USDA award to qualify for matching funds from MARBIDCO
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Washington County Department of Business Development at 240-313-2280 or 100 W. Washington Street, Suite 1401, Hagerstown, MD 21740 for information on specific programs. Different programs have different application processes: MARBIDCO-administered programs require applications through MARBIDCO; USDA programs accessible through respective USDA offices; Maryland agricultural programs through state agencies. Applicants should review program-specific guidelines and contact the relevant administering agency. For detailed information and current deadlines, consult the Agriculture Incentives & Financial Programs document at www.washco-md.net. Additional resources available through Tri-County Council for Western Maryland at www.tccwmd.org.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program that provides grants to eligible entities for projects aligned with Appalachia's economic and community development goals, including economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure, natural and cultural assets, and leadership capacity building.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for projects in five strategic areas: economic opportunities (entrepreneurial and business development), ready workforce (education, skills, and health), critical infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water/wastewater systems), natural and cultural assets (community and economic development), and leadership and community capacity. Prioritized project types include Technology Development, Broadband, Education and Workforce Development, Tourism, Energy, Recovery Ecosystems, and Traditional Infrastructure. Requires a 50% match from applicants, with matching funds identified and committed at time of application. Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact. Grant amounts may be reduced by the review committee to maximize the number of Washington County projects funded.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY27 Project Submission (Preliminary Project Description) is April 3, 2026; formal grant application due by November 15, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible entities in Washington County seeking to advance economic and community development projects aligned with Appalachian Regional Commission strategic goals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects related to economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water/wastewater, combined stormwater overflow systems), natural and cultural assets, leadership and community capacity building, technology development, tourism, energy, and recovery ecosystems. Projects should be part of an overall plan for stimulating economic development and demonstrate measurable outputs and outcomes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves Washington County, which is part of the Appalachian region eligible for ARC funding.
requirements_list: Project must align with one or more of five ARC investment goals (Building Appalachian Businesses, Building Appalachia's Workforce Ecosystem, Building Appalachia's Infrastructure, Building Regional Culture and Tourism, or Building Community Leaders and Capacity)
Project must align with corresponding state objectives and strategies from the 2024-2028 State Strategic Goals and Objectives
50% matching funds must be identified and committed at time of preliminary project description submission
Projects must demonstrate measurable outputs and outcomes using ARC's acceptable performance measures with quantifiable values and defined timeframes
Projects should be referenced to any plan and/or economic documents showing the project is part of an overall plan for stimulating economic development
Preliminary Project Description (PPD) and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources forms must be submitted to Washington County Office of Grant Management
Organization must demonstrate capacity to administer a federal grant, including description of recent awards
All matching fund commitment letters must be attached with the application
Applicant must provide minimum funding amount needed for project to move forward (for review committee consideration)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit Preliminary Project Description (PPD) and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources forms to the Office of Grant Management by April 3, 2026 (email to mkramer@washco-md.net). Confirmation email sent within 24 business hours. Projects are reviewed and ranked by Washington County Commissioners based on alignment with ARC goals and state objectives, measurable outcomes, and consistency with economic development plans. County-ranked projects are submitted to Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for regional ranking. Top-ranking projects receive a letter in early Fall inviting submission of a formal grant application to the Appalachian Regional Commission (due November 15, 2026). Applicants should consult the ARC 2024 Strategy Statement, State Strategic Goals and Objectives 2024-2028, and the Guide to ARC Project Performance Measures when preparing submissions.

structured_extraction.program_description: Washington County provides financial support to charitable organizations within Washington County that provide services which improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. The program implements a prioritized approach to funding local non-profits based upon addressing specific community needs, with emphasis on efficient use of funds and achieving results-based programmatic outcomes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Board of County Commissioners determines the annual allocation set aside for the Community Organization Fund. For Fiscal Year 2027, $1,200,000 is allocated across six priority service areas: Families and Children ($494,400), Domestic Violence ($386,400), Arts & Cultural ($135,600), Seniors ($136,800), Recreation ($33,600), and Other ($13,200). Awards are made to organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List (1-108 list). Grant awards are disbursed in four quarterly installments (25% each quarter) beginning July 2026. All funds must be expended between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027. Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of the total request amount. Applicants may request funding for operating expenses, capital expenses, or a combination thereof. Capital projects must be completable within the one-year funding period.
