structured_extraction.contact_name: Maria Kramer, Director, Office of Grant Management; Carsten Ahrens, Senior Grant Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charitable organizations located in Washington County that are included on the Board of County Commissioners Recognized Non-Profit List (Public Local Laws § 1-108). Organizations must be 501(c)(3) tax-exempt entities incorporated and in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support programs and services that improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. Eligible expenses include operating costs and capital expenses/projects that address one of the six priority service areas: Families/Children, Domestic Violence, Arts & Cultural, Seniors, Recreation, or Other. Funds may not be used for endowments or to benefit individuals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland only. Organizations must be located within Washington County and provide services to Washington County citizens.
requirements_list: Organization must be included on the Board of County Commissioners Recognized Non-Profit List (1-108 list)
Organization must be a charitable, non-profit entity recognized by the Internal Revenue Service as a 501(c)(3) with Valid status

Organization must be incorporated as a business entity with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and be In Good Standing at the time of application submission; proof required
Organization must have an office located in Washington County and provide services within Washington County
Application must be submitted during the published application window (by January 6, 2026 at 3:00pm)
Applicant must complete all required application forms and documentation and submit signature of authorized representative
Applicant must submit six hard paper copies and one electronic PDF copy of the complete application
Organization must not have unpaid liens, judgments, or past due obligations to Washington County Treasurer or any other government entity
Organization must have submitted required grant reports if funded in prior fiscal years (FY26 grantees must submit grant report by June 30, 2026)
Organization must submit most recent certified audit or detailed financial statement signed by fiscal representative
Organization must submit copy of IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter
Organization must submit proof of SDAT status in good standing
Organization must submit copy of most recent IRS Form 990
Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of total request amount
Organization must provide evidence addressing at least one of the six priority service areas
Letters of support are highly encouraged
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List receive Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) with application procedures and deadlines. The Office of Grant Management provides application materials online by December 1, 2025. Applicants complete the Community Organization Funding application packet which includes: Overview form, Statement of Need (1 page max), Past Performance (1 page max), Organizational Capacity and Staffing Plan (2 pages max), Program Plan (4 pages max), Collaborations/Partnerships section (1 page max), letters of support, authorized representative signature, FY27 budget spreadsheet, IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter, SDAT proof of good standing, most recent audit or financial statement, copy of IRS Form 990, and W-9 form (if applicable). Completed applications must be submitted in six hard paper copies (unsecured by staples, binder clips, or rubber bands in a manila envelope) and one electronic PDF copy, both by the deadline of January 6, 2026 at 3:00pm, to the Office of Grant Management, 100 West Washington Street, Room 1601, Hagerstown, MD 21740. Electronic copy must be emailed to cahrens@washco-md.net with cc to jmackereth@washco-md.net. OGM staff will not check applications for accuracy or completeness at time of submission; applicants must verify completeness using the Submittal Checklist. Applications are rated using a scoring rubric with maximum 100 points across criteria including Application Submission (10 points), Statement of Need (20 points), Past Performance (5 points), Organizational Capacity and Staffing (10 points), Program Plan (30 points), Collaborations/Partnerships (10 points), and Budget/Narrative (15 points). The COF Committee reviews and ranks applications. Funding awards will be determined when the Board of County Commissioners approves the County budget in May-June 2026. Applicants will be notified in writing upon completion of the budgetary process. Technical assistance workshops are offered (December 2, 2025 at 9:00-10:30am or 3:00-4:30pm via Zoom). Questions may be directed to mkramer@washco-md.net or cahrens@washco-md.net or 240-313-2040.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commuter and Shuttle Bus COVID RELIEF Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Supports Maryland commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus. Established in 2021 through bipartisan legislation with $8 million in state relief funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $8 million in state relief funding provided through the program established by bipartisan legislation in 2021.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland commuter and shuttle bus companies facing financial impacts from COVID-19
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Relief for financial impacts from COVID-19
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that works in conjunction with the Federal Farm Service Agency's CREP Contract Program to make CREP Contract Areas permanent through state-funded conservation easements. Landowners can add up to ten times the acreage in their CREP Contract to their CREP easement to maximize land preservation and easement value.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program makes CREP Contract Areas permanent through state-funded conservation easements. Landowners with existing FSA CREP Contracts can apply and may add up to ten times their contract acreage to their easement. Once sold, the easement remains effective in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with existing FSA CREP Contracts in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Conservation easements on CREP Contract Areas
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must have an existing FSA CREP Contract
Land must be eligible for CREP easement under program criteria
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners with existing FSA CREP Contracts apply through the County's Land Preservation Office. Once the easement is sold, it remains effective in perpetuity.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Gaming Commission distributes funds from The Washington County Gaming Fund to eligible charitable organizations and non-profits in Washington County. The Commission reviews applications and awards grants according to State Statute and County Regulations. Monies collected from tip jars are deposited into a dedicated Gaming Fund account, with 50% allocated to the Washington County Volunteer Fire & Rescue Association and the remaining 50% allocated to local charitable organizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are distributed from The Washington County Gaming Fund to eligible applicants. Maximum distribution per application is $100,000. Organizations may apply for multiple projects by submitting separate applications for each project. The specific amount and terms of awards are determined by the Gaming Commission during their review of applications. The grant performance period is one year from award announcement (typically early August). Any funds not spent within the performance period must be returned to the fund.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Susan M. Buchanan, Director; Staff contacts: J. Mackereth, S. Lapole, S. Buchanan
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) charitable organizations and non-profits located in Washington County that provide support for health and human services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, educational and cultural activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds must be used exclusively in Washington County and cannot be distributed outside of the County. Funds must be used for purposes that generally benefit health and human services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, or educational and cultural activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. All funds must be used exclusively in Washington County and cannot be distributed outside of the County.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) charitable organization with valid status, located in Washington County
Must provide services without discrimination on the basis of race, creed, sex, age, color, national origin, marital status, familial status, sexual orientation, or disability
Must submit a completed application form signed by an authorized official (President, Executive Director, CEO, Chairman, etc.)
Must comply with State Statute and County Regulations
Must provide organization's most recent annual financial statement showing revenue and expenses
Must provide a completed 2019 Gaming Fund Grant Report (or most recent year if applicable); if organization has never received Gaming Funds, must include statement confirming this
Must provide evidence of how funds most recently received from Gaming Commission were expended (invoices, proofs of purchase, or cancelled checks required)
Must provide completed W-9 form and Washington County vendor forms
Unincorporated associations must complete and submit a Notice of Responsible Person form
Organization must be a corporation, limited liability company, or unincorporated association
For corporations, articles of incorporation or organization must not be forfeited or not in good standing with State Department of Taxation

If booster organization or other entity partners with Washington County Public Schools, must provide letter signed by Superintendent indicating schools will hold no ownership rights to real property, goods, or materials (unless requesting funds for activity fees, transportation, or similar purposes)
Churches (religious entities) are not eligible; separate organizations operating within church facilities with own 501(c)(3) status may be eligible
Organizations holding annual tip jar operator's licenses are not eligible
Political or governmental organizations or sub-organizations are not eligible
Umbrella organizations are not eligible (except United Way of Washington County)
Maximum distribution per application is $100,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download application materials from the Office of Grant Management website at https://www.washco-md.net/grant-management/charitable-gaming-program/ beginning April 1, 2020. 2. Complete the Gaming Commission Grant Application form along with all required supporting documents including: signed request form, most recent annual financial statement, 2019 Gaming Fund Grant Report (or evidence of prior fund expenditures), W-9 form, Washington County vendor forms, Notice of Responsible Person form (if unincorporated association), and any additional supporting documentation. 3. Label each attachment according to requirements (REQUEST, FINANCIALS, GRPT, DOC, NORP, W-9). 4. Submit completed application electronically via email as a PDF to jmackereth@washco-md.net, copying slapole@washco-md.net, no later than 3:00 P.M. on May 6, 2020. No hard copies accepted. Applications with missing components may be denied. 5. Optional: Schedule a public hearing time with Office of Grant Management; hearing scheduled for June 23, 2020. Early scheduling recommended. 6. Gaming Commission reviews all applications and makes funding recommendations. 7. Final awards announced during Board of County Commissioners meeting in August 2020. Award letters sent and funds disbursed several weeks after announcement.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to organizations operating within Washington County for one-time projects or events that were not budgeted or anticipated. It helps organizations address current financial issues or situations requiring prompt response and resolution, and supports projects that would not otherwise qualify for other general fund community organization or hotel rental tax funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Board of County Commissioners appropriates a portion of the General Fund Contingency annually to be awarded to targeted organizations meeting the funding goals. Grant awards are limited to a maximum of $2,000. The total cost of your event or project may exceed this amount, but no amount greater than the maximum award can be approved. Grants are paid to the applicant, not to vendors for products or services. Unused funds must be returned to the Office of Grant Management within 30 days of the completion of the event. The portion of available funding may be adjusted annually at the discretion of the Board of County Commissioners.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Office of Grant Management
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations operating within Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One-time projects or events that were not budgeted or anticipated; addressing current financial issues or situations requiring prompt response and resolution
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Have an unexpected circumstance requiring prompt resolution
Have provided evidence that the request meets a critical need in the community
Do not have an alternative source of funding
Have proven to be a valuable community resource
Requests that benefit individuals are ineligible; this does not exclude individuals participating in a group event, activity, or project from receiving funding
Normal and routine operating and administrative expenses of an organization are ineligible
Organizations that support political candidates or organizations whose primary purpose is to influence or attempt to initiate legislation are ineligible
For-profit ventures are ineligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding. Complete the General Fund Contingency Funding Grant Application and submit it to the Office of Grant Management either online at www.washco-md.net, printed and mailed, or emailed. Upon receipt, the OGM will: 1) Determine if the applicant is qualified to receive funding; 2) Determine if the event or project is qualified to receive funding; 3) Determine if the request meets the funding goals of the County Commissioners; 4) Approve or deny the request with the concurrence of the County Administrator; 5) Notify the applicant in writing as to the approval or denial of their request. All organizations receiving grant funding will be required to complete a General Fund Contingency Grant Report and submit it with supporting documentation within 60 days of the completion of the event or project. If unable to provide this report within the allotted time period, the organization must notify the OGM of the deficiency along with a projected submittal date.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides financial incentives to property owners who undertake qualified rehabilitation work on historic properties located within designated historic districts or overlay zones in Washington County. The program offers stackable tax credits up to 70% when combined with state and federal credits.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Property owners who complete qualified rehabilitation work on historic properties can claim tax credits consisting of: 25% County Tax Credit, 20% State Tax Credit, 20% Federal Tax Credit, and 5% Additional Tax Credit for new construction (up to 70% total stackable credits). The program requires submission of a three-part application documenting the property's historic significance, proposed rehabilitation work (which must be approved before work begins), and final project completion with detailed expense documentation. Unused credits can be carried over for up to 5 years or until expended.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial property owners with historic properties in designated historic districts, Antietam Overlay zones, Historic Rural Villages, or eligible municipalities in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified rehabilitation expenses (QREs) including roof repair/replacement, chimney repair/replacement, window restoration, new storm doors/windows, masonry re-pointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental on historic properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties located within: Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay Districts, Antietam Overlay Zones (AO1 or AO2), contributing structures to surveyed and adopted Historic Rural Villages (Antietam, Cavetown, Fairplay, Highfield, Leitersburg, Pen Mar, Ringgold, Rohrersville, Sandy Hook, Tilghmanton), contributing structures within towns listed on the National Register of Historic Places with appropriate zoning and design guidelines, or structures under Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) Easement in Washington County
requirements_list: Property must be located in a designated Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay District, Antietam Overlay Zone, Historic Rural Village, eligible municipality, or under MHT Easement
Property must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties
Work must qualify as historic rehabilitation minimizing destruction of historic fabric with thoughtful and sympathetic design
Must submit three-part application with project documentation, photographs, and detailed expense records
Application for Part II (rehabilitation work description) must be submitted and approved BEFORE any work begins
Property owner must comply with all federal, state, and local laws including zoning, building, and safety codes
For Part III, must provide itemized expenses with copies of invoices/receipts and proof of payment for all project expenses (both eligible and ineligible)
If applicant is not fee-simple owner, must provide Owner's Representative Affidavit
Project completion and final documentation must be submitted within timeframe specified in Part II approval
Rehabilitation work must be consistent with Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and Washington County Design Guidelines for Historic Structures
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application consists of three parts submitted to the Washington County Historic District Commission at 747 Northern Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21742 or via email at askplanning@washco-md.net. Part I (Evaluation of Significance) establishes that the property qualifies as a historic structure in an eligible area (not required if property has HP Overlay). Part II (Description of Rehabilitation) must be completed and approved by the HDC before any work begins; it includes detailed descriptions of all proposed exterior work, estimated qualified rehabilitation expenditures, and supporting photographs and drawings. After work is completed, Part III (Request for Certification of Completed Work) is submitted with the final project data, itemized expense spreadsheet with all invoices and proof of payment, and photographs of completed work. The HDC reviews all documentation, may conduct site visits, and determines eligible expenses. The credit amount is then forwarded to the Treasurer's Office for property tax bill updates.

structured_extraction.program_description: A funding program that provides grants to stimulate tourism attractions, enhance economic development, and support cultural and recreational projects in Washington County. The program aims to help organizations undertake activities that would not be possible without special funding, with the goal of establishing events and activities that can eventually succeed independently.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County collects a 6% Hotel Rental Tax and reinvests these funds back into the community through grants to local municipalities, businesses, and organizations for tourism, economic development, and cultural and recreational projects. Grants are paid to the applicant, not to vendors. Grant applications requesting $25,000 or less are reviewed and approved by the Office of Grant Management with concurrence of the County Administrator. Applications requesting more than $25,000 are reviewed by the Office of Grant Management and County Administrator, with final approval by the Board of County Commissioners. Any changes exceeding 10% of approved line items require approval from the Office of Grant Management. Unused funds must be returned to the County within 30 days of project completion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding
structured_extraction.program_audience: Washington County local municipalities, businesses, organizations, residents, and visitors
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Developing tourism attractions, enhancing economic development, and supporting cultural and recreational projects. Grants can support: advertising and marketing for tourism attractions, strategic planning and research for tourism development, tourism-related facilities (conference centers, convention centers, visitor information centers), projects that enhance economic vitality through job creation and retention, cultural projects related to County history and culture, and recreational activities and events that promote tourism and lodging.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland only
requirements_list: Project must generate overnight stays in Washington County
Project must encourage support of County business, restaurants, and attractions
Project must reach a broad segment of the community
Project should seek multiple sources of support rather than rely solely on Hotel Rental Tax Funding
Project must yield benefits to the community proportional to resources invested
Project should promote cooperation among event organizers to reduce costs
Project must enhance or improve the community
Applicant must be a non-profit organization or government entity (for-profit ventures are ineligible)
Applicant cannot be an individual
Organization cannot support political candidates or have political influence as primary purpose
Organization cannot have budget deficits prior to application
Requests cannot fund normal and routine operating and administrative expenses
Requests cannot fund endowments
Organization must complete a Hotel Rental Tax Grant Report within 60 days of project completion with supporting documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding. The application can be accessed from the County's website under the Office of Grant Management, submitted by email, or printed and mailed. All applications are received by the Office of Grant Management (OGM). Upon receipt, the OGM will: (1) Determine if the applicant is qualified to receive funding; (2) Determine if the event or project is qualified to receive funding; (3) Determine if the request meets the funding goals of the County Commissioners and the purpose of Hotel Rental Tax Funding; (4) For requests of $25,000 and below, approve or deny the request with concurrence of the County Administrator; (5) For requests over $25,000, process the application and forward to the County Administrator for review, and upon favorable review the County Commissioners will hear the request; (6) Notify the applicant in writing of approval or denial. The application must be saved to the applicant's computer before completion to avoid loss of entered information. Recipients must submit a Hotel Rental Tax Grant Report with supporting documentation (budget itemizations and receipts) within 60 days of project completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that accelerates land preservation by allowing agricultural landowners in Washington County to sell agricultural preservation easements to the County and receive payment through an Installment Purchase Agreement over ten years at a fixed interest rate. The program is competitive and depends on the current economic climate.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases agricultural preservation easements on contiguous acreage (less one acre per existing dwelling) with payment via an Installment Purchase Agreement. Payments are made over ten years with ten percent of principal paid at settlement and ten percent paid annually for the remaining nine years at a fixed interest rate. The program is competitive and depends on the current economic climate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County seeking to sell development rights
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment and ongoing payments for the purchase of agricultural preservation easements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Owner must have agricultural land meeting minimum qualifications
Property must be entire contiguous acreage less one acre per existing dwelling
Must meet minimum qualifications
Program is competitive and depends on current economic climate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible landowners apply to sell an Agricultural Preservation Easement to the County. Once an offer is accepted, an Installment Purchase Agreement is written that specifies the total payment amount, fixed interest rate, and payment terms for annual installments over ten years (ten percent at settlement and ten percent annually for the remaining nine years).

structured_extraction.program_name: LMB ENOUGH Capacity Building Fiscal Year 2026
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding to support the Local Management Board's work in underserved communities by addressing gaps in healthcare access and transportation services. The program funds innovative projects that bridge transportation and healthcare to provide greater access to healthcare for seniors, individuals with disabilities, and low-income households with children who face significant mobility barriers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $40,000.00 available through 1-3 grants ranging from $10,000.00 to $40,000.00 per award. Total funding pool is $74,000.00. Performance period runs from May 15, 2026 through September 30, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and local government agencies providing services exclusively to Washington County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects addressing non-emergency medical transportation (NEMT) for primary care, dialysis, mental health services, or pharmacy pickups; expansion of existing transportation networks such as volunteer driver programs or specialized transit services; or last-mile solutions for underserved areas not reached by public transit. Funds support programs that improve healthcare access for seniors, individuals with disabilities, and low-income households with children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must provide services exclusively to residents of Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Be a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or local government entity
Be in Good Standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Provide services exclusively to residents of Washington County, Maryland
Demonstrate a proven track record of fiscal responsibility and programmatic impact
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application electronically to cahrens@washco-md.net by the deadline with all required documents including: Application Submission Form, program budget including funds not supplied by Washington County, letters of support, 501(c)(3) nonprofit determination letter from the IRS, and proof of Good Standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (screenshot of current SDAT page).

structured_extraction.program_name: MARBIDCO Next Generation Farmland Acquisition (Next Gen) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides down payment assistance to buyers of agricultural properties that qualify for the County's Ag District program. Buyers receive up to 51 percent of the land-only Fair Market Value appraisal of the property for purchase assistance, capped at $500,000.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides down payment assistance to agricultural property buyers. Assistance is 51 percent of the land-only Fair Market Value appraisal, capped at $500,000. After real estate settlement, the landowner must actively pursue a different permanent easement through an approved program and enroll in the County's Ag District program. If after seven years no permanent easement is procured, the land becomes preserved through a MARBIDCO permanent easement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young and beginning farmers and agricultural property buyers in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for the purchase of agricultural properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Buyer must provide a signed sales contract for the farm
Property must qualify for the County's Ag District program
Property must be eligible agricultural land
After settlement, landowner must actively pursue a different permanent easement within seven years and enroll in County's Ag District program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Buyers must provide a signed sales contract and complete the application with the County's Land Preservation Office, which then submits to MARBIDCO. The approval process takes approximately six months to complete.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF) - Direct Assistance to Local Jurisdictions
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to local jurisdictions for local economic development infrastructure and planning needs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Total assistance cannot exceed $3 million unless the jurisdiction is a qualified distressed county. Funds may be used for land acquisition, infrastructure improvements, acquisition of fixed assets, leasehold improvements, up to 70 percent of feasibility study costs, and up to 50 percent of local economic development plan preparation costs

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition, infrastructure improvements, fixed assets, leasehold improvements, feasibility studies, economic development planning
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland jurisdictions

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each jurisdiction may receive a grant of $250,000 annually. Local government must provide matching grant of funds to the local revolving loan fund
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and regional economic development agencies
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capitalization of local or regional revolving loan funds
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland jurisdictions
requirements_list: Applicant must be a county or regional economic development agency
Local government must provide matching funds

Financing provided by financial institution

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides certificates of deposit in certain rural areas with qualifying high unemployment as a funding source and pricing incentive for financial institutions to offer below-market rate loans to eligible small businesses
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Certificate of deposit provided to lender as funding source and pricing incentive. CD is not a guaranty or collateral to the loan

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business financing

Must be a small business

structured_extraction.program_description: Assists nonprofit organizations whose critical operations have been financially impacted by COVID-19 and the state emergency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Governor Hogan allocated $50 million to assist nonprofit organizations financially impacted by COVID-19 and state emergency.

structured_extraction.program_description: A transportation service that helps elderly people and individuals with disabilities meet their transportation needs by providing general purpose transportation for those who cannot use fixed-route buses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants purchase vouchers at a reduced rate that provide at least 50% savings compared to regular taxi fares. Vouchers come in various denominations and are used to pay drivers for rides with registered service providers. A set number of vouchers can be purchased each month.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People age 60 or older and individuals with disabilities who cannot use Washington County Transit fixed-route buses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General purpose transportation services using vouchers with registered taxi providers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or older OR have a disability
Must be unable to utilize Washington County Transit fixed-route buses for one or more reasons
If under age 60, must have application certified by a healthcare professional acknowledging disability
Must have an annually updated application on file
Applications expire June 30 of each year and must be renewed annually to continue using the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the WCT office at 240-313-2750 to request an application by mail, or visit 1000 West Washington Street, Hagerstown, MD in person to pick one up. If under age 60, have a healthcare professional certify your disability on the application. Mail or drop off the completed application at the WCT office (faxes not accepted). You will be notified by mail of your eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides up to a fifteen year tax credit on the County portion of real estate taxes for qualified businesses that either expand or locate in Washington County and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds. It helps attract new companies and supports existing companies that expand in Washington County.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to fifteen years of tax credit on the County portion of real estate taxes for qualified businesses that expand or locate in Washington County and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds. The credit amount and duration depend on the project tier: Tier 1 provides 55%, 40%, and 25% credits over 3 years for existing businesses expanding by at least 1,500 sq. ft. and creating at least 5 new full-time jobs within 12 months; Tier 2 provides 55%, 55%, 40%, 40%, 25%, and 25% credits over 6 years for new businesses obtaining at least 2,500 sq. ft. and creating at least 25 new full-time jobs within 24 months; Tier 3 provides 75% for the first five years, then reduced by 5% annually over the next 10 years until it reaches 25% (15 year total) for major investments of at least $20,000,000 in capital improvements and creation of at least 200 new full-time jobs within 24 months, with 80% of new full-time employees paid at least 200% of Maryland State minimum wage.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, before project construction is complete and before occupying space or hiring employees
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and existing businesses that expand or locate in Washington County and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied to the County portion of real estate taxes on the increased value of a business's real property after it expands or builds a new facility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The business property must be located in a Priority Funding Area in Washington County. Businesses located in an Enterprise Zone are not eligible for this program. Eligible properties must be newly constructed, renovated, expanded, or previously unoccupied and can be owned or leased.
requirements_list: Must be located in a Priority Funding Area
Cannot be located in an Enterprise Zone
Must apply before occupying space or hiring employees
Submit an intent letter on company letterhead
Submit completed application before construction is complete
Meet specific investment thresholds
Meet specific job creation thresholds
Either expand existing business or locate new business in the county
Tier 1 (Existing Business): Expand by at least 1,500 sq. ft. and create at least 5 new full-time jobs within 12 months paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage
Tier 2 (New Business): Obtain at least 2,500 sq. ft. of space and create at least 25 new full-time jobs within 24 months paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage

Tier 3 (New or Existing Business): Invest at least $20,000,000 in capital improvements and create at least 200 new full-time jobs within 24 months, with 80% of new employees paid at least 200% of Maryland State minimum wage
Must provide annual employment reports by February 1st to maintain the credit
Must continue to meet all applicable program requirements for each year receiving the tax credit
If business fails to meet requirements, credit is forfeited for that year and becomes due and repayable with interest at the rate applied to overdue property taxes
Any unpaid credit becomes a lien on the business entity's real and personal property
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Businesses must engage with the Washington County Department of Business and Economic Development early in their planning process. First, submit an intent letter on company letterhead to the Board of County Commissioners through the Department of Business and Economic Development. Then, submit a completed Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit Application and Employee Certification Report before project construction is complete and before occupying space or hiring employees. The Department will verify the company's eligibility and provide certification. After construction is complete, notify the Department and provide square footage documentation and a signed copy of the lease or similar document verifying the space. Create the required number of new full-time positions within 12 months (Tier 1) or 24 months (Tiers 2 and 3). Each year by February 1st, submit an Annual Employment and Certification Report including employee's first initial and last name, last four digits of Social Security Number or unique identification number, home city and state, start and end dates of employment, annual salary, number of hours worked during the reporting period, and indication of whether benefits are provided. This report is required for three taxable years after any year the tax credit was earned.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant and loan program that provides funding to capital infrastructure projects and business development projects to improve economic conditions in Western Maryland. Projects must create substantial economic impact with significant employment opportunities and/or increase the tax base in the region.
structured_extraction.agency: Western Maryland Economic Future Investment Board, Tri-County Council of Western Maryland
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and loans available for infrastructure projects (broadband, road access, utilities, property, building/housing construction) and business development projects. Infrastructure funding requires a minimum 20% match of total project costs from local government, business, or other sources. Business development funding requires a minimum 10% match of total project costs. New jobs created must pay at least 120% of State Minimum Wage. Minimum grant amount is $150,000, though projects below this may be considered case-by-case.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, organizations, and government entities in Western Maryland seeking to develop capital infrastructure or business development projects that create jobs and economic impact.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital infrastructure projects including broadband connectivity, road access improvement, utility connections, property purchases, building and housing construction and improvements. Business development projects that create new jobs paying at least 120% of State Minimum Wage.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Western Maryland region served by Tri-County Council of Western Maryland
requirements_list: Project must create new jobs paying at least 120% of State Minimum Wage
Infrastructure projects require minimum 20% match of total project costs from local government, business, or other sources
Business development projects require minimum 10% match of total project costs from local government, business, or other sources
Higher matching contributions receive preference
Project must demonstrate substantial economic impact with significant employment opportunities and/or increase to tax base
Minimum grant amount is $150,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Executive Director (Jake Shade), a Board member, or the Economic Development Director in the county where the project will take place. The Board reviews, evaluates, and rates applications. A new application process was adopted in January 2024.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 12-month FAA Part 147 certified training program that prepares students for Airframe and Powerplant (A&P) certification in aviation maintenance. The program is operated by the University of Maryland Eastern Shore at the Salisbury-Ocean City: Wicomico Regional Airport and creates a pipeline of qualified mechanics to enhance the aviation and aeronautics sector.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides 12 months of FAA Part 147 certified training to prepare students for Airframe and Powerplant (A&P) certification. The initial cohort began with 25 students in spring 2024, with the first graduating class in 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking training to become aviation maintenance technicians and certified mechanics.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and education in aviation maintenance and Airframe and Powerplant (A&P) certification.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Located at Salisbury-Ocean City: Wicomico Regional Airport (SBY) in Wicomico County, Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program for commercial property owners to finance clean energy improvements on their properties. The program establishes eligibility criteria, loan surcharge calculations, recorded agreements, collection procedures, and default protocols.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides loans to commercial property owners for clean energy improvements. Loans are structured with specific terms including a clean energy loan surcharge that is calculated based on program criteria. A recorded agreement is required as part of the loan process. Loan payments are collected according to program terms and collection procedures are established for the loans. Default protocols are specified to address non-payment situations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners in Wicomico County seeking to finance clean energy improvements on their commercial properties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Clean energy improvements and installations on commercial properties, including renewable energy systems and energy efficiency upgrades
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Wicomico County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be commercial
Property owner must meet program eligibility criteria
Property owner must record a clean energy loan agreement
Borrower must comply with loan payment terms and collection procedures

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that helps households struggling to afford internet service during the COVID-19 pandemic by providing a monthly discount toward broadband service and a one-time discount toward computer equipment purchases.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible households receive a monthly discount of up to $50 toward broadband service. Households can also receive a one-time discount of up to $100 to purchase a laptop, desktop computer, or tablet from participating providers if they contribute more than $10 and less than $50 toward the purchase price.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Households struggling to afford internet service during the COVID-19 pandemic who meet income or program participation eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Broadband service subscription costs and computer equipment purchases (laptop, desktop computer, or tablet).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available nationwide through participating broadband providers. This page is specific to Wicomico County, Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Household member has income at or below 135% of Federal Poverty Guidelines or participates in SNAP, Medicaid, or Lifeline
Approved for free or reduced-price school lunch or breakfast program including USDA Community Eligibility Provision in 2019-2020 or 2020-2021 school year
Received a Federal Pell Grant during the current award year
Experienced substantial loss of income due to job loss or furlough since February 29, 2020, with household income in 2020 at or below $99,000 for single filers or $198,000 for joint filers
Meets eligibility criteria for a participating provider's existing low-income or COVID-19 program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible households can apply in three ways: contact their preferred participating broadband provider directly, apply online at GetEmergencyBroadband.org to find participating providers, or call 833-511-0311 to request a mail-in application and return it with proof of eligibility documents to the Emergency Broadband Support Center. After receiving eligibility determination, households contact their preferred service provider to select an eligible service plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to help Wicomico County and Maryland better compete for large-scale economic development projects by reducing the time to construction by encouraging shovel-ready sites through upfront and creative financing. The program supports sites that are prepared and ready for immediate development by tenants or buyers, encouraging site preparation and improvements to attract qualifying industrial businesses and other large-scale economic development projects.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loan financing provided upfront to encourage preparation of large-scale industrial sites ready for immediate occupancy. Typical loan structure includes interest only for a period of time, with principal payment due once the property is sold or leased. Loan amount is typically determined by scope of work estimate provided by a licensed site development firm or individual. Loans must be fully collateralized as determined by committee. Final loan terms are determined by committee and based on project risk. Program is subject to fund availability. Proposed site improvements must be offered for lease or sale to attract qualifying industrial businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers, property owners, and project sponsors seeking to create industrial sites ready for immediate occupancy by manufacturing, logistics, or other industrial companies, as well as those pursuing large-scale economic development projects in Wicomico County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Site improvements and preparation to make industrial properties shovel-ready for tenant or buyer development, including utilities, transportation network readiness, site preparation, grading, drainage, stormwater management, erosion/sediment control, facility preparation, architectural design, and other development costs for economic development projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Wicomico County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Minimum ten acres or ability to support a minimum 100,000 square foot facility (ideally expandable to 200,000 square feet)
All utilities must exist and be located at the site (electric, natural gas, municipal water and sewer, fiber and internet)
All utilities must have capacity to accommodate significant new development
Transportation network must exist with capacity to accommodate significant new development
Zoning must be light industrial, heavy industrial, industrial park, or planned development district
Applicant must evidence legal site control
Proposed site improvements must be offered for lease or sale
Targeted economic sectors include manufacturing, logistics, or other industrial uses
Targeted minimum of 100 jobs
Targeted for single user occupancy
Site readiness for large-scale economic development projects
Loan must be fully collateralized as determined by committee
Loan must comply with fund availability
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact SWED directly at 410-749-1251 or info@swed.org to discuss specific projects, financing structures, and opportunities. Applicants should prepare comprehensive project information including project details, land ownership, deed and plat references, zoning classification, lot size, and coordinate with licensed site development firms or engineering firms for scope of work estimates. The application process involves providing land surveying information, comprehensive development plans, stormwater management plans, forest conservation plans, construction drawings, and other detailed site planning documentation as outlined in the SWED Shovel Ready Checklist.

Loans are available at favorable interest rates. A single application is used for all grant and loan programs. The program offers both grants and loans to help qualified homeowners make necessary improvements to their properties.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: General rehabilitation, home replacement, and lead abatement services for owner-occupied properties

Applicant subject to credit check

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Community Development Division for application forms and assistance. Submit complete application packet including: SLP Application form, Credit Check Form, and Lead in Your Home documentation if applicable. Applicants are encouraged to contact the Community Development Division for guidance and support throughout the application process.

structured_extraction.program_name: USDA Rural Development Housing Rehabilitation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Also known as the Section 504 Home Repair program, this program provides loans to very-low-income homeowners to repair, improve, or modernize their homes. It also provides grants to elderly very-low-income homeowners to remove health and safety hazards.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides subsidized loans to very-low-income homeowners for home repairs, improvements, and modernization. Grants are available to elderly very-low-income homeowners (age 62 or older) to remove health and safety hazards if they cannot repay a repair loan. Loans are provided at favorable terms with interest rates set by USDA. Maximum loan amounts and terms vary based on household income and project needs. Grants do not require repayment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Very-low-income homeowners in Wicomico County; elderly very-low-income homeowners age 62 and older for grants
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home repair, improvement, modernization, and removal of health and safety hazards from owner-occupied homes
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Wicomico County, Maryland (rural areas served by USDA Rural Development)
requirements_list: Must be the homeowner and occupy the home as primary residence
Must be unable to obtain affordable credit elsewhere
Household income must not exceed very-low-income limits set by USDA (income limits vary by household size and are published annually)
For loans: must demonstrate ability to repay
For grants: must be age 62 or older and unable to repay a repair loan
Property must be in a rural area as defined by USDA Rural Development
Must have acceptable credit history or extenuating circumstances explanation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the USDA Rural Development Hagerstown Office at (301) 797-0500 extension 4 for information and applications. Complete the Uniform Residential Loan Application (RD 410-4) and submit with required documentation including: employment and asset certification (RD 3550-4), authorization to release information (RD 3550-1), and completed checklist of items to accompany application (HB-1-3550). Income limits documentation must be provided. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
